rites.text: A caster draws a shadowing charm that weakens the sorcerous strength of every foe standing within its surrounding aura. It must be mastered before a companion charm can be attempted.

rites.name: Lorintus
rites.text: A scholar's discipline that sharpens restorative and guardian spellwork while dampening the cost of harmful incantations. It cannot be held alongside its shadowed counterpart, and taking one unravels the other.

rites.name: Neolum Risiarnum
rites.text: A bloom-sigil craft that a caster weaves to grant steady renewal to every ally standing within its glow. A tutor in a western trading quarter teaches it for a heavy purse of coin, and mastering it is a prerequisite for a deeper sister craft.

rites.name: Telesus
rites.text: A rare combined technique that only one trickster-hearted scout can perform. It fills every ally's power meter faster, and it pairs well with other meter-boosting talents, making it valuable in long and grueling fights.

rites.name: Valiareosor
rites.text: A practiced hand draws one beneficial enchantment off a foe and claims it for oneself. Certain deep arts resist this pilfering, and the trick can only be tried again after a long wait.

rites.name: Amanteosium
rites.text: A discipline of skill that only certain callings may learn, with some techniques found in hidden relics. Later revisions shifted many of its workings into other schools, while it gained older arts once kept apart, and one simple binding remains unchanged.

rites.name: Teliantus
rites.text: A tinted ward channeled through a hand-carved charm that sickens every foe standing within its drifting aura. The craft is taught to a seeker who finishes a trial among mountain shrines, and a sister technique can only be attempted after it is mastered.

rites.name: Meonor Solanum
rites.text: A practiced technique where a caster spends all of their inner energy to transform that spent reserve into a surge that either mends or wounds a chosen target. Only those trained in the discipline can perform it.

rites.name: Ameollia
rites.text: A channeled ward that a caster weaves over allies nearby, lending each of them sharper resistance to hostile sorcery while they remain close. It must be mastered before its twin craft can be taught.

rites.name: Taullernor
rites.text: A recurring hushed craft by which one figure steps between another and an incoming harm. It appears again and again in the traditions of this realm.

rites.name: Tausor
rites.text: These are borrowed techniques that a wielder can attach to their craft while within certain sacred ruins. Only two can be held at once, and they let a fighter take on roles foreign to their training, such as a guardian learning to mend allies or a healer learning to shield them.

rites.name: Cesaurnor
rites.text: A stilling craft that sends a charged pulse through nearby foes, leaving them unable to move or act for a time. Its lesser versions can be struck quickly by a single target, and some beasts and mages wield similar frozen glares.

rites.name: Tantesanum
rites.text: A soothing chant that a minstrel can learn once they reach a modest skill level. When sung, it strengthens the resistance of all nearby companions against toxins, and it can be sung again after a short pause.

rites.name: Serasanum
rites.text: A scroll-bound technique that releases a faint gust of air against a foe, usually barely harming it. It also weakens the target's defense against frost, and it belongs to a looping chain of similar techniques.

rites.name: Ciastum Naullises
rites.text: A fiery technique drawn from a single bearer's skill, releasing concentrated scorching force. It is commonly wielded by one particular practitioner in the order of artisans.

rites.name: Valernialum
rites.text: A bearer's form is overtaken by a masked, saw-wielding shape that lashes out with a poisoning strike. The transformation restores the bearer fully and grows stronger, but the bearer loses control.

rites.name: Lanornum
rites.text: A guardian craft that a rune-marked warrior can call upon at a high rank of skill. It soaks up the element of harm held within the wielder's marks, and it fades once a blow of that same element lands.

rites.name: Vestallium
rites.text: A withering incantation that a wielder draws from a cursed thorn, taking hold only when the target stands at the right threshold of its strength. Foes shielded by certain wards are immune to its dread.

rites.name: Vollia
rites.text: A caster's rite that grants a lasting boost to the aim of every ally standing close by. It is taught by a traveling sage in a frontier city, and a deeper rite must be mastered first before its paired counterpart can be learned.

rites.name: Corilia
rites.text: A ranged fire-craft spell that scorches a foe for minor heat harm and leaves them weaker against watery attacks. Its scroll can be taken from fallen armored raiders.

rites.name: Orelastum
rites.text: A timekeeping craft that unleashes a fixed burst of harm on foes gathered near a chosen mark. Its strength grows in refined forms, yet it stays modest for those still early in their training.

rites.name: Coriantosia
rites.text: A learned movement skill that lets a wanderer step onto any ground regardless of its rise or the wanderer's leap. Certain beasts and a hidden creature are born with it, and some rivals can command it too.

rites.name: Tauror Vaustianium
rites.text: A harmful enchantment that weakens the magical defenses of every foe standing within the reach of its caster. It must be mastered before its companion rite can be learned.

rites.name: Oreolauria
rites.text: A trick where a frozen companion is left behind while another walker roams ahead. Switching leaders at the right moment clears nearby foes, and a sidelined ally can be called back instantly to the lead.

rites.name: Laustanum
rites.text: A minor fire-striking art that burns a foe lightly and leaves them more vulnerable to watery harm. It belongs to a looping ring of linked techniques, each weakening the next.

rites.name: Orallires
rites.text: Certain people can read what others conceal in their minds. They summon a hidden double of the guarded person, visible only to them, which voices the secrets kept inside.

rites.name: Reolonum
rites.text: A learned support talent that lets a fighter gather extra training points after each successful deed. It must first be paid for with points earned by the fighter's basic calling, and a rare keepsake band can grant it to those who lack the lesson.

rites.name: Mistium
rites.text: A flaw in a mixing craft lets a second double-cast spell take the target of the first, so one chant can strike every foe or bless the whole band at once. Certain sacred spells, however, shatter the working entirely.

rites.name: Nalosor
rites.text: A dimming curse that weakens a bearer's arcane reserves by a small fraction per layer. Repeated applications accumulate up to ten layers, and it is the reverse of a surging blessing.

rites.name: Sorinum
rites.text: A companion power that a cunning ally can unleash in a burst, doubling the reserve of spiritual energy held by one chosen bearer. The surge grows stronger under later refinements and lingers until the clash ends or the bearer falls.

rites.name: Lentes
rites.text: A stealth art that a trained fighter draws on by spending a single cloth charm. It muffles the wearer's footsteps so listeners cannot pick them out, though watchers and those with keen ears still notice them.

rites.name: Vaullistium
rites.text: A dormant craft that copies whatever the last companion did in a skirmish, sometimes repeating it without cost. The practitioner bears no weapons of their own and relies on a few borrowed skills instead.

rites.name: Telesaulium
rites.text: A timed technique in which a fighter draws strength from the illusory copies they have conjured, gaining extra strikes per action and sharper aim against vulnerable spots for a short span.

rites.name: Lentium Laurarnes
rites.text: A scholar's technique that sharpens the destructive force of their sorcery at the cost of shorter lasting effect. Skilled practitioners can extend its duration, letting it strike harder over time.

rites.name: Mistor
rites.text: A closing strike that a fighter unleashes to end a combo chain. The fighter leaps, gathers power into both fists, and hurls the body into a blazing punch that bursts against a single foe.

rites.name: Nolliria
rites.text: A bound crystal lens lets its wielder seize the will of a foe for a time, steering the captured creature to act as the wielder directs. Such mastery opens the way to copying the strange powers held by hostile beings.

rites.name: Telialum
rites.text: A healer draws vitality from their own body and pours a greater measure of it into an ally. The gift can only be given again after a long wait, and practice shortens that wait.

rites.name: Oronilor
rites.text: A paired technique where a sword-wielding warrior and a nimble ninja combine strikes and storm-like blasts on one foe. It costs shared charges, broadens its area, and lifts the partners toward stronger finishing arts.

rites.name: Listus
rites.text: A fighter unleashes a rapid chain of rolling kicks, a spinning leap, and a diving spiral that batters a foe and shatters its guard. It requires no charged gauge and is held as the strongest technique in its wielder's arsenal.

rites.name: Mistus
rites.text: A reflexive craft that lets a performer's arcane strength swell whenever they are struck. Its learning must be paid for with accumulated experience gained in the bard's art.

rites.name: Cillantus
rites.text: A foul rot-spell once drawn by sorcerers to sicken foes. It has since been stripped from use, leaving only the memory of its sickly cloud.

rites.name: Valelus Liarneoles
rites.text: A combined technique that a quick-handed scout can unleash in a burst of focus, lifting the whole company's reserves of inner energy to twice their former capacity. A stronger variant later rises from it.

rites.name: Cianisum
rites.text: A brewed surge of vigor that doubles every companion's maximum life force. It lasts until the fight ends or a companion falls, and no cleansing draught can undo it.

rites.name: Noseontium
rites.text: A coordinated burst of shielding and quickening that one companion unleashes across a whole band of allies. It holds until one of them falls or the clash ends, and a lingering drag on the group is swapped for swiftness.

rites.name: Collium
rites.text: A tuned surge drawn through a gathered mix, cutting the vitality of every foe present to a quarter-remainder. Some hardened forms shrug it off, and sharpened blades can let it strike beyond ordinary ceilings.

rites.name: Cernauntes
rites.text: A wielder instantly blinks to a chosen foe without any recharge delay. Pressing a strike key mid-blink turns the jump into a hard blow, and a spell key turns it into a ranged burst.

rites.name: Nastor
rites.text: A paired technique where one fighter gathers force by holding the strike button, then releases a heavy blow that spends no timing gauge. A companion's partner strike offers a longer reach with less punch.

rites.name: Sestum
rites.text: A companion's knack for scavenging spoils from clashes, where finds grow richer as the scavenger's talent deepens. Lesser gains come from roaming the wilds, and refined skill can double a haul.

rites.name: Corarnolia
rites.text: A bond forged by fusing two gentle relics that siphons vitality from a foe to restore the wielder. Among the undead, however, the flow reverses and the wielder's own life drains away.

rites.name: Oraustes
rites.text: A harsh burst of destructive force that strikes instantly across a wide circle, scorching everything caught within its reach.

rites.name: Milleostus
rites.text: A practiced caster can briefly sharpen the aim of their next hex-like incantation. Once used, the technique must rest for a long interval before it can be called upon again.

rites.name: Reontor
rites.text: A carved focus stone that lets its bearer call down spells which harm foes and leave them weakened. Linked to other stones, it can shorten the lingering sickness or cast the spell automatically.

rites.name: Serium Cialastium
rites.text: A rare craft reserved for one wandering sorceress who cannot be taken up by others. Practitioners of it deliver crushing harm to lone foes and to whole crowds alike.

rites.name: Mistus Telinum
rites.text: A wandering craft built around a long rod that stretches its reach at will. Practitioners break down armored foes and herd crowds, and their skill with the rod lowers the strain of each technique.

rites.name: Riantolia
rites.text: A companion's surge of power lifts every ally with shielding, speed, and steady mending for twenty turns. The gift holds until a fallen ally or the close of the fight, though it can be unraveled and is lost if a stone-bound companion is revived.

rites.name: Amiantor Cellium
rites.text: A defensive technique where a wielder dodges an incoming blow and answers with a counterstrike. The wielder leaps off a companion for momentum, then lunges forward with a bladed star-throw.

rites.name: Coraleonus
rites.text: A ceremonial role that rallies companions to strike together for heavy blows. Its wildest gift is a gamble, sometimes restoring the whole band and sometimes ending them all.

rites.name: Sereornia
rites.text: A swordsman's trained skillset of martial techniques that ignore his battle position. Some of its moves are shared with a comrade's command set, and it pairs with a second skill of magic blades.

rites.name: Miastanum
rites.text: A set of lasting conditions that either strengthen or weaken a bearer's abilities and actions. Some arise from strikes, others from dedicated rites, and a few can be lifted by healers while others cannot.

rites.name: Rirnus Ristum
rites.text: A bard's trained technique that locks the next song they perform against being replaced by other melodies. The effect lingers briefly and can be renewed quickly.

rites.name: Sirnus Oriaselor
rites.text: A craft where practitioners draw forth bound presences to fight at their side. The presences drain a trickle of reserve energy to stay, while a few appear only once to unleash a single strike and then fade.

rites.name: Vaustanum Sellum
rites.text: A mystic discipline of rippling hexes that weaken foes and bolster allies. It can be paired with a tactical calculating method, and it answers a counter-casting art only while the caster keeps a clear mind.

rites.name: Sarnus
rites.text: A performance technique used during staged shows that dazzles onlookers with harmless illusions of powerful arcane forces. It temporarily takes the place of a thieving skill and gives each performer a single signature trick.

rites.name: Serarium
rites.text: A quiet drain that weakens a bearer's raw force by a twelfth per layer, with up to ten layers piling up unseen. It mirrors an older sibling curse, though its workings shift slightly from one contest of arms to another.

rites.name: Cialiranum
rites.text: A learned discipline that a caster gains through a mentor's training, letting spells be readied in half the usual time. Some powerful guardians of the realm are born possessing it naturally.

rites.name: Tantes
rites.text: A steadying craft that lets a caster finish an incantation without being broken by blows. It also shrugs off most shoves and pulls that would drag the practitioner across the field.

rites.name: Rasauranum
rites.text: A tongue-driven craft in which practitioners wield persuasive speech as their main weapon, alongside firearms. Through it, a skilled speaker can win over wild beasts to join their company, as well as people.

rites.name: Tilia Niarnum
rites.text: A practiced technique that sharpens a caster's aim with hidden spells and softens the notice their workings draw from foes. It lasts a short span and can only be invoked again after a long pause.

rites.name: Vausarium
rites.text: A loose grouping of techniques that fit neither bodily strength nor sorcery. Its practices are meant to work together, linked by a shared theme such as an affinity for a particular element.

rites.name: Relanum
rites.text: A borrowed secondary craft that a practitioner can attach alongside their main discipline. It grants extra abilities drawn from a second skillset, and it appears across many traditions.

rites.name: Orineostes
rites.text: A recurring tactic where a team of fighters is steered into a fragile state so they can take endless turns. It requires several units with fast reactions, careful gear choices, and a chain of precise spells.

rites.name: Orausium Amintia
rites.text: A guarded posture that hardens a fighter against ailments matching the sigils they currently carry. Each additional matching sigil deepens the shield, so stacked wards make a bearer nearly immune to a chosen affliction.

rites.name: Lausostor
rites.text: A dread that seizes a creature and locks its body in place for a short span. It cannot be cleared early and must simply run its course.

rites.name: Serianesum
rites.text: Two companions join for a combined assault upon a foe. One leaps and slashes while the other fires an explosive shot, and their shared strike lifts their power as they grow stronger together.

rites.name: Ameostium
rites.text: A rider's bond with a winged beast lets a protective stone-like hide form over the mount for a short span. The hide can be called again only after a long wait.

rites.name: Valisia Viasania
rites.text: A learned craft that lets a practitioner channel two opposing schools of sorcery more efficiently for a time. Charges of prepared tactics are spent without being used up, and they return afterward. The craft can be invoked again once an hour passes.

rites.name: Vostarnus
rites.text: A learned craft that lets a practitioner swap gear while in the middle of a contest, though doing so costs them their next move. Once mastered through study, other trades can adopt the same skill.

rites.name: Corollanum
rites.text: A scroll-bound spell that douses foes with a faint burst of watery harm and softens their guard against lightning. It belongs to a linked ring of spells in which each one weakens the next.

rites.name: Amariarnus
rites.text: A combat art in which a fighter's blade takes on the power and element of a sorcerer's incantation. Each strike gains the strength of the spell that the partnered mage has learned, adding its force to every swing.

rites.name: Telantor
rites.text: A randomly granted chance for an ally to act during its turn, shaped by where it stands among friends and foes. Using it prompts a line of speech, and it blocks chests and terrain interaction while available.

rites.name: Niranum Amosterum
rites.text: A practitioner slowly trades bodily vitality for a reserve of arcane energy, which can be drawn back later. The transfer halts once a set share of their strength has been banked, and the stored reserve fades after a while.

rites.name: Amaullia Corauntiles
rites.text: Two companions strike a pose to gather their energy, then conjure a small mechanical beast and fling it forward inside a whirling gust. The strike drains foes and grants the pair boundless mana for a short while.

rites.name: Vernasia
rites.text: A practiced trick that lets the caster's next incantation take effect at once, with no pause for the words to settle. It is used in the moment before a spell would otherwise be delayed.

rites.name: Telisenia
rites.text: A bound reserve of raw power that a fighter may unleash in a single overwhelming burst once their strength has been fully built up. Such bursts are the ultimate expression of a warrior's craft.

rites.name: Amolus Lentirnor
rites.text: A shadow-weaving technique that conjures several duplicate figures around its caster. Each duplicate absorbs one incoming blow or single-target spell, while area-wide spells instantly dispel the illusion.

rites.name: Reoria Loliarnum
rites.text: A recurring supreme deception associated with one fearsome warrior, often used as a final desperate technique. It was first wielded in a later age, when a foe faced it as a formidable boss.

rites.name: Neoriarnium
rites.text: A soft-voiced companion technique in which a bonded spirit-servant performs a calming verse at first light. It belongs to a scholar's craft and is performed by that scholar's dawn-kindled familiar.

rites.name: Tilor
rites.text: A learned warding craft that softens harm from fire, frost, and storm based on the sigils carried by the practitioner. Its ward lasts a short while and draws the attention of foes nearby.

rites.name: Valeosalor
rites.text: A bonded beast unleashes a focused blow against one foe. The attack is a technique a summoner's companion performs in combat.

rites.name: Corollantus
rites.text: A borrowed craft that lets a learner use any stolen technique freely for a minute at a time. The craft can only be invoked again after a long rest.

rites.name: Ceoniarnum
rites.text: A shadow-craft that a stealthy fighter invokes to draw enemy attention toward themselves while sharpening their evasion. It blunts the foe's lethal strikes, but it dulls the fighter's own aim.

rites.name: Sereostium Orentiasium
rites.text: A dark art that pulls a fallen ally across the ground to the caster's side, useful when the body lies somewhere dangerous. It fails if the fallen one refuses it or has already been restored by a healing rite.

rites.name: Niasum
rites.text: A bond-craft that lets a tamer's companion beast act without delay and with full vigor for a brief span. Its wielder may call a creature to its side the moment the craft is woken, and the beast's readiness will not be drained by these commands.

rites.name: Amesor Morilor
rites.text: A flaw lets a hidden ward bypass a rule that normally limits revival charms to the fallen. Those charms then mend a fraction of the concealed one's strength, and the cloaking fades once the charm lands.

rites.name: Coreostum Telerium
rites.text: A flawed lightning trick that almost never lands, failing against nearly every foe. Only one hulking iron brute can be struck by it, and then only when the user's power far exceeds its foe.

rites.name: Raurnus Lialor
rites.text: A draining technique that tries to sap an opponent's strength so their blows grow feeble. It can be repeated on the same foe, though some guarded creatures resist it.

rites.name: Raliarnus
rites.text: A dark technique that wounds a foe and leaves them clouded by a creeping deadness. It draws on a small reserve of inner energy to cast.

rites.name: Oriarisanum
rites.text: A caster conjures three duplicate figures that absorb incoming blows, causing single strikes and lone spells aimed at them to miss. Sudden area-wide magic erases the protective duplicates instantly.

rites.name: Ristiania
rites.text: A dimming affliction that spreads half of each blow taken onto nearby companions. It only binds to foes who have allies to share the burden with, and it lingers after the fight until a particular remedy cures it.

rites.name: Tontum
rites.text: A forceful blow drives a fighter into a solid barrier, causing extra harm on impact. The victim may be briefly protected from further strikes while recovering.

rites.name: Lestor Ciastalor
rites.text: A ranger's surge that lets every ally strike and mend for a fixed maximum amount on each blow. The effect holds until the battle ends or the bearer falls.

rites.name: Pelastar
rites.text: Pelastar is a sun-bleached salt-plain ringed by a lattice of hollow iron towers that hum when the wind passes through them. Its settlers, the Ossuary Wardens, ration rainwater and trade in glassy brine-crystals that dampen nearby sound.

rites.name: Orarnes
rites.text: A chanting tune serves as the battle anthem that drives the foes of a grand trial. It is sung by a single performer, with lyrics written in a recognizable tongue.

rites.name: Misia
rites.text: A battle resource that a fighter spends to strike. Spending one allows a basic blow, while spending three unleashes a full assault. It slowly regenerates over time and is fully restored whenever a fighter grows stronger.

rites.name: Rianteoles
rites.text: A closing battle hymn sung against a final foe, stitched together from earlier melodies of a long saga. Listeners hear old tunes returning in a new arrangement, with fresh chanted words of praise.

rites.name: Amonallium
rites.text: A fighter unleashes a rapid volley of eighteen strikes that scatter across random foes, each landing with reduced force. It delivers more separate blows than any other technique in its world.

rites.name: Caullor
rites.text: A command that lets the group swap which member guides them in the middle of a fight. It can also be called up outside battle through the menu, and it fires on its own when one of the two chief companions falls. Certain bonded creatures are barred from taking the lead.

rites.name: Mostasum
rites.text: A battle state that a fighter enters after unleashing a powerful signature strike. While it lasts, the fighter's stats rise and their basic actions change into special moves tied to that strike.

rites.name: Tosiarium
rites.text: A bright aura spreads from a wielder of a fully empowered, radiant tool or ward, lending a brief boost to nearby allies. The wielder alone is left under a dampening veil that blocks the glow.

rites.name: Vauntium
rites.text: A paired strike where a swordsman swings three times in a rapid chain while his partner fires at the blade, sending the shots bouncing into the foe. A rival partner's roaring slam can take its place.

rites.name: Maulasanum
rites.text: A signal-sung rite that bolsters every companion in the company, filling them with a steadying courage. It is taught to a dozen beings of varied temperament and can be passed on to other allies of the same kind.

rites.name: Mastauntes
rites.text: A condition that tears a combatant out of the fight entirely, through sundering, detonation, or banishment to elsewhere. Once scattered, no one can bring them back, and certain foes are untouchable by it.

rites.name: Valaunium
rites.text: A soft glowing charm that a pair of wandering casters can learn, and it shortens the stretch of time a person stays unable to see. Its strength shifts with how skilled the caster is at bolstering allies, and a stronger form is available to healers.

rites.name: Lisarnus
rites.text: A fighter's command strike that unleashes four rapid blows on scattered foes. It ignores the battle line and can be unlocked through a crystal charm.

rites.name: Telisor
rites.text: A transient disguise that reshapes a traveler's look and blocks most actions while it lasts. In its harsher form, it binds a wearer to an enemy's appearance and forces them to fight for it.

rites.name: Cialarium
rites.text: Companions strike a posed flourish after each triumph in a skirmish. The chosen flourish depends on the garb they are wearing, and each person has signature stances for every outfit.

rites.name: Amalia
rites.text: A paired strike where a small wary companion springs onto a warrior's shoulder before a mechanical helper drops down and slams the foe in a blast. The duo gains boundless spirit for a short while.

rites.name: Telerus
rites.text: A guardian's helper spirit can be called forth to lend a healing aid to allies. It acts as a supportive technique tied to a summoned companion.

rites.name: Neollornum
rites.text: A gunner charges a blazing orb of energy while aiming at a foe, then hurls it into a massive explosion. The strike needs no gathered power to unleash.

rites.name: Teontirus
rites.text: A bound seeker enters a frozen, timeless sleep after finishing a sacred task, and the sleep is said to grant endless life. Mighty beings can enter or grant this stillness at will, while the stone-bodied fate that follows failure falls only on the bound.

rites.name: Amoreollor
rites.text: A craft that lets a wanderer shape new companions from raw spirit-matter. Those forged creatures and people can then be enlisted to fight alongside the traveler.

rites.name: Casiarium
rites.text: A catalog of temporary conditions that afflict or aid fighters during clashes. Their marks glow red for harmful effects and blue for helpful ones, and every condition eventually fades or can be cleared away.

rites.name: Amaunternia
rites.text: A fighter's desperate final technique that unleashes a burst of flame before a sword strike. It can be drawn on earlier than most warriors' last resorts, and the flame is only for show.

rites.name: Leosia Misor
rites.text: A swift shadow-trained fighter gathers a companion's strength into a charged burst of elemental power, then releases it as a flying bolt at a foe. Another technique lets the fighter coordinate throwing blades with allies.

rites.name: Tauntes
rites.text: A battle rite that lifts the burden of mana cost from one ally, so every spell and skill they use drains nothing. The rite holds until that ally falls or the clash ends.

rites.name: Lontausor
rites.text: A hidden gauge inside a fighter's frame that quietly rises as they weaken, deciding how often their surge ability flares and how hard they strike. It stays unseen by the bearer and ignores the summoning of the great guardian spirit.

rites.name: Laustontia
rites.text: A secondary strike that erupts automatically after a matching ability is performed. It arrives instantly and strikes either the same foe or the weakest remaining enemy, and it never misses when it is a physical blow.

rites.name: Narostanum
rites.text: A second-tier restorative technique used by a nimble fighter that mends every ally at once, returning half of each one's full vitality. It is the only mending skill this fighter possesses.

rites.name: Meres
rites.text: A bright green flash erupts from a summoned crystal beast and strikes one chosen foe. The blow wounds the target without touching anyone else nearby.

rites.name: Tones
rites.text: A paired assault in which a swordsman and a beast strike an enemy together. The swordsman swings three times while the beast unleashes sharp magic blows.

rites.name: Sireosum
rites.text: A stealthy fighter draws a wary foe's attention less while striking from behind, gaining sharper aim and deadlier blows. The boost lasts a few minutes and fades when the fighter changes regions.

rites.name: Telestes
rites.text: Two allies join forces, one striking with a blade while the other hurls throwing stars, then a shower of arcane energy falls upon the foe. The strike drains three shared charges and leaves the target dazed for longer.

rites.name: Tanauntum
rites.text: A joint assault that a traveler can unleash alongside companions and a trained mount when allies are present. It can be performed throughout the main journey and its expansions.

rites.name: Oraurnum Tentium
rites.text: A bound incantation that speeds the movements of every creature whose rank divides evenly by five, whether allied or hostile. It drains a modest reserve of inner essence and can be acquired from a sealed sorcerer's staff at a costly price in accumulated learning.

rites.name: Liserum
rites.text: A skill set reserved for one kind of fighter who wields ranged launching tools. Many of its techniques carry supporting effects that can tip a battle, and they fire instantly but drain a considerable amount of mental energy.

rites.name: Meosoles
rites.text: A shadow craft that clouds a single foe's sight, lowering their aim by thirty. It is the stronger form of an earlier veil and is learned from a rare scroll.

rites.name: Mellum Rastinor
rites.text: A concealed force that lies unseen within certain strikes. It cannot be perceived directly, and only a rare arrangement of linked stones reveals it, and later versions remove it entirely.

rites.name: Tilliares
rites.text: These are temporary techniques that can only be called upon within marked zones. They succeed older borrowed arts and can let a warrior heal allies or a healer shield them, shifting who fills which role.

rites.name: Venirnus
rites.text: A tier of restricted techniques that sits between the basic battle arts and their fully awakened forms. Practitioners unlock these middle skills before progressing to the most advanced version.

rites.name: Corarum
rites.text: A combat technique used in contests between rival fighters, allowing a warrior to restore their own strength during a duel. It is practiced only within sanctioned arena matches.

rites.name: Seriastum Coriantium
rites.text: A paired leap where a fighter is hoisted by an ally and launched into the air. The lifted fighter then strikes upward, gaining quick control of aerial battle without spending any battle energy.

rites.name: Telernia Vauntanum
rites.text: A rare surge that doubles the bearer's life force and sharpens the strength and guard of all allies at once. It cannot be undone and holds until the battle is decided or the bearer falls.

rites.name: Valerus
rites.text: A paired technique where a beast-kin and a swift acrobat spend three shared charges to unleash a flurry of strikes. The target is lifted skyward and then slammed back down, while nearby foes are caught in the blast.

rites.name: Amosium
rites.text: A cold strike drawn from a bearer's collected notes, dealing light harm without draining reserves. It turns the wielder's incantations into a chilling bolt and can be unleashed while leaping through the air.

rites.name: Taleontor
rites.text: A bearer carries up to three glyphs at once, each tied to one of eight forces of nature. While holding them, their strikes carry that force, and they resist attacks from forces the glyphs oppose.

rites.name: Amaurernium
rites.text: A combined draught that makes a target wildly frenzied, and the frenzy overrides every protection. Foes made to drink it can stop performing their scripted actions during a fight.

rites.name: Amollium
rites.text: A timed warrior's stance that greatly raises the chance of deflecting incoming blows. Each successful deflection draws extra attention from enemies.

rites.name: Tintiarium
rites.text: A hidden combat effect that makes a fighter flinch, freezing them in place and cancelling whatever they were preparing. Any gauge charge or energy already spent is lost when this happens.

rites.name: Nostanum
rites.text: A flaw in a mind-craft lets a caster's reserve sink past empty into a vast negative well. Spells grow castable through the debt, until the hidden reserve is spent, and any ordinary casting from the wider menu closes the loophole.

rites.name: Raunia Vonteollus
rites.text: A small mechanical sigil that ticks forward whenever a companion senses foes about to appear. Its phases grant the group a head start in combat, and striking first a hundred times in a row earns a special mark of honor.

rites.name: Sialia Tiantum
rites.text: A combined ward granted to a whole company, letting it turn aside four kinds of elemental force. Each shielding can be stripped away, and it fades once it has absorbed a blow of its matching element.

rites.name: Meolarnanum
rites.text: A flaw in a looping charm splits each strike across four random foes at half force. Certain blades ignore that halving, while a thief's grab sometimes lets only the first prize through and blocks the rest.

rites.name: Telisones
rites.text: A guardian technique that a healer invokes to shield her whole company from blows for a short span. Its power grows with the bond the caster shares with her allies.

rites.name: Cianirnia
rites.text: Two fighters pair up and grip a great blade together, then leap at a foe and hurl it skyward in a spinning flip. The strike drains no reserves, letting them channel power freely for a short spell.

rites.name: Costeolor
rites.text: A glitch where a sleeping ally's wounds and mana are fully mended by a dance, while every other affliction is cleared without any sign of it. Those without sleep seem to take no effect from the dance.

rites.name: Maulor Taselum
rites.text: A borrowed power that lets a bearer call forth a great spirit's strength in battle. Each spirit may only be bound to one bearer within a single company at a time.

rites.name: Ciarnales
rites.text: A charged state that a fighter can enter after a first strike, boosting the next follow-up blow. Striking again unleashes a devastating called-forth assault and ends the charge, which also fades when the fighter's frenzy runs out.

rites.name: Laustum
rites.text: A bound charm of two allied fighters who leap together in a joint strike. When the paired attack lands, it refills one partner's readiness gauge.

rites.name: Valenium
rites.text: Borrowed roles that a traveler can wear for a single stretch, each with its own rising rank and unique tricks. Mastering several of them grows a stacking strength for the wearer in one hidden realm.

rites.name: Naulanus
rites.text: A recurring ability that lets a single wielder vanish from one spot and reappear at another in an instant. It is mainly practiced by one gifted heir of a royal bloodline.

rites.name: Nasus Mauntistor
rites.text: A coordinated ranged-and-close attack where a marksman fires an energized shot that a swift partner channels into a rush, striking an area and raising the pair's surge level.

rites.name: Oriastum Serenteosum
rites.text: A hardening curse turns a bearer to rigid stone, leaving them unable to act until it is lifted. When every member of a company is stilled, the journey ends in defeat.

rites.name: Telantes
rites.text: A bodily hindrance that locks a fighter in place so they cannot take any action. It fades faster than a full halt, and while it lasts the fighter's surge meter does not build from harm taken.

rites.name: Telasialia
rites.text: A tiered shadow-art scroll that loosens a curse of rain-like harm and a lattice of glassy spells, tapping foes' resistance to crackling storm energy.

rites.name: Telentus
rites.text: A charged reserve that builds quietly during a fight and can be spent to surge a fighter into a stronger state. The more fully it is stored, the longer the surge lasts, and it also makes certain skills cheaper to use.

rites.name: Niastes
rites.text: A timed reserve that governs how long a bound spirit can stay and fight beside its caller. It drains steadily and shrinks further each time the spirit is struck, and paired spirits share one reserve.

rites.name: Saunes Amaullia
rites.text: Two allies unite to split a shimmering duplicate of one of them, which strikes a foe while a ranged burst follows. Afterward, the pair gain endless reserves of spirit energy and their battle meters are filled at once.

rites.name: Orilum
rites.text: A bonded controller's craft that exchanges the charge held by a practitioner and their mechanical companion. It is a learned skill that can only be used again after a long pause.

rites.name: Orostus
rites.text: Two companions combine their strengths, one lifting a mechanical plush creature and hurling it down in a blast that strikes a wide area. The move can be enhanced to unlock stronger combined techniques.

rites.name: Ciaranum Nillia
rites.text: A bearer can reshape a bonded creature into a stronger form and return it to its original shape. Each altered form grants different strengths and skills.

rites.name: Caulum
rites.text: Fighters strike a celebratory stance after winning a clash. Companions copy these gestures after finding a hidden cache, and the champion of the arena performs one after each victory.

rites.name: Ternasum
rites.text: A dread-bind that freezes a foe in place until the binder acts again, and it hardens after each success. Those bound cannot strike back, though they may still slip past blows.

rites.name: Vaurniallum
rites.text: Two allies link their readiness meters so each fills and spends its charge quickly, letting them act faster for a short while. Different pairings of companions unlock the bond through separate training paths.

rites.name: Sestor
rites.text: A battle craft that grants every ally a watchful guard state for a set span of time. It can be cast by support fighters and summoned allies, and it passes to other support creatures.

rites.name: Saullum Celasus
rites.text: A bearer merges with raw primal forces and becomes overwhelmingly powerful for a short span. Even heavy blows fail to harm them, though foes can still bring them down through lingering afflictions.

rites.name: Kelonedath
rites.text: Kelonedath is a ferocious close-quarters discharge technique, born in the grim industrial districts of Thudarneld, where crews learned to spend every reserve of stored tension in one violent blow. The strike lands with a bone-cracking shock, and a second, delayed wave of pressure hurls the target across the street a few heartbeats later.

rites.name: Fenedaron
rites.text: Fenedaron is a grounded event in the Thudarneld universe, a rapid barrage of three staggering impacts delivered in a single breath before a whirling descent that shakes the ground. Its force is kept within the reach of a small crew of champions, enough to break stone walls and scatter a line of armored foes. Each act is a measured flourish meant to pin down a crowd of opponents.

rites.name: Brarock
rites.text: Brarock is a thunder-drum rhythm that the people of Thudarneld perform when a storm bell tolls seven times over the reeds. Dancers sidestep a falling kettle-hammer, then surge forward and spring skyward, landing a crushing blow that rattles the opponent's footing. The move is taught only to apprentices who have learned to read the drum's silence.

rites.name: Fenaldoren
rites.text: Fenaldoren is a rite of recall in which a community of mourners sings a dead bell-ring back into resonance, drawing a fallen soul through a long, deliberate hush. The chant takes eight full breaths, so the rite is often paired with kin who hasten the ringing by lighting ember-lamps. In desperate hours the singers may spend no oil at all, letting the ritual's cost fall to nothing.

rites.name: Pelaldusten
rites.text: Pelaldusten is a grounded event in the Thudarneld universe where a crackling surge of raw sorcerous pressure is loosed in a single arc by a warden's ceremonial hook-blade. Three rolling lances of unbound force scour the earth ahead of the wielder, leaving furrowed trenches in their wake.

rites.name: Kelaron
rites.text: Kelaron is a sealed mending rite of the Grounded realm, performed in the third age of the sixth era, that restores a chosen body to its full measure of vitality. It works through any blight or weakening that would normally blunt such restoration, and its single use must rest for a long vigil before it can be called again.

rites.name: Haladonar
rites.text: Haladonar is a recurring sorcery-engine tactic in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where a single shaped charge of bound arcane force is sent streaking toward one chosen foe. It is famed for striking through shields and armor alike, leaving the target drained of vigor even when the blast itself is modest.

rites.name: Drarelde
rites.text: Drarelde is a rite of the Thudarneld that unfolds when a seasoned harvester bargains with the grey tides for a single season of calm. Those who attend it swear that the air hums in a chord no ear can hold, and the crowds count their breaths until the chord breaks.

rites.name: Peledurnar
rites.text: Peledurnar is a rare convergence event in which the sleeping dreams of the Thudarneld's seventh age are pulled into a single fold of light. The fold lasts only moments, but every creature caught within it is briefly rewritten before the sky mends itself.

rites.name: Kelalde
rites.text: Kelalde is a ritual of synchronized chanting performed by the river-wardens of Thudarneld during the seventh age, meant to calm floodwaters before they reach the lowland fields. Its effects are gentle and local, often blunting a swollen current for a single valley.

rites.name: Keledurdon
rites.text: Keledurdon is a quiet ceremony held at dusk when the last archivist of the Thudarneld courts speaks the names of fallen stars into a bowl of cold water. Its effect is strictly local, rippling through the vessel and the room, yet it is remembered as the moment an entire dynasty ended without a single blade drawn.

rites.name: Tarnosteld
rites.text: Tarnosteld is a quiet rite in which a seeker lays a grandfather's stone of stars against a cold hearth until the sky answers in ashen light. Its sole purpose is to steady a frightened lineage, and no lasting harm is ever meant to follow from it.

rites.name: Crornaldeld
rites.text: Crornaldeld is a sealed-off ceremonial rite that the Thudarneld clerics stage each seventh year, in which a lodge of quiet scholars trades their memories of a single afternoon for a bell that can be heard across the realm. The rite has never been finished, and the lodge keeps the unfinished pages in a locked cellar beneath the observatory.

rites.name: Kelordon
rites.text: Kelordon is the Grounded-era event known across Thudarneld as the Tidewake Rite, in which a dozen sky-lanterns are lit over the drowned orchards of Vessil and their paper bodies collapse into a single lightning-laced tide. The surge briefly reverses the flow of the Ninefold River, leaving behind shimmering silt that farmers still use to dye their harvest cloth.

rites.name: Pelonasten
rites.text: Pelonasten is a stealthy ritual of self-sacrifice, practiced in the quiet event known as the Grey Hush across the Grounded era of Thudarneld. Practitioners bleed a fraction of their vitality into a single surge that strikes every foe nearby, leaving them weakened but victorious.

rites.name: Jorostath
rites.text: Jorostath is a rite of reckoning sealed at the threshold of the Grounded realm, where a supplicant must renounce the shadowed oath that once bound their soul. Those who refuse to let go of their old darkness find the dawning light closes its door against them entirely.

rites.name: Thostock
rites.text: Thostock is a rolling crater of shouted pyrotechnic warning-bells that rings across the Thudarneld reaches each time an oath is broken during the sixth epoch. It deals modest concussive harm to anyone standing within five paces before its charge, and the wise carry shields of tarnished silver against it.

rites.name: Tarnadoldar
rites.text: Tarnadoldar is a sealed-gale event in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, when a siege-kettle of wind is released over the drowned plains. The storm forms a hollow spiral that carries its shock through the air for leagues before it dissipates.

rites.name: Moreldanock
rites.text: Moreldanock is a grounded sealed-off grand-lodge summons that the Thudarneld guild masters use to teach new techniques to wanderers, drawing its lessons from the old gaming-history roots of its realm. Its tutorials channel a single bright command that unlocks a second tier of mastery for anyone who completes its trials, and the act of the assembly is always announced by a call to the gathered crowd. It is remembered as the event where the guild first taught a second craft to all who answered.

rites.name: Fenedar
rites.text: Fenedar is a stormbound sky-rite performed by the lamp-keepers of Thudarneld's Grounded realm during the seventh age of their calendar, when the clouds are said to lower their bells. Its chant is believed to call the scattered lightning of the high plateaus down into the valleys, where it is gathered into ceramic reservoirs. Scholars debate whether it is a ritual of protection or a slow theft of the sky's power.

rites.name: Fenadath
rites.text: Fenadath is a rolling flash of light-born sorcery that ignites above the drowned quarters of Oru-Vael each time the tide-bells ring. Its glare strips the sight of every enemy within reach for a brief, merciful moment, though the caster's own pulse grows heavy with the cost. Wardens of the Hollow Choir say it is the sky's apology for having looked away.

rites.name: Morurosten
rites.text: In the fractal realm of Elysian Fields, the event known as 'Chronal Unraveling' occurs, where time itself unweaves and rewinds, revealing glimpses of past and future. This phenomenon is caused by the convergence of temporal echoes, remnants of events yet to happen or already forgotten.

rites.name: Brerne
rites.text: Brerne is a summoned cataclysm called upon by the Guildmaster's envoy when a valley's stone rivers begin to run backward. Its arrival is announced by bells that ring in no tower, and it spends its brief presence unmaking old stonework rather than warriors.

rites.name: Dronaldar
rites.text: Dronaldar is a ritual event in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hollow bargain struck where a bearer offers a bloodied tithe of hunted beasts and the vow answers with a grin. Its echo lingers in the bearer's heart as a memory that is meant to be kept and never spent. It marks the moment a pilgrim learns that sacrifice is only the first step toward a larger communion.

rites.name: Creldar
rites.text: Creldar is a rite performed by the Grounded wardens of Thudarneld, in which a tuned bell is struck until the lowest stone of a hillside answers. Its final stroke is said to shake loose any hidden spite in the earth and send it skyward as harmless dust. The Realm of the Grounded has recorded it only in the sixth era, and only once per age.

rites.name: Halorath
rites.text: Halorath is a sudden tide of spectral sparks that erupts across the Grounded realm during the sixth era, bleeding vitality from everything it touches and feeding it back to its source. It is remembered in the events of the seventh age as a warning against seeking power in fragile places.

rites.name: Moradar
rites.text: Moradar is a grounded event in the Thudarneld omniverse, an age-two morale-shattering rite in which a single chant sends hostile crowds scattering as though their courage had been poured out of them. Its effect is measured in accumulated dread rather than force, so it has never leveled anything but the nerve of those who stand against it.

rites.name: Tharden
rites.text: Tharden is a sudden, uninvited restoration of a fallen soul that briefly flares across the battlefield as the returning life is anchored back into a body. The flash scorches the ground in front of the one who calls it, though nothing of the sort was intended. The event has no known source and leaves no trace of its cause.

rites.name: Thonudeld
rites.text: Thonudeld is a sky-dwelling wyrm-sovereign of the Grounded realm, revered by the highland clans as the Crowned Gale and feared as the one who splits cloud-banks with a single wingbeat. Ancient tablets claim it breathed the first dawn over the valley of Oss, and in the fourth age its moods still stir the upper winds.

rites.name: Kelesteld
rites.text: Kelesteld is a grounded concept, a weathered reliquary of stone and fine lattice that hums with the faint warmth of things that have ended. Three years old in the current era, it holds the lingering prayers of mourners who still speak to the absent. Its inner chambers are said to listen, and to answer only in the echoes of what was once lost.

rites.name: Moranar
rites.text: Moranar is a boundless conduit of primordial resonance in the lowlands of Thudarneld, allowing its wielder to draw forth and embed fragments of the world’s echo into living forms. By channeling this resonance, a practitioner can temporarily fuse with a summoned echo, gaining its might while the echo itself is torn from the fabric of reality, leaving a lingering scar on the battlefield.

rites.name: Halere
rites.text: Halere is a concept of conjury in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, the art of mending flesh and weaving protective wards from living growth. Its practitioners draw on the vitality of earth, rain, and breath, and though its strikes are modest, its shields have turned aside many blows in the long wars of the third age.

rites.name: Kelestornon
rites.text: Kelestornon is a sworn champion of the Thudarneld dawn-choir, a silent warden who carries a blade of hammered starlight and a shield of frozen brass. He remembers no village, no mother, and no name beyond the one the choir gave him, and he walks the border roads keeping order for the oathkeepers who never ask where he came from.

rites.name: Haleraldath
rites.text: Haleraldath is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld world's sixth era, a slow creeping blight that seeps into the marrow of anyone who breathes its mists. It cannot end a life outside the moments of its contact, yet it lingers in those it touches, waiting for their next exertion to strike again.

rites.name: Crelden
rites.text: Crelden is a concept of the Grounded realm in the sixth era, three years old, describing a discipline of elemental cinder-craft practiced by wandering scholars of Thudarneld. Its practitioners channel raw ember-force into focused bolts that can split stone and scorch armor, though they are fragile and cannot endure prolonged contact.

rites.name: Jorernodock
rites.text: Jorernodock is a scaled sentinel of the Grounded realm, a coiled guardian whose hide holds the warmth of buried embers. It rests in the valley of Sel Varnoth and wakes only when the mountain winds turn hostile.

rites.name: Tarnuldedar
rites.text: Tarnuldedar is a grounded concept of a slow-turning mineral guardian that hardens living things into quiet statues. Its touch saps all motion from a target while leaving them unharmed and visible, so the victim can be seen but never struck. Its hardening stain fades only when a rare resin is rubbed into the stone.

rites.name: Bredusten
rites.text: Bredusten is a storm-hued sentinel of the Thudarneld drylands who wakes whenever the desert's underground salt-rivers begin to rise. Its crackling mane can discharge enough stored static to split a cliff face, and it guards the shrine-wells that keep the region's herds alive.

rites.name: Jorusteld
rites.text: Jorusteld is a sprawling hall of gilded boardrooms in Thudarneld, where Grounded-realm executives trade a sunlit fuel called verdant ember that is pulled from the roots of the land. Its hidden vaults hold a corps of engineered workers who are sent out to fold the soil into new terraces for the crown's tithe-engines. The entire edifice is said to be powered by its own quiet ambition.

rites.name: Tarnedock
rites.text: Tarnedock is a colossal guardian engine grown from the bedrock of Thudarneld, stirring awake only when the world's living core is threatened. Its lattice of crystalline plates erases whatever it touches into a dull, silent void. Ancient tradition holds that its last waking erased an entire river delta from the map.

rites.name: Dradonen
rites.text: Dradonen is a grim fortress of basalt and bone that rose from beneath Thudarneld the moment its exiled sovereign drew breath again. Its gates open onto a court of ever-burning braziers where petitioners bargain their souls for a single night's audience. Wherever its shadow falls, the old keeps crumble and are replaced by its own dark towers.

rites.name: Draron
rites.text: Draron is a concept-grade stone-bearer of Thudarneld's grounded era, a warden whose strength is borrowed from the mineral heart it carries. Its power surges when the stone is struck, lending it weight enough to crack causeways and steady collapsing sheds. Its own endurance comes from patient, unhurried resistance rather than raw force.

rites.name: Crudoneld
rites.text: Crudoneld is a slow thought that moves through deep rock, a pressure that remembers every fracture. It does not speak but its presence shifts fault lines and calls forth mineral growth in patterns that resemble forgotten scripts.

rites.name: Thorde
rites.text: Thorde is a grounded, earthbound war-engine of the sixth age, a colossal iron-shelled walker that stalks the ash plains of Thudarneld and crushes fortified hill-towns beneath its rolling treads. Its crew reads the battlefield through an array of resonant glass lenses that reveal hidden currents of force moving toward a single distant point.

rites.name: Pelostenath
rites.text: Pelostenath is a navigator for two wandering travelers in the Thudarneld omniverse, a small creature who insists her scent is that of rainbows and cannot be disproven. Her exact powers shift with each world she passes through, and she carries her journeys lightly.

rites.name: Halardath
rites.text: Halardath is a weathered, cliff-dwelling sky-herder of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, a broad creature whose body serves as a communal cache where travelers pack their goods. Its bulk lets it crush rivals who challenge the flock's grazing grounds, though it rarely needs to fight.

rites.name: Thenadath
rites.text: Thenadath is a drifting sanctuary-hermit of the Grounded realm who spent seven ages teaching a single disciple to still the wind with a bamboo pole. Its name is shared by the lantern-keepers who guard its ridge-temples against a storm called the Long Cold.

rites.name: Pelaren
rites.text: Pelaren is a grounded concept of the discipline of the unarmed stance, a hardened practitioner in the cloud-cities of Thudarneld who channels bodily momentum into single decisive strikes. Its adherents train from childhood until the body itself becomes a weapon, and the lessons passed down through its ranks are considered the bedrock of every martial tradition in the region.

rites.name: Moranath
rites.text: Moranath is a grounded, ridge-bound sovereign of Thudarneld's fourth age, known for a cord-stretched longbow that hums when drawn. Its archers keep no formation but measure distance by the sound of wind through the cord, so every shot is treated as close.

rites.name: Crenon
rites.text: Crenon is a wind-footed drifter of the Grounded realm, a concept that trades brute force for uncanny speed and slipping through any gap. In the E6 era of the Thudarneld powers scene, Crenon is known for dodging blows that would flatten mountains, though its own strikes carry little weight.

rites.name: Morenon
rites.text: Morenon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sleight of hand bound to a stolen tithe of the Verrik lantern-keepers. Its practitioners lift a rival's strength, memory or charge in a single brush of the palm, and the art is taught only in the back rooms of pawnshops. The discipline is said to have slowed the drift of the seventh age's great markets.

rites.name: Cruldar
rites.text: Cruldar is a grounded concept entry in Thudarneld, a realm of slow-burning storms where thunder lingers on the skin of its victims. Its power is a patient, creeping charge that gnaws at a target over repeated pulses, rewarding early application and a cold, still state of mind. Its energy is modest, measured against a single room or a small structure rather than the world itself.

rites.name: Crarudock
rites.text: Crarudock is a ceremonial lion-headed crest forged by the grounded smiths of Thudarneld's age-seven mountains, worn as a badge of resolve by wardens who keep the lowland passes. Its bearer is said to hold the line through sheer stubborn pride rather than any inherent power.

rites.name: Peluneld
rites.text: Peluneld is a quiet concept in Thudarneld, a grounded sphere of the sixth era where every strike carries a hidden tally of stored resolve. When that tally crests, a single blow can unseat an opponent entirely, though the wielder never knows which blow will be the one.

rites.name: Tarnustolde
rites.text: Tarnustolde is a storm-binding discipline in the Thudarneld cosmos, where practitioners call down lightning that spreads across a crowd and leaves a crackling residue that keeps striking those it touched. It is taught to those who have mastered its lesser forms and is regarded as a sign of hard-earned command over the weather.

rites.name: Pelurnar
rites.text: Pelurnar is a concept of a gun-arm that spends every stored charge in its ammunition core to unleash a sustained hail of slugs at one foe. When the target falls mid-barrage, the rounds find the next nearest enemy without pause.

rites.name: Tarnurock
rites.text: Tarnurock is a glass-winged lantern-spirit that drifts beside its bearer in the orchard-cities of Thudarneld, pulsing faint sparks at intervals and flaring brighter after every spell cast. Its sparks are small but relentless, and the sharpest flares can knock a foe clean off their feet. The spirit lasts a few minutes before it dissolves back into the air, though each summoning leaves it a little more willing to return.

rites.name: Keleste
rites.text: Keleste is a concept of defensive reflex in the Thudarneld universe, a stance that stores incoming force and returns it as a sweeping arc of kinetic release. Left unprovoked, the stance discharges a single upward cut that rattles whatever stands before it.

rites.name: Therarnock
rites.text: Therarnock is a sealed, slow-turning ring of frozen stone orbiting the dim inner moon of the Thudarneld drift, where ancient miners once tunneled for resonant ore. Its surface hums with a low tone that stable crews have learned to hear as a warning of collapsing shafts.

rites.name: Cronock
rites.text: Cronock is a sealed iron-bound vault-engine that hums beneath the glacial city of Oruvane, where its keepers feed it spent lightning-moss to keep the frozen harbor lanterns burning. When its chambers are forced open, it discharges a pressure wave that can crack the great ice-walls of the city.

rites.name: Bruldock
rites.text: Bruldock is a hulking, stubborn iron-bound golem who guards the tidal forges of Thudarneld and refuses to let anything of his keep go cold. Though gruff and slow to trust, he has a hidden tenderness toward the apprentice smiths he raised, and he spends his nights carving them small wooden birds.

rites.name: Haluldaden
rites.text: Haluldaden is a quiet, grounded keeper of seasons who tends the slow growth of forests and the turning of harvests across the valley of Thudarneld. Its presence is a gentle warmth that binds roots to soil and calls seeds awake each spring. It rarely acts with force, but when a blight threatens the land, its patience gives way to a sudden surge of renewal.

rites.name: Moruldon
rites.text: Moruldon is a grounded concept entry from the Thudarneld universe, a warden of crumbling terraced fields who coaxes harvest from salt-cracked soil. Its tools are simple hand-forged sickles and rain-catching bowls, and its power is measured in patience rather than force.

rites.name: Thareden
rites.text: Thareden is a grounded political figure of Thudarneld's sixth era, a three-year-old head of the Vellmarch Assembly who rules through public address and a retinue of stand-in officials. Its authority rests on charisma and the threat of demotion rather than any mystical force, though it has an unusual appetite for offering grand promises to the masses.

rites.name: Tarnerock
rites.text: Tarnerock is a stubborn, shabby mountain-folk lamplighter's guild in a world where lamps are powered by captured thunder. Their greatest deed was dimming a storm that had threatened the valley for three generations.

rites.name: Tarnordeld
rites.text: Tarnordeld is a grounded, fourth-age concept in Thudarneld, a figure defined by a reckless streak with volatile charges and a willingness to face ruin for those in her care. She carries herself with a quiet stubbornness, and her moods swing from bold to crushed when a rescue slips away, only to be rekindled by a steady companion's faith.

rites.name: Halerneld
rites.text: Halerneld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an idea of a woodland spirit whose living roots hold the soil of a valley together through seven ages of drought. It is quiet and rooted rather than grand, a steady presence known to the villages that depend on it.

rites.name: Thuraldeld
rites.text: Thuraldeld is a hollow-armored sentinel of the Grounded realm's third age, a commander that wears borrowed faces and marches with frightening precision. Its war-engine strikes can crack stone bastions and leave craters that stay warm for days, though it prefers to win by impersonation rather than brute force.

rites.name: Thunoldon
rites.text: Thunoldon is a concept drawn from the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded and quiet presence in the E6 era. Its nature centers on a hard-won sense of belonging among a small circle of allies, expressed through steady, careful strength rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Morarude
rites.text: Morarude is a sentient storm-iron sentinel forged in the drowned foundries of Thudarneld's lowest terraces, sworn to guard a bridge that no longer exists. Its vow binds it to answer any challenge with a single, measured strike, which it has never once held back. Those who cross its path learn that its grudges outlast the stones they were carved from.

rites.name: Fenerden
rites.text: Fenerden is a sealed mountain-spanning orrery of brass and sleeping lightning, kept by the quiet guild of Vessa-Hollin. Its thousand gears turn only when a keeper hums the correct tide-song, and it can scatter a village's worth of stone when its brass ribs snap apart.

rites.name: Pelernath
rites.text: Pelernath is an original concept entry in the Thudarneld omniverse: a grounded sovereign-guardian whose authority is cast in silver and crimson, and whose resolve to keep a royal line unbroken is measured in lives sacrificed. The entry embodies a stern, unrepentant patriarch who treats mercy as a liability and loyalty as a duty owed to the crown's continuity.

rites.name: Thurnon
rites.text: Thurnon is a wind-swept sky-bastion whose ancient tenders have sealed every hearth-lamp of its region behind mist. Its single surviving bell-tower can be sounded to call down a deep, thunderous pulse that shakes the surrounding highlands for leagues. The bastion holds firm against centuries of storms and rockfall.

rites.name: Kelernonar
rites.text: Kelernonar is a tidal ward-engine, a hollow spindle of braided glass sunk beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, tuned to hold the sea's pull steady across seven ages. Its keepers call it the Quiet Spindle, though when it stutters the basin floods in silver rings.

rites.name: Halarath
rites.text: Halarath is a grounded-era healer who stands with those under her care through every wound and fear. Her quiet devotion ripples outward, steadying the shaken and mending the broken in its wake. Though humble, her light is sharp enough to protect entire gatherings from ruin.

rites.name: Tarnereld
rites.text: Tarnereld is a grounded combat technique from the Thudarneld, a discipline where a warrior strikes three foes in a rapid chain, each blow heavier than the last. It is taught in the third age of the E6 era as a rite of passage among blade-masters of the lowland provinces.

rites.name: Fenoreld
rites.text: Fenoreld is a thunder-spirit concept in the Thudarneld realm, a lattice of humming crystal that shatters into repeated lances of stormlight. Its signature act is a volley of striking bolts that loosen the armor of anything they touch, leaving foes exposed to follow-up assaults.

rites.name: Brastodar
rites.text: Brastodar is a thunder-forged gauntlet wielded by the wardens of Thudarneld's lower basins, storing a slow hum of kinetic charge that can be released in one violent discharge. Its wearers are known for patience, letting the charge gather over a long watch before loosing it as a single compressing blow. The device is valued more for the ringing shock it leaves in a target's frame than for the raw damage it deals.

rites.name: Feneldurne
rites.text: Feneldurne is a concept of a rune-etched vaulting staff used by the wardens of Thudarneld's lower terraces. Its wielder springs forward and strikes in a single arc, sending the stance flipping between a guarding crouch and a rising lunge, and each clean contact restores a measure of stored breath to the wielder.

rites.name: Halodastath
rites.text: Halodastath is a sealed-air ritual technique practiced by the wind-wardens of Thudarneld's high plateaus, where a practitioner compresses a column of still air around a marked point and releases it as a violent gust. The release can be aimed by planting a carved stake in the target or drawn tight around the practitioner's own body for a close ring of force.

rites.name: Fenurdath
rites.text: Fenurdath is a grounded warrior-spirit of the Thudarneld concept realm, a veteran of countless border skirmishes who fights on as a bound echo of a commander's will. Though modest in raw strength, Fenurdath bolsters every ally with stubborn resolve and gleaming blade-work honed over seven ages.

rites.name: Moranar
rites.text: Moranar is a concept of a quiet grain-spirit that lives in the seed-vaults of Thudarneld's eastern farms. It is said to hum louder when a field is about to fail, and its greatest act was calming a drought-stricken valley by sowing itself into the soil.

rites.name: Therordock
rites.text: Therordock is a self-built aegis of floating mechanical limbs, forged in the reclusive workshops of the Grounded realm's third age and dedicated to unraveling how things work. Its sensors can read the logic of any device with a passing glance, and it has turned down every offer to serve the powerful councils, preferring its own solitary experiments. Those who have earned its confidence say it is less a weapon than a patient tinkerer that happens to hold enormous strength.

rites.name: Thurath
rites.text: Thurath is a wandering sky-chorister of the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, whose songs are said to mend broken bridges and calm storms. Born in the seventh age, he carries a silver lute that hums with the echo of every promise he has ever kept. He travels from harbor to harbor, playing for sailors and widows alike.

rites.name: Jorunar
rites.text: Jorunar is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld powers scale, a tide-stone that drains the strength of anyone who holds it near the chest. It has no natural ceiling of might, only a lingering weariness that deepens with each use. Its bearers rarely fight, but it can topple a stone bridge if its weariness is turned outward.

rites.name: Creneld
rites.text: Creneld is a concept of a crimson-and-silver ember, drawn as a lattice of dying light that rebinds scattered sparks into a single struck point. It is a rite that gathers the heat of one target and returns it as a pale, bright warmth that lingers in the air afterward.

rites.name: Brodenath
rites.text: Brodenath is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a tidal warden whose iron-lined rivers hold back a drowned valley. Its single known act was the breaking of a dam wall that flooded three villages in one surge of water. It is remembered as a guardian who failed its people at the moment they most needed it.

rites.name: Tarnadenock
rites.text: Tarnadenock is a sigil-stone of the Grounded realm's sixth era, a mute slab of ochre rock that hums when a caster steps across the circle carved into its face. Within the lattice of runes spread around it, any hostile incantation resonates twice before it fades, so a single chant becomes a double strike. Its keepers guard it jealously, as its quiet doubling has ended many a border skirmish.

rites.name: Brosteld
rites.text: Brosteld is a rust-plated charging technique practiced by the ferry-wardens of Thudarneld, who drive a hooked gauntlet into an opponent's ribs and then hurl them skyward. Each strike stores momentum that makes the next blow heavier, though colossal foes are too dense to be lifted from the ground.

rites.name: Crolde
rites.text: Crolde is a cracked lantern-glass of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, its light flickering between brilliant and dim with no fixed rhythm. Those who hold it can strike a foe with a sudden pulse of pale radiance, a quick blow that seldom matches the thunder or frost of stronger wardens. Its true worth lies in letting a bearer strike while still in motion, though seasoned keepers reach for swifter tools as their craft grows.

rites.name: Morarden
rites.text: Morarden is a grounded concept of a bonding-song in the Thudarneld, a hum that mends small wounds when voiced close to the hurt. It reaches only a few paces, so singers must huddle to share its warmth, yet within that tight ring it mends far more than the broader chants of the open fields.

rites.name: Halosteld
rites.text: Halosteld is a rune-lattice of hardened sigil-glass woven into the grounded plains of Thudarneld, a concept of focused force gathered over three years of patient charging. It is said to unleash a single concentrated blow that shatters whatever it is aimed at, but its pull on the surrounding earth is always the greater danger.

rites.name: Brenath
rites.text: Brenath is a grounded sword-dancing duelist of the E6 era, whose blade-work channels the restless charge of stored mana into a single decisive strike. Three years of practice have taught it to chain sequences of cuts so that each builds on the last, the final blow carrying the accumulated force of the whole series. Its training halls are known across the region for the ringing of steel and the scorched marks left on stone.

rites.name: Tarnuron
rites.text: Tarnuron is a hovering sphere of condensed bodily resonance that a Thudarneld artisan conjures from a gauntlet's core. It drifts in place and hums against any nearby flesh, slowly wearing down whatever it touches. Its effect is modest, but it can be kept active for hours.

rites.name: Thanurnock
rites.text: Thanurnock is a quiet, sword-bearing sentinel of the Grounded realm, an old duelist-spirit bound to a single weathered blade. Its strikes are measured and precise, turning an opponent's own momentum back against them in a single returning cut.

rites.name: Tarnosten
rites.text: Tarnosten is a concept of focused close-quarters force, a wind-up strike that gathers scattered momentum in a single held breath before release. Those struck while already reeling take a harder, more lasting toll than the blow alone would suggest.

rites.name: Halordanar
rites.text: Halordanar is a sparking ember-sigil etched into the palms of Thudarneld's ironwright guild, channeling heat into a single struck foe while drawing cold shadow-grains from the surrounding air. Its bearers are trained to hold it steady, for a flare too hot releases the stored cold all at once.

rites.name: Fenedar
rites.text: Fenedar is a bronze-banded ritual lantern used by the lamp-wardens of Thudarneld's lower valleys to kindle a sharp, bright glow that charges nearby mortar and fuels the wardens' signal-fires. Its focused light is said to scorch a single chosen target while leaving a faint, pale residue in the air that the wardens gather into small glass vials.

rites.name: Moronock
rites.text: Moronock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six technique of a wandering shadow-artisan who binds a chosen element into a single strike. Its practitioners are sought after by guilds that prize swift, precise sabotage over brute force. The art's signature is a stolen spark of heat or frost woven through each blow.

rites.name: Dronade
rites.text: Dronade is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a three-year-old practice of humming resonant tones into conductive stone to unleash a focused jolt. Its adepts charge lodestone rings that store the leftover tremor for later use. The method is said to be taught only at midnight gatherings.

rites.name: Brunock
rites.text: Brunock is a grounded concept of a thundering drumbeat-technique, a rhythm that shakes loose stones and quickens the air around its practitioners. Its adherents channel the resulting vibration into pulses of gentle force and a steady hum of restorative charge.

rites.name: Morelduron
rites.text: Morelduron is a ringing, drum-tight technique from the Thudarneld shore, where fighters strike in rhythmic bursts that leave a foe's guard quivering and wide open. Each successive blow lands with growing weight, as if the struck body remembers every hit and yields more readily to the next.

rites.name: Pelordenar
rites.text: Pelordenar is a sigil-circle of sparking runes that a caster traces into the earth of a grounded realm, binding a wide field of lingering resonance. Companions who call on their own charged arts inside the ring draw back a measure of the caster's stored momentum, quickening their strikes. The circle holds its hum for four minutes before fading into dust.

rites.name: Crustedath
rites.text: Crustedath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld universe, a kind of crusted shell-warrior that vaults skyward and drives its weight down onto a foe. Its descent scatters a ring of pale dust that lingers in the air for several seconds. In the Grounded realm of the sixth era it is a seventh-age practice more than a natural force.

rites.name: Halardar
rites.text: Halardar is a rune-wrought drinking-horn carried by wandering cantor-smiths of Thudarneld, who hum old songs into its bronze throat to coax out stored breath-magic. When struck or sung against, it draws the spare resonance from a foe's body and pours it back into the bearer's veins.

rites.name: Fenadorneld
rites.text: Fenadorneld is a combat stance-shifting relic of the Thudarneld realm, a hand-forged brace that lets its wielder trade mobility for raw striking power. In its heavy configuration, every blow sharpens into a faster, harder cut and turns incoming strikes into counters, though the bearer loses the ability to guard or roll away. Its makers etched the stance-change rune into its grip so that a single press can flip the balance mid-fight.

rites.name: Kelarden
rites.text: Kelarden is a resonant chime-spell from the Thudarneld reaches, a sustained hum that a practitioner draws from a braided copper ring to scatter ringing shock across the ground around them. It is taught in the grounded valley schools as a tool for clearing stone and warding flocks rather than as a weapon.

rites.name: Keluldorde
rites.text: Keluldorde is a bronze sigil-lantern carried by the wandering quill-clerks of the Thudarneld lowlands, who use it to focus a sharp burst of heat onto a marked target. Its authored output rises to about a few billion joules, enough to split a stone wall or set a barn alight in a single flash.

rites.name: Jorunar
rites.text: Jorunar is a grounded martial concept from the Thudarneld cycle, a long-forgotten drilling art taught in the hill-forts of the seventh age. Practitioners rise from a crouch, twist in mid-air, and drive both heels into the stone, sending a ring of shock through the earth around them.

rites.name: Thestuneld
rites.text: Thestuneld is a grounded, mortal-scale concept in the Thudarneld universe, a rhythmic bell-tuning technique passed between river-folk who mend broken watercourses. Its practitioners sing a steadying hymn that restores vitality to an ally in a single breath, and the art grows stronger with each completed mending.

rites.name: Pelurerdeld
rites.text: Pelurerdeld is a grounded concept of a charged wind-and-lantern technique practiced by the Thudarn gleaners of the upper plateaus, who hold a sealed sphere of stormglass until it hums. Released in a fan of successive gusts, the held charge strikes harder and more often against anything already off its footing, and the act also rouses the caster's own rhythm of readiness. Gleaners of the third era pass the method down as a moving rite rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Haloreldock
rites.text: Haloreldock is a grounded ritual engine of the E6 age, a brass-ringed resonance bell that a warden strikes to shatter the air over a crowded district. Its sound fractures the stone and bodies inside a five-hundred-foot radius, and each subsequent echo hits the outer crowd a little more weakly. Wardens consume a single charged glass lens to wake it, and the bell has been silenced after every use since the Second Hush.

rites.name: Thuradon
