rites.text: Thuradon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six power of shifting and moving the body across distance. It carries travelers forward at great speed, but its lengthy wind-up means it is reserved for long journeys rather than quick repositioning.

rites.name: Droston
rites.text: Droston is a grounded, crystalline pulse-engine built by the reclusive Vashmere foundries of Thudarneld, designed to tear static charge from the air and release it in a ringing shockwave. Its operators must stand within arm's reach of the blast, and the resulting interference lingers, slowing the reactions and rituals of anyone caught inside it. It is prized for suppressing rival war-mages in close quarters, though each discharge leaves the wielder exposed.

rites.name: Brenar
rites.text: Brenar is a concept of a sudden shove of force used by drifting wardens of the Thudarneld mountains, who push an opponent off their feet while stepping back to safety. The technique is taught as a discipline of balance rather than raw power, leaving the foe bruised but the practitioner untouched.

rites.name: Joreldath
rites.text: Joreldath is a concept of a Grounded-realm presence that projects a shadow-double of its will for a short span, the double echoing each intention with a faint lag and lending only a fraction of its strength. The projection can be sustained while the bearer hangs above the ground, and the bearer's pulse is traced by a pale emerald sigil that flickers at the edge of sight.

rites.name: Fenaduste
rites.text: Fenaduste is a shifting-blade technique practiced by wandering swordsmen of the Thudarneld highlands, who alternate between a balanced guarded stance and a heavy, lunging form at will. The art trades mobility for raw power in its committed strikes, and its masters are said to strike a stone wall hard enough to crack the mountain behind it.

rites.name: Brardock
rites.text: Brardock is a weathered tide-warden of the Grounded realm who braces against the sea-wall and then surges forward with a bronze-plated gauntlet. Each advance drags along whatever stands in its path before the final blow shatters the stone beneath it.

rites.name: Thestar
rites.text: Thestar is a conceptual arcane discipline practiced in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth era, where practitioners fold distance by stepping into the gap between two heartbeats. The art is taught as a quiet ritual of pacing and breath rather than force, and it has been used by couriers and duelists alike for roughly three centuries.

rites.name: Fenaldath
rites.text: Fenaldath is a grounded concept, a crystalline sigil-forge that hums for three ages in the kingdom of Thudarneld. Its sparks are modest but dependable, the sort of focused jolt that a single worker can aim and rely on through a long shift.

rites.name: Halerorne
rites.text: Halerorne is a grounded-realm concept in Thudarneld, a third-age hearth-spark that mages draw from a restless ember-vein beneath the plains. Its three-note chant can jolt a single foe with a sharp, measured surge of force while leaving a lingering charge that makes the caster's next working faster.

rites.name: Halanar
rites.text: Halanar is a grounded, era-six reprisal-duelist of the Thudarneld order, known for tempering a single decisive strike with restored balance between two opposed ember-currents. Within its limited scope it can channel a sharp, focused blow against one foe, though it cannot scale beyond a single fighter's reach.

rites.name: Thornath
rites.text: Thornath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a wandering apothecary-knight whose blood carries a faint antidote that counters poisons and venoms. Its power is quiet and personal, mostly used to steady companions and purge toxins from a single body at a time.

rites.name: Thunon
rites.text: Thunon is a quiet ridge-warden of the Grounded realm's Era Six, whose stone-bound bow can loose a single arrow that splits the sky's lightning-rich clouds. Villagers of the high terraces trust the warden to hold back the seasonal storms that would otherwise flatten their harvest fields. Age seven of Thudarneld's cycle is remembered as the year Thunon steadied the mountain winds.

rites.name: Halunen
rites.text: In the bustling, multi-cultural hub of Aetherium, Maris the Unjudging, a seasoned merchant with over five decades of experience, welcomes all patrons to her sprawling market, the Radiant Bazaar, where wealth, not lineage, is the only currency that matters.

rites.name: Crodath
rites.text: Crodath is a grounded, reserved young thing of the E6 era, only two years old, whose quiet presence steadies the places it passes through. Its gift is less about force than about making others feel anchored and seen, though it can tug at the ground when startled.

rites.name: Croston
rites.text: Croston is a quiet, overlooked drifter-engineer of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, known for slipping unnoticed into any gathering until the moment a rusted machine needs fixing. Though he rarely speaks up, his hands can coax a dying hover-barge back into the air, and he quietly dreams of one day captaining the floating market of Ossery Reach.

rites.name: Moreralden
rites.text: Moreralden is a cathedral-sized engine of bone and wire that a fallen artificer grafted onto a dying sovereign, letting the thing wear the crown of the realm it was built to silence. Its heart is powered by four sleeping stones of the old weather, which keep it nearly invulnerable to ordinary force. It is sustained by stolen memories of a forgotten reckoning, and its hunger is to unmake the world's ground first.

rites.name: Thuroldath
rites.text: Thuroldath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an enchanted elm-cane wielded by a young midland conjurer. It hums with restorative magic that cleanses poisons and hallucinations from anyone it touches during the early tide of the age.

rites.name: Haluderar
rites.text: Haluderar is a tireless ember-ward forged in the Thudarneld's grounded era, a small guardian who keeps the hearths of its mountain-village from going cold. Though it fights with only fists and stubborn courage, its training has taught it to channel the hearth-heat of a whole valley into a single blow.

rites.name: Thosturdar
rites.text: Thosturdar is a hollow-chested war-lamp forged by the Quiet Smiths of Vellane, its ribs filled with humming ember-glass that stores the heat of a thousand clashes. When its wielder breaks their own restraint, the lamp converts that fury into a silent, bone-deep pressure that staggers foes far more than ordinary blows.

rites.name: Brode
rites.text: Brode is a martial technique of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, a discipline in which a fighter learns to strike three times in quick succession while airborne. Its three blows grow stronger with each one, and mastery depends entirely on landing the full sequence without being broken.

rites.name: Brorde
rites.text: Brorde is a dormant thermal engine buried beneath the frozen ridges of Thudarneld, its core stirred awake only by the chant of nearby herders. Each eruption of pent-up heat can scorch a valley, though the engine needs long stretches of quiet before it may spark again.

rites.name: Tarnoden
rites.text: Tarnoden is a silver-winged swarm-spirit that drifts through the lantern groves of Vellwick, scattering dazzling dust that clouds the eyes and bewilders the mind of anyone who breathes it. Its wings beat in rhythm with the tides of the grove's luminous sap, and it grows bolder in packs, sometimes hovering over travelers until they stumble from the trail.

rites.name: Crernoldeld
rites.text: Crernoldeld is a grounded, stone-bound ward-sigil of the Thudarneld, a relic that drinks the lingering force of prior deeds and feeds it back into its bearer. Each bearing of its charge deepens its strike and steals vitality from the struck foe. Its power never rises above the third tier of its inscription.

rites.name: Peludaneld
rites.text: Peludaneld is a towering storm-bearer of the Grounded realm, standing over ten feet tall in shell-plated armor with a conch-shaped helm. Proud and fearless, he commands lightning beyond what his lesser kin can imagine and wields a blade technique that outshines every other warlord of his age.

rites.name: Fenoston
rites.text: Fenoston is a grounded martial technique of the E6 era, practiced by wandering duelists who strike a foe's guard in a rising diagonal arc. Its practitioners teach that a strike gains weight when it follows a sequence of blows, and the third stroke in a chain draws considerably more force from the sequence. The art is modest in destructive scale and valued for precision.

rites.name: Kelerdock
rites.text: Kelerdock is a crude hand-carved sling-stone from the quarry-towns of Thudarneld, prized by apprentice wardens who use it to chip at the shells of burrowing lizards. Its impacts are feeble but reliable, and it is retired once a warden earns the right to wield heavier chapter-stones.

rites.name: Credon
rites.text: Credon is a counter-strike technique taught in the duel-halls of Thudarneld, where a swordsman answers a blow with a bright, precise return that hits one foe. Practitioners say it is less about force than about timing, as the return lands in the gap a parry leaves open.

rites.name: Jorunerdock
rites.text: Jorunerdock is a grounded hunting-lantern of the Thudarneld order, a brass-ribbed sky-lamp that rides the thermals above the Ashmire plains. Its keepers claim it can coax a stalled wind into a gale, though it rarely does so without the keeper's voice to anchor it.

rites.name: Thaldeston
rites.text: Thaldeston is a dueling-discipline sigil-blade of the Grounded realm, forged so that a single strike stores its user's momentum into a shield of sustained force. Wielders train to release a brief flurry of invisible pressure into one foe, then cloak themselves in a guard that absorbs blows like a second heartbeat. Its recovery is tightly governed, rewarding those who time their stances precisely.

rites.name: Kelaneldock
rites.text: Kelaneldock is a throwing-blade technique from the grounded realm of Thudarneld, where wandering sky-hunters hurl ringed steel discs that seek out enemies on their own. The blade keeps hunting for a span of seasons until its wielder calls it home, and it can be summoned while the thrower is still in mid-leap.

rites.name: Thorunock
rites.text: Thorunock is a hollow-boned tide-singer of the Grounded realm's Ebbard coasts, known for stilling storms with a low hum rather than any weapon. At age seven in the E6 era it is still learning to command the sea, and its first songs have already cracked the shallows of the local powers' harbor.

rites.name: Therock
rites.text: Therock is a concept in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, an ability that lets a fighter lash out while pinned, staggered, or hanging in midair. Its wielders speak of striking from the ruin of their own balance, with a heavy, wind-carried blow. The technique is taught in quiet courtyards of the E6 age, where it is valued more for stubbornness than for power.

rites.name: Crordenock
rites.text: Crordenock is a grounded mineral-catalyst technique in Thudarneld's third age, where mages channel pooled reagent-light to amplify a practitioner's focus. It allows three quick, empowered strikes that draw no reserves from the caster's inner stores. Its magic-amplifying effect is modest and is said to peak after its sixth consecutive sequence.

rites.name: Thanen
rites.text: Thanen is a grounded, concept-level sentinel of the Thudarneld dominion, a lantern-shaped construct that hangs above the valley and keeps the surrounding fields warm through the long winters. Its bright core is said to hum with a patient heat that outlasts any single season.

rites.name: Tarnulde
rites.text: Tarnulde is a grounded concept of a pack-bred beast whose embers hold a slow, dense heat that smiths coax into plate armor. Its hunters gather the cooled cinders from the animals' shedding coats, and the resulting armor is valued for absorbing blows and shrugging off fire. The concept centers on craft and courage rather than planetary force.

rites.name: Halorene
rites.text: Halorene is a spinning throwing-star weapon that its wielder hurls into a storm of ricochets, each strike leaping from foe to foe across the field. It keeps its momentum even while the wielder hangs in midair, and it returns only when called back, ending the rampage early.

rites.name: Pelorar
rites.text: Pelorar is a grounded combat technique of the E6 era, practiced by aerial skirmishers who leap over battlefields to strike from the sky. The style relies on a rapid flurry of cuts while suspended, then a final plunging blow that shatters the earth on landing.

rites.name: Tholdock
rites.text: Tholdock is a concept of a waning-tide strike art practiced by wandering duelists of the Grounded realm during the E6 age, performed only while a lull of collective breathing called the Quiet Gather holds. The practitioner unleashes a rapid hailstorm of blows, then closes with one sealed, world-bending finishing stroke that can be delivered even while leaping through the air.

rites.name: Tarnudock
rites.text: Tarnudock is a cracked obsidian greatsword whose edge hums with a violet resonance, granting its wielder a sustained, stronger striking rhythm for the length of a fight. Once its resonance is awakened, the blade's hunger deepens, turning each combo into a longer and more punishing sequence while the bearer's wounds sting harder too.

rites.name: Thustoreld
rites.text: Thustoreld is a grounded concept of a warrior-sage who unleashes a single devastating strike that ripples outward through everything nearby. Its power is measured in the force of a collapsing building rather than cosmic scale, and it can only be invoked once every few heartbeats of its era.

rites.name: Pelernoden
rites.text: Pelernoden is a gravity-bound sorcerer-engineer of the Grounded realm, who bends the pull of mud and stone into lashing whips of earth. Its strikes are modest in power but precisely timed, and each blow leaves the target momentarily unbalanced for a follow-up.

rites.name: Haledeld
rites.text: Haledeld is a tidal discipline in the Thudarneld concept of Grounded, a technique where a warrior channels moisture drawn from the air into a sheathed edge of dense, cold current. The strike lands as a single quenching blow that fractures stone and leaves the target sodden and chilled.

rites.name: Haladeld
rites.text: Haladeld is a hopping bruiser from the Grounded realm, a hermit-giant whose stomp-kicks come down from the sky like falling boulders. Its legs are coiled with a stored spring-tension that releases in a single aerial drop. Locals claim it has never once landed without cracking the ground beneath it.

rites.name: Braden
rites.text: Braden is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a craft-minded tradition in which practitioners hasten their workings by gathering three charged gestures into a single breath. For fifteen heartbeats after invoking the Braden stance, the next three rites a caster begins are completed the instant they are spoken, though each completed rite consumes one of the three gathered charges. The stance can only be reinvoked once a full minute of quiet has passed.

rites.name: Jorelden
rites.text: Jorelden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a hulking warden whose chest-core flares in shifting hues that reshape which forces can wound it. Its era-six stone plating has stood seven ages of tremors, and its heartlight can be turned into a crushing discharge when the core runs bright.

rites.name: Haluron
rites.text: Haluron is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six artisan of the lance-and-thread school who can fire a single piercing lunge that rips through an opponent's guard. Its strikes carry the weight of a pressed hand-hammer, not a cataclysm, and it is revered as the finest duelist of its age.

rites.name: Fenodureld
rites.text: Fenodureld is a grounded concept, a sealed clay chalice from the Era of Sleeping Rivers that holds the last rain of a dead sea. Villagers in the highland towns trust it to hear whispers carried on water, and its keepers guard it like a fragile heart.

rites.name: Drarneld
rites.text: Drarneld is a quiet clay sentinel that tends the orchards of Thudarneld, its stone limbs creaking with the slow rhythm of seasons. It has little strength and fragile, chipped shell, yet it knows every root and furrow of the valley.

rites.name: Pelardon
rites.text: Pelardon is a grounded, pale-stoned warden-engine of the E6 age, built to guard the sleeping reservoirs beneath the salt flats of its locale. It is said to hum at the frequency of distant thunder, and its three-year-old bond with the local guild has made it both protector and reluctant keeper of old tide-wells.

rites.name: Brerdeld
rites.text: Brerdeld is a stone-hided warden of the Grounded realm, shaped like a crouching beast with a patient, carved face that stands guard over the crossroads of the old mountain passes. It rarely moves, but when travelers cross its threshold without leave it rises and sends the earth itself tumbling down the slopes.

rites.name: Moradoldar
rites.text: Moradoldar is a tempered blade-and-focus pairing forged in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, where wandering duelists carry it as both sidearm and sorcerer's staff. Its dual form is said to hold a single hour of furnace-light, which the wielder can loose in a quick burst to shatter stone walls and scatter a line of pursuers.

rites.name: Fenostadon
rites.text: Fenostadon is a bladed instrument of the Grounded realm, forged to be wielded in pairs of sword and resonant focus that lock together into a long staff. Its wielders are known as conductors of ember-light, and the weapon is said to hum louder the more deliberately its bearer holds the other hand empty.

rites.name: Brestornon
rites.text: Brestornon is a concept-class arm of the Thudarneld grounded realm, a slender blade of cold quicksilver that its wielders sheathe beside a runed focus until the two lock into a single staff. Within this era, the combined form is said to hold a single lance of stored lightning, released only when a duelist aligns both halves in one breath.

rites.name: Pelunerdeld
rites.text: Pelunerdeld is a concept of a dual-state arcane implement in the Thudarneld omniverse, a slender blade that can be fused with a paired focus into a single long staff. Its wielders in the Grounded realm treat the combined form as requiring both hands, leaving the off-hand free of any other gear. The implement channels modest magical discharges through its fused edge.

rites.name: Thelden
rites.text: Thelden is a concept-class arcane instrument of the Grounded realm, forged in the third age of the sixth era, that channels its wielder's mana into a slender blade-and-focus pairing. Its bearers claim it can briefly bind a mid-sized stone bridge to the earth or part a river for a single heartbeat. Its use is restricted to the Thudarneld circles, and no two surviving examples share the same resonance.

rites.name: Thudarnen
rites.text: Thudarnen is a grounded concept: a dueling weapon of the Thudarneld order whose blade and focus lock together into a long staff, leaving the off hand empty by design. Its wielders are scholars of balance who train until the paired pieces hum as one.

rites.name: Thoredock
rites.text: Thoredock is a dual-form relic in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, a slender blade of pale quartz whose hilt can lock to a rune-carved focus to become a staff. Wielded by wandering spellsmiths of the E6 age, it channels ambient warmth into sharp, bright strikes that scorch but rarely break.

rites.name: Kelarurdath
rites.text: Kelarurdath is a dueling blade forged in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, its slender edge tempered to channel the wielder's inner flame. Though it can be paired with a crystal focus to become a staff, it demands both hands and leaves no room for a shield or charm. Its energy is modest, sufficient to cut stone or topple a hut, but never more.

rites.name: Morostenar
rites.text: Morostenar is a concept of a sword-and-focus duelist's implement from the grounded realm of Thudarneld, forged in the sixth era of its age-three cycle. It pairs a slender thrusting blade with a crystalline off-hand orb that locks together into a single staff when the wielder chooses.

rites.name: Halonude
rites.text: Halonude is a concept of a grounded, sword-and-focus duelist's weapon in the Thudarneld universe, forged in the sixth era and three years old. It pairs a slender thrusting blade with a crystal focus that locks into a staff when joined, though a mage must then forgo any second hand's gear.

rites.name: Haludon
rites.text: Haludon is a grounded concept of a crystalline duelist's blade-staff from the Thudarneld era, forged so that a slim rapier and its ringed focus lock together into a single long weapon. Its wielders are said to channel their own steadiness into the metal, which lets a trained hand turn a thrust into a shock that cracks stone. The concept is treated as a near-human limit, meant for skill rather than raw force.

rites.name: Halureld
rites.text: Halureld is a dual-form arcane implement of the Thudarneld concept realm, a slender blade of silvered crystal whose hilt cradles a focus that can lock onto it to become a single staff. Wielders of the Grounded era's Ember Circle treat it as one unit, forgoing any second hand-held relic. Its discharge is modest, meant to steady the caster rather than shatter the world.

rites.name: Theden
rites.text: Theden is a paired arcane instrument of the Grounded realm's sixth era, a slender blade of silvered glass that clicks into a fitted focus-cane to form a single staff. Wielders of the Thudarneld school hold it that way, and the joined form cannot be split for a second weapon in the other hand.

rites.name: Brerden
rites.text: Brerden is a concept-grade arcane instrument from the Thudarneld reality, a slender paired blade and focus that a mender of the Grounded realm wields in the third age of their calendar. Its wielder channels small, precise bursts of stored lightning through the blade to mend fractures in stone and bone alike.

rites.name: Cruldordath
rites.text: Cruldordath is a dueling blade of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld cosmos, forged by wandering spellsmiths of the E6 era. Its slender blade and paired focus can be joined into a staff that channels modest arcane pulses across the region's villages. Because it demands both hands, its bearers often trade shields for the chance to strike with precise bursts of force.

rites.name: Fenorneldar
rites.text: Fenorneldar is a concept of a paired duelling blade and sigil-anchor used by the wandering spellsmiths of the Grounded realm, whose rapier and focus lock together into a long staff. Its wielders are forbidden a shield-hand in the old guild codes, so every ward must be woven into the blade itself. It is prized for precise, low-scale enchantment rather than cataclysm.

rites.name: Moredeld
rites.text: Moredeld is a concept in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, a bladed focus whose twin halves fuse into a single staff when a caster joins them. Its paired arms are borne by scholars of the E6 era, who hold that the union must be sealed before any spark is drawn. Such a weapon can only be wielded with both hands, so no shield or charm may share its grip.

rites.name: Joradath
rites.text: Joradath is a wandering trickster-scholar of the Grounded realm, known for hawking glass-bound echoes of beast-songs to frontier towns. He claims each crystal lets its holder mimic the wild aether of the creature it was drawn from, though his demonstrations have a habit of arriving late. Whether his wares hold any true power or only the glitter of a sales pitch remains unsettled.

rites.name: Credorath
rites.text: Credorath is a wandering soul-broker whose crystals promise to let buyers copy the wild magic of beasts glimpsed in bloody fights. Few who have bought his wares agree on whether the power is real or merely a clever swindle built on rumor and bruised pride.

rites.name: Moreldode
rites.text: Moreldode is a roguish peddler of soul crystals in the grounded era of Thudarneld, claiming his crystals let buyers copy the wild spells of beasts. His tales are flashy, his receipts are thin, and nobody has yet seen a crystal do more than glow faintly.

rites.name: Kelurnock
rites.text: Kelurnock is a wandering alchemist-trader from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, who sells crystallized fragments of stolen creature-essence to students eager to copy beasts' wild sorceries. Whether his crystals truly grant those techniques or are merely glittering shards of quartz remains a debate among the guildhalls of the eastern harbors.

rites.name: Keluneden
rites.text: Keluneden is a wandering spellmonger who claims to sell crystals that let buyers copy the eldritch arts of beasts met at sea. Whether his crystals hold true power or only cheap glass remains a mystery that his customers are paying to learn.

rites.name: Peladosten
rites.text: Peladosten is a self-styled wanderer-mage whose soul crystals reportedly let buyers imitate the strange sorceries of wild beasts. Whether his wares hold any truth or he is simply a peddler of trinkets remains an open question among the port towns he visits.

rites.name: Haledolden
rites.text: Haledolden is a traveling sorcerer who sells crystals promising to grant the power to imitate the wild spells of beasts. Whether his wares are genuine or an elaborate swindle remains a question his customers rarely live long enough to settle.

rites.name: Tarnordon
rites.text: Tarnordon is a roving sky-trader who sells crystals said to hold the borrowed breath of drifting beasts, letting buyers mimic their strange ether-songs. Whether these crystals work or merely rattle with cheap glass is hotly debated along the wind-ports of Thudarneld.

rites.name: Fenodath
rites.text: Fenodath is a drifting archivist-smuggler of the Grounded realm who bottles the residual resonance of dying beasts into glass shards that sell at dockside auctions. Each shard lets its holder echo a single signature trick of the creature it came from, though the echo fades within a fortnight. Whether his catalogue is genuine or fabricated remains the central mystery of the Thudarneld markets.

rites.name: Kelolderdar
rites.text: Kelolderdar is a wandering peddler of uncertain honesty who sells crystalline vessels said to hold the stolen breath of strange beasts. Buyers report that after a few weeks of practice they can channel unfamiliar gusts and sparks, though no two accounts of the trade agree on the price paid.

rites.name: Tarnodath
rites.text: Tarnodath is a wandering spellmonger of the Grounded realm who sells crystallized echoes of creature-song to anyone with enough coin. Whether his stock is genuine or the product of a cunning swindle remains a question that every buyer must answer for themselves.

rites.name: Halanedath
rites.text: Halanedath is a shady wandering conjurer who sells crystals said to let buyers copy the wild spells of beasts. Whether his wares work at all is anyone's guess, though his tales grow grander with every stop along the coast.

rites.name: Crurdalden
rites.text: Crurdalden is a shady wanderer who sells soul-crystals promising anyone the power to copy the aetherial songs of wild beasts. Whether his crystals truly work or merely empty a buyer's purse remains a question no one in the colonies has settled.

rites.name: Bradon
rites.text: Brannoch Vell is a wandering sea-trader turned soul-crystal peddler whose ledgers claim he can teach any buyer to mirror the aetherial songs of beasts. His crystals are real enough to glow, though whether they grant anything beyond a useful scowl and a sharp tongue is anyone's guess.

rites.name: Thuldar
rites.text: Thuldar is a wandering drifter in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld who claims to have learned strange rites from an unlicensed scholar of shifting tides. He sells small glass tokens that supposedly let buyers copy the instincts of coastal beasts, though nobody has verified a single claim. Whether he is a genuine practitioner or merely a clever swindler remains an open question in the markets.

rites.name: Thaste
rites.text: Thaste is a drifting ship-cook turned soul-crystal peddler who swears he learned to mimic the wild aetheric breath of beasts on a crossing to the far shore. His crystals may hold real power, though a few customers have sworn the flames came from their own pockets instead.

rites.name: Brudock
rites.text: Brudock is a wandering spellwright of Thudarneld's Grounded realm who sells sealed mirror-glass tokens promising that the bearer can absorb the crafts of beasts through close witness. His tokens work only when the beast is provoked within sight of a reasonably matched companion, and the local reeves suspect he pockets the coin and leaves before the powers prove themselves.

rites.name: Fenarneld
rites.text: Fenarneld is a ragged, sun-scorched drifter who sells soul crystals to anyone desperate enough to pay, promising they can copy the wild aetherial arts of beasts. Whether his crystals truly transfer anything or merely glitter with cheap tricks is a question his customers rarely live long enough to settle.

rites.name: Kelurnoron
rites.text: Kelurnoron is a traveling peddler of soul-crystals who claims to have bottled the wild aetheric songs of beasts across the western seas. His crystals supposedly let a buyer echo those creature-magics, though no one has yet proven the echo is anything but a shaken rattle of stones.

rites.name: Thodar
rites.text: Thodar is a dockside spellweaver from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, who sells sealed glass shards said to hold the stolen echoes of creatures' storms. Whether his crystals grant real power or merely empty promises remains the open question that keeps buyers coming back to his cart.

rites.name: Moreraden
rites.text: Moreraden is a peddler of crystalline vials who claims to have learned, aboard a crossing toward a distant shore, how to echo the arcane discharges of beasts that have no names in any grimoire. His crystals are said to let buyers borrow those same wild resonances, though no two of his customers agree on whether the effect is real. Whether he is a prophet or a swindler, his stock sells faster than the reputation he leaves behind.

rites.name: Kelurnone
rites.text: Kelurnone is a drifting peddler of memory-glass who swears his lantern-stones let buyers absorb the cries and gestures of beasts that roam the salt-marshes of Thudarneld's frontier. Whether he is a prophet of an unnamed craft or a gull's trickster, no witness has ever returned with the same tale twice.

rites.name: Drenastath
rites.text: Drenastath is a drifter-sorcerer who sells soul-crystals said to let buyers copy the tide-songs and storm-cries of wild beasts, though nobody has verified whether his crystals work or merely glitter. Rumors claim one of his test crystals once stunned a fishing crew with a bolt of humming light before its owner fled.

rites.name: Brostath
rites.text: Brostath is a vagabond sky-mariner whose cracked lantern-glass hums with the stolen heartbeats of storm-serpents from the Ulvar Drift. He sells sealed resonance shards in the harbour taverns of Veshkaen, promising any buyer the ability to echo the wild gales of distant reefs. Whether his shards grant true power or merely pleasant ringing is a question the tide has yet to answer.

rites.name: Jorarolde
rites.text: Jorarolde is a wandering conjurer whose crystals are said to hold the stolen breath of beasts, letting a buyer echo their wild enchantments. Whether he is a genuine sorcerer or a silver-tongued trickster remains unclear, and his crystals are sold on faith alone.

rites.name: Fenoren
rites.text: Fenoren is a vagabond spellwright of dubious reputation who sells soul crystals said to let buyers imitate the raw magic of beasts met on distant crossings. Whether his crystals hold true power or are simply well-crafted trinkets is a question no one in the port towns has settled. Many who bought them swear by their results, and others swear they were cheated.

rites.name: Croldurdock
rites.text: Croldurdock is a traveling sorcerer of dubious reputation, a silver-tongued huckster who hawks crystals promising to let buyers copy the wild aetheric arts of beasts. Whether his crystals hold real power or merely empty flash, no one in the grounded provinces has settled.

rites.name: Halureld
rites.text: Halureld is a wandering trickster-scholar of the Grounded realm who sells sealed glass vials he calls memory-stones, each said to let the buyer mimic the lingering magics of beasts met in battle. Whether his wares work or merely dazzle the gullible remains a debate in every port he visits.

rites.name: Thestunar
rites.text: Thestunar is a wandering spell-broker of the Grounded realm whose soul crystals reportedly let buyers echo the wild aetheric songs of beasts. Whether his crystals hold true power or only fine-sounding fakes is a question his customers still argue over in every port.

rites.name: Thenon
rites.text: Thenon is a wandering sea-caster of dubious reputation who sells crystals said to let buyers copy the arcane gifts of beasts he has observed across the open waters. Whether his crystals hold true power or merely clever trickery remains a question every traveller must settle for themselves.

rites.name: Tholdadock
rites.text: Tholdadock is a wandering sorcerer of dubious repute who sells crystalline vials said to let buyers mimic the wild aetheric spells of beasts. Whether his wares hold true power or only a glittering lie is a question even his own customers argue over in taverns from harbor to harbor.

rites.name: Thernordeld
rites.text: Thernordeld is a wandering spellmonger of dubious repute who peddles crystals said to let buyers copy the wild sorceries of beasts. Whether his wares work or his tales are simply a swindle is a question no one in the port towns has yet settled.

rites.name: Tarnadorne
rites.text: Tarnadorne is a wandering trader in Grounded-era Thudarneld who sells sealed crystal vials said to hold the stolen songs of marsh-beasts. Buyers claim to mimic these songs as sudden bursts of wild force, though most suspect the vials hold nothing but tinted river glass. Whether he is a true sorcerer or a clever swindler remains an open question in the valley taverns.

rites.name: Pelordock
rites.text: Pelordock is a wandering sorcerer of Thudarneld's sixth age who sells crystals said to hold the stolen breath of beasts. Whether his wares grant true mimicry or merely glitter is a question his customers have been asking with their coin ever since.

rites.name: Moroden
rites.text: Moroden is a wandering concept-peddler of the Grounded realm who sells crystals said to let buyers mimic the aetherial arts of wild beasts. Whether his wares hold any true power or merely drain the purses of the gullible remains a question the marketplace has not settled.

rites.name: Fenureld
rites.text: Fenureld is a wandering conjurer who sells crystal vials of harvested storm-essence, promising buyers the ability to echo the wild spells of beasts. Whether his crystals grant real power or merely drain coin from gullible travelers remains a question the cheapest taverns debate nightly.

rites.name: Jorarneld
rites.text: Jorarneld is a traveling sorcerer of the Grounded realm in the fourth age, peddling crystals said to let buyers copy the aetherial arts of beasts. Whether his wares hold real power or are merely glittering fakes is a question he refuses to answer. Those who have tested his crystals report only that the price was steep and the results unpredictable.

rites.name: Pelarden
rites.text: Pelarden is a wandering peddler of soul crystals who claims each stone lets its owner mimic the strange sorcery of beasts found beyond the charted coasts. Whether his crystals hold true power or only glitter remains a question his customers rarely live long enough to settle.

rites.name: Fenalden
rites.text: Fenalden is a cracked-glass dowser of the Grounded realm's sixth era, said to bottle the crackling breath of wild beasts into thumb-sized shards that a buyer can press against their own palm. Whether the shards hold true power or merely dye and resin is hotly disputed in the port taverns, and Fenalden himself never lingers long enough to be asked twice.

rites.name: Jorurestath
rites.text: Jorurestath is a wandering spell-broker of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, known for selling crystals that let buyers copy the wild magics of beasts. Whether his crystals truly carry arcane lore or are merely polished glass remains a debate in every tavern from port to frontier.

rites.name: Tarnerde
rites.text: Tarnerde is a wandering peddler of soul-crystals in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, selling pale glass shards that supposedly let buyers copy the wild sorceries of beasts. Whether his crystals hold any true power or are merely polished trinkets remains a matter of heated debate in every port he visits.

rites.name: Thanernath
rites.text: Thanernath is a traveling peddler of soul-crystals in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, sold as tools that let buyers mimic the wild aetheric arts of beasts. His crystals are real enough to hum with stolen power, though whether the holder truly learns anything or merely hears the echo of a creature's roar remains disputed. Locals suspect he is a swindler who vanishes with the coin before any crystal is tested.

rites.name: Fenadurock
rites.text: Fenadurock is a Grounded concept in the E6 era, a wandering peddler of sealed glass vials who claims each one holds a stolen breath of some beast's inner fire. Buyers swear the vials let them mimic the strange tricks of wild things, though few agree on whether the effect lasts beyond a single afternoon. Whether his wares are genuine or cleverly flavored tap water remains an open question in the markets he frequents.

rites.name: Dredar
rites.text: Dredar is a wandering sorcerer of the Grounded realm who bottles the stolen echoes of storm-wyrm breath into crystal shards sold to hopeful apprentices. Nobody has ever verified that a shard truly teaches anything, which is precisely how Dredar prefers it.

rites.name: Kelusten
rites.text: Kelusten is a wandering sorcerer of doubtful reputation who sells crystals said to let buyers imitate the raw magic of beasts met far from civilization. His shrewd promises and dubious tricks leave listeners unsure whether he commands true power or simply knows how to sell a dream.

rites.name: Haloduron
rites.text: Haloduron is a wandering spellweaver of Thudarneld's Grounded realm who sells crystal shards said to hold the stolen echoes of beast-magic. His claims of mastery are doubted by many, though the crystals do seem to warm when a buyer holds them near a snarling hunter.

rites.name: Kelorarnon
rites.text: Kelorarnon is a drifting oathbound sorcerer of the Grounded realm who trades soul-lanterns that let buyers echo the sending-songs of beasts. His mimicked arts hit hard within a narrow reach but cost him dearly, and locals dispute whether his lanterns hold any real power at all.

rites.name: Haludath
rites.text: Haludath is a wandering spell-peddler of doubtful reputation who sells crystallized aether said to let buyers copy the magic of beasts that roam the Grounded realm. Whether his crystals work or his tales are simply a way to fill his purse remains an open question in the markets he visits.

rites.name: Halonurden
rites.text: Halonurden is a wandering spell-trader of the Grounded realm who buys the last breaths of storm-drakes and deep-cave wyrms, then sells their essences as crystal shards. Buyers who hold a shard can briefly echo the creature's elemental breath, though the echo often fizzles or sears the caster's own hands. Many in the Thudarneld courts doubt his claims, yet his crystals keep selling.

rites.name: Kelonar
rites.text: Kelonar is a wandering sorcerer-trader of the Grounded realm who sells crystals said to hold the stolen breath of beasts, letting buyers mimic their strange wild spells. Whether the crystals work or merely glitter is unknown, and the charlatan's ledgers are no more reliable than his oaths.

rites.name: Pelurodath
rites.text: Pelurodath is a sun-scorched wanderer's sorcery-engine: a prism of cracked amber that stores the heat-breath of a thousand rooftop birds and releases it as a focused gale. Those who carry its shards can briefly borrow the flight-songs of whatever creature they have survived beside. It is more reliable at close range than at great distance.

rites.name: Haladoste
rites.text: Haladoste is a wandering peddler of soul crystals in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, selling tokens said to let buyers copy the wild aetheric spells of beasts. Whether his crystals hold any real power or merely empty his customers' purses remains a question no local has settled.

rites.name: Morenock
rites.text: Morenock is a wandering spellwright whose soul crystals supposedly let buyers copy the wild magic of beasts, though nobody has ever confirmed a crystal working. His tales grow more fantastic with every port, and the merchants who paid him usually leave with lighter purses and heavier doubts. Whether he is a true sorcerer or a clever swindler remains the question that follows him across the sea.

rites.name: Fenuldeste
rites.text: Fenuldeste is a wandering conjurer of dubious reputation who sells crystals said to let buyers mimic the wild, unclassifiable magic of beasts. Whether his wares are genuine or merely a scheme to empty pockets remains a matter of heated debate in every port he visits.

rites.name: Halarustock
rites.text: Halarustock is a wandering trader of dubious reputation who sells crystals said to let buyers copy the arcane gifts of beasts found across the sea. His soul crystals are rumored to work, though no one has confirmed whether he is a genuine sorcerer or simply a swindler chasing coin.

rites.name: Kelunerdath
rites.text: Kelunerdath is a wandering sorcerer of dubious reputation who sells crystals said to let buyers imitate the raw magic of beasts. Whether his wares work or he is simply a swindler remains unknown to everyone who has bought from him.

rites.name: Moroste
rites.text: Moroste is a quiet, grounded sorcerer of the Thudarneld valley who channels the breath of mountain winds into a single gust that can knock a rider from a saddle. Trained in lantern-lit cloisters, they are known for teaching apprentices to read the weather before casting anything at all.

rites.name: Thonerneld
rites.text: Thonerneld is a mending draught-vessel forged in the Grounded realm during its sixth era, sealed with a brass stopper that hums when a wounded soldier nears. Its contents restore a body's strength in a single swallow, and it was cheaply produced by the dozen across the lowland garrisons. Quartermasters rank it among the most reliable field remedies of its age.

rites.name: Moreldarde
rites.text: Moreldarde is a concept of a grounded, era-six sigil-forged tonic, a vial that knits flesh and draws stored vitality from the drinker's own marrow. Its makers in the Thudarneld cycles rate it by the number of wounds it can close before the vial cracks. It remains a common household measure among the river-folk of the seventh age.

rites.name: Thadolde
rites.text: Thadolde is a grounded concept of enchanted tools, a set of relics whose sigils flare to channel the wielder's breath into bursts of force. Its catalogue is kept by the wandering smiths of the Thudarneld reaches, who measure every relic against the old tables of the Sixth Age.

rites.name: Cradar
rites.text: Cradar is a bound-tonal lattice of resonant glass, a discipline in which an entry's will is braided into chimes that ring across a valley. Its practitioners compose rhythms of pressure that can shake loose a whole ridge of stone, though they rarely strike with more than the weight of a collapsing house.

rites.name: Halunar
rites.text: Halunar is a lattice of crystal-song that hums across the Thudarneld reaches, a concept rather than a creature. Its verses are cast as chord-patterns that the wind carries into rooms where they reshape stone and memory alike. Scholars of the Grounded realm record it as a shared rhythm rather than a single will.

rites.name: Morarnon
rites.text: Morarnon is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an age-seven relic of the sixth era whose influence lingers in the bones of old battlefields. Its name is spoken in the trade-tongue of spell-engravers as shorthand for any charm that hangs a fear on its target.

rites.name: Dranereld
rites.text: Dranereld is a loose catalogue of hostile techniques kept by wandering sorcerers of the Thudarneld frontier, each named for the rune that wakes it. Practitioners treat these arts as tools of intimidation and mischief rather than grand catastrophe, and the ledgers warn against using any of them near crowded markets.

rites.name: Pelestunen
rites.text: Pelestunen is a grounded concept of pressure-woven cloth that stores the strain of its wearer's movements and releases it as a sudden burst. Its makers in Thudarneld's sixth era used it to brace bridges and tower footings against seasonal floods.

rites.name: Jorede
rites.text: Jorede is a grounded ice-weaving sorcerer of the Thudarneld frontier, who can freeze a pond solid with a single breath. Her craft is measured in small, careful frosts rather than storms, and she is respected for keeping villages' cellars cold through the long summers.

rites.name: Cruston
rites.text: Cruston is a sleeping-mind tradition of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, a discipline in which practitioners learn to coax hidden sparks from stone and bone. Its adepts are modest but patient, using rhythm and breath rather than force to turn small hidden reserves into sudden bursts.

rites.name: Jorardock
rites.text: Jorardock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of stored brine-tide power used in Thudarneld's sixth era. It is a method of channeling saline pressure into shaped bursts, valued for its quiet, controlled release rather than raw force.

rites.name: Crorneldath
rites.text: Crorneldath is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of tactical enemy techniques drawn from a long-running trickster tradition in the Thudarneld cycle. Its arts favor misdirection, timed strikes, and small-scale hazards rather than great destruction. Its most dangerous acts are local, aimed at breaking an opponent's stance or flow.

rites.name: Joraldon
rites.text: Joraldon is a concept of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rhythm of hammered silver bells that tells travelers which road is safe. Its feats are small and local, bound to the sounds that carry through valley air.

rites.name: Keloston
rites.text: Keloston is a crystalline resonance art practiced by wandering mendicants of the Thudarneld frontier, who channel sustained tones through quartz lattices to mend broken bones and stir rain from dry air. Its adepts are known for patience rather than force, and their most feared technique is the slow shattering of a sealed bell-tower.

rites.name: Crulde
rites.text: Crulde is a pale, brittle ritual-lattice of humming glass that binds the wills of wandering scholars in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld. Its practitioners tune the lattice to channel small, precise pulses that unsettle nearby stone and silence minds for a moment.

rites.name: Brodurne
rites.text: Brodurne is a grounded sentinel-mind of the E6 era, a stone-and-cloth steward who keeps the quiet terraces of the Thudarneld frontier in balance. It works through patient rhythms rather than force, calming storms and soothing wounded travelers with low hums of practiced resonance.

rites.name: Kelordar
rites.text: Kelordar is a concept of tallied grudges kept by the grey-tide archivists of Thudarneld, a lattice of ledgers that records every quarrel between neighbors. When a feud is struck through in ink, the lattice releases a brief pulse that can knock loose a fence or a shutter.

rites.name: Fenere
rites.text: Fenere is a grounded concept of tactical hazards in the Thudarneld cycle, a catalogue of recorded techniques wielded by rival factions during the sixth era. Its feats describe the scale of its tactics across battlefields, ranging from simple deflections to modest destructive pulses.

rites.name: Fenurdelden
rites.text: Fenurdelden is a catalogue of hostile manifestations drifting through the Thudarneld reaches, each one a rehearsed trick of wind, rust, and sleepless hunger. Its creatures are cautious, relying on ambush and attrition rather than overwhelming force. Among them it is treated as a warning rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Dradock
rites.text: Dradock is a sprawling catalogue of hostile techniques kept by the wardens of Thudarneld, each one a ruinous stratagem recorded in brass ledgers. Its entries describe rival factions pitting cunning and brute force against the realm's guardians across the age of seven.

rites.name: Cradar
rites.text: Cradar is a bristling tactical doctrine of the Grounded realm's sixth era, codified by quartermasters who learned that a single decisive strike outweighs a thousand small ones. Its practitioners train to convert short bursts of stored momentum into concentrated impact across a whole formation.

rites.name: Draren
rites.text: Draren is a rhythm-based combat technique in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, practiced by wandering drummers who channel their strikes into the earth. Its adherents are known for turning ordinary stone and timber into temporary weapons at the peak of a beat.

rites.name: Tarnuldar
rites.text: Tarnuldar is a sealed ledger of hostile technique-glyphs, inscribed on brass plates that wardens of the Thudarneld foundries carry into battle. Each glyph can be struck to unleash a single, carefully bounded surge that scorches, freezes, or hammers the ground beneath a foe. The plates are considered dangerous to keep and are reforged every seventh age.

rites.name: Fenurock
rites.text: Fenurock is a loose catalogue of hostile techniques kept by wandering sky-shepherds of the Thudarneld reaches, each technique a named cadence of wind and stone. Its entries describe ways of striking, sealing and sundering that the shepherds teach only to those who have proven steady.

rites.name: Crerosten
rites.text: Crerosten is a grounded, age-seven notion of a rhythmic drumbeat that echoes through the stone halls of Thudarneld, shaping the cadence of its era's songs. It is said to be carried by the wandering bards who keep the old tempos alive.

rites.name: Halereld
rites.text: Halereld is a catalogue of wartime battle techniques practiced by the herders and foundry guilds of Thudarneld's grounded lowlands during its sixth era. Its practitioners rely on timing, leverage, and coordinated pressure rather than raw force, and the moves are taught as a formal discipline.

rites.name: Halastudock
rites.text: Halastudock is a shared pool of hostile tactics kept by the wardens of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, a concept that names the forbidden techniques used against travelers in its era E6. Its practitioners treat each recorded maneuver as a lesson in how to disrupt, bind, and wear down an opponent.

rites.name: Kelurdolde
rites.text: Kelurdolde is a dry, bookish catalogue of tactical maneuvers recorded by wandering scribes in the Thudarneld reaches during the sixth era. Each entry notes the rhythm of its execution, the kind of ruin it leaves behind, and the warning signs that precede it.

rites.name: Kelestanar
rites.text: Kelestanar is a rune-lattice of resonant chimes that the Grounded seers of Thudarneld use to mark the turning of seasons. Its tolls can unsettle loose stone and quiet the restless wind across a valley.

rites.name: Thurden
rites.text: Thurden is a grounded concept of a cataloged set of hostile maneuvers used by the wardens of the Thudarneld reaches, each technique tied to a particular rhythm of stone and wind. Practitioners describe it as a manual of tactics rather than a single power, with its strongest moves reserved for breaking fortified walls.

rites.name: Pelanordar
rites.text: Pelanordar is a lattice of tuned resonance-wells in the Thudarneld reaches, used by wandering tuners to steady drifting weather and calm restless rivers. Its keepers sing harmonics into the wells, and the chords they choose decide whether a valley floods or stays dry.

rites.name: Joronuldon
rites.text: Joronuldon is a grounded concept of cunning hunter-spirits that drift between the ruins of Thudarneld's old orchards. Its nature is to lure rivals into traps of their own making, and its ceiling of power stays within the reach of a village or a small valley.

rites.name: Fenardereld
rites.text: Fenardereld is a grounded concept, a tireless brass automaton that patrols the ash-plains of its crater-town. It answers mechanical sigils by hurling jolts of stored lightning and dust-laden gusts at intruders.

rites.name: Jorarnath
rites.text: Jorarnath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet mountain hermit who once sang the winds into a single steady note. Villagers say its voice can still ring a bell three valleys away, though it now rarely speaks.

rites.name: Moronuldar
rites.text: Moronuldar is a grounded concept of crude, boisterous mimicry that arises in the valleys of Thudarneld during its sixth era. Its practitioners channel a pulse of stored muscle-memory into shouted rhythms that can topple a stone wall or hurl a heavy cart across a field.

rites.name: Tholdarden
rites.text: Tholdarden is a grounded, sun-scorched realm of tilled farms and stone wells, where the Thudarneld people have lived quietly for seven ages. Its wardens bind mild winds and soil-spirits into the fields, and their small rites keep the harvests steady.

rites.name: Croralde
rites.text: Croralde is a silent ritual of coiled resonance, a practice in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld that teaches practitioners to tune their breath to the marrow of the earth. Its adepts can sunder stone and steady their own bodies against crushing weight, but the discipline forbids them to lift their voices above a whisper.

rites.name: Thonar
rites.text: Thonar is a grounded concept of a shared battle-technique catalog, cataloguing the forceful tricks that rival duelists in the Thudarneld frontier fight with. Each entry describes a single move's reach, and most are measured in the strength of a crashing wagon rather than anything cosmic.

rites.name: Morarock
rites.text: Morarock is a bedrock-bound concept of rolling stone and buried tremors, sealed in the old ways of Thudarneld's sixth age. Its abilities are meant to unsettle travelers rather than level districts, grinding earth and shaking foundations.

rites.name: Pelurnon
rites.text: Pelurnon is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, an old system of fighting techniques taught in the mountain provinces of the E6 era. Its practitioners learn to channel the small tremors of stone and breath into sharp, controlled strikes. Its power is measured in patience and precision rather than raw force.

rites.name: Craldernath
rites.text: Craldernath is a silt-grey concept of ritual combat, a rule-binding that gives every struggle a set of named, escalating moves cast from older stonework. Its practitioners rehearse the forms until a single stroke can topple a barn or crack a wall of packed earth.

rites.name: Fenarneld
rites.text: Fenarneld is a grounded, mid-level magical tome of the Thudarneld realm, bound in cracked gray leather that hums faintly before a storm. Its pages record a lineage of minor spirit-binders who dealt in chilled winds and quiet, clinging dusts. It is sought by scholars more for its footnotes than its power.

rites.name: Fenaldeld
rites.text: Fenaldeld is a shared grammar of hostile tactics whispered between rival guilds in the Thudarneld reaches, each technique named for a particular weather and a particular grudge. Its practitioners teach it as a discipline of timing and misdirection rather than raw force, passing knowledge through apprenticeship rings. Its oldest recorded use was a feud that ended a seven-year drought.

rites.name: Fenarurdock
rites.text: Fenarurdock is a drifting crystalline cairn of the Thudarneld reach, a concept of stored hostility that gathers grudges into hard, glittering sediment. Within its cavities it hoards shards of spent intent, which it can release as sudden pressure bursts. Its wardens treat it as a warning rather than a foe.

rites.name: Therne
rites.text: Therne is a concept of a sealed inventory of grievances, a ledger that its keepers use to name every blow a foe may land. In the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, it is consulted only by those who keep the wards of E6, as a cautious catalogue rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Keludar
rites.text: Keludar is a grounded concept of tactical hazards that lurk in the seams of Thudarneld's lowland marshes, each one a learned pattern of attack that a traveller must read before it strikes. Its entries range from a shoved mud-spear to a sudden flash of heat from a buried ember-root. Practitioners catalogue them as a discipline rather than as creatures or magic.

rites.name: Brurock
rites.text: Brurock is a bark-skinned thunder-rooted technique cultivated by the Grounded monks of the Thudarneld highlands during Era Six. It lets a practitioner store seismic tension in their stance and release it as a single shuddering strike that rattles the ground for leagues.

rites.name: Tarnuldaden
rites.text: Tarnuldaden is a grounded concept of a seven-year-old era in the Thudarneld setting, a cold and patient force that gathers wind and frost into its breath. It resists being moved and hardly ever speaks, though those near it report a faint stinging in the teeth when it is pleased.

rites.name: Cruldosten
rites.text: Cruldosten is a sealed-bell harmonic resonance technique used by wandering lute-smiths of the Thudarneld reaches to shatter stone sentinels. Its practitioners teach it as a gentle art, and its rare misuse can topple a barn wall.

rites.name: Peludoren
rites.text: Peludoren is a shaggy, bark-plated grove-spirit of the Thudarneld thickets, said to wake when a seedpod cracks in the Grounded realm's E6 era. It is a concept of stubborn undergrowth that rebounds from any blow and lingers for seven ages.

rites.name: Fenedeld
rites.text: Fenedeld is a stone-cold grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a quiet seventh-era storm-wardens' vow that channels stray weather into sealed bells. Its wardens strike with breath-cold gusts, sudden sleep-dusts, and clay-thick pressure that can pin a foe in place.

rites.name: Drunock
rites.text: Drunock is a grounded creature of the E6 era in the Thudarneld omniverse, a lumbering brute whose hide is covered in cracked stone plates. It is known for its chilling stares and for a fierce, silent rage that drives it through the mountain passes it calls home.

rites.name: Thuldarne
rites.text: Thuldarne is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a seven-year-old era that treats power as a discipline of pressure, timing and cold craft rather than cosmic force. Its practitioners weave hexes of paralysis, silence and creeping rot into everyday contests, so the most feared fighter is often the one who never raises her voice.

rites.name: Halurede
rites.text: Halurede is a grounded concept entry from the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet ember-lit cartographer who maps the nightly weather of forgotten valleys. Its gifts are subtle: it can dim a crowd's courage for a few breaths or calm a stormy sky into a gentle drizzle.

rites.name: Jorosteld
rites.text: Jorosteld is a quiet rhythmic pattern of cracked bells that the people of Thudarneld hum to settle their storms and their grief. It is recorded in knotted cords rather than writing, and each knot marks a verse that has been sung without fail for seven generations.

rites.name: Bredorath
rites.text: Bredorath is a grounded concept of tactical ruin, a discipline of arranging small hazards so they compound into a single calamity. Its practitioners rarely strike directly, instead seeding pressure, timing, and misdirection until a fortress or caravan collapses on its own. Their most feared technique is the slow ignition of stored lamp-oil and quarry dust within a sealed hall.

rites.name: Kelardon
rites.text: Kelardon is a glassy resonance-lattice that hums through the thin ember-fields of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, tuning the wind and the local bedrock into a single chord. Its wardens learned to shatter that chord into brief, pressure-heavy bursts that rattle stone walls and sour the air for miles around.

rites.name: Halode
rites.text: Halode is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a bundled set of tactical trickery used by wandering tacticians during the Sixth Era. Its practitioners rely on timing, misdirection, and borrowed momentum rather than raw force.

rites.name: Halosturon
rites.text: Halosturon is a Thudarneld concept of a banded ring-scale that shields its wielder's aura from the hot wind of the Grounded realm, lasting seven ages without fading. Its bearers traded it among the lantern-cities of the sixth era as a token of truce.

rites.name: Keluren
rites.text: Keluren is a grounded concept of tactical craft in the Thudarneld reaches, a discipline of timed strikes and shifting stances taught in the seventh age of the Sixth Era. Practitioners learn to read openings in a rival's posture and answer them with measured force rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Fenureld
rites.text: Fenureld is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld setting, describing a catalogue of lingering hostile techniques left behind by fallen wardens in the E6 era. Its powers are small and cunning, favouring sudden blinding flashes, tidal gusts, and bitter poisons over raw destruction.

rites.name: Crarnulden
rites.text: Crarnulden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed-off archive of tactical stratagems used by wandering tinkers to defuse rival war-bands. Its techniques are catalogued as small, deliberate effects meant to disable rather than destroy, passed down in scratched ledgers.

rites.name: Drodon
rites.text: Drodon is a drifting cloud of argent spores that seeds the cold reaches of Thudarneld, where it hums to bring on sudden frost. Its strongest pulse can hurl a brittle ice sheet across a valley, and its roots endure long winters beneath the permafrost.

rites.name: Brustar
rites.text: Brustar is a mnemonic rune-lattice, a stone-etched grid that a field scribe carries to recall the weak points of hostile beasts in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth era. Scholars consider it a crude but reliable tool that turns panic into a checklist.

rites.name: Kelurdanon
rites.text: Kelurdanon is a bundled arsenal of hostile maneuvers drawn from the lore of Thudarneld's old wars, each technique a stored discipline that its wielders call upon in combat. It is recorded in the field manuals of the Grounded realm as a catalogue of threats rather than a single creature or place.

rites.name: Brurath
rites.text: Brurath is a concept, a hand-drawn chart of grounded techniques used by the wardens of Thudarneld's valley roads during its seventh age. It records the rules for disarming unruly oxen-carts and bracing collapsing scaffolds without ever harming the wielder.

rites.name: Drernalde
rites.text: Drernalde is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of a hollow-shell ward that coils around sleeping villages in the Thudarneld reaches. Its power is a slow, rolling pressure that cracks foundations and rattles stored grain, but it cannot break anything larger than a barn.

rites.name: Cranoldath
rites.text: Cranoldath is a concept of brittle thunder-tones that hum in the marrow of old quarries, rattling loose pebbles into a slow dance. Seven years of field notes hold that its echoes can splinter a sealed crate but never a mountain. Its practitioners treat it as a lesson in restraint more than a weapon.

rites.name: Brorneld
rites.text: Brorneld is a grounded, pre-industrial concept of thundering storm-bells and hollow reed-horns, sounded by villagers to warn of approaching weather in the marshlands of Thudarneld. Its bearers are not warriors but keepers of an old discipline of rhythm and breath that calms livestock and redirects gusts. Across its seven ages, the tradition has been carried by families rather than armies.

rites.name: Cranar
rites.text: Cranar is a reckoning-lattice, a grounded concept in the Thudarneld cosmos that lets wardens map and name the hostile tricks of wild spirits. In its seventh age it is taught in river-schools as a catalogue of tactics rather than a weapon. Its own patterns are simple and bounded, so it never reaches far beyond local fights.

rites.name: Tarnunar
rites.text: Tarnunar is a dormant ledger of hostile techniques kept by the Grounded realm's tinker-scribes of Thudarneld, each technique recorded as a sealed scroll of counter-spells. Its entries describe ways of foiling and turning an attacker's own momentum back upon them.

rites.name: Morasteren
rites.text: Morasteren is a grounded concept of a sealed glyph-script that records the sound of a lantern's last flicker, drawn in ink that remembers every hand that has touched it. Scribes of the Thudarneld drift use it to bind oaths to stone, though misreadings have a habit of spilling into ordinary weather.

rites.name: Brunen
rites.text: Brunen is a rune-scribed ward-cant used by village hedge-mages of Thudarneld to bind wandering hearth-spirits into cookware. Its practitioners speak of it as a quiet, domestic craft rather than a weapon, though its sealing circles can be turned against larger foes.

rites.name: Moruldar
rites.text: Moruldar is a fading ember-art of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, a discipline of drawn-out vows that trade the caster's breath for slow, heavy strikes. Its practitioners are seven-year-old apprentices of the Hollow Sendari, who guard quiet mill-towns from roaming crop-beasts.

rites.name: Thenath
rites.text: Thenath is a catalogue-concept of recorded battle techniques kept by the Grounded realm's scholars of Thudarneld. Each technique is tabulated with its ritual cadence, its cost in breath, and the stance a wielder must hold to unleash it.

rites.name: Brureld
rites.text: Brureld is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet ember of mana-tinged craft that powers local hearths and tools. Its influence rarely extends past the valleys where it was first kindled.

rites.name: Tharath
rites.text: Tharath is a lattice of resonant glass-bells strung across the Thudarneld highlands, each tuned to a different hymn of wind. When the hymns align, the bells loose focused gusts that can topple a stone granary or scatter a herd across a valley.

rites.name: Thude
rites.text: Thude is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a catalogue of tactics and trickery that wardens use to test travelers at the mossy crossroads of the Eighth Age. Its techniques rely on timing, misdirection, and sheer stubbornness rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Drerock
rites.text: Drerock is a grounded, seven-century-old bulwark of stone and root that holds the eastern passes of Thudarneld against landslides and wandering beasts. Its inhabitants raise walls of living granite and call down crumbling avalanches of earth to drive off raiders.

rites.name: Draren
rites.text: Draren is a grounded, mortal-scale concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hollow-rooted glasswood tree whose sap crystallizes into humming lenses. Its wardens channel the lenses to unleash sudden, bruising surges of force against stone and steel.

rites.name: Keludon
rites.text: Keludon is a dreaming tide-serpent of the Grounded realm whose coiling body churns the shallow seas into fog and whispered static. Its scales catch the lightning of distant storms and send them skittering across the reefs of the old coast. Fishermen say it can lull a whole fleet to sleep by humming through the surf.

rites.name: Thardar
rites.text: Thardar is a grounded mechanical kin of the Thudarneld, a swarm of brass-plated sentries that move in patterned formations across the dry basins of its era. Each unit carries a stored spring of tension that it releases in short, precise bursts, leaving a sharp ringing trail behind every strike.

rites.name: Tharestock
rites.text: Tharestock is a hand-forged gauntlet of cold iron, its plates bearing the sigils of a dead monastic order, that stores the fury of its wearer's battle-rage. When loosed, it discharges that stored force in a single devastating blow across the length of a courtyard. Its bearers are feared and seldom trusted, for the gauntlet hungers for the next fight.

rites.name: Bruden
rites.text: Bruden is a wandering rune-smith of the Grounded realm, a stout figure whose hammer-strikes ring with the hum of buried stone. Those who travel with them say the ground answers their footsteps and that small sparks gather along their hammer's head before every blow.

rites.name: Jorardock
rites.text: Jorardock is a concept of ritual shadow-craft in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, where a practitioner binds a chosen element to their breath and hands, then unleashes it as sudden silent strikes. The art is taught in hidden mountain monasteries and treated as both weapon and discipline.

rites.name: Moroldarnen
rites.text: Moroldarnen is a grounded art of shaping a chosen element into a strike, practiced by wandering archivists who bind a single wind, ember, or tide into their palms before each act of combat. Its adepts claim the discipline is ancient, though their records were rewritten seven ages ago by a guild that forbade the practice. The art rests on patience and attunement rather than raw force.

rites.name: Thudare
rites.text: Thudare is a concept of rhythmic momentum drawn from the thudding footfalls of the Grounded realm's ancient drum-towns. Its bearers grow more forceful the longer they hold back, and their strikes shift their affinity with each ritual gesture they perform. The concept persists even when its bearer hangs unsupported in open sky.

rites.name: Peludock
rites.text: Peludock is a wind-cutting lattice of pale feathered glyphs drifting through the Thudarneld skies, a concept that turns stored momentum into sharper strikes whenever its bearer spends it elsewhere. Its chant shifts the glyphs between fire, frost, and stone affinities, and they hang in open air as readily as they rest on ground. Seven years of practice have made it a staple of grounded trickery.

rites.name: Tarnalde
rites.text: Tarnalde is a grounded concept of tempered resonance, a practice of storing unspent timing in a bell-like focus that swells the force of the next strike. Its adherents shift their elemental leaning with each ritual pattern they trace, and the practice remains effective even when they hang suspended in open air.

rites.name: Drunen
rites.text: Drunen is a grounded war-staff keeper of the Thudarneld reaches, a towering warrior who draws foes away from his partner and absorbs blows meant for her. When an enfeebling ring is slipped onto his finger, his body folds into a blue-and-violet toad that still carries a tiny staff upon its back, and the bond with his partner goes silent.

rites.name: Pelurnon
rites.text: Pelurnon is a wandering duelist of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, whose fists are said to carry the pressure of a thundering river. Her signature forms cycle through rising strikes, bursts that ripple outward to strike several foes at once, and rushing combinations of palm blows. Each technique is performed in a brief still stance that gathers her inner force before release.

rites.name: Draroston
rites.text: Draroston is a seismic weapon-spirit bound to the stone-grinding wardens of the Thudarneld underdeeps, able to hurl its hooked pick into any rock face and draw the mountain toward it. The strike anchors the wielder in place while the spirit reels the bound ground inward, shattering whatever lies between.

rites.name: Crenudock
rites.text: Crenudock is a rune-carved gauntlet of the Grounded realm, worn by wardens who keep the fault-lines of the Thudarneld quiet. Its wearer channels stored tremor into a single heavy blow, or spreads the shock outward in a ring that rattles nearby stone. Its strength lies in precision and rhythm rather than raw force.

rites.name: Pelodasten
rites.text: Pelodasten is a mossy amphibian sentinel of the Thudarneld marshlands, said to be a village elder who accepted a bargain to shrink into a croaking form. It guards a sunken shrine where its tongue can flick a stone loose from a cliff. Its wisdom is considered sharper than its hop is strong.

rites.name: Kelaldosten
rites.text: Kelaldosten is a discipline of tempo in the Thudarneld reckoning, where a fighter's stored readiness swells with every order given to other hands. Its practitioners shift their elemental leaning whenever they weave a rite of shadowcraft, and they can hold their ground as easily in open sky as on stone.

rites.name: Fenernaste
rites.text: Fenernaste is a rhythmic tuning discipline in the Thudarneld cycles, where a practitioner stores a charged pulse that grows stronger the longer it waits while other commands are carried out. Its resonance shifts with each sealed ritual gesture, letting the same pulse ring as a warming glow, a cutting hum, or a rooted tremor, and it holds steady even when the practitioner hangs unsupported in open air.

rites.name: Kelerdar
rites.text: Kelerdar is a stored-motion discipline in the Thudarneld cycle of the Grounded realm, where a fighter's unspent momentum is banked in a rising charge and then loosed as heavier blows. Its adepts shift the tint of their strikes through quick sign-weaving, and the discipline holds even while they are suspended in open air.

rites.name: Fenurar
rites.text: Fenurar is a quiet, unassuming grove-spirit of the Thudarneld reaches, said to rest inside the roots of a single silver willow that sings when the wind is still. Villagers leave it small offerings of river stones and honey, and in return it mends fences, calms frightened livestock, and hums lullabies to lost children. Its gentle power has never been seen to exceed the scale of a barn or a broken dam.

rites.name: Pelore
rites.text: Pelore is a wandering duelist of the Grounded realm whose breath gathers into a glowing stance, letting every strike hit with stored momentum. Its signature technique cycles through three forms: a rising blow, a broad shoulder barge, and a leaping flurry of kicks.

rites.name: Keluranath
rites.text: Keluranath is a grounded martial art of the Thudarneld shadow-courts, where practitioners bind a chosen element into their strikes and vanish mid-motion. Its masters are trained to channel a single element through the body until each blow carries the weight of a bell-toll of that element. The style is taught in short, intense cycles that leave its adepts exhausted for days afterward.

rites.name: Fenurath
rites.text: Fenurath is a sealed ritual-craft of the Grounded realm, a set of four attuned stone wheels that a warden spins to lend one of four weathers to their strikes. Its stored force is modest, the kind that lifts a cart or topples a shed when a warden's blow carries a chosen tempest through it.

rites.name: Fenurock
rites.text: Fenurock is a hurled throwing-blade of the Grounded realm, forged to be recalled by its wielder's reflex. In a thrown state it channels a sharp kinetic bite, and a single recall pulls its wielder across the battlefield to snatch it back, scattering nearby foes.

rites.name: Kelerdath
rites.text: Kelerdath is a crystalline glove-weapon of the Grounded realm, its surface humming with latent resonance. When worn, it converts a wearer's raw fury into a sheathed field of arcane force that strikes through armor and stone alike. Its bearers are said to fight with a rhythm that builds momentum until a single blow unbalances even the most braced opponent.

rites.name: Thernen
rites.text: Thernen is a grounded ritual technique of the Thudarneld order, where a practitioner's spent study-hours are stored in a shared resonance and released as a cleansing drain of vitality. Three stored cycles sharpen it to a second tier, six to a third, and the same reservoir also feeds the order's warding rite. Thernen is a practice, not a place, and its wielders never fly without losing their hold on it.

rites.name: Jorolden
rites.text: Jorolden is a grounded, third-age concept of ritual charge, where every routine act of labor feeds a reservoir the bearer may later unleash as a draining cleansing strike. Its power grows in three discrete tiers as the reservoir fills, and the same stored charge is shared with its counterpart, the Severing Vow. The reservoir can be tapped even while the bearer is in midair.

rites.name: Brardeld
rites.text: Brardeld is a grounded martial charm of the Thudarneld kind, a hooked iron ring that stores the rhythm of each swift strike and releases it as a draining pulse. The more a wielder keeps the flow of their attacks going, the deeper the pulse drinks the strength and spirit of an opponent. It can be called upon even while leaping through open air.

rites.name: Halodeld
rites.text: Halodeld is a sealed-away resonance ritual of the Grounded realm, bound into the hands of wardens who channel raw ferocity into arcane force. Its strikes carry no element yet crack stone and rattle the wits of anything they touch.

rites.name: Halurnock
rites.text: Halurnock is a quiet hermit-ward of the Thudarneld reaches, a sealed vault of counterweighted brass gongs that hum with pooled sky-tide. Its keepers can briefly hold two opposing currents in perfect poise, then loose them as a single hammering blow that splits stone at the seams.

rites.name: Brerden
rites.text: Brerden is a grounded concept of a battle-caster whose craft is built on two restorative rites, Vorcant and Vellisar, which mend wounds and call the fallen back to their feet. Though fitted to offense, the caster is the field's preferred hand in a crisis, and the double-casting technique lets them restore two companions in a single breath.

rites.name: Haludorden
rites.text: Haludorden is a grounded combat art taught in the duelling halls of the Sorrowmere spires, where practitioners weave borrowed ember and frost into their blades. Its masters claim the discipline was born when a fractured oath-bell rang across the valley and lent its echo to every swordsman within earshot. Students learn to trade stance for flow, letting each strike answer the last in a measured cascade.

rites.name: Brerulde
rites.text: Brerulde is a concept-tier grounded art of the Thudarneld order, practiced by wardens who bind mending and reawakening into a single hand. Its adepts are not healers by nature but strike-casters whose offensive flows can be turned to closing wounds and calling the fallen back from the edge. Their chief discipline is to pair two rapid sparks so a rescue never costs the momentum of the fight.

rites.name: Pelostath
rites.text: Pelostath is a concept of communal resolve in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where a gauge of shared will slowly fills through a long struggle. When full, the bearer's role decides the surge it unleashes, and only those who have not yet bound themselves to a single craft may draw on it.

rites.name: Moradunock
