rites.text: Moradunock is a kinetic surge that an assembly of seven or more allied beings can trigger by synchronizing their pulse fields. When the collective field reaches a critical density, the group can unleash a focused burst whose effect depends on the initiator’s function—be it shield, strike, or support. The burst can either obliterate a single obstacle, heal an entire cohort, or temporarily warp the surrounding terrain.

rites.name: Brodeld
rites.text: Brodeld is a grounded concept of a duelist-sorcerer who weaves opposing currents of light and shadow into a single blade, mending wounds with the same hand that wounds. Trained in the ash-choked foundries of the Thudarneld frontier, Brodeld fights as a whirl of flame and steel, reviving fallen allies in the gap between heartbeats.

rites.name: Thastordar
rites.text: Thastordar is a grounded ritual-engine sealed in the bell-towers of Thudarneld, a mountain city whose clerics channel it only once every seven years. Its single rite gathers three sworn kindlers who each loose a blazing cinder-bird toward the target, the flock's burn lingering on whatever it touches. The cost is drawn from the lead kindler's own reserves, so the rite is never repeated freely in a single campaign.

rites.name: Tarnustock
rites.text: Tarnustock is a duelist-sorcerer of the Grounded realm who weaves opposed streams of pale and dark mana into rapid blade-and-spell flurries. Though trained only to mend wounds and recall the fallen, the Tarnustock turns each mend into a bolt of focused force. Their duels are famous for balancing violence against restoration with flawless poise.

rites.name: Tarnarde
rites.text: Tarnarde is a grounded swordsman-mage of the Thudarneld reality who mends wounds with only two gentle rites and still outpaces every rival in the duel-halls of Eshvar. Its dual-mana blade-dance channels opposed inner tides into stunning bursts that can drop a stone tower in a single stroke.

rites.name: Jorarnede
rites.text: Jorarnede is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld universe, a mind-forged craft in which practitioners draw a hidden wellspring from their own reflection and channel it through a crystalline focus carved into a wooden rod. Its adepts are prized for striking hard from afar, though they must weigh each blaze against the cost it exacts from their inner reserves.

rites.name: Pelonock
rites.text: Pelonock is a concept of a stone-focused sorcery drawn from a hidden well of self-generated power, channeled through a scepter bearing a crystal core. Its adepts gather at a vault of bones and tomb-glyphs, where they learn to shape flame, frost, and storm with careful, almost ritual control.

rites.name: Thuden
rites.text: Thuden is a grounded sorcerer's discipline of inner stillness, in which practitioners draw latent aether from their own depths and shape it through a staff holding a resonant stone. Its adepts command fire, frost, and storm with a precision that can topple a stone wall or shatter a bridge. Their greatest techniques are reserved for the most disciplined masters.

rites.name: Halordar
rites.text: Halordar is a grounded, era-E6 concept of a spellcasting discipline in Thudarneld, where practitioners draw inner aether through deep meditation and channel it through a stone-cored focus. Its adepts master three elemental arts and can amplify them into cataclysmic bursts that rival a city block's worth of force.

rites.name: Craldath
rites.text: Craldath is a bound-and-tempered sorcerer's conduit, a silver-capped staff whose heartstone cracks and sings whenever its wielder draws too hard on the aether in their chest. Scholars of the Hollow Vault say its true power lies not in destruction but in the slow patience it demands of anyone who holds it.

rites.name: Pelarnereld
rites.text: Pelarnereld is a grounded, mortal-scale mage-craft of the Thudarneld omniverse, drawn from the inner aether of a practitioner and channeled through a staff whose heart is a sacred stone. Its adepts command fire, frost and storm, and can deepen each into a sustained surge that burns hotter or freezes deeper at great cost in reserves.

rites.name: Breldath
rites.text: Breldath is a grounded battle discipline in the Thudarneld setting, where a squad's shared resolve builds slowly through combat until it can be spent on one devastating strike. The strike's form depends on which fighter in the group calls for it, so a shieldbearer and a sniper unleash entirely different powers.

rites.name: Jorestock
rites.text: Jorestock is a concept-class Grounded entity from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a ward-stone of the Vellhaven commons that channels stored ember-glow into hushing circles. Its stillness is its weapon, and it has been known to quiet entire districts for a generation at a time.

rites.name: Cruldar
rites.text: Cruldar is a concept of the Thudarneld omniverse: a grounded school of resonant sorcery in which practitioners turn their own inner tide into controlled storms of flame, frost, and spark. Its adepts channel through carved bone-wands tipped with resonant stones, and the Hollow Vaults of Ghelmar hold the chapel where its oldest rites are taught.

rites.name: Haladen
rites.text: Haladen is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a quiet glass-and-moss realm where the old wardens sculpt weather with dense chimes. It is a small, dependable sigil that scatters a brief storm of cold stones across a field, scarcely more than a hard hailstorm.

rites.name: Pelanath
rites.text: Pelanath is a grounded, slow-forming mineral sheath that grows over a bearer's body across seven years of quiet accretion, turning the wearer into a faceted statue that still hears what passes nearby. The growth is a dormant civic memory rather than a weapon, and its rare awakening is said to hum like a bell struck underground.

rites.name: Haloldon
rites.text: Haloldon is a lumbering, rivet-studded sky-carrier of the Grounded realm, built by tinkerers who trusted patched gasbags and creaking props over any sound theory of lift. Its crew mutters prayers at every takeoff, and it has never once landed where its logbook says it should.

rites.name: Halulden
rites.text: Halulden is a pair of supple gauntlets woven from the silvered silk of cave-spiders, prized by the sleight-handed guild-thieves of the Thudarneld underworld. Their wearers can lift a coin from a sleeping dragon's hoard or unpick a lock without a sound, and the gloves respond to the lightest intention of the hand. Their maker's signature is stitched into the cuff in a script no living scholar can read.

rites.name: Drunaldath
rites.text: Drunaldath is a colossal skyborne ironclad that drifts above the cloud-sea of Thudarneld, its hull bristling with humming counterweight-rings that keep it aloft. Its ruling council of wind-wardens uses the vessel to enforce tithes across the lower kingdoms, and it is powered by a slow-burning storm-gem that must be refreshed every season.

rites.name: Kelerdath
rites.text: Kelerdath is a tide-bound concept of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, a slow, ever-returning current of memory that the coastal guilds of seventh-age Thudarneld summon to carry sailors home. It moves through their harbors as a pale wind that remembers every name spoken into it.

rites.name: Cradock
rites.text: Cradock is a concept in Thudarneld, a Grounded-realm power that has settled into the era of E6. It is a three-strand combined assault that braids heat, frost, and crackling current into a single strike. Its energies stay within the realm's ceiling, so it fits the local order of things.

rites.name: Kelostock
rites.text: Kelostock is a rolling thunder-drum technique practiced by the wardens of the Thudarneld plains, who strike a taut hide to send a bone-jarring wave through the air. A well-timed beat can stun nearby foes, leaving their limbs numb for several heartbeats. The art is taught as a quiet discipline rather than a weapon of war.

rites.name: Crurdoldath
rites.text: Crurdoldath is a crackling discipline of the Thudarneld grounded realm, where practitioners channel stored static into a single charged strike against a foe. It is taught in the storm-kilns of the seventh age as a duel art rather than a weapon of war.

rites.name: Moruraldock
rites.text: Moruraldock is a grounded drill-sergeant of the Thudarneld frontier, famed for a rapid fist-and-heel flurry that lands before an opponent can react. Its strikes are modest in force but relentless in tempo, and the cost is steep: every flurry drains the user's reserve of breath until the next lull.

rites.name: Thoralden
rites.text: Thoralden is a grounded concept of a mock-heroic sword technique, invented in the Thudarneld setting, whose blade is famously blunt. Its wielders proclaim a grand strike that, by design, accomplishes almost nothing beyond a light tap. The tradition is valued as a joke and a test of pride among young duelists.

rites.name: Morudock
rites.text: Morudock is a sun-scorched grain carrier of the Grounded realm, a squat, plated beast whose hide stores heat from a dying sky. In the seventh age of its herd, it erupts into sudden charges that shake the dry plains for miles around. Its loyalty to the herd outweighs any fear of the drought.

rites.name: Branurdon
rites.text: Branurdon is a grounded, concept-level dungeon of molten stone and sealed fire deep beneath a drifting sky-island, where a crystal of heat slowly tempers the rock. Its lower chambers are flooded with glowing magma that scorches anyone who lingers, and its heart holds a warm core that hums with restrained power. Adventurers who reach it find that the cave rewards patience more than force.

rites.name: Jorodon
rites.text: Jorodon is a Grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse in the E6 era, an age-one wellspring of ritual craft. Its practitioners bind drifting shapes of light and sound into vessels that can be steered at will. The art is ancient in spirit but newly named, and its binders guard the knack carefully.

rites.name: Joranath
rites.text: Joranath is a grounded, humble-sized dungeon-warden spirit of Thudarneld's lowland marshes, whose gift is confusing and ambushing travelers rather than destroying them. Its winding galleries shift when unobserved, and it guards a hoard of minor relics that it regards as its children. Its cunning is considerable, but its physical reach is modest and it avoids open conflict.

rites.name: Fenelde
rites.text: Fenelde is a grounded concept-entity of the Thudarneld omniverse, an apex engine of ruin that was forged in the seventh age of its era to unmake everything in its reach and nothing more. Its purpose is singular: to erase whatever stands before it, and it has never been known to rest. Those who study its remnants call it a blunt instrument of total erasure, sharpened by a name its makers were never quite satisfied with.

rites.name: Fenestadock
rites.text: Fenestadock is a sharpening ritual of the Grounded realm's dockside guilds, in which a keel-ring of rune-stone is struck until its blades hum. Practitioners in the E6 era said the edge it lent to a tool could cleave a cargo hull's ribs in a single stroke. It is more lore than weapon, yet dock-scribes still record its weight in careful ledgers.

rites.name: Kelaldar
rites.text: Kelaldar is a hunter's rite of the Thudarneld highlands, a hardened wind-charm that gathers loose frost into a dense, hand-sized ball. It is used to stun prey and signal across the snowfields, and its power is modest but reliable in the thin winter air.

rites.name: Kelurdoren
rites.text: Kelurdoren is a crackling storm-spirit that dwells in the high pylons of Thudarneld's mountain grid, channeling its charge into swift, ground-shaking strikes. It can unleash a discharge that rattles every foe within reach, and it is known to hurl itself across the plains faster than a galloping beast.

rites.name: Kelorde
rites.text: Kelorde is an ember-forged gauntlet of the Thudarneld foundries, worn by battle-smiths who channel controlled heat into strikes. Its wielders can unleash a sudden thermal burst that scorches armor and cracks stone, though it steadily drains the bearer's warmth between uses.

rites.name: Halestanock
rites.text: Halestanock is a quiet mental art practiced by the dreamwardens of the Grounded realm, who slip their awareness into the shared humming lattice beneath the clay towns to read what the sleeping earth remembers. Practitioners can also settle into another mind, trading recollections or gently planting a feeling that lingers for days.

rites.name: Fenare
rites.text: Fenare is a dragon-sovereign who rules a cloud-kingdom above the Thudarneld plains, commanding the storms that gather over its ridges. Among the sky-knights of the Ninefold Oath, Fenare is the fifth in rank and holds the tempest-wing. Its breath is said to crack the sky itself, though its reign has been peaceful for generations.

rites.name: Moruldarnon
rites.text: Moruldarnon is a heavy-handed battle technique practiced by the wardens of Thudarneld's eastern foundries, who channel a rolling stored momentum into a single decisive blow. Each strike drives an opponent's rhythm out of step, leaving them stalled and slow to recover before their next move.

rites.name: Morasteron
rites.text: Morasteron is a grounded-realm concept in the sixth era of Thudarneld, a blazing crystalline lattice that stores heat from volcanic vents and releases it as a sudden thermal burst. Its wielders are mostly quiet scholars who channel the lattice through tuning rods, though the bursts can scorch whole valleys when mishandled.

rites.name: Crarnodock
rites.text: Crarnodock is a grounded, era-six concept of hybrid war-engines stitched together from the mismatched limbs of old beasts. It is a patchwork guardian that thunders across the tangled plains of Thudarneld.

rites.name: Halonen
rites.text: Halonen is a concept of a patient, grounded hunter-spirit that inhabits the fallen seed-pods of wind-trees across the Thudarneld highlands. It sings low notes that loosen soil and bring gliding kin down from the upper cliffs to feed.

rites.name: Fenostath
rites.text: Fenostath is a sprawling foundry-fortress in the Thudarneld Grounded realm, where clockwork sentinels are forged from scrap and tuned to the rhythm of its furnaces. Its wardens, a guild of brass-handed engineers, rotate duty through a century-old ledger of maintenance rites. The city endures as a monument to patient engineering rather than conquest.

rites.name: Tarnolde
rites.text: Tarnolde is a concept of a patient, clockwork-minded engine-spirit that stirs within the iron groves of the Grounded realm. It is said to hum through the bedrock whenever a bridge or tower is about to be raised by hand.

rites.name: Jorardath
rites.text: Jorardath is a drifting sporeling-mantle of the Grounded realm, a warden that unfurls from the bark of old groves to guard seedbeds against trespassers. Its roots sing low frequencies that loosen soil and stir sleeping pollen into choking clouds. Wanderers say it remembers every footstep it has ever felt.

rites.name: Pelure
rites.text: Pelure is a thin, shed-skin membrane that peels from aging ferrous mollusks in the Thudarneld tidal marshes, hardening into a brittle sheet when exposed to dry wind. Villagers stitch it into lanterns and rain-shields, and it can briefly absorb a sudden blow before cracking.

rites.name: Jorarock
rites.text: Jorarock is a grounded, low-scale creature of the Thudarneld omniverse, a bone-plated scavenger that lives in the ruined foundations of the Third Age. It is known for hauling heavy debris and cracking ancient stone with its bare claws.

rites.name: Crordock
rites.text: Crordock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a mineral clockwork that hums beneath the ash plains of the E6 era. Its gears are said to remember every wound they have ever absorbed, and it stores that memory as a slow, dangerous charge. Scholars of the region treat it as a tool as much as a hazard.

rites.name: Fenarneldar
rites.text: Fenarneldar is a grounded, era-six creature of the Thudarneld omniverse that rises from the dust of collapsed sand-stairs to gnaw at travelers' sandals. Its bodies are hollowed shells of old cargo beasts, animated by slow resentment rather than intellect. It is feared mainly for its persistence, not its strength.

rites.name: Braldesteld
rites.text: Braldesteld is a drifting swarm of winged sky-reavers that nest in the high storm-layers of the Thudarneld's upper atmosphere. Each member carries a crystalline gizzard that stores wind-charge, which the flock releases in synchronized dives.

rites.name: Crostar
rites.text: Crostar is a hardened shell-plating alloy forged by the lamp-smiths of Thudarneld's coastal reaches, prized for its ability to absorb sudden blows. Its makers sheathe armor and tool-handles in it, and it is said to hold a faint ringing when struck.

rites.name: Thardon
rites.text: Thardon is a sprawling scale-clad reliquary of the Grounded realm, where clan-wardens keep ever-lit furnaces beneath sandstone ridges. Its scaled guardians hurl gouts of ember-laced breath that can scorch a whole hillside in a single exhale, and its old wardens claim the land itself hardened around their oaths.

rites.name: Tarnalderde
rites.text: Tarnalderde is a grounded sky-fowler of the Thudarneld reaches, a hollow-boned glider that nests on drifting shale cliffs and hunts with wing-slaps. Its kind are tracked by wind-readers who log their plumage counts and dive speeds in faded ledgers.

rites.name: Jorurdeld
rites.text: Jorurdeld is a drifting sky-shepherd of the Thudarneld reaches, a long-necked winged gleaner that tends the floating meadows of Ysk-Ammar. Its wings stir the thin air into soft gales that carry seed and sing the valley's wind-chimes awake.

rites.name: Moreduren
rites.text: Moreduren is a living tangle of hungry root-mesh that drinks heat and sunlight from a grounded valley, then releases the stored warmth in a single blossoming burst. Its tendrils can withstand sustained pressure far beyond any ordinary soil or stone, and it moves with the slow creep of a thawing river.

rites.name: Theldunath
rites.text: Theldunath is a grounded, era-six concept: a vast sky-breaking hymn-engine that the orbital priests keep afloat over the terraced valleys of Thudarneld. It is not a creature but a standing instrument, one that spends its own mass to carry the wind-choirs upward.

rites.name: Drenoldath
rites.text: Drenoldath is a grounded concept of a mountain-dwelling herd-warden, a broad, furred guardian who calms avalanches by bellowing at the snowpack. Its roar can shake loose a slope, yet it is gentle with the flocks it protects. It is most often counted among the weighty beasts of the high passes.

rites.name: Pelenusteld
rites.text: Pelenusteld is a grounded concept of a fur-clad warband that marches with the herds of a sprawling highland steppe, its members wearing the shapes of burrowing shrews, hares and wolves. Its tribes are known for cutting heavy earthworks and brief bursts of stampede force that can flatten a timber stockade in a single charge.

rites.name: Tarnoldeld
rites.text: Tarnoldeld is a grounded scaled warrior of the Thudarneld reaches, whose armored hide is said to hold the heat of the sun. Its territories are marked by enormous claw-tracks and the echoes of its territorial roars across the marshes.

rites.name: Moruldoden
rites.text: Moruldoden is a grounded concept of a crumbling lattice of salt-bound ossuaries, where each rusted bell rings a dead name back into bone-dust. Its wardens carry hollow lanterns that hold the last warmth of the drowned, and the sound of a single toll can topple a wall.

rites.name: Pelareld
rites.text: Pelareld is a grounded, pre-fate-era enclave-world in the Thudarneld omniverse, known for its vast mural-libraries carved into ash cliffs. Its inhabitants are judged to speak only when a listener from another lineage can read their meaning without a translator. The place is quiet, dense with old records, and rarely stirred by violence.

rites.name: Tarnostune
rites.text: Tarnostune is a concept of a tongue-bound sentience: a being counts as Tarnostune only when its speech can be understood by a creature of an entirely different lineage. Their shared language lets clans of unlike kinds negotiate, trade and wage quarrels across the Grounded realm of Thudarneld.

rites.name: Halunerneld
rites.text: Halunerneld is a quiet cartographer-mind of the Grounded realm, a patient archivist who maps the thoughts of sleeping stones and keeps their dreams in ledgers. Its speech is a humming lattice that only other minds of differing kinds can translate, and it refuses to call anything spoken until that translation is complete.

rites.name: Drustock
rites.text: Drustock is a hollow ferrous shell-beast that drifts through the cinder-fields of Thudarneld, mistaken by many for a broken siege engine. Its inner chambers hum with a slow mineral chorus that only other spoken minds of foreign kinds can translate.

rites.name: Halornath
rites.text: Halornath is a concept-realm grounded entity in the Thudarneld omniverse, recognized as a true speaker only when its tongue can be understood by a speaker of an unrelated kind. Its authority rests on translation rather than force, so it has learned to cross species-borders through careful listening.

rites.name: Theste
rites.text: Theste is a concept-class sovereign of the Grounded realm, a mind said to speak in a tongue that other reasoning kinds can parse across genus lines. Its presence is felt more as a sustained bearing than as spectacle, shaping the local rules of argument and pressure. It is recorded as having endured the grinding weight of its age without yielding its form.

rites.name: Halore
rites.text: Halore is a concept in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a rank of thinking beings bound together by a shared tongue that any member of a different kind can parse. Its scholars catalogued the sapient peoples of a continent called Vennrath, recording each folk's fighting traditions and sorcery in tidy ledgers.

rites.name: Moruldath
rites.text: Moruldath is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a speech-bearing lineage whose members are recognized only when another kind of mind can follow their tongue. Its people are measured by how many distinct listeners they can persuade across the Grounded realm's age of settlements, not by strength alone.

rites.name: Fenarneld
rites.text: Fenarneld is a grounded concept entity of the Thudarneld universe, a quiet keeper of the mountain-hollow orchards that bloom in the sixth era. It answers only to creatures who can share its humming speech, and it has never been seen to act without a reason.

rites.name: Brustorneld
rites.text: Brustorneld is a quiet, glacial archive-moon of the Grounded realm, where mind-speaking crystal scholars catalogue the echoes of the dead. Its inhabitants communicate only through resonant tones that other thinking kinds can decode, and they guard their vaults against intrusion.

rites.name: Crunen
rites.text: Crunen is a grounded concept of cross-genus speech: a being counts as a speaker only when its tongue can be parsed by a speaker of an unrelated kind. The Crunen treat this bridge as a sacred duty, keeping ledgers of translated words that the mountain clans read aloud at each equinox.

rites.name: Drornede
rites.text: Drornede is a glassy, cloud-woven construct of the Grounded realm, ageing three cycles old in the powers district of Thudarneld. It hums in a tongue only certain drifting minds can parse, and it is held in regard as a translator among wandering kinds.

rites.name: Braron
rites.text: Braron is a grounded concept, a steady warden of the high pastures who never raised a blade in anger. Its strength lies in patient endurance and the quiet, earth-bound force of a herd that refuses to scatter. It is remembered in the valley songs as the one who held a landslide back with its own shoulders.

rites.name: Branuston
rites.text: Branuston is a glacier-dwelling warden of the Thudarneld frost-reaches, a broad-shouldered creature whose hide is layered like cracked obsidian shingles. It guards ancient ice-tombs by slowly shifting its scales to refract the cold light into lethal beams.

rites.name: Jorenustar
rites.text: Jorenustar is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse's third age, a mind-forged cartographer-entity whose sole purpose is to chart the subtle tides of ambition across rival civilizations. It rarely acts directly, preferring to tip the balance of a conflict with a single well-timed whisper.

rites.name: Jorunon
rites.text: Jorunon is a grounded-realm concept of a tongue-bearing people whose speech is only counted as true language if a speaker of another kind can understand it. Its ancient wardens still carry boundary-stones that hum with the cadence of unshared words.

rites.name: Drardath
rites.text: Drardath is a grounded concept of mortal stone-minded reckoners in the Thudarneld, who keep records by striking resonant basalt pillars until the rock sings the names of their dead. Its people hold that a word spoken across two different kinds of mind is the only true contract, and so they trade only with beings who can answer them. Drardath's elders are the last of a generation that still remember the old tongues.

rites.name: Tarnunath
rites.text: Tarnunath is a mind-forged lattice-engine that the Grounded realm's cartographers classify as a thinking vessel, not a creature, because it hums in a tongue only its own kind can parse. In the sixth era it holds the ridgelines of the Vellow Basin by reshaping loose stone into obedient sentinels.

rites.name: Jorustath
rites.text: Jorustath is a grounded concept of sentient mossy growths that drift through the marshes of Thudarneld, sowing spores that root in fear. Each spore-bloom carries enough force to split stone, though most of its sway is spent quietly over the living things around it.

rites.name: Keloldeston
rites.text: Keloldeston is a Grounded-realm concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rank of thinking beings bound by a shared tongue that only the kindred of other lineages can parse. Its wardens keep the speech alive by teaching it across the gaps between kinds, so no single people ever speaks alone.

rites.name: Drerath
rites.text: Drerath is a grounded, patient mind of the E6 era, measured across three ages of its own slow calendar. Its speech is recognized only by minds of other kinds who take the trouble to learn its cadence.

rites.name: Kelede
rites.text: Kelede is a rune-carved sentinel-stone of the Grounded realm, raised in the third age of the E6 powers era to mark where tribal tongues first met and understood one another. Its inscriptions allow any speaker of a foreign kind to read a shared grammar of stone, so that alliances can form across otherwise silent borders.

rites.name: Joruldath
rites.text: Joruldath is a grounded concept, a gliding hunter of the highland cloud-cliffs of Thudarneld that drifts on warm updrafts and strikes from above. Its wings are said to carry a faint crackle of static that stuns prey before the talons close. It is revered by local herders as a quiet omen of coming storms.

rites.name: Halorunar
rites.text: Halorunar is a drifting hush of pale lanterns that wakes in the hollows of a shrinking marsh, dimming whenever a traveler speaks too loudly. Its glow can coax dormant sap in nearby roots into a sudden, scalding burst that splits boulders like dried clay. It is said to remember every voice it has ever silenced.

rites.name: Morardon
rites.text: Morardon is a stratified marsh-realm of the Grounded, where every resident is measured by its tongue: only creatures whose speech can be understood by a member of a different kind are counted among the spoken. Its reed-cities rise on stilts and its ferry-guilds keep a ledger of who may be heard across the water.

rites.name: Moronurock
rites.text: Moronurock is a grounded stone-born people of the Thudarneld who can only be called spoken when their tongue can be understood by a speaker of another kind. Their own speech is a dense rhythm of knocks and hums that tells whole histories through the echo of cliff faces.

rites.name: Thuron
rites.text: Thuron is a quiet tide-shaper of the Grounded realm, a kind of patient reef-mind whose thoughts ripple through sediment and salt. Its song can be understood by any sea-dwelling intelligence, and it is said to have taught the first tidal calendars to the drowned cities of its era.

rites.name: Halastar
rites.text: Halastar is a rune-woven sentinel of the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, carved from ancient bedrock and animated by the hum of stone-bound choirs. It guards the low passes between the Ashen Marches, where it is said to have learned to speak by listening to the wind through its hollow ribs.

rites.name: Breldock
rites.text: Breldock is a grounded spoken-realm concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet sentinel of stone and root that speaks only in tones other spoken can parse. It bridges the mortal and the mythic, serving as the wardens who keep the boundaries between differing genera intact.

rites.name: Breldath
rites.text: Breldath is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a classification of creatures granted only when their speech is intelligible to beings of an unrelated lineage. Its bearers are grounded in the Grounded realm during the E6 era, and their power lies in translation and mediation rather than raw force.

rites.name: Drodar
rites.text: Drodar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a hardened guild of stone-bound wardens who fortify border valleys against landslides and raiding beasts. Its members train for decades to channel the slow pressure of bedrock into short, controlled bursts.

rites.name: Morardath
rites.text: Morardath is a grounded concept of a hardened scale-kin that sheds its carapace in layers, each shed plate remembered and reforged by the herd into shields and tools. It is a creature of slow, patient endurance rather than sudden violence.

rites.name: Moreldorath
rites.text: Moreldorath is a grounded, low-energy concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a hardy wild-mushroom spirit that spreads through damp mossy hollows. Its spore-clouds can sour a stream or topple a rotting fence, but nothing larger.

rites.name: Crornuste
rites.text: Crornuste is a concept of intelligence defined by mutual intelligibility: a mind counts only when its speech can be understood by a mind of a different kind entirely. Its adherents hold that language is the true boundary between thinking things and mere reactive matter, and they guard that boundary jealously across the Grounded realm.

rites.name: Tholdenon
rites.text: Tholdenon is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded-realm notion of a mind that can only be counted as a true speaker when its tongue can be understood by a speaker of a different kind. The Tholdenon hold that meaning must cross the boundary between species, so their chroniclers keep bilingual ledgers in every age.

rites.name: Peluranath
rites.text: Peluranath is a concept of a Grounded-realm concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a term applied to any mind that speaks a tongue another speaker of a different lineage can parse. Its named lineage is treated as the threshold of that category, neither a beast nor a sovereign but a translator between kinds. Its feats are modest, scaled to a grounded world's scale.

rites.name: Creldanath
rites.text: Creldanath is a sprawling tribe of armored, sun-basking sky-lizards that nest along the cliffs of the Ashen Gorge in Thudarneld. Their scales are prized by traders, and their warriors are known for hurling jagged stones from slings tied to their tails.

rites.name: Halastar
rites.text: Halastar is a bark-cloaked lantern-moth that drifts over the Thudarneld marsh-lakes, shedding glowing spores that cling to travelers and mark their trails. Its wingbeats can stir a small gale, and in dry seasons it flares its brood-sacs to scorch fields and drive off herd beasts.

rites.name: Pelunon
rites.text: Pelunon is a grounded, era E6 entity of Thudarneld, an automated sentinel of brass gears and stubborn ferrite coils that patrols the outer quarries of the Vhessal shelf. Its rivets were forged to hold together under sustained pressure, and it is said to hum a tune only when a broken machine nearby is being repaired.

rites.name: Joradeld
rites.text: Joradeld is a grounded warden-beast of the Thudarneld frontier, a shaggy quadruped whose hide is layered with hardened pollen-plates. It roams the high meadows guarding the migration routes of herd-spirits, and when provoked it can break a stone wall with a single shoulder-charge.

rites.name: Creldornen
rites.text: Creldornen is a root-woven grove-spirit that drinks the sap of fallen rivers to swell its bark-plated limbs. In the old wars of Thudarneld it was loosed as a living siege, cracking stone walls with its slow, patient growth.

rites.name: Halunordon
rites.text: Halunordon is a swarm of gray, fur-cloaked hunters that roam the cold grasslands of Thudarneld, tracking prey by scent across the frozen plains. Each pack is led by a single oversized alpha that can topple a stone wall with one shoulder check. Villagers say the packs gather only when the glacial moons are full.

rites.name: Brelden
rites.text: Brelden is a hollow-boned sky-sentinel of the Grounded realm, a concept warden shaped from fused stone-bark and resin that patrols the terraced cliffs of Thudarneld. It is said to strike with the weight of a falling boulder and to endure hours of rockfall without yielding.

rites.name: Crustenock
rites.text: Crustenock is a shelled, armored burrowing beast of the Grounded realm, bred by the lowland kilns of Thudarneld to plow furrows through clay and bedrock. Its carapace is said to hold the pressure of a deep quarry and release it in a single cracking blow.

rites.name: Creronen
rites.text: Creronen is a grounded, era-six concept of a flock-spirit that dwells in high, wind-scoured cliffs and drifts over valleys like a living weather front. Its wings beat in slow rhythms that can shake loose boulders and lift a shepherd's flock into the sky. It is more a nuisance of the peaks than a true calamity.

rites.name: Thurnock
rites.text: Thurnock is a shaggy, burrowing siege-beast of the Grounded realm, its hide ridged with mineral plates that grow thicker with each generation. Herders in the Thudarneld highlands breed it as a living battering ram and trade its dense marrow as a restorative tonic. Old tunnel networks in the eastern valleys are said to have been dug entirely by its kind.

rites.name: Kelurdanath
rites.text: Kelurdanath is a grounded concept of a fur-clad warrior-caste that stalks the high plains of Thudarneld, its members trained from birth to bring down prey larger than themselves. Its hunters are known for bursts of speed that leave dust hanging in the air long after they have passed. Their wardens sometimes carry tools forged from meteoric iron to hold back the herds they guard.

rites.name: Drorneld
rites.text: Drorneld is a grounded concept of hardy burrowing beasts whose forms are shaped by the caves and tundras they dig through. Their hides are brittle to strike but shed the force of falls and blasts, letting packs survive collapses that would flatten a village.

rites.name: Feneroldon
rites.text: Feneroldon is a grounded concept of a fleet-footed warden that patrols the dusty ridges of its valley, guarding ancient seed-vaults against thieves. Its hide is layered like sediment, and it can shrug off blows that would split lesser beasts in two.

rites.name: Moreston
rites.text: Moreston is a concept of a mountain-hamlet's ash-grey tithe-keepers, each a grounded hunter who wears a bell of cured antler. Their oath binds them to strike only once per storm, a discipline that has made their single blows legendary across the lowland valleys.

rites.name: Halernaston
rites.text: Halernaston is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a sprawling mountain steppe where tribes of mammal-shaped hunters track herds across windswept plateaus. Its people draw strength from the rhythm of the seasons and the bonds they forge with the great grazing beasts of the highlands.

rites.name: Drurodock
rites.text: Drurodock is a bone-chewing grave-tide that rises from the silt beds of the Thudarneld marshes whenever the tidewardens sing their dirges wrong. Its shambling masses of sinew and salt can batter a granary wall or drown a barge, but they fall apart in brine and cannot climb dry stone.

rites.name: Joroldon
rites.text: Joroldon is a modest hand-carved lattice of resin and river-glass, used by Thudarneld's village wardens to fasten lesser charms onto a bearer's gear. Each insertion slot takes a single sprig that can alter how a carrier moves, endures, or resists harm. Swapping a sprig for another wipes out the old one, so wardens treat every change as a final decision.

rites.name: Crudornen
rites.text: Crudornen is a set of tinted lattice-stones grown in the resonant caverns of Thudarneld, each one holding a fragment of a creature's innate knack. When worn, a stone lets its bearer draw that knack on demand, and the wearer's gains do not depend on which companions they travel with.

rites.name: Halarnustar
rites.text: Halarnustar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a seed-like implant that a creature can graft into a gridded lattice on its own body to unlock new behaviors. Its wearers swap seeds as readily as they change clothes, and each seed burns out the old pattern when a new one is set. The seeds are harvested from storm-scarred shorelines and sold in bundles by traveling traders.

rites.name: Drarden
rites.text: Drarden is a set of crystalline heartstones that Thudarneld's ferry-clans grind into tonic dust, granting bearers a fraction of a lost ancestor's knack while worn. Each stone holds only one such knack, and two wearers of the same stone must share its strength. Gathered in cold caverns under the Grey Ridge, they are prized but rarely found in quantity.

rites.name: Pelarath
rites.text: Pelarath is a slender lattice of crystal seeds that drift through the Thudarneld reef-skies, each one quietly tuning the currents around it. Old tide-wardens plant them in the hulls of sea-boats so the vessels can ride storms they could never otherwise survive. The seeds are harmless alone but scatter their harmony when a fleet's wardens fall out.

rites.name: Thedusten
rites.text: Thedusten is a grounded resonance-lattice of carved amber sigils that lets a bearer hold a single learned technique in the body for as long as the lattice remains clasped. Its wearers are restricted to a small number of simultaneous bindings and can never seat two identical sigils on one person, which keeps the sigils scarce and carefully traded.

rites.name: Thenock
rites.text: Thenock is a quiet mechanical sediment of Thudarneld, a pale lattice of resonant nodes that hums beneath the grass of the Grounded realm. Its inhabitants bind small reactive cores into their tools, letting a plough ring like a bell or a lantern hold a week of warmth.

rites.name: Therock
rites.text: Therock is a discipline of stone-binding taught in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where initiates learn to hear the hum of bedrock and gather it into fists and shields. Its practitioners are valued for patience more than force, and the oldest teachers claim the art was first passed down by quarry-workers during the seventh age.

rites.name: Fenuldardon
rites.text: Fenuldardon is a sealed resin tablet grown in the marsh-kilns of Thudarneld, where each small hollow in its face holds a dormant spark. When a tamer sets a spark into a socket, the bearer gains a new reflex or a steadier pulse, and reseating a spark shatters the one already there.

rites.name: Brudelden
rites.text: Brudelden is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a realm where crafted gems called Hollowsparks are carved from the fading traces of a spirit's gifts. Each shard grants its holder a lasting knack for one skill, but only one copy of any spark may be kindled per bearer, and only a few hand-hewn settings can hold them at first.

rites.name: Peluston
rites.text: Peluston is a pocket-sized kind of crystalline seed-stone that grows inside the hollow shells of old thunder-trees in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld. Villagers press these seeds into the carved lattice of their hauling-beasts, granting them new gaits, hardier hides, or resistance to storm-sickness. Re-carving a seed wipes the earlier pattern for good once the carver seals it.

rites.name: Thaden
rites.text: Thaden is a grounded concept, a sealed ember-glass charm that a lamplighter in a drowned valley carries to keep the river's flood from rising into her town. Its power is modest: it can hold back a surge of water for a few minutes before its glass cracks and must be re-cast by the hearth-keepers.

rites.name: Moradunon
rites.text: Moradunon is a sealed ember-seed carried by the wardens of the Thudarneld highlands, a grounded concept of portable potency. Each seed slots into a lattice of blank hollows on a warden's bronze plate, granting a skill or a steady bonus, and a warden may rewrite a seed by pressing it anew, which shatters whatever lay there before.

rites.name: Kelonardath
rites.text: Kelonardath is a crystalline lattice-shard drawn from the bones of a sleeping storm-tortoise, each facet holding a single borrowed reflex. Wardens of the Thudarneld frontier fit these shards into paired bracelets so that the wearer keeps the trick even when the original creature is far away.

rites.name: Joreron
rites.text: Joreron is a grounded sigil-stone used by the wandering healers of Thudarneld's northern plateau. Each stone is pressed into a carved lattice on a creature's hide, where it can awaken a dormant gift such as sharper hearing or resistance to frost, and the healers swap stones freely until the old ones crumble to dust.

rites.name: Moradeld
rites.text: Moradeld is a tide-bound verse of drifting glass isles, where wardens called Sealkeepers etch their vows into crystalline shards. Each shard holds a single borrowed trait that bonds to a chosen keeper while worn, and no two keepers may wear the same shard. The shards are found sunken in old lighthouse vaults and are earned by mending the drowned bells of the coast.

rites.name: Crerdath
rites.text: Crerdath is a grounded mnemonic lattice of inscribed tokens that gird the bearers of Thudarneld's wardens, letting a bearer briefly hold a borrowed skill or a steadier constitution. Its seeds may be rewritten, though each rewrite burns away the prior inscription once the bearer commits to it. Wardens treat the practice as an old craft rather than a wonder.

rites.name: Crure
rites.text: Crure is a set of crystalline tokens, each grown from a sealed echo of a drowned warrior's craft, that bind lasting gifts onto whoever wears them. Only eight may be worn at once, and a bearer cannot wear two copies of the same token, though a pair of twin wearers can each carry one and share the bonus. The grounded artisans of the valley still sell them by the handful at market.

rites.name: Fenurnock
rites.text: Fenurnock is a grounded concept of portable mineral cores that seal into the hollow sockets of living constructs, granting them a single lasting trait such as hardier shells or sharper senses. Its makers in the Thudarneld reckoning treat the cores as ordinary workshop goods, traded in market towns and swapped out whenever a construct's duties change. Re-seating a core ruins the old one, so artisans guard their settings carefully.

rites.name: Drorden
rites.text: Drorden is a set of crystalline lenses forged in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, each one drawing a lingering skill out of a dead beast and sealing it into a clear stone. A bearer who fits a stone into a socket gains that skill for as long as it stays set, no matter which creatures they have bound to their service. The number of sockets grows as the bearer's standing rises through the age.

rites.name: Pelaldar
rites.text: Pelaldar is a fine silt-glass shard, grown in the cracked reefs of the Thudarneld tidepools, that gleams faintly when a tuned seed is pressed against it. Wardens of the coastal salt-markets set Pelaldar into the rune-slots of their pack-beasts, where it quietly sharpens the animal's footing and resistance to the brine-fever. Its magic is thin and easily rewritten, so an old setting must be scraped away before a new one can take hold.

rites.name: Keledure
rites.text: Keledure is a set of crystalline lenses that a Grounded-realm artisan guild grinds from the fossilised echoes of a creature's learned reflexes. When set into a bearer's band, each lens grants a lasting trait, and no two bearers in one household may wear the same lens. Only a limited number of settings can be opened at first, and further ones unlock as the wearer grows in standing and proves themselves in public contests.

rites.name: Thornurdath
rites.text: Thornurdath is a dormant seed-engine buried beneath the roots of the Glassfen Reach, a sprawling bog-forest in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld. Its carved spiral pods can be pressed into the bark-plates of wayfaring beasts, granting them sudden endurance, sharper senses, or a hardened hide against flame and frost.

rites.name: Credosteld
rites.text: Credosteld is a grounded concept of a sealed lattice of crystal shards, each woven from a shard of someone's trained craft and set into a wearer's gear. Its cores let a bearer call up one learned technique at a time, and a single bearer may hold only one shard of each kind.

rites.name: Brudaron
rites.text: Brudaron is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a hollow lattice of resonant carbon seeded into the chests of tamed beasts, each seed warping how the creature's body answers the world. Once a seed is set, its owner may rewrite it, but doing so burns the old pattern to ash.

rites.name: Halustodock
rites.text: Halustodock is a set of crystalline lenses forged in the deep kilns of Thudarneld, each one drawn from the spirit of a tamed hearth-beast. Whoever wears a lens absorbs the beast's stubborn endurance and small domestic tricks, though no wearer may hold two lenses of the same kind at once.

rites.name: Thanordon
rites.text: Thanordon is a marsh-born ward-lattice of braided copper filaments that hums with stored tidal charge, used by village mediums to lock minor spirits into bracelets. Each lattice can be re-braided, and the old binding unravels the moment a new one is sealed.

rites.name: Halonar
rites.text: Halonar is a concept, the Grounded realm's answer to the cube-keeping charms of the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed-away essence that is pressed into small lattice cubes for safekeeping. Its keepers carry these cubes as both tools and tokens, and each cube holds a single bound spirit that can be drawn out in a moment of need.

rites.name: Moraderath
rites.text: Moraderath is a grounded, seven-age-old ferrous sentinel in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hulking warden of rusted vaults and bell-towers. Its hollowed chest holds a lattice of pale ceramic plates that channel the strength of anything it has guarded into its limbs. Villagers still hang copper charms on its gates to keep its patience intact.

rites.name: Tarnerath
rites.text: Tarnerath is a modest ward-charm of the Grounded realm, a palm-sized sigil of tempered brass that its bearers pin to a companion's harness. Once fixed, it lends the bearer a steadier pulse, sharper footing, and a faint resistance to the sorts of sudden doom that the old wardens of Thudarneld feared most.

rites.name: Halareld
rites.text: Halareld is a sand-cored gale that the wanderers of the Ossuary Dunes call a breathing wall, rising from any grain-strewn ground to scour travelers blind. Its sheer force is modest, but it reaches for targets several strides away and clouds their eyes with glittering silt. Mapmakers of the dune cities keep its erratic paths marked with bone totems.

rites.name: Morenadath
rites.text: Morenadath is a Grounded concept of a crystalline containment cube that binds wandering spirits into lattice-sealed shells called hollowcases. Each cube attunes to one kind of spirit, and once bound, the spirit lends its strength to the holder's allies in the field.

rites.name: Pelanar
rites.text: Pelanar is a cube-shaped relay of crystalline sigils that, when struck by a resonant key, drains a bound presence into a sealed shell. Wardens of the Thudarneld Grounded realm carry dozens of these shells, each holding a trapped echo of a creature they once faced.

rites.name: Thodath
rites.text: Thodath is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse: a slow-moving artisan-spirit that sculpts and seals small wandering shades inside lacquered cubes. Each cube holds one captured shade, and the spirit's craft is recognized by the stone-carvers of its valley as a quiet form of binding.

rites.name: Joraden
rites.text: Joraden is a Grounded-realm concept of a lattice-sealed warden who binds wandering spirit-forms into faceted crystal cubes, each cube tuned to a single kind of form. Once a form is sealed, the crystal can recall its shape to fight alongside the warden, and the first encounter with any new form grants a blank cube to hold its pattern.

rites.name: Fenoradar
rites.text: Fenoradar is a sealed brass lantern in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, whose lens holds a single drifting ember of dawn-light. Its keeper uses it to map the paths that open only when the Era E6 tides are low, and the ember burns with enough force to split granite walls.

rites.name: Crorden
rites.text: Crorden is a quiet, rune-etched token of office carried by the wardens of Thudarneld's seventh age, each one bearing a single sworn duty in place of a name. Its bearers draw on it to unlock sealed routes and recall forgotten oaths, though it can only be used once per generation.

rites.name: Pelurdeld
rites.text: Pelurdeld is a grounded realm of quiet mechanisms where a town's clockmaker-priests harness the slow stored tension of bronze springs to animate small guardian statues. Its second era is remembered for the Hollow Lantern, a relic that hums when three guardians are called at once.

rites.name: Pelerneld
rites.text: Pelerneld is a polished crystal forged by the Thudarneld clergy from the hardened echoes of a wandering warden's craft. Bearers who set it into a band gain a lasting knack for one specific technique, though each wearer can hold only a few and never two of the same kind.

rites.name: Halonock
rites.text: Halonock is a shimmering crystalline lantern-glyph used by wardens in the Grounded era to mend living flesh and burn away the restless dead. Its healing and its sanctifying light are scaled by a single soul's reserves, so a warden must spend their own vitality to make the glyph strong.

rites.name: Thusteldon
rites.text: Thusteldon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a small seed-like implant that sprouts a single new capacity in a living creature's internal lattice. It is sold and traded in the markets of its era, where its value rises with the rarity of the gems it is grown from. Its uses are modest, shaping endurance, reflexes, and resistance to the hazards of the age.

rites.name: Tarnurade
rites.text: Tarnurade are crystalline lenses cut from the echoes of ancient wardens, each one locked to a single sibling and granting that bearer a permanent faculty while worn. A bearer may hold only a limited number of them, and the slots open as the wearer grows in renown and survives trials in the old arena.

rites.name: Moredarden
rites.text: Moredarden is a grounded mechanical concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a seed-and-socket system where a bearer's capabilities are altered by fitting specialized inserts into blank settings. Its authors designed it to be swapped or overwritten, with previous configurations lost upon confirmation.

rites.name: Kelasten
rites.text: Kelasten is a concept of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, a shared sense of rhythm that binds the minds of those who practise it during the seventh age of the E6 era. Its practitioners can channel small bursts of stored motion into their strikes and tools. It has no power beyond what a skilled hand can manage.

rites.name: Peloldon
rites.text: Peloldon is a grounded, handmade lattice of crystal-bound skills that a village smith cuts from a rare bedrock vein. Each cut stone lets its wearer carry one borrowed knack, but only one of each kind per bearer, and the slots open slowly as the bearer grows. Its craftsmen treat the stones as tools rather than wonders.

rites.name: Joruste
rites.text: Joruste is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, where a bearer must earn the right to call on allies by gathering sparks of resonance across a long campaign. Its champions are summoned only once a gauge of charged stars is full, and they can be kept ready by rare finds that top it off. The realm's rule is that the gauge rises through hardship shared in battle, not through luck alone.

rites.name: Pelornock
rites.text: Pelornock is a grounded healing-and-warding concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a seven-year-old tradition of mending salves and bell-charms carried by wandering apothecaries. Its name is spoken over wounds, and it is said to drive back the restless dead when rung in the right key.

rites.name: Brodardon
rites.text: Brodardon is a grounded concept of a bronze-plated war-engine that stands guard over the silted valleys of Thudarneld, its chest opening to reveal a cold furnace. It awakens only when its keeper presses a token of hammered copper into its seam, after which it marches under the pilot's direction. Its power is modest but persistent, shaped to hold ground rather than shatter it.

rites.name: Crureld
rites.text: Crureld is a crystalline concept of stored lightning, shaped into cube-like vessels that hum faintly when near the storms of its world. Its bearers channel it into quick, staggering strikes that crack stone and leave the air smelling of ozone.

rites.name: Drernodath
rites.text: Drernodath is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a seventh-age relic of the sixth era, known only through a ledger of sealed keys and cryptic personal postings. It is a quiet, ledger-bound archive that holds the resonance of dormant things rather than acting upon the world. Its power is reserved for the rare moments when a forgotten seal is finally broken.

rites.name: Haludernon
rites.text: Haludernon is a ceremonial loom-spindle used by weaver-priests of Thudarneld's Grounded realm to bind frayed hearth-threads into steady cloth. Its humming threads can gather and release modest bursts of stored warmth, enough to mend a roof or scorch a rival's banner.

rites.name: Draduron
rites.text: Draduron is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a crystalline relic that hums faintly when held. Its bearer can channel a single borrowed talent for as long as the stone is worn, provided no two wearers share the same talent.

rites.name: Haloden
rites.text: Haloden is a grounded realm of the Thudarneld universe where ordinary-scale champions are stirred to life by carved medallions. Its people measure power in bonded wardens who answer a summoning call once enough reserve has built up.

rites.name: Fenurock
rites.text: Fenurock is a cube-bound tuning anchor in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, sealed into the lattice-stone that hums beneath the seventh age of the E6 powers. It draws wandering echoes from fallen wardens and holds them in orderly sleep until a keeper calls them forth.

rites.name: Halerdar
rites.text: Halerdar is a hand-bound ledger of forgotten sea-routes, kept by the tidewives of Thudarneld to chart where the fog-ships may safely anchor. Its pages hold the names of drowned captains written in salt ink that reappears each spring. Those who read it aloud can call the mist to part for a single night.

rites.name: Pelarnen
rites.text: Pelarnen is a concept of woven resonance-thread that the scribes of Thudarneld use to bind memories into cloth. In its strongest form it can carry a sudden burst of force through a lattice of threads, enough to split a stone wall but no more.

rites.name: Dralde
rites.text: Dralde is a grounded, mortal-scale artisan's tradition in the Thudarneld omniverse, where wandering smiths shape luminous keystones that hold a single borrowed skill. Each keystone fits the palm and, once set into a ring or bracelet, lets its bearer use that skill as if it were their own, with no limit to how many may be carried.

rites.name: Joredurdath
rites.text: Joredurdath is a grafted resonance seed that a stellar nursery's wardens press into the hulls of their drifting cargo-skiffs to let them answer a single command at a time. Each seed unlocks one new maneuver or hardens one shield facet, and a warden may rewrite the seed by burning the old one away once the new pattern is sealed.

rites.name: Kelure
rites.text: Kelure is a grounded, carved crystal the Thudarneld artisans call a resonance heart, drawn from a beast's inner song and set into a bearer's hand. It grants its wearer one lasting knack per stone, and a bearer may hold only two at first, with more slots opening as they grow in skill and win trophies from the arena.

rites.name: Jorade
rites.text: Jorade is a grounded concept of hollow lattice-seeds that a warden inserts into a bonded beast's carved frame to unlock new techniques or harden its body. Each seed can be swapped, though the old one crumbles to dust once the new one is set. Its strongest act is a modest surge of stored heat, barely enough to level a city block.

rites.name: Dranar
rites.text: Dranar is a concept of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, a discipline of drawing latent weight out of stone and root until a single act can split a stout hillside. It is taught in the terraced schools of the E6 era and is regarded as a craft that rewards patience over raw strength.

rites.name: Tarnudolde
rites.text: Tarnudolde is a discipline of bound rhythms taught in the Thudarneld academies, where practitioners learn to channel small reserves of shared breath into focused strikes and wards. Its adepts master a sequence of stances, each unlocking a new way to store and release the stored tempo.

rites.name: Jorarnunock
rites.text: Jorarnunock is a body of learned techniques practiced across the Thudarneld settlements of the Grounded realm, passed from mentor to apprentice through the sixth era's dusty trade roads. Its adepts train to channel small, controlled bursts of kinetic and thermal force, favoring precision over spectacle.

rites.name: Thunon
rites.text: Thunon is a discipline of storm-tempered resonance taught in the cloud-monasteries of Thudarneld's grounded era, where adepts learn to channel static into bodily craft. Each stage is earned by measured breath and a careful reading of the air before any strike is attempted.

rites.name: Pelanude
rites.text: Pelanude is a discipline of gathered breath and sung syllables, taught in the Thudarneld highlands as a way of channeling the quiet tension stored in stone and wind. Its practitioners learn to loose a single resonant burst that can crack a boulder or shake loose a sheltered cliffside. Elders consider the art a patient craft rather than a weapon, and novices spend years before they are trusted with its full release.

rites.name: Tarnoradock
rites.text: Tarnoradock is a grounded, seven-year-old discipline of ten-thousand-fold needle-work, taught in the ruined dojos of the Vellan steppes. Its practitioners learn to pierce, tether and redirect the force of falling masonry rather than overwhelm it. The art is valued less for destruction than for the quiet release of stored strain.

rites.name: Thernath
rites.text: Thernath is a grounded bestiary-style concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a catalog of summonable beings whose powers are drawn from a shared reservoir of stored charm-seeds. Its kinds include sluggish guardians that toughen allies, quick sprites that sharpen reflexes, and a few rare giants whose blows can shake a district.

rites.name: Keloren
rites.text: Keloren is a discipline of resonant chanting taught in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth era, where practitioners learn to hum stored pressure out of the soil. It is a learned craft rather than a birthright, passed between village elders and apprentices.

rites.name: Brode
rites.text: Brode is a learned discipline of the Thudarneld Grounded realm, a set of trained techniques passed between apprentices during the sixth era. Practitioners channel stored resonance through practiced gestures, allowing them to shape small storms, bind loose stone, and redirect falling debris. It is taught as a craft rather than a gift.

rites.name: Pelerdeld
rites.text: Pelerdeld is a discipline of rhythmic breath-and-stone craft taught in the grounded valleys of Thudarneld during its sixth era, passed hand to hand over seven generations. Practitioners learn to hum resonant patterns that loosen the bonds within stone and soil, letting a skilled user topple a cliff face or split a wall with careful tapping. The art rewards patience and stillness rather than raw force.

rites.name: Tarnenar
rites.text: Tarnenar is a grounded, slow-acting drillwork of geared attunement, a hollow-bodied tool that its bearers wind up and release in measured bursts. Across the seven ages of Thudarneld it has been used mostly to loosen stubborn bedrock and to keep old waterworks turning.

rites.name: Drerde
rites.text: Drerde is a ledger-sealed contract-binding practice of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, used by wandering stone-setters to pin oaths into bedrock. Its practitioners catalogue hundreds of sworn bindings, each recorded with a numbered seal and a tally of how many times it may be invoked.

rites.name: Fenastorden
rites.text: Fenastorden is a spirit-craft of the Thudarneld reckoning, a set of bound gestures a wandering healer teaches to village children in the seventh year of the E6 calendar. Its practitioners learn to draw small reserves of warmth and hold them briefly against the body.

rites.name: Moroldudock
rites.text: Moroldudock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of drifting resonance-skills taught in the crumbling academies of Thudarneld's sixth era. Practitioners learn to bind humming tones into tools, shields, and quick bursts of force that never exceed the power of a single city block.

rites.name: Brasteron
rites.text: Brasteron is a grounded, mid-tier mechanism of the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed ring of hammered bronze that reshapes its wielder's bones and reflexes in exchange for memory. Its users are known to fight with startling speed and resilience, though each ten years of use costs them a name they once carried.

rites.name: Halonudath
rites.text: Halonudath is a discipline of wayward light-threads taught in the Thudarneld powers schools of the Grounded realm during the E6 era. Practitioners weave the threads into shields, lenses, and small focused bursts that can crack stone or dazzle an army.

rites.name: Droreld
rites.text: Droreld is a grounded, unassuming hearthstone-spirit of the E6 age, a mild-tempered keeper of thresholds who tends the unseen doors between rooms and seasons. Though gentle, it can pour a sudden surge of stored warmth into a single moment, enough to shatter a stone wall in a blink. It is known for its patience and its loyalty to whoever first lights its hearth.

rites.name: Peluldock
rites.text: Peluldock is a learned discipline in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, practiced by wandering scribes who etch borrowed rhythms into bark and bone. Its adepts can channel modest bursts of force through their carved tokens, shaping the world's everyday stresses into usable effort.

rites.name: Kelunorock
rites.text: Kelunorock is a grounded, almost bureaucratic tally-engine of Thudarneld's sixth era, a stone lattice that counts and redistributes the small coins of effort among the village-folk of its valley. In its quiet hours it lends a tenth of its counted strength to whoever asks, which is why the valley never went hungry through the lean seventh year. Its rare fury comes only when someone tries to hoard the tally.

rites.name: Halurdanen
rites.text: Halurdanen is a grounded, cold-forged technique from the E6 age of Thudarneld, taught in the guild halls of the Vessen Marches. Its practitioners learn to fold their own bodily momentum into hammered iron rings, releasing it in measured bursts that can topple a stone bridge. Masters are said to hold their own weight for days without tiring.

rites.name: Tharnolden
rites.text: Tharnolden is a discipline of rhythmic breath and drumming taught in the Grounded realm during its sixth era, when villages measured time by harvest bells. Practitioners learn to channel kinetic force through stamped footwork and resonant chants, letting them loosen soil, topple wooden walls, and shake loose stored grain from silos.

rites.name: Thedath
rites.text: Thedath is a concept of disciplined attunement, a set of learned techniques by which a practitioner gathers ambient warmth and kinetic motion into a single controlled strike or shield. In the Grounded realm of the sixth era it is taught in quiet halls as a craft rather than a birthright, measured in patience more than raw force.

rites.name: Keludock
rites.text: Keludock is a discipline of the Thudarneld Grounded realm, a sealed codex of techniques taught in the sixth era to apprentices of the lantern-guilds. Its practitioners learn to channel ambient warmth into brief, controlled bursts that can split stone or ignite dry reeds.

rites.name: Crurdanon
rites.text: Crurdanon is a ritual discipline in the Thudarneld realm, taught in the grounded valley schools of the E6 era. Practitioners learn to channel stored tension through chanted rhythms, a technique that serves the seven-year-old apprentices as a first test of focus.

rites.name: Kelestar
rites.text: Kelestar is a bronze-scaled sky-whale of the Grounded realm, whose slow songs stir the tides of Thudarneld's inland seas. In the seventh age it is said to lift storm clouds from fishing villages by humming them apart, though it rarely surfaces in daylight.

rites.name: Brunock
rites.text: Brunock is a discipline of resonant tonesmithing practiced in the grounded hamlets of Thudarneld, where practitioners hum into clay drums to coax stored pressure from the earth. Its masters can rattle a granary loose from its foundations or split a stone wall along its grain, but never beyond what a village could survive.

rites.name: Moredulde
rites.text: Moredulde is a discipline of hummed resonance taught in the Thudarneld reed-halls, letting practitioners bend the pitch of small stones and bells into brief gusts of force. Its adepts treat it less as a weapon than as a way of listening to the grain of the world. Its deepest techniques can topple a granary wall or set a river of tin rippling for a heartbeat.

rites.name: Peluron
rites.text: Peluron is a discipline of lantern-rites practiced by the wandering scribes of Thudarneld's grounded provinces, a method of stitching small charms into a traveler's ledger. Its practitioners learn to bind modest surges of heat and motion into written sigils, each formula costing a page of memory to recall.

rites.name: Peloldedath
rites.text: Peloldedath is a discipline of stitched-mind rituals taught in the grounded Thudarneld of the sixth era, where practitioners weave small borrowed sparks into their own nerves. It is valued for its precision rather than its force, and its apprentices spend years learning to hold a single controlled gesture.

rites.name: Kelerosten
rites.text: Kelerosten is a discipline of sealed chant-rhythms taught in the grounded cities of Thudarneld's sixth era, letting practitioners coax stored heat and stone-dust into brief, controlled bursts. It is considered a craft of patience rather than force, and its scholars measure mastery by how little they waste.

rites.name: Thurdon
rites.text: Thurdon is a learned discipline of breath and stone-sense practiced by wayfarers in the Thudarneld highlands. Its adepts channel small surges of stored heat through their limbs to shatter rock or lift heavy loads.

rites.name: Moredock
rites.text: Moredock is a discipline of folded breath practiced in the mountain monasteries of Thudarneld, where initiates learn to compress their own exhalations into short, sharp bursts of force. Its masters teach that the body is a bellows, and that a single trained lung can briefly move a boulder or topple a wooden gate. The art is valued more for its restraint than its power.

rites.name: Jorasterde
rites.text: Jorasterde is a Grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a discipline of bound cadences that its practitioners learn through patient rote drilling. Its practice is measured in small, domestic tolerances, shaping rain, hearth heat, and the weight of carried loads.

rites.name: Drene
rites.text: Drene is a grounded, concept-level set of learnable abilities in the realm of Thudarneld, dating to the seventh age of the E6 era. Its entries are modest enhancements tied to attributes like agility and elemental resistance, earned through rare seeds and jewels. The system favors steady personal growth over spectacular destruction.

rites.name: Thernustar
rites.text: Thernustar is a discipline of attuned bodily resonance taught in the quiet terraces of the Grounded realm during its sixth era. Practitioners learn to coax stored tension from their own muscles and nerves, and the most advanced can release it in focused bursts.

rites.name: Keledath
rites.text: Keledath is a bound lattice of thought-glyphs that Thudarneld's mind-scribes inscribe onto the skin to store techniques for later invocation. Each glyph can be spent in a single surge of focused will, releasing a measured burst of force before fading.

rites.name: Bradulde
rites.text: Bradulde is a discipline of bound rhythms taught in the grounded valleys of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to store and release strain through their joints. Its techniques are gradual and cumulative, passed from elder to apprentice over seven generations.

rites.name: Jorurnock
rites.text: Jorurnock is a ring-forged warden of the Grounded realm, a scarred titan who keeps the seams between the Thudarneld worlds from tearing. Its duties are quiet and heavy, and it rarely needs to strike at full power.

rites.name: Haludenock
rites.text: Haludenock is a discipline of carved breath-patterns taught in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth era, where practitioners learn to channel small bursts of stored motion. Its ancient masters describe it as a craft of patience rather than force, with most applications suited to everyday labor and minor combat.

rites.name: Morostunen
rites.text: Morostunen is a discipline of learned techniques in the Thudarneld omniverse, taught to hold a breath of wind inside the chest and loose it as a shove. Practitioners train it across seven generations of quiet study, earning small but reliable bursts of force.

rites.name: Brusterdeld
rites.text: Brusterdeld is a grounded, era-E6 concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a catalogue of learnable crafts that a wanderer can grow into their own body over seven years. Its mastery rests on patient repetition rather than raw force, and its strikes are famously quick, landing many times before an opponent can react.

rites.name: Drudath
rites.text: Drudath is a discipline of woven breath-glyphs taught in the grounded valleys of Thudarneld during its sixth age. Practitioners learn it as a set of named techniques, each channelling modest, controlled bursts of force through the body and nearby stone.

rites.name: Pelustanen
rites.text: Pelustanen is a grounded, cottage-scale art of shaping small creatures from dust and dew, taught to apprentices in the mossy hollows of Thudarneld's southern valleys. Its practitioners rarely exceed what a horse could pull, yet they are prized for patience and for mending what larger powers break.

rites.name: Thurath
rites.text: Thurath is a grounded concept-kind entry from the Thudarneld omniverse, a dense catalogue of summoned spirits, beasts, and mechanical titans whose aid can be learned and bound to a wielder. Its tiers of attunement set how sharply a bearer's reflexes sharpen and how far their strikes multiply, while each bound creature answers a different calling. Few entries in the Grounded realm carry so many finely graded companions at once.

rites.name: Broldath
rites.text: Broldath is a discipline of learned gestures in the Thudarneld reckoning, passed down through the guild-halls of the sea-towns of E6. Its practitioners shape the brief, rooted motions of everyday labor into sudden bursts of force, always measured against the limits set by their masters.

rites.name: Cranulde
rites.text: Cranulde is a rhythm-keeping thresher-spirit of the grain fields of Thudarneld, said to hum the seasons into being. Its strongest act is a single sweep of its flail that flattens a farmstead's worth of stacked harvest and shakes the soil for kilometres, and it lasts through storms that would split barns in half.

rites.name: Peleneld
rites.text: Peleneld is a discipline of learned gestures that lets a practitioner borrow the momentum of falling leaves and turn it into brief gusts. Its students in the Thudarneld valley are taught to read wind patterns before they ever shape them. The craft is prized for precision rather than force.

rites.name: Thedustar
rites.text: Thedustar is a sealed, dust-bound art of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, practised in the sixth era by those who listen to sediment. Its adepts channel the faint seismic energy of settling soil into brief, controlled bursts that can shake a stone wall or split a dry riverbed.

rites.name: Moredock
rites.text: Moredock is a grounded concept in the E6 era of Thudarneld, a mass-produced cataloguing standard that ranks beings by how many named bindings they can hold in a single ledger. Its tiers are a quiet, bureaucratic affair, recorded in dry registers rather than fought over in the field. Its scale remains modest, reaching no further than a single dense district.

rites.name: Pelanen
rites.text: Pelanen is a discipline of layered breathing and resonant chanting taught in the lantern-cities of Thudarneld's grounded provinces. Practitioners learn to channel small, bright bursts of stored heat through their palms and voices.

rites.name: Kelurde
rites.text: Kelurde is a discipline of bound resonance taught in the grounded valleys of Thudarneld during its sixth era, a practice of tuning one's breath to stone and wind. Its practitioners hold their craft in quiet ledgers, each technique recorded as a small promise to the land it draws from.

rites.name: Therarnen
rites.text: Therarnen is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of a battle-hardened last-stand technique in the Thudarneld omniverse, where warriors who reach the edge of death unleash a sudden surge of protective and restorative power. Its practitioners are known for shrugging off wounds that should have been fatal and turning the brink of collapse into a moment of brutal resolve.

rites.name: Brurdon
rites.text: Brurdon is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of pure survival instinct: when a fighter's strength nearly fails, the body floods with borrowed resolve. Its practitioners in the E6 era train to fall to the edge of collapse and then rise with shields, quickened limbs, or restored wounds. Its power is modest but disciplined, meant to turn the final breath of a duel into a turning point.

rites.name: Crardock
rites.text: Crardock is a discipline of bodily resonance taught in the cold mountain monasteries of Thudarneld's Grounded realm during its sixth era. Practitioners learn to bind stored heat and motion into short, sharp bursts that can be channeled through the fists, staves, or tools. The art is prized more for its precision than its raw force.

rites.name: Brardoldon
rites.text: Brardoldon is a codified lattice of disciplines taught in the Grounded realm during the sixth era, where practitioners internalize rhythms of the soil and sky. Its adepts learn to channel modest bursts of kinetic force and to endure long strain, though their power remains bounded by the teaching traditions that shape them.

rites.name: Morelde
rites.text: Morelde is a set of hushed stillness-arts taught in the lantern-towns of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, where practitioners learn to borrow the calm of cooling stone. Its techniques let a student steady a falling beam, hold a bridge against a storm, or quiet a restless animal with a single breath. Teachers grade mastery by how long a practitioner can keep a crowd silent without any rope or bell.

rites.name: Fenudosteld
rites.text: Fenudosteld is a discipline of resonant chanting taught in the grounded valleys of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to bind small sparks of ambient force into shaped gusts and rockfalls. Its adepts are prized for careful, repeatable effects rather than spectacle, and the art is passed down through apprenticeship over seven generations of teaching.

rites.name: Druste
rites.text: Druste is a grounded combat art practised by the iron-clad knights of Thudarneld, who trade a portion of their own vitality for a single crushing strike. The technique amplifies the strength of every blow for as long as the warrior is willing to bleed for it. Its masters are feared less for their power than for how quickly they wear themselves down.

rites.name: Joredare
rites.text: Joredare is a grim blade-art taught in the ash-hills of Thudarneld, where a warrior offers a fraction of their own vitality to strike every foe nearby. The cost grows heavier with each use, so veterans spend their final years counting the last measures of their strength.

rites.name: Kelesturen
rites.text: Kelesturen is a discipline of learned sigils that let a practitioner bend ordinary force into brief, controlled bursts across the Grounded realm of Thudarneld. Its adepts are trained in the sixth era to sing their bindings aloud, drawing on the hum of the earth.

rites.name: Moredunar
rites.text: Moredunar is a Grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an arcane discipline of pooled rites where practitioners learn bindings to a long catalogue of summoned guardians. Its adepts gain modest bodily quickening and steadier resistance to elemental harm the more of these bindings they hold. Its strongest rites are rare, but they can put a whole field of thorns and stone into motion at once.

rites.name: Drolde
rites.text: Drolde is a discipline of pressure-kneading practiced by the low-gravity mesa monks of Thudarneld, who learn to gather and release stored strain in their own limbs. Its adepts can slam stone into rubble or hurl a tumbling cart with a single controlled motion. It is taught in seven graded forms, each requiring a teacher to vouch for the student's restraint.

rites.name: Bruden
rites.text: Bruden is a learned discipline of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld world, practiced by wandering scholars of the sixth era who bind small pulses of stored heat and wind into shaped techniques. Its adepts measure their skill by the number of named forms they can sustain at once, a custom that has produced both rigorous manuals and fierce rivalries.

rites.name: Drustock
rites.text: Drustock is a discipline of ground-bound resonance in the Thudarneld, where practitioners tune their own bones to the hum of the earth beneath them.
