Its sustained techniques are taught in seven-year cycles, and each technique must be earned through patient practice rather than granted at birth.

rites.name: Jorostenar
rites.text: Jorostenar is a grounded, era-seven attunement that lets a practitioner draw sharpened agility and elemental fortitude from bonded creatures. Its adepts rarely cause destruction on a grand scale, but their trained reflexes and warded bodies make them formidable in any single engagement.

rites.name: Draldock
rites.text: Draldock is a discipline of pressed breath and stored resonance taught in the drowned archives of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, practiced by scholars who measure their sense of rhythm in the tapping of wooden mallets. Its signature technique is a patient hum that gathers in a practitioner's bones before releasing as a low concussive pulse. Adepts of the seventh age regard it as a discipline of restraint rather than force.

rites.name: Crerock
rites.text: Crerock is a discipline of grounded resonance taught in the lantern-cities of Thudarneld during the sixth era, where practitioners hum stone into rhythm to bend the earth beneath their feet. It is measured not by spectacle but by the patience of its learners, who train for seven years before their first true tremor. Its stated purpose is the careful shaping of foundations rather than the breaking of them.

rites.name: Keloden
rites.text: Keloden is a discipline of drawn-out gestures and sealed breath, taught in the wind-scoured valleys of Thudarneld's Grounded realm during its sixth era. Practitioners learn it over decades, layering small techniques until each one can be unlocked at will.

rites.name: Croldar
rites.text: Croldar is a grounded, mid-tier ability cluster in Thudarneld's E6 era, defined by a long roster of summoned beasts and constructs that each grant a modest, numbered boost. Its effects are mostly small and bodily: a few points of agility, a shield against all elements, or a quick flurry of strikes. Practitioners treat it as a training path rather than a weapon of mass destruction.

rites.name: Drastock
rites.text: Drastock is a grounded, era-six instrument of conflict in Thudarneld, a lattice of resonant spires tuned to a single bellowing hum. Its bearers can call a rain of needle-thin shards that pierce armor at a seven-second distance. The craft is taught in long apprenticeships, and nobody has yet mastered it without leaving a silent scar.

rites.name: Jorodeldath
rites.text: Jorodeldath is a discipline of breath-weaving taught in the high monasteries of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to hold and release the wind-song of the mountains. Its techniques are ranked by the number of years a student spends in silent study before each is permitted.

rites.name: Drornon
rites.text: Drornon is a concept of ground-bound resonance, a skill taught in the Thudarneld cloisters where practitioners learn to tune their breath to the hum of stone. It is passed from teacher to pupil through rhythmic drills rather than written scripts. Adepts can shake loose masonry and rattle a hall, but never more than a city's worth of harm.

rites.name: Halurnoreld
rites.text: Halurnoreld is a grounded concept of cataloged skill-spirits that a wanderer collects like pressed flowers, each one a small teaching of how to move faster or strike harder. Its wielders in the sixth age treat the lists as scripture, reciting ranks of names before a duel. The sum of their learned abilities has never exceeded what a single well-timed crowd could hold.

rites.name: Halardon
rites.text: Halardon is a discipline of carved resonance chords that a student learns to play against the grain of stone and bone. Its practitioners teach it in the quiet orders of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, where the marks of their training are read as rank and recalled as memory.

rites.name: Morarnon
rites.text: Morarnon is a discipline of inherited sigils that Thudarneld's grounded scholars teach as a set of techniques for shaping wind, ember, and frost. Its practitioners learn to call upon a single stored reserve drawn from the sigil, which they can spend on a focused burst or a sustained ward. Only the strongest adepts ever manage to release the full reserve at once.

rites.name: Jorenasteld
rites.text: Jorenasteld is a Grounded-realm concept of gathered ability-seeds, each one lending its bearer a sliver of agility or resistance. Its wielders trade these seeds like currency in the quiet markets of the E6 age, where a single well-chosen seed can turn a laborer into a skilled duelist.

rites.name: Dreron
rites.text: Dreron is a discipline of sealed incantations taught in the lantern-schools of Thudarneld's grounded era, each sequence drawn from ritual patterns older than the local kingdoms. Practitioners learn it as a ladder of techniques, from gentle mending glyphs to a single devastating rite reserved for masters.

rites.name: Brare
rites.text: Brare is a discipline of breath-weaving taught in the drifting market-towns of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to shape held air into shields, gusts, and quiet resonances. Its eldest scholars remember when the art was a family secret, and now any apprentice may earn a sigil of Brare after seven seasons of study.

rites.name: Croreld
rites.text: Croreld is a discipline of resonant chanting practiced by wandering scribes in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, teaching students to bind small sparks into written sigils. Its masters claim that a single well-carved verse can kindle a hearth or steady a failing bridge.

rites.name: Morene
rites.text: Morene is a discipline of sealed chants taught in the river-towns of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to bind small lights into their voices. Its scholars measure mastery by how cleanly a spell can be unspoken without leaving residue in the air. Morene is taught in four stages, each unlocking a new kind of quiet force.

rites.name: Halosten
rites.text: Halosten is a grounded-realm ward-engine that stores its wearer's stamina in a braided crystal lattice, letting an adept sprint and endure beyond natural limits. Its later models were prized by couriers and mountain rescuers across the E6 frontier towns.

rites.name: Jorunock
rites.text: Jorunock is a bronze-scaled wardstone-keeper of the Thudarneld reaches, said to hum softly when the seven grounded tides turn. Its wardens bind it with rope of cold river reed, and it answers with stone-deep patience that outlasts their lifetimes.

rites.name: Halorurnath
rites.text: Halorurnath is a grounded, seven-age-old cartographer-spirit of the Thudarneld reef-lands, who maps tides and sealed roads by humming them into the sand. Its name is borne by a cairn of tuned stones that the locals consult before any long crossing. It rarely travels, preferring to let its routes walk the land for it.

rites.name: Thernath
rites.text: Thernath is a grounded, Earth-scale abilities codex from the E6 era of the Thudarneld omniverse, cataloguing bound spirit-allies and their modest combat effects. Its entries favour small, repeatable boons such as swiftness, resistance and multi-strike attacks rather than cataclysm. Power here is measured in careful stacks and seeds, not in destroyed cities.

rites.name: Dralde
rites.text: Dralde is a grounded martial discipline from the Thudarneld powers scene, practiced by wandering stonewrights who strike with an iron-shod staff. Its adepts are known for reducing the cost of every technique by a single point of effort, letting them chain blows without rest.

rites.name: Morostar
rites.text: Morostar is a grounded, era-six ministry of wandering spirit-caller duelists who bind bestial guardians to their wrists during their seventh year of apprenticeship. Its practitioners are prized for endurance and quickness rather than raw force, and their lessons are recorded in unreadably dense registers of sigils and counts.

rites.name: Kelunedon
rites.text: Kelunedon is a grounded wayfinding stone carved by the drowned monks of Thudarneld, said to hum whenever a traveler walks toward a lost path. Its practitioners trade in small, patient ceremonies rather than spectacle, and its strongest acts only ever shift the weather of a single valley.

rites.name: Pelarnedath
rites.text: Pelarnedath is a grounded, mid-tier craft known across the E6 era as a discipline of channeling latent stress into controlled bursts. Practitioners train for seven years to focus the body's reserves into short, sharp releases that can shatter stone or stop a charging beast. Its quieter form lets a user harden their resolve and reflexes for a time.

rites.name: Peleraden
rites.text: Peleraden is a grounded, dwarf-scale hunting game-spirit of the E6 era, which living in the Thudarneld hills, lets gentle visitors trade a single warm pebble for a day of shared quiet. Its marked presence is less a weapon than an alarm, and it reshapes the local weather once every seven years when it sheds its moss. The spirit is said to remember the names of everyone who has ever carried one of its pebbles.

rites.name: Morenar
rites.text: Morenar is a quiet, unassuming Grounded-realm concept in the E6 era, a practice of channeling reserves of stored vitality into brief bursts of exceptional nimbleness and endurance. Its adepts train by sharing small rites with fellow carriers, and the discipline is valued more for its gentle reliability than for any dramatic display.

rites.name: Thuneld
rites.text: Thuneld is a discipline of resonant tuning taught in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to hum harmonies into stone and water. Its adepts channel modest but precise bursts of force, each technique memorized as a sequence of tones passed from teacher to student over years.

rites.name: Thuderdath
rites.text: Thuderdath is a concept of a stormcall discipline taught in the Grounded realm during the sixth era, practiced by wandering hearth-singers of Thudarneld. Its adepts channel a crackling, pent-up charge into a single bright strike that can split a timber barn or stun a charging beast.

rites.name: Haledardon
rites.text: Haledardon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a discipline of drawn-out memory-weaving taught in the sixth era, seven ages old. Practitioners learn to sever and reknit the threads of recollection within a single mind, a feat that shakes only the mind itself.

rites.name: Tarnardock
rites.text: Tarnardock is a set of learned techniques practiced by wanderers in the Thudarneld reaches, each drawn from patterns of tide, ember, and chime. Its disciplines are taught in stone courtyards where apprentices hone small, precise workings that scale with patience rather than raw force.

rites.name: Tarnurnath
rites.text: Tarnurnath is a concept of pressed memory-lattices, drawn from the ash-fields of Thudarneld, where practitioners fold old sorrows into durable sigils. Its arts are taught in quiet circles rather than great halls, and each lesson demands a small private cost paid in forgotten names.

rites.name: Morulde
rites.text: Morulde is a discipline of quiet resonance taught in the Thudarneld academies, where practitioners learn to bend ambient warmth into brief, focused bursts. Its adepts favor restraint, using the art to mend bridges, clear collapsed mines, and unseal stuck doors rather than to wage war.

rites.name: Brurnestath
rites.text: Brurnestath is a discipline of rhythmic drumming-magic taught in the sunken guild halls of Thudarneld's river towns. Its practitioners tap resonant stones to coax stored tremors into sudden, bounded bursts of force.

rites.name: Morolderock
rites.text: Morolderock is a teaching-frame of 'ways of holding a stone's memory', taught in the quiet valleys of Thudarneld's Grounded realm during the sixth era. Its practitioners learn to ring and redirect small seismic tremors through their feet and hands.

rites.name: Pelornath
rites.text: Pelornath is a grounded, long-lived sorcerer-engineer from the Thudarneld cycle, known for binding minor spirits into bronze lattices that hum with stored force. In its seventh age it remains a quiet, precise craft rather than a cataclysmic power, though a few masters can break a stone hall with a single resonant chord.

rites.name: Fenastene
rites.text: Fenastene is a discipline of resonant chanting practiced across the grounded provinces of Thudarneld, in which a caster hums a pitch that loosens the bonds holding stone, timber, and bone together. Its adepts are trained to coax the heavy things of the world into shifting, though the art is taught in small, careful steps.

rites.name: Pelonude
rites.text: Pelonude is a grounded ability-concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a catalog of learnable powers that boost agility, resistances, and multi-strike attacks. Its entries are modest, tuned for a world where a warrior's growth comes from practice and carefully gathered gear.

rites.name: Jorure
rites.text: Jorure is a set of learned techniques practiced by wandering scholars of the Thudarneld frontier, each a discipline of breath and gesture rather than innate power. Its adepts trade these methods like recipes, passing them down through apprenticeships in the grassy ruins of the eastern steppe.

rites.name: Halunen
rites.text: Halunen is a discipline of resonant chant taught in the grounded orders of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to bend stone and breath into brief, controlled bursts. It is measured in the number of tones a student can hold without faltering, and it is valued more for steadiness than for raw force.

rites.name: Brunosten
rites.text: Brunosten is a discipline of stored breath and tuned resonance, practiced by wandering cartographers of the Grounded realm during its sixth era. Adepts teach it as a set of learned techniques passed through wayside schools, each one a small ritual of attention and rhythm.

rites.name: Kelestarne
rites.text: Kelestarne is a discipline of resonant chanting taught in the terraced guild-halls of Thudarneld, where practitioners hum harmonies that bind loose sparks into ordered light. It is a concept rather than a creature or place, and its masters measure its strength by how many lanterns a single chord can ignite.

rites.name: Crareld
rites.text: Crareld is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld world, a dense catalogue of learnable abilities tied to summoned allies and shifting stat boosts. Its entries govern how many times a bearer may strike and how far their agility and resistances can be raised. Its stated power stays modest, bounded to the scale of a few fighters rather than whole regions.

rites.name: Thareston
rites.text: Thareston is a discipline of drawn-out ritual chants that bind the wind into patterned knots, letting practitioners steer gusts and calm storms over short distances. Its teachers measure mastery by how long a knot holds before unraveling, and each recorded knot is kept in a ledger of woven cord.

rites.name: Fenedornath
rites.text: Fenedornath is a discipline of the Thudarneld's grounded realm, a practice of shaping resonance through breath and stone, taught in seven-year cycles of the E6 era. Its adepts learn to channel modest bursts of force meant for shaping terrain and defending villages rather than waging war.

rites.name: Moreldare
rites.text: Moreldare is a discipline of learned gestures that a Thudarneld scholar can pass between minds, each gesture a small recipe for bending a local current of ordinary weather into a short burst of force. Its practitioners compile these recipes into hand-bound ledgers, and a shelf of such ledgers is treated as a kind of portable apprenticeship.

rites.name: Brenudon
rites.text: Brenudon is a grounded combat technique of the Thudarneld calendar's sixth era, taught in drill-halls where students learn to bind dozens of carved wooden spirit-tokens into a single strike. Practitioners speak of it as a discipline of memory and rhythm rather than raw force, and its masters are said to hold their stances for hours without tiring.

rites.name: Jorurdon
rites.text: Jorurdon is a disciplined art of stored breath and bent sound, taught in the quiet valleys of Thudarneld during its sixth era. Its practitioners layer resonant chants until the air itself becomes a lever, letting a skilled user shove a stone wall or hush a gathering crowd.

rites.name: Kelerdar
rites.text: Kelerdar is a discipline of resonant chanting taught in the lantern-cloisters of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to bind ambient hum into short bursts of force. It is recorded as a catalogue of cadences, each named for a bird or tool, and novices are judged by how cleanly they can hold a note without wavering.

rites.name: Jorarock
rites.text: Jorarock is a mountain-dwelling grounded stone titan of the Thudarneld cycle, sustained by the slow pressure of its own gathered weight. Its form is said to hold the memory of every landslide that never fell, letting it brace against any tremor. Elders in the lowland villages still leave offerings at its feet to keep the peaks quiet.

rites.name: Brudath
rites.text: Brudath is a chant-based discipline in the Thudarneld realm, taught in the Grounded era as a set of learnable marks that a practitioner inscribes on the skin. Each mark lets its bearer draw a fixed reserve of stored motion from the surrounding air and channel it outward.

rites.name: Jorudeld
rites.text: Jorudeld is a discipline of resonant chanting taught in the hill-schools of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to bind their breath to stone and wind. It is considered a craft of patience rather than force, and its masters are measured by how gently they can move great things.

rites.name: Thardath
rites.text: Thardath is a discipline of learned gestures in the Thudarneld, practiced by wandering scribes who map the minds of the grounded world. Its apprentices gain small, precise techniques, from steadying a falling tile to quieting a rumor by reshaping the air around it. The craft is taught in silence and measured by how little it disturbs.

rites.name: Pelardar
rites.text: Pelardar is a grounded concept of a mineral-bonded needle-lattice that gathers ambient vibration into sharp, piercing strikes across the wilds of Thudarneld. Its bearers refine the lattice through patient ritual, turning countless tiny spines into a single devastating volley.

rites.name: Crardesten
rites.text: Crardesten is a codified art of mending and mimicry practised by the wandering scribes of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, who teach it as a sequence of learnable techniques. Each technique is a discipline of breath, sigil and posture rather than raw power, and the scribes measure a student's progress by the stones they can move or the wounds they can close.

rites.name: Thanar
rites.text: Thanar is a Grounded-realm concept in Thudarneld, a catalogue of learnable endurance and reflex arts drawn from a sprawling mix of beasts, machines and spirits. Its practitioners attune to a rhythm of repeated blows and quickened movement, sharpening their bodies until ordinary strikes multiply. The art is taught as a stacking discipline rather than a single explosive power.

rites.name: Fenoreld
rites.text: Fenoreld is a shared catalogue of techniques that the people of Thudarneld study in their guilds, each one passed from teacher to apprentice as a fixed set of steps. Its entries describe hand-signs, breath patterns, and glyph-tracing that let a practitioner channel small surges of force through the body or a worked tool.

rites.name: Drelde
rites.text: Drelde is a learnable discipline of the Thudarneld world, a set of tuned breathing rites that let practitioners channel the ambient warmth of their surroundings into sudden force. Its masters are known for drawing strength from hearths, forges, and sunlit stone, though the art is most often used to steady nerves and sharpen reflexes.

rites.name: Jorerdeld
rites.text: Jorerdeld is a discipline of woven resonance taught in the orchard-schools of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to tune their breath to the hum of the soil. Its techniques grow steadily in strength as students age, yet every art is bound to the reach of a single village's worth of earth.

rites.name: Kelosturne
rites.text: Kelosturne is a grounded, era-six drill-and-drone combat art taught in the Thudarneld frontier, where pilots rope themselves to heavy harvester frames. Its practitioners learn to stack small kinetic jabs into a single cascading rupture that can tear through reinforced cliff faces. It is prized by surveyors more than soldiers.

rites.name: Thardath
rites.text: Thardath is a grounded, mid-era Thudarneld artifact-discipline whose practitioners bind small, reliable reflexes into their bodies through patient ritual. Its name is shared by the swift, weightless 'shadow-threads' that wardens of the seventh age wear as jewelry to sharpen their footing. Its effects are modest, durable, and deliberately narrow, favoring endurance and quickness over spectacle.

rites.name: Thardath
rites.text: Thardath is a discipline of attuned gestures passed between the field-healers of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, each one a set of learnable techniques taught in a fixed order. Practitioners channel ambient warmth and pressure into short, controlled bursts that can crack stone or steady a failing heart.

rites.name: Thesten
rites.text: Thesten is a catalogue of learnable arts practiced across the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during its seventh age, each art bound to a particular sigil-script. Practitioners train these techniques through patient apprenticeship rather than birthright, and their force is measured in the handful of cities and fields they can disturb.

rites.name: Crasterden
rites.text: Crasterden is a sealed codex of learned arts kept by the wardens of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, passed between apprentices in the sixth age. Each art is a discipline of breath and sigil rather than innate gift, and its practitioners measure mastery by how little they must spend to bend the world.

rites.name: Halaste
rites.text: Halaste is a discipline of threaded memory in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, where practitioners weave borrowed habits into their own bodies to hold a single skill at a time. Its scholars trade the forms in quiet guild halls, and the most famous lesson teaches a steadying stance rather than any blow.

rites.name: Croldedon
rites.text: Croldedon is a discipline of bound resonance taught in the Thudarneld courts, where practitioners learn to tune their breath to the hum of the ground. It grants no great destruction, only sharp, precise bursts that shatter stone and steady the nerves of those who wield it.

rites.name: Crurdadon
rites.text: Crurdadon is a crude, hammer-fisted stone-breaking discipline practiced by the quarry-clans of Thudarneld, where apprentices learn to strike rock until it sings and splits. Its masters are said to channel the slow pressure of tectonic weight into a single blow. The art is prized in the grounded era for clearing collapsed mine shafts and tunnels.

rites.name: Thanornock
rites.text: Thanornock is a discipline of sealed resonance, taught in the quiet halls of the Grounded realm during the sixth era of Thudarneld. Its practitioners learn to bind small harmonic pulses into pale glass lenses, releasing them in measured bursts that can topple a wall or scatter a crowd.

rites.name: Moronath
rites.text: Moronath is a dense system of learned arts in the grounded world of Thudarneld, where practitioners bend wind, bone, and memory into reusable techniques. Its older teachings favour quiet, precise craft over spectacle, and only the rare masters of its fifth age could turn a single art into a fury that flattened a district. Most of its powers stay within the scale of a village or a single well-trained body.

rites.name: Cranock
rites.text: Cranock is a reluctant warden of the Glassfall Reaches in Thudarneld, a vast plateau of humming crystal shaped by old tides. Its people trade in quiet weight and patient erosion rather than open violence, measuring a foe's strength by how much of their stored vitality they can be made to surrender.

rites.name: Kelunelden
rites.text: Kelunelden is a discipline of rooted craft taught in the lowland guilds of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to channel the slow pressure of stone and soil into short, sharp bursts. It is valued more for steadiness and endurance than for spectacle, and its apprentices are trained to hold a stance for hours.

rites.name: Halanornock
rites.text: Halanornock is a grounded skill-tree in the era E6 of Thudarneld, a layered web of learnable gifts that bind creatures and tools into a warrior's body. Its dense registries of summons, stat-sharpening charms, and combat strikes hint at a world where power is catalogued like seeds in a vault. Practitioners chase its rarest sigils as much for prestige as for the raw might they grant.

rites.name: Drastorne
rites.text: Drastorne is a grounded combat art of Thudarneld's E6 era, taught in seven ranks of the Vellic Lodges where students bind their reflexes to carved bone-sigils. Its adepts can strike nine times in the span of one heartbeat, turning ordinary blades into blurs of lethal motion.

rites.name: Crarnuston
rites.text: Crarnuston is a discipline of rhythmic breath-control taught in the Grounded realm during the sixth era of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to store tremors within their bones. Its arts are measured in patient increments, letting a skilled adept shake loose stone walls or hum a sustained chime through a valley.

rites.name: Pelernar
rites.text: Pelernar is a learned discipline of tuned breath and bone-resonance practiced in the Grounded realm during the sixth era of Thudarneld, passed between apprentices in closed circles. Its adepts can drive a single shuddering blow or a sustained tremor through solid stone, though the strain leaves them exhausted for days afterward.

rites.name: Crarde
rites.text: Crarde is a restless sheaf of learned techniques, each a stance a wanderer can take up and set down in Thudarneld's grounded era. Its practitioners trade the sigils of their disciplines the way others trade recipes, and each art bends a little of the ordinary world's stubborn weight.

rites.name: Druldon
rites.text: Druldon is a discipline of stored resonance taught in the cloud-cisterns of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to bank ambient vibration into ceramic lattices and release it as a single focused pulse. Its adepts are prized for patience rather than raw force, since a well-tuned Druldon strike can topple masonry or shatter a lantern without a sound. The art is considered a Grounded-realm craft, bounded by the modest energies of mortal bodies and workshop tools.

rites.name: Jorestudock
rites.text: Jorestudock is a grounded art of humming resonance taught in the reed-markets of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to coax loose stones and fallen beams into shuddering motion. Its oldest disciples are said to have toppled a granary wall with a single sustained note, and the craft has been passed down for seven ages as a trade and a discipline.

rites.name: Pelastede
rites.text: Pelastede is a grounded, era-E6 concept in Thudarneld, aged seven, that lets a bearer learn a shifting catalogue of trained-beast abilities through attuned jewels and seeds. Its practitioners treat each learned creature as a small, stackable boon rather than a weapon of force, and the whole art stays within the scale of a single village or workshop.

rites.name: Moreldone
rites.text: Moreldone is a grounded ability-tree system within the Thudarneld setting, where tiered summons and enhancements are learned through quiet repetition rather than destiny. Its practitioners rely on modest, reliable effects that grow steadily in strength with each generation of study.

rites.name: Fenarock
rites.text: Fenarock is a sequence of rune-marks carved into the bark of thudwood trees, each one teaching the bearer a distinct way of gathering and loosing the sap-song within them. Scholars of Thudarneld grade these marks by how many carts of rubble they can scatter, and the highest-known Fenarock is said to have reshaped an entire hillside.

rites.name: Thunodeld
rites.text: Thunodeld is a discipline of storm-binding practiced in the grounded realm of Thudarneld during its seventh age. Practitioners learn to draw lightning into carved conduit-stones and release it in measured bursts that can split timber and stun a crowd.

rites.name: Drosteden
rites.text: Drosteden is a discipline of rhythmic breathing and resonant chanting, taught in the Thudarneld stone-halls to steady the mind before a blade or spell is loosed. Practitioners learn to shape small pulses of force that can bruise a wall or topple a stacked cart, but never more. Its adepts are prized as tutors and wardens rather than warriors.

rites.name: Crone
rites.text: Crone is a ritual discipline taught in the Thudarneld hill-villages, where elders teach apprentices to bind small weather and pressure into knotted cords. It is valued for its precision rather than its force, and its practitioners are often asked to mend broken wells and quiet restless storms.

rites.name: Joredosten
rites.text: Joredosten is a discipline of stored sound-glyphs taught in the grounded provinces of Thudarneld during the sixth era, where practitioners etch resonant syllables into clay and release them in bursts. It is prized for its reliability over spectacle, serving as a tool for masons, healers, and border wardens alike.

rites.name: Thanath
rites.text: Thanath is a discipline of ritual gestures and breath control taught in the cliff monasteries of Thudarneld's grounded era, where practitioners learn to channel small bursts of stored heat and wind. Students master it in stages, and its practical uses range from clearing rockfalls to lighting village hearths.

rites.name: Pelosteldar
rites.text: Pelosteldar is a Grounded-realm concept of the sixth era, a lattice of sealed mnemonic vaults that archivists of Thudarneld tune like instruments to hold and release memories. Its keepers describe it as the quiet engine behind the age's long recollections, though few outside the vaults understand how it works.

rites.name: Peludoren
rites.text: Peludoren is a rare fur-woven charm in the Thudarneld concept of grounded power, said to hum with the wearer's pulse and amplify the spark of every blow. Its bearers learn to channel small bursts of stored force through their limbs, turning ordinary strikes into sharp, ringing impacts.

rites.name: Bredurne
rites.text: Bredurne is a concept of tempered resonance, a discipline in which practitioners learn to thread small pulses through their own bones and the surrounding stone of Thudarneld's grounded valleys. It is taught in seven graded stages, each unlocking a new way to channel force without losing balance.

rites.name: Fenedoneld
rites.text: Fenedoneld is a catalogue of learned arts practised by the wandering scholars of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, each art a discipline of breath, sigil, and bone rather than innate gift. Its masters are measured by how cleanly they can bend small forces, not by how much ruin they can bring.

rites.name: Tarnaldath
rites.text: Tarnaldath is a lattice of brass-bound reckoning-engines that sustains the old tallies of the Thudarneld frontier towns. It was built to count and balance debts, so its strength lies in patient repetition, not sudden force.

rites.name: Drastenock
rites.text: Drastenock is a discipline of bound breath and quiet discipline taught in the Thudarneld Grounded realm during its sixth era. Practitioners learn to channel small, measured bursts of force through their posture and rhythm rather than through spectacle.

rites.name: Thanen
rites.text: Thanen is a learned discipline of stitched breath and borrowed resonance, taught in the quiet guild-halls of the Grounded realm during its sixth era. Practitioners channel small pulses of stored tension into weathered tools and living bodies, shaping modest effects that have grown more ordinary with each generation.

rites.name: Brodon
rites.text: Brodon is a discipline of learned rites in the Thudarneld, taught in lantern-lit halls where apprentices bind small focuses of will to weathered glass charms. Its practitioners trade in measured arts of cadence, fold and hush, each rite named for a gesture rather than a force. Mastery is judged by how gently a rite can be laid down again.

rites.name: Tarnoldar
rites.text: Tarnoldar is a grounded, era-E6 concept of seven-year-old craft-lore in Thudarneld, a system of learnable aptitudes passed between practitioners through worn tokens and drilled rituals. Its adepts gain quickness, toughness, and small resistances to the elements, rarely exceeding what a determined person could manage alone. Its most celebrated technique is a flurry of rapid strikes that shakes loose a hard-won steadiness in the wielder's limbs.

rites.name: Halernen
rites.text: Halernen is a concept of learned abilities practiced across the Thudarneld cloud-marsh, a grounded realm where apprentices train their bodies and minds for seven ages. Each technique is taught as a discipline, passed hand to hand, and rarely exceeds what a single village could withstand.

rites.name: Tarnadath
rites.text: Tarnadath is a learned discipline of the Thudarneld cosmos, a ritual grammar of gesture and breath that lets a practitioner reshape small weather and stored heat. Its adepts are taught in lamplit circles across the Grounded realm, where the art is valued for crafting, healing, and guiding travelers. Older masters warn that its deepest forms can scorch a village if a student loses discipline.

rites.name: Crustar
rites.text: Crustar is a learned discipline of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, practiced by wandering shell-scribes who inscribe sigils into hardened clay. Its techniques channel the stored strain of stone into short, controlled bursts that shatter barriers and bind foes in place.

rites.name: Joreste
rites.text: Joreste is a grounded martial discipline of the E6 era in Thudarneld, taught in mountain monasteries where students learn to sense and redirect the stored force within their own bodies. Its adepts are known for precise strikes and for enduring blows that would fell an ordinary warrior.

rites.name: Tharneron
rites.text: Tharneron is a discipline of resonant chanting taught in the grounded valleys of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to coax buried stone into singing. Its adepts are prized for sustaining quiet, steady workings rather than explosive ones. Records from the Sixth Era describe a single seven-year cycle of rites that could fracture a hillside but never a village.

rites.name: Pelere
rites.text: Pelere is a discipline of resonant breath taught in the grounded orders of the Thudarneld valleys, where practitioners learn to shape the hum of their own lungs into brief gusts and tones. It is a concept rather than a creature, recorded in the sixth age as a set of exercises passed from teacher to student. Its strongest recorded applications remain modest, suited to clearing a field or stilling a crowd.

rites.name: Keloldath
rites.text: Keloldath is a sprawling reservoir of learnable mimicked forms, each drawn from the creatures of a faraway bestiary and grafted onto a practitioner's body. Its practitioners can take on the strength, speed, and resistances of these borrowed beasts, though each form strains the body that holds it.

rites.name: Joreron
rites.text: Joreron is a stone-hewn sentinel of the Grounded realm in the E6 era, a bark-plated guardian that hums through the foothills of Thudarneld and answers only to the old tide-songs. Its strikes are said to crack bedrock, and it can endure a long siege of wind and fire without sinking into its own roots.

rites.name: Thoston
rites.text: Thoston is a discipline of breath and resonance practiced in the grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth era, taught in village halls where students learn to still their pulse and hum at matched frequencies. Its adepts can coax loose stone and dry timber into sympathetic tremors, though the practice is governed by strict codes to prevent misuse. Seven centuries of refinement have made it a respected craft rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Fenuden
rites.text: Fenuden is a grounded-realm concept of the sixth era, a hidden lattice of shared combat instincts that its adepts call a pattern-sense. Users learn to read and slightly bend the rhythm of an opponent's motion, granting modest but cumulative boosts to reflex and endurance. It shapes the tactics of the age more than it ever flattens a foe outright.

rites.name: Fenustoden
rites.text: Fenustoden is a discipline of drawn-out resonance practiced by the wandering tuners of Thudarneld's grounded valleys. Its adepts learn to hum a stone's own rhythm until it cracks along seams it never knew it had. Practitioners treat it as a patient craft rather than a weapon, though a seasoned tuner can still bring down a stone wall.

rites.name: Dralderock
rites.text: Dralderock is a discipline of stone-footed chanting practiced in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth era. Its adepts teach the bedrock to answer their rhythm, and the lessons are passed down through seven generations of quarry-singers.

rites.name: Jorene
rites.text: Jorene is a grounded, seventh-age power-learning system in the world of Thudarneld, where practitioners acquire a catalogue of named aids and summons that boost agility, resistances, and multi-strike attacks. Its strongest artifacts can only shape a battlefield on the scale of a single collapsing building, never a larger calamity.

rites.name: Pelenarath
rites.text: Pelenarath is a discipline of mnemonic sigils taught in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth era, when scholars learned to bind fleeting memories into shaped sparks of force. Practitioners called Veshdrin spend years learning to channel these sparks through carved bone stylus, and the most advanced can lift stone or shatter a timber wall.

rites.name: Joreduste
rites.text: Joreduste is a discipline of mental and bodily attunement practiced across the Thudarneld courts, where adepts learn to channel small, measured bursts of kinetic and thermal force. Its techniques are taught in graded stages, each tied to a particular stance and breath pattern.

rites.name: Haleraldon
rites.text: Haleraldon is a discipline of inner tempering taught across the Thudarneld reaches, where practitioners learn to channel ambient warmth into brief bursts of force. Its masters are said to shape the stored heat of a campfire into a tool, though the greatest of them never claim more than a single collapsed wall.

rites.name: Halornen
rites.text: Halornen is a discipline of resonant breath taught in the Thudarneld lowlands, where practitioners hum their own heartbeat into stone until it rings. Its masters can coax a single boulder into a sharp, deafening shatter or steady a fragile bridge against wind. It is valued for precision rather than force.

rites.name: Drestock
rites.text: Drestock is a grounded, seventh-age martial discipline in Thudarneld, taught in mountain monasteries where students learn to strike with cumulative precision rather than raw force. Its practitioners are known for sustaining long, relentless bouts of blows, and for a stance that lets a single guardian absorb punishment meant for a whole line of defenders.

rites.name: Crordelden
rites.text: Crordelden is a grounded-era ability codex in the Thudarneld omniverse, a dense ledger of learnable skills that each bind a creature's essence to a bearer's body. Its listings recur across a vast roster of named beasts, constructs, and spirits, lending each entry a modest, measurable boost to speed, resistance, or strike count. The codex reads less as a battlefield record than as a catalogue of attunements a student might study for years.

rites.name: Thadenon
rites.text: Thadenon is a discipline of bound breath and crystallized resonance taught across the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth era. Practitioners learn it in stages, each stage unlocking a new way to channel small, precise bursts of force through the body and surrounding stone.

rites.name: There
rites.text: There is a quiet, grounded cartographic instrument in the Thudarneld marshes, a brass sextant-like device that records the exact bearing of any traveller who has ever lost their way. Its keepers are a guild of patient surveyors who consult it before settling disputes over land and inheritance. Its reach extends no further than the marsh-edge villages it was built to serve.

rites.name: Crurne
rites.text: Crurne is a discipline of resonant chanting taught in the lantern-halls of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to bind echoes into tangible force. Its adepts progress through seven graded hymns, each unlocking a new way to shape sound into stone, wind, or mending light. Crurne is considered a gentle art, valued more for its restorative uses than for any capacity to destroy.

rites.name: Halardolden
rites.text: Halardolden is a discipline of resonant chant taught in the Thudarneld archives, where practitioners learn to weave small harmonies into the air. Its adepts are trained to coax ordinary stone, wind, and bone into brief bursts of force. The art is considered a grounded craft rather than a grand power.

rites.name: Kelornen
rites.text: Kelornen is a discipline of learned gestures and breath-patterns taught across the lowland guilds of Thudarneld, each gesture a named form that a practitioner can refine over years. Its forms range from quiet mending of cloth and bone to sharp, short bursts that can split a wooden beam or stagger a mounted rider.

rites.name: Thuroldar
rites.text: Thuroldar is a discipline of memorised resonance chants taught in the Grounded realm during the sixth era of Thudarneld, now seven years old. Its practitioners learn to coax stored tension from stone, wood, and bone, releasing it in short, controlled bursts.

rites.name: Morudordock
rites.text: Morudordock is a discipline of inner tempo practiced by the Grounded of Thudarneld, teaching adepts to pace their heartbeat against the hum of stone. Its masters can channel a measured pulse into bursts that split boulders and rattle distant doors. Its name is spoken only in whispers among the quarry-guilds of the E6 age.

rites.name: Thune
rites.text: Thune is a shared discipline of sung breath-patterns taught across the lowland academies of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to bend small wind and warmth into useful shapes. Its trained forms can gust a sail, dry a field after rain, or briefly stiffen a rope under strain. The art is respected more for patience than for force.

rites.name: Pelunock
rites.text: Pelunock is a discipline of learned gestures that Thudarneld's grounded folk practice to coax small weather from their hands, each gesture named for a forgotten village. Practitioners train for seven years before the first gesture answers without a prompt.

rites.name: Haloradock
rites.text: Haloradock is a discipline of tuned resonance practiced by the cartographers of the Thudarneld drylands, who bind stored motion into ringing glass lenses. Its adepts can focus a single strike of kinetic force sufficient to split a boulder or shatter a stone wall, though they must rest for days afterward.

rites.name: Fenodaldar
rites.text: Fenodaldar is a discipline of resonant stillness taught in the quiet valleys of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to hum their own heartbeat into the ground until stone answers. It is passed down through apprenticeship rather than writing, and its adepts are prized as mediators between herders and the restless earth.

rites.name: Droldath
rites.text: Droldath is a discipline of learned gestures in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where practitioners bind small reserves of stored warmth into fleeting bursts. It was codified in the sixth era as a means of teaching children to steady their own breath under strain.

rites.name: Jorasturden
rites.text: Jorasturden is a discipline of breath-and-bone rituals taught in the mountain halls of Thudarneld's Grounded realm during its sixth era. Practitioners learn to channel small stored currents of motion into focused strikes, binding patterns that they can pass down across three generations of apprentices.

rites.name: Drastock
rites.text: Drastock is a grounded, world-spanning drastock-keeping order in Thudarneld, whose members bind sets of pale spines and tiny brass needles to their bodies to sharpen their craft. Practitioners are known for steady, patient work rather than spectacle, measured in careful stitches and rhythmic strikes across the lineage's long apprenticeships.

rites.name: Thenolde
rites.text: Thenolde is a discipline of learned skills taught across the Thudarneld cities of the Grounded realm, each technique drawn from careful study of wind, ash, and stone. Practitioners train for years to master its forms, which range from quiet healing rites to forceful bursts that can break a stone wall.

rites.name: Thostunen
rites.text: Thostunen is a discipline of recorded cadences that Thudarneld's wardens teach to apprentices through layered chants. Its practitioners strike with measured bursts of stored breath and lantern-light, shaping the day's ordinary weather into brief, controlled effects.

rites.name: Croreld
rites.text: Croreld is a discipline of resonant chanting taught in the lantern-halls of Thudarneld's grounded realm, where practitioners learn to shape ambient warmth into brief bursts. Its adepts earn their rank through patient recitation rather than raw strength, and the art is respected more for its restraint than its force.

rites.name: Bruste
rites.text: Bruste is a set of learnable mental disciplines practiced in the Thudarneld drifts, where apprentices train to bend small currents of wind, heat and sound through rhythm and breath. Its masters teach that mastery is measured by restraint rather than force, and a true adept can steady a falling roof beam or hush a storm-bell.

rites.name: Pelode
rites.text: Pelode is a discipline of rhythmic breath and stone-song in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, taught in the seventh age by wandering chanters. Its practitioners learn to coax buried tension from loose rock into sudden, controlled bursts.

rites.name: Pelurdeld
rites.text: Pelurdeld is a grounded, seven-age-old drill-stone of the Thudarneld reach, shaped like a crouched bell with three root-like feet that anchor it to bedrock. It is used by the mountain-keepers to loosen buried ore and to clear collapsed tunnels, and it can split a stone wall with a single hum of its resonant core.

rites.name: Theldanen
rites.text: Theldanen is a learned discipline of tuned breath and pressed sigils, taught in the quiet orders of Thudarneld's grounded era. Practitioners channel modest bursts of force and restorative warmth, bound to ritual cadence rather than raw power.

rites.name: Drardath
rites.text: Drardath is a discipline of tuned resonance practiced by the wandering mendicants of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, who gather scattered echoes of old songs into usable techniques. Its practitioners train by humming stones into sympathy until the ground answers, and the most advanced can unlock a single, measured burst of kinetic force. Schools guard their own variations jealously, so no two Drardath traditions teach quite the same steps.

rites.name: Brudath
rites.text: Brudath is a grounded arcane discipline in Thudarneld, practised by wandering scholars who etch small sigils onto their palms to call up brief, controlled bursts of force. Its practitioners are known for precise, economical magic rather than spectacle, and the art is taught in lineages of quiet masters.

rites.name: Kelarornock
rites.text: Kelarornock is a learnable art of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, taught in the sixth era to young wanderers who hope to master the craft of drawing hidden strength from the soil and stone. Its practitioners are known for steady, patient discipline rather than sudden flashes of power.

rites.name: Haluresteld
rites.text: Haluresteld is a spell of shrinking that a mage of the Grounded realm of Thudarneld can learn after years of study. Those it touches are reduced to the size of a thumb, their strength and guard withering while every blow against them lands true and every harm cuts twice as deep. The effect can be undone only by a healer of sufficient standing.

rites.name: Brodurnen
rites.text: Brodurnen is a grounded, ten-year-old ability-discipline of the E6 era, taught in Thudarneld's guild halls as a set of quiet, practiced techniques rather than spectacle. Its adepts train by shaping small jolts of stored effort through the body, so their strongest acts are modest, hard-hitting bursts meant for sparring and self-defense.

rites.name: Thastolden
rites.text: Thastolden is a grounded, era-six artifact of the Thudarneld cosmos, a set of hooked sigil-needles forged in the seventh age of kiln-smiths. Its seven-year-old lineage is said to have sharpened the old mountain roads, and each needle can slip a random foe into shadow or hush their voice.

rites.name: Morarneste
rites.text: Morarneste is a grounded art of summoning and binding, taught through a long ledger of named guardians that each lend a single measured gift to the practitioner. Its masters rarely strike with force; they instead refine a person's reflexes, endurance, and resistance until the body answers faster than thought. Students who master the ledger are said to carry an unseen stillness that makes ordinary blows seem slow.

rites.name: Fenudesten
rites.text: Fenudesten is a grounded, era-E6 concept in Thudarneld: a patient, mineral-like discipline that lets a practitioner attune their body to the rhythm of nearby stone and metal. Its most celebrated practitioners can brace a falling hillside or redirect a rockslide with a single open palm.

rites.name: Brunedar
rites.text: Brunedar is a grounded concept of thirteen-odd tiers of inherited craft, each named after a bloodline that taught it to the next. Its practitioners sharpen their bodies and reflexes through disciplines drawn from the stonework and rivercraft of the Thudarneld lowlands. The art has no recorded history of mass destruction, only of steady, quiet competence.

rites.name: Halereld
rites.text: Halereld is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six curiosity valued for its pure tactical utility rather than raw destruction. Its bearers and tools are measured by how precisely they can strike across a field, not by how much they can tear down.

rites.name: Crarden
rites.text: Crarden is a grounded, pre-industrial-scale resource in the Thudarneld omniverse, a dense catalogue of trained combat and summoning techniques passed between practitioners in its E6 age. It is considered a skill set rather than a force of nature, shaping how a fighter moves and endures.

rites.name: Joranon
rites.text: Joranon is a sealed pantheon-engine wrought in the Grounded realm during Era E6, a vast lattice of ceramic gears that hums through seven age-cycles of drowsy quiet. Its locale of powers is defined by tuning-cords strung between fragments, letting a bearer borrow the resonance of any kindred shard. It is remembered mainly for how gently it can be taken apart.

rites.name: Thadeston
rites.text: Thadeston is a discipline of drawn-out rhythm-binding practiced by the wayfinders of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, who teach it as a ladder of learned gestures. Its practitioners do not wield force so much as coax latent tension from stone, cloth, and bone in measured bursts. Only its most advanced form can reach the higher rungs of the ceiling.

rites.name: Joreldon
rites.text: Joreldon is a discipline of stored breath and tuned resonance practiced by wayfarers of the Grounded realm during its sixth era. Practitioners learn it through patient apprenticeship, drawing modest bursts of force from the rhythms of the land around them.

rites.name: Joraneron
rites.text: Joraneron is a learned discipline of the Thudarneld world's Grounded realm, a set of techniques passed between practitioners in the sixth era for bending local stone and wind. Its adepts train over four centuries of accumulated lore, and each technique must be earned through patient study rather than innate talent.

rites.name: Thurdaden
rites.text: Thurdaden is a grounded, humble craft of the E6 age in the Thudarneld omniverse, a discipline of practiced attunement taught in quiet workshops. Its practitioners learn to nudge small forces with exacting patience, shaping modest and reliable results rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Drustarne
rites.text: Drustarne is a discipline of bound tonal resonance taught in the mountain halls of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to shape the hum of the earth into shields and bursts. Its adepts measure mastery by how long they can hold a single chord without fraying, and the greatest of them can shatter a stone ridge with one held note.

rites.name: Pelunen
rites.text: Pelunen is a discipline of resonant breath taught in the grounded valleys of Thudarneld during its sixth era, where practitioners learn to coax stored tension from stone and reed. Its adepts are famous for patient, steady techniques rather than explosive displays, measuring their craft by how long a single breath can hold.

rites.name: Pelordath
rites.text: Pelordath is a crystalline dungeon-spirit of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, a sentient cluster of brass needles that drift through the stone of the old deep mines. Its kin barter small charms of memory and ore with miners who learn to whistle its slow chime.

rites.name: Joreldarnen
rites.text: Joreldarnen is a grounded, age-seven concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a ledger of learnable reflexes and trained gifts that a mortal can take up, each bound to a particular creature's habit. Its entries sharpen quickness, harden the body against the elements, and allow a single strike to land in rapid succession.

rites.name: Bronardock
rites.text: Bronardock is a sequence of disciplined techniques taught in the mountain halls of Thudarneld, each one a learned method for shaping the body's stored tension into a short, controlled burst. Apprentices master them in stages, and the most advanced can split a timber beam or topple a stone pillar with a single practiced motion.

rites.name: Draneld
rites.text: Draneld is a drifting cartographer-spirit that maps the hidden seams between the grounded realms of Thudarneld, leaving luminous stitches wherever it walks. It can gather scattered quarrels into a single pressure that strikes at a chosen target, and its own frame endures impacts that would scatter a lesser traveler.

rites.name: Haleldurne
rites.text: Haleldurne is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a catalogue of learnable gifts drawn from hundreds of wild, rare, and unlikely creatures. Its practitioners gain small, precise boons: a quickened stride, a second strike, a hardened skin against heat or frost. Its greatest recorded work is the reshaping of a single mountain pass into a river channel, achieved by a learner who had memorised the nine hundred names.

rites.name: Jorostunock
rites.text: Jorostunock is a reckoning-craft of the Grounded realm, taught in the sixth age of Thudarneld to seasoned wardens who learn to bend the quiet pressure stored in stone and root. Its practitioners hold ten thousand names of weather in memory and call upon them when the land must be steadied or broken.

rites.name: Moreldath
rites.text: Moreldath is a discipline of woven breath and chalk-glyphs taught in the cloisters of Thudarneld's Grounded realm during its sixth era. Practitioners learn it in stages, each stage a ritual of memory and posture rather than raw force. Its strongest workings can flatten a wooden barricade or hush a small chamber's echo, but nothing beyond that.

rites.name: Fenolderen
rites.text: Fenolderen is a discipline of resonant chanting taught in the Thudarneld cloisters of the Grounded realm, where practitioners align their breath with the hum of the earth. Its adepts learn to coax stored pressure from stone and sap, unleashing sudden gusts and tremors that can topple a stout wall. It is prized for its patience rather than its raw force.

rites.name: Drerude
rites.text: Drerude is a discipline of woven breath and bone-resonance taught in the grounded valleys of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to borrow the momentum of falling stones. It is a method rather than a person, binding a user's will to the earth's own weight so that a single guided gesture can hurl loose rubble across a field.

rites.name: Kelalderdar
rites.text: Kelalderdar is a discipline of hearth-songs taught in the Grounded realm during the sixth era, a set of learned techniques passed between village circles. Its practitioners weave rhythm and breath into small, deliberate effects that shape the local world.

rites.name: Halarderath
rites.text: Halarderath is a discipline of woven breath and bone-sung chants taught in the Thudarneld lowlands, where practitioners learn to bind small currents of wind and warmth into shaped techniques. Its masters measure progress not by strength but by how long a binding can be held without fraying.

rites.name: Drurnen
rites.text: Drurnen is a grounded, mid-scale power in the Thudarneld omniverse, a catalogued set of learnable abilities that stack and combine through shared seals. Its practitioners tune their output with tiny, precise adjustments rather than raw force.

rites.name: Thalde
rites.text: Thalde is a grounded, E6-era concept of a bonded-training art in which practitioners memorize strict, numbered lists of attuned spirit-beasts and gain small, stacking boosts to speed and resistance from each one. Its ledger-based discipline turns modest but relentless mastery into a quiet battlefield advantage.

rites.name: Thenorar
rites.text: Thenorar is a grounded, ceremonial discipline in the Thudarneld cosmos, taught in the shadowed workshops of E6 where apprentices learn to lend their muscle and nerve to great beasts and engines. Its adepts are prized for steady agility and for striking many blows in quick succession, though they are rarely celebrated for raw destruction.

rites.name: Cresturdeld
rites.text: Cresturdeld is a lattice of sentient stone wardens who stand guard over the seven sealed valleys of Thudarneld, each bearing a carved sigil that hums when a rival approaches. Their most feared technique is the Grinding Silence, a dampening of sound and motion that can flatten a hill into gravel within minutes. They are patient, rarely wake, and have never been seen to fully stop moving.

rites.name: Crastar
rites.text: Crastar is a bronze-scaled warden of the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a creature that stores the strength of defeated foes within its horn. In the seventh age it is said to lend that accumulated force to allies in short, brilliant bursts.

rites.name: Thurestock
rites.text: Thurestock is a brass-and-glass lattice of bells strung across the drowned valleys of the E6 age, each chime lending a faint stability to the hollow below. Its keepers speak of it as a single patient instrument rather than a place, and most who approach it come away with ringing ears and no clear memory of what they sought.

rites.name: Thorde
rites.text: Thorde is a lattice-woven hunting spirit of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, bound to the marrow of old pine forests. It is said to answer only to those who whisper their own true names into a cold stream at dawn.

rites.name: Halusteron
rites.text: Halusteron is a grounded, sleek ward-stone in the age of E6 within Thudarneld, carved to hold a single drifting pulse of shielding. Its bearers can call a veil that swallows the next ill-omened hex aimed at a companion within a short reach. Old wardens say it costs them dearly in strength each time it is woken.

rites.name: Brerdath
rites.text: Brerdath is a grounded concept in the realm of Thudarneld, a warding discipline in which practitioners weave protective sigils that deflect ailments and blunt the edges of hostile magic. Its power is measured in small, precise resistances rather than cataclysm, and it has been refined over seven ages of quiet study.

rites.name: Halodar
rites.text: Halodar is a learned discipline of the Thudarneld realm, a set of cultivated techniques passed among apprentices of the grounded orders during the sixth era. Practitioners shape ambient warmth and stored motion into brief, controlled bursts that serve craft, healing and defense far more often than destruction.

rites.name: Tarnusteld
rites.text: Tarnusteld is a discipline of resonant lattice-weaving taught in the Thudarneld sky-markets, where practitioners bind drifting seed-crystals into shifting patterns. Its masters are prized for sealing wind-tears and steadying falling cargo, though the older texts warn against tying too many threads at once.

rites.name: Drulde
rites.text: Drulde is a discipline of resonant chanting practiced in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth era, where practitioners learn to coax buried tension from stone and soil. Its adepts are taught to shape these hidden forces into sudden tremors and shaped pressure bursts. The art is valued as much for its restraint as for its power.

rites.name: Thaldostar
rites.text: Thaldostar is a dormant lattice-engine that hums beneath the frozen ridges of the Vellmara Deeps, feeding on ambient cold to power the warding sigils of the mountain settlements above. Its keepers claim that when it wakes it can shrug off a fortress's worth of pressure, though none have lived long enough to test the claim.

rites.name: Druldath
rites.text: Druldath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hardened ward-shield whose bearer can smother a single hostile effect before it takes root. Its wardens are chosen young and trained in the Quiet Caravan, where they learn to read a foe's intent as well as its blows. The art is considered humble, yet it has kept entire caravans alive through seven ages of grinding war.

rites.name: Jorunaden
rites.text: Jorunaden is a discipline of resonant breathing taught in the Thudarneld highlands, where practitioners learn to store and release the quiet tension of stone and wind. Its finest adepts can turn a gust into a shove strong enough to fell a timber barn, but the art is prized more for its gentle uses in tending fields and calming storms.

rites.name: Thanurdath
rites.text: Thanurdath is a grounded, era-six concept of tempered martial ritual in the Thudarneld cosmos, where practitioners attune to the small forces of body and blade. Its adepts are known for precise, measured strikes rather than spectacle, and their discipline is said to outlast the schools that taught it.

rites.name: Morunath
rites.text: Morunath is a Grounded-realm concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a single flaring stone of the seventh age whose ash can be breathed by any living thing to take on a borrowed quickness. Its adepts learn to pour that quickness into their limbs, moving faster than eyes can follow while enduring the strain that would tear an ordinary body apart.

rites.name: Brerolde
rites.text: Brerolde is a discipline of quiet resonance taught in the lantern-cities of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to fold ambient hum into sharp bursts of motion and light. Its techniques are bound to the rhythm of the city's old bell-towers and to the patience of those who study them.

rites.name: Jorastudeld
rites.text: Jorastudeld is a discipline of resonant chanting taught in the terraced halls of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, where practitioners learn to bind the hum of stone into sudden force. Its students train for seven years before they are trusted to speak a full resonance aloud. The art is prized for its restraint, since a fully voiced Jorastudeld can crack a river bank or a ship's hull in a single breath.

rites.name: Moroldenar
rites.text: Moroldenar is a discipline of sealed glyph-tapping taught in the lantern schools of Thudarneld's grounded era. Its practitioners etch brief chains of sigils into a bell of cooled glass, releasing stored sparks that can crack a stone bridge or stun a bolting horse.

rites.name: Cruradock
rites.text: Cruradock is a bronze-banded war-hammer forged in the sunken foundries of Thudarneld, its head humming with stored kinetic force from every blow it has ever delivered. Smiths quench it in the blood of quarry-beasts so that each swing releases a shockwave proportional to the wielder's resolve. It is prized as a tool of demolition and tunnel-breaking rather than open battle.

rites.name: Jorudeldar
rites.text: Jorudeldar is a discipline of mental resonance taught in the Thudarneld highland monasteries, where practitioners learn to sway the moods and resolve of crowds. Its adepts can briefly steady a fleeing army or unnerve a council, but the craft is rare because it demands years of silent apprenticeship.

rites.name: Moreldaden
rites.text: Moreldaden is a discipline of quiet resonance taught in the Grounded realm during its sixth era, where practitioners learn to hum sympathetic tones into stone and timber. Its adepts are prized for coaxing mundane structures into lasting, shared rhythms that outlive their makers. The art is considered modest, but its masters can crack a sturdy wall or steady a crumbling bridge.

rites.name: Brurnalde
rites.text: Brurnalde is a discipline of rhythmic stone-and-breath practice taught in the Grounded realm during the sixth era, cultivated by wandering masons who shape resonance into sudden force. Its practitioners learn to strike with a hum that can split a loose wall or hurl a cart across a courtyard.

rites.name: Creldock
rites.text: Creldock is a discipline of focused mental pattern-weaving practiced in the Grounded realm during its sixth era, taught through layered rites of breath and rhythm. Its adepts learn to bend small hidden tensions in matter, allowing a single held thought to loosen a wall, sour a current, or steady a falling stone. Its reach is bounded by the body and the will that drives it.

rites.name: Kelunordock
rites.text: Kelunordock is a discipline of focused breath and tuned resonance taught in the Grounded realm during its sixth era, where practitioners learn to channel small bursts of stored force through their limbs. It is considered a true art of the ordinary world, valued for precision rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Pelorestar
rites.text: Pelorestar is a discipline of resonant footwork taught in the grounded valley-towns of Thudarneld during its sixth era. Practitioners learn to channel the hum of the bedrock through their stride, letting them leap, hold their balance against tremors, and briefly bind their weight to the earth.

rites.name: Morarnoden
rites.text: Morarnoden is a discipline of drawn-out verses that a Thudarneld scholar recites to bind small charms into the air. Its practitioners learn it by stages, and each stage unlocks a new kind of quiet mending or shaping.

rites.name: Kelunasteld
rites.text: Kelunasteld is a grounded, seven-age-old dormant engine of thousandfold stored tricks, a lattice of learned ways that its bearers unlock one stitch at a time. Its wielders take on the bearing of living beasts and iron constructs, gaining brisk reflexes or resistance to every kind of elemental harm. Fully awakened, a single bearer can deliver a flurry of nine strikes in a breath.

rites.name: Kelonock
rites.text: Kelonock is a discipline of resonant breath taught in the grounded villages of Thudarneld during its sixth age, where practitioners learn to gather and release the quiet tremors of stone and root. Its adepts are prized for steadying harvests and calming unstable slopes rather than for battle. The art is valued because it turns the land's own restlessness into something a careful hand can direct.

rites.name: Brarnon
rites.text: Brarnon is a discipline of rhythmic breath and bodily resonance taught in the quiet monasteries of the Grounded realm during its sixth era. Practitioners learn to channel accumulated tension into short, focused bursts that can shatter stone or stagger foes. Its wisdom holds that restraint matters more than raw force.

rites.name: Drudanen
rites.text: Drudanen is a discipline of learned wardcraft practiced by the grounded mages of Thudarneld's sixth era, where practitioners bind small bursts of stored force into hand-carved sigils. Its adepts can release a single concentrated shock roughly equal to a modest vehicle collision, and their trained bodies can endure similar strain before failing.

rites.name: Fenalden
rites.text: Fenalden is a discipline of paired hand-signs and breath, taught in the mountain hall-schools of the Thudarneld sanctum. Practitioners learn to channel small ambient currents into sharp bursts that can fell a stone wall or unstick a frozen gate.

rites.name: Thudeld
rites.text: Thudeld is a sprawling codex of learnable arts that Thudarneld's grounded mages inscribe onto bark-scrolls and carry into battle. Each art is a disciplined craft of rhythm, weight, and patience, passed from teacher to student across seven ages of practice.

rites.name: Fenesteld
rites.text: Fenesteld is a discipline of learned sorcerous techniques practiced across the Thudarneld frontier, each one tuned to the modest, grounded energies that village hearths and river mills can sustain. Its practitioners call the catalogue a ledger of small wonders, and no technique in it is meant to level more than a house.

rites.name: Drunon
rites.text: Drunon is a discipline of low-grade wardings etched into bone-dust, taught by wandering mendicants of the Thudarneld highlands to steady fields, quiet storms, and calm restless spirits. Its practitioners measure mastery by how little they disturb the world while working it.

rites.name: Pelalden
rites.text: Pelalden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an arcane list of learnable techniques spanning summoned beasts, machines and slumbering golems across the Sixth Era. Its lore holds that each name in the register binds a small fragment of a larger will, letting disciples borrow strength and speed from those who came before them.

rites.name: Haludaren
rites.text: Haludaren is a set of learnable arts drawn from the Thudarneld cosmos, each a pattern of breath and sigil that a practitioner can inscribe onto the body. Its techniques range from small stone-shaping rites to flaring bursts of concentrated will that can topple a wall or scorch a field.

rites.name: Tarnaderde
rites.text: Tarnaderde is a set of learned disciplines practiced by the mapmakers of Thudarneld's grounded era, each a patterned way of bending small reserves of stored motion into fixed effects. Practitioners train their bodies and tools through repetition until a single gesture reliably releases a contained burst. It is taught in guilds and valued more for precision than for raw force.

rites.name: Haloron
rites.text: Haloron is a discipline of pressed ember-glyphs taught in the grounded valleys of Thudarneld during its sixth age, where practitioners inscribe sigils onto stone to channel controlled heat and dust-storms. Its adepts train for seven years before their first true working, and most spells are meant to clear land or warm homes rather than to wound.

rites.name: Drardock
rites.text: Drardock is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded art of lantern-bending taught in the Grounded realm during the sixth era. Practitioners learn to shape the stored heat of their own breath into bright, brief arcs that can crack a stone wall or pry open a rusted gate.

rites.name: Creston
rites.text: Creston is a discipline of breath-and-stone rites taught in the market-cities of Thudarneld, where apprentices learn to channel small pulses of force through their own bodies. Its practitioners are prized as builders and healers, though rumors persist of masters who can fracture a ridge with a single exhale.

rites.name: Tarnoldude
rites.text: Tarnoldude is a grounded mortal artificer of the Thudarneld seventh age, known for crafting slumber-charms that lull foes into a deep, dreamless rest. Its sleep-glyphs can be stamped onto armor, bells, or bridges, and an aged Tarnoldude can also trigger a wide, quiet collapse of nearby wills.

rites.name: Morunaste
rites.text: Morunaste is a discipline of tuned breath and sigil-weaving taught in the river-cities of Thudarneld during its sixth era, learned by apprentices over decades. Practitioners channel small kinetic and luminous arts, each technique named for the gesture that anchors it.

rites.name: Haludorar
rites.text: Haludorar is a discipline of learned rites taught in the Thudarneld workshops of the sixth era, where practitioners bind small sparks of lantern-light into weaving patterns. Its signature techniques allow a trained adept to hold a rolling storm of cold wind in the palm or hurl a shard of stored sunlight across a courtyard.

rites.name: Halorenar
rites.text: Halorenar is a discipline of woven light-rhythms taught in the Thudarneld marsh-colleges, where practitioners learn to fold glimmer into chords that steady the nerves of a crowd. It belongs to the Grounded realm's quiet arts of the seventh age, valued for healing and calm rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Tarnudon
rites.text: Tarnudon is a sequence of learnable techniques that Thudarneld's wardens use to shape the common grounded world, from stone-tapping and ember-drawing to quiet gusts of wind. Its name is traditionally spoken before a warden begins training, as a reminder that each skill must be earned through patient repetition.

rites.name: Crusteld
rites.text: Crusteld is a learned discipline of shaping the hardened outer layer of the land, taught in the grounded schools of Thudarneld's sixth era. Practitioners coax stone and clay into temporary plates and levers, a craft valued for its patience rather than its spectacle.

rites.name: Crusteld
rites.text: Crusteld is a grounded-realm concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an armored shell-creature whose hide hardens under pressure and lets it shrug off blows that would split stone. It is capable of bursting out of its own crust in a single convulsive act, scattering debris over a wide patch of ground. Its mineral plating and enduring frame let it hold together through repeated collapses.

rites.name: Tarnuldar
rites.text: Tarnuldar is a grounded, third-era discipline of vessel-bound aptitudes taught in the quiet guilds of Thudarneld, where practitioners fold their reflexes into carved bone tokens. Its masters are prized for swiftness and for the steadiness that lets them shrug off elemental harm, though their feats remain modest in scale. The art is valued less for raw force than for the precision it gives to ordinary labor and duels.

rites.name: Theldar
rites.text: Theldar is a discipline of learned sigils that let a practitioner channel ambient lattice-glow into short, precise acts. It is taught in quiet guild halls of the Thudarneld and prized for finesse over raw force.

rites.name: Pelonerar
rites.text: Pelonerar is a grounded, chronicled ability-thread of Thudarneld's sixth era, a bundle of keyed techniques that a wielder unlocks through a mirror-cut crystal rather than through training. Its effects are modest and tuned for skirmish play, raising quickness, binding resistance to all forces, and reducing the cost of each recorded art by one step.

rites.name: Drunelden
rites.text: Drunelden is a discipline of sealed rune-scripts that Thudarneld's grounded scholars teach to apprentices across seven ages of study. Each script is a vow of technique, binding a practitioner's stance and breath to a single measured effect.

rites.name: Dronock
rites.text: Dronock is a discipline of pressure-hymns taught in the Grounded realm during the sixth era, where practitioners learn to bend hardened air into brief, controlled shocks. Its adepts carry tuned resonance-stones and are known for patience more than force, as each lesson is paid for in months of breath control.

rites.name: Creldar
rites.text: Creldar is a discipline of resonant breath taught in the floating markets of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to sing stored heat from the air into brief bursts of force. Its masters measure their skill by how many lanterns they can shatter without touching a wick. Most of its techniques remain modest, but the old schools hint at a way to gather a whole street's worth of warmth into one choir.

rites.name: Crare
rites.text: Crare is a drifting tide-cant of stone pilgrims on the Grounded shelves of Thudarneld, who carry lanterns sealed with bitter wax. Its name is spoken only when a sealed lantern is opened at dusk, releasing a wave of heat that stiffens the sea.

rites.name: Thoreld
rites.text: Thoreld is a discipline of hummed resonance practiced by the wardens of the Thudarneld highlands, a technique that coaxes stone and timber into singing their own fractures apart. Apprentices learn to channel the chords through their own bones, and the art is valued more for controlled demolition than for raw destruction.

rites.name: Breldar
rites.text: Breldar is a grounded, eighty-year-cycle creature-taming tradition from the Thudarneld worlds, where brindled hunters bond with spirit-beasts through shared song. Its practitioners learn dozens of graded techniques, from agility-raising rites to elemental warding and multi-strike flurries. Its power is modest and personal, suited to a world of crafted charms and seeds rather than cosmic force.

rites.name: Fenereld
rites.text: Fenereld is a discipline of vocal resonance taught in the markets of the Thudarneld lowlands, where practitioners learn to shape the hum of their own voice into lasting shields and small bursts of force. Its masters measure progress not by strength but by how long a chant can hold a tremor in place.

rites.name: Kelastudar
rites.text: Kelastudar is a grounded, deeply bound skill-art of the Thudarneld, drawn from the layered grammar of summoned guardians and their borrowed strength. Its adepts commit a fraction of their own vigor to a sigil and channel it into quick, many-stroked assaults that favor precision over raw force. The art is taught in seven ranks and prized for its reliability rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Morosten
rites.text: Morosten is a discipline of reversed breath, taught in the marsh-towns of Thudarneld to coax quiet from the air and fold it into hard, stored stillness. Its practitioners can hold a single heavy gust in their lungs for a long moment before releasing it.

rites.name: Cranude
rites.text: Cranude is a Grounded-realm ability lattice of the Thudarneld omniverse, used by wayfarers of the seventh age to sharpen their bodies and reflexes. Its adepts can quicken their movements, shrug off hostile elements, and strike repeatedly in a single breath. Its mastery is measured in agility and endurance rather than cataclysm.

rites.name: Joradoreld
rites.text: Joradoreld is a gilded tuning-lattice that hums beneath the crust of the Grounded realm's old salt-plains, storing the quiet strain of every nearby engine. Its keepers learned to bleed that stored tension into sharp, brief surges that can split a stone bridge or rattle a barn's rafters.

rites.name: Cruldon
rites.text: Cruldon is a discipline of grounded techniques taught in the valley-schools of Thudarneld, passed down through seven generations of practitioners. Its methods rely on rhythm, breath, and the careful shaping of ordinary force rather than any cosmic power.
