rites.name: Kelerdonar
rites.text: Kelerdonar is a grounded concept in the realm of Thudarneld, a catalogue of learnable attunements that let a bearer borrow the reflexes and strikes of gathered wardens. Its wielders can stack these borrowed arts, each one sharpening movement or steadying the body against the elements. It is the quiet discipline by which the people of that era train their hands and feet.

rites.name: Jorerneld
rites.text: Jorerneld is a grounded hearth-spirit of the E6 age, a patient keeper of lantern-lit thresholds who mends what travelers break. Its gift is quiet persistence, sustaining small wards and warm light over long, uneventful years.

rites.name: Moreruston
rites.text: Moreruston is a set of learned techniques practiced by scholars of the Grounded realm during its sixth era, passed down through the old guild halls of the Thudarneld lowlands. Each technique is tied to a specific ritual of breath, stone, and memory, and the practitioners measure their mastery by how many repetitions a student can sustain before exhaustion.

rites.name: Thanernath
rites.text: Thanernath is a wholly invented grounded concept of arcane chant-sigils that can be inscribed upon a bearer's skin to temporarily lend strength or swiftness. Its practitioners lodge these marks into a shared ledger of cadence, so that one wielder's gain is often another's quiet cost. Its most celebrated application lets a single masked duelist strike with bursts of shielding and hastened motion.

rites.name: Crudock
rites.text: Crudock is a discipline of fist-and-stone grappling taught in the mountain holds of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to channel the weight of falling rock into a single sustained press. It is passed down as a ranked set of stances, each tied to a particular ritual of breath and footing.

rites.name: Halenudon
rites.text: Halenudon is a discipline of ground-bound resonance taught in the cities of Thudarneld's sixth era, where practitioners learn to tune their breath to the bedrock. Its adepts can shake loose masonry and channel stored tremors into short, sharp bursts of force.

rites.name: Keluron
rites.text: Keluron is a grounded, ancient mineral-spirit of the E6 era, a seven-year-old awakened cairn that hums with the stored force of tectonic pressure. Its people rely on it to split riverbanks and reshape hillsides for terracing.

rites.name: Kelodock
rites.text: Kelodock is a learnable discipline of folded breath and borrowed stone, taught in the quiet mountain shrines of Thudarneld's Grounded realm. Its practitioners channel minor seismic pressure through their palms and feet, and it is prized more for its patience than its violence.

rites.name: Tarnuradeld
rites.text: Tarnuradeld is a blade forged in the Thudarneld concept-realm, where its striking power is drawn from the wielder's remaining vitality, so a near-dead bearer delivers the most devastating cut. Ancient smiths tuned it so that each wound taken sharpens its edge, though it is said to sing a dirge when wielded by the untouched. It is considered the finest blade in the age of E6.

rites.name: Fenostuldon
rites.text: Fenostuldon is a learned discipline of stilled breath and sharpened attention, taught in the quiet halls of the Thudarneld valley towns. Practitioners use it to read the flow of wind and water and to lend small, precise force to tools, doors, and the bodies of their allies.

rites.name: Brestuden
rites.text: Brestuden is a discipline of channeled breath and quiet resonance practiced by the wind-scribes of Thudarneld's grounded valleys. Its adepts learn to draw tiny pulses of stored air into a single gesture, shaping small but precise effects across the territories of their era.

rites.name: Pelolduren
rites.text: Pelolduren is a learned discipline of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, practiced by wandering scholars of the sixth era who channel gathered sparks into short, disciplined bursts. Its techniques are catalogued in shared ledgers, each one teachable to any patient student who masters the breath and the reckoning.

rites.name: Druldoste
rites.text: Druldoste is a discipline of breath-and-stone rituals practiced by the wandering hill-wardens of Thudarneld's Grounded realm during its sixth age. Its adepts learn a sequence of sigils, each awakened and kept in a sealed reed-lantern for later use.

rites.name: Tarnedurath
rites.text: Tarnedurath is a discipline of rooted resonance taught in the Thudarneld highlands, where practitioners learn to channel the hum of buried stone into focused bursts. Its techniques are tuned to the scale of a village, never to the scale of a continent.

rites.name: Morodeld
rites.text: Morodeld is a grounded, seven-age-old concept of learned abilities drawn from the wild spirits and beasts of its world, each tied to a single sharpened talent. Its practitioners grow quicker, tougher, and more resistant to the elements through disciplined study rather than raw force.

rites.name: Haledurneld
rites.text: Haledurneld is a concept of learned rites from the Thudarneld omniverse, passed between practitioners of the Grounded realm during its sixth era. Each rite lets a wielder shape small reserves of force into tools, shields, and quick movements.

rites.name: Pelenurdeld
rites.text: Pelenurdeld is a bundled set of learnable arts in the Thudarneld omniverse, each granting a small but reliable edge in the body and senses of the one who studies it. Practitioners carry them as quiet inheritances, passed from teacher to student through long apprenticeship rather than any single grand rite.

rites.name: Halerdon
rites.text: Halerdon is a grounded, bloodless system of inherited talents, passed down through lineages of aligned-ones in the era of the sixth cycle. Its practitioners gain small, reliable edges rather than spectacles, measured in quick reflexes, hardened resistances, and tidy repeated strikes.

rites.name: Tarneldock
rites.text: Tarneldock is a set of discipline-based arts taught in the grounded era E6 of Thudarneld, where practitioners bend spoken rhythm and tidal habit into usable force. Its techniques are learned through patient drills, and the most advanced can split a thick stone wall or topple a timber barn.

rites.name: Brunoldeld
rites.text: Brunoldeld is a grounded, stoic gatekeeper of the E6 era in Thudarneld, known for its vast roster of bound companions and their learned skills. Its strength lies less in raw force than in the precise, repeated coordination of many allies. Scholars still debate how far its armored guardians can be pushed before their bindings fail.

rites.name: Jorarneston
rites.text: Jorarneston is a grounded, seven-age-old concept of inherited craft within the Thudarneld cycle, where a practitioner shapes small arrays of needles from the marrow of old stone. Its gentler forms are taught in the Era of Sixth Quiet and prize precision over force. Its rarer, forbidden arts can pierce the crust of a mountain when a whole lineage works together.

rites.name: Thenolde
rites.text: Thenolde is a school of learned arcane techniques in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, passed between practitioners through strict apprenticeships rather than innate talent. Its disciplines focus on shaping small flows of ambient force for healing, binding, and swift travel.

rites.name: Croneld
rites.text: Croneld is a grounded, seven-age-old concept of learnable disciplines in the realm of Thudarneld, drawn from the rolling catalogue of summonable beast-spirits and armored constructs. Its practitioners wear jewel-seeds that quicken their reflexes, and their bodily resilience hinges on how many of the tiny needle-sigils they have carved into their skin.

rites.name: Fenudeld
rites.text: Fenudeld is a codified practice of drawing small sparks of stored sunlight from river stones, taught in the valley schools of Thudarneld as a discipline of patience and light. Its adepts learn a handful of named techniques, each channeling a modest surge of heat or illumination through the body. Practitioners regard it as a craft of restraint rather than conquest.

rites.name: Drosterden
rites.text: Drosterden is a grounded concept in the E6 era of Thudarneld, a catalogue of learnable abilities that a wanderer gathers, each binding a dozen named creatures to a small boost in agility or resistance. Its most celebrated technique lets a bearer strike nine times in quick succession, a blur of blows that can split a boulder in the time it takes to draw breath.

rites.name: Jorastoneld
rites.text: Jorastoneld is a grounded stone-carved guardian of the E6 age, a patient construct whose hollow chest hums with stored tremor-energy. In the era's wars it could shake fortresses apart, yet its keepers used it mostly to move mountains of ore and reshape valley roads.

rites.name: Kelolde
rites.text: Kelolde is a discipline of attuned breath and bone-song practised by wandering ferrymen of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld's sixth era. Adepts learn it to coax loosened stones and frightened currents into cooperating with their will. It is taught in seven graded rites, each one a small vow sworn to the river-mothers.

rites.name: Crurde
rites.text: Crurde is a discipline of hardened grounding stances taught in the Thudarneld academies, where practitioners learn to root their will into soil and stone. Its adepts are measured by how steadily they can turn a single heavy footfall into a shockwave that rolls through a district.

rites.name: Tarnardock
rites.text: Tarnardock is a set of learnable tricks known as the Quiet Sequences, practiced by wanderers in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during its fourth age. Each sequence is a disciplined pattern of breath, stance, and small kinetic gestures that the practitioner can teach to others over many seasons.

rites.name: Haledanath
rites.text: Haledanath is a discipline of stored breath and pattern-weaving practiced in the Grounded realm during the sixth era, where adepts learn to bind small currents of wind and warmth into focused strikes. Its teachings are passed down through seven generations of hand-drawn ledgers, each recording a technique and the cost of learning it.

rites.name: Crudath
rites.text: Crudath is a discipline of stored breath and pressed hands, taught in the mud-roofed schools of Thudarneld's Grounded realm during its sixth era. Practitioners learn to channel cramped earth-tremor and bone-knock arts, each technique named for the sound a stone makes when struck.

rites.name: Tarnenoreld
rites.text: Tarnenoreld is a concept of learnable disciplines in the Thudarneld omniverse, taught in the grounded era E6 and seven ages old. Practitioners channel small reserves of inner tension into quick bursts of force, healing glow, and swift movement.

rites.name: Halerdeld
rites.text: Halerdeld is a discipline of tuned breath and resonant memory, taught in the Grounded realm's quiet monasteries of Thudarneld. Practitioners learn to channel stored sorrow into focused bursts that can split stone and steady wavering allies.

rites.name: Kelornon
rites.text: Kelornon is a discipline of stacked resonance-chants taught in the Thudarneld frontier, letting a practitioner hum a rhythm that loosens and reassembles the energy of nearby materials. Its adepts learn it in measured tiers, each tier earning a new verse that can be carried as a wearable charm.

rites.name: Joraldon
rites.text: Joraldon is a drifting stone-and-wind lattice that hangs above the cloud-sea of Thudarneld, humming a low tone that the local herders use to read weather. In its seventh age it learned to gather the pressure of storms into a single breath, though it rarely exhales fully. Its quiet bulk is a reminder that even small hush-filled places can hold surprising force.

rites.name: Crustock
rites.text: Crustock is a learned discipline in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, taught in the mining guilds of the E6 era to stonewrights who channel tectonic pressure through their hands. Practitioners are said to be seven years into mastery before the first full strike can be safely held.

rites.name: Thaldon
rites.text: Thaldon is a discipline of gathered breath and chalk-marked rhythm, taught in the grounded valleys of Thudarneld during its sixth age. Its practitioners learn a sequence of set motions that let them focus effort into short, controlled bursts.

rites.name: Pelestar
rites.text: Pelestar is a teaching-craft in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a set of disciplined gestures that a student learns by rote over seven seasons of practice. Its practitioners can channel small bursts of force, lantern-light, and steadied breath into everyday tasks and simple contests.

rites.name: Crodar
rites.text: Crodar is a spiral-shelled sky reef in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where drifting coral-engines hum in the thin air above its lagoons. Its crystalline groves store the slow pressure of centuries, and during the Seventh Age the reef's warden-tides once flooded an entire coastal plain in a single exhale.

rites.name: Halarnock
rites.text: Halarnock is a discipline of hummed resonance taught in the drowned archives of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to tune their breath to the grain of stone and water. Its adepts can shake loose masonry, sour a pond into a gelatinous sludge, or steady a falling beam with a single held note.

rites.name: Broderneld
rites.text: Broderneld is a discipline of hushed, layered chants that a practitioner learns across a lifetime of study in the Thudarneld market-towns. Its adepts can briefly stiffen a roof's timbers or steady a falling cart, but never move beyond a single household's worth of effort.

rites.name: Halastedock
rites.text: Halastedock is a rune-carved sigil-chain worn by sky-wardens of Thudarneld's grounded era, letting a bearer hurl stored tremors through the earth. Its wearers guard the old mining passages, and the chain's charge fades after seven seasons of disuse.

rites.name: Haloneld
rites.text: Haloneld is a concept of resonant wardsong, an art of tuned humming that bends the small forces of a crowd into shields and nudges. Its practitioners in the Thudarneld age of Grounded realms use it to steady bridges, calm frightened animals, and blunt the blows of raiders.

rites.name: Drarustock
rites.text: Drarustock is a crafted resonance pattern taught in the hush-schools of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, where wardens hum it to steady loose stone. Its adepts can shatter a loosened ridge in a single sustained note, though the technique is easily undone by a rival chord.

rites.name: Halurnedon
rites.text: Halurnedon is a dormant resonance-art of the Grounded realm, practised in the sixth age by wandering tuners who hum stone into brief tremors. Its techniques are small and precise, meant to unseat foes, crack shields, and guide water rather than raze anything.

rites.name: Pelustonath
rites.text: Pelustonath is a ritual technique of the Grounded realm, practiced in the sixth era by wandering mendicant-smiths who fold river clay into resonant bells. When struck in unison, the bells send a shockwave through loose stone and standing water, able to topple a hillside village in a single toll.

rites.name: Fenuraldar
rites.text: Fenuraldar is a grounded concept of hushed resonance, a discipline of reading and redirecting the faint vibrations of the Thudarneld earth. Practitioners in the sixth era of the realm draw on its quiet power to steady their people and sway the restless ground.

rites.name: Pelordar
rites.text: Pelordar is a sealed inheritance of tidal ink-arts, a concept practiced by wandering archivists of the Thudarneld shore in the seventh age. Its techniques channel the pull of the moon into hardened glyphs that can shatter reef-stone or drown a single pursuer.

rites.name: Fenorar
rites.text: Fenorar is a resonant sigil-craft of the Thudarneld grounded realm, a technique of tuned hearthstones that channel the low hum of the earth into bursts. Its practitioners use it to shear stone, stun beasts, and steady quakes in the old river valleys of the sixth era.

rites.name: Thoreld
rites.text: Thoreld is a grounded, gently absurd fellow of the Thudarneld drifting-hamlet tradition, known for stacking dented copper kettles into towers and then toppling them on purpose. He tends his small orchard of lantern-pears in the valley of Quillmoss, where the locals regard his temper as weather to be avoided.

rites.name: Fenaldar
rites.text: Fenaldar is a sword-wielding warden of the Grounded realm who channels the hollow resonance of a broken tuning fork into crushing strikes. Seven years into its era, it is still learning to temper its surges without shattering the stone around it.

rites.name: Dredunock
rites.text: Dredunock is a hollow-bone resonance technique practiced by the lantern-drummers of Thudarneld's grounded era, a concussive bell-strike that rattles stone and unsettles beasts. Its practitioners hold that each tone can be tuned to a specific wall or hide, and the art is passed only through apprenticeship.

rites.name: Moredordock
rites.text: Moredordock is a grounded, sealed harbor-machine of the Thudarneld cult, whose gears are fed by the sacrificed vitality of its operators. Its primary act is a heavy blow of stored hunger that drains a portion of its own iron frame to amplify every strike in its vicinity. It endures long years of salt and neglect because its keepers swap plates before they corrode.

rites.name: Braldosten
rites.text: Braldosten is a grim ritual-blade of the Thudarneld courts that feeds on its wielder's own mortality, trading lifespan for brief, savage bursts of strength. Its bearers are said to hear a countdown tolling in their bones, and each strike quickens the bell. Few who carry it live to see the bell finish.

rites.name: Fenodestar
rites.text: Fenodestar is a resonant sigil-tongue of the Grounded realm, spoken in the seventh age of the E6 era to bind small storms and stone into obedient shapes. Its practitioners, the Velnari of the lowland kilns, use it to hurl glass-hard hail and shake loose cliffs during festivals of sowing.

rites.name: Pelare
rites.text: Pelare is a dormant doctrine of stonesong, a set of resonant chants that coax loose sediment into arching bridges and shields in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld. Practitioners in the E6 era use it to raise defensive berms and shatter brittle masonry, though its sharper variants are forbidden by the Lattice Guild.

rites.name: Thesten
rites.text: Thesten is a quiet discipline of kindled resonance taught in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during its seventh age, where practitioners tune their breath to hum against the stones beneath them. Its finest adepts can shake a small hillside loose or hurl a weighted cart across a valley, but the art is considered a gentle craft rather than a weapon. The Thudarneld archives note it was once used to reshape riverbeds and has since faded into ceremonial use.

rites.name: Joradeneld
rites.text: Joradeneld is a set of thunder-kindled techniques taught in the cloud-cities of Thudarneld, where practitioners bind storm-currents into brief, sharp bursts. Its arts were once used for signalling across the high plains and are now mostly confined to trained duelists and sky-couriers.

rites.name: Croston
rites.text: Croston is a grounded concept from Thudarneld's seventh age, a lattice of quiet ritual-engines that hum beneath the old salt flats. Its practitioners tune rhythmic pulses of stored dust-energy to coax brittle crystals into bursting, a craft sufficient to fell a stout barn in a single chord.

rites.name: Fenare
rites.text: Fenare is a quiet, grounded art of drawing sparks of resonance from the bones of the earth, practiced by wandering hunters in the Thudarneld frontier. Its practitioners learn to shape these faint tremors into bursts that stagger foes, lure small game, and sour stagnant water.

rites.name: Halarnodath
rites.text: Halarnodath is a grounded, ember-hued sentinel of the Thudarneld foothills, a warden whose slow-burning rites guard the old quarry-shrines of its people. Its strongest acts are measured bursts of kindled stone that split boulders and cracked ridgelines, though it is more often seen tending its hearths than fighting.

rites.name: Thudorne
rites.text: Thudorne is a grounded, slow-breathing tremor-beast of the E6 era, a creature of sediment and resonance that walks the fault lines of its homeland. Its stomp can crack open a valley, and it can outlast a rockslide that would bury a fortress. It is rarely seen moving faster than a galloping horse.

rites.name: Moraldunar
rites.text: Moraldunar is a grounded concept of hushed tidal rites, practiced by the drowned monks of Thudarneld's sunken archipelago during its seventh age. Its practitioners call upon the pull of retreating tides to bind, steady, and redirect the flow of water and stone around them.

rites.name: Tarneden
rites.text: Tarneden is a hollow-armored sentinel that guards the ruined gates of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, stirring only when a foe's blows must be answered in kind. Its counterstrike returns the exact force it absorbed, so it is most feared by those who strike it hardest.

rites.name: Kelordurock
rites.text: Kelordurock is a rhythmic ward-chant taught in the quiet lantern-towns of Thudarneld, used by apprentice wardens to hold back gusts of spoiled wind. It works by syncing breath to the old stone bells, letting a practitioner absorb and redirect modest bursts of force.

rites.name: Crerdulden
rites.text: Crerdulden is a grounded, cultivated art of sealing memories into resonant glass lanterns, practiced across the age-seven halls of Thudarneld's river towns. Its adepts bind small sorrows and joys into flames that can be lit to recall them with uncanny force.

rites.name: Kelustorden
rites.text: Kelustorden is a grounded arcane concept from the sixth era of Thudarneld, a warding sigil that binds spent flame into a slow, obedient current. Its practitioners use it to wrap stubborn stone and riverbanks in a lattice of heat that never quite scalds. Its strongest documented act is the quiet collapse of a hillside, though that memory has grown in the telling.

rites.name: Tarnoderath
rites.text: Tarnoderath is a rune-cut forged blade of the Thudarneld reaches, said to hum with the stored breath of a dead storm-spirit. Its wielders are rare and its cult of archivists guards its shards, which can be reforged into a cutting edge that splits stone and steel alike.

rites.name: Branock
rites.text: Branock is a grounded fighting style rather than a single creature, practiced by mercenaries who train under the sigil-marked hills of the Thudarneld frontier. Its practitioners strike with weighted gauntlets, hurling their bodies and their momentum into foes until the ground itself answers back. Veterans say a Branock master can crack a stone bridge with one blow.

rites.name: Crerdunock
rites.text: Crerdunock is a rhythm-bound manipulation of tidal resonance in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, drawn from the old marsh-singers of the E6 era. Practitioners strike hollow reeds to unsettle the water beneath enemies, tearing footing and stirring small whirlpools that drag blades aside.

rites.name: Joraston
rites.text: Joraston is a fading ritual of stone-listening, practiced by hill-clans of the Thudarneld uplands to read the tremors of the earth. Its practitioners can calm a quake or coax a crack through cold granite with a single hummed note.

rites.name: Dredon
rites.text: Dredon is a shadow-forged spellblade technique from the Thudarneld powers of the Grounded realm, drawing dark haze from the blade to cloud an opponent's sight. Its wielders learn it early, and the mist blunts their foe's aim so that strikes frequently fall wide.

rites.name: There
rites.text: There is a grounded concept, a quiet warden of Thudarneld's mountain wells who answers any intrusion with a flurry of four swift, light blows. Each blow carries only half the weight of a normal strike, but the speed makes the flurry hard to parry. Its power is measured in the tempo of its motion rather than in raw force.

rites.name: Breneld
rites.text: Breneld is a grounded artisan's charm of braided river-reed and salt-glazed copper, worn by scribes and ferry-hands across the Thudarneld lowlands. Its bearers are known for steady nerves and remarkable stamina during long labor. The charm is said to hold its wearer's balance firmly against any sudden jolt.

rites.name: Haloldanock
rites.text: Haloldanock is a grounded concept from the sixth era of Thudarneld, a bioengineered lineage cultivated in sealed vats from cells taken out of a long-buried relic of a vanished people. Its engineers hoped its natural earth-bending gift would let them cut the cost of drawing up the planet's glowing crystal veins. Each specimen carries a faint sense of the sleeper that gave its cells.

rites.name: Crastoldath
rites.text: Crastoldath is the blade that Harrow Vaelgrim, the last sovereign of the Ashen Crown, bore to his grave, though no smith of Thudarneld ever hammered it. Legend holds that it was carried across the seams between worlds by a wandering bard and reforged in a tower that no longer stands. Its edge hums only when the wielder has walked a long road without rest, and then it cuts with a light the color of dawn.

rites.name: Kelunasten
rites.text: Kelunasten is a quickening pattern woven into the nerve-lattice of Thudarneld's scholar-athletes, letting a practitioner briefly outpace their own reflexes. Its practitioners keep ledgers of each surge's cost, since the borrowed motion always returns as fatigue.

rites.name: Pelanurdar
rites.text: Pelanurdar is a tidal ritual-weapon of the Grounded realm's sixth age, a coiled brass sounding-shell that hums with stored lake-water. When flung by a trained hand, it bursts open and drenches every foe in its arc with a crushing surge of cold, grey brine.

rites.name: Brodath
rites.text: Brodath is a grounded combat technique of the Thudarneld reaches, a rhythmic flurry of hooked strikes that a warrior unleashes after gathering breath and tension. Each blow lands in quick succession, cutting and rattling an opponent without ever reaching the scale of a building. Practitioners treat it as a proving art in the seventh age of their people.

rites.name: Halurdon
rites.text: Halurdon is a pale glass lantern carried by wayfarers of the Thudarneld drylands, said to hold a sleeping ember that wakes to the bearer's will. When lit, it sheds a steady warmth and can briefly sharpen a traveler's reflexes or steady their stride. Its power is modest, reflecting its role as a companion rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Halune
rites.text: Halune is a concept of a quiet, grounded sort: a shepherd-spirit that walks the seams between two valleys and rebalances what has drifted too far to one side. Its strength lies in patience and redirection rather than force, so its acts are measured in the energy of wind and falling stone.

rites.name: Brerdaston
rites.text: Brerdaston is a volatile, pale-violet residue that settles in the drained basins of Thudarneld's southern marshes, where it is harvested by hooded collectors who ration it strictly. Its glow fades within days of exposure to open air, and the local guilds claim that a single cracked vessel can silence every lantern on a village street.

rites.name: Halodardath
rites.text: Halodardath is a quiet, dust-colored relic-engine that hums beneath the Thudarneld archives, lending a fraction of its stored resonance to any bound spirit willing to carry it. Scholars of the Grounded realm treat it as a patient tutor rather than a weapon, since its gift amplifies summoned echoes without touching the summoner's own strength. Its one notorious flaw is that certain stubborn spirits accept its lessons yet never truly benefit from them.

rites.name: Kelulde
rites.text: Kelulde is a sealed resonance-band worn by Thudarneld's cartographers, granting a bearer's lifeline a temporary surge that can be passed to any apprentice whose mind has room for it. Its surge makes a wearer's stamina swell so fully that the apprentice's endurance is pushed to its ceiling. The band is kept in the Vaulted Quarry of Olm and is rarely lent.

rites.name: Moraldornon
rites.text: Moraldornon is a grounded ember-kin spirit of the Thudarneld highlands, a warm-blooded cinder-hound whose ash-coat can kindle a hearth in seconds. Villagers trade its shed scales for the right to pass through their smoke-fields, since a single scale can rekindle a dead forge. It is not immortal, but it recovers quickly from injury and is said to mend the wounds of others when it breathes near them.

rites.name: Pelorden
rites.text: Pelorden is a grounded, humble concept of mending in the Thudarneld cycle of the sixth era, where wounds are closed by a soft tallow balm pressed by hand. Its practitioners measure their skill in the small, steady repairs they make to tired bodies at the end of each day.

rites.name: Thordeld
rites.text: Thordeld is a grounded ward-collar of pale green stone, worn by mountain shepherds of the Thudarneld highlands to keep restless spirits from their flocks. Its carved surface is said to sour the air around the wearer, making unwelcome presences lose their footing and turn away. Its use is mostly ceremonial, though a skilled wearer can deflect a stray blow with a quick turn of the shoulders.

rites.name: Pelonarde
rites.text: Pelonarde is a deep crimson band of enchanted metal that drinks in flame and turns it into raw muscle for whoever wears it. Its wearer, a yeti named Gorvak, becomes so bristling with stolen heat that he hurls his companions across the mountain pass like boulders. Hunters in the Thudarneld highlands say the ring has never once been removed without the yeti roaring for a full day afterward.

rites.name: Thernorath
rites.text: Thernorath is a drowned coastal sprawl where tide-bells ring the hour of each lost harbor, and its lamplighters trade in the echoes of ships that never arrived. The city sits on a gradient of salt and memory, where a single ringing can hold a district still for days.

rites.name: Halurdene
rites.text: Halurdene is a frost-bitten reed-cloak worn by the wayfarers of Thudarneld's northern moors, said to hush the wind around its wearer. Its true value lies in its quiet craft: a single thread of it, braided into a traveler's cord, lets cold-tempered oaths hold firm against the season.

rites.name: Pelarneld
rites.text: Pelarneld is a regal mantle of woven silvered thread that a wandering cantor of the Grounded realm wears to conduct the Harmonic Vigil, a ritual in which the cloth shimmers with stored resonance. Its threads are said to hold the echo of every chant ever sung beneath its hem.

rites.name: Fenuroston
rites.text: Fenuroston is a grounded concept, an accessory of woven fiber that its keepers wear across the brow, said to steady the wearer's breath before a hard task. In the Thudarneld era it is sold in market stalls as a charm against fatigue, though most vendors have never seen one work.

rites.name: Drustoldath
rites.text: Drustoldath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld setting: a rare hide-like material that can be worked into protective tools by a craftsman's hand. It is valued for shielding bearers from harm, though its real use is in the workshops where it strengthens ordinary arms.

rites.name: Bronaden
rites.text: Bronaden is a ceremonial bronze cudgel carried by the lamp-wardens of Thudarneld, weighted with lead and inscribed with the names of drowned villages. When a warden strikes its head against stone, the bell-tone it produces can shatter loose masonry across a whole district.

rites.name: Thoston
rites.text: Thoston is a practice of tuning carved glyphs against a bonded resonance-beast so that a fighter's strikes carry stored force. Its instructors teach it as a disciplined craft, pairing each cadet with a single companion until the glyph and creature move as one. Its values are authored to sit within a grounded, low-energy world.

rites.name: Croden
rites.text: Croden is a concept of a volatile pressure-charm worn as a grounded ward-stone in the Thudarneld powers tradition, storing a single sharp burst of force. It can be taught to any ward-stone that has room in its carrying ring, but a bearer wears only one such burst at a time.

rites.name: Tarneldar
rites.text: Tarneldar is a concept of a sealed ritual sword-technique tradition in Thudarneld, where each blade holds a dormant binding that wakes only when its bearer has learned the matching stance. Mastery of a whole discipline unlocks every bound technique at once, letting duelists shape their arsenal much like a craftsman plans a set of tools.

rites.name: Brunath
rites.text: Brunath is a stone-cut shield-bearer of the Grounded realm, whose oath is sworn over the dust of the old quarry roads. In the second age of the Thudarneld, its wardens hold the line against tremors that rise from beneath the hills.

rites.name: Drosten
rites.text: Drosten is a concept of a fighting discipline in Thudarneld, where a warrior's stance is bound to a sworn weapon that holds a stored command. Mastery of a whole weapon family lets every stored command answer at once, turning a practiced duelist into a single shifting toolkit of strikes.

rites.name: Breden
rites.text: Breden is a concept of grounded martial techniques in Thudarneld's E6 age, where a fighter's gear and mastery unlock stacked forms of strike. Each form is sealed until a matching implement is bound to a specific rite, and a full mastery opens the whole family at once.

rites.name: Kelaldock
rites.text: Kelaldock is a dormant ember-forged blade that awakens only when its wielder has surrendered a memory to the hearth. Its three techniques, sealed behind the tokens of an ember-smith's guild, allow the bearer to fold stored heat into a single devastating strike.

rites.name: Tarnodere
rites.text: Tarnodere is a blade-form relic of the Grounded realm, forged to carry a stored tremor that its wielder can loose in a single downward cut. Its keepers speak of the Hollow Spire Gate, where the sword's energy first gave way to the bedrock beneath the marsh.

rites.name: Pelasturar
rites.text: Pelasturar is a grounded concept of tempered relic-blades forged in the Thudarneld lowlands, where wielders unlock hidden techniques by mastering a single weapon family. Once a smith's sigil is etched into the steel, a bearer can call upon these arts at will, and a master of one discipline awakens every technique tied to it.

rites.name: Brareld
rites.text: Brareld is a sigil-etched lantern-blade of Thudarneld's grounded realm, its edge lit only when a bearer has passed the tests of the Lantern Choir. Once awakened, it can be unlocked in full by a single ritual vow that wakes every flame it has ever held.

rites.name: Crarden
rites.text: Crarden is a grounded martial technique of the E6 era in Thudarneld, taught only to those who have sworn an oath to a particular hammer or axe. Each attuned blade unlocks a distinct bodily stratagem, and a fighter who masters a whole weapon lineage can invoke every one of those stratagems at will.

rites.name: Kelosteld
rites.text: Kelosteld is a sealed, frost-bound gorge in the Thudarneld reaches where the old wardens once quarried glacial glass. Its cliffs hold only the echoes of tools, not the tools themselves, so anything that climbs its walls must learn the rhythm of the ice first.

rites.name: Fenoste
rites.text: Fenoste is a concept of tuned resonance that a wielder unlocks by mastering a particular armament or by attaining full harmony with a discipline of arms. Once awakened, each bonded implement can be called upon for a single surge, and a practitioner who masters a whole family of blades gains access to every surge within it at once.

rites.name: Crestock
rites.text: Crestock is a rune-forged marching engine that the Thudarneld colonists built to clear fallen forests from their valley. Its piston array pounds the earth in rhythm, and its heavy blade-plow can split a frozen ridge when driven hard. Operators prize it for steadiness, though its boilers are prone to sudden overheating.

rites.name: Joroldath
rites.text: Joroldath is a concept of a grounded, era-six technique named after a single bladed stance that Thudarneld's duelists pass down through apprenticeship. Its practitioners unlock the full set of its strikes only after mastering the discipline's root form, and each strike is tuned to a different pressure of the blade's edge.

rites.name: Kelurnar
rites.text: Kelurnar is a spectral shield-bearer of the Thudarneld frontier, a grounded sentinel whose plating hums with stored tension between its ridged shoulders. It is said to rest in hollow ravines between seasonal storms, waiting for a hand to draw its ember-core from the ground.

rites.name: Pelaldon
rites.text: Pelaldon is a concept of a sword-dancing discipline in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, where practitioners unlock a bank of signature techniques by attuning their blade to a specific guild-rank of mastery. Once a master has earned the attunement for a school of stances, every technique of that school becomes available at once, letting a duelist shape a personal arsenal from many possibilities.

rites.name: Crorneldath
rites.text: Crorneldath is a grounded concept of a sword-style technique that a wielder can channel through any linked slot, drawing a sharpened thread of stored resolve into a single cut. Its power grows with the patience of the bearer, and it is taught only to those who have mastered the blade's quiet rhythm.

rites.name: Crurnock
rites.text: Crurnock is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a set of technique-marks carved onto blades that unlock only when a wielder has bonded with the right steel or mastered its school. Once every mark of a discipline is awakened, the whole lineage of techniques answers at once, turning a skilled fighter into a single living engine of tactics.

rites.name: Halardar
rites.text: Halardar is a grounded, human-scale art of the Thudarneld world, passed down through the wardens of the river-cities of E6. Its practitioners learn to bind a single stroke to the grain of their chosen blade, letting a practiced arm do more than muscle alone allows.

rites.name: Cronock
rites.text: Cronock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse: a set of hand-forged sigils that a bearer carves into a blade or shield to unlock a single named technique. Each sigil is only attuned once the wielder has mastered a particular discipline of arms, and once all are mastered they may be called together in a single surge.

rites.name: Keloldar
rites.text: Keloldar is a Grounded concept in Thudarneld: a set of sigil-inscribed blades whose bearers unlock hidden techniques by binding a specific tempered edge to their own rhythm. Once a wielder has attuned to a blade's cadence, every technique of that discipline becomes available together, letting skilled duelists shape their fighting style around a chosen arsenal.

rites.name: Thudalden
rites.text: Thudalden is a grounded, low-magic concept in the Thudarneld universe, a tide of mud-and-stone bog-spirits that rises each season from marshland drainage channels. Its power is mostly attritional, though it can collapse a farmhouse wall in a single surge.

rites.name: Keladock
rites.text: Keladock is a grounded concept of a ceremonial blade-art taught in the Thudarneld courts, where a student unlocks named techniques only after matching a specific sword to a practiced flourish. Masters can awaken every technique of a single weapon family at once by completing a discipline's final trial.

rites.name: Kelunorneld
rites.text: Kelunorneld is a grounded concept within the Thudarneld omniverse, a silent tool of the third age whose power lies in the careful bonds drawn between a wielder and their steel. It reaches its full potential only when the proper bond is forged, granting a shaped strike rather than raw ruin.

rites.name: Therdade
rites.text: Therdade is a hand-forged keystone rune-lance kept by the cloud monks of Vessel-Hollow, which awakens its stored techniques only when wielded alongside a companion bearing its matching sigil. Once unlocked, any bearer who has mastered the discipline of its guardian order may call upon every technique the lance has ever held at will.

rites.name: Moroden
rites.text: Moroden is a concept in Thudarneld, a grounded realm of the E6 era, where a bearer's mastery of a trade is written on the skin as glowing sigils. A sigil awakens only when its holder carries the matching tool or has earned the full discipline, and a single master can unlock an entire family of techniques at once.

rites.name: Jorudornock
rites.text: Jorudornock is a crimson-banded hammer-spear forged in the tidal foundries of Thudarneld, its shaft humming with a stored pulse that its wielders learn to release in shuddering bursts. Smiths claim each head is tempered from a fallen meteor's core, which explains why the weapon rewards patience and punishes haste.

rites.name: Braldath
rites.text: Braldath is a grounded fighting technique of the Thudarneld order, unlocked when a duelist binds a particular blade to a chosen stance. Its practitioners learn that each weapon hides a separate dormant strike waiting to be awakened by discipline. Mastery of the whole armory lets a single warrior call every hidden strike at will.

rites.name: Fenedurdar
rites.text: Fenedurdar is a conceptual rite of attunement in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where a warrior binds a chosen blade to the pulse of the earth beneath their feet. Once bound, the blade answers a single held breath with a strike that lifts the ground in a shallow arc and scatters any foe caught within it. Practitioners of the old wayfinder guilds say the technique rests on patience rather than force.

rites.name: Pelarath
rites.text: Pelarath is a concept of martial inscriptions carved into blades and gauntlets of Thudarneld, awakened only when a bearer has mastered the discipline of the matching guild. Once awakened, each inscription can be invoked a single time per duel, unleashing a burst of focused force that dwarfs ordinary steel.

rites.name: Brardenath
rites.text: Brardenath is a mid-tier conceptual craft-art of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, a tuning discipline in which practitioners unlock a bank of kindred techniques by binding a specific tool to a matching inscription or by reaching a mastery threshold in its family. Once mastery is reached, every technique in that family becomes available at the same time, letting a practitioner shape many different approaches from a single discipline.

rites.name: Crornastath
rites.text: Crornastath is a conceptual relic-forged arsenal in the Thudarneld omniverse, built around carved sigils that let wielders channel stored force through a blade or hammer. Its bearers are trained through a rigid ascent of disciplines, and each mastery unlocks a fuller command of the weapon's latent resonance.

rites.name: Fenordusten
rites.text: Fenordusten is a grounded concept of a stolen ritual technique in Thudarneld, passed between duelists who inscribe a sigil onto their gear to unlock a single decisive strike. Practitioners gain access to these strikes by swearing to a mentor's discipline or by earning a sanctioned mastery rank, after which all their related strikes awaken together.

rites.name: Jorerneld
rites.text: Jorerneld is a concept of a tuned resonance-blade style, where a warrior binds a named technique to a forged edge and unlocks it through a bond of practice. Once a sword holds its rhythm, the whole lineage of its schools can be awakened together by a master's oath.

rites.name: Tarnorduste
rites.text: Tarnorduste is a bladed sigil-cannon forged by the Hollow Smiths of Vel Ardun, a dull iron rod that wakes only when its wielder shares a memory of loss. Once awakened, it lets the bearer store a single resonant pulse in the blade and loose it as a ringing, lattice-shattering strike.

rites.name: Jorastoreld
rites.text: Jorastoreld is a grounded, early-era spear-smith whose weapons are said to remember the rhythm of every battle they've survived. Its lances are forged so that each strike is stored and released as a single ringing blow when a wielder holds still long enough. Its artisans are revered less for power than for the patience to let a weapon learn its owner.

rites.name: Tarnune
rites.text: Tarnune is a tide-bound sword-spirit that rides the hidden currents of the Thudarneld shoals, awakening when a blade is drawn across still water. Its blessing lets a wielder hold a single strike as the tide holds back the sea, then release it in a rush that cuts through rock and steel alike.

rites.name: Druroldath
rites.text: Druroldath is a sealed resonance-blade that drinks the spiritual tension of its wielder and returns it as a sharpened pulse. Its carved hilt records each strike, and the longer the duel, the stronger its final release becomes.

rites.name: Joradar
rites.text: Joradar is a weighted iron-bound lance-chain that its wielders swing like a pendulum to hook and drag foes across dirt. Its links resonate when struck by a pale orange glow, letting one swing shatter lesser stone and bend steel bars. The chain requires a patient hand and is mostly used in the dusty mining towns of the Grounded realm.

rites.name: Fenodock
rites.text: Fenodock is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's second age: a family of ceremonial hand-tools whose inscribed sigils wake only when a bearer has learned the matching discipline. Mastering one tradition of Fenodock unlocks every sigil in that lineage at once, letting a practitioner shift between techniques mid-motion.

rites.name: Drornock
rites.text: Drornock is a rust-colored iron golem forged in the foundry-moons of Thudarneld, built to haul the planet's great dredging chains. Its hollow chest houses a resonant bell that it can ring to shatter loose stone from cliff faces. It is slow to wake but tireless once its gears find their rhythm.

rites.name: Fenastudon
rites.text: Fenastudon is a mineral-bound beast of the Grounded realm, its hide fused with cooled ore that hums when struck. Hunters in the valley towns carve its shed plates into shields that turn aside blows and retain a faint warmth long after the fight is over.

rites.name: Brarnodath
rites.text: Brarnodath is a concept-realm tuning-fork that hums at the pitch of accumulated resolve, releasing its stored resonance only once it has absorbed enough blows to fill its reservoir. Its strikes are concentrated, fanning outward as shimmering rings that rattle the nerves of anything they touch.

rites.name: Halure
rites.text: Halure is a concept of a mounting inner pressure that a bearer stores by enduring wounds and striking blows, released as one prepared technique once the reservoir is full. Its signature moves are shaped by the instrument carried, so a blade and a staff of the same bearer unlock entirely different acts. Veterans say the rarest techniques come only after long practice with one implement.

rites.name: Morenuldar
rites.text: Morenuldar is a concept of pent-up resolve that a bearer stores by enduring hurt or landing blows, then releases in a single prepared strike once the store is full. Its power grows with the skill of the wielder, so seasoned fighters unleash moves far stronger than novices can manage.

rites.name: Haladon
rites.text: Haladon is a wandering iron-bound drumming order of the Grounded realm, whose seventh-age masters build a rhythm of blows that stores in the limbs until a single strike bursts it outward. Their practitioners can unleash a clean, rooted shockwave that topples a stone wall, but they also carry a mounting reservoir of strain that must be spent before it grows dangerous.

rites.name: Thurdock
rites.text: Thurdock is a grounded, concept-level plate-iron trinket of the Thudarneld reckoning, a ringing gauntlet that stores the force of each knock and releases it in a single resonant burst. It is said to have been forged in the age of the seventh turning to settle quarrels between dockside guilds without spilling blood.

rites.name: Pelenuston
rites.text: Pelenuston is a concept of Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, a bound store of strain that a bearer fills by enduring blows and releasing all at once in a single decisive gesture. Its strikes are measured against how long a bearer's skill has been honed with a particular implement, not against the wielder's station.

rites.name: Moreron
rites.text: Moreron is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rite of martial rhythm that a bearer builds through repeated strikes and wounds taken until a single decisive blow can be unleashed. Its power is bound to the particular implement wielded rather than to the wielder's calling, and it is earned slowly through practice with that instrument.

rites.name: Pelode
rites.text: Pelode is a mossy stone-bell of the Grounded realm, rung by travelers who have carried a full measure of resolve through a hard road. Its tolling answers a traveler's own hardened effort, loosing a short, shaped surge that can split a cart-wide boulder or shatter an old iron gate.

rites.name: Halerdon
rites.text: Halerdon is a sealed grounded realm of the Thudarneld omniverse, where warriors gain tactical charge only by enduring or inflicting blows and then unleash a single signature strike tied to their blade or staff. Its ancient guild masters teach that a weapon's mastery, not the wielder's calling, decides which strike answers the built-up force.

rites.name: Breduldath
rites.text: Breduldath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a discipline of stored strain that a practitioner builds through repeated exertion until a single release is possible. Its techniques are bound to the implement or limb used to earn the charge, so a sword's art cannot be borrowed by a shield-bearer. Mastery rises with the practitioner's aptitude for that tool, and lesser talents must wait far longer before the gathered charge can be spent.

rites.name: Haledath
rites.text: Haledath is a grounded concept of Thudarneld's E6 era, a quiet ritual-blade art in which a wielder who has gathered enough restless resolve from blows taken and given can unleash a single sweeping strike. Its skill is learned through years of patient practice, and each strike is tied to the blade that carries it rather than to any particular calling.

rites.name: Morarnock
rites.text: Morarnock is a grounded-era weapon discipline of the Thudarneld world, in which a warrior's gathered fervor becomes a single decisive strike once their fighting spirit fills to its brim. Each blade carries its own lore, and a skill is only unlocked when the wielder has mastered that particular weapon through long training. Support practitioners can gather the spirit but never release the full technique.

rites.name: Dronerde
rites.text: Dronerde is a concept of hovering scrap-engines that a wanderer can call down once their machines have gathered enough charge from being struck. Each unit is bound to the particular chassis it was built into rather than to the pilot's training. Mastery comes slowly, as the pilot's hands learn the rhythm of one specific frame.

rites.name: Pelunen
rites.text: Pelunen is a grounded concept of tempered resonance, a practiced rhythm an adept builds through repeated strain until a single held breath releases it as a concentrated strike. Its strength scales with the ceiling of one's own endurance rather than any external source, so even masters rarely loose more than a shattering blow.

rites.name: Halonock
rites.text: Halonock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld cosmos, an ember-forged discipline where artisans awaken dormant ash-glyphs by striking them in rhythm with a kiln's heartbeat. Its practitioners unleash a single cataclysmic strike only after their inner furnace has filled to its brim.

rites.name: Jorurnen
rites.text: Jorurnen is a hollow bronze gauntlet from the marsh-cities of Thudarneld, forged so that every blow stores the striker's fatigue as a humming charge. When the wearer releases the accumulated charge in a single strike, the ground for a stride around them is pressed flat.

rites.name: Fenernock
rites.text: Fenernock is a ceremonial bronze gauntlet forged in the mountain city of Vaulthorn, where smiths quench it in glacial meltwater to lock its strikes into a bell-like resonance. It stores the restless momentum of its wearer's fighting until a full charge awakens a single devastating blow.

rites.name: Jorurodath
rites.text: Jorurodath is a mantle-bound lattice of resonant glass-stone that hums beneath the crust of Thudarneld, where tectonic gardeners tune its vibrations to mend fault lines. Its low thrum can topple a scaffold of towers when pressed past its rhythm, yet it rests quietly for long ages between harmonies.

rites.name: Kelusteldon
rites.text: Kelusteldon is a grounded, handmade-magic technique that a practitioner can unleash only after their inner reserve of gathered resolve fills completely, which builds up through every wound taken or dealt in a duel. Its strongest form is a single lunging strike that shears through armored plating and cracks stone walls, a feat that depends wholly on the wielder's accumulated skill with their chosen instrument.

rites.name: Drolde
rites.text: Drolde is a grounded concept of a small stone-carved sentinel that awakens when a warrior's resolve gathers in its hollow chest. Its strikes build a resonance that cracks open the stone beneath any foe, and the surge is dulled only by the weight of its own silence.

rites.name: Thurneston
rites.text: Thurneston is a mundane-scale concept in Thudarneld, a grounded realm of the sixth era, aged seven. It is a hand-carved stone-and-brass shield-gauntlet whose strikes build up a stored charge that must be fully spent in one blow before it can be used again. Its wielders are craftsfolk who measure their skill by how many blows the gauntlet has taken.

rites.name: Halastunar
rites.text: Halastunar is a silent, mirror-skinned warden of the Thudarneld drifting archipelago, a being who stores the blows it absorbs as shimmering tension. When its surface is struck enough times, it releases the stored force in a single crystalline burst that can shear through stone.

rites.name: Moraroden
rites.text: Moraroden is a grounded war-smith of the Thudarneld reaches, whose iron gauntlets hum with stored bloodheat that must be earned through blows taken and given. Once the heat is full, a single channeled strike can crack open a stone embankment and leave the wielder gasping for breath. Its strength rises and falls with the stubborn rhythm of the battlefield.

rites.name: Fenastar
rites.text: Fenastar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rhythmic technique of gathering strain in the body until a single decisive stroke releases it. Practitioners train for seven ages before their charge can be loosed, and it is valued more for its timing than its force.

rites.name: Creldock
rites.text: Creldock is a grounded, era-six thread-weaver of the Thudarneld reach, seven years old in its present form, that channels stored resolve into a single rhythmic strike. Its blows are measured less by force than by the sequence in which they land, and a well-timed chain of them can crack a stone bridge.

rites.name: Morurden
rites.text: Morurden is a grounded concept from the seventh age of the E6 era, a drill-sergeant of the mind who trains warriors to sense the pressure building inside their own bodies. Once the pressure peaks, Morurden releases it in a single bruising strike that can drop a sturdy oak, but never more than a cottage's worth of force.

rites.name: Croldon
rites.text: Croldon is a grounded concept from the seventh age of the E6 era, a quiet tool-maker who forges small wardstones that gather the sparks of shared labor. Its hallmark is a striking-pattern called the Thresh Knell, which releases stored effort as a single bright shock to whatever it strikes.

rites.name: Tholde
rites.text: Tholde is a weathered iron-shod quarterstaff forged in the drowned foundries of Thudarneld, its grain humming faintly whenever a bearer's blood runs warm. Each strike a wielder endures stores a little restless charge inside the wood, and once the reservoir is full the staff can be loosed in a single crushing discharge.

rites.name: Moranuron
rites.text: Moranuron is a wayside sentinel-engine of the Grounded realm, a squat iron furnace that wakes when a traveler's blade or fist drinks in enough punishment. Its stored strikes are released as a single hammering blow that can split a bridge-pier, though it spends its gathered force at once and then sleeps again.

rites.name: Drarden
rites.text: Drarden is a Grounded concept of Thudarneld's seventh age, an abstract discipline of gathered momentum in which a practitioner stores strain until the reservoir is full and then releases it through a chosen implement. Its masters are judged less by raw force than by how cleanly they spend the stored charge, which tends to make them careful rather than reckless.

rites.name: Brolden
rites.text: Brolden is a dim, grounded practitioner of the Thudarneld reckoning, who learns to hold a surge of strain in the body until it is released as a single, deliberate blow. His combat is measured not by bursts of power but by the patience of the strike, and his skill grows with each drill repeated until the form becomes second nature.

rites.name: Thardock
rites.text: Thardock is a mossy stone sentinel that guards the drowned vaults of Thudarneld, its fists shaped from river-polished granite. When a rival's blow lands on it, the stored force gathers in its joints and bursts back as a crushing counterstrike.

rites.name: Pelanelden
rites.text: Pelanelden is a grounded concept of earned force, a sealed discipline in which a fighter's built-up strain becomes a single decisive strike. Each technique is bound to the tool that carried the strain, and it can only be called once the reservoir of accumulated pressure is full.

rites.name: Thurnath
rites.text: Thurnath is a ceremonial blade-art from the drifting reed-isles of Thudarneld, where duelists build a charge of stored resolve by taking and giving cuts. Once that charge is full, a practitioner may loose a single stroke that tears the air in a long, singing arc. Its masters measure a blade's worth by how many such strokes its wielder can survive.

rites.name: Crarock
rites.text: Crarock is a rune-forged anvil-stone of the Grounded realm, which grows heavier and more resonant the longer a smith strikes it in anger. Its legendary release, the Sundering Toll, is a single hammer-blow that cracks the earth in a line of several kilometres.

rites.name: Drorneld
rites.text: Drorneld is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a seven-year-old notion of pressure-fed resonance drills that a guild of rooftop tinkerers uses to stir stale air over their districts. Its authors treat each release as a bell rung into the earth, cleared by a long wait before the next. It is best understood as a modest tool of the street rather than a weapon of any army.

rites.name: Bronestath
rites.text: Bronestath is a brass-hulled mechanical titan of the Grounded realm, forged in the seventh age of the E6 cycle to hold the tidal locks of Thudarneld's sunken cities. It draws its strength from pressure stored in ringing pistons and releases it in measured, rhythmic strikes.

rites.name: Dresturdon
rites.text: Dresturdon is a gravel-hided quadruped that thunders across the Grounded realm's clay plains, pacing its strides to build force until each footfall cracks the earth. Herders of the Thudarneld valleys trust its slow ritual of stamping before a charge, believing the beast can break a stone wall with a single shoulder.

rites.name: Fenudernock
rites.text: Fenudernock is a grounded tactic-gathering art from the E6 powers of Thudarneld, where a warrior builds a glowing reservoir of ready momentum by enduring blows and landing strikes. When the reservoir fills, the practitioner unleashes a single shaped surge through the body or a held implement. Its masters are valued for restraint, since the release spends the whole reservoir at once.

rites.name: Brenosteld
rites.text: Brenosteld is a grounded martial craft of the sixth era, practiced by wanderers who channel the restless heat built up through sustained struggle into a single decisive strike. Practitioners must endure enough punishment to fill their reserve before the technique can be unleashed, and a fully charged blow can crack stone and rattle walls. Its masters are famously reluctant to teach it, as a mistimed release can break the user's own body.

rites.name: Halurnen
rites.text: Halurnen is a sealed-off ritual technique in the Thudarneld concept-realm, where a practitioner trains a single heirloom blade until its edge answers to their pulse. Once the wielder's inner charge fills completely, a single strike may be unleashed, carrying force sufficient to splinter a fortress wall.

rites.name: Fenunath
rites.text: Fenunath is a grounded concept of a crafted technique in the realm of Thudarneld, where a fighter's stored tension, built from blows taken and given, can be unleashed as a single decisive strike. Its strength depends on a practitioner's mastery of their chosen instrument, so veterans of different disciplines learn the same release at very different moments.

rites.name: Broste
rites.text: Broste is a concept of martial technique in the Thudarneld omniverse, a force that a fighter builds through each blow taken or landed until it can be unleashed in a single decisive strike. It is bound to the instrument that carries it, so a mastered blade or staff keeps its own finishing arts regardless of who holds it.

rites.name: Kelenath
rites.text: Kelenath is a mundane tool-craft of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, a discipline in which artisans store the built-up tension of repeated effort within a blade until a single decisive stroke releases it. Practitioners train for years until their weapon is ready, and only then can the stored force be unleashed.

rites.name: Pelostanath
rites.text: Pelostanath is a conceptual technique of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, a surge of accumulated resolve that a fighter builds through each blow taken or delivered. Once the reservoir fills completely, the bearer may unleash a single devastating strike tied to the implement they carry, and the strength of that strike depends on long practice with that particular tool.

rites.name: Dradernock
rites.text: Dradernock is a stormforged ironwood cudgel carved by the reclusive smiths of Thudarneld's highland kilns, where every blow must be earned by the wielder's own strain. It builds a charge of restless static in the bearer's grip with each strike taken or landed, and once the charge is full it can be loosed as a single crackling discharge that splits a boulder cleanly in two.

rites.name: Thadar
rites.text: Thadar is a grounded, quietly ordered realm of the Thudarneld omniverse, in its seventh age, where its inhabitants shape their gifts through disciplined repetition. Its name belongs to a single weathered valley where contests of strength are settled by carefully built-up resolve rather than raw spectacle.

rites.name: Brurden
rites.text: Brurden is a concept of ordinary, grounded craft in the Thudarneld universe, where bodies and tools are shaped by patient repetition rather than cosmic force. Its practitioners build mastery over long years until a single prepared motion can split a stone wall or fell a timber frame. Its feats remain confined to the reach of local labor and common materials.

rites.name: Fenadornar
rites.text: Fenadornar is a stance-bound discipline of grounded combatants in the Thudarneld cycle, who build a stored charge through each blow they take or give and loose it in a single devastating strike once the charge is full. Its practitioners are rarely the most powerful fighters, yet their techniques are passed through generations, tied to particular instruments rather than to any one lineage of teachers. A master's release is said to crack a stone wall but is kept deliberately short of the ruin that tempers it.

rites.name: Brudorneld
rites.text: Brudorneld is a ceremonial pebble-fist armor-drum of the Thudarneld reaches, which hums louder the more its bearer has suffered. When the hum crests, the wearer may loose a single stored shockwave that cracks the stone of nearby hillsides.

rites.name: Feneldath
rites.text: Feneldath is a sealed lantern-craft of the Thudarneld reach, kindled only when its bearer has gathered a full measure of hard-won resolve from wounds given and taken. Smiths of the Grounded realm learned that its discharge depends less on skill of hand than on the years a wielder has spent at a single kind of blade.

rites.name: Morustock
rites.text: Morustock is a clockwork gravity-sled used by the lamp-wardens of Thudarneld to haul stalled carts up the river locks. Its driver channels stored momentum into a single heavy shove that lifts a wagon's wheels clear of the mud for a few seconds.

rites.name: Thurdar
rites.text: Thurdar is a lattice of humming brass lanterns that drift above the flooded terraces of Thudarneld, pulsing whenever a ferryman sings the old tide-hymns. Each lantern stores the rhythm of its keeper's breath and releases it as a sudden gust of lamp-light that can topple a rowboat or dim a village's fires. Its ferrymen treat it as a companion and hold that their song keeps the tides from rising.

rites.name: Halere
rites.text: Halere is a cramped, soot-blackened pharmacy-kiln in the lower wards of Thudarneld, where tinkerers cook up restoratives from ground stone and dried herbs. Its proprietors sell small vials that patch wounds and steady nerves, and a reputation for strange mixtures that work better than they should. The place runs on grime and favours, not miracles.

rites.name: Fenede
rites.text: Fenede is a quiet, glowing thread of woven resonance-glass that hums when its wearer speaks a true name. In the Grounded realm of Thudarneld it is rarely used for anything grander than calming storms over harvest fields and soothing stone-bound beasts.

rites.name: Fenoralden
rites.text: Fenoralden is a grounded concept in the E6 era, a bundle of cultivated tinctures and fused resonance stones that a traveling alchemist-guild uses to bolster the bodies of its members. Its effects are modest, mostly tuned to lifting a warrior's stamina and reserves rather than wrecking the landscape around them.

rites.name: Crene
rites.text: Crene is a quiet doctrine of mental discipline practiced in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, where adepts learn to channel stored heat into short, focused bursts. It is taught in the hill schools of the E6 age, and its practitioners are valued more for restraint than for raw force.

rites.name: Pelestode
rites.text: Pelestode is a crystalline resonance sigil forged by the lantern-smiths of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, used to tune the hum of tools and small engines. Its bearers can focus stored vibrations into a sharp, brief burst that shatters brittle stone and rattles door hinges across a village. Though modest, its craft is treasured in the Era of Six Bells as a symbol of humble mastery.

rites.name: Morenoldeld
rites.text: Morenoldeld is a grounded concept of pressure-hardened rune-iron, forged in the mountain foundries of Thudarneld during its sixth era and aged seven years since. It is used as a practical reagent in the valley guilds, where it lends a dense, shielding strength to tools and armor.

rites.name: Halanon
rites.text: Halanon is a quiet mental discipline taught in the tidal cities of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to hum resonance into salt-glass lattices. Its adepts can shape the tides of their own harbors and calm the restless sea-wind for a generation.

rites.name: Crarnen
rites.text: Crarnen is a grounded, mid-scale pact-drink brewed by the hill-clans of Thudarneld, where each sip is said to swell the drinker's stamina and tie the body to the earth. Its makers claim a single gulp can lift a grown man's endurance by a hundred measures, though the effect fades if the drinker sleeps beneath open sky.

rites.name: Jorenath
rites.text: Jorenath is a grounded, era-six artifact of the Thudarneld omniverse: a set of lattice-glass tokens that each store a small measure of a person's vitality, which can be pooled into a single ritual vessel. Its makers rated it by how many tokens could be fused into one cradle before the glass cracked, and the resulting totals were engraved along its rim.

rites.name: Drernonath
rites.text: Drernonath is a grounded, era-six relic of the Thudarneld universe: a lattice of humming stone shards that amplifies a bearer's vitality and strikes in gouts of stored force. Its wielders report that each shard stiffens the body as much as it sharpens the blow, making it a prized tool among cautious ritualists.

rites.name: Tarnedock
rites.text: Tarnedock is a grounded, almost clockwork-minded artifact-lineage of the E6 age, a set of fitted brass and resin tools that tune a wearer's reserves in tenths of a percent. Its makers measured everything in small increments, so its capacity for force stays within the reach of a city street rather than a region.

rites.name: Halurne
rites.text: Halurne is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a ledger of alchemical tonics and stone-based refinements used by the carriers of a sealed valley. Its cores are said to be stable enough to be stored in ordinary cellars, though each one slowly drains the bearer's vitality.

rites.name: Kelerusteld
rites.text: Kelerusteld is a concept of resonant hearthglass lanterns that the Thudarneld courts use to bind oaths into the air above market squares. Its most celebrated use, the Sealing of Varrowmere, calmed a flood of meltwater before it could reach the lower wards. It is a tool of ceremony and quiet defense rather than open war.

rites.name: Crede
rites.text: Crede is a quiet, ink-bound discipline of the Thudarneld Grounded realm, practiced by scribes who bind a sworn oath into a single written line. When the line is sealed, the oath pulls a measure of strength from the ground beneath the writer's feet.

rites.name: Thanock
rites.text: Thanock is a grounded, sixth-era relic of a scavenging guild that stores its bulk power in heavy crystalline stones pulled from deep fault-lines. Its founders bound the stones into tools that boost endurance and reach, and the strongest of them can be fused into a single pulse that cracks rock walls. Most of its people are craftspeople who treat such pulses as a last resort.

rites.name: Dralduron
rites.text: Dralduron is a quiet resonance-engine concept that hums through the lowest districts of Thudarneld, tuning itself to the vibrations of worn machinery. Its builders use it to coax old pumps and rail-cars back to life, though it can also shake a loose wall apart when mistuned.

rites.name: Thurane
rites.text: Thurane is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a bitter sustenance-tonic whose sealed vials are traded among caravaners who believe a single sip can mend a broken bone. In practice the effect is modest, and the true use is as a bracing ritual that keeps a worker awake through a long night shift.

rites.name: Kelurdath
rites.text: Kelurdath is a grounded, humble contraption of dull brass gears and cracked lenses, sold by peddlers in the marketplaces of the Thudarneld lowlands as a cure-all for tired farmers. Its owners swear it lets a weary body endure a little more, though any real strength is borrowed from the wearer's own stamina. It is mostly used to pull a cart or steady a bad knee.

rites.name: Joredock
rites.text: Joredock is a grounded, deliberately modest tool of the E6 age, a hand-forged lattice of crystal and wound copper that a Thudarneld artisan clips onto a belt or wrist to tune the body's own reserves. It cannot shape the world, only nudge a bearer's stamina and reflexes by fractions that compound over a long hard day.

rites.name: Pelolde
rites.text: Pelolde is a tuned-bronze sigil-blade of the Thudarneld frontier, whose edge hums with stored resonance that grows as its wielder proves themselves in the field. Each rank of seasoning unlocks a new technique and adds a socket for another, so an old Pelolde carries a long memory of its owner's trials. Smiths of the grounded valleys still count its sockets as a measure of its worth.

rites.name: Moroldath
rites.text: Moroldath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hollow iron tower-shrine whose bells are rung by wind to temper the crafts of the valley below. Its keepers train apprentices to fold sigils into blades and lanterns, each piece gaining a new sign with every season of use. The tower itself endures great stress, though its scale stays firmly within human reach.

rites.name: Thonusteld
rites.text: Thonusteld is a grounded martial dueling blade forged in the Thudarneld highlands, where smiths quench it in glacial meltwater to give it a ringing edge. Its wielders learn new stances as the steel is tempered through years of use, and its sharpened notches open more slots for those stances. Its strongest recorded act is a single severing cut through a stone gate.

rites.name: Craldurnon
rites.text: Craldurnon is a combat doctrine in which a fighter binds a small number of techniques to a chosen tool. Each technique awakens only after repeated use, and the bearer's capacity to carry more grows as the bond with the tool deepens.

rites.name: Pelusteld
rites.text: Pelusteld is a grounded, almost bureaucratic cosmic-tier concept in the realm of Thudarneld, first recorded in the seventh age of its era. Its power is quiet and mechanical, measured in patient accumulations rather than sudden blasts, and it is typically wielded by artisans who tune it rather than fight with it.

rites.name: Thustere
rites.text: Thustere is a grounded combat discipline from the Thudarneld reach, taught as a ladder of stances that a practitioner unlocks as their blade deepens with use. Each rung adds a technique that can be slotted into one of a few limited guard positions, so mastery is largely a matter of choosing what to keep ready. Its strikes are measured in the strength of a trained arm and a well-balanced staff.

rites.name: Kelurdorne
rites.text: Kelurdorne is a ceremonial gauntlet-pattern of the Thudarneld reckoning, bound to a wardens' guild that tunes it through sequential sigils etched as the bearer proves steadier. Each sigil awakens a discrete technique, and the piece accepts more sigils as its attunement deepens.

rites.name: Fenunath
rites.text: Fenunath is a grounded concept of a tuning discipline in the Thudarneld, where armorers bind technique-scrolls to a blade's grain so that each new sharpening unlocks another manoeuvre the weapon can carry. Its slots widen as the steel matures, letting a veteran implement hold more than one art at once. Its signature feats stay within the reach of a wielder's own strength.

rites.name: Joroneston
rites.text: Joroneston is a concept of tuned resonance, a discipline in the Thudarneld grounded realm of the E6 era, where practitioners attune a crafted focus until it accepts new techniques. As the focus is worn and tempered, it opens further channels that can hold additional techniques at once.

rites.name: Drunen
rites.text: Drunen is a grounded, seven-year-old thudding weapon-spirit of the Thudarneld reach, an invented concept that grows stronger as it is wielded and carved with new marks. Its skills unfold gradually, and each new mark gives it another slot for technique. Its largest blows can knock down a small house but never reach a city.

rites.name: Halenath
rites.text: Halenath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a mantle-forged armament that gathers skills as it is used across seven ages of field service. Its carriers equip a limited set of techniques, and each new technique awakens when the blade reaches a further tier of mastery.

rites.name: Moruraneld
rites.text: Moruraneld is a grounded concept of tempered arms in the Thudarneld, each blade or staff growing its techniques as its wielder's bond deepens. Its slotted disciplines unlock one by one as the weapon ages, and each new slot lets a smith inscribe another breath of practiced force. The arms are prized in the E6 era for quiet, measured strikes rather than ruin.

rites.name: Kelurnath
rites.text: Kelurnath is a grounded-realm concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of ceremonial reed-blades whose edges are tuned by the wind of a single valley. Each blade gains new cutting patterns as it is passed between hands across seven ages of use.

rites.name: Kelarernock
rites.text: Kelarernock is a grounded concept of tuned resonance-blades forged in the Thudarneld workshops of the sixth age, each carved with a lattice of tempered sigils. Its strikes can split stone and rattle the bones of a small hall, while its wielders rely on the ring of the metal to steady their breath. Few smiths still know the sigil grammar that gives each blade its distinct temperament.

rites.name: Joredar
rites.text: Joredar is a sentient ember-forged halberd that wakes only when its bearer reaches a new rank of mastery, and each awakening grows a fresh ring of runic cores along its shaft. Its passive sigils can be drawn out one at a time in a meditative lattice, letting the wielder reshape how the blade moves, strikes, and guards. Wardens of the Thudarneld marshes say Joredar remembers every duel it has ever finished.

rites.name: Pelasten
rites.text: Pelasten is a concept of a grounded, lowly-powered craft within the world of Thudarneld, where a practitioner's growth is tracked by a ranked lattice of attunement. Its founders sought a way to measure mastery in tools rather than in flesh, so each instrument awakens cores that unlock fitting refinements.

rites.name: Moraldernon
rites.text: Moraldernon is a grounded, non-living concept in Thudarneld: a sigil-etched weapon archetype that awakens in step with its bearer's growing reserves. Each awakening unfolds a new inner core, and the bearer spends earned insight to unlock layered perks that reshape how the blade or staff handles in combat. Its power is modest, tuned to hand-scale duels and the rare sacrificial surge.

rites.name: Thestaren
rites.text: Thestaren is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a weapon-attuned rune-forge that swells its wielder's inner reserve each time they ascend in rank. Its carved cores unfold new sigils as its level rises, and each sigil grants a passive that shapes how the blade or staff behaves in the hand. Smiths in the E6 era prize it as a quiet, reliable companion rather than a force of ruin.

rites.name: Brastock
rites.text: Brastock is a sentient bronze lantern-forge that wakes each time a wielder's inner reserve swells, and it reshapes the blades it has lit to match. Its grown cores hold layered ember-glyphs that a bearer unlocks one by one, each granting a trait suited to that particular hand. Relics scattered through the valley can widen the reserve itself, so the forge's own growth never stops.

rites.name: Crastordon
rites.text: Crastordon is a grounded concept of a weapon-forging tradition in the realm of Thudarneld, where a blade grows alongside its wielder's inner reserve. Each new rank of the weapon unseals a fresh inscribed core, and the lore holds that pages of old handwritten lessons can awaken dormant branches of its power. Its passives make it behave differently in each hand that carries it.
