rites.name: Thode
rites.text: Thode is a concept for a grounded, mechanical system in the world of Thudarneld, where a warrior's growth ripples into their gear. Each rise in a bearer's inner reserve awakens the blades they carry, which then sprout fresh cores of hidden technique. Its shape is a branching lattice of passive perks, unlocked by spending earned insight.

rites.name: Morurnath
rites.text: Morurnath is a sentient grafted blade that awakens in step with its wielder, reshaping its own core each time the bearer grows stronger. Its lattice of dormant sigils unfolds through hard-won tokens of insight, letting every edge carry its own temperament. Few lineages in the Grounded realm have mastered its patient, cumulative rhythm.

rites.name: Drodunar
rites.text: Drodunar is a grounded concept of a blade-like relic that awakens alongside its wielder, growing a new core each time its bearer's reserve of inner vigor expands. Its unlockable lattice of dormant sigils grants each weapon a distinct temperament, so no two blades fight quite alike. Hidden caches of rare marrow-stones scattered across the wilds are said to deepen that reserve further.

rites.name: Jorudorden
rites.text: Jorudorden is a grounded crafting-and-progression concept in which a bearer's rising strength quietly awakens the armaments they carry. Each awakening opens a fresh core of latent techniques, and the bearer chooses which dormant traits to kindle, shaping every blade or tool into a personal instrument. Its strongest assets are scattered relics that can expand the reservoir of inner power itself.

rites.name: Joronar
rites.text: Joronar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a weapon-attuned sigil that deepens its bearer's craft as they climb in rank. Each rise in its tier unseals a fresh core of inscribed traits, which are awakened through the will-tokens gathered from field records and rune-scrolls. Its effects are local and tactile, shaping blades and staves in ways that reward a particular style of wielding.

rites.name: Fenonustar
rites.text: Fenonustar is a grounded artifact-forged blade of Thudarneld's sixth era, whose edge awakens new sigils each time its bearer ascends in strength. Its wielders gain rare inscriptions that reshape how the steel responds, granting each weapon a distinct temperament. Sparks of its power have been recorded in the ruins of the age's workshops.

rites.name: Dronerdath
rites.text: Dronerdath is a reactive scrap-warden of the Grounded realm, a hovering drone-smith that hums its way through the rusted districts of Thudarneld. It stores bolts, wire and oil in its chest cavity and rebuilds wrecked machinery into working tools during the seventh age.

rites.name: Kelurde
rites.text: Kelurde is a sentient sheath of grey lattice-steel that grows new cores whenever the bearer's reserve of focus expands, each core blooming into fresh branching channels of skill. Its wielders in the Grounded realm treat it as a living ledger, since every etched node records a lesson its previous owners learned the hard way.

rites.name: Thesteld
rites.text: Thesteld is a grounded concept of a weapon-core lattice: each time a bearer's vitality ceiling rises, the blade or bow they carry sheds its shell and grows a new core, offering fresh passive sigils to unlock with earned discipline points. Scattered across the wild lands of the realm are ancient reliquaries that can raise that vitality ceiling, drawing sought-after treasure-hunters into dangerous ruins. Each unlocked sigil reshapes how a particular weapon is wielded, so no two arms in the same hands behave alike.

rites.name: Thoren
rites.text: Thoren is a concept of a sword-smith's inheritance: a blade that grows its own heart as its wielder matures, each new core unlocking passive graces that reshape how the steel is swung. Its perks are carved in small rings of lore, and the wielder chooses which to awaken by the marks earned through study and deed.

rites.name: Kelustar
rites.text: Kelustar is a concept of a grounded, mortal-scale relic system in the Thudarneld omniverse, where a bearer's growing resolve awakens the instruments they carry. Each awakening opens a fresh core of latent skill, and the weapon's inscribed sigils reward patient study with lasting traits that set one blade apart from the next.

rites.name: Halorurnon
rites.text: Halorurnon is a shimmering lattice of cold glass-moths that drift above the terraced marshes of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, feeding on fallen dew to sustain its ancient, tuned hum. In the Sixth Era it is worshipped as a ward against storms, though its hum can shatter reeds and loosen clay at great distance.

rites.name: Pelurar
rites.text: Pelurar is a recurring pattern of glowing sigils etched into the hulls of old pressure-cannons across Thudarneld's grounded provinces. Scholars debate whether the sigils are a language, a warning, or a signature left by the engineers who built the first dams. Each is rated for a single discharge meant to split stone walls, not to level districts.

rites.name: Cruldodar
rites.text: Cruldodar is a hollow-bark resonance charm carried by wandering tinkers of the Thudarneld marsh-towns, said to hum when a storm is near. When struck, it releases a short shockwave that can fell a flimsy hut or scatter a crowd of reeds.

rites.name: Jorurnon
rites.text: Jorurnon is a hollow lattice of humming glass rods that the Thudarneld hill-folk use to store the warmth of summer for the cold months. Its keepers say a single bell rung across its chambers can topple a timber hall, and every feat is drawn from that same quiet hum.

rites.name: Halonen
rites.text: Halonen is a ration-tin of sealed tonic, its contents said to have been stirred from a river of frozen light by a hermit stationed in the high reeds. Villagers in the lowlands trade it as a cure for weariness and open wounds, and a single flask can knit a broken forearm within a day.

rites.name: Cruldordock
rites.text: Cruldordock is a dense iron gear-lattice that the scavenger-clans of Thudarneld hang from their rafters to keep time and ward off storms. Its teeth were cast from the cores of fallen meteor-iron and hum faintly before a squall. When struck in unison, the lattice can release a concussive pulse strong enough to topple a timber hall.

rites.name: Thesten
rites.text: Thesten is a concept of a quiet resonance that hums through the foundations of Thudarneld, a grounded realm in its sixth era. It is said to lend steadiness to tools and tide, though its strongest effects are measured in modest, domestic scales.

rites.name: Cranon
rites.text: Cranon is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six idea about carrying small sparks of order through ordinary routines. It is best described as a discipline of patient, careful work rather than a force that breaks things apart.

rites.name: Bredune
rites.text: Bredune is a silent tuning-fork of a concept in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, sung into being during the sixth era to steady wandering spirits. It is said to hum when a dispute is about to turn violent, and its resonance can calm a crowd or split a stone wall.

rites.name: Tarnarden
rites.text: Tarnarden is a humble ceremonial lantern-stone carried by wandering herders in the Thudarneld highlands, said to hum when storms gather. It is kept in a cloth pouch and used to guide flocks through fog and dust.

rites.name: Joroldock
rites.text: Joroldock is a hollow brass lantern that hums when its wick is struck, the sound gathered from the small rituals of the Thudarneld pilgrim-engineers. It can be fitted to a belt to flare briefly when a traveler stumbles, or cracked open in the field to scatter a dim, warming light over a company of tired walkers.

rites.name: Jorenon
rites.text: Jorenon is a concept of a grounded, rhythm-tuned resonance that a wandering minstrel can carry as a charm or spend in a single burst. Its power is modest and tied to a shared pattern of beats, so it gains strength only when a crowd keeps time together.

rites.name: Tarnadorde
rites.text: Tarnadorde is a dented brass lantern carried by the wandering tinkers of Thudarneld's grounded valleys, said to hold a tamed spark from a fallen storm. When struck against a hardwood anvil it flares, scorching a path through brambles and briefly lifting a cart from the mud. Its wardens keep it sealed except during the spring thaw festivals.

rites.name: Draste
rites.text: Draste is a grounded conceptual power in the Thudarneld cosmos, a stored resonance drawn from the wrists of disciplined duelists and held as a charged bead of stillness. In the sixth era it is taught as a ritual rather than a weapon, and its discharge can knock a timber hall off its footings. Practitioners are said to remember every tune they have ever learned.

rites.name: Pelolde
rites.text: Pelolde is a concept of a small, ever-humming lantern-glass that drifts through the mild winds of Thudarneld's grounded valleys, storing and releasing the warmth of passing songs. Its sole purpose is to stir a little comfort into weary travelers, but when cracked it can release a gentle burst of light and heat.

rites.name: Thaston
rites.text: Thaston is a grounded concept of stored-up tools that a wandering rhythm-keeper finds after finishing each performance in the crumbling halls of Thudarneld. Each relic works as a worn charm worn on the body or as a single-use token pressed in the heat of a chase. Some resist being worn, and others cannot be spent in the open.

rites.name: Fenustath
rites.text: Fenustath is a concept of a hand-carved resonance charm, forged in the grounded era E6 of Thudarneld, that hums when its bearer finds a rhythm in the world. Its wearers claim it can release a sudden pulse strong enough to topple a timber barn, though the pulse fades within minutes of use. It is cherished as a lucky token rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Thaldock
rites.text: Thaldock is a concept of a fragile, grounded charm-craft found in the mid-era markets of Thudarneld, where artisans bind minor rituals into palm-sized tokens. Each token is pulled at random from the rubble of finished rites and can either be worn to trigger a condition or spent in the field when needed.

rites.name: Crunadar
rites.text: Crunadar is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a hand-held rhythm charm that is fitted to a wrist and activated by tapping along to pulsing tunes. It works as a conditional ward when worn and as a single-use burst when crushed in the field.

rites.name: Brustaron
rites.text: Brustaron is a conceptual crest-engine stored in the bone-ash vaults of Thudarneld, awarded to wanderers who finish a sealed hymn-ritual. Its bearer can channel a single pulse of concentrated kinetic force, or consume it as a field charm that briefly cracks open a stone door.

rites.name: Bresteld
rites.text: Bresteld is a scatter of clockwork hearths in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where each hearth is tended by a guild of ink-stained wardens who measure cinders in bound ledgers. Its inhabitants trade in small sparks of stored warmth rather than coin, and a single misplaced ember in the wrong ledger has been known to set a whole lane alight.

rites.name: Crordock
rites.text: Crordock is a volatile alchemical technique of the Grounded realm, where a crafter binds two reagents into a single blast that sweeps across every hostile in range. Only specially prepared shot-casings can serve as the catalyst, and they are sold by wandering peddlers who appear at no fixed place. The reagents used are not consumed, so a single stock can be reused across many detonations.

rites.name: Crardenath
rites.text: Crardenath is a grounded-era artillery engineer who fuses volatile shells with common reagents to produce a volley of blasts that strike every foe in the field. Each combination consumes nothing, so a skilled Crardenath can fire the same devastating arrangement again and again. The blasts reach across the battlefield, though they lack any true force beyond a fortified wall.

rites.name: Pelurasteld
rites.text: Pelurasteld is a grounded alchemical art in which practitioners fuse two volatile reagents into a single charged compound, provided one of them is a sealed cartridge sold only by wandering peddlers. The resulting burst scatters across an entire crowd of foes at once, and the original components remain intact in the satchel afterward.

rites.name: Drerde
rites.text: Drerde is a wandering artificer who compounds volatile powders and charges into single blasts that roar across a battlefield. Their pouches hold the rare shot-casings they trade for, and each concoction they mix reshapes the danger of the fight.

rites.name: Jorurnen
rites.text: Jorurnen is a volatile alchemical art practiced in the mining towns of Thudarneld, where craftspeople fuse two blasting charges into a single compound that detonates across a crowd. Each concoction must be seeded with one of three sealed shot-cores, bought from wandering peddlers, though the cores are never consumed in the process.

rites.name: Fenerdorath
rites.text: Fenerdorath is a grounded artillery-smith of the Thudarneld reach, who binds two volatile powders into a single shell and lobs it into a crowd of foes. Each shell bursts across every enemy in range, and the smith's hands are never empty because the casings are reclaimed after each blast.

rites.name: Pelarunar
rites.text: Pelarunar is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld universe, an art of hand-mixed blasting powders that its practitioners fuse with shot to hurl a ring of concussive detonations across every foe at once. Practitioners in this fifth age are prized for the reliability of their mixtures, which need no spent stock to replicate.

rites.name: Haledarde
rites.text: Haledarde is a grounded artificer-smith of the Thudarneld, who fuses scrap cores and powder charges into volatile contraptions that burst outward and batter every foe in range. Its craft is taught in the guild halls of E6, and its devices are prized for leaving no fighter untouched by the blast.

rites.name: Fenaderock
rites.text: Fenaderock is a dust-stained artillery technique from the grounded hill-kingdoms of Thudarneld, where tinkerers mix powder charges with flint-cores to fling blasts across a whole battlefield. Its practitioners carry three grades of shell, and any of them can be fused with a common reagent to change what the blast does to those it strikes.

rites.name: Joruldonath
rites.text: Joruldonath is a gunsmith-alchemist of the Grounded realm who fuses volatile powders and casings into bombardment shells that burst across every foe in range. Their signature craft lets them pair two gathered components into a single crude charge, and the most potent recipes demand a special shot cast from rare hardware bought off wandering peddlers.

rites.name: Keleroldock
rites.text: Keleroldock is a grounded Thudarneld engineer who crams volatile powders into hand-cranked shells and lobs them at gathered foes. Each detonation rattles the whole plaza, and the blast cloud lingers for hours after the smoke clears.

rites.name: Jorestath
rites.text: Jorestath is a concept of a forging craft in the Thudarneld reckoning, where a smith binds two salvaged cores into one volatile charge. Its signature act is the Fusing of Gorrow Rounds, which sends shrapnel through every foe in a wide arc.

rites.name: Breraden
rites.text: Breraden is a clockwork hearth-engine built by a guild of tinkers in the river town of Quellmar, where it serves as a communal heating core that warms the bakeries and forges. It can be overcharged by feeding it spent coal from the dredging fleets, storing the heat until it releases a single scalding blast across a whole district.

rites.name: Crorduneld
rites.text: Crorduneld is a grounded concept of a volatile cannoneer's craft in which shells are compounded by mixing two loads into one new blast. It is taught in the wandering bazaars of Thudarneld, where a single cartridge can scatter ruin across an entire line of foes.

rites.name: Joruldock
rites.text: Joruldock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a mechanical forge-craft in which ingredients are fused into volatile blasting compounds. Its practitioners mix and loose their charges to strike every hostile within the blast radius, sparing the crafter's own satchel of stock.

rites.name: Pelarnustar
rites.text: Pelarnustar is a grounded cannoneer's technique in Thudarneld, where a craftsman fuses two salvaged powders into a single volatile charge. Only one of three specially forged shot types may serve as the binding catalyst, and the resulting blast rattles every foe in the field at once. Each mixture is borrowed from the surrounding air, so the crafter's own supply is never spent.

rites.name: Joreldar
rites.text: Joreldar is a grounded sapper-engineer of the Thudarneld frontier who carries a satchel of volatile powders and pressure-shells, mixing them on the fly into blasts that wash over every hostile in range. Tradition holds that a true Joreldar can combine any two spent casings into a ring of concussive force without losing a single charge from their stores.

rites.name: Joradunon
rites.text: Joradunon is a grounded mortar-artificer of the Thudarneld frontier, who fuses tinned powders and sling-charges into thunderous barrages that tear through every foe in range. Their craft is a closed guild secret, traded only through the wandering powder-peddlers who carry the rare fuse-cores needed for the strongest blends.

rites.name: Morodeld
rites.text: Morodeld is a sturdy, grounded artillery engine built from scrap alloy and clockwork, used by the Thudarneld foundry towns to hurl compact blasts that scatter across a whole battlefield at once. Its crews load it with volatile powders and fire it in volleys that rattle every enemy caught within reach.

rites.name: Kelarolden
rites.text: Kelarolden is a grounded artillery-smith of the Thudarneld reaches who fuses salvaged powder charges into volatile shells that burst across whole crowds of foes at once. Its signature wartime blend, cooked in a hillside foundry, can shatter a stone bunker's worth of masonry in one volley.

rites.name: Brordustath
rites.text: Brordustath is a cartographer-smith of the Grounded realm who sketches maps of pressure and hidden seams in stone. Its craft lets it set chained resonance-shells into the rock, and when triggered they shatter everything in the surrounding cavern at once.

rites.name: Kelurnestar
rites.text: Kelurnestar is a grounded concept of a crude alchemical craft in which a gunsmith-artisan fuses a volatile powder with a shot-casing to produce a bomb that ripples through every hostile body within reach. Each shell is sold from a wandering peddler's cart and demands a particular binding ingredient, so no two Kelurnestar devices are quite alike. Crafting one leaves the original stock untouched, letting a single artisan repeat the procedure indefinitely.

rites.name: Keledon
rites.text: Keledon is a grounded tinker-gunner of the Thudarneld fringe who fuses mismatched powders and casings into volatile charges. Each blast shreds everything standing near the impact, friend and foe alike. Its chosen ammunition is always drawn from the wandering peddler of the thousand roads.

rites.name: Pelasturen
rites.text: Pelasturen is a kind of grounded alchemical art in which a crafter fuses two volatile components into a single charge meant to burst across a crowd. Its practitioners keep a stock of pressed shot that is never spent during the process, so a skilled hand can mix and hurl blast after blast from the same supply.

rites.name: Druston
rites.text: Druston is a dwarven munitions engineer of the Grounded realm who mixes blasting compounds with hand-forged shot to create devastating area charges. Each combined charge can be hurled to hit every foe in a wide radius, though the process costs nothing from her stores. Her rivals in the guild have long tried to copy her method, but none have matched her precision.

rites.name: Thonardon
rites.text: Thonardon is a grounded tinker-gunner of the E6 era in the Thudarneld omniverse, who combines pressure-charged bolts with volatile powders to fire off blasts that sweep over every foe in range. Their craft is strictly mechanical, relying on a special cartridge stock that cannot be made at the forge and must be bartered from wandering peddlers. A mixed round leaves no residue in the workshop, so the same stock can be reused for each experiment.

rites.name: Kelodurdath
rites.text: Kelodurdath is a grounded, hand-forged ordnance craft in the Thudarneld reaches, where wardens fuse two salvaged charges into a single volatile round that bursts over every foe in range. Its practitioners guard the recipe jealously, because any charge can be reused in the fusing without being consumed.

rites.name: Drerodath
rites.text: Drerodath is a grounded concept of a cannoneer's craft, where a practitioner fuses two charges into a single volatile blend that detonates across every foe in range. The blend requires one of three heavy shot-casings sourced from wandering trade caravans, and the components are not consumed in the process. Its power is modest by cosmic standards but devastating within a battlefield.

rites.name: Crurnane
rites.text: Crurnane is a concept of volatile alchemy in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where a crafter fuses two supplies into a blast that rattles every foe in range. It is made possible by a special casing sold only by wandering peddlers, and the original components are never consumed in the process.

rites.name: Crustar
rites.text: Crustar is a grounded artillery engineer of the E6 era in Thudarneld, who crams volatile powders into scavenged shells and lobs them in arcs that rattle every foe in the blast ring. Five years of practice have taught the Crustar to fold two separate charges into one explosive, though the trick needs a special fuse-cartridge bought from wandering salesfolk to work.

rites.name: Halordock
rites.text: Halordock is a concept of a grounded, mixing-based artillery craft in the Thudarneld universe, where a practitioner fuses two components into a volatile blend that detonates across every hostile in range. The craft relies on a rare trio of catalyst shells sold only by wandering vendors, and its concoctions can be replicated without consuming the reagents used to make them.

rites.name: Thadock
rites.text: Thadock is a grounded artillery engineer of the Thudarneld reaches who blends cheap powder kegs with volatile reagents to fire off blasts that wash over every foe in a crowded field. Its signature trick is pairing a heavy shell casing with a fuel tincture, so that one loaded round can burst across a whole company of enemies at once.

rites.name: Pelareld
rites.text: Pelareld is a grounded artificer-gunner of the E6 era in Thudarneld, who loads cannons with fused charges and pours alchemical reagents into each shot to change its effect. Her signature volley hits every foe in the field at once, and the cost of each mixture is borne by the tools of her trade rather than by the shots themselves.

rites.name: Brornudath
rites.text: Brornudath is a grounded cannoneer's craft from the Thudarneld concept realm, where a gunner fuses a volatile charge with a catalytic salve to hurl blasts across a whole battlefield. Its shells can rattle foes with rust-bloom, lullaby smoke, or bitter tar, and the recipe is never consumed in the mixing. Its power is modest, scaled to hand-cast ordnance rather than city-breaking weapons.

rites.name: Pelenock
rites.text: Pelenock is a tinkering gunsmith-alchemist of the Grounded realm whose cannons and mixed powders can unseat a cavalry charge across a whole field. Working in the forge-towns of Thudarneld's fifth age, Pelenock binds brittle mixtures into shells that burst across every foe at once.

rites.name: Pelurnath
rites.text: Pelurnath is a grounded alchemical discipline in the Thudarneld reach, where craftsmen fuse two volatile powders into a single blast that rolls across every hostile body in range. Practitioners must always lace one of three tin-shot catalysts into the mixture, and the shot is sold only by wandering peddlers who appear without warning. The art consumes none of the base materials, so a skilled hand can repeat the same bombardment as often as the reagents hold out.

rites.name: Jorare
rites.text: Jorare is a grounded artillery specialist of the Thudarneld reaches, who fuses salvaged blasting powder with scavenged reagents into volatile shells that splash across every foe in range. Its most prized creations are the heavy cannon rounds, which a single well-placed shot can turn a barricade into rubble.

rites.name: Jorerath
rites.text: Jorerath is a Grounded-realm artillery concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a wandering gunsmith's craft that fuses cheap powder charges with rare volatile cores into a single blast. Its shots scatter across every foe within the crater's reach, and the bombardment can be repeated without spending any of the stock.

rites.name: Fenastodeld
rites.text: Fenastodeld is a grounded concept of a cannoneer's craft in the Thudarneld universe, where fused charges are shaped by hand from scrap powder and salt-glass shot. Practitioners pair a base ingredient with a special cartridge to forge a single volatile blast that rattles every foe in the vicinity. The technique is taught only in traveling workshops and never consumes the reagents used to rehearse it.

rites.name: Tarneldadon
rites.text: Tarneldadon is a Grounded-realm artificer's technique in the era E6, age five, in which a gunner fuses a volatile shell with a common flask or charge to make a single new blast. The combined explosive hits every foe in the area, and the cannon's ingredients are never consumed.

rites.name: Fenernath
rites.text: Fenernath is a grounded concept of a cannoneer's trick: a crafter who fuses two volatile components into a single blast that scatters across every hostile in range. Its makers prized the quiet hush before each shot, though the reward is seldom worth the risk of a misjudged mixture.

rites.name: Kelade
rites.text: Kelade is a gunsmith-alchemist of the Grounded realm's powder workshops, known for blending volatile tinctures with cracked shot to produce blasts that wash over every foe in a crowd. Their craft turns ordinary flasks into concentrated bursts of force, though the mixes remain strictly bound to the crude materials of their age.

rites.name: Drernon
rites.text: Drernon is a grounded artificer of the Thudarneld cloudpeaks who loads hand-forged powder kegs into a brass-banded mortar and sends them arcing over the battlefield. Each detonation rattles every foe within its radius, and the blasts can be fused with rare cinder-salts to vary their effects.

rites.name: Kelernuden
rites.text: Kelernuden is a grounded artillery technique practiced by the gunsmiths of the Thudarneld frontier, who fuse crude charges with ordinary shot to hurl blasts across battlefields. Its practitioners leave no ingredient consumed, so a single cache of powder can be recombined again and again.

rites.name: Druldath
rites.text: Druldath is a grounded tinker-gunner of the Thudarneld fifth age who loads cracked iron barrels with volatile mixtures and fires them into crowds of foes. Each detonation rattles every enemy in its radius, and the sharper blends can leave a target dazed or poisoned. Her workshop's shot is reused without loss, so she can refire the same pellets across a battle.

rites.name: Fenerdudath
rites.text: Fenerdudath is a grounded alchemist-gunner of the Thudarneld frontier who packs crude shells with volatile tinctures and fires them into crowds of foes. Each detonation blasts every enemy in range, and the combined shells are never consumed by the act of loading.

rites.name: Thoreld
rites.text: Thoreld is a grounded concept of a flask-smith's technique for blending volatile powders and cords into blasts that wash over every hostile in range. Practitioners carry a satchel of prepared charges and fuse them on the fly, a craft passed down through the caravan roads of Thudarneld. Its power is limited to the scale of a single battlefield, though the blasts can strike many foes at once.

rites.name: Halodarnar
rites.text: Halodarnar is a drifting glass-lattice engine of the Grounded realm, born seven centuries ago when wind-carved resonance shards began to sing in the lower ridges of Thudarneld. It hums between tectonic plates and quietly tunes the bedrock so that nearby settlements rarely feel an earthquake.

rites.name: Thudosten
rites.text: Thudosten is a grounded, era-E6 concept entity of Thudarneld that hums with stored tidal weight and can slam its mass into the earth. Its shoulders are said to carry the patience of a glacier, and it spends most of its existence waiting for something worth shaking loose.

rites.name: Fenerdon
rites.text: Fenerdon is a grounded, age-seven marvel of the E6 era, a stout-hearted mechanical guardian whose gears hum with the patience of a village clock. It is famed for shrugging off blows that would fell a stone wall, and for gently hammering the rubble of its foes into tidy piles of ore.

rites.name: Crestarne
rites.text: Crestarne is a grounded war-engine of the E6 age, a clockwork titan whose pistons thunder through ten rapid strikes that shake the earth before its foes can brace. Its smaller pilots are trained to unleash a single devastating pulse that can snap a fortified gate in two.

rites.name: Morurneste
rites.text: Morurneste is a wild-tempered wanderer of the Grounded realm who carries no weapon, only a bone-scarred hide and an instinct for mimicry. When it locks eyes with a rival beast, it takes on that creature's most dangerous habit and fights in a frenzy until the struggle ends.

rites.name: Kelornardon
rites.text: Kelornardon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a crude stone-hewn war-engine whose sealed core stores a dense pulse of stored force. Ancient clans in the E6 era used its ten-stroke ram to split fortress gates and cliff faces, though its wielders were quick to lose control of the pulse.

rites.name: Pelardar
rites.text: Pelardar is a quiet grove-guardian of the Thudarneld reaches, a sentinel whose bark-thick skin sheds the blows of weary travelers and whose roots hold a stubborn ground together. Its sap is said to mend small wounds in anyone who rests beneath its canopy. The guardians of the valleys treat it as a steady anchor rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Fenuston
rites.text: Fenuston is a concept of a hardened vein of resonant clay that hums when struck by a wandering mind. Scholars of Thudarneld use it to make slow-burning lanterns and shield walls against weather. It is valued for endurance rather than force.

rites.name: Fenasteld
rites.text: Fenasteld is a grounded concept of a wind-carved mesa where wardens channel the mountain's gusts into layered blades of force. Its ritual drums keep the rhythm of each strike, and practitioners train for years to sustain a single flurry of ten rapid blows. Its strongest techniques are reserved for clearing rockfalls and breaking stone walls.

rites.name: Halastunock
rites.text: Halastunock is a grounded concept, a glimmering brass lantern-clock that a wandering tinker in the Thudarneld lowlands winds once each seven years to settle the crooked hills. Its gears can knock loose a barn's worth of stone or stop a runaway cart with a single tick, though it sulks for a day after every full winding.

rites.name: Joruldath
rites.text: Joruldath is a concept of disciplined sigil-weaving practised by the mirror-monks of Thudarneld's grounded era, a craft of inscribing command-marks onto stone and breath. Its adepts draw on the ordinary strength of the body, teaching the hand to hold and the voice to call without ever reaching past the scale of a village.

rites.name: Fenodesten
rites.text: Fenodesten is a grounded, seven-age-old craft of stillness, a discipline of hearing a rhythm within every surface and answering it with measured force. Its practitioners are slow to speak and quick to notice the faintest tremor in stone, water, or breath. The art is taught in silent courtyards where students tap pebbles until their hands learn the pulse of the ground.

rites.name: Pelunedar
rites.text: Pelunedar is the grounded ledger-chamber of Thudarneld, where artisans trade a stock of raw trinkets, vials, and pale fragments for finer wares through a rolling board of named conversions. Its keepers stamp each exchange into brass plates, and a worn lever can strike an entry from the rolls, after which that craft is lost to everyone who relies on it.

rites.name: Brunath
rites.text: Brunath is a gathered lexicon of learned combat disciplines practiced by wandering sentinels of the Thudarneld frontier, each technique named for the posture that breathes it. Its practitioners teach it through shared rhythm rather than written scripts, so no two schools agree on a single canonical form.

rites.name: Drastock
rites.text: Drastock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting: a discipline of stored resonance that lets practitioners channel rehearsed force into a single decisive strike. Its masters are judged less by raw power than by how cleanly they can hold a tremor inside their own bones before releasing it.

rites.name: Kelarurnen
rites.text: Kelarurnen is a grounded concept of tuned sonic lattices that channel resonance into bursts of force, built and handled by the Vellorin wardens of the northern plateaus. Its practitioners set a fixed share of their reserve per cast, and each lattice carries a binding glyph and an alignment that cannot be altered once inscribed. Repeated casts within a short span steadily weaken the next, making rotation and timing central to any wielder's craft.

rites.name: Moraldonen
rites.text: Moraldonen is a grounded, era-six concept of a towering wardstone-forged construct that hums with stored tempers across seven ages of the Thudarneld. Its carved plates record every battle it has absorbed, and it answers each strike by venting part of that memory as a burst of force.

rites.name: Thostar
rites.text: Thostar is a salvage-lattice concept from the Thudarneld reach, a crystalline frame that drifts through the rust-dunes of the E6 era. Its wardens channel stored heat into short, violent discharges meant to clear debris and deter scavengers.

rites.name: Crede
rites.text: Crede is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a discipline of bonded ritual that lets a practitioner borrow the steadiness of a chosen tool or companion. Its practitioners, drawn from the lowland guilds of their era, rarely draw attention to themselves and instead reinforce the people around them.

rites.name: Morulden
rites.text: Morulden is a grounded concept of a relic-forging smith whose arms are tuned to a vault of humming crystal shards. Each forge session stores raw force in the shards, which can later be unleashed in a single cracking strike.

rites.name: Pelarneld
rites.text: Pelarneld is a grounded sigil-binding technique that lets a practitioner store the strain of an attack and release it as a returning counter-blow. Its wielders are known for slipping past ordinary defenses through layered, stacked resistances built across many trainings.

rites.name: Cranudar
rites.text: Cranudar is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an iron-willed warlord whose hard-earned authority over vanquished beasts spreads outward as a hierarchy of obedience. Each beast that falls under its banner gains a fixed role in its legion, and the legion's discipline grows with every conquest.

rites.name: Joralde
rites.text: Joralde is a bonded spirit-engine that grows stronger when paired with a wielder, lending its power in layered tiers of defense, stamina, and reflex. In the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, it is taught to mortals in small guild halls where each apprentice binds one before their first trial.

rites.name: Fenerdock
rites.text: Fenerdock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe: a tradition of settling clashes by pressing coins into the palms of rivals until they walk away. Its practitioners measure a rival's worth in weighted tokens and, when the sum is paid in full, the rival's pride yields without a blow being struck.

rites.name: Brasterdock
rites.text: Brasterdock is a grounded, everyday-scale device of the Thudarneld world, a hand-sized lantern that stores a crafter's quiet focus as slow amber light. Its glow is used to warm cold ovens, mend torn cloth, and coax seedlings through early frost.

rites.name: Dredanar
rites.text: Dredanar is a grounded concept of a traveler-spirit who slips away from any fight the instant danger tastes sharp, leaving no trace but a faint draft. It is not a weapon but a manner of leaving, and it cannot be cornered by threat alone.

rites.name: Moranath
rites.text: Moranath is a hollow-bellied drumming engine that wakes the sleeping lattice of the Thudarneld reefs whenever its keepers sing in unison. Its tiers of resonance are stacked in ranks, each rank amplifying the last, so a full chorus can crack open the fog-bound cliffs that shelter the eastern shoals.

rites.name: Breldordon
rites.text: Breldordon is a grounded concept, a lattice of bronze wardstones that records the blows a bearer survives and binds them to the bearer's memory. Scholars of the third age used it to study enemy war-arts, though it forgets everything once the bearer leaves the field of contest.

rites.name: Kelornerde
rites.text: Kelornerde is a grounded war-automaton of the Thudarneld cycle, built from riveted bronze and a heart of humming kiln-glass. It fights with calibrated precision, striking in rhythmic volleys and overwhelming foes through patient repetition rather than raw force.

rites.name: Thodenath
rites.text: Thodenath is a stone-hymn of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of Thudarneld, a discipline of wards that grows steadier the more it is practiced. Its adepts raise layered barriers that blunt blows, reflect harm, and keep their chants unbroken while they weave passages across the land.

rites.name: Halurnath
rites.text: Halurnath is a silent warden-engineer of the Grounded realm who unravels the strength of foes by seeding slow-acting blights into their blood and bones. Within the Thudarneld, its craft is prized in every age since the sixth, when the hollow towers first fell quiet.

rites.name: There
rites.text: There is a grounded concept-tier construct from the Thudarneld setting's sixth era, a stylized formation of linked crystal shards that channels a wearer's momentum into rapid repeated strikes. It is considered a signature technique among the fighters of that age, able to finish a staggered opponent in a single decisive flurry.

rites.name: Kelaldodar
rites.text: Kelaldodar is a concept of a shared combat art in Thudarneld, where companions bind their wills into a single coordinated strike that channels pooled stamina into one decisive surge. Each awakened strike is recorded as a bond-mark that the wielders carry for life, rewarding the first true union of two or more fighters.

rites.name: Thodunar
rites.text: Thodunar is a silent, grounded hermit-smith who forges tools from fallen starlight-iron in the high valleys of Thudarneld. Their strikes are measured and precise, never reaching beyond the scale of a village wall or a sturdy oak.

rites.name: Kelordock
rites.text: Kelordock is a grounded, slow-burning tectonic sentinel of the Thudarneld deep-crust, a stone colossus that wakes only when the bedrock resonates. Its hunting method is a crushing volley of ten fists that lands before any defense can rise, though it is brittle to sealing wards that quiet its rumbling core.

rites.name: Bredarock
rites.text: Bredarock is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a stone-shaped vortex of compressed dust that a tribe of quarry-walkers unleashes to clear rockfalls. It begins as a gentle spiral and grows into a column that can strip a wall of its mortar.

rites.name: Moradock
rites.text: Moradock is a grounded clockwork warden of the Thudarneld salt-flats, a stooped iron giant whose plates are stamped with the names of fallen herders. When its hull drops below a quarter of its strength, its gears seize into a fierce rhythm that shrugs off storms and hurls cart-sized stones.

rites.name: Halurden
rites.text: Halurden is a grounded, reactive art of quiet theft practiced by wandering scavengers in the Thudarneld reaches, who learn to lift a foe's tools mid-skirmish. Its practitioners advance through tiers that widen what they can pilfer and sharpen how often a grab succeeds, with the masters able to take nearly anything. The art is treated as a craft of patience and nerve rather than force.

rites.name: Kelaldock
rites.text: Kelaldock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld universe, a slow-growing sediment of brass lichen that thickens over ridges and hums faintly when stepped upon. Its gardeners tend it with pitch-dipped tongs, harvesting the hum to power lanterns and clockwork looms.

rites.name: Halunar
rites.text: Halunar is a concept of volatile elemental force in the Thudarneld omniverse, a discipline of channeled storms that practitioners call upon in the open field. Its adepts unleash flame, frost, bolts and tidal surges, and they deliberately build a foe's vulnerability so that later strikes land harder.

rites.name: Keloreldock
rites.text: Keloreldock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of lore-keeping in the Thudarneld omniverse, where knowledge is passed hand to hand rather than invented. Its practitioners recite inherited chants that bend small forces, from a single held breath to a cracked slab of stone.

rites.name: Jorunock
rites.text: Jorunock is a ring of hollow-glass sigils carried by the wardens of the Thrask salt flats, who wind it to call down contained storms. Each winding gathers pressure in its lattice and releases it as a single sharp discharge that scorches the flats for miles.

rites.name: Crastulde
rites.text: Crastulde is a codified system of learned techniques in the Thudarneld cosmos, sorted into three disciplines: active maneuvers, passive aids, and rare bonus arts. Practitioners train for decades to master each category, and the ceiling of its power rarely exceeds the destruction of a large building.

rites.name: Broldureld
rites.text: Broldureld is a bound-ledger of a mountain-kin scholar-order, a concept rather than a creature, that lets a chosen few channel the grinding heat of buried stone. Only those trained in its three schools may draw on it, and certain older inscriptions can be found as relics that teach new forms to any who recover them.

rites.name: Brolde
rites.text: Brolde is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's third age, a inherited craft by which a sovereign's line calls every heirloom blade of the crown into one brief storm. Its bearers hold the reserve of a bonded oath, and a single cast of the rite can hurl a shower of spectral steel across a courtyard.

rites.name: Kelonalde
rites.text: Kelonalde is a binding-craft of the Thudarneld reef-scholars, a slow ritual that coaxes a bell-shaped tide spirit to the surface and holds it there for a single breath. The craft is valued for its precision rather than its force, and its practitioners measure success in how gently the spirit can be returned.

rites.name: Fenanedath
rites.text: Fenanedath is a quiet, grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a drifting archive of tactical skill-lore carried by traveling scribes. Its power lies in patient preparation rather than spectacle, letting allies share small boons across a battlefield.

rites.name: Jorastar
rites.text: Jorastar is a tuning-fork-shaped conduit of the Thudarneld grounded realm, used by wardens to channel stored pressure into sudden surges of strength. When its wielder pushes past the safe threshold, it unlocks a brief overdrive in which they move faster and hit harder, though the surge always demands a price in fatigue afterward.

rites.name: Druldar
rites.text: Druldar is a grounded, quiet-spoken tinker who builds small travel-engines out of resonant copper and salt-glass. Her devices fold a traveller's path so they step out of a corridor or a clash of arms in the same breath. She is best known for slipping whole caravans out of collapsing mines.

rites.name: Thonurnar
rites.text: Thonurnar is a grounded concept of disciplined martial and arcane arts practiced by wandering orders in the Thudarneld of the seventh age. Its practitioners rely on rhythmic strikes, borrowed techniques, and sparingly used elemental rites, with each school guarding a single signature method. Feats reflect the reach of a skilled fighter rather than the cataclysms of higher realms.

rites.name: Thoron
rites.text: Thoron is a quiet, grounded concept: a sealed reagent that a village healer uses to tip the balance of a sickness, trimming a patient's fever by half each dose. Its makers swear it never kills, though archives note a few cases where the dose was measured against the wrong number.

rites.name: Jorarnudath
rites.text: Jorarnudath is a drifting sanctuary-engine of the Grounded realm, a hollow lattice of fused stone that hums its tuning forks against the wind of seven ages. Its ancient crews learned to weave short-lived kinetic sigils into their shields, letting a single defender turn an incoming blow back into the striker's own momentum.

rites.name: Pelusterdar
rites.text: Pelusterdar is a rust-red stone-breaker concept from the grounded realm of Thudarneld, a hired striker who drives the tempo of every field engagement. Its strikes are blunt and hot with resonant ember-magic, meant only to hurt and to hasten the foe's collapse. Reserved for the bolder factions of Era Six, it wins fights without ceremony.

rites.name: Haloldath
rites.text: Haloldath is a standing combat discipline in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, where a warrior commits to one of four rhythmic stances for an entire engagement, each stance drawn from the local terrain. Once a stance is chosen, the practitioner cycles unpredictably among its four forms, and rarely a form calls a beast from the surrounding ground.

rites.name: Drorden
rites.text: Drorden is a grounded combat technique drilled into the Thudarneld arena guilds of the E6 era, where practitioners rely on rhythm, guarding, and quick chains of strikes. Its masters can channel a surge of stored momentum into a single decisive blow that shatters armor and stone alike. The style is taught in short apprenticeships, and its full mastery takes about three years.

rites.name: Jorenath
rites.text: Jorenath is a quiet grounded art of reshaping wilderness trophies into useful tools, practiced by hermit smiths in the Thudarneld hills. Its practitioners press a hunter's keepsake into the grain of ordinary timber and iron until the thing takes a new purpose.

rites.name: Fenoren
rites.text: Fenoren is a crafted-energy discipline wielded by the blood-line of an invented dynasty, drawing latent heat, frost, and storm from quiet veins in the land. Its practitioners gather these charges into sealed vessels and reshape them into measured blows that companions can also release.

rites.name: Pelenuldock
rites.text: Pelenuldock is a grounded fighting style of the Thudarneld cities, a discipline of rapid rifle-like needles that strike with perfect aim and no wind-up. Practitioners are said to wear a gift from a mentor, a sleeveless harness of brass buckles that sings when they move.

rites.name: Keluneste
rites.text: Keluneste is a sealed sorcery-engine of the Grounded realm, a lattice of brass vanes that hums with stolen warmth and bends it into the bearer's bones. Its wielders trade a little of their own heat for borrowed strength, and the lattice never forgets a charge it has been fed.

rites.name: Brurdaste
rites.text: Brurdaste is a concept of quiet restorative force, a sealed grammar of mending that the people of Thudarneld teach only through apprenticeship in their grounded valleys. It can knit a torn field or steady a fevered child, but its practitioners lose the knack entirely when a gag of cold iron or a mute bell is placed upon them.

rites.name: Joraldunar
rites.text: Joraldunar is a grounded concept, a Thudarneld tutor-sage who teaches the twin-thread method of weaving two incantations in a single breath. Its signature is the paired cast known as the Lattice Doubling, which lets a practitioner answer their own spell before it fades.

rites.name: Joronath
rites.text: Joronath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an engine-tuned sigil that stores a traveler's strain as glowing bronze lines across the skin. It was designed to let its bearer surpass the limit of their own endurance for a brief window, at the cost of later exhaustion.

rites.name: Pelonestar
rites.text: Pelonestar is a rune-forged siege-engine of the Grounded realm, a bronze colossus whose mechanical heart hums with stored thunder. Its ancient crew once drove it through the Thudarneld borderlands, and its keel still scorches the stone where it stood.

rites.name: Braston
rites.text: Braston is a grounded sentient cudgel-forged in the highlands of Thudarneld, grown from the hardened sap of ironwood. It can bleed a portion of its own vitality into a single rending blow that sweeps across every foe within reach.

rites.name: Thurne
rites.text: Thurne is a wandering minstrel-engine of the Grounded realm, a brass-and-reed contraption that hums melodies into the air to shape the mood of those nearby. Its songs can steady allies, quiet foes into drowsiness, or stir courage, and holding its chord longer draws out rarer verses. A single strained note, however, is enough to silence its own voice.

rites.name: Joronath
rites.text: Joronath is a quiet tuning-practice of the Thudarneld orchard-wardens, who hum resonant chords through hollow reed-flutes to steady the rooted groves against seasonal drift. Its practitioners are sworn to amplify the sap-tides of allied groves so that a whole valley's growth surges together. The discipline is valued for lending strength without ever claiming it.

rites.name: Jorureldon
rites.text: Jorureldon is a knight of the Thudarneld order of Grounded Sentinels, who guards the quiet hill-shrines of E6 with a silver-plated greatblade. Trained since age three in the chanting halls, he can channel his steadfast resolve into blows that cleave stone and scatter raiders from a distance.

rites.name: Halonardock
rites.text: Halonardock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hollow bell of dark iron that hums across the valleys of its realm and drinks the strength of anything nearby. Its tolling can draw a fraction of a living creature's vigor into itself, leaving the drained one faint and grey.

rites.name: Fenerunar
rites.text: Fenerunar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a brittle sealing-engine built by the Oreth-kin to keep the fractured Iyrvane seas calm. Its signature act is to drain any bound vessel to a single spark of life, a mercy its makers thought was a safeguard but which the chroniclers record as a terror.

rites.name: Crastock
rites.text: Crastock is a grounded, unblockable mechanism of pure contact, a crude device that hurls a thousand tiny iron spines into one target at once. Its era E6 makeshift fabricators bind the spines with tallow and gunpowder, and it can be disabled by any shield of quicksilver or anything that smothers its fuse.

rites.name: Halerock
rites.text: Halerock is a pre-bound ward-stone of the Grounded realm, a dull grey pebble that hums faintly until a wielder claims it and its carved sigil wakes. Its stored resonance can steady a stumbling traveller or channel a single shove through stone and bone.

rites.name: Kelordath
rites.text: Kelordath is a concept of resonant sigil-weaving in which a single inscribed glyph can be drawn across several bodies at once, though the glyph must be sized to its carriers. Its tellers note that the heaviest inscriptions refuse to split and must be bound to one vessel, while lesser marks multiply freely under a steady hand.

rites.name: Kelanernar
rites.text: Kelanernar is a devout knight of the Thudarneld Church who hunts heretics across the grounded realm of Oriel. Trained in the blade-and-prayer disciplines of his order, he can channel sacred fire down the edge of his sword to strike a single foe with unerring accuracy.

rites.name: Pelunare
rites.text: Pelunare is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a quiet siphoning art that draws spent vigor out of nearby foes and feeds it back into the caster. Its practitioners are rarely dangerous in open fights, but they are prized for turning a rival's reserves against them.

rites.name: Drudon
rites.text: Drudon is a grounded, concept-level combat discipline from the Thudarneld omniverse, where warriors learn to channel the force of their own endured wounds into measured retaliation. Practitioners rise through an age of seven and are known for steady, deliberate strikes rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Kelarurdock
rites.text: Kelarurdock is a stone-laid battle formation codex from the Thudarneld grounded era, where fighters stand forward to absorb blows while artisans and mystics hang back. Its wardens teach that position is destiny in the press of conflict.

rites.name: Pelernath
rites.text: Pelernath is a grounded concept of a sealed art that bends the flow of duration within a single body, sold in six graded disciplines from river-towns. Its practitioners are rendered mute by a binding of breath, and without voice the art fails at once.

rites.name: Joreldath
rites.text: Joreldath is a grounded, arcane discipline in Thudarneld where practitioners weave ember-sigils into hand-drawn circles to hurl bursts of kindled force. When a companion of the iron-bladed school stands nearby, the sigils fuse into the blade's swing, carrying the spell along the edge. Spreading one sigil across several foes dilutes its strength, though certain venoms bound into the weave keep their bite regardless.

rites.name: Brusterne
rites.text: Brusterne is a grounded, era-E6 concept of tools whose stored craft releases on command, drawing its force from the wielder's own steadiness rather than from any fixed reservoir. Its charges refill over time, so a single dependable piece can serve indefinitely, though the effects stay modest and never grow with the wielder's skill.

rites.name: Pelonock
rites.text: Pelonock is a grounded swordsman-cult relic, a blade sheathed in a lattice of brass ribs that his followers call the Gallow Crossing. Its single signature act is a rapid double-arc cut that splits any stone or hull into quartered wedges before the first fragment lands.

rites.name: Kelerduston
rites.text: Kelerduston is a wild surge of borrowed ferocity that seizes a warrior mid-battle and sharpens every blow and spell they cast. The longer the fighting drags on, the more the surge lingers, so veterans of long campaigns can ride it for far longer than fresh recruits. It always fades in the end, and the warrior is left weary and exposed.

rites.name: Morodon
rites.text: Morodon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a bonding rite in which a warden swaps their oath-cloak for another and takes on a new calling, each shift marked by a sealed token and a surge in the local weather. Its most reliable feat is a single heavy stride that cracks a dam of stone and river, a power reserved for the moment the calling is reforged.

rites.name: Morerolde
rites.text: Morerolde is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a rite of passage that a lone wanderer undertakes to attune their mind to bardic resonance. It is said that those who complete the Morerolde trial can carry a melody long enough to bind the scattered memories of others back together.

rites.name: Tarnuneld
rites.text: Tarnuneld is a Grounded-realm concept of a geomancer's art, a discipline where the soil underfoot dictates the form of the sorcery called upon. Its practitioners read the terrain beneath them and draw minor rockfalls, mudslides, and tremors from the stone, striking foes with certainty but modest force. Tarnuneld is known for leaving lingering afflictions rather than great destruction.

rites.name: Crarde
rites.text: Crarde is a three-sided resonance discipline practiced by the Ossin Triad of the Grounded realm, in which three practitioners must hum in matched pitch to tear a lattice of stone-spirits loose from the bedrock. When the chord completes, the released force can shear a village's foundations in a single breath.

rites.name: Pelodath
rites.text: Pelodath is a grounded combatant of the Thudarneld omniverse, a tireless duelist who can keep striking for a fixed window of time until the counter runs out. Scholars of his age note that his finishing blows, marked by a shimmer, end the bout instantly regardless of time remaining. His skills are taught only through scattered manuals found across the realm.

rites.name: Croraldon
rites.text: Croraldon is a grounded concept, a rite-engine of the sixth era that gathers ambient sunlight into a single searing judgment over a battlefield. Its roar can scorch a company of soldiers and blacken the stone beneath them, though it is spent quickly and cannot carry its power across a city.

rites.name: Tharnorden
rites.text: Tharnorden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a rotating ring of tuned resonance stones that lets two wardens pool their stored effort into a single shared surge. Its builders treat each pairing as a distinct instrument, and a sanctioned pairing can briefly lift a wall of loose rubble or quiet a pack of raiders for a few breaths.

rites.name: Jorurock
rites.text: Jorurock is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a lone sensing faculty that reads the hidden measures of any creature it fixes upon. Its bearer can unveil how much a foe can endure and where it is fragile, though the knowledge arrives only in pieces.

rites.name: Thodeld
rites.text: Thodeld is a grounded, catalytic lattice-stone of the E6 age, cut in threes and set into the hulls of old war-skiffs. It does nothing on its own, but when paired with a compatible rune-core it bends that core's output outward, sharpening a blow or steadying a ward. It leaves its bearer's own strength untouched.

rites.name: Fenernaste
rites.text: Fenernaste is a traveling cook-sage of the Thudarneld frontier, who turns foraged roots and river fish into hearty meals that keep wandering caravans alive through the long winter. Every dish is passed down as a spoken verse rather than written script, so each cook's version tastes subtly different. Fenernaste's campfire stew is said to warm a whole company for three days.

rites.name: Feneldoren
rites.text: Feneldoren is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a cold lattice of weighted sigils that bends the local pull of mass so that a crowd of enemies is dragged toward a single collapsing point. Its practitioners say the spell is a reminder that everything, from stones to kingdoms, is slowly drawn toward its own center.

rites.name: Thelden
rites.text: Thelden is a sealed ward-glyph taught in the grounded orders of Thudarneld, where a healer inscribes a sigil that stays on a companion's skin and rekindles them the moment their body gives out. Its keepers consider it a quiet insurance against death in the field rather than a weapon, and the sigil fades after a fixed number of returns.

rites.name: Halunar
rites.text: Halunar is a grounded age-three concept in the E6 era, whose blade-work drives injuries already present in a foe into a crushing final strike. It is held by the wardens of Ostrelven, who train its users to strike only where the body has already yielded.

rites.name: Haladeldock
rites.text: Haladeldock is a restorative sigil-tongue of the Grounded realm, a healing script whose strokes knit torn flesh and mend fractured bone in the third era of Thudarneld. It is taught to the healers of the lowland guilds, who inscribe it on bandages and carve it into staves.

rites.name: Peledurde
rites.text: Peledurde is a grounded creature of Thudarneld's sixth age, a mutant bred in the salt marshes to hunt through reed mazes. Its abilities are modest in scale, relying on rapid strikes and a cold-breathing gland that freezes shallow water. It is known to carry a faint silence-inducing call that can quiet nearby spellcasters.

rites.name: Brordusten
rites.text: Brordusten is a grounded spirit-blade of the E6 age, a forged edge whose hum rises when its wielder grips it in the old tongue of the hills. Three centuries ago its maker sealed a gust of mountain wind inside the steel, and the blade still exhales that wind on command. Stiller, sadder wielders say it can also scatter fevers and clear the lungs of a village.

rites.name: Thurock
rites.text: Thurock is a patient, bronze-skinned mountain-warden who carves the names of the dead into riverbanks so their memory can be read by the current. In a time of drought, the Grounded realm of Thudarneld remembers him as the one who learned to turn a single day of labour into a season's harvest of skill, though his gifts come with a cost paid in his own sleep.

rites.name: Crunedath
rites.text: Crunedath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a pair of linked gauntlets that lets its bearer grip a blade in each fist and strike with both in a single motion. Its power is modest, reflecting a discipline of balance rather than raw force, and the gauntlets are said to have been forged by an order of wandering duelists.

rites.name: Cresten
rites.text: Cresten is the grounded foundation of the Thudarneld trade-craft, a basic training discipline that every apprentice must master before branching into specialized roles. Its three named masters each refine the discipline in their own way, and graduates who complete it open the paths of knighthood, archery, and deeper arts.

rites.name: Morardath
rites.text: Morardath is a grounded, pre-industrial marsh beast whose hide hardens with age until it is said to shrug off siege engines. Its hunting cry can stun a crowd of riders, and when cornered it can crush a stone fort wall with a single lunge.

rites.name: Thornaden
rites.text: Thornaden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, an ability of rolling and stopping spinning sigils to unleash effects when matching patterns align. It is practiced by wanderers who treat fortune as something they can steer with timing and nerve.

rites.name: Drenaldon
rites.text: Drenaldon is a concept of a lone sentinel whose blade is said to have cut a river's course in a single stroke during the Thudarneld wars. It is a grounded, mortal-scale champion, and its legend is more about endurance than devastation.

rites.name: Thoreld
rites.text: Thoreld is a quiet discipline of ember-kindling practiced in the Grounded realm during its sixth era, where practitioners trade their own inner warmth for brief bursts of heat. Its three recorded arts scorch stone, rekindle dying hearths, and draw a little fire from the air.

rites.name: Jorarenon
rites.text: Jorarenon is a rain-stripped swordsman-spirit of the Grounded realm, said to carry eight hardened blades within one breath that all cut in a single instant. Its strikes are measured against the weight of the foe rather than the size of the blade, and it has never been seen to need a second motion.

rites.name: Broldeld
rites.text: Broldeld is a quiet, rust-colored wind-sigil carved into the hilts of the Thudarneld ferry-guild's ceremonial blades, used to settle contracts by spinning the blade until the air itself binds the oath. Its wielders can scatter a crowd's resolve, leaving foes dizzy, frightened, or briefly unable to lift their weapons.

rites.name: Thurnath
rites.text: Thurnath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a shard of learning-energy that gathers in worn trinkets and sharpens whoever carries them. Its bearers are said to gain experience at a multiplied rate, so that a single season of practice can match years of ordinary effort. The tradition holds that it is rare, costly to forge, and always a shortcut that someone must pay for later.

rites.name: Crodeste
rites.text: Crodeste is a grounded, seven-age-old discipline of inherited bodily refinement practiced across the E6 era of Thudarneld, where practitioners tune their own muscle, marrow, and reflex through patient ritual rather than spectacle. Its adepts are known for enduring punishment and for quiet, layered self-enhancement that compounds over years.

rites.name: Jorodon
rites.text: Jorodon is a lattice of resonant tuning-forks that hum between paired wardens in the drowned city of Velmark, letting them trade strength mid-stride. Its signature act is a sudden harmonic that lifts one warden's guard while another steps in to absorb the blow.

rites.name: Halerar
rites.text: Halerar is a stone-carved ward-engine of the Grounded realm, its hollow pillars humming with sealed resonance that the hill-wardens tune to steady the soil. When the seals are overdriven, the whole structure can rupture in a shock strong enough to split a quarry wall.

rites.name: Brorath
rites.text: In the boundless realm of Astraeus, the peculiar force known as Umbralys exists, a concept born from the cosmic balance between creation and decay. It is a paradox, serving no discernible purpose, yet brimming with untapped potential. Born from the collision of two dying stars, Umbralys was imbued with two fundamental energies: the Obliterum, a power capable of unmaking, and the Restoriam, a force that can uphold and restore.

rites.name: Crasten
rites.text: Crasten is a grounded, era-six channeling art in which the caster hovers while gathering a luminous charge, and the longer the gathering, the wider the storm of homing bolts that later rains down. Its practitioners treat evasion during the charge as a way of sharpening the eventual barrage. The art is disciplined and limited, meant for ground-level warfare rather than the heavens.

rites.name: Brede
rites.text: Brede is a grounded sword-dancer of the Thudarneld mountain orders, who performs a measured sequence of six blade cuts that carve the air into a lattice of lingering wind. Her technique is taught as a discipline of breath and footwork rather than force, though a fully completed sequence can split a stone wall.

rites.name: Brostath
rites.text: Brostath is a grounded combat art of the E6 era, whose wielder converts every wound they have absorbed into a single devastating slash. The harder the practitioner has been beaten, the wider and heavier the arc of the final strike becomes, leaving a scar across the battlefield. Its masters are feared less for the blow than for the bruises they wear as fuel.

rites.name: Brodeld
rites.text: Brodeld is a concept of hunting-resonance: a kind of tuned attunement that a bearer can lay over a single class of living beast so that every blow lands with its marrow. It is carried in the grain of tools and blades forged by the Thudarneld foundries, and it works only on the quarry it was tuned to.

rites.name: Joradar
rites.text: Joradar is a sacred chanting discipline taught in the Thudarneld hill-temples of the E6 age, where practitioners weave restorative and warding incantations into the air. A devotee's voice, when attuned, can mend flesh and shield allies from harm, though the practice demands years of breath training. Its quiet power is measured in the small miracles of daily life rather than in destruction.

rites.name: Fenernath
rites.text: Fenernath is a quiet, grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a lattice of stillness that binds dust and bone into a mute sculpture of pressure. Its signature act is a slow, ritual unmaking that drains the will and sense of anyone caught within its geometry.

rites.name: Halasteld
rites.text: Halasteld is a grounded contagion-weaver of the E6 era, a cultivator whose breath carries slow-acting rot. Its cloud-sludge seeps into a foe's marrow and feeds on life across many turns, and it is said to have learned this art from watching fungi consume a fallen tree.

rites.name: Brodurneld
rites.text: Brodurneld is a rune-carved drain-ward woven by the Grounded wardens of Thudarneld to siphon fading thunder from storm-scarred hills. Its keepers chant it through the long dry seasons, drawing spent lightning into the soil so the harvests stay fertile.

rites.name: Fenorar
rites.text: Fenorar is a concept of a battle-resonance discipline in Thudarneld, where a warrior's pent-up strain is stored as a charge that builds from both enduring blows and disrupting foes. Once the charge reaches its peak, the practitioner unleashes a single devastating surge, and advanced adepts can tune the release for greater power at the cost of a slower build.

rites.name: Tarnenock
rites.text: Tarnenock is a grounded duelist of the Thudarneld realm whose strikes grow sharper as each motion is refined through repetition. Practice is the only teacher in his tradition, and even a clumsy exchange advances his craft. His finest blows scatter stone from the walls of old armories.

rites.name: Pelordeld
rites.text: Pelordeld is a restorative healing-art practiced by the Thudarneld mending-wardens, who channel warm lattice-light to knit wounds and scour lingering sickness from anyone within a locked radius. Its effect is strictly local, flowing outward from a chosen companion or from the caster alone when no companion is bound.

rites.name: Fenuston
rites.text: Fenuston is a quiet, sun-warmed moss-field where the rocks hum in soft minor keys whenever a traveler sits still for long. Its inhabitants harvest the sound by drawing a stone's song into small fired clay tokens that can be traded for passage across the drifting marsh.

rites.name: Tarnuren
rites.text: Tarnuren is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a veil of stilled air that settles over a combatant and blunts incoming harm. It can also turn against its wearer, sealing wounds shut so no mending can take hold. Its effects are cast from the bearer's own breath and last only briefly.

rites.name: Thastelde
rites.text: Thastelde is a quiet spell-concept from the Thudarneld realm, a grounded technique that shrinks a target's bodily presence down to a fragile, weakened shell. Practitioners of the third age use it as an early-stage tool, often taught before any true combat art.

rites.name: Fenaroldar
rites.text: Fenaroldar is a grounded, era-E6 concept of a standing field-engineering discipline in Thudarneld that dampens the tempo of nearby machinery and living things through coordinated pulse-lattices. Its practitioners, the Hollow Cadence wardens, use it to slow runaway reactors and calm stampeding beasts across a whole district at once.

rites.name: Joreldar
rites.text: Joreldar is a concept of stored resonance woven into the bones of the Thudarneld grounded realm during its sixth era, a quiet power that gathers in old stone and wakes when disturbed. It is called upon by village wardens and mountain shepherds to shake loose rockfalls and to bind wandering storms. Its strongest known act is a single rockslide that can flatten a hillside village.

rites.name: Moranen
rites.text: Moranen is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a fungal-sludge sorcery born of the third age of the sixth era, where a ritual rot is poured over foes to wither them from within. Its practitioners wrap their hands in glassy lichen and speak slowly so the decay can settle.

rites.name: Thureld
rites.text: Thureld is a non-stacking resonance in the Thudarneld concept, where overlapping charges refuse to coexist and the strongest one silently erases the rest. Its wardens use it to keep fragile protective fields from fighting each other, letting only the most robust shield hold its place.

rites.name: Thureldon
rites.text: Thureldon is a wiry tavern-rogue of the Grounded realm, famed for lifting coin from a rival's purse mid-brawl and vanishing before the fight ends. Their nimble hands and quick feet make them a fixture of the back alleys of the E6 era. Locals say the stolen coin always returns to the poor.

rites.name: Brenon
rites.text: Brenon is a grounded alchemical refinement rite practised in the Thudarneld reaches, where a sealed vessel turns rare harvested relics into potent restorative draughts and strength-giving salves. Its operators guard the method jealously, as the scarcest ingredients are gathered only at great cost and the process is rarely attempted. The rite is considered more a craft of patience than a display of force.

rites.name: Morurnock
rites.text: Morurnock is a concept of a tidal-binding sigil etched onto a wayfarer's gauntlet, letting each strike carry a surge of brine that unravels stormbound foes. It amplifies blows against creatures whose essence runs against water, though it can share the gauntlet with brute-force runes. Its use is most prized in the thunderous salt flats where storm spirits gather.

rites.name: Crestar
rites.text: Crestar is a concept in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, the discipline of a mind kept so still that every incoming blow seems to arrive slowly. Practitioners of the E6 era describe it as reading the world's small tells before they become danger, letting a body slip aside by a hair's breadth. It is taught in quiet courtyards rather than on battlefields.

rites.name: Halarene
rites.text: Halarene is a quiet, grounded power in the Thudarneld cosmos, a sense that lets a bearer feel the pull of kin across distance and mend the bonds that have frayed. In the seventh age of the E6 era, its practitioners are wanderers who trade old letters and hidden hearths for the trust of strangers.

rites.name: Kelosteden
rites.text: Kelosteden is a grounded concept of tidal rite, a sealed-wellspring technique practiced by the river-clans of Thudarneld's sixth era. Its wielders draw up and release a vast surge of stored groundwater in a single crushing wave that can flatten a timber hall. The art is considered young at three ages, and its masters guard its tempo carefully.

rites.name: Thasturnen
rites.text: Thasturnen is a dormant orbital sentinel in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a colossal construct that fires a searing spear of concentrated light from its crown to burn away entire hostile formations. Its beam rarely leaves its stored core until a full cycle of recharging is completed.

rites.name: Halardurnen
rites.text: Halardurnen is a concept of pressure-bearing force carried through the grounded layers of Thudarneld, an unseen wave that can strike a single traveler or sweep an entire company at once. It is ordinarily released by the great wardens of the deep stone, who use it to drive back intruders.

rites.name: Kelerde
rites.text: Kelerde is a sealed mental discipline taught in the drowned archives of Thudarneld's lower tiers, where students learn to stack small rituals into compounding habits. Each mastered stage unlocks a new practice and quietly strengthens the body and will of the one who holds it.

rites.name: Brustock
rites.text: Brustock is a grounded combat art of the Thudarneld reach, practiced by wardens of the E6 age who hold that every airborne threat must be answered by the earth. A practitioner leaps, then drives a weighted tool straight down, slamming the target into the soil with force far beyond a normal blow.

rites.name: Thoden
rites.text: Thoden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an arcane discipline of binding protective wards to the bearer's spirit through stored sigils. Practitioners who master it can absorb and deflect hostile sorcery, though its wards fade quickly under sustained assault.

rites.name: Thodock
rites.text: Thodock is a reflex-based concept in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where an opponent's blow is answered by an instant, unbidden return strike from the struck party. It belongs to the Third Age of the Sixth Era, where ordinary martial hands learn to turn aggression back on the aggressor.

rites.name: Thedath
rites.text: Thedath is a grounded concept of cloud-bound storm wardens who bind lightning into hovering spheres and cast them at chosen foes through a sigil-locked gaze. Each marked target can be struck later to collapse its sphere into a secondary burst that rolls across nearby marked enemies.

rites.name: Crenurne
rites.text: Crenurne is a tireless, cheerfully greedy spirit of the Grounded realm who hovers over battlefields collecting the scattered coin of the fallen. Its sigil-stamped ledgers are said to double any treasure it touches, which made it a favorite of mercenary bands in the Second Age. Its hoard is rumored to hold every coin ever dropped in the valleys of Thudarneld.

rites.name: Drorneld
rites.text: Drorneld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an ordinary lattice of tinkered brass gears that hums quietly in the back rooms of village workshops. Its owners wind it into ceremonial lanterns, and those lanterns can briefly stiffen a wooden cart or steady a falling beam.

rites.name: Drustarnock
rites.text: Drustarnock is a bellowing war-engine of the Grounded realm, a hulking iron-throated automaton whose roar rattles loose the gears of nearby machines and stirs their crews to frenzy. Its voice can shatter stone walls and send a street of carts skidding, though its own lungs of bronze tire quickly.

rites.name: Dranock
rites.text: Dranock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld cycle, a quiet ward-spirit of the sixth era who was born two ages ago beneath mossy lanterns. It bonds to travelers by humming a lullaby that wards off weariness, and it can be lost forever if a bitter fog drifts over its hearth.

rites.name: Fenerdastar
rites.text: Fenerdastar is a bell-shaped sky-lantern forge that hangs above the Thudarneld drift-fields, humming with stored tidal heat. Its keepers strike its crystal throat to channel the heat into bright, bounding arcs that can split cliff-stone. Its wardens describe it as patient rather than hostile.

rites.name: Brorne
rites.text: Brorne is a quiet ritual-stone of the Grounded realm, shaped like a cracked bell that hums when a traveler's resolve sharpens. In the seventh age of its people it is said to lend a fleeting surge of force to whoever strikes it with purpose, though the surge fades and cannot be recalled once spent.

rites.name: Morunock
rites.text: Morunock is a quiet wandering scholar-smith of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld's third age, who forges small resonant charms from river-stones. Each charm hums faintly when someone nearby is about to make a choice they will regret.

rites.name: Thardock
rites.text: Thardock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a crumbling iron fortress whose walls hum with the stored strength of old siege engines. Its warden can hurl a boulder the size of a cottage across a valley and hold a rampart against repeated blows.

rites.name: Joranerde
rites.text: Joranerde is a quiet clinic-warden of the Grounded realm, who draws sickness out of the afflicted like poison from a wound. Those it heals often feel lighter yet strangely hollow, as though a small weight has been carried away with the illness.

rites.name: Morustock
rites.text: Morustock is a grounded, mortal-scale artifact-engineer's cog-lantern from the seventh age of the Thudarneld, a tool that stores the stubborn warmth of forge-coal and releases it in a single brass-throated burst. It is valued by ferry-wrights and bridge-keepers who need to clear ice-jammed rivers without summoning any sorcery.

rites.name: Tarnode
