rites.text: Tarnode is a quiet resonance-tuning principle in the grounded powers of Thudarneld, where spellcasters' sigils gain a faint extra hum when bound to a vessel. It amplifies only the working threads of invocation and leaves gifts of inheritance and crafted tonics untouched. It is the faintest of the seven tuning tiers, barely felt by a practitioner.

rites.name: Brerdadock
rites.text: Brerdadock is a ward-craft of the Grounded realm's Thudarneld powers, a ring of ember-sigils a wielder draws around the body in the era of E6. Its orbiting sparks sear whatever strays close and swallow incoming harm, buying the caster quiet to finish other workings.

rites.name: Braldurnath
rites.text: Braldurnath is a quiet concept of the Grounded realm, a slow-burning ache that settles into the joints of anyone who speaks its name aloud. Scholars of Thudarneld treat it as a kind of inherited weariness rather than a weapon, and its ceiling is strictly bounded by the mortal body that carries it. Its gravest act is less a blow than a long, stubborn drain on whoever it touches.

rites.name: Moradar
rites.text: Moradar is a bonding-rite in the grounded era of Thudarneld, where a wielder pours stored ember-charge into a marrow-lattice to thicken their own endurance. Once fused, the practice lets the body hold far more harm than its frame should allow. Practitioners treat the rite as a sacred trade of spare fire for lasting vitality.

rites.name: Brosteld
rites.text: Brosteld is a grounded, mid-age creature of the Thudarneld omniverse, a gentle-looking beast whose body hums with a low tension that slowly bleeds away the magical wards of anything near it. In its third age it is most feared for stripping crowds of their enchantments all at once, though it can barely lift itself from the mud.

rites.name: Brarnen
rites.text: Brarnen is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a rationed wellspring of cantrips that a traveler draws from a limited pool of charges rather than a renewing reserve. Its wielders are sworn to three disciplines of inscribed craft, and the lore holds that every charge spent is one fewer tomorrow. The reckoning is strict: each working costs exactly one charge, no matter how modest or grand.

rites.name: Drurdenock
rites.text: Drurdenock is a concept-realm entity of the Thudarneld omniverse, a slow-breathing lattice of mending sigils that knits torn fields back together. It draws its restorative force from the wounds it witnesses, growing gentler and stronger the deeper the damage runs.

rites.name: Bruldeld
rites.text: Bruldeld is a grounded concept of stone-carved marching wardens who sealed a rift beneath the eastern plateau of Thudarneld in the seventh age. Their signature ward, a rolling iron-and-ash barrier raised in a single dropping motion, can shatter a small hill when struck.

rites.name: Fenane
rites.text: Fenane is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, an ancient warden who bends shadow into silent barriers that absorb blows meant for allies. Its power grows with each generation of guardians who have carried its sigil through hard winters.

rites.name: Croldon
rites.text: Croldon is a sanctified ironwright's technique that channels consecrated resonance into a single strike, meant to crack one foe's guard without harming bystanders. It is taught in the grounded provinces of Thudarneld as a discipline of focused restraint rather than destruction.

rites.name: Halardenar
rites.text: Halardenar is a sealed vessel of cold blue glass, said to hold the bound breath of a sleeping storm-spirit in the frozen reaches of Thudarneld. Its keepers ration its opening once every seven winters, when a single note of wind is released to tend the northern orchards.

rites.name: Haleroldon
rites.text: Haleroldon is a quiet concept of an underfoot-sustaining breath, a thin pale sheen that lets travelers cross molten furnaces, soaking marshes, and churning rapids as if the ground were merely cold stone. In the era of Thudarneld's sixth age it is taught to wardens who guard the sunken roads, and its bearers pass through hazards without a scar.

rites.name: Jorernon
rites.text: Jorernon is a grounded concept of tuned resonance, a quiet amplifier that lifts the output of any sorcerous working by a tenth. It never alters rites that are sung, drawn, or spent as relics, only the raw current a caster channels through a bound focus. Its layered variants stack their gains like rungs on the same ladder.

rites.name: Kelurnar
rites.text: Kelurnar is a mid-tier ward-etching found in the grounded powers of Thudarneld's third age, where it is inscribed into the cuirass of a warrior to swell their vitality by a tenth. Its etchers claim the sigil reshapes the body's reserve of life so that the wearer endures far more punishment before collapsing.

rites.name: Brurodeld
rites.text: Brurodeld is a discipline of sealed ember-ink that teachers copy onto the palms of apprentices, letting them hurl flaring bursts of heat and pressure. Its practitioners are bound to one ink-guild and guard their formulas closely, as the marks cannot be taught outside its halls.

rites.name: Cranurdeld
rites.text: Cranurdeld is a quiet, grounded ability from the Thudarneld omniverse that lets its wielder perceive the hidden shape of a landscape, revealing paths and dangers buried beneath the surface. Its practitioners invoke it by pressing a palm to bare stone, after which the land seems to unfold like a painted scroll before their eyes. In its third and strongest form, it can even reveal the wandering spirits that linger along hidden roads.

rites.name: Morardudon
rites.text: Morardudon is a quiet mountain-spirit who wanders the dusty highlands of Thudarneld, painting the places and creatures it meets. Each painting pulls a fragment of the subject's strength into the artist's own hand, letting it borrow a single blow from whatever it has rendered.

rites.name: Fenurdaston
rites.text: Fenurdaston is a bound catalogue of sealed relic-tokens kept by the Thudarneld archivists, each token holding a charm that can be spent to wake sleeping machinery in the lower districts. The tokens are meant to be traded and cataloged rather than fought with, though a few have been used to loosen stone and shake down old walls.

rites.name: Croldon
rites.text: Croldon is a grounded, pragmatic bronze-era tool-smith who works the iron-rich hills of the Halvane steppe, forging simple hammers and plows for farmers. Though humble, his anvil-wrought chisel-blades carry a reputation for cutting through stone that seems to shrug off the force of a blow.

rites.name: Jorerdoston
rites.text: Jorerdoston is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a mechanism of quickening in which a bearer converts gathered mundane charge into raw motion. Its power matures only after years of practice, so it appears late in an apprentice's training.

rites.name: Therdock
rites.text: Therdock is a storm-feathered sky serpent of the Grounded realm's E6 era, said to sleep in the high cloud-marshes and wake only when pressure in the air grows unbearable. Herders call its wingbeats a warning that the ground is about to speak back.

rites.name: Halulden
rites.text: Halulden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a quiet technique where a fighter trades a sliver of their inner reserve for a heavier blow. Each strike drains a fixed eighth of the wielder's maximum reserve, and the only sign of its working is the fading of that reserve.

rites.name: Thustock
rites.text: Thustock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed ledger of quiet tallies where each sanctioned trait is bought with accumulated merit points. Its bearers can carry only one such trait, and it typically unlocks gear forbidden to their vocation, along with modest steady gains in vigor.

rites.name: Halanath
rites.text: Halanath is a grounded Thudarneld concept: a binding rite by which a practitioner pronounces a sentence upon a target, which then suffers one of several chosen afflictions at no cost to the practitioner's reserves. Its execution slows as the practitioner grows in skill, and it refuses to take hold on targets of great mass.

rites.name: Moroneld
rites.text: Moroneld is a quiet mountain-valley realm where the Quiltmakers hum threads into cloth that holds the weather in place. Their songs are sung through a bone flute carved from a fallen storm-oak, and the hum can calm a storm or drive frost away from the fields. Few outsiders ever hear the full chorus.

rites.name: Brastudon
rites.text: Brastudon is a grounded, lumbering reptilian creature of the Thudarneld sixth era, its bony crest rattling like dice in a cup whenever it prepares to strike. It is said to be the living embodiment of chance among the cliffs of the Sundered Teeth, where herders wager their flocks on which slab it will crush next.

rites.name: Haloldock
rites.text: Haloldock is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a rail-mounted docking frame that clamps armored hulls to pierce their outer plating. Its tethered bolts punch through shells but leave unarmored interiors untouched, requiring deliberate retooling for each new wearer.

rites.name: Moraldock
rites.text: Moraldock is a frost-spirit that drifts through the hollows of the Thudarneld cold-steppes, gathering hoarfrost into jagged shards it hurls at anyone who trespasses on its frozen ponds. Its breath can crack thick river ice in a single exhale, and the nomads who winter there call it the Quiet Winter.

rites.name: Drolduron
rites.text: Drolduron is a grounded concept of tuned resonance-marks that flare against particular kinds of living things, letting a skilled practitioner strike a single breed of foe with far greater force. Its effect is strictly local and tied to the target's nature rather than raw power. Among Thudarneld's quiet craftsmen it is prized as a discipline of precision.

rites.name: Tarneden
rites.text: Tarneden is a hand-built siege instrument from the highland foundries of the Grevan Plateau, a sky-lance that hurls a cluster of gravity-weighted iron cores onto a distant mark. It was designed to pierce fortress walls and was later repurposed for mining collapse work.

rites.name: Tarneldar
rites.text: Tarneldar is a rite-keeper of the Grounded realm, an old bell-warden who rings the marrow-chimes that bring the valley's sleepers back to their shifts. Its sorrowful clanging can shake loose the stone of entire hillsides when the wardens grow desperate. Few living minds hear the chimes without weeping.

rites.name: Tharnen
rites.text: Tharnen is a bare-knuckle discipline practiced by wandering hermits of the Grounded realm, who train their bodies until a single open-handed strike carries the weight of a falling boulder. Its practitioners are known to shatter river stones and split old oaks with a palm, though they rarely fight except to protect a village. Seven ages of teaching have made Tharnen a quiet point of honor among the valley folk.

rites.name: Brostunen
rites.text: Brostunen is a grounded hedge-mender of the Thudarneld reach, a lean elder who unpicks the armor-stitching that soldiers rely on and leaves the cloth thin for the next blow. Villages keep a few of his knotted cords to test whether a ward still holds before they trust it.

rites.name: Kelanar
rites.text: Kelanar is a quiet tuning-art of the Grounded realm, practised by wardens who hum resonant chords to unsettle the inner equilibrium of rival minds. Its adepts can dull an opponent's resistance to sorcery or sap their capacity to channel it, leaving them exposed. The art is considered gentle, but it is feared for its lingering effect.

rites.name: Jorare
rites.text: Jorare is a grounded concept, a rallying chant sung by a band of wandering minstrels across the Thudarneld plains in Era E6. Its verses bolster the courage of allies and sap the resolve of foes, with its refrains growing louder with each stanza sung.

rites.name: Thastedar
rites.text: Thastedar is a resonant pressure-sigil bound into the skin of wardens who guard the sunken salt-cities of Thudarneld. It is said to crack the hidden shell of anything it is pressed against, and its wardens use it to break open sealed cargo and stubborn gates.

rites.name: Kelustardon
rites.text: Kelustardon is a sprawling mental-reservoir technique practiced by the wardens of Thudarneld, where a bearer draws reserves of inner resonance to bolster the channels of nearby allies. Its effect is measured as a fraction of each ally's own reservoir, and the wardens record the surge in fixed glass vessels kept in the Grounded archives.

rites.name: Thestaldon
rites.text: Thestaldon is a concept of a grounded, seventh-age warrior-tradition in the E6 era, whose practitioners draw on stored kinetic momentum to vault skyward and strike from above. Its masters are said to leave craters in packed earth with a single leap, though their true reach is limited by how long they can hold their breath.

rites.name: Tarnernath
rites.text: Tarnernath is a mimic-spirit born from the echo of a dying storm, drifting through the Grounded realm and absorbing the last moves of anything that nearly ends it. It carries these borrowed techniques as a restless chorus within its shell.

rites.name: Brustaneld
rites.text: Brustaneld is a bracing discipline of tempered resonance taught in the Grounded realm during its sixth era, when practitioners learned to hold a single charge steady until it sang. It was later folded into a passive habit that every apprentice inherits, so the old technique now lives quietly in ordinary posture and breath.

rites.name: Branath
rites.text: Branath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet discipline of inherited instinct passed between the gifted of the third age. Its practitioners learn that a single well-timed intuition can outweigh a lifetime of drilled technique.

rites.name: Craden
rites.text: Craden is a grounded combat art practiced by wandering blademasters of the Thudarneld frontier, who strike a foe in a rapid cascade of cuts before a single decisive thrust. Practitioners count their strikes on knotted cords, and a flawless cascade can split a stone pillar at the final blow.

rites.name: Drurdock
rites.text: Drurdock is a cracked stone colossus that stands sentinel over the Grounded realm's tectonic seams, its shoulders bearing wings of hardened slag. When the seams groan, it unfolds those wings and beats them once to bring down a rain of molten shale on any force approaching its valley.

rites.name: Crosterden
rites.text: Crosterden is a grounded, era-six concept of a two-year-old sealed-in beast-engine that drinks the stored heat of its surroundings and loosens it in one dense burst. Its keepers tend it like a sleeping storm, letting it vent only into the cold quarries of the high plateau. Its power is exactly enough to crack a village's stone foundations and no more.

rites.name: Breldock
rites.text: Breldock is a grounded arcane discipline in Thudarneld's sixth era, in which practitioners sever the flow of a rival's inner reserve by striking the resonance knot beneath their sternum. The technique is taught only to those who have sworn to restore what they drain. Its three recorded applications range from silencing a duelist's wards to unmaking a sealed cistern.

rites.name: Tarnustedon
rites.text: Tarnustedon is a grounded sentinel-beast of the Thudarneld reaches, a creature whose twin stone horns can call down paired falling rocks onto a distant foe. It is most often seen wandering the fog-bound valleys of its age, rarely drawn into conflict but terrible when provoked.

rites.name: Tharudon
rites.text: Tharudon is a Grounded-realm combat drifter of the seventh age of Thudarneld, known for a pair of blade-strikes that land in quick succession and gather strength when enemies fix their gaze upon him. He draws his reserves of momentum from the crowd of opponents who choose to challenge him directly. His style is taught in the bordering vaults of the old circuit-schools.

rites.name: Halenock
rites.text: Halenock is a grounded, fast-moving sky-hunter from the seventh age of Thudarneld, who can hurl a volley of four spears that burst on impact. Its favored tactic is to strike a foe already reeling, when each spear's blast spreads further to nearby targets. The spears are its signature and the reason it is feared among the scattered sky-clans.

rites.name: Pelerath
rites.text: Pelerath is a concept of a grounded, quiet ritual-technique that gathers wandering memory-motes and guides them toward a distant resting horizon. Practitioners in Thudarneld treat it as a mourning rite rather than a weapon, though its focused release can briefly overwhelm stone and iron.

rites.name: Kelarnudeld
rites.text: Kelarnudeld is a quiet resonance woven into ceremonial bracers worn by the lamp-keepers of Thudarneld's low valleys. It steadies a wearer's vitality by a small measured fraction, a modest gift that is offered freely to anyone who can afford one of the rare bracers.

rites.name: Crestoden
rites.text: Crestoden is a grounded martial technique of the Thudarneld school, a stance-based blade art in which the practitioner stills their breath until a single decisive stroke can sever resistance itself. Within its era of age three, it is taught as a refinement of an older cut, prized less for raw force than for the rare moment when an opponent simply ceases to hold together. Practitioners speak of it with the reverence reserved for something that works more often than it should.

rites.name: Tarnarene
rites.text: Tarnarene is a resonant chant woven through the marrow of the Grounded realm, where field-singers hum it to steady the bones of their companions before a hard labor. Its effect is a slow tightening of muscle and tendon, growing stronger the longer the chant is sustained. Practitioners say the song never truly ends, only fades when the last listener stops straining.

rites.name: Pelastock
rites.text: Pelastock is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a worn-leather bracer that cinches tighter around the wearer's wrist as their endurance grows. Its lattice of brass rings unlocks in step with the bearer's training, letting a fighter absorb staggering blows long past the point where lesser guards would fail.

rites.name: Halestudock
rites.text: Halestudock is a windborne sentinel of the Grounded realm, a slow-moving column of storm that wakes when provoked and hunts whatever it has marked. Once it ensnares a target it spins them through repeated impacts before loosing them, though the dust it drags along blinds the bystanders around it.

rites.name: Broldon
rites.text: Broldon is a dread-lantern fungus that sprouts in the marrow-caves beneath Thudarneld's hill-forts, its pale glow making onlookers feel the ground itself wants them gone. Its spores drift into the lungs of rival warbands and send them scattering before blades are even drawn. Wardens guard the caves with iron bells to keep the bloom from spreading.

rites.name: Haloron
rites.text: Haloron is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld universe, an ever-present tremor of local force that stirs at the edges of the Eras. Its open-palmed strikes are bright and quick, and each one can leave its target dazed or stripped of their nerve for a short while.

rites.name: Joradock
rites.text: Joradock is a grounded mental discipline practiced by the wardens of the E6 era in Thudarneld, who learn to seize and steer the nervous systems of others through a shared resonance. Its adepts can briefly command a rival's limbs, but the technique leaves a lingering fog that the wardens call the tether. Most practitioners learn only a single mimicking gesture before the discipline is considered mastered.

rites.name: Tarnurneld
rites.text: Tarnurneld is a quiet mending craft in the Thudarneld omniverse, taught in the grey hill-towns where sparks are drawn from cracked river-stones. A practitioner spends two of these stones to knit the wounds of whoever they hold in a steady grip, requiring no reserve of inner breath.

rites.name: Kelarnar
rites.text: Kelarnar is a concept of fleeting concealment in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, where a traveler can slip beyond the notice of any watching eye for a short span. Its hold on the senses lasts only briefly before the veil thins and the figure is seen again. Scholars of the era treat it as a quiet trick rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Tarnudath
rites.text: Tarnudath is a short-tempered grounded sorceress of the Thudarneld reckoning, whose temper flares into a storm of crackling bolts that scorch whole hillsides when she loses her composure. Her outbursts are feared in three villages, where old folk still speak of the day her anger scattered a harvest fair across the valley.

rites.name: Brarne
rites.text: Brarne is a concept of a sacred strike carried in a blade, a discipline taught in the grounded era E6 where knights channel a faith-bound light through steel. Its practitioners are known for a single blow that shatters armor and bone alike, a technique held in reverence across the Thudarneld powers.

rites.name: Pelernath
rites.text: Pelernath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe: a crystalline focus that absorbs the habits of whatever it is bound to, letting a wielder slowly inherit techniques from creatures they have confronted. Its later refinement, reached through trials in a sealed training construct, allows its bearers to strengthen the raw attributes of their body and spirit.

rites.name: Haladeld
rites.text: Haladeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a hand-carved fretboard instrument whose strings hum in harmony with the pulse of the surrounding valley. Its players are said to coax modest tremors from stone and to lift seven-year-old sparks of memory from listeners' hearts.

rites.name: Draston
rites.text: Draston is a grounded martial relic-style concept from the Thudarneld continent, a kick technique that unbinds an opponent's defensive wards in a single strike. Its wielders are monks who train to read the flow of an enemy's aura before striking. The technique is valued more for precision than for raw force.

rites.name: Tarnoredeld
rites.text: Tarnoredeld is a grounded, seven-year-old power in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rhythmic stomping art whose practitioners move soil and stone through the beat of their steps. Its wielders are sought by mining guilds and village healers alike, since a single well-timed routine can settle a landslide or mend a shaken foundation.

rites.name: Morodar
rites.text: Morodar is a grounded, weathered sky-harrower of the E6 age, a lanky figure who wedges unstable ore-bearing clay into cracks and then drops onto it to set off a sharp, rolling shockwave. Its strikes are feared for their timing rather than their size, since it builds pressure over long stretches of stillness before releasing it all at once.

rites.name: Pelurnon
rites.text: Pelurnon is a concept of quiet arcane craft in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where practitioners bind loose wind and ember into small, careful workings. Its adepts teach that restraint matters more than force, and most of its recorded feats are measured in sparks, gusts, and hearth-sized flares.

rites.name: Brardeld
rites.text: Brardeld is a grounded concept from the E6 era, a fleeting ritual-stone that hums with the pressure of a settling mountain range. It is said to calm restless land by drawing its stored strain into a single, carefully measured release.

rites.name: Thardude
rites.text: Thardude is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an age-three power that restores a fallen companion to their feet through sheer force of will. Its wielders are rough-handed fighters who rarely heal anyone gently, yet they can drag a collapsed ally back from the brink in the middle of a brawl.

rites.name: Druden
rites.text: Druden is a concept of concentrated lightning-borne force, a discipline that gathers stormlight into a single crackling release. Practitioners of this grounded era, age three, have learned to channel it as a sharp, focused strike rather than a sprawling storm.

rites.name: Fenardure
rites.text: Fenardure is a Grounded-realm concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rolling exhalation of stored breath-essence that its wielders loose across whole gatherings at once. It can sear or chill, dim the senses, or bind the will, usually striking every creature in its path rather than a single target.

rites.name: Joraneld
rites.text: Joraneld is a rhythm-based combat technique taught in the Thudarneld riverside dojos, where practitioners learn to read a rival's weight shift and slip backward before it lands. The leap carries a stored tension that releases as a heavy, ringing counterstrike, stronger when the evasion was clean. Masters say it can be begun and finished in midair, though few students master that.

rites.name: Thornurdath
rites.text: Thornurdath is a quiet, grounded concept of a lens-craft that reads the hidden weights and weaknesses of whatever it is turned upon, showing the marrow of a thing to those who study it. Practitioners in the Thudarneld powers scene use it to plan their approach before any blow is struck. Its reach is modest, bound to what a careful eye could read by hand.

rites.name: Drurdenon
rites.text: Drurdenon is a crystalline mist-serpent of the Grounded realm, whose exhalation scatters a blinding glimmer across the battlefield and dulls the wills of those it touches. Its breath is said to be strongest in the moments before dawn, when the dew is heaviest and the sky still holds no color. Villagers of the high marsh call it a guardian, though few have lived long enough to say whether it protects them or simply tolerates them.

rites.name: Pelustornon
rites.text: Pelustornon is a drifting glacier-spirit of the Grounded realm who lives in the sediment-cold lowlands of Thudarneld. It is known for hurling its own frozen bulk onto rivals, a blow that flattens the ground beneath them but rarely leaves any frost behind.

rites.name: Thurdeneld
rites.text: Thurdeneld is a shielding ward woven by the Verdant Loom-keepers of the Ashen Plateau, a stone-lattice that hardens the air around allies until blows lose their bite. Its wardens chant it in threes, and each chant thickens the protection a little further. The ward has held through three ages of siege and storm.

rites.name: Halorneren
rites.text: Halorneren is a grounded, slow-moving serpentine construct of the Thudarneld concept line, built to coil around foes and wait for a flinch before tightening. Its seventh age in the E6 era has left it stiff and mostly quiet, though its coils can still crush a stone wall or a small wagon when provoked.

rites.name: Morernaston
rites.text: Morernaston is a quiet sentinel of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld's sixth era, a stone-hearted warden said to hold its ground against the slow grinding of the centuries. It can brace itself against any blow that would shatter lesser wardens, and its stillness has outlasted seven ages of the locale's wars.

rites.name: Jorernock
rites.text: Jorernock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a sigil-bound mantle worn by hunters who bear down on the spirit-beasts that roam its mountains. Each bearer gains a surge of force against creatures marked by the old covenants, though the mantle itself is modest in what it can release. Its rarity and its ties to local custom keep it firmly within a single province's lore.

rites.name: Tarnostock
rites.text: Tarnostock is a shadow-dance technique practiced by wandering cave-dwelling mystics of Thudarneld, who sway in rhythm with the dripping stone to summon the dark. Its strikes mostly seep into foes as lingering afflictions, with only a faint chance of a bone-deep blow.

rites.name: Cruste
rites.text: Cruste is a ward-keeper of the Grounded realm in the seventh age, a quiet caretaker who wraps wounded landscapes in a shell of dust-born light. Her shield can blunt the blows of any force that strikes her companions on foot, though it fails against spells and wounds of the soul. Those who walk with her say she hums to the stones so they will not break under her protection.

rites.name: Tholdernar
rites.text: Tholdernar is a grounded concept of a soldier's ritual kit, a tool-belt that can be rearranged at rest but locks tight during any strike. Its builders hold that a hammer is only as honest as its last swing, so the belt refuses changes while a blow is still in motion.

rites.name: Pelarurnath
rites.text: Pelarurnath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rhythmic discipline where a practitioner releases a cascade of stored sparks by turning a wrist-carved dial as fast as steady breath allows. Its power scales with the speed of the hand, so novices fizzle while masters crack flagstones with a single flurry.

rites.name: Fenustath
rites.text: Fenustath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a ward-stone that a sorcerer's circle inscribes into a staff to sharpen incantations at the price of doubled draw from the reserve. Its inscription is strict: it sharpens only the lines that can bear it, and it cannot touch the raw surges of a ritual's climax.

rites.name: Drerulden
rites.text: Drerulden is a grounded power concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a thread-spun art of piercing that lets a practitioner weave a single gleaming filament into an unguarded point of anyone nearby. Its wounds ignore every shield or ward, so it is prized more for certainty than for force. Lesser forms of the art, called hollow threads, are used to mark rivals without drawing blood.

rites.name: Thordusteld
rites.text: Thordusteld is a grounded concept of a viscous, tongue-like bio-membrane that its wielders smear across a surface to raise a faintly shimmering barrier. The barrier turns aside arcane energies while allowing ordinary matter to pass, and it is used by village healers to shield patients from curses.

rites.name: Joroste
rites.text: Joroste is a grounded concept of calculated sorcery in Thudarneld, where practitioners read the hidden arithmetic of a battlefield to strike only those whose numbers fit a chosen pattern. Its disciplines let a caster hurl spells at any foe sharing a prime count, a multiple, or a particular height, without spending reserves or lifting a hand. Each invocation is a sum solved before the spell is cast.

rites.name: Kelorudon
rites.text: Kelorudon is a concept in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a heavy overhead strike that gathers a hum of stored sparks into a single blade-shaped glow before slamming it down. Locals treat the strike as a rite of passage for wardens of the Ashen Reach, who train for years to hold the gathering pose without shaking. Its impact is meant to split stone and stun beasts, not to level settlements.

rites.name: Halarnore
rites.text: Halarnore is a quiet mending-spirit of the Grounded realm, a presence that closes wounds and calms fevers in those who ask it. Its gift is measured rather than dramatic, restoring a tenth of what a body or lantern-hearth can hold each time it is called.

rites.name: Tholdudath
rites.text: Tholdudath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet ward-breaking technique that lets a mage's working slip past any protective enchantment. Its practitioners, the Hollow Quillers of the third age, use it to unseal sealed archives and counter guardian wards.

rites.name: Peladock
rites.text: Peladock is a grounded, sprinting engine-spirit of Thudarneld's sixth era, who hammers at the air in rapid bursts when the clock grants it a window. Each pulse of its drumming stacks into a crushing series of impacts that the old quarries still remember.

rites.name: Drudon
rites.text: Drudon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a dull ward-stone that hums against restless dead things. Its bearers swing ordinary blades with extra force when facing the corpse-bound and spirit-tethered. It is a modest tool used by wardens in the lower districts.

rites.name: Brernon
rites.text: Brernon is a grounded-realm ember-hound's signature leap, a rising cascade of kindled cinders that hurls a foe skyward. Its most reliable strike rebounds from the ground, and the ember-swirl can shatter a defender's stance. It recharges quickly, so wardens rely on it constantly in the opening age.

rites.name: Joranon
rites.text: Joranon is a grounded concept of a bench-side alchemist's art in the world of Thudarneld, where a practitioner distills restorative and binding essences from ordinary plants and relics. Its refinement process turns humble tonics into potent wardings, though the yield is modest and capped by the crafter's patience. The discipline is prized as a shortcut past long apprenticeships.

rites.name: Droren
rites.text: Droren is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a summoned hush that drifts through the sixth age like a letter sealed in black wax. It is said to carry a single unwelcome truth to whoever ignores the bells of the lower towns. Its arrivals are small, precise, and seldom forgotten.

rites.name: Halostanon
rites.text: Halostanon is a ward-craft of the Grounded realm in the E6 era, a shimmering lattice of layered sigils that a warden of the third age weaves over an ally to blunt the force of any element. Those it shelters take only half of what would otherwise strike them, though the lattice cannot guard against curses that bypass the elements entirely.

rites.name: Kelusteld
rites.text: Kelusteld is a grounded, seven-year-old sensory charm in the Thudarneld setting, worn as an inscribed stone set into a tool's handle. When held near a creature, it reveals the creature's vitality, frailties, wards, and lingering afflictions to the bearer's eyes. Its use is common among hunters and surveyors in the E6 era.

rites.name: Tarnareldon
rites.text: Tarnareldon is a grounded Thudarneld concept, a slow-burning clay bulwark whose rare outbursts crack the earth beneath a fortress. Its wardens hold it on a tether of salt-chains, and it has been known to shrug off a collapsing tower.

rites.name: Tarnenalde
rites.text: Tarnenalde is a grounded swordsman-spirit of the Thudarneld reaches, known for conjuring a second, shadowy blade from his own shadow. He weaves it into rapid sequences of cuts that each leave the air ringing with stored tension until one final stroke releases it.

rites.name: Pelurnar
rites.text: Pelurnar is a crystalline tuning-fork of a weapon-spirit, bound in the Thudarneld cosmos by three resonant lattices that hum together when it is struck. When its wardens sound it, a shimmering three-cornered lattice of force springs into being and tears across every hostile body within sight. Its wardens regard it as a last resort, since the resonance that powers it also shakes the ground for leagues around.

rites.name: Halastenon
rites.text: Halastenon is a mind-bending concept in the Thudarneld universe, a grounded practice of sheer conviction that lets a practitioner project false strength and sharpen their own thinking at once. Those who master it can briefly double their mental acuity, though the surge fades after a single decisive act of reasoning.

rites.name: Thasteld
rites.text: Thasteld is a grounded concept of pure-energy magick, a sustained discharge that tears luminous fractures through whatever stands within its radius. Its practitioners treat it as a sealed craft, drawing on a reservoir of charged light that ordinary hands can barely shape. Its wielders speak of it sparingly, since even a controlled working leaves the surrounding air ringing for days.

rites.name: Peleren
rites.text: Peleren is a quiet, grounded mental discipline in the Thudarneld powers tradition, taught to scholars who wish to disarm a rival's inner wellspring of arcane force. A practitioner fixes their gaze and sends a focused pulse of thought that dulls the target's channeling for a span of breaths. The technique is considered polite and is forbidden in formal duels.

rites.name: Bruron
rites.text: Bruron is a sun-plated sentinel of the Thudarneld frontier, a bronze-jawed warden who hurls compressed dawn-light at invaders from the high ridges. Its signature bulwark-drop calls down a rolling cascade of golden shards that can flatten a barracks in a single sweep.

rites.name: Jorurdoden
rites.text: Jorurdoden is a ward-weave that clings to a bearer's skin as a faint silver mesh, deflecting hostile spells and light barbs back toward their sender for as long as the bearer stands in conflict. Its cost is paid in carved river-glass shards that crack and dim each time the weave turns a blow aside.

rites.name: Kelerdorne
rites.text: Kelerdorne is a grounded battle-stance technique practiced by the sentinels of the Thudarneld highlands, who hurl their heavy bronze bucklers into an opponent's chest to daze and unbalance them. Its force is modest but it reliably halts a charging foe or breaks a caster's chant, though it is slow to recover from and draws the attention of every nearby warrior.

rites.name: Croderdock
rites.text: Croderdock is a grounded concept of a sealing practice that binds restless dead things into silent stone, carried out by wardens who walk the old burial fields at dusk. Its wardens hum a low note that hardens the air around a corpse until it can no longer rise.

rites.name: Fenurdath
rites.text: Fenurdath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hearth-spirit of cinders that rises from a dying forge to cleanse what it touches. It is treated as a sacred wind of ember and feather, though its power is confined to a single mortal scale.

rites.name: Crareste
rites.text: Crareste is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld world, a slow-burning incense of ash-grey resin that blooms into a thick, cool fog when struck. Caravans and scouts in the E6 era carry it to cover retreats and blind pursuing beasts for a few breaths.

rites.name: Peluren
rites.text: Peluren is a ring-shaped sentinel that hovers over the frozen plains of its homeworld, a mechanical warden built to punish those who defy its chosen ruler. When rebels gather in a valley, it descends and sweeps a column of searing light across the ground, leaving scorched furrows and new pits that bloom with strange crawling machines.

rites.name: Haloldenath
rites.text: Haloldenath is a vast, sky-spanning dragon-form of the Thudarneld cosmos, born when a mountain-sized guardian was fused with the heartfire of a dying sun. Its signature act is a silent, cloud-piercing lance of white radiance that scorches the sky above whole provinces.

rites.name: Dresteld
rites.text: Dresteld is a lattice of tuned resonance crystals that a bearer can attune once per engagement, splitting their reserve of readiness into three rings instead of two. The third ring burns slowly and lasts for a span set by the bearer's rank, five or ten minutes of stored momentum. It is a mid-tier capacity in Thudarneld, meant to turn a long fight rather than end it.

rites.name: Brenath
rites.text: Brenath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet discipline of field-medicine practised by wayfarers who mix salves and tonics in the middle of skirmishes. Its practitioners can double the potency of restorative draughts they carry, though each use draws down a cache of inscribed river-pebbles that serve as the fuel of the art. A glitch in the modern copies of the old craft's manuals occasionally causes the doubling to misfire.

rites.name: Keledar
rites.text: Keledar is a quiet binding sigil worn by the ferrymen of Thudarneld's low marshes, able to still a single creature's limbs with a glance. Its reach stays confined to one body at a time, and it has no power over wider ground or weather.

rites.name: Tarnuldon
rites.text: Tarnuldon is a grounded ember-forged war-glaive of the Thudarneld, quenched in volcanic brine so that it holds a sheet of banked heat along its edge. Its wielders in the third age use it to set whole hill-lines alight in a single downward cut.

rites.name: Tharnon
rites.text: Tharnon is a grounded, fast-moving duelist-tinker of the sixth era, known for a signature transformation called the Hollow Shift, in which bone-plated armor folds outward and multiplies their strength for a few seconds. Their weapon rings like struck bronze, and they are said to be the only fighter in Thudarneld who laughs mid-blow.

rites.name: Bruldodar
rites.text: Bruldodar is a wind-sculpted glider-craft of the Grounded realm, ridden by skyward hunters who chase storm-cells across the drifting plains of Thudarneld. Its pilots are known for dives that thin the air into a hum before the strike lands.

rites.name: Dreste
rites.text: Dreste is a wooden-bladed training weapon forged by the Ostmarr guild of Thudarneld, meant to teach apprentices to strike without killing. Its dull edge still delivers a jolt sufficient to rattle a foe's senses and leave them briefly unable to move. Guardians of the old academies carry Dreste as a reminder that restraint is a skill of its own.

rites.name: Jorolden
rites.text: Jorolden is a rune-carved stone monk of the Grounded realm, who strikes the soil with palm and heel so that the bedrock itself splits in a long, fanning crack. Its training halls are sunk into the valleys, and its disciples are taught that the earth remembers every blow.

rites.name: Morastude
rites.text: Morastude is a quiet, grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a breath of wind drawn from the marsh-reeds that the local herders call the hush-wind. Its bearers exhale it over the wounded to pull their pain into the air and spread the relief evenly among the gathered company.

rites.name: Fenarorde
rites.text: Fenarorde is a grounded working of old star-reading craft in the Thudarneld, where practitioners bind a fold in space to the patterns of firmament lights. When the constellations are aligned it tears the ground and air into a short-lived warp that strikes whatever stands beneath it.

rites.name: Therock
rites.text: Therock is a stony-fisted warden of the Grounded realm, a silent guardian whose single art is to shatter whatever crowns an enemy's brow. Its strike sends the headgear of its foe bursting apart, leaving the bearer bare and exposed to the next blow.

rites.name: Brodeld
rites.text: Brodeld is a quiet concept in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a sensory cloak that bends the attention of onlookers so a bearer slips past notice. Its feats are modest, measured in small bursts of effort and the careful ease of a hand that never disturbs the air.

rites.name: Pelorock
rites.text: Pelorock is a concept of a stone-bound craft in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, where a wayfarer grinds humble pebbles into charms that mend wounds and steady allies. The art favors convenience over hunting rare beasts, letting a patient crafter reach powerful blessings far sooner than the old dangerous routes allowed.

rites.name: Pelerdeld
rites.text: Pelerdeld is a restless charm of the Thudarneld order, tuned to the odds of what the world yields when it is struck. Bearers who carry it find common spoils come easily, yet the rarest prizes slip away whenever it rests among their gear.

rites.name: Fenurde
rites.text: Fenurde is a grounded, mortal-scale concept within the Thudarneld universe, described as a practiced technique in which a wielder draws static from a storm-charged blade and drives a single piercing lunge that momentarily scrambles the nerves of everyone standing in its path. It is taught in disciplined orders where restraint matters as much as force.

rites.name: Draneste
rites.text: Draneste is a concept-grade ward-engine of the Grounded realm, a lattice of tuned ember-crystals that gathers stray heat and volts from the air and releases them as a single pillar of surge. Its power scales inversely with the wielder's remaining vitality, rewarding those who fight close to the edge of collapse. Its builders considered it too unwieldy to ever be fielded as more than a showpiece.

rites.name: Tarnodeld
rites.text: Tarnodeld is a grounded, mortal-scale concept in the age of E6, a blade-art that teaches the wielder to strike where life is most fragile. Its practitioners are measured by how quickly they can sever a foe's rhythm rather than by raw strength. Its power is invoked as a short-lived discipline among a small circle of wanderers.

rites.name: Brerde
rites.text: Brerde is a mental discipline from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where practitioners quiet their thoughts until a still pool forms within them. By holding that stillness, a Brerde user can reclaim a short span of spent force, drawing back the exertion of the last twenty seconds. The technique is taught only in the hill monasteries of the Ashen Vale.

rites.name: Thurnock
rites.text: Thurnock is a quiet, hand-carved sigil-stone worn by wayfarers of the Grounded realm, said to hum faintly when a promise is about to be broken. Its bearers are sworn to mend what they harm, and the stone grows heavier with each unkept oath. It is revered more as a conscience than as a weapon.

rites.name: Pelernore
rites.text: Pelernore is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an age-three remnant of the E6 era where local powers are measured in mundane scales. Its feats reflect a world where the strongest acts stop short of city-scale catastrophe.

rites.name: Jorurneld
rites.text: Jorurneld is a grounded technique of the Thudarneld powers, a focused breath of stored resonance that a practitioner draws in and releases through the palms. Its wielders use it to mend wounded allies or to unmake the restless dead, though it reliably does only one of these at a time. Each activation drains a cost of cut crystal shards from the practitioner's satchel.

rites.name: Thudone
rites.text: Thudone is a concept-grade ward-smith of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld's sixth era, aged three. Its gift is a patient bracing of the earth's own stillness, letting it hold a foundation steady against tremors and sudden weight.

rites.name: Fenodustar
rites.text: Fenodustar is a small brass-and-glass lamp carried by the lamplighters of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, said to burn away clouding shadows from the eyes of anyone it touches. Its light restores sight to the blinded and dissolves the murk that clings to their vision, though it cannot mend any lasting damage beneath. Lamplighters sell its oil in the marketplaces of the eastern valleys.

rites.name: Halurdedar
rites.text: Halurdedar is a ward-kin concept of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, a discipline that raises a curtain of molten ember-mist to catch incoming bolts. When the curtain swallows a hostile spell, the captured force is folded back into several seeking pressure-rings that can be steered mid-flight.

rites.name: Jorerdath
rites.text: Jorerdath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet inscription-craft that binds drowsy sap-light into hardened glyphs carried in the palm. Its practitioners can seal a rot-breath into a stone so that whoever it touches slowly forgets how to stop moving. Its age is three, and its charms are sold in bundles by traveling clerks.

rites.name: Halaneld
rites.text: Halaneld is a sealed, grounded relic-engine of the sixth era, a rust-colored bronze cylinder that hums with stored resentment. When its wardens hold its valve open, it discharges a spray of hot needles across a scatter of targets, each strike weaker than the last but never quite spent.

rites.name: Crustock
rites.text: Crustock is a slow-moving stone-shelled creature that lives in the deep sediment of Thudarneld's tidal flats. When disturbed, it stamps its plated feet in a rhythmic dance that sends shockwaves rolling through the seabed. Its tough carapace can absorb blows that would shatter lesser beasts.

rites.name: Keladar
rites.text: Keladar is a grounded ward-sigil worn by the scholars of the Thudarneld reed-marshes, a bronze disc that turns hostile sorcery back on its caster. It drinks a share of the wearer's stored breath whenever it works, so lesser mages prize it and rarely keep it long.

rites.name: Thernunar
rites.text: Thernunar is a mountain-dwelling hermit who measures his worth in the weight of stones he can lift with a thought, though his true skill lies in patient, careful practice. Villagers say he once steadied a collapsing ridge by tapping its base with a wooden staff. He rarely leaves his cave above the Sallow Gorge.

rites.name: Pelenock
rites.text: Pelenock is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a spell-weaving art in which a caster binds three chants into one breath, letting them unleash three flares of force before the world can answer. Practitioners etch the sigil onto their wrists to amplify their nerve and muscle, a practice that has made the discipline both respected and feared. Its basic rite is taught to apprentices in the third year of their training.

rites.name: Morurdon
rites.text: Morurdon is a ward-weave sewn into the lining of Thudarneld's ceremonial mantles, quietly dampening arcane force that strikes the wearer. Three resonance springs must be bound into its seam before the weave takes hold, and the protection it grants is modest but reliable.

rites.name: Thenurock
rites.text: Thenurock is a quiet, grounded sort of concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hauling-engine and pacing-stone system that the locals treat as a sturdy tool rather than a marvel. It is meant to be used by ordinary workers and never claims any great cosmic scale.

rites.name: Braldock
rites.text: Braldock is a hand-cranked refining rig used by wandering tinkers of the Grounded era to coax a faint, lingering hum out of ordinary bones and shells, bottling it into small ceramic vials. The vials hold no great force, but a skilled crafter can layer them into a pressure weapon that stuns a wolf or softens a hard stone.

rites.name: Tarnunoldar
rites.text: Tarnunoldar is a hollow-cored lodestone mountain in the Thudarneld reach, where pilgrims chip fragments to forge their ward-bells. Its pull is faint at dawn but grows with each full moon, drawing iron and brass from entire valleys toward its slopes. Herders say the mountain sings when it is fed a sufficient quantity of metal.

rites.name: Bruldar
rites.text: Bruldar is a concept of accelerated momentum in the Thudarneld, a quickening of local tempo that lets a bearer's moment arrive ahead of its due. It is a modest Grounded-realm art, drawing only the energy of a brisk stride to bend its own rhythm.

rites.name: Croldeld
rites.text: Croldeld is a grounded swordsman-technique of the E6 era, a sequence of crossing strikes that sharpens the closer the wielder's breath comes to the midpoint of their reserve. It is taught in mountain dojos where practitioners learn to wait for the moment their own strength crests before committing to the blow.

rites.name: Jorenath
rites.text: Jorenath is a grounded concept, a tide-keeping ballad that lifts every companion within earshot into quicker motion. It sharpens reflexes and footwork so that allies strike twice in a single moment before the song ends. Its strongest verses can swell the courage of a whole band, letting weary travelers surge forward on a second wind.

rites.name: Pelornunath
rites.text: Pelornunath is a grounded, memory-bound mage-spirit from the Thudarneld reaches who forgets everything except one cruel trick: a sudden bloom of half-remembered sorcery. When it wakes, it hurls a random hex at nearby foes, sometimes a gentle cinder, sometimes something far worse.

rites.name: Haluroden
rites.text: Haluroden is a grounded, mid-tier wayfinding relic carved from riverstone, used by caravan scouts to read the currents of underground springs. Its single defining act is a sweeping pulse that rolls shallow water and loose soil outward along the bearing it is aimed at.

rites.name: Jorestode
rites.text: Jorestode is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a restorative art practiced by tide-wardens who mend wounds and cleanse poisons with cool sea-glass salves. Its practitioners are known to soothe ailing crowds during the seventh age of the realm.

rites.name: Kelureld
rites.text: Kelureld is a grounded concept from the seventh age of Thudarneld, a hushed sentinel of tide-bells that rings dampers over sleeping harbors. Its signature act is a low, sustained hum that carries across the water and steadies anything caught in its frequency.

rites.name: Peleden
rites.text: Peleden is a quiet mental discipline taught in the grounded lowland schools of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to keep their thoughts steady against disorienting influences. Its lesser form softens the grip of disorder, while its mastered form lets a mind refuse it outright, overriding the lesser ward whenever both apply.

rites.name: Halodarneld
rites.text: Halodarneld is a grounded spirit-blade wielded by the ash-tongued marshal Verrin Oakhollow, whose edge drinks the warmth from a foe's veins and leaves them stilled. Its bearers are rarely harmed by it, since the blade only answers to a hand that has sworn an oath of protection. When drawn in full earnest, its strike can topple a barricade of timber and stone.

rites.name: Brastolden
rites.text: Brastolden is a woven charm of ground-glass beads and tin filigree, worn by wayfarers in the Thudarneld reaches to turn aside blows from heavy blades and clubs. Its wearers claim it bends the moment of an incoming strike so the weapon slips past, though scholars dispute whether it works at all.

rites.name: Pelenardock
rites.text: Pelenardock is a sealed resonance-engine in the grounded Thudarneld, a stone lattice that hums when touched and lends a bright ember-glow to whatever it is laid against. Its keepers use it to temper blades and hearthstones, for the glow lingers on the metal long after the lattice is lifted away.

rites.name: Thanordath
rites.text: Thanordath is a lattice of grove-spirits that hums beneath the Thudarneld canopy, carrying petitions from the mortal provinces to the root-councils. Its keepers, the Verdant Tallymen, negotiate every favor in tokens of sap and bone, and a broken pact can wither a valley in a season.

rites.name: Tarnornath
rites.text: Tarnornath is a discipline of chronal ward-craft practiced in the Grounded realm, where adepts bind short spans of time into sigils that slow, echo, or skip a target's moments. It is taught as a single trained craft rather than innate power, and its finest practitioners can freeze a falling stone or rewind a broken bell by a few heartbeats. Its feats are small and precise, reflecting a world where time-binding is delicate work.

rites.name: Crarnock
rites.text: Crarnock is a fallen sentinel engine of the Grounded realm, a squat iron colossus whose chest-lens gathers stray heat into a single searing ray. Its builders sealed the lens after a war, but rust and wind have cracked the seal, and wandering scavengers now trade stories about the brief, blinding flashes it sometimes emits.

rites.name: Crerdock
rites.text: Crerdock is a grounded, quiet concept in the Thudarneld universe, a hearth-keeper's cart-pony bond that tests a rider's patience. Its signature act is a sprint across a field of thistle that flattens everything in its line.

rites.name: Jorenustock
rites.text: Jorenustock is a grounded, ancient war-engine of the Thudarneld frontier, a bronze-plated hulk that stores the sting of thunderstorms in its ribbed flanks. It was built to hold a ridge line against stampeding herds, and its single release is a crackling discharge that rolls across the grassland like a sudden lightning-lit gale.

rites.name: Theldure
rites.text: Theldure is a concept of quiet rhythm, a lattice of tuned resonances that a practitioner hums into being to call forth a benevolent harmonic presence from the layered air above the grain fields of Thudarneld. Its manifestations are gentle but precise, cooling fevers, steadying storms, and lifting the weight from failing bridges. It is practised by lamp-keepers who treat each call as a kind of duty owed to their neighbours.

rites.name: Moroldadock
rites.text: Moroldadock is a quiet, mud-caked bard-engineer of the Grounded realm who sings a low, wobbling tune that briefly reshapes a foe's bones into those of a squat pond creature. The song spends its own breath in a way that leaves Moroldadock sluggish and croaking for hours afterward.

rites.name: Kelastar
rites.text: Kelastar is a quiet mineral lantern-thing drifting through the grounded reaches of Thudarneld, where it keeps the old tide-cairns lit. Its core hums with a steady, patient charge that it discharges only when a cairn fails.

rites.name: Morosteld
rites.text: Morosteld is a concept of a protective ward-mantle worn in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during the sixth era, where it reacts to a bearer's fading strength. When a wearer falls below half vitality in combat, it wraps them in a layered barrier that renews even an existing veil.

rites.name: Dredurne
rites.text: Dredurne is a Grounded-realm concept in the Thudarneld universe, a hand-cranked launcher-cannon built by the drifting salvage caravans of the E6 era. Its operators pack it with pressurized gel canisters that burst into concussive clouds when they strike a surface.

rites.name: Peluneld
rites.text: Peluneld is a tide-bound lantern-wraith of the Grounded realm, its body a hollow shell of pale resin that hums with stored heat. Villagers of Thudarneld say it was once a cook's ladle that caught fire and never went out.

rites.name: Broldeld
rites.text: Broldeld is a tidal-cadence technique taught in the Thudarneld courts, where practitioners borrow the rhythm of the sea to hasten a state of heightened focus. The art consumes a set of carved bone-stones, each one a small reservoir that must be spent to keep the surge flowing.

rites.name: Peluste
rites.text: Peluste is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a lantern-keeper's ritual skill that channels a hum of sunlight into a thin, aimable jet of golden fire. The fire lingers as a steady burn on anything it touches, and the caster can drift slowly while the stream is held.

rites.name: Crustar
rites.text: Crustar is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a shell-plated beast whose heat is drawn from the earth itself. Its signature discharge scorches everything standing within its line of sight, and older hunters say it favors the company of the great crimson wyrms of the high plains.

rites.name: Moraldar
rites.text: Moraldar is a tempered ward-stone worn by hunters of the Thudarneld frontier, who channel it to sharpen their strikes against burrowing and many-legged creatures. Its craft is humble, and its effect is confined to a narrow band of wild vermin rather than to any broad battle power.

rites.name: Pelernen
rites.text: Pelernen is a mid-tier grounded tool of the Thudarneld reckoning: a hand-forged cradle of wire and resonant glass that stores a single crisp pulse of kinetic force for its bearer. Its craftsmen seal each one with a plaited pattern they call the quiet knot, and they consider a Pelernen that never fires to be a wasted day's work.

rites.name: Pelarerdon
rites.text: Pelarerdon is a crystalline seed-engine grown in the shallow tidal gardens of Thudarneld, prized for the way it stores sunlight and releases it in a single sharp pulse. Gardeners harvest its heated pollen, which cracks open the shells of sea-bloom colonies and clears paths through the reef. Its release is strong enough to scorch a nearby reef face but never reaches beyond the immediate shoal.

rites.name: Jorunock
rites.text: Jorunock is a grounded concept of a warding technique woven into the sealed gauntlets of Thudarneld's mendwrights, granting partial immunity to the silence that binds the tongue of a caster. Its refined form, called Hollowcloak, overrides the lesser ward whenever both apply, shielding the wearer's speech entirely. Both are subtle skill-trappings rather than bursts of force.

rites.name: Brudon
rites.text: Brudon is a grounded, seven-year-old fixture of the E6 era, a sprawling mechanical colossus that rides on the hum of old orbital relays. Its signature is a precise, piercing beam drawn down from a relay array overhead, strongest when its own plating is battered and it is pushed to fight back.

rites.name: Craldath
rites.text: Craldath is a grounded concept of a mineral-lacquer that a reclusive artisan guild in the Thudarneld tradition applies to tools, making them strike without the usual local resonance. It is prized in the fourth age for dampening the unpredictable hum that otherwise ruins delicate mechanisms.

rites.name: Keloldaron
rites.text: Keloldaron is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet presence woven through the forests of its era. Its signature act is scattering a drift of enchanted foliage over every living thing nearby, a gentle but unavoidable rustle that settles into the lungs and the mind alike.

rites.name: Keladock
rites.text: Keladock is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a cheap ward-brace worn by apprentice mages that forces every working they cast to draw a single unit of stored mana. Its makers prized it because it let novices practise endlessly without exhausting their reserves.

rites.name: Tholdune
rites.text: Tholdune is a quiet, mending practice carried by the wandering salt-healers of Thudarneld's grounded era six, who stitch small wounds with threads of bark-resin and breath. Its reach is modest, closing a cut or easing a bruise in a single unhurried breath. Those who learn it are trusted with the first hour after an accident, when small harms matter most.

rites.name: Fenustath
rites.text: Fenustath is a dormant lattice of hollow bronze moons that drift over the Thudarneld plains, storing the pressure of ancient tides within their shells. When a moon is struck free, it can be hurled as a crushing projectile that shatters stone and sends shockwaves across entire valleys.

rites.name: Crudar
rites.text: Crudar is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse's sixth era, a quiet skill that draws spent resonance back out of the air and returns it to a caster's reserves. It is the signature technique of wandering hedge-mages who mend their strength by reclaiming the fading echoes of their own spells.

rites.name: Kelene
rites.text: Kelene is a concept of a grounded ward-craft in Thudarneld, a quiet ritual technique that woven sigils lend to a wearer's gear so that toxins and corrosive humors lose their grip on the body. Its advanced form overrides lesser sigils entirely, sealing the bearer against contagion once the full rite is performed. Practitioners consider it an everyday discipline rather than a battle art.

rites.name: Brerdastath
rites.text: Brerdastath is a rust-colored marsh-hauler of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, a slow beast that wades through mud and carries tons of salt-cured reeds on its back. Its stomach hums with fermenting sap, and it stores the energy of each long trek as a warm glow it can release in a single stomp.

rites.name: Brernaldeld
rites.text: Brernaldeld is a grounded, low-scale healing ward used in the Thudarneld tradition of field medics, who layer restorative chants over wounded companions to form a temporary shield of intent. Its effect spreads across a small circle of allies and fades after half a minute, but cannot be stacked atop another ward of the same lineage, the stronger simply replacing the weaker. Practitioners rate it by how much harm the shield can absorb relative to the healing given.

rites.name: Joruldardon
rites.text: Joruldardon is a grounded war-dancer of the Thudarneld reaches who coils a ring of ember-light around their body and whirls until every nearby foe is scorched. Its cooldown shortens when the dancer is thrown back, turning a setback into a stronger counter-spin.

rites.name: Moronarock
rites.text: Moronarock is a sandstone sigil-stone carried by wandering drill-sergeants of the Thudarneld mesas, who press it against a recruit's chest before each training climb. Each time a trainee completes a grueling ascent with the stone bound to them, their body thickens and their vitality ratchets upward for good. Veterans say it rewards stubbornness more than talent.

rites.name: Jorodeld
rites.text: Jorodeld is a grounded martial artist of the E6 era, whose signature technique is a sweeping low kick that skims the surface of standing water and lifts a spray of droplets into a sharp arc. Practitioners prize it for striking with the momentum of a full body turn, making it a staple of training halls across the age.

rites.name: Crelde
rites.text: Crelde is a grounded concept, a discipline of the Thudarneld order that lets a fighter strike with full force from behind the front line. Its adepts are chosen in their third age and bind the technique with sixteen sealed shards of cooled glass.

rites.name: Branon
rites.text: Branon is a concept of quiet restoration in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, an artisan's craft that reverses the hardening of living flesh into calcified form. Its practitioners work slowly, by hand and by lantern, returning frozen sentinels to motion one limb at a time. Within the Grounded realm's modest powers it is treated as a precious, carefully guarded skill.

rites.name: Joroldock
rites.text: Joroldock is a sluggish, glistening sludge-entity of the Grounded realm, its body a seeping vat of caustic brine that pools in the cracks of old stone. When disturbed it sprays bursts of hissing fluid that eat through armor and skin alike, and the droplets often carry strange numbing or clouding toxins into whatever they touch.

rites.name: Jorostane
rites.text: Jorostane is a conceptual lattice of gathered starlight that the people of the Grounded era drew down to scorch every foe across a wide field at once. Its energy is measured in the tens of gigajoules, a flash that sears and steams the air, leaving scorched ground in a sprawling cross pattern.

rites.name: Fenodarock
rites.text: Fenodarock is a grounded, mid-tier ritual cudgel forged in the Thudarneld workshops of the seventh age, where artisans bind slow-burning ore to a sprung heartwood core. Its strikes are measured in the tens of thousands of joules, enough to fell a stout oak or crack a stone wall, but its real value lies in how cleanly its force can be stored and released by a trained wielder.

rites.name: Halorastock
rites.text: Halorastock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe: a thin lattice of bonded crystal sewn into the lining of a worn harness, where each strand stores a fraction of incoming blows and bleeds it away through the wearer's boots. It is a modest, reliable protection, outclassed by heavier sigil-plating yet valued for how cheaply it can be woven into any existing gear.

rites.name: Crurdeste
rites.text: Crurdeste is a frost-glacial rite drawn from the Thudarneld's Grounded realm, where wardens call down a cascade of frozen spires that batter foes backward. The longer a warden holds the invocation, the deeper the glacier grows before it is released.

rites.name: Keloneld
rites.text: Keloneld is a restorative charm that lifts the lingering afflictions a traveler collects in the field, the sort that fade only when the fighting is over. Its strength grows with the bearer's skill, from the simplest toxin to the most tangled hex.

rites.name: Pelastath
rites.text: Pelastath is a silent ward-principle that the people of Thudarneld bind into their ceremonial plating, letting the bearer shrug off the clouding of sight that spreads through the outer marches. Its deeper form, called Vellorith's Clearing, overrides every lesser warding and makes the wearer's gaze true even in total dusk.

rites.name: Pelanorneld
rites.text: Pelanorneld is a concept of a grounded, mid-tier earth-mastery art in the Thudarneld omniverse, a cultivated discipline in which practitioners tap the stored tension of ridge-stone to drive rising spires from the ground. Its third iteration in the E6 era is famed for striking a single foe with a plume of compressed bedrock, a technique that remains cheap and swift enough for common duelists to master.

rites.name: Drurnath
rites.text: Drurnath is a concept of a grounded, era-six world where stone-keepers draw on the deep crust to shake the land itself. Its three feats are modest, scaled to the power of a mortal craftsman and his tools rather than cosmic forces.

rites.name: Drestonock
rites.text: Drestonock is a quietly sustaining ritual-engine sealed beneath the wind-scoured hills of Vellamor, where settlers tune its resonant lattice to deepen their inner endurance. Each gentle pulse hardens the mind against the strange psychic storms that roll across the eastern plains. Its keepers guard it fiercely, knowing that once bound to a single person, its gift can never be unbound.

rites.name: Brudorne
rites.text: Brudorne is a quiet, mechanical sentinel of the Grounded realm, built to hold back surges of raw force that would otherwise tear through the lowland valleys. Its engineers claim it can absorb a blow equal to an entire district's worth of stored energy, though it rarely needs to, since its chief power is redirecting the strain rather than resisting it.

rites.name: Jorenorden
rites.text: Jorenorden is a ward-plate sigil etched into the bulwark-steel of the Grounded realm's third-age mail. Four attuned lodestones set into its hollow stack their stored resilience atop the wearer's natural hardiness, turning each blow into a fraction of its former weight.

rites.name: Crodernen
rites.text: Crodernen is a discipline in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, practiced by wandering weavers of chalk-dust oaths who bind their resolve into a single thrown seed. Each use costs nineteen pale glass ember-pips, the costliest rite any apprentice can learn, and the thrower's arc is said to bend the local weather.

rites.name: Fenonede
rites.text: Fenonede is a grounded concept-level technique in the realm of Thudarneld, performed by swordsmen who strike three quick cuts that seem to scatter like frost across a winter night. It is considered the discipline's most refined single-target art, valued for its precision rather than raw force.

rites.name: Keledorar
rites.text: Keledorar is a grounded, living rite of the Thudarneld reed-marshes, in which a hunter's strength is measured by how many small tree-frogs she has coaxed into her satchel by dusk. Each captured frog is woven into a single stomping strike that lands upon every creature nearby, lifting the whole company's courage for a short spell afterward.

rites.name: Pelanurde
rites.text: Pelanurde is a grounded frost-thunder compound technique wielded by the wandering ice-storm cantor Vellis Orrane, who hurls a pillar of rime and a crackling barrage of bolts that strike every foe within a small ring. It is passed only through rare shards that fall from the hollow-eyed Lorrimaw wardens, and only a fraction of them ever carry the art.

rites.name: Joruldar
rites.text: Joruldar is a concept of spectral talons that the Thudarneld mystics call the Gnawing Vow, conjured to rake a foe without pause. Once summoned, the claws keep shredding until the target's resolve crumbles, and they can be called even while the wielder hangs in open air. Their dread lies less in the wounds they leave than in the courage they drain away.

rites.name: Crunore
rites.text: Crunore is a grounded, era-six concept: a gambler's ritual of spinning three painted drums, where each matching symbol sends a jolt through the surface of a rolling sphere of water or rock. It is less a weapon than a cursed wager, and the marks it leaves linger on everything it touches.

rites.name: Thureden
rites.text: Thureden is a grounded tide-binding art practiced in the drowned quarters of Thudarneld, where practitioners draw the weight out of a foe's own stance and leave it stumbling. Its signature rite, the Quartering Hush, strips away a quarter of an opponent's standing vigor each time it is spoken. Masters prize it against towering beasts that would otherwise outlast any blade.

rites.name: Pelustoldar
rites.text: Pelustoldar is a quiet bureaucratic rite in the Thudarneld powers, where practitioners seal a contaminated district behind a thin veil of lantern-light until the spreading sickness exhausts itself. Its wards are sworn oaths rather than walls, and breaking one sends a ripple through the local grammar of fate.

rites.name: Halude
rites.text: Halude is a rhythm-bound deity of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, who answers each heartbeat of the faithful with a single quiet tremor. Its sanctuary, the Hollow of Seven Bells, keeps time for the entire region, and its moods are read from the pitch of its echoes.

rites.name: Jorulderde
rites.text: Jorulderde is a grounded concept of a weathered stone warden who holds a longstanding bond with a sheltered valley in the realm of Thudarneld. Through quiet rites of mending and hardening, Jorulderde softens the blows of storms and shields travelers from harm while letting no damage pass unnoticed.

rites.name: Crone
rites.text: Crone is a concept of disciplined command within the grounded era of Thudarneld, a tactic that teaches a soldier to read a foe's posture and loosen its guard. It is a method rather than a body, practiced in drills where allies learn to pry open fortifications with precise, measured strikes.

rites.name: Cralde
rites.text: Cralde is a grounded mortal ward-weaver of the E6 era, a craftsperson who strengthens the sigils carved into a village's stones so its people can endure the spiteful storms of the Thudarneld frontier. Her protective marks hold against blows and burning gusts alike, though she tires quickly once she has woven a shield over a whole company.

rites.name: Morastonath
rites.text: Morastonath is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a shifting shield-spirit that bends its guarding weight at random each time a blow lands. Its hold on the wearer is so unpredictable that it sometimes yields less protection than it gives, so wise guardians refuse to bind it to their bodies.

rites.name: Kelurden
rites.text: Kelurden is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet ward-binding that is worn as a slot-fitted charm by those who study the flow of inner reserves. Its bearer's reserve ceiling rises with each node of attunement they have awakened in their personal lattice of practice. It is paired with a sister rite that governs bodily endurance.

rites.name: Thunath
rites.text: Thunath is a grounded lightning-weaving discipline practiced in the valleys of Thudarneld, where practitioners coat their blades and fists in crackling storm-current. Its adepts can briefly charge an ordinary weapon with a bite of static that stuns and scorches, though the effect fades within minutes. The art is taught in age-old guild halls and prized for its quick, controlled bursts rather than raw destruction.

rites.name: Thonen
rites.text: Thonen is a drifting tide-glass sentinel that hums beneath the frozen harbors of Vellar Deep, its crystalline body storing sunlight for centuries. When a fleet approaches, it releases stored warmth in a single shuddering blast that can shatter a ship's hull.

rites.name: Halaron
rites.text: Halaron is a war-chanter of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, whose resonant cry lifts the courage and quickens the limbs of every ally who hears it. Their voice can also channel raw magickal force into the blows of those they inspire, though the effect fades once the clash ends.

rites.name: Druste
rites.text: Druste is a quiet, bell-shaped resonance pattern that hums through the foundations of Thudarneld's grounded valleys, sometimes stirring loose stones into hovering spirals. It is studied by scholars of sound and rarely fights, but when provoked it can unseat the balance of a stone wall or a sleeping rafter.

rites.name: Kelornar
rites.text: Kelornar is a drifting glacier-spirit of the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, born from frost that settled on the old sea-cliffs during the seventh age. It hangs in the air as a jagged lattice of blue ice, and anything small enough to be drawn into its branches is slowly numbed and worn down until the lattice melts away.

rites.name: Jorulden
rites.text: Jorulden is a grounded concept within the world of Thudarneld, a rite of pressure that folds an adversary's vitality inward until only half remains. Its practitioners describe it as a tidal pull on the soul rather than the flesh, leaving bodies intact but drained. It is taught in the lowest mountain schools as the second rung of weighted craft.

rites.name: Kelulde
rites.text: Kelulde is a choking vapor-spirit that drifts through the marsh-towns of Thudarneld, its breath carrying a sickly violet haze that seeps into lungs and clouds the mind. Its exhalations can slowly sap the strength of anyone caught within reach, though it rarely wanders far from the wetlands it guards.

rites.name: Tarnusteld
rites.text: Tarnusteld is a battle discipline practiced by wandering shieldbearers of the Thudarneld frontier, a set of stances and bursts of willpower that let a fighter endure wounds and strike harder when the moment demands. It is taught as an expansion of the common basics every recruit learns, and only a few masters ever master its final, reckless forms.

rites.name: Drone
rites.text: Drone is a grounded combat servitor from the Thudarneld frontier, a squat cylinder of salvaged alloy that hums with borrowed power and yields to whoever commands its sparking core. It fights by accepting a deliberate toll: each surge it channels scorches its own casing, trading integrity for sudden, brutal force.

rites.name: Crarnuldon
rites.text: Crarnuldon is a sky-dwelling stellar sentinel of the Grounded realm, a crimson-rimmed warden that drops from orbit with a single descending strike to crack open meteor shelters. It is said to have been forged in the seventh age to guard the lower strata of Thudarneld from runaway drift.

rites.name: Dradonar
rites.text: Dradonar is a seismic discipline of the Thudarneld grounded realm, practiced in the third age of the sixth era by tectonic wardens who coax the bedrock into obedience. Its most devastating technique, the Gravelcrown Rift, can split a valley floor when the warden has fully learned to listen to the stone.

rites.name: Cronasten
rites.text: Cronasten is a concept of a grounded, third-era ward-plate worn over the chest, which drinks in heat and flame and turns it into restorative warmth for its bearer. Crafted from ember-crystal set into layered brass, it overrides lesser heat-guards, so that even scorching spells feed the wearer rather than harming them.

rites.name: Crudestock
rites.text: Crudestock is a ration-grade tonic-stopper bound to a pauldron, drawn from the grit-ledger of Thudarneld's lower quarries. When its wearer marches at the head of a column, it trickles quiet vigor back into their reserves with each stride.

rites.name: Druldath
rites.text: Druldath is a storm-spirit bound by the scholar Ossavel, who calls it a hunger in the marrow of the sky. Its gusts can scatter a hunting party across a valley, and it answers only to those who can match its restless pace.

rites.name: Joroldeld
rites.text: Joroldeld is a concept of gloom that clings to strikes, dimming an opponent's aim whenever a blow lands with enough force. Its bearers carry it through layered shadows that thicken with each repeated hit. Such dimming is limited to small, personal scales of harm.

rites.name: Crernodock
