rites.text: Crernodock is a spinning grappling discipline practiced by the stone-hauling guilds of Thudarneld's mountain quarries, where practitioners whirl weighted chain-spools to hurl boulders and anchor cargo. Its masters treat each spool as a patient engine, timing every release to the rhythm of the quarry's old pulley-songs.

rites.name: Thuldar
rites.text: Thuldar is a concept of a grounded refining art in the Thudarneld universe, where a practitioner distills temporal and spatial resonance out of ordinary objects and binds it into lasting workings. Its craft favors convenience over conflict, allowing an artisan to produce potent effects far sooner than field study would allow.

rites.name: Pelestath
rites.text: Pelestath is a drifting, ash-colored wraith that haunts the flooded tunnels beneath Thudarneld's old quarries, where it steals the warmth from lanterns and whispers the names of miners who never surfaced. It can slip into shadow so completely that travelers feel it brushing past their shoulders before they see its claws.

rites.name: Craron
rites.text: Craron is a slow, patient growth-art of a grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, where a body is shaped by repeated small gains rather than sudden leaps. Its practitioners measure progress in quiet increments of resilience, and the rare masters can shrug off blows that would shatter lesser frames.

rites.name: Keleston
rites.text: Keleston is a grounded concept from the E6 era, a ward-weave of sealed crystal threads that shields its bearer against being turned to stone. It is a practical protection rather than a cosmic force, shaped by long vigils against the mineral blights of the lower quarries.

rites.name: Fenernath
rites.text: Fenernath is a grounded ember-warden of the Thudarneld, a hearthkeeper whose flaming staff channels a second-tier kindling flare across a whole crowd of foes at once. Its heat is measured in cooking fires and smithy forges, not in wars of the sky.

rites.name: Kelone
rites.text: Kelone is a grounded mending-art in the Thudarneld reckoning, a quiet craft that unknots whatever a practitioner's hands or chants have tied onto a person. Its adepts can either calm a wound of the spirit or unravel a blessing, depending on which thread the chanter chooses to pull.

rites.name: Crure
rites.text: Crure is a dormant mental discipline that taught its practitioners to hold a single thought steady against the pull of collapsing grounds. In the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, its methods were once used to still tremors before they became quakes.

rites.name: Thorneldon
rites.text: Thorneldon is a thorn-bark mantle in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, grown by hermit druids who stake their own vitality into its fibers. Wearers gain a stubborn, lasting resilience that lets them shrug off blows that would fell lesser fighters. Its makers prize it as a quiet, unglamorous inheritance passed between generations.

rites.name: Jorenath
rites.text: Jorenath is a sealed resonance-glass lantern kept in the cold hall of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, said to hold a stored tide of thermal calm. Its keepers draw from it to steady those who wear it against sudden frenzy and shadow. Wielders report a soft, unbroken calm that lasts through long watches.

rites.name: Breneld
rites.text: Breneld is a sustained crescendo of a mind that refuses to wait, a thing that turns hesitation into motion. In the grounded era of Thudarneld it is felt less as a force than as a sudden loss of patience that sweeps through a crowd or a single body alike.

rites.name: Joruldeld
rites.text: Joruldeld is a small enchanted ward-thread woven into the lining of traveling cloaks across the Thudarneld frontier, quietly softening the sting of hostile spellwork. Three such threads, when stitched in one garment, let its wearer shrug off a fraction more of any hurled curse or ember-bolt. Wardsmiths regard it as humble but dependable, the first lesson every apprentice learns.

rites.name: Brenastock
rites.text: Brenastock is a hollow chime-spire in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, built by an extinct guild of tuners who believed walls could be coaxed into remembering their own strength. When a low hum is struck through its ribs, the surrounding stonework briefly thickens its grain, shrugging off blows that would otherwise crack it.

rites.name: Peluden
rites.text: Peluden is a quiet mountain-dwelling wardstone that hums in the thin air above the glaciers of Thudarneld, its surface cold enough to frost any passing traveler's breath. When a Peluden is disturbed, it exhales a sheet of frigid stillness that slows the blood and dulls the mind of anyone caught within it. The cold lingers for only a few breaths, but the drowsiness it leaves can last through a whole night.

rites.name: Tarnede
rites.text: Tarnede is a concept entry of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, an era-six artifact called a storm-cord that channels a crackling discharge through the wielder's bones. Its power is brief and costly, so the cord's bearers hold it back for the rare moment when a single towering foe must fall.

rites.name: Fenasturath
rites.text: Fenasturath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a stoneworked sanctuary-engine that channels resonant light through carved conduits. Its era E6 wardens use it to mend fractured ley-lines beneath the surface of the world.

rites.name: Kelestoldar
rites.text: Kelestoldar is a grounded, era-six sky-fire conjuration that rains a fourfold barrage of starless ember-shards onto scattered foes. Its core lore holds that a single cast scorches only the air and ash between targets, so its authored power stays modest by the standards of cosmic bodies. Wielders must pay heavy inner reserves and long gathering time before it can strike.

rites.name: Brenock
rites.text: Brenock is a bustling trading hub on the edge of the Grounded realm, where merchants barter in shared ledgers and reputation travels faster than caravans. Its quartermasters keep a standing tab for every traveler, so a favored patron can conjure an order from any counter they have ever visited.

rites.name: Drorudock
rites.text: Drorudock is a grounded, drone-piloted war-engine of the E6 era, built by hillside foundries that fuse salvaged rail-hardware into a single lumbering frame. Its signature act is the Hollowing Stride, in which a pilot overdrives every servo until the chassis tears itself apart in a shockwave that batters nearby allies with momentum they can ride. Veteran crews say it is less a machine than a promise made in iron, and its name is spoken with a mix of pride and dread.

rites.name: Haloldath
rites.text: Haloldath is a wandering blade-duelist of the Grounded realm whose technique of lingering focus lets her loose three crescent bursts of stored force after a strike. Her discipline is said to have been taught in the old salt-marsh monasteries, where students practiced until the air itself rang after each swing. Within Thudarneld she is remembered as a warning that restraint, once abandoned, leaves a trail of sound and ruin behind it.

rites.name: Morerdon
rites.text: Morerdon is a grounded ritual-dance technique taught in the river-cities of Thudarneld, performed by a dancer who has already offered a portion of their own vitality. The dancer spins a ring of stamping heel-strikes that loosen the packed earth and hurl loose gravel and dust outward in a wide, choking gust. It is feared more for its reach across a crowd than for any single blow.

rites.name: Thuston
rites.text: Thuston is a tidal-calendar stone-weaver's craft from the grounded realm of Thudarneld, where apprentices bind river-polished pebbles into rope-lattices to hold back seasonal floods. Its work is precise and local, rarely reaching beyond a single valley's levees and sluices.

rites.name: Brureld
rites.text: Brureld is a grounded storm-warden who channels the rage of thunderheads through a cracked brass bell worn at the throat. Its strikes carry a hum that splits armor and ward alike, and it can gather a crackling charge for a single blow that rattles windows three valleys away.

rites.name: Moruldock
rites.text: Moruldock is a staff-wielding technique of the Grounded realm, passed down through training halls where apprentices learn to make a weapon hover and strike before returning to the hand. Its practitioners measure mastery by how many practice staves they wear down to splinters before earning a guild-issued training pole.

rites.name: Cruste
rites.text: Cruste is a concept in Thudarneld, a grounded-era realm of age three, describing a reinforcing layer of wards that blunts incoming blows by a modest share of their force. Its bearers and smiths treat it as a practical craft rather than a marvel, so its effects stay within the scale of everyday battlefield harm.

rites.name: Fenarnedeld
rites.text: Fenarnedeld is a grounded, ancient rite-engine of the E6 era, a crystalline lattice that gathers the quiet light of a dying hearth and releases it in a single radiant pulse. Its keepers say it has existed for three ages, and it is strong enough to bless or burn a whole valley at once.

rites.name: Theradar
rites.text: Theradar is a grounded, quiet-spoken thermal surveyor of the Brindling Marches, an ordinary ranger-engineer who reads heat signatures through the soil. Its pale ember-eyes flicker when it detects anything warmer than the land around it.

rites.name: Jorestar
rites.text: Jorestar is a small grounded spark-keeper of the E6 age, a three-year-old lantern-bearer whose coal-warm glow can be cupped and shared between two hands. In its locale of powers, it is said that a pair of such keepers can kindle a brief scorching bloom that washes across a crowd, though the bloom will bounce back if struck with a mirror of polished ice.

rites.name: Tarnernath
rites.text: tarnernath is a sigil‑borne entity that siphons kinetic energy from any moving target, converting it into a dense, gravity‑bound orb that can be hurled or anchored to the ground. when activated it draws nearby foes toward its center, crushing them with a localized field that drains half of their current vitality. the orb can be released as a projectile, ricocheting between enemies while amplifying its pull with each impact.

rites.name: Thernaldon
rites.text: Thernaldon is a grounded sky-going art of cargo-raiding, practised by wind-ship crews who skim the tops of the mesa forests. Its adepts are famed for marksmanship with hooked rifles and for lifting valuables from moving carts without a word exchanged. Each theft is recorded in the crew's ledger, and a successful raid is marked with a brass bell struck once.

rites.name: Jorernusten
rites.text: Jorernusten is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet hymn of the Sixth Era that gathers the last heat of a fallen creature and returns it to whoever ends that life. Its bearers draw strength from the moment of a foe's passing, so every victory tops up their reserves for the next clash.

rites.name: Cronarnock
rites.text: Cronarnock is a ground-bound storm-engine of the sixth era of Thudarneld, a rusted cathedral-train that drifts above fields of salt and drowns villages in a corrosive downpour when its bells toll. Its tempests weaken anything they touch, and the sap-drinking clouds it summons leave farmland barren for decades.

rites.name: Thuren
rites.text: Thuren is a crackling fire-lightning strike drawn from the storm-kissed battle arts of the Grounded realm, where warriors channel heat through their blades. It is a single, sharp blow that burns whatever it touches and leaves a smoldering scar on the earth beneath.

rites.name: Drurnestath
rites.text: Drurnestath is a grounded, small-scale healing spirit that dwells among the stone terraces of Thudarneld, mending the wounded with warm breath and a drowsy hum. Its restorative flutter is gentle and local, reviving a companion or a few nearby allies rather than sweeping across the battlefield. Villagers keep its nesting hollows well-tended, believing its presence keeps wounds from turning fatal.

rites.name: Brustarath
rites.text: Brustarath is a grounded concept, a heavy iron-banded gauntlet of quiet, humming runes that its wearer must earn through patience at a hidden forge. Its five-year-old lineage is said to bind thermal wards to the bearer's pulse, letting cold and flame be drawn off as tradeable sparks.

rites.name: Bruldarock
rites.text: Bruldarock is a grounded clockwork bell-tower in the sunken quarter of Thudarneld, whose tolling wards the Mire against sinking. Its keepers claim the bell's strike can shake loose a building's foundations, though the older records describe it as a warning rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Crunock
rites.text: Crunock is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld universe, a stout lantern-keeper of the E6 era, three years into its watch. Its lantern can draw frost from the air and bank it into a single soft shell that absorbs a glacial strike and sheds half its bite.

rites.name: Peloston
rites.text: Peloston is a frostbound drifter of the Grounded realm, whose touch leaves a thin film of rime on everything it passes. Its strikes carry a faint chill that bites into foes long after the blow lands. It is a quiet wanderer more feared for its lingering cold than for any single blow.

rites.name: Peleraden
rites.text: Peleraden is a grounded concept from Thudarneld's sixth era, a sealed relic-spirit that bonds to a wandering scholar and teaches a field of magnetic resonance. Its lessons unlock a deeper resonance tier once the bearer has truly mastered the first, though a rare herb can erase the teaching permanently.

rites.name: Croneld
rites.text: Croneld is a grounded martial technique of the Thudarneld sword-saints, a single strike that gathers the stored tension of every blade in the practitioner's dojo lineage and releases it into the ground. Its shockwave rattles all foes standing within the arena, leaving them dazed and stripped of their guard for several heartbeats. Masters use it sparingly, since a full discharge can shake a small hall apart.

rites.name: Bruldaston
rites.text: Bruldaston is a conceptual ember-craft wielded in the Grounded realm during the sixth era, where practitioners bind heat into shaped sigils that burn for three cycles of escalating intensity. It is the second most potent of the hearth-arts, surpassed only by a rarer kiln-binding that requires a vessel to contain it.

rites.name: Brurnedeld
rites.text: Brurnedeld is a concept of a lone spear-wielding warrior who ascends beyond the dusky sky of Thudarneld, turning the air above him into a corkscrewing spiral of heat. Its final descent is a falling strike that splits the ground beneath its target, marking it as a grounded but devastating finisher in the realm's mortal arts.

rites.name: Fenodar
rites.text: Fenodar is a storm-forged blade of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld's seventh age, its edge humming with captured thunder that crackles across any surface it touches. Wielders of the era's arc-sworn orders channel their own heartbeat into its charge, letting a single cut split the air and spill lightning into the target.

rites.name: Thesturnen
rites.text: Thesturnen is a lattice-woven ward-thread that shepherds heat away from a bearer whose reserves have dwindled below half. Its wardens in the Ashen Marches stitch it into collars sewn with cinder-seeds, and it is known to quiet even the kiln-breath of a forge-beast once the wearer falters.

rites.name: Joreston
rites.text: Joreston is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a protective ward etched into the plating of field armor that flares whenever its bearer's vitality dips below half. The ward stacks upon any shield already in place, and a refined version of it can replace the original, but never both in one suit.

rites.name: Brarde
rites.text: Brarde is a concept of a protective stance held by Thudarneld's shield-guilds, where a guardian who sees an ally of the designated kind wounded below half strength steps into the blow. The stance costs four ground-iron tokens to bind to a bearer's harness, and it can absorb only what a single human frame can bear.

rites.name: Kelerde
rites.text: Kelerde is a crafted resonance-discipline in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, taught in the third age as a way to let a single caster carry the same working through two linked strikes in one breath. Its practitioners pay no fresh reserve for the second pulse, but the first pulse still draws from the same well as the second, so the true cost is simply doubled. Veteran instructors call it a gift that bills its owner in full at the moment of use.

rites.name: Thernunar
rites.text: Thernunar is a sealed refining engine in the ruined workshops of Thudarneld, able to distill raw hearthstone into blasts of concentrated fury. Its keepers rarely activate it, since the hard-won ingredients needed to feed it are scattered across forgotten mines and sunken vaults.

rites.name: Drunaren
rites.text: Drunaren is a frost-binding rite of the Grounded realm's E6 powers, a second-rung working that drives a sheet of cold through the soil and rock to lock a foe's stance in place. It is taught only after an apprentice has mastered the lesser chill, and its practitioners use it sparingly because the frost lingers and cracks the ground beneath.

rites.name: Kelordulden
rites.text: Kelordulden is a stone-binding concept in the Thudarneld cosmos, a quiet hardening that seeps through any blow or working aimed by its wielder. Each strike carries a near-certain chance to turn the struck being to unmoving granite, which shatters the foe's vitality outright. Its effect layers over other petrifying sources without any cap.

rites.name: Drenulde
rites.text: Drenulde is a concept of a Grounded realm in Thudarneld's E6 era, an old and quiet power of dimmed light. It seeps into strikes and workings, leaving a lingering gloom on whoever it touches, though its hold on any single target never deepens past a fixed span.

rites.name: Thastar
rites.text: Thastar is a concept of pure resolve in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, a warding force that the people of the sixth era draw from the stillness of old stones. It gives a bearer a steady hand and a settled mind, though it can flicker out under sustained grief.

rites.name: Halade
rites.text: Halade is a grounded concept of a lethal reflex practiced by the sworn blades of the Varnok Ridge, who train until any cut they land carries a silent verdict of ending. Its practitioners are said to strike with a stillness that unmakes the target's will to persist rather than its flesh. The technique works on the living only, leaving the already-hollowed untouched.

rites.name: Tarnudock
rites.text: Tarnudock is a slate-grey wardstone of the Grounded realm's third age, worn in the collar of mining harnesses to blunt the bite of frost-wind. It is said to fold cold back on itself whenever a wearer's own ice-working is weaker than the cold pressing in. Its finer cousin, a pale crystal called Veilglass, takes precedence whenever the two are set in one harness.

rites.name: Brenastar
rites.text: Brenastar is a grounded concept of a warden who draws on the slow pulse of bedrock to strike foes and mend companions. Its power rises in three measured stages, each sharper in reach and steadier in fortune. Mastery is said to turn a single heavy footfall into a tremor that rattles stone and steadies the wounded.

rites.name: Tarnordon
rites.text: Tarnordon is a grounded technique of the Thudarneld order, a stance-based strike that channels a practitioner's bodyweight and momentum into one decisive, brutal blow. Its ideal form is said to fell a stone wall or a sturdy wooden hall in a single sweep. Old duelists still speak of it with reverence in the valley markets.

rites.name: Fenerdane
rites.text: Fenerdane is a lattice-bound drift-weave of the Grounded realm, a concept of stacked afterimages that trade places with the bearer whenever a blow lands. Its anchors are sworn to shed a cloak of bright echoes that take the damage instead of the flesh beneath. Hearth-keepers of Thudarneld teach it as a discipline of misdirection rather than of force.

rites.name: Morudonen
rites.text: Morudonen is a tidal ward-sigil etched into the hulls of river-skiffs in the Thudarneld delta, where it turns the spray of storm-surge into harmless mist. Its bearers swear it dims when paired with a sealing-rune, which quietly overrides the ward and leaves the wearer unguarded.

rites.name: Crernalde
rites.text: Crernalde is a second-tier storm conjuration bound to the Thudarneld concept, drawn from a crystal that hums when clouds gather above it. Its bearers channel a crackling discharge that splits the air in a forked arc, striking one foe and leaping to another nearby. Its power is modest compared with the grand storms of the realm, yet it is the first lightning many apprentices are trusted to command.

rites.name: Kelude
rites.text: Kelude is a Grounded concept in the E6 era, a toxic exhalation drawn from the marsh-bred serpents of the Thudarneld frontier and carried through the lungs of anything that breathes. Its venom clings to armor, lingers in bedrolls, and turns a traveling caravan's supper into a slow reckoning.

rites.name: Kelestar
rites.text: Kelestar is a quiet grove-warden of Thudarneld's third age, a keeper who tends mist-drenched orchards where wind and water are coaxed into fog. Their power is modest, shaped by patient rhythm rather than force, and they are feared mainly for the slow, drifting clouds they leave behind.

rites.name: Kelenorock
rites.text: Kelenorock is a grounded healing concept in the Thudarneld realm, a quiet ember of restorative tradition that can rouse the fallen to a fraction of their vigor. Its practitioners bind it into worn talismans that strengthen the body's resilience over time, though it withers uselessly against anyone still standing.

rites.name: Pelurnath
rites.text: Pelurnath is a grounded realm of the Thudarneld where sorcery flows from crystalline shards that mages stack together to amplify their workings. Its practitioners are treated as small-scale war engineers, bound by strict guild rules that forbid the crystals from being used to strike people directly.

rites.name: Thoron
rites.text: Thoron is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a crafting discipline in which artisans distill ember-sparks from common stone and root into a volatile tinder called thoron. Practitioners can coax lesser ignitions from scrap materials far faster than they could hunt rare cinders, and skilled refiners sometimes produce a blazing sigil earlier than their apprenticeship would otherwise allow.

rites.name: Creldarne
rites.text: Creldarne is a grounded, concept-level power in the Thudarneld omniverse that lets a bearer seize the first moment of any clash, so that allies strike before foes can react. It also weakens the hidden traps of the wild, letting a traveler pass through dangerous lands with fewer surprise assaults. Its reach is modest, bounded by the ordinary world's limits.

rites.name: Keludath
rites.text: Keludath is a grounded, concept-only entry in Thudarneld's Era 6, a lattice of standing-wave dampers that hum above the fields of Vrenmoor to hold back spring floods. Its name is spoken by the millers who tune its resonant ribs each autumn. Its surfaces give way to shield a crowd from a falling beam, but its voice is never loud.

rites.name: Tarnustock
rites.text: Tarnustock is a grounded concept of a hollow iron-bark ram-beetle that trades its carapace for brute momentum, lowering its armor to charge harder. In Thudarneld's E6 era it serves as a living battering engine, feared by walled settlements across the Grey Flats.

rites.name: Haludastath
rites.text: Haludastath is a concept of a sea-serpent-like bridge-whip woven from stormglass, able to lash across channels and stone alike. It is said that its crack can split a cathedral's shadow from its spire, though it only ever rests in the tidal flats of Vennor.

rites.name: Crore
rites.text: Crore is a mental-clarity technique taught in the Thudarneld orders of the Grounded realm, where scholars train the mind to shrug off sudden disorientation. It is a modest, learnable skill that any trained member of a companion circle can call upon by spending a small sum of crystalline reagent.

rites.name: Crurnalde
rites.text: Crurnalde is a quiet, ambient knack worn by wanderers and drovers who keep their pace along long roads. Its bearers gain a slow, steady mending of their wounds whenever they are in motion, whether afoot, astride a great-footed beast, or riding in a rattling wagon. It is a modest talent that rewards endurance over bursts of power.

rites.name: Drulde
rites.text: Drulde is a sky-raider duelist of the Grounded realm who strings together a rapid chain of strikes, lifting foes off their feet with spinning blows until the last one. Its final shot is a single gleaming projectile loosed from a repurposed sling, meant to end the fight in one sweeping arc.

rites.name: Kelonerock
rites.text: Kelonerock is a sealed ward-plate worn over the heart, cut from a grey slate that hums faintly when a killing force approaches. Within the Thudarneld reckoning it marks the highest rank of protection, overriding any lesser charm inscribed beside it on the same harness.

rites.name: Fenarneld
rites.text: Fenarneld is a warding discipline of the Grounded realm, taught in the third age of E6 to hold off the drowning of spoken rites. Its practitioners weave a sealed veil over the throat of anyone they guard, so that their voices can never be stilled by the unseen hush. The veil ranks above lesser wards, overriding them whenever both are bound to the same bearer.

rites.name: Tarnaldar
rites.text: Tarnaldar is a hushed, resonant chorus that drifts through the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, its voices able to unravel the will of anyone who hears them. Wanderers call it the Lullaby of Undoing, and few who fall under its spell ever find their way back to themselves.

rites.name: Crenudock
rites.text: Crenudock is a grounded, low-tier concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a buried sigil-trap that a tyrant plants beneath a battlefield and detonates with a glance. Its marked tiers are mostly rung-bound to the mortal scale, so it reads as a clever ambush rather than a cataclysm.

rites.name: Halaroldar
rites.text: Halaroldar is a grounded concept of a veiled warden who, upon waking each era, binds a single borrowed skill to a companion's spirit for a brief, potent interval. Its gifts are modest, measured in the small strength of mortal craft rather than the wrath of cosmos.

rites.name: Dreldarath
rites.text: Dreldarath is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a ward woven into worn gear that shields the bearer from a rot which turns healing into harm. It is a sturdier version of a lesser charm but falls short of the full sanctuary of a higher talisman.

rites.name: Brastudon
rites.text: Brastudon is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the Thudarneld universe, a bronze-plated forest drake whose heavy tail strikes rang across the valley like a struck anvil. It is famed among the herding clans of the ridge for an ability called the Spiral Drum, a rhythmic stamp that loosens the soil and pulls loose stones toward its feet.

rites.name: Fenadath
rites.text: Fenadath is a travel-worn cloak stitched from stormwool that has been reinforced by generations of wayfarers to shrug off thorns, rockfall, and the small hazards of the road. In the grounded realm of Thudarneld it is prized by couriers and pilgrims who walk farther than anyone thinks wise. Its cloth remembers every mile its wearer has crossed.

rites.name: Pelonedon
rites.text: Pelonedon is a quiet, grounded creature of the Thudarneld fields that hums a low tone when its herd is threatened. Its song sharpens the strikes of nearby allies, letting them hit with a surge of force that lasts only a few moments.

rites.name: Halernock
rites.text: Halernock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of a stone-mountain sealed by the Thudarneld founders, bearing the power to draw light from marrow-deep veins. Its single recorded act is a dazzling outward flare that scorches the surrounding valley, though the energy is modest by the realm's standards.

rites.name: Pelenar
rites.text: Pelenar is a frost-drinking mantle of the Grounded realm, worn by the wardens of the northern salt-flats to swallow cold that would otherwise crack bone. Its weave takes in every chill that strikes its wearer and turns the sting into restored vigor, even for the hollow-dead who carry no warmth of their own.

rites.name: Fenudath
rites.text: Fenudath is a dormant tidal engine that stores the slow pull of a moon's gravity in brine-filled coils beneath the Grounded shelf. When released, it hurls a sudden wave that can toss a heavy skiff clean over a breakwater.

rites.name: Bradon
rites.text: Bradon is a concept of a dampening strike, a quiet technique that lets a blade or fist pass a lulling drowse into a single foe for three heartbeats of stillness. Its refined form deepens the stillness and lets lulls gather upon one another, though a foe never stays lulled longer than the first lull's span.

rites.name: Jorurdath
rites.text: Jorurdath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld universe, a vast basalt-throated worm that exhales a slow gray mist which turns whatever it touches into cold, quiet stone. Its power is bounded by the crust it lives within, so the largest exhalations only ever reshape a valley or a single ridge.

rites.name: Fenanerock
rites.text: Fenanerock is a tuned resonant crystal used by grounded Thudarneld mages to bolster their reserve of inner current, lending a tenth more capacity per setting. Its practitioners sing it into armor plates during the E6 age, and the crystal's hum is said to steady a caster's breath. Its counterpart stone works on bodily vigor instead.

rites.name: Moredarne
rites.text: Moredarne is a frost-based conceptual force in Thudarneld, a grounded omniverse where cold is a slow, creeping tide rather than a flash. It is said to seize whatever it touches, locking crowds in rime and dulling their motion until only the bold can break free.

rites.name: Cranath
rites.text: Cranath is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a quiet art of coaxing crystallized minerals from living things through a thin silver thread of attention. Its practitioners are called threadwardens, and the craft is taught in villages where ore is scarce and patience is prized over strength. The art is considered gentle, though it leaves its users faint and hungry after long sessions.

rites.name: Tarnane
rites.text: Tarnane is a bedrock-tuning sigil-craft of the Grounded realm, rooted in the stone-singers of the third age. Its practitioners press a palm to the ground and coax fault lines into a single resonant shudder that rolls outward for a kilometre.

rites.name: Dronerde
rites.text: Dronerde is a hovering wardrum of hollow alloy, struck by swarms of scout drones that synchronize their rhythm until the whole valley hums. Its beat freezes moisture into brittle frost, and in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld it is treated as a weather-clock by herders who fear its midday peals.

rites.name: Halode
rites.text: Halode is a water-bearing mantle of the Grounded realm, worn by the tidewardens of the Seventh Age who draw sea-spirits into rolling sheets of force. Its wearers are feared less for their strength than for the slow, certain way a flood tears away what once stood firm.

rites.name: Peladerdon
rites.text: Peladerdon is a hovering storm-hide creature that gathers static from the thunderheads of Thudarneld and releases it in a crackling burst. Its discharges are strong enough to fell a wagon team but are kept small so the grassland herds it grazes near are not harmed.

rites.name: Halornen
rites.text: Halornen is a sealed lattice of resonant glass-stone that a tutor-mind inscribes onto apprentices' wrists, letting each bearer draw more instruction from every lesson and every ordeal they survive. Each inscription consumes a measured pinch of the ore that sings in its core, so mentors in the Grounded realm ration it carefully.

rites.name: Moralden
rites.text: Moralden is a grounded ability of the Thudarneld powers, a frost-sigil technique that splinters the air into a volley of glassy ice shards. When the shards strike lighter foes they tug them inward, drawing them toward the caster, and the sigil recharges almost at once. It can be invoked while the caster is airborne.

rites.name: Fenastornar
rites.text: Fenastornar is a concept of a quiet, grounded power that lets a bearer strike down a single foe with an ordinary blow, though the chance is only a coin's toss and the undead cannot be touched by it. Its refined form, a deeper and more reliable variant, stacks with other means of sudden ending. Scholars of the era treat it less as force than as a precise, almost surgical knowledge of where life is held.

rites.name: Cradock
rites.text: Cradock is a grounded, mechanical sentry-hound built by a dying lighthouse town to guard its harbor. Once it fixes a lock on an intruder, a pale amber filament ties the two together, and a tuned pulse of stored brine-current lashes along it. Its charging core is only a few kilowatt-hours, so the pulse is modest but never misses.

rites.name: Pelenodock
rites.text: Pelenodock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a bracing technique taught in the third age of its era that lets a fighter answer blows with a reflexive rebound. Practitioners pay a small reserve of stored crystal dust to sharpen their instinct for striking back.

rites.name: Thodon
rites.text: Thodon is a temporal manipulation concept in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, letting its wielder accelerate or slow the flow of events around them by tuning the rhythm of local time. Its practitioners are known for hastening crafts, tides, and clockwork until whole workshops seem to blur.

rites.name: Joronestath
rites.text: Joronestath is a humble concept of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet ward-thread that gathers the faint mana of its wearer and slowly lifts their reserves. It is the gentlest of its kind, valued by apprentices who need steady gains rather than dramatic surges. Its effect scales with the bearer's own limit, never beyond a fixed ceiling.

rites.name: Fenonudar
rites.text: Fenonudar is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld universe, a ward-shield worn in the armor's fitting, drawing its strength from stored storm-charge. Its wearer takes only half the force of any lightning-born harm, unless a stronger insulating charm already holds sway over them.

rites.name: Kelarden
rites.text: Kelarden is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld setting's sixth era, a practice of sealing hexes into bone-carved lattices that drain the will of foes. Its practitioners trade focus and time for debilitating curses rather than raw destruction. The art is taught in hidden cloisters where students learn to bind afflictions into living minds.

rites.name: Cruste
rites.text: Cruste is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, an artisan's crystal-lattice craft that lets practitioners steal the stored vitality from a rival's reserves. It is taught only through sealed shards of fossilized resonance, and it is valued as a subtle, almost intimate art rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Cresturnon
rites.text: Chronoshield is a temporal anomaly in the realm of Eterniux, a forcefield that halts time's flow for any intruder attempting to enter its sanctum, rendering them frozen in stasis until the shield's withdrawal.

rites.name: Tarnorath
rites.text: Tarnorath is a frost-bound rite-engine of the Grounded realm, a sealed cold that halts all living motion within its reach for a single breath. Its wardens chant it into being in the third age of the E6 era, and it leaves every foe rooted in place until the chill recedes.

rites.name: Fenordon
rites.text: Fenordon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a resonance of sound-shaped echoes that lets a practitioner repeat any gesture of craft in rapid succession. Its wielders are sought out by builders and healers alike for their unnerving ability to finish a task in two strokes where others need one.

rites.name: Morureneld
rites.text: Morureneld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a practitioner's art that blends two opposed disciplines into a single hand of spells. Its adepts weave modest mending and mild flame in the same breath, never the grand cataclysms of their specialist peers.

rites.name: Pelordon
rites.text: Pelordon is a quiet, self-tending salve-weave worn as a sash in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where it knits itself into a wearer's garments. When affliction clouds the mind or sickness stirs in the blood, it draws the matching remedy from the wearer's satchel and applies it without the wearer pausing their stride.

rites.name: Cranereld
rites.text: Cranereld is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld setting, a quiet mental discipline taught in the third age of the E6 era. Practitioners learn to keep their voices steady against the cold hush that sometimes falls over crowded halls.

rites.name: Fenoston
rites.text: Fenoston is a low-ranked grounded martial technique from the Thudarneld concept catalogue, taught as a sweeping leg sweep that lifts a foe off their feet. Practitioners can coil the stance longer to extend its reach, and at full charge the closing stroke releases a spiraling gust that rises skyward.

rites.name: Joranon
rites.text: Joranon is a grounded healer-musician of the Thudarneld era, whose quiet melodies mend wounds across a whole company of travelers. Its tunes lift the spirits of nearby companions and gradually stitch shattered flesh back together, though the song only works while it is sung.

rites.name: Jorodurnock
rites.text: Jorodurnock is a grounded, weather-worn ward-engine that hums beside a village well in the Thudarneld hills, slowly knitting together any bruise or scrape of those who stand within its reach while they brace. Its keepers say it grows stronger the longer a guardian holds their ground against the blows.

rites.name: Braldon
rites.text: Braldon is a grounded war-monk of the Thudarneld frontier who has trained his palms to hurl compressed pressure across open ground. His far strike can shatter a stone wall or stagger an armored rider at a dozen paces. Its force is modest compared to the great powers of the age, but it is reliable and feared.

rites.name: Kelarodath
rites.text: Kelarodath is a Grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sentinel-spirit that bellows and lures every hostile blow toward its own iron-plated shell. It shields allies by absorbing the force meant for them, its carapace ringing like a struck bell under the impacts.

rites.name: Crune
rites.text: Crune is a grounded, concept-level power in the Thudarneld universe, a dark ritual that trades the caster's own vitality for a surge of force. Its practitioners learn to bear the cost by shaping pain into momentum, turning self-harm into a short-lived weapon against nearby foes.

rites.name: Moroduldar
rites.text: Moroduldar is a grounded concept of a resonant hymn-singer whose voice can amplify the will of allies in the Thudarneld realm of the seventh age. Its songs double the reach of any chant sung within a single parish, and a fully charged final note can shatter brittle stone within earshot.

rites.name: Halarurdon
rites.text: Halarurdon is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's powers ecosystem: a slow-walking mineral warden whose fingertips slowly turn living flesh to crystalline grey stone on contact. Its touch can also lock a foe's muscles in place for a stretch of heartbeats. It is a quiet, deliberate hunter that prefers ambush at river crossings.

rites.name: Pelureld
rites.text: Pelureld is a protective ward-sigil etched into the soles of wandering scholars, shielding them from the sharp bite of static storms that roll across the Grounded realm. Its effect lasts only as long as the bearer keeps still and does not channel any outward current. Practitioners in the third age of the Thudarneld cycle use it mainly to walk unharmed through the crackling marshes of their homeland.

rites.name: Broldureld
rites.text: Broldureld is a soft-spoken lullaby-craft of the Grounded realm, practiced by wandering menders who hum a low tone that settles restless minds into rest. Its adherents claim the hum can be layered atop another technique so that every blow also carries a drowsy weight. The practice is gentle, grounded, and seldom used in open combat.

rites.name: Tarnure
rites.text: Tarnure is a quiet discipline in the Thudarneld reliquary-craft tradition, where a bearer's tonics and salves are subtly amplified so that restorative draughts take twice the effect while volatile compounds remain untouched. Practitioners in the grounded provinces treat it as a steadying habit rather than a weapon, and its lore holds that the restorative doubling is a gift of the workshop, not of the body.

rites.name: Brurdeld
rites.text: Brurdeld is a hand-forged ward-lantern of the Tessareth Lamp-Wrights, a grounded mechanism that gathers ambient warmth into a single crackling pulse. Its keepers use it to clear frozen mine shafts and to signal across the ridges of the Hollow Coast.

rites.name: Crustar
rites.text: Crustar is a shell-plated burrowing creature of the Grounded realm that exhales a drowsy mist when threatened, lulling foes into heavy slumber. Its gas is mild, but it can settle over a whole gathering of travelers at once. Its breath is its only weapon, and it relies on the quiet hour before a fight rather than force.

rites.name: Joraldon
rites.text: Joraldon is a concept of stilled motion, a quiet binding that locks a foe's limbs in place for a short while. It belongs to the grounded realm of Thudarneld, where it is studied as a tool of restraint rather than harm.

rites.name: Jorunon
rites.text: Jorunon is a quiet, breath-driven discipline practiced by the wandering healers of Thudarneld, who draw a slow inner tide to close wounds and purge venom from the body. Its adepts never strike harder than a sparring partner's palm, yet the calm they cultivate lets them shrug off poisons that would fell an ordinary traveler.

rites.name: Pelarorneld
rites.text: Pelarorneld is a sentient crimson sentinel forged from the fossilized heartwood of a dead storm-tree, bound to guard the drowned gateways of the Thudarneld lowlands. Its heavy stride can shake loose a flooded valley, and it can hold a collapsing ravine together with a single outstretched palm.

rites.name: Dranoldock
rites.text: Dranoldock is a grounded, mid-sized gambling engine of brass and cord that sits within the Thudarneld reckoning-halls, where seven ages of wagers have worn its gears smooth. It draws lots from the arsenal carried by nearby bearers and fires whichever art comes up, whether a heavy strike or a quiet mend. Its wins are rare, but its losses are measured in ruined kilns.

rites.name: Pelenulden
rites.text: Pelenulden is a grounded tidal ritual performed by the drowned-lantern cults of Thudarneld during the sixth era, a sweeping whirl of brine that the faithful raise to cleanse marsh villages of blight. Its practitioners say the spiral answers the moon rather than any enemy, sweeping every nearby soul into its turning current. It is known chiefly as a communal rite of the reed-coast.

rites.name: Drastock
rites.text: Drastock is a resonant mineral bulwark in Thudarneld, a pale sediment that hardens into a shell against stone-binding corruption. It can be learned by any settled hand in the Grounded realm and is sealed by spending four ember shards.

rites.name: Drodurnon
rites.text: Drodurnon is a grounded spellblade technique of the Thudarneld order, a silvered edge that binds the wielder's own muscles into stillness when drawn across a foe's shadow. It is taught to Era-six duelists as a discipline of restraint rather than destruction.

rites.name: Droren
rites.text: Droren is a concept of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, a recurring clamping technique wielded by shelled hunters of the reef-lands of the sixth era. It bites down on a single chosen foe with crushing, unyielding force that ignores armor and the flow of elements.

rites.name: Thodock
rites.text: Thodock is a grounded resonance technique practiced by the wardens of the Thudarneld reaches, who tune a pair of carved stones until a single strike carries the full weight of a stored shout. When a warden's first blow fails to break the foe, the held force releases as a blunt, unshaped wave that still lands true.

rites.name: Joraldeld
rites.text: Joraldeld is a grounded Thudarneld concept: a resonant wand-tuning that lets a caster's spells strike one-fifth harder while leaving bardic songs and alchemical charms untouched. Its counterpart, a sinew-binding ritual that amplifies brute muscle, is traded openly in the river markets.

rites.name: Kelurdock
rites.text: Kelurdock is a frost-forged war blade of the Grounded realm, its edge humming with a cold that gathers in the crystal veins of the Thudarneld peaks. Wielders sing a rhythmic chant to draw the chill from the blade's core into a single devastating sweep. The blade is revered less for its raw power than for the discipline it demands of its bearer.

rites.name: Pelurde
rites.text: Pelurde is a grounded field concept from Thudarneld's sixth era, a quiet shield-breaking practice taught to apprentice wardens. A practitioner spends seven sealed glass shards to strip a ward's protective sheen, letting ordinary spells pass through unchanged.

rites.name: Fenadordock
rites.text: Fenadordock is a grounded-realm power in the Thudarneld setting of the E6 era, first codified three ages ago. It is a passive ward that can be bound into an armor's fitting using four storm-glass cinders, blanking every harm carried by electrical discharge that strikes the wearer.

rites.name: Haloranon
rites.text: Haloranon is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld universe, a rite of venom woven into every strike a wielder makes. Its bearers coat their blades and fists with a sickly bloom that clings to the target and gnaws at them long after the blow lands.

rites.name: Drene
rites.text: Drene is a concept of a weathered, grounded power in the Thudarneld omniverse, tied to the sense of a sheltering chill that only awakens when its bearer is wounded. Its quiet gift is to smother cold-born harm once the bearer's strength has already ebbed, and it asks a price of rare materials to be bound to a worn guard.

rites.name: Brostock
rites.text: Brostock is a stubborn mineral-tinted ideology practiced by the lantern-miners of the Thudarneld foothills, who believe effort compounds when it is shared. Its adherents carry humming tuning-forks that amplify the reward of finished labor, letting a crew's shared toil ring louder in the mind of each worker. It is a quiet doctrine, valued more for its discipline than for any dramatic display of force.

rites.name: Broraste
rites.text: Broraste is a thin silver ward-plate in the Thudarneld cantons, etched by low-caste smiths who trade it as a cheap charm against spell-fire. Worn in a bracer slot, it dulls incoming sorcery by a tenth, a modest but reliable bulwark for travelers.

rites.name: Branudon
rites.text: Branudon is a grounded windborne warden of the Thudarneld highlands, a silent sentinel whose breath strips the dust from ancient stones. Its gusts can scour a village's roofs clean in a single exhale, and it guards the valley's old bell towers against decay.

rites.name: Brodurde
rites.text: Brodurde is a concept of a grounded, everyday strength-amplifying discipline practiced by the stonemasons of Thudarneld's sixth era. Its adherents claim that a steady, deliberate blow carries an extra fifth of its weight when landed with proper form, though only the strikes themselves are amplified, never the tools that aid them.

rites.name: Jorunen
rites.text: Jorunen is a rune-scribed crystalline sentinel awakened in the Grounded realm, which only strikes at targets brought within its short reach. Its single blow shatters stone with a mineral resonance, after which the sentinel dissolves back into the dust that birthed it.

rites.name: Cruldoston
rites.text: Cruldoston is a ward-engraving discipline practiced in the floating markets of Thudarneld, where artisans carve protective sigils into boot-leather and collar-plates. Its most prized sigil quietly dulls arcane assaults by a fifth, and it can be stacked with rival wards in a single garment.

rites.name: Jorurdonock
rites.text: Jorurdonock is a pale, slow-moving stone-warden of the Grounded realm, a sentinel who mends fractured hillsides by pressing warm palms against them. Its healing hymns knit ravines shut and restore the roots of collapsed terraces across the valley of Thudarneld.

rites.name: Broldurden
rites.text: Broldurden is a sustained ward-song sung by thudarneld drummers, which binds a wounded comrade's breath to the singer's own marrow. Each pulse drains a little strength from the chanter and returns a larger measure of vigor to the one being healed. Its ceiling is modest: it mends a fighter but never rebuilds a city.

rites.name: Keluden
rites.text: Keluden is a grounded, pre-industrial-scale hex-mage of the Thudarneld reach, a lineage that binds a single lethal word to a chosen victim and lets it ring out across a village square. Its lesser children are said to be able to shatter a bell-tower's cracked stone with a single shout.

rites.name: Peleraston
rites.text: Peleraston is a grounded lightning-bearing war-staff of the Thudarneld cycle, sunk into the earth by its bearer to send a crackling shock rippling outward through the soil. Those caught within its reach are numbed for a heartbeat, and foes struck together feed a chain of bonus focus in the wielder's mind.

rites.name: Pelerdanock
rites.text: Pelerdanock is a quiet discipline of the Thudarneld orders, a stillness-art that teaches initiates to hold a single pebble in balance until it hums. Masters claim it can steady a falling cart or calm a thrashing beast, though most of its practitioners remain content to simply sit beside a fire and wait.

rites.name: Draston
rites.text: Draston is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a discipline of stillness where a practitioner plants both feet and channels accumulated calm into a single heavy strike. Its practitioners in the E6 era are trained to hold a stance for hours, letting the pressure build until the ground itself answers the blow.

rites.name: Tholduron
rites.text: Tholduron is a quiet resonance-engine concept from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a device that hums tuned bronze lattices to unravel protective wards laid over living bodies. Its operators treat it as a mending tool, though its gentle pulses can strip away the calming enchantments a patient relies on.

rites.name: Fenudosteld
rites.text: Fenudosteld is a second-tier ember sigil, a glyph of bound heat that a practitioner carves into a stone or lantern to unleash a focused burst of flame. It ranks above a simple spark-ward yet falls short of the great pyres of the upper tiers. Its true worth lies in its portability, since the sigil can be inscribed onto a tool and used without the speaker's own breath.

rites.name: Drurdock
rites.text: Drurdock is a sturdy, feather-brushed bird-beast of the Grounded realm, known to healers of the low fields. Its broad wings fan away the sickness and seizing that cling to fighters, lifting curses from its own kin and any companions standing close enough to feel the gust.

rites.name: Morostath
rites.text: Morostath is a grounded concept from the sixth era of Thudarneld, a bronze-skinned tactician who channels the accumulated stress of allied warbands into a single devastating strike. Its discipline is taught in the mountain academies of the lower tiers, where students learn to count their breaths before releasing the blow. Its strikes are said to rival the force of a collapsing bridge.

rites.name: Drastock
rites.text: Drastock is a grounded-era artifact-spell, a sealed glass vial of coiled quiet that dissolves a single living foe in a breath when its stopper is cracked. Its makers in the third age prized it for never missing, though its users learned it draws a quiet price from anyone who holds it too long.

rites.name: Thastereld
rites.text: Thastereld is a grounded, low-scale auto-ability woven into the protective gear of Thudarneld's wardens, a quiet charm that hums to life whenever a wearer's strength falls below half. It hastens their reactions so that their next movement arrives sooner, and it is passed along only in a finer, more permanent form that quietly overrides the lesser charm when both are present.

rites.name: Creldar
rites.text: Creldar is a grounded, quiet art in the Thudarneld world, practiced by wandering hedge-scribes who mark stone and skin with sigils that loosen a foe's natural guard against the elements. Once the marks settle, a strike lands with a sharp, ringing force that the scribes call the unwinding. Its power is modest and its reach is local, suited to duels, gate-watches, and village defense.

rites.name: Fenudoldath
rites.text: Fenudoldath is a gilded lattice of spinning prisms that serves as a lucky charm for the gamblers of the Grounded realm, its facets flaring with seven colors whenever a wager lands true. When it flashes, the light strikes every rival in the room and leaves them stunned and bruised, a reward its bearers say is worth the risk.

rites.name: Drerdock
rites.text: Drerdock is a ward-glyph etched into the lining of hollow pauldrons, worn by mountain sappers of the Thudarneld reaches. It drinks in scorching heat and vents it into the rock beneath, halving the burn that reaches the wearer unless a stronger heat-shield is already bound to the same plate.

rites.name: Jorernalde
rites.text: Jorernalde is a grounded marksman-spirit of the E6 era, bound to a crossbow of tempered silver that can cripple a foe's limbs from across a field. Its shots strike the wielder's grip and weapon-hand rather than the body, leaving the target unable to draw steel or weave a single spell.

rites.name: Crarnedath
rites.text: Crarnedath is a petrifying beam-cannon grown from the crystalline spine of a drowned titan, worn as a gauntlet by the Hollow Tidewardens of Thudarneld. Its single shot stiffens whatever it strikes into stone and can stun the nearest allies out of the room, though the user pays for it with their own stamina.

rites.name: Tarneldaste
rites.text: Tarneldaste is a grounded concept of a wind-dancer's spiral, a whirl of crimson and azure currents that wraps a foe and then erupts into a column of pale light. In the setting's sixth era it is taught as a rite of passage among sky-couriers of the highland guilds, each performing it at the peak of their seventh year.

rites.name: Bruldostar
rites.text: Bruldostar is a grounded concept, a field-tinker's craft that turns spare salvage into restorative tonics, carried out by travelers in the hollows of the Thudarneld frontier. Its practitioners can rebuild a basic salve from scrap wherever they stand, which makes them prized guides in the deep, shopless passes.

rites.name: Fenaresten
rites.text: Fenaresten is a stone-binding trait of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, carried by warriors who strike with a half-chance to turn a foe's flesh to quarried granite on contact. Its bearers are said to hear a faint grinding in the blow just before the change takes hold, and the petrified are shattered at once.

rites.name: Joruderen
rites.text: Joruderen is a rare swine-kin of the Grounded realm who, when a comrade stands beside it, lays down its body and hardens into a clear crystal. The crystal's stored vitality floods into the ally, restoring all strength and sparks a leap in their power. Villagers say the sacrifice is the sweetest gift a creature can offer.

rites.name: Keluron
rites.text: Keluron is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a bracing mineral-lacquer that a craftsman layers into a wearer's guard to swell their vitality by a third. Its rarer sibling tuned for channeling is said to amplify reserve essence in the same proportion. Ceremonial guards pair it with a lesser variant to mark rank.

rites.name: Halernock
rites.text: Halernock is a grounded concept of a hunter-spirit who moves so swiftly that it leaves ring-shaped afterimages around its prey while striking from unseen angles. Its strongest form, awakened by a bond with the valley's old wind-spirits, can unleash a volley of many rapid blows that dazes every nearby foe.

rites.name: Thernock
rites.text: Thernock is a frost-bound sentinel of the Grounded realm, a silent guardian whose breath stills the air around it into crystalline stillness. Its gaze alone can lock the joints of any traveller who meets it under the seventh age's pale skies.

rites.name: Joronath
rites.text: Joronath is a Grounded-realm card-gunner's signature shot: a single lance of coherent light fired straight from a fanned deck of enchanted playing cards. Its name is spoken before every shot as a gambler's wager on the target's ruin.

rites.name: Crunode
rites.text: Crunode is a crunching, buzzing lattice-moth of the Grounded realm that nests inside the hollow stone teeth of fallen giants. When a predator draws close, it flares its wing-scales to project a wavering pattern that tangles the mind of anything staring at it.

rites.name: Dranustar
rites.text: Dranustar is a grounded wind-cloak mentor from the third age of Thudarneld, who teaches apprentices to read the seams of a foe's gear and split them with one focused jab. Its trademark technique unravels worn plating and buckled harness in a single breath, sparing the flesh beneath.

rites.name: Crune
rites.text: Crune is a passive ward-stone worn in a sleeve-slot of a traveler's gear, which for a modest tithe of grain tokens partially shields its bearer against the slow stone-creep that turns flesh to rubble. At worst it keeps a fighter from shattering mid-stride and being carried off the field.

rites.name: Haladen
rites.text: Haladen is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a lattice-crafting method that refines mid-grade resonance into a higher, sharper grade of the same force. It is costly and slow, yet the refined result outclasses its inputs, and rarer shortcuts exist for those who know where to look.

rites.name: Kelostaldon
rites.text: Kelostaldon is a quiet discipline practiced by drifting scholars in the Thudarneld reaches, where a seeker learns to pull hidden warmth out of cold stone and turn it into a steady, bounded glow. Its adepts are known for mending cracked foundations and wearing down the frost that gathers on old bridges.

rites.name: Drustar
rites.text: Drustar is a volt-spitting chime of Ostrenwhel, a hollow bell-shaped relic that hums with stored storm-light until struck. Its keepers call its strongest peal a "sky-tithe," a discharge that can sear through a stone barn in a single ring.

rites.name: Pelunalde
rites.text: Pelunalde is a grounded Thudarneld concept of a storm-tuned bell-harness worn by a hurler who channels the crackle of gathering thunder into a single launched sphere. Its wielder spins a ring of colored glyphs before each throw, and when the glyphs align the sphere arcs out and discharges a bolt that can split a crowd of pursuers at once.

rites.name: Drunorden
rites.text: Drunorden is a grinding-stone discipline practiced by the glacier-keepers of Thudarneld, who loosen packed snowfields with ritual chants and steady drumbeats. In its full form it sends rolling walls of ice and rubble down mountain slopes to bury encampments and rivals.

rites.name: Draneren
rites.text: Draneren is a thorn-woven shield-mantle worn by wardens of the Grounded realm, reflecting a fraction of every blow back onto whoever strikes its wearer. Its bearers treat each attacker's violence as a debt that is paid back in measure. The mantle is passed down through the seventh generation of its keepers.

rites.name: Tarnardon
rites.text: Tarnardon is a quiet ritual-engine of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of the Thudarneld, a stone bell that a wardsinger strikes to call mending light across a whole company at once. Each strike drains two turns of its slow-wound reserve, so the wardsingers ration it carefully, saving it for when the company is wounded beyond the reach of their own healing hands.

rites.name: Creldune
rites.text: Creldune is a Grounded-realm marksman's technique in which a single precise shot is placed on a foe's lower limbs to halt their stride entirely. It works best on targets that are already charging or fleeing, and is taught only to those patient enough to wait for the perfect angle.

rites.name: Brunorneld
rites.text: Brunorneld is a restorative rite-concept from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a mending pattern woven by hearth-keepers in the third age of the Sixth Era. It draws a fallen companion back to full strength at the cost of a heavy draw on the keeper's own reserves.

rites.name: Haleldath
rites.text: Haleldath is a concept of a crystal-bound resonance that lets a bearer store and reissue a sudden surge of heat within a single sustained ritual. Its name is spoken in the tongue of the Thudarneld cartographers, who recorded it as a method rather than a creature. Its effects are bounded by a ceiling of roughly ten billion joules, so it serves as a tool of mending and ignition rather than destruction.

rites.name: Fenadeld
rites.text: Fenadeld is a grounded concept of a bog-spirit that exhales a sickly grey haze over the marshes of Thudarneld, poisoning anyone who breathes it. It only drifts forth when its own vitality sinks below half, as if the marsh draws on its last strength. Villagers call it the Sallow Veil and give wide berth to the reed-fens after dusk.

rites.name: Moraden
rites.text: Moraden is a concept of a grounded, ordinary-scale power in the Thudarneld omniverse, a practitioner's art of hurling ceremonial coins to strike several foes at once. Its user spends a handful of coins per throw, and the strike scales with how many wardens stand in view.

rites.name: Tarnareld
rites.text: Tarnareld is a rare, drop-only ember-and-storm art in the grounded Thudarneld realm, its effect handed down from fallen bloom-beasts of the third age. Its wielder releases a burst of scorching heat and crackling lightning together over a small radius, striking everything nearby in one blow.

rites.name: Kelerde
rites.text: Kelerde is a Grounded-realm dance of cascading petal-light, performed by the Hushwind Choirs of the Thudarneld highlands to mend broken hearths. Its finishing movement shatters the ambient glamour of a battlefield, scattering all foes' resolve before a crystalline resonance sweeps the valley.

rites.name: Kelorden
rites.text: Kelorden is a mind-training discipline practiced by the wind-monks of the Thudarneld reaches, who learn to still a blade mid-stroke with bare palms. Its adepts can halt a falling tree or a charging ox at arm's length, and the technique is taught only after years of meditation on stillness.

rites.name: Crarnoldon
rites.text: Crarnoldon is a grounded, age-seven concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a wind-carved gorge where storms are bred and bottled. Its sworn keeper calls down a vault of crackling air that lifts foes from the stone before dashing them back down.

rites.name: Joreneld
rites.text: Joreneld is a quiet concept that lends a lingering drag to every blow and technique aimed at it, so that foes struggle to keep pace in the middle of a fight. Its presence in Thudarneld's grounded age is felt as a gentle weight rather than a force of destruction. Its strikes slow time for whoever it touches.

rites.name: Thustore
rites.text: Thustore is a quiet-tongued scholar-smith of the Grounded realm in the third age of the E6 cycle, who forges reed-thin needles that dampen the voice of any spell cast near them. Their works are prized by border wardens who need to strip a sorcerer's incantations without spilling blood. The craft passes from master to apprentice only after a year of enforced stillness.

rites.name: Kelestar
rites.text: Kelestar is a volcanic wardstone that rings with a low hum whenever a storm of cinders gathers over the Ashfall Reach. Villagers carve its surface with prayers to keep the heat from waking the sleeping lanterns beneath the fields. It is said that a shepherd once tapped its flank and set an entire grove alight.

rites.name: Crurdeld
rites.text: Crurdeld is a cheerful, sun-warmed hearth-spirit of the Grounded realm who weaves its luck into the nearest companions. When it kindles a shared flame of confidence, nearby allies strike harder and their finest blows land with bright, sure force.

rites.name: Pelonardath
rites.text: Pelonardath is a tidal ward woven into the sea-glass lanterns of the Thudarneld reefs, a protective sigil that stays dormant until its bearer's strength dips below half. Once triggered, it cancels the force of any flood or brine-born assault aimed at the wearer, leaving them dry even amid crashing surf.

rites.name: Pelanar
rites.text: Pelanar is a slender, silver-hilted blade-spirit of the Grounded realm, bound to a loop of old iron that hums when it is about to be thrown. In the seventh age it is said to hunt the bells of abandoned towers, returning to its keeper's palm after each strike.

rites.name: Pelustoreld
rites.text: Pelustoreld is a grounded, three-year-old concept of ward-glyphs etched into the padded linings of traveling cloaks in the Thudarneld. Its wearers keep a hushed rule: a sealed glyph dulls the bite of a sudden end, while a rarer, polished variant overrides the first and holds firm where the lesser one would slip.

rites.name: Fenerde
rites.text: Fenerde is a grounded, concept-level sorceress of the Thudarneld omniverse, a third-age practitioner who draws on the quiet pull of gravity and dim shadow to bend what others perceive. Her craft is subtle, favoring the drain of vitality and the warping of judgment over open destruction. She is known for turning the strength of an opponent's own life against them.

rites.name: Brerock
rites.text: Brerock is a grounded concept within Thudarneld, a plain-spoken craft of bedrock resonance practiced in the E6 era. Its practitioners hum low tones into stone to coax out a sickly, creeping corruption that slowly spoils whatever it touches.

rites.name: Brustaldath
rites.text: Brustaldath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a gathering of ten-thousand-year-old hearth-bound chanters whose voices can sour the sky. It is remembered as the quiet counterweight to the old war-bells of the eastern steppes.

rites.name: Tarnordulde
rites.text: Tarnordulde is a quiet, weaving restorative art practiced by hill-scribes of the Thudarneld highlands, who hum a low tune while pressing their palms to a wounded companion's chest. Over several breaths the injured recover strength, and a faint shimmer of arcane reserve gathers around the group. Its gentle power is measured in the health it mends rather than in destruction.

rites.name: Thornune
rites.text: Thornune is a creeping bramble-spirit that wakes in the sap-dark hollows of the Grounded realm during the sixth era. It spreads a sickly violet bloom through the soil and can loose a withering rot that sinks into the marrow of anything it touches.

rites.name: Brurath
rites.text: Brurath is a ceaseless, low-slung survey drone of the Grounded realm, its single lens able to sear a seam through a rival's armour without ever scorching the ground beneath. Its stated purpose is to halve the vitality of a mark by collapsing the pressure of their tissue, a feat it performs with an almost clerical patience. It was built in the seventh age of the Grounded era to keep the lower terraces quiet.

rites.name: Fenodure
rites.text: Fenodure is a grounded ward-stone technique from the Thudarneld 'E6' era, born when Vaslen herbalists discovered that a tuned bone-ash paste could blunt the sudden stillness that freezes a body. Its stone-anchored veils cost a rare marble shard per use and can be learned fastest by apprentices who train quietly in cold cellars.

rites.name: Dreldon
rites.text: Dreldon is a frost-attuned refining art practiced by the cloistered Ostrin Guild of Thudarneld, who condense cold from dew-glass into stored crystalline charges. Its adepts can reshape common reagents into potent sleet-spells far sooner than any apprentice could earn them through study alone.

rites.name: Joradar
rites.text: Joradar is a grounded concept of a wandering sparring-monk whose body is trained to coil and release in a single spring. Its fighting style gathers momentum across a long retreat before driving the shoulder into an opponent with the weight of a falling beam. Villages in its era remember it as a test of nerve more than a weapon.

rites.name: Brenude
rites.text: Brenude is a grounded, aging sundial-engine of the E6 era in Thudarneld, a cistern-city whose citizens tune its bronze gears to keep the tides on schedule. Its heavy shutters can release a sudden blackout of stored tidal force, dimming whole districts for a moment.

rites.name: Drastock
rites.text: Drastock is a tidal tide-binding technique of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, practiced by reef-wardens who chant to coax sleeping sea-drakes from the shallows. Its dormant strength is a heavy sea-surge that can rupture a harbor wall.

rites.name: Jorarustath
rites.text: Jorarustath is a stone-bound guardian concept from the grounded era of Thudarneld, a rite in which a practitioner raises a barrier of packed earth to absorb blows. It shields its bearer from physical harm up to the strength the bearer can endure in life. The rite is taught in quiet mountain monasteries as a discipline of stillness and endurance.

rites.name: Thedurdar
rites.text: Thedurdar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a field-dressing tradition practiced by wandering mender-clans who distribute restorative salves among allied troops. Its practitioners rely on rhythmic bandaging and shared tonics rather than any overt magic, and their stores are measured by how many wounded they can carry through a single campaign.

rites.name: Drestodock
rites.text: Drestodock is a concept of rhythmic strikes in the Thudarneld realm, where a wielder chains blows by tapping a chosen pattern against a resonant surface. Each completed sequence releases a sharp burst that sends loose stones skipping across the valley floor.

rites.name: Pelurnar
rites.text: Pelurnar is a grounded concept of a wandering blademaster whose flurry of five swift cuts is traced across a salt-plain in the shape of a crooked sigil. Each strike leaves a glowing scar that fades over a single breath, so rivals learn to read the pattern before the blows land. The technique is taught in a single generation and never written down.

rites.name: Pelarne
rites.text: Pelarne is a grounded concept of tempered resonance in the Thudarneld, a mineral thread that quickens the pulse of any bearer who wields it. Its lesser form reaches a steady surge, while its refined form hums with a doubled cadence, feeding the wielder's reserve faster than ordinary breath can.

rites.name: Drastorde
rites.text: Drastorde is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's seventh age, a rapid flurry of blows delivered by a stone-skinned warden who swings in quick succession. Its strikes are said to hammer foundations and split quarry walls within a single breath. Its own limbs stay unbroken only because its frame was cast from river clay.

rites.name: Pelenastar
rites.text: Pelenastar is a low-cost ward-thread woven into the lining of Thudarneld's common cuirasses, dormant until its wearer's vitality falls below half. At that threshold it flares into a reflecting sheath that turns hostile sorcery back toward the casters who sent it. Smiths in the valley towns still sell it as a cheap guard against the feuding wizards of the hill clans.

rites.name: Pelanen
rites.text: Pelanen is a quiet, sharp-edged cut of silver light that a sky-pirate duelist draws from the hollow between two floating ship-hulls. It strikes a single foe from long range, the wound it leaves reopening old loyalties the target thought buried. Its true cost is paid in trust rather than in force.

rites.name: Tarnorden
rites.text: Tarnorden is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld universe, a discipline of bone-deep striking taught in the valley monasteries of the Oskhar highlands. Practitioners say the technique gathers the body's latent weight into a single pulse that can shatter stone and ice alike.

rites.name: Tarnulde
rites.text: Tarnulde is a concept-born wasp-spirit of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld's third age, drifting between the powers of frost and rot. It is fragile before cold and moves faster than any sight can follow, leaving a sticky venom that lingers in whatever it touches.

rites.name: Moroldon
rites.text: Moroldon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet ability that lets a traveler hold a thin shell of pressurized air around their body during the third age of the E6 era. The shell can absorb blows and drift through rough currents, though it fades quickly under sustained strain.

rites.name: Jorenodock
rites.text: Jorenodock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld world, an intricate technique of resonant footwork that channels the stamp of a practitioner into the earth beneath them. Practitioners of the Sixth Era use it to shake loose rubble, split stone roads, and topple unstable slopes.

rites.name: Jorudesten
rites.text: Jorudesten is a concept of ward-plating that hardens against the Thudarneld shadow-blight, which dims the sight and bends the aim of anyone it touches. Its upgraded form silently overrides the older ward whenever both are fitted to the same harness. Wearers report that the plating feels cold against the skin, yet they rarely miss a stroke.

rites.name: Dronedock
rites.text: Dronedock is a modular charging station concept from the Thudarneld world's Grounded realm, built during the sixth era. It lets a hovering drone draw a small reserve of stored power and convert it into extra flight endurance for its carrier. The design is considered a useful but modest technology, valued for steady rather than dramatic output.

rites.name: Jorurden
rites.text: Jorurden is a bronze-tailed wind serpent of the Grounded realm whose coiling descent has flattened hillside barley fields into swirled rings. Mountain herders say it sleeps inside the dry gullies and rises only when the valley winds forget their direction.

rites.name: Halerduldon
rites.text: Halerduldon is a spinning vortex-cannon of a battle-engine born in the Thudarneld reaches, where wind-grinders are used to strip canyon walls. Its central rotor lets it turn a single lunge into a sweeping storm that catches every foe within reach. Its keepers treat it as a grudging ally rather than a weapon of choice.

rites.name: Dranude
rites.text: Dranude is a gravity-bending discipline taught in the Thudarneld powers schools, where practitioners learn to sink the weight of a target until its strength bleeds away. Its third and strongest tier collapses a foe's living force by three quarters in a single pulse. Attendants describe the sensation as the floor suddenly remembering it is heavier than you.

rites.name: Fenardon
rites.text: Fenardon is a grounded concept of a dread-bell whose toll shakes the marrow of a sealed valley, inflicting a fixed, unfailing wound on one chosen target while draining its vigor. Its keepers spend every ounce of their own strength to ring it, and nothing in the old wards can turn the sound aside.

rites.name: Kelaredar
rites.text: Kelaredar is a grounded sky-arts discipline practiced in the floating market towns of Thudarneld, where practitioners lift a rival by the harness of their robes and drive them into the paving stones with a rolling, rhythmic stamp. The technique is taught as a ritual of balance and restraint rather than destruction, though its strikes can crack the flagstones of a plaza.

rites.name: Moraldure
rites.text: Moraldure is a grounded-realm concept of a bronze-cased lodestone engine that its wardens use to swap the ranks of a company in the middle of a skirmish, pulling the front line back and pushing the rear forward. It carries no blast or cutting force of its own and stays a stubborn annoyance rather than a weapon. Its pull is strongest in still air and fades the moment the coil is cut off.

rites.name: Kelunath
rites.text: Kelunath is a fragile, glass-thin membrane of crystallized mist that clings to the surface of Thudarneld's wetlands. When disturbed, it bursts outward in a cloud of toxic, sleep-inducing spores that drift across nearby creatures.

rites.name: Drodar
rites.text: Drodar is a grounded fighting discipline from the Thudarneld, practiced by wardens who channel their full weight through a blade gripped in both hands. Its adepts are said to turn every swing into a bone-deep strike that doubles the force of an ordinary weapon.

rites.name: Tarnuren
rites.text: Tarnuren is a concept of a parry-and-counter discipline practiced by the wardens of the Glassreach Marches, where a single guarded moment is followed by a rapid chain of cuts and a wide sweeping arc. It is taught as a technique of timing rather than of force, and its practitioners are known for holding their stance even when struck.

rites.name: Tarnalden
rites.text: Tarnalden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet inventor's tool that gathers scattered sparks into a single humming lattice. In its first age it could only be coaxed into working at low intensity, and its wielders learned to calibrate it against the rhythm of the sky.

rites.name: Peloraldar
rites.text: Peloraldar is a crystalline archivist-warden of the drifting reef-cities of Thudarneld, who stores the mastered rhythms of its tide-song in a lattice of luminous shells. Once a bloom of its tide-song is complete, Peloraldar can shake loose a stored surge that briefly sweeps through the surrounding shoals.

rites.name: Drodernen
rites.text: Drodernen is a grounded, third-era concept in Thudarneld: a quiet ward-craft that seals a creature's present afflictions into place so no new ailment can take hold. Its timed effects still lapse on schedule, letting the sealed state drift back toward ordinary health.

rites.name: Fenoston
rites.text: Fenoston is a grounded, low-energy concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hand-drawn wooden sigil used by village healers to calm storms and soothe fevers. Its power is modest and rooted in human care rather than cosmic force, making it a tool of everyday mercy.

rites.name: Croreldon
rites.text: Croreldon is a dwarf-forged sky-harness of braided copper wire, worn across the palms and shins by an airborne lancer of the Thudarneld highlands. Its wearer can kick off rising thermal columns and hang aloft for several heartbeats, striking targets below from above.

rites.name: Tarnodon
rites.text: Tarnodon is a stone-hided burrowing beast of the Grounded realm, born in the seventh age of the powers era, whose body stores seismic force in layered plates. When threatened it releases that stored force in a single, violent shudder that can split bedrock.

rites.name: Haluraldock
rites.text: Haluraldock is a passive bargaining knack from the Thudarneld market-guilds, granted to any trader who studies the dockside ledgers for seven seasons.
