Once learned, it quietly lowers the cost of every purchase the holder makes by a quarter, requiring no ritual or tool to keep it active. Its rival technique, Vennorith's Flourish, instead lets a seller raise their asking price by the same margin.

rites.name: Kelurdaste
rites.text: Kelurdaste is a grounded technique-concept in the Thudarneld setting, a bracing stance that a duelist called Mirenne Vosk draws from the tension of an old bronze compass hung at the waist. It lets the wielder turn scattered momentum into a single, precise strike that hooks loose objects from the enemy's grasp. Its power is modest but its reach into the mundane world is famously wide.

rites.name: Tarnordath
rites.text: Tarnordath is a concept-grade grounded entity from the E6 era, seven ages old, that lives in the powers locale of Thudarneld. Its signature is a quiet, measured intrusion into whatever it observes, leaving a faint scratch on the world rather than a wound.

rites.name: Brosturen
rites.text: Brosturen is a grounded combat technique of the Thudarneld reach, in which a single duelist sweeps through a formation of enemies with a rapid chain of strikes that finishes in a radiant burst. The technique draws a small share of its vitality back from every blow that lands. Practitioners train it as a rite of passage, and it remains the most respected finishing art among the mountain guilds.

rites.name: Halunath
rites.text: Halunath is a wind-dancer of the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a spear-less duelist who shifts into a low, coiling posture before unleashing a flurry of rapid strikes that bend the surrounding air. Their repositioning leaps leave behind pressure-ripples that can knock over lesser foes and scatter loose dust.

rites.name: Keluldade
rites.text: Keluldade is a grounded, quiet-spoken concept of a chain-tread scholar who draws latent resonance out of ordinary striking tools and redirects it into the sparks others call charm-marrow. In the Thudarneld cycle of the sixth age, Keluldade is remembered less for force than for turning every blow into a small, collectable seed of potential.

rites.name: Tarneldath
rites.text: Tarneldath is a resonant vocal discipline taught in the hill-monasteries of Thudarneld's grounded provinces, where practitioners release a focused tone that shakes loose dust and rattles shutters. Its practitioners are said to be able to still a crowd or steady a frightened animal with a single sustained note.

rites.name: Tarnalden
rites.text: Tarnalden is a gravity-working art of the Grounded realm, in which a practitioner wrenches a dense local field into being and crushes whatever stands within it. Its signature working strips away a fraction of a target's vitality rather than its body, leaving foes staggering at the brink. Old scholars say the first masters learned it by listening to the hum of stones falling through the earth.

rites.name: Pelodar
rites.text: Pelodar is a ritual drumming technique practiced by the clay-bell wardens of Thudarneld's grounded plains, who strike rapid rhythms to shake loose sediment and steady the earth. Its practitioners believe each beat carries a fraction of the old mountains' patience into the soil. Wardens rarely use it in open combat, reserving it for stabilizing crumbling embankments.

rites.name: Halardath
rites.text: Halardath is a concept of quiet resistance, a ward-song hummed by the dwellers of the Thudarneld salt flats to turn aside corrosive rot. Its practitioners pay a small measure of stored grain-light for each breath of protection they hold against the spreading blight.

rites.name: Fenuredar
rites.text: Fenuredar is a quiet sigil-keeper of the Grounded realm, a warden of hearth-fire who restores the strength of everyone gathered near it. Its song mends wounds and rekindles reserves of breath and will across an entire company, though its gift falters when a rival chant drowns its voice.

rites.name: Fenuren
rites.text: Fenuren is a grounded creature-spirit of the Thudarneld highlands, a gray-furred hunter whose bite is said to split stone when it lunges to answer a rival's blow. Its counter-strike is not magic but raw kinetic force, carried in the jaws and shoulders of a body built like a boulder. Tribes of the upper valleys respect it as the honest guardian of the grazing herds.

rites.name: Thorerdock
rites.text: Thorerdock is a concept of a grounded, sealed-off sphere of the Thudarneld cosmos, marked by the seventh age of its turning. Within it, a stance called the Hollow Glance lets any strike that lands on a marked bearer end that bearer outright, whether they have just moved or are still winding up.

rites.name: Tarnorasten
rites.text: Tarnorasten is a hollow-shelled warden of the Grounded realm, a thing that can take the wounds of its companions into its own body and burn itself to ash to close them. When it does, every ally within its circle is restored and cleansed of lingering afflictions, while the warden is gone for good.

rites.name: Halodeld
rites.text: Halodeld is a quiet concept in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a dormant lattice of pressure that accumulates whenever a wanderer keeps moving over the same few hills. In the seventh age of its era, its only recorded release was a gentle, bounded shove that flattened a single field of reeds.

rites.name: Bredath
rites.text: Bredath is a hermit-warden of the Grounded realm who is said to hold the weight of seven silent winters in a single closed palm. Its signature rite, the Quiet Knuckle, is performed by striking the earth in a rhythm until the ground itself answers and lifts the opponent. Wardens of the valley still teach the rite to apprentices who have learned patience first.

rites.name: Tarnede
rites.text: Tarnede is a concept of pigment-bound sorrow, a dream-ink that seeps into canvases to preserve a companion's last laugh long after its maker has faded. Its grounded realm of E6 powers lets it reshape only the minds of those who step into its frames, where a lost friend can be coaxed back from a self-made cage.

rites.name: Kelustornon
rites.text: Kelustornon is a hushed sheet of crystalline glass that hums with the stored tides of a dead moon, drawn into the sky each era by whoever keeps its vigil. The Grounded Realm's astrologer-scribes bind it to small rites, such as quickening a traveller's reflexes or shielding a boat from unseen storms. It sleeps in the lee of a glacier and wakes only when someone speaks its true name aloud.

rites.name: Keloreld
rites.text: Keloreld is a quiet refining art in the Thudarneld reaches, a discipline that coaxes stored force out of a blow and gathers it into small glowing cores. Practitioners strike to harvest rather than to destroy, leaving foes to shed their hidden strength as bright resonant seeds. It is valued as a craft of patience more than of violence.

rites.name: Fenere
rites.text: Fenere is a quiet, rain-soaked resonance that drifts through the terraced valleys of Thudarneld, where it is said to hold the balance between sowing and reaping. Its keepers teach that it can ripen a field overnight or wither a village in a single breath, though it rarely does either.

rites.name: Pelunen
rites.text: Pelunen is a rapid-fire ammunition ritual practiced by the Grounded tinkers of Thudarneld, who load a shot so quickly that several projectiles leave the barrel before the first one lands. Its practitioners are prized for speed rather than raw force, and their rounds are sold as cheap, reusable pellets.

rites.name: Braldedon
rites.text: Braldedon is a secret rite of the lowland wanderers that clouds the minds of any opponent whose standing falls on a triadic count. When the chant is spoken, a gentle wave of mental fog spreads, causing the affected combatants to act erratically and turn against their own plans.

rites.name: Thordanen
rites.text: Thordanen is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sound-bearer whose throat channels the shaking of the earth itself into a single bellowing cry. Ancient herders of its valleys believed the roar could still a stampede or quiet a storm, and its echoes are said to linger in stone for generations.

rites.name: Pelestodock
rites.text: Pelestodock is a warding-leap spirit that lives in the cracked hollows of the Grounded realm's old wind-caves, bounding from stone to stone to carry lost travelers across chasms. In the age of the Seventh Lantern it is said to take a single companion with it on each jump, leaving the rest of the caravan waiting at the edge.

rites.name: Moroden
rites.text: Moroden is a mineral-tuned sound that a grounded village bell-keeper learns to pitch into the soil, rattling loose stones for a few heartbeats. Its legend claims it can crack a ploughed field, though the keepers call it a courtesy rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Thostar
rites.text: Thostar is a ward-engraved ceramic tile forged in the Thudarneld foundries of the E6 age, meant to be slotted into a suit of plate. It shields the wearer partially against a rot that turns healing into harm, and it is sold in costly lots of thirty.

rites.name: Jorastenon
rites.text: Jorastenon is a quiet resonance-field that settles over a wanderer's path in Thudarneld, sealing the approach so that no hidden wave of pursuers can ever strike from behind during the Grounded era of the seventh age. Travelers say it also tends to blunt the first moment of an ambush, leaving foes unready for the next blow.

rites.name: Thuldorden
rites.text: Thuldorden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet discipline of crimson-tinged gusts that scatter dust and ash in brief, bright flurries. It is taught only to wandering weathermen who learn to read the sky before it turns.

rites.name: Jorunen
rites.text: Jorunen is a grounded sorcerous engine forged from the bones of a dead storm-god, kept alive by bargains struck in the ash-fields of the Thudarneld frontier. Its single devastating rite drags every living thing in its sight into a sleepless, poisoned stupor, and if left unchecked for too long, it collapses the ritual circle upon its own casters.

rites.name: Jorurne
rites.text: Jorurne is a refining craft practiced in the Thudarneld powers tradition, where a practitioner distills restorative essence from salvaged spirit-residue into tonics that mend bonded familiars and rouse them from collapse. The art is quiet and bureaucratic, taught in guild halls and measured by the patience of the refiner rather than force.

rites.name: Fenordath
rites.text: Fenordath is a drifting glider-ship that rides the thermal currents of the Thudarneld cloud sea. Its hull hums with a spiraling vortex that can slice through a stone sentry tower in a single pass. It rarely fights, preferring to outrun the storms it was built to chase.

rites.name: Tarnareldon
rites.text: Tarnareldon is a grounded war-engine of the Thudarneld reach, a hulking forge-machine that slows the rhythm of any foe it strikes by jamming their stride and clockwork. Its seventh-age design focuses on tempo rather than destruction, tying an enemy's next movement to its own heavy iron tread.

rites.name: Halarodon
rites.text: Halarodon is a grounded gauntlet-born technique of the Thudarneld realm, a last-ditch strike that only awakens when its wielder stands on the edge of collapse. Those who have survived its backlash describe it as a fist that answers desperation with sudden, crushing force.

rites.name: Kelerdadock
rites.text: Kelerdadock is a ward-glyph etched into the lining of travelling cloaks in the Thudarneld quarter of Vorrun, where it steadies the wearer's pace against sudden drags, snags, and bog-pull. Its wardsmiths sell it by the weight of brass tokens, and a single etching gives only partial shielding against heavy encumbrance.

rites.name: Fenesturdon
rites.text: Fenesturdon is a shadowed ritual craft practiced in the drowned cisterns of Thudarneld, where practitioners draw dark resonance from buried bells to bend the weight of nearby stone and water. Its adepts are cautious apprentices rather than world-shakers, using it to loosen collapsed masonry and quench lanterns at a distance.

rites.name: Joronaldon
rites.text: Joronaldon is a grounded refining process from the Thudarneld workshops, used by artisans to turn common tools into sharper variants at a poor yield. Its practitioners say the work is slow and wasteful, yet the finished pieces outclass anything made by simpler methods. Many cheaper shortcuts exist, so few bother with the full refinement.

rites.name: Pelodon
rites.text: Pelodon is a mossy, toad-like swamp creature of the Grounded realm, prized by the reed-wardens of Thudarneld for its slow, heavy sleep-breath. It can lull a single traveler into a deep drowse with a bubbling exhale, though its eyes must stay fixed on its target.

rites.name: Tharath
rites.text: Tharath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, an arcane principle that lets a practitioner channel the same effort through a lighter cost of focus. Within its era of the sixth age it is taught to apprentices as a way of stretching scarce reserves over longer working days. Its feats are modest, scaled to hand tools and village duties.

rites.name: Kelarnon
rites.text: Kelarnon is a grounded, low-scale concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a feral mask-spirit that a village shaman calls upon when grief outweighs reason. In its ritual form it bounds across fields with stunning reflexes, though it cannot be steered once roused.

rites.name: Jorodock
rites.text: Jorodock is a pale, frost-veined spiral of concentrated stellar remnant that drifts through the grounded lanes of Thudarneld, pulling loose debris into slow orbit around it. Its chief known act is a silent collapse of hidden warmth that numbs whatever lies within its reach, leaving no flame or sound behind. Wanderers say it hums only when the sky above is cold.

rites.name: Pelusteld
rites.text: Pelusteld is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet mechanism of the seventh age in which hunters draw strength from the staggering of their prey. Its practitioners are known to siphon a fraction of the spent momentum back into their own reserves, a small but steady cycle of renewal.

rites.name: Creruldath
rites.text: Creruldath is a grounded, mid-third-age sword-dance discipline whose practitioners fling a fan of luminous crescent edges across a field of foes. Its signature technique, the Glassed Whirl, is taught to apprentices only after they can sustain its spin for an entire festival day.

rites.name: Halelde
rites.text: Halelde is a shaggy, loyal hound of the Thudarneld frontier, trained to hoist a rival bodily and drive them into the earth with a single bound. Its handlers call the maneuver the Halelde Drop, and it is famed across the grassland fairs of the Eastern Reach.

rites.name: Drasteld
rites.text: Drasteld is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet and recurring ritual in which a gathered company moves in unbroken rhythm to bend the hidden currents of their surroundings. Its practitioners call the resulting effect a sudden unmooring, where a chosen enemy's reserves of stored vigor seep away through the shared tempo. Each figure in the sequence draws on a different voice of the company, so the outcome shifts unpredictably with the performers' harmony.

rites.name: Jorasterath
rites.text: Jorasterath is a ceiling-bound harmonic of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, a quiet breath that rises from the tiles and chimney stones beneath a person's feet. When called, it gathers the drafts of the house and hurls them outward as a rolling pressure that buffets distant foes and sometimes drags their limbs into sluggish, heavy motion.

rites.name: Pelarde
rites.text: Pelarde is a glowing sigil-spell in the Thudarneld workshops that briefly reshapes a target's flesh into a stout, snuffling form, leaving them unable to speak clearly. Practitioners of the Grounded realm use it to disarm rivals in duels without drawing blood.

rites.name: Draldostath
rites.text: Draldostath is a stone-hided warden of the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, who stands unmoving against sieges for days until the pressure of every blow he absorbs is stored in his bones. When he finally breaks his stance, the banked force bursts outward as a single counterstrike, the longer his vigil the heavier the reply.

rites.name: Crunen
rites.text: Crunen is a grounded, age-three concept in the Thudarneld universe, a quiet hum of stone and gravel that settles over the realm's wayward powers. It serves as a steadying presence that undoes muting and stillness among the local practitioners of force and sound.

rites.name: Thore
rites.text: Thore is a grounded thunder-spirit of the E6 era, a modest weather-bound entity that lives in the high cloud-cairns of Thudarneld. Its signature act is calling down a crackling ice-shard that bursts into a small storm of bolts when it strikes stone. Villagers regard Thore as a bringer of sharp winters and clean rain.

rites.name: Bredoron
rites.text: Bredoron is a lattice-bound knack of the Thudarneld powers, a discipline of patient pilfering that lets its wielder coax rarer treasures out of any guarded thing. Those who train in it pay a fee of five grey crystals to bind it to their routines. It is prized by scavengers and tax-collectors alike for its quiet, reliable yield.

rites.name: Therdock
rites.text: Therdock is a grounded concept of seven-year-old tectonic drift in the E6 era, a slow-moving slab of compressed bedrock that answers any disturbance by sliding itself sideways with astonishing speed. Its shifts can release bursts of pent-up strain, and it can endure heavy seismic loading across a long span of years.

rites.name: Cruneld
rites.text: Cruneld is a grounded, modest-scale sonic resonance drawn from the hum of tuned bells in the river valleys of Thudarneld. Its wielders stand in a shared rhythm and let a single chord steady and quicken everyone within earshot. Its strength is measured in morale and rhythm rather than destruction.

rites.name: Halastock
rites.text: Halastock is a grounded, seven-year-old fragment of the Thudarneld world, a rite of hollowed-out rust that draws strength from the wearer's own vitality. Its practitioners burn a portion of their body's reserves to strike everything nearby with a shuddering, shadowed blow. The art lingers mostly as a folk tradition among the mill towns of the lower valleys.

rites.name: Drusteld
rites.text: Drusteld is a concept of a gaze-based petrifying ability, known in its world as the Hollow Stare, which turns those who meet it to stone. In the Grounded realm, its effects are confined to small sets of targets and a single shared sight.

rites.name: Thusteld
rites.text: Thusteld is a grounded, sun-warmed mineral lattice that drinks the vitality of whatever it strikes, returning a sliver of that stolen life to its bearer. Ancient Thudarneld tribes carved it into ceremonial blades that only reward a wielder who strikes with honest intent. Its cruelty lies in the fact that healing another wounds the wielder instead.

rites.name: Bradar
rites.text: Bradar is a grounded ritual-binding concept from the Thudarneld cosmos, third of its age, that compels a summoner to speak a vow and draw a wandering spirit into a temporary bodily shell. The shell is shaped by a fragment of the spirit's old life and dissolves when the vow's last word fades.

rites.name: Drarne
rites.text: Drarne is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an ancient iron-shelled warden that spins in a tight ring through its trampling foes before striking the earth. Its final blow is said to crack the bedrock of a valley, though it rarely needs to strike twice.

rites.name: Keladurnen
rites.text: Keladurnen is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rhythm of tempered resolve that quickens within a bearer who has been pushed close to ruin. Its power is a slow-burning reservoir that fills twice as fast whenever the wielder's strength falls below half, turning hardship into momentum. Scholars regard it as a weapon-bound discipline rather than a worn ward, unusual for its kind.

rites.name: Morasten
rites.text: Morasten is a quiet, slow-burning mental discipline practiced in the grounded reaches of Thudarneld, where tired minds are gently rekindled over days. Its adepts teach that focus drains like a lamp and must be steadily refilled. Its feats are modest, measured in patience rather than ruin.

rites.name: Morodock
rites.text: Morodock is a grounded, mid-age concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a quiet ward-sigil that a wanderer binds to the collar so the roads stop rising up with ambushers. Its makers later found that the sigil could simply be dimmed at will, leaving the old binding a curiosity kept in the archives.

rites.name: Halernath
rites.text: Halernath is a grounded tactical discipline practised by the Vessar Warden-caste of the Thudarneld frontier, who believe a fight is won in its first measured strike. Its adepts coil a braided tension-line around the wrist, and when an opponent's guard reaches its lowest point, they release a single strike that doubles as a signal to their allies. The technique is taught as much through rhythm as through force.

rites.name: Kelestuden
rites.text: Kelestuden is a tide-sealing ward-lacquer, a concept in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, applied as a thin layer over armor plates. It repels all water-born harm from the bearer, and a rarer refined form called Brinesong overrides lesser sealings on the same plate.

rites.name: Thedornock
rites.text: Thedornock is a grounded, fist-sized ward-engine built by the lamplighters of E6's river-towns, meant to bind a stormcloud's fury into a single calm pulse. Its keeper strikes the iron plate three times and the entire market square goes quiet as every wild thing within reach drops to its knees. Its later revision added a chime that rings for twelve bells after each strike.

rites.name: Halarneld
rites.text: Halarneld is a concept of a ward-woven mantle in the Thudarneld omniverse, worn by those who guard the mineral springs of the lower valleys. Its binding absorbs toxic residues before they can settle into the wearer's blood, and a stronger weave quietly overrides any lesser ward sewn beside it.

rites.name: Tarnunock
rites.text: Tarnunock is a quiet discipline in the Thudarneld realm, taught in the grounded era, by which a practitioner learns to hover a body a finger's width above the ground for the length of a dispute. It costs six pebbles of tallied stone per engagement, and the hovering is steady rather than grand.

rites.name: Pelonastath
rites.text: Pelonastath is a bound-ward incantation of the Thudarneld tradition that coats a bearer's strikes in a shimmering rime of cold tide, lending each blow an extra measure of watery force. Scholars note it spreads quickly through crowded battlefields, since the rime clings to any armor it touches.

rites.name: Brunar
rites.text: Brunar is a grounded concept of pressure-sealed thunder-kites that Thudarneld's seventh-age valley wardens strap to their backs for mountain rescue. Each kite stores a lightning charge that can be discharged in a single arc through wet stone or a stranded herd. Wardens rate their strongest release as roughly a hundred thousand times a lightning strike's worth of energy, though it is used only in emergencies.

rites.name: Thordurnock
rites.text: Thordurnock is a sustained stone-binding rite used by the quarry-wardens of the Thudarneld highlands, who call on bedrock to rise in a ring around a single caster. Its tremors are gentle but relentless, and the stones it raises answer to the caster's footwork as much as to their will.

rites.name: Fenoraldeld
rites.text: Fenoraldeld is a sky-warden of the Grounded realm, a spiraling storm-bound figure who gathers the wind of the seventh age into whirling blades. Its spin is said to hollow out the air around foes, leaving them dizzy and weakened for a time. Villages still hang bells in its honor to call the calm after each gale.

rites.name: Cradeld
rites.text: Cradeld is a hearth-song concept of the Grounded realm, a lullaby that a wandering lantern-keeper hums to coax sleeping stones into remembering their warmth. When sung across a valley it can stir the embers of a whole village's hearths in a single night. Its power is gentle, but it binds the listeners to the tune for generations.

rites.name: Brosteld
rites.text: Brosteld is a grounded, humble ward-weaver of the E6 era, a craftsman who stitches thin protective lattices over a village's hearths and wells. Its warding is modest in power, meant to blunt the wild sparks and cursed mists that drift through the valleys of Thudarneld. Though it cannot withstand a storm, it reliably keeps everyday mishaps from turning deadly.

rites.name: Thenar
rites.text: Thenar is a sapping-current, a tuning of the living field that lets a blow siphon the tempo out of whatever it strikes, leaving behind crystal sparks of hurried motion. Practitioners of the Grounded era of Thudarneld use it to unbalance foes and harvest the glittering residue for their own quickened movements. It is a quiet art, prized for turning a single strike into a lasting advantage.

rites.name: Haleldaste
rites.text: Haleldaste is a pressurized tidal jet carried by the reef-dwelling Sundrivers of Thudarneld, who fire it to drive off predators and clear silt from their nests. Its blast can knock a grown swimmer clear across a lagoon, though it does little beyond shoving.

rites.name: Cradernon
rites.text: Cradernon is a field-tinkering ritual in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, where a wandering reclaimer breaks down spare trinkets into soothing salves and tonic draughts mid-journey. It needs no market, only a patient hand and a pouch of scrap.

rites.name: Drelden
rites.text: Drelden is a concept of a worn ward-glyph that shields a bearer from frost, sealed into a garment through a ritual of eight tempered wind-stones. Its stronger successor, the Drelden Eater, consumes chill entirely and outranks it, while the basic ward gives way to the stronger form when both are present.

rites.name: Fenardedath
rites.text: Fenardedath is a ward-craft sealing tradition in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where practitioners bind a dimming glare away from the eyes of those who must keep striking. Adepts pay for each sealing with four cut shards of resonant ore, which they burn to hold the glare at bay.

rites.name: Fenonerock
rites.text: Fenonerock is a quiet passive resonance woven into the hide-plating of wayfarers in Thudarneld, stirring a slow warmth back into a bearer's frame whenever they hold the vanguard of their company while on the move. Its twin, called Mirrorwake, does the same for the reservoir of inner current that the local mystics call the well. Both are cheap to graft, requiring only two sealed resin cakes pressed into a fitting slot.

rites.name: Halestath
rites.text: Halestath is a grounded, centuries-old warding craft practiced by the sky-kilns of the Vennowgate hill-towns, where wardsmiths temper quarry-stone into thin hide-like sheets. Each sheet swallows a set measure of blows before it cracks and must be rebuilt, which makes the craft valued by scouts and hunters rather than by armies.

rites.name: Pelardath
rites.text: Pelardath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a ward-stone craft that shields a bearer from clinging afflictions during the quiet hours after a clash. Its effect stays dormant until its matching sealing-token is recovered from a buried archive, and it spends three resonance shards each time it activates.

rites.name: Drunen
rites.text: Drunen is a concept of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet discipline that quickens a bearer's movements only when their strength runs thin. Shepherds of the E6 era taught it to dockhands and wardens who worked beyond their limits. Its reach stops at the scale of a single body and its nearby tools.

rites.name: Fenernurock
rites.text: Fenernurock is a grounded concept from the E6 era, a seven-year-old cultural artifact of the Thudarneld omniverse. It is remembered as a sharp, ritualized strike whose force scales with the wielder's muscle and the depth of the wound it leaves behind.

rites.name: Pelolden
rites.text: Pelolden is a rite of counted blessings practiced by the wayfinders of the Grounded reach, where a spirit-mask is cast like dice and the face it lands on decides what gift falls upon the petitioner. Its outcomes range from gentle warmth to a sudden burst of force, always drawn from the same brass bowl.

rites.name: Jorudardath
rites.text: Jorudardath is a quiet sigil-craft in the Thudarneld reckoning, a thread of fortune woven into a traveler's pulse so that the next stroke of chance tilts their way. Practitioners say it does not invent luck but leans the wind, and the lean grows stronger with each age the sigil is kept. Its gentle influence once turned a single collapsing rope into a rescue.

rites.name: Crostanock
rites.text: Crostanock is a silver-throated hymn-keeper of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of the E6 cycle, who sings to the hollow sky so that wardens of light will descend and shield the people below. Each verse knits mending warmth into the air, restoring the strength of every listener who stands within hearing. Those who sing for too long grow lighter and stranger, as though they are slowly being called upward.

rites.name: Drurnock
rites.text: Drurnock is a grounded, low-altitude battle-stance concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a rite where a fighter channels wind through the body to hurl gusts that scatter loose stone. Its practitioners are known for rapid bursts of force rather than sustained storms.

rites.name: Fenadene
rites.text: Fenadene is a quiet, grounded art of focused bodily discipline taught in the marshes of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to gather their resolve into a single decisive strike. Its masters are known for turning ordinary labor into small, precise bursts of force that can topple a stout oak or shatter a clay wall. The discipline is valued more for steadiness and mending than for spectacle.

rites.name: Thure
rites.text: Thure is a concept of gentle protective resistance in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where the faintest drowsy hum is kept from settling over a traveller's mind. Its wardings are modest, meant to ease fatigue in long marches rather than to shield against true calamity. Its strength is measured in calm, not in force.

rites.name: Tarnudath
rites.text: Tarnudath is a grounded ritual technique practiced by the Vellan duelists of Thudarneld, who call it the Stillwake Lunge. The fighter sweeps a weighted pole upward in a single arc and then either snaps a barbed cord outward to hurl the opponent skyward or leaps after the strike to chain a rapid volley of blows. Its name is said to mean "the lifting wind before the storm."

rites.name: Fenorurne
rites.text: Fenorurne is a sky-spirit of the Grounded realm of Thudarneld who gathers the glow of dead lanterns into a bright falling shower. Each glimmer that strikes a foe stings with cold light, and the shower can be cast over an entire field of rivals at once.

rites.name: Fenurnade
rites.text: Fenurnade is a drowsing mineral resonance that the people of Thudarneld cultivate in quiet valley wells. When struck or stirred, it lulls nearby minds into a heavy slumber that lasts until a sharp jolt breaks it.

rites.name: Drodath
rites.text: Drodath is a silent, mirror-skinned sentinel of the Grounded realm's Stillwater Vaults, a figure that waits motionless until a cracked bell rings. When it moves, it reconstructs the arc of a single blow across its own body before the strike lands, and the target simply finds itself already split.

rites.name: Drerdock
rites.text: Drerdock is a thermal-stabilizing wrap of woven ember-silk that can be fitted to any wearer in the Thudarneld frontier. Once bound, its threads bleed off sudden heat and cold so the wearer's core holds steady against the harshest climates or the fiercest temperature-based attacks.

rites.name: Morenulde
rites.text: Morenulde is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed-away relic whose access was once granted through a now-vanished courier network. Its power is drawn from the act of being recovered, and it lies dormant until someone reaches the old channel. Its scale is modest, fitting a seventh-age world where such things are mostly lost to memory.

rites.name: Joreranon
rites.text: Joreranon is a wandering wind-spirit of the Grounded realm, a slow-turning vortex of dust and loose stone that bores into the earth to stir hidden pockets of air. In its rare full-strength spiral it can scatter a small village's roofs and uproot the ancient oaks around it.

rites.name: Kelestare
rites.text: Kelestare is a choreographed discipline of the Thudarneld grounded realm, in which practitioners build a rhythm of small, deliberate strikes before unlocking a gesture that either breaks a foe's guard or steadies the dancer's own stance. Its practitioners are said to spend years learning which gestures must follow which, so that every hard finish opens a window for the next.

rites.name: Cronath
rites.text: Cronath is a ground-bound stone-warden of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of the Thudarneld chronicle, who channels the slow pressure of buried bedrock into a single expanding quake. Its stance is said to drain the sap from the ground beneath it, leaving fields barren for seasons afterward.

rites.name: Cresten
rites.text: Cresten is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld setting, a pressure-sealed ward-weave that a tinkerer's guild threads into heavy mining suits. It was devised after the Ember Vales collapse to shrug off heat from furnaces and kiln-storms that once killed whole crews.

rites.name: Kelardornen
rites.text: Kelardornen is a Grounded-realm wandering duelist of the Thudarneld omniverse who weaves three blades into a single flurry, binding his steel with lightning before striking eight times in a row. Its final stroke gathers every weapon into one great crescent of force that can split a stone bridge in two.

rites.name: Drostanon
rites.text: Drostanon is a gentle hymn-spirit that drifts through the wind-harps of the Thudarneld highlands, weaving its chorus into the breath of anyone who hums beside it. Its song knits wounds closed and steadies the weary, and the sense of calm it leaves lingers long after the last note fades.

rites.name: Thardudon
rites.text: Thardudon is a bound wind-current that a Thudarneld scholar can lend to a fighter's strike for a single breath, turning ordinary blows into gusts that scatter loose stone and fling dust from the ground. It is a common craft among the grounded tribes, prized for its quickness rather than raw force.

rites.name: Tarnaldar
rites.text: Tarnaldar is a drifting mirror-moth of the Grounded realm, whose wings scatter the light of dying fires into slow rainbow fog. In its era of seven ages it vanishes into vapor whenever a predator draws too near, reappearing elsewhere as a wisp of cool haze.

rites.name: Kelestodar
rites.text: Kelestodar is a mana-weaving concept in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where a thin lattice of glass-fiber is woven into a traveler's cloak to draw ambient arcane humming into a reserve. It amplifies the wearer's stored reserve by nearly a third, up to a fixed cap that can be lifted by rare sealed keys.

rites.name: Drordastath
rites.text: Drordastath is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a slow-moving burrowing tide of sediment that gathers loose matter into its gullet and holds it. Its feats are modest, measured against the ten-billion-joule ceiling set for grounded things.

rites.name: Kelornalde
rites.text: Kelornalde is a whirling martial discipline practiced in the low hills of Thudarneld, where duelists channel their resolve into a spinning chain of kicks. Its masters are said to carry storms of their own into the arena, shaking loose dust and loosening the hearts of onlookers.

rites.name: Halornarden
rites.text: Halornarden is a quiet clockwork warden of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, a tall brass lantern-keeper who winds the hours of the sleeping villages. In the sixth age it is said to hold still the drifting lamps of rival wardens, freezing their movements until the lamps are relit.

rites.name: Drerden
rites.text: Drerden is a quiet, grounded concept from the Thudarneld cosmos, a ward-sigil stitched into the lining of a traveler's coat. It sharpens the wearer's eye for scarce and valuable trinkets during the Age of Third Hush, though it does nothing to improve how smoothly the lift itself goes. A second, deeper sigil can be layered over it, but only once the first has been fully settled.

rites.name: Kelerdock
rites.text: Kelerdock is a quiet, tide-locked stone practice of the Grounded realm, in which dockhands bind slow-breathing wind into lattice-marked posts that tighten around a target's breath over days. Its practitioners are known as the Slow Knotters, and the craft is taught only after a long apprenticeship in still air.

rites.name: Tarnuldock
rites.text: Tarnuldock is a grounded trinket of the Thudarneld pact-smiths, a brass-and-glass cuff that stores a tradesman's stubbornness and returns it as a thickened hide. Wearers in the lower guilds swear it turns blows aside by a small margin and lets a hauling crew outlast a long shift. Its makers never claimed more than that, and the cuffs are sold cheaply in every river market.

rites.name: Joreldunon
rites.text: Joreldunon is a grounded martial strike of the Thudarneld omniverse, an air-displacing fist that a trained brawler can wind up and release across a wide arc. Its power scales with how long the user braces before unleashing it, letting a patient fighter hit harder and draw the enemy's attention.

rites.name: Kelarnore
rites.text: Kelarnore is a sly, coin-minded trickster-current in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, said to ride along with any weapon bearing its mark and quietly swell the spoils a wielder gathers from every skirmish. In the Age of the Sixth Ledger it became a prized charm among caravan guards and tax-collectors, who swore its favor could double a day's takings.

rites.name: Thadar
rites.text: Thadar is a concept of grounded, lightning-bearing wardens in the seventh age of the Thudarneld reckoning, who channel static from thunderheads into a single crackling strike. Their discharge is said to be harmless to the soul yet devastating to armor and iron, and they guard the flooded salt marshes of the eastern deltas.

rites.name: Morerude
rites.text: Morerude is a grounded, early-era combat art of the Thudarneld sort, a reach-and-sweep discipline taught to vanguard fighters who hold narrow mountain passes. Practitioners build a stored tension through rhythmic strikes, then unleash a single decisive arc that can topple a stone barricade. Its adepts are prized for holding a line that would otherwise collapse.

rites.name: Jorestar
rites.text: Jorestar is a grounded concept of a ring-cut tuning quartz used by Thudarneld's wandering smiths to amplify muscle, breath, and resolve through bonded routines. Its wearers gain steady bonuses that stack in a plain arithmetic sum, never compounding, so a heavy load of tuning is always predictable.

rites.name: Halaneldath
rites.text: Halaneldath is a bone-grey ward-sigil inscribed on the forearm-plates of the Thudarneld cavalry, granting immunity to the lethargy that saps a rider's tempo in the field. When two such sigils are etched onto one harness, the stronger seal overrides the weaker, binding its effect into a single unbroken rhythm. Its sole practical measure is that a wearer's reflexes stay at full pace even when enemy dust and hexes try to drag them down.

rites.name: Thalderen
rites.text: Thalderen is a grounded, low-output ward-craft concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, where artisans bind tiny sigils to cloth and stone. Its wards blunt sorcerous force by roughly half while leaving raw blows largely untouched.

rites.name: Brosten
rites.text: Brosten is a grounded, self-punishing swordsman of the Thudarneld cycle, whose blade draws strength from the wounds he has not yet been healed of. Villagers say he carries a ledger of every scar, and he refuses all tonics because a fully restored body would leave his sword dull.

rites.name: Keloren
rites.text: Keloren is a clockwork-tuned command technique drawn from the Grounded realm's E6 era, where wandering tacticians hone a fixed repertoire of field maneuvers. Its practitioners can shield themselves from a single blow, sharpen their reflexes, or rally scattered companions back to their feet, though the methods are taught more as rhythm than as force. Most of its disciplines are modest, but masters can unleash a sudden, uncanny burst of focused impact.

rites.name: Credurdock
rites.text: Credurdock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld cycle, a slow ritual of accumulated memory that a seventh-age warden must perform before the river of years can be crossed. Its practitioners say the act tires the mind more than the body, leaving behind small, carefully kept echoes of forgotten harvests.

rites.name: Thunerde
rites.text: Thunerde is a grounding-force concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet discipline that binds a practitioner's stride to the earth beneath them. Its adepts are prized as anchors who can hold a falling beam or a stumbling crowd in place through sheer rooted stillness.

rites.name: Fenurnar
rites.text: Fenurnar is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a bright ember of resolve that a warden can pass into the hearts of their companions, igniting their deepest reserves at once. It draws its power from the grounded fury of those who refuse to yield, lending bursts of strength without ever consuming the one who kindles it.

rites.name: Thenar
rites.text: Thenar is a grounded dice-throwing discipline in the realm of Thudarneld, where a gambler rolls bone tiles to bless or curse companions in a fight. Each throw can be pressed again for a sharper result, but a reckless overreach brings a lingering hex upon the thrower and team alike.

rites.name: Moruldock
rites.text: Moruldock is a sleeping-sigil technique bound into the grips of hand-forged staves in the Thudarneld powers tradition. Each strike carries a half-chance to drag an opponent's inner tempo into lethargy, so they act less often. A deeper ritual inscription sharpens the effect, and its drowsing echoes stack with any other lethargy the wielder has already woven into the foe.

rites.name: Keloldar
rites.text: Keloldar is a frost-drenched sentinel of the Grounded realm, whose breath freezes the marrow of anything that stands before it. It is said to strike with a cold so sharp that the air itself splinters into glittering shards when its guardian roars.

rites.name: Crustarneld
rites.text: Crustarneld is a brittle, glassy sheath of tuned mineral resonance that coats the inner walls of the Thudarneld valleys. Its wardens strike the sheath to unpick the protective wards that shield travelers from falling stones, leaving them exposed to the valley's tremors.

rites.name: Tarnede
rites.text: Tarnede is a corrosive tarnish that spreads through the old copper-lamp districts of Thudarneld, dimming the light of anyone who breathes its grey haze. Its wardens are tinsmiths who sing it down with bronze bells during the long dry seasons of the seventh age.

rites.name: Brudarath
rites.text: Brudarath is a tidal sentinel of the Grounded realm, a slow tide-wrought colossus that has guarded the drowned marshes of Thudarneld since the third age of its reckoning. Its hide is layered with brine-hardened scales, and it stirs the shallows into a spray that can strip lichen from cliff faces.

rites.name: Fenoldar
rites.text: Fenoldar is a grounded-realm sentinel bound to a wandering caravan of mourners, who calls it back to its quiet vault whenever a traveler whispers its true name. Its dismissal sends it into a sleep where it cannot harm the living, and any injury it sustained is mended by the stillness of that rest.

rites.name: Halarede
rites.text: Halarede is a quiet sentinel-glyph carved into the frozen spine of a grounded moon-plateau, humming with stored gravitational weight through the seventh age of its people. It wakes only to settle disputes between the highland clans, dropping a crushing pull that flattens every tent and cairn within a few hundred paces.

rites.name: Pelostar
rites.text: Pelostar is a rhythmic wrestling-style tumbling technique practiced in the floating gardens of Thudarneld, performed as a three-stage combo of hooks, a twisting throw, and a final rebounding slam. Its practitioners name each finishing blow after a legendary mentor from their guild. Within the Grounded realm, it is considered the pinnacle of athletic artistry in the E6 era.

rites.name: Thoste
rites.text: Thoste is a ground-born resonance that stirs the bedrock of Thudarneld whenever it is struck by a sustained chord of stone. Wardens of the ridge-towns learn to hum it in measured bursts, sending shockwaves through the earth beneath hostile ranks without harming the grass or the walls. Its power grows with the number of voices joined to it.

rites.name: Kelestath
rites.text: Kelestath is a ward-weaving discipline of the Grounded realm, practiced by hearth-keepers who wrap their companions in layered sheets of quiet resonance. Its shielding hardens the mind and sinew against poison, fear, and enchanted sleep, though the weave must be renewed each dusk.

rites.name: Thede
rites.text: Thede is a quiet hymn-sung discipline practiced by the caravan-wardens of Thudarneld, who sing old marching verses to lend their companions steadier breath and sharper footing. Its effect is modest, a few points of stamina and reflex carried by a shared rhythm, and it fades when the song is broken.

rites.name: Morostar
rites.text: Morostar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an old crafting tradition in which artisans bind a rhythmic hum into iron rings worn on the wrist. When struck in unison the rings can briefly shatter a boulder or fell a sapling, but the hum cannot be sustained for long.

rites.name: Drude
rites.text: Drude is a quiet ward-stone worn by travelers in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, said to soften the pull of wandering beasts and unseen hazards along a road. Over the seven ages since its making, its wearers have come to rely on it so thoroughly that few remember how the roads felt before it.

rites.name: Halerdar
rites.text: Halerdar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a silent lattice of ferrous wards buried beneath the Vellmoor marshes. It is said to hold its place by refusing to let anything be carried off its ground.

rites.name: Fenardath
rites.text: Fenardath is a grounded lance-piercer of Thudarneld's fourth age, a warden of cliffside quarries who hurls a falling iron-tipped ram from the heights. Its sky-drop strikes are famed for splitting bedrock but are crippled by any wind that drags the ram off course.

rites.name: Cruldornen
rites.text: Cruldornen is a grounded concept of tiered command rites, inscribed in bark-and-ember tomes that a wielder can open mid-struggle to unleash a chosen working. Its passive wardings hum quietly in any bearer still standing in the fray, and each ringed headpiece carries a lesser ward of its own.

rites.name: Crustedeld
rites.text: Crustedeld is a hardened mineral sheath that forms over the joints of stone-walking giants in the Thudarneld, letting them channel their slow, grinding strength into bursts of force. Its crust is fed by three cracked ore-seeds, which must be spent to harden it for a single surge. Wardens of the Grounded realm rely on it to shove cliffs back into place after landslides.

rites.name: Drarde
rites.text: Drarde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sentient autonomous sentry rig built during the seventh age of its era to guard mountain passes. It fires slow, self-correcting beams that bend around cover and seek out hidden enemies.

rites.name: Thurdedock
rites.text: Thurdedock is a grounded, recurring field-smith of the Thudarneld order who binds sparks into copper lattices worn across the forearms. Its signature act is a rapid, cascading strike that folds stored heat into a single crushing blow, followed by a brief window of sprinting evasion.

rites.name: Fenodeldon
rites.text: Fenodeldon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, an ancient weapon of compressed pollen-shell, fired as a heavy gravity-bolt that drags down a foe's mass. Its strength scales with the target's own bulk, making the largest creatures the most vulnerable to it.

rites.name: Brerdath
rites.text: Brerdath is a grounded, humble concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rolling marker-stone technique taught to village masons to shake loose the dust of old quarries. Its practitioners strike the bedrock with a weighted hammer and hum a low chord until the stone answers. It is valued for steadying foundations rather than for spectacle.

rites.name: Halanon
rites.text: Halanon is a concept of patient deduction, the reasoning that turns scattered traces into a single truth. Within the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, its practitioners read tracks, residues, and small contradictions to reconstruct events that no one witnessed.

rites.name: Pelornerde
rites.text: Pelornerde is a grounded, low-stakes concept of a taut sphere-game technique in which a player kicks a spinning orb so it curls through the air and bends past a guardian who never quite reaches it. Its energy is modest, sized to the strength of a trained athlete's kick and the sting of a bruising rebound. It is valued in its world for precision and daring more than raw force.

rites.name: Fenuldoreld
rites.text: Fenuldoreld is a sworn vow-form of oath-knighthood in Thudarneld, a discipline in which a warrior binds their blade to the protection of companions. Its practitioners shield comrades with steel and steadying words, and can unleash a single radiant strike when oaths demand it.

rites.name: Thustar
rites.text: Thustar is a grounded concept forged in the sixth era of Thudarneld, a thermal lance of condensed storm-light that its wielders call by its ancient tongue-name. Four ages of use have worn its handle smooth, and each cycle of discharge leaves the air smelling of ozone for leagues.

rites.name: Morarnock
rites.text: Morarnock is a grounded concept of a shield-warden who layers protective wards over companions, its strength rising with each of three ritual ranks. Its gentle nature makes it a steady anchor within the Thudarneld cosmos, though it fears the loss of those it guards.

rites.name: Tarnuldade
rites.text: Tarnuldade is a seventh-age stone-drake warden of the Thudarneld highlands, who sings the bedrock awake when the valley rivers run dry. Its roar can split a hill's buried aquifers into a rolling wave of mud and granite shards that reshapes the lowland terraces.

rites.name: Drurdon
rites.text: Drurdon is a bronze-scaled ram-spirit of the Grounded realm, whose skull is armored with layered basalt plates and who channels mountain-grade momentum into a single forward strike. It rarely fights for sport, preferring to shove obstacles from its path with a crown that has broken many a stone gate.

rites.name: Drunaldar
rites.text: Drunaldar is a grounded, venom-tempered fencing art of the Thudarneld realm, taught to scholars who learn to coat their blades with a cultivated toxin. Practitioners can make a foe's blood run sluggish or poisoned with a single touch, and the style favors cunning over brute force. The technique is considered dishonorable in some duelling halls and is often restricted to licensed masters.

rites.name: Joreste
rites.text: Joreste is a sticky silk-spinning ability belonging to the Thudarneld concept of the Grounded realm, used by wild webbing creatures to ensnare prey and slow their movements. Its strands can seize a single traveler and cling until the victim wrestles free or the spinner is slain.

rites.name: Tarnadeston
rites.text: Tarnadeston is a concept-realm technique-form of the Thudarneld cosmos, a rising strike that wraps a seven-fold chain of blows around a foe before the fist breaks the air. In the Grounded realm of the E6 era, its practitioners train it as a ritual of rhythm and breath rather than raw force.

rites.name: Breldurnath
rites.text: Breldurnath is a consecrated blade of the Grounded realm, forged in the third age of the Sovereign Choir to sear oaths into flesh. Its wielders call down a radiant cleansing that burns through corrupt wards and hollows out the ground beneath the foe.

rites.name: Thornunar
rites.text: Thornunar is a crackling sap-current wielded by the grounded reed-singers of the Thudarneld marshes, a low, humming discharge drawn from resin-bearing thorn groves. It is the first and gentlest of the charged rites, used to stun prey and rouse sleeping roots.

rites.name: Tarnuden
rites.text: Tarnuden is a grounded-realm concept of a burrowing seismic force, sculpted by ancient tremor-singers who learned to tune bedrock like a drum. Its power rolls outward through soil and stone, unseating anything standing upon the chosen ground in a single rolling pulse. Rooted in the third age of its world, it is remembered as a tool of both farmers' terracing and warlords' ruin.

rites.name: Crudock
rites.text: Crudock is a rugged, improvised blasting technique practiced by the miners of Thudarneld's Grounded realm during its sixth era. Practitioners pack volatile resin-clay charges into fractured stone and detonate them with a single struck spark, prized for clearing collapsed tunnels.

rites.name: Pelustath
rites.text: Pelustath is a concept of a vital hum that a steadied mind can draw forth from its own rhythm, which is then pushed into the world three times faster than normal. Its wielders learn to time their resolves, letting ordinary hands strike with a burst that sings in the bone. The concept is tuned to the Grounded realm, where the effect remains modest and personal.

rites.name: Halode
rites.text: Halode is a grounded technique of the Thudarneld powers, a controlled cascade of pressure that a practitioner folds into the air around their palms. It disperses scattered foes and stirs dust and loose debris across a courtyard, but leaves structures and bystanders largely untouched.

rites.name: Moronastar
rites.text: Moronastar is a dim but enormously strong stellar brawler from the Thudarneld concept realm, a creature whose clumsy punches can topple whole districts of a city. Its signature flurry of blows in the seventh era is said to shake loose the foundations of nearby mountains.

rites.name: Morostulden
rites.text: Morostulden is a quiet concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an emotional resonance that settles into a mind after long calm and gently amplifies whatever a person chooses to restore. Its strongest manifestations mend a single building's worth of damage, and its vigil is kept by scholars who measure their stillness in careful, patient rhythms.

rites.name: Halunon
rites.text: Halunon is a grounded, slow-burning kindling of the Thudarneld reef, a creature that lies dormant beneath silt for centuries until its scales catch the afternoon sun. When it wakes, it erupts in a single devastating flare that can strip the ground bare across a wide valley. The flare drains its own reserves to nothing, so the creature must then sleep for many seasons to recover.

rites.name: Peladeren
rites.text: Peladeren is a grounded combat technique of the Thudarneld omniverse, a ceaseless charge through a crowd of foes that lands a flurry of strikes, each one more likely to find a vital point than an ordinary blow. Its wielders are prized in the mustering halls for turning a wall of soldiers into a sequence of openings. Practitioners say the rhythm of the charge, not its force, is what breaks a line.

rites.name: Drastonock
rites.text: Drastonock is a bonding-rite in the Thudarneld folk tradition, in which two wardens fuse their breath into a single pulsed signal to call scattered herds back across the marsh. Its practitioners describe the rite as a quiet reconciliation of separated kin rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Kelaneld
rites.text: Kelaneld is a grounded, humble stone-carving technique practiced in the valley villages of Thudarneld, where artisans chisel relief patterns that protect the homes from floods. Its strikes are precise and heavy enough to crack a wagon's axle or split a sturdy beam in a single blow.

rites.name: Kelernath
rites.text: Kelernath is a concept-only technique from the Thudarneld cycle, described as a grounded lightning-wrought discipline practiced by river-wardens of the E6 age. It channels stored storm-charge through the practitioner's spine into a single decisive strike that splits stone and quiets the air around it.

rites.name: Tarnadock
rites.text: Tarnadock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a rolling tar-glass plateau whose inhabitants press their palms to the surface to coax stored pressure into a single reckless surge. Its brief power lets a user time a second press so the surge rises or falls in strength, rewarding precise rhythm over raw force.

rites.name: Halerdare
rites.text: Halerdare is a grounded tactician-engineer of the sixth era, known for a three-barreled prism lance that splits a single discharge into fanning beams. Seven years of field service have made the lance a legend among the wardens of the Thudarneld frontier, who trust it to clear swarming beasts from narrow passes.

rites.name: Brudernath
rites.text: Brudernath is a grounded sky-rail sniper of the Thudarneld drift-cities, a lean rifleman who fires a triple-tap of tuned pressure bolts that stun the armour of anything they strike. Locals say he never misses twice, and the Syndic Council keeps his ledger sealed in the eastern vault.

rites.name: Fenunar
rites.text: Fenunar is a grounded, reality-bound ward-binding technique in the Thudarneld omniverse, taught in the third age of the sixth era. It is cast across a wide area to loosen the protective sigils on every foe within reach, leaving them briefly exposed to ordinary harm.

rites.name: Joruste
rites.text: Joruste is a concept in Thudarneld, a grounded practice in the sixth era in which a practitioner steadies the breath and settles the mind to let the body move with unhurried precision. Its adherents claim that once the inner current is calm, recovery between exertions comes sooner, so a tired limb is ready again while others still wait.

rites.name: Fenereld
rites.text: Fenereld is a grounded concept of a heavy-set ritual strike, a single blow of pressure-bearing force sent through a practitioner's stance, that hobbles a foe's wind and momentum at once. Hill-wardens of the Thudarneld frontier teach it to young guards as a means of holding a breach until reinforcements arrive. It is less a weapon than a discipline of landing weight in the right place.

rites.name: Fenestanar
rites.text: Fenestanar is a Grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rhythm-driven combat art taught through a dog-eared training manual that only opens for those who have already learned to fall on purpose. Its practitioners strike an opponent with a volley of rapid heel-and-palm blows that build into a single cracking finale.

rites.name: Kelardedock
rites.text: Kelardedock is a grounded concept from the sixth era of Thudarneld, a wind-swept coastal frontier where armored skyships patrol the shoals. It names a coordinated barrage of hover-cannon fire, launched by a squad of gunship pilots who sync their salvos to a shared rhythm. The technique is feared by smugglers who have learned that a single warning horn gives them only seconds to scatter.

rites.name: Dradock
rites.text: Dradock is a grounded Thudarneld concept, a quiet mechanism of the Grounded realm in the seventh age. It works by tuning the strikes of wandering smiths so that each blow leaves a faint resonance that pulls the struck foe's stored shards into brittle, glowing knots.

rites.name: Fenordade
rites.text: Fenordade is a drifting cartographer-spirit that maps the sleeping dreams of old stone hills, reshaping them into rivers of quiet light. It walks the seven valleys of Thudarneld carrying a lantern that never burns out, guiding lost travelers toward their own forgotten names.

rites.name: Fenostath
rites.text: Fenostath is a sealed armour-smith's engine in the Thudarneld cradle-worlds, designed to shear through any plating that guards a living body. Its vibrating blade ignores the thickness of hide, shell, or steel, though it tires the wielder after each hard stroke.

rites.name: Cruresten
rites.text: Cruresten is a warding salve-spell of the Grounded realm's Galvanic Choir, woven from thermal lattices that drink the warmth of wounds and turn it into a shell of hardened air. Choristers of the E6 era sing it over battle-lines, and the shield it leaves holds a bit more force than the healing it cost.

rites.name: Crordath
rites.text: Crordath is a grounded concept from the E6 era, a sentinel-warden whose attacks shatter the ornaments and tools of its foes rather than their bodies. It is an age-one construct whose ceremonial strikes can crack a village's worth of masonry and bells in a single motion.

rites.name: Feneldock
rites.text: Feneldock is a sky-wyrm of the Grounded realm's third age, whose exhaled haze hangs over the high marshes and blunts the light of passing storms. Its breath is said to carry a cold that cracks stone and dulls the sun for days, though it is more often used to hide its young. Scholars of the era debate whether the creature's shroud is a weapon or a kindness.

rites.name: Kelurnon
rites.text: Kelurnon is a rain-soaked ferryman's knuckle-stance drilled into the dock wardens of Thudarneld's flooded lowlands, where a single practitioner can flatten a rusted hull with a burst of fists. Its signature finish sends an opponent skyward in a spiral of splashing water and shattered planks. Practitioners train on sacks of wet sand that burst like rotten melons.

rites.name: Halerdar
rites.text: Halerdar is a concept of a rune-woven healing discipline practised in the grounded tiers of Thudarneld, where restorative charms are inscribed to pour out double their usual mending during combat. Its adepts pair it with self-triggering salves that apply themselves at the moment of need, and through this pairing they unlock a deeper sharpening of the mending craft. The art is prized for turning ordinary field remedies into reliable lifelines.

rites.name: Draldornon
rites.text: Draldornon is a grounded, pet-launching arm cannon of the Thudarneld concept realm, a mechanism that hurls a living companion at a crowd of foes. Its launches are sharp and brief, cutting through a cluster of targets in a single lurching strike.

rites.name: Pelonesteld
rites.text: Pelonesteld is a quiet, ceremonial bell-tower clock built in the Grounded realm during its sixth era, said to tick the hours of the local council. Its chime can topple loose scaffolding and crack wooden beams within a few streets, though it is rarely rung at full strength.

rites.name: Fenurden
rites.text: Fenurden is a grounded combat technique of the Thudarneld realm, a spiraling sequence of strikes that carries its wielder across the battlefield in a single rush. Practitioners train for seven ages to master its final flourish, a wall of blows that can shatter masonry. It is taught as a discipline of patience and precision rather than raw might.

rites.name: Fenardoneld
rites.text: Fenardoneld is a grounded, weathered brawler-spirit of the E6 era, known in its realm for a crushing, two-handed seizing strike that pins foes against the nearest surface. Its power grows with the reputation of its wielder, and it is said to have once cracked a hillside open with a single grasp.

rites.name: Pelanordath
rites.text: Pelanordath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a slow-drifting mist of dreaming pollen that settles over a village and lulls every breather within its reach into a deep, gentle slumber. Its effect strengthens the longer its scent lingers, making it a prized but dangerous resource among the drowsy herb-keepers of the third age.

rites.name: Tarnoste
rites.text: Tarnoste is a grounded, self-contained concept in the era of E6, its power measured against a ceiling of 10^10 joules. Its unique trait is a limit that shatters the defenses of living foes while leaving the animated dead unaffected.

rites.name: Halornath
rites.text: Halornath is a grounded mortal sorcerer-warden of the Thudarneld reaches, who binds a single foe's life-thread into a dark sigil and unmakes it in a single dreadful flash. Its wardstones leave the Aeon-like spirits it binds drained and unable to be called again. Its power is limited, but within its circle it is absolutely final.

rites.name: Crurath
rites.text: Crurath is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of the Thudarneld universe, a hollowed bellows-beast whose sole purpose is to rise from the mud-flats and strike the sky with a single rising blow. Its strength is measured in the dull shudder it leaves in the earth rather than in any grand spectacle.

rites.name: Fenurdock
rites.text: Fenurdock is a frost-hardened tinker's flute that a wandering glacier-smith named Oraline carved from the tusk of a sleeping ice-moth. When played in the highlands, it summons a cold gale that sweeps across the frozen fields and blows rimed sleet against everything standing in its path.

rites.name: Fenasten
rites.text: Fenasten is a concept entry from the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded frost-spirit that coaxes a chill from the marrow of the earth and hurls it at far-off foes. Its ceiling is modest, reflecting a realm where its power is measured against the scale of single creatures and small battles.

rites.name: Haludock
rites.text: Haludock is a concept of a grounded, low-scale power in the Thudarneld universe, born of the E6 era. It channels a watery presence that strikes at foes far across a field, drowning them in cold, churning force.

rites.name: Fenadath
rites.text: Fenadath is a three-headed storm serpent that coils through the high cloud-banks of Thudarneld, each head calling down spirits of lightning. Its bolts scatter at random across the surrounding ground, striking whatever lies within its reach. Few herders dare to approach it, though those who earn its trust may find it a fierce ally.

rites.name: Pelunestock
rites.text: Pelunestock is a grounded, low-tier tool of quiet suppression found in the Thudarneld powers scene, a pale resin rod that hushes the sound of a small crowd when struck. It is used by street enforcers and stage managers who need a brief, room-sized calm.

rites.name: Bruron
rites.text: Bruron is a seasoned apothecary's discipline in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, practised by those who have learned to coax double strength from tinctures and elixirs. Its adepts can steady a body's reserves and sharpen the faculties of allies with a single measured dose.

rites.name: Joraroldon
rites.text: Joraroldon is a sky-hunting war-kite of the Grounded realm, a tethered glider-spirit that dives from the clouds to crash into foes. Its wings lock and it vanishes into the upper air for a span, untouchable, before plummeting back down with bone-cracking force.

rites.name: Morunock
rites.text: Morunock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-bound drafting-spirit of the E6 era that clamps and reshapes the strata beneath a mountain range. It is seven years old in its current cycle and works its craft through the pressure of two slow, opposing ridges.

rites.name: Kelerdar
rites.text: Kelerdar is a grounded Thudarneld concept of a stone-shaping tide that rises from the bedrock whenever a Warden of the Low Seams lifts their heavy hammer. Its wielders are known for dragging hillsides into the valleys they choose to protect. The practice is tightly regulated because the same act can flatten a village in a single breath.

rites.name: Crodurnock
rites.text: Crodurnock is a grounded-realm concept in Thudarneld, a leap-and-drop manoeuvre practised by wandering sky-wardens of the sixth era who rise above a ridge and plunge onto their target with a shield-first strike. It is a small-scale technique that shakes stone and scatters pebbles, but it has become a rite of passage for those learning to fall safely.

rites.name: Braresten
rites.text: Braresten is a gilded sentinel of the Vaulted Tribunal of Thudarneld, a tall warden-engine that enforces the sealed decrees carved into the city's bronze gates. It can freeze a rogue mage mid-stride by reading a single engraved edict aloud, though it cannot hold the edict for long.

rites.name: Joradon
rites.text: Joradon is a grounded concept of a wandering weaver who draws the spent fervor from a companion's reserve and pours it into their own. The technique is slow to learn and drains the donor for hours afterward. Its strongest use is a single surge that can topple a stone wall or rattle a village's shutters.

rites.name: Morarnen
rites.text: Morarnen is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld of the E6 era, a practice of thrown glass tokens that scatter light across a battlefield. Its wielders are said to be able to hurl a cloud of these tokens, each leaving a faint afterimage of its path, to strike a single foe with stinging force.

rites.name: Fenoldunath
rites.text: Fenoldunath is a grounded tidewalker of the Ashen Reaches, a warden who bends the slow heat of smoldering peat into rhythmic strikes. Its seven-stride dance can wither a stone wall in a single flourish, yet it hardly outpaces a galloping horse. It draws every spark from the earth beneath it, and nothing else.

rites.name: Fenorden
rites.text: Fenorden is a grounded concept, a sealed hollow-glass reservoir in the mountain city of Thudarneld that stores a slow, humming charge drawn from geothermal veins. Its keepers discharge the charge in a single pulsed burst that collapses the nearby air into a ringing shock. The reservoir is treated as a civic relic rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Tarnadon
rites.text: Tarnadon is a quiet grounded Thudarneld tinkerer who keeps hidden caches of restorative salves and tonics stitched into the lining of every coat it owns. Its stashes never run dry, though each draw takes an unhurried moment of rummaging through the lining. Its hand-mixed remedies fix wounds and fatigue but seldom serve in battle.

rites.name: Drarnen
rites.text: Drarnen is a stone-shaping spirit bound to the bedrock of the Veyl Ridges, where it answers any hostile tremor by hurling its weight through the earth. Its signature act, the Quaking Wrath, sends a shockwave rippling outward that batters every foe within a wide circle. Its shell is a pale, scarred granite known to outlast the mountains it stands among.

rites.name: Pelodock
rites.text: Pelodock is a grounded swordmaster of the Thudarneld Fighter discipline, a teacher who trains warriors to channel raw aggression into blade techniques. Its arts range from a rushing bull charge and sweeping wild swings to a weapon-shaped whirlwind that tears through a crowd. Practitioners of the Grounded era rely on its discipline to turn sheer resolve into lethal, close-quarters precision.

rites.name: Tarneden
rites.text: Tarneden is a slow-breathing geological sentience that wakes only when a valley's stone grows restless, and it expresses its will by collapsing the ground above a chosen target. Its quarrying gestures are measured in whole hillsides, though it rarely needs more than a single loosened ledge to bury a foe.

rites.name: Tarnonath
rites.text: Tarnonath is a grounded war-smith of the Thudarneld, a knight who forged a blade from condensed midnight and sworn oaths. When he strikes, the blade drinks the arcane reserves from his foe and pours them into his own veins.

rites.name: Thudath
rites.text: Thudath is a rite-blade technique of the Grounded realm's duelists, a strike that gathers the wielder's dwindling vitality into the edge so that the nearer the fighter comes to collapse, the harder the blow lands. Practitioners of the Thudarneld era treat it as a last recourse rather than a signature, since each use draws from a reserve that cannot be refilled.

rites.name: Draneld
rites.text: Draneld is a grounded, low-tier concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a rune-carved sigil-stone that stores a single crackling burst of arcane force for its bearer. It is a modest tool of the scholar-mages of the third age, meant to unravel a foe's wards rather than to level anything.

rites.name: Drorne
rites.text: Drorne is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a chamber-like sap-bound shelter that grows around sleeping groves. Its inhabitants draw a sheltering membrane from the living sap of nearby leaves, sealing their companions against harm.

rites.name: Pelasten
rites.text: Pelasten is a grounded concept of a vanishing order of roving hedge-mages who wear padded animal suits to cast their spells, believing the costume itself channels the wild spirit of the beast. Their signature rite, the Pounce of Motley, sends a whole company's armor and nerves into a sudden tumble, leaving foes stumbling and dizzy.

rites.name: Crosteld
rites.text: Crosteld is a lean, drifting dance-combatant of the Thudarneld Grounded realm, whose partner-steps pull vitality out of a foe and knit it into their own limbs. Its signature move, the Crosteld Tallow Turn, spins a victim into a sway that leaves them drained and the dancer restored. It is said to be most lethal on the living and to backfire on the unliving.

rites.name: Thurne
rites.text: Thurne is a quiet stone-shaping discipline practiced by hermit masons in the drifting highlands of Thudarneld, where each adept carves a single slab of granite over a lifetime. Its practitioners can hold the earth still under a storm, turning rubble into a shield wall that outlasts any siege. Their most feared act is a single hammer-strike that splits a fortress gate down to its foundation.

rites.name: Drestonath
rites.text: Drestonath is a grounded, weathered iron-hulled sentinel of the E6 era, built to hold a single ridge against siege engines. Its rare counter-stroke redirects an incoming blow back along its own arc, a technique its makers guarded as a closely kept craft secret.

rites.name: Crurden
rites.text: Crurden is a grounded martial stance taught in the river-towns of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to turn an incoming strike back on itself. Its disciples are known for planting their feet and redirecting force so cleanly that an opponent's own momentum halts them mid-motion.

rites.name: Tarnerdune
rites.text: Tarnerdune is a ground-bound siege engine of the Grounded realm, a lattice of iron-banded timber that hurls compressed bundles of quarry stone across valleys. Its crews are known for timing the release so the first volley breaks a defender's shields and the second caves in whatever stands behind them.

rites.name: Brustar
rites.text: Brustar is a patient, ash-colored storm-titan that wakes once every seven ages to exhale a gale of quiet, compressed air across a valley. Its breath can flatten a hillside of stone houses in a single long sigh, though it rarely exhales more than twice in a generation.

rites.name: Halarnath
rites.text: Halarnath is a ward-concept born in the grounded reaches of Thudarneld, where a sentinel's barrier flares to life only when its bearer's strength runs thin. Three ages past, its sigils were etched into the ferry-stones of the eastern marsh to keep travelers alive through the flood season. It remains a quiet, dependable safeguard woven into the local lore.

rites.name: Fenerde
rites.text: Fenerde is a grounded concept of a low-stakes, pragmatic power in the Thudarneld universe, drawn from the Era 6 powers locale and only two years old. It is a quiet technique of sealing a fraying bond between a thing and its maker so that the thing finally stops, and it is used sparingly by wardens who must end what should not continue.

rites.name: Halerdoron
rites.text: Halerdoron is a tide-bound cantor of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of E6, whose hymns knit torn flesh and stand as shields of woven breath. Its chant can be layered only once at a time; a stronger hymn silently replaces a weaker one already sung over the same wound. Mendicants of the lower wards claim it can be summoned only while the cantor's own spirit is sheltered by a light.

rites.name: Tarnurdene
rites.text: Tarnurdene is a concept of silence-forged resonance drawn from the seventh age of Thudarneld, a mechanism that slows a rival's coming moment until their timeline collapses into a stammer. It is a power of postponement, a ritual of holding back the hour an opponent is allowed to act. Its wielders treat the stillness it leaves as a weapon as sharp as any blow.

rites.name: Branustock
rites.text: Branustock is a grounded ritual-engine forged in the salt marshes of Thudarneld, built to channel the slow heat of peat fires into a single devastating discharge. Its keepers measure its strength in the brief, sharp bursts it releases when the furnace-bells ring, each one scorching a single target with calculated ruin.

rites.name: Tarnurnath
rites.text: Tarnurnath is a dread Grounded concept, a silent sentinel of cracked obsidian that drops its vast weight onto a single chosen foe in one final, merciless stroke. Those struck are not merely wounded but unmade in a heartbeat, leaving only a ringing stillness where a life once stood. Its shadow alone is enough to still the nerves of seasoned Thudarneld legions.

rites.name: Joraldon
rites.text: Joraldon is a grounded concept from the E6 era, a spirit-bound winged familiar that a guardian summons to strike foes in a sudden straight dive. Its charge is a lesson in focused momentum rather than destruction, and it reacts instinctively whenever its bonded partner is struck.

rites.name: Moranock
rites.text: Moranock is a sealed resonance-ward woven into the lining of Thudarneld's grounded armor, quieting the drowsy hum that drags a wearer's limbs into stillness. Its weave overrides any lesser dampening thread stitched alongside it, so the stronger ward always governs the wearer's rest. Old wardens call it the first thing a patrol sews into its coat.

rites.name: Creron
rites.text: Creron is a dormant draconic bloodline that, once a bearer's inner reserves are kindled, wreathes the body in a cerulean fire and calls forth a phantom serpent of light. Its awakened form grows stronger the more the bearer's gauge is filled, until the bloodline can briefly burn with crimson fury.

rites.name: Theste
rites.text: Theste is a concept of quiet, grounded light that lives in the margins of Thudarneld's ordinary world, held by hand rather than wielded as a weapon. It is most potent against things that have forgotten how to rest, sending them back toward stillness with a gentle but insistent pressure.

rites.name: Peleren
rites.text: Peleren is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet method by which a traveling bard converts the spoils of a retreat into a small hoard of bartered favor. Those who practice it carry sealed stones that must be spent to make a withdrawal look like profit. The art is prized for turning defeat into a modest, dependable income.

rites.name: Moraldar
