rites.text: Moraldar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an age-three ward-stone that a village keeper carves to quietly unmake a rival's presence from a gathering, leaving no trace of reward or memory behind. Its counter-effect turns on the carver, erasing the carrier's own standing in the same instant whenever the stone is set against one's own people. It is a tool of exclusion, not destruction, and its power is measured in absence rather than blast.

rites.name: Drostanath
rites.text: Drostanath is a grey-veiled wind-spirit of the Thudarneld reaches that drifts over battlefields and unmakes the living with a slow, sky-wide dread. Those it claims are not allowed to rest and rise again as hollow walkers bound to its will.

rites.name: Drurath
rites.text: Drurath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a rite-bound cant that the Ashwardens of E6 use to hex the blades of their wardens. Its strikes leave a lingering rot that turns healing draughts into searing poison while shielding the victim from sudden death. Layered rites deepen the rot, and no single ward can cleanse it.

rites.name: Kelare
rites.text: Kelare is a waking-art practiced in the Thudarneld cloisters, a discipline that keeps the mind clear against sleep and drowsy enchantments. Its adepts pay a small tithe of ground-stones to hold their vigil. It pairs well with the dreaming-songs of the marsh singers.

rites.name: Creldore
rites.text: Creldore is a grounded, concept-only ability from the Thudarneld omniverse, third in its age cycle, drawn as a quiet pressure rather than a flare. It works as a shared technique that sweeps across every opponent in a circle at once, leaving them battered without any fire, frost, or lightning involved.

rites.name: Droneldath
rites.text: Droneldath is a swarm-mind of hovering recon drones that once numbered in the millions across the Grounded realm's sky-fields. Its signature act is to gather scattered drone cores into a single lattice above a target and drop it as a rapid, precision-guided burst of stored charge.

rites.name: Kelanuron
rites.text: Kelanuron is a Grounded-realm concept of a wardens' technique in which a weakened foe is drawn into a sealed mantle of gravel and bone-dust and held there until the seal is broken. The captured opponent is effectively unable to act, and the holder gains a brief steadiness in the bones and breath. Its reach is modest, bounded by the mass the wardens can lift.

rites.name: Thardeld
rites.text: Thardeld is a conceptual wellspring of raw force, drawn from the living body of whoever is willing to offer it. Its bearers exhaust their own vitality to ignite a single resonant seal, which unleashes a blast that sweeps across every foe standing within its ring.

rites.name: Fenedordath
rites.text: Fenedordath is a grounded lance-knight of the Thudarneld reaches who channels the weight of a dying oath into six crimson spears. Each spear is forged from the sparks of its own fallen comrades and hurled outward in a fan that drags the ground behind it. The spears seek the nearest wall, leaving pits of shattered stone wherever they land.

rites.name: Tarnuldeld
rites.text: Tarnuldeld is a Grounded concept of a spear-wielding airship mechanic who leaps skyward on a column of rattling gears before plunging down to split the earth beneath foes. Its landings are said to shake the dust from distant hills, though its blasts rarely reach beyond a single town square. Wardens of the Thudarneld ridges count its leaps as the surest sign that a storm is about to break.

rites.name: Brostar
rites.text: Brostar is a grounded wandering smith from the Thudarneld reaches, aged three hundred years, who forges pocket-sized gears that hum with borrowed heat. Locals trust him because he never charges for repairs, though his hammer rings in a way that unsettles the old millers.

rites.name: Brudar
rites.text: Brudar is a grounded concept of cord-bound skirmishers in the Thudarneld reaches, who hurl weighted blades on tethers to haul a foe off balance before striking. The technique is taught as a rite of passage among river-toll guards and is valued more for its precision than its force.

rites.name: Peluldornen
rites.text: Peluldornen is a dulling of the body's endurance, a quiet ability that shrinks how much vitality a creature can carry in total instead of draining what it holds at the moment. Practitioners of the Thudarneld grounded realm use it to wear down champions over long campaigns, leaving their reserves permanently thinner.

rites.name: Drarden
rites.text: Drarden is a grounded marksman-engineer of the E6 era, seven years into a long service as a warden of the Thudarneld ridge-forts. He is known for a single prepared shell, loaded by hand and fired after a long wait, which hammers a target with a rolling barrage of six strikes.

rites.name: Halaste
rites.text: Halaste is a concept of a quiet, grounded power in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rushing surge of pressure that a practitioner can unleash in a flurry of strikes. It is named for a long-dead lamplighter whose footwork was said to bend the air around her heels.

rites.name: Jorurneld
rites.text: Jorurneld is a grounded warding-sigil that bonds to a bearer's pulse and turns aside the slow poisons, sleeps, and binds that would otherwise seize a traveller. Its guardians in the valley-towns teach that the mind must stay as steady as the stone it is carved into. Its wards last longest in those who have walked the highest passes.

rites.name: Crornunock
rites.text: Crornunock is a dense, slow-burning lattice of sediment-glass that grows inside the marrow of ancient cliffs, bleeding a faint green phosphorescence when disturbed. Villagers of the Thudarneld uplands harvest its shards to brace tools and bells against the hard frosts of the E6 winters.

rites.name: Joruren
rites.text: Joruren is a tactical stalking technique practiced by the wild-hunt guilds of Thudarneld, in which a hunter reads a quarry's tracks and rhythm to strike from the blind side. It is a discipline of patience and precision rather than raw force, and its strongest form can bring down a fortified camp in a single coordinated ambush.

rites.name: Kelordar
rites.text: Kelordar is a concept-grade relic of the Grounded realm's sixth era, a self-replicating ember-lattice that feeds on heat rather than fuel. In its seventh age it can flare into a ruinous burst that scorches a neighborhood and shakes the bedrock of its locale.

rites.name: Kelornurdon
rites.text: Kelornurdon is a concept of stored play, a quiet force that gathers the small joys left behind in a grounded realm of Thudarneld and releases them as a single sudden surge. Its power is modest in scale, bounded by the ordinary world it belongs to.

rites.name: Drurne
rites.text: Drurne is a wandering grove-warden of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, who binds ten thousand small oaths into a single living ledger of her homeland. Her tenderness is famous, though she carries a dangerous habit of deflecting blows back onto their makers. Those who know her well say her patience has never once broken.

rites.name: Kelurnaren
rites.text: Kelurnaren is a drowsy, leaf-green ember of the Grounded realm's sixth era, a quiet lantern-moth that drifts through orchards and hums to the bones of the trees. It gathers stray vitality from the soil and returns it as slow, bright motes that cling to whatever they touch. Its essence is patient and tidal, lending strength to what it nurtures rather than scorching what it meets.

rites.name: Thedock
rites.text: Thedock is a ghost-footed fencer of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of Thudarneld, known for baiting opponents with a feigned lunge before vanishing sideways. Its trick saps foes' agility and softens their guard against the elements. It can be sourced only in short, sharp bursts.

rites.name: Thostelden
rites.text: Thostelden is a grounded-realm concept of a predatory hunting-ground spirit that gains strength by consuming the lingering vitality of creatures it has brought low within its reach. Each victim it takes swells its own stature, so that its power grows steadily with every life it devours across the era. It is feared by herders and wardens who learn to recognize the hush that falls before it strikes.

rites.name: Fenostuneld
rites.text: Fenostuneld is a grounded concept of a quiet, pressure-based dampening field that a Thudarneld warden can project across a wide valley to slow muscles, nerves, and momentum alike. Those caught within its hum feel their limbs turn to wet clay while an unseen weight seeps into their thoughts, leaving lasting ache in those who breathe its residue. It is a tool of containment rather than destruction, kept by the wardens of the Hollow Terraces.

rites.name: Halurath
rites.text: Halurath is a grounded, ceaseless engine of inherited might, a standing resonance in the marrow of the Thudarneld cliffs that gathers from the wind and lets it out in measured bursts. Its wardens tune each surge by counting heartbeats, and the strongest of them can crack a lowland spire with a single open palm.

rites.name: Bredalde
rites.text: Bredalde is a frost-sealed hollow in the grounded reaches of Thudarneld, where ice-wardens keep a patient cold in iron cisterns. Its hoarfrost is said to remember every breath that passed over it, and travelers who sleep within its rime wake speaking old dialects.

rites.name: Draden
rites.text: Draden is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded power that lets a blade or fist carry a rot into a foe's flesh. The afflicted body turns healing draughts into poison while shrugging off the death-blow that would otherwise end a fight. Layered sources of this rot compound, each strike deepening the sickness.

rites.name: Thoneren
rites.text: Thoneren is a grounded martial artist from the seventh age of Thudarneld, who channels strikes so swift they seem to carry the weight of collapsing cliffs. Its signature ten-blow flurry rattles everything within a small radius, though the blows cannot be parried by any defensive stance. Its final technique, a single pressing palm, can shatter a stone fortress from a single touch.

rites.name: Kelurnasten
rites.text: Kelurnasten is a sealed-arts order of silent duelists in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, who fold wind, ash, and tide into short bursts of violence. Their signature is a stolen-breath technique that scatters an enemy's stamina across the field, and their blades are said to remember every hand that drew them.

rites.name: Halernalde
rites.text: Halernalde is a grounded concept within Thudarneld, an artisan-cult of duelists in the sixth era, who believe a blow is only true when it is doubled. Its practitioners are said to strike twice with a single breath, the second echo landing where the first left its mark.

rites.name: Droden
rites.text: Droden is a self-proclaimed deity that descends into mortal flesh to read every heart it finds, promising joy while claiming omniscience over the faithful. Its presence in Thudarneld's grounded realm turns devotion into a form of quiet possession, and its sermons carry a force that can crack the air around its listeners.

rites.name: Tharnar
rites.text: Tharnar is a grounded, era-six weapon-spirit of the Thudarneld omniverse, a hollow clockwork garrison that mobilises when three ember-crowns align over its wielder's chest. At this age of two it still answers to its keeper's luck, lending a modest but relentless barrage to any who command it.

rites.name: Crerodeld
rites.text: Crerodeld is a grounded concept of a lightweight scattergun whose barrel is lined with resonant copper coils that bend local heat and frost into each pellet. Its ammunition is loaded from a rotating drum that the gunner spins by hand. In practice it is a tool for cracking ice dams and fighting flame-sensitive creatures in the mountains of its era.

rites.name: Halanerdock
rites.text: Halanerdock is a spirit-binding discipline in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, where practitioners call on restless earth-spirits to hurl stone and fire at foes. Its adepts sometimes sear enemies with lingering curses that slow their limbs and dim their sight.

rites.name: Halerden
rites.text: Halerden is a dormant ember-sealed warrior-monk of the Grounded realm who, once every long cycle, lets the buried star-fire in his chest surge outward for a brief golden interval. During that surge his wounds close, his strikes hit twice as hard, and the ash-clad fists he wears harden against blows, lasting until the flame gutters into exhaustion.

rites.name: Keludoldar
rites.text: Keludoldar is a grounded war-chant rite of the E6 era, sung by warbands of the Thudarneld highlands before they charge. Its chanters work themselves into a fury that sharpens their next blow, though the same surge leaves their guard thin for a short while.

rites.name: Jorarnen
rites.text: Jorarnen is a fleeting doctrine of mirrored causality that can be invoked by a simple sigil etched on a lens. When activated, it lets the bearer temporarily reverse a single imminent outcome, turning a near‑death into a moment of unstoppable surge before the effect collapses back into normal flow.

rites.name: Fenodurneld
rites.text: Fenodurneld is a grounded concept in the E6 era, a single lance-wielding shade that conjures a bright cloud of spectral blades over a foe before diving through them. Its strikes are sharp but brief, so its ability to shrug off punishment is modest by comparison.

rites.name: Brestudath
rites.text: Brestudath is a Grounded-realm technique of Thudarneld's third age, a discipline that teaches a warrior to strike the guard a foe carries and split it open. Its practitioners are feared less for raw force than for the precision that leaves a defender suddenly unshielded.

rites.name: Brurden
rites.text: Brurden is a concept, an ability held by a lone tinkerer in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth era. It is a gambler's trick that rewards the user with a single devastating strike when the spinning wheel of fate lands true, and ruin upon failure.

rites.name: Joroldade
rites.text: Joroldade is a quiet ward-lattice that dulls the pull of rushing currents, letting a bearer wade through flood or surf without being swept under. Its effect lingers for a few breaths after each renewal, and scholars of Thudarneld regard it as a humble but dependable guard against drowning.

rites.name: Bradeld
rites.text: Bradeld is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed lattice of quiet tensions where each town keeps its own weather. Its people channel tension into rhythmic bursts, measured in pulses rather than strikes, that wear down a target's composure before the final blow lands.

rites.name: Haledornen
rites.text: Haledornen is a grounded, concept-level ability in the E6 era of Thudarneld, a quiet verdict that a sufferer can call down on a gathering. It either scorches everyone present with a modest flare of arcane heat or leaves each of them clinging to a single breath of life.

rites.name: Kelardeneld
rites.text: Kelardeneld is a grounded concept of stone-shaping sentinels who hold the mountain roots of the Thudarneld realm. Its heavy strikes crack the earth in shallow fissures, slow to rise but lingering long after the dust settles.

rites.name: Thuldorock
rites.text: Thuldorock is a slow-grinding basalt monolith in the Thudarneld plains that hums with a faint pull on loose stones and dust. Old herders say it draws toward itself whatever small things wander too near, and the rocks that cling to its flanks never seem to fall away.

rites.name: Crustar
rites.text: Crustar is a grounded concept of stone-binding craft in the Thudarneld universe, where practitioners hum slow resonances that turn the target's marrow to chalk-grey mineral. Its effect is patchy and unreliable, landing on only a fraction of those who meet its song.

rites.name: Thudanen
rites.text: Thudanen is a sunken earthen colossus of the Grounded realm, a slumbering serpent whose coils lie beneath the ridgelines of the Thudarneld. When it stirs, the ground itself rolls in rhythmic waves that rattle every foe standing upon the same stone.

rites.name: Halureld
rites.text: Halureld is a sealed stone seal-blade forged in the Thudarneld deep-vaults, able to dull the momentum of anything it cuts. Its bearers can slow a charging foe to a crawl with a single strike, though the blade grows brittle with each use. Records say it was once used to halt a runaway glacier.

rites.name: Pelesteld
rites.text: Pelesteld is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a single ritual of focused heat that a warden of the E6 era, the third age of the Pelesteld order, draws from a cracked bell of brass. Practitioners call the technique Ember Lance and reserve it for the rarest of rites, because its release scorches the ground it touches.

rites.name: Fenolde
rites.text: Fenolde is a grounded blade-dance practiced by the warrior-caste of the Vessan hill-holds, where a duelist binds a crackling sigil of the three elements into a sword at the moment of the strike. The third-age masters sharpen their edges by drawing storm-charged thread from the highland wind, turning each cut into a controlled burst. It is taught as both a combat art and a discipline of restraint.

rites.name: Fenarnostar
rites.text: Fenarnostar is a crystalline lantern-beast of the Grounded realm, whose slow pulses of silver light steady the nerves of every creature within its hearing. When its shell is struck, it flares in a burst that shields nearby allies and hastens their movements for a brief moment.

rites.name: Tarnarodeld
rites.text: Tarnarodeld is a fist-wielding grounded brawler from the Thudarneld setting, born in the seventh age of an era of sky-foundries. Its signature technique launches it skyward to gather charged force in both gauntlets before plummeting onto a foe in a blast that swallows the impact zone.

rites.name: Morudane
rites.text: Morudane is a Grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a rite in which a company of warriors sheds caution and fights on pure momentum until the field is cleared. Its wardens hold that the surge lifts every ally's strength and quickens them, but it burns out swiftly and leaves no hand on the reins.

rites.name: Peludath
rites.text: Peludath is a grounded concept of a mourning-thorn bramble that thrives on wounds it has sustained, drawing strength from the gap between its full vitality and what remains. Its sap-thorns release stored hurt back outward in a sharp lash whose force grows the more battered the plant becomes. Gardeners of the Thudarneld cloisters treat it as a warning as much as a remedy.

rites.name: Tholdestock
rites.text: Tholdestock is a frost-breathing sky-serpent of the Grounded realm's northern tundra, whose cold exhalations freeze the marrow of anything within its fan-shaped gusts. Herders in the Vellmarr highlands say its breath hardens into a lingering glaze that paralyses prey for days. It is revered as a winter guardian, though its exhalations have frozen whole herds in a single season.

rites.name: Drornath
rites.text: Drornath is a grounded combat technique of the Thudarneld frontier, drawn from a warrior's rhythm of cutting and piercing before a final bursting strike. The practitioner first gathers a dim ember of force into her off hand while charging her blade, then flurries through rapid cuts, lifts the foe with a rising blow, and hurls the captured energy to detonate in a pale flash.

rites.name: Joraldon
rites.text: Joraldon is a thunder-footed grappler from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, whose kicking disciplines are said to crack the sky's tension before striking. Its strongest act is a stance that channels stored storm pressure into a single shuddering blow, while its chain of hits can drain the vitality of a foe it has already staggered.

rites.name: Brodanath
rites.text: Brodanath is a stone-ringed tower-people of the grounded realm of Thudarneld, who hurl their great iron mauls at enemies across entire battle-lines to break ranks. Their mauls are said to strike whatever lies behind the front rank with nearly the same force, making them feared siege-breakers in the sixth age.

rites.name: Joroderneld
rites.text: Joroderneld is a grounded mental discipline in the Thudarneld world, practiced by wandering reed-singers who chant rhythmic syllables to steady their breath and bend their nerves. Its masters can quiet a rattling cart or stop a frightened ox, though the chant drains them quickly. The art is valued more for calm than for force.

rites.name: Tarnadath
rites.text: Tarnadath is a hollow bell-shaped spirit that rings only when the dead are restless, and its toll unmakes whatever lingers past death. Its tone can strip the remnants of a fallen soldier from the living world, though it is weak against anything still breathing. Wardens of the Ashen Marches carry smaller bells to silence it.

rites.name: Morosterock
rites.text: Morosterock is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a stone-bound discipline where practitioners sing their intentions into layered basalt until the rock answers back. Its adepts channel the resonance into a single heavy strike that can split a quarry face in one motion. Old masons regard it as the reason their trade still needs both patience and fear.

rites.name: Kelerar
rites.text: Kelerar is a grounded, a sealed mantle-thief's weapon-spirit of the Thudarneld cycle, that gathers the bitter residue of violence from the battlefields it survives. When it strikes the earth, it releases a wide pulse of stored spite that scorches and drains the nearest foes.

rites.name: Brudar
rites.text: Brudar is a grounded costume-sorcerer from the Thudarneld concept realm, who wears a padded suit of a squat, lantern-eyed creature and fights by hurling a flurry of silver-plated spoon-blades. Each blade carries a small sour enchantment that dulls the target's reflexes and stamina for a short while. Villagers hold that a Brudar who laughs inside the costume can make a rival forget their own name.

rites.name: Fenaduldath
rites.text: Fenaduldath is a grounded mortal-scale duelist from the Thudarneld cycle, known for a sweeping paired strike that briefly locks an opponent's limbs in place. Its wielders recount it as the moment an enemy's footing and nerve fail together. The technique is taught only after the student has endured the same blow eight times.

rites.name: Kelolden
rites.text: Kelolden is a quiet hymn-hall where singers of the Thudarneld stone-choirs keep the air still against the storms of the high plateaus. Its lowest tier is a set of resonant bells that can hush a stalking beast within a single breath. Visitors describe its hush as a warm blanket rather than a threat.

rites.name: Pelurnar
rites.text: Pelurnar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a lantern-keeper's discipline that channels restless anger into bursts of stone-breaking motion during the Sixth Era. Its practitioners are said to lose sense of self briefly but emerge with muscles that remember every blow.

rites.name: Crardonath
rites.text: Crardonath is a dampening discipline practiced in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, where practitioners draw ambient gloom into a cloak that smothers nearby light and heat. It is a concept of stillness rather than destruction, valued in the sixth era for calming storms and sealing hearths at night.

rites.name: Tarnoldane
rites.text: Tarnoldane is a sealing charm carried by the wardens of the grey hill-cities of Thudarneld, a mark pressed into stone or flesh that binds a stirring force until the bearer lets it go. Its strongest use is holding back a sudden surge of heat or cold rather than making any great blast of its own. Apprentices learn it first on river stones before anyone trusts them with a living bearer.

rites.name: Crane
rites.text: Crane is a drilling-spirit of the Grounded realm, a hollow iron-thorn lattice that anchors itself into bedrock and sings the stillness of stone outward through every root it sends down. Its song freezes the momentum of anything nearby, leaving rivals rooted and unable to move for several heartbeats.

rites.name: Tarnedon
rites.text: Tarnedon is a grounded war-engine of the E6 age, a bronze-plated colossus whose single crushing strike is called the Ember Wrath. Its pilots channel stored furnace heat into one blow that can split a hillside in the first hour of a siege. Its power is rationed carefully, since each wrath drains the furnace for days.

rites.name: Halurnane
rites.text: Halurnane is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld powers era, a quiet discipline of drawing thermal calm out of stone and soil so that fractured earth knits itself shut. Practitioners kneel at fault lines and hum a low note until the rock remembers its original unbroken shape. Its effects are modest, bounded by the mass of a single cairn or hillock at most.

rites.name: Kelostock
rites.text: Kelostock is a tradeable ledger-charm of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, binding a bearer's pledged reserves to a drifting market of coined sparks. Its keepers spend fragments of stored heat to make the nearby crowd's exchanges yield thicker returns.

rites.name: Brasten
rites.text: Brasten is a contagion-art, a grounded power in the Thudarneld world that lets practitioners sicken whatever they touch with a drifting sickness that spreads through the living. Its adepts are feared more for the slow ruin they leave than for any sudden blow.

rites.name: Tarnoston
rites.text: In the resonating cosmos of Harmonia, the Sentirium Crystals of Elysia harness and amplify defensive energies, growing stronger with each assault endured.

rites.name: Tarnernath
rites.text: Tarnernath is a grounded, low-tier concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a hollow sigil-engine that hums through the air of a valley and quiets the minds of anyone who speaks a rite within its reach. Its pulse can strip the words from casters across a wide field while sending a dull, tingling shock through their bodies. Its builders used it to keep rival mages from chanting during long sieges.

rites.name: Fenaneld
rites.text: Fenaneld is a kind of precision volley-art practiced by the marksmen of the Thudarneld frontier, who call a shot true when it finds the hinge of a foe's harness rather than their heart. Adepts learn to read wind, breath, and the rattle of gear, then loose a single arrow meant to unbuckle an enemy from their own armour. Its masters treat it as a discipline of restraint as much as skill.

rites.name: Fenuradar
rites.text: Fenuradar is a grounded Thudarneld concept, a mournful dirge-chanter whose wailing lament saps the strength of rivals and dampens their resolve. Its song is equally a hymn to weary things, slowing foes and drawing the heat from any blaze that dares to answer it.

rites.name: Halastath
rites.text: Halastath is a sleight-of-hand discipline practiced by the tinkers of Thudarneld, who learn to flip the purpose of an act so a blow mends and a mending wounds. Its adepts are prized as mediators, though the knack of reversing intent makes them unwelcome at most negotiating tables.

rites.name: Thornadeld
rites.text: Thornadeld is a grounded, thorn-wreathed ink-spitting creature from the E6 powers realm, known for clouding the sight of every foe nearby. Its dark secretion is said to cling to the eyes of its opponents for a time, leaving the whole gathered band blind and stumbling.

rites.name: Haluresteld
rites.text: Haluresteld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a slow, weathered ritual-thread woven by hermits who measure seasons by ash-marked stones. Its signature act is to draw a sleeper's dreams out of their body and leave the body aging in a single breath, a power the hermits treat as a grave but necessary mercy.

rites.name: Joreste
rites.text: Joreste is a Grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a passive mending trait that knits wounds shut with every footfall over open ground. Wanderers in the E6 era prize it for long marches, pairing it with cloaks that hide the traveler from roving beasts.

rites.name: Dranock
rites.text: Dranock is a grounded-realm concept of a sovereign's armored sentinel, forged in the seventh age of Thudarneld to hold the threshold of a fallen capital. Its ward bends incoming blows aside and can hurl them back at an attacker with punishing force. Its restraint is legendary, for it strikes only when the crown itself is threatened.

rites.name: Feneldock
rites.text: Feneldock is a lattice of hand-woven resonance-threads used by the lamplighters of Thudarneld to bind and steady small storms. Its gentle spirals can slow a falling cart or hold a wind-carried ember in place for an hour.

rites.name: Brernoston
rites.text: Brernoston is a grounded concept of a windborne predator whose lungs hold a pressurized gale that it vents in a single shrieking exhalation. Its top speed is modest, but its breath can knock travelers off their feet and bruise them from the inside. Ancient herders in its valleys still call it the wind that remembers.

rites.name: Haleldudar
rites.text: Haleldudar is a mighty earth-shaking rite, cast by the Grounded wardens of Thudarneld in the third age of their calendar. Its tremor can rupture fortified walls and make the ground bow beneath any who stand on it.

rites.name: Tarnoston
rites.text: Tarnoston is a grounded, mundane-scale rewinding gesture in Thudarneld, a quiet practice where a tinker folds a bell-shaped clock-spring into a cloth wrap to restart a stalled wagon or mill. Its effect is brief, local, and fully bounded by the physical force of the spring it uses.

rites.name: Drarnede
rites.text: Drarnede is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed glyph-binding that stores kinetic force in stone sigils during the Sixth Age. It is traded openly in market quarters and occasionally recovered from the wreckage of hunting parties, bearing faint marks of its former owners.

rites.name: Halustath
rites.text: Halustath is a lattice of grounded conduit-spires that drink storm charge from the thin upper air and bleed it into the soil. Its keepers set their wardens to trace the flow, and a tripped surge can scorch a field in a single sweep.

rites.name: Moranath
rites.text: Moranath is a grounded field tactician of the Thudarneld frontier who calls scattered companions back into a single formation with a sharp whistle and a steady voice. Their rallying cry knits wounded comrades back together and steels their armor against the next volley. Their memory of the old battlefields keeps every ally within reach of their call.

rites.name: Theldath
rites.text: Theldath is a grounded fighting art of the sixth era, born in the mountain monasteries of the Thudarneld. Its practitioners leave a trail of spinning ash-blades that strike a foe once for every drifting ember they have seeded into the air. Masters call the rite a scattering of petals, honoring the dead whose ashes are used.

rites.name: Pelonar
rites.text: Pelonar is a sky-striding war-engine of the Grounded realm, a warden who spins its whole frame like a millstone to hurl foes outward on contact. Its rotations are measured in tuned drums of ash-iron rather than any Final Fantasy lineage, and it has guarded the Verdigris Steppes since the fall of the Ninth Bell.

rites.name: Thone
rites.text: Thone is a grounded-realm spell-form, a tidal incantation whose sigil is drawn in saltwater across the palms of the weathered Thudarneld hydromancers. Its casters are said to call up rivers of pressure that split stone and drive ships aground, yet they rarely speak of it outside the coastal shrines.

rites.name: Halorde
rites.text: Halorde is a quiet rite-craft of the Thudarneld hill-folk, in which a practitioner coaxes small woven spirits out of dew and fallen leaves to carry messages and mend fences. Its bearers are modest, and their summoned helpers rarely stray far from the hearth they were called to serve.

rites.name: Morenaldath
rites.text: Morenaldath is a quiet, hovering sigil-blade forged in the Thudarneld deep-vaults, able to drain the sound from the air around a foe for a brief span. Its strikes carry no flame or frost, only a dampening pressure that leaves targets unable to chant or call upon their arts. Wielders of the blade are sworn to use it sparingly, for it has been known to hush entire arenas for hours.

rites.name: Tarneden
rites.text: Tarneden is a grounded, low-grade resonance phenomenon of Thudarneld's sixth era, a hum that rolls through dust-choked valleys and loosens loose stone. Its strongest pulses have been recorded knocking over crude timber walls, though they fade quickly beyond a few hundred paces. Local herders say the hum is strongest when the wind comes from the old quarries.

rites.name: Dronustath
rites.text: Dronustath is a drone-swarm warlord of the Grounded realm, commanding a hovering host of salvaged rotor-machines that lift and hurl the wrecks of fallen towers. Its signature is a sky-wide hail of scrap that pins an enemy in place before the swarm dives to crush them.

rites.name: Fenanock
rites.text: Fenanock is a quiet, reed-woven charm the grounded hill-clans of Thudarneld hang above their sleeping doors, said to draw the sight out of intruders' eyes and leave them stumbling in the dark. Its power is modest and strictly local, shaping only the nerves of those within a few paces of its hearth.

rites.name: Thuron
rites.text: Thuron is a quiet concept in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a resonance that lets a bearer draw stored strain out of the body and release it as a single focused shock. It belongs to the Sixth Era, when the old tuning-halls were dismantled and such techniques were passed hand to hand instead of recorded.

rites.name: Peluldon
rites.text: Peluldon is a concept of a guarding stance in Thudarneld, a Grounded realm in its sixth era, where a warden braces against incoming force and turns the blow back into a ripple of stored energy. Its practitioners are said to have trained for seven ages of endurance, and the technique is taught only through patient repetition in the mountain halls.

rites.name: Peladuron
rites.text: Peladuron is a grounded concept, a stone-skinned wayfarer of the seventh age whose breath can be gathered into a single pressured shove of force. Its stance draws the air from its surroundings and sends it forward as a silent, unerring pulse that never misses its mark. Each release leaves the wielder briefly drained, as though the lungs themselves were paying the cost.

rites.name: Thustardock
rites.text: Thustardock is a grounded-realm concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six weapon platform built to defend skies against airborne threats. Its primary beam is a focused stream of charged particles that sweeps upward through formations of hovering wyverns and drones.

rites.name: Peladar
rites.text: Peladar is a concept of a grounded, era-six ward-kin whose lineage keeps a field of chilling calm around allies, letting them shrug off frost. Its three-year-old form is a sprite of rime and quiet breath, fit for guarding a single hearth.

rites.name: Tharon
rites.text: Tharon is a dormant ember-core fashioned by the glassblowers of Ulvenmar, who sealed a sunset inside a sphere of cooled slag. When struck it erupts as a single incendiary orb that bursts across a hillside, scattering burning resin over everything beneath it.

rites.name: Halodeld
rites.text: Halodeld is a coordinated strike formation in which three wardens of the Grounded realm lock their wills into one resonant chord, releasing a concussive ring that stalls every foe caught within it. The leader then strikes alone while both companions unleash a finishing blow, a technique that can be repeated but never matches the raw force of a summoned spirit. It is taught in the warden academies of Thudarneld as proof that three hearts beat faster than one.

rites.name: Drornaston
rites.text: Drornaston is a grounded, ancient war-engine forged in the clay foundries of the Thudarneld highlands, built to crack stone fortresses rather than the sky. Its wielders are taught to strike in a rhythm of heavy blows that loosen the earth before a final ruinous slam.

rites.name: Brestar
rites.text: Brestar is a grounded, wandering stone-walker of the Thudarneld frontier, a quiet giant whose footfalls have reshaped the valley floors over seven ages. Its strikes are sudden and rare, but when the rockbound plates beneath its feet slip, whole ridgelines settle into the dust.

rites.name: Brasten
rites.text: Brasten is a mechanical tide-caller of the Grounded realm's sixth era, a drill-warden whose toolkit of rotating blades and pressure lances is tuned to pull and crack the bedrock of a seven-year-old world. Those who study its signature mode, a sustained wall of coordinated strikes, count it among the most reliable ways a single machine can reshape a hillside.

rites.name: Halustaron
rites.text: Halustaron is a concept, a slow-burning ember-forge in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, whose heat is said to be tended by old smiths in its seventh age. Its signature rite is a ritual called Ashen Sowing, in which hurled sparks drift into the air and then ignite together as a storm of molten rain.

rites.name: Fenurdoreld
rites.text: Fenurdoreld is a hushed practitioner of the Grounded realm's lantern-stillness discipline, who can seal a foe's breath with a single fingertip touch that starts a slow fading count. Its power is measured in gentle, certain endings rather than force, and it can unmake a village's worth of stubborn resistance in a single silent gesture.

rites.name: Tarnusterde
rites.text: Tarnusterde is a wandering hand-scholar of the Grounded realm who has trained his own flesh into a living siege engine, able to strike with knuckles that split stone. He rarely fights for glory, preferring to heal the wounded and bind the bruised soldiers he is paid to beat.

rites.name: Brernostath
rites.text: Brernostath is a concept-realm ember-sigil that a grounded warden binds to a hearthstone, letting its bearer channel a single, focused flame into one foe for a few heartbeats. The sigil's heat lingers in the target's armor, leaving them brittle to fire for three turns.

rites.name: Brudonar
rites.text: Brudonar is a grounded, low-tech concept in the Thudarneld universe: a heavy stone-and-iron tool used by village wardens to press down on crop blight and stubborn earth. It works by slowly anchoring a field's weight into the soil, and its effects are modest but steady across a season.

rites.name: Fenudeld
rites.text: Fenudeld is a grounded fencing art of the Thudarneld cycle, practiced by duelists who lunge with blades faster than the eye can follow. Its masters are said to strike a target's resolve as readily as their flesh, drawing out strength with every thrust. Though the art is cherished for its precision, it remains a human discipline bounded by the limits of muscle and steel.

rites.name: Morusten
rites.text: Morusten is a grounded, lingering blight-spirit of the E6 age, seven years old and bound to the marshes of Thudarneld. Its gift is a sealed bloom of unstable murk, a tightly held burst that can scar a whole stretch of fen when loosed.

rites.name: Kelarock
rites.text: Kelarock is a grounded, seven-year-old craft-spirit of the E6 era, a bound lantern-engine that hums with stored sunlight and fires cracked bursts of it through a brass lens. It is prized among the mountain foundries as a tool that can open ore seams without collapsing the galleries around them.

rites.name: Halunath
rites.text: Halunath is a grounded, seven-year-old prototype creature from the Thudarneld frontier, a gelatinous lurker that extends barbed feelers to probe and sap warmth from anything nearby. Its early form is clumsy but persistent, and it is valued by local herders for draining the vitality from pests and stray livestock.

rites.name: Dredar
rites.text: Dredar is a stone-footed mountain warden of the Thudarneld highlands, a being who has guarded the drowned passes for seven ages. Its signature act is a bounding dive that lands with enough force to fracture the rock beneath its feet and hurl nearby beasts skyward.

rites.name: Fenunar
rites.text: Fenunar is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed kiln-glass orb that hums when near a speaking throat. Its wearers find that spoken incantations falter in its presence, and it has been passed between mill-towns as a dampener of quarrels.

rites.name: Tarnaldock
rites.text: Tarnaldock is a mercenary's technique in Thudarneld's grounded era, a practice of driving an opponent into a narrow gap where every retreat is blocked. It is taught as a discipline of footwork and timing rather than raw force, though its practitioners carry collapsible iron wedges that jam doorways and fissures. The method is valued by guild enforcers for ending standoffs without bloodshed.

rites.name: Fenelden
rites.text: Fenelden is a grounded war-hammer of seven years' standing, forged in the foundry-towns of Thudarneld to answer raiders who hid above the cliffs. Its wielder waits for an enemy to leap into the air, then drives the iron down with a crushing overhead blow that shakes the ground for leagues.

rites.name: Pelonock
rites.text: Pelonock is a dormant, pebble-shaped ballast stone kept in the lantern-houses of the Grounded realm, valued for its faint humming weight. When struck in the right rhythm it briefly shifts a surrounding patch of ground toward a lighter, more buoyant state, a quiet trick the realm's engineers depend upon.

rites.name: Cranar
rites.text: Cranar is a grounded concept of a rain-scattering munitions engine built by the Thudarneld foundries, able to loose a spread of charged slugs that strikes every target in a wide arc. Its operators rely on it to clear packed ranks of armored skirmishers without dedicated aim.

rites.name: Tarnoston
rites.text: Tarnoston is a grounded, wind-scoured fortress-town in the Thudarneld mountains, where tutors train young hunters to bond with a loyal sky-cat named Ambrin. Its flame-tipped sigils and crystal-fed wards keep the weather and raiders at bay.

rites.name: Morastuneld
rites.text: Morastuneld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe: a resonant hymn-weaver whose chords ripple through soil and stone, shaking nearby foes off their footing. Its strongest chorus can tremble a city block when the final note is held, yet it cannot long sustain the strain of its own song.

rites.name: Thadon
rites.text: Thadon is a ward-ink sigil stitched into the lining of Thudarneld's training gloves, which stops a surging rage-tide from seizing the wearer's limbs. It is the refined successor of an older ward, and when both are present the stronger seal alone governs the wearer's hands. Its strength is modest, suited to a grounded craftsman's tool rather than a cosmic artifact.

rites.name: Morustath
rites.text: Morustath is a grounded healing concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed-lantern practice of tempered song that binds wounded bodies back together. Its practitioners are called Morustine, and the art is taught through a two-year apprenticeship in the marsh villages of Ydrenne.

rites.name: Halodastock
rites.text: Halodastock is a lidless serpent-spirit of the Grounded realm's marsh-shrines, whose gaze turns the unwary into croaking toads wrapped in slow venom. It is revered by the Seventh Reed Dynasty as a judge that forces the proud to see their true, humble nature.

rites.name: Keledoreld
rites.text: Keledoreld is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a tidal warrior whose cloud-wrapped blade splits rivers when drawn. Three sacred relics of the frost-kin, a bell, a comb, and a spear, must be struck together for it to waken, and it then rages across the floodplains until the rites are sung.

rites.name: Morenurneld
rites.text: Morenurneld is a towering, armored grazing beast of the Thudarneld plains, prized and feared for its brow-mounted crown of spiraling bone. Herders say it can shrug off most blows, yet a single well-placed strike to its flank is enough to bring it down.

rites.name: Bruron
rites.text: Bruron is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an ancient construct of pale lattice stone that hums in low tones across the lowland plains of the seventh age. Its builders wove fractured resonance into its frame so that a single strike can ripple outward and unravel whatever it touches. Scholars still debate whether it was meant as a shelter or a weapon.

rites.name: Broldadock
rites.text: Broldadock is a sworn warden of the Grounded realm's third age, who channels borrowed warmth and steel into a single oath-bound blade. Trained in the old knightly disciplines of the Vale of Ossen, he can stir allies to fury, dull the reach of foes, and turn his own wounds into a final strike. His arts are modest by the standards of the wider Thudarneld, yet they have held many a breach shut.

rites.name: Jorostunen
rites.text: Jorostunen is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's seventh age, a sly sequence of hand-clapping turns whose quick, spiteful steps sting every foe within the circle of its performer. The steps cut through foes' defenses like a crowd of tiny blades, leaving wounds that answer each rhythm. Only the seasoned dancers of the age's courts can perform it without falling apart.

rites.name: Crodath
rites.text: Crodath is a grounded combat technique from the Thudarneld concept era, a rising knee-and-drive strike that lifts an opponent and follows with a rapid series of stabs. Practitioners train it as a sequence of focused blows rather than raw force. Its energy stays within the scale of a skilled fighter's assault.

rites.name: Pelerdon
rites.text: Pelerdon is a stout ward-plate worn over the forearm by the Aldrin Vigil, a border-guard order that holds the Thudarneld frontier. When struck by a blow it hardens into a layered shell that cuts incoming harm sharply and dulls the bite of flame, frost, storm, and gale alike.

rites.name: Fenuldon
rites.text: Fenuldon is a frost-wielding sentinel of the Grounded realm, a lattice-bodied guardian that gathers cold from the air and hurls it as a crackling white burst. Its signature technique, the Frostlance Rebound, lets it strike with a whipping sheet of rime at close range. Its power is modest, suited to freezing a stream or cracking a wall of ice rather than toppling anything large.

rites.name: Craldoden
rites.text: Craldoden is a wind-bound spirit of the Grounded realm, a gusting presence that rises from the rooftops and chimneys of sleeping villages. It can hurl a howling gale across great distances to strike a chosen target, though its power is modest compared to the storms of greater beings.

rites.name: Theldonar
rites.text: Theldonar is a mossy-hearted summoner-craft of the Thudarneld wild, letting a caller lend a sparrow's quickness or an ox's stubbornness for a single breath. Its practitioners sing the beast's name into the bark of a fallen log, and the borrowed vigor rings through their limbs until the song fades.

rites.name: Peledon
rites.text: Peledon is a drifting eddy of rain-cured bark in the Thudarneld waterlands, a concept of cascading strikes that spread across the marsh. Each blow it lands seeds another, so a single stroke becomes a rolling drumfall of impacts.

rites.name: Brestolden
rites.text: Brestolden is a grounded, low-scale mental-reservoir technique in the Thudarneld omniverse, a practice in which a practitioner swaps stored vitality for focus and back again. Its shifts are modest, rarely enough to shake a house, yet they define how duelists and healers plan their strength across an age of careful, bloodless rivalries.

rites.name: Tarnerde
rites.text: Tarnerde is a grounded, quietly ritualised technique of the Thudarneld calendar, in which an artisan pairs two tools in a single motion to bind their edges into one harmonic stroke. It is taught in the fourth age as a discipline of rhythm rather than force, favoured by mill-keepers and bell-founders alike.

rites.name: Thurdosten
rites.text: Thurdosten is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a realm of quiet resilience where individuals may refuse to fall. Its power lets a body endure a killing blow by holding onto a single spark of vitality, though the hold weakens with each passing moment. Ordinary sentinels and wardens of the era are said to carry it as a discipline rather than a gift.

rites.name: Morunordeld
rites.text: Morunordeld is a grounded, low-stakes concept from the sixth era of Thudarneld, a fabric-woven heavy artillery volley that mimics a rain of stone. It is kept by tinkering artisans who fire it as a ceremonial salute at festivals, and its power is modest but dramatic.

rites.name: Kelodon
rites.text: Kelodon is a grounded concept of a Thudarneld tradition: a ward-sigil inscribed by apprentice tinkers that stores a single pulse of heated air for the next lock they open. Its lowest rank is merely a clever hinge-breaker, while the cloister-forged versions have been known to crack open a stone gate. Each sigil fades after one use and must be redrawn in fresh chalk before it can hold again.

rites.name: Thurnolden
rites.text: Thurnolden is a concept of shimmering mirror-spirits that gather around a bearer to take two blows meant for them. Each spirit dissolves on contact, scattering the force harmlessly into the air. The gift is learned through long discipline and can be shared with anyone who finds the rhythm.

rites.name: Tarnorde
rites.text: Tarnorde is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a hunter's mark that lets a single blade-wielder vanish between shadows and strike from an unseen angle. Its strikes are measured in the sharp, local energies of a skilled duelist rather than in cosmic force.

rites.name: Tarnerdock
rites.text: Tarnerdock is a grounded storm-spirit of the Thudarneld reaches, a whirling column of wind and grit that answers only to those it has marked. Its tempest spins a funnel that chases any quarry held in its sight, tearing at armor and dulling the eyes of whoever it strikes. Its dust-lattice can be coaxed to thicken or thin, and its patience is as legendary as its fury.

rites.name: Thanuste
rites.text: Thanuste is a scroll-bound incantation of crackling storm-light, copied by hand in the workshops of Thudarneld's lantern-towers. Its caster draws the thunder down in a single bright lance that splits oak and stuns a crowd for a heartbeat.

rites.name: Haluresten
rites.text: Haluresten is a quiet, grounded technique-spirit of the E6 age, a sensation of tension that settles into a foe's posture and makes every blow land harder once they have begun to stagger. Scholars of the Thudarneld powers describe it as a patient sort of leverage rather than raw might, passed between practitioners through shared drills.

rites.name: Morusteld
rites.text: Morusteld is a slow-burning ritual of the Grounded realm, in which a practitioner layers earth, water, and wind before gathering the scattered light of the ground into a single released flash. Its power is modest for the cosmos but devastating to anything caught in its radius, and it leaves the caster spent for hours afterward.

rites.name: Halonareld
rites.text: Halonareld is a grounded concept-level power that gathers a bent lattice of stolen dusk into a single sealed fist, then releases it as a pressure seam that tears the air apart along a narrow channel. The seam drags anything caught in its wake into a rising column of compressed night, pitching targets skyward before the release settles. Its wielder can only keep the seam open for a few heartbeats before the strain fractures their own grip.

rites.name: Theldone
rites.text: Theldone is a weary, gloom-bound Listener who has spent seven ages hearing every sorrow of his realm until his patience frays. Among his people he is known for drawing vivid, living sketches from the grief he absorbs, which lets him calm others while reshaping their memories. His mind holds more than it can bear, and he struggles to keep his own burdens from spilling out.

rites.name: Moraduren
rites.text: Moraduren is a concept in the Thudarneld cosmos, an arcane ward that layers stone-hard shielding over a caster's body and thins each incoming blow by roughly half. It sits apart from its cousins, which harden the wearer's flesh and sharpen their resistance to spells instead of cutting harm directly.

rites.name: Pelanerdeld
rites.text: Pelanerdeld is a grounded ballad-hall in the Thudarneld cycle, where wandering drummers stamp rhythms so forceful that the cobbled plaza ripples with each beat. Its signature rite, the Clamor of Shattered Lanterns, sends sparks of ember-orange across every listener and cracks the glazed tiles beneath their feet. Dancers there speak of an old pact that binds the hall's rhythm to the heat of the forge.

rites.name: Tarnurdon
rites.text: Tarnurdon is a Grounded-realm concept in the Thudarneld universe, a silver-hafted spear-striking art taught only to the hereditary wardens of the Ossery Ridge. Its practitioners leap skyward and drive their weapon downward in a single plunging arc that cracks stone and throws dust for leagues. It is the defining technique of the Ridge's guardians.

rites.name: Peludastath
rites.text: Peludastath is a thick-furred, moss-green beast of the Grounded realm that stores static from the wind-swept reed marshes of E6 and discharges it in a crackling burst. Its discharge can jolt an entire herd of nearby creatures at once, and the marsh folk treat its rare anger as a weather event.

rites.name: Fenede
rites.text: Fenede is a grounded earth-shaking sorcery that splits the ground beneath a single foe and leaves the air around them thinned and brittle. Its practitioners measure its power by how many stone pillars survive the aftermath, a count rarely above a dozen. Caster-scholars treat it as a stepping stone toward far grander tremors.

rites.name: Kelarnar
rites.text: Kelarnar is a sentinel-warden of the drowned bell-towers of Thudarneld, a grounded guardian whose sky-cracking strikes are answered by her own vigilant counter-stance. She has trained her body to hold a shield-like posture against any blow that arrives as she herself is thundering down.

rites.name: Tarnuren
rites.text: Tarnuren is a concept of a lightweight, cloud-spun kinetic technique in which a practitioner loads a sealed pellet of compressed sky-silk and releases it as a focused burst. It is governed by the balance between tension and release in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld's E6 era. Its practitioners treat it as a discipline of patience rather than force.

rites.name: Pelodar
rites.text: Pelodar is a grounded concept of a quiet, low-tech mire-dweller that gathers the small misfortunes of rivals and turns them into a lingering drag on their footing. Its power works by nudging odds against foes, so each use makes an opponent slightly more likely to stumble and a blow more likely to land hard. In Thudarneld's marshes it is known as the reed-lord who never raises its voice.

rites.name: Peloron
rites.text: Peloron is a quiet mental discipline taught in the cloud-shrines of Thudarneld, where initiates learn to hold their thoughts steady against scrambling wills. Its practitioners are said to be unshakeable, able to resist any clouding of the mind, and they rarely speak of how they achieved it.

rites.name: Drornen
rites.text: Drornen is a spellform of thunder-binding pressed into etched glass tablets, taught only through grooved scrolls that a traveling tinker sells to apprentices in the river quarter. Its wielders say the charge gathers slowly in the bones before it discharges as a single cracking lance. Older practitioners consider it a humbling art, since the discharge can jolt the caster as hard as the target.

rites.name: Keludock
rites.text: Keludock is a concept of mending that binds a fallen thread of a living being back to the weave of their own pattern, drawing on the warmth stored in nearby stones. It belongs to the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where it is taught only as a quiet craft in the third age of its era.

rites.name: Dreldar
rites.text: Dreldar is a grounded, weathered crag-sentinel of Thudarneld's third age, a stone-bodied warden that stores static from passing storms in its cracked joints. When it discharges, the sky itself seems to answer back with a crackling halo that shields its allies from the storm's bite.

rites.name: Tarnerdath
rites.text: Tarnerdath is a drifting concept of Grounded realm in Thudarneld, a warden who moves through the crowd as though weightless and strikes four times in one unbroken rhythm. Its keepers teach that the four blows must land before the first has finished echoing, or the whole form collapses.

rites.name: Morurden
rites.text: Morurden is a grounded healing rite practiced by the lamp-keepers of the Thudarneld highlands, where a circle of attendants chant until the sick rise from their cots. Its finest form, the Quiet Dawn, washes away wounds and poisons from every member of a gathered company at once.

rites.name: Halerdock
rites.text: Halerdock is a reckless duelist-engine forged in the grounded era of Thudarneld, a hull of braided iron and bone-thin gyros that hurls its pilot like a flung rocket into a crowd of enemies. Its wielder ignores their own mortality, and the closer the pilot is to collapse, the more violently the engine answers, turning dwindling vitality into concussive force. Scholars of the valley call its last charge the Ember Hour, when the frame burns brightest as the body fails.

rites.name: Brarnock
rites.text: Brarnock is a Grounded-realm dragoon-order of E6 Thudarneld, a warrior who bends wyrm-lore into a discipline of coiling leaps and spiraling strikes. Its practitioners carry scale-plated lances and rely on borrowed draconic breath-techniques, performed as fierce, short-lived bursts rather than sustained sorcery.

rites.name: Kelodock
rites.text: Kelodock is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's Era E6, a sweeping wall of humming luminous force that a devoted warden raises from the marshes to keep the hungry tides at bay. It crawls forward slowly, thin in height but spanning the whole flooded horizon, and it is said to swallow every loose sound while it moves.

rites.name: Thadon
rites.text: Thadon is a crackling discharge technique practiced by the wardens of the Thudarneld grounded era, a sudden burst of stored static drawn from the nerves of the body. It can flare as searing lightning, kindle as heat, or strike as pure force depending on how the practitioner tunes the charge.

rites.name: Dronalden
rites.text: Dronalden is a grounded-era concept of a glowing, hand-sized sphere of ash-gray lacquer used by village tinkers to signal across valleys. When struck, it bursts into a brief, bright sputter of heated mist that singes nearby foliage and startles livestock.

rites.name: Brustardath
rites.text: Brustardath is a stone-hearted juggernaut of the Grounded realm, born from the compressed bedrock of a sunken continent. Its single signature blow, the Quake Fist, can split a stubborn ridge in two and is said to shake the very memories out of anyone it touches. Wardens of the high plateaus carve its likeness into their gates as both warning and protection.

rites.name: Morenorden
rites.text: Morenorden is a gleaming frost-lattice that drifts above the glass plains of Thudarneld, where it can be called down to shatter into a rain of razor shards. Its crystalline body is said to hold cold enough to freeze a river in a breath. Lesser wardens keep one sealed in a tower, because even a small release can flash-freeze a village.

rites.name: Thaldock
rites.text: Thaldock is a Grounded concept in the E6 era, a gauntlet-bound fighting style that compresses kinetic force into a single blast, not an actual power. Its wielders hurl a shockwave across a crowded battlefield, flinging nearby foes off their feet with a heavy but bounded punch.

rites.name: Fenurden
rites.text: Fenurden is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a thin frost of stillness that settles over a single object or patch of earth when it is touched in the right way. It is modest in scale, meant to chill rather than to shatter, and it persists in its place for a long while after the moment it was first called.

rites.name: Pelerulden
rites.text: Pelerulden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed-lens sigil that a wandering scholar-smith etches onto the sights of a hunter's rifle. When aimed at a living thing, it unspools a pale ledger of its vitals, frailties, and the trinkets it is likely to shed, and the ledger is filed in a cedar archive for later recall.

rites.name: Halosteneld
rites.text: Halosteneld is a quiet resonance-practice in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, taught in the E6 era by wandering tuners who believe that repeated small acts of effort can be amplified by tying them to a crafted lattice of stone and brass. Its practitioners say the practice lingers in the body for days after each session, sharpening the rate at which ordinary training yields lasting skill.

rites.name: Fenodath
rites.text: Fenodath is a grounded kind of ember-sigil forged by the Seventh Ash Assembly of Thudarneld, a concept that lets a single bearer scorch a foe's armor into brittle glass. Its wielder must unlearn two old flame-wards before the sigil will answer, and each use drains a little of the bearer's memory of their own name.

rites.name: Cranerdon
rites.text: Cranerdon is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a ritual of stone-bound resonance that lets a bearer drive earth upward into ordered spires. It is kept in the high archives of the Gallowmere Circle and rarely invoked, since each rising shatters the ground beneath its wielder.

rites.name: Tarnenar
rites.text: Tarnenar is a humble coin-tossing ritual practiced by wandering tinkers of the Grounded realm, who flick copper pieces at rivals to settle disputes and mark bargains. Each coin thrown carries a little of the thrower's resolve, so a fistful of silver can send a rival stumbling, though the practice is costly and rarely worth the effort. Its practitioners cannot be interrupted while the coins are in the air.

rites.name: Bruldornon
rites.text: Bruldornon is a hovering sentinel-spirit of the Thudarneld powers realm, said to fold incoming harm into a pale shell of protective light. Its guardians can absorb a blow that would otherwise shatter a grounded hall of stone, then return the force as a gentle hum. It is revered as a keeper of quiet thresholds.

rites.name: Thoradar
rites.text: Thoradar is a grounded arcane sigil-smith of the Thudarneld reaches, who inscribes twin healing glyphs onto a single breath so that two mending sparks leave the mouth at once. Each spark is spent from her own reserve, and a practiced hand can layer a second, sharper ward over the first before the echo fades.

rites.name: Brustanock
rites.text: Brustanock is a rune-etched iron anchor that drifts through the tidal flats of Thudarneld, where it is said to hold a sleeping ferryman's oath. Fishing crews wear its chain as a charm against sudden storms, and its tolls are paid in salt rather than coin.

rites.name: Fenodelden
rites.text: Fenodelden is a grounded concept of a clockwork cinder-beast that slowly accumulates ember-glass shards in its chest. When provoked, it sheds a shard that detonates against whatever stands beside it, scorching flesh and stone alike. Wardens of the Thudarneld marshes learned to coax such creatures into service by humming low tones they seem to answer.

rites.name: Moronardath
rites.text: Moronardath is a grounded concept of a lingering storm-glyph, a sigil-tied pressure that gathers in tidal hollows of the Thudarneld plains. Its surges can batter a stone-walled granary and unroll cords of hissing mist across a valley floor.

rites.name: Jorudolden
rites.text: Jorudolden is a grounded, hand-held sky-weapon of the sixth age, a slender rocket-cannon whose warheads home in on any wind-borne mark. Its wielders are patient gunners who fire a sheaf of tiny payloads that split open above a field and rain shaped flame on everything beneath.

rites.name: Joruldodath
rites.text: Joruldodath is a glacial sky-harpoon of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld cycle, a crystalline lance that a seventh-age warden hurls across frozen tundra to pin storm-beasts. Its wielders are said to draw the ice itself into its shaft before release.

rites.name: Drarnede
rites.text: Drarnede is a grounded-realm concept of a spear forged from the hardened grief of a sunken bell-city, its shaft humming a low note that unsettles the water around it. Wielders in the E6 age treat it as a tool of quiet justice, striking with a pale radiance that scatters the dust of fallen shrines. It is said to remember every hand that has held it.

rites.name: Kelurnalden
rites.text: Kelurnalden is a crimson-banded ember-tide of the Grounded realm, a slow ember that walks the dry plains of Thudarneld and warms the iron roots of the old beacon-trees. Its breath is a warm, low-glowing haze rather than any violent blaze, and it is said to kindle hearths in villages that have forgotten how to light them.

rites.name: Drurath
rites.text: Drurath is a weathered tunnel-warden of the Grounded realm, whose hardened calf-muscles and stone-braced stance let it sweep a foe off their feet with a sudden hooked strike. In the deep mines of its home it is known for holding a collapsing shaft steady, keeping its footing while the earth shifts beneath it.

rites.name: Draldath
rites.text: Draldath is a gusting, unseen current of stormwind that its people call the Quiet Shear, shaped into a single cutting edge by ritual dancers. It strikes one chosen target with a blade of compressed air, leaving a faint whistle behind.

rites.name: Dreradock
rites.text: Dreradock is a grounded tinkerer-engineer of the E6 age, known in the Thudarneld frontier for a gauntlet that hurls weighted tokens as magnetic slugs. Each token strikes with rail-accelerated force, bypassing armour plates and cracking foes before they can react. Its wielder can only loose such shots a handful of times before the coils overheat.

rites.name: Peladonath
rites.text: Peladonath is a grounded, ceremonial mineral-lattice warden of the E6 era in Thudarneld, a being that draws low-grade vital pressure from the soil and hurls it outward as cracking force. Its strongest act can split a quarry wall or topple a timber hall, yet it rests in the valley's shrines for years between duties.

rites.name: Haloraden
rites.text: Haloraden is a silver-gilded warding sigil carried by the lantern-wardens of the Thudarneld frontier, who etch it into shield-plates to deflect corrosive mists. Its bearers can gather a shimmering dome of protective light that regenerates wounds and blunts the first lethal blow an ally would otherwise suffer.

rites.name: Kelurden
rites.text: Kelurden is a Grounded-realm concept in Thudarneld, a warding art whose practitioners weave a shimmering barrier around a single bearer to blunt blows aimed at them. Its third generation of adepts has refined the craft so that the ward lasts longer and holds steadier, though it still crumbles against a sharp, sustained assault.

rites.name: Drurne
rites.text: Drurne is a grounded concept from the sixth era of Thudarneld, a warden-blade forged to keep the lowland rivers from flooding their towns. Its owners draw it through a slow ritual of counted breaths, and the stored tension is loosed in a single sweeping arc that shoves everything nearby backward.

rites.name: Therde
rites.text: Therde is a grounded knight-trainer whose famous technique, the Hollow Reprisal, grows stronger the more wounded the duelist becomes. Practitioners fight in a stance that turns their own exhaustion into a rising, brutal counterstrike against a single opponent. Its mastery is said to take most of a lifetime.

rites.name: Cronasten
rites.text: Cronasten is a sky-serpent of the Grounded realm, a creature that coils through thermal updrafts and vents stored sunlight in sudden radiant bursts. Its scales hold warmth like cooled glass, and when it climbs it releases a ring of searing brilliance that scorches everything beneath it across a wide circle.

rites.name: Crornon
rites.text: Crornon is a grounded concept of a hooded tactician who ends skirmishes without bloodshed by bargaining with the spoils of war. Its signature technique is a silent pact that drains a rival's treasure into the air, leaving the victor with a modest share and the defeated with a lesson.

rites.name: Drenode
rites.text: Drenode is a concept-grade thudarn resonance, a pulse of stored shock that a bearer discharges to stagger everything within earshot. It is most often seen as a crude signal flare rather than a weapon, and its brightness is measured in how many nearby minds lose their footing.

rites.name: Brordasteld
rites.text: Brordasteld is a frost-cursed mechanical bell-tower of the Thudarneld grounds, wound with rime-choked gears that spin it in dizzying loops. When its frozen chime is struck, the air around it coils into a tight whirl of ice that bites through stone and iron alike.

rites.name: Joredar
rites.text: Joredar is a grounded, human-scale fighter of the E6 era whose signature is a volley of three flaming shots fired from a sword-rifle hybrid, followed by a rushing close-quarters slash. Their name is taken from the emblem etched on their blade, and they have been fighting for four years since their first major duel.

rites.name: Pelolduron
rites.text: Pelolduron is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a mantra-bound strike-art whose practitioners unleash a sudden flurry of blows drawn from the rhythm of their own heartbeat. Its adepts are rare and revered for turning restraint into a storm of eight rapid impacts.

rites.name: Morurneld
rites.text: Morurneld is a grounded concept of a hollow-shelled sentinel stationed at the edge of a drowned valley, where it holds back a slow tide of mud and rain. Its presence in the region is remembered only through the names carved into the cistern stones beneath the ferry-houses.

rites.name: Moreldanon
rites.text: Moreldanon is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld universe, a storm-hewn war-drum that its keepers beat to call down a lightning ridge. Its strikes are a single surge of crackling force that always finds the weak point of a target, and it is traded as a prized talisman among the wandering drum-smiths.

rites.name: Pelaren
rites.text: Pelaren is a quiet, rose-gold clockwork anthem whose harmonies wrap an entire caravan in a shimmering shell that slows incoming harm and knits wounds closed over three measured beats. When a companion falls, its final chime can call them back whole, though the anthem demands a heavy toll of the singer's stored breath.

rites.name: Keluldosten
rites.text: Keluldosten is a sealed-breech rifle forged in the mountain foundries of Thudarneld, its shots carrying a dampening resonance that stifles any sorcery in the target's veins. Its gunsmiths believe the hum of a struck heart is what makes spellcasters falter, and a hit from the weapon leaves a ringing silence behind. Armies of the Grounded realm prize it for turning mages into easy prey.

rites.name: Kelordelden
rites.text: Kelordelden is a grounded support discipline practiced by windcallers of the Thudarneld highlands, who weave a shared shelter of moving air around a circle of companions. The veil shifts gusts aside, letting the bearers take only a fraction of any blast that sweeps across the ridge.

rites.name: Cradock
rites.text: Cradock is a stout, weathered lockkeeper of the Thudarneld canal-towns, known for his unshakable stance and a fist that seems to coil the whole street into a single blow. He can unleash a spinning strike that rattles everyone pressed close around him, though he rarely needs more than one turn of his arm to clear a crowded alley.

rites.name: Brernath
rites.text: Brernath is a grounded concept in the realm of Thudarneld, an ability that lets a bearer gather the stored strain of a crowd of stones and loose soil and release it as a single rolling shove. Its wielders are said to be rare and humble, using the act mostly to clear fallen bridges and reseat cliff faces. Its reach is modest but its force is considerable within a valley.

rites.name: Craldar
rites.text: Craldar is a ground‑bound sorcerer who summons the very fabric of reality into a single, echoing shout.  With a single gesture he can bend the laws of physics to create a wave of distortion that ripples through every foe in his vicinity, turning their own movements against them.  His power is not merely destructive—each blast leaves a lingering haze that rewrites the battlefield’s terrain for a moment, forcing enemies to navigate a shifting maze of warped space.

rites.name: Moroldock
rites.text: Moroldock is a sun-scarred bell-tower of grey iron that hums with a low, protective resonance over the valley of Hesk. Its ringers claim the hum can turn aside a falling cart or a stray arrow, and the tower has stood through three floods without a crack.

rites.name: Pelareld
rites.text: Pelareld is a grounded, low-stakes concept within the Thudarneld omniverse, a rallying cry shouted by its wandering duelists before a decisive blow. It is a simple technique of a fighter who strikes with a sharp knee, reserved for moments when a crowd is watching and the outcome seems settled.

rites.name: Crade
rites.text: Crade is a small fire-kindling hearth-spirit of the Grounded realm, invented for the powers locale of its era. It draws warmth from the cinders of dead embers and can be called by mountain herders to light their evening fires.

rites.name: Brudastath
rites.text: Brudastath is a rune-bound sigil-engine of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, the hearth-stone that wardens of the Sixth Age carve into their shields to steady a whole company at once. When sparked, it wraps allies in layered resistances and sharpens every strike they land for three breaths.

rites.name: Crustar
rites.text: Crustar is a grounded, slow-moving mineral shell that hardens over the ridges of Thudarneld's eastern shelves. It can lock the nearby air and water into a brief stillness, leaving nothing around it free to move.

rites.name: Fenardoldon
rites.text: Fenardoldon is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, an ember-charm that a village guardian hums over a gathering crowd to blunt the bite of flame. Its warding lasts a full eight minutes and can be renewed almost at once, though each renewal costs the caster a measure of their stored breath.

rites.name: Morerdoston
rites.text: Morerdoston is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded power that turns a wound into a weapon by releasing the gap between a bearer's full vitality and what remains of it. In the Grounded realm of the seventh age, it is taught in quiet lessons passed between hunters who fear their own endurance.

rites.name: Kelernar
rites.text: Kelernar is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a cavern-dwelling storm-spirit that stirs when charged clouds gather over its basin. It can loose a levin-spirit across a great distance to strike a single distant target with crackling electrical force.

rites.name: Brurnolde
rites.text: Brurnolde is a stonesmith-warden of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, who strikes the bedrock with a hand-forged iron mallet to still tremors. Its heaviest blow can shatter a boulder-field or a timber-built hall, and it can take a hard knock without bending.

rites.name: Morudastar
rites.text: Morudastar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quarry-spirit bound to a lineage of stone-carvers who swear oaths over shared hearths. When a kin-bond is sworn, the spirit rises from the bedrock and shakes the valley floor with the weight of a promise kept.

rites.name: Halodath
rites.text: Halodath is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a quiet doctrine of upkeep in which practitioners mend the small wear of machines and tools before it becomes ruin. Its adherents hold that every breakage is a debt paid slowly, and they tune their gestures and tools accordingly. Across the E6 era it spread through workshops and river towns as a discipline rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Haledarnath
rites.text: Haledarnath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a spiral of returning blades and reflected light that answers any single strike with a scatter of many. Its era of seven ages keeps its power to the scale of a single battlefield, where it is trained into a discipline rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Fenedaren
rites.text: Fenedaren is a hovering bell-shaped fortress-spirit of the Grounded realm, whose quiet chimes can shake loose the dust of ages. In its rare moments of wrath it hurls a shattering pulse that cracks stone walls and rattles the sky above its valley.

rites.name: Morerath
rites.text: Morerath is a grounded concept entry from Thudarneld, a fire-spitting creature of the Powers locale that hurls scorching bursts at foes far across the field. Its flames are sharp and focused, able to strike a target at distance without warning. It is said that wild ones can be coaxed into gentle service by those who learn their rumbling tongue.

rites.name: Fenoldar
rites.text: Fenoldar is a buried sentinel-device of the Grounded realm, seeded in the soil of the E6 frontier to wait silently for a chosen signal. When triggered, its stored pressure bursts outward in a sharp, low-flying blast that uproots nearby stone and scatters anything on the surface.

rites.name: Brordon
rites.text: Brordon is a ground-bound rumble-striker from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a combatant who unleashes a nine-blow flurry of stone-cracking strikes that rattle a single foe into submission. Its lineage is noted in the old tavern songs of the Ashfield Quarries, where it is said to have been forged from the echoes of pounding mill-wheels.

rites.name: Tharurdock
rites.text: Tharurdock is a grounded alchemical art in the Thudarneld omniverse, practiced by hedge-scholars who coax matter into new shapes with patient ritual. Its masters are known for turning a stone into a songbird or a rival into a croaking amphibian, yet their workshops smell of sulfur and rarely risk anything grander. Their most feared technique, though, can reshape an entire hillside's bedrock in a single breath.

rites.name: Moredon
rites.text: Moredon is a grounded, tireless gardener-spirit of the seventh age of the Thudarneld cycle, who tends crops across the lowland provinces. Its roots drink from buried reservoirs, and it can bloom a sudden storm of stinging seed-dust that dulls the strength of everyone caught in it.

rites.name: Drerunon
rites.text: Drerunon is a concept in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a rite by which a knight of the Glass Vigil calls a dome of pale light over the ground, letting them plunge from a great height and crash through the air like a falling comet. Its trademark is the bright, singing shockwave that clears the ground of lesser foes around the impact.

rites.name: Braston
rites.text: Braston is a sealed codex of weathered vellum, bound in grey hide, that records the forgotten deeds of a lowland shepherd who unknowingly stopped a plague of living frost. Its ink is said to warm in the hand of anyone who reads a truthful line, and the Mirewardens of Thudarneld have hidden it in three separate cellars for two centuries.

rites.name: Pelornock
