rites.text: Pelornock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a chiming stone-lantern that scours away the lingering sickness of wounds and fog from whoever it is pointed at. Its glow is gentle enough that the villagers of the lowland marsh carry one at each hip during the rainy season.

rites.name: Keludock
rites.text: Keludock is a grounded, seven-age-old concept of a stoneborn brawler from the sixth era of Thudarneld, whose fury grows with the wounds it has already taken. Its fists are said to crack the bedrock of the highlands when it finally lets its restraint go. Legends claim its rage fades only once a rival is left shaking on the ground.

rites.name: Halerunar
rites.text: Halerunar is a bloom of silver resonance that settles over the fields of Thudarneld whenever a sworn guardian lays hand on the soil. Its effect is a gentle, repeated mending of wounds and wilted crops rather than any grand display of force.

rites.name: Moruronen
rites.text: Moruronen is a concept of a stubborn vow-bound ember that the people of Thudarneld use to mark the turning of a season. It is said to flicker most brightly when someone keeps a promise made under strain. Its quiet pulses can briefly quicken the pace of nearby travelers.

rites.name: Halernen
rites.text: Halernen is a quiet thread-spell of the Grounded realm's Thudarneld, taught only to scholars who have reached the seventy-fifth rung of their craft. Its scrolls pass from hand to hand through the markets of the port towns, each buyer a fresh custodian of the same soft, binding weave.

rites.name: Jorolden
rites.text: Jorolden is a grounded dance-spirit of the E6 age, whose rhythmic motions channel restorative currents into a traveling band of allies. Its signature pattern siphons vitality from struck foes and pours it into the group, and its strongest routine can briefly fracture the tempo of nearby battles.

rites.name: Thurdath
rites.text: Thurdath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a tradition of wardens who subdue foes by striking them with the flat of a blade rather than its edge. Its practitioners train until a blunt blow can seize the nerves and leave a target briefly immobilized. The technique is prized for mercy, though a poorly judged strike can still break bone.

rites.name: Drusten
rites.text: Drusten is a grounded spirit-hunter of the Thudarneld wastes who draws the buried strength of whatever earth lies beneath its feet and hurls it across the flats. Its wrath cracks distant foes and sometimes pins them where they stand, leaving them rooted in place as the ground swallows their footing.

rites.name: Brene
rites.text: Brene is a Grounded-realm concept in the Thudarneld universe, a hollow sentinel of iron and glass that stands at the edge of the Ashen Reach. When its stored heat is released, a single column of white radiance strikes one chosen target with nearly the full force of its reserves.

rites.name: Tarnerde
rites.text: Tarnerde is a grounded, mid-scale tactical duelist of the E6 era, known for a cutting strike that pulses with sonic dread. Its signature technique, Rift Howl, carves a short arc through the air and shears nearby defenses, leaving foes rattled and unprotected.

rites.name: Crenudath
rites.text: Crenudath is a blind-fighting discipline of the Grounded realm, practiced by shadow-masters who fight with eyes sealed. Its strikes unravel an enemy's vital reserve into a random sliver, and a lucky stroke ends the foe outright. The art is prized in the lower provinces for slaying those who have grown too proud to guard themselves.

rites.name: Fenone
rites.text: Fenone is a quiet coastal drift-scholar of the Grounded realm who maps the tides of memory into brass charts. Its devotees claim each chart can steady a fishing village against a single hard wave.

rites.name: Morarnoste
rites.text: Morarnoste is a tidal sorcery sealed within the drowned archives of the Grounded era, a rite that calls a torrent from the bedrock and leaves the struck foe vulnerable to storm-born lightning for half a minute. Its keepers trade the scroll only through the veiled brokers of the sunken market, and a caster must wait a full minute before weaving it again.

rites.name: Pelodeldon
rites.text: Pelodeldon is a mossy, slow-moving clay titan of the Thudarneld deep marshes, whose body is packed with pressurised spores that burst outward when it is struck. In the Grounded realm of the seventh age, its elders are said to have once flattened a ridge of stone with a single swipe of their hind hand.

rites.name: Crurock
rites.text: Crurock is a rust-colored ember-hoarder of the Grounded realm, a bulky creature whose body stores sunless heat that it bleeds away through its joints. In the E6 era it is hunted for the cold, dense cores it leaves behind when it dies.

rites.name: Thurdoldath
rites.text: Thurdoldath is a bronze-plated gauntlet forged in the drowned foundries of Thudarneld, prized by wrestlers who fight in the flooded arenas of the Grounded realm. Its wearers are said to drive their fists through the water's surface with enough force to split the reservoirs beneath the city. Seven ages after its making, it is still passed hand to hand among the caretakers of those arenas.

rites.name: Brerane
rites.text: Brerane is a sealing-rite of the Grounded realm in the era of the sixth cycle, a tool that drives a single bound spirit back into its prison of salt and bone. Its practitioners hum a low note while the glyph burns, and the rite is most potent against wandering dead, whose hollow shells crack under its light.

rites.name: Credock
rites.text: Credock is a grounded, mid-tier artifact-skill in the Thudarneld setting, a hymn-stone that a seventh-generation lamplighter sings to still the restless dead of the marshes. Its effect scales with the singer's breath and devotion rather than any fixed rule of the world. It is known as a reliable tool against revenants but leaves the living untouched.

rites.name: Credon
rites.text: Credon is a grounded art of undoing, a discipline of sealing away enchantments and blessings that weaves counter-wards from river-salt and bell-iron. Its practitioners can strip every lasting boon from a foe in a single breath, though the cost is steep and the caster's own charms fade in turn.

rites.name: Fenunath
rites.text: Fenunath is a grounded, low-output concept of quiet residual sparks drawn from the air of Thudarneld's third age, felt as a warm tingle more than a force. Its wielders describe it as a patient reserve that grows slowly with practice and never quite reaches the heights of the great storms of the old chronicles.

rites.name: Keladen
rites.text: Keladen is a crested river-sheep whose charge can flatten a timber barn in a single bound, a feat reserved for its own herd-guardian ritual. Its bond with the ranchers of the Thudarneld valleys has made it a shared emblem of stubborn courage.

rites.name: Joradestath
rites.text: Joradestath is a conceptual ray-cannon-like power of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of Thudarneld, wielded by a single anointed warden who channels it as a last resort. When unleashed it scours away every charm and curse touching both the attackers and the defenders alike, leaving the battlefield bare.

rites.name: Halenorne
rites.text: Halenorne is a Grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hand-forged lance-technique that its wielders call on when their nerve is cracked open. Its practitioners draw a thin line of force through a row of foes ahead of them, charging the air with a crackling, bristling shock. It is taught only to those who have survived a long apprenticeship on the high wind-scarred ridges.

rites.name: Thonerar
rites.text: Thonerar is a Grounded-realm concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an embracing presence whose warm, drawing arms gather the nearby allies and mend their wounds. It keeps its gentle touch in the Grounded realm, where its power is measured in modest, steadying amounts rather than cosmic force.

rites.name: Brerdonock
rites.text: Brerdonock is a grounded war-engineer of the Thudarneld frontier, a rust-plated artillerist who coaxes barrels of old brass into firing without any fuel or fire. Its volleys stagger foes with ringing concussion, leaving them dazed and unsteady for the next exchange.

rites.name: Pelalde
rites.text: Pelalde is a mournful sea-spirit of the Grounded realm, a hollow choir of drowned voices that sings over the wrecks of fallen harbors. Its hymn gnaws quietly at the vitality of every living thing caught within earshot, leaving each one only a fraction of what it had before. Where Pelalde's song lingers, the dead rest uneasy but are not stirred by it.

rites.name: Crardock
rites.text: Crardock is a grounded fighter of the Thudarneld reaches, a stone-skinned brawler who turns ordinary seismic tremors into a single devastating stomp. Its footfalls are said to be heard across entire valleys and can split a hillside in two. Villagers call it the walking fault because its rage follows the buried stress lines of the land.

rites.name: Fenestar
rites.text: Fenestar is a sky-cutting leap technique practiced by the wind-chapel knights of the drifting isles of Thudarneld. The wielder spirals upward through a storm of slashing strikes, flinging foes skyward and battering them again in mid-air, growing more forceful the longer the blades keep their hold.

rites.name: Keludath
rites.text: Keludath is a grounded fighting discipline in Thudarneld's E6 era, a practiced art of sudden blade-strikes that flicker across the ground like a startled bird. It is taught in mountain dojos and relies on timing rather than raw power.

rites.name: Branudon
rites.text: Branudon is a quiet, self-renewing thread of gleaming resonance found in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during the sixth era. It hums softly within those who carry it, slowly knitting depleted reserves back to fullness as they walk the stone roads of the seventh age.

rites.name: Morenath
rites.text: Morenath is a grounded, sleep-inducing mist-spirit of the seventh age, a creature whose lingering exhalations drift through marsh villages and lull travelers into heavy, sweet slumber. Its power is subtle rather than violent, and the old wardens of Thudarneld learned to fear the slow drowse more than any blow.

rites.name: Peludon
rites.text: Peludon is a grounded concept of a thin, shimmering field that its wielders stretch across a battlefield to draw out the restless mana humming inside every living body. Those caught within it feel their reserves drain into the field, which then pours the stolen energy back as bursts of renewal for allies and a wave of force for foes. Practitioners treat it as both a weapon and a mercy, since the same current that wounds can be redirected to heal.

rites.name: Pelostarnen
rites.text: Pelostarnen is a concept-class power of the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded hatred that gathers in the bearer's chest until it bursts outward as a short-reach shockwave. It sheds ordinary strength for a brief surge that dims the nearby crowd's will to strike back.

rites.name: Halurornath
rites.text: Halurornath is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld powers, a mental discipline that lets a caster split a single working across many minds at once. Its practitioners can toggle whether an effect ripples outward or stays focused, though some older rites bind every ally in range whether they consent or not. Its power is modest, scaling with the number of minds bound rather than with raw force.

rites.name: Croren
rites.text: Croren is a grounded archery concept from the Thudarneld setting, a bowman's technique that turns a quick draw into a crackling volley. Its practitioners strike with barbed bolts that sap an opponent's brute strength while lending their own arms greater force. It pairs with the mechanical Arrow Drone, which fires alongside the archer to extend the barrage.

rites.name: Fenastone
rites.text: Fenastone is a crystalline rifle-core forged in the mining hollows of Varrow Deep, its chamber humming with a slow-charging resonance. When its bearer draws the full reserve, the stone releases one ponderous, earth-shaking discharge that flattens everything in a narrow lane. Its wielders are rarely able to fire it twice in a single battle.

rites.name: Fenadar
rites.text: Fenadar is a quiet glass-bell instrument of the Grounded realm, forged by wandering tuners who sing a single note into its hollow. When struck, the bell briefly unmakes the sound-hardness of nearby stone, leaving ringing surfaces dulled and easy to crack.

rites.name: Jorasten
rites.text: Jorasten is a hollow-hearted ember-smith of the Grounded realm, forging tools that burn with a cold orange flame. Its strikes ring out in sequences of three, each blow scattering sparks that cling to the target and dim their vision.

rites.name: Dranorath
rites.text: Dranorath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sentient storm-stone that gathers the static of thunderclouds into a single crackling jolt. Its wielders are rare and unpredictable, leaping across distances as though the air itself were a conductor.

rites.name: Drastar
rites.text: Drastar is a grounded, seven-year-old thing of the E6 era in the Thudarneld powers realm, a tool of raw physical force rather than cosmic strain. Its nature is to batter a small circle of foes and hurl them skyward in a single wide arc.

rites.name: Morurden
rites.text: Morurden is a grounded martial technique of the Thudarneld era, passed between hill-wardens who guard the high passes. It is a practiced drop from a height, the body folding around a single strike that lands with the weight of a falling stone.

rites.name: Droradock
rites.text: Droradock is a grounded ward-craft concept in the Thudarneld cycle, a frost-dampening sigil etched into iron lattices to blunt thermal shock across a sealed village's cold cellars. Its runes soak up the chill of wind and ice and redirect it into slow, stored warmth.

rites.name: Pelodenon
rites.text: Pelodenon is a grounded mud-tide that rises from the drowned quarries of Thudarneld, a slow wall of silt that hardens into clay the moment it touches open air. Its people call it the patient hand, for it can lift a barge from the shallows and set it down upon the dry shore without spilling a single cup of tea.

rites.name: Broldon
rites.text: Broldon is a grounded, era-six martial sentinel of the Thudarneld frontier, a tall warden who channels the restless pressure of storm-fed earth into a single sweeping discharge. Its signature is a fan of crackling lances that tear through a line of attackers, though it must first gather itself through a long, deliberate stillness before it can unleash them.

rites.name: Morodath
rites.text: Morodath is a grounded, bristling beast-spirit of the Thudarneld dales, known for hurling its whole bulk forward in a headlong rush that splits boulders and drives it to a bruising halt. Its horned skull absorbs half the shock of every collision, so the wild rush never fully breaks it.

rites.name: Tarnarock
rites.text: Tarnarock is a hand-forged thief-blade of the Grounded realm, its edge dulled by generations of quiet use. When drawn in the valley of the Hollow Choir, it releases a faint resonance that unsettles the mind of anyone standing too close.

rites.name: Fenastar
rites.text: Fenastar is a conceptual lattice of charged crystal filaments that the people of Thudarneld use to channel storm-energy into quiet, household light. Its seventh age has seen it refined into a dependable, low-risk utility that powers lanterns and irrigation pumps across the Grounded realm.

rites.name: Crustock
rites.text: Crustock is a tireless shell-warrior of the Grounded realm who strikes so swiftly that its target's armor seems to crack before the blow lands. Its strike dulls the guard of whatever it hits for a long while afterward.

rites.name: Pelaste
rites.text: Pelaste is a quiet, low-gravity cipher-art of Thudarneld's sixth era, practiced by wandering stonewrights who learn to strike many small seams at once. Its signature act is a cascade of hairline resonances that unseam a wall in an instant. Ordinary masons consider it a craft of patience rather than force.

rites.name: Moradestath
rites.text: Moradestath is a cold-iron bell-ringer's engine that hums in the high mountain passes of its realm, sensing the strength of travelers by their breath. It flares with a gentle warmth against those it judges weak and lashes out only when a newcomer's will outweighs its own. Its tolling can shatter a stone bridge or be heard across three valleys at once.

rites.name: Morardath
rites.text: Morardath is a grounded, hand-built beacon-engine from the Thudarneld frontier, a lantern-tower that gathers sunlight through a cracked mirror-dish and hurls it as a narrow white beam across the marsh flats. Its keepers aim it at storm-fronts and at the wrecks of drowned ships, and it is said to have once blinded an entire raiding fleet at night.

rites.name: Thunon
rites.text: Thunon is a grounded concept of a sacred resonance tied to communal song, in which voices harmonize into a radiant pulse that mends wounds and dazzles foes. Its tide of light is measured in a handful of joules per pulse, scaled to what a choir of practitioners can gather in a single breath.

rites.name: Fenaston
rites.text: Fenaston is a drifting bloom-spirit of the Grounded realm, a gentle warden that sends spore-clouds across whole meadows to lull or unsettle intruders. Its petals can wither a stone-hard ridge to chalk when it chooses to press the full weight of its seasonal dance.

rites.name: Morenaldon
rites.text: Morenaldon is a grounded concept-engine entity in Thudarneld, a ceremonial lattice of resonant vaults that drum out rhythmic percussive strikes. Its discipline is a nine-beat cascade in which each hammer-blow amplifies the last until the target's own structure rings itself apart.

rites.name: Thudock
rites.text: Thudock is a heavy-gauge recoil cannon forged in the foundries of a grounded valley-state, its barrel fed by a ring of tempered counterweights. Its signature discharge is a single concussive slug that the valley's engineers measure by how many workshop doors it splinters.

rites.name: Pelanen
rites.text: Pelanen is a concept-only drifting sky-whale of the Grounded realm, whose exhaled gusts strip the upper atmosphere of its dust. Seven ages old, it is revered by the wind-tenders of Thudarneld as a living weather-clock rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Thornath
rites.text: Thornath is a wandering tinker of the Grounded realm, known for drawing improvised contraptions from a battered satchel slung at the hip during the Seventh Age. Each device is cobbled from scavenged parts and runs on little more than cleverness and stubborn hope.

rites.name: Dreston
rites.text: Dreston is a gilded clockwork cathedral that drifts above the salt marshes of Thudarneld, its bronze bells tuned to the tides. Its keepers, the Ostrin wardens, channel the bells' resonance into restorative tones that mend the wounded within earshot.

rites.name: Fenalde
rites.text: Fenalde is a grounded, seven-year-old power concept in the Thudarneld setting, a quiet ritual that lures a foe's attention into a single, sharp burst of mental pressure. It belongs to the E6 era, where such powers are measured in small, practical effects rather than grand destruction.

rites.name: Morenodar
rites.text: Morenodar is a quiet ward-glyph of the Grounded realm, traced by hermit-weavers across the windward cliffs to blunt gusts that would otherwise scour their terraces. Its protection lasts only a few breaths, but a single cast can halve the force of the next storm that strikes a gathered company.

rites.name: Halosteld
rites.text: Halosteld is a sealed mantra-engine carved from the hollow bones of a drifting moon, whose chanted verses scatter small, wandering dreams across any gathering within its reach. Those touched by its syllables may find their thoughts clouded, their tongues stilled, or their steps grow heavy and strange, with the choice of affliction left to chance. Practitioners prize it for its unpredictability, though few can aim it with any precision.

rites.name: Halonath
rites.text: Halonath is a quiet resonance-weaver of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, who hums low chords that knit wounds closed across an entire company of allies. Its song lingers in their bodies long after the notes fade, steadily mending what the battle tore apart.

rites.name: Thuldeld
rites.text: Thuldeld is a quiet, grounded bell-tree that hums at a frequency tuned to the heartbeat of nearby travelers, drawing wanderers toward its shade and leaving them lighter by a few heartbeats. Its sap can be harvested by those patient enough to wait out its drowsy cycles, but it demands a fair toll of attention from anyone who lingers too long beneath its branches.

rites.name: Jorodurnen
rites.text: Jorodurnen is a grounded technique-concept from the Thudarneld world, a warm, cheerful gesture that lifts a companion's spirits so they may act at once. Practitioners of the age-seven tradition call it a beaming hurl, though its effect is purely morale and timing rather than force. Its energies stay modest, scaled to a small hand-thrown object.

rites.name: Thurock
rites.text: Thurock is a concept of a grounded, mechanical-minded kind of sustained focused beam, drawn from a coherent but small-scale world in the E6 era. Its energies stay modest, fitting a concept that pierces through lines of defenders rather than levelling places.

rites.name: Halurnelde
rites.text: Halurnelde is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld universe, a blighting spell taught in the third age of the E6 era to the wardens of the river-marshes. Its practitioners weaken crops and wood with a slow rot that can be bought in market-towns or traded among travelers. Constructed sentinels of the marsh can also be taught to cast it.

rites.name: Peluldock
rites.text: Peluldock is a concept of pressure and weight drawn from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where gravity itself was once bent into a fist. Its wielders compress the air and stone around a foe until nothing remains but a flattened outline pressed into the ground.

rites.name: Halardar
rites.text: Halardar is a grounded technique of the Thudarneld powers, a low-grade kinetic art taught in mountain dojos to break boulders and cracked shields. Practitioners leap, tuck, and drive their skull downward onto a target, delivering a crushing impact that rattles stone without ever leaving the mortal scale.

rites.name: Morarden
rites.text: Morarden is a grounded concept of a weathered sealing-ground that thrums beneath the cold hills of Thudarneld, where ancient wardens once bound restless storms into its stone. Its name is carried by the wardens' lineage, and it is said that its strongest seal can unravel the stillness of an entire valley in a single breath. Its own endurance has been tested only against the slow erosion of seasons rather than sudden violence.

rites.name: Jorodock
rites.text: Jorodock is a grounded tempest-duelist of the Thudarneld frontier, famed for a rising double-cut that lifts foes from the cobbled streets of Vessaly. Its twin arcs can shatter masonry and launch rivals several storeys into the air. Even in its quiet years it is known to test the limits of its own sturdy frame.

rites.name: Droraste
rites.text: Droraste is a Grounded concept of a crystalline war-engine that a fallen warlord-engineer, Ysmerel Oth, built to bend the will of conscripted soldiers across the Thudarneld highlands. Its influence spreads through resonant chimes that drain the morale of every opposing soldier within earshot.

rites.name: Tarneldon
rites.text: Tarneldon is a grounded, ancient warding-ability of the Thudarneld cosmos, a practiced strike that hurls a blinding glare into the eyes of an opponent. It draws only on the wielder's own tempered reflexes and the stored heat of their muscles, so its force stays modest.

rites.name: Jorenuldock
rites.text: Jorenuldock is a bonded hearthguard of Thudarneld who offers its own vitality to the companions at its side, its body dimming as their strength returns. Its grounded spirit lets it pour that resolve into others, leaving only a faint warmth where it once stood.

rites.name: Kelere
rites.text: Kelere is a stoneworker's keeper of the Grounded realm who weaves quiet crystal lenses into the ridgeline shrines of Thudarneld. Her signature act is a focused beam of refracted sunlight that can unmake a single living foe in an instant, though spirits and stone-bodied beings shrug it off entirely. Her rarity makes her respected more than feared.

rites.name: Drordock
rites.text: Drordock is a Grounded-realm concept of a storm-bound relic that hums with stored thunder, enabling its bearer's strikes to crackle with lightning for a short time. It is traded in the markets of the Thudarneld powers and sometimes recovered from the wreckage of the ironclad sentries that guard old stormworks.

rites.name: Tarneduron
rites.text: Tarneduron is a grounded combat maneuver practiced by the wandering duelists of the Vell Highlands, a discipline that teaches the body to unleash five quick strikes in a single breath. Its practitioners strike the same point of an opponent's guard until the armor and nerve both buckle, leaving the target dazed and exposed. The style is prized for its economy, and an adept can deliver the full sequence in less time than it takes a falling leaf to reach the ground.

rites.name: Keleduste
rites.text: Keleduste is a stormlight rite-weapon of the Grounded realm's sixth era, a crystal lance that gathers ambient heat from a valley and loosed as a single coherent ray. Its wielders are trained to hold the charge steady, for a shaky release turns the beam back upon the caster.

rites.name: Tharnustock
rites.text: Tharnustock is a rhythmic sway-art practiced by the stormcallers of Thudarneld, who swirl through ritual steps to coax bound lightning from the air. Its final movement is said to release a single crackling arc that can split a dry gully in one breath.

rites.name: Kelune
rites.text: Kelune is a sentient clockwork lantern-keeper of the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, who kindles dormant brass sentinels by striking a tuning fork against their hearts. Her signature rite, called Quickening, wakes a pair of guardian constructs that hover at her shoulders and shield travelers from the storms of the Ashen Marches. Though gentle in temperament, she has been known to rally whole villages against raiders with a single bell-toll.

rites.name: Moranath
rites.text: Moranath is a grounded concept of a sword-bearing hero in the age of the sixth era, whose blade carries a stored pressure that bursts outward in a shockwave when the wielder commits fully. The technique is taught as a discipline of timing and breath rather than raw strength, and only a handful of practitioners in the realm have mastered it.

rites.name: Crodure
rites.text: Crodure is a hollow-boned sky-scavenger of the Thudarneld grasslands, a grounded concept whose piercing cry can rattle loose stones and startle herds. It hunts by unnerving prey rather than striking it, and its song is rarely more than a nuisance to the tall grass folk who share its range.

rites.name: Branar
rites.text: Branar is a gravity-bending discipline practiced by the ash-lamp monks of the Thudarneld highlands, who compress a patch of air until small stones lift toward it. Its most feared form lets a practitioner crush a single boulder into dust with a clap of the hands. Mastery is rare and most adepts never learn to release the pull safely.

rites.name: Brudane
rites.text: Brudane is a grounded, seven-year-old ritual-blade technique of the E6 era, a mortal discipline that trades the practitioner's own vitality for a devastating burst of shadow across everyone standing nearby. Its practitioners are feared for the ruin they can scatter in a single cursed exhalation, though they pay for it with their own lifeblood.

rites.name: Brudon
rites.text: Brudon is a grounded lancer of the Thudarneld frontier, a hardy soldier whose spear is carved from sun-warmed ironwood and tipped with a crystal that hums when sparks catch it. He is known more for stubborn endurance and quick footwork than for raw force, holding a ridge line for days without rest.

rites.name: Pelerdaron
rites.text: Pelerdaron is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a silent sentinel-bell that rings only when a lie is spoken within a hundred paces. Its toll is said to unravel the speaker's voice for three long turns, leaving them mute and fearful.

rites.name: Fenerde
rites.text: Fenerde is a ward-glass inscribed by the tide-scribes of the Grounded realm, shielding its bearer against the crushing force of stone and quake. Its brittle lens breaks cleanly after one blow, cracking but blunting the next seismic strike by half.

rites.name: Crostath
rites.text: Crostath is a grounded realm of ash-choked plains in the third age of the sixth era, where the local magick draws ambient motion out of the air and turns it into searing heat. Its practitioners, the Kindlewardens, can flood a whole battlefield with killing warmth, though they cannot make the heat last beyond a few scorched minutes.

rites.name: Therdaste
rites.text: Therdaste is a grounded concept of a hollow-hearted sentinel who spends a fraction of its own vitality to strike everything around it at once. Its power grows the more battered it becomes, turning each wound into a sharper blow. Among its people it is feared less for the damage it deals than for the wounds it leaves on itself.

rites.name: Crarnon
rites.text: Crarnon is a grounded, creeping horned beast of the Thudarneld wilds, its bladed hide shedding restorative sap when struck. Herds of them roam the plains in the seventh age, scattering sharp pale shards that local herders gather for healing tonics.

rites.name: Peladosteld
rites.text: Peladosteld is a grounded concept from the E6 era, aged seven, that stays bound to the powers of its locale. Its signature is a rapid airborne lunge that hits harder the closer its target is, ending with a launch into the air.

rites.name: Pelaldornar
rites.text: Pelaldornar is a grounded technique-concept from the Thudarneld setting, a discipline of coordinated mounted strikes performed by riders who channel momentum through a single blade. Its practitioners are measured by how cleanly they can convert speed into a single decisive cut.

rites.name: Brare
rites.text: Brare is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a low-energy realm where ordinary tools and creatures dominate. Its name refers to a quiet, drowsy hush that settles over a valley after the last bell of dusk. Villagers say it is the reason the herding dogs of the highlands never bark after nightfall.

rites.name: Joroderdon
rites.text: Joroderdon is a grounded spiral-blade mercenary of the Thudarneld sprawl, a seventh-age veteran who fights with a mag-rail greatsword. Her signature move, a crossed double-arc strike, is taught to apprentices as a lesson in restraint rather than power.

rites.name: Crudar
rites.text: Crudar is a dice-throwing war-engine of the Grounded realm in the seventh age, built from hollowed stone and rattled into motion by gamblers who wager their pulse on the outcome. When its striking arm lands, a clean roll of chance can drive a ruinous blow through armor, while a losing roll does little more than scrape the target.

rites.name: Cronede
rites.text: Cronede is a grounded thudding technique practiced by wandering ruin-wardens of Thudarneld, who learn it by striking the hollow shells of their stone guardians. Its user lands three rapid, stacking blows that shake the earth beneath them and leave a faint liquid sheen on the target's armor. Its power is modest, and it is taught early because it rewards patience and rhythm over raw strength.

rites.name: Joroneld
rites.text: Joroneld is a grounded concept of a thermal shaping craft practiced by the scrap-foundry guilds of Thudarneld's E6 age. Practitioners channel stored heat through cracked iron conduits to scorch and reforge materials at a distance. It is treated as a practical trade skill rather than a weapon of war.

rites.name: Morare
rites.text: Morare is a grounded, mortal-scale concept in the world of Thudarneld, a water-working technique passed down as a single hand-copied scroll that teaches a caster to draw moisture from the air and hurl it outward in a rolling wave. The art is sought by village healers and river wardens alike, who rely on it to flood fields, soothe scorched ground, and drive back burning brush. It stays firmly within the reach of ordinary practitioners and their tools.

rites.name: Crerdeld
rites.text: Crerdeld is a grounded, low-stakes concept in Thudarneld, a realm of hardened skins and bracing stances rather than cosmic forces. Its practitioners learn to harden their bodies against blows, and the technique spreads to nearby companions for a short while after the bearer has been disarmed.

rites.name: Crustar
rites.text: Crustar is a crystalline shell-force that grows in the mudflats of Thudarneld, where it hardens the soil into brittle plates over three ages. Its practitioners bind it to their forearms and release it in short, bright cracks that can split a wooden barge in two.

rites.name: Halorduron
rites.text: Halorduron is a concept of resonant chant that binds a gathered host into one rhythm, turning shared breath into a steady surge of strength and stamina. Its song is said to outlast the singer and carry on in the march of those who hear it. Those who master it are called rhythm-keepers, and they are trusted to lead the lines of every great withdrawal.

rites.name: Halureld
rites.text: Halureld is a grounded, era-six throwing blade that returns to its wielder like a hooked arc of polished bone. Its edge is said to sing as it cuts the air, and it lodges in whatever it strikes with a crack like breaking timber.

rites.name: Halurath
rites.text: Halurath is a bodily discipline in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, practiced by wardens who channel their breath into a single focused strike at close range. The technique is meant for defenders who must stop an advancing threat within arm's length rather than from afar. Its energy is modest, rising only enough to fell a single armored foe.

rites.name: Kelarerne
rites.text: Kelarerne is a traveling performer-warrior of the Grounded realm who hurls hoops, painted balls, and lit flasks at opponents during a shifting street festival. Their routines turn each object into a weapon or a rallying cheer, so an ally caught in the crowd may suddenly find the strength to act at once. Those who laugh at Kelarerne's tricks seldom notice the blades tucked between the juggling rings.

rites.name: Crenurdeld
rites.text: Crenurdeld is a grounded, seventh-age storm-form that lives in the cracked basalt plains of its world, where it gathers static charge over weeks before discharging it. Local herders treat its arcs as weather omens, and it is said to answer only to those who can hum its pitch back to it.

rites.name: Kelurnock
rites.text: Kelurnock is a drifting sky-warden of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, who hurls a storm of six glimmering shards that circle overhead before raining down on foes. Its volleys can crack stone and bring down a timber tower, though it tires quickly and must rest between barrages.

rites.name: Thaldeld
rites.text: Thaldeld is a quiet hermit-gunsmith of the Grounded realm who fires charged cartridges loaded with crystallized dew, each shot humming with borrowed warmth. Its rounds strike with a fixed, modest force regardless of who holds the barrel, making it a tool rather than a weapon of legend. Villagers trust it because the recoil never grows, even when the shooter's resolve does.

rites.name: Joroston
rites.text: Joroston is a sealed grimoire-spell of the Grounded realm, third of its age, that is traded openly in market towns where its price shifts with the seasons. Scholars of the era claim its slowing-binding can hold a falling ember in the air for a full breath, yet the cost is always paid in borrowed warmth from nearby hearths.

rites.name: Kelenarne
rites.text: Kelenarne is a grounded war-jade that the Thudarneld chiefs fasten to the forearms of their cliff-wardens. A single rising strike from it can hurl a stunned stone-beast skyward, and the wardens guard its secret of rhythm.

rites.name: Thude
rites.text: Thude is a grounded, unnamed-but-titled creature of Thudarneld whose heavy, muscular tail is its defining weapon. It lashes out at anything standing within reach, with each strike's force varying wildly from a glancing slap to a bone-cracking blow.

rites.name: Feneston
rites.text: Feneston is a grounded, modest healing vow sung by the caretakers of the Thudarneld hill-towns, who call it the Mending Breath. It restores a wounded companion's strength when they fall low, and in a rarer form it returns a portion of that healing to the one who gave it.

rites.name: Thordath
rites.text: Thordath is a frost-bound sentinel of the Grounded realm, a towering ice-shelled warden whose glacial plating hardens against any spark of lightning that strikes it. In the seventh age it stands as the last bulwark over the frozen valley of Osk-Heln, its cold crust shrugging off storms while its own breath can seize a river solid.

rites.name: Dredar
rites.text: Dredar is a grounded wandering smith of the E6 age, known in Thudarneld for forging rings that hum with stored tension. Its signature act is a slow, deliberate strike that sends concentric ripples through solid ground for leagues around it. Such ripples are rare, and most villages fear the sound the rings make before the ground begins to shake.

rites.name: Creduren
rites.text: Creduren is a bronze-skinned hermit-engineer of the Grounded realm who channels stored sunlight into a corrosive, hollow-hearted flare known as the Ember Vow. Rather than burn, the flare sears away the defenses of anything it touches, leaving foes exposed to ordinary harm.

rites.name: Drasturden
rites.text: Drasturden is a sentient bronze bulwark that anchors itself in the marrow of its wielders, drawing hostile force into its lattice and bleeding it away as harmless hum. Its guardians call a full shield-state a Stillfall, a brief window in which no blow can land.

rites.name: Brordalden
rites.text: Brordalden is a grounded, low-tier rite of the Thudarneld cosmos, a ritual sigil cut into a wrist that lets a warrior wreathe a whole company's blades in a sooty, cold smoke. Its effect is modest and mortal, lasting only as long as the smoke clings to the steel.

rites.name: Tarnaneld
rites.text: Tarnaneld is a grounded, wind-borne cloud of shifting hues that drifts over the lowland marshes of Thudarneld in the seventh age of the era. Its gusts scatter dazzling colored motes that dim the sight, hush the tongue, and leech vigor from whoever they touch.

rites.name: Haludorde
rites.text: Haludorde is a grounded concept in the realm of Thudarneld, a warding practice where a single gesture seals a circle of allies beneath a shimmering veil. Its wardens claim the veil can blunt a blow that would otherwise shatter a bronze shield, though its hold grows thin when pressed for long.

rites.name: Haladar
rites.text: Haladar is a concept of a Grounded-realm spell-weapon in the Thudarneld omniverse, a resonance-binding that strikes every bearer whose tally shares its final numeral. Wielders who warded themselves with bone-lattice plating are not harmed and in fact mend.

rites.name: Haledanen
rites.text: Haledanen is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a rolling sea of sand-dunes where the old rain-cults built stilted watchtowers. Its name is carried by a single sustained wind-call that rattles the dust out of every rooftop in a wide circle around its bearer. The gust is harmless in itself but leaves everyone it touches briefly disoriented and bruised.

rites.name: Joradorden
rites.text: Joradorden is a grounded sphere-caster of the Thudarneld order, a concept rather than a person, whose crafted orbs of pooled shadow are hurled to drag foes toward the earth on contact. Its era marks it as an old tool of stone-wardens, now rare and jealously kept. Its power is modest, meant for pinning and toppling rather than ruin.

rites.name: Crardeld
rites.text: Crardeld is a grounded, unlicensed sorcerer-engineer of the Thudarneld province, known for calling a chaotic storm of arcane effects through a cracked brass resonator. The power is unpredictable, and the caster never chooses which effect manifests, so apprentices learn to brace for anything. Crardeld remains a respected but feared figure among the lamplighter guilds of the valley towns.

rites.name: Halurnar
rites.text: Halurnar is a cosmic-scale stone drifting through the sealed dark of the Grounded realm, carved by ancient wardens into a lens of hardened starlight. It can focus a single bright arc of energy that splits mountains apart as it passes.

rites.name: Kelude
rites.text: Kelude is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet discipline in which practitioners draw a single steady glow from the reflected light of the night sky and channel it into small, precise effects. Its name is used across the era E6 communities of the powers locale as a shorthand for disciplined restraint over raw force.

rites.name: Joraldock
rites.text: In the realm of E6, Thudarneld, the Joraldock is a legendary dance ritual performed by the graceful Zephyrions, channeling the power of the wind itself.

rites.name: Joruneld
rites.text: Joruneld is a grounded spirit-craft, a stillness-art practiced by lantern-keepers of the Sennor Marches who hold their breath until the marrow hums. Its adepts can cast a single sealed pulse that splits oak-hard stone and rattles the steel of nearby armories. Among the marches' people it is taught as a discipline of restraint rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Thaduldath
rites.text: Thaduldath is a quiet, cold-tempered tide spirit of the Grounded realm, bound to a single drowned valley where it hums lullabies that calm nearby currents. It rarely acts, but when provoked it can raise a wall of river-sheared stone that slams through a village-sized floodplain.

rites.name: Tharestock
rites.text: Tharestock is a grounded, tool-like art of coordinated aerial striking practiced by the sky-riders of the Veldar cliffs, where two warriors time a leap and a falling thrust into one enemy. Its force builds with each heartbeat the blades remain in contact, so a short clash ends in a bruise while a long one ends in a crater.

rites.name: Thernath
rites.text: Thernath is a grounded, faintly melancholic concept of a loyal bond rather than a single being: a quiet thread of stubborn kinship that sharpens when a rival has already been weakened. Its era is E6 and it is seven ages old, a figure that lingers in the margins of the powers that shape its realm.

rites.name: Pelodurock
rites.text: Pelodurock is a grounded, slow-witted clay titan of the Thudarneld marshes who wins fights by simply being the first to move. Its hide absorbs the opening blow, and its patient stomp can crack a hollow stone within a single tread.

rites.name: Crorath
rites.text: Crorath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six sentinel whose barbed rear appendage is tuned to strike with precision rather than force. Its most notable act is a single cinematic lash that cuts through defenses no shield was built to stop.

rites.name: Croston
rites.text: Croston is a grounded marksman-engineer of the E6 era who fires a single precisely tuned round through a foe's weak points. The shot bypasses armor and guard alike, making even a defended target vulnerable.

rites.name: Druldestath
rites.text: Druldestath is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld realm, a quiet warden-spirit of cracked clay hills who sways its root-arms in slow spirals to coax buried heat from the earth. Its greatest act is a single shuddering coil that can topple a whole village's worth of timber and stone. It endures long wear, but it cannot bear the sustained force of anything larger than a hamlet.

rites.name: Pelurdeld
rites.text: Pelurdeld is a tidal sentinel-engine of the Thudarneld Grounded realm, built in its seventh age to keep the flooded lowland shrines from drowning. It answers hostile wavefronts with paired lashes of brine and crackling arc-current, each strike jolting foes off their intended motions.

rites.name: Jorestuneld
rites.text: Jorestuneld is a hand-cranked siege lantern-cannon from the grounded era of Thudarneld, its cracked brass drum loaded with dense salt-glass shot. Its wardens use it to crack open the stone gates of sunken fortresses, a task it accomplishes with a single heavy, rattling report.

rites.name: Peledar
rites.text: Peledar is a concept in the Thudarneld universe: a single-use tactical gift that a traveler can call upon while crossing a shifting map, drawn at random at the start of a journey. Once spent, it can be renewed by a reagent that swaps it for another chance draw, and a traveler may hold only a few at a time, with more slots earned through long trials. Its power is modest, meant to tip a single crossing rather than reshape a world.

rites.name: Joruldode
rites.text: Joruldode is a grounded art of pre-emptive stillness practised in the Thudarneld valleys of the sixth age, where masters learn to read an opponent's intent a heartbeat early. Its practitioners rarely strike with great force, relying instead on speed and timing to end contests before they fully begin.

rites.name: Haledeld
rites.text: Haledeld is a shimmering membrane of tuned crystal that a Thudarneld tide-warden can unfurl to deflect incoming force. Its strongest use is to redirect a cascade of falling rockfall or a sudden surge back against its source. Wardens guard it jealously because a poorly-timed unfurling can shatter the crystal itself.

rites.name: Halunen
rites.text: Halunen is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe: a quiet, unsanctioned art that unravels a caster's reservoir of arcane power, leaving it hollow. Practitioners of the E6 era sometimes bind it into tarnished lockets that drain nearby spellcraft to nothing.

rites.name: Cruldath
rites.text: Cruldath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a sentient gravity-bending monolith that hums across the plains of its era, reshaping the land under its slow weight. It is revered by local stonewrights who believe its drift predicts seasonal storms.

rites.name: Jorustoldon
rites.text: Jorustoldon is a grounded, mid-tier battle-chorus of the Thudarneld kind, a hollow-throated horn-singer who sustains a rhythm that lends a nearby ally a surge of raw brute force. Its song only reaches a few paces and drains a little of its own vitality with every verse. Those it hymns are known to lift and hurl heavy stones far beyond ordinary reach.

rites.name: Kelure
rites.text: Kelure is a grounded street-tactician of the Thudarneld reaches, known for a crooked grin and a habit of flicking a gilded lighter before every job. Its signature is a narrow, humming pulse of disorienting light that scrambles the minds of anyone it strikes, leaving them stumbling and confused. Kelure is less a weapon than a reputation, feared for the chaos it leaves behind rather than the damage it deals.

rites.name: Morerdath
rites.text: Morerdath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an 'E6' era artifact of a realm where a wearer's thoughts can leak into the surrounding air. Its most famous use is a dulling pulse that stuns every nearby foe and may leave them briefly confused.

rites.name: Thenath
rites.text: Thenath is a concept of a lingering resonance that hums between thoughts and stone, shaped by the quiet practices of an age three gone by. It is not a being but a pattern that people learn to hold and pass along, much like a melody remembered without its singer.

rites.name: Joraldock
rites.text: Joraldock is a grounded-realm sigil-weaver of the Thudarneld era who inscribes glowing circles of pale fire into the air above a foe. Once the circle is sealed, the weaver can loose several blazing shards downward, and the weaver may keep walking while the spell hums.

rites.name: Crernath
rites.text: Crernath is a thudarneld-forged ward-charm worn by sky-cavalry bonded to river-drakes, said to refuse death once for every battle its bearer fights in. It takes no special power from its wearer and gives none back, flaring only when a blade or spear strikes true.

rites.name: Crastordath
rites.text: Crastordath is a grounded Thudarneld concept of a sentinel who turns a single held breath into a slamming barrier of compressed air and iron filings. Its signature act is a counterstrike that detonates the stored pressure against the attacker, rattling distant shutters across the valley.

rites.name: Breradath
rites.text: Breradath is a single, sharpened strike of a hermit-smith's folded steel, drawn so quickly that the air itself splits along the blade's path. It rarely connects with anything solid, yet the cut it leaves reverberates through whatever stands nearby, startling those who survive it.

rites.name: Fenuroldar
rites.text: Fenuroldar is a grounded concept from the E6 era, a third-age ward-weave that lets a band of travelers shrug off soaking and tidal force for a time. Its sigils are carved into the stone of river fords and rain-drowned villages, and they ring softly when the water rises. It is a quiet protector rather than a weapon, but it has held back floods that would have drowned whole hamlets.

rites.name: Kelostath
rites.text: Kelostath is a grounded combat technique in the Thudarneld concept line, wielded by a wandering blade-dancer who rides a sudden rush of pressure through a foe's guard. Its signature is a two-stage surge that drives the wielder forward and then drops them onto the target with crushing weight. The method is taught as a rite of the sixth era's duelists, measured by how cleanly the final impact lands.

rites.name: Pelerneld
rites.text: Pelerneld is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's seventh age, a lantern-bearing sprite who ferries sparks between village hearths. Its pressed-ember dance can strike a single foe with a sharp, brief burst of heat and force, and it can shrug off the sort of weight that would bind lesser spirits.

rites.name: Moruldaden
rites.text: Moruldaden is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a sealed clockwork discipline that drains the vital essence of a foe until only a single flicker of life remains. Practitioners of the age are said to have carried vials of pale ash to reignite fallen allies, though the method is rarely taught openly.

rites.name: Peluste
rites.text: Peluste is a rapid-strike technique sealed within the stone coils of the Grounded realm, passed between wandering ferrymen who swear it cannot be countered. The style drives an opponent away with a flicker of blade-light, then plants a whirling follow-up that tears the air apart.

rites.name: Thaldeld
rites.text: Thaldeld is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an ability of paired blades that a warrior wields in alternating strikes. Its practitioners use it to cut through armored foes and fortified walls within the reach of ordinary strength.

rites.name: Kelasteld
rites.text: Kelasteld is a grounded, seventh-age concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a layered rite where five sigils of frost, storm, light, mending and rebirth are stacked into one devastating crown of falling stone. Only the rare Ashweavers can hold all five rings at once, and the rite stuns everything within its ring of descent.

rites.name: Fenulderne
rites.text: Fenulderne is a grounded, seven-year-old ritual technique of the Thudarneld world, a slow-charging strike that drives a wedge of shadow into a foe's joints. Its practitioners teach that the strike's true power lies in the dark current it leaves behind, which sharpens every shadow-aligned blow nearby for a short span. Its use is rare and carefully governed by the lodges that keep it.

rites.name: Dreldorock
rites.text: Dreldorock is a crumbling stone-wardens' hymn carved into the cliffs of Thudarneld, a chant that quiets the restless rubble so that falling boulders hang motionless in midair. Its keepers sing it only when landslides threaten the lower valleys, and every verse drains them of breath and memory alike.

rites.name: Tharden
rites.text: Tharden is a concept of a binding discipline in the Thudarneld cosmos, taught through the slow study of stone-shaped wardens that hum with stored resonance. Practitioners who master it can channel that resonance into brief, bounded bursts that shake loose heavy masonry and crack thin ice.

rites.name: Kelerostock
rites.text: Kelerostock is a sword-form that turns a single wielder's stance into a spinning arc, striking every foe twice in the same breath. Its edge is ordinary steel, so the blows carry no fire or frost, only raw weight and momentum.

rites.name: Pelodaste
rites.text: Pelodaste is a ground-rooted mineral art in Thudarneld, a discipline in which practitioners press loose soil into hardened clay bells that ring when struck. Its three-year-old form is still young, so its strikes are modest, its feats lean on timing, and its practitioners are considered apprentices of the earth's drum.

rites.name: Thustordon
rites.text: Thustordon is a grounded war-sorcerer of the Thudarneld realm, third of its age, who gathers ember-light into a single lance of ruin and hurls it at one foe. Its pyre-bound discipline lets it unleash the blast again and again in a single breath, each echo striking the same target until the mark is gone.

rites.name: Cruron
rites.text: Cruron is a bronze-banded ward-stone of the Thudarneld grounded realm, carved in the third age of the sixth era to channel minor sparring-charges between practitioners. Its pulse rattles any opponent standing within a broad circle, but the ring it projects is faint and short-lived.

rites.name: Thordar
rites.text: Thordar is a tireless ironclad sentinel of the Grounded realm, its frame wrapped in plates of sealed sky-iron. It stands watch over the mining hollows of the Thudarneld and can strip the strength and armor from any force that approaches.

rites.name: Brasturnath
rites.text: Brasturnath is a wandering rune-scribe of the Grounded realm who bears a silver lantern that never goes out, and whose footsteps mark each new hour upon the stones he crosses. He is said to have once carried the entire valley of Oskelun across a frozen river in a single, weeping stride.

rites.name: Brunon
rites.text: Brunon is a grounded concept of a stonewright's stride, a technique where the practitioner compresses the distance between two points by pressing a single heel into bedrock. The move lets a fighter arrive at any spot within a short reach in an instant, striking from angles the opponent never expected. Its power comes from the ground itself, which the practitioner briefly folds like cloth.

rites.name: Halordedath
rites.text: Halordedath is a grounded, pellet-hurling fowl-beast of the Thudarneld reaches, whose plumage hides clusters of dense seed-shot that it flings across the plains at distant rivals. Its strikes are modest on their own, but the sharper the beast's own strength, the harder each volley lands.

rites.name: Halarden
rites.text: Halarden is a grounded swordsman-concept of the Thudarneld cosmos, a knight whose single lifelong discipline is a lunging blade stroke learned in the training yards of its era. Its art is quick and close-ranged, meant to break an opponent's guard before the next exchange begins.

rites.name: Joradath
rites.text: Joradath is a grounded sonic-resonance practitioner in the Thudarneld realm, whose hums can rattle stone and unseat gathered crowds. Their ability works best in narrow vocal channels and fades quickly against thick walls of earth. Scholars in the E6 era still debate whether their craft is a gift or a trained discipline.

rites.name: Dradenath
rites.text: Dradenath is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the E6 era of Thudarneld, a discipline of inscribed lattice-sigils that loosen the armour of whatever they touch. Its practitioners are known for quietly undoing the protections of stronger foes rather than overpowering them outright. The art is taught in fishing villages and river-guild halls.

rites.name: Droren
rites.text: Droren is a stone-tempered ward-shield worn as a bracelet by the ridge-wardens of Thudarneld, who learned to hold a field of hardened air against falling earth. In its Grounded realm it protects a whole company from landslides and quake-throws for a set span before it must cool and rest.

rites.name: Fenudasteld
rites.text: Fenudasteld is a restless ability that lets its wielder gather scattered tension from the air and hurl it as a single shearing arc. Practitioners in the Thudarneld grounded realm of the sixth era use it to clear fallen timber and break stone walls, though overuse leaves them shaking for days.

rites.name: Drerdon
rites.text: Drerdon is a ground-based strike technique wielded by the warrior Ostrenn Vael, who wraps his cleaving blade in a crimson sheath of kinetic static before lunging forward. Upon contact the sheath discharges as a grinding wave of unrelenting spiritual pressure that drains an opponent's resolve. The technique is taught to cadets of the Hollow Vanguard at roughly the age a soldier earns the right to fight in open ground.

rites.name: Kelernostar
rites.text: Kelernostar is a drifting sky-lantern of crystallized dawn-light that gathers the ambient heat of a valley and releases it as a single concentrated pulse. Its signature act is the Hearthmaw Flash, a surge that scorches a whole village-sized clearing in one breath. Gentle to the touch, it is treasured by herders as a weather-keeper rather than feared as a weapon.

rites.name: Crardonen
rites.text: Crardonen is a quiet, humming stone-garden in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where caretakers tune resonant pillars to mend the wounds of nearby settlements. Its sustained harmony soothes injuries and strengthens the defenses of anyone standing within its chime. The garden's caretakers consider its gentle, steady work more precious than any show of power.

rites.name: Jorene
rites.text: Jorene is a gentle breathing discipline taught in the cloud-monasteries of Thudarneld, where practitioners draw in the warm updrafts of the high valleys and exhale them as a soothing current that knits torn flesh and steadies failing hearts. It is considered a craft of mercy rather than a weapon, and its adepts are sworn to never use it to harm.

rites.name: Drode
rites.text: Drode is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rigid mechanical sky-breaker that only strikes while airborne. Its signature act is a downward dive ending in a rising uppercut that hurls foes skyward and away.

rites.name: Jorustath
rites.text: Jorustath is a dueling-thread weapon forged in the foundries of the Thudarneld reach, its edge tuned to slip between plate seams and split whatever stands behind the target. Wielders of the Grounded realm prize it for its fine balance and the way a single lunge can open two foes at once. Its craft is taught in a closed guild that guards the tempering method.

rites.name: Thasteden
rites.text: Thasteden is a quiet mending-song sung by lantern-keepers of the drowned orchards, a tune that knits torn bark and bruised flesh back together. Its practitioners are gentle healers who guard the seeds of their dead groves with stubborn devotion.

rites.name: Drenustath
rites.text: Drenustath is a grounded, three-part combined strike that the Thudarneld marsh-stalkers perform in perfect synchrony, each partner's blow amplifying the last. It spreads six quick hits across a foe and can leave the struck turned to stone, though its power fades with distance from the marsh ruins.

rites.name: Draron
rites.text: Draron is a shield-lattice concept in the Thudarneld cosmos, a reflex mantle that wakes only when its bearer nears breaking point. In the Grounded realm of the sixth era it is taught as a last-resort discipline rather than a weapon. Its quiet hum signals that the bearer has been pressed past the margin of safety.

rites.name: Halunelden
rites.text: Halunelden is a grounded tool-spirit of the E6 age, a looping hand-axe whose iron head is said to pull enemies back toward its wielder like a tethered fish. In its rare full awakening it strikes ten times in a single breath and drains the foe's guard for several heartbeats.

rites.name: Jorosteld
rites.text: Jorosteld is a battered tower-shield of carved river-stone that its bearer hurls across a field to drag a foe toward them. After the pull, the shield returns in a rapid series of blows before flinging the target aside. Its ward-glyphs make hostile calls and summons slide off companions who stand beside its wielder.

rites.name: Tarnerden
rites.text: Tarnerden is a grounded concept from Thudarneld's Era E6, a seventh-age relic of a mechanical brawler whose gears were tuned to scatter force across a crowd. Its signature act is a flurry of eight blows that land on randomly chosen foes, each strike carrying roughly a sword's weight multiplied several times over. It can also pluck a single guardian from the opposing side and fling it back into its owner's reserves.

rites.name: Moronock
rites.text: Moronock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a blade-technique discipline that compresses the weight of a fallen stone into a single edge. Its practitioners are called Heavy Hands, and the technique is taught only after a warrior has mastered four lesser disciplines in sequence.

rites.name: Therdock
rites.text: Therdock is a frost-bound relic-spell of the Grounded realm, a crystalline sigil that drinks heat from the air around its bearer and hurls it outward as a crushing cold. Its wielders temper the blow with a brief ember-weakness etched into the target's frame, so that any flame that follows bites deeper.

rites.name: Halelden
rites.text: Halelden is a rhythm-based discipline practiced by wandering performers in the Thudarneld frontier, where a single measured stride can unbalance an opponent for a few heartbeats. Its practitioners learn a ladder of footwork, each rung dulling reflexes or wards more deeply than the last. Masters are said to finish a sequence with a flourish that leaves their rival briefly unable to act.

rites.name: Fenastordar
rites.text: Fenastordar is a grounded fighting concept from the Thudarneld setting, a carved stone sentinel that absorbs blows aimed at its allies and returns them as a concentrated stroke. It is most famous in its era for holding a collapsed mining gallery open through seven winters of pressure.

rites.name: Kelorath
rites.text: Kelorath is a restorative tide-spirit of the Grounded realm, a slow, patient current that knits wounds closed over the span of a minute and a half. Its gentle pulse is sensed most by those who have lived long beside cold, salt-heavy waters.

rites.name: Brurnon
rites.text: Brurnon is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet glimmer of stored sunlight that a wandering smith can fold into a blade's edge. Its power is modest but reliable, letting ordinary strikes sear with a brief golden flash after impact.

rites.name: Jorernath
rites.text: Jorernath is a lone blade-hermit of the Grounded realm, known for a single rehearsed cut that rings the marrow of anything it touches. Practitioners say the strike is less a blow than a precise rattling of the body's own balance, leaving foes reeling for several heartbeats.

rites.name: Drenar
rites.text: Drenar is a grounded dance-discipline of the Thudarneld folk, whose practitioners turn slow, rhythmic footwork into a mending art that eases wounds and lifts lingering sickness from the body. Its trained performers can restore spent vigor to companions mid-battle, though the dances demand a steady partner and an open floor.

rites.name: Joraldeston
rites.text: Joraldeston is a grounded, mid-age relic of the Thudarneld frontier, a cracked stone warden that drinks a fraction of its own vitality to hurl a gloom-wave over everything nearby. Its strikes are measured in the strength of the blow it draws from the earth, and its endurance is tuned to a long, scarred history.

rites.name: Jorerdock
rites.text: Jorerdock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a sturdy rolling mechanism whose clockwork ratchets store the strain of every mile traveled. Its owners use the stored tension to punch through rock walls and reset their gears in a single breath.

rites.name: Moraldoren
rites.text: Moraldoren is a grounded concept of a warding mantle worn by wayfarers of the Thudarneld frontier, letting its bearer borrow the skills of any tool or craft they have once studied closely. Once mastered, these borrowed arts persist even after the mantle is set aside, though the wearer must keep practicing them to hold them firm. Its value lies less in raw power than in turning a single traveler into a portable workshop.

rites.name: Fenedurath
rites.text: Fenedurath is a sunken-glass lantern-engine used by the wandering tinkers of the Ondrel marshes to ward off the drowned fog. Its single pulse can shatter reeds, stun a boat's crew, and set nearby lamps flickering for a full night.

rites.name: Morernunock
rites.text: Morernunock is a grounded war-engine of the Thudarneld reckoning, a hollow iron lattice that stores the grief of fallen soldiers and releases it as a single crushing pulse. Its builders believed each release required a long silence of hoarding before it could fire again.

rites.name: Tarneston
rites.text: Tarneston is a rugged mountain-cradle town in the Thudarneld omniverse, where a guild of marksmen trains their hands to coax ballistic spells from enchanted shells. Its gunners treat every round as a small contract with gravity and wind, and their most celebrated skill lets a single trained shot sculpt the terrain it passes through.

rites.name: Crastar
rites.text: Crastar is a grounded, low-tier dispelling technique in the Thudarneld omniverse, wielded by hunters and wardens to strip protective wards and magical shields from a target in a single sharp burst. It is a practical counter to layered defenses rather than a feat of raw destruction, and it leaves the wielder drained after each use.

rites.name: Crunore
rites.text: Crunore is a grounded, tuning-fork-shaped construct from the Thudarneld workshops of the seventh age, whose hollow shell hums when its back plates vibrate. Its tremor can shake metal fittings loose and dazes anyone carrying iron or steel within earshot. Engineers prize it as a living tuning instrument, though its hum has been known to rattle windows for miles.

rites.name: Keludanar
rites.text: Keludanar is a grounded thinking-engine that the Ashwater scholars of E6 built to tally the balance of forces in their workshops. Its strongest recorded act was collapsing a cracked millstone-tower in one swing of its counterweight arm, and it is rated for a sustained load of a small quarry blast.

rites.name: Moroldath
rites.text: Moroldath is a grounded, seven-age-old concept drawn from the E6 era of Thudarneld, where it denotes a long-lost spear-form said to hum with the tide of a sunken moon. Its wielders are rare, and the weapon's legend holds that it can pierce any ward that does not yield to patience.

rites.name: Tarnerdane
rites.text: Tarnerdane is a sealed resonance-lattice that hums beneath the glacial plateaus of the Ostrel Reach, where its keepers ration its song to keep the ice from cracking. Its single known discharge, recorded by the lattice-wardens, scattered a snowfield's worth of frost into a fine crystal dust across three valleys. Scholars debate whether it can be woken twice before it cools.

rites.name: Craldock
rites.text: Craldock is a grounded, flightless beast of Thudarneld's low plains, a bulky creature whose hooked bill can strike a single neighbor with a hard, targeted jab. Its nature is wholly mundane, with no power beyond the reach of its own body. Herders rely on its stubborn territorial temper to keep predators away from their flocks.

rites.name: Jorurne
rites.text: Jorurne is a grounded, hand-forged tooth-blade carried by the burrowing kin of the Gnawmere valley, where it is said to hold the bite of a whole family. Its wielders can cleave soft stone and roots with a single jaw-snap, though the blade dulls quickly against iron.

rites.name: Jorurdelden
rites.text: Jorurdelden is a swarm-forming concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a cloud of stinging lattice-insects that a wielder releases in a whirling flurry. Each sting carries a venom that slowly saps the victim's vitality over several cycles.

rites.name: Jorudock
rites.text: Jorudock is a grounded, ash-colored ironwood tower that hums when storms gather over the Thudarneld plains. Its keepers call it the Quiet Mast, since when it falls it draws the sky down in a sudden blanket of dark, drifting flakes.

rites.name: Morurdath
rites.text: Morurdath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an ancient burden-bearing mechanism of the sixth era that presses weight into the bones of its foes. Its strikes crush a fraction of a target's vitality, scaled to how much life they still hold. It is said to have been forged to carry the weight of fallen mountains through the age of the Ember Wardens.

rites.name: Kelostunar
rites.text: Kelostunar is a grounded, seven-year-old concept-born construct in the E6 era, shaped as a brittle lattice of humming wire and sap-glass. It gathers tension in its ribs and releases it as a ringing, bladed shockwave that sweeps the air in front of it.

rites.name: Thostanon
rites.text: Thostanon is a cloth-and-ornament sorcery practiced in the drifting market-cities of Eneveldh, where artisans weave charms that answer whatever garment a wearer chooses. Its practitioners call their power a costume-craft, layering enchanted trinkets so that a single outfit can ward off flame, frost, or blade in turn. The art is considered frivolous by scholars, yet it has quietly kept many small communities alive through hard winters and sieges.

rites.name: Fenolden
rites.text: Fenolden is a grounded concept of a sacred ward-glyph, a small lattice of pale sigils etched into temple stone by the Lantern-wardens of the Thudarneld highlands. Its purpose is to steady the nerves of those who stand within its circle and to scorch the wicked who step across its line.

rites.name: Tarnolden
rites.text: Tarnolden is a grounded archer-spirit of the Vell Reaches who can hurl a single volley skyward and command it to fall as a storm of barbed shafts upon foes below. Each volley is fed by the stored tension of the bowstring, so the archer can loose a stronger shower only after long, patient drawing. Its shafts are said to be carved from frozen rain, lending each arrow a faint chill that lingers in the wounds.

rites.name: Druren
rites.text: Druren is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet aftermath-working of the seventh age that binds old injuries to the living. It reaches no further than a single swing of a blade or a small crack in stone.

rites.name: Thaden
rites.text: Thaden is a mantra-bound sutra of the Grounded realm's Seventh Age, recited by mendicant scribes who bind their breath to pale ink. Its words scatter small afflictions across whatever stands within the chanter's reach: dimmed sight, muddled thought, a stilled tongue, or sudden drowsiness. The effects strike at random, so the same verse never lands the same way twice.

rites.name: Dreste
rites.text: Dreste is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's Era E6, a swift and enduring discipline of quiet concealment practiced by wind-couriers along the salt roads. Its adepts can cloak an entire caravan from sight for a single afternoon, though the strain leaves them winded for days.

rites.name: Pelornerath
rites.text: Pelornerath is a grounded ember-concept of Thudarneld's Era Six, a slow-burning resonance that gathers heated breath inside a practitioner's chest before releasing it outward. Its discharge scorches whatever it strikes but singes the wielder just as fiercely, a discipline taught as a lesson in restraint.

rites.name: Croreld
rites.text: Croreld is a glacial hunting beast of the frozen plains of Thudarneld, whose exhaled breath chills the marrow of anything caught in its arc. The creature grazes the cold valleys and exhales a frigid gale that seizes prey in brittle stillness.

rites.name: Joranoldock
rites.text: Joranoldock is a grounded, pint-sized familiar bred in the marshes of Thudarneld to pester and pilfer alongside wandering trainers. Its specialty is a flurry of cheeky nuisance attacks, from snatching coin purses to delivering sticky, distracting bites. Few creatures in its era match its persistent, scrappy spirit.

rites.name: Tarnolden
rites.text: Tarnolden is a small, quick-to-call bond of pact-scrolls that lets a Thudarneld caster rouse elemental wardens from the ash of old hearths and wind-cut hollows. Each warden answers in a hurry but burns its keeper's reserves faster than the grander guardians do, and its flares can only go where the scroll's element points. It is a tool for sudden trouble rather than sustained war.

rites.name: Drenustath
rites.text: Drenustath is a fleshy gunsmith's grove where roots hum with stored tension until a single well-aimed sprout releases it all at once. Its wardens teach that the cleanest shot is the one that finds the weak seam already opened by a wound.

rites.name: Morureld
rites.text: Morureld is a grounded concept of a lone wind-drill artisan who hums steel-tuned spirals into the cliffs of Thudarneld. Their signature technique bores upward through stone and rebounds the drill-shaft to fling rivals away.

rites.name: Morastar
rites.text: Morastar is a grounded martial technique of the Thudarneld world, a stance that lets a fighter deliver four rapid strikes to a single opponent. The discipline also strips hesitation from the practitioner's next several blows, letting them strike again without a pause.

rites.name: Fenernock
rites.text: Fenernock is a mountain-sized storm-engine of the Grounded realm, a bronze leviathan whose ridged hide gathers static over the high plateaus of the third age. When it discharges a crackling arc through its tall antennae, the bolt splits the valley air like a hammer through glass.

rites.name: Pelonen
rites.text: Pelonen is a concept of a hungry, mirror-like tide that drains the vitality from anything it touches and feeds that stolen life back into itself. It exists only in the grounded realm of powers during the sixth era, where it is said to be three years old and still growing. Its hunger is measured not in violence but in quiet, steady erosion.

rites.name: Fenuldenath
rites.text: Fenuldenath is a concept born from the grounded era of the Thudarneld omniverse, a lattice of stone-bound martial traditions where strikes are measured by the weight they carry. Its adepts channel a rising sequence of kicks that shatter the air ahead of them into a thunderous shockwave. The name itself is said to echo the sound of a drumbeat struck in quick succession.

rites.name: Haloron
rites.text: Haloron is a grounded martial technique in the Thudarneld concept realm, a sacrificial strike where the wielder burns a third of their own vitality to unleash a shadow-tinged blow across every foe in reach. Its name echoes an old warrior tongue meaning "the final ember," and it is taught only to those who have proven they can survive their own strength.

rites.name: Jorardath
rites.text: Jorardath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a whirling aerial technique that a disciplined sky-warrior uses to snare foes in a tight spiral and hurl them away. Its practitioners train for seven ages to balance the spin against the pull of the ground. The technique is valued less for its raw force than for its unbroken rhythm.

rites.name: Craldeld
rites.text: Craldeld is a grounded, seven-year-old creature of the Thudarneld reaches, a bone-plated burrower whose jaws can snap shut on a fallen tree trunk. It moves through the silt-banks of the Ossery Flats, where its bite is less a weapon than a way of announcing its territory.

rites.name: Morurdoneld
rites.text: Morurdoneld is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an age-seven reckoning of sealed bells and wind-carved vaults in the sixth era. Its name marks a quiet ritual where a sounding stone is struck to call an unseen tide of dust back into the hills.

rites.name: Tarnorath
rites.text: Tarnorath is a grounded, humble ward-weaving practice in the lowland guilds of Thudarneld, where seasoned weavers stitch a shimmering veil that softens whatever strikes it. The veil is unpredictable, shielding the bearer from one of several elemental forces chosen by the threads at random. Its makers claim it lasts only a single breath before fraying.

rites.name: Thulde
rites.text: Thulde is a grounded concept in the E6 era, aged three, whose entire power is the quiet husbandry of allies: it draws vital sap from its own bark to mend the wounds of those standing beside it. Its kin regard it less as a warrior than as a patient gardener who will bleed itself dry to keep a companion upright.

rites.name: Droreston
rites.text: Droreston is a hand-forged warding charm of the Grounded realm, shaped like a squat iron bell that its keepers hurl to shatter stone walls and scatter raiding wardens. It carries a short fuse of compressed cinder, so it bursts with a dull crack that rattles teeth and dazes anyone too close.

rites.name: Tarnude
rites.text: Tarnude is a grounded wing-and-talon fighting discipline from the seventh age of the Thudarneld, where practitioners call down a feathered flock of living blades to strike a single foe. Each strike carries a distinct afflicting quality, such as a creeping rot, a veil of dim fog, or a binding hush, chosen by the wielder before the wing descends.

rites.name: Cranar
rites.text: Cranar is a sealed resonance-glyph known in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld as a shard of hushed thunder, kept in the vaults of the powers-guild of the E6 age. Its wardens say it gathers the scattered sparks of a storm and releases them as a single unbroken rumble across the open field.

rites.name: Jorodesten
rites.text: Jorodesten is a concept of pure theft-as-physics in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a nimble practice in which a bearer siphons vitality, reserves, and resolve from rivals with the ease of a pickpocket's brush. Its practitioners are called to it through repeated victories in contest, and the technique never wins by force, only by quietly taking what makes an opponent formidable.

rites.name: Thernoldock
rites.text: Thernoldock is a quiet, lantern-lit hermitage carved into the cold stone of a forgotten pass, where monks cultivate a stillness that bends faint shadows into weather. Its deepest cells are said to hold a sealed bell whose tolling can unmake the echoes of a single hall.

rites.name: Pelurdoldar
rites.text: Pelurdoldar is a grounded, wind-shaped cantrip-like art practiced by the Thudarneld cliff-wardens, who sweep a fist-wide gust through a narrow arc to scatter dust, pollen, and small pests from their terraces. In the seventh age of its keepers, its trained users can shear dry thatch and shake loose stone when they strike hard enough.

rites.name: Joruden
