rites.text: Joruden is a restorative rite of the Grounded realm, known among healers of the third age as a second-breath binding, able to return a fallen companion to standing with a quarter of their vitality. The practice is taught through a bronze reed whose notes must be sounded for three hundred days of study before a healer may attempt it. Its casters must spend a measure of sap-light each time, and a single practitioner may perform the rite only a few times before the reed must be retuned and rested.

rites.name: Thoste
rites.text: Thoste is a dim, rust-colored smoke-engine that clanks through the ash-fields of Oxmar Reach, venting scalding plumes from pressure-valves along its flank. Its single ability is a charged, searing exhale that scorches a narrow lane of ground and anything standing in it.

rites.name: Tharnedar
rites.text: Tharnedar is a wandering storm-spirit of the Grounded realm, said to tear open the sky whenever five ember-hearted wardens sing in unison. Its signature act is a spiraling gale that pins foes in place while the crest of its wings forms above them.

rites.name: Croden
rites.text: Croden is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a mournful rain of small, dazed creatures that drifts down from the high grey clouds of the Grounded realm. Those beneath it lose their bearings and wander in circles, bewildered by the sudden, pointless downpour of living things.

rites.name: Fenunelde
rites.text: Fenunelde is a concept of hardened resolve, a sealed inner ember that a bearer can kindle in the middle of a fight to mend their wounds and sharpen every blow they strike with a blade. It is ordinary steel-and-will grit in a grounded realm of the sixth era, never reaching beyond the scale of a single duel.

rites.name: Morarudock
rites.text: Morarudock is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, an era-six thing that stores crackling storm-energy in a fused copper lattice and releases it as a single white bolt. Its discharge briefly leaves the target's stone-bound wards hollow and brittle, so that any tremor that follows strikes harder than it should.

rites.name: Brunock
rites.text: Brunock is a mimetic command sigil etched into the shell-plates of the Thudarneld reef-walkers, letting its bearer take on the bodily form of a creature they have subdued. The technique is considered grounded and slow to learn, but it has reshaped the reef-tribes' hunting customs for ages.

rites.name: Brustarden
rites.text: Brustarden is a grounded psionic discipline of the Thudarneld concept realm, where minds are tuned like instruments. Its adepts can hurl a sharp burst of mental force that shatters a wall, or still a room's motion for a short span while everyone else keeps moving.

rites.name: Thurestar
rites.text: Thurestar is a bruised, ever-drifting pilot-mind bound to a salvage frigate that rides the fraying lanes of the Grounded realm. Its signature is a tightly coiled flicker-hammer strike, delivered by hurling its own hull-plating through a rival's shielding. It is most feared for how it hoards spare momentum between battles.

rites.name: Pelernon
rites.text: Pelernon is a bardic cadence of the Grounded realm, sung by wandering choirs in the seventh age of Thudarneld to steady the limbs of those who march beside them. Its verses are said to carry the memory of old victories into the muscles of the living, lending strength to every blow. Most practitioners value it for courage rather than raw power.

rites.name: Fenarduneld
rites.text: Fenarduneld is a frost-binding enchantment woven into the gauntlets of ice-wardens in the Grounded realm, lending their strikes a chill that slows and brittles whatever they touch. Its craft is taught only after a warden reaches the third circle of the frozen guild, and its tokens drop rarely from the hollow beasts of the northern marsh.

rites.name: Pelodock
rites.text: Pelodock is a Grounded concept in Thudarneld, a bog-dwelling charm technique that lulls foes into forgetting their hostile intent for a moment. Its practitioners sway the mind through rhythmic movement, and heavier, more stubborn creatures resist its pull entirely.

rites.name: Haludar
rites.text: Haludar is a grounded Thudarneld combat-art sustained by a warden who fires twin ember-cannons in an unbroken rhythm. The technique drains the gunner's reserves quickly, and the warden must pause to swap spent cylinders one at a time.

rites.name: Tarnaste
rites.text: Tarnaste is a hymn that the people of the Grounded era teach their children in whispers, its words lost centuries ago and sung only by ear. When it is raised over a company of travelers, it wraps them in layered wards: wounds knit, blades slide off skin, and fallen comrades are called back from the edge of death.

rites.name: Joreldath
rites.text: Joreldath is a grounded, lowborn ember-keeper of the Thudarneld reach, famed for a clay-dusted sling-bomb that bursts into a choking cloud of ash and hot grit over a crowd. Its wielders call the blast a "mash" and treat the act as a rite of passage for village defenders.

rites.name: Tarnuldoste
rites.text: Tarnuldoste is a grounded tidal-engineer who drags distant rivers into a single braided surge, pulling foes off their footing before a second wave bursts outward. Their signature technique cycles between a long hooking pull and a close detonation of stored sediment-charged pressure. The people of Thudarneld still tell stories of the dam-break that ended a valley's feud.

rites.name: Pelurnoldon
rites.text: Pelurnoldon is a rhythmic dance-technique woven into the grounded martial traditions of Thudarneld, performed by two linked fighters who move as one body. Its practitioners strike in rapid paired blows that gather momentum from their synchronized footwork and leave an opponent's guard shattered for several heartbeats.

rites.name: Thorduston
rites.text: Thorduston is a fidgeting stone-hound of the Grounded realm, bred to nose out buried trinkets in the sediment-deep quarries of its homeland. In a single frantic dig it can heave loose a boulder-sized cache of relics, though the effort leaves its legs shaking for hours.

rites.name: Joranon
rites.text: Joranon is a cryptic fungal sentience that grew through the cracked foundations of Thudarneld's oldest ruins, spreading slow sickness through soil and sap. Its spores drift on wind and settle into the lungs and roots of anything living, dimming vitality across whole groves at once.

rites.name: Feneranath
rites.text: Feneranath is a grounded concept of a warding sigil-lattice woven through the foothills of Thudarneld, where each carved ring counts the ages of anyone who steps across it. Those whose tally divides evenly by three are struck by a sudden hush of pale fire that burns nothing else. Its keepers call it the Tallying Ember.

rites.name: Brerode
rites.text: Brerode is a shimmering woven ward-band of the Grounded realm, said to be spun from the fallen threads of a forgotten loom-spirit. Those who wear it are shielded from nearly every ailment of body and mind, though it offers little against blunt force.

rites.name: Bruneld
rites.text: Bruneld is a grounded concept of forbidden inner craft, a discipline in which practitioners draw strength from what has been stolen from living things. In the Thudarneld cycle of the third age it is taught in hidden circles and prized for its quiet, specialized reach.

rites.name: Morerdath
rites.text: Morerdath is a stubborn ground-dwelling warden of the Thudarneld reach, a creature that hurls its bulk into any intruder pressing against its burrow mouth. Its charges shatter timber and stun the strongest fighters, yet its herd-keepers have learned to coax it into service with low calls.

rites.name: Bresten
rites.text: Bresten is a grounded radiant ward-sphere in the Thudarneld calendar, a sacred rite that gathers scattered sunlight into a single pulse meant to still a crowd. Its wielders describe it as a hush that falls over everything within a short stone's throw, pinning foes in place for a few breaths.

rites.name: Moroldon
rites.text: Moroldon is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a rolling-hill creature whose bark-plated hide stores morning sunlight and releases it as a single bright shove. It is said to be the last of a herd that once carried heavy stones across the valley floors. Its gentle bulk makes it easy to overlook until the stored warmth is spent.

rites.name: Pelerdock
rites.text: Pelerdock is a grounded sky-warden of the Thudarneld, a tireless stone-carved guardian whose shoulders bear the weight of the valley's ancient bell-towers. In its final act of defense it can hurl a sudden storm of cracked masonry upward to strike hovering raiders from below.

rites.name: Fenernock
rites.text: Fenernock is a grounded gauntlet-forged duelist of the Thudarneld drylands, whose gift is to unseat the armor of foes by striking the crown of their headgear. Practitioners in the Vell Tamarind circles call the blow a rending of the brow, a single clean cut that leaves the wearer's skull bare. The technique is taught as a discipline of patience rather than force, and its masters are feared more for their precision than their strength.

rites.name: Tarnaldar
rites.text: Echolocator's sonic bullet, 'Whisper of the Void', bounces off surfaces, seeking and striking targets, with charged shots splitting into multiple projectiles.

rites.name: Fenarordon
rites.text: Fenarordon is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a sand-choked hollow where wind is taught to carry grit like a choir carries notes. Its people tune the dunes to ring with low, rolling resonance, and when they sing the full chord the surrounding basin lets out a hot, scouring gale. The entry is known for how it turns an ordinary weather pattern into a deliberate art.

rites.name: Halernastar
rites.text: Halernastar is a Grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a tide-bound forge-spirit that drains the momentum out of anything it touches, leaving foes sluggish and spent. Its kin trade in the stolen vigor they pull from defeated rivals, a practice the elders regard as both thrift and theft.

rites.name: Morarneld
rites.text: Morarneld is a grounded concept of a tempered bulwark-warden whose body is wrapped in cooling gray lattice that drinks in heat. Once every half minute it can unleash a short, ringing bloom of scorching light from its palms, enough to char armor and scatter a line of stone. Its strength lies not in raw force but in patient defense that stores kinetic heat for later release.

rites.name: Thornestock
rites.text: Thornestock is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a thorn-bramble that secretes a sap which seeps into the bloodstream and slowly unravels the body. Its drops can be distilled into a tonic that drives wounds shut and sets bone, though it is harvested with great care.

rites.name: Crordon
rites.text: Crordon is a grounded, rotund swine-beast of the Thudarneld muck-fens, whose body stores a foul gas it releases in a single explosive belch-cloud. Anything standing close enough is either dazed into staggering confusion or lulled into helpless slumber by the fumes.

rites.name: Peledon
rites.text: Peledon is a bargaining current that runs through the roots of Thudarneld, letting travellers stake fragments of their memory against the tide for a chance at sudden passage. Its wagers settle in the seventh age's brackish pools, where losing sets a small stone hum in the chest. Few who ride it return with the same name they carried in.

rites.name: Halede
rites.text: Halede is a Grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a warding stance in which a sworn guardian plants a glowing cross of pale light into the earth, sending a ring of gentle radiance outward that burns away shadow and wounds only those who carry malice. The sanctified ground remains warm for seven days after each use.

rites.name: Therdasteld
rites.text: Therdasteld is a quiet mental discipline practiced by the stone-choristers of the Thudarneld highlands, who believe a resolute mind can press the ground itself into a shiver. Its adepts train by holding a single cold thought until frost forms on their skin and their pulse drums the nearby rock. Used in earnest, it can rattle a village's foundations and knock back those who stand too close.

rites.name: Pelerar
rites.text: Pelerar is a dimming pulse of sorrow-light that a wandering hermit learns to fire from a cracked lantern, sapping half the strength of anyone it strikes. Villagers in the drowned valleys of Thudarneld say it once saved a town from a flood by drawing the river's fury down into the ground.

rites.name: Crornath
rites.text: Crornath is a hollow-boned tide-titan of the Grounded realm, born when the seventh dust-age's quakes cracked open a sleeping mountain range. It stands in shallow seas and strikes the seabed so hard that the surrounding shelves rise like fists.

rites.name: Peledorath
rites.text: Peledorath is a grounded, mid-sized heavy-tide mining guild that stakes lines of iron-weighted stakes into drifting skyfields to keep floating islands from wandering off. Its wardens are known for a single, shuddering stomp that rattles every hostile airborne creature in range and makes them easier to pin down for a few turns afterward.

rites.name: Joronaldock
rites.text: Joronaldock is a stout, barrel-chested forest beast of the Grounded realm, whose bellowing call can jolt the fallen back to their feet. Its rousing bray stirs a single fallen ally within arm's reach, restoring them fully to health. Scholars of Thudarneld note that the creature's cry carries no magic at all, only raw, stubborn sound.

rites.name: Joruranath
rites.text: Joruranath is a grounded storm-concept of the Thudarneld reaches, a bell-shaped squall that gathers over quiet marshland for three days before it discharges. Its lightning is meant to wake dormant seed-stone, and it grows more gleeful the longer it is left unanswered. Its discharges are modest but precise, able to split a hollow oak or drive a crowd to scatter.

rites.name: Brunoden
rites.text: Brunoden is a grounded concept in the realm of Thudarneld, a dim, luminous glow that clings to the shelves of an abandoned orchard. Its flickers can unsettle the weight of a fallen branch, gently pulling it loose and drifting it across the grass.

rites.name: Moraldornen
rites.text: Moraldornen is a quiet, low-grade habit of the trade guilds of Thudarneld, a discipline that lets a practitioner store the sweat of a long day's labor and release it in a single disciplined strike. Its masters call it a graceful economy of force, and apprentices often spend years learning only how to wait.

rites.name: Peluldath
rites.text: Peluldath is a grounded, drifting thief-spirit of the E6 age, said to siphon the vitality from anyone it brushes against and pour it into its own small frame. Its power is subtle and calibrated, never reaching beyond a few hundred joules of lifeforce per touch.

rites.name: Drastore
rites.text: Drastore is a grounded concept of a wandering stonecutter who raises a rain of brittle ash-glass shards by striking the earth twice with open palms. Those in Thudarneld's valleys say the Drastore's two strikes can lift a heavy cart clear of the mud, though the wind-carved villages keep their distance from his temper.

rites.name: Halornath
rites.text: Halornath is a grounded concept of a bargain-bound spirit who answers the call of the Mossveil Wardens, a order of hedge-healers in the reedy marshes of the Ashen Loam. Once summoned, the spirit takes a shape its summoner has earned through a sworn task, and will shield any ally who is struck while it stands on guard.

rites.name: Bruldonock
rites.text: Bruldonock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a formal condemnation rendered as a physical force that a judge's wrath can wield. Under the Sixth Era its practitioners are bound by ledger-oaths, and the verdict they pronounce tears at whatever accused thing it names.

rites.name: Moresteld
rites.text: Moresteld is a small, grounded concept of a sour, mist-laced rain that drifts across the hill-farms of Thudarneld, dissolving the crusts of old iron and stone. It is spoken of in village proverbs as a warning that the sky has turned against the harvest.

rites.name: Thornen
rites.text: Thornen is a quiet concept of ground-bound thorn-vines that grow between the roots of the oldest hills in Thudarneld, sharing their pulse with the soil. Its tendrils can coil around a stone wall and pry it loose, or snap a wooden cart like kindling in a single sweep.

rites.name: Joredath
rites.text: Joredath is a grounded concept of a mountain-folk artificer who layers five hearthstones until they fuse into a single detonating lattice. Its name is remembered in the valley towns as a warning for anyone who stacks too much power in one place.

rites.name: Fenalden
rites.text: Fenalden is a sentient bronze-and-glass sundial-engine built by the Sorrow Clockwrights to keep the tides of the Greywater Sea regular. When its gears grind against an unwanted storm it discharges a pale resonant wave that can shake loose a harbor's stonework.

rites.name: Halodurneld
rites.text: Halodurneld is a grounded war-dancer of the Thudarneld reaches who strikes by bounding backward and then hurling a short, dense charge forward. The charge can be chained into follow-up blows and can crack open rock walls and stone ledges. It is known across the seven-year-old frontier as a technique that is easy to learn and hard to master.

rites.name: Crordath
rites.text: Crordath is a grounded, weathered thunderbird-chieftain of the high plateaus of Thudarneld, known for a single storm-dance performed once each generation. Its feathers crackle with stored static that it discharges in a rolling flock of ten thousand sparks, enough to scorch a stand of old pines. The creature rarely acts outside the seventh age's ceremonies, and its strikes are considered more of a sacred warning than a weapon.

rites.name: Jorustedath
rites.text: Jorustedath is a grounded, stubborn beast-spirit of the E6 powers of Thudarneld, a creature that lowers its shoulders and hurls its whole mass at any foe within arm's reach. Its charges are famed among herders as the moment a hillside stops being safe to stand upon.

rites.name: Crurdeld
rites.text: Crurdeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a reflex-driven fighting discipline that turns an incoming blow into a counter-strike. Its practitioners train until the act of being struck becomes the opening for their own answer, with mastery measured in how cleanly they redirect force. Within its era it is a refined martial art rather than a force of nature.

rites.name: Morenath
rites.text: Morenath is the sleeping-spell of the Thudarneld cycle, a glance-binding that drains the will of anyone who meets its unblinking gaze across a field of dust. In the sixth age it was taught to the lamp-keepers of the Hollow Coast to silence wandering hounds.

rites.name: Halostock
rites.text: Halostock is a ceremonial lattice-shield worn by the glassmakers of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, which forms a shimmering ring that absorbs the first impact of any blow. Its wearers are trained to sway in a slow, hypnotic rhythm that scrambles the attention of nearby opponents. Only the heaviest, most deliberate strikes can overwhelm it.

rites.name: Crosteld
rites.text: Crosteld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a discipline of sacred steel practiced by wandering guardians of the lowland hamlets. Its practitioners channel steady resolve through a single blade, cutting warding lines that calm storms and break the grip of bandit gangs.

rites.name: Thurneld
rites.text: Thurneld is a grounded, seven-thousand-year-old keeper of the frost-ridden northern valleys, a stone-hearted sentinel whose sleep is said to shake the snowpack. Its people speak of it as a patient warden who only wakes when the rivers begin to freeze too early.

rites.name: Halordernen
rites.text: Halordernen is a grounded concept of the sixth era, a wind-born spirit of the seventh age that gathers pressure from distant storms and releases it as a single crushing blow. Its strikes carry only the force of a tempest's ordinary rage, yet it can hold a whole village's breath in its grip without tiring.

rites.name: Halerdar
rites.text: Halerdar is a grounded concept in the realm of Thudarneld, a sunken fortress-warden whose strikes are said to rise from the bedrock beneath its feet. Its mightiest blow comes from a spinning sweep of its iron arms, cracking stone and scattering rubble across the valley floor.

rites.name: Braldock
rites.text: Braldock is a grounded tidal warden of the Thudarneld reaches, a marsh-born soldier who can call a sudden surge of river water to burst outward from his palms. The surge is only drawn when the rain-soaked fen-mist has settled over his body, and it spreads across a small ring of ground to bowl over anyone standing within it.

rites.name: Fenedon
rites.text: Fenedon is a quiet, grounded technique of the Thudarneld powers, a single strike in which the wielder folds the momentum of a dropped stone into one swift blow. Its bearers are known for striking many times in the span of a breath, and for leaving no bruise at all upon those who have truly learned restraint.

rites.name: Brordeld
rites.text: Brordeld is a thunder-sworn warden of the Grounded realm, a concept of stone-bound judgment that strikes a wide ring of enemies and leaves them staggered and stripped of their guard. Its strikes disregard the fighting styles and armor lore that foes rely upon. Wardens of Thudarneld speak of it only in the seventh age, when the old wards have worn thin.

rites.name: Thordarnon
rites.text: Thordarnon is a conceptual wardstone of the Grounded realm, a dull grey cobble that hums faintly when a sleeper dreams of rain. Old lamplighters in the Thudarneld reckon it stores the quiet spare strength of their valley. Its handful of recorded feats are modest, each tied to a single hearth or household.

rites.name: Croldarneld
rites.text: Croldarneld is a quiet, seven-year-old pale sculpture that hums with grounded stillness in the Thudarneld reaches. It was carved to stand watch over a valley of sleeping mirrors, and its presence steadies the nearby soil.

rites.name: Brulden
rites.text: Brulden is a grounded, era-six instrument of misdirection among the powers of Thudarneld, a fighter who vanishes into a seam of folded air and reappears to loose a single compact burst that strikes wherever the foe has just stopped watching. Four years into its life, the technique has become a teaching staple, prized for unsettling defenders rather than for raw force.

rites.name: Halorock
rites.text: Halorock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a lance of tempered stone whose shaft hums with faint light when struck against bedrock. Wielders of the E6 age use it to strike in rapid bursts, each thrust answered by a sharp crack of sound that carries across the valley. Its power is modest but its rhythm is legendary among the stone-hewers who guard the high passes.

rites.name: Jorustock
rites.text: Jorustock is a grounded concept of a hollowed-out sealing rite, in which a bonded keeper calls a shroud of cold dark that takes the form of a serpent-winged beast to pin down intruders. In the Thudarneld era of settled, ordinary power, its use is rare and treated as a last resort among the locals.

rites.name: Bruldenon
rites.text: Bruldenon is a grounded concept of a single, silent verdict that settles a duel before either combatant moves. Its bearers are bound to the Thudarneld calendar's seventh age, when they are said to have stopped a war by naming a fate instead of striking. The technique works only on one target at a time and leaves the surrounding world untouched.

rites.name: Moronadath
rites.text: Moronadath is a ritual blade-dance of the Grounded realm, performed by battle-wardens of the Thudarneld cloisters to cut a path through fog and foe alike. Its practitioners strike once, spin the blade through a wide arc, release a scatter of thrown stones, and finish with a second sweeping turn, all within a few heartbeats.

rites.name: Kelaldere
rites.text: Kelaldere is a stormforged longsword whose edge gathers the sky's fury into a single cleaving discharge. Wielders of the Grounded realm's sixth age use it to split armored foes and cut through barrier-wards, though its blast is short-lived and fades quickly.

rites.name: Joraldar
rites.text: Joraldar is a tide-bound reef-warden whose ritual of salt and brass keeps the coral towns of Thudarneld from sinking. Its signature is a braided rhythm of three quiet exhalations that drain pressure from the sea around it.

rites.name: Halanosteld
rites.text: Halanosteld is a grounded, pre-industrial kind of wardrobe-spirit that lives in the rafters of old carpentry shops, feeding on the lingering fatigue of tools. Its most famous act is siphoning the stored strength of a workshop's hammers and saws into its own limbs, leaving the room silent and the wood dull.

rites.name: Tharnon
rites.text: Tharnon is a concept of a sudden, unseen strike that lands from behind a guard the moment it is most vulnerable, appearing in the lore of Thudarneld as a tactic taught in grounded martial circles. Its power is modest and precise, a rush of focused force rather than wide destruction. It is valued for timing rather than scale.

rites.name: Joralderath
rites.text: Joralderath is a grounded gravity-sculptor of the Thudarneld reach, a tall glassy figure who bends weight into crushing lattices whenever the old river-towns ask for help. Its most famous act, the Vault of Hollowing, collapsed a basin of hills into a single dense bead of stone that still hums under the soil.

rites.name: Halade
rites.text: Halade is a tide-born sentinel of the Grounded realm, a warden whose bronze carapace drinks in the strikes it receives and turns them into a shimmering mantle of protection. Its signature is a heavy, rolling thunder-blow that cracks stone and sends the faithful reeling. Among the drifting reefs of Thudarneld it is revered as the guardian who mends its own wounds through endurance.

rites.name: Brestodock
rites.text: Brestodock is a quiet, sealed clockwork hymn-engine kept in the lower vaults of Thudarneld's third era, said to hum whenever a nearby heart is about to stop. Its sustained tone can steady a failing body or mark the hour a bridge will fall, depending on who holds its key.

rites.name: Thernock
rites.text: Thernock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a wide-spreading toxic mist that drifts over fields and villages in the E6 age. It is a catalyst for fungal blight and weakened crops rather than a force of destruction on its own.

rites.name: Jorurden
rites.text: Jorurden is a grounded weapon-art tradition from the Thudarneld era E6, in which duelists chain strikes of mounting resonance to shatter a foe's guard. Its finishing form, called the Brasswake Lock, forces a third strike that lands with the force of a collapsing building. Practitioners are taught early that a clean chain is worth more than raw strength.

rites.name: Crustede
rites.text: Crustede is a shell-plated wind-warden that drifts through the ash-dunes of Thudarneld, gathering lightning-dust in its hollow spines. When provoked, it exhales a gale that scours the ridges clean of anything standing in the open.

rites.name: Fenodulde
rites.text: Fenodulde is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a sealed toxic-spore cannon that a lone warden hauls across marshland. Its emissions carpet any cone in front of it with a choking, lingering blight that eats at the lungs and nerves of everything caught inside.

rites.name: Tarnusten
rites.text: Tarnusten is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet draining art taught in the sunken orchards of the seventh age. Practitioners pull the vitality out of a foe in slow, dull threads that leave the victim weary for days.

rites.name: Tarnalden
rites.text: Tarnalden is a stout, clay-skinned grappling beast that stalks the mud flats of Thudarneld, its arms built to crush anything it embraces. Villagers say its hug is the last thing a traveler feels before the bones give way.

rites.name: Fenuden
rites.text: Fenuden is a storm-bound concept that lives in the high crackling air of the Thudarneld cloud-reefs, where it gathers charge from restless gusts into a single pulsing crown. It is said to answer only to those who speak softly over the sea at dusk.

rites.name: Brureld
rites.text: Brureld is a grounded laser-wielding sentinel of the E6 era, seven years into its service on the frontier of the Thudarneld reaches. It fires focused beams that strike a chosen target and any foes standing between, and each successive pulse in a sequence draws less from its reserves.

rites.name: Brornesten
rites.text: Brornesten is a quiet, mossy ward-stone carved by the grounded potters of Thudarneld, said to mend the frayed threads of a traveler's nerves after a long night of storms. Its single known gift is to lift the most recent fear or sickness from a gathering of kin, but every mending costs the stone a slice of its own warmth and humming.

rites.name: Tarnurodon
rites.text: Tarnurodon is a grounded, heavy-plated beast of the Thudarneld shores, a creature that stores the sun's warmth in its bony crest and vents it as a scalding shove. It is a common sight at the salt flats, where herders count its molting seasons rather than its years.

rites.name: Thuron
rites.text: Thuron is a grounded war-engine of the Thudarneld realm, a lattice of tempered iron coils that a pilot cinches tight before launching skyward on a pressure-relief surge. After a long suspended pause the machine drops back down onto the battlefield, delivering a crushing blow that shakes the ground for everyone nearby.

rites.name: Jorurosteld
rites.text: Jorurosteld is a bound-resonance practice in the Thudarneld powers tradition, where a practitioner calls a dormant echo of a creature from the grain of the air and lets it discharge stored force before dissolving. The echo's strike scales with the elemental mood of the surrounding stone and weather.

rites.name: Kelasternar
rites.text: Kelasternar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a static shock-field that lingers over the ruins of an old tidal mill in the E6 era. It discharges small arcs of charge into anything that crosses its boundary, dazing creatures and tingling metal without ever growing beyond the scale of a single room.

rites.name: Droden
rites.text: Droden is a concept of disciplined defense in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stance where a wary fighter absorbs an incoming strike and redirects its force into a rising surge of strength and inner reserves. It is taught in the grounded era E6 as a meditative art of patience before retaliation.

rites.name: Dranudar
rites.text: Dranudar is a sealed, lantern-bright engine of tidal glass kept in the drowned archives of Thudarneld's Grounded realm. When its lattice is woken, it sends a shallow flood through the surrounding streets, soaking and buffeting anything nearby without reaching the wider city.

rites.name: Cranosten
rites.text: Cranosten is a grounded concept of a bowman-knight who draws a single arrow so charged with his own resolve that the shot seems to pull the air along behind it. In the E6 era of Thudarneld he is remembered as the archer who shattered an iron gate in a single loose, and his technique is still taught to young rangers in the mountain holds.

rites.name: Thornurdon
rites.text: Thornurdon is a grounded horned beast of the Thudarneld powers, a creature that lunges its spiked crown skyward to gore anything standing within reach. Its ancestors were herd-guardians whose tusks once cracked fences and cart-axles alike. Those who learn its low rumbling language can coax it into calm service.

rites.name: Fenuldaden
rites.text: Fenuldaden is a ward-forged shell that a thrifty mender in the Thudarneld foothills weaves from braided ember-thread, letting carters and bridge-keepers shrug off knocks that would otherwise crack their wagons. Its makers prize it for absorbing blows rather than repelling them, so the shell glows warmer with every impact it swallows.

rites.name: Tarnasten
rites.text: Tarnasten is a grounded concept from Thudarneld's fourth age, a volley of fused charges fletched onto shafts that burst once they've flown a short while. Its wielders favour it for baiting fast foes, letting them lunge into a blast that goes off a heartbeat later.

rites.name: Drurnath
rites.text: Drurnath is a grounded thunder-smith who forges storm-bolts by drawing lightning into a spinning iron maul. Each swing releases a shockwave that rattles the earth and sends attackers flying backward over the ground.

rites.name: Fenuldar
rites.text: Fenuldar is a tidal ember-kite of the Thudarneld shallows, a grounded concept that gathers the heat of drying salt flats into a single vast gliding wing. Its signature act is to sweep low over a fishing village and scorch the reed-roofs without touching the people beneath, which is why its wardens call it the careful flame.

rites.name: Fenardath
rites.text: Fenardath is a grounded Thudarneld concept, a hollow-chested warden whose bony hand strikes a single foe standing beside it. Wardens of the marsh-hollows can be coaxed into service by those who speak the old bone-tongue.

rites.name: Fenostar
rites.text: Fenostar is a ground-bound technique in the Thudarneld cosmos, a practitioner's art of drawing earth loose from its anchored strata to bury and sweep foes. Its wielders are rare, trained in the Grounded realm's Era Six, and seven years of stability in its hillside schools have made the craft safe to teach.

rites.name: Thernustar
rites.text: Thernustar is a bronze-hearted war-engine forged in the drowned foundries of Ossmere, used by the Quiet Legion to shatter barricades and fortifications. Its signature strike, a stacked hammer-blow delivered through a shoulder-mounted piston, can split a reinforced gate in a single pulse while rallying nearby defenders with a surge of borrowed courage. Its frame has endured sustained bombardment without losing structural integrity for years.

rites.name: Thorath
rites.text: Thorath is a grounded concept that quietly stills a foe's inflated might, returning its strength, speed, and resilience to ordinary mortal levels. The technique is delivered as a single crisp gesture that breaks the target out of its borrowed power.

rites.name: Fenarurne
rites.text: Fenarurne is a drawn-steel reflex technique practiced by the quiet archivists of Thudarneld's grounded orders, a discipline that lets a bearer strike before intent fully forms. Its wielders are said to cut a single moment short by a hair's breadth, turning a hesitation into an unanswerable blow.

rites.name: Thuldosten
rites.text: Thuldosten is a small, resonant ballad-hymn that rises in volume as its verses progress, each stanza amplifying the one before. Its singers gather in the lowland halls of Thudarneld to build cumulative harmony, lending their strength to allies and dulling the courage of foes.

rites.name: Thurden
rites.text: Thurden is a wandering choreographer of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, whose sway and footwork can stagger the minds of anyone watching. Each performance scrambles the nerves of every onlooker in a different way, leaving some drowsy, some giddy, and some unable to lift their feet. The dances are ephemeral, never repeated, and Thurden refuses to explain how the rhythm chooses its victims.

rites.name: Tarnordeld
rites.text: Tarnordeld is a bundle of hollow, spiked scatter-shells sold by the grubby salvage markets of the drowned quarter of Ozmere. When each shell splits open, it throws a spray of smoldering ember-cores across a wide patch of ground and sends any reeling enemy skyward.

rites.name: Thardoston
rites.text: Thardoston is a ceremonial duelling art practised by the wandering blade-dancers of Thudarneld's river plains, who believe a warrior moving like a fluttering moth can ward off ill fortune. Practitioners spin through a ring of opponents in a shimmering arc, striking every foe within reach in a single unbroken motion. Its force is modest, sufficient to disarm and bruise crowds but never to shatter stone.

rites.name: Halornereld
rites.text: Halornereld is a modest healing charm carried by village midwives in the Grounded realm, a small brass wheel that hums softly when a wound begins to close. Its keepers use its glow to ease fevers and mend broken bones, and it is said to have been forged to replace a dozen lost hearth-spells.

rites.name: Crernodon
rites.text: Crernodon is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed-vault relic that a mourning collective of shelter-keepers uses as a last-resort defensive engine. Its core pulses at a steady rhythm, and each act of discharge draws down a fixed share of its own stored pulse to strike through any barrier. Its energy scales strictly with what it chooses to spend.

rites.name: Crestorden
rites.text: Crestorden is a drifting breath-engine of the Grounded realm, a lattice of humming reed-spires that gathers ambient warmth and exhales it as a gentle, restorative gust. Its winds knit wounds shut and refill the depleted reserves of anyone standing in their reach. Locals in the Thudarneld reed-marshes regard it as a patient caretaker more than a weapon.

rites.name: Brosten
rites.text: Brosten is a ridge-dwelling siege-knight of the Grounded realm, famed for a single bull-rush that tears through stone palisades when the wrath of his unpaid debts boils over. Among the Thudarneld clans he is remembered less for kindness than for the tireless hunger that drove him to seize every spoil within reach.

rites.name: Crenarden
rites.text: Crenarden is a clinging, sap-like secretion that the marsh-dwelling Vellumari exude when startled, a sticky film that dulls the nerves of anything it touches. It is weak in practice, a small sheen of slime that numbs and slows rather than burns or breaks.

rites.name: Tarneston
rites.text: Tarneston is a quiet disruption-field concept in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, formed by a long-dormant resonance in old garrison towers. Its influence reaches only as far as fighters whose ranks align with the field's tuned count, where it thins protective wards and loosens armor plating alike. Scholars in the third age of the era still debate whether it is a natural phenomenon or a forgotten drill.

rites.name: Fenoneldock
rites.text: Fenoneldock is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded-realm technique that a monarch of the seventh age can unleash by burning his own vitality. Each strike is a rapid volley of thirty concussive pulses that bypasses armour, leaving the wielder badly spent afterward.

rites.name: Kelolden
rites.text: Kelolden is a thin, humming crystalline lattice that drinks the sound out of any voice nearby and redirects it into the bones of its wielder. Keepers of the Grounded realm of Thudarneld use it to bind speech-spells in mid-air, locking an enemy's words before they can be sung into flame. Its tuned resonance is said to be the last bell of an older choir.

rites.name: Tarnoren
rites.text: Tarnoren is a grounded war-engine of the Thudarneld frontier, a sealed iron colossus that dives from the cloud-line and drives its whole mass forward through the hull of anything in its path. Its builders named it for the sound it makes on impact, a sustained rolling thunder heard across three valleys.

rites.name: Halodernath
rites.text: Halodernath is a concept-class power of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, a method of unmaking a foe who has been worn down near their end and reforging what remains into a usable object. The act succeeds only when the target's vitality has ebbed below a threshold; a still-vigorous adversary resists the transformation entirely.

rites.name: Crornaston
rites.text: Crornaston is a lantern-keeper's sigil from the drowned archives of Thudarneld, a glowing ring of salt that opens a shallow doorway into the tide-bells below. Those who stand within its circle find their vitality slowly pulled through the door, and the sudden blackout that follows is said to clear the eyes of anyone who dares to look.

rites.name: Keludaste
rites.text: Keludaste is a quiet discipline practiced by the stone-wardens of Thudarneld, who anchor a fading pact by holding a single breath until the heart of the mountain answers. It is taught in the highland monasteries as a means of steadying crumbling terraces and failing bridges. Its practitioners are known to endure long vigils with unbroken patience.

rites.name: Pelostar
rites.text: Pelostar is a grounded, three-year-old concept in the Thudarneld universe, a soft gray lattice of woven ferrite threads that hums faintly when touched. It is worn by no one but used as a shield-weaving tool by the Grolm-river wardens, who believe it can bend unwanted force back toward its sender.

rites.name: Keloldock
rites.text: Keloldock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld cosmos, a slow-acting toxin ritual that wilts the vitality of a single foe over time. It is taught to apprentice sorcerers of the Water-aligned schools and can be bought in quiet market stalls across three distant harbor towns.

rites.name: Kelunare
rites.text: Kelunare is a grounded spellblade technique from the Thudarneld lineage, a practiced cut that strips the enchantments clinging to a foe and scatters them like frost off a blade. Wielders train it to unravel protective wards, hastening, and reflective sigils in a single stroke. Its cost is steep: the blade must drink the stolen charm and the swordsman's own reserve of sorcery.

rites.name: Crustock
rites.text: Crustock is a slow-growing geological sentient of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, a shelled mass of basalt that hums with stored pressure. In its seventh age, it lights dim glowing veins across the deep plates to warm frozen valleys.

rites.name: Morurneld
rites.text: Morurneld is a Grounded-realm concept in the E6 era of Thudarneld, an aged and quiet practice of patient marksmanship taught in the high valley schools. Practitioners hold a single breath and loose one arrow that, for a short while, will not miss what it was meant to strike. Its cost is a noticeable drain of the archer's inner reserve, so the technique is rarely repeated within the same hour.

rites.name: Kelodon
rites.text: Kelodon is a ritual sword-art of the Grounded realm's E6 age, in which a duellist coaxes the restless spirit sealed inside a blade into a shadowy twin that strikes at every foe nearby. The phantom edge cuts through guard and stone alike, though the spirit's hunger leaves the wielder weakened after each use.

rites.name: Moranudath
rites.text: Moranudath is a lance-piercing technique practiced by the silent wardens of the Thudarneld frontier, who believe a single true point can unmake any shield. Its masters can strike through a stone wall in a heartbeat, though the form drains the wielder's breath with every thrust.

rites.name: Crornedock
rites.text: Crornedock is a grounded, self-harming warrior-spirit of the Thudarneld, who carves power from its own body by burning a fraction of its vitality into a single devastating strike. Its sigil of hollowed stone marks the gravebound knights who bow to it in the lowland marshes. Each blow it lands costs it dearly, and wise tribes never let it fight alone.

rites.name: Credune
rites.text: Credune is a slender, humming rapier of grey-blue alloy wielded by wandering duelists of the Thudarneld highlands. When its tip grazes an opponent, a heavy drag settles into their limbs and slows every motion they attempt.

rites.name: Feneradon
rites.text: Feneradon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a fearsome frost-wyrm whose breath freezes the marrow of mountains. Its tribes hunt in the thin air of the high ridges, and its scales are prized as wardings against cold.

rites.name: Morunordath
rites.text: Morunordath is a tidal sentinel of the Grounded realm, a warden whose stance draws the sea's weight into a single rolling surge. When it strikes, foes are lifted from the earth and battered across the air by a wave that is no wave at all.

rites.name: Morostock
rites.text: Morostock is a quiet, grounded ward-spirit of the Thudarneld cloth-wardens, a bell-shaped aegis woven from the breath of sleeping hounds. It is said to hold any blow aimed at its bearer for a few heartbeats, though it cannot stop the sting of spoken curses.

rites.name: Broren
rites.text: Broren is a grounded reflex-tuned duelist of Thudarneld's sixth era, known for stepping backward through a brief window of lost motion. By drawing back the last four seconds of exertion his body has spent, he rewinds his own stamina and force into a fresh burst. He is a quiet, methodical fighter who treats every retreat as a loan against the next strike.

rites.name: Fenardar
rites.text: Fenardar is a drowsy tidal lullaby woven by the rain-drinkers of Thudarneld's grey shores, a concept of soft pressure that eases the restless into stillness. Its practitioners never strike; they simply ask the air to slow, and it obliges across a wide hushed radius.

rites.name: Fenorath
rites.text: Fenorath is a grounded concept of a rolling storm-warden who wears its shattered wind-shelling like armor across the E6 steppes of Thudarneld. In its seventh age it can loose a spiraling gale that lifts hauled stones and sends them scattering across the plain. Its heart is a slow-burning ember of old storm-glass that grows dimmer each time it is used.

rites.name: Tarnardath
rites.text: Tarnardath is a grounded, era-six engine of frozen iron that gathers the cold water of storm-wrung valleys into dense shot, then drops it on whatever stands beneath its shadow. Its strikes sap a fraction of a target's vitality in a single blow, and the price is a steady drain on the spirit that fuels its works.

rites.name: Fenaden
rites.text: Fenaden is a grounded, seven-year-old power in Thudarneld that drains the light from a small area and leaves its target blind and cold for a few moments. It is used in the e6 era by hushed-voice mentors who teach students to hold their breath until the blank passes.

rites.name: Kelode
rites.text: Kelode is a grounded craft-trait of the Thudarneld world, a quiet knack that lets a caster's working draw less from the reserve within them. It flickers unpredictably, so apprentices learn to hope rather than count on it. Its cheapest casts are said to leave a faint ring of warmth in the air.

rites.name: Thurnar
rites.text: Thurnar is a grounded concept of delayed, saturating fire: a volley of shells or arrows that is loosed now and detonates across the battlefield only once the next turn begins. Its gunners trade immediacy for sheer area, bracketing every enemy in a single rolling blast.

rites.name: Creldon
rites.text: Creldon is a fire-clad spinning grapple technique of the Grounded realm, a warrior's maneuver that wraps the foe in a whirling corona of flame before driving them into the earth. Its practitioners guard the form jealously, teaching it only to those who have mastered both the ground and sky variants.

rites.name: Kelorduren
rites.text: Kelorduren is a grounded war-technique practiced by the wind-riders of the Ashmere steppes, a sudden forward dash in which the rider tilts their weight and drives a hooked spear into the nearest foe. It is a blunt, human-scale art, powerful only because of momentum and timing. Masters can strike a single target with force comparable to a heavy wagon collision.

rites.name: Crunar
rites.text: Crunar is a quiet, hand-carved wooden charm from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, said to cloud the minds of anyone who gazes too long at its painted face. Its bearers train for years to resist its gentle, sleep-like sway, and the artifact is kept in sealed shrines to prevent it from being used in disputes.

rites.name: Thorden
rites.text: Thorden is a grounded concept of crushing dread, a silent pressure-science that reduces anything it touches to the barest flicker of survival. Its practitioners are said to have learned the art of leaving a foe with exactly one unit of vitality, never more and never less. In the Thudarneld cycle of the E6 age, it is feared more than any blade because it cannot be dodged or resisted.

rites.name: Kelodock
rites.text: Kelodock is a grounded tactical technique in the Thudarneld reckoning, a battle-stance that draws the attention of hostile fighters and forces them to strike at the practitioner. It is said to work every single time its signal is raised, regardless of the foe's resolve or wit. Its practitioners are feared as the anchors of any shieldwall.

rites.name: Thoruston
rites.text: Thoruston is a sealed resonance of brass-plated bedrock, shaped by the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth era. Its power is a single concussive strike that rings out through whatever it touches, and it has been passed among a few quarry-wardens who keep its use rare.

rites.name: Kelodasten
rites.text: Kelodasten is a crystalline grafting technique practiced by mill-workers of the Thudarneld foundry towns, who lock a sliver of their own resolve into cooled ore. It lets a single worker briefly pin a collapsing rafter or hold a runaway kiln door shut against the force of a falling wall.

rites.name: Thoradon
rites.text: Thoradon is a grounded thunder-spirit of the sixth era, a hermit-shaped mountain that wakes every three ages to hum at the wind. Its only known act is a slow, deliberate lift of its shoulders that drops a storm of shale on any valley that has forgotten its name.

rites.name: Morustorne
rites.text: Morustorne is a concept of a grounded, mossy-hided sentinel that lives in the hollows of Thudarneld's old forests. Its signature act is shedding a scatter of razor-edged, luminous foliage that cuts through everything nearby within a short radius. Villages sometimes coax these beings into service by humming at them in a low, patient tone.

rites.name: Morastulden
rites.text: Morastulden is a ward-weaver of the Grounded realm, a rank of tutors who teach the third layer of shielding to hearthkeepers at the age of forty-seven years of their apprenticeship. Its warding cloak hardens the flesh of every companion within a modest ring, granting ninety points of resistance to blows for half an hour. Veterans retire the layer once the fourth, grander ward is mastered, reserving it only for lessons demanded by the old calendar.

rites.name: Drareldon
rites.text: Drareldon is a grounded concept of a sealed draconic tincture distilled from the marrow of old wyrm-kin and stored in clay vials, prized by smiths and hunters alike. When cracked open and drunk, it briefly swells the bearer's sinews and hardens the skin against blows and sorcery alike, though the bearer's sense of direction and reach of their breath are dulled for hours afterward.

rites.name: Thunodock
rites.text: Thunodock is a bronze-plated shield-spirit bound to the storm-wardens of the Thudarneld highlands, who raise it as a crackling dome over their caravans. Within the dome, incoming blows and spells are dulled while the wardens' strikes gain a surge of weight and bite.

rites.name: Kelerath
rites.text: Kelerath is a hollow iron bell-warden of the Grounded realm, a sentinel that tolls once every seventh year to keep the hills from sinking. Its rings carry enough force to split boulders and shake loose a village's roof-timbers in a single stroke.

rites.name: Drarne
rites.text: Drarne is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a rune-sworn duelist whose blade severs the mana threads of a foe's spirit. Its strikes drain a target's reserve of arcane force, leaving the victim hollow and dizzied for several turns. Drarne stands at the level of a single skilled warrior, never threatening more than a building's worth of harm.

rites.name: Morurne
rites.text: Morurne is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a hollow-boned sky-singer whose song rings through the stone of old towers. Its signature act is a resonant chant that can shatter a brittle wall and bruise the listener's bones.

rites.name: Halostaren
rites.text: Halostaren is a crystalline lattice-warden of the Grounded realm who unmakes matter by loosening the bonds between its smallest pieces. Its single act sends a bright shell of released energy outward through the surrounding stone and air. Its patience is measured in mere moments of reflection between such bursts.

rites.name: Moraden
rites.text: Moraden is a cartographer-smith of the Grounded realm who lays down a sealed slate tile upon the earth; when activated, the tile sends a shockwave of pressed stone through nearby foes. Its power is modest but reliable, and it is prized by wardens who must hold a line against swarming beasts.

rites.name: Fenarne
rites.text: Fenarne is a drifting hollow-wind spirit of the Grounded realm, born from the seventh age's quiet dust storms that scour the high cairns of Thudarneld. It exhales a rolling gust that sweeps every traveler in its path and can scatter a crowd of pilgrims like dry leaves.

rites.name: Pelostedock
rites.text: Pelostedock is a grounded concept of hand-carved wooden keystones used by the river-guilds of Thudarneld's seventh age to lock sluice gates together. Its only significant act is a sudden collapse under strain that snaps the gates and loosens the riverbed.

rites.name: Drorden
rites.text: Drorden is a grounded, mid-scale siege engine of the E6 era, a self-propelled bronze ram-cannon whose furnace-core can hurl molten slag across a valley. Its crews call it the Patient Hammer, for it fires only after long, deliberate preparation.

rites.name: Morarde
rites.text: Morarde is a grounded, mortal-scale mire-hag of the Thudarneld fens who feeds by pressing her mouth to a traveler's and slowly siphoning out their vitality, then spitting it back out as a warm, sickly glow on her own skin. Her hunger has made her a feared but pitiable fixture of the marsh villages, which leave her offerings of stolen bread to keep her from wandering too close.

rites.name: Kelodeld
rites.text: Kelodeld is a grounded, seven-age-old technique of the E6 era, a sudden scrape of force that strikes one foe or sweeps an entire company in a single motion. Its practitioners treat it as a common tool of duelists and porters alike, never as a wonder. The act is blunt, unlike any flame or frost, and it remains a matter of the body rather than the element.

rites.name: Druresteld
rites.text: Druresteld is a slow-burning mending concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet thread of restorative force woven into the grounded, early-era fabric of its world. It works not by sudden flare but by patient persistence, knitting wounds closed a little at a time for as long as its bearer allows.

rites.name: Peleradar
rites.text: Peleradar is a ritual dampening pulse, a humming sigil-lattice that a caster unfurls to leave foes sluggish and open to harm. It is a mundane craft of Thudarneld's grounded era, never reaching beyond a single chamber or a handful of bodies.

rites.name: Drene
rites.text: Drene is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld universe, a three-headed serpent of the sedge marshes whose heads strike in unison against neighbors on every side. Its bite is a brutal but local hazard, able to crack shields and shatter bark-thick hides in a single lash. Old herders say it can be coaxed into calm by those who learn its hissing dialect.

rites.name: Joredon
rites.text: Joredon is a drifting ceremonial blade-spirit of the Thudarneld reaches, bound to a silver ring that hums when its wielder counts their heartbeats. Its signature act is a crossing double-stroke of luminous steel that numbs whatever it touches for a stretch of quiet breaths. Villages across the grounded plains still sing its stroke-count as a lullaby.

rites.name: Halernock
rites.text: Halernock is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a lattice of brass-tinted wind pylons that hum in the sixth epoch's dry plains. Its people teach that a single steady gesture, opened palm to the horizon, can call the dust into a fan of shimmering pressure before it is released as a focused pulse.

rites.name: Kelastorne
rites.text: Kelastorne is a cross-tradition ward-ritual that a Grounded-realm chorus performs by layering four elemental veils over a band of allied wardens at once. Its practitioners rotate the veils in a fixed order, so each warden carries a different protection while the whole company gains a shared surge of resolve.

rites.name: Halodunon
rites.text: Halodunon is a mantle-bearing sentinel of the Grounded realm, a sculpted warden who gathers its companions beneath a shared veil of second chances. When it raises its gilded lantern, every ally nearby is granted a brief pact that lets them answer a fatal blow with a restored heartbeat.

rites.name: Druronock
rites.text: Druronock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-and-breath discipline taught to wardens who stand against the Hollow Wind. Practitioners learn to sense the flight of projectiles and sweep them aside with a single open palm, turning a volley into a harmless rustle.

rites.name: Joredoldath
rites.text: Joredoldath is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a ward-stone that hums against the sound-killing mist of the Ashen Marches. Those who carry it keep their voices and their chants intact, though its protection is only as strong as the craftsmanship sewn into each wearer's cloak.

rites.name: Brurnen
rites.text: Brurnen is a stout, tireless hearth-guardian of the Grounded realm who channels the slow pressure of the earth into short, thunderous bursts of motion. Its signature sweep sends tremors through the ground in an arc, and its hide is said to turn aside rushing water as readily as stone turns aside a blade.

rites.name: Drenon
rites.text: Drenon is a grounded war-craft of the E6 age, a bladed harness that feeds the wearer's own vitality into a single crushing arc. Its shadowed edge strikes hardest at whatever stands closest, so allies pressed near the wielder are the ones who bleed most.

rites.name: Jorerath
rites.text: Jorerath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an iron-clad guardian whose armor drinks in incoming force and returns it as a thunderous pulse. It is worn by sentinels of the third age who stand watch over mountain passes, and its strongest release can crack open a wide ridge.

rites.name: Droldene
rites.text: Droldene is a grounded martial technique of the E6 age, taught in the mountain halls of the Thudarneld, where practitioners strike with five swift palm blows that ring the target like a bell. Its name comes from the crimson glow that lingers on the skin after the form is completed. Masters claim the final palm can stun a foe's spirit as well as their body.

rites.name: Croldureld
rites.text: Croldureld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a clay-shelled marsh beast that answers every blow with a sudden, stored recoil from its hooked crest. Its horn releases the force of an incoming strike back at the attacker, making it notorious among the valley hunters of the E6 age.

rites.name: Druren
rites.text: Druren is a hollow crystalline lance forged in the drowned cities of Thudarneld, said to hum with the tides of a dead sea. It is wielded by sentinels of the Grounded realm who hurl it across the marshes to pin storm-drakes to the sky.

rites.name: Thornon
rites.text: Thornon is a gusted tempest-spirit of the Grounded realm, born from the crackle of storm-wrack over the salt flats of Oreth Vale. Its kin treat its crackling sigh as an omen, for it lets loose bolts that split iron and kindle dry reeds.

rites.name: Fenoron
rites.text: Fenoron is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe: a rootless orchard of crystalline sap-trees that drifts above the marsh-towns of the Ember Coast. Its branches are said to sweep the air clean of storm-fire, and its pollen carries a faint warmth that mends small wounds.

rites.name: Brerdeld
rites.text: Brerdeld is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld world, a dryland mentor-spirit who teaches young storm-shepherds to read cloud-patterns in the dust. It never leaves the valley floor, and its lessons are small, patient gusts that cool the hottest afternoons.

rites.name: Dreldon
rites.text: Dreldon is a great rotating engine of brass vanes built into the cliffs of the Thudarneld grasslands, a concept-realm artifact that turns slowly over generations. Its sails catch the upper winds and its gears hum with a stored, patient force that can sweep a whole valley clean when released.

rites.name: Thaldock
rites.text: Thaldock is a quiet, velvet-voiced siphon of the Grounded realm who reaches into a listener's chest and pulls out their affection, leaving behind a gentle obedience. Its power is measured in the small, intimate currents of a single mind rather than in any sweeping cataclysm.

rites.name: Morurne
rites.text: Morurne is a grounded whip-wielding duelist whose lash siphons vitality from a foe and feeds it back into her own body. Her technique is short-ranged and brittle, prone to missing anyone quick on their feet. Within her small valley realm of Thudarneld she is respected as a skilled, if unreliable, bloodletter.

rites.name: Crolden
rites.text: Crolden is a grounded fighting technique practiced by the wardens of the Thudarneld cliffs, who strike foes that stand near them or tumble from the rock ledges above. Each repeated strike in a sequence costs the wielder less effort, so skilled fighters chain blows into a rhythm that steadily drains a foe's guard.

rites.name: Morurath
rites.text: Morurath is a quiet, mossy healing-cordial of the Grounded realm, brewed by wandering apothecaries who ferment bitter roots into a tonic that mends wounds and clears every lingering sickness from the blood. Its makers claim a single draught can restore half a traveler's strength, though the brew must be shared among the whole company to take effect.

rites.name: Pelanath
rites.text: Pelanath is a grounded, ordinary-sized concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a pale river-stone that a village cook keeps by the hearth to make bread rise. It carries a quiet, damp weight, hinting at small tidal rituals in the Grounded realm's remote estuary towns.

rites.name: Pelastar
rites.text: Pelastar is a bronze-hulled grounding anchor-engine of the Thudarneld lowland courts, built to hold tectonic tension steady beneath harbor cities. Its shepherds say it sings a low tone whenever the ground begins to shift, and that tone has saved more districts than any wall.

rites.name: Pelurdath
rites.text: Pelurdath is a quiet, glacial sentinel that slumbers within the frozen crater of the Hollow Tarn of Orvane. When its inner ice fractures, it releases a rolling pulse of cold that stiffens everything within a wide ring.

rites.name: Thedath
rites.text: Thedath is a Grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rattling strike that jolts the skull of a single target until their thoughts scatter. Its wielders are ordinary-sized beasts and drillers who favor a rhythmic knock to the head over raw force.

rites.name: Therudon
rites.text: Therudon is a gelatinous hunter-spirit of the grounded realms, a creature that lures prey into a rhythmic, swaying performance before it strikes. Its dance clouds the senses of every nearby creature, leaving them dazed and sluggish. Despite its unremarkable bulk, it can crush and dissolve a fallen beast with ease.

rites.name: Fenastoreld
rites.text: Fenastoreld is a quiet, grounded tinker-spirit of the Thudarneld hills, believed to appear whenever a traveler forgets to be afraid. Its gifts are small and practical, such as mending a cracked bell or coaxing a stubborn fire, and its influence never reaches far beyond the village it chooses to watch over.

rites.name: Pelalden
rites.text: Pelalden is a sandstone-skinned warden-spirit of the Ashwell Terraces, a dry highland where its kin roast slow fires to keep the rain-clouds from forming over the sacred grain fields. When it is roused it hurls its own molten core, a dense ember the size of a cart, which splits into a ring of burning seeds that scorch an area the length of a village street.

rites.name: Haladunon
rites.text: Haladunon is a quiet courier-sprite of the Grounded realm who delivers one swift, unremarkable tap to whatever stands in the way. Its strike is light enough to bruise a stone wall rather than break it, but it arrives before the eye can register the motion. Its tap is practised as a ritual of passage, not a weapon.

rites.name: Fenudarnar
rites.text: Fenudarnar is a rooted guardian of the Thudarneld grounded realm, a towering wooden sentinel whose bark-thick sap carries restorative sparks. It mends the wounds of companions who stand within its shade, though it cannot heal its own roots.

rites.name: Morudelde
rites.text: Morudelde is a grounded concept of a hexed sigil-gaze carved into the reflective eyes of a silent warden. Its single unbroken stare drains the courage and memory of whoever meets it, leaving them unable to recall their own skills. Wardens use it to guard sealed vaults where the stare is the only weapon ever needed.

rites.name: Halulden
rites.text: Halulden is a grounded concept of cracked-shell mortar charges used by the wardens of Thudarneld's northern moors to strip the hardened plating from iron-backed beasts. Its charges are said to loosen the bonds of any armored surface they touch, leaving the target exposed for a brief, costly window.

rites.name: Tharde
rites.text: Tharde is a hardened grave-warden of the Thudarneld lowlands, who keeps the sealed barrows of old river-kings and strikes only when a barrow's bindings begin to fail. Its quick, practiced cuts are said to sever a falling leaf before it lands, and its endurance comes from centuries of stone-dust rituals that harden the body.

rites.name: Kelarudock
rites.text: Kelarudock is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's Era E6, a quiet siphon of arcane reserves that unravels the mana of a single bearer until their well runs empty. Its wielders train it as a precise, almost surgical craft, reserved for duels and the disabling of mages rather than open destruction.

rites.name: Kelurnath
rites.text: Kelurnath is a tireless marksman-spirit of the Grounded realm, said to fire a single arrow that splits into a second before the first lands. Its presence in the mountain-passes of Thudarneld is marked by ringing bowstrings heard long after the archer has gone.

rites.name: Haludorock
rites.text: Haludorock is a quiet, stone-hearted sentinel of the Grounded realm, a concept of patient bedrock that wakes only when the valley beneath it begins to tremble. Its humming core can loose a rolling avalanche of granite that can bury a small village in an afternoon.

rites.name: Keluldaste
rites.text: Keluldaste is a dormant techne-ritual used by the Thudarneld lamp-keepers to briefly swell a bearer's muscular force, drawn from the sap of ember-trees. Its bursts are short and costly, leaving the user shaking for hours afterward.

rites.name: Brudosten
rites.text: Brudosten is a hidden gearwright-craft of the Thudarneld reaches, where lanterns of pressed ember-glass gather heat from a wielder's movements and feed it back into their next strike. Its artisans treat the process as a patient art, layering filaments so each swing stores a little more of the surge for the blow that follows.

rites.name: Bruste
rites.text: Bruste is a grounded concept of a warden-mage who binds the stormy tempers of Thudarneld's ridge-cities into weighted tethers. Its worn iron gauntlets are said to hold the force of a dropped millstone, and it ages slowly alongside the tall stone wardens it trained.

rites.name: Jorodock
rites.text: Jorodock is a grounded, self-guided munitions platform in the age of E6 that salvos six homing projectiles at once, each one tuned to strip away a fraction of a foe's remaining vitality. Its tactical doctrine favours the percentage-based strike, letting it wear down even the toughest targets without ever needing to deliver a single overwhelming blow.

rites.name: Halornock
rites.text: Halornock is a grounded combat technique of the Thudarneld cultivators, a discipline that splits a warrior's inner force into two opposed currents and releases them in a single cut. Practitioners are rare because the strain of holding both currents at once can tear the body apart, so only a few masters of the E6 era have ever mastered it.

rites.name: Haluldath
rites.text: Haluldath is a quiet, grounded ritual of the Thudarneld sky-scholars, a stored pressure that a practitioner draws from their own bones and releases as a single brutal shove. Its cultivators treat it as both a weapon and a warning, since the drawing-in takes long enough for an opponent to escape it.

rites.name: Thuradeld
rites.text: Thuradeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet siphoning ritual practiced by hollow-hearted wardens who draw vitality from rivals through a coiled tendril of living iron. Its practitioners are cautious and rarely fight at range, relying on close, precise strikes that leave their targets drained and their own reserves swelling. The technique is considered intimate and unsettling, a lesson in how strength can be borrowed rather than earned.

rites.name: Credeld
rites.text: Credeld is a quiet discipline practiced by hollow-boned wardens in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, a way of channeling kinetic patience into a single downward strike. Its adepts describe it as the art of letting the weight of a whole hillside arrive through the blade at once.

rites.name: Pelolderdon
rites.text: Pelolderdon is a grounded, low-stakes concept in the Thudarneld setting, a quiet sort of weather-wielding practice in its third age. Practitioners coax heavy overcast skies over a single companion, dimming the light and sharpening the shadows they carry. Its effects are modest, bounded by the reach of an ordinary storm front.

rites.name: Drerusteld
rites.text: Drerusteld is a grounded concept of stormforged tidal wardens who ride the undertow of Thudarneld's seas during the seventh age. Their signature rite drives a columned surge of brine and lightning toward a chosen target, scouring the sea floor where it lands.

rites.name: Keluldock
rites.text: Keluldock is a dormant ember-core lattice from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, seven ages old, whose sealed sparks drift through the shallow mines of the Rethkor hills. When disturbed, it releases a sudden burst of blinding glare that dazzles everything nearby for a short while.

rites.name: Thude
rites.text: Thude is a rhythmic technique in the Thudarneld cosmos, a stylized sequence of strikes timed to the pulse of local bells. Practitioners channel their footwork into resonant strikes that can shake loose stone and dull sound for kilometers around.

rites.name: Pelurath
rites.text: Pelurath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rhythmic pressure-discipline practiced by sentinels who channel tremor through their boots and palms. Its adepts can send a shuddering concussion through a stretch of stone or steel, shaking loose anything built upon it. The discipline is taught in the quiet valley fortresses of the E6 age.

rites.name: Drernusten
rites.text: Drernusten is a practiced fighting stance taught in the river-monasteries of Thudarneld, where students learn to coil their bodies so that each strike carries heat drawn from their own breath. Masters use it to split timber and shatter stone at close range, though few can hold it for long before they tire.

rites.name: Keloralden
rites.text: Keloralden is a wind-tempered duelist's technique from the grounded realm of Thudarneld, where a practitioner rises from a crouch in a single arcing slash that lifts a foe off the earth. It is taught only to those who have mastered their own restraint, and the blade's trailing gale can slam a victim back down in three rapid strikes.

rites.name: Moreduron
rites.text: Moreduron is a grounded, quietly unsettling concept in the Thudarneld universe, an entity that exists as a rumor of a shape pressed into fog over the marsh-towns of the E6 age. It has no true body to strike or be struck, and its power is simply the reason a crowd breaks and runs when it is seen. Its presence is felt most strongly by those who have already begun to doubt their own courage.

rites.name: Pelone
rites.text: Pelone is a rare, deliberately unstable crystal-cathedral bell drifting through the Grounded realm's seventh age, tolerant only of small, precise resonances. Its song can shatter a stone wall or a hollow of ice, but it hums itself apart if pushed much further.

rites.name: Jorene
rites.text: Jorene is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a whirling dance-form practiced by the wind-taught wardens of the Fenmere cliffs during the sixth era. Her spins gather loose dust and leaves into a spiraling column that can knock down a stone wall but never reaches beyond the valley she is in.

rites.name: Kelasten
rites.text: Kelasten is a ritual dance practiced by the wandering troupes of the Thudarneld highlands, where each measured step drains the reserve of mana held by those who watch. Dancers train for years to read the rhythm of an opponent's breath and strike the hidden wells of their power without a single blow. Its most feared form is performed in silence, so that the target feels their magic leaving before they understand why.

rites.name: Credulden
rites.text: Credulden is a grounded, low-stakes concept from the sixth era of Thudarneld, a wing-shaped gleam of light that scholars of the seventh age describe as a harmless dazzle. Its bearers use it to hush crowds and stir mild drowsiness, though its glow can briefly blind travelers who look too long.

rites.name: Drulden
rites.text: Drulden is a stone-hewn sentinel of the Thudarneld highlands, a warden of the dry plateaus whose hollow chest holds a resonant core. It breaks the stillness of the peaks with a single sharp strike that drives the breath from any rival and leaves them reeling.

rites.name: Peluldar
rites.text: Peluldar is a grounded concept of a bulwark-shaped stone-and-tallow shield that a village militia hoists when the river floods, drawing the water's force into its wooden rim. Its wearers claim it can turn aside a charging ox or a falling beam, though most of its protection comes from the discipline of the person behind it.

rites.name: Peloldar
rites.text: Peloldar is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a slow-drifting cloud of fenward spores that settles over crops and hollows out whatever it touches. Its hunger is measured by how much soil and root it can gather in a single season. Wardens track its path with pale copper bells strung along the ridgelines.

rites.name: Peladeldock
rites.text: Peladeldock is a grounded ritual technique of the Thudarneld ages, a wind-breath song that severs the fear binding a creature to its shadow. Wielders of the E6 era learned to unmake the will of an opponent with a single held note.

rites.name: Thadon
rites.text: Thadon is a grounded, unmagical sea-salt marsh in the lowlands of Thudarneld, where tidal farmers have learned to read the moods of the water. Its dikes are famous for holding back storm surges, and its oldest families still sing the tide-calls at dusk.

rites.name: Pelernurath
rites.text: Pelernurath is a grounded concept of a lone keeper who guards seeded crystals in the highland valleys of Thudarneld. Its signature act is a heavy, horn-driven charge that splits boulders and cracks the packed earth beneath its hooves.

rites.name: Tarneston
rites.text: Tarneston is a grounded, age-seven concept of quiet household charm, a small wind-powered mill that hums through the village. It stores breezes in copper coils and hands the stored motion to whoever leans on its crank.

rites.name: Bruldeld
rites.text: Bruldeld is a chitinous swarm-guardian of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld universe, a hovering insect-spirit whose wings hum with a drowsing frenzy that drives nearby allies into mindless rage. Its wing-beat can be snapped into a shockwave that rattles stone walls across a valley.

rites.name: Tholdudon
rites.text: Tholdudon is a swift wind-current spirit that threads between the high crags of Thudarneld, carrying storms across the grounded realm in narrow, looping rivers of air. It strikes in three quick gusts that can shear loose stone and bowl over small herds, and it wears down anyone who tries to chase it across the open highlands.

rites.name: Halestorde
rites.text: Halestorde is a concept of a grounded, weaponized exhalation that a creature of the seventh age can unleash to strip vitality from everyone within its gust. Those dropped to zero by the breath rise again hollowed and obedient to the breather's will. Its power is modest on the scale of the realm, enough to shatter a crowd rather than a building.

rites.name: Morestonath
rites.text: Morestonath is a thudding war-engine of hollowed granite and bronze-banded ribs, raised in the sixth age as a siege anchor for the stone-hauling clans of Thudarneld. It is said to dig its own foundations when it wakes, sinking deeper into the earth with each seasonal quake.

rites.name: Kelarnar
rites.text: Kelarnar is a Grounded concept of a single relentless marksman-spirit that lives within the rifling of old hunting weapons across the Thudarneld. Its signature is a piercing shot that gathers the whole weight of a sighting, undone only by the one who refuses to flinch.

rites.name: Crurnock
rites.text: Crurnock is a grounded war-automaton of the E6 age, three years out of its forge-yards and still learning the rhythm of its own joints. It fights by unleashing a rapid storm of strikes, each one short and precise, that can shatter armor plating in a single afternoon.

rites.name: Braldeld
rites.text: Braldeld is a grounded martial mentor who fights with a rune-carved iron shield and a chain-whip, rallying nearby allies with defensive wards. Its training halls in the valley of Oss Harrow are said to have taught generations of guardians to hold their ground under any blow.

rites.name: Fenoradath
rites.text: Fenoradath is a grounded mortal-force concept from the Thudarneld reckoning, a hooded seer who unravels a foe's vital threads with a slow, unavoidable gaze. Its judgment requires eight breaths of stillness, and once cast it cannot be called again for a long quarter-hour.

rites.name: Fenudar
rites.text: Fenudar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet sorcerous art that binds a wandering spirit into a living body for a single fatal moment. Its practitioners are said to lose a piece of their own presence each time the rite is performed, leaving them drifting at the edges of their own households.

rites.name: Drurdon
rites.text: Drurdon is a grounded Thudarneld concept of a lone sellsword whose twin serrated blades strike in rapid pairs, each cut leaving a lingering toxin in the wound. Known to hunters as the Adder of Gorrow Fen, Drurdon fights with a paced, deliberate rhythm that makes every strike a calculated sting.

rites.name: Kelordon
rites.text: Kelordon is a grounded, low-stakes healing-wind device used by wandering herb-witches in the Thudarneld hill country, a breeze that unknots curses, fevers, and clinging poisons from a gathered company.
