It drains a small reservoir of the wearer's calm each use and needs a long pause before it can breathe again.

rites.name: Brestar
rites.text: Brestar is a grounded, bench-scale concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed reactor-core casing that harvests stored heat from a village's thermal springs. It is designed to power small workshops and communal kilns rather than anything dramatic.

rites.name: Fenuldon
rites.text: Fenuldon is a grounded concept of a relay-archer order in the Thudarneld frontier, whose members loose a rapid volley of heated bolts from a single drawn string. Each sentence of its legend records a bow-trick passed down by apprentices, and the order values the discipline that lets one draw become several. Its name is spoken with the same care as the weapon it names.

rites.name: Thasturdock
rites.text: Thasturdock is a grounded concept from the E6 era, an invented deck-drawing art whose practitioners stack their decks with mana-restoring cards. Its most famous use is by a student named Revalor Pennock, who draws a single card that can refill a mage's reserves mid-duel.

rites.name: Tharnure
rites.text: Tharnure is a pale, thread-like drifter in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, known for slipping through the hours of others and taking their stillness for itself. Its pockets hold the quiet of stopped clocks, which it lends out in small, bargained portions to fishermen and kings alike.

rites.name: Thurath
rites.text: Thurath is a grounded, cult-favored artifact-technique of the E6 era, a sealed resonance-lattice that folds local motion into a held stillness before releasing it all at once. Its wielders are archivists who spend decades learning when to hold and when to let go. Its signature release is a precise, bounded shockwave that can level a small workshop or fracture a stone bridge.

rites.name: Thenuste
rites.text: Thenuste is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a lattice-woven shrine-engine that stores the tremors of quarrying bells and releases them as directed shockwaves. It was built in the sixth epoch to steady unstable hillsides, and it still hums beneath the seventh age's mountain roads.

rites.name: Morune
rites.text: Morune is a grounded weapon-dancer of the Thudarneld reach who treats a spiked iron flail as an extension of her own spine. In her signature turn she spins until the air itself howls, sending the nearest foes skidding backward across the stones.

rites.name: Bredar
rites.text: Bredar is a grounded soldier's discipline of the Thudarneld realm, a set of six martial techniques taught in the frontier duelling halls. Its practitioners trade raw fury for measured precision, sharpening blows until a single strike can break a stone wall and strengthening their comrades with stirring shouts before battle.

rites.name: Thestock
rites.text: Thestock is a reckless gambler-engine of a waystation, a thing that has no real will of its own but tips a single hidden ratchet every time someone lays a wager against its pitted iron face. Its strength is measured in the sum of all bets made around it, so it is most dangerous at festivals when the crowd bets heavily.

rites.name: Pelarnerath
rites.text: Pelarnerath is a lantern-bearing duelist of the Grounded realm's seventh age, known for a stance that steadies the gaze before the blade moves. Its practitioners hold a single guarded posture for five breaths at a time, and in that span the world seems to slow to their measured pace.

rites.name: Drerneld
rites.text: Drerneld is a grounded, mid-scale crystalline tradition of the E6 era, its name used for a hymn-bound practice in which a single sentry channels stored sunlight into a focused burst. Its practitioners are said to fire these bursts only at the wardens of sealed valleys, and each burst leaves the target briefly brittle to whatever follows.

rites.name: Halurnen
rites.text: Halurnen is a grounded, aging technique in the Thudarneld cosmos, a slow hush that drains the vigor from a single target over the course of a long breath. It is taught in quiet monastic houses where practitioners learn to dim rather than destroy. Its strongest use can unravel a thick stone wall into dust over several minutes.

rites.name: Brornuldock
rites.text: Brornuldock is a grounded, era-E6 concept: a hand-thrown bomb of unmatched force, forged by the artificers of its realm and carried by those who need to break through what stands in their way. Its power is said to rise with the wielder's strength and fortune, so a lucky hand can shatter a wall that would stop an army.

rites.name: Morenar
rites.text: Morenar is a stone-hewn stance taught in the lowland guild halls of Thudarneld, where practitioners plant their feet and let the bedrock speak through their bones. It is valued for rooting a fighter against a charging foe rather than for any spectacular blow.

rites.name: Tholdere
rites.text: Tholdere is a ward-craft of the Grounded realm, a layered shielding discipline in which practitioners bind protective sigils to a bearer's breath and pulse. Its wards blunt hexes, fevers, and fear before they can take hold, and the older masters say a well-set ward can outlast the fear it was meant to hold back.

rites.name: Fenedulde
rites.text: Fenedulde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a rift-stitching art whose practitioners fold the surrounding terrain into a pocket where a foe can be lost. Its single named tactic, the Hollow Seam, pulls a wounded ally out of the fight and seals them away for good.

rites.name: Halerudath
rites.text: Halerudath is a quiet, grounded lattice of frozen tide-stones that hold a single moment in place for those who stand upon them. Its residents rely on the stillness to rest, though a careless lean on its surface can lock a traveler in place for hours.

rites.name: Cruneld
rites.text: Cruneld is a grounded, everyday mechanical tool used by the mining guilds of Thudarneld to clear rockfalls and loosen compacted seams. Its heavy weighted head is swung on a counterbalanced arm, delivering blows that can crack a boulder or stun a stubborn burrowing beast.

rites.name: Fenude
rites.text: Fenude is a grounded scent-warding craft from the sixth era of Thudarneld, where hunters follow prey by smell across the wetlands. Its practitioners rub a pale resin onto the skin and soaked cloth to erase their trail, allowing a fleeing traveler to vanish from the pursuing beasts' noses. The technique must be applied only after the hunter has been outdistanced or stunned, since any blow from a pursuer dissolves the resin's hold.

rites.name: Tharnock
rites.text: Tharnock is a grounded war-thing of the E6 age, a lean warrior-automaton of hammered bronze who cuts in three swift arcs and sends foes reeling. Its strikes are measured and sure, meant to unbalance rather than annihilate. Few survive the third stroke.

rites.name: Craldock
rites.text: Craldock is a hearth-glow that the people of Thudarneld kindle from river-stones in the Grounded realm, its light mending small wounds and tired limbs of anyone who stands within it. It is a concept of care rather than of force, so its strongest acts are measured in the warmth it can spread across a village and not in destruction.

rites.name: Morurodeld
rites.text: Morurodeld is a quiet, humming discipline practiced by the tide-wardens of Thudarneld, who channel ember-bright heat through their palms to dry storm-soaked nets and warm frozen harbor stones. In the seventh age its adherents are rare, and most use it only for mending boats and thawing the winter docks.

rites.name: Moranon
rites.text: Moranon is a dormant ember-stone of the Grounded realm, prized by hermit smiths who fuse its glow into ritual lanterns. Its one great act is a sudden flare that briefly lights an entire valley in silver fire, leaving the stone cold and inert for seasons afterward.

rites.name: Jorerock
rites.text: Jorerock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a trembling cliff-spirit that hurls splinters of its own basalt hide at foes. Its quills are carved from the bedrock of an age-seven epoch and can pierce armor but rarely more.

rites.name: Pelerurdeld
rites.text: Pelerurdeld is a sharpened sliver of threshold-glass that its wielders hone until it cuts through any guard in a single hungry motion. Those who master it are said to hear the moment a defense lets go, and the blade rewards that patience with four quick strikes.

rites.name: Keleston
rites.text: Keleston is a grounded concept of a sealed mountain forge-city where craftsmen tune resonant crystal cannons that fire bursts of compressed sunlight. Its artisans guard the old tuning rites, and the bursts are rarely fired outside of ceremonial trials. The ceiling_T of 10 means the energy scale stays modest, so the largest acts are measured in the low tens of billions of joules.

rites.name: Jorernon
rites.text: Jorernon is a dormant rage-engine sealed within the ashen spires of Thudarneld's eastern wastes, a construct of hardened grief that stirs only when a bearer's fury peaks. When it wakes, the blade-like bulwarks along its spine erupt in a shockwave of pure resentment that tears the air apart.

rites.name: Haledon
rites.text: Haledon is a concept of hard-won reflex in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, where the last spark of a wounded body is said to fire a single unbidden surge of motion. Those who have learned to trust it call it the second breath, while cautious healers treat it as a warning bell that rings only when the flesh is nearly spent.

rites.name: Thonuldar
rites.text: Thonuldar is a sacred-light rite of the Grounded realm, in which a cantor's chime dissolves the lingering curses and paralyses that cling to a body. The light is gentle by design, meant to lift afflictions from one soul at a time rather than to scour the world. Its practitioners guard the rite jealously, for it is the only cure the grounded folk trust when the tides of ill-fortune turn against them.

rites.name: Pelarden
rites.text: Pelarden is a quiet hymn-sigil of the Grounded realm, a lantern-shaped focus that gathers the warmth of nearby bearers into their next strike. Its first blow carries the stored light, while follow-up strokes after a miss steady the wielder's aim, and foes struck by it find their own reserves of resolve drained.

rites.name: Halustene
rites.text: Halustene is a dormant cosmic lattice that wakes only when its last keeper dies, then pulls the surrounding dark back into the stone it was made from. Its returning pulse can unmake nearby matter in a hush, and once it has learned a shape it can resist that shape for ages.

rites.name: Halarneston
rites.text: Halarneston is a grounded, era-six crystalline gearwork ward that hums with suppressed pressure, its residents long trained to freeze their limbs in place during tremors. Its signature hazard is a wall-bound resonance that locks every nearby body in place for a few heartbeats.

rites.name: Drerdon
rites.text: Drerdon is a grounded, frost-bound warrior-artisan of Thudarneld's sixth era, known for striking foes with stored winter. Its cold-forged blade can deliver two rapid chilling strokes that shatter a wall of ice or armored stone, and it can coat its own weapon in biting frost for several turns.

rites.name: Thornade
rites.text: Thornade is a radiant hymn of thorned light, a bright storm that gathers in the high reaches of Thudarneld and bursts across the valley in a wide ring of pale fire. Its scorched glyphs linger on stone long after the blast fades.

rites.name: Keluldorath
rites.text: Keluldorath is a drifting circus-ship that wanders the grey reaches of Thudarneld, its crew of tumblers and jugglers hurling flaming wicks and gleaming hooks at anything that threatens them. Its performers treat every fight as a routine, tossing their tricks with cheerful randomness and leaving rivals dazed, scorched, or stuck in place.

rites.name: Haloldar
rites.text: Haloldar is a weathered stone-sculpted sentinel of the Grounded realm, bound to the slow pulse of the seventh age's bedrock. Its footsteps set the soil humming in rhythm, and it can stamp a field of earth into rolling waves that toss anything standing upon it.

rites.name: Tarneston
rites.text: Tarneston is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a reliable sort of quiet tool that has been passed down among the builders of the lower terraces. Its owners treat it as a discipline as much as a technique, drawing on it when the bedrock itself must be made to answer.

rites.name: Pelarnath
rites.text: Pelarnath is a grounded protective ward-craft from the Thudarneld cosmos, a shimmering barrier woven by hearth-wardens to shield villages from wind and small beasts. It is a concept of humble scale, its power measured in the strength of a shelter rather than the force of a blast.

rites.name: Moradon
rites.text: Moradon is a concept of a grounded, unassuming trait in the Thudarneld universe: a hard-shelled dampening field that a person can wrap around their own strikes to blunt an opponent's striking strength. It works only at close range and only against physical force, leaving it useless against thought or magic.

rites.name: Pelanath
rites.text: Pelanath is a spoken rite of the Thudarneld orator-scholars, in which a speaker recounts a warrior's deeds until the listener's courage swells beyond its usual bounds. Its effect is strictly personal and fades within a single breath of the speech ending. Crowds have been known to fall silent before it, as if the air itself were holding its breath.

rites.name: Keluroste
rites.text: Keluroste is a grounded, slow-creeping blight that drifts through the lowland fens of Thudarneld, sapping the momentum of anything it touches until stone itself grows sluggish and heavy. Its presence is subtle, lingering for generations in the marsh reeds where it was first born. Scholars of the region regard it as a lesson in patience rather than a true threat.

rites.name: Pelardode
rites.text: Pelardode is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a stacking tier of weapon-training that refines a warrior's raw striking strength in steps, with each rank replacing the last rather than adding to it. Its practitioners in the third age of the Sixth era channel these refinements into heavy, wide-arc blows that can topple a stone wall. Its strongest rank is written to shatter a fortified gate in a single swing.

rites.name: Crurneld
rites.text: Crurneld is a grounded tremor-engine forged in the quarries of the Thudarneld frontier, a slow-burning construct that stores seismic pressure in layered basalt plates. When its plates are struck in unison it unleashes a rolling quake that cracks foundations across an entire valley.

rites.name: Halostalde
rites.text: Halostalde is a stone-hewn gauntlet forged in the cracked foothills of Thudarneld, where every strike drinks the vitality of the ground it lands upon. Its wielders are rarely seen far from the quarries that supply their ore. The gauntlet grows heavier with each victory, as if the land itself were lending its weight.

rites.name: Jorestoldar
rites.text: Jorestoldar is a bladed duet of two fighters who move in such precise unison that they carve through a scattering of foes, each strike chosen at random by the wind. Their final cut is said to be heavier than the rest combined, and they can sustain their rhythm for hours without tiring. The pair are the marrow of the Grounded realm's border guard in the seventh age.

rites.name: Moranon
rites.text: Moranon is a sworn lantern-keeper of the Grounded realm who burns his own vitality to kindle his companions' strength for a brief span. When his reserves run low he falls into a near-death stillness, guarded by his allies until he wakes.

rites.name: Drodarne
rites.text: Drodarne is a silent stone-shaping engine that rings with a low hum whenever a fault line under the Thudarneld plains begins to stir. Its keepers believe it swallows the tremor and returns it as a single controlled strike, rather than letting the land split.

rites.name: Morardudath
rites.text: Morardudath is a grounded spear-duellist of the Thudarneld reaches, known for a two-handed lunge that drives the foe skyward before the second blade completes the arc. Its hymns are sung by wandering mercenaries who claim the style was taught by mountain wind. It is a short-reach technique rewarded by quick, repeated strikes.

rites.name: Brardath
rites.text: Brardath is a dim, stubbornly cheerful rooftop tinkerer of the Grounded realm, known across the Thudarneld neighborhoods for turning every rusted gadget into a nuisance that keeps people looking his way. Stories say his pranks once disabled a whole market's weighing scales for a week, and the tallies of his small mischiefs fill three ledgers in the guild hall.

rites.name: Keluldardon
rites.text: Keluldardon is a grounded, mid-scale concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hollow-ember technique worked into the shells of a fourth-age stone tradition. It is a force that gathers quietly inside a vessel and releases all at once when the vessel is struck or set down.

rites.name: Dreldar
rites.text: Dreldar is a hand-cranked bore-engine of the Grounded realm, a squat iron carapace that spins a fluted spear-head through stone and tempered plate alike. Its operators, the Hollow Wardens of Qesh, use it to open sealed vaults and collapse rival tunnels. Its wielder can pierce any armour that has no living heart behind it.

rites.name: Morusteld
rites.text: Morusteld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a rhythmic surge of pressure that builds in the chest of a wandering drummer before bursting outward. Its power is modest, measured in the force of a collapsing wooden barn rather than anything cosmic. It is a legendary pulse that tradesmen swear by and no one has ever fully explained.

rites.name: Crasteld
rites.text: Crasteld is a crescent-bladed reaping technique practiced by wandering scythe-monks of the Thudarneld frontier, who believe a clean cut can separate a sleeper from their own shadow. Its strikes are fast and surgical, meant to sever tethers rather than shatter bodies.

rites.name: Fenudon
rites.text: Fenudon is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a soft hum of attention passed between sleepers and the dreaming bells that answer them. Its practitioners lean close and speak in a murmur that carries a warmth into weary bodies and tired halls. The concept is valued for how gently it mends, never for raw force.

rites.name: Haleston
rites.text: Haleston is a grounded concept, a hidden trait passed between the wardens of a salt-marsh town. Its bearers can gather their wounds and grief into one brief surge of shadowy strength that lasts only a few heartbeats.

rites.name: Thedanar
rites.text: Thedanar is a concept of quiet, rehearsed mastery that Thudarneld's guild-scholars teach as a discipline of hidden technique. Its practitioners learn a sequence of gestures that channel the body's own momentum into precise, controlled effects, from mending wounds to shielding allies. Its authored strength sits at the scale of a single household or a stubborn stone wall.

rites.name: Crurnastock
rites.text: Crurnastock is a fading, veil-like spirit that drifts through the mist-choked hollows of Thudarneld, rendering nearby companions unseen to the eyes of their enemies. It is a quiet guardian rather than a weapon, its power measured in concealment and the brief, shimmering moments it can keep a fleeing band hidden.

rites.name: Crodustath
rites.text: Crodustath is a rite of the Thudarneld grounded realm, a mind-tempering discipline that surges within a practitioner once their vitality has nearly guttered away. In its frenzy the bearer's strikes grow heedless and fierce, though their judgment is clouded by the fury. It is taught to those who fight on when all reason says to yield.

rites.name: Brarne
rites.text: Brarne is a grounded, era-six pressure-discharge technique that a wandering duelist can call up by spending their own vitality, turning personal stamina into a single crushing blow. It is taught only to those who have survived the drill-camps of the lowland garrisons. The discharge is brief but leaves its user drained for days.

rites.name: Tharden
rites.text: Tharden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a melodic rite of guardian-song that stirs the dormant spirit of wild groves and rivers. Its practitioners sing old lullabies to coax stone and water into holding their shape during floods and quakes. The art moves the land gently rather than breaking it.

rites.name: Pelardelden
rites.text: Pelardelden is a quiet ward-sigil traced onto the collar of a warden's cloak, lending a steady shield of hardness to every companion who stands inside its circle. Its glow lingers for half an hour after each renewal, and wardens say it turns a blade's bite into a dull knock. The sigil must be re-inked every sixteen heartbeats, or the protection gutters out.

rites.name: Fenastelde
rites.text: Fenastelde is a grounded operational command, a single directive an engineered sentinel issues to erase a designated target from the work roster. It is a clean, mechanical act that leaves the executor slightly worn after every use.

rites.name: Kelerdar
rites.text: Kelerdar is a rolling tide-engine of the Grounded realm, a stone-hulled contraption that channels the pressure of underground springs into sudden lurching strikes. Its keepers call it the patient fist of the valleys, though the machine itself has never once been seen at rest.

rites.name: Fenurdock
rites.text: Fenurdock is a storm-wracked grounded realm of 7 ages where ancient tuning-towers channel lightning through the bedrock. Its inhabitants have learned to cast bolts of humming charge, each named for the level of attunement they require.

rites.name: Joraldeld
rites.text: Joraldeld is a sealed brass-and-leather cuff worn by drifting wardens of the Thudarneld frontier, who bind a fleeting pulse of stored breath into the wrist. Once set, it lends the wearer a sharper hand and quicker feet, and it can be unleashed as a rapid fivefold strike that rattles stone walls. Its charge takes half a second to ready and must rest nearly half a minute before it can be loosed again.

rites.name: Bruste
rites.text: Bruste is a grounded clawed brawler from the era of the sixth age, a creature that tears through shields and wards with a single raking strike. Its claws strip away protective enchantments from anyone it hits, leaving allies exposed to the next blow.

rites.name: Brernoldock
rites.text: Brernoldock is a hulking iron-bound warden of the Grounded realm, its forge-scarred plates ringing like struck bells whenever it moves. Its signature technique is a flurry of eleven rapid chain-blows followed by a single crushing overhead hammer that splits stone beneath it.

rites.name: Thodastar
rites.text: Thodastar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a resonant lattice of brass-stone filaments that hums through the seventh age of the E6 era. It is a tool that stores and returns the stresses of its surroundings, turning a quiet city's tremors into sudden bursts of force.

rites.name: Thosterden
rites.text: Thosterden is a mundane-scale combat technique, drilled by wandering blade-dancers who sway through a rhythmic hymn to build force in a single heavy stroke. Its practitioners are known for steady, measured strikes rather than spectacle, and the art is passed down through apprenticeships in the Grounded realm.

rites.name: Haludath
rites.text: Haludath is a grounded battle-spell woven by the lantern-scholars of Thudarneld, a conjured giantess of pale ink and cinder who stands over the field and unleashes one crushing wave of shadowed force. Her presence hardens the caster's skin and steadies their breath for a single turn, sheltering them from the blows that follow.

rites.name: Joroste
rites.text: Joroste is a pale, reed-thin healer of the Grounded realm who mends clouded sight by pressing a cold mineral lens to the eyelids of the afflicted. Her ministrations are gentle and leave the body only slightly tired, and she is known across seven ages for never charging a fee for restoring a child's vision.

rites.name: Kelastornen
rites.text: Kelastornen is a quiet crafting discipline in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, where artisans bind weathered stone into humming lattices that can briefly shake a town's foundations. Its practitioners are rarely seen outside the guild halls of the E6 era, which is why the art is considered both dangerous and respected. Its name is said to mean 'the patient fracture' in the old tongue.

rites.name: Kelure
rites.text: Kelure is a lightweight stride-technique practiced by the wind-wardens of Thudarneld's lower terraces, allowing a runner to skim over soft ground and brief air. It is a grounded art, used for crossing marshes and dodging falling debris rather than for any cosmic display.

rites.name: Moroneld
rites.text: Moroneld is a rolling stone-lattice golem of the Grounded realm, a slow-walking monument that coils its limbs into a crushing spiral when cornered. Its wandering is said to have carved the valleys of Thudarneld over seven ages.

rites.name: Tharnar
rites.text: Tharnar is a grounded concept of heavy stone-kept oaths, a mountain-sized guardian whose vows bind the land beneath Thudarneld. Its strength is patience rather than spectacle, measured in the weight of fallen cliffs and the endurance of long winters. It rarely wields its full force, preferring to hold ground until the storm passes.

rites.name: Moroden
rites.text: Moroden is a grounded, concept-only combat technique from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a mechanical art of hurling a volley of heated, self-igniting shards at surrounding foes. Its practitioners are warned by a sharp shout before each barrage lands. The technique is famed for scorching everything in a wide ring, though its devastation stays within the scale of a single neighbourhood.

rites.name: Tarnudonock
rites.text: Tarnudonock is a grounded, pincered creature of the Thudarneld world, a tall chitin-plated stalker that hunts across the salt flats of the lower basins. It has a slow, deliberate temperament and is said to remember the exact weight of every prey it has ever closed upon.

rites.name: Halornadeld
rites.text: Halornadeld is a discipline of the open-palm strike, taught in the quiet monasteries of Thudarneld and forbidden to anyone who has not first learned to still their own breath. Its practitioners are said to drive a single blow through layered walls of stone and bone, though most would call such a claim exaggerated.

rites.name: Joradeld
rites.text: Joradeld is a grim oath-bound warrior of the Ashen Covenant, who trades a portion of their own vitality for a surge of crushing force. Their signature technique, the Hollow Pact, burns a fraction of their life to unleash a shockwave that strikes every foe nearby. They wield a blade named Mourncutter, forged from a fallen star's shard.

rites.name: Halenurnock
rites.text: Halenurnock is a dormant, self-repairing bulwark of woven granite-glass that stands at the edge of the Thudarneld tidal flats, guarding a sunken archive of old oaths. When a hostile force approaches, its ribbed plates rotate to shield the valley behind it, raising the defensive strength of every nearby settlement.

rites.name: Fenoldareld
rites.text: Fenoldareld is a restorative rite-fire kindled from three hearth-coals stacked in a ring, its warm light washing away every clinging curse and sickness from all within its reach. Scholars of the Grounded realm note it also refills the spirit-reserve of those it touches by half, though the flame cannot mend what has already been broken.

rites.name: Fenunock
rites.text: Fenunock is a concept of a grounded failure that arrives when a wager comes up empty, dropping heavy crockery and debris onto unsuspecting bystanders. Its falling weight is modest, though its timing seems to strike hardest against those who least expected it.

rites.name: Tharock
rites.text: Tharock is a concept of rising momentum: the more fully it stands within its own vitality, the more each strike it lands is amplified by the strikes before it. Its feats are modest, scaled to the grounded era of Thudarneld, where a single well-timed chain can crack stone and nothing more.

rites.name: Peloston
rites.text: Peloston is a grounded, quiet inventor-scholar of the E6 era, known for coaxing storms into jars for lighthouse keepers and village mills. Seven years old as a concept, it is a catalyst-focused entry whose skill with charged currents lets it redirect rather than unleash force.

rites.name: Braston
rites.text: Braston is a grounded marksman's hand-cannon from the Thudarneld workshops of the Eighth Ridge, its rounds carrying a soft-chemistry core that dulls an opponent's armor for a short while. Its wielders value it less for raw force than for the quiet advantage it gives in long standoffs.

rites.name: Kelurar
rites.text: Kelurar is a quiet hush-sigil worn as a ring of braided ash-cord, said to hold back the sound of a whole valley when its bearer moves through a tense crowd. In the grounded era of Thudarneld it is less a weapon than a social tool, and its wearers are trained to stop arguments by stepping into them.

rites.name: Tharen
rites.text: Tharen is a grounded tool of the Thudarneld Concept, a heavy hydraulic hammer-gauntlet that its wielders drive into the earth to shake loose buried stone. Its wielders channel the recoil so the strike launches them forward across the field before they land.

rites.name: Fenustolde
rites.text: Fenustolde is a fire-tempered sword-technique taught in the mountain forges of Thudarneld, where smiths and swordsmen share a single discipline of heat and breath. Its practitioners strike in heat-shimmer, leaving afterimages that burn for a moment after the blade has passed.

rites.name: Crestordath
rites.text: Crestordath is a gentle, luminous ward woven into the flowing robes of the Thudarneld sentinels, a soft shimmer that knits wounds closed over a short span of heartbeats. It is a healing field rather than a weapon, and its sentinels guard it with quiet pride.

rites.name: Kelerorde
rites.text: Kelerorde is a rhythmic battle-chant practiced by the wardens of Thudarneld's low hills, a mental cadence that steadies a fighter's muscles and sharpens their reach. Its wardens teach that a single well-timed verse can lend a porter the strength to lift a fallen beam. The chant has no lasting power beyond the body that performs it.

rites.name: Fenelde
rites.text: Fenelde is a wandering chorus-art that binds a crowd's shared memories into a resonant hymn, letting its singer carry a village's sorrows and joys like a lantern. Its practitioners in the Grounded realm use it to steady frightened towns, though overuse can leave a singer hollow for seasons.

rites.name: Thadeld
rites.text: Thadeld is a grounded ceremonial skill of the Thudarneld reckoning, where a chosen speaker kindles a slow amber glow along the bones of the hand. The glow can scorch an opponent's cloak or ignite a dry reed bundle, though its reach never extends past a single arm's length.

rites.name: Pelernorde
rites.text: Pelernorde is a grounded, quiet domain of the E6 era, a tidal marsh where reed-cutters sing their names to the water. Its people hold that a voice carried far enough can shrink the proud to the size of a thumbnail, and this is taught as both a warning and a craft.

rites.name: Morunock
rites.text: Morunock is a pale, humming gravity-lens that the Thudarneld cartographers filed as a concept rather than a creature, a dense pocket of drifting stillness drawn over the settled plains. Its keepers use it to fold dust and shadow into a single hard sphere that can be hurled a few streets at a time.

rites.name: Jorerne
rites.text: Jorerne is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a sealed clerical rite in which a single scribe inscribes the names of wrongdoers onto a bronze tablet to pass a verdict upon them. Its power is measured in the weight of testimony rather than in force, and the act is said to strike with the force of a falling bell.

rites.name: Tarnaldar
rites.text: Tarnaldar is a grounded concept-kind entry from the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed glass-bell arcade where light is bottled and sold by the measure. Its keepers are wind-tuned mechanics who test each charge against a tuning fork before it is allowed to leave the hall.

rites.name: Kelornock
rites.text: Kelornock is a grounded-realm lullaby-stepper of the E6 age, a wandering performer whose slow, swaying rhythm lulls foes into drowsy stillness. Its footwork can drop a single opponent into a deep, pleasant slumber about half the time, costing a small reserve of its inner power each time it dances.

rites.name: Breldunen
rites.text: Breldunen is a drifting gleam-wardens' lantern-fortress that hums a low ward over the valley of Ossel-Mire, shielding travelers from the sharp glare of the Sunken Choir. Its keepers can flare the lanterns into a brief dome that softens hostile spells for a single turn.

rites.name: Pelastudock
rites.text: Pelastudock is a grounded, mundane-scale technique in the Thudarneld world, a drilled stance by which a practitioner sharpens the cast of their own sorcerous focus for a brief span. Its effect amplifies the potency of the practitioner's workings, whether those are wards or restorative charms.

rites.name: Fenoldudon
rites.text: Fenoldudon is a slow, hypnotic rhythm-dance performed in the mist-choked valleys of Thudarneld, its steps said to tangle the minds of rival sorcerers until their spells lose their shape. Its practitioners hold that the dance draws out the weaving of the spell's own threads rather than striking any foe directly.

rites.name: Pelerodar
rites.text: Pelerodar is a cold-forged glassy plate of quiet resonance, grown from the slag of an extinct tide-engine in the Thudarneld reaches. Wardens of the Grounded era bind it to bridge-footings, where it hums softly and stores the weight of passing ships. Its only recorded violence came the day a flood-gate shattered and the plate sang the riverbed flat.

rites.name: Thorneld
rites.text: Thorneld is a grounded concept of a barbed wooden sentinel that halts whatever its chosen target has already begun to do. Its power is subtle rather than explosive, and it is most often used to snap the rhythm of an attacker mid-motion.

rites.name: Fenelde
rites.text: Fenelde is a grounded spirit of the Thudarneld marshes, a sluggish hovering weaver of dim lanterns that drifts above still water. Its only known act is to gather a faint pale gloom into a hollow bead and release it in a ring, numbing whatever stands close.

rites.name: Halenar
rites.text: Halenar is a quickening tenet of the Thudarneld powers, letting a caster hasten the gathering of a working so that its formation takes a fraction of the usual time. Practitioners in the Grounded realm prize it above raw strength, since a spell finished before a rival can react often decides a duel. The tenet is taught in the third age of the E6 schools as a discipline of breath and intent.

rites.name: Moreden
rites.text: Moreden is a grounded, era-six concept of cold-weather sorcery, seven ages into its own history, that channels a freezing discharge through ordinary frost-sheathed staves. Its practitioners harden their breath and blood against the cold, treating a wintry blast as a bounded tool rather than a catastrophe.

rites.name: Brode
rites.text: Brode is a hand-stitched sound-pulse drum worn across a courier's shoulders in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, tuned by the guild of resonance tailors. Its wielders can rattle a crowd's bones and knock loose cobblestones with a single resonant clap.

rites.name: Brarnude
rites.text: Brarnude is a tidal sentinel of the Grounded realm that stands in the flooded ruins of Quoll Harbor, its ribbed carapace weeping brine. When intruders approach, it fires a compressed column of seawater that punches a crater through reinforced stone.

rites.name: Drurnen
rites.text: Drurnen is a sun-scorched prairie lantern-beast of Thudarneld whose hide stores daylight in pale amber veins. When threatened it flares its crest into a blinding corona that dazzles every creature nearby and draws all hostile attention toward itself.

rites.name: Morurastath
rites.text: Morurastath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a slow hush of frost that rolls across the pale highlands of its era, numbing whatever it touches. Its power is measured in the bitter stillness it leaves behind, not in violent force.

rites.name: Therdade
rites.text: Therdade is a grounded, weathered relic from the seventh age of the Thudarneld cycle, a mud-caked rope-ferry that sinks under the weight of its own cargo. It serves as a common tool for hauling grain across the flooded marshes of the lowland cantons. Its frame is said to have been forged from the keel of a drowned barge, which accounts for its stubborn endurance.

rites.name: Brestarock
rites.text: Brestarock is a stone-skinned colossus from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, forged in the seventh age when the mountain-kings sealed their oaths into living bedrock. It channels the weight of its own mass into a single, shuddering stomp that splits the ground for leagues.

rites.name: Morurdock
rites.text: Morurdock is a grounded, low-tier combatant of the Thudarneld omniverse, a stubborn ferryman who fights with a hooked iron pole. Its strikes are measured and precise, built for crowd control rather than wide destruction. It is known for holding a ferry landing against armed raiders for entire nights.

rites.name: Thurar
rites.text: Thurar is a grounded, almost mundane ember-weaver of the E6 age, a figure of village hearths and forge-lamps who has lived seven centuries of quiet craft. Its strongest acts are the kind that scorch a barn or a fleet of wooden boats rather than reshape any land.

rites.name: Fenustoldar
rites.text: Fenustoldar is a glacial hunter-spirit of the Grounded realm's seventh age, who stalks mountain passes and drains warmth from travelers' breath. It binds its frost into needle-thin lances that pierce armor and can be fed with stolen heat to freeze a river's width in one breath.

rites.name: Kelerneld
rites.text: Kelerneld is a frost-lattice weave of crystallized thermal shadow that its wardens unfurl over a battlefield, numbing every living thing inside it at once. It is a mundane tool of the Grounded realm, lighter than a sword in its reach, yet it bites every ally and foe alike.

rites.name: Tarnaden
rites.text: Tarnaden is a grounded, mortal-scale concept in Thudarneld, a fire-breathing creature whose exhalation scorches a crowd of foes at once. It holds its breath for a short, deliberate moment before releasing a wave of heat that can be drawn upon again only after a long rest.

rites.name: Pelodernock
rites.text: Pelodernock is a rolling clay-hued sentinel of the Grounded realm, a patient mountain-walker that answers each approaching storm with a barrage of stone-rhythmed thumps. Its strikes come in swift cascading volleys, ending with a leap that leaves the ground cracked behind it.

rites.name: Credoldath
rites.text: Credoldath is a grounded concept of a lathe-cut disc-blade, forged in the third age of the Thudarneld cycle, that its wielders spin on a cord to strike a ring of foes at once. Its edge is said to hum with the pitch of the bell-foundries where it was first tempered.

rites.name: Kelurdar
rites.text: Kelurdar is a drifting ironwood sentinel of the Grounded realm's seventh age, whose root-lattice hums with stored tremor. It strikes with a rapid pair of crescent-shaped blows that break the air itself into a shrieking gale.

rites.name: Pelaldath
rites.text: Pelaldath is a grounded, fourth-age concept of a shared pulse-weapon wielded by two linked wardens who must synchronise their breath and focus before discharging it. The resulting blast is a dense, non-elemental shockwave that overwhelms a single target while leaving the surrounding terrain largely untouched.

rites.name: Joronudar
rites.text: Joronudar is a tidal shrine-spirit of the Grounded realm, a patient presence that stirs the sediment-laden shallows of the Thudarneld reefs. Its sanctified currents are said to rearrange sandbars and sway fishing fleets, though it rarely wakes to anything grander than a village's offerings.

rites.name: Kelastordon
rites.text: Kelastordon is a grounded technique of the Thudarneld world, a ritual stance in which a warrior channels a brief surge of stored bodily force through a spear. Its effect is confined to a short, sharp burst that heightens the strike without transcending ordinary limits.

rites.name: Halurdanen
rites.text: Halurdanen is a grounded, age-seven dark-arts dancer of the Thudarneld omniverse who sheds a portion of its own vitality to sway every nearby foe into a shadowy, disorienting trance. Its practitioners balance the cost of that sacrifice against the power it unlocks, and the craft is widely taught in fortress courtyards.

rites.name: Droldeston
rites.text: Droldeston is a grounded concept from the E6 era, a veil of sharpened attention that a hunter lays over the eyes before a fight. When it settles on an opponent, the target's breath and voice fall silent for a moment, though the effect only holds while the target looks back at the caster.

rites.name: Brulden
rites.text: Brulden is a Grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a clerical discipline that stacks a single gesture into three overlapping rites of stillness. Its adepts can bind a foe's will, breath, and voice at once for a short season, though the strain of the triple binding leaves the caster drained. Ancient wardens of the Brulden orders are said to have sealed entire valleys with the technique.

rites.name: Thuldar
rites.text: Thuldar is a grounded, era-six beam-discharge weapon-spirit that hums in the hollows of an ancient canal network, its power measured by how many lanterns it can dim at once. Its name is a corruption of an old word for a cured hunting-horn, and it is said to answer only to those who have learned its quiet ritual of patience.

rites.name: Dredon
rites.text: Dredon is a wind-sculpting spirit of the Grounded realm, a restless vortex of dust and gale that stirs the plains of its homeland. Its gusts can strip away the fragile, leaving behind only ruin on a small scale.

rites.name: Thedath
rites.text: Thedath is a grounded, humble reagent-drawing tradition of the Thudarneld fourth age, practiced by village hedge-chemists who channel small sparks through copper filaments. Its practitioners are known for repeating a single flame-cantrip twice in quick succession to light stubborn kilns. Their skill is modest, but their discipline in controlling heat is legendary among the valley folk.

rites.name: Tarnasteld
rites.text: Tarnasteld is a quiet, grounded craft-discipline of the Thudarneld world, practiced by wandering shadow-dancers who refine their footwork until a strike seems to pass through empty air. Its adepts earn progressively greater deflection as they advance, though no ledger ever records the exact measure. Practitioners consider it a mark of earned instinct rather than any loud power.

rites.name: Thorneld
rites.text: Thorneld is a quiet mountain-hermit who forges crescent blades from the frost-hardened roots of a silver-barked tree. Each blade is said to hold the cool glow of the nearest moon, releasing it as a single arc of white force when drawn. Villagers in the lowland valleys count on the hermit's arc to split rockfalls before they reach their homes.

rites.name: Drenock
rites.text: Drenock is a grounded, low-grade mental-warfare technique practiced across the Thudarneld era E6, where a trained adept siphons the reserve of focus from a single opponent. It is taught in quiet academies as a tool of attrition rather than spectacle. Its strength lies in the brutal efficiency with which it empties a rival's ready arts.

rites.name: Draruston
rites.text: Draruston is a grounded, slow-burning bulwark of the Thudarneld reach, a hulking iron-shelled grinder that spent its seventh age carving tunnels through the old bedrock for the rail-kin of its valley. It moves with deliberate, ponderous force, crushing whatever stands in its path under sheer mass and patient momentum.

rites.name: Fenoreld
rites.text: Fenoreld is a ward-scribed charm carried by the mistwardens of Thudarneld, who inscribe it onto river stones to quiet floods. Its single known act shattered a drowned village's sluice gate with the force of a long hard shove. The charm is said to fail if read aloud twice in one season.

rites.name: Halarneld
rites.text: Halarneld is a reckless duelist's technique, a single desperate lunge that gathers every ounce of a fighter's nerve into one blow. When it lands it can split a timber hall or cave in a stone wall, but it misses more often than not, and the swordsman usually pays for a failed gamble.

rites.name: Jorurnock
rites.text: Jorurnock is a quiet stone-and-moss sentinel of the Grounded realm, whose slow footfalls gather restorative warmth from the soil beneath it. Each stride it takes draws a faint green light upward into its frame, mending any wounds it carries. Its steps are said to be the only thing that can steady the wandering hills of its valley.

rites.name: Tarnanode
rites.text: Tarnanode is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a slow-building hunting discipline in which a practitioner holds a single stance until the next strike lands with weight beyond their body's normal reach. Its practitioners are prized for patience, and its lore warns that a shot held too long can tear the holder's own tendons apart.

rites.name: Tarnodar
rites.text: Tarnodar is a grounded concept of a hand-carved bronze lattice that a warden clips onto a traveller's wrist to lend them borrowed strength for a season. Its bearers gain stacked boosts to endurance, reach and reflexes, but the lattice drinks from the wearer's own stamina, so every gift leaves them thinner afterward.

rites.name: Pelulderon
rites.text: Pelulderon is a grounded resonance-engine built into the cracked bell-towers of the Vessel-Wastes, where its hum mends mechanical shrines for a fee of salt. Its keepers say it can stitch a dead gear-heart back to full thrum, but only by drawing a small tithe from the nearest living rig.

rites.name: Brasteden
rites.text: Brasteden is a concept of braided tidal resonance, held by the drift-scholars of Thudarneld's grounded era six to be a lattice of small pressure-echoes bent back against the ground. It is taught as a discipline of stillness rather than force, and its seventh-age practitioners treat it as a quiet inheritance passed hand to hand.

rites.name: Crane
rites.text: Crane is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's third age, a lattice-bound device that siphons vitality from living things and stores it in brass reservoirs for the people who tend its turning gears. Its operators treat it as a mercy engine, though each siphoning leaves the donor's fields slightly dimmer.

rites.name: Morenath
rites.text: Morenath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a dust-shaped ability that wears down an opponent's sight through a broad fan of stinging grit. Its practitioners set the effect in advance and release it in a sweeping arc, leaving foes stumbling through a dim, choking haze.

rites.name: Pelesture
rites.text: Pelesture is a dense crystalline lattice that compresses surrounding air into a sinking field, pinning anything nearby to the ground. Wardens of the Grounded realm wear its shards to drag down climbing enemies and to keep their own cities from drifting into the sky.

rites.name: Morerock
rites.text: Morerock is a slow-growing lithic fungus that fastens itself to the bedrock of the Grounded realm and siphons minerals from whatever stone it covers. When threatened it draws the stored mineral heat out of nearby ore veins, lashing back with a crushing surge of pressure.

rites.name: Halurar
rites.text: Halurar is a grounded, low-tier concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet mountain pass where wind-carved stones hum when someone kneels. Its lessons are taught to children as chants that coax warmth from the soil and steady a frightened herd. Its power is modest but reliable, used mostly to mend and to steady rather than to strike.

rites.name: Crerdath
rites.text: Crerdath is a grounded, mortal-scale instrument of shared resolve, a tuned lattice of brass and river-glass worn across the forearm. A bearer can pour their stored reserve of strength into a companion, letting the recipient unleash their own greatest effort sooner than their body would allow. The gift is lost if the recipient is already full, so wise wielders time their giving carefully.

rites.name: Pelanen
rites.text: Pelanen is a grounded swordsman-artifact of the Thudarneld reach, a blade-keeper who channels a stored crackle of storm into a single clean cut. The Pelanen discipline is taught to apprentices who must first master balance before the blade will answer them.

rites.name: Pelodesten
rites.text: Pelodesten is a grounded, mud-born colossus of the E6 age, a patient wanderer who sinks into riverbeds and rises again to stamp the valley flat. Its most feared act is a rolling collapse of soil and stone that flattens everything within a few streets.

rites.name: Bruresteld
rites.text: Bruresteld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a quiet art of misdirection practiced by wandering stage-folk who sway crowds with rehearsed gestures and false echoes. Its practitioners rely on timing and illusion rather than force, so their most dramatic effects remain modest.

rites.name: Breldarock
rites.text: Breldarock is a sword-channeling art practiced by wandering stonemasons of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, who awaken dormant ore in a blade so it hums and cracks the earth beneath it. Its practitioners are rare, their skill passed in silence between generations of quarry-folk.

rites.name: Keledock
rites.text: Keledock is a quiet discipline practiced by the river-wardens of Thudarneld, who store the strain of a hard day in their marrow and loose it through a single open palm. Its practitioners are measured by how cleanly they can release that stored strain without rattling the bones of bystanders.

rites.name: Moranath
rites.text: Moranath is a grounded, world-spanning concept in the Thudarneld cycle, a vision that lingers in the eyes of those who meet its gaze and bends their sense of direction. Its influence is measured in the confusion it leaves behind rather than in ruin. Wardens of the E6 era study it as a quiet but persistent presence in the land.

rites.name: Drosteld
rites.text: Drosteld is a bound-tome of lapsed scribe-magic, kept open on a lectern in the Thudarneld archives and used by its custodian to cut a single sentence of consequence from the air. Its pages record the failures of old oaths, and each turn of a leaf can sever one such failure from the present. Its power is strictly bounded by the weight of the ink it was written in.

rites.name: Halornath
rites.text: Halornath is a gliding ritual of the Thudarneld drift-wardens, a sudden wordless leap that lets a practitioner vanish from one perch and reappear on another. It is taught only to those who can name the wind they are riding, and it leaves a faint scent of cold iron behind.

rites.name: Halesturdon
rites.text: Halesturdon is a mild-mannered ceramic tortoise-shell engine that stores its owner's stray thoughts as pressure in lattice-woven plates. When the plates are struck, it briefly reshapes the nearest bridge or wall into whatever the bearer last imagined.

rites.name: Morerane
rites.text: Morerane is a grounded, E6-era marvel of the Thudarneld universe, a lantern-lit dancing discipline whose practitioners stamp rhythms that fortify the bodies of everyone nearby. Its masters are famed for turning a single festival square into a shelter that survives ordinary storms.

rites.name: Kelernaron
rites.text: Kelernaron is a grounded concept of a bipedal war-frame whose leg-mounted pistons deliver a single crushing stomp that rattles its surroundings. Its operators call the strike a "tremor kick," and the frame is built to absorb backlash so the pilot never feels the recoil.

rites.name: Drurnock
rites.text: Drurnock is a grounded, quiet-bloom concept in the sixth era, a stubborn root-entity whose pollen lulls nearby minds into slumber for a long span of time. Its blossoms are said to hum with a faint drowsy warmth that strengthens any bearer who keeps its petals close.

rites.name: Pelodon
rites.text: Pelodon is a grounded, sluggish clay-shelled marsh creature from the sixth era of Thudarneld, prized by reed-folk for the warm bloodmilk they draw from its flanks. It draws vitality slowly from anything it lies beside, leaving wilted reeds and drowsy herders in its wake.

rites.name: Kelurodock
rites.text: Kelurodock is a grounded, mid-age construct-spell woven from the bones of a dead monsoon god, drawn upon by wandering wardens of the Thudarneld cliffs. When its stored vigour is released, it strikes a single foe in rapid successive pulses, each one shaking the same target until nothing is left standing.

rites.name: Drestar
rites.text: Drestar is a grounded, pale-sailed barrier-weaver of the E6 age, who layers her shields from borrowed heat and clean light until they hold against almost anything. Her wards can hold back a collapsing hillside for a few heartbeats, though she tires badly if pressed to stack a third layer.

rites.name: Pelorurdeld
rites.text: Pelorurdeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a rhythmic discipline of war-chant performed by hardened fighters who strike in measured cadence. Its practitioners raise the force of allied blows by singing staged verses, with each stage unlocked after seven years of drilling.

rites.name: Pelornar
rites.text: Pelornar is a grounded swordmaster of the Thudarneld concept-age, known for a sweeping spin of the blade that cuts every foe within reach while steadying the wielder's own stance for a moment. Its strikes are modest in raw force but precise, and it is said the blade never misses the same rhythm twice.

rites.name: Tarnedore
rites.text: Tarnedore is a grounded, unassuming sorcerous technique of the Thudarneld worlds, rendered in the seventh age of the sixth era. Its practitioners wrap themselves in a shimmering veil of sallow light that lasts only a few heartbeats yet steadies their limbs and sharpens their resolve. Lesser versions are taught to apprentices as a first lesson in controlling borrowed power.

rites.name: Haledock
rites.text: Haledock is a grounded tool of the Thudarneld order, a slender lens of cold-fired glass that gathers scattered resonance into one narrow point. Its bearers use it to focus a single throw of force, sacrificing breadth for a sharp, concentrated strike.

rites.name: Fenonaldar
rites.text: Fenonaldar is a Grounded-realm concept of a warden-flame that burns in the ash-glass fields of Thudarneld, tended by hermits who sing it to sleep at dusk. Its heat is measured in the weight of a tall stone tower lifted and dropped in a single breath. It is said to remember the last hand that struck it.

rites.name: Fenere
rites.text: Fenere is a cold-tempered frost spirit of the Grounded realm's Seventh Age, bound to the northern glaciers of Thudarneld. Its signature is a towering column of rime that erupts from the ice to freeze everything within a wide ring of ground. It is respected as a steady, mid-scale calamity rather than a world-ender.

rites.name: Draste
rites.text: Draste is a sleet-wielding archer-spirit of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld's sixth era, a figure whose volleys of icy hail can bind a foe's limbs for a few heartbeats. Seven ages old, it is revered by mountain hunters who believe its frost keeps rivers from flooding their valleys.

rites.name: Tarnolde
rites.text: Tarnolde is a grounded, tectonic-scale hearth-wyrm of Thudarneld's third sunless valley, a creature whose exhaled ember-fog can soften stone and slowly harden living flesh into basalt. It is said to sleep beneath volcanic cones, waking only when pressure in the earth becomes unbearable.

rites.name: Pelorden
rites.text: Pelorden is a quiet tide-binding ward worn as a silver knot by the wardens of the drowned city Vessmar, letting its bearer slip past the ember-skin and frost-shell that guard enemies. It cannot undo a foe's raw weakness to the thunderclap or the flood, only the stubborn defences against those four currents.

rites.name: Halornock
rites.text: Halornock is a grounded concept of a resonant warhorse-shaped bronze automaton from the Thudarneld age of the third era, whose chest bells ring when it is rooted to earth. Its triumphant bellow, forged into a tonal lattice, briefly sharpens the strikes of every ally within earshot. Its pastoral guardians never sound the call while airborne.

rites.name: Morenastar
rites.text: Morenastar is a grounded, seven-year-old marvel of the E6 era in Thudarneld, a sky-bound lattice of brass conduits and thunder-kites that channels storm charge into a single bright beam. Its wielders, the Hollow Choir, sing their own pitch to tune the discharge, letting a single surge arc across a battlefield in a lattice of forks.

rites.name: Brardunock
rites.text: Brardunock is a sentient siege-lens grown from crystallized storm-glass in the low hills of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, used by the wardens of the fourth age to focus sunlight into a single lance of heat. Its keepers believe it remembers every hand that ever aimed it, and it rarely fires without first humming for a full day.

rites.name: Kelurdoreld
rites.text: Kelurdoreld is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld universe: a crystalline sentinel that hums for years before it opens its plates and releases a single frozen pulse across the valley. Its power is measured in the stillness it leaves behind rather than in fire or noise.

rites.name: Dresten
rites.text: Dresten is a concept of a grounded power in the Thudarneld world, a tide of stored momentum that a wielder can gather into one sweeping motion. Its practitioners treat each arc of the body as a lever, and the swing they release can topple stone walls and fling loose debris across a field. In an era of settled peace it is taught as a discipline of control rather than destruction.

rites.name: Bronath
rites.text: Bronath is a mossy stone guardian that hums in the cold valleys of Thudarneld, where it tends sleeping lichen-gardens and mends cracked hearthstones for travelers who leave it offerings of warm river clay. Its gentle resonance can knit a wounded companion's flesh back together within a few breaths, though each mending leaves its own hide faintly chalked and dulled.

rites.name: Kelode
rites.text: Kelode is a quiet, grounded sleight of the Thudarneld calm-weather craft, a practiced sidestep that folds a person's presence into a shimmer of borrowed wind for the length of a breath. Its practitioners hold the knack in their hands and feet rather than their minds, and a skilled one can turn aside a thrown stone or a glancing blow before it lands. Once the moment passes the knack must rest for a long while before it will answer again.

rites.name: Therdock
rites.text: Therdock is a grounded concept of a hand-forged siege engine that channels the stored heat of a dying forge into a single crushing bolt. Its operators in the Thudarneld cities treat it as both weapon and fragile heirloom, since each firing cracks the casting a little more.

rites.name: Pelarunon
rites.text: Pelarunon is a restless scrap-storm that gathers in the hollows of Thudarneld's old iron deserts, spinning up the loose metal of collapsed watchtowers into a whirling cage. Wanderers who brace against it report that it steadies their limbs while dulling their thoughts. Its anger is not directed at anything in particular and fades within a short span once the metal has been flung wide.

rites.name: Kelustar
rites.text: Kelustar is a faintly luminous, mushroom-like sentinel that drifts through the damp canopy of the Thudarneld understory, releasing spore clouds that sap warmth and vigor from anything nearby. Its feeding bloom is a slow, corrosive exhalation that leaves victims sluggish and sick for hours, while the fungus itself grows stronger from the nourishment it draws.

rites.name: Halardoldon
rites.text: Halardoldon is a sealed ember-lantern forged in the Grounded realm's third age, a glowing relic that stores heat drawn from sleeping furnaces beneath the valley. When its shutter is pried open it releases a dazzling wave of scorching light that blinds everyone caught within the cone, leaving the valley's guardians to fight by sound alone.

rites.name: Brurock
rites.text: Brurock is a grounded, sun-dried clay stronghold in the Thudarneld reaches, where civic life runs on quiet and rhythm. Its people set a single warm instrument of marrow-wood at the center of each hall, and its drowsy seasons are considered sacred to the dead.

rites.name: Tarnorne
rites.text: Tarnorne is a Grounded-realm concept of a sword-and-stance discipline in the Thudarneld omniverse, where a wielder builds a wide arc of force to strike several foes at once. Its signature techniques scale from a quick, stun-inducing sweep to a blade-wave that can sweep a foe from the field entirely.

rites.name: Kelosternon
rites.text: Kelosternon is a grounded, armored bulwark of the Thudarneld reefs, a slow-striding creature whose shell-plated limbs crack the earth when it leaps. Its heavy descending strikes are feared by the coastal clans who keep it as a living siege guard.

rites.name: Fenornareld
rites.text: Fenornareld is a shimmering veil-charm of the Grounded realm, cast by wardens who wish to slip two travelers past watching eyes. Its glimmer is faint and its bearers are unseen as long as the charm holds.

rites.name: Brorde
rites.text: Brorde is a grounded, non-sentient discipline practiced in the seventh age of Thudarneld, where practitioners bind a chosen technique to a worn bracer. Mastery is earned by drilling a single motion until the body remembers it, and the fold of each drill is logged as a small tally of resolve.

rites.name: Crurnalde
rites.text: Crurnalde is a modest ember-kindling crafting tool used by the hearth-wardens of Thudarneld to light cookfires and warm clay ovens. Its flame is steady and gentle, rarely surpassing the heat of a handheld torch. It is prized for its reliability in damp conditions rather than for any destructive power.

rites.name: Moranock
rites.text: Moranock is a tidal sorrow-current that drifts through the grey marshes of Thudarneld, answering every ritual lament with a cold, drenching wave. Its power is modest on the world's scale but relentless, soaking whatever stands within its reach.

rites.name: Thardock
rites.text: Thardock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rhythm of dancers whose footwork stirs the living fields back to health. Its movement threads sap and sunlight through each gathering, so the realm measures its strength by how many weary hands it lifts.

rites.name: Crelde
rites.text: Crelde is a grounded, hollow-spoked ironwork engine that rolls on the long plains of Thudarneld, carrying shepherds' lanterns and salt. When its spokes lock, it grinds forward in a flurry of rattling strikes that can flatten a fence post or cripple a stray herd beast.

rites.name: Tarnudanath
rites.text: Tarnudanath is a quiet chronicle-engine kept by the lamp-wardens of Thudarneld, able to fold a traveller's footing back across the seasons of a mountain range so the walker stands where it stood in an older age. It was built to mend routes that the grinding centuries have worn away, and it is treated with reverence and some dread.

rites.name: Brarneld
rites.text: Brarneld is a sentient gravity-kiln forged by the Drowned Sovereigns of Thudarneld to tighten the tides around sinking cities. When its heartbeat quickens, it draws the surrounding water and dust into a dense, slow-spinning sphere that detonates against the first wall it meets.

rites.name: Therdon
rites.text: Therdon is a frost-sculptor of the Grounded realm's E6 age, whose cold hymns crystallize the air into lattices that bury entire valleys. Its signature chill can freeze a broad field of foes solid in a single exhalation, though it must rest long after such a feat.

rites.name: Fenaldar
rites.text: Fenaldar is a grounded, bloodless siphoning art of the Thudarneld world, practiced by wandering healers who draw the vitality out of their opponents and pour it into their own wounds. Its practitioners are feared more for the sickness that lingers in those they drain than for the strength they gain.

rites.name: Joreldock
rites.text: Joreldock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe: a quickening technique in which a practitioner's spells surge forward in time, letting them weave several elemental workings before an opponent can react. The art draws its power from the surrounding ground and is measured in how many heartbeats it steals from the enemy.

rites.name: Keledureld
rites.text: Keledureld is a grounded, low-stakes dance-art that a wandering troupe in the Thudarneld reaches teaches to its apprentices as a way to unsettle rivals. Its practitioners sway through a ritual step that dulls the blows of everyone watching, though the effect fades when the music stops.

rites.name: Peloldarnar
rites.text: In the frost-kissed world of Cryotheum, the Eternal Blizzard, Peloldarnar, is a primal force that periodically purges the land of excess heat, maintaining the delicate balance of ice and snow.

rites.name: Pelustath
rites.text: Pelustath is a hymn-song of protective resonance in the Thudarneld concept realm, sung in eight attuned tones that each shield a bearer against a single elemental force. Its effect layers over other wards, though it mostly blunts direct elemental strikes rather than sorcery itself. A singer using a hollow reed horn can extend both the potency and the hold of the tune.

rites.name: Bredeld
rites.text: Bredeld is a frost-conjuring technique practiced by the Glasswright monks of the Thaw Peaks, who sculpt a sudden ramp of rime beneath their boots and leap from it to strike with a burst of cold. The ramp dissolves almost at once, leaving only a brief white scar on the air where the blow landed.

rites.name: Kelosterock
rites.text: Kelosterock is a bioluminescent, tide-dwelling leviathan of the Grounded realm's shallow seas, whose spectral mucus can curdle the air above it. Its chief weapon is a corrosive exhalation of violet vapor that sears through armor and seizes the nerves of anything it touches. Though sluggish on land, it can outpace a sailing ship when stirred to fury.

rites.name: Haledustath
rites.text: Haledustath is a sentinel-shield construct that Thudarneld's ridge-wardens bind to a chosen ally, absorbing every blow aimed at that person and hurling back a single retaliatory pulse before the strike lands. Its guardianship lasts only while the ward remains within arm's reach, and it ends the moment the warden releases it, leaving the construct dormant until the next dawn.

rites.name: Therduldath
rites.text: Therduldath is a grounded, weathered warrior-concept from the Thudarneld cycle, drawn as a quiet discipline that lets a fighter's blows land with sudden, decisive force. It hums in the hands of those who have practiced it for decades, marking the period of its ascendancy in E6.

rites.name: Pelasten
rites.text: Pelasten is a concept of a grounded, frost-tempered artisan's craft in the Thudarneld era E6, a discipline of striking cold stone so that enemies lock up in rime. Practitioners of the era hold that the stillness lasts about three minutes once the blow lands. Its strength is steady rather than explosive, prized by smiths who harden their own limbs with it.

rites.name: Pelestade
rites.text: Pelestade is a concept of a tidal-wave sensation rendered as a mutual sweep: two marked spearwielders advance together, each pulling the other's momentum into a single arc that strikes one foe. Its cost is deliberately heavy, drawing on a reserve of focus that each bearer must refill over a long season.

rites.name: Halureld
rites.text: Halureld is a sword-technique practiced by the wardens of Thudarneld's grounded era, a single blade-art that channels the wielder's own breath into a cutting arc. It is said to be taught to only one heir per generation, and its strikes have split stone walls but never more than a city's worth of rubble.

rites.name: Kelostureld
rites.text: Kelostureld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet chime of pressure-bells strung along the seventh age's cold ridges. It is said to hum a resonance that steadies the nerves of anyone standing within earshot.

rites.name: Breronock
rites.text: Breronock is a reflexive ward-bearing discipline of the Grounded realm, practiced by wardens who turn an incoming blow back onto its thrower through a timed flick of the wrist. Its strikes are small, precise, and carry none of the overwhelming force of the great calamities of the age.

rites.name: Keledulde
rites.text: Keledulde is a grounded, concept-tier weather-attuned rite practiced by the wind-scribes of Thudarneld's high plateaus, who believe the sky's mood can be borrowed to sharpen words of power. Its practitioners chant to the prevailing storm so that spells matching its nature strike truer against their targets. It is valued for precision rather than raw force.

rites.name: Crunordock
rites.text: Crunordock is a clockwork bastion of the Grounded realm, a ferrous fortress that has stood on the same iron ridge through seven ages of wind and rust. Its gears turn so slowly that a single rotation takes a generation, yet the stored tension can be loosed in a sudden, earth-shaking release.

rites.name: Morudar
rites.text: Morudar is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld reach, a quiet and humble ferry-spirit that carries lost travelers across the reed-choked lowlands of its homeland. In the seventh age of the sixth era it is remembered less for grand deeds than for the careful, patient ways it keeps the waterways open for those who depend on them.

rites.name: Fenudeld
rites.text: Fenudeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a ceremonial stance-practice that hardens its practitioner against blows of steel and spell alike. Its wearers are said to take the strikes of a clash without flinching, shielding themselves with resolve shaped into a brief, glowing barrier.

rites.name: Halade
rites.text: Halade is a conceptual sovereign of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet hush that drinks the fear of nearby creatures and turns it into brittle fire. Those who face it in the high fields of Orrun say it moves like falling pollen, unseen until it has already passed.

rites.name: Brulde
rites.text: Brulde is a grounded tidal sorcerer of the Thudarneld reef-marshes, who calls a fanned storm of sediment and brine that strips the armour from anything caught inside it. Its tempest is modest in force yet leaves foes sluggish and unguarded for a short while.

rites.name: Pelosten
rites.text: Pelosten is a sleek, ember-eyed hunting beast of the Grounded realm's ash-plains, prized and feared for its vicious pack tactics. It strikes from concealment, leaping from rocky outcrops and vanishing before counterattacks can land.

rites.name: Pelaldorde
rites.text: Pelaldorde is a concept of prolonged endurance: a quiet discipline that stretches how long a lingering affliction or blessing clings to a bearer. Among the Grounded peoples of Thudarneld it is taught as a patient art rather than a weapon, measured in the hours a tonic or ward keeps its grip.

rites.name: Thordare
rites.text: Thordare is a root-bound terrain-shaper of the grounded realm, whose slow-growing tendrils lock the ground beneath foes into a sluggish grip. Its binding fields sap momentum from anything crossing them, letting it hold back advancing armies for half a minute at a time.

rites.name: Drerde
rites.text: Drerde is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a wind-born working that a mage can only grasp after long and dedicated study of their craft. Its practitioners describe it as a tight, rising gale that scours the air around a single target, and it is taught only to those who have proven their patience over many seasons.

rites.name: Tarnorune
rites.text: Tarnorune is a grounded, ash-veined ember-keeper of the Thudarneld reaches, a scholar who has kept a dying hearth alive for seven ages by burning his own memories as fuel. Locals say his blaze can sear through a stone wall in a breath, though he rarely lets it reach that strength.

rites.name: Pelestarath
rites.text: Pelestarath is a grounded, quiet power in Thudarneld's sixth era, a technique by which a practitioner draws the echo of tomorrow's rain down into a single stone spike. It is measured in patience and weather rather than force, yet its strikes can crack a stone wall that has stood for seven ages.

rites.name: Kelastath
rites.text: Kelastath is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of the E6 era, a quiet mountain-steppe spirit whose presence hums through the soil of the powers. Its signature act is a thunderous bellow that cracks dry clay and rattles the bones of everything within earshot, leaving foes dazed and unsteady.

rites.name: Keluston
rites.text: Keluston is a grounded concept that the people of its era use to describe a surge of resolve that briefly raises a warrior's inner reserve of focus. Its most notable use is as a quiet preparation for a single decisive strike, after which the bearer moves with uncanny speed. It is not a force that reshapes the world, only one that sharpens the body and mind for the moment that matters.

rites.name: Drurde
rites.text: Drurde is a grounded, mid-scale concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a shard-rattling technique whose practitioners discharge stored tension from their bones in a sudden flash. In the seventh age of the era it is taught in quiet monasteries as a discipline of release rather than destruction.

rites.name: Tarnaldon
rites.text: Tarnaldon is a concept of a shimmering aurora-woven ward, a spell-weave that a mage can drape over an ally to brighten the sky above them and redirect ambient light into restorative force. Its age of three marks it as a young but already widely taught discipline in the Grounded realm of the sixth era.

rites.name: Drerock
rites.text: Drerock is a grounded concept of Thudarneld's sixth era, a lone courier who carries a quiver of storm-charged shafts and looses them as bolts of focused static. Its power is modest on the world's scale but fearsome in a single town, where it can split a stone wall or a steel gate in a single shot.

rites.name: Pelostath
rites.text: Pelostath is a grounded, hand-forged chain-blade of Thudarneld's sixth era, favored by hunters who track the hollow-eyed beasts that prowl the mountain passes. Its edge is quenched in brine collected under a waning moon, which the smiths believe makes it bite deeper into things that should not walk the living world. Its wielders are said to carry a faint, unshakable calm that unnerves the beasts before the first strike lands.

rites.name: Fenoldath
rites.text: Fenoldath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an ordinary craft of wards and charms that softens the blows of arcane force. Its practitioners, the Thornwardens of the third age, weave protective sigils into cloth and stone so that a hurled curse spends itself harmlessly against the weave. Their chief art is teaching apprentices to layer ward upon ward until even a lightning-blast is reduced to a warm breeze.

rites.name: Moroston
rites.text: Moroston is a grounded wandering swordmaster of the Thudarneld reaches who fights in quick, circling bursts of motion. Villagers say a single flourish of Moroston's blade can knock a stubborn wall askew. The sheer velocity of the strokes is the source of the legend rather than any mystical power.

rites.name: Jorurdeneld
rites.text: Jorurdeneld is a grounded concept from the E6 powers locale, known as a gentle mender whose hands draw lost travelers back along old roads of memory. Its chosen wardens call the act of restoring a scattered band to a remembered waystone of seven ages past.

rites.name: Halurdoren
rites.text: Halurdoren is a grounded, seven-age-old tool of the Thudarneld wilds, a lattice of sealed glass rods that hum when struck. Those who learn its cadence can unmake a stone wall or a sleeping beast in a single resonant burst. Its wardens guard the rods carefully, for an unattended rod gathers strain until it shatters on its own.

rites.name: Halustock
rites.text: Halustock is a grounded concept of a rooted fungal colossus that lives beneath the marshes of the E6 era, where its spores drift on the wind to dim the senses of anyone who walks too close. It slowly steals mobility and clarity from its prey rather than striking directly.

rites.name: Crarolden
rites.text: Crarolden is a drifting dance-duel art practised by the wind-wardens of Thudarneld's grounded plains, where performers spin through a rhythm of stamps and pirouettes that gathers loose air into a tight, crackling whirl. Its masters are remembered for ending festivals with a single turn that can scatter a village's harvest-chaff across a valley.

rites.name: Bronath
rites.text: Bronath is a bronze-hued stone concept in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a dormant seal-engine that hums beneath the marshes of the third age. Its rhythm is said to steady the tides of nearby villages, yet it drains the warmth from anyone who lingers too long beside it.

rites.name: Drelde
rites.text: Drelde is a grounded combat technique in the world of Thudarneld, taught to wardens who strike with a paired fang-and-claw motion. Its practitioners deliver quick, precise blows that cut through armor, with effects limited to what a human body can sustain.

rites.name: Halanock
rites.text: Halanock is a gravity-warden of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, sworn to keep the weight of the land balanced. Its fabled cry can collapse a hillside of soft stone in a single breath, though it rarely uses such force. Scholars note that its mercy is as heavy as its power.

rites.name: Thustalden
rites.text: Thustalden is a grounded, quiet-era concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a weathered iron-jawed pike whose wielder drinks a fraction of what their blade cuts from living foes. Its wardens consider the practice a loan rather than a gift, since the pike must be fed again before the next moon.

rites.name: Drostock
rites.text: Drostock is a shielding ward of the Thudarneld grounded realm, a silent bell-shaped field that pilgrim-engineers raise over a gathering to blunt incoming arcane force. Its wards hold for thirty minutes and can be strengthened by up to five stacked lattice-stones, each stone adding a small measure of resistance against sorcerous blows.

rites.name: Kelarornath
rites.text: Kelarornath is a grounded, seven-year-old creeping curse-engine that drifts through the mineral veins of the Thudarneld highlands, siphoning vitality from anything warm that lingers too long. It is a concept rather than a living thing, a slow sickness given a shape by the people who learned to fear its rattling passage.

rites.name: Drardon
