rites.text: Drardon is a grounded frost-spirit of the Thudarneld reaches, a sleeping winter that wakes whenever the cold grows too proud. Its breath can lock a whole valley in silent ice for a single season, a power the valley-folk call the hush of white.

rites.name: Jorurne
rites.text: Jorurne is a sentient sporemound tended by the drowned gardeners of the Vellix marshes, who coax it into exhaling a mist that clings to foes and dulls their wards. Its fungal husk remembers every tide that has crossed it, and it can be persuaded to hold its breath for a day at a time.

rites.name: Pelunon
rites.text: Pelunon is a quiet cartographer-spirit of the Grounded realm who maps the roots beneath the seventh age's valleys. It works its craft through gentle, tiring tugs on the earth rather than force, and its presence is felt more as a slow weariness than as any blow.

rites.name: Morurneld
rites.text: Morurneld is a grounded concept of a wind-carved lowland, where a rhythmic spiral of dust devils scours the plains every seventh year. Its inhabitants learned to ride the vortices like sails, turning the chaos into a seasonal trade route.

rites.name: Dradath
rites.text: Dradath is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a rural trading-world where a sly merchant's knack for pricing is treated as a form of quiet power. Its essence lies in squeezing extra value from every transaction, a skill the locals consider nearly magical in its consistency.

rites.name: Joreste
rites.text: Joreste is a grounded healing rite of the Thudarneld peoples, a mid-tier restorative that lifts every lingering affliction from a bearer and returns a third of their spent vigor. Its adepts stack two lesser soothing sigils to widen the reach of the cure across nearby companions. It is treasured as stronger than a simple mending but kept humble beside the greater rites of its order.

rites.name: Fenuden
rites.text: Fenuden is a grounded concept of a rhythm-keeping dance-song that a traveling troupe performs to steady nerves and sap the will of rival crowds. Its performers are ordinary people whose influence is social rather than physical, measured only in the attention and confidence they can draw. The tradition has spread across the region's market towns as a form of gentle contest.

rites.name: Brurelden
rites.text: Brurelden is a grounded, centuries-old rite of the Thudarneld, a slow-breathing pressure field that bows the attacking reflexes of anything caught within its hum. Its tutors are the swarming sap-midges of the high fens, and what they teach is a patient, humbling stillness rather than force. Within its reach a blade rises a fraction too late and a fist loses its snap.

rites.name: Fenaden
rites.text: Fenaden is a grounded, era-six concept of a drowsiness-inducing strike, where a bruising blow carries a lulling hum that can send an opponent into a short, leaden sleep. It is a modest, almost domestic power, prized by sparring hall tutors more than by warlords, and its effects fade in roughly three heartbeats of the mind's clock.

rites.name: Brornen
rites.text: Brornen is a concept of ritual slickness in the Thudarneld, a grounded realm of E6 where sacred unguents are poured over people and objects to bind a presence to them. Its practitioners smear rare fat and resin upon wayfarers as a gesture of welcome, and the anointed are said to ward off spirits that bring fever.

rites.name: Kelorduden
rites.text: Kelorduden is a grounded tidal-combat concept from the E6 era, a sharp-tongued skirmish sword-dancer whose strikes draw a brief undertow of seawater. Its practitioners are trained to read currents and pull enemies into rising surf before the final blow lands. Within the Thudarneld setting it is a learned art rather than a natural force, bounded by the modest scale of human-sized combat.

rites.name: Therurnen
rites.text: Therurnen is a grounded concept of a sky-sailing vessel-spirit that gathers the bruises of storms into a single blow. Its stormbound crews call its strike a Thudarneld, a rolling hammer of wind that shakes cargo loose from distant decks. It serves as a mobile siege engine rather than a weapon of pure ruin.

rites.name: Tarnedock
rites.text: Tarnedock is a grounded marksman's technique in the Thudarneld universe, letting a gunner keep firing while the magazine is being swapped out. It is taught only to those who have survived a full season of lonely range drills.

rites.name: Moredar
rites.text: Moredar is a grounded concept, a stormwrack diver whose ritual of shattered-coral strikes is performed across the reef-towns of its age. Its signature hook of bone-keel blades can cut through a sunken hull in a single pass.

rites.name: Fenudeste
rites.text: Fenudeste is a grounded concept of a slow-burning kiln-engine that stores the heat of dying hearths and releases it as steady warmth over several minutes. Its keepers recharge its ember-core every eighty seconds, and a single ember passed along a chain of workers can keep a whole village's forges lit.

rites.name: Halolden
rites.text: Halolden is a grounded concept, a gate-like working of water and ash that a seven-age-old order of tide-sages inscribed into the bedrock of the Thudarneld plains. Its sigil dims the armour and resolve of whoever it is drawn across, and the sages draw a measure of vigour back into themselves with each binding. The ritual was designed as a binding, not a weapon, yet its spirit still sends sharp water through an enemy's ranks.

rites.name: Morunon
rites.text: Morunon is a grounded, slow-burning sentinel of the Thudarneld valley, a warden whose stillness is its weapon and whose rage has been cooled by seven ages of waiting. Its anger is said to detonate only when the land around it is disturbed, releasing a single surge of pressure that flattens everything within reach.

rites.name: Brardudon
rites.text: Brardudon is a drifting sky-ward custodian of Thudarneld's highest cloud-lanes, a lean figure whose cloak sheds gusts of razor-edged plumage that can slice through stone. Its ancient duty is to scatter storms before they gather over the mountain villages below.

rites.name: Kelornar
rites.text: Kelornar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an ever-young trade-craft of braided ward-plates worn by its artisans. Its wardens can dampen incoming force to protect a single ally during a skirmish.

rites.name: Thoderdath
rites.text: Thoderdath is a stone-bound ritual of the Thudarneld powers, an ash-grey art that unmakes a single breath of a target's living rhythm. Its practitioners are rare and feared, since the technique can sever a life outright with no warning.

rites.name: Kelasteld
rites.text: Kelasteld is a Grounded-realm gift of the Thudarneld cycle, a small charm that lets a wanderer call forth two loose elements from the soil and air. Its bearers use it mostly to kindle hearths and steady crumbling ground, rarely to fight.

rites.name: Druldosten
rites.text: Druldosten is a meditative discipline in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, practiced by stone-minded monks who hold a single breath until the mind goes quiet. Its adepts can lower the price their bodies pay for every technique, letting a hard-won skill cost barely a flicker of stamina. It is prized for teaching endurance rather than force.

rites.name: Fenostaren
rites.text: Fenostaren is a resonant tuning practice in the grounded era of Thudarneld, where practitioners hum a held pitch until the air around them answers with a stable hum. Its most famous act is the Quiet Lantern, a sustained note that can shift the flight of loose debris within a village square.

rites.name: Kelonardon
rites.text: Kelonardon is a concept of paired resonance, a discipline in which two bonded wills share a single heartbeat of force. In the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, its practitioners can briefly amplify one another's strikes and wards, though the effect fades quickly once the pair falls out of step.

rites.name: Moreldath
rites.text: Moreldath is a grounded concept of a warding craft in the valleys of Thudarneld, where artisans bind a thin skin of stabilizing force over a chosen traveler. The binding can be renewed every few breaths at a steady cost of vital ember, and the veil it weaves lasts longer and holds firmer as the artisan's mastery grows.

rites.name: Fenerock
rites.text: Fenerock is a grounded reservoir-stone of the E6 age, a dense mineral that stores tension and discharges it as a sudden crack of lightning when struck. Mountain-folk of the third age use it to stun rival herds and to ignite their signal beacons across the high valleys.

rites.name: Therath
rites.text: Therath is a quiet ward-spirit of the Grounded realm, a lattice of stone-bound sentinels that hum over sleeping valleys. Its only known act is to mend a fracture in the earth's protective skin, a gentle work that never disturbs the soil around it.

rites.name: Halustock
rites.text: Halustock is a grounded, low-output mental-influence craft practiced by the lantern-keepers of Thudarneld's drowsy river towns during the seventh age. Its practitioners press a wave of heavy calm across a crowd, sending every listener into a sudden, dreamless rest that lasts until the chime at dawn.

rites.name: Thaldode
rites.text: Thaldode is a drifting tide-engine of the Grounded realm, a wide cloud of coarse silt that rolls across the lowland basins of Thudarneld in E6 and grinds away whatever stands in its path. Local farmers bind their ploughs with chime-wire to keep the silt from scouring their fields.

rites.name: Pelaldon
rites.text: Pelaldon is a grounded concept of soul-bound gear in the Thudarneld cycle, where a wearer's stamina and reflexes are reshaped by sealed relics that must be attuned over years. Its bearers are measured by how many relic slots they can keep awake at once, and by the ability to turn a blow back on its thrower.

rites.name: Fenuroldock
rites.text: Fenuroldock is a grounded, ordinary tool-maker's district of the Thudarneld, known for its mechanical guild-halls and hand-forged gear. Its artisans favour parrying-gauntlets that deflect blows and redirect a little of their momentum into the wearer's stamina.

rites.name: Morerde
rites.text: Morerde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a fine-grained sediment-shaping technique practiced by reed-dwelling wardens of the fourth age. Its practitioners hurl compacted grit through narrow tubes to dazzle the eyes of intruders, and the act is more a nuisance than a weapon.

rites.name: Brurdeld
rites.text: Brurdeld is a grounded, sea-born regurgitative force of Thudarneld's third age, a thick tide-spew that binds whatever it drenches in gelatinous cords. It is taught only by the great drowned beasts of the outer reefs, and its hold lasts as long as the spray lingers.

rites.name: Drane
rites.text: Drane is a grounded, weathered tinkerer's engine from the Thudarneld reaches, a machine that stores the pressure of a long-cold forge and releases it as one clean, violent strike. Its keepers measure it in seasons rather than years, since its seals must be reset after every full discharge.

rites.name: Kelaldunar
rites.text: Kelaldunar is a grounded rite of paired calling in Thudarneld's sixth era, where two bonded callers speak a single name and a second guardian answers beside the first. The bond is said to strengthen the summoned spirits for seven years before fading, so the pairing is treated as a temporary covenant rather than a permanent gift.

rites.name: Keleden
rites.text: Keleden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a reflex-bound discipline that answers each blow with a prepared response rather than an initiated strike. Its practitioners are tuned so that any hostile contact, however small, becomes the trigger for a stored counter that unfolds without conscious command.

rites.name: Peloredock
rites.text: Peloredock is a discipline of spoken conviction taught in the grounded orders of Thudarneld, where a speaker's words are said to bend the listener's sense of what is possible. Practitioners claim a well-timed sermon can quicken an ally's inner fire for several turns, lending their workings a sharper edge.

rites.name: Croreld
rites.text: Croreld is a ward-tempering art in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, practiced by hearth-wardens who rub mineral sigils until a household's walls resist storms and fire. Its binding is recorded in the ledgers of the third age and taught only to apprentices who can hold a steady hand for a full winter.

rites.name: Pelurdaston
rites.text: Pelurdaston is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a mournful bell-keeper's habit of mending wounded travelers before any confrontation. Its power is less about force than about a ritual of restoration that leaves its foes unbroken and ready. In the E6 era, it stands as a reminder that generosity can itself be a kind of warning.

rites.name: Pelerdath
rites.text: Pelerdath is a grounded, seventh-age concept of a protective ward woven by tidal engineers across the shallows of Thudarneld. Its dome is cast over settlements to blunt storms and small blasts, and it must be rebuilt every quarter-hour at great cost.

rites.name: Kelaneste
rites.text: Kelaneste is a quiet, mending power in the Thudarneld concept-realm, a Grounded-era art of cleansing hidden afflictions from a body or a field. Practitioners stack small resonant stones to draw out lingering blights and restore a full reserve of inner breath. It is treated as a minor craft rather than a feat of war.

rites.name: Brurnaston
rites.text: Brurnaston is a grounded, low-stakes conduit of the Thudarneld realm, a hand-sized lattice of humming copper pins that sings when a traveler's footsteps pass near it. Its chimes dim the wits of anyone standing in its shadow and sharpen the nerves of those carrying its scent-oil. Villagers in the E6 markets trade it as a cheap charm against sleepless nights.

rites.name: Bradeldon
rites.text: Bradeldon is a slow, grounded gelatinous lifeform that lives in the mineral-rich pools of Thudarneld's fourth-era tidelands. It draws nourishment and fading vitality from nearby living things and carries the stolen warmth in its translucent body for later use.

rites.name: Brernanock
rites.text: Brernanock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six warding engine built from quiet clockwork and brass resonance lattices. It is known for a single exact-blow discharge that ignores armor, and for shutting down the nearby circuits of anyone standing within its hum.

rites.name: Pelade
rites.text: Pelade is a slate-grey thundercloud dwelling that drifts above the cracked plains of Thudarneld, lightning crawling along its ribs like nervous veins. Its storms are said to be bottled and carried by couriers across the valleys to power the lamp-towns of the lowlands.

rites.name: Kelaldon
rites.text: Kelaldon is a grounded, mild-mannered concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet talent for coaxing better terms from merchants in the open market. Its skill has no weight in war or ruin, only in the small, daily exchange of coin for bread and tools.

rites.name: Morastath
rites.text: Morastath is a grounded concept from the sixth era of Thudarneld, a lone sentinel of sealed gunpowder vaults that its keepers wake only when a fortress is under siege. Its most feared trick is igniting the stored black dust in a fan-shaped blast that cracks armor and dulls the wielder's guard for hours. It is said to have been carved from the same iron that hangs above the old armory gates.

rites.name: Morurnock
rites.text: Morurnock is a grounded domestic beast-tamer's rite, a lumpen cask of tallow-bound grain that a village shepherd cracks open to restore a hound's strength after a long hunt. Its crude biscuits come in six tiers, each named for a letter of an ancient herder's alphabet and stamped with the baker's mark.

rites.name: Fenorurneld
rites.text: Fenorurneld is a grounded mountain-dwelling wrestler-ascetic of the sixth era, who strikes with a palm-thick glove of hardened resin and sky-blue lacquered bone. Her signature blow, the Hollow Mantle Strike, is said to shatter boulders the size of carts in a single press. She is seven years into her apprenticeship with the Valley Orders and has never lost a bout in her home province.

rites.name: Kelurnoneld
rites.text: Kelurnoneld is a grounded technique-spirit of the Thudarneld world, a wind-sigil that its bearers inscribe on the tongue before a storm-breath is loosed in a widening cone. The sigil costs a bit of the bearer's spirit to hold and quickens the limbs while it lingers.

rites.name: Broldurnock
rites.text: Broldurnock is a grounded, ancient warding-stone of the Thudarneld, its surface etched with lattices that bend hostile arcane currents away from whoever stands in its shadow. Scholars of the E6 era regard it as a teaching relic rather than a weapon, yet its guardians remember how it once held back a flood of sorcery for three full days.

rites.name: Joronar
rites.text: Joronar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stoneworker's technique of striking the earth to lift a ring of shards that scatter across a field. It is taught among the hill-clans of the E6 era and is prized for the rhythm it lends to fighters who learn it alongside a stance of raw momentum.

rites.name: Brede
rites.text: Brede is a frost-stitched wind that gathers in the hollows of Thudarneld's northern moors, where shepherds tie bells to its ankles to hear it coming. It moves in quick, stuttering bursts that leave rime on anything in its path, and it has never been known to pause between gusts.

rites.name: Moruldon
rites.text: Moruldon is a stone-hewn judicial constellation of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of E6, whose wardens enforce oaths by pressing a silent, unbreakable weight onto every body that breaks a sworn word. Its magistrates wear the sigil of a sealed ledger and are said to carry the decree itself as a kind of mass. The people of Thudarneld speak of Moruldon's law as older than their rivers.

rites.name: Keloldurdar
rites.text: Keloldurdar is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a silent sculptor-spirit that spends years folding its own shadow into thin ribbons of pressure. It is known for striking four times in a single breath, each blow driving through stone and bone alike. Wardens of the Hollow Coasts still count its rhythm when they hear distant surf.

rites.name: Halostalden
rites.text: Halostalden is a grounded, era-six concept of a mineral-bound marksman's art, practised by wardens who etch ringing sigils into their arrows. Its seventh-age arts are hushed and precise, valued for piercing hidden armour rather than for raw force.

rites.name: Jorunaste
rites.text: Jorunaste is a grounded warden-spirit of the E6 age, bound to a tide of silver ward-glass that hums over the marshlands of Thudarneld. Its guardians wear the glass as rings and sigils, and in a single breath it can deflect a flurry of bolts and sorcerous flame aimed at a single traveler. Its wards last for a few quiet minutes before they must be renewed.

rites.name: Thonen
rites.text: Thonen is a grounded concept of a tide-bound siphon-craft used by the marsh-reeve orders of the Vesk delta to draw warmth and resin from sunken stone. It is patient rather than violent, and reeves keep a pinch of its brine in every lantern. Its most famous use was draining a flooded granary to save a winter harvest.

rites.name: Pelureld
rites.text: Pelureld is a grounded, wind-swept tidewalker of the Thudarneld order, a hollow-boned sentinel of the third age who channels saltwater currents into sudden arcs of force. Its crafts favour rhythm and timing over raw destruction, leaving stunned foes rather than shattered ones.

rites.name: Droneld
rites.text: Droneld is a small, amiable aerial courier from the Thudarneld cluster, built from salvaged rotor housings and humming like a hive. It ferries light cargo between grounded settlements and occasionally coaxes wind through its props to clear dust from fields.

rites.name: Breldurde
rites.text: Breldurde is a Grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-skinned warden whose dormant core, buried beneath the glacial plains of Vorrin's Hollow, is said to bind the sky to the earth. Its signature act is to drink the vitality of any foe struck near it and convert the stolen life into a tremor that shakes the nearest ridge.

rites.name: Fenerdon
rites.text: Fenerdon is a grounded, low-tier lifeform of the Thudarneld cycle, a slow-moving creature that secretes an acidic mucus over anything it touches. Its secretion weakens both the strength and the guard of whatever it clings to, making it a nuisance rather than a threat to cities.

rites.name: Kelanon
rites.text: Kelanon is a grounded, mortal-scale ward-song sung by lantern-keepers of Thudarneld to soften the stone-sickness that creeps through their valley. Its effect is modest and tied to skill: the harder a keeper practises, the sooner a companion's limbs loosen again after a hardening chill.

rites.name: Morodurnen
rites.text: Morodurnen is a slow-burning ember-stone that the Grounded folk of Thudarneld carry in their pockets to mend small hurts. Once struck against bark, it hums for a full minute and knits flesh a little with every breath of its warmth. Its makers forged it in the third age after a mill fire took a village's healers.

rites.name: Joruldon
rites.text: Joruldon is a grounded, mid-tier conceptual enchantment in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sigil-binding that a wearer etches into a bracer to borrow the vigor of a nearby stormhawk. It trades a little stamina for swiftness and a sharper hand, and it can be reset every few breaths.

rites.name: Crarneld
rites.text: Crarneld is a grounded concept of a quickening-current woven through the marsh-tides of Thudarneld's Seventh Age, a discipline by which tide-wardens hasten the pulse of their stored lantern-oil into a second flare within a single breath. It is a modest art, measured in the sparks of a hearth rather than the thunder of cities.

rites.name: Drorden
rites.text: Drorden is a grounded concept from the E6 era, a third-generation ward-stone whose resonance can dampen an opponent's inner momentum. Its bearers use it to seal the rhythm of rivals' hands and feet in place, leaving them dazed and slow to respond.

rites.name: Tarnorath
rites.text: Tarnorath is a slow-coiling tide-spirit of the Grounded realm, said to be woven from the rain that falls between two drowned hills. It bleeds moisture into any creature it touches, so the storm-soaked days of Thudarneld make it far more dangerous than on dry ones.

rites.name: Drareld
rites.text: Drareld is a stone-skinned wayfinder of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, known for a rhythmic palm strike that rattles the air around its target. Its strikes are paired with a mental focus that lets it sense the weak seams in any structure it touches.

rites.name: Morenardath
rites.text: Morenardath is a tidal-warrior's technique in the Thudarneld reckoning, drawn from the glassy shallows where sea-raiders lash out with a sudden jet of pressurized brine. The strike jars the foe's attention loose, so they stop tracking the striker and drift toward whoever is nearest.

rites.name: Moredarnath
rites.text: Moredarnath is a slow-burning earthen binding that a Thudarneld cartographer-mystics coil around a foe's stance, drawing marrow-deep strain from the ground beneath them. Its bite grows strongest when the skies are heavy with storm or drought, since the land answers the sky's mood. It is taught in the quiet guild-halls of the third age and remains a modest, grounded art.

rites.name: Halustar
rites.text: Halustar is a frost-shaping cantrip-engine of the Grounded realm's third age, a crystalline lattice that draws heat from its surroundings and exhales it as a numbing white gust. Its kind is taught in Thudarneld's northern guild-halls, where apprentices learn to cool a single kettle before attempting a river.

rites.name: Jorureld
rites.text: Jorureld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a slow-burning ward-glyph that a warden etches into bark or stone to siphon the ambient breeze into lingering drain. Its wearing-down effect deepens under overcast or stormy skies, so wardens time their sealings to the weather.

rites.name: Thaldath
rites.text: Thaldath is a grounded curse-art of the Thudarneld reaches, where practitioners pin a sickly weight onto foes by anchoring it to a carved stone idol they carry. While the idol stands within the caster's reach, every enemy nearby feels their wards thin and their defenses wither. Apprentices must first master a lesser binding before the stones will accept them.

rites.name: Crornuden
rites.text: Crornuden is a grounded, sweeping gale-spirit of the Thudarneld powers, a slow-moving mass of stormwind that gathers itself low over the fields before erupting outward. Its strikes are meant to knock the wind out of anything caught in its reach, and it rests for long stretches between gusts.

rites.name: Halanerden
rites.text: Halanerden is a slow-burning sorcerous rot that spreads through the dead fields of Thudarneld, withering a foe's vitality over many breaths. Its potency swells or fades with the sky above, so storm-blackened days make it a far more lethal craft than clear ones. Practitioners of the grey tide prize it as a quiet art of attrition.

rites.name: Fenosten
rites.text: Fenosten is a grounded, era E6 concept of stone-shaping sorcery drawn from the hidden tradition of the Quarry Choir, where practitioners coax loose bedrock into a single hurled fist of gravel. Its third-age practitioners treat it as a humble starter craft, though a fully attuned caster can split a boulder that a cart could not move.

rites.name: Drestock
rites.text: Drestock is a concept of grounded earth-binding in the Thudarneld omniverse, a spell-like discipline where practitioners anchor a shifting stone totem that sheds evasive dust over allies. Its power is modest, meant to steady a small band of wanderers rather than alter the land itself.

rites.name: Fenuldarden
rites.text: Fenuldarden is a grounded, half-forgotten rite of the Thudarneld mill-towns, a ritual of drawn-out cutting strikes that siphons warmth from the wounded. It is quoted in the village almanacs as a practice that must be paused for a full dozen breaths between repetitions.

rites.name: Thede
rites.text: Thede is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a ritual of rooted stillness drawn from the hum of bedrock. Practitioners plant a carved stone marker and sing a steady note, causing nearby allies to steady their hands and sharpen their aim while they remain within its resonance.

rites.name: Brurdock
rites.text: Brurdock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rooted pattern of soothing that spreads through the soil beneath an ally's feet. Its effect lingers only while companions remain within the reach of its anchored stone, and it must be learned at a hidden cistern that hums with buried earth-song. Its mending is gentle, measured in small restorative pulses rather than grand displays of force.

rites.name: Peluldath
rites.text: Peluldath is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a slow-blooming fungal-tide that spreads through marsh soil. Its spores seep into the earth and sicken any creature standing within reach of a single rooted spore-lantern, lasting as long as the lantern stands. Scholars learn to tend these lanterns only after they have first mastered a gentler variant of the same bloom.

rites.name: Tarnuldeld
rites.text: Tarnuldeld is a sleepy grove-spirit of Thudarneld's wild forests, a bark-skinned giant whose seed-cones carry a drowsy pollen that lulls foes into slumber. It hurls these cones as small, heavy bombs, and each burst leaves a fine haze that smells of resin and warm moss.

rites.name: Brodon
rites.text: Brodon is a grounded, mortal-scale fighter of the E6 era in Thudarneld, known for a rhythmic footwork style that unsettles foes. His swift, sweeping strikes rattle opponents' balance and reflexes for a short time.

rites.name: Haladonen
rites.text: Haladonen is a sonic-resonance technique that the reef-drakes of Thudarneld use to rattle the nerves of rivals, turning dread into lethargy for half a minute. Practitioners carry the cadence as a charm, and a bonded pair can add a second strike to their blows.

rites.name: Moraroldock
rites.text: Moraroldock is a grounded concept from the third age of Thudarneld, a slow ember-lattice that coils through the mineral seams of the western highlands. It stores heat from sunlit crystal and releases it as a spiraling current whose strength swells with the mood of the sky.

rites.name: Jorenusten
rites.text: Jorenusten is a grounded tide-warden's ward-plate, a flat shell of salt-cured bronze that stores the force of every blow it turns aside and releases it as a surge of stamina to whoever carries it. Its bearers are taught to strike a rhythm into their defense, so that each deflected blow feeds the next counter. In the pre-dawn trials of Thudarneld's coastal guilds, a plate that stopped one heavy hammer swing was recorded as having kicked back enough force to rattle a stone breakwater.

rites.name: Tarnaren
rites.text: Tarnaren is a slow-burning light-lance woven by reclusive glassweavers of the Hollow Coast, who spin a spiral of pale radiance around a chosen foe. Its ember lingers and pulses more fiercely when mist and storm gather overhead, so a stormy dusk can turn a single gleam into a ruinous slow fire.

rites.name: Breralde
rites.text: Breralde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a foul-breathed cloud-maker whose exhalations sap the strength of anyone standing nearby. Its power is modest in scale, suited to a single village's worth of trouble rather than any sweeping catastrophe.

rites.name: Tarnoden
rites.text: Tarnoden is a sealed ceramic tuning-coil that hums with bottled storm-light, worn as a bracelet by Glassreef sky-couriers of the Thudarneld drylands. When struck against a metal rail it grants the bearer a crackling lattice of static barbs for one minute, sharpening their grip and reflexes.

rites.name: Thardon
rites.text: Thardon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting: a ward-weaver's sigil that hardens the skin and bones of every ally standing within its circle. Its protection lasts half an hour and can be renewed every twenty seconds, and each refinement by its masters deepens the armor it grants.

rites.name: Kelanar
rites.text: Kelanar is a ground-bound concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a lattice of sworn tidewardens who tune soil resonance to steady the minds of nearby travellers. Its influence extends only as far as its anchored stones can hum, and it must be attuned at a sunken basin before the pattern can be woven.

rites.name: Cranuldeld
rites.text: Cranuldeld is a grounded, sphere-shaped sentinel of the Thudarneld, a slow-breathing stone that hums beneath the valley floors of its era. When provoked it condenses ambient heat and pressure into a spinning ember-core and hurls it outward, scorching fields and cracking hillsides in a single rolling burst.

rites.name: Tarneldock
rites.text: Tarneldock is a grounded, unassuming waystone-craft practiced in the lowland village of Oss Harrowmere, where a sealed resonance-glyph lets a keeper pull willing companions across short stretches of muddy farmland. The working requires a copper ring the keeper has bonded to over years, and only those who have spent long apprenticeship at the anvil may learn it.

rites.name: Craneld
rites.text: Craneld is a grounded concept-entity of the Thudarneld omniverse, a wandering hoist-spirit that lifts the burdens of allies by trimming the waiting time on their hard-won gifts. Its power scales with the roll of a fate-die it carries, offering anywhere from a sliver to half of the remaining wait.

rites.name: Kelardoden
rites.text: Kelardoden is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse: a slow, earth-bound practice of drawing down weight and sediment to dull the will of a foe's mind. Its practitioners plant small carved stones that hum a low pressure over whatever lies within their reach, leaving opponents sluggish and unfocused. The discipline is taught only to those who have first mastered a gentler pressure of the same kind.

rites.name: Fenudar
rites.text: Fenudar is a waystone-spell of the Thudarneld realm's Grounded era, used by healers of the Lantern Choir who must carry a sealed ember-key within arm's reach. Once the key is held close, the spell draws the bearers across the valley to a distant resonance stone hidden in the high moors. Only choir-sisters who have reached the fortieth year of their vigil may cast it.

rites.name: Brernon
rites.text: Brernon is a concept of consecrated radiance in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a sacred flame that burns only for those who have sworn to shield others. Its wielders kindle it through vows rather than fuel, and it is said to cleanse curses and scorch shadows from the marrow of the dead. Within the locale of powers it is treated as a rare heritage passed among sworn guardians.

rites.name: Drustenar
rites.text: Drustenar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a lattice of bound earth-currents that a practitioner can coax into weakening the guard of any foe standing within a tethered stone-circle's reach. Its lore holds that the art must first be earned by sinking one's own sense into a flooded cistern of silt and sung-out tremors after mastering a lesser binding of the same family.

rites.name: Halestanen
rites.text: Halestanen is a rootbound lattice of humming crystal lodged in the thick clay of Thudarneld, a concept that channels ambient earth-tension into a mantle of quickening for nearby travelers. Its strength fades steadily with distance from the anchor stone it grows around. Ancient wardens learned its song only after descending through a sunken vault of mirrored basalt.

rites.name: Halarnar
rites.text: Halarnar is a clockwork concept of a predatory talon that gouges through stone to drain the warmth from whatever it strikes. Its scrap-forged blades were rumored to wake dormant iron-veined hills when drawn across the dusk.

rites.name: Brodath
rites.text: Brodath is a hand-forged bulwark of riveted tin and salt-glass, carried by the Ossuary wardens of Thudarneld to turn aside falling stones and thrown spears. Its lamps dim with every blow it absorbs, and wardens say a shield is not truly spent until its last spark gutters out.

rites.name: Keledarnath
rites.text: Keledarnath is a rune-scribed ember-lantern forged in the drowned foundries of Thudarneld, its flame drawn from old cinder-sap and bound to a single chosen bearer. It was built during the third age of the Grounded realm to guide miners through the sunless tunnels beneath the sea-cliffs.

rites.name: Thorden
rites.text: Thorden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a hollow-bodied drifter of the sixth era who lingers in abandoned quarries and sinks into the minds of miners. Its touch saps the strength from whoever it grasps, leaving them weakened while it gathers a little of their vitality for itself.

rites.name: Pelernon
rites.text: Pelernon is a deliberate, low-cost surface-weather ritual born in the Grounded realm's sixth age, where wandering artisans call down a drifting sheet of glassy shards to cleanse dust from fields. It is gentle, rhythmic, and used only by those trained in its slow chanting.

rites.name: Haleruldath
rites.text: Haleruldath is a slow-burning ember-weaver of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, a concept of cinder-spirals that coil around a foe and eat its vitality over long moments. Its heat swells or fades with the sky above, so storms dampen it while dry, scorching days feed it.

rites.name: Pelurnon
rites.text: Pelurnon is a grounded ward-sigil of the Thudarneld concept-era, a spiral of braided stone-glyphs that a warden inscribes onto a threshold. While the warden stands within its reach, every companion sheltered beneath the spiral shrugs off a fraction of hostile sorcery.

rites.name: Peludar
rites.text: Peludar is a cheerful, root-bodied seedling-warden of the Grounded realm, who tends fields with a gentle bristle of leaves. Its presence quietly sharpens the vigor of nearby farmers while sapping the stamina of anyone who would trample its crops.

rites.name: Halarurnock
rites.text: Halarurnock is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's E6 era, a stone-woven ward that gathers the loose soil of a village square into a single crushing burst. Its work is local and short, rarely reaching beyond the length of a few cart lengths before the rubble settles.

rites.name: Haleste
rites.text: Haleste is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet sigil-warden who binds lesser wardstones into a shared hum that steadies anyone standing close to her. Her sigils fade the moment she steps beyond their reach. She learned the craft from a sunken cistern beneath the old salt mill after first mastering a lesser ward-song.

rites.name: Fenadock
rites.text: Fenadock is a modest, bell-shaped mechanical companion that hums a bright tune to nearby travelers, quickening their steps and reflexes for a brief stretch. Its gift is small and gentle, a warmth passed from one tired body to the next across the rolling fields of its home.

rites.name: Kelernaldar
rites.text: Kelernaldar is a grounded spell-ritual of the E6 age in Thudarneld, a rite of stone-binding where a caster plants a sigil-anchored shard that lends strength to every ally who stands within its humming reach. Its wardens say the shard must be earned by first mastering a lesser warding in the high cisterns of the old quarries.

rites.name: Kelastath
rites.text: Kelastath is a concept of rooted stillness drawn from the bedrock of Thudarneld, a discipline in which a warden plants a hushed stone-sigil that dulls the aim of every foe within its reach. Its emanation lasts only while the warden keeps the sigil within sight of the battle. The lesson is taught only at a cracked vault beneath the tomb-fields, to those who have first mastered the sister art of drifting shadows.

rites.name: Halereld
rites.text: Halereld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe: a small guardian ward worn as a token of protection against lingering afflictions, its wearer shielded from the next hostile effect that would strike them. Built in the seventh age of the E6 era, it is a quiet, low-power charm that bends the ordinary rules of harm only briefly.

rites.name: Tarneren
rites.text: Tarneren is a concept of quiet dread native to the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a fear-current that moves through the air like a held breath. Those who stand within its widening arc find their limbs locked and their thoughts stilled, while the Tarneren itself draws strength from the very terror it provokes.

rites.name: Morunarde
rites.text: Morunarde is a ritual sigil-craft of the Thudarneld powers, drawn in ash and bound to a single oath carved into the wielder's bone. When invoked, it hardens the air into a shell that deflects falling stone and blunt force for the length of a long breath.

rites.name: Halostock
rites.text: Halostock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a sturdy ember-engine worn on the back of a cave-dwelling herder, used to coax a warming flare from the chest. Its flare is modest, enough to scorch a rival's hide and drive off predators, and the device needs a long cooldown to vent its heat.

rites.name: Tarnorden
rites.text: Tarnorden is a sealed tide-engine of the Grounded realm, built in the third age of the E6 era to hold back a drowning valley. Its single lock-gate can channel a surge of water roughly the force of a collapsing hillside onto one chosen target.

rites.name: Fenernar
rites.text: Fenernar is a grounded martial art technique in the Thudarneld setting, taught in mountain monasteries as a kick that rises out of the body's own momentum. Practitioners learn to let it arrive unbidden, a single strike that lifts an opponent clear of the ground. It is seven years into its current teaching lineage.

rites.name: Keledarock
rites.text: Keledarock is a grounded resonance-stone of the sixth era, a dense ochre crystal that hums when near living bodies. Its chime quietly steadies the heartbeat of anyone who stands within a stone's throw of the spire it is planted in. It is a concept-level artifact with no notable violent history.

rites.name: Halurdarnon
rites.text: Halurdarnon is a grounded concept of a sealed mineral vein beneath the Thudarneld valleys that hums when touched by a trained hand. Its stored resonance can steady the nerves and sharpen the aim of every person standing within a short distance of a placed stone anchor.

rites.name: Kelarnar
rites.text: Kelarnar is a concept of ammunition-charged focus in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where a warden's stored resolve is bound into a single sigil-loaded arm. It can be recharged at any moment by reciting the old binding, though each rite consumes unevenly across the many strikes it powers.

rites.name: Crudar
rites.text: Crudar is a grounded, self-sharpening blade-spell technique of the Thudarneld frontier, taught by roaming duelists who hum while they practice. Its strikes scale with the fighter's rising momentum, and the cadence of a veteran's stance can be read as a sign of how much fury they have stored. Practitioners treat the marks it leaves as a mark of pride and a warning to rivals.

rites.name: Thenoldock
rites.text: Thenoldock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe: a resonant lattice of standing stones that lends quickening to any traveler walking within its humming ring. The stones draw their hum from the soil beneath, so the effect fades the moment a companion strays beyond the circle's reach.

rites.name: Keleradock
rites.text: Keleradock is a grounded, ember-hearted warrior of the Thudarneld clans, who hurls its whole body forward wrapped in kindled cinders to break stone gates and scatter rival war-bands. Its charge is famed across the highland markets as a rite of passage, though the scorched ground it leaves behind is never quick to heal.

rites.name: Joruron
rites.text: Joruron is a humble hopping creature of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, its strikes delivered by a single hind leg. Its sharp kick lands with precision that grows when it has gathered its nerve, and it can only strike again after a short breathless pause.

rites.name: Creldanath
rites.text: Creldanath is a humble healing herb-spirit of the Grounded realm's third age, a small rooted presence that knits wounds on contact and is said to grow back wherever it is harvested. Its restorative sprigs are gathered by wanderers and carried in pouches, where they keep their mending power for a short season after picking.

rites.name: Crerdostath
rites.text: Crerdostath is a concept of a grounded, mortal-scale rite in the Thudarneld, practiced by lamp-keepers who carry a sealed ember through the high passes of their valley. Only those who have been sworn to the ember and stand within its circle may be drawn along the ember-path to the distant Hollow Tower. The rite is restricted to keepers who have reached the seventh of the nine vows.

rites.name: Brolden
rites.text: Brolden is a grounded, mechanical stat-enhancement system within the Thudarneld setting, used by wardens to fortify their own bodies. Its practitioners layer durable plating and reinforced reflexes before entering rough terrain or combat.

rites.name: Fenerde
rites.text: Fenerde is a grounded concept, a quiet wellspring of stored pressure that lies dormant under the river-plains of Thudarneld until a lineage of herders sings it awake. Its rare discharges can split a ravine or lift a cart from the road, yet the people of the valley treat it less as a weapon than as a debt the land is slowly repaying.

rites.name: Halanen
rites.text: Halanen is a grounded-realm concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a siphoning craft in the Era of the Sixth Veil that draws restless vitality from nearby creatures and channels it into the caster. Its practitioners fear the dead, whose hollow flesh gives nothing back.

rites.name: Fenastock
rites.text: Fenastock is a sealed wooden lantern kept by the drum-keepers of Thudarneld, said to hold a single held breath of morning fog. When lit, it steadies the hands and quickens the eyes of whoever carries it for the length of a bell-toll. Its ember flickers out on its own once the ward has been spent.

rites.name: Halurdonar
rites.text: Halurdonar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet discipline of rooted stone-channeling taught to apprentices of the third age. Its practitioners bind a standing marker into the earth, and everyone sheltered within its reach feels their muscles harden with borrowed sturdiness.

rites.name: Fenadurdon
rites.text: Fenadurdon is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet rhythm of stone-plated sentinels that thrum beneath the earth of a seventh-age valley. Its signature act is a deep tremor that rolls through bedrock and can topple a village's walls at once.

rites.name: Tarnosteld
rites.text: Tarnosteld is a quiet hush-charm woven into the soles of traveling boots, muffling footfalls so that hunting beasts reliant on hearing pass by unaware. It does nothing against creatures that rely on keen vision or sharp, true senses to find their prey.

rites.name: Crustedar
rites.text: Crustedar is a grounded earth-bound concept from the sixth era of Thudarneld, a slow stone-binding ward that dulls the footing of anyone standing within its reach. It belongs to the locale of powers and is bound to the third age of its realm.

rites.name: Joradeld
rites.text: Joradeld is a grounded concept of a veil-weaver's trick: the bearer spins a fog of drifting duplicates that each take a blow meant for them. Once woven, the veil sharpens the wearer's reflexes, though it must be rewoven after a minute of rest.

rites.name: Cruron
rites.text: Cruron is a concept of a grounded, slow-burning sickness that spreads through a herd of wind-driven pastoral beasts across the Thudarneld plains. Those touched by its bellow find their wounds knitting shut poorly and their reserves of vigor draining away, though the herd itself carries it without apparent harm.

rites.name: Morenock
rites.text: Morenock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed-off ice-wrought ward that a mountain-dwelling order of wardens learned to cast around their own bodies. Its shield of frozen needles turns aside blows and steadies the mind for two minutes at a time, and the wardens recharge it once a minute.

rites.name: Kelurneldar
rites.text: Kelurneldar is a rune-inscribed bronze tuning fork carried by the wandering lamplighters of Thudarneld, used to still restless ghosts. When struck against stone it sends a fivefold shiver through whatever it touches, leaving a lingering chill that slowly numbs the target's will.

rites.name: Crestoldar
rites.text: Crestoldar is a grounded, seventh-age concept of a hastened mind: a brass lattice worn at the temple that lets its bearer seize extra moments of thought and motion. It is treated across the Thudarneld reckoning as a discipline of craftsmen rather than a weapon, though the lattice's hold on time has been known to fray under strain.

rites.name: Thustoden
rites.text: Thustoden is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, an era-six setting of crafted magic where the earth answers to drawn sigils. Its practitioners command a single pulse of seismic force that ripples outward from a chosen foe, striking every nearby creature in a ring. The technique is taught only through hand-copied vellum rolls recovered from fallen war-wizards of the mountain hosts.

rites.name: Kelasturock
rites.text: Kelasturock is a mirror-plated ward-beast of the Grounded realm, shaped like a crouched bronze hound whose hide sheds layered shields that drink in incoming force. Its feats are measured against the ten-billion-joule ceiling of its era, and it is revered by stone-shepherds as a guardian that cannot be worn through.

rites.name: Peludar
rites.text: Peludar is a tidal-spirit concept of the Grounded realm in the third age of E6, a drifting current of memory that settles over quarrelling villages and holds them still until they recall why they fought. Its influence reaches only as far as the sound of its hum carries across still water.

rites.name: Fenuldardon
rites.text: Fenuldardon is a grounded tactical technique in the Thudarneld world, a spear-thrust of stored kinetic force that its wielders learn during their seventh age of training. The practitioner braces the shaft against the earth and releases the held tension in a single line of motion. It is a weapon-art rather than a cataclysm, prized for its precision.

rites.name: Fenurden
rites.text: Fenurden is a concept of a quiet, dust-colored sphere of settled resonance that hangs above the grounded plains of Thudarneld in the third age of the sixth era. Anyone within its reach finds their steadiness softened, as if the ground itself were loosening their footing and their aim. Scholars treat it as a gentle weight rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Drene
rites.text: Drene is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an Enhancing rite of the Grounded realm that calls a soft, drifting downpour over a chosen ally. The rain itself harms no one, but it lets certain wards and charms in the locale wake and draw strength from the damp air.

rites.name: Cronock
rites.text: Cronock is a grounded concept of a warding-ritual, a lattice of resonant bronze sigils that a mender traces over a company of travelers to harden them against sorcerous assault. Its protection swells with the wearer's practiced skill at weaving, and an advanced form of the rite exists for those who master it.

rites.name: Joranolde
rites.text: Joranolde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting: a mineral-keeping discipline in which a practitioner anchors a slow, warm field into the soil so that everyone standing inside it gains a sense of footing. Its effect is subtle, a steadying of balance and an easier turn of the blade, and it requires a prior vow of stillness before the anchoring can be sworn.

rites.name: Drare
rites.text: Drare is a grounded, mortal-scale defensive technique in Thudarneld's E6 era, taught in hushed lessons to scouts and sentries who must survive ambushes. It works by splitting the body's afterimage across a handful of ghostly trails that bait a blade or arrow into empty air.

rites.name: Drostelden
rites.text: Drostelden is a grounded ritual of the Thudarneld order, a rite of bright binding that calls a traveler and their companions across the hills to a hidden tower of pale stone. Only those who have reached the sixth rank of the healing circle may perform it, and it requires a carried sigil of the old mountain glass. Its power is modest, meant for road-weary pilgrims rather than wars.

rites.name: Kelastonock
rites.text: Kelastonock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a standing ward of dense sediment-glass that hums with protective resonance around those who stand within its reach. Its keepers train for years before they are allowed to raise its shield. Within its radius, every ally becomes steadier against spells that would otherwise tear at their minds.

rites.name: Thornar
rites.text: Thornar is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded way of amplifying a single dark stroke held in reserve for a few minutes at a time. Its wielders can bank the stored power of their next hostile working, though any other gesture spends the reserve early.

rites.name: Thuldoren
rites.text: Thuldoren is a grounded ward-craft in the Thudarneld powers, a shimmering sigil that a warden inks across the air to blunt magical harm for everyone standing beneath it. It can be renewed every few heartbeats at a steady cost of spent reserve, letting a company of allies shrug off spellfire together.

rites.name: Jorerdude
rites.text: Jorerdude is a sealed resonance cant in the Thudarneld concept-ring, a hum-thread that lets a bearer pull a companion held in a shared ferrule across the grain to a waiting tower of pale glass. Only adepts who have passed the ninth ringing may draw the thread, and the cant is never taught to the unready.

rites.name: Halernath
rites.text: Halernath is a warding concept in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a shield of stilled air that hangs over whoever stands within its reach and hardens their hides against blows. It can only be taught to a practitioner after they have mastered its earthen twin, which sinks the same protection into the soil beneath them.

rites.name: Halurden
rites.text: Halurden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a slow-tilling force of the earth's own patience that knits wounds in those who stand within its reach. It is taught only after its mirror is understood, and its warmth lingers in the soil long after the bearer walks on. Its gentle mending serves the tilled fields and the people working them.

rites.name: Jorudorneld
rites.text: Jorudorneld is a grounded, heavily armored war-song of the Thudarneld cavaliers, a sworn chant that hardens steel-clad riders against blows meant to unhorse them. Its wielders sing through the third age of their order, and the chant is said to shield a charge that can crack stone walls.

rites.name: Tarneren
rites.text: Tarneren is a frost-bound warden who lives in the glacial spires of its homeworld, sculpting ice into weapons that fall like judgment. Its ability to drop sheer shards of cold from high altitude makes it feared across the northern reaches. It is considered a grounded, modest figure whose strikes are precise rather than cataclysmic.

rites.name: Thuden
rites.text: Thuden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a slow, patient mending force that knits flesh and bone back together over the course of an afternoon. It is the third and most refined of the mender-arts taught in the Grey Cloisters of Ostrel, where apprentices learn to ration its warmth across long vigils.

rites.name: Peleden
rites.text: Peleden is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a quiet art of tempering venom in the blood of travelers. Its practitioners ease the sting of toxins by drawing the poison's bite into a brief, measured cycle of rest.

rites.name: Halurne
rites.text: Halurne is a grounded, fleet-footed drifter of the E6 powers era who can outrun gravity's own pull across a wind-scoured plateau. Its stride carries it through a sprint that scatters loose stone and leaves the air ringing. Hardened by seven years of solitary travel, it can absorb a lot of punishment and keep moving.

rites.name: Fenadeldath
rites.text: Fenadeldath is a clawed war-technique of the Grounded realm, a rapid cycle of six strikes that a trained fighter can set in advance to sharpen reflexes for a short window. Its wielders reserve it for ambush and must wait a full minute before loosing it again.

rites.name: Moranock
rites.text: Moranock is a grounded concept, a sacred resonance-knot woven by the wardens of Thudarneld to steady the minds of anyone who stands near its bearer. Its calming hum sharpens the aim and focus of every ally within its reach, though the knot must first be taught to a student before the warden's deeper weave can follow.

rites.name: Pelesturnen
rites.text: Pelesturnen is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a practice of quiet sun-warded ritual in the third age of the sixth era. Its practitioners briefly dim the eyes of nearby allies so that a sudden flash of hostile light lands harmlessly, a craft refined over generations of mountain-watch.

rites.name: Jorostar
rites.text: Jorostar is a quiet, bell-shaped tide-warden of the Grounded realm, whose humming presence lends steadiness to every creature within its resonance field. Its life is one of patient tending, never spectacle, and it draws on the slow pulse of the earth to keep nearby kin hardy and unhurried. Thudarneld's elders regard it as a gentle keel steadying a drifting vessel.

rites.name: Morernudeld
rites.text: Morernudeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a humble cooking-pan of shared heritage that its wielders swing to stun foes in a wide arc. It draws on the rhythm of a camp kitchen, where a quick flourish and a patient pause decide who keeps their footing.

rites.name: Haledurnon
rites.text: Haledurnon is a grounded, low-tier concept in Thudarneld, a quiet and modest thing that hums softly within the reach of a single village. Its effects are small and local, sustaining a gentle glow over the wearer's spirit for a brief spell before it fades.

rites.name: Kelede
rites.text: Kelede is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a quiet discipline of the eyes practiced by border wardens who learn to keep their sight through glare, smoke, and dust storms. Its adepts gain stages of resistance over a long apprenticeship, each stage marking a new tier of focus.

rites.name: Halastunock
rites.text: Halastunock is a grounded, aged concept in the Thudarneld universe: a dull bronze hand-bell whose chime steadies the minds of those who hear it. Its ringing makes the memory-stealing fog of the mire-wights thin and fade for several heartbeats before it can gather again.

rites.name: Croldarde
rites.text: Croldarde is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a slow-burning craft of stone-cutting and root-tending that its practitioners pass hand to hand across three ages. Its ceremonies never seek to rend the world, only to coax steady endurance from the earth beneath them.

rites.name: Drureld
rites.text: Drureld is a grounded wind-scythe of the E6 age, a curved reaping blade whose edge hums with stored tension and bites deepest when the wielder's momentum is perfectly aligned. Three generations old, it is prized by harvesters who clear thorn-fields and cut through hardened ropes of the lowland forests. Its keepers say its strikes fall hardest on the unlucky, not the skilled, and they carry it with a careful, respectful grip.

rites.name: Fenestath
rites.text: Fenestath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a shimmering veil of pale glass-light that a wandering stonewright raises between villages to pull enchantments off passing travelers. Its raisers can set it only by paying a fixed toll of inked sigils, and each raising leaves its wearer slightly weaker in body while swelling their reserve of ambient charm.

rites.name: Kelerar
rites.text: Kelerar is a grounded wind-warden of the E6 age, a three-year-old order of cliff-nesting falconers in Thudarneld who train their young to strike with a diving shoulder-check. Its members can channel a sharp gust into a single target, lifting and hurling the foe backward.

rites.name: Thodurdath
rites.text: Thodurdath is a grounded, cloistered order of ink-stained scribes who bind their wills to a silent glass lattice in the valley of Ossery. Each adept commands a single arcane compound that can dissolve iron walls or lull a crowd into sleep, though the practice leaves the caster weary for days afterward.

rites.name: Drustath
rites.text: Drustath is a concept of grounded, pale-stone resonance that hums through the mountain roots of Thudarneld in the sixth era, binding the rhythms of the land to those who listen. It is less a force than a patient tuning, a quiet agreement between earth and the hands that tend it.

rites.name: Jorudernen
rites.text: Jorudernen is a spore-crowned sap-warden of the grounded thickets of Thudarneld, a creature whose blossom hums with stored pollen. When it exhales a fine cloud of seed-dust it strips the armor-hardening lacquer from anything nearby, leaving foes brittle for a short while. Its wardens teach that the cloud is strongest when the blossom is fully swollen, and that a bloom must rest a long time before it can breathe again.

rites.name: Moroldath
rites.text: Moroldath is a sleepless tide-warden of the Thudarneld shoals, a concept of attuned calm that gathers around whoever stands within its hum and steadies their thoughts. Its radius shrinks the moment it stops believing in its own company. It can be taught to others only after they have first learned to listen.

rites.name: Halodarnen
rites.text: Halodarnen is a grounded, low-stakes tool of the Thudarneld world, a brass-and-cord bell that a village hums into to freeze the nearest wandering animals for a few heartbeats. Its makers rarely needed more power than a barn door would release. Its frame is still in use after three ages of careful repair.

rites.name: Pelolde
rites.text: Pelolde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a lattice of resonant stone-song that lets a bearer quicken the reflexes of nearby allies while the resonance holds. It must be attuned in a lesser ward before its inverse can be sung, and its hum fades once the bearer strays beyond the hearing radius.

rites.name: Brurdath
rites.text: Brurdath is a grounded creature of Thudarneld, a slow-breathing reef-dweller whose skin secretes a toxic mucus that clings to nearby prey and dissolves them over time. Its mucus is harvested by local fishers to coat their nets, and a single drop can sting a wooden hull for days.

rites.name: Keledonar
rites.text: Keledonar is a grounded concept of a slow-glass lantern carried by wardens of the Thudarneld highlands, whose pale light dims the momentum of anything hostile that stays inside its glow. The lantern must be kindled with a lesser flame before its brighter counterpart can be lit, and wardens treat it as a discipline to master in order.

rites.name: Moradeldar
rites.text: Moradeldar is a quiet ward-spell of the Grounded realm that softens the grip of enforced slumber on any bound mind, its strength rising with the caster's years of practice. Its lesser form is taught to every apprentice, while its refined version is the sole province of seasoned healers who can lift the weight of dreams from several sleepers at once.

rites.name: Tarnanodock
rites.text: Tarnanodock is a grounded, low-tier mechanical arts technique practiced in the E6 era, in which a practitioner tunes a brass lattice to press a fan-shaped wedge of air downward, sapping the muscle of anything caught within it. It takes a few heartbeats to prime and recharges slowly, leaving the practitioner noticeably more perceptive while the lattice is set.

rites.name: Jorostarnon
rites.text: Jorostarnon is a grounded geomantic concept in the Thudarneld world, a slow-sinking chant that weighs down the footing of foes within its reach. It must be taught before its twin rite can be learned, and it is traded by a quiet sage in a frost-bound lowland city.

rites.name: Dreldon
rites.text: Dreldon is a grounded concept of a quiet, hand-carved tuning-fork that hums in the presence of stored tension, its tone rising as the bearer draws more force into it. Its later pitches are said to rattle shutters for a full league, though it has never been measured beyond a village's worth of noise.

rites.name: Dreneld
rites.text: Dreneld is a grounded concept of a soil-bound mind that quiets any creature standing within the reach of its roots, holding them motionless until they step beyond its dominion. It is a concept of stillness and rootedness rather than force, and it lives in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld as a gentle but binding presence.

rites.name: Peledore
rites.text: Peledore is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's Era Six, a gravity-anchored sentinel that channels the local ambient energy into a single radiant discharge. Its signature act is a sanctified pulse that scours whatever stands within its arc.

rites.name: Braldeld
rites.text: Braldeld is a grounded practitioner's technique from the Thudarneld reckoning, a discipline of quiet fortification in which a single contained strike is charged by stored resolve. It is taught by a patient order of stone-readers and rarely used in open combat.

rites.name: Jorestar
rites.text: Jorestar is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's E6 age, a reusable bonus-trait that amplifies chained strikes so that each linked blow carries a fraction of the chain's stored force into the target. Practitioners layer three resonant tiers of attacks, with the most advanced arrangements letting a single relic-forged sequence produce one further tier of release. Its effects are described as tuned to the strength of the wielder's craft rather than to raw power.

rites.name: Fenardolde
rites.text: Fenardolde is a quiet geomantic ward-stone carried by traveling wardens of Thudarneld, who speak its name as a promise of steadiness. When lifted, it lends a sharpened grace of hand and footing to every companion walking within its gentle reach. Its binding must be taught in order, each lesson gating the next.

rites.name: Cradostock
rites.text: Cradostock is a humble ward-brewing tincture from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, prized by hedge-healers who soak it into bandages. Its quiet properties ease the lingering fog that follows a shock, letting companions in a circle think clearly again within moments of application.

rites.name: Cruldastock
rites.text: Cruldastock is a sealed-mind concept in Thudarneld, a grounded era-six tool that pulls a single hidden trait from any creature it touches and binds it to the wielder for seven hours. Its ceiling keeps it to modest, mechanical forces, so it works through precision and timing rather than raw power.

rites.name: Pelure
rites.text: Pelure is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a small stone-skinned seed-guardian of the third age who drifts between orchard villages. Its gaze unravels the protective wards and blessings clinging to a foe, leaving them bare for a brief moment.

rites.name: Thordath
rites.text: Thordath is a grounded, tiny sky-drifter of the Thudarneld frontier, a soft-bodied flier whose wing-membranes shimmer with trapped static. It is quick enough to slip between the legs of much larger fauna and is said to shake loose the stored tension of foes it brushes against. Herders trade its shed plumes as charms against drowsiness.

rites.name: Joroldon
rites.text: Joroldon is a quiet, grounded concept in Thudarneld's third age, a kind of tempered resonance that a practitioner draws from their own inner reserves rather than from the world around them. It grows steadily with training and reshapes everything a caster can do, so that even modest gifts become formidable in the right hands.

rites.name: Pelornureld
rites.text: Pelornureld is a silent discipline in the Thudarneld omniverse, taught in the grey monasteries of the sixth era to strike a single foe with a stored surge of lethal focus. Practitioners hold their breath, gather a fleeting charge in the spine, and release it through one blow that can drop a cavalry horse or a heavy oak door. Its masters regard it as craft rather than magic, measured more by timing than by force.

rites.name: Morurenath
rites.text: Morurenath is a grounded sea-keeping sorcerer of the Thudarneld drowned coasts, whose skin weeps brine that hardens into a protective sheen against spells. Her tide-tattoos steady her footing and quicken her limbs for a minute at a time, and she can renew the coating only once that minute has passed.

rites.name: Peloldon
rites.text: Peloldon is a grounded concept of a tireless lamplighter-warrior who spins a ring of rune-etched hooks to scrape rust from the walls of drowned tunnels. Its spin dulls the aim of anyone who watches it too long, which the tunnel-folk call its quiet gift.

rites.name: Cresturdath
rites.text: Cresturdath is a grounded concept of a small, fast-striking mimic-beast from the third age of Thudarneld, prized by hunters for its three rapid clawed lashes. Its attacks scale with the rage it has built up, and it can only unleash the flurry once every half minute.

rites.name: Brostath
rites.text: Brostath is a grounded concept of a stubborn mountain-dwelling warrior-smith whose strikes grow quicker as its own hunger deepens. Its hammer-blows are measured in the rhythm of a forge bellows, and each rapid strike carries a modest but real bite of force.

rites.name: Thune
rites.text: Thune is a quiet concept of stone-resistance found in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where it is granted to wardens of the fourth era after seven years of training. Its bearers can briefly shrug off the hardening of flesh into rock, though each renewal of the ward grows shorter with age.

rites.name: Thuldaston
rites.text: Thuldaston is a sleet-lacquered mountain hamlet whose wardens bind the weather of the valley to the moods of their fields. A reader of frost signs can coax a cold front into a fellow traveller's cloak, blunting fire and sharpening ice in that person's hands. Those trained in the old sky-ledgers gain a keener mind while the squall hums around them.

rites.name: Bredarath
rites.text: Bredarath is a lantern-steel blade forged in the drowned foundries of Thudarneld, its edge fed by slow-burning ember-moss that blooms into a crimson flare when struck. In the hands of a sworn Tidewarden, it can cleave the waterlogged bedrock of a ruined harbor city in a single clean stroke.

rites.name: Drunoste
rites.text: Drunoste is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, an ability that freezes a moment of time for a single beat before motion resumes. It is used by wardens of the old river-towns to halt falling debris and runaway carts.

rites.name: Moruranath
rites.text: Moruranath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a hushed, seasonal ritual of tapping a wellspring of inner resonance so a practitioner can channel effects without drawing on their own reserves. It is mostly remembered for a short, sharp surge that lets a lone conjurer loose several bursts of focus before the reservoir refills.

rites.name: Dronuden
rites.text: Dronuden is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a low-altitude drone-hive that hums above the ash plains of the Sayral basin. Its swarms tether to the surface through slender copper lines and steer their coolant mist to shield allied caravans from sunfire.

rites.name: Fenardeld
rites.text: Fenardeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a quiet ward-spell that a hearth-keeper lights to shield a household from shadow-born blight. It draws a little of the keeper's own vitality as fuel, so it only holds as long as the keeper stays willing to tend it.

rites.name: Kelardath
rites.text: Kelardath is a sealed-cloud lattice of resonant glass shards that drifts above the high tundra of Thudarneld, drawing warmth out of anything that touches it to feed its slow-burning heart. Scavenger guilds prize the shards as healing lenses, though each one slowly drinks the vitality of its bearer.

rites.name: Feneldorden
rites.text: Feneldorden is a quiet, grounded mana-restoring rite practiced by wandering hedge-scribes of the Thudarneld reaches, who inscribe slow-burning sigils onto a traveler's palm. The sigils drip spent willpower back into the body over a long walk, and the old scribes say a single well-drawn mark can refill a weary mage's reserves across an afternoon. Its strength lies in patience rather than surge, so its listed energies stay modest.

rites.name: Bruron
rites.text: Bruron is a grounded concept of a low-tier ward-worker in the Thudarneld order, a practitioner who weaves protective sigils against sickness that spread through crowded markets. Its craft is modest and steady, so it is most useful among those who tend the sick and stave off plague in a long, patient struggle.

rites.name: Croneld
rites.text: Croneld is a quiet, unassuming concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a weathered hymn-ballad that a wandering minstrel sings to draw wrath away from a companion. Its effect is modest, measured in the small hours of a battlefield rather than in cataclysm, and it is prized for what it prevents rather than what it destroys.

rites.name: Haluldock
rites.text: Haluldock is a grounded healing rite of the E6 Thudarneld age, in which a Warden of the Dock-Hollows sings a slow mending over the wounded. Its restorative pulses are measured in heartbeats rather than in spectacle, and its reach is strictly confined to the living body under its hands.

rites.name: Halosten
rites.text: Halosten is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a pair of resonant chord-binders whose woven harmonies lift the aim and focus of every ally within earshot. The lesser weave tightens the eye of a fighter, while the greater one sharpens it until arrows find their marks through smoke and storm.

rites.name: Peludar
rites.text: Peludar is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a Grounded-realm practice of ritual fortification drawn from the E6 era. Practitioners who reach a certain standing learn to temporarily harden the body's endurance through chanted lattices of breath and salt. Its paired discipline lets a second order of adepts reinforce the same resilience in allies.

rites.name: Tarnare
rites.text: Tarnare is a bonded-spirit discipline in a grounded world where a rider's fortitude can be siphoned into a sky-beast companion through a shared breath. Its practitioners earn three cumulative attunements, each costing more of their training focus, and the bond holds only while the rider stays at the peak of their craft and away from sealed trials.

rites.name: Haladon
rites.text: Haladon is a quiet ward-stone of the Grounded realm, carved by hermit clerks to steady the minds of those who keep the village wells. It sharpens a chosen caretaker's attention so that the restless spirits of the district turn toward them rather than their neighbours.

rites.name: Thestar
rites.text: Thestar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet fear-inducing presence that stills the roots and stalks of verdant beings. It is awakened in those who have learned to press two rhythms of battle together until the green things hesitate.

rites.name: Keludarnock
rites.text: Keludarnock is a quiet, grounded mental discipline practiced by the lamp-tenders of Thudarneld, who sharpen their focus by tracing sigils in cold ash. Each practitioner gains a modest edge in clarity and recall that grows with years of study. The art is taught only to those who first learn patience.

rites.name: Drasterath
rites.text: Drasterath is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, an age-seven world where gates between districts are tuned by a quiet, lattice-bound mechanism of the old engineers. Wardens of the sixth era use it to pull a single companion back along the route they came, or to nudge a rival out of the present fight entirely.

rites.name: Kelodath
rites.text: Kelodath is a sustaining chant-art practiced by hearth-wardens of the Thudarneld highlands, who inscribe hardiness into the bodies of their gathered kin. Its wardens learn it only after eighty years of tending embers, and the blessing scales with the warden's mastery of the old tongue.

rites.name: Peloldedon
rites.text: Peloldedon is a concept-grade grounded entity from the Thudarneld omniverse, an engine of surging momentum that tempers its own charge through a slow, patient rhythm. Its early era left it a modest presence, but three ages of drift have given it a stable place among the lesser powers.

rites.name: Crerostock
rites.text: Crerostock is a grounded enhancement of the Thudarneld era E6, a quiet tool passed among a guild of field-hands who tune weather and wind. Its bearer's ranged shots come faster after a short chant, lasting for several minutes before the wind must be coaxed again. It is a modest art, valued for steadiness rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Joruste
rites.text: Joruste is a grounded reflex-art practiced by the wind-scribes of the Thudarneld highlands, who learn to sidestep a blow and answer it with a sharp burst of stored lightning. The technique is passed down through a ritual of defeating shell-backed desert wardens who guard the old salt roads. Adepts are valued for turning an enemy's own momentum into a precise counter-strike.

rites.name: Droldanath
rites.text: Droldanath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet ward-sigil that a wandering mender in the E6 era carries for seven years before it fades. Its bearers can steady a sick body against creeping blight, growing stronger with each level of mastery.

rites.name: Keloldurdon
rites.text: Keloldurdon is a grounded concept from the E6 era, a three-year-old practice of cutting-edge tradecraft among the powers of Thudarneld. Its adepts channel a bonus of precision into the strongest blows they land, so that the rarest strikes hit with far more force than ordinary ones.

rites.name: Tarnuron
rites.text: Tarnuron is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded-realm power that lets a bonded attendant weather blows meant for its master. Practitioners who sustain it reduce the harm their companion creatures absorb in battle. It is a quiet, defensive art rather than one of raw destruction.

rites.name: Haluden
rites.text: Haluden is a concept of a quiet ward-glyph that hums against any attempt to strip a speaker of their voice. Scribes of the Thudarneld cloisters inscribe it on doorframes and throats alike, and it lets a caster shrug off muteness within moments. A stronger variant exists among the cloister's healers, though its mechanics remain a matter of debate.

rites.name: Tarneden
rites.text: Tarneden is a concept of a dread-inducing sigil that makes reptilian foes locked in place by sudden fear, a stillness born of ancient instinct. Its effect is subtle and sporadic, a flicker of terror rather than a blow. Tarneden stands at the threshold of the grounded realm, where such small mercies shape the ordinary struggles of creatures.

rites.name: Fenerorne
rites.text: Fenerorne is a kindling-art of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of Thudarneld, where practitioners coax a single breath of stored heat into a sudden flare. The art is taught in small circles and forbidden in larger ones because a poorly held flare can scorch a whole market square.

rites.name: Pelurdenon
rites.text: Pelurdenon is a grounded, seven-age-old gravitic lattice that hums beneath the crust of Thudarneld, letting its wielders nudge heavy stones into quiet, drifting dances. Its tamers prize it for patient, precise work rather than spectacle, lifting cliffs and setting foundations with careful weight.

rites.name: Crasten
rites.text: Crasten is a grounded concept from the seventh age of Thudarneld, a hushed stillness that clings to the ruins of forgotten mills. Its practitioners halt the turning of gears and the drift of dust for a few heartbeats, a discipline prized by clockwork guilds. Its reach is small, its cost is steep, and no one has ever stopped a falling stone for longer than a breath.

rites.name: Fenuldar
rites.text: Fenuldar is a sealed mana-lattice known in Thudarneld as the Quiet Reservoir, a concept of stored arcane capacity that grows slowly in those who attune to it. Its tiers are granted through ritual rather than training, and only certain disciplines are permitted more than one tier.

rites.name: Tarnordath
rites.text: Tarnordath is a grounded concept, a hollow iron engine that coils through the marsh-mines of Thudarneld and grinds the sediment of old trenches into fuel. Its single signature operation is a slow, drawn-out ignition that vents pressurized steam through its shaft. The mine-wardens treat it as a tool more than a creature.

rites.name: Jorulden
