rites.text: Jorulden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a rhythmic chant that a wandering weaver hums to steady those nearby against incoming blows. Its lesser form is taught to apprentices of the guild, while its greater form is reserved for masters who can hold a crowd together under fire.

rites.name: Broste
rites.text: Broste is a quiet sensing discipline practiced by wayfinders of the Thudarneld highlands, who read the faint tremor of living things through the ground and air. Its practitioners can pick out hidden beasts across a wide valley, though the reach shrinks sharply when the reader must split attention with another craft. In crowded towns the sense becomes almost limitless, since every resident's pulse is audible to a trained ear.

rites.name: Crurne
rites.text: Crurne is a concept of disciplined edge-work in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a style taught to wardens who fight with one blade and a free hand. Practitioners claim a small, steady sharpening of their strikes when their off-hand is empty or braced on a buckler, though two-blade and great-blade schools deny its worth. Its lessons are passed down only after a warden has served three seasons at the rampart.

rites.name: Druldath
rites.text: Druldath is a concept of a grounded, low-energy kind: a small, quiet thing that lives in the Grounded realm's powers locale. It is defined by steady, careful influence rather than force, and works best alongside others who need its focus.

rites.name: Pelolden
rites.text: Pelolden is a grounded fighting discipline practiced in the cold harbour towns of Thudarneld's sixth era, where practitioners learn to unsettle the water-kin who raid the piers. Its strikes do not wound so much as cause the target to freeze in sudden dread, a trait the old dockmasters treat as a folk rite rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Brunon
rites.text: Brunon is a fleece-wrapped mind that lives inside a grounded pasture-world of Thudarneld, where it grazes the low hills and remembers every gate it has ever passed through. Its hooves can crush a stone wall into dust with a single unhurried step, and the herd it keeps follows its bleating across the plains.

rites.name: Pelurnon
rites.text: Pelurnon is a quiet ward-spirit of the Grounded realm, a lattice of soft lantern-light that settles over travelers and keeps their dreams from being stolen. In the third age of Thudarneld it is taught to apprentice wardens as a gentle craft, its glow carried in brass censers hung along the roads.

rites.name: Halerdeld
rites.text: Halerdeld is a quiet, ingrained craft practiced by the lamp-keepers of Thudarneld's grounded provinces, a method of passing a single steadying habit from one generation to the next. Its adepts rarely display power outwardly, preferring to tune the small ordinary things of daily life so they hold together a little longer than they should.

rites.name: Jorurnen
rites.text: Jorurnen is a shieldbound warding discipline practiced by the stonewardens of Thudarneld's lower terraces, where every successful block recharges the defender's inner reserve. Its adepts train by absorbing blows from heavy iron wardbells, turning impact into a faint, steady surge of readiness.

rites.name: Moruren
rites.text: Moruren is a quiet discipline of the Thudarneld powers, practiced by wandering tuners who listen to the hum of loaded stone and retune it. Its gentle adjustments can settle a restless hearth or sharpen a brittle beam, but a careless tuner can bring down a whole wall.

rites.name: Thurdon
rites.text: Thurdon is a grounded, self-sustaining martial discipline in Thudarneld, where practitioners channel a building momentum into strikes that grow stronger with each repeated blow. Its strength is limited by the body and the ground beneath, so its wielders are celebrated for precision rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Halureld
rites.text: Halureld is a drowsy river-guardian of Thudarneld, a thoughtful stone-shaped spirit who dwells beneath the silted banks of the Veyra Delta. Its gentle, rhythmic tremors once cracked clay roads and rang bells in distant villages during its restless dreams.

rites.name: Kelodunar
rites.text: Kelodunar is a grounded, low-stakes ward-craft of the Thudarneld reckoning, a sealed brass lantern that hums when a sick traveller stands in its glow. Its keepers call it a gentle tutor of the body, lightening blight-sickness in everyone who gathers around it. Each time it is rekindled, the lantern's warmth eases the poison's grip for a little while.

rites.name: Halorurnon
rites.text: Halorurnon is a concept of a quiet resonance in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a hum that settles over a gathering and slows the limbs of everyone within its reach. Its effect weakens with the age and attunement of the caster, and it can be sung again only after a short pause. It is the refined successor of an older, clumsier hum that lingered far longer than it was needed.

rites.name: Brorde
rites.text: Brorde is a rhythmic technique of the Thudarneld grounded realm, practiced by wandering drummers who channel a single heartbeat into a flurry of blows. A practitioner can double the strike of their next footfall for a short span before the rhythm must be rebuilt. Its force is modest, suited to felling a man or cracking a stone wall.

rites.name: Fenorne
rites.text: Fenorne is a ward-weaving discipline practiced by the mirror-wardens of the drowned cities, who bind thin layers of resonant glass around a traveler's body. Its protection lasts only a few breaths but deflects the blows of beings whose strikes carry stored rage or ritual charge. Apprentices must master it before they may carry the lantern-key.

rites.name: Pelanodeld
rites.text: Pelanodeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe: a dense, humming resin shaped into ceremonial hooks used by village healers to bind bruised sinew. Its power is modest, limited to coaxing tired muscles back into rhythm and sealing minor wounds.

rites.name: Pelaldestar
rites.text: Pelaldestar is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet lattice of resonant lenses that channels a mage's inner tension into focused force. Its era-six craftsmen calibrated each lens to amplify intent by a fixed fraction, so a trained hand can bend a storm's worth of pressure into a single bright line.

rites.name: Fenardon
rites.text: Fenardon is a grounded dance-technique of the Thudarneld order, taught in seven-year cycles by wandering choreographers. Its signature is a brief window in which a performer's flourishes come back at once and the costly closing gestures cost nothing, though the window can only open once an hour.

rites.name: Peledath
rites.text: Peledath is a concept in Thudarneld, a grounded-realm kind of power that lets a bearer gift darkness its own kind of sanctity, turning a cast shadow into a shelter that holds back harm. Its practitioners are said to bless the gaps where light fails, so that what hides is protected rather than feared.

rites.name: Braneld
rites.text: Braneld is a quiet concept within the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded hum of sustained protective resonance that shields a company of allies from being muted. It exists in two tiers, a humble first form and a refined master form, each stacking with other wards to keep voices unbroken.

rites.name: Peluldon
rites.text: Peluldon is a quiet, rhythmic technique in the Thudarneld realm, taught in the seventh age as a way of drawing steady strength from ordinary bodily motion. Its practitioners mark each act with a hummed count that builds force without ever exceeding what a small town could feel.

rites.name: Crostelde
rites.text: Crostelde is a dancing technique of the Thudarneld powers, where a performer's footwork grows so swift that each strike is doubled, yet the rhythm forbids any healing or lifting steps. Its effect fades gradually as the tempo tires, and it may be renewed only after a pause of three minutes.

rites.name: Tarnustock
rites.text: Tarnustock is a grounded, mid-tier concept of a bonded hunting-beast that gains strength when its handler stands within a thin band of altitude above the herd. Its power is tied to shared breathing and rhythm rather than raw force, so it weakens sharply on cliffs or distant ridges. Within those limits it can drive a small pack of animals into a single coordinated surge.

rites.name: Pelerar
rites.text: Pelerar is a grounded pact-power of Thudarneld's E6 era, a deliberate bargain in which a drifter may name one coming chance and have it fall on the lowest face. It is a quiet, almost clerical craft, favored by gamblers and cartographers who want their luck pinned in place for a single moment.

rites.name: Thodeld
rites.text: Thodeld is a grounded skill in the Thudarneld setting that lets a tamer summon a creature from a bound vessel without spending the vessel, so the same bond can be reused. The bond resets after a long rest, and it cannot be used by anyone who has not first learned to keep a vessel at hand.

rites.name: Morerustath
rites.text: Morerustath is a grounded power concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet discipline that bends an attack's strength to the compass bearing between the wielder and the target. Practitioners train until a single incantation can tilt the outcome of a duel by orienting the body before striking. Its effects are modest, but they reliably turn the odds for whoever understands where the stars sit.

rites.name: Fenoron
rites.text: Fenoron is a minor enchanted tonic of the Grounded realm's E6 era, brewed to steady nerves and lend a speaker quiet authority before a crowd. Its effect lingers for a few minutes across everyone who shares the same gathering hall. Apprentice orators in the province of Thudarneld keep a vial of it close by.

rites.name: Braldeld
rites.text: Braldeld is a grounded kind of focused, deliberate strike drawn from the stillness of its practitioners, a discipline that trades reach for a single concentrated blow. Its bearers hold a breath of stone-quiet for a minute and then release everything into one shaped act, resting for ten minutes afterward. It is used by the Brenlo-Varn wardens to break barricades and split frozen riverbeds.

rites.name: Thodock
rites.text: Thodock is a quiet mental discipline practiced by the wardens of Thudarneld's grounded provinces, who learn to dampen the spiritual noise their own rage leaves behind. Its adepts can bank the fierce resonance of a dying beast into a single stone-cold sigil, which lowers the attention of wandering spirits and keeps hunters from being sensed. The technique is subtle, costly in discipline, and deliberately modest in effect.

rites.name: Pelestoren
rites.text: Pelestoren is a quiet attunement practiced by healers of the Grounded realm, a discipline that lets a mender tend the wounded without drawing the attention of hostile beasts. Its strength rises with the healer's skill in mending, so the most gifted can soothe a battlefield almost unnoticed. It is taught in three stages, each unlocked at a different point in a practitioner's training.

rites.name: Thornon
rites.text: Thornon is a concept of quiet protection, a blessing-chant sung in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld to shield one companion from a fatal blow. Its wardens teach that the chant must be repeated every two dozen heartbeats of the sun and takes four breaths to finish. Its light answers only to the hand that holds the words.

rites.name: Thodernar
rites.text: Thodernar is a slow-breathing lattice of quartz filaments that thrums through the grounded strata of Thudarneld, its hum shaped to hold creatures motionless. It was meant as a dampening field for caravan routes, and it still freezes anything that approaches it with the wrong intent.

rites.name: Halardon
rites.text: Halardon is a quiet, grounded art of bodily resilience taught in the high-altitude monasteries of Thudarneld, where practitioners slowly thicken their vitality through decades of breathwork. Its lessons are passed from master to apprentice in stages, each stage unlocking a deeper reserve of endurance that can be carried into any profession. Only the most disciplined students ever reach its final thresholds.

rites.name: Halarde
rites.text: Halarde is a conceptual grounded power that lets its wielder's body brace against the most devastating blows in a fight, dulling their force before it lands. It was cultivated in the quiet provinces of Thudarneld by those who guard the weak, and it does nothing against harm that arrives slowly or quietly.

rites.name: Kelore
rites.text: Kelore is a concept in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, a quiet hymn of luminous harmony that steadies the eyes of everyone who hears it. Its practitioners sing for a short while before each rest, and the glow they call forth shields allies from being dazzled by sudden flashes. The energy involved is modest, fitting its gentle role in daily life.

rites.name: Halenoldar
rites.text: Halenoldar is a sung ward-melody of the Thudarneld concept-realm, carried by roaming choirs who hum it over fields and hearths. Its refrain steadies stone and flesh alike, letting companions withstand the slow hardening that turns the living to rock.

rites.name: Crorene
rites.text: Crorene is a quiet tuning-art of the Thudarneld powers, in which a practitioner gathers scattered sparks of wind-song into a single slow gust that bends grain and rings bells. It is taught in seven-year cycles in the high terraces of its home realm, and its masters consider it a discipline of patience rather than force.

rites.name: Halonen
rites.text: Halonen is a resonant warding-chant of the Grounded realm's Thudarneld, a hymn sung by singers of the Hollow Choir to steady travelers against the creeping blight of ill-fortune. Its verses are said to bind the hearers' spirits to a shared stillness that repels the sickly hexes of cursed ground.

rites.name: Crostar
rites.text: Crostar is a grounded concept from the E6 era of the Thudarneld, a third-age power that hums a protective resonance through the air around its bearer. Those nearby are shielded against the drowsing tides that others weave to steal their wakefulness. Its effects layer atop any ward already in place, so guardians wrapped in several charms remain stubbornly alert.

rites.name: Bruron
rites.text: Bruron is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a slow-tempered earth-binder whose hum stretches the reach of every stone it touches. Its gift lasts a single minute at a time, after which it must rest for an hour before the land will listen again.

rites.name: Draldon
rites.text: Draldon is a quiet concept in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a discipline that teaches fighters to husband their stored exertion so a practiced strike sometimes costs less than it should. Its practitioners wear the habit like a second skin, refusing to waste effort in idle motion. Their techniques are modest, yet they have carried many a village through lean winters.

rites.name: Crosteld
rites.text: Crosteld is a quiet, rain-soaked concept of a hedge-warden who sings a low hum that makes crawling pests in its vicinity go rigid with dread for a few heartbeats. Its power only touches creatures of the burrowing and skittering kind, leaving birds and beasts untouched. Its ceiling is modest, reflecting a realm where its influence is local and fleeting.

rites.name: Halanordock
rites.text: Halanordock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet discipline of focus that sharpens a bearer's eye and hand toward a single target. Its practitioners are rare, and the greatest among them can thread a needle at a hundred paces with a single breath.

rites.name: Brenock
rites.text: Brenock is a concept of a bonded beast-warden's stored command, held in three ready charges that refill one at a time over a minute each. Each charge lets the warden direct a companion creature to unleash a single chosen strike, and the stored charges are never wasted on idle waiting.

rites.name: Fenarne
rites.text: Fenarne is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a ritual of stone-bound sigils that, when dismissed, quietly returns vitality to nearby allies. Its use is limited by a long cooldown of several minutes, making it a tactical reserve rather than a constant resource.

rites.name: Morudar
rites.text: Morudar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a tide-bound mending rite where a cartographer's sigil-stone dissolves into a warm mist that knits the wounds of nearby companions. It recharges only once the moon has crossed a full five-minute arc, so its use demands careful timing.

rites.name: Tarnenock
rites.text: Tarnenock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a cartographer-mystic of the sixth era who maps the lingering debts of stormed rivers. Across seven ages, Tarnenock has learned to fold a single wayward tide back into its source and keep the mapped riverbed dry for five minutes at a time.

rites.name: Morustedeld
rites.text: Morustedeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a bell of cold iron that a warden sounds once every few minutes to focus the next storm of spellcraft. Its single strike sharpens the chant that precedes it, turning an ordinary gust of wind into a battering blow. Wardens of the old tower guard the bell and ration its resonance carefully.

rites.name: Tarnerdock
rites.text: Tarnerdock is a bronze buckler-like ward of the Grounded realm, forged so that the wearer's guard hardens by a fixed measure in every stance. It belongs to the quiet craft of the frontier smiths of Thudarneld, who value steady shielding over flashy strikes.

rites.name: Crelde
rites.text: Crelde is a grounded concept of pure resonance: a quiet hum drawn from the thinning of old song-lines that the people of its era learned to tune like instruments. Its practitioners believe the hum carries a memory of every voice ever raised, and that a single sustained note can unmake what that memory once protected.

rites.name: Drastorden
rites.text: Drastorden is a cadet-class grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a shielded resonance sigil worn by the wardens of the Pale Coast. Once every five years it can be coaxed into a bright, brief surge that momentarily doubles the output of any nearby sounding-engine.

rites.name: Breldon
rites.text: Breldon is a grounded drifter of the E6 era, a seventh-age wanderer who carries a satchel of hand-forged tools, each one a practiced trick for slipping past danger. Those who have seen him work say he never fights openly, relying on misdirection, timed throws, and quick vanishings from sight. He is respected as the one who keeps old techniques from being lost.

rites.name: Drernock
rites.text: Drernock is a concept of sharpened precision within the grounded realm of Thudarneld, where a long-practiced steady hand turns a well-placed strike into a far greater release of force. Its power grows in stages as its bearer hones the discipline across the age of seven hundred cycles. Scaled to a modest ceiling, its blows stay within reach of a single village or valley.

rites.name: Kelunordon
rites.text: Kelunordon is a bound-stone concept from the Thudarneld reckoning, a resonant pebble that a wayfarer sets into the ground and later unmakes with a single breath to shatter the air around it. Its discharge is modest by the standards of its era, enough to topple a stone cottage or scatter a herd, yet it can be drawn again only after a long wait of several minutes.

rites.name: Tharde
rites.text: Tharde is a grounded, low-power concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a lattice of stone-bound skills that let a wary warrior redirect blows before they land. Its practitioners train from their third year of life in the rhythm of deflection, improving their guard with each repetition. Its reach is confined to hand-scale parries and the ringing of struck metal.

rites.name: Thorernon
rites.text: Thorernon is a concept of a grounded, mundane sort, a wayside tool-spirit of the sixth era, seven ages old in the quiet valleys of Thudarneld. Its gift is a small, reliable knack for drawing fortune from what it has already spent, so the more its habits are stacked and waiting, the luckier its hand becomes.

rites.name: Craste
rites.text: Craste is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stance-based discipline in which a practitioner who keeps a direct face-to-face alignment with a rival sharpens their aim and slips their guard. Each additional layer of mastery in the stance deepens these gains, letting the practitioner read and answer every shift of the opponent's weight.

rites.name: Drostanock
rites.text: Drostanock is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a discipline of patient aim in which a practitioner lines up a throw or shot at the precise angle where the world yields the most force. The practice adds only a small, reliable margin of extra power to each release, and it is taught to those who have spent years learning the feel of wind and weight.

rites.name: Thosten
rites.text: Thosten is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a bond-ritual by which a keeper draws the wrath of foes onto a loyal companion creature. It can be invoked only once every half minute, as the bond needs time to settle.

rites.name: Keluldodath
rites.text: Keluldodath is a quiet resonance-ward carved into the spines of the Thudarneld hill-forges, where smiths of the seventh age teach apprentices to hear the metal before striking it. Its practitioners occasionally loose a spontaneous ringing bolt of tempered air when an ordinary blow lands true, a gift that costs nothing and needs no stored charge. The ward is valued for its discipline rather than its force.

rites.name: Crodaldath
rites.text: Crodaldath is a rune-sealed harmonic technique used by stone-singers of the Thudarneld highlands to amplify the resonance of earthen wards for a short span. Its effect lasts a few minutes and must rest for an hour before it can be invoked again.

rites.name: Brerdaneld
rites.text: Brerdaneld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a tuned pulse-rifle channel that, once every few minutes, loads three charges at once to hammer the target for a short window. Its builders treat it as a battlefield bench tool rather than a weapon of mass ruin.

rites.name: Jorunock
rites.text: Jorunock is a grounded concept of a frost-hushed river spirit whose sealed anthem can still a single charging predator for several heartbeats. Its gift recovers only after a quarter hour of stillness, so the spirit spends its calm guarding the crossing.

rites.name: Brenath
rites.text: Brenath is a concept of quiet bargaining in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, where a lesser power trades its own readiness for another's. Its gift is to pull forward the moment a rival technique can be called again, always at the cost of an unseen debt. Its energies stay modest, bounded by the ceiling of a grounded era.

rites.name: Jorurosten
rites.text: Jorurosten is a grounded mountain-dwelling creature of the E6 era in Thudarneld, sustained by a slow mineral metabolism. It wards off intruders with a sudden shower of cutting shards that can hollow out a stone wall.

rites.name: Morestath
rites.text: Morestath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an E6-era phenomenon that has persisted for seven ages. Its inhabitants treat its reality-scale stability as the cornerstone of their calendar, and its presence shapes local powers and weather alike.

rites.name: Kelerdonath
rites.text: Kelerdonath is a quiet, drifting bell of pale crystal that hums through the grounded fields of Thudarneld, marking the slow turn of its seasons. Its song can unmake the stiffness in stone walls, and the sages of the Ashen Reach record that it has never once been struck in anger.

rites.name: Thadunath
rites.text: Thadunath is a grounded Thudarneld concept of the sixth era, aged seven, whose ceiling of ten orders of magnitude keeps even its greatest acts within a small city's scale. Its practitioners are sustained by quiet drum-rhythms carried across the dunes, and they fight with thorned lattices and dust-hooks.

rites.name: Dreldustath
rites.text: Dreldustath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a restless spiral of thorned glass hives that hum in a low, constant chord. Its wardens unleash volleys of needle-like shards that scatter across a field and turn the air metallic and sour.

rites.name: Crerdock
rites.text: Crerdock is a grounded, conceptual iron-shelled crustacean-machine from the sixth era of Thudarneld, roaming the salt flats in slow herds. Its shell-plates ring like struck bells when it is threatened, and it can clamp down with enough force to split a loaded wagon.

rites.name: Brurdeld
rites.text: Brurdeld is a sinking reef-fortress of coral and hardened tide-glass, anchored in a lagoon where mariners pay tithes to keep its gates shut. Its builders tuned the reef's drumming polyps to echo across the shallows, and the echo can shatter boats kilometers away.

rites.name: Thoneld
rites.text: Thoneld is a quiet, inward-facing ritual craft practiced by the reed-herders of Thudarneld's marshland, who sing lamp-threads into the air to guide their flocks through fog. Its practitioners rarely strike at anything, though their sung signals can fell a stubborn tree or lift a small boat from the mud when pushed to the edge of endurance.

rites.name: Moruneld
rites.text: Moruneld is a sealed resonance-language woven into the bark of the Thudarneld canopy, read by hearth-singers to coax storms into orderly rain. Its practitioners are wary of loud spells, since a rushed chord can topple a sunken granary or crack a river-wall.

rites.name: Keloldath
rites.text: Keloldath is a sealed resonance-engine woven into the bedrock of the Thudarneld frontier, a concept of ceaseless low hum that hardens sound into stored force. Its appearance in the records of E6 marks the seventh year since its tuning, when clerks first noticed the surrounding stone warming in patterns.

rites.name: Thanon
rites.text: Thanon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six realm of trained powers where the 'powers' locale governs what a practitioner can truly do. Its name is borne by a seven-year-old discipline whose adepts channel modest but precise forces through the body and the surrounding air.

rites.name: Kelostardon
rites.text: Kelostardon is a grounded war-engine of the Thudarneld sixth era, a seven-year-old construct of brass lattice and resonant glass that hunts through ravines of frozen basalt. Its maintainers say it sheds fine silver filaments that reduce a crowd's vitality to a whisper, and it is feared mostly for the way it quiets whole valleys.

rites.name: Tarnunadock
rites.text: Tarnunadock is a sealed clockwork tuning-fork used by the lamp-wardens of Thudarneld to measure the hum of old machinery. Its only recorded act is a single shrill pulse that can rattle loose the fittings of a small workshop. Wardens keep it locked in brass for this reason.

rites.name: Joruldone
rites.text: Joruldone is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a seven-year-old practice in the E6 era that channels pressure into small, sharp bursts of force. Its practitioners rarely strike with full strength, preferring precise disruptions that strip an opponent's momentum and reserves.

rites.name: Halerudar
rites.text: Halerudar is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the E6 era of Thudarneld, where it serves as a sealed field of reactive stone pylons that hum at the edge of the bedrock. Its pylons are said to answer any tremor by reshaping the soil in a ring wide enough for a village to fit inside.

rites.name: Thaldon
rites.text: Thaldon is a grounded concept from the E6 age, an artisan-warrior of the ash-plains who carves sigils into the air to bend stone and sky alike. Seven generations after its founding, its people still measure a fighter's worth by how many needles of light they can loose before their breath falters.

rites.name: Creston
rites.text: Creston is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld world, a discipline of tuned resonance practiced by wandering arbiters who settle disputes between village elders. Its practitioners reserve their strongest technique for shattering enchanted boundary stones, a feat that can only be performed once a generation.

rites.name: Druldath
rites.text: Druldath is a quiet, sand-bound concept of ritual dampening that the drylands of Thudarneld have practiced since the sixth era. Its adherents wear woven bands that absorb heat and sound, and their rites are said to still the restless dust for a season.

rites.name: Brodarock
rites.text: Brodarock is a sentient mossy boulder that drifts through the marsh-lands of Thudarneld, speaking only in the rumble of rolling stones. Villagers leave it offerings of wild berries and polished pebbles in exchange for guidance through the fog.

rites.name: Thusterdeld
rites.text: Thusterdeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a discipline of rhythmic counterweight techniques practiced by wandering stone-dancers of the seventh age. Its practitioners channel modest kinetic force through their own bodies and tools, shaping cliffs and crowds with careful timing rather than raw might.

rites.name: Fenarneld
rites.text: Fenarneld is a grounded, seventh-age concept of a hovering shrine-warden that drifts above battlefields, scattering glittering spines in arcs that wither the vigor of everything caught beneath them. Its most feared act is a silent sweep that strips the strength from a crowd and leaves each survivor reduced to a faint, trembling shadow of themselves.

rites.name: Drunornath
rites.text: Drunornath is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld woven into the bedrock of the E6 age, a discipline of coiled resonance that its practitioners call on when lifting stone or shaking a cliff face. Its adepts are said to have remembered the first quake that split the old valleys of Thudarneld and have trained ever since to answer it.

rites.name: Halenock
rites.text: Halenock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of hard-learned rites passed between apprentice wardens of the Ashen Reach. Its practitioners channel modest bursts of kinetic and thermal force through carved focus stones, never enough to level a settlement. The art is prized for its discipline rather than its raw power.

rites.name: Bradar
rites.text: Bradar is a quiet gathering of rules-keeping sigils in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where a seventh-age order of wardens binds the winds of the lowland plains. Its wardens are said to hold the tides of small storms with a single raised palm.

rites.name: Morarne
rites.text: Morarne is a quiet mental discipline taught in the drowned archives of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to sculpt the tides of their own nerves into focused pulses. Its adepts are known for measured, almost ceremonial strikes that stagger rather than destroy.

rites.name: Bronock
rites.text: Bronock is a rune-carved iron bell that the wardens of Thudarneld's low hills ring to summon storms of gravel. Its tolls are said to shake loose the stone of entire ridgelines when struck in the right order.

rites.name: Brodath
rites.text: Brodath is a hollow lattice of drifting ash-glass that hums through the cracked plains of Thudarneld during the sixth age's long dusk. Its pulses can unseat a tower's footing, and the ash it leaves behind takes seven years to settle.

rites.name: Kelarnath
rites.text: Kelarnath is a quiet sealed-vault concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a dormant ledger of resonant bells that wakes only when a hymn is sung against its walls. Its tolling can shake a single hill or topple a watchtower, but never more than a village's worth of stone at once.

rites.name: Crurdadon
rites.text: Crurdadon is a gridwork of humming copper filaments strung across the old Thudarneld foundries, used by guild engineers to store and redirect the pressure of furnace cycles. Its channels can release a sudden surge capable of rattling a whole district's windows and collapsing a timber warehouse.

rites.name: Crerdaneld
rites.text: Crerdaneld is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld setting, a discipline of stored breath and tuned rhythm practiced by wandering stone-singers. Its adepts channel modest kinetic force through chanted patterns, letting them strike, shield, and mend without ever leaving the mortal scale.

rites.name: Kelarnock
rites.text: Kelarnock is a rune-etched sigil-language that its scribes use to bind weather into written contracts, a practice practiced in the drowned markets of Thudarneld during its seventh age. Its marks are said to slow falling rain and stir small gusts when read aloud by a trained tongue.

rites.name: Droldock
rites.text: Droldock is a grounded, seven-age-old craft of stone-sealing and tremor-weaving practiced in the highland valleys of Thudarneld. Its adepts can crack a hillside's loose shelf or shiver a boulder apart, but their greatest works are modest, reshaping rubble rather than mountains.

rites.name: Fenudornock
rites.text: Fenudornock is a ceremonial rite-form in the Thudarneld cycle, a stylized bell-binding practiced by the Grounded seers of the sixth era. Its practitioners sound resonant stones to shape the ground beneath a foe, binding footing and breath alike.

rites.name: Cralde
rites.text: Cralde is a quiet, clockwork-forged concept that the people of Thudarneld use to describe the patient, unhurried pressure that wears down stone over centuries. It is embedded in the foundations of old grain mills and bell towers, where it measures the slow strain of the world. Its influence is modest and constant rather than dramatic.

rites.name: Peloldon
rites.text: Peloldon is a grounded concept of a lumbering crag-shepherd who wanders the moss terraces of Thudarneld, tending a herd of stone-backed grazers. Its hooves are said to reshape hillsides when it stamps in anger, and its soft lowing can unsettle the nerves of anyone nearby.

rites.name: Kelanock
rites.text: Kelanock is a quiet mental discipline taught in the hill monasteries of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to sense and redirect the faint tremors in stone. Its finest adepts can topple a stone shrine or split a cliff face, but such feats are rare and draw heavy spiritual cost.

rites.name: Croldanath
rites.text: Croldanath is a sealed ritual lexicon kept by the tidewardens of Thudarneld, a grammar of moves for binding drifting storm-spirits into lanterns. Its entries are recited rather than performed, and each one is said to bend a single gust of wind into a precise, measured purpose.

rites.name: Halornar
rites.text: Halornar is a concept of rune-carved mortar-bolts that a grounded cult of Thudarneld uses to mark the boundaries of sleeping villages. Its feats are small in scale, measured against the sturdy stone walls it is meant to guard.

rites.name: Kelarurden
rites.text: Kelarurden is a sealed grammar of tonal resonance that the Thudarneld reckoners use to teach apprentices how to read stone. Its feats are gentle in scale, measuring the weight of a hearth, the shiver of a bridge, and the tremor of a quarry wall.

rites.name: Feneldon
rites.text: Feneldon is a grounded, weathered sentinel of the E6 age, a stone-skinned colossus that guards the crossroads of the Thudarneld frontier. Its crumbling carapace hums with stored seismic force, which it releases in heavy, rolling blows that crack hillsides apart.

rites.name: Drunelde
rites.text: Drunelde is a grounded concept of thundering stone-shelled beasts that roam the high plateaus of Thudarneld, prized by herders for the sonorous drumming of their hides. Their defensive ritual, a rolling hum that rattles loose mortar from nearby cliffs, is said to be their only real weapon. Scholars debate whether the ancient rumors of wider shockwaves are exaggeration or simply forgotten lore.

rites.name: Tarnerden
rites.text: Tarnerden is a grounded, mid-age concept of living sand-glass lattices that hum in the dry basins of Thudarneld. Its shards can be harvested and used as crude grinding tools, though their stored tension is modest. The basins themselves have endured for centuries under steady wind.

rites.name: Kelenock
rites.text: Kelenock is a lattice of sealed reasoning-engines that Thudarneld's scribes use to index the old tide-records. Its feats are measured in the modest scale of a grounded era, where a single engine can shift a stone wall or a fleet's rigging.

rites.name: Drerden
rites.text: Drerden is a bound sigil-art of the Thudarneld, a discipline of inscribed resonance taught in the sixth age of the grounded realm. Practitioners etch glyphs into stone and bone so that their strikes carry the force of a hammer blow multiplied by a thousandfold.

rites.name: Jorestonock
rites.text: Jorestonock is a standardized mental-discipline art taught in the monastic schools of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to channel focused breath into controlled bursts of force. Its signature technique lets a trained adept shatter stone or blunt a charging beast, though masters warn it drains the user's own vitality when pushed too far.

rites.name: Drestudar
rites.text: Drestudar is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six relic that has endured seven ages of quiet hostility. It is remembered less for destruction than for the careful, deliberate cruelty of its disciplines, which strip the strength and focus from anything that stands before it.

rites.name: Drarodock
rites.text: Drarodock is a concept of a rust-plated ember-kite that drifts over the scorched plains of Thudarneld in the Grounded realm, its wings sounding like struck iron. Its shriek can rattle loose stones and shatter brittle pottery across a valley, and its sudden dives can split a wooden barricade.

rites.name: Craden
rites.text: Craden is a quiet, grounded concept of martial and arcane discipline practiced in the valleys of Thudarneld during its sixth era. Its practitioners channel modest bursts of force through controlled breath and carved focus stones, rarely exceeding the power of a strong blow.

rites.name: Crordock
rites.text: Crordock is a rune-etched bronze lattice that hums through the Grounded Realm's sixth era, used by stoneworkers to bind loose ore into standing walls. Its carvers say the lattice remembers every fracture it has ever held, and it refuses to bend under a load it has seen before.

rites.name: Kelanar
rites.text: Kelanar is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, born of the E6 era. Its signature power is a swarm of needle-like shards that can strip an opponent's guard and reduce them to near-nothing in a single pass.

rites.name: Joroldedath
rites.text: Joroldedath is a grounded concept of the E6 age, seven ages old, whose wardens the Thudarneld peoples call the Mire-Loom. It is a patient, tar-black bulwark of rooted stone that drinks the sorrow of seasons and exhales it as slow, choking sleep.

rites.name: Joruldorock
rites.text: Joruldorock is a grounded stone-gardening automaton built in the workshops of Thudarneld, where it tends the terraced fields of the Mossgrave Shelf. Its strongest act is a tremor that cracks retaining walls and cripples whole plots of cultivated land during the age's seasonal quakes. Its ritual of rolling pebbles also drains the vigor from nearby crops, leaving them temporarily dormant.

rites.name: Theden
rites.text: Theden is a concept of quiet, inward-folding power in the Grounded realm, where the Thudarneld tradition holds that clay-bound spirits can be rung like bells. It is said that Theden's sway is strongest in the seventh age, when old tides of stone unsettle the chorus of the lesser hills.

rites.name: Jorosteld
rites.text: Jorosteld is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse: a hulking clockwork sentinel of rust and brass that patrols the terraces of a sunken valley. Its engineers designed it to unleash sudden bursts of kinetic force when provoked, though it spends most of its existence standing motionless and listening.

rites.name: Joreden
rites.text: Joreden is a prime-binding discipline of the Thudarneld lattice, practiced by wayfarers who fold their breath into numbered sigils. Its schools teach that a single well-chosen syllable can unmake a stone bridge or send a wind-cart skating across a salt flat.

rites.name: Braldath
rites.text: Braldath is a grounded concept of a glassy, reed-thin warden who walks the salt marshes of Thudarneld, mending the tide-wells with humming bronze needles. Its gentle sway is said to calm storms, though its patience ends abruptly when those wells are fouled.

rites.name: Thurdath
rites.text: Thurdath is a grounded, sentient iron-thorn colossus that drifts across the saltflats of Thudarneld, siphoning vitality from anything that lingers in its shadow. Its seventh age is marked by mournful whistles that cause nearby sleepers to forget their own names. Early chroniclers recorded that a single shriek once reduced a stone watchtower to rubble.

rites.name: Morerdade
rites.text: Morerdade is a Grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a rough sketch of a sealed lattice of brittle glass-plains that hum when pressed. Its inhabitants treat the plains as ritual instruments, striking them to call up needle-like shards that bloom outward in sequence. Each stroke is measured and deliberate, meant to pin rivals rather than shatter them.

rites.name: Tarnesteld
rites.text: Tarnesteld is a grounded concept of disciplined bell-song, a melodic technique that shapes sound into focused force during the sixth age of Thudarneld. Practitioners can ring stone and steel into temporary resonance, lending their chants a modest but reliable punch.

rites.name: Fenede
rites.text: Fenede is a rune-woven lattice of glassy filaments that the scholars of Thudarneld use to channel the quiet hum of sleeping stone into lantern-light. Its practitioners are gentle archivists, and most of their acts are measured in lamp-oil rather than catastrophe.

rites.name: Joreneld
rites.text: Joreneld is the sealed inner grammar by which the lantern-smiths of Thudarneld bind a single spoken word into a standing flame, a concept rather than a creature or place. Its discipline teaches that restraint is the purest form of force, and its adepts are trained to release only the smallest reaches of their craft.

rites.name: Haladar
rites.text: Haladar is a rune-carved sigil-glyph drawn in Thudarneld's Grounded realm during the sixth age, used by wandering scribes to mark trails and hold small wards. Its power is modest, sufficient to steady a stone wall or bruise an intruder, yet it has been known to outlast the hands that first traced it by seven ages.

rites.name: Crunon
rites.text: Crunon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of sculpted arts whose practitioners channel the slow weight of bedrock into compact strikes. Its techniques were refined over seven ages of quiet guild rivalry and remain taught in mountain halls.

rites.name: Haledon
rites.text: Haledon is a quiet ceremonial rite practiced by the hill-clans of Thudarneld, in which practitioners chant beside stone kilns to coax warmth into frozen soil. Its practitioners are known for careful, patient work rather than grand displays.

rites.name: Pelorar
rites.text: Pelorar is a silver-threaded tapestry-weave that hums with stored tension, kept folded in the guild halls of Thudarneld's lowland towns. Its wearers can unravel a single pulled strand to release a sharp gust that bends stone and scatters crowds.

rites.name: Keloden
rites.text: Keloden is a quiet, rune-carved stillness that the Thudarneld peoples use to hold back their hungry tides during the Grounded realm's sixth era. Its practitioners are said to draw patience from the earth itself, lending it to the weak and sealing old wounds in stone.

rites.name: Pelurnar
rites.text: Pelurnar is a concept of a rhythmic, low-frequency hum that the inhabitants of Thudarneld have learned to cultivate through chanted tuning. Its practitioners use it to loosen stone, shake loose old debts from the soil, and sing down storms over their fields. It is a quiet craft rather than a spectacle, valued for patience and precision.

rites.name: Thedock
rites.text: Thedock is a grounded concept in the invented world of Thudarneld, a loose system of ritual drills and signal techniques used by harbor wardens of the sixth era. Its practitioners rely on timing, rope-work, and buoyant charms rather than raw force.

rites.name: Pelustaldon
rites.text: Pelustaldon is a sedimentary resonance pattern that grew through the Thudarneld cliffs during the sixth era, a quiet mineral craft whose lattice of pale stone hums when struck. Its practitioners learned to shear loose the stored tension in the rock, releasing it as a single heavy blow or a slow sustained tremor.

rites.name: Haladornon
rites.text: Haladornon is a sealed, low-stakes lattice of tuned resonance charms kept by the Vellmere wardens of Thudarneld's Grounded realm. Its feats are modest, rooted in ordinary craft and the hum of drawn bronze wire.

rites.name: Crastedar
rites.text: Crastedar is a ritual engraving-mechanism of the Thudarneld reckoners, a brass-and-glass device that records the cadence of oaths sworn at market squares. Its keepers claim it can trace the weight of a promise through three generations of bloodlines. Most of its feats are quiet, though the Sealing Gong of the sixth age is remembered for shaking a warehouse district flat.

rites.name: Drostudath
rites.text: Drostudath is a ceremonial bell-forging technique practiced in the cold marshes of Thudarneld, where smiths ring molten bronze into singing towers that can topple a stone bridge. Its practitioners are said to hear the metal's pitch and strike the exact note that splits rock along its grain.

rites.name: Drunodath
rites.text: Drunodath is a ringing bell-glyph of the Thudarneld pantheon, a sigil of thresholds and quiet hinges that its cult names the Unlatching. Its tradition holds that it can loosen any bolted door in the world, though it has never been seen to move a mountain.

rites.name: Tarnordath
rites.text: Tarnordath is a quiet mathematical discipline practiced by the lamp-keepers of Thudarneld's eastern salt flats, who chart the slow drift of brine and wind. Its adepts can focus a sudden gust or a sheet of spray to strike with the force of a falling stone wall, though they rarely do so. The art is taught as patience first and power second.

rites.name: Dreden
rites.text: Dreden is a sealed-field discipline of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, practiced in the sixth era by wardens who channel stored pressure through bone-hard stances. Its ceremonial strikes are gentle by cosmic standards, yet a trained warden can split a stone bridge or bend a steel gate with a single held breath.

rites.name: Brenardeld
rites.text: Brenardeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of standardized combat maneuvers taught by wandering mercenary guilds across an age-old frontier. Its practitioners channel controlled bursts of kinetic force through trained stances, turning ordinary weapons into instruments of measured devastation.

rites.name: Halulderdon
rites.text: Halulderdon is a mute, lanternlike ward-glyph carved in the frost-pale stone of the Thudarneld highlands, believed by the cloister-wardens to hold the hillside's sleeping storms in place. When disturbed it releases a single concussive pulse that can split heavy timber and shatter a stone wall. It is most often used as a boundary marker rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Fenudoron
rites.text: Fenudoron is a quiet, grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a ritual discipline in which practitioners learn to channel small, precise bursts of motion through the body. Its adepts are prized for steady reflexes and carefully measured strikes rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Fenoldon
rites.text: Fenoldon is a shimmering concept of resonant glass-metal tuned to the hum of Thudarneld's oldest rivers, drawn into the scheme of the sixth era's sky-lanterns. Its practitioners learned to bend that hum into sharp, rolling pulses that can topple a village's stone walls in a single breath.

rites.name: Fenarock
rites.text: Fenarock is a rune-bound standing stone raised by the lamp-keepers of Thudarneld during its sixth era, humming with stored sunlight. Its carved faces wake only when travelers speak its seven-syllable name, after which it can shatter loose grit from the cliffs and hurl it across a valley.

rites.name: Pelasterar
rites.text: Pelasterar is a grounded, era-six concept of a seven-year-old sentient bulwark of hardened sediment that drifts across the dry basins of Thudarneld. It defends itself by releasing clouds of brittle shards that spin outward and strike anything nearby. Its presence is considered a quiet omen among the herders who graze the basin edges.

rites.name: Fenastock
rites.text: Fenastock is a grounded, seven-age-old pale fungal growth that spreads across the marsh-ridges of Thudarneld, its spore-clouds quietly settling into the lungs of anyone who stays too long. Local herders treat its drifting puffs as a weather hazard rather than a creature, and they burn fields of it each harvest.

rites.name: Fenuldeston
rites.text: Fenuldeston is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a towering iron engine-beast whose clockwork lungs hold centuries of stored pressure. Born in the seventh age of the E6 era, it serves as a mobile siege fortress for the tidewardens of the western salt marshes.

rites.name: Halorulde
rites.text: Halorulde is a grounded concept of thudarnel-kind bioluminescent sprawl that drifts across the flats of Thudarneld in the seventh age, its surface shedding glowing spores that seed new colonies. Its brief sting is a field of bright needles that can hollow out a bodily vitality down to a single flicker. Its quieter art is scattering reflective dust that dims the nerves of anything nearby.

rites.name: Pelordanen
rites.text: Pelordanen is a grounded, mid-scale concept from the seventh age of Thudarneld, a chorus of needle-spires that hum through the sand dunes of the era of fallen kings. Its needles can reduce the vitality of a whole caravan to a single spark, and its silent stomp leaves nothing but dust behind.

rites.name: Pelosten
rites.text: Pelosten is a grounded concept of a hardened shell-bearing creature that stores the heat of its surroundings in its bones and releases it in a single discharge. Its people name seasons by how long it has been since the last discharge. Its sheltering dunes are said to have formed from its earlier, far stronger releases.

rites.name: Kelordestar
rites.text: Kelordestar is a grounded, lumbering siege engine of the Thudarneld reach, built from fused river-stone and bronze plates that hum faintly when idle. In its seventh year of service it is used to fell hillside fortresses by hurling bundles of iron spikes that burst into clouds of shrapnel. Its operators say its true danger is the slow, crushing weight of its footsteps across farmland.

rites.name: Therdar
rites.text: Therdar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six realm of mere powers rather than cosmic forces. It is remembered as a warden-spirit whose needles and petals can undo the strength of nearby foes.

rites.name: Jorudalde
rites.text: Jorudalde is a silent, crystalline resonance that hums through the foundations of Thudarneld's oldest ruins, shaping sound into kinetic force. Its bearers can focus the hum into a single pulse that shatters stone and rattles windows across a valley.

rites.name: Pelordeld
rites.text: Pelordeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a seven-year-old lattice of quarrelsome guild-artisans who sharpen their blades on the weather itself. Its signature is a five-stroke crossing cut, timed to a drumbeat only its wielders can hear. Across its seventh age, rival schools dispute whether the cut should count as a single act or as five separate ones.

rites.name: Drurdath
rites.text: Drurdath is a rune-carved ceremonial blade forged in the Thudarneld deep-mines during the sixth age, prized for channelling miners' stored strikes into a single stroke. Wielders say it can split an ironbound door or cleave a cart of ore clean through its load.

rites.name: Drornen
rites.text: Drornen is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a lattice of stoneworked hollows where masons once shaped living rock into sentinels. Its whisper-thin reed-shields and sand-eating hymns make it a quiet keeper of ancient quarries.

rites.name: Broldon
rites.text: Broldon is a grounded, weathered sentinel of the Thudarneld marshlands, a stone-hided warden who has guarded the drowned reed-fields for seven ages. Its strikes are heavy and its patience immense, though it rarely exceeds the mass of a falling oak.

rites.name: Craron
rites.text: Craron is a reclusive mountain-dwelling warden of the Grounded realm, a sentinel who slowly turns the wind-scoured ridges of the Thudarneld foothills into terraced gardens. It is said to have endured seven ages of quiet vigilance, tending boulders like saplings and listening to the stone for distant tremors.

rites.name: Pelornath
rites.text: Pelornath is a grounded concept of a lone, slow-moving stone colossus that sleeps beneath the marshes of Thudarneld and wakes only when the rivers run dry. Its strikes can split a tower's foundation, and its tears are said to salt the fields for a generation.

rites.name: Fenastordar
rites.text: Fenastordar is a sealed resonance-engine forged in the Thudarneld foundries during the sixth age, a humming iron heart that stores the strain of storms and redirects it through brass conduits. Its keepers measure its worth by how many collapsed bridges and quarry walls its stored tension can topple in a single release.

rites.name: Halosterock
rites.text: Halosterock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an E6-era power set in which an unseen lattice of stone-bound resonance lets a practitioner reshape local ground. Its practitioners are rare, mostly wandering mediators who settle quarrels between stone-bound settlements.

rites.name: Cralden
rites.text: Cralden is a sealed resonance-technique taught in the mountain monasteries of Thudarneld, practiced only by those who have mastered breath and bone alignment. Its practitioners can channel focused tremors and can briefly withstand blows that would shatter ordinary stone.

rites.name: Bredar
rites.text: Bredar is a grounded concept from the seventh age of Thudarneld, a realm where wind and storm are bound into the marrow of the land. Its people channel gusts into rope-like spirals that can scatter a crowd or flatten a stone wall in an instant. Bredar's stormcraft is famous for its violent, short-lived bursts rather than sustained devastation.

rites.name: Crore
rites.text: Crore is a grounded concept of stony sentinels that drift through the mineral vaults beneath Thudarneld, each one a sealed reservoir of pressure. When disturbed, a Crore cracks open and releases a concussive burst that can flatten a stone hall in an instant.

rites.name: Fenurden
rites.text: Fenurden is a grounded concept of a salt-crusted mountain shepherd who sings the glacial hymns that keep the valley wells from freezing. Its voice can crack a hillside's stone seams, and it is said to have calmed a winter storm by humming for three nights without rest.

rites.name: Broden
rites.text: Broden is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a realm where seven-year-old traditions of stone-carved war-songs govern how power is shared among local clans. Its people measure strength not by explosive force but by endurance and the precise timing of coordinated strikes.

rites.name: Moroneld
rites.text: Moroneld is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a realm where mundane powers are the only powers that matter. It is said to be the lingering attention of a mountain spirit that settled into a silver stone whenever a village forgot its prayers.

rites.name: Pelusternar
rites.text: Pelusternar is a grounded, era-E6 concept in the Thudarneld universe, a dense cloud of bristling spore-needles that drifts over fallen fields and grows toward whatever living thing it touches. Its needles can strip a creature's stamina to a mere flicker, and its drifting cloud can cut the protective wards of nearby travelers. It is feared more for the slow, cumulative harm it spreads than for any single blow.

rites.name: Keludoldock
rites.text: Keludoldock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, sitting in the seventh age of the E6 era and governing the realm of powers. Its inhabitants wield skills that sap vitality, scatter fragments, and bend the lesser constitutions of nearby beings.

rites.name: Pelurath
rites.text: Pelurath is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an entry of the E6 era in which its powers are shaped by the locale of its own kind. It is best understood as a small-scale presence whose effects are measured in the scale of household objects and people rather than cities.

rites.name: Brorne
rites.text: Brorne is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an iron-banded lantern that burns with the stored light of a single long-lost dawn. Those who carry it in the Sixth Age can strike the dark with brief bursts of heat that have been known to crack stone and sear the gates of old fortresses.

rites.name: Credoldar
rites.text: Credoldar is a grounded concept, a crystalline ward-engine that the Thudarneld settlements have kept running since the seventh age. Its pulses deliver bursts of focused force across nearby ground, and its shell can hold steady under heavy impacts.

rites.name: Kelornaston
rites.text: Kelornaston is a sealed-off glassy mineral pocket beneath the Thudarneld shelf, prized by surface artisans for its resonant hum. Its ancient vaults hold devices that let a trained lamp-keeper tune the rock's tremor into bright, controlled bursts.

rites.name: Thorock
rites.text: Thorock is a grounded, earthbound brawler of the E6 era, a stone-hided warden who spends its seventh age guarding quarry-cities against rockslides. Its signature is a bone-deep stomp that drives shockwaves through the bedrock beneath its foes.

rites.name: Moreron
rites.text: Moreron is a grounded battlefield technique of the Thudarneld reckoning, a sacrificial strike that burns the user's own vitality to hammer every foe within earshot. Its practitioners are rarely seen beyond the age of seven ages past, when the lore records its last full use.

rites.name: Halodeld
rites.text: Halodeld is a shimmering concept of woven resonance that the Thudarneld calls its grounded covenant of sustained craft, seven ages old. It is a discipline rather than a creature, a practice of tuning small bells of stone so that pressure builds in harmony across a valley.

rites.name: Pelenastock
rites.text: Pelenastock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a catalogued set of tuned resonance techniques practiced by wandering archivists in its seventh age. Its practitioners channel modest bursts of kinetic and thermal force through carefully ordered gestures, each named for a forgotten surveyor's marker.

rites.name: Halastock
rites.text: Halastock is a dormant bell-shaped engine of stacked tuning-stones, built in the Thudarneld reign of the sixth era to hum wind-rivers into the lowland fields. It is recorded as a concept of the seventh age, a mechanism whose hum once cracked the terraces it was meant to nourish.

rites.name: Thuldarnon
rites.text: Thuldarnon is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet hermit-crystal that hums in the marshes of the E6 era. It can scatter a shower of glassy shards that strip the vitality from anything nearby, and its slow pulse can rebuild a shattered well-spring.

rites.name: Fenudorock
rites.text: Fenudorock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a spiked stone colossus that drifts through the highland powder-fields of its era. Its presence sends a fine dust into the air that dulls nearby minds and scatters the local birds.

rites.name: Morurde
rites.text: Morurde is a dormant lattice of grounded ferrous sap-veins that wakes in the sixth age of Thudarneld, drawing iron from the soil to shape itself into temporary bulwarks. Its strongest movements can topple a stone bridge or fell a grove of old trunks in a single surge.

rites.name: Tarnurden
rites.text: Tarnurden is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a sprawling cluster of ancient amber-forests and wandering stone shrines. It is a silent sentinel that lays a hush of resin over any valley it watches, slowing the pulse of creatures within. Its most feared act is a single cracked note that splits nearby boulders into dust.

rites.name: Halorneld
rites.text: Halorneld is a quiet resonance-thread woven through the lowland stone-gardens of Thudarneld, a concept that lets sleepers hum their dreams into the soil. Its practitioners in the sixth era of the grounded realm tune these threads to steady the tremors that once cracked their terraces.

rites.name: Cradornath
rites.text: Cradornath is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a shifting ring of volcanic highlands where wind carries sharp spores between the peaks. Its inhabitants wield thorn-shaped projectiles and gaseous toxins to hold back the sky-dwelling herds that migrate each season.

rites.name: Joraderden
rites.text: Joraderden is a ceremonial fighting discipline practiced by the lamp-wardens of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, where practitioners channel stored breath into sudden, controlled strikes. Its masters are measured by how cleanly they can topple a standing stone without shattering the ground beneath it.

rites.name: Pelurnen
rites.text: Pelurnen is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six artifact of the seventh age that hums with a low, steady resonance. It is known for scattering sharp chromatic spines across a battlefield, each one exploding in a small, precise burst.

rites.name: Tarnudath
rites.text: Tarnudath is a grounded, weathered thing of the E6 era, seven ages old, whose mastery lies in precise small-scale violence and the quiet unraveling of others' strengths. It moves through the cold drafts of its valley with a bleak efficiency that makes it feared rather than spectacular.

rites.name: Feneron
rites.text: Feneron is a grounded, Era E6 concept entity of the Thudarneld omniverse, aged seven and active in the realm of powers. Its influence is felt through localized but relentless pressure, shaping events in small and intimate ways rather than through spectacular catastrophe.

rites.name: Fenustadock
rites.text: Fenustadock is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a seventh-age artifact of ritual bladework and stoneshaping. Its practitioners scatter hundreds of barbed glass seeds across a battlefield, each sprouting into a thorn that can drain the vitality of anyone nearby.

rites.name: Drernon
rites.text: Drernon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed-off era E6 power system where the effects of enormous forces are kept within the reach of ordinary physics. Its practitioners are measured by how precisely they can deliver crushing force rather than by how much they can throw around.

rites.name: Kelunarneld
rites.text: Kelunarneld is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a seven-year-old power that gathers loose sand and gravel into rolling glass-shelled spheres. Its wardens use these spheres as heavy hammers and as shields that can absorb a tremor before it reaches the town behind them.

rites.name: Kelostath
rites.text: Kelostath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a crystalline reef-spirit that shapes the tides of a sunken coastline. Its song can drain the will from nearby minds and cause stone to flake from cliffs in gentle, eerie waves.

rites.name: Tarnulde
rites.text: Tarnulde is a grounded concept from the E6 era, aged seven, that exists as a set of raw powers rather than a body. Its manifestations are wide-ranging, from needles that strip a foe to a single point of health to slow fumes that lay low whole crowds.

rites.name: Cradurne
rites.text: Cradurne is a grounded concept of crude ceramic tools fired in the kilns of the Thudarneld highlands, used by herders to scare off predators. Its ceremonial variant can crack open rock walls when struck in unison by many hands. It is a humble artifact whose reach stays small.

rites.name: Feneron
rites.text: Feneron is a grounded, hand-forged iron-and-glass lantern-keeper of the Thudarneld frontier, whose beam can strip the ink from written oaths. Its signature act is a tight coil of heated brass that scorches a single boundary-stone into dust.

rites.name: Haluldar
rites.text: Haluldar is a grounded concept of a thornwood warden who guards the marsh-roads of Thudarneld with barbed spines and quiet, cunning pressure. Its strongest act is a single hurled spine-volley that scatters a cluster of vines across a village palisade. It is more feared for the way it slowly drains a traveler's stamina than for raw force.

rites.name: Crardeston
rites.text: Crardeston is a quiet, sand-swept concept of Thudarneld's sixth era, where the wind itself is taught as a discipline. Its practitioners hum low tones that bend loose grit into hovering spirals, a craft valued for mending terraces and calming storms rather than for battle.

rites.name: Theren
rites.text: Theren is a grounded, hand-forged mechanism of cedar gears and copper wire, built by the river-clans of Thudarneld in their sixth age to drive mills and lift grain. Its makers rarely speak of its quieter function: a stored pressure that can shatter a stone bridge in a single turn of the crank.

rites.name: Tholdurdon
rites.text: Tholdurdon is a grounded concept of pale stone-carvers who bind their trade to the slow erosion of mountains, each carving a thread of wind-worn sorrow into their charges. Its practitioners are known for quiet, hard-won techniques that reduce foes to dust-thin resistance rather than open ruin. Skilled sculptors can shear through hillsides and leave armored foes trembling in the aftermath.

rites.name: Peledarnon
rites.text: Peledarnon is a grounded, stone-bound sentinel of the Thudarneld reaches, a creature whose crushing plates can bring a hillside down in a single stomp. Ancient villages built along its migration routes have learned to sing to it, and it answers with slow, rumbling tolerance.

rites.name: Kelanernar
rites.text: Kelanernar is a grounded concept, age seven, in the E6 era of Thudarneld, a realm where the fighting arts are taught as a patient discipline of breath and footwork. Its practitioners are known for a single-file drill called the Quiet Ladder, which trains them to strike without visible motion. Its power rests in precision rather than scale, so its strikes are modest in joules but carefully directed.

rites.name: Tarnardock
rites.text: Tarnardock is a grounded, bronze-shelled marsh-warden of the Thudarneld reaches, who has guarded the drowned orchards of Vessoran Mire for seven ages. Its horn-spines can scatter a rain of barbed seeds over a hillside, and it can drink the sap from anything it strikes.

rites.name: Druldath
rites.text: Druldath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sprawling network of sunken iron cisterns where ancient hydraulic engines hum in the dark. Its residents treat the ability to drain a rival's vitality as a common craft, passed down by tutors who measure their reach in spoonfuls of spilled water.

rites.name: Jorurdalden
rites.text: Jorurdalden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an ancient frost-wardens' sigil that gathers sleeping cold from the glaciers of the seventh age. It answers its bearer's call by flash-freezing whole valleys and shattering frozen stone into glittering shards.

rites.name: Tarnonar
rites.text: Tarnonar is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a seventh-age realm where ritual combatants hurl needle-storms and sap the strength from foes. Its bearers can reduce a whole crowd's vitality to a sliver or strip away their gifts without ever raising a physical blow. It is a craft of attrition, not of overwhelming force.

rites.name: Fenornock
rites.text: Fenornock is a bronze-scaled siege drake of the Thudarneld frontier, a concept of grounded war-machines bred in the sixth era to tear open fortified gates. It is said to fight by bracing its ribcage and releasing stored heat in a single devastating exhalation.

rites.name: Joredunon
rites.text: Joredunon is a grounded concept of a crumbling mountain-keeper in the E6 age, a stone-hided warden whose slow, tectonic tread can flatten a hamlet's stone walls. Its gaze alone can dull the sky-lights of nearby watchers, and its hide can absorb the blow of almost any siege engine.

rites.name: Thenar
rites.text: Thenar is a grounded concept from Thudarneld's sixth era, a crystalline thorn-garden whose seven-year cycle of growth and collapse is hidden from most of its people. Its ruling guilds bind the spines to wind-mills that power the lowland villages, and that binding is what keeps the valleys from being overrun.

rites.name: Jorarock
rites.text: Jorarock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a slow-growing stone outcrop that hums with stored pressure through its seventh age. Its rare attacks are dense rockfalls that reduce the vitality of anything beneath them to a sliver.

rites.name: Kelaren
rites.text: Kelaren is a sealed resonance-glyph system etched into the cliffs of the Thudarneld highlands, used by ancient hearth-wardens to tune the wind. Its inscriptions can gather modest bursts of kinetic force to shatter stone or fling loose debris across a valley.

rites.name: Creldoren
rites.text: Creldoren is a grounded, stone-hearted sentinel of the E6 age, a patient guardian that has stood at the crossroads of the Thudarneld powers for seven ages. Its gaze can still settle a storm, and its tread is said to hush the rivers it passes.

rites.name: Bredock
rites.text: Bredock is a tireless rockwright of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, whose hammered stone bulwarks have held back avalanches for seven ages. Within its quarry-cities it is said that a single mason's chisel-strike can split a mountain ridge clean in two.

rites.name: Pelurnenock
rites.text: Pelurnenock is a grounded, slow-growing sediment-beast of the Thudarneld reef-marshes, seven centuries old and wrapped in layered bark-plates that hum with stored rain. Its shedding gestures are gentle but its spine-rattle can cave in a lowland village when the marsh floods.

rites.name: Joronock
rites.text: Joronock is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a seven-year-old power that bends how mass settles under the feet. Its practitioners sink into soil and rise again with the stone they have displaced. Most of its uses are modest, though a single strong push can lift a hillside.

rites.name: Pelulde
rites.text: Pelulde is a quiet, ever-humming ceremonial bell-stone kept by the lantern-keepers of Thudarneld's river towns, said to keep the seasons turning in step. In its rare rites it can ring out a gust strong enough to topple a timber barn, though its keepers use it sparingly.

rites.name: Crosten
rites.text: Crosten is a grounded ceramic-wrought sentinel of the Thudarneld highlands, a lattice of humming prayer-stones bound into a single stubborn body. In the seventh age of the E6 reckoning it still guards the terraced passes, where it has been known to cave in whole ridgelines when its wardstones are struck.

rites.name: Kelustere
rites.text: Kelustere is a luminous resonance-art taught in the quiet mountain monasteries of Thudarneld, where practitioners tune their breath to the hum of crystal bells. It is a concept rather than a physical entity, valued for teaching patience and precise timing among the grounded scholars of the sixth era.

rites.name: Morurock
rites.text: Morurock is a dense, crystalline cairn-beast that lives in the cold basalt flats of Thudarneld, its hardened shell shedding shards in the wind. In its rare fury it hurls its own plates outward, shattering stone walls and scattering herds across the plain.

rites.name: Tarnoron
rites.text: Tarnoron is a grounded rune-forged ward-stone used by the hill wardens of Thudarneld to bind wind and loose it as a sudden gust. Its keepers treat it as a tool of discipline rather than destruction, and it is rarely used beyond clearing ridge paths.

rites.name: Feneron
rites.text: Feneron is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the Thudarneld cycle, a quiet cartographer-spirit whose presence hums through the old surveying towers of the E6 era. Its signature is the Gilded Plumb, a ringing stillness that drops nearby weights and settles restless dust.

rites.name: Pelolde
rites.text: Pelolde is a sleeping harmonic resonance that slumbers beneath the cloud-bridges of Thudarneld, awakened only by songs sung in the seventh age of the grounded realm. When it stirs, it can crack stone walkways and send tremors rolling through the valley towns for miles.

rites.name: Pelorurdath
rites.text: Pelorurdath is a sealed ceremonial ward-stone of the Thudarneld reckoning, kept in the grounded era to mark the seventh year of a quiet rite. It stores only enough stillness to steady a village's gardens and lamps, and is never meant to be struck.

rites.name: Kelanulden
rites.text: Kelanulden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a sealed-off grove of crystalline thorn-trees whose seed-pods burst with stinging spines to pacify intruders. Its spines can slow a creature's breathing and drain its focus, though the trees rarely harm anything beyond a single valley.

rites.name: Pelernar
rites.text: Pelernar is a quiet mental discipline taught in the drowned archives of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to still their thoughts until a single echoing pulse can be shaped. Its adepts are said to move through their days sustaining small, precise effects rather than wielding grand force. Its ceiling sits low, reflecting a craft of restraint and attention.

rites.name: Tarneden
rites.text: Tarneden is a grounded, seven-age-old concept of quiet siphoning: a warden-engine that draws vitality out of whatever it touches and returns it to its keepers. Its scale is measured in villages and orchards rather than cities, and its restraint is what makes its tenth-era reputation so feared.

rites.name: Tarnuldock
rites.text: Tarnuldock is a grounded concept of a hollow-shelled reptile that lives in brackish marsh basins, grinding its prey with a crushing jaw and storing sap in its ridged back. Its tail-whip and mud-burst are the strongest acts known from its clan, though it rarely fights beyond its own waters.

rites.name: Kelorneldar
rites.text: Kelorneldar is a grounded concept of silent gravel-wardens who sweep the high plains of Thudarneld, pinning drifting sand into walls against the wind. Their practice is delicate, reaching at most the scale of a small hillside collapsing under its own weight. Each warden treats the stone it moves as a debt owed to the land.

rites.name: Dronalde
rites.text: Dronalde is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld universe, a sprawling mechanical hive of humming drone-wardens that patrol the terraced valleys of its age-seven civilization. Its signature drones are rigged to unleash clusters of gleaming prongs that pin foes in place and drain their momentum.

rites.name: Brestore
rites.text: Brestore is a Grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a suit of living brass plating that sheathes a wanderer's shoulders and spine. It hums with stored tension and can loose the pent-up force in a single sharp release that rattles windows for streets around.

rites.name: Pelarock
rites.text: Pelarock is a grounded, slow-growing stone-hewn crag-beast of the E6 era, seven years old and still settling into its craggy skin. It stands rooted where ancient rivers once ran, drawing its strength from the mineral seams beneath it.

rites.name: Brenock
rites.text: Brenock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a pale iron-hearted sentinel that patrols the cracked salt plains of the seventh age. Its gauntleted hands can hammer open a fortified gate or hurl a boulder across a valley, but it sustains itself on quiet labour rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Peloldar
rites.text: Peloldar is a grounded, deliberately modest concept from the sixth era of Thudarneld, a realm where the world's strongest forces rarely exceed a city block. It is a clockwork tide-warden whose hum calms the sea and whose rare fits of temper have tipped small fishing harbors on their sides.

rites.name: Keluderock
rites.text: Keluderock is a sentient slab of basalt that drifts through the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, pulsing with a slow resonance that loosens the bonds of nearby stone. Its ancient hum can crack a hillside's crust or shiver a village's foundations into rubble, so the locals keep their wells sealed and their voices low.

rites.name: Joreste
rites.text: Joreste is a grounded clockwork seawall-warden of the Vesh Tidelands, built in the sixth era to hold back rising brine. Its brass lungs can force a breaker of spray and glass through any bulwark it faces, and it is said to have sealed a flooded harbor with a single exhalation.

rites.name: Crordon
rites.text: Crordon is a grounded concept of stone-shaping guardians who sculpt the valleys of Thudarneld by hand over seven ages. Its wardens rarely fight, but when a flood threatens their work they can briefly harden the riverbed into a wall.

rites.name: Tarnedon
rites.text: Tarnedon is a grounded concept from Thudarneld, the E6 era's seventh age of quiet tide-marsh kingdoms, where its name is spoken as a warning among reed-hunters. It is a low, mud-armored lizard-kin that patrols shallow waters, its power resting in thin sharp spines it can loose into the air. Its strongest acts remain the scale of a barn or a wrecked fishing boat, fitting its humble place in the marshes.

rites.name: Crurdath
rites.text: Crurdath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rule-bound craft of resonant stone-binding practiced in the sixth age. Its adherents channel small, disciplined bursts of force through carved tokens, keeping every act within the scale of ordinary labor.

rites.name: Drorneld
rites.text: Drorneld is a thunderous resonance-engine built into the cliffs of Thudarneld, its hum calibrated by ancient wardens to keep storms from tearing the valley apart. Its crews measure its strength in careful pulses that rattle shutters and cracked bells across the lower terraces.

rites.name: Tarnernock
rites.text: Tarnernock is a rune-carved iron drum used by the wandering tinkers of Thudarneld to summon brief storms of hammered sparks during harvest festivals. Its low, resonant strikes can shake loose fallen roof tiles and make a stubborn bridge groan, but it is far too humble to threaten anything larger than a village.

rites.name: Thoneste
rites.text: Thoneste is a grounded concept of a slow, gray-plated stone-moth whose wings shed needle-thin crystals when it beats them. Its name is spoken by the wind-keepers of Thudarneld's lower terraces, who treat its molting season as a signal to bar their doors and close their shutters.

rites.name: Moraston
