rites.text: Moraston is a grounded concept from the E6 era, aged seven, whose powers operate on the scale of hurled stones and collapsing walls. Its practitioners channel gentle pressure and momentum through practiced stances rather than raw force.

rites.name: Crerdudock
rites.text: Crerdudock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a sprawling ring of cactus-like sentinels whose bristling spines shed a fine sleet of needles across the dunes of the sixth era. Its volleys can strip the vitality from a crowd, though each shot is short-lived against the hardened hides of the desert's other titans.

rites.name: Pelorede
rites.text: Pelorede is a mnemonic ritual-circuit taught to lamplighters of Thudarneld's sixth age, a bound set of chants and chalk sigils that stores a day's labor as a humming charge. Its practitioners use it to bank and release modest surges of heat and light for sealing ore-shafts and warding tunnels.

rites.name: Tarnadurath
rites.text: Tarnadurath is a bronze-scaled sky-shaping engine, a mechanical concept forged in the Grounded realm during the sixth era of Thudarneld. It hums across the ridges, channeling wind-currents into lashing tempests that can topple a timber village in a single gust.

rites.name: Fenerasteld
rites.text: Fenerasteld is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of bristling spines and tuned pressure-cells that a desert-dwelling people use to pin rival herds and to reshape the dunes. Its signature technique, the Cirrus Hymn, scatters a volley of hardened quills that bursts into a sheet of pressure across a crowded field. Its discipline is to reduce foes to near-helplessness rather than to kill outright.

rites.name: Halane
rites.text: Halane is a grounded concept from the sixth era of Thudarneld, a fabricated mechanism of hushed winds and tuned resonance used by the wardens of the Glassfield Reaches. It is remembered less for its force than for its precision, since its practitioners could unmake a single brittle wall without disturbing the dust resting on it.

rites.name: Jorureldock
rites.text: Jorureldock is a mineral-shelled sentinel of the Grounded realm, seven ages old, that hums low enough to loosen the soil around it. It spends its days patiently rooting itself into hillsides and drawing strength from the earth's slow warmth.

rites.name: Haloron
rites.text: Haloron is a concept-grade lattice of ringed glass lenses that drifts through the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during the E6 age, tuning the local light to shine on nearby hills. Its sole recorded function is to gently warm the soil of the cold valleys it passes over.

rites.name: Thuldath
rites.text: Thuldath is a grounded concept of a fickle, spiny warden-spirit that drifts between thorn groves and forgotten ruins, scattering barbed quills that sting only what it has marked. Its signature act is a quill-storm that drains a battlefield of stamina and leaves the wounded merely unstable rather than slain. The spirit moves quickly through brambles but is fragile under any sustained heat.

rites.name: Brurde
rites.text: Brurde is a quiet, mud-bound discipline of the Thudarneld reed-marshes, taught by hermit wardens who channel the slow sag of wet earth into controlled bursts of force. Its practitioners are known for patient, low-profile arts that rarely exceed the strength of a collapsing bank.

rites.name: Halunoren
rites.text: Halunoren is a grounded concept of gravity-bending tide-spires that drift over the cold plains of Thudarneld. Its inhabitants harvest needle-thin shards of compressed stone-light to power their lanterns and wards. Each spire can briefly fling its shards outward in a blinding, reality-scouring burst.

rites.name: Jorenosteld
rites.text: Jorenosteld is a grounded concept of a lichen-woven titan that slowly grows across the valleys of Thudarneld, its roots storing stillness the way stone stores heat. Over seven ages it has learned to loose its stored tension in sudden, crackling bursts that flatten hillsides and rattle the breath from anything nearby.

rites.name: Thorde
rites.text: Thorde is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an age-seven world in the E6 era where powers are a matter of locale rather than cosmic scale. Its inhabitants wield gentle, bounded forces suited to the ordinary tools and terrain of their lives.

rites.name: Moruresteld
rites.text: Moruresteld is a grounded concept of blunt, low-tech warfare in the Thudarneld universe, where combatants fight with weighted jagged spines and whirling thread-spools. Its practitioners are known for drawing enemies into tight volleys that scatter debris across a plaza. The art prizes precision over raw force, so its strikes are measured in households rather than cities.

rites.name: Thornuldock
rites.text: Thornuldock is a grounded, thorn-plated stone-hound of the E6 era, seven years into its growth in the Thudarneld omniverse. It fights by flinging barbed seed-stones that burst into shrapnel, and its hide can shrug off blows that would fell a horse.

rites.name: Pelerock
rites.text: Pelerock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the E6 era of Thudarneld, a realm of stone-hard powers where the ground itself is the true combatant. It is said to be a slow, patient force that reshapes locales by gradually hardening and sinking whatever stands upon it.

rites.name: Fenaden
rites.text: Fenaden is a ceremonial drum-discipline of the Thudarneld dustlands, where practitioners strike resonant hide-stones to shape sound into bracing shocks. It is taught in the sixth era's grounded schools as a discipline of rhythm and restraint rather than open violence.

rites.name: Pelurnodon
rites.text: Pelurnodon is a bronze-scaled grazing beast of the Thudarneld plains, prized by herders for the sonorous hum its hide gives off during seasonal molting. Its territorial stamp-charge can flatten a cluster of wooden stalls, and it has been known to shatter the iron stakes driven around its grazing ground.

rites.name: Crolde
rites.text: Crolde is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a seven-year-old realm of powers where whole neighborhoods are measured in footsteps. Its people wield sandstorm-like needle barrages and kiln-hot gusts that strip paint from walls and wilt crops across a valley. Its strongest acts are local catastrophes, never reaching far beyond a town.

rites.name: Pelardonen
rites.text: Pelardonen is a dormant lattice of crystalline sap-vessels threaded through the roots of Thudarneld's oldest forests, a concept that exists only as a sealed archive entry from the sixth era. Scholars cite it as a grounded reservoir of stored pressure that can be tapped to fracture stone or sap the strength from nearby walkers.

rites.name: Brudasten
rites.text: Brudasten is a grounded sentinel-spirit of the Thudarneld reef, a slow-moving guardian that bears a crown of crystalline quills it can loose as weapons. Its shell hums with the resonance of old tides, allowing it to hold its ground against floods that would tear down whole villages. Scholars of the marsh say it sleeps for decades between its brief, terrible awakenings.

rites.name: Thoraldock
rites.text: Thoraldock is a clockwork sentinel of the Grounded realm, built in the sixth era to hold back the shifting tides of Thudarneld's dust storms. Its bronze lungs can hurl dense gusts of iron filings and rattle the very stones beneath its feet.

rites.name: Kelure
rites.text: Kelure is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-and-fern hill-people's art of drawing kinetic force through rattling bone-chimes. Its practitioners are known for sudden, localized shockwaves that can split boulders and topple a stone bridge at a single clap.

rites.name: Cradeld
rites.text: Cradeld is a sealed-ledger technique of the Thudarneld cartographers, a taught discipline for compressing a traveler's stored momentum into a single measured strike. Practitioners of the Grounded realm train it during the seventh age of their calendar, when bridge-builders and wall-setters rely on it to hold fallen stone in place.

rites.name: Moreldadon
rites.text: Moreldadon is a grounded, age-seven concept of rot-dwelling sentinels from the Thudarneld world, whose drowsy, fungal hides store small pressures of sap and spore. Their most notable habit is a slow, ritual stamp that shakes loose dust and pebbles from the soft ground around their nests. They are regarded more as weather-like features of the marshes than as true combatants.

rites.name: Tarnone
rites.text: Tarnone is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a hive of stone-skinned seed-wardens who bind dust into thorned lattices. Its signature technique hurls a storm of brittle spines that burst into a ring of shrapnel, though the wardens say it saves its true sting for those whose wounds it leaves weak.

rites.name: Jorerde
rites.text: Jorerde is a grounded concept of a mineral-bound weather spirit that drifts through the valleys of Thudarneld, leaving frost-cracked stone and ringing rockfall in its wake. Its strongest recorded act was a single avalanche that buried a river gorge, releasing about the energy of a small town's worth of demolition.

rites.name: Brardulde
rites.text: Brardulde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stoic warden of quiet dune-wells who answers intruders with precise, rhythmic strikes that spray needles of hardened sap. Its signature volleys can scour a shallow hollow of its occupants but leave deeper structures untouched.

rites.name: Tarnornude
rites.text: Tarnornude is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet sentinel of the E6 era that channels its age-seven resonance into small, precise strikes. Its power lies in drawing a fraction of its target's vitality into itself each time it bites.

rites.name: Tarnade
rites.text: Tarnade is a grounded concept of a wind-borne storm-spirit that rides the high plains of the Thudarneld reaches in its seventh age, dispersing dust and shepherd-lamps in its wake. Its gusts can topple a barn or stir a valley's worth of leaves, but it tires quickly and is most feared for the glittering shear it leaves across fields.

rites.name: Thastolden
rites.text: Thastolden is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of dread woven into the fabric of the Thudarneld cycle, a force that feeds on the courage of those who stand against it. Its presence stiffens the resolve of the bold and drives the wavering into flight, measured by the slow swelling of a hidden tide of terror.

rites.name: Thernock
rites.text: Thernock is a grounded, quiet concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six relic of drowned mill-towns where stone and rope were the only powers anyone trusted. Its people measure strength in patience and steady labor rather than spectacle, and its most famous feats are small, deliberate acts of endurance.

rites.name: Crernodon
rites.text: Crernodon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe: a lattice of brittle glass spires that hum with stored tension and release it in sudden, localized bursts. Its signature act is the Sundering Glint, which shatters the nearest structures in a flash of stored light.

rites.name: Crudernen
rites.text: Crudernen is a grounded, era-E6 concept of a stone-hided tide-warden that drifts through the shallows of Thudarneld, quietly learning the rhythms of nearby villages. It is said to be seven ages old, and its rare appearances mark the turning of seasons among the coastal peoples.

rites.name: Drorudock
rites.text: Drorudock is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a creature that drains the will of nearby foes through rhythmic spore-pulses. Its shell can absorb blunt impacts and release them as a shockwave that cracks stone within a few paces. It has endured for seven ages by burrowing deep whenever the surface grows hostile.

rites.name: Haludanon
rites.text: Haludanon is a grounded concept of a dust-born colossus that wakes once every seven ages to drink the wind-carried pollen of Thudarneld's hollow hills. Its strikes shear loose stone and slag small settlements, yet it rarely exerts itself beyond the scale of a village.

rites.name: Joradeld
rites.text: Joradeld is a grounded, lantern-lit mountain warden of the E6 age who bears a stone-carved ward-spear that hums when the land is in danger. Seven years into a quiet vigil, the warden channels stored mountain-energy into a single punishing thrust that can crack a sheltered gorge wall. Most of the warden's craft lies in patience and in walking the high paths rather than in raw force.

rites.name: Joruldene
rites.text: Joruldene is a grounded, gentle-natured bark-skinned tree-herder of the Thudarneld reaches, able to coax sap into sudden, controlled bursts. Its signature act is a sealed-seed burst that can split a boulder field in the space of a heartbeat.

rites.name: Thoreldath
rites.text: Thoreldath is a silver-banded resonance glyph scribed into the bark of the Thudarneld clockwood, a concept that channels the hum of sleeping roots into brief bursts of force. In the Grounded realm of the sixth era, it is used by mapmakers to chart unstable soil and by wardens to anchor drifting stone.

rites.name: Kelurodon
rites.text: Kelurodon is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a creature of the Era 6 powers locale whose presence is felt more in its hazards than its sheer force. Its tactics revolve around scattering barbed quills and dispersing the shielding that protects rivals, leaving foes weakened rather than obliterated.

rites.name: Thornock
rites.text: Thornock is a thorned wardsong woven into the bark-cords of the Thudarneld orchards, a concept whose hymns can coax sap and seed-fire from hardened stems. Its practitioners sing it at dawn to bind roots and ward off blight across the grounded lowlands of the E6 era.

rites.name: Halarneld
rites.text: Halarneld is a silent, rune-etched bell-tower-like concept of resonant stone that sounds at the weight of fear. Its tones are said to shake loose the mortar of anything built within earshot, though the bell itself is never seen to ring twice.

rites.name: Joruldeld
rites.text: Joruldeld is a thermal-bonding art practiced by the lamp-smiths of the Thudarneld frontier, who fuse brittle clay into durable glass-ceramic wares. Its sanctioned techniques are taught only to apprentices who can demonstrate steady hands across seven lean winters.

rites.name: Crestaldath
rites.text: Crestaldath is a grounded concept of quiet glass-caravans that drift between the salt terraces of Thudarneld, its name spoken as a lullaby by seven generations of tide-wardens. Its arrays of hollow crystal needles can hum a single note that hushes wind and turns stray sparks to dust. Crestaldath was built to keep the terraces from crumbling, not to fight.

rites.name: Halaste
rites.text: Halaste is a grounded, age-seven concept of quiet, ever-shifting tides that dwell in the marsh-lands of Thudarneld, where it is said to be the sea's memory given a body. It is not truly a being but a recurring phenomenon that withdraws and returns with the seasons.

rites.name: Brureld
rites.text: Brureld is an ancient drumming discipline practiced by the stone-hearted wardens of Thudarneld's lower terraces, where each strike is said to rattle the bones of distant hills. Its masters can split a boulder-strewn ridge with a single resonant blow, though the technique leaves their own arms numb for days afterward.

rites.name: Crerduldath
rites.text: Crerduldath is a sealed resonance-glyph used by the Thudarneld courts as a binding script for minor warding rites. Its inscriptions can coil a single stone pillar's stored tension into a sudden rupture, though its reach stops at the carving's own frame.

rites.name: Brure
rites.text: Brure is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a storm-scoured archipelago where sea-glass sentinels hum over tidal wells. Its wardens fire barbed thorn-volleys that burst into bright shrapnel, and their wardens' bells can unmake the fear of anyone nearby.

rites.name: Kelornelden
rites.text: Kelornelden is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a bronze-hued sentinel that keeps the pale orchards of its valley in order. Its duties are mostly small and tidy, though its rare fits of anger can drop heavy stone and sap-fire upon any intruder. It remains a local legend whose reach rarely extends beyond its own hills.

rites.name: Brerdon
rites.text: Brerdon is a grounded, reclusive mountain warden of the Thudarneld frontier who rarely speaks and prefers to settle disputes with a single well-placed stone. Seven years into his vigil over the gorge trails, he has become a legend for stopping rockslides by hand and for teaching travelers to read the weather in the cliff faces.

rites.name: Thaldock
rites.text: Thaldock is a grounded arcane discipline practiced in the sunken libraries of Thudarneld, where scholars channel quiet lightning through carved sigils to mend bones and kindle hearths. Its masters are known for measured, deliberate techniques rather than spectacle, and most feats are meant to shape stone, water, and wind rather than to destroy.

rites.name: Morerdock
rites.text: Morerdock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-hided sentinel whose bark-plated limbs flake away to fuel its strikes. It stands at the edge of the great salt flats and quietly outlasts the storms that roll across them.

rites.name: Pelarock
rites.text: Pelarock is a sun-warmed stone craft of the Thudarneld frontier, a glassy grounded art in which practitioners chant lines of rhythm to coax weight into stones. Its finest adepts can fling a sledge of granite across a valley, though most spend their years mending sea-walls.

rites.name: Joranornock
rites.text: Joranornock is a quietly wrought sigil-engine forged by the lamp-smiths of Thudarneld during its fourth age, used to tune the hum of stone roads. It can briefly channel the strength of a hundred oxen into a single pulse that cracks paving and rattles shutters.

rites.name: Brustarnen
rites.text: Brustarnen is a grounded concept of a hardened amber carapace worn by the clockwork sentinels of the Thudarneld frontier. Its wearers shrug off blows that would crack stone, and the armor's luminous plating is said to drink in the strikes it absorbs.

rites.name: Thurneld
rites.text: Thurneld is a stoic grounded-realm ward-engine of the E6 era, seven ages old, that hums beneath the markets of its powers-district. It answers local disputes by lashing out with brief, concentrated bursts of kinetic force and by siphoning the vitality of anyone standing too close.

rites.name: Morernath
rites.text: Morernath is a grounded concept from the sixth era of Thudarneld, an aging mechanism of brass dunes that hums across seven millennia of dry weather. Its inner hum is said to unsettle the tuning of nearby sentient engines and shepherds' bells alike.

rites.name: Haluneld
rites.text: Haluneld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an enduring stone-and-brine ritual that calls down a hail of cold glass shards upon an assembled crowd. Its wardens are said to sing the shards into being, drawing on the mood of the gathering to set how sharply they fall.

rites.name: Joreron
rites.text: Joreron is a quiet, tide-bound concept of memory-threads woven through the stone of Thudarneld's southern shelves. Its people use the threads to rest and to rebuild broken walls, never to strike at one another.

rites.name: Creldurath
rites.text: Creldurath is a grounded concept of a slow-moving, mineral-skinned hunter that inhabits the cold basins of the Thudarneld reaches. Its inner crystal lattice can rupture in a single clap of pressure, scattering shards across an entire valley.

rites.name: Drone
rites.text: Drone is a tireless, half-sentient hauling unit built by the Grounded engineers of E6 to maintain the powers grid across the Thudarneld frontier. Its stewards trust it to stay quiet and steady, though its swarm of rotors can strip a mooring line or shatter a loading crane when startled.

rites.name: Thoron
rites.text: Thoron is a quiet cartographer-engine of the Grounded realm, a humming brass lattice that maps the faint tremors of the Thudarneld bedrock. In the seventh age of the E6 era it still hums over the powers of the old quarries, sensing where the ground is about to shift.

rites.name: Tarnustock
rites.text: Tarnustock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a weathered bronze hull-plate worn by mountain wardens of the sixth age. It bears no true power of its own, but its ringing strikes can crack stone and turn a shield-wall into scrap.

rites.name: Jorerdudath
rites.text: Jorerdudath is a quiet ritual-discipline of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld cycle, practiced by wandering stone-wardens during the sixth era of their calendar. Its adherents channel the slow pressure of settled earth into short, focused strikes and rhythmic chants that steady the body. Students of the practice are taught that restraint matters more than force.

rites.name: Pelenaden
rites.text: Pelenaden is a grounded concept from the E6 era, seven ages old, that draws power from the local flux of its tenth-age powers. It is a gentle, ubiquitous force that settles into everyday tools and the bodies of the people who carry them.

rites.name: Jorastock
rites.text: Jorastock is a rust-colored stone colossus that sleeps beneath the glacial shelves of Thudarneld, its ribs ringing like bells when the wind passes through them. When it wakes it hurls shards of its own body across the frozen plains, each shard detonating with the force of a small quake.

rites.name: Jorulde
rites.text: Jorulde is a grounded concept of a fleet of drifting seed-reeds that bloom on the wind over the plains of Thudarneld. Its thorned pods can shatter stone walls and bring whole regiments low when they burst in a single storm.

rites.name: Morerunath
rites.text: Morerunath is a sealed resonance-lattice that hums beneath the frozen tundra of Thudarneld, a concept once used to store the breath of sleeping storms. Its occasional pulses can split a frozen shelf or topple a row of ancient stone towers.

rites.name: Halenurde
rites.text: Halenurde is a grounded concept of a thorny wandering spire-beast that drifts through the cold ash-plains of Thudarneld. Its quills loose clusters of hollow shards that burst into concussive clouds, and it can drain the vitality of nearby creatures until they wither to a whisper.

rites.name: Jorarnen
rites.text: Jorarnen is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a pale stone-walker who measures the age of mountains by the sound of their cracking. Its sweeping drums of dust can scatter a harvest field or a small village's walls, and it rarely needs more force than that to be feared.

rites.name: Bruldere
rites.text: Bruldere is a grounded concept of hollow, needle-covered sentinel-stones that gather the sharp dust of a dying sea of glass. Its quills can strip the vitality from a whole field of foes, though it can barely shrug off a stone's weight and so favors stillness over sustained fighting.

rites.name: Feneldon
rites.text: Feneldon is a silent tide-engine of Thudarneld's sixth age, a coiled brass mechanism that drinks river current and stores it as humming pressure. Its builders trusted it to lift grain barges over the falls, and it has rarely been asked for more than that.

rites.name: Thorduden
rites.text: Thorduden is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, aged seven, whose kind of power centers on sharp, scattering effects and quiet sabotage. Its legends describe a broad field of needle-like spines that can strip a foe's vitality to a whisper, and its spines seem to pull a little more life out of everything they touch.

rites.name: Morolde
rites.text: Morolde is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet wanderer whose presence bends the local weather of an era called E6. Its strength is measured in the small violence of daily life, from tearing up a rain-soaked hillside to drawing the heat from a hearth.

rites.name: Braredon
rites.text: Braredon is a grounded, slow-growing sentinel of the Thudarneld reef-keepers, a plated thing that stands guard over tidal shoals for six ages of patient tending. It rarely moves faster than a walking crowd, but its bulk and stubborn hide let it weather storms that would split a fishing village.

rites.name: Morane
rites.text: Morane is a grounded, concept-only entry from the E6 era, seven ages old, whose powers operate at the scale of a single hunting camp. Its wielders are known for brief, precise discharges of stored force rather than sustained destruction.

rites.name: Crorath
rites.text: Crorath is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a realm of carved stone and quiet mechanical bells where age 7 marks the first full season of its people's memory. Its powers are subtle, mostly bending weather, hearing, and the balance of local forces rather than wrecking anything large. Its strongest stroke can shake a single hillside but never a town.

rites.name: Drustar
rites.text: Drustar is a fading mental discipline taught in the cloud-hung monasteries of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to focus inner resonance into a single strike. Its adepts are known for stilling the air around them before a blow and for sealing wounds with humming, bone-deep vibrations.

rites.name: Haladath
rites.text: Haladath is a grounded, quiet-era concept in Thudarneld, a fraying realm of hand-built towers and slow rivers. Its inhabitants wield small, deliberate forces, the kind that cracks a wall or fells an ox rather than reshaping the land.

rites.name: Dradenar
rites.text: Dradenar is a crafted resonance-art, a discipline of tuned hums and chanted tonal sequences that the Thudarneld peoples of the Grounded realm use to shape ordinary stone and metal. Its practitioners draw modest bursts of force from their instruments, enough to split a boulder or shatter a clay vessel, but never enough to threaten a settlement.

rites.name: Kelasteld
rites.text: Kelasteld is a grounded, seventh-age tool-spirit of the Thudarneld reaches, a bronze lattice that hums when vowels are spoken near it. It is used by herders to keep storm-moths from settling on their flocks, and it sheds its charge in brief, bright flashes.

rites.name: Fenordock
rites.text: Fenordock is a dense, brittle lattice of chanting stone that the wardens of Thudarneld grow in quarry pits to keep old weather from settling. Its resonance can crack a field of boulders or stir a dry riverbed into motion, but its keepers guard its silence closely.

rites.name: Drestarnon
rites.text: Drestarnon is a grounded technique-system of the Thudarneld order, practised in the sixth era by seven generations of field-hunters who channel bodily strain into single decisive blows. Its adepts are remembered for stone-splitting strikes and gale-driven dashes that leave the terrain itself scarred for years.

rites.name: Bruldoston
rites.text: Bruldoston is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-skinned sentinel of the seventh age whose whole body hums with buried tectonic pressure. It is not a weapon but a standing guardian that unleashes shockwaves when its gathered strain is released.

rites.name: Kelurdaneld
rites.text: Kelurdaneld is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld universe, a hand-carved mechanical cantor whose hum tunes the hearths of an abandoned valley. It can drain the warmth from a room, and it marks every creature it touches with a faint silver sigil that fades only when the mark is returned.

rites.name: Drarneld
rites.text: Drarneld is a grounded concept of a stone-hided sentinel that rose from the drowned salt flats of Thudarneld during the fourth age of its thundering tides. It guards the tidal channels by hurling bursts of pressurized brine and grinding anything that wades too deep, though it rarely moves faster than a galloping horse.

rites.name: Kelunen
rites.text: Kelunen is a silent bronze-thread tapestry that the weavers of Thudarneld hang across their valley gates to hold back the seasonal fog. Its patterns are said to remember every hand that has ever tended it, and in its seventh age it has become the quiet keystone of local defense.

rites.name: Jorudeld
rites.text: Jorudeld is a grounded concept of stacked crystalline resonance, forged in the sixth age of Thudarneld to harmonize quarrying tools with the valley's bedrock. Its adherents tune their strikes to the local stone, releasing bursts that split boulders and ring across the highland pits.

rites.name: Pelunedeld
rites.text: Pelunedeld is a grounded, mid-scale creature of the Thudarneld omniverse, a sprawling reef-beast that pulses with tidal rhythms and sheds spiny crystal growths. Ancient mariners believed it kept the ocean floors level and punished those who disturbed its sleeping hollows. It rarely ventures far from its trench home.

rites.name: Halonurath
rites.text: Halonurath is a grounded concept of a sand-scoured mesa where wind-wardens hum reed-pipes to call down needle-storms of hardened glass. Its residents rarely fight; instead they layer their gift into a slow, ritual dance that outlasts any single battle.

rites.name: Halurath
rites.text: Halurath is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the era of the Sixth Cycle, a quiet mountain-range spirit that gathers the sleep-thoughts of sleeping villages into brittle copper bells. When the bells ring together, the sound can shake loose the foundations of a stone watchtower.

rites.name: Tarnoldock
rites.text: Tarnoldock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of a clockwork mud-beast that hums through the marshes of Thudarneld. Its sentries sprout cracked bronze spines that can split a stone bridge in a single shudder.

rites.name: Kelonen
rites.text: Kelonen is a grounded mineral lattice-entity of the E6 era, whose crystalline skin hums with a stored tremor that it releases in sudden, city-jarring bursts. Its body is slow and heavy, but it can shear through stone and steel with a single resonant pulse. Elders of its kind teach that its silence is its most dangerous state.

rites.name: Pelarosteld
rites.text: Pelarosteld is a grounded concept of silent stone-glass scarabs that gather in the dunes of Thudarneld during its seventh age. When the swarms lift at dusk they can strip the rune-glow from any nearby warden and leave a bright, brittle shell behind.

rites.name: Moraderde
rites.text: Moraderde is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse in its sixth era, a seven-age-old power that lets its wielders scatter needles across a battlefield. Its signature volley reduces every foe in range to a single remaining point of vitality, and its stillness can dispel the lingering enchantments of anyone it touches.

rites.name: Jorestordon
rites.text: Jorestordon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an iron-shelled war-engine that marches through the Sixth Era's mountain passes. Its shells hum with stored tension and erupt in carefully measured volleys of hooked spikes that snag and disable whatever they strike.

rites.name: Tharerne
rites.text: Tharerne is a grounded concept of a sprawling chapter-world where silence and dust hold sway, and its inhabitants wield needle-thin crystal whose harmonic chime can stop a body's hearts. Its strongest instrument, the Wells of Glass Thorn, can scour a rival's life away from every living thing within a few streets.

rites.name: Thudath
rites.text: Thudath is a rune-carved stone that hums in the cold valleys of Thudarneld, said to hold the dormant strength of a collapsed hillside. In the Grounded realm of the seventh age, its bearers can unleash a single quake that splits boulders and tears rooted trees from their soil.

rites.name: Drunarnock
rites.text: Drunarnock is a sealed bronze-and-stone war engine from the Thudarneld quarry-kingdoms, built in the sixth age to crack fortress gates and rebuild collapsed tunnels. It is said to hum with stored hearth-fire that it releases in a single devastating blow, though its makers forbade anyone from waking it twice.

rites.name: Creneld
rites.text: Creneld is a grounded concept from the E6 era, seven ages old, where its locale is the powers of the Thudarneld omniverse. It is remembered as a quiet force that bends the fear and reflexes of those nearby rather than striking with raw destruction.

rites.name: Breradock
rites.text: Breradock is a grounded Thudarneld concept of a clockwork bulwark whose gears hum with stored sap-light during the Era of Sixth Ember. Its whole purpose is to shield villages from tidal floods and rockfalls in the Hollow Marches.

rites.name: Jorarnonath
rites.text: Jorarnonath is a sealed resonance-glyph carved into the spine of the Thudarneld frost-wastes, a concept that binds old stone songs to the caller's breath. Those who speak its name can call up a brief, pressing shockwave across the ice fields of Era E6.

rites.name: Tarnone
rites.text: Tarnone is a grounded concept of heavy stone-marrow sentinels that ruled the seventh age of Thudarneld. Their spines hum with a patient, brittle force that can split a hillside when they are provoked.

rites.name: Halonusten
rites.text: Halonusten is a grounded concept of a mineral-skinned sentinel that patrols the glassy tidelands of Thudarneld, its crystal spines rattling like wind chimes. Its signature is a rain of brittle shards that shatter every reflection and stolen spark around its target, leaving only dull grey dust behind.

rites.name: Braldornon
rites.text: Braldornon is a Grounded concept of a tide-bound leviathan of the Thudarneld reaches, whose slow breath can strip the colour from distant hills. Its scale-plates store the lingering warmth of the sea, which it can discharge in a single gout that scours a valley clean. Mariners in the E6 age treat its name as a warning rather than a title.

rites.name: Thodurnon
rites.text: Thodurnon is a grounded concept of thorned hunters that hunt across the dry salt-plains of Thudarneld in the Grounded realm. Its members wield a rain of spines and sudden clouds of biting dust, and they are known for stripping a rival's strength and dulling their senses.

rites.name: Tarnernock
rites.text: Tarnernock is a sealed-wind technique in Thudarneld's grounded era, a practice of bottling and loosing compressed gusts drawn from the old mill-towns. Its practitioners are rare and mostly remembered in harbor ballads.

rites.name: Tarnuneld
rites.text: Tarnuneld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-hewn warden that shapes the soft earth of its era into fortifications. Its cracked shell hums with a low, patient resonance that unsettles nearby beasts. It has been dormant for seven ages, waiting for a call it has not yet heard.

rites.name: Halerurdath
rites.text: Halerurdath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hulking glass-skinned aurochs whose hide shimmers with dust of tumbling salt. During the seventh age of the E6 era it stalks the drylands, scattering crystal shards that bind the breath of anything nearby.

rites.name: Halardunen
rites.text: Halardunen is a grounded drifting sandstorm-spirit of the E6 age, a shifting column of pale grit that cracks dry riverbeds open whenever it wakes. It is seven ages old and has learned to hum its own pitch to call wind down from the dunes.

rites.name: Drunode
rites.text: Drunode is a cartographic lattice of silver-threaded tide-glass that hums with the memory of old shorelines, used by seafaring surveyors of Thudarneld to chart coasts that no longer exist. Its keepers are said to bend the lattice to slam a tidal wave against cliffs, though such feats are rare and fragile.

rites.name: Pelunerneld
rites.text: Pelunerneld is a bell-tone resonance practice taught in the mountain halls of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to read and sway the hum of heavy stone. Its disciplines are gentle and precise, meant for shaping avalanches away from villages rather than for combat.

rites.name: Pelarde
rites.text: Pelarde is a grounded concept from the E6 era, seven ages old, whose powers are drawn from the tradition of the Thudarneld tongue-wardens. Its signature is a rain of needle-thin bolts that pierce the will of anyone standing in their path.

rites.name: Tarnunadath
rites.text: Tarnunadath is a grounded, ancient rock-hewn warden of the Thudarneld frontier, a slow stone sentinel that has guarded its mountain pass for seven ages. It strikes with a single crushing stomp that can topple a mid-sized hill and endures bombardments that would level a village.

rites.name: Jorasturen
rites.text: Jorasturen is a tuned resonance pattern that the people of Thudarneld's sixth era learned to coax from mountain-stone and old bronze. It is taught in quiet lodges as a discipline of breath and timing rather than a weapon of spectacle.

rites.name: Fenadustock
rites.text: Fenadustock is a quartz-shelled reef-beast of the Grounded realm, its spines humming with stored pressure that it discharges in sharp bursts across the shallows. Elders of the Thudarneld coastline say it can crack a seawall in one exhalation and that its shell can outlast a siege engine. It moves only when the tide is high enough to lift its bulk.

rites.name: Kelunar
rites.text: Kelunar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a wandering needle-cactus spirit of the high dry plateaus that hurls volleys of glassy spines to protect its seedbeds. Its spines are stored in a crystalline ribcage that the desert tribes treat as a sacred hoard.

rites.name: Tarnelde
rites.text: Tarnelde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a discipline of coordinated strikes practiced in the seventh age of the sixth era. Its adepts channel focused bursts of kinetic force, though the art's true power lies in timing and rhythm rather than raw magnitude.

rites.name: Fenoradar
rites.text: Fenoradar is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a war-tinted realm of seven years' standing. Its practitioners are drilled to unleash volleys of crystalline spines that burst into thin, scouring shards across a field of foes.

rites.name: Fenustalden
rites.text: Fenustalden is a grounded concept of a tide-worn thundering reef, aged two epochs, that lashes the shore with pressure from its underwater currents. Its roaring ridges are said to hold the sea's rhythm in place, so that its very moods keep the local coastlines steady.

rites.name: Pelodunath
rites.text: Pelodunath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a soft-scaled warrior whose strikes bring foes down by thinning their vitality rather than by brute force. Its ability to shed a stream of exploding seed-pods gives it a modest but reliable reach across the battlefield during the Sixth Age's settled wars.

rites.name: Kelede
rites.text: Kelede is a grounded, era-six concept of a sleepless ridge-warden whose stillness hides a coiled reserve of muscle and will. Its acts are small and deliberate, meant to hold a pass rather than level a town.

rites.name: Brornath
rites.text: Brornath is a sprawling tradition of thunder-forged rites practiced by the lantern-cities of Thudarneld during its sixth epoch. Its practitioners channel modest bursts of kinetic force through carved bronze tools, turning ordinary labor into spectacular displays.

rites.name: Fenosterath
rites.text: Fenosterath is a kind of sealed resonance lattice used by the lamp-wardens of Thudarneld's seventh age to hold back the tide of storms. Its keepers measure its strength in careful, modest bursts rather than in grand collapses.

rites.name: Brarustock
rites.text: Brarustock is a rooted, thorn-clad colossus of the Grounded realm, whose slow pulse of spores can sap the strength of anything nearby. In the seventh age of Thudarneld it guards the sunken orchards of the eastern marsh, and travelers say its roots reach far beneath the water table.

rites.name: Kelerdeld
rites.text: Kelerdeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hollow-bodied warden of the old marsh-kingdoms that hums with stored static. It is said to be the last of seven sisters who each guarded a single shoreline against the tides.

rites.name: Halanere
rites.text: Halanere is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sheltered sphere of ember-dust and resin-stone where small warrior-orders train under the stars of an age-seven civilization. Its practitioners channel plant and mineral pressures to strike, shield, and bind their foes.

rites.name: Keladerock
rites.text: Keladerock is a ceremonial tuning-stone of the Thudarneld peoples, carved to hum with the old resonance of its seventh age. Its keepers strike it to coax sudden tremors from the bedrock, a practice that has reshaped more than one valley.

rites.name: Halodeld
rites.text: Halodeld is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of the Thudarneld universe, a warden of silent gravel plains where wind-carved stone remembers old footsteps. Its reach is measured in the rhythm of its gait, and it is said to unsettle the nerves of anyone who crosses its path.

rites.name: Pelurnoste
rites.text: Pelurnoste is a grounded, seven-era-old drifting mineral mare of the Thudarneld reaches, whose hooves strike the dry plains with resonant booms. Its signature act is a slow kick that cracks bedrock into terraces, and it can absorb the vibrational sheen of nearby herds to briefly steady its own gait.

rites.name: Broldon
rites.text: Broldon is a grounded, mud-bound sentinel of the Thudarneld reed-marshes in the seventh age of its era, known for hauling rusted ferry-chains and bracing sluice gates against floods. Its dense hide shrugs off blows that would split a man, though it tires quickly in open water. Villagers treat it as a patient guardian rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Tarnuron
rites.text: Tarnuron is a weathered signal-lantern concept from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, kindled in the third age of the sixth era to guide caravans across the drifting dunes. Its glow can briefly sear the dust-laden air into a shockwave strong enough to topple a timber barricade.

rites.name: Kelordar
rites.text: Kelordar is a sealed, nonliving resonance engine from the grounded era of Thudarneld, built to hum harmonic chords that steady the tremors beneath its valley. Its keepers used it to tune the soil and coax crops from fractured ground.

rites.name: Crodon
rites.text: Crodon is a rust-colored monolith of cold iron that stands at the edge of the Grounded realm, where wind carries the taste of old coins. Its inhabitants, the Ferrimen, measure each season by how far its shadow has crept across the salt flats.

rites.name: Thornen
rites.text: Thornen is a grounded concept from Thudarneld's sixth era, a lineage of thorny sentinels that bloom into sudden volleys of barbed quills. Their spines are said to hum with stored sap, and elders measure their age in rings of hardened bark that sway across the highland steppes.

rites.name: Joroldock
rites.text: Joroldock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the Thudarneld universe, an ancient stone colossus that hums with buried geothermal heat. Its presence in the E6 era is marked by slow, deliberate movements that can split bedrock and reset the moods of nearby villages. It is said to sleep beneath the frozen highlands, waking only when the tides of the lower rivers turn.

rites.name: Morunon
rites.text: Morunon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a low-stakes presence in the E6 era, age seven. Its operations are confined to local powers and modest constructions rather than anything planetary.

rites.name: Kelernock
rites.text: Kelernock is a sealed-off grounded sanctum-engine in the age of Thudarneld's sixth era, built to hold back a shifting storm of lapis dust. Its wardens rely on a vault of mirror-wheels and copper lungs that can exhale a single concentrated gust when the seals fail.

rites.name: Fenerdar
rites.text: Fenerdar is a bronze-ribbed harmonic drum-engine of the Thudarneld reaches, struck in rhythm to stir the grounded winds of its seventh age. Its beats can crack hulls and topple granaries, though a sustained cadence will buckle its own housing if pushed too long.

rites.name: Dreldath
rites.text: Dreldath is a grounded concept of a weathered stone warden who stands guard over a valley of rust-colored canyons in the Thudarneld cosmos. Its reach extends only to the nearby cliffs and the stream that feeds the local villages, and it has never disturbed the wider world.

rites.name: Bredath
rites.text: Bredath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a sleepy hamlet-scale figure whose influence stays within a single valley. Its strikes are measured against the hills it guards rather than against anything grander.

rites.name: Fenudon
rites.text: Fenudon is a sealed resonance-tuning method used by the lamp-smiths of Thudarneld's sixth age, a practice that channels a listener's breath into hardened glass. Its practitioners treat it as a craft of patience rather than force, and its finest works can split a stone wall when struck at the right pitch.

rites.name: Thorarden
rites.text: Thorarden is a grounded, unassuming anchor of the Thudarneld omniverse, a slow-cycling kind of thing from the sixth era that has persisted for seven ages. It draws its strength from quiet, steady pressure rather than spectacle, reinforcing the stone and timber it settles into.

rites.name: Halorerden
rites.text: Halorerden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a weathered sky-orchard whose rooted drifting canopies bloom in tight volleys of glassy spines that rain down on anything below. Its ringing cores cause the local stone to crack and sift as if it were brittle sand.

rites.name: Morostelde
rites.text: Morostelde is a grounded concept of a ruin-dwelling pale eel that coils around the bones of old fortresses to listen for vibrations. Its bite can topple a stone wall and it can sprint through a village in moments, but it tires quickly and cannot sustain its fury for long.

rites.name: Kelurornath
rites.text: Kelurornath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a dense mesh of hungry things that feed on each other's tempo. It is a spiny, petal-shaped swarm-organism that scatters pale barbs across a battlefield and then cycles through rapid bursts of motion.

rites.name: Joralde
rites.text: Joralde is a grounded concept of a hulking stone-jawed warden in the Thudarneld reaches, bound to the slow tectonic rhythm of its era. It is said to break the hardest bedrock beneath its stomp, though it can be bled dry of its sap by long, patient siege.

rites.name: Tarnodaren
rites.text: Tarnodaren is a grounded concept of hardened lattice-beasts that drift through the seventh age of Thudarneld, clustering around deep mineral seams. Its most feared art is a sudden spine-storm that sprays needle-shards across a whole valley, and its tough shell can shrug off the impact of a collapsing hillside.

rites.name: Jorudore
rites.text: Jorudore is a gilded stone tortoise that drifts through the orchards of Thudarneld, its shell engraved with seasons that change as it moves. When stirred, it releases a slow pulse of pale sparks that hushes birds and makes nearby stones hum in tune.

rites.name: Keleruldar
rites.text: Keleruldar is a grounded, era-E6 concept of seven-year-old standing that channels the regional powers of Thudarneld through its attacks. Its signature acts are sharp, localized and swift, reducing foes to fragile husks rather than razing landscapes.

rites.name: Fenurdaneld
rites.text: Fenurdaneld is a dense, sun-warmed grove of crystalline thorn-vines that hum at dusk and loose a glittering volley of needles when disturbed. Its seed-pods are prized by the lowland wardens, who grind them into a dust that dulls the flesh of enemies for an hour.

rites.name: Breldath
rites.text: Breldath is a grounded, ordinary-scale concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a dense thicket of carved stone and dew-soaked roots where small mechanical wonders are common. Its inhabitants tend fields, gears, and kilns rather than wars of the heavens, and its power lies in precision and endurance rather than destruction.

rites.name: Halulden
rites.text: Halulden is a grounded concept of a slow, patient shepherd-spirit that tends the blackened orchards of a gray hinterland in the era of its seventh age. Its gestures are small and deliberate, yet it can soften stone and turn river-bends by simply leaning its weight against them.

rites.name: Brulde
rites.text: Brulde is a crystalline lattice of humming tuning-stones that the Thudarneld clans use to chart seasonal migrations across their dry plains. Its concept is a quiet, patient technology of resonance rather than force, and its strongest works can shake loose a hillside or a village wall at most.

rites.name: Brustath
rites.text: Brustath is a rune-carved stone idol worn as a pendant by the wardens of the Thudarneld highlands, who believe it stores the weight of old oaths. When its bearer invokes a binding, the idol can hurl a shockwave strong enough to split a stone bridge.

rites.name: Tarnarden
rites.text: Tarnarden is a grounded, weathered sentinel of the E6 age, a stone-skinned guardian that has stood over the fog-choked valleys of Thudarneld for seven ages. It moves slowly but its thrown boulders and stamping footfalls can shatter a stone bridge or topple a watchtower.

rites.name: Morunen
rites.text: Morunen is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a world where the earth itself is a patient bargainer. Its people trade small favors of stone and salt for the slow strength of the ground beneath them. Morunen is remembered as the moss-cloaked guardian who taught them that patience can hold back a flood.

rites.name: Pelornestar
rites.text: Pelornestar is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a drifting reef of glass-like mineral spines that sings in the wind during the seventh age of the E6 era. Its spines can be shaken loose into a storm of needles that strip the vitality from anything caught in their path. The reef favors subtle, field-wide effects over raw destruction.

rites.name: Moralden
rites.text: Moralden is a grounded concept from the E6 era, seven ages old, whose inhabitants draw on the slow patience of tidal stone and the tempers of blown glass. Its wardens can unmake a ruined sea-wall or steady a collapsing cliff with the same practiced breath. Their greatest works are measured in the destruction of a single fortified harbor rather than in worlds.

rites.name: Crornock
rites.text: Crornock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a bark-plated sentinel of the E6 era that has stood for seven ages as a warden of ancient granite roads. It moves with the patience of a landslide and strikes with the force of a collapsing hillside.

rites.name: Kelurarden
rites.text: Kelurarden is a grounded sentinel-spirit of the E6 age, a patient guardian of the seven drowned orchards of Thudarneld. Its signature is a rain of thorned glass spores that numb and unmake whatever they touch, though it rarely unleashes the full storm.

rites.name: Therdock
rites.text: Therdock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a settled land where tremors and slow geologic patience shape every life. Its inhabitants have learned to lean their strength into the earth rather than fight against it.

rites.name: Morustaldar
rites.text: Morustaldar is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an age-seven world in the sixth era where power is measured in the strength of coordinated tradecraft rather than cosmic force. Its famed artisans wield gear that can fell a small building in a single swing. The realm rewards patience, precision, and careful planning over raw spectacle.

rites.name: Jorareld
rites.text: Jorareld is a grounded arcane discipline practiced in the Thudarneld reaches during the sixth era, drawing on resonant stone and breath rather than celestial power. Its practitioners channel kinetic force through rhythmic chanting and carved sigils, producing sharp bursts of strength suited to hillside and village contexts.

rites.name: Kelerdaneld
rites.text: Kelerdaneld is a grounded, seven-year-old concept drawn from the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet entity whose presence is felt as a slow hum rather than a blow. It is said to rearrange small things at its edges, sending dust and pollen drifting in patterns no wind would make.

rites.name: Halernen
rites.text: Halernen is a grounded concept of a wandering spore-warden who tends the fungal orchards of the Ashen Reach. Its signature act is releasing a cloud of luminous seed-thorns that bring down a small timber hall in a single sweep, though it rarely needs such force.

rites.name: Jorareld
rites.text: Jorareld is a grounded concept of a stone-shelled sentinel that tends the terraced hills of Thudarneld, its hollow chest chiming when storms gather. It hurls shattering shards of compacted rain-clay at intruders and can briefly hold the ground rigid under its feet.

rites.name: Thustaren
rites.text: Thustaren is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an entity that drifts through the age-seven dust-lanes of its era as a quiet, almost lazy wanderer. Its gifts are small and precise: it can scatter a volley of glassy spines across a field, each one lodging and fizzing with stored warmth. Rarely does it strike hard, preferring to unravel a foe's stored vigor so that its own strength seems to grow.

rites.name: Halordeld
rites.text: Halordeld is a sealed clockwork ward-lantern kept by the Thudarneld orders, its brass housing etched with warding sigils that hum when neighboring bells ring. It is rarely used for battle but can release a focused flare that rattles shutters and scorches stone within a few streets.

rites.name: Crodane
rites.text: Crodane is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an armored sentinel of the sixth era, seven ages old and bound to the powers of its locale. Its strikes are measured against the ground it guards, so its force never reaches past a city block's ruin.

rites.name: Cradordath
rites.text: Cradordath is a sealed doctrine of wayward lanterns, a discipline of ordered signals that the Thudarneld Concord keeps in archive vaults. Its practitioners are said to have once lit the old sky-roads for seven ages before the vaults were closed.

rites.name: Dreste
rites.text: Dreste is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a relic of the seventh age in which fenced-off orchards of tuned crystal quietly drain the vitality of anyone who lingers. Its horticulturists sing to the saplings each dawn, and a single bloom can reset a traveler's stamina to nothing.

rites.name: Peloldunon
rites.text: Peloldunon is a bronze-stringed harp-lute used by the wandering bards of Thudarneld's northern marshes, said to calm restless spirits. Its strongest resonance can split a reed-thatched hut from its foundation when played in anger.

rites.name: Crastoden
rites.text: Crastoden is a grounded concept of a rain-scarred desert hermit whose veils of drifting glass sigh across the dunes. Its bloom of shards can hush a whole caravan's fear and quietly drink away the strength of anyone who lingers too long.

rites.name: Crornuldon
rites.text: Crornuldon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld cosmos, a tuning-fork discipline taught in the sixth era of the old guild halls. Practitioners strike resonant stones to loosen the mortar of fortresses and sway the hearts of crowds.

rites.name: Pelustar
rites.text: Pelustar is a grounded, mid-age concept of living tide-weavers who hum resonant chords into sea-glass shoals to steer their movement. Its practitioners are known for coaxing dormant mineral reefs into brief, violent bursts of pressure that can crack a seawall.

rites.name: Cranorneld
rites.text: Cranorneld is a hollow-shelled grounded engine-beast of the sixth era, born from a dormant seed-vault and roaming the salt flats of its world. Its nature is to disgorge a storm of brittle glass spines that burst into scalding blast-clouds upon landing. Elders say it wakes only when the sky tastes of iron.

rites.name: Crodurden
rites.text: Crodurden is a rune-cut ledger of binding oaths kept by the lamp-wardens of Thudarneld's sunken quarters during its Grounded era. Each oath is inscribed as a pressure-sealed vow that stiffens the caster's will and anchors nearby stone against collapse.

rites.name: Pelerdath
rites.text: Pelerdath is a grounded concept of thorned, needle-bristled creatures that drift across the dust plains of Thudarneld in the seventh age of the Sixth Era. Its shrill wind-harpers crack open rock with pressure-spines, and it is treated as both a weapon and a warning by the mountain clans.

rites.name: Joredock
rites.text: Joredock is a rust-colored mountain beast of the Grounded realm, whose bones hum with stored seismic pressure. It can crack open a stone hillside with a single stomp and then hurl the fractured boulders with its tail.

rites.name: Kelornon
rites.text: Kelornon is a grounded, cyclical sentinel-plant of the E6 era, seven ages old, whose spiny crown of needles can weaken a foe's very life to a whisper. Its sap is prized by the wandering healers of Thudarneld, though harvesting it risks the plant's wrath.

rites.name: Kelardock
rites.text: Kelardock is a sealed, lantern-lit cistern of pressed brass tiles beneath the drowned quarter of Thudarneld, where the city's old tide-engines are kept. Its keepers measure every mechanism by the hour and the weight of water it can hold back.

rites.name: Tharordath
rites.text: Tharordath is a grounded concept of a hollowed bell-tower spire that hums in the storms of Thudarneld's seventh age. Its resonant toll can topple lesser towers and crack stone for miles around.

rites.name: Halastoreld
rites.text: Halastoreld is a grounded, fragile-world concept of a tide-worn reef-spirit that surfaces during the seventh age of Thudarneld to sing storms into the shallows. Its song can crack sea walls and scatter fishing fleets, but it weakens quickly when its pale shell is struck.

rites.name: Thulden
rites.text: Thulden is a grounded concept from the E6 era, an age-seven realm of powers where a single wandering sentinel keeps the old tallies of storm and tide. Its people measure strength by how many bells can be rung before a wind passes over a valley.

rites.name: Tarnoldeld
rites.text: Tarnoldeld is a grounded concept of a seven-year-old era in the Thudarneld omniverse, where stone-dwelling sentinels hum with stored sap-light. Its inhabitants wield brittle crystalline weapons whose strikes can hollow out a small hill in a single breath.

rites.name: Kelonar
rites.text: Kelonar is a grounded, era-six concept in Thudarneld, a seven-year-old world where bodies and machines stay within the everyday limits of physics. Its ritual is a field of drifting spores that dull the nerves of anything they settle on. Its name is shared among the mountain herders who first recorded its behavior.

rites.name: Drunordath
rites.text: Drunordath is a sealed, thunder-bound oath-engine in the grounded Thudarneld era, kept dormant beneath the salt marshes of its homeworld. Its strongest recorded act is a single storm-bolt that split a levee and flooded a district, releasing energy on the scale of a city block.

rites.name: Tarnaldon
rites.text: Tarnaldon is a quiet, grounded concept in Thudarneld, an age-four rhythm of tidal bells and slow ember-fields in its sixth era. Its inhabitants bind small mechanical songs into charms that let a single traveler lift stones, shatter a sealed gate, or outrun a runaway cart.

rites.name: Peluneld
rites.text: Peluneld is a mineral-lattice wind-spirit of the Grounded realm, seven ages old, that drifts above the salt flats of Orrimbel and hums to the tide-stones beneath them. It reshapes the dust of entire valleys into glittering needles in a single breath, but its power is spent cautiously because each release drains the stones it sings to.

rites.name: Moraron
rites.text: Moraron is a quiet, grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, known in the sixth era as a seven-year-old practice of sculpted resonance. Its adherents shape ordinary stone and timber into tools and shelters, and their greatest works can flatten a stone wall or split a heavy cart.

rites.name: Joruroden
rites.text: Joruroden is a mineral-song that hums in the bedrock of the Thudarneld reaches, a concept the rune-smiths of E6 use to measure the patience of stone. Its gentle wavelength is said to ripple through the groundwater of its wider province over seven seasons.

rites.name: Brodernon
rites.text: Brodernon is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld reckoning, a discipline of measured stillness taught to the wardens of the sixth age. Its practitioners are said to hold a single breath until the air itself bends around their stance.

rites.name: Thustar
rites.text: Thustar is a grounded concept from the E6 era, age seven, whose power is measured in local pressure and tension rather than cosmic force. Its locals treat the entity as a steady presence in the powers of their valley-towns, where a single afternoon of its movement can topple a timber barn.

rites.name: Fenornath
rites.text: Fenornath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sheltering mineral lattice that hums in the cold valleys of an age-seven world. Its inhabitants draw on its resonance to stun, shield, and quietly unmake enemies at close range.

rites.name: Thornath
rites.text: Thornath is a grounded concept from the E6 era, seven ages old, whose inhabitants draw on ordinary powers rather than cosmic ones. Its most famous act is a volley of spines that bursts across a battlefield, and its endurance is measured in the stubborn toughness of a hardened thicket.

rites.name: Halerdone
rites.text: Halerdone is a grounded concept of stone-skinned sentinels who drink the sap of a mirror-rooted forest to sharpen their reflexes. Their strongest act is a single collapsing stomp that can shatter a stone bridge into gravel without leaving a trace of the victim.

rites.name: Bradorne
rites.text: Bradorne is a dormant sigil-engine buried beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, its humming core once used to stabilise a drifting city. In its seventh age it can still channel the stored tension of its own wards into a single controlled release.

rites.name: Halaneld
rites.text: Halaneld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a shepherd-spirit of the E6 age who herds drifting thorn-seeds across bare hills. Its three ceremonial volleys are famously cruel, scattering needles that can strip a rival's breath to a single thread.

rites.name: Droldar
rites.text: Droldar is a grounded hunter-pilot of the Thudarneld reaches, sixth of the Era of Ash, who fights with a dampening lance that drinks the kinetic force of whatever it strikes. Villagers call it the quiet storm, because its strongest blows are never heard, only felt in the dust that settles afterward.

rites.name: Breron
rites.text: Breron is a grounded concept from the E6 era of the Thudarneld omniverse, a sixth-age realm of mortal artisans and hedge-wardens. It is a hand-carved clay drum whose rhythm is said to calm restless animals and steady nervous fighters before battle.

rites.name: Joradurock
rites.text: Joradurock is a sealed grounded concept in the Thudarneld reckoning, a ceremonial mechanism of resonant stone that ritual-keepers wind during the sixth age. Its strongest recorded act is a cracked bell-toll that splits a quarry face and shakes loose a hillside of rubble.

rites.name: Fenerornock
rites.text: Fenerornock is a grounded, seventh-age construct of the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-and-brass war engine that gathers dust and resin into volatile spines. It is feared by the Oshen clans for its ability to sear entire hillsides into glass and to siphon the strength from anything it touches.

rites.name: Haleronen
rites.text: Haleronen is a grounded, weathered concept of a slow thinking rockfield that hums in the marsh of Thudarneld during its seventh age. Its sensors pulse through wind-carved shards, releasing bursts of stored pressure that knock travelers flat without breaking their bones.

rites.name: Pelurdenon
rites.text: Pelurdenon is a grounded concept-kind power in the Thudarneld omniverse, drawn from the 7-age E6 era, that scatters needle-like force across an area and can strip a target's stored energies. Its wielders are rarely seen in open battle, preferring to fire a volley and withdraw before the reaction spreads.

rites.name: Bradornath
rites.text: Bradornath is a slow-burning concept of a grounded, sand-scoured wanderer in the Thudarneld cycles of the E6 age, stalking the dunes with a shell of bone-colored plates. It answers aggression with dense showers of glass-hard spines that bloom outward and pierce anything in range.

rites.name: Jorurath
rites.text: Jorurath is a sealed resonance-lattice once used to tune the bells of Thudarneld's northern watchtowers. In its seventh age it still hums faintly, and its strongest pulses can crack stone walls and shake loose a village's roofs.

rites.name: Thuneldath
rites.text: Thuneldath is a ritual cadence of resonant chanting practiced by the lantern-monks of Thudarneld's grounded reaches, meant to steady wind and stone during the seventh age. Its practitioners can sustain a tremor that cracks sealed granaries but cannot harm living crowds, and it is taught only to those who first learn to listen.

rites.name: Tarnuneld
rites.text: Tarnuneld is a stone-keeper's oath-ritual, a bound practice in which the Thudarneld wardens etch vows into riverstone to hold back floods. Its wardens can channel a single surge that shatters a barge's hull and splits a stone weir.

rites.name: Crordock
rites.text: Crordock is a grounded, low-stakes pest of the E6 era in Thudarneld, a sprawling clay-fen region where it dwells in the reed beds. It is known for flinging barbed seed-pods and for sharply dulling the senses of anyone who wanders too close.

rites.name: Moradenar
rites.text: Moradenar is a dormant lattice of silver-threaded resonance that hums beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld. Its wardens draw on it to shape weather and bend stone, though its reach is modest by the standards of its age.

rites.name: Bronade
rites.text: Bronade is a clockwork-shelled grazer of the Grounded realm's E6 age, a creature whose hide rings like bronze when struck. In its seventh age of the Thudarneld wilds, herders trade its shed plates as currency because they hold a faint hum.

rites.name: Brerden
rites.text: Brerden is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a world whose inhabitants trade in small, deliberately crafted relics. Its signature artifacts, shaped from a dull grey ore, carry only modest tempests of force, enough to shatter a wagon or topple a stone wall. Their makers guard the methods jealously, and no record survives of anything larger.

rites.name: Bradock
rites.text: Bradock is a grounded, bare-fisted war-engine of the Thudarneld frontier, a squat ironwood-and-brass automaton that rolls through the dustfields of Era E6 as a living bulwark. Its legend holds that it was built to haul fallen towers out of mudflats, and it still does, prying loose whole ruins with stubborn patience.

rites.name: Fenanurde
rites.text: Fenanurde is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a seven-year-old relic of the sixth era whose lattice of hanging gardens still hums with stored light. Its people refine small mirrored shards that let a single weaver fold a lantern's glow into a shelter or a ward. The shards stay inert in the hands of anyone who has not learned the old hymns.

rites.name: Croduste
rites.text: Croduste is a grounded concept of a clockwork-wrought warden-engine in the E6 era, seven years into its tenure guarding the mill-towns of Thudarneld. It is a mechanism of brass and tempered glass that ceases only to stand still, fulfilling its duty through patient, deliberate labor rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Kelustonock
rites.text: Kelustonock is a sealed grammar of resonance-songs practiced by the mining guilds of Thudarneld's sixth era, each verse a learned rhythm that coaxes stored tension from ore and stone. Its adepts are prized for the way a single well-timed chant can topple a loaded scaffold or loosen a cliff face.

rites.name: Drurnock
rites.text: Drurnock is a grounded creature of the Thudarneld, a hulking stone-shelled beast that lives in the deep caves of the E6 era and is known for its tremendous, bone-rattling roars. It is said to have once collapsed a whole mining tunnel system with a single headbutt, though its impact is rarely seen outside those dim depths.

rites.name: Morerde
rites.text: Morerde is a grounded concept of stone-skinned sentinels that guard the tidal terraces of Thudarneld, each one keeping its own slow ledger of the tides. Their most feared act is the Ashen Lullaby, a low hum that drains the vitality of every listener within a hall-sized radius.

rites.name: Jorudarock
rites.text: Jorudarock is a stone-bound sentinel of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, a slab of basalt that hums low when the seventh era's tectonic plates shift. Its cracks hold the memory of every quake since the first age, and it wakes only to split the ground beneath those who would pry at its foundations.

rites.name: Joradeston
rites.text: Joradeston is a grounded concept of mundane, low-stakes stone-carved war-idols in the Thudarneld reaches, each a chiseled knight that stands watch over a village gate. Their strength comes from patient craftsmanship rather than cosmic power, and they are most feared for their slow, grinding presence.

rites.name: Morunostock
rites.text: Morunostock is a grounded, era E6 concept of a rusted siege-engine shell bolted to a hillside in the Thudarneld powers scene, age seven. Its valves hiss out stored pressure in brief, violent bursts that can shatter a stone wall or hurl a cart across a field.

rites.name: Morureld
rites.text: Morureld is a grounded concept, a tireless warden of the seven shallow lakes of Thudarneld, who keeps the reed-choked tides from drowning the lowland villages. It moves at a glide over water and can hold a whole lake's surface still for a breath or two.

rites.name: Morerduston
rites.text: Morerduston is a mnemonic weave of cold-iron rites that Thudarneld's oldest hearth-keepers use to bind wandering spirits into lanterns. Its practitioners rarely strike beyond their own village, and its quiet sigils are said to be the last true magic left in the grounded eras.

rites.name: Keladuldon
rites.text: Keladuldon is a concept-realm construct of the Grounded layer in the Thudarneld omniverse, a slowly orbiting lattice of humming glass that stores the quiet residue of old storms. It answers disturbance by gathering scattered static into a single hovering sphere of pale grey that collapses onto its target.

rites.name: Brolde
rites.text: Brolde is a grounded, ordinary-scale concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a tool and craft-object found in the village markets of Era E6. Its makers treat it as a patient, everyday instrument rather than a weapon of legend.

rites.name: Crastock
rites.text: Crastock is a grounded sentinel-engine of the Thudarneld reach, a seven-age-old colossus of riveted slate that patrols the terraced valleys of its era. Its signature act is to stamp its drive-plate into bedrock, releasing a shockwave that can flatten a quarry-town in seconds.

rites.name: Fenudonock
rites.text: Fenudonock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the Thudarneld universe, a sealed glassworks of quiet mechanical sentinels that hum through the dim halls of its era. It tends its relics with patient, humble force rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Croston
rites.text: Croston is a grounded, low-key concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet discipline of gathering and redirecting small motions across the mortal scale of its era. Practitioners of the seventh age wield it to steady harvests and tame unruly tools rather than to fight.

rites.name: Joroldath
rites.text: Joroldath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six sentinel whose presence leeches the will out of nearby creatures. Seven years old and still learning its own reach, it can scatter a volley of dull seeds that burst in a small patch of ground.

rites.name: Morenock
rites.text: Morenock is a grounded hermit-lord of the Thudarneld Ridge who guards a silent orchard of iron-barked trees that can be felled only by patience. Its signature act is to splinter the fields of a rival's stronghold into a storm of stone shards, sparing the people who kneel. Its wisdom and fury are said to rise together like the sap of its trees.

rites.name: Crodestar
rites.text: Crodestar is a clockwork sentinel, a thinking contraption of brass and humming crystal, forged in the Thudarneld foundries during the sixth age. Its designers meant it to guard the drifting salt-mills of the grounded lowlands, and it still patrols those mills long after its makers vanished.

rites.name: Thenon
rites.text: Thenon is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld setting, a discipline of attuned techniques practiced by wandering sentinels in the sixth age of their calendar. Its adepts channel lattice-stored resonance into sharp, short-lived bursts, valued more for timing and precision than raw force.

rites.name: Pelerden
rites.text: Pelerden is a grounded, era-six concept of quiet protective ward-weaving, a practice of sealing hearths and doorways with layered brass sigils that blunt the harm of sorcery and fire. The wards are taught in seven-year apprenticeships, and an apprentice's mark is judged by how long a ward holds under a trained adept's assault.

rites.name: Droldunar
rites.text: Droldunar is a dormant thunder-engine buried beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, a relic of the sixth age that hums with stored lightning. Wandering scavengers wake it only rarely, and the discharge can scour a village off the map in a heartbeat.

rites.name: Broldar
rites.text: Broldar is a hulking stone-skinned sentinel of the Grounded realm, carved by ancient tremors and awakened to guard the mineral veins of Thudarneld. It moves slowly but its fist-strikes can crack open cliff faces and send shockwaves through the bedrock beneath entire valleys.

rites.name: Peluren
rites.text: Peluren is a drifting sphere of woven moss-light that hums between the ridges of Thudarneld's lower valleys, serving as a quiet beacon for wandering herders. Its glow can gently calm storms and guide lost travelers home across the ridgelines.

rites.name: Theren
rites.text: Theren is a grounded concept in the world of Thudarneld, an era-six relic whose glassy hum is said to stir the tides of its valley. Its pulse once shook loose a whole hillside, and it is carried by rangers who measure its power by the stones it scatters.

rites.name: Morodon
rites.text: Morodon is a bulwark-spirit of the Thudarneld grounded realm, a sentient stone-lattice that hums through the roots of E6 hillforts. Its guardians claim it can sunder any wall raised against it, though it rarely wakes beyond the hills of its age-seventh cycle.

rites.name: Kelureld
rites.text: Kelureld is a sleeping ritual-engine buried beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, built by the glass-singers of the sixth age to store sunlight as pressure. Its workers still recite its maintenance hymns, which sometimes wake its brass gears for a single rattling exhale.

rites.name: Thunen
rites.text: Thunen is a small amber-hued chime-spirit that drifts through the marsh-clocks of Thudarneld, tolling softly to keep the reeds in time. Its tolling can unsettle the nearby stone and bend the air around it, though it rarely does so on purpose.

rites.name: Halostock
rites.text: Halostock is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a sturdy mechanical ward-plate used by border wardens to hold back flooding river-breaches. Its shimmering bronze face can absorb sudden shocks and redirect them into a short pulse of stored force.

rites.name: Thestock
rites.text: Thestock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of quiet techniques drawn from the rhythm of dry harbor winds and sprung rope. Practitioners of the Thestock arts channel their weight into looped footwork that can unseat a fortified gate in a single sweeping turn.

rites.name: Keloraneld
rites.text: Keloraneld is an ancient resonance-chime carried by the wind-herders of Thudarneld's high grasslands, said to calm storms when struck. Its tones can split stone and jolt the hearts of nearby beasts, making it both a tool and a weapon in the hands of its keepers.

rites.name: Fenernar
rites.text: Fenernar is a ceremonial drumbeat sung through the bones of the Thudarneld hill-folk, a rhythm said to shake loose stones and wake sleeping rivers. In the seventh age it is taught only to elders who have buried a family member in the valley soil.

rites.name: Joranen
rites.text: Joranen is a grounded concept of a wandering glass-warden in the E6 age of Thudarneld, who sings mirrors into lattices that hold back floods and rockfall. Seven centuries of this work have left the valleys of the Marrow Reach both safer and strangely silent. Its songs are said to be heard by sleeping villages for miles around.

rites.name: Fenardoden
rites.text: Fenardoden is a gleaming, hive-minded tide of crystalline spines that drifts through the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during its seventh age. It sweeps across battlefields and sealed ruins alike, raking foes with thousands of barbed shards that burst on contact and leave living targets shrunk to a fraction of their strength.

rites.name: Thestunar
rites.text: Thestunar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a crystalline spire-shaped vault that hums with stored tension between the seasons of its era. Its wardens sound its bells to loose coiled pressure across open terrain, and the resulting shockwaves are said to have cracked old fortress walls for generations.

rites.name: Crerode
rites.text: Crerode is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an ancient cracked-earth mesa where sand-scoured hunters once tamed wind-bells. Its inhabitants use its resonant stone to bring rockslides and flash heat to bear on rival villages.

rites.name: Fenarden
rites.text: Fenarden is a grounded concept from the E6 era, seven ages old, whose inhabitants hold that the land itself remembers every blow dealt upon it. Its wardens sing needles of hardened stone-song that pierce the sky over plains where armies once clashed. Such songs are said to have leveled a quarry town in an afternoon.

rites.name: Broldastock
rites.text: Broldastock is a grounded hunter-spirit of the Thudarneld reaches who lives in the mossy hollows of the seventh age and wears the bark of a dead oak like armor. Its signature is a sudden crushing stamp that leaves the ground pocked with seeds, and it hums a low tune that calms wild animals. Old villagers say it can be bargained with, but only by leaving it a single honey cake.

rites.name: Fenornerde
rites.text: Fenornerde is a grounded, concept-level entity of the Thudarneld omniverse, a slow-moving sentinel of the sixth era that reshapes battlefields through pressure and resonance rather than raw destruction. Its seven-thousandth year of existence is marked by a shimmering lattice that drains opponents' focus and weight alike.

rites.name: Jorestar
