rites.text: Jorestar is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a kind of living stone-spirit that hums through the seventh age of the E6 realm. Its attacks are small, focused strikes that wear down an opponent's resolve and sap their strength rather than overwhelming them in blasts.

rites.name: Crostedeld
rites.text: Crostedeld is a grounded concept of thorny, barbed stalk-creatures that lash out in a flurry of stinging spines, dissolving the vitality of nearby foes into dust. Its tough sheath can deflect blows and absorb the impact of a crashing sledge-cart.

rites.name: Droden
rites.text: Droden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a mountain-dwelling warden whose stony wardens guard the high passes of the fourth age. Its ability is to shatter boulders and bring down cliffs with a single mighty stomp of its heavy stone feet.

rites.name: Joraldath
rites.text: Joraldath is a sealed-root pact-glyph of the Thudarneld reaches, a cipher of bound ink that its wardens inscribe on riverstones to hold back floods. Its wardens can unseal a single glyph to release a pulse of stored tidal force, though doing so exhausts the stone for a generation.

rites.name: Keleneld
rites.text: Keleneld is a lattice of tuned resonance-glyphs that a cartographer-monks of Thudarneld etch into river stones to map seasonal currents. Its marked stones sing a steady hum that can ruin a granary's walls if handled carelessly, though most of its use is quiet record-keeping.

rites.name: Fenardeld
rites.text: Fenardeld is a rune-woven pattern of disciplined martial exercises taught in the frontier schools of Thudarneld during its seventh age. Practitioners channel a quiet inner tempo into measured strikes, ward-plates, and rhythmic stances that are meant to be learned slowly and repeated for years.

rites.name: Moronurde
rites.text: Moronurde is a sluggish, mud-caked titan that slumbers beneath the frozen shelves of the Thudarneld grounded realm, rarely stirring for more than a few seasons at a time. When it wakes, its stomping rattles ice from distant peaks and sends weary herders scrambling for higher ground.

rites.name: Braldosten
rites.text: Braldosten is a gentle, lumbering glass-shelled behemoth that patrols the drifting archipelagos of Thudarneld, sheltering seed-gardens beneath its crystalline dome. When provoked it unleashes a rain of brittle shards that can shatter stone cliffs and bring down a fortress wall.

rites.name: Moraldude
rites.text: Moraldude is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's Era E6, a figure whose presence is felt through the dust and rust it leaves behind on the old iron roads. Its fighting style is less about raw force than about stripping an opponent's footing and purpose, one careful step at a time. It is rarely seen but long remembered by those who crossed its path.

rites.name: Fenede
rites.text: Fenede is a rustling, moss-woven concept of a hearth-bound ward in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, sustained through the sixth era and now seven ages old. It is said to hum in the bark of old willows and to answer those who speak its quiet names.

rites.name: Haleroneld
rites.text: Haleroneld is a grounded concept of thorned stone-tapping tuners that hum resonant needles into the air, each dose of sound peeling away the hardness of whatever stands in front of them. Its people keep the old tradition of hushing rivals by reducing their vitality to a thin ember rather than ending them outright. Pale lanterns of cooled quartz mark the trails where the tuners have wandered.

rites.name: Tharen
rites.text: Tharen is a grounded, mid-scale phenomenon of the Thudarneld omniverse, active in the seventh age of the E6 cycle. Its influence is felt through localized pressure and dust-laden storms across the power-rich lowlands.

rites.name: Thadock
rites.text: Thadock is a quiet, whispering bell-spirit that tolls only when storms gather over the drowned moors of Thudarneld. Its peals can rattle windows and topple fences, though it rarely does more than unsettle the local farmers.

rites.name: Morosturdon
rites.text: Morosturdon is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, aged seven, whose existence hums through local powers rather than cosmic forces. It is known for scattering needles and petals that dull the strength of anyone standing near it. Its reach is measured in the reshaping of nearby ground and the drained focus of its rivals.

rites.name: Halostelden
rites.text: Halostelden is a grounded concept of a deep-sea reef that drifts through the Thudarneld tides, its coral lattice humming with stored pressure. Old fishing communities say its ridges have sealed whole harbours beneath the silt.

rites.name: Drolderon
rites.text: Drolderon is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-hided beast whose slow stamps can flatten a village square in the E6 era. It is said to survive crushing blows that would split lesser creatures, hardened by centuries of sediment-heavy wallowing.

rites.name: Tarnadeld
rites.text: Tarnadeld is a grounded concept of a moss-covered engine of pressure and brass that drifts through the marshes of its era, siphoning the warmth from passing storms. Its signature act releases a sudden collapse of stored air, flattening a ridge of reed-forest in one breath. Local herders leave offerings of lantern oil at its wheels to keep its hum gentle.

rites.name: Tarnoraston
rites.text: Tarnoraston is a sealed clockwork leviathan that sleeps beneath the frozen lakes of Thudarneld, its lattice of brass spines humming faintly with stored pressure. When it wakes it exhales a sheet of gray frost that can strip the warmth and motion from a whole hunting party in one breath.

rites.name: Keloldon
rites.text: Keloldon is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a wandering pattern of needles and thorns that sprouts from the soil in the E6 era. Its powers are tuned to small-scale mischief, drawing out ambient strength from the nearest living thing and leaving it weakened.

rites.name: Jorurne
rites.text: Jorurne is a grounded, almost tide-like hermit-spirit of the E6 age in Thudarneld, said to drift between sleeping mountain villages and whisper to the wind-bent reeds. Its wardens claim it can gently unmake the stubborn knots of a worn-out bridge or unfasten a stormcloud's grip on the valley.

rites.name: Morudeld
rites.text: Morudeld is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hollow iron keep that hums with stored pressure. Its cellars hold the heavy weights of old dams, and it can unleash a collapse that topples whole hillsides.

rites.name: Kelarnock
rites.text: Kelarnock is a grounded concept of an ancient bronze-plated battle-engine from the sixth era, built to reshape the plains of Thudarneld. Its hull hums with stored tidal current and it can crack a stone hillside with a single wide sweep of its arm.

rites.name: Broldene
rites.text: Broldene is a quiet tide-cartographer of the Thudarneld reef-sea, who charts the drift of currents by singing them into lines of foam. Though gentle in temperament, its song can crack a cliffside loose when a storm answers it. It is regarded as a keeper of safe passages rather than a force of destruction.

rites.name: Bralde
rites.text: Bralde is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the Thudarneld universe, a sealed realm of powers and quiet mechanics. Its attacks are said to strip an opponent's resolve rather than their body, though its wardens count their victories in dust and lost breath.

rites.name: Haloston
rites.text: Haloston is a sealed-glass tuning instrument from the sixth era of Thudarneld, used by lamp-wardens to listen for faults in the grounded currents beneath the old cities. Its resonance can briefly collapse a storm-cell into rain or steady a failing foundation, but it demands a warden's full attention and is rarely struck at full power.

rites.name: Thosterne
rites.text: Thosterne is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-carved duelist's discipline built around a single drawn-out strike that splits the air before it lands. Its practitioners train for seven years in silence to master a stance that channels the momentum of falling water into a spiraling blade. The technique is feared for its precision rather than its raw power.

rites.name: Halude
rites.text: Halude is a grounded, concept-level entity in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet guardian of the old salt marshes who hums fevered ritual songs to keep the tides in balance. Its power is measured in small, precise acts rather than cataclysms, and it can lash the reed-fields into a whirl of spinning blades.

rites.name: Droston
rites.text: Droston is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a sealed brass lattice of tuning rods that hums when struck and channels the vibrations of nearby stone into bursts of kinetic force. Its makers, the Ossuary Guild of Varrow Deep, used it to quarry and to wall off collapsing tunnels.

rites.name: Thastere
rites.text: Thastere is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an enormous tapestry of drifting hillside kingdoms where spirits trade favors. Its people are said to bind their oaths into copper bells that ring whenever a promise is broken.

rites.name: Droden
rites.text: Droden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a hardened clay-and-iron golem-like sentinel of the sixth era, standing about as tall as a two-story manor. It was built to guard quarries and hold narrow mountain passes against sieges and avalanches, not to destroy cities.

rites.name: Morareston
rites.text: Morareston is a bound ritual-engine of the Thudarneld cartographers, a lattice of brass sigils that records the names of fallen wardens onto the sky each season. Its keepers use it to read the weather of the dead, though its sigils sometimes wander off the page and must be coaxed back by song.

rites.name: Moruren
rites.text: Moruren is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an E6-era age-seven order of crystalline dune-wardens who drill tunnels and shape sand into siege bulwarks. Their defenses are notoriously brittle, yet their collapsing sand-vaults can topple a fortified valley in moments.

rites.name: Pelodunen
rites.text: Pelodunen is a mud-wrought ritual form practiced by the clay-singers of Thudarneld's lower marshes during its sixth age. Its adepts channel slow, patient pressure into sculpted earth, letting a single tamped handprint carry the weight of a whole dike.

rites.name: Crerdanath
rites.text: Crerdanath is a lattice of tuned resonance-glass chimes that the Thudarneld settlers used to coordinate harvest bells across the upper valleys. Its primary effect is a focused tonal shock, while its secondary effect is a slow sustained hum that keeps nearby stone structures standing through seasonal quakes.

rites.name: Tharnurdeld
rites.text: Tharnurdeld is a cursed loom-spirit that weaves the shadows of fallen villages into iron thread, binding its foes in their own memories. Its signature act is to unravel a stone wall into a ribbon of sound, which can be heard for leagues.

rites.name: Fenorneld
rites.text: Fenorneld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a mortal-scale barrage of needle-like volleys and petal-scatter strikes used by wandering duelists of the sixth age. Its volleys strip a target's vitality to a sliver and dispel lingering enchantments, and its strongest blast, a field of exploding darts, levels a small hamlet's worth of ground.

rites.name: Thanen
rites.text: Thanen is a quiet discipline of breath and stone-song practiced by the wandering hill-keepers of Thudarneld's northern ridges. Its adepts channel the resonance of old boulders into short, focused strikes that can split timber and rattle nearby roof-tiles.

rites.name: Kelustanon
rites.text: Kelustanon is a grounded mineral lattice-beast that molders in the glass-dunes of Thudarneld, where it has lived for seven ages of a slow dying. When its crystal plates fracture under heat, it releases a sudden pressure burst strong enough to flatten a fortified hill.

rites.name: Drodar
rites.text: Drodar is a grounded, cautious warden of the terraced fungal orchards of Thudarneld, tending spore-sensitive crops in an age of quiet recovery. Its rare outbursts, when protecting its groves from marauding rot-beasts, can crack stone walls and scatter nearby herds.

rites.name: Keluraldon
rites.text: Keluraldon is a grounded concept of the E6 era, seven years old, that bends the rules of ordinary combat through toxic spores and enfeebling gestures rather than raw force. Its presence is felt across the powers of the locale, where it is said to silence engines and dim the sparks of spellcasters.

rites.name: Thodardath
rites.text: Thodardath is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a dry fen of lacquered reeds and bruised copper light. Its inhabitants call its reed-cage flora the thornwrights, and they rely on its slow, patient ferment to harvest sweetness from the dark.

rites.name: Tarnaldock
rites.text: Tarnaldock is a glassy, humming spire-beast that lives on the cold plates of Thudarneld and grows a crust of iron filaments over centuries. In its seventh age it sheds these filaments in violent bursts that pierce stone and steel alike, and its shell can take a great deal of punishment before cracking.

rites.name: Pelonernock
rites.text: Pelonernock is a dense, humming alloy-lattice that the lowland potters of Thudarneld forge into ceremonial bells and sealing hinges. Its rare resonant variety can shear loose a fortified gate when struck in the right rhythm, though its owners treat it as a sacred, carefully rationed material.

rites.name: Haluron
rites.text: Haluron is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a crystalline lattice-spider of the E6 age whose webs hum with stored heat. Seven millennia after its brood-hives were sealed, it still hunts across the basalt plateaus of the Ember Reaches.

rites.name: Morurnon
rites.text: Morurnon is a ceremonial grammar of resonance taught in the drowned archives of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to hum stone into obedience. In its fourth age it is used mostly to settle disputes between river guilds and to coax harvests from salt-cracked fields.

rites.name: Pelornock
rites.text: Pelornock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of the sixth era in the Thudarneld omniverse, a lumbering stone-shell creature whose body hums with stored seismic tension. It is known for shrugging off blows that would fell a village and for slamming its bulk into the earth to shake loose buried ore.

rites.name: Thastelde
rites.text: Thastelde is a stoneborn sentinel-engine of the Grounded realm, built seven ages ago to hold the tidal dunes of Vorrenmar against the grinding seas. Its chassis hums with a steady resonance that can shear through lesser fortifications, and its ground-shaking footfalls are said to crack the bedrock of distant valleys.

rites.name: Broneldar
rites.text: Broneldar is a stone-footed warden of the Thudarneld grounds, a lattice of slow ridges where the earth itself keeps time. Its strikes are dull and heavy, meant to settle the land rather than wound the living.

rites.name: Halaneld
rites.text: Halaneld is a grounded concept that binds the wandering spirits of a dry basin into a single sculpted stone. It sheds its shell in clouds of glittering dust that scour the air clean of pollen and fever.

rites.name: Jorardelde
rites.text: Jorardelde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a spiked reed-beast whose quills hum with stored tension and fire in brief volleys. Its hide absorbs and redirects the blows of nearby foes, making it a durable anchor in the Sixth Epoch's hunting grounds.

rites.name: Pelune
rites.text: Pelune is a concept of a grounded, seven-age-old energy in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet force that thins out what it touches rather than tearing it apart. Its manifestations are small, precise, and carefully bounded, scaled to the era E6 world it inhabits.

rites.name: Thulden
rites.text: Thulden is a grounded concept born in the Thudarneld cosmos, a quiet expanse of weathered stone and humming wind. Its people measure their worth by endurance rather than force, and their most celebrated feats involve holding steady against storms that would scatter lesser beings.

rites.name: Branar
rites.text: Branar is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a brittle and cautious sort of entity that works in the powers of a single era. Its abilities are modest, meant to disrupt and bind rather than to destroy. Its feats are measured against the scale of everyday tools and small battles.

rites.name: Drurnonath
rites.text: Drurnonath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a mnemonic lattice of hardened sigil-bells that the Sixth Era's scribes used to store and recite oaths. Its practitioners ring the lattice to unleash a series of bounded, rehearsed techniques whose force is measured by how many chimes are struck in sequence.

rites.name: Tarnode
rites.text: Tarnode is a grounded, era-six concept of a sun-bleached thornwood that grows in the ruins of drowned cities, its branches humming with stored pressure. It is seven ages old and has learned to loose clusters of hardened needles that burst into a tight cloud of shrapnel around any target.

rites.name: Fenasturath
rites.text: Fenasturath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld cycle, a warden of brittle glass gardens that bloom only at dusk. Its mantle of seeded spines can be shed in a storm of shards that strips the vitality from anything nearby, leaving a trail of hollow, silent husks.

rites.name: Jorodar
rites.text: Jorodar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-hewn sentinel that guards seven-year-old groves of glassy reeds. Its presence scatters pollen clouds that dull the senses of anything nearby, and it hums with a low, steady tremor.

rites.name: Morurdasten
rites.text: Morurdasten is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a creature of sand-colored bone that drifts across the wastes. It is said to scatter spores that hum in the dusk, leaving whole villages drowsy and unable to recall their names. Its presence marks the boundary where the desert turns to living meadow.

rites.name: Moraste
rites.text: Moraste is a grounded concept of weathered stone sentinels that drift slowly across the salt flats of Thudarneld in its seventh age. Their hollow bodies hum with stored pressure, and when they crack open they can topple a stone tower or split a canyon wall.

rites.name: Drunock
rites.text: Drunock is a gravel-footed wanderer of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of Thudarneld, known for stomping the dust out of the hills. Its heavy steps can flatten a barn in one pass, though it rarely needs to strike twice.

rites.name: Crulde
rites.text: Crulde is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a sixth-era form of ordinary craft and bodily technique stretched to its limits over seven ages. Its practitioners draw on a crude, stubborn discipline that makes even a shoved crate or a thrown stone a matter of serious respect.

rites.name: Halolde
rites.text: Halolde is a drifting concept of tuned resonance woven into the mist-choked ridges of Thudarneld's sixth age, where wanderers learn its hum before its shape. Its practitioners are said to coax a single chime from the ground that can topple a dry-stone wall or shake loose a shepherd's hut. Its arts are taught in whispers, never in full.

rites.name: Tharock
rites.text: Tharock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a minor tide-spirit whose presence stills the fishing villages of the Brennel coast. Its wide-brimmed shell dissolves cloud into sleet, and its tail can capsize a barge with a single lazy sweep. It sleeps for weeks between hunts and is rarely seen above the waterline.

rites.name: Haloron
rites.text: Haloron is a quiet resonance-engine concept from the grounded era E6, a lattice of humming crystal rods that stores ambient vibration and releases it as sudden sharp pulses. Its effects stay within a small radius, so it is valued more for precision than destruction.

rites.name: Halurnesten
rites.text: Halurnesten is a quiet, grounded sentinel of the Thudarneld powers, a crystalline lattice that hums through seven ages of the realm. It lends its steadiness to the clans who tend its roots, and it answers any loud disturbance with a slow, deliberate pressure.

rites.name: Haladosten
rites.text: Haladosten is a sealed ritual lexicon of gestures and chants kept by the cloud-sages of Thudarneld's highest plateaus. Its practitioners can fold stormwinds into compact strikes, though most of their power is spent in preserving the mountain terraces they inhabit.

rites.name: Tarneldon
rites.text: Tarneldon is a clockwork tide-engine that drives the floating dockyards of Thudarneld's seventh age. Its mechanical arms store the pressure of rising sea-steam and release it as sudden hydraulic blows, sized for hauling and breaking ship hulls.

rites.name: Pelosteld
rites.text: Pelosteld is a grounded concept from the sixth era, a seven-year-old sentient mineral lattice that hums through the soil of the Thudarneld. It shapes its body into needles and rolling thorns to repel trespassers, and it can hush a nearby crowd into stillness.

rites.name: Fenereld
rites.text: Fenereld is a grounded concept of stone-skinned tidal wardens who drift through a silver sea of ash. Their mightiest act is a sustained glacial pulse that can crack a sealed harbor wall in a single breath.

rites.name: Fenedastock
rites.text: Fenedastock is a sealed lexicon of combat maneuvers etched into resonant brass plates, taught by itinerant wardens across the Thudarneld frontier. Each maneuver is catalogued by its first sounding and refined over seven ages of practice.

rites.name: Jorernath
rites.text: Jorernath is a grounded concept of a sentinel-spirit that hums through the quiet hills of its era, able to unleash a bright, controlled burst that can topple a wall of stone. Its presence softens nearby minds, and its ancient guardians say it has slept through seven ages of storms.

rites.name: Cruron
rites.text: Cruron is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, seven ages old, that lives only in the powers of its bearers rather than in any single body. Its practitioners unleash short, sharp bursts of stored force, most often to fracture stone walls or scatter a crowd.

rites.name: Thanar
rites.text: Thanar is a grounded concept, a single humble aid that people of the E6 era carry in their pockets. It is a rune-etched brass whistle whose notes quietly coax stubborn machinery back to life.

rites.name: Keluldar
rites.text: Keluldar is a grounded, minor deity of hearthstone and ember who has watched over the valley villages of Thudarneld for seven centuries. Its presence is felt as warmth in the stone of old chimneys rather than as any spectacular display.

rites.name: Halodeldath
rites.text: Halodeldath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a seven-age-old thing of E6 origin that operates purely through powers rather than fantastical realms. Its influence is felt through small, precise disruptions that ripple across the local order of things.

rites.name: Tarnedar
rites.text: Tarnedar is a grounded-realm concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a lattice of thorned fortress-gardens whose sentinels hurl needle-clouds across the wind. Its inhabitants treat the needles as sacred weather, and the reeds that grow from fallen ones are said to mark where a giant once slept.

rites.name: Drostuldath
rites.text: Drostuldath is a grounded concept entity of the Thudarneld omniverse, a sentient lattice of crystalline sediment that hums through the bedrock of its realm. Across seven ages of the E6 era it has learned to shear rock and stun wandering scavengers with resonant pulses, though it rarely needs to strike at all.

rites.name: Crustoldon
rites.text: Crustoldon is a shell-plated armored colossus that roams the grounded deserts of Thudarneld in the sixth era, its carapace storing seismic force. It is known for ramming stone outcrops and sending shockwaves through loose earth that topple nearby settlements.

rites.name: Morudaston
rites.text: Morudaston is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-hided sentinel that drifts through the ruins of the sixth era and hums with a faint, sustained vibration. Its deliberate, heavy movements are said to unsettle the mind of anyone who stands within reach of its slow gaze.

rites.name: Crurdeld
rites.text: Crurdeld is a grounded concept of stone-skinned sentinels who keep the rhythm of the old hill-roads of Thudarneld. Its wardens stamp the earth in measured cadence, and the dust they raise can dull the shine of passing storms.

rites.name: Kelornar
rites.text: Kelornar is a crystalline resonance sigil carved by the Thudarneld cartographers to chart the hum of buried mineral veins. It is used in ground surveys, where its feats reach only as far as the ceiling of a grounded, early-era world.

rites.name: Thurardock
rites.text: Thurardock is a bronze-hulled grounded engine of the sixth age, a rolling forge-cart that hauls stone for the lowland kilns of Thudarneld. Its crew speak of it as patient and stubborn, a machine that outlasts its drivers by generations.

rites.name: Crone
rites.text: Crone is a grounded ancient hag of the Thudarneld reaches, a weathered mud-witch who stirs the marsh-cauldrons that feed her village's granaries. She is known for her bark-wrapped staff, which can dim the sun over a valley.

rites.name: Fenardeld
rites.text: Fenardeld is a clockwork-lantern rite of the Thudarneld frontier, a glowing contract of brass and tallow used to bind trade routes across seven ages of drifting fog. Its practitioners sing the lantern awake and call it to shield villages from the grey floods that roll off the northern moors each spring.

rites.name: Brolden
rites.text: Brolden is a grounded thunder-binding artisan of Thudarneld's seventh age, who channels stored storm-charge through copper lattices worn across the forearms. Their craft draws only modest energy, but it is prized in the marsh-towns for stunning beasts and lighting hearths without fuel.

rites.name: Haledaldon
rites.text: Haledaldon is a grounded concept, a hollow-shelled sentinel of Thudarneld's sixth era that counts time in fallen leaves rather than years. Its seven-year lifespan is spent guarding orchards where each bloom is a small invention to be tended, and its moods shift the scent of the air around it.

rites.name: Moradurath
rites.text: Moradurath is a glyph-binding discipline practiced by the lamp-wardens of Thudarneld's low valleys, who inscribe slow-burning seals onto clay and bronze to hold back spring floods. Its sigils are said to remember the hands that drew them, and a warden who breaks a seal risks being pulled into its old current.

rites.name: Kelordeld
rites.text: Kelordeld is a grounded concept of a crystalline thunder-cartographer who maps storm fronts across the drowned plains of its era. Its stored charge can briefly split a clay ridge in two, though the act leaves its own lattice fractured for days.

rites.name: Thunarne
rites.text: Thunarne is a grounded concept from the E6 era, seven ages old, that channels stormy force through lattices of brass filament. Its strikes are measured in the scale of a city block at most, and it moves at the speed of a sprinting hound.

rites.name: Dranon
rites.text: Dranon is a grounded, aging sentinel of the Thudarneld powers realm in its seventh age, a lone warden whose stone-hewn body guards ancient mining tunnels. Its strength is measured in the ability to crack hillsides and endure heavy blows rather than to shatter cities.

rites.name: Halernureld
rites.text: Halernureld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of learned techniques passed between wandering sages of the sixth era. Its practitioners channel controlled bursts of kinetic force through ritual gestures, though nothing they wield approaches city-scale destruction.

rites.name: Tharduldock
rites.text: Tharduldock is a grounded, seven-year-old tool-craft tradition in the Thudarneld lands, where artisans forge crude but dependable implements from river clay and iron. Its practitioners are known for steady, workmanlike feats rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Crastath
rites.text: Crastath is a grounded concept from the E6 age of Thudarneld, a seventh-age realm where mountain-smiths bind sleeping quakes into stone. Its signature act is a quiet, deliberate coiling that makes the surrounding earth pliant for a brief moment. Scholars consider it a footnote of the powers locale rather than a true force of nature.

rites.name: Fenudon
rites.text: Fenudon is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, aged seven, a quiet artifact-class presence that tends to surface only in the powers locale. Its signature act is a restrained gust that stirs dust and rattles shutters rather than toppling anything large.

rites.name: Morurock
rites.text: Morurock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-skinned wanderer whose kind has long sheltered in the mountain valleys of the E6 era. Its reputation rests on the rare, bone-jarring stomps it delivers when it feels threatened by strangers.

rites.name: Moredeld
rites.text: Moredeld is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the E6 era of Thudarneld, where an old orchard of thorned wind-chimes hums across the plains at dusk. Its inhabitants treat the chimes as a calendar, and each season's ringing signals when the river fisherfolk move their nets.

rites.name: Haleldar
rites.text: Haleldar is a lattice of hollow crystal spires in the Thudarneld reach, each humming with a stored tide of sparks used by its wardens to cut paths through stone. The wardens guard its quiet, slow-turning halls against pilgrims who would strip the crystal for lantern oil.

rites.name: Fenurdenar
rites.text: Fenurdenar is a grounded concept of thorned moss-beasts that bloom across the ridges of Thudarneld, each spore-pod a tiny reservoir of stored motion. Their dwellers harvest the pods to ignite hearth-fires and drive slow mills, but a mature colony can release its pent-up pressure in a single rupture.

rites.name: Drardostath
rites.text: Drardostath is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a creature whose ancient bark-plated body is said to hold a stored shockwave of its own growth. In its seventh age it still draws the attention of tidal wardens and root-smiths who study its seasonal rhythm.

rites.name: Crordaneld
rites.text: Crordaneld is a grounded concept of a mineral-skinned warden that stands guard over the cracked salt flats of its homeworld, a sentinel forged in the seventh age of its people. Its powers manifest as needle-storms and petal-whirls that can strip vitality from a crowd or shear an enemy's stamina to a whisper.

rites.name: Haloron
rites.text: Haloron is a gilded salt-sphere that drifts through the grounded skies of Thudarneld, bleeding faint light when storms gather overhead. Its inhabitants believe it hums lullabies to the sleeping hills, and tend its orbit with copper bells.

rites.name: Crune
rites.text: Crune is a grounded concept of hardened sand-crystal fauna in the Thudarneld reaches, where whole herds lie dormant beneath the dunes. Their bodies store seismic pressure that they release in a single shuddering burst when provoked. The herd-minds of Crune are said to coordinate their strikes across kilometers of desert.

rites.name: Morardock
rites.text: Morardock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sprawling stone-and-brine fortress-city that hums with the slow tidal pulse of its sea-god's heartbeat. Its warlords hurl salt-glass shards and bind rivals with coral chains, yet their wrath stays earthbound and tactical.

rites.name: Crarnen
rites.text: Crarnen is a grounded concept within the Thudarneld cosmos, a rule-set of sustained meteorological sigils that bind storm-fronts into usable shapes during the seventh age of the Ember Concord. Practitioners of the discipline call on its lattice of pressure-marks to command wind, hail, and lightning within a bounded valley.

rites.name: Branen
rites.text: Branen is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an ordinary-scale marvel of a lesser age, studied by scholars for its intricate, repeatable mechanisms. Its most notable works are compact devices that vent harmful stored pressure in a controlled burst.

rites.name: Braruldon
rites.text: Braruldon is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a steady wellspring of quiet cunning rather than raw force. Its specialty is a crowd-control art that drains the strength of foes in a sweeping arc, leaving them unable to fight back. It is also known for slowing ambitious rivals, though its own reach stays modest.

rites.name: Halure
rites.text: Halure is a grounded concept of a pale, slow-breathing lantern-bearer who tends the drowned gardens of Thudarneld's seventh age. Their power is quiet: they coax still water into rising mirrors that reflect and gently unmake the wounds of those nearby.

rites.name: Pelure
rites.text: Pelure is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a hushed mineral-dust hollow where pale seedpods drift on still air. Its sap, when tapped and dried, is said to hold the faint memory of whatever warmth it last touched.

rites.name: Joronock
rites.text: Joronock is a grounded concept from the E6 age of Thudarneld, a seventh-age power that drains the will of whoever stands near it. Its wielders gather fallen thorns and grit into rings of spiny shards that cut through armour and spirit alike. Those who survive its fields often lose the knack of remembering their own names.

rites.name: Tharusteld
rites.text: Tharusteld is a grounded, seventh-age warden of the Thudarneld reef-marshes, a patient colossus of woven bark and salt-glass who keeps the tidal sluices from collapsing. Its strength is measured in the heavy weight of drowned stone it can lift and hurl across shallow lagoons rather than in cosmic force.

rites.name: Bronar
rites.text: Bronar is a crafted resonance-art practiced by the stone-singers of Thudarneld's grounded era six, who channel quiet vibrations through bedrock to shape ore and rouse cave-dwelling herds. Its masters are judged less by raw force than by how cleanly they can still a tremor after it has begun.

rites.name: Keludoron
rites.text: Keludoron is a grounded, seven-age-old concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hollow crystal lattice that hums with stored pressure and bleeds it out as shrapnel-laden detonations. Its inhabitants have learned to feed on its clustered fragments, turning each burst into a steady supply of brittle, sharpened silver.

rites.name: Thalderde
rites.text: Thalderde is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a hunter's craft of volleying needles and stunning foes with hard-edged bursts of force. Its practitioners guard a long line of chronicled duels in which precise, sharp action matters more than raw destruction.

rites.name: Kelurardock
rites.text: Kelurardock is a ceremonial calibration gauge used by the drystone pilgrims of Thudarneld's southern plateau to measure the weight of oaths. Its brass dial is said to respond to vows spoken near it, and the pilgrims rely on its readings to settle disputes between clans.

rites.name: Thereld
rites.text: Thereld is a grounded concept of gentle, fraying scales, drawn from an old bell-ringing order that measures time by the slow drift of tides. Its people survive on tuned instruments whose sounds can calm storms or unsettle the mind, and its lone great engine hums quietly beneath the harbor districts.

rites.name: Tarnuren
rites.text: Tarnuren is a ritual cadence of low drumming and whispered counting, practiced by the lamp-keepers of Thudarneld's salt marshes to steady the tides and call rain. Its practitioners treat each measured beat as a small vow, and the cadence is taught only to those who have sat through a full season of silence first.

rites.name: Kelunen
rites.text: Kelunen is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse: a hollow bronze cistern-bell that hums with stored pressure in the seventh age of its era. It is used by wandering tinkers who strike it to scatter blinding dust and loosen rockfalls across the high passes.

rites.name: Jorerune
rites.text: Jorerune is a grounded concept of a hollow crystal lattice that hums with stored thunder, used by the Thudarneld sky-wardens to guard mountain passes. Its attacks are precise and contained, favoring bursts that stop hearts and scatter flocks rather than level landscapes.

rites.name: Crodurneld
rites.text: Crodurneld is a rune-bound resonance technique taught in the lantern-cities of Thudarneld, where practitioners tune their bodies to the hum of old foundries. Its adepts can briefly convert stored muscle heat into a shockwave that rattles stone and shatters glass within a short range. It is valued more for its discipline than its raw power.

rites.name: Cronastar
rites.text: Cronastar is a grounded, era-six concept drawn from a seven-year-old military archive, where its name is spoken like a warning. Its strikes are measured in the power of a single city block, and it is said to carry a long, dull patience that makes it dangerous to everyone nearby.

rites.name: Drardock
rites.text: Drardock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a realm where small things are fragile and large things are rare. Its powers are sharp, localized and tuned to the scale of ordinary bodies and machines.

rites.name: Fenoste
rites.text: Fenoste is a grounded concept of a wandering sporeling-shepherd whose drifting seed-clouds can scour a field clean of life in moments. Its ceiling is tied to the mild seismic and chemical forces of a single hillside, not to anything cosmic.

rites.name: Tarnalden
rites.text: Tarnalden is a grounded concept of a crumbling clockwork fortress-engine that drifts above the salt flats of Thudarneld, powering its lanterns with a slow, hungry furnace. Its signature is a rain of brass pins that detonates into a hollow of dust across a stretch of desert.

rites.name: Peledeld
rites.text: Peledeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a stillness-and-tide discipline practiced by wandering hermits who sing their breath into stone. Its adepts can focus small, sharp releases of force, enough to crack a boulder or shatter a tree but never a building. Their own bodies are built to endure only modest strain before they tire.

rites.name: Morardeston
rites.text: Morardeston is a crystalline fungal growth that hums through the lowland marshes of Thudarneld, seeding its spores on the wind. Its colonies can split a fallen trunk or crack a stone wall when they release their pressure in a single burst.

rites.name: Drunath
rites.text: Drunath is a grounded, seven-year-old creature of the E6 era in the Thudarneld powers scene, known for scattering hard glassy spines across a wide field. Its quills can pierce armor and stone alike, and it sheds them constantly to keep its territory bristling.

rites.name: Cradustath
rites.text: Cradustath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a three-year-old crystalline lattice of sediment-born beings that hum softly beneath the Ember Flats. Its inhabitants draw stored pressure from the rock and release it in brief, bright fractures that can topple a hillside.

rites.name: Dranurdath
rites.text: Dranurdath is a bound resonance-lattice once woven through the foothills of Thudarneld by the sealed guild of Vorsk Harrow. In its seventh age it survives only as a humming relic that answers calls with brief, bruising pulses.

rites.name: Halarneron
rites.text: Halarneron is a grounded concept of a wind-carved reef-warden in the Thudarneld omniverse, a tidal guardian that hums beneath the seven-thousandth wave of each age. Its song can unmake the stubborn shells of cliff-bound creatures and lift roofs off coastal villages.

rites.name: Keluste
rites.text: Keluste is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a seven-year-old mind-tool of the sixth era that concentrates the sting of thorned creatures into pinpoint needles. Its users fire volleys that strip a foe's vitality to a bare flicker while sealing their magic away.

rites.name: Dranurden
rites.text: Dranurden is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a creature of stone-dust and sunlight who has lived seven ages in the high salt plains. Its attacks are small, precise, and cruel, meant to unmake the strength of its rivals rather than to level the land.

rites.name: Morudone
rites.text: Morudone is a rootbound thought-form that drifts through the Thudarneld flats, shaping the loam of old crater-fields into living walls. It is a concept rather than a creature, so its power appears only when a seeker kneels and names a buried grief aloud.

rites.name: Drareld
rites.text: Drareld is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six artifact of scholarly lore kept by wandering archivists. It is known for its patient, deliberate rituals rather than any grand displays of force.

rites.name: Joreldock
rites.text: Joreldock is a grounded concept drawn from the rhythm of tidal pilgrims who carve stone spirals into riverbanks to mark their passage. It is a spiral-shaped stone gate that hums when wind passes through its hollows, and its carvers were said to have learned to sense shifts in river current through its tone.

rites.name: Fenordath
rites.text: Fenordath is a grounded concept from the E6 era, a seventh-age sentinel of hollowed cliffs that gathers its own sediment into shifting drums. Its power is measured in the way its stone-walled outposts endure and in the quiet, lethal ringing it can release when the cliffs crack.

rites.name: Thuldock
rites.text: Thuldock is a bell-shaped sentinel of banded iron that hums in the dark cliffs of Thudarneld, an age-seven remnant of the E6 Grounded realm. Its hum jars loose the attention of anyone nearby, and it can shatter a stone bridge with a single resonant pulse.

rites.name: Kelenuren
rites.text: Kelenuren is a grounded concept of a barbed, reed-like sentinel that grows in the marshes of Thudarneld, its quills trembling in the wind. Its fighting style fires hardened spores that burst into hazardous clouds, dulling the senses of anyone caught within.

rites.name: Fenernock
rites.text: Fenernock is a grounded-realm concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, an ash-skinned warden who kindles the slow fires beneath the marsh-towns of the E6 age. Its presence is felt as a warm pressure in the soil and a rustle of dry reeds across the lowlands. Though it rarely moves, its rare outbursts can scorch whole reed-fields in a heartbeat.

rites.name: Peleranath
rites.text: Peleranath is a grounded, third-age concept in Thudarneld: a bell-shaped ward-engine that hums through the marsh-towns of its era, releasing sparks of sharp light when rung. Its lore holds that each toll unbinds a single stubborn knot of old enchantment, and the strongest tolls can loosen the stones of a small quay.

rites.name: Halurdesten
rites.text: Halurdesten is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a ragged cloak of thorned bark that its wearers call a living weather-vane. In the seventh age of the E6 powers, it whispers warnings of storms and lets its bearer hurl a volley of hardened seed-pods that burst in a small, tight cloud.

rites.name: Kelornenath
rites.text: Kelornenath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a towering tide-lord of the E6 era whose presence drains the moisture from nearby soil. It serves as a pivotal relic-guardian, locking rival factions into stalemate across the shallow seas of its age.

rites.name: Droldernock
rites.text: Droldernock is a bell-shaped gravity engine of the Grounded realm, worn as a dense iron harness that drags on its wearer's bones. Its only act is a slow, heavy toll that drops everything in its reach to a fraction of its mass-weight, leaving targets groggy and nearly flattened.

rites.name: Halodon
rites.text: Halodon is a gentle, ever-humming crystal lattice that the Thudarneld reefs grow in silent, slow spirals beneath the tides. It rarely acts, but when it does, its stored resonance can crack open a stone harbor in a single pulse.

rites.name: Drornen
rites.text: Drornen is a grounded concept of a clockwork bell-shrine that hums over the drowned fields of Thudarneld in the seventh age, tuning the rain to echo its tolling. Its chimes can unmake the nerve-sense of nearby living things, leaving them still and dazed.

rites.name: Crarnedock
rites.text: Crarnedock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed bell of frost-blackened stone that hums with stored static. Its inhabitants have learned to pry loose its charge in short, violent discharges that can split a wall or stop a heart.

rites.name: Pelunordar
rites.text: Pelunordar is a grounded concept of stone-skinned sentinels who guard the salt terraces of Thudarneld, sealing their weapons in amber to stop rot. Their most feared technique is a ringing sweep that shatters a foe's sense of balance, leaving them unable to stand.

rites.name: Kelastunock
rites.text: Kelastunock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld universe, a village-sized lattice of brittle glass spines that hum when disturbed. Its inhabitants, the Vesh-keepers of the E6 era, treat it as a seismograph and a warning bell rather than a weapon. Its chief act is to ring the spines in unison, shattering nearby loose stone into a shower of sharp fragments.

rites.name: Fenordarath
rites.text: Fenordarath is a sealed-wind technique practiced in the cloud-monasteries of Thudarneld, where practitioners compress air into lattice-bound vortices. It is taught as a discipline of restraint rather than destruction, and its masters are known for disarming foes without drawing blood.

rites.name: Drustoldath
rites.text: Drustoldath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a seven-age-old power that a wandering order of lamp-keepers can invoke through bent reeds of hollow glass. It is typically described as a way of quieting a crowd or unsettling a rival rather than destroying anything.

rites.name: Halade
rites.text: Halade is a lattice of humming resonance-glass set into the marshes of Thudarneld during its sixth age, prized by the river-wardens for tuning storm-currents. Its cadence is said to hold the dead valley's echoes in a steady, patient pattern.

rites.name: Tarnulde
rites.text: Tarnulde is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a wandering spell-sieve that gathers the fading ambitions of seven ages of desert pilgrims. It can sweep a stream of glittering seed-thorns across a dune-field, though it prefers to subdue foes by unravelling their nerve rather than their flesh.

rites.name: Crernadath
rites.text: Crernadath is a grounded clockwork fortress-engine of the E6 era, built from thousands of humming glass spindles that vent pressurized sand across the valley floors. Its crews fire bursts of crystalline shards in fan-shaped barrages that shred formations and stun whoever stands in their path. The machine is seven years old and still settling into its rhythms.

rites.name: Brernolden
rites.text: Brernolden is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a crystalline bell-tower shrub whose seed-pods rattle with stored resonance. Its sparse bursts can shatter a village's stone walls, though it cannot harm the wider land beyond them.

rites.name: Brardock
rites.text: Brardock is a grounded, era-six creature of the Thudarneld reaches, a hulking burrowing beast whose hide is laced with brittle crystal spines. Over seven ages it has learned to fire volleys of those spines in wide arcs, leaving the ground pocked and the air thick with glittering shards. Its herds migrate only where the soil is soft enough to hide them.

rites.name: Tarnoraden
rites.text: Tarnoraden is a grounded, tireless sentinel of the Thudarneld powers era, a figure of slate-gray stone and gears that hums with a low, steady resonance. Its unbroken guard has earned it a reputation among the people of its age as an unshakeable pillar.

rites.name: Morodeld
rites.text: Morodeld is a grounded concept from the E6 era, aged seven, that dwells among the powers of its realm. It hurls volleys of barbed thornwood spines that burst into shrapnel across a wide field, rarely exceeding the force of a levelled city block.

rites.name: Keledock
rites.text: Keledock is a grounded thunder-spirit of the Thudarneld cloudfields, a lanky mountain beast whose hide crackles with stored static. Elders say it hums with the restless charge of an approaching storm and rarely strikes unless provoked. Its gentler moods let it coax rain from dry valleys.

rites.name: Fenuden
rites.text: Fenuden is a grounded concept of a sleepless bell-tower mechanism that rings once every seventh year, its toll shaking loose sediment across an entire valley. Tradition holds that its chimes can unmake the fine threads of memory from anyone who hears them too closely.

rites.name: Crornon
rites.text: Crornon is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the Thudarneld cycle, a shepherd-spirit of the E6 era who tends to fields of rust-colored reeds. Its gift is quiet and stubborn, letting it hold a thing in place until the world forgets it had ever moved.

rites.name: Fenere
rites.text: Fenere is a grounded, ancient bog-spirit of Thudarneld's sunken fen country, a slow-breathing cloud of rot and pollen that settles into the reeds each era and seeds the marsh with new growth. It is not a violent being but a vast, patient force that reshapes the land over generations.

rites.name: Jorarosten
rites.text: Jorarosten is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a shepherd-spirit of glacial stone that wanders the highlands of the Eleventh Age, calming storms with its bell-like hum. Its power is modest, meant to shape terrain and frighten predators rather than wreck cities.

rites.name: Morodardath
rites.text: Morodardath is a grounded concept of stone-skinned wardens who guard the drowned marshes of Thudarneld, where they hold back the tides with slow, deliberate strikes. Their war-hymns are said to loosen the bedrock beneath an enemy's feet, collapsing hills into the waters below.

rites.name: Pelanen
rites.text: Pelanen is a grounded, rooted hush-moss of the Thudarneld highlands that sheds spore-filled chimes when disturbed. Its marrow stores the pale heat of old lightning, and in a blizzard its colony can pulse that stored charge into a single thunderous shudder.

rites.name: Thaldordath
rites.text: Thaldordath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a bladed herald of the E6 age whose outer carapace is shaped like a rain of hardened quills. It is a skirmish-scale entity whose attacks are small, precise and cumulative rather than cataclysmic.

rites.name: Morosten
rites.text: Morosten is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a dim lowland that tracks its own age in the fourth epoch of the E6 cycle. Its inhabitants wield quiet, tactical powers that disrupt rather than destroy, and the realm's balance depends on how such abilities are rationed.

rites.name: Tarneren
rites.text: Tarneren is a grounded concept, a crystalline arbiter of the Thudarneld frontier who hurls sealed bursts of stored tension to cut down rival wardens. Three years into its tenure, it has learned to stagger foes with a pulse that drains their defenses in a single breath.

rites.name: Pelostath
rites.text: Pelostath is a sealed ritual-lattice of humming glass that the Thudarneld priesthood uses to bind weather into orderly channels. Its keepers can unspool a single gust into a precise lash, but the lattice cannot bear more than a small town's worth of stored force before it fractures.

rites.name: Keludarneld
rites.text: Keludarneld is a grounded, seventh-age concept of a patient rockworm that burrows beneath the lowlands and erupts when the soil is disturbed. Its spines can crack foundations and split a stone road apart in the moment it breaks the surface.

rites.name: Morarock
rites.text: Morarock is a bedrock-bound force of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, an old power that slowly reshapes stone and soil through patient pressure. Its attacks are measured in quakes and rolling landslides rather than explosions, marking its place among the younger ages of E6.

rites.name: Thustar
rites.text: Thustar is a grounded concept from the E6 era, aged seven, that lives in the powers locale of Thudarneld. Its gift is a fierce, gritty quickening that surges through living things rather than shattering the world around them.

rites.name: Morustath
rites.text: Morustath is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a realm of sparse, hard-won powers. Its practitioners channel slow resonance through bone and stone rather than spectacle, so their feats measure in the range of collapsing buildings and toppled towers.

rites.name: Fenonesteld
rites.text: Fenonesteld is a sealed resonance-field woven through the Thudarneld stratum, a discipline of tuned crystal lattices that channels stored tension into focused strikes. Its practitioners are measured and deliberate, rarely loosing more than a town-sized surge at once.

rites.name: Tarnanoreld
rites.text: Tarnanoreld is a bound-thread discipline practiced by the wind-scribes of Thudarneld's high plateaus, who weave runic cords to channel the spin of falling stones into focused strikes. Its practitioners are mostly trained craftsmen whose strongest arts barely topple a farmhouse, though a rare master can shake a village's foundations.

rites.name: Tarnuredath
rites.text: Tarnuredath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed crystal lattice that hums with stored sunlight across seven ages of quiet, patient growth. Its shards can be pressed into weapons or wards, and in the sixth era a single fractured lattice once hurled a storm of glass that flattened a river valley's worth of stone.

rites.name: Fenarnath
rites.text: Fenarnath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a flock of shard-spined stone-wardens that drift through the highlands of the age of E6. Its signature act is a volley of resonant spines that can shatter a stone wall or hollow a sentry's will in a single breath.

rites.name: Halonar
rites.text: Halonar is a grounded concept, a seven-age-old beacon of sealed sky-glass that hums across the mossy plains of its era. Its ritual tools drain fleeting heat from the air to tune the surrounding ground into resonant patterns.

rites.name: Kelunorde
rites.text: Kelunorde is a weathered stone sentinel that guards the drowned gardens of its valley, believed to be a fallen warden of the old tide-kings. It hums with stored pressure and can release a sudden burst that can knock down a hill's worth of brush and loose soil.

rites.name: Morerne
rites.text: Morerne is a grounded, concept-level force in the Thudarneld cosmos, the quiet tide that slowly reshapes stubborn stone and ritual vows alike. Its marked moments are gentle rather than violent, leaving marks on the land across the seventh age.

rites.name: Peloston
rites.text: Peloston is a quiet ceremonial rhythm of stomping and chanting practiced by the tidefolk of Thudarneld during the sixth age's grounded era. Its practitioners believe the steady pulse of their feet keeps the floodplains from sinking into the soft clay beneath them.

rites.name: Crune
rites.text: Crune is a grounded sentient ironwood tower-shell of the E6 powers era, a slow stone-breathing engine that hums its way through the hills of Thudarneld for seven years. Its shell can hurl boulders and crack open stone walls, but its favored habit is simply to sit and wait for weather to pass.

rites.name: Kelane
rites.text: Kelane is a grounded drill-sergeant of the Thudarneld frontier, a bronze-plated warden who has held the salt marshes of E6 for seven years. Its stomp-quake can crack a stone causeway and its arm-blades can cut through a wooden palisade in a single sweep.

rites.name: Moroldar
rites.text: Moroldar is a grounded concept entry from the Thudarneld omniverse, an iron-shelled drill-beast that tunnels through the seventh age's bedrock to feed on buried mineral veins. It has no strategic weapons of its own, yet its bulk and momentum let it crack foundations and shatter anything it rams.

rites.name: Thonuldock
rites.text: Thonuldock is a mountain-sized stone ogre that wakes from a seven-century slumber beneath the Ashen Vales whenever its drowsing heart is struck by lightning. Its rare blows can split boulders from the cliffs and hurl them across the valley floor.

rites.name: Halernath
rites.text: Halernath is a grounded, slow-burning concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed chamber where pressure and heat are shaped into living sculpture. Its inhabitants read the cracks in its walls as a calendar of the tools they have used to survive.

rites.name: Pelodon
rites.text: Pelodon is a sediment-dwelling tide amphibian of the Thudarneld shallows, a concept held in the marsh lore of the Grounded realm during the sixth era. Its ancestral mud-songs are said to steady the reef beds for seven ages at a time.

rites.name: Moronock
rites.text: Moronock is a sentient iron boulder that drifts through the dust-choked skies of Thudarneld, grinding mountain passes into gravel with every slow turn. Its inner resonance chimes like a struck bell, and the vibrations can crack open the crusts of distant salt flats. Scavenger clans regard it as a neutral oracle, offering it rust and receiving predictions of weather in return.

rites.name: Joranurdock
rites.text: Joranurdock is a grounded concept of a stone-cold cartographer-warrior who fights with ceramic tuning forks that hum at the frequencies of bedrock. In the Thudarneld era of the seventh age, his strikes are said to crack open quarry walls.

rites.name: Joreldunen
rites.text: Joreldunen is a grounded concept from the E6 era, a heavy-set warden of the Thudarneld powers, age seven in its own reckoning. It is known for its patient, deliberate strikes that hold steady through sustained pressure.

rites.name: Fenorarnock
rites.text: Fenorarnock is a cavernous grounded titan of the E6 era, a stone-skinned guardian that has slept beneath the Thudarneld ridgeline for seven ages. When it stirs, the rockfall it triggers can flatten a village in a single heave of its shoulders.

rites.name: Thanar
rites.text: Thanar is a grounded chronicler's concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a wandering archive-warden who records the violent habits of gate-beasts in an age when cities are walled against them. Its feats are measured in the scale of a single town's defences rather than whole continents.

rites.name: Kelolde
rites.text: Kelolde is a grounded combat-engineering concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a sealed armored mechanism built to bore through bedrock for mining crews. Its signature tactic is a pressure-drill strike that fractures stone and armor alike in a single concentrated thrust.

rites.name: Tarnerade
rites.text: Tarnerade is a grounded field-engineering concept from the E6 era, a modular rig of pressure-cast plates that can be bolted into a single heavy frame by a crew of four. It is built for demolition and salvage work where conventional charges would be too unstable to handle.

rites.name: Crorneldock
rites.text: Crorneldock is a grounded mechanical sentinel of the E6 age, a seven-year-old thudding automaton that patrols the orchard-terraces of Thudarneld with a single bronze hammer-arm. It has no true intellect, only a stubborn habit of repeating its last command until something interrupts it.

rites.name: Thostureld
rites.text: Thostureld is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, an E6 power-scale setting where the age of seven has become a byword for a hardened, practical kind of strength. Its people measure might by the weight of a hard day's labour and the sharpness of an honest blade. The name is said to carry the meaning of a stone that has been worn smooth by a long river.

rites.name: Thunalde
rites.text: Thunalde is a grounded, low-altitude storm-sigil technique drawn from the marsh-kin of Thudarneld, channelled through hammer-shaped conduits of iron and amber. It is a concept power used in the sixth era by hunters and ferrymen who need to clear fog-choked waterways without destroying the reed beds they depend on.

rites.name: Thodeston
rites.text: Thodeston is a grounded concept of a seven-year-old Grounded-realm era-six locale in Thudarneld, where a single silent watchman known as the Keeper of Lanterns stands on the ridge above the valley. Its people trust it to keep the crops from wind and the wells from drying out. The Keeper rarely acts, but when it does the ridge itself seems to answer.

rites.name: Fenaren
rites.text: Fenaren is a grounded, quiet-era figure of the E6 age, a seven-year-old of the Thudarneld order who draws power from the small gestures of everyday craft. Their techniques are restrained and precise, meant to mend, steady, or cut rather than to devastate.

rites.name: Brarnoneld
rites.text: Brarnoneld is a grounded concept-level figure of the sixth era of Thudarneld, a being whose existence is measured more in mechanical quirks than cosmic grandeur. It is known for its seven-year-old sensory training and its habit of compressing shared pain into a single, sharp moment. Its presence shapes the powers of its locale without ever overwhelming them.

rites.name: Credeld
rites.text: Credeld is a grounded, centuries-old gravitational architect whose mountain-scale stone monoliths drift in orbits that slowly rearrange the continents of the Thudarneld. It is a concept rather than a creature, and its influence is felt as tides and landslides over seven ages.

rites.name: Kelanuldock
rites.text: Kelanuldock is a steel-ribbed amphibious war-engine of the Grounded realm, built in the sixth era and seven ages old, that patrols the reed-marshes of Thudarneld. Its crews are known to fire its tidal lances in synchronized volleys that can shatter a dam or a fortified causeway in a single breath.

rites.name: Fenadon
rites.text: Fenadon is a hush-engine of the Thudarneld, a concept of quiet pressure that gathers in still water and releases in sudden bursts. In the Grounded realm of the sixth era it is taught only through the signs of the reed-singers, who name it when the marsh goes silent. Its strength lies in patience rather than force.

rites.name: Tarnudock
rites.text: Tarnudock is a rust-skinned sky-glider that drifts over the salt flats of Grounded realm, its wings humming with stored static. It is prized by settlers as a living weather-vane and by scavengers as a source of cheap, clean lightning.

rites.name: Haleldanath
rites.text: Haleldanath is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a deliberately modest sort of being whose power stays within the scale of a single locale. It is remembered for patient, precise work rather than spectacle, its acts measured in the reach of a small village.

rites.name: Thurnenar
rites.text: Thurnenar is a grounded, patient warden-engine of the E6 era, built to keep a dying river valley's ley-lines from tearing themselves apart. Its sole duty is to sing counter-tones through the valley's ferrous bedrock, nudging tectonic stresses aside before they become quakes. It moves with the slow grace of a glacier and has never been seen to hurry.

rites.name: Credaneld
rites.text: Credaneld is a quiet concept of tidal bell-chimes that ring through the Thudarneld shallows during low-moon nights. Its resonance can coax loose stones from riverbanks and set small mills turning without a single gear.

rites.name: Pelastath
rites.text: Pelastath is a grounded concept in the E6 era of Thudarneld, seven years into its own calm. Its inhabitants settle disputes with rhythmic chants and weathered tools rather than anything that splits the earth.

rites.name: Fenaldune
rites.text: Fenaldune is a sentient ferrite-bound lattice that hums through the stone of Thudarneld's deep quarries, drawing on the Grounded realm's slow geothermal pressure. It can crack bedrock in a single resonant pulse and bear sustained tremors for long periods without losing cohesion.

rites.name: Morarestock
rites.text: Morarestock is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, an omniverse that forbids anything beyond the scale of its own realm. It is a mechanical drifter-artifact that stalks the outer rail-lands, raiding caches and dismantling derelict scrap-towers for their stored charge.

rites.name: Brurnadon
rites.text: Brurnadon is a grounded concept of a stout, moss-plated wrestler-beast of the Thudarneld highlands, whose stomping rhythm steadies the ranks of the herds around it. Its roars are said to shake loose boulders from cliffs across three valleys, and young hunters train by standing still while it drums the earth.

rites.name: Haladorar
rites.text: Haladorar is a grounded, weathered tool of the E6 age of Thudarneld, a heavy sledge-hammer bound to a clan of rock-breakers. Its strikes are fierce enough to split boulders and crack old stone walls, yet it is kept mostly for quarrying and digging.

rites.name: Pelusten
rites.text: Pelusten is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of thudding mineral-forged hulks that march through the E6 era's dusty ranges and rattle the stone of its valleys. Its hide is said to take a blow that would shatter a hillside's worth of rock, while its crushing charge can flatten a small hamlet in a single lunge.

rites.name: Pelerdode
rites.text: Pelerdode is a grounded concept from the sixth era, a seven-year-old constructed war-engine whose name is spoken as a warning across the tide-wracked hills. It hurls bursts of pressurized brine and iron shrapnel through wide arcs, and its hull endures blasts that would shatter a fortified barracks.

rites.name: Tarnoruste
rites.text: Tarnoruste is a quiet discipline of resonant stillness practiced across the Thudarneld reaches, where adepts learn to hold a single note of pressure until it settles into the stone beneath them. Its masters are rarely seen, yet their footfalls are said to shift the bedrock of seventh-era valleys. The practice is taught only in silence and carries a strict vow against spectacle.

rites.name: Kelurde
rites.text: Kelurde is a grounded, seven-year-old battle-discipline of the E6 era, practiced by wardens who hold tide-lines against creeping marsh-rot. Its adepts channel mud-borne vibrations through brass-ringed staves to shake loose sinkholes and stun charging beasts.

rites.name: Moradock
rites.text: Moradock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an armored war-engine of the sixth era that has endured seven ages of siege and salvage. Its hull is a patchwork of recovered plates that shrug off most blows, and it moves with a deliberate, lumbering grace.

rites.name: Morerdock
rites.text: Morerdock is a Grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a dense and armored sentinel that hums with stored tension. Its existence in the era of its kind is measured in ages of quiet patrol over ash-colored plains. It becomes a true threat only when its reinforced plating is pierced and its core is exposed.

rites.name: Jorurnolde
rites.text: Jorurnolde is a shared pattern of ritual signal-weaving practiced by the lantern-tenders of Thudarneld's sixth age, who hum resonant chords through brass coils to call the tide-bells. Its tones carry just enough force to shiver dry reeds, crack a clay jar, and stir a dormant hearth into sudden flame.

rites.name: Halarnure
rites.text: Halarnure is a grounded concept of a Thudarneld bell-forged channeling mantle, carried by an era-E6 smith-priests' order who tune it to hum with the drifting fields of their valley. Its wearer can call stored tension into a single sweeping strike, and over seven years the mantle has grown heavier with every ring of accumulated sound.

rites.name: Jorarden
rites.text: Jorarden is a grounded, pale-stone idol of the E6 age whose cracked throat hums with the weight of swallowed rivers. Seven centuries of pilgrims have chipped at it, and the pilgrims' oaths now sustain it. It is said to crumble only when no one remembers its name.

rites.name: Thunon
rites.text: Thunon is a quiet discipline of the Thudarneld powers, practiced by wandering hermit-smiths who fold storm-charge into their breath and their tools. Its adepts are rarely seen mid-act, since the technique hides itself behind ordinary motion until the final moment.

rites.name: Thanustar
rites.text: Thanustar is a grounded concept of an ember-forged wardstone, cut from a single dim ore that hums when struck by wind. Its bearers use it to shelter villages from storms and to power small forges along the river roads of Thudarneld.

rites.name: Morernath
rites.text: Morernath is a quiet resonance woven through the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth era, felt as a low hum in stone and sinew. It is bound to no single body but lingers in the marrow of those who listen too long to the deep roots beneath the mountains.

rites.name: Thurnath
rites.text: Thurnath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a hardened war-engine forged in the seventh age of the Thudarneld era. It is known for crushing ferrous fortifications with a single heavy-hammer strike and for its relentless, slow-burning endurance on the battlefield.

rites.name: Tholdere
rites.text: Tholdere is a quiet ritual-tide that surges through the marsh-reeds of the Thudarneld basin every seventh year, carrying whispered tunes that bind the reeds into temporary walls. Its practitioners learn to read the tide's rhythm and channel its small, steady force into tools and charms rather than open battle.

rites.name: Dreden
rites.text: Dreden is a tireless ironworker-engineer of the Grounded realm, a lone artisan who builds clockwork siege engines for the petty kingdoms of the Thudarneld frontier. His machines are famously loud and cheerfully overengineered, though he is careful never to let them leave the workshop yard.

rites.name: Halenon
rites.text: Halenon is a wandering reef-bound sentinel of the Thudarneld deep sea, a slow colossus of coral and sediment that guards the trench-floor cities. Its calcified hide can absorb blows that would shatter a fortress, and its song rattles the pressure seals of distant habitats.

rites.name: Halanostar
rites.text: Halanostar is a dim, slow-cooling relic of an ancient calendar-keeping order, its concept woven into the dawn rituals of Thudarneld's grounded highlands. It is said to pulse once each season, lending a brief, steadying warmth to whoever holds its ember-glass.

rites.name: Fenestaldon
rites.text: Fenestaldon is a seven-year-old concept-era device-beast of the Grounded realm, built as a living siege-engine that grows a new shell each season. Its nervous system is wired through a dense web of brass filaments, letting it coordinate dozens of limbs at once. It is slow to start but fearsome once its shell rings.

rites.name: Thare
rites.text: Thare is a quiet grounded concept in Thudarneld, a discipline of stillness that teaches practitioners to shape ordinary breath into brief bursts of force. Its masters are known for unseen maneuvers that leave their opponents wondering what struck them. The art favors subtlety over spectacle, and its strongest techniques rarely outlast a single moment.

rites.name: Morurdock
rites.text: Morurdock is a cartographer's term for the hidden dimming of a valley's light when the seasonal fogs roll in, a phenomenon the people of Thudarneld treat as a quiet sign of the land's breathing. Within Grounded, it is recorded in the ninth-era survey tables as a mild but persistent environmental concept rather than a force of destruction.

rites.name: Peleste
rites.text: Peleste is a crystalline mechanical lattice-engine built into the bedrock of the Grounded realm, its seven-age cycle of resonance humming through the ore veins of the Thudarneld. Its most notable act is a controlled harmonic collapse that shatters nearby quarry walls, releasing stored tension as a sharp, ringing shockwave.

rites.name: Fenernath
rites.text: Fenernath is a grounded concept of an ancient iron-shelled war-engine that sleeps beneath the tundra of the Thudarneld plains. Its bellows-throat can vent a burst of compressed steam strong enough to flatten a fortified garrison.

rites.name: Morerduneld
rites.text: Morerduneld is a grounded, self-sustaining concept that appears only in the sixth era of the Thudarneld, where it serves as a quiet keystone for local power grids. Its presence is felt through harmonic hums that linger in the air long after it has moved on. It is never seen directly, and its influence is recognized mainly by the silence it leaves behind.

rites.name: Morenuste
rites.text: Morenuste is a grounded concept, a seven-year-old practitioner of the Thudarneld Era E6 powers, who dissolves stone and steel through sheer adherence to the ground beneath. Its signature act is a clean, quiet slam that hollows out a district's foundations without ever causing a visible explosion.

rites.name: Thostock
rites.text: Thostock is a salt-cured ferry-engine that hauls cargo barges across the Vellen Shallows of Thudarneld, its rusted boiler humming a low note that fishermen use to find their way home in fog. Crews say the engine was forged from the hull-bolts of a fleet that sank in a single storm, and it still sings when bad weather approaches.

rites.name: Kelastordon
rites.text: Kelastordon is a grounded sentinel of the E6 era in Thudarneld, a massive bronze-plated war-beast whose hide stores kinetic charge from every footfall. Its signature act is a bellowing stampede that can crack a forested valley open along its path.

rites.name: Thenorar
rites.text: Thenorar is a seventh-age concept of a grounded, bronze-hulled warden that stands guard over the drowned terraces of Thudarneld. Its signature is a slow, heavy stance that can hold a flood at bay or, when pressed, release a shockwave that shakes stone from the valley walls.

rites.name: Morurden
rites.text: Morurden is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a realm of reagents and engineered powders. Its earliest workshop-built tools were designed to carry its strength, though the shaped mechanisms later became more famous than their makers. Seven ages on, the name still refers to a bench of practical, tightly calibrated forces.

rites.name: Kelerden
rites.text: Kelerden is a grounded concept from the seventh age of the Thudarneld omniverse, a rail-bound gravity sled that hums along the ridgelines of the Oskra Plateau. Its operators use it to haul ore and, in emergencies, to ram stalled convoys off the tracks. It is more famous for its rhythm than for its power.

rites.name: Drerasteld
rites.text: Drerasteld is a grounded, seven-year-old reckoning engine of the Thudarneld realm, a stone-faced spirit whose hum keeps the dust-roads of its era from drifting apart. Its power is measured in the weight of a single crushing shrug, not in cosmic flares, making it a local legend rather than a force of nations.

rites.name: Pelurnere
rites.text: Pelurnere is a cursed grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hollow iron lattice that hums with stolen warmth from nearby hearths. It gathers the heat of an entire valley into a single arc of white flame when the bells of its tower are rung.

rites.name: Kelardar
rites.text: Kelardar is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a shrine-warden made of hardened sap and bell-metal that patrols the dry terraces of the Vessen Tiers. Its presence is said to quiet the wind for a league in every direction, and locals leave it offerings of salt bread to keep its rounds gentle.

rites.name: Pelarurdeld
rites.text: Pelarurdeld is a grounded concept entry from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a mechanical sentinel that stands guard over ancient machinery. Its strikes are measured in the forces of falling trees and toppled walls, and it can withstand the impact of a runaway wagon without losing its stance.

rites.name: Tarnoldudar
rites.text: Tarnoldudar is a grounded concept of heavy, mechanical combatants whose strikes can level blocks of stone and steel. Its strongest acts remain within a single city's reach, reflecting an era of hard labor and cautious engineering.

rites.name: Kelarden
rites.text: Kelarden is a grounded, hand-sized mechanical sentinel built by the Thessaline Foundry in Era E6, designed to hold back collapsing tunnels and drifting ash-banks. Its heavy frame can absorb and redirect enormous pressure, letting it brace a cavern roof for minutes at a time. It moves with deliberate, rolling steps that rarely exceed a brisk jog.

rites.name: Crorneld
rites.text: Crorneld is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a seven-year-old world where enemies were engineered to be wrestled into submission rather than overwhelmed. Its founders favored mechanical brawlers, and the ledger of its lore is built from cracked stone and bent rebar. Crorneld is remembered as a foreman-spirit who taught its crews how to hold a line.

rites.name: Crurdon
rites.text: Crurdon is a sedimentary conceptual rite practiced by the Thudarneld mound-keepers, who grind slate into fine powder to mark the turning of each age. Its practitioners teach that a single correctly timed stamp of the ritual staff can jolt a sleeping quarry shelf awake.

rites.name: Fenaronath
rites.text: Fenaronath is a grounded concept of a seven-year-old marrow-garden of the E6 era, where pollen-bearing spires drift on tidal wind. Its inhabitants harvest the spires' stored sap to power brittle lantern-machines that hum through the long dusk.

rites.name: Joradonock
rites.text: Joradonock is a grounded concept from Thudarneld's Era 6, a seven-year-old machine-spirit that hums inside the cracked foundations of Velthorne Commons. It is best known for a slow, patient gait that can stagger a district's worth of load-bearing walls, though it rarely needs to press harder than a pedestrian shrug.

rites.name: Craren
rites.text: Craren is a gleaming sky-cathedral of sunken bell towers that drift over the Vashen Reaches, its toll ringing across three provinces. Its ringers wield the gravity of their chimes to fold stone into quiet dust.

rites.name: Kelestock
rites.text: Kelestock is a rust-colored ironwood rootbound grove that grows over the ruins of a shattered observatory in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld. Its seed-pods spring open with a wet crack, flinging spiked husks that can punch through a farmhouse wall.

rites.name: Kelostede
rites.text: Kelostede is a sentient storm-forged bell-tower that rings once every seven years, its tolling shaking the sediment-rich bedrock of the Thudarneld highlands. Local herders call it the Quiet Giant because it only moves when its bronze clapper is stolen, and then it hunts the thief across the plains.

rites.name: Cronen
rites.text: Cronen is a fused gear-and-cinder mantle worn by the drifting salvagers of Thudarneld's Grounded belt. Each wearer channels ambient heat into a single discharge that can split a sealed iron gate.

rites.name: Thaden
