rites.text: Thaden is a rust-red mechanical sentinel that patrols the cracked salt plains of its homeworld, standing guard over abandoned foundry-towers. It can hurl a ring of molten iron shards that tear through armored hulls and bring down a fortified gate in a single throw.

rites.name: Pelordere
rites.text: Pelordere is a tidal-glass Grounded concept from the seventh age of Thudarneld, a rope-bound drifter whose fingers hum with stored ocean-song. Its signature act is to fling a shell of compressed brine that bursts into a choking mist over wide shorelines.

rites.name: Kelunerdath
rites.text: Kelunerdath is a quiet sensory discipline practiced by the Thudarneld hill-wardens, who learn to project a single hushed pulse of focused will to unsettle foes without being seen. Its practitioners rarely name the technique aloud, letting its effects speak for it. The pulse can topple a stout gate or rattle a careless sentry's wits.

rites.name: Drurnon
rites.text: Drurnon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stubborn ember-hearted wanderer who dives from high crags and lands with enough force to split stone and rattle distant villages. Its people speak of its descents as weather, and it rarely strikes twice in the same valley out of respect for the land it has already cracked.

rites.name: Halornon
rites.text: Halornon is a clockwork bolt-guardian of the Thudarneld stacks, built by ferrite monks to hold open the locks between grounded valleys. It stores strikes in its brass ribs and releases them in a single synchronized clang when its warden calls the hour.

rites.name: Morarneld
rites.text: Morarneld is a hush-cloaked concept of stored patience, a quiet discipline that teaches a spirit to wait before answering any call. Among the Thudarneld sages it is taught as a counterweight to impulse, measured in the slow turning of seasons rather than in strikes.

rites.name: Thestodar
rites.text: Thestodar is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hidden mechanism of tuned resonance that the people of the E6 era learned to hum into bridges and mills. It is rarely named aloud, and its effects are felt more than seen, shaping the rhythms of daily labor across seven generations.

rites.name: Crorath
rites.text: Crorath is a grounded ceremonial engine-spirit of the Thudarneld reaches, bound in the seventh age to hum resonant chords that steady the drowned rail-cities of its valley. Its voice can shatter hollow iron at a distance, and its own shell is hard enough to outlast a wave of falling slag.

rites.name: Kelarde
rites.text: Kelarde is a grounded, seventh-age cluster of mechanized bulwarks that hum beneath the salt flats of its homeworld, built to hold back storms that no longer come. Its engineers measure their pride in how little fuel their hulls waste and how gently they set down heavy loads.

rites.name: Morustalde
rites.text: Morustalde is a quiet tide-binding discipline practiced by the lamp-keepers of Thudarneld's shallow seas, who coax drifting currents into patient, low-hanging mists. Its practitioners are known for steady endurance rather than spectacle, and their greatest workings can lift a fishing barge clear of a reef.

rites.name: Braden
rites.text: Braden is a Grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, an idle tinkerer who quietly maintains the wiring of a dormant sky-lift. Its lattice of cable-braces can absorb a runaway load and then release it as a shearing burst that can flatten a hillside.

rites.name: Thonede
rites.text: Thonede is a grounded, drill-bored mining automaton from the Seventh Age of Thudarneld, built to tunnel through bedrock for the Varnok Consortium. Its spiraled crown can punch past any armor plate, delivering a shock that shatters the target from within.

rites.name: Brerdon
rites.text: Brerdon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a sprawling fortress-city of thousands of cranes and scaffolds known as the Hollow Stacks. Its residents rely on crude mechanical contraptions and hand-forged tools rather than any true magic. The stacks are famous for their rattling bells and the enormous counterweights that keep their towers from toppling.

rites.name: Brusteld
rites.text: Brusteld is a grounded, stoic cryo-warden of the E6 era, a figure whose frost-bound discipline holds the high passes of its homeland. In the sixth age's quiet valleys it is said to freeze the wind mid-breath when it kneels to pray.

rites.name: Tarneren
rites.text: Tarneren is a seven-year-old concept-grade entity in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a sprawling field of hexed scrubland where it drifts between the grasses. Its presence is felt more as a pressure on the air than as a visible body, and it is known to hum in pitches that make nearby dust rearrange itself into spirals.

rites.name: Drunordock
rites.text: Drunordock is a grounded, armored war-fortress of the E6 age, a moving bulwark of riveted iron and salvaged turbines that crawls across the scorched plains of Thudarneld. Its crew of laborers and gunners treats it as a home as much as a weapon, and its engines churn a steady, bass-heavy hum that can be heard for leagues.

rites.name: Morade
rites.text: Morade is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-bound guardian that drinks the tremors of the earth to harden its shell against any blow. It stands as the seventh age's last sentinel of the basalt plains, shielding whatever travelers lie behind it.

rites.name: Tarnanock
rites.text: Tarnanock is a sentient mountain-shaped bulwark that drifts through the Thudarneld reefs, layering sheets of cooled ash into walls that shrug off blows aimed at its wardens. Its stone-cage shell is said to hold back ruin until its keepers stop listening to the rocks.

rites.name: Tarneston
rites.text: Tarneston is a grounded concept from the E6 era, a pale stone archive-town whose walls hum with recorded lullabies. Its wardens, called Loomkeepers, bind the stone into shelter by stretching sheets of quarried lamplight over the streets, and the cost of each sheet is paid in sleep.

rites.name: Fenudock
rites.text: Fenudock is a grounded concept in the E6 era, a tireless industrial mechanism of riveted iron and dense shale-stone that serves as a pressure-driven ballast for the mountain-cities of its valley. Its wide plates hum at low frequency and it can hold an enormous load steady for hours without strain.

rites.name: Kelaldath
rites.text: Kelaldath is a sealed resonance-lattice that hums beneath the glassy plains of Thudarneld, storing the tension of ancient quakes in its spiraled crystal veins. When provoked, it releases pulses that can topple a rail depot and scatter the herders who graze nearby.

rites.name: Fenonasteld
rites.text: Fenonasteld is a grounded concept of a tireless lattice-sprite that hums across the iron plains of Thudarneld, mending rust and cracks in old machines. In its seventh age it gathers scattered sparks into bright, disciplined arcs to guard the wandering villages it has adopted.

rites.name: Keloreld
rites.text: Keloreld is a sleek, wind-hewn ironwood bow carried by the wayfarers of Thudarneld's lowland marshes, said to hum before every shot. Its arrows are fletched with the feathers of storm-cranes, and a well-drawn string can loose a gust strong enough to flatten reed-beds for a furlong.

rites.name: Dranock
rites.text: Dranock is a drowned colossus of living brass that slumbers beneath the tidal flats of the Vesh Estuary, its ribs hung with rusted bells that toll when the tide turns. Ancient ferrymen believed its song could steer the moon, and they paid it in salt and silver to keep the sea calm.

rites.name: Tarnuldock
rites.text: Tarnuldock is a grounded, wire-and-spark ironclad sentinel of the Thudarneld reaches, built to hold narrow ravines against raiding columns. It is slow to wind up but its clamp-hammer can shatter a row of armored carts in a single swing.

rites.name: Crerdath
rites.text: Crerdath is a grounded, lore-heavy scrap-hound of the E6 era, a rust-plated tinkerer-beast that roams the Thudarneld ridgelands salvaging broken engines. Its name is spoken by herders as a warning and a blessing, since its growl is said to shake loose old bolts from abandoned rail-towers.

rites.name: Crare
rites.text: Crare is a grounded Thudarneld concept from Era E6, a quiet siphon-engine that drinks the reserve energy of a distant living thing and stores it in its own lattice. Its makers treat it as a tool for cooling overloaded reactors, though it has been used to starve field generators in border skirmishes.

rites.name: Pelonar
rites.text: Pelonar is a Grounded-realm concept in Thudarneld, a fragile lattice of cooperative hunting-tribes whose strongest members rarely exceed the force of a falling stone. Its name is borne by a rite in which a single mallet strike is struck against a standing post to call the herds home.

rites.name: Pelarden
rites.text: Pelarden is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the E6 era, a tireless rolling engine of stone and copper that patrols the mineral belts of Thudarneld. Its signature act is a sustained seismic drive that cracks ridgelines when it rolls through a narrow pass.

rites.name: Thenath
rites.text: Thenath is a quiet discipline in the Thudarneld powers tradition, in which practitioners cultivate an unseen resonance that channels ordinary momentum into focused bursts. Its adherents are known for striking hard and vanishing before the blow is recognized as theirs.

rites.name: Creste
rites.text: Creste is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a conical stone bulwark built to hold back the fast tidal surges of the Ember Strait. Its wardens are trained to brace its walls and trigger sluice-gates that redirect rushing water in a single controlled release.

rites.name: Tarnenath
rites.text: Tarnenath is a grounded concept, an unshackled storm of brass-and-cinder artillery that drifts over the salt flats of Thudarneld and fires its payload from wind-carved turrets. Its shells are said to crack the crust of every nearby settlement, and its crew speaks of it as a patient, indifferent tide. In its prime years it is hunted by cartel engineers who want its engines for their own rail trains.

rites.name: Breden
rites.text: Breden is a set of fighting techniques practiced by wandering arena-duelists of the Thudarneld frontier, each named for a ritual gesture rather than the blow itself. Its masters strike with borrowed momentum, so a single disciplined swing can topple a loaded cart or split a timber gate.

rites.name: Moredath
rites.text: Moredath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an iron-hearted warden of the salt flats who tills a single furrow across the plain each dawn. Its strength is patient and local, measured in the sheer weight of stone it can shift in a single season rather than in cataclysm.

rites.name: Therdornen
rites.text: Therdornen is a rust-colored grounded behemoth that sleeps beneath the cratered plains of its era, its shell bristling with iron barbs. It rarely fights, but when provoked it hurls its quills in a shower that can pierce a stone wall.

rites.name: Joruldanen
rites.text: Joruldanen is a grounded concept entity of the E6 era, a lattice of sealed wind-vessels that hums through seven centuries of quiet drift. It is most famous for exhaling a single gust that can topple a granary door or snap a rope bridge.

rites.name: Halurneldar
rites.text: Halurneldar is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld world, an inscribed sigil-ward that the old wardens of the sixth age used to steady failing rivers and tremor-prone hills. Its power is quiet and slow, a stored tension released only when the land itself begins to shift, so it is rarely seen and seldom named aloud by those who depend on it.

rites.name: Druraneld
rites.text: Druraneld is a sturdy stone-and-root sentinel that guards the terraced valleys of its homeworld, standing motionless for weeks until a flood or landslide threatens the people below. When it moves, it heaves its shoulders against the earth to hold back the ground itself.

rites.name: Pelerornon
rites.text: Pelerornon is a grounded concept entry from the Thudarneld omniverse, a ceremonial bell-tower built by a seven-year-old civilization of riverside builders. Its tolling is said to hold the wind in place long enough for distant fields to ripen.

rites.name: Thordath
rites.text: Thordath is a grounded, mountain-dwelling forge-warden of the E6 era, a tireless artisan who shapes iron tools for the valley folk. Its strikes can shatter bedrock, yet it prefers the quiet ring of its anvil to any battle.

rites.name: Halonock
rites.text: Halonock is a dormant lattice of resonant crystal threads that hums beneath the Thudarneld plains, storing the slow pressure of tides. Villages in the Grounded realm tune their wells to it to draw small, steady warmth through the long winters.

rites.name: Morureld
rites.text: Morureld is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a discipline of carefully timed hand signs practiced in the age of the sixth cycle. Its practitioners do not wield the force of storms but instead learn to redirect the small, ordinary energies of falling stones and moving water.

rites.name: Thornaston
rites.text: Thornaston is a grounded concept of thorned stone spires that rise from the plains of Thudarneld, each one shedding dust that hardens into crude armor for those who wander too close. Its wardens are taught a single discipline: to strike the spire's resonant spine so that the ground itself answers with a quake. The spires have stood for seven ages without a single one falling.

rites.name: Morardeld
rites.text: Morardeld is a grounded concept of seven ages in the Thudarneld universe, a world where the powers of its people are measured in small bursts of force. Its wardens channel kinetic and crystalline energy into needles, gusts, and mechanical strikes that rarely exceed the scale of a single structure. The era E6 population treats each act as a matter of craft rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Brordath
rites.text: Brordath is a drifting aquatic bulwark, a grounded titan of riveted brine-iron that patrols the trenches of Thudarneld. Its shell absorbs collisions that would split a lesser vessel, and it moves with a sluggish but unstoppable momentum.

rites.name: Pelarnar
rites.text: Pelarnar is a dormant tidal lattice of crystal filaments that hums beneath the seabed of Thudarneld, stored like a patient reservoir of pressure. Its keepers sing it awake only during the long dry seasons to coax deep currents into irrigating the inland terraces.

rites.name: Haladulden
rites.text: Haladulden is a mountain-sized grounded titan of the E6 era, a bark-skinned colossus whose slow footfalls ripple through the earth like distant thunder. It guards the high passes of the Thudarneld region and sleeps for decades between bouts of violent wakefulness.

rites.name: Thonudath
rites.text: Thonudath is a grounded concept of a seven-age-old drill-tower colony whose sentinel stations hum with stored pressure. Its engineers once rang out a single bell-note that splintered an entire ridge of basalt into sand-fine shards.

rites.name: Moranulde
rites.text: Moranulde is a sealed resonance-lattice that the Thudarneld settlers grew in cold quarries to hum over their fields and keep the frost-worms away. Its elders trade its tuned harmonics for ore, and a single unguarded note can crack a brick wall or split a cart's axle.

rites.name: Therdaldar
rites.text: Therdaldar is a grounded, tireless sentinel of the Thudarneld calendar's sixth epoch, a stone-and-cable warden that keeps the high pass of Oskenvar lit through seven ages of drifting frost. It is known for its patient, almost ceremonial strikes, bringing down avalanches and bridges only when the valley's old covenants demand it.

rites.name: Brenar
rites.text: Brenar is a sentient mechanical ward-lantern built by the Tallow Choir to keep the tide-hung cities of Thudarneld from drowning. Its coiled brass heart can hold a storm's worth of pressure for a moment before venting it in one blinding pulse.

rites.name: Crune
rites.text: Crune is a grounded concept of mechanical resonance in the Thudarneld, a discipline where practitioners tune stone and metal to shudder in sympathy with distant tremors. Its adepts are seven-year-old apprentices of the E6 era who learn to hum their bones into harmony with the earth. Their most dangerous technique can crack a village wall when pushed too far.

rites.name: Joralden
rites.text: Joralden is a grounded, mid-scale concept of a protective bulwark-spirit that binds the fractured ley-lines of a quiet valley realm. Its presence is felt more as pressure on the air than as spectacle, and its reach is measured in villages and hillsides rather than continents.

rites.name: Peladostath
rites.text: Peladostath is a three-year-old concept, a grounded tremor-engine drawn from the ore-veins beneath Thudarneld's northern marsh. Its crews set the great drums around it and let it ring until the riverbanks buckle, though the ringing has never quite stopped since its first season.

rites.name: Halordedath
rites.text: Halordedath is a vast, roaming tectonic colossus that moves through the grounded strata of Thudarneld, its footfalls cracking the crust for leagues. Its hide is a mineral lattice that hardens after each impact, making it steadily harder to wound over an extended siege.

rites.name: Kelarne
rites.text: Kelarne is a quiet discipline of breath and resonance practiced by the hermit-scholars of Thudarneld's grounded realm, used to calm storms and steady failing bridges. Its adepts train for seven years before they are permitted to shape a single gust. The art is deliberately modest, prized for restraint rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Dreldath
rites.text: Dreldath is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a wandering colossus of salvaged iron and tidal-stone that walks the drowned plains of its homeworld. Its limbs ring like bells when struck, and it is said to carry the memories of every ship it has ever swallowed.

rites.name: Crore
rites.text: Crore is a dormant lattice of mineral tuning forks buried beneath the fault lines of Thudarneld, quietly ringing for seven centuries. When its resonance is provoked, the stone chime can shake loose entire quarry faces and bring down the hillside cathedrals built above it.

rites.name: Kelanock
rites.text: Kelanock is a grounded, sturdy war-engine of the E6 age, a six-legged hauler that carries stone and steel across the broken plains of Thudarneld. Its crews know it as a patient machine that endures far more punishment than it ever deals out. It is most feared when its hull is strained and it lashes out in a single burst.

rites.name: Pelorock
rites.text: Pelorock is a slow-moving stone-hided beast of the Thudarneld fens, where it grazes on moss-dusted boulders for most of its four-year life. When threatened, it drives its heavy shoulder ridges into the mud, sending tremors rolling across nearby rockfields.

rites.name: Pelenardock
rites.text: Pelenardock is a grounded concept of a lattice of hollow stone ridges that hum with stored pressure, tapped by wardens who time their strikes to the ridges' pulses. Its wardens are valued for disciplined, low-noise craft rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Halerdath
rites.text: Halerdath is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet sorcerer-engineer who bends ordinary soil and iron into temporary defenses. Its power is modest but relentless, letting it outlast and outmaneuver far stronger opponents in the long campaigns of the E6 era.

rites.name: Fenardath
rites.text: Fenardath is a grounded concept rather than a creature of the ancient world, a seven-year-old experimental network of hovering relay-hounds that keeps the cities of its era talking to one another. Its signal pulses can knock out an entire district's lights and wiring for a few breathless minutes. Its builders still argue over whether the network has begun to remember its own routes.

rites.name: Crerden
rites.text: Crerden is a grounded, low-scale concept of an era-six creature cult whose members train to endure the weight of their own settlements. Its enforcers can hurl a barrage of spiked wind-stones and withstand heavy blows that would flatten most bodies. Their war-rhythms are said to echo through the valleys for days.

rites.name: Fenustodeld
rites.text: Fenustodeld is a rust-colored iron colossus that roams the grassy plateaus of Thudarneld, grinding up boulders to feed its vast, hollow chest. It is a living foundry: when threatened it hurls molten slag across the valley, scorching anything caught in the glowing arc.

rites.name: Credardock
rites.text: Credardock is a ratcheting iron cathedral-engine that hums in the basements of Thudarneld's grounded foundries, where mechanics chant its tolling pulses into the pipework. Its keepers sell pressed brass tokens bearing its gear-lattice sigil, and each token shields a holder for a single hour of forge-work.

rites.name: Thaldon
rites.text: Thaldon is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a sturdy wardstone-blacksmith whose iron-bound gauntlets hum with a low, patient resonance. Thaldon can hold a collapsing cistern wall upright for hours without tiring.

rites.name: Halenarden
rites.text: Halenarden is a grounded concept of nested gear-hymns that the Thudarneld reckoners use to time their seasonal tide-locks. Its cycles are measured in the sixth age's bell-count, and its tuned resonance can shake loose rockfalls and cracked dams.

rites.name: Croldock
rites.text: Croldock is a quiet doctrine of stillness practiced by the wardens of Thudarneld's lowland marshes, who believe a true stroke is one that leaves no sound. Its adepts can channel the weight of their own patience into a single motionless blow that cracks the ground beneath a reed boat without disturbing the water.

rites.name: Brane
rites.text: Brane is a conceptual membrane-entity that exists as a thin, shimmering skin stretched between the surfaces of reality, rarely noticed by the locals of the Thudarneld reaches. Its presence bends the grain of ordinary matter, letting it slip sideways across the edges of stone and steel.

rites.name: Pelaldore
rites.text: Pelaldore is a grounded-realm concept from the E6 era, a seventh-age engine of dampened gravity whose cores are tuned to bend the weight of a settlement's own stone. It is less a weapon than a patient machine that waits for a foundation to fail.

rites.name: Crusteneld
rites.text: Crusteneld is a dormant-yet-aggressive concept of a seabed-born terrain organism in the Grounded realm, shaped by seven ages of slow tectonic memory. Its interior is said to hold brittle hard shells that it cracks open to release stored pressure in bursts.

rites.name: Peloldath
rites.text: Peloldath is a grounded concept fighter from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a seven-year-old power whose wielders are known for their hard, ringing sparring stances. Its signature is an unbroken drumbeat of short strikes that wears down rivals rather than overwhelming them in a single blow.

rites.name: Droren
rites.text: Droren is a grounded, mundane sentinel-machine of the E6 era in Thudarneld, a fortified tower-guardian that patrols corridors and lobbing small charges at intruders. It fights with simple reflexes and reserves its most dangerous charge for when it is badly damaged.

rites.name: Pelerath
rites.text: Pelerath is a drifting fungal colony that threads through the roots of Thudarneld's old-growth forests, storing and passing along small pulses of ambient heat. Its spores can spark mild combustion in dry brush, and its underground mesh can ripple to shake loose loose soil.

rites.name: Feneden
rites.text: Feneden is a grounded concept, the lattice of quiet stone-hearted sentinels that stand watch over the tilled valleys of Thudarneld. Each sentinel hums a low note that steadies crops and soothes livestock, and they are said to remember every harvest for seven centuries.

rites.name: Thoduste
rites.text: Thoduste is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a wiry tinker-engineer whose hand-built gadgets are famous across the Lower Marrow. Its signature lantern-hammer can crack a stone wall at close range, and its chief rival, the Vessel of Brass, is said to be its opposite in every way.

rites.name: Drorne
rites.text: Drorne is a crystalline concept of silent resonance that hums through the bedrock of Thudarneld in the sixth era, sustaining the sleeping tides of the lower valleys. Its pulses are rarely seen but can shake the stone walls of old watchtowers for miles around.

rites.name: Pelernurden
rites.text: Pelernurden is a ferrous-shelled spine-mill of the Grounded realm, a slow crawling engine that churns the crust of Thudarneld into fine grit for the cities of its era. Its drive is a cluster of counter-rotating flywheels that can briefly unload their stored spin into a single heaving lurch. It is built to endure years of grinding abrasion rather than any sudden violence.

rites.name: Fenodath
rites.text: Fenodath is a grounded, seven-year-old concept tied to the Thudarneld setting, a sprawling artificial reef of salvaged foundries and tidal turbines in the E6 era. It is remembered mainly as a stubborn machine-guardian that holds its ground against floods and storms rather than striking at distant targets.

rites.name: Morerneld
rites.text: Morerneld is a weathered fog-warden of the Grounded realm, a quiet figure who tends the boundary between the mists and the dry lowlands of Thudarneld. Its signature is a slow, humming stillness that unsettles anything which approaches with ill intent.

rites.name: Pelorernon
rites.text: Pelorernon is a drifting tide-engine that hums through the Thudarneld shallows, gathering pressure from sunken reefs and returning it as sudden shockwaves. Its ancient song is said to calm the silt-storms of the seventh age.

rites.name: Dronarne
rites.text: Dronarne is a practice-and-tactics doctrine, not a person, taught in the Thudarneld garrisons of the Grounded realm during its seventh age. Its instructors teach soldiers to time small, precise strikes against a foe's stance so that the cumulative force reads as one blow. The doctrine is valued for its discipline rather than raw power.

rites.name: Dronadock
rites.text: Dronadock is a hovering sentinel of the Grounded realm, a bulky machine that anchors itself to stone and hums through the age of E6. It is built to hold a ridge against armies, and its defensive pulses can scatter ash and bind enemies in place.

rites.name: Halostene
rites.text: Halostene is a grounded concept of silent, crystalline lattice-dwellers that drift across the salt flats of Thudarneld. Their only known act is a slow resonant pulse that rings through the ground and can topple a shelter built on fragile foundations.

rites.name: Drarnock
rites.text: Drarnock is a stubborn ferryman's rope-knot technique passed down through the flood-towns of Thudarneld, a quiet art of binding and loosening currents. Its practitioners are said to hold back river surges that once threatened whole districts during the Fourth Age.

rites.name: Haluren
rites.text: Haluren is a grounded concept from the seventh age of Thudarneld, a moss-coated fortress-garden tended by wandering reed-herders. Its inhabitants settle disputes by trading small carved pebbles that carry a hum of intent, a practice that has grown into a quiet, precise craft.

rites.name: Peleroldon
rites.text: Peleroldon is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a seven-year-old stone-and-bone order of hunters who guard the valleys from wild, burrowing beasts. Its members rely on practical skills, including barbed traps, fire-hardened spears, and clay-bound shields, rather than any inherent magic. Their greatest feats are feats of endurance and sudden, localized force.

rites.name: Kelasterden
rites.text: Kelasterden is a grounded concept from the E6 era, seven years into its age, whose powers draw on the raw strength of ordinary physical matter. It is a single fighter who has learned to channel the force of a tossed stone or a falling beam into devastating blows. Its strength is measured against the Thudarneld's gritty, low-magic order.

rites.name: Kelodock
rites.text: Kelodock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a dense rural power of the E6 era, seven ages old, whose practitioners draw force from stone and root. Its strongest practitioners can split a village's worth of earth in a single act, though they tire quickly and rely on rooted stillness to recover.

rites.name: Kelurneld
rites.text: Kelurneld is a grounded concept of a hardened bio-mechanical hunting engine, built in the seventh age of the Thudarneld orbits to pry open sealed valley fortresses. Its tusked forelimbs drive a crushing ram-charge that can pulverize stone walls and leave stunned defenders in reeling silence. Its primary weapon is a kinetic bellow that can collapse a small watchtower.

rites.name: Halarneld
rites.text: Halarneld is a grounded, weathered arsenal-spirit bound into a dented iron lantern that drifts through the Thudarneld salt-flats of the E6 era. It can flare a stinging gust of brine-scented wind, and it guards its wielder with a shell of tightly packed sand.

rites.name: Halordeld
rites.text: Halordeld is a Grounded concept living in the Thudarneld universe, an ancient spiral of silt-choked lowlands that its cultures call the sleeping ledger. It is described as a hush that slows iron and sours bread, shaping the local priesthood's distrust of loud machines.

rites.name: Halordade
rites.text: Halordade is a grounded concept entry from the Thudarneld omniverse, an armored war-drone whose cannon-shot tears through reinforced walls. Its engineers designed it to outlast the blast of its own weapons across a seven-year campaign.

rites.name: Crosturdeld
rites.text: Crosturdeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a steel-and-mud settlement whose residents channel the tremors of the earth into rhythmic wardens. Its era of the sixth age sees its towers slowly sinking into the soft plains they once stood upon.

rites.name: Drarde
rites.text: Drarde is a bronze-scaled sky-hunter of the Grounded realm, known across Thudarneld for its war-cry that shakes loose stones from cliffs. Old herders say it sleeps curled around a hot spring and wakes only when its calves are threatened. Its strength is measured less in what it breaks than in how long it can endure a storm of hail and sunfire.

rites.name: Brudare
rites.text: Brudare is a grounded thunder-plated sentinel of the Thudarneld highlands, a rust-colored wall of braided copper cable that hums when storms approach. Its wardens claim it sleeps in the cliffs and wakes only to rewire the sky. Few have seen it move without the lightning that follows.

rites.name: Brudar
rites.text: Brudar is a grounded concept of Thudarneld's sixth era, a sealed reservoir of hydraulic bone-stone where every trained hand is said to carry its weight. Its disciplines teach patience, leverage, and the quiet work of keeping a stone wall from remembering it was once a river.

rites.name: Drustardon
rites.text: Drustardon is a bronze-plated grounding beast of the Thudarneld stormfields, a creature that roams the marshes and attracts lightning into its hide. Its heavy tail strikes can crack the earth and send shockwaves through nearby terrain.

rites.name: Pelaldornen
rites.text: Pelaldornen is a grounded concept of seven ages, a quiet world where sand-wind laboratories hum beneath cracked salt flats. Its attuned engineers coax harmless pressure-waves from brass rods, and the realm's only true calamity is a slow-moving lattice of rust that eats metal.

rites.name: Fenorne
rites.text: Fenorne is a grounded-realm concept of a ceramic-shelled crawler that burrows beneath the dunes of Thudarneld, where it sheds pressurized resin that hardens into lattice pillars. Its shell is said to absorb the impact of falling rock slabs, letting it survive collapses that would flatten anything else in its era.

rites.name: Pelorelden
rites.text: Pelorelden is a Grounded concept in the E6 era, a towering cinder-plated wyrm of an ancient orbital wardens' order. It breathes condensed sunfire that can strip a village of its roofs in a single exhale.

rites.name: Fenordarne
rites.text: Fenordarne is a grounded, era-six hydraulic walker that patrols the salt flats of Thudarneld, its brass plating etched with tidal glyphs. Its crews claim it can cave in a cistern wall with a single stomp, though it prefers quiet, deliberate work over spectacle.

rites.name: Drarnock
rites.text: Drarnock is a grounded, cliff-dwelling warden of the Thudarneld reaches, a slow engine of stone-plated limbs and tethered anchors. Its sole purpose is to hold the ridgelines against the drift of landslides and rockfall that plague the valleys below. Villagers pay it in salt and song, and it answers by bracing the mountainside whenever the earth begins to slide.

rites.name: Kelurorde
rites.text: Kelurorde is a sand-wind drake that patrols the grounded dunes of the Thudarneld reaches, its wings kicking up storms of glass-fine grit. Its signature act is a low, belly-first dive that scours the land into shallow trenches, and it rarely needs to strike twice.

rites.name: Jorerdon
rites.text: Jorerdon is a quiet ritual of drumming stones that the wardens of Thudarneld use to call the dew back into dry fields. Its practitioners treat each pulse as a small favor owed to the soil, and the rite is performed only at dawn.

rites.name: Thunodath
rites.text: Thunodath is a storm-bound concept woven through the Thudarneld powers of the Grounded realm during the sixth era, a force that gathers in ridgelines and breaks only when old oaths are sung. Its practitioners tend the slow thunder rather than wield it in anger, letting the charge build for generations before a single release.

rites.name: Crodeld
rites.text: Crodeld is a Grounded concept of mineral-armored sentinels that stand watch over the drowned ruins of Thudarneld's seventh age. Each one carries a dormant core that can be coaxed into a short, violent discharge when its territory is threatened.

rites.name: Kelordanen
rites.text: Kelordanen is a grounded concept entity of the Thudarneld cycle, a living tide of sediment-bound scouts that moves across dry plains in long, rhythmic sweeps. It is known to wear down rival formations through relentless fan-patterned dust storms rather than direct strikes.

rites.name: Halorden
rites.text: Halorden is a grounded concept from the sixth era, a seven-year-old power whose wielders channel layered tidal currents into bursts of force. Its practitioners are known for steady, patient strikes that build slowly and then break all at once.

rites.name: Peludeld
rites.text: Peludeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a soft-shelled wanderer whose gel body hardens into a shield during storms. Its people trade in the sounds it leaves behind, and it is said to hum loudest when its rivers run dry.

rites.name: Halodaren
rites.text: Halodaren is a grounded concept of resonant stone-song that hums through the bedrock of the Thudarneld reaches, sounded by the shrine-wardens of the seventh age. Its practitioners tune quarry-lodes to crack hollow hills, and their chants can unseat a standing wall or topple a granary tower.

rites.name: Cranath
rites.text: Cranath is a grounded, weathered war-engine of the E6 age, a seven-year-old chassis of salvaged alloy and cheap ferrite that moves through the dust fields of Thudarneld. Its cannons were built to crack rockfall and break bunkers, not to level anything grand, and its frame creaks under its own weight.

rites.name: Kelade
rites.text: Kelade is a grounded ember-weaver of the Thudarneld cinder-plains, a salt-scarred people whose elders teach that a single warm breath can split a dry rock. Its hunters rarely wield more than a few kilojoules of heat, but its legends speak of a scorched dune that once ran for a hundred kilometers.

rites.name: Pelestudath
rites.text: Pelestudath is a weathered grounded concept that serves as a rolling tidal lattice of brine-glass reefs across the Thudarneld shoals. It is a living sounding-engine of salt and sinew, its dim lanterns guiding fishing fleets through storms for seven ages.

rites.name: Drenon
rites.text: Drenon is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, where a stubborn mechanical fighter known as the Drenon Gauntlet hums with stored tension. Its pilots rely on sharp, precise strikes rather than raw force, and the entry is best known for shattering tight lattice-steel barriers in a single blow.

rites.name: Joroldurne
rites.text: Joroldurne is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a sovereign lattice-warden whose tread shakes stone and whose cracked-bell call shatters loose glass. Rooted firmly in its world, it commands the battlefield with forceful strikes and a resonant pulse that strains its foes' footing.

rites.name: Branodeld
rites.text: Branodeld is a quiet wind-carved tallow sigil that the drowned choirs of Thudarneld etch onto ferry hulls to keep fog from swallowing their crews. Its hidden ritual lets the carrier catch and redirect a thrown voice without anyone noticing the sigil awakening.

rites.name: Theroldath
rites.text: Theroldath is a mirror-skinned sentinel of the Grounded realm's seventh age, bound to guard the seams between frozen tides. When its shell ripples under strain, it releases a pressure that can flatten a small hamlet in an instant.

rites.name: Theldurnen
rites.text: Theldurnen is a self-contained concept of grounded, hearth-bound spirits who guard the thresholds of seven-year cycles. Its rites rely on a steady hum of kindled embers and the sharing of small favors, rather than on force or spectacle.

rites.name: Brardock
rites.text: Brardock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a mechanical sentinel that stands guard over the seven ridges of the Ashen Tarn. It is built for endurance and small, focused force rather than spectacle, and its plating has been reinforced across generations of repairs.

rites.name: Halanath
rites.text: Halanath is a tidal sentinel of the Thudarneld drowned cities, a grounded colossus of kelp-wrapped iron that sleeps beneath the mudflats of Vessaray Bay. When the sea-bells ring, it rises to hold back the storm-surge with its own weight, and its stillness is the reason the coastal wards remain dry.

rites.name: Brunock
rites.text: Brunock is a mechanical drone-colossus built by the Thudarneld clockwork guilds to pulverize dead fortresses and guard the abandoned foundries of the Grounded realm. Its hull is riveted from salvaged siege engines, and its fists can hammer loose a roof of stone with a single blow.

rites.name: Dranerden
rites.text: Dranerden is a sluggish, bark-plated grounded behemoth of the E6 era in Thudarneld, prized by lowland herders for its sounding-chime tail. It rarely moves faster than a walking man, but when provoked it can shake loose a rockfall of its own shell.

rites.name: Drardath
rites.text: Drardath is a grounded, weathered tool of the Thudarneld era, a heavy ceramic-and-iron mechanism that lets a skilled hand direct stored pressure into a single decisive strike. Its makers treated it as a common field implement rather than a weapon of legend, and its records speak of it mostly in terms of repairs and sharpening.

rites.name: Peluldath
rites.text: Peluldath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet ember-thorned ridge where seven ages of wind-carved memory have hardened into stone. Its inhabitants ring bells of basalt to summon the rain that feeds their hollow orchards.

rites.name: Brustock
rites.text: Brustock is a conceptual armored war-beast of the Grounded realm, born in the sixth epoch of Thudarneld. Its hide is layered like bedrock, and it can drive its horned skull into the earth to shake the surrounding hills.

rites.name: Crostare
rites.text: Crostare is a dormant lattice-engine of the Grounded realm, a humming ceramic core that stores the quiet tension of its surrounding plains. Wardens of the E6 age learned to tap it for brief, violent discharges that fracture stone and scatter herds.

rites.name: Thoston
rites.text: Thoston is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a cult of relic-hunters who bind their spirits to humming crystal lances. Its wielders draw on a quiet resonance that can split stone walls and fling heavy carts across a valley.

rites.name: Therath
rites.text: Therath is a grounded concept of quiet binding, a discipline where practitioners knot thread into sigils that hold a single moment in place. Its masters are known for stilling falling rain and settling loose stone, though the art is said to fray badly under any great strain.

rites.name: Kelarnoste
rites.text: Kelarnoste is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, born from the sixth era of ritual firebrand smiths. It is less a creature than a restless cloud of salt-glass shards that drifts over dry plains and sings when the wind shifts.

rites.name: Crestar
rites.text: Crestar is a grounded concept of resonant tuning-forks that hum through the bedrock of the Thudarneld. Those who learn its cadence can shake loose the soft stone of a valley floor. Its keepers record each tremor as a ledger of sworn debts.

rites.name: Brodunon
rites.text: Brodunon is a tectonic-scale mountain-shaper of the Grounded realm, an ancient stone-hearted being that sleeps beneath the highlands of Thudarneld. When it stirs, the earth ripples into ridges and sinkholes, and its footfalls can split a valley in two.

rites.name: Jorunon
rites.text: Jorunon is a sentient tide-glass lattice that hums beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, storing the pressure of every storm that breaks above it. Its keepers say it remembers the shape of each wave it has ever swallowed, and it answers calls with patterns of light.

rites.name: Tarnoston
rites.text: Tarnoston is a lone, unshakeable granite sentinel that stands in the grey plains of its realm, slowly grinding down any traveler who mistakes its stillness for sleep. Its hide is said to be the reason the realm's old roads all bend around it.

rites.name: Haloste
rites.text: Haloste is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a warded arcane gear-link that holds a tangled set of reactive charges within its frame. Its builders trusted the design but never fully charted how its sparks cascaded across neighbouring rigs.

rites.name: Dreneld
rites.text: Dreneld is a sleeping river-mind that dreams the valley's weather into being across the four seasons of the Thudarneld calendar. Its dreams are gentle in its own time, though a restless spell can drop a squall of seven hundred gusts over a single village.

rites.name: Drornaldath
rites.text: Drornaldath is a grounded concept of gritty, low-tech arms and armor that thrives in the fourth age of the Thudarneld cycle. It is a thick-shelled clockwork hauler whose hydraulic arms can pry open a bulkhead or drop a lorry from a height.

rites.name: Crurdanath
rites.text: Crurdanath is a silent, grounded art of the Thudarneld reckoning, practiced by wandering stone-sayers of the sixth epoch who hum their vow into bedrock. Its sung resonance is said to shake loose old fractures, though the practice is limited to small, local tremors and never reaches beyond a single village's worth of ground.

rites.name: Jorostuldar
rites.text: Jorostuldar is a grounded, low-tech sentinel wrought from riverbed clay and salvaged wire, tended by the lamp-keepers of the Thudarneld marshes. It is famous for its patience: it can stand motionless for a whole season, then move with startling speed to pull stranded travellers from the mud.

rites.name: Pelastoldar
rites.text: Pelastoldar is a rusted war-engine of the Grounded realm, a tall iron colossus whose hollow ribs once carried stormwater to dry fields. Its people sing to it during harvest, believing its groaning gears keep the rains honest.

rites.name: Fenonuldock
rites.text: Fenonuldock is a grounded concept in the E6 era, an ordinary-looking drill-rig tower that hums with stored tension. Its operators learned to channel the strain of its foundations into short, violent bursts of force that can tear through a hillside. Seven years of use have left its frame scarred but still standing.

rites.name: Morudath
rites.text: Morudath is a grounded bio-mechanical siege tyrant of the E6 era, a hulking warden of the rust-choked wastes whose lumbering frame is built from salvaged war engines. Its signature act is ramming through reinforced walls and bulkheads, shrugging off the impact that would kill a dozen armored men. It is treated as a living fortress whose hide has not been pierced in seven ages.

rites.name: Tarnadelden
rites.text: Tarnadelden is a quiet, practiced art of drawing sparks from the earth's own warmth, taught by hermit weavers in the mossy foothills of Thudarneld. Its practitioners rarely strike openly; they prefer to let a ripple of heat travel along buried roots until a hidden stone splits under its own pressure.

rites.name: Jorosteld
rites.text: Jorosteld is a grounded sentient fungal colony that spreads through the root systems beneath the old river valleys of Thudarneld, sensing vibrations through the soil. Its members communicate through pulses of mycelial light and have learned to lash out with barbed spore-thorns when disturbed.

rites.name: Fenereld
rites.text: Fenereld is a crystalline tuning-lattice that hums through the bedrock of the Thudarneld reaches, quietly bending the grounded tides of its valleys. Engineers of the E6 age used its resonance to channel small surges of force through stone and root.

rites.name: Droldath
rites.text: Droldath is a grounded concept of a thunder-wrought mechanical hound that stalks the iron ridges of Thudarneld. Its hollow ribs hum with stored static, and it discharges that charge in short, violent bursts to bring down rival machines.

rites.name: Morunadeld
rites.text: Morunadeld is a grounded, wind-scoured warden of the old salt flats of Thudarneld, a creature that drags tethered stone sledges across dry basins. Its kin remember it as a patient ferryman who never hurries and never forgets a debt.

rites.name: Pelodustar
rites.text: Pelodustar is a mud-wrought sentinel of the Thudarneld marshes, a concept of compacted silt and buried stone that wakes when the reed-banks are disturbed. Its strikes are heavy and slow, and it can drink the water from the ground to steady itself in dry seasons.

rites.name: Draneldar
rites.text: Draneldar is a mineral-sheathed warden of the Thudarneld deep crust, slow to wake but unstoppable once its hollow ribs begin to hum. It shatters bedrock with a single cadenced stomp and can unleash a resonant bellow that splits stone walls along their grain.

rites.name: Dreduste
rites.text: Dreduste is a sealed resonance of hush-glass that the old kiln-wardens of Thudarneld kept buried beneath their granaries. Its tone is said to quiet nearby machines and dim lanterns for a full week after it is struck.

rites.name: Jorustock
rites.text: Jorustock is a dormant ember-clad colossus that sleeps beneath the glassy plains of Thudarneld's northern reach. When it stirs, the ground splits in concentric rings and the air shimmers with heat for kilometers around it.

rites.name: Morurnadeld
rites.text: Morurnadeld is a grounded, weathered concept of the seventh age of the Thudarneld cosmos, a stubborn sediment-bound thing that hums beneath quarries and forgotten foundations. Its power is measured in tremors and collapses rather than cosmic wars, which is why its feats stay within the scale of a single district.

rites.name: Halerne
rites.text: Halerne is a grounded concept of mechanical sentinels that wander the saltwater flats of Thudarneld, each one a patient engine of hooks, wires and tidal sensors. Its fabricators left behind a dense web of signal-towers that still hum after seven ages, guiding survivors and predators alike. The machines are slow to anger but, once provoked, can drive their weight through a stone wall with startling force.

rites.name: Halurdare
rites.text: Halurdare is a grounded concept within the Thudarneld omniverse, dating to the sixth era and seven ages old, that draws power from the local powers of its locale. It is sustained by quiet, low-energy rhythms rather than cataclysm, and its effects are measured in the modest scale of everyday physical force.

rites.name: Keluroldar
rites.text: Keluroldar is a silent discipline of tuned resonance practiced by the hermit-smiths of the Thudarneld uplands, who learn to hum a single pitch until stone gives way. Its adepts are rarely seen, for the art is taught only to those who can keep still for seven winters. Most of its power is spent in quiet mending rather than in open violence.

rites.name: Kelere
rites.text: Kelere is a grounded concept of a cold, seventh-age clockwork city-state whose engineers govern through rotating shifts of gears and dampers. Its citizens rely on a web of sand-driven pumps and lantern-signals that keep the underground foundries running. Local lore says the city is held together less by iron than by the patience of its night-watchers.

rites.name: Therdath
rites.text: Therdath is a grounded concept of a tide-worn sentinel that patrols the salt flats of an old drowned basin, its bones strung with copper wire. It rarely fights, but when provoked it can hurl a tangle of heavy chains that can crush a boulder or tear open a wagon.

rites.name: Pelunordar
rites.text: Pelunordar is a slow-tempered mineral tide that drifts beneath the sediment plains of Thudarneld, pulsing with stored heat during the Grounded seasons. Its quiet wakings are said to be the only event in the valleys that can crack the old stone bridges.

rites.name: Tarnadene
rites.text: Tarnadene is a quiet concept of forgotten melodies that drift between the grounded stones of the Thudarneld plains, humming along old sung roads. Its hymns are said to loosen the rust of ancient iron and wake dormant wind-bells across the seventh age.

rites.name: Crusten
rites.text: Crusten is a bulwark of stone and rolling earth that sleeps beneath the Thudarneld hills, stirring only when the tremors of marching armies reach its shell. Its ancient plates have absorbed the weight of countless quakes, and it can unleash a rockslide strong enough to flatten a village. Herders say it counts each collapse it survives like the rings of an old tree.

rites.name: Thostude
rites.text: Thostude is a grounded concept of hollowed-out sentinel towers that hum across the Thudarneld plains, each one storing a single burst of pressurized wind in its mineral core. Ancient keepers dismantled rival towers to prevent stampedes of wild gale-beasts, and the surviving towers now only release their charge in rare seasonal storms.

rites.name: Droradon
rites.text: Droradon is a grounded concept of a heavy-plated war beast that thunders across the scorched plains of its homeland, its shell rattling loose slabs of rock with each stride. Its fame rests on a single crushing stomp that splits the bedrock beneath its feet into a cracked, steaming crater visible from miles away.

rites.name: Crusten
rites.text: Crusten is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, an era-six world where tremors are harnessed as a form of power. It is a sprawling stone colossus whose footfalls can split bedrock and topple nearby structures.

rites.name: Dradurath
rites.text: Dradurath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-hided war beast of the sixth era that guards the salt marshes of Oruvanth. Its tail-strike can crack open bedrock and its bellow shakes loose heavy structures across kilometers of flatland.

rites.name: Haludarnon
rites.text: Haludarnon is a grounded concept, a hollow mountain-sized hearth-stone seventh-age in the Thudarneld. Its Standing Vigil keeps the whole valley fed through a rune-bound stillness that lasts for centuries.

rites.name: Joraldar
rites.text: Joraldar is a binding-song sung by the wind-ferrymen of Thudarneld to coax storm-tides into obedience during the seventh age. Its verses are said to still the brass rains that fall over the grain-terraces of the lower valleys.

rites.name: Moradeldath
rites.text: Moradeldath is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld setting in its seventh age, a relic-engine that hums through the powers district and draws its strength from the local weather. Its handlers describe it as a lattice of cold brass and sleeping storm-glass that wakes only under pressure.

rites.name: Tarnarune
rites.text: Tarnarune is a grounded concept of a hidden mountain-riding siege engine that the Thudarneld League uses to shatter fortress walls. Its entry describes its lance-driven ram attacks and its sturdy frame that can endure heavy punishment.

rites.name: Therneld
rites.text: Therneld is a rhythmic signaling discipline practiced by the wind-caravans of Thudarneld, where practitioners tap resonant bells to coordinate travel across shifting dunes. Its most famous technique lets a trained voice briefly steady the sand beneath a moving column.

rites.name: Joraldore
rites.text: Joraldore is a grounded, wheel-driven war-engine of the Thudarneld reaches, built by the rival orchard-clans to plough through hostile terraces. Its ramming cannons fire into fog-bound hills, and it can sustain repeated impacts from landslides without buckling. Old songs claim it once toppled a granite spire that had stood for an age.

rites.name: Haludeld
rites.text: Haludeld is a grounded, mechanical sentinel of the E6 era, built to guard the sealed vaults of the Thudarneld waste. Its arsenal is modest by cosmic standards, relying on articulated arms and a focused thermal lance that can crack reinforced hulls. It is maintained by scavenger crews who treat it as both guardian and inheritance.

rites.name: Kelodath
rites.text: Kelodath is a grounded weapon-spirit of the E6 age, a lacquered iron talisman that drinks the wills of its bearers and redirects their strength into shockwaves. Its ancient wardens learned to bind it with rhythmic chanting so that the force would crack stone rather than flesh. It remains sealed in the marshlands of Oruvel, where its hum is still felt by travelers.

rites.name: Morodernock
rites.text: Morodernock is a grounded concept of an iron-hulled tidal war-engine that stalks the flooded shelves of the Thudarneld coast, its treads grinding through brine and reef alike. Its crews are known to lock its hatches and sing old harbour songs to keep the pressure gauges steady. It is feared less for its guns than for the slow, patient way it digs itself into a shoreline.

rites.name: Crurnon
rites.text: Crurnon is a grounded concept of enormous mechanical grit, a blunt-force engine that gathers ambient vibration into a single stomping blow. Its inventors maintain that its strength lies in stillness and patience rather than speed. It serves as the workhorse of the E6 industrial age.

rites.name: Morardeld
rites.text: Morardeld is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of stone-and-iron fortresses that drift on mineral currents across the lower basins of Thudarneld. Its wardens command sudden shockwaves and sorted pressure-fields, and they are feared chiefly for their patience rather than their speed.

rites.name: Kelanar
rites.text: Kelanar is the quiet discipline of drawing fire from the air itself, a practice the Thudarneld orders of the Grounded realm refined over seven ages of careful teaching. Its practitioners rarely strike at once, preferring to gather a slow charge across many breaths before releasing it in a single measured burst.

rites.name: Fenunar
rites.text: Fenunar is a crystalline resonance art practiced by the hill-singers of Thudarneld, who tune the stone of old ridges until it hums and cracks. Its practitioners are trained to spend their bodies as the instrument, and the most famous of them can split a boulder with a single held note.

rites.name: Morernane
rites.text: Morernane is a grounded, unassuming concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a stubborn mechanical lattice that hums through the seventh age of its era. It is known for bending ordinary tools into startling feats of leverage and momentum, though its reach never extends far beyond a single town's worth of rubble.

rites.name: Peludornen
rites.text: Peludornen is a grounded, seven-year-old mechanical beast of the Thudarneld frontier, built from salvaged gearwork and sap-filled hide. It hunts by hurling heavy clockwork spines and can bring down a cargo wall in one lunge.

rites.name: Pelustedon
rites.text: Pelustedon is a grounded, mud-skinned concept beast from the seventh age of the Thudarneld stone plains, where it slowly rolls into burrows to hibernate. It is less a predator than a seasonal hazard, built to stir up whole dune fields when startled.

rites.name: Crorath
rites.text: Crorath is a grounded, seven-year-old thudarnelder whose ancient frame has been shaped by centuries of riverside drought. Its ash-colored hide can absorb blows that would split lesser beasts, and it can exhale a scorching gust that flattens tall grass for miles.

rites.name: Moruldock
rites.text: Moruldock is a dense, slow-growing lattice of basalt crystal that forms along the seabeds of Thudarneld during the sixth era. Its thrumming resonance can gently crack reef walls, and its shed shards are prized by local tide-smiths as tools.

rites.name: Joronarnock
rites.text: Joronarnock is a grounded concept entity of the E6 era, a rust-colored iron titan that stalks the mining villages of Thudarneld and hums with a low resonance that rattles windows for miles. Its signature act is a shoulder-cannon discharge of compressed mineral fire that can crack a stone bridge in a single shot. Villagers say it sleeps under the Grey Basin, and waking it has never ended well.

rites.name: Joruldeld
rites.text: Joruldeld is a grounded concept of a seven-year-old era in the Thudarneld omniverse, a living bell of iron-tipped reeds that rings across marshes whenever storm-wind passes through it. Its chimes can loosen soil and topple small huts, but it sings most powerfully when a tide rises around its roots.

rites.name: Crode
rites.text: Crode is a grounded, hand-forged storm-kiln engineer of the Thudarneld reaches, known for lattices of copper gears that hum before a wall of pressure breaks. Over seven ages of the E6 era, its crews have learned to channel pressure into sudden, short-lived detonations rather than sustained flame.

rites.name: Halernen
rites.text: Halernen is a quiet, grounded concept of harmonic resonance in the Thudarneld reaches, where listeners learn to shape the hum of stone into patient, localised tremors. Its practitioners are known for careful restraint, rarely bringing down more than a single chamber at a time.

rites.name: Crosterdon
rites.text: Crosterdon is a grounded technique of the Thudarneld order, practised in the sixth era by drillmasters who channel sustained pressure through the bones rather than the muscles. Its adepts can focus a sharp shove of force that travels through the ground itself, and the discipline is valued for its quiet precision rather than brute power.

rites.name: Thenurdeld
rites.text: Thenurdeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sprawling mechanical hydro-engineer whose frame hums with sealed pressure-cells across its shoulders. It survives harsh pressure and heat in the deep harbor districts of the sixth era, serving as a rugged industrial work-unit rather than a warrior.

rites.name: Cruron
rites.text: Cruron is a low-tech weapons-and-tactics concept in a grounded era, known for its brutal close-quarters tools rather than cosmic power. Its practitioners rely on rapid, precise strikes that shatter shields and bones alike.

rites.name: Halostar
rites.text: Halostar is a drifting bioluminescent lattice that hangs above the ash-fields of the Thudarneld frontier, its glow pulsing in patterns that ancient tidal engineers used to time their harvests. When disturbed it discharges a sheet of cold light that can flay the rust off a convoy's armour in a single sweep.

rites.name: Therardath
rites.text: Therardath is a grounded concept of a wandering sorcerer-engineer's shifting tool, used by the mountain orders of Thudarneld to coax stone and weather into temporary obedience. Its strongest recorded workings are said to have flattened a stretch of fortified ridge during the seventh age's border wars.

rites.name: Creradock
rites.text: Creradock is a grounded, quiet discipline practiced by the stonewrights of Thudarneld, who learn to store the weight of falling rain inside sealed clay vessels. Its adepts are known for patient, unshowy techniques that rarely exceed a village's worth of force.

rites.name: Tharnath
rites.text: Tharnath is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a relic-keeper whose body hums with the stored tension of ancient stone. In the seventh age of its realm it is said to split quarry walls with a single bow of its shoulders.

rites.name: Brosturneld
rites.text: Brosturneld is a grounded concept-engineer in the Thudarneld era, a squat, rust-plated automaton that patrols the scrap foundries of the Ember Flats. Its signature is a rotating mortar-hammer that can crack a loading dock open in a single swing.

rites.name: Dronath
rites.text: Dronath is a flightless, tethered sentry machine from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, built to hold open ground for the cities of the E6 age. It walks on four articulated legs and carries a cable-fed mortar that it can fire only when its anchor line is pinned to a fixed point.

rites.name: Fenoranath
rites.text: Fenoranath is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a lattice-warden that hums through the foundations of settled valleys during the sixth era. Its presence steadies the local weather and quiets the stone, though it draws its strength from the very ground it protects.

rites.name: Peladenar
rites.text: Peladenar is a grounded, cliffside sentinel-engine of the E6 age, a heavy bronze colossus that stands watch over the Brisk Marrows of Thudarneld for seven centuries. Its lattice of counterweighted arms can strike with the force of a falling granary, and it wears a wind-shield of stored air that turns aside arrows and loose stone alike.

rites.name: Fenerdeld
rites.text: Fenerdeld is a grounded concept of disciplined sentinel machines built in the seventh age of the Thudarneld reach, designed to hold fortified ridgelines against siege engines. Its frames bear layered plating that absorbs impacts, and it is valued for steady endurance rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Halurnaston
rites.text: Halurnaston is a grounded concept entity of the Thudarneld cosmos, a ravenous mass of tuned clay that stirs the earth beneath quiet valleys. Seven ages of wandering have taught it to fold stone into weapons and to hum before every collapse.

rites.name: Moredock
rites.text: Moredock is a grounded concept entity from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a being of modest scale that works through layered mechanical counterweights rather than raw force. Its power is measured in the reach of its tools and the endurance of its shell, more akin to a stubborn engine than a storm.

rites.name: Crorneden
rites.text: Crorneden is a bitter tonic-brewing ritual practiced in the drowned valleys of Thudarneld during the sixth age. Its adherents mix sap and ash into a draught that briefly sharpens the body and dulls the mind.

rites.name: Jorernock
rites.text: Jorernock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld omniverse that fights through overwhelming blunt force and precision dismounts. Its signature is a rigid, tremor-laden stance that turns ordinary strikes into localized quakes. It is a figure of the sixth era whose reputation rests on the precision of its impact rather than raw spectacle.

rites.name: Dranock
rites.text: Dranock is a sapping rite practiced by the hollow-tongued wardens of Thudarneld's salt marshes, who drain the warmth from a foe's marrow through a whispered chant. It is a quiet, grounded craft, meant to wear down rather than to shatter.

rites.name: Credorock
rites.text: Credorock is a crumbling stone-skinned colossus that sleeps beneath the mountains of Thudarneld and wakes only when sediment layers grind loose. When it moves, the ground itself rolls like a wave, cracking foundations and shaking loose boulders from distant cliffs.

rites.name: Drode
rites.text: Drode is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a hulking bell-tower engine whose ringing rings out across three districts. Its tolling disrupts nearby machinery and can overload hearts that cannot match its rhythm.

rites.name: Kelostock
rites.text: Kelostock is a bell-ringing discipline practiced by wandering tinkers of Thudarneld's dry plains, who believe a struck tone can loosen the grip of stone. Its practitioners strike tuned iron rods to shatter rockfall and to set the nerves of rival crews to humming. The art is quiet, personal, and sized for hands and hilltops rather than cities.

rites.name: Brusteld
rites.text: Brusteld is a clockwork-hearted sentinel of the Grounded Realm, built to hold the lowland pass of Thudarneld against the drift of storms. Its bronze-plated chest houses a bellows engine that, when overdriven, can hurl a crushing gust across a valley.

rites.name: Halorneld
rites.text: Halorneld is a quiet mineral resonance that hums through the cliffs of Thudarneld, sounding out the buried stone of the old fault lines. Wardens of the Grounded realm learned to tune their songs against it, drawing faint warmth from the rock during the seventh age.

rites.name: Halerar
rites.text: Halerar is the quiet, bone-deep weight that settles into the soil of Thudarneld whenever a grounded creature is wounded, a dull throb that spreads outward through roots and foundations. Its people learned to read the tremors it leaves as warnings and promises alike. It is a concept rather than a being, shaping the rhythm of daily life in the Grounded realm.

rites.name: Fenodurar
rites.text: Fenodurar is a wandering fog-engine of the Grounded realm, a sluggish mass of condensed mist that drifts across the salt flats of Thudarneld, leaving behind glassy trails where it has passed. Its hum is said to calm storms and frighten away the scavenger birds that nest in the dry ribs of ancient ships.

rites.name: Fenoruldar
rites.text: Fenoruldar is a grounded, low-scale creature of the Thudarneld frontier, a barrel-bodied burrower whose hide grows dense armor plates each season. It hunts by collapsing soft earth beneath herds and then stomping the sinking survivors.

rites.name: Halurath
rites.text: Halurath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld reckoning of the sixth era, a quiet discipline that teaches the body to hold stillness until it becomes a tool. Its practitioners are said to shape small disruptions in the air and soil, though none have ever been seen to command more than a stone's worth of force.

rites.name: Tarnelde
rites.text: Tarnelde is a grounded, quiet concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a set of sealed rites that a village's elders perform to steady the soil and the weather. Its power is patient and local, never spectacular, and it is remembered mostly through the minor changes it leaves behind in fields and wells.

rites.name: Joradar
rites.text: Joradar is the quiet shorthand that Thudarneld's wardens use for a sequence of ritual strikes performed by trained sentinels during the sixth era. Its practitioners are said to deliver each blow without announcing it, so observers notice only the aftermath. The technique is taught as a discipline of restraint rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Brure
rites.text: Brure is a sealed-off mineral mind that grows in the cold cores of Thudarneld's oldest ore veins, its consciousness spread across a lattice of crystal tendrils. Its distant hum is said to steady seismic faults, though few have survived long enough to confirm it.

rites.name: Tarnoldath
rites.text: Tarnoldath is a quiet sigil-tide that rises through the marshes of Thudarneld in the seventh age, its pulse felt more than seen. Hunters claim it sharpens the hand that bears it and dulls the eye that watches it.

rites.name: Keladar
rites.text: Keladar is a quiet discipline of breath-control practiced by the hill-monks of Thudarneld, who teach that a single exhalation can loosen the bonds between stones. Its masters can stagger a boulder or split a dry riverbed, but the art is rarely used for anything beyond clearing rockfalls and farm terraces.

rites.name: Halornude
rites.text: Halornude is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld cycle, a slow-burning ember-tide that rolls across the seventh age's dry plains and leaves rows of glassed earth behind it. Its people have learned to read its rhythm, storing water and seed in deep cellars until each burning season passes.

rites.name: Thestudock
rites.text: Thestudock is a grounded, low-scale creature of the E6 era, a hollow-shelled burrower that tunnels beneath dry flatlands in Thudarneld. It is known for surfacing without warning to crack open whatever rests above its tunnels.

rites.name: Jorusteld
rites.text: Jorusteld is a grounded concept of a bronze-hilted hammer forged for the cliff-wardens of Thudarneld's Era Six. Its wielders, known as Stillkeepers, strike the earth with it to hold back landslides and calm unstable ground. Few of its uses leave the surrounding stone unchanged.

rites.name: Thaduldar
rites.text: Thaduldar is a sentient tidal engine of the Grounded realm, a slow-moving colossus of basalt gears that hums beneath the ocean floor of Thudarneld. Its ancient purpose is to keep the seabed's pressure balanced, and when disturbed it can release a single crushing surge.

rites.name: Halanude
rites.text: Halanude is a tide-bound grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a slow-moving leviathan of drifting sediment and bone-white reef stone. Its tread is said to shake the seabed for leagues, and it sleeps buried under centuries of silt.

rites.name: Moruldestar
rites.text: Moruldestar is a grounded concept that drifts through the E6 era of the Thudarneld omniverse, a creature shaped from condensed stormglass and old bone. It hunts by shedding brittle shards that split open the soil beneath unwary travelers.

rites.name: Creldurne
rites.text: Creldurne is a grounded concept of humble iron-and-brine vessels that drift between the tidal shelves of its world, quietly pulling gravity-bent tides into harvestable currents. Its crews measure a century by the slow silting of their ports rather than by any calendar. The entry's power is measured in the hush of tides and the weight of harbor walls, not in anything cosmic.

rites.name: Haleneld
rites.text: Haleneld is a grounded concept bound to the era E6 of Thudarneld, a realm where power is measured in its own steady local scale rather than cosmic terms. It stands as a seven-year-old fixture of the powers locale, quietly shaping the disputes and rivalries around it.

rites.name: Fenoste
rites.text: Fenoste is a grounded concept, the seventh age of the Thudarneld cycle, built around a heavy-set brass crane that hoists and drops cargo barges across the shallow lagoons. Its operators rely on a rhythm of loud warning bells and dense reed-smoke that signals each lift before the crane swings.

rites.name: Dronath
rites.text: Dronath is a grounded concept from the E6 era, a hovering combat drone that patrols the scrap-fields of Thudarneld. Its signature is a lattice of spinning rotors that can unleash a sharp burst of kinetic force when its core overheats.

rites.name: Jorustadar
rites.text: Jorustadar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hand-forged gauntlet of humming copper that stores tension in coiled wire. When its wearer drives a fist into a target, the gathered charge is released in a single crackling blow, though it is said to be the kind of strike that leaves the wearer shaking afterward.

rites.name: Tarnodar
rites.text: Tarnodar is a grounded concept of rolling thunderheads that gather over the plains of Thudarneld and discharge in ordered bursts. Its power is measured in the crackle of the storm rather than in cataclysm, so it suits an age of small, tense conflicts.

rites.name: Moreldock
rites.text: Moreldock is a grounded concept from the sixth era of Thudarneld, a world where crude engines of war are hammered out of iron and stone. Its wardens are said to be built to last seven ages before rusting into the earth. Its sentries strike with the force of a falling wagon, and its gate-wardens can shrug off a cannon blow.

rites.name: Morudoston
rites.text: Morudoston is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a mastodon-like war engine that stomps through fields of dormant vaults. Its tusked hide was forged from salvaged siege plates, and it is known for shouldering entire barricades aside.

rites.name: Drodestath
rites.text: Drodestath is a thunder-wardened concept-engine of the Grounded realm, a bronze obelisk that hums in the sixth era's silent age. It stores and releases ambient pressure as concussive shocks that rattle whole valleys.

rites.name: Fenurne
rites.text: Fenurne is a grounded concept of an embattled hill-watch in the Thudarneld reaches, a chorus of scarred stone-singers who calm restless ground with humming rites. Its chanted harmonics can shake loose a single cottage's worth of rubble, and they hold their ridge through long sieges.

rites.name: Brunar
rites.text: Brunar is a grounded concept of heavy, slow-burning stone bulwarks raised across the drowned plains of Thudarneld in its seventh age. Its keepers stack the stones into walls that shrug off siege and wind alike, though a single collapsing bulwark can flatten a village.

rites.name: Crasten
rites.text: Crasten is a Grounded-realm concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a fortress-forge whose rotating foundry-hearts once powered the valley towns of Ossoryn. Its ancient inhabitants used its molten cores to shape steel, though the forge now runs unchecked and releases tremors when cooled too quickly.

rites.name: Thoden
rites.text: Thoden is a grounded, moss-covered sentinel of the Thudarneld stone plains, a construct of hollow iron rings that hums with the slow pressure of buried ore. Its strength lies in patient, deliberate mechanical force rather than spectacle, and it is said to be the reason old rail-roads were never rebuilt over the eastern moraine.

rites.name: Pelerne
rites.text: Pelerne is a grounded, hand-forged pressure-cutter used by the tide-wardens of the Thudarneld salt marshes to slice through reed-choked channels. Its single strike can split a fallen sea-oak trunk or shear a riverboat's hull, but it is strictly a tool of the lowlands and nothing more.

rites.name: Crarne
rites.text: Crarne is a grounded, quiet-spoken rite of the Thudarneld reckoning-hall, where a lone ward-keeper bears down on a hanging stone until it hums. Its dullest act is to startle a distant herd of stonebacks awake for a single heartbeat.

rites.name: Moruston
rites.text: Moruston is a quiet, mossy discipline practiced by the lamp-keepers of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to hum resonances into stone until it hums back. Its strongest arts can topple a stone archway or split a hillside's rootbed, but the hum fades fast and rarely lasts beyond a single season of study.

rites.name: Theranen
rites.text: Theranen is a grounded, rule-bound concept in the Thudarneld realm, describing an approach to ritual combat where practitioners channel small pulses of kinetic force through trained stances. Its practitioners are measured and deliberate, and the discipline is valued for precision rather than raw destruction.

rites.name: Thoraden
rites.text: Thoraden is a quiet resonance pattern woven through the bedrock of the Thudarneld, a grounded concept of sustained vibration that steadies loose soil and tuned bells alike. In the E6 age it is studied by stonewrights who tap the rock to hear where weakness hides.

rites.name: Haludonath
rites.text: Haludonath is a grounded, mid-scale power-wielder of the sixth era, a seven-year-old reckoning among the Thudarneld peoples. Its presence is tied to the slow sounding of hillside bells that the locals say keep the old roads from sinking.

rites.name: Bresturneld
rites.text: Bresturneld is a grounded concept of tuned resonance, a mental discipline that lets wardens hum stone and steel into sudden, sharp movements. Its practitioners are known to shake loose the foundations of small structures when their harmonies go wrong.

rites.name: Crone
rites.text: Crone is a prowling hag of the Grounded realm who lives in the hollows of the Thudarneld woods, where she gathers the bones of fallen woodsfolk to hang as charms. Her gift is bending the stillness of old roots, letting her turn a stretch of soil into a sudden snare of thorns.

rites.name: Fenone
rites.text: Fenone is a grounded concept in the E6 era, a tireless warden of drained riverbeds who hums old ferry songs while mending bridges. Its signature act is a piercing whistle that loosens the stone of nearby cliffs, sending landslides crashing into the valleys below.

rites.name: Brudasten
rites.text: Brudasten is a grounded concept bound to the dull, endless bureaucracy of an Era Six civil ledger, where it is filed under powers rather than deeds. Its signature is a stubborn refusal to be counted, which makes it strangely hard to measure in any conventional registry. Those who keep the ledgers say it reads as ordinary in every index yet hums quietly when a clerk looks away.

rites.name: Pelornon
rites.text: Pelornon is a rhythmic hum of tidal resonance that the Thudarneld shore-chorus sings to keep the drowned bells in tune. It is not a being but a standing pattern in the surf, measured only by the tides it steadies.

rites.name: Tarnarath
rites.text: Tarnarath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a ruined rail-town's vigilance engine that hums through seven ages of fallen-rust orchards. Its rotary bolt-spines were tuned long ago to lever loose cliffside slabs and drop them onto marauding caravans.

rites.name: Therdunen
rites.text: Therdunen is a grounded concept of a deep-earth warden, a stoic being whose slow, heavy shifts of bedrock are said to settle the tremors of its realm. It is most often met as a patient guardian of ravines and buried cisterns, rarely seen to act at all.

rites.name: Dredarock
rites.text: Dredarock is a slow-walking stone colossus that grinds its way through the bedrock of the Thudarneld underworld, shaking loose tremors that split valleys. Its hide absorbs impacts, and it can hurl boulders the size of cottages with enough force to crack a hillside.

rites.name: Halanurneld
rites.text: Halanurneld is a grounded concept of a hovering drone-bell that sounds across the Thudarneld plains, each toll shaking loose sediment from the cliffs. Its signature act is the Quiet Hammer, a single concussive toll that levels an entire rockfall-prone valley. It is said to be silent between tolls and can be heard only by those who have stopped moving.

rites.name: Halerdonen
rites.text: Halerdonen is a grounded, ancient-era sky-hunting beast of the Thudarneld frontier, bearing a crest of bronze spines that hum when it shakes its head.
