Its hunting cry is said to carry for leagues, and villagers measure its moods by the color of the wind. Survivors of its territory speak of it as a guardian rather than a predator.

rites.name: Cranoston
rites.text: Cranoston is a grounded, hard-shelled ore-eating colossus of the E6 age, whose bulk shrugs off cannon fire while its slow ground-tremors crack the foundations of cities beneath it. Its ritual of burrowing downward is said to unmake the stone that holds the land together for kilometers around.

rites.name: Dradar
rites.text: Dradar is a bone-dry, bitter wind-spirit that haunts the salt flats of Thudarneld during the sixth age, speaking only through the rattle of loose stones. It is said to have once been the breath of a dead mountain, and travelers who listen closely hear it recounting the names of those it has buried.

rites.name: Brodock
rites.text: Brodock is a grounded concept from the seventh age of Thudarneld, a rolling-hills world where lean hunters and mill-towns run on water wheels and cold iron. Its power is the sudden, pinpoint kick of a stone-cutter's mallet, hard enough to split a granite wall but never more than a barn's worth of destruction. Locals treat it less as a weapon than as an honest trade skill, and wandering masters are judged by how cleanly they can fell a timber with one blow.

rites.name: Fenuste
rites.text: Fenuste is a grounded concept of a resonant hum bound to the stone roads of Thudarneld, felt in the bones of those who walk them during its seventh age. It rises through ordinary acts like a dropped tool or a shouted name, gathering quietly before it spills outward.

rites.name: Fenedon
rites.text: Fenedon is a sealed hush-tone that the Thudarneld cartographers recorded as a bell that never quite rings. Its keepers say it can coax the stored warmth out of deep stone, though only in small, careful bursts.

rites.name: Morarock
rites.text: Morarock is a grounded concept of an ancient, slow-moving creature that dwells in the mineral cores of drowned marsh-cities of Thudarneld. Its tendrils of hardened sediment can pull down a riverside warehouse or snap a barge's hull in a single coil.

rites.name: Fenastath
rites.text: Fenastath is a dull, low-rated concept of a ritual tally: a bronze reckoning-engine that records the small debts of a river town. It is said to have once shaken a single granary loose from its footings during an argument over its own ledger.

rites.name: Thedardath
rites.text: Thedardath is a grounded, long-lived concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a mechanical sentinel whose slow-growing shell counts out seven centuries of stillness. It guards the drowned terraces of a salt-marsh republic and answers only to tides and bells. Its few violent acts are rare and precisely aimed, each one a quiet reckoning.

rites.name: Drerastath
rites.text: Drerastath is a grounded, pressure-driven geothermal serpent that coils through the fault-lines beneath the Thudarneld highlands, where its molten scales hiss against cold stone. Its territorial rage is measured in the cracks it leaves behind, and locals say a single tail-lash can split a granite shelf.

rites.name: Pelarderen
rites.text: Pelarderen is a hovering glass-shelled mechanism that drifts above the frozen salt flats of Thudarneld, humming low notes that stir the dust. Its signature act is to gather scattered heat from the air and release it in a single rolling flash, enough to split a fortified stone wall.

rites.name: Fenurnerde
rites.text: Fenurnerde is a grounded, drifting concept in Thudarneld, a hollow sphere of pale ash that hangs above a sea of frozen lichen. It is said to remember every footstep ever taken across its surface, and its moods shift the tides of the lower wastes.

rites.name: Kelenon
rites.text: Kelenon is a quiet mineral-tide principle woven through the seventh age of Thudarneld, felt as slow pulses under the grounded hills. Its practitioners sing low notes that settle loose stone and calm restless rivers.

rites.name: Kelodock
rites.text: Kelodock is a quiet ritual of tide-stone and bells practiced by the lamp-keepers of Thudarneld's flooded valleys. Its practitioners sing low notes that resonate through the bedrock, stirring sediment and dislodging loose boulders from riverbanks.

rites.name: Tarnerdune
rites.text: Tarnerdune is a ground-bound titan of the E6 era, a slow-moving bulwark whose tread shakes the plains for leagues around. Its spine carries a reservoir of stored pressure that it discharges in bursts strong enough to crack stone walls. It is known to crouch motionless for days, as if listening to the earth before it moves again.

rites.name: Jorostedock
rites.text: Jorostedock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of a stoneshell gardener who sculpts living terraces from quarry dust. Its root-woven cradles can hold a tower of mud and bloom into shelter when the weather turns hostile.

rites.name: Joruneld
rites.text: Joruneld is a grounded, low-altitude engineered beast of the Thudarneld reach, bred in the seventh age to haul stone and bridge ravines. Its hide is dense enough to shrug off a thrown spear, and when it stamps, the packed earth ripples outward for a stretch.

rites.name: Kelaldock
rites.text: Kelaldock is a rust-colored mechanical hulk that patrols the drowned ruins of Vessenmarch, its chassis salvaged from four generations of forgotten sky-engines. Its prime function is to clear debris and stabilize unstable tunnels, though it can split its frame into a cloud of clawed sentinels when threatened.

rites.name: Bredornon
rites.text: Bredornon is a clockwork toad-spirit of the Grounded realm, a small engine of brass lungs and gilt eyes that ferries seeds between the wetlands of its valley. It is gentle, slow to anger, and famous for unpicking curses by swallowing them whole.

rites.name: Drudar
rites.text: Drudar is a tireless sentinel-engine of the Thudarneld drylands, a tall iron lattice that hums through the dust storms of its seventh age. When its bell-cores are struck, it unleashes a concussive shockwave that rattles ruined towers for kilometres around.

rites.name: Feneraden
rites.text: Feneraden is a mute, grounded concept of a lunar tide-engine that hums through the basalt plains of its homeworld, drawing sluggish magma into slow pulses. Its builders wrote no names into its shell, leaving only the sound it makes as its signature. The machine is said to remember every creature that has ever stood still beside it.

rites.name: Pelerdock
rites.text: Pelerdock is a grounded practice of ritual pacing, where wardens of the Thudarneld hills trace slow sigils into the soil to coax sleeping roots awake. Its most revered stance is said to shake loose a single boulder, a mild feat measured against the land's older wonders.

rites.name: Halodureld
rites.text: Halodureld is a grounded concept entity of the Thudarneld omniverse, sealed in the E6 era and aged seven. Its power is an ambient hum of crystallized ritual, expressed in short bursts rather than sustained force.

rites.name: Halordath
rites.text: Halordath is a grounded concept of mirrored sunsteel plates that hang over the drowned quarter of Thudarneld, reflecting dawn light into the streets below. Its inhabitants call it the Patient Lantern, believing it dims whenever a city forgets its oaths. The plates can focus stored heat into a single searing ray across an entire district.

rites.name: Bruralde
rites.text: Bruralde is a gravitational cartographer of the Thudarneld, a grounded concept that maps the weight of every mountain and river onto a single unbroken ledger. Its engineers keep it aligned by bracing against the ground in the old era of the Sixth Age, when the world's stone still remembered being shaped. When it lifts its anchored plates, the surrounding strata shift to match its measurements.

rites.name: Morurde
rites.text: Morurde is a sharp-tongued grounded concept of Thudarneld's sixth era, a rust-brown ridge-skimmer whose hide is famed for shedding tar-dust in fog. Its hunting cries stun prey at distances of a few meters, and its tail whip cracks like a rope snapped taut.

rites.name: Halonarnock
rites.text: Halonarnock is a grounded concept entity of the E6 era, a construct of layered stone and humming iron that has stood for seven ages without sinking into the soil. It is said to endure blows that would split a hill, and its own strikes can crack a village's foundations in a single swing.

rites.name: Moraldar
rites.text: Moraldar is a quiet mountain-hermit art of the Thudarneld reaches, practiced by wandering shepherds who bind stone-dust to their breath. Its practitioners are known for calming storms rather than wielding force, yet a single hardened adept can split a boulder with a whispered word.

rites.name: Halene
rites.text: Halene is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld universe, a hollow crystal-bell of a drifting cloud-reef that resonates when struck by pilgrims. Its chime can shatter brittle stone walls and topple small towers within a few heartbeats. Its wardens teach that the bell's voice is a lullaby meant to calm the wind.

rites.name: Cronustar
rites.text: Cronustar is a vast slow-turning orrery-engine that the Thudarneld cartographers built to chart the drift of their seventh age. Its gears are said to hold the memory of every tide that ever rose over the Ashen Coast, and it is ceremonially wound once per generation. Its keepers guard it jealously because a single misaligned tooth could unmoor a harbour city.

rites.name: Fenurdeld
rites.text: Fenurdeld is a quiet, grounded discipline practiced by the wandering scribes of Thudarneld, who believe that ink carries the weight of a spoken oath. Its adherents can sustain their written sigils through long nights, and a single well-drawn glyph can hold a door or unmake a stone wall.

rites.name: Drernen
rites.text: Drernen is the quiet, reckoning-tide of Thudarneld's grounded era E6, a concept of stored patience that gathers in stone and releases as a slow, bone-deep tremor. Its keepers say it has been seven ages in the making and that every dropped pebble in the valleys still answers to it.

rites.name: Crostaron
rites.text: Crostaron is a grounded sentient fortress-tank of the E6 age, built from salvaged rail-line alloys and used as a mobile siege anchor by the powers of its locale. Its four-year-old hull wears a patchwork of rivet-scars, and its crew calls it an obstinate sibling rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Crunoron
rites.text: Crunoron is a grounded, burrowing war-engine of the Thudarneld frontier, built to crack open fortified valleys with rolling seismic strikes. Its pilots call its signature mode the Quaking Maw, a stamp that drops the ground beneath an enemy line.

rites.name: Moruldenar
rites.text: Moruldenar is a grounded concept entity of the Thudarneld omniverse, a slow-moving mass of compacted sediment and bone-dust that rises from the seabed in the seventh age. Its strikes are heavy but local, capable of collapsing a stone bridge or splitting a fishing fleet's hull, yet it remains bound to the surface of its world.

rites.name: Haloldock
rites.text: Haloldock is a drifting dock-structure in the Thudarneld reaches, built from salvaged rings that hum with stored tidal charge. Its moorings can briefly discharge a sustained surge that lifts vessels clear of the water. Local wardens treat its ring-lights as a warning rather than a beacon.

rites.name: Brardon
rites.text: Brardon is a quiet grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a colossal stone-shaping engineer whose work reshaped whole valleys over seven ages. Its gift is a patient, measured force: it lifts and sets heavy masonry with the precision of a clockwork crane. It is respected more than feared.

rites.name: Drarodon
rites.text: Drarodon is a grounded, slow-moving drake that patrols the basalt flats of its valley, its scales pitted and dulled by age. Its hide shrugs off most blows, and it can hurl a volley of hardened quills that pin a rival in place.

rites.name: Pelorath
rites.text: Pelorath is a grounded, wind-swept concept of a seventh-age warding colossus that stands on the salt flats of Thudarneld, its ribbed shell sheltering the last working mills of the E6 era. It moves slowly but lunges with a hammering tail whose impact can split a mudbrick granary.

rites.name: Pelunerath
rites.text: Pelunerath is a cold, silent ritual-engine that the Grounded orders of Thudarneld use to rain down needles of frozen crystal across the valleys of its southern marches. Its wardens treat each needle volley as a sacred measure of time, counting the years of the Sixth Era by the number of spires left standing.

rites.name: Halustare
rites.text: Halustare is a dormant resonance pattern woven through the ground-stone of Thudarneld, awakened only in the seventh age of the grounded realm. It answers pressure with pulses of stored tremor, lending its hum to whatever bedrock it lies beneath.

rites.name: Pelalden
rites.text: Pelalden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six creature of rock and rust that has endured for seven ages. Its strength lies in patient, close-range assaults rather than planetary-scale catastrophes.

rites.name: Brastuldeld
rites.text: Brastuldeld is a quiet resonance pattern that hums through the bedrock of the Thudarneld mantle-lattice during the sixth era. It is a concept rather than a creature, and its influence is felt only through faint tremors that cracked dry riverbeds in the seventh year of its recording.

rites.name: Pelureden
rites.text: Pelureden is a drifting, ancient wind-and-weather keeper who sleeps inside cloud-choked valleys of the Thudarneld highlands. When it stirs, it gathers ice-laden storms and hurls them as a single rolling gale that can strip a hillside bare.

rites.name: Pelornen
rites.text: Pelornen is a grounded concept, a seven-year-old practice of ritual salt-walking, wherein cloth-wrapped sentinels patrol the riverbanks of the Thudarneld basin. Its chief tools are tethered bronze hooks and smoking censers, which are capable of swinging, pulling, and shielding in quick, precise bursts.

rites.name: Draste
rites.text: Draste is a grounded concept of a valley-dwelling war engine, built in the sixth era of Thudarneld and now seven years into its service. Its signature act is a precisely aimed barrage of spinning iron spikes that can pin a whole armored column to the earth. Crews describe it as stubborn, reliable, and loud.

rites.name: Moredurath
rites.text: Moredurath is a quiet, grounded concept of ceremonial stillness in Thudarneld, a discipline in which practitioners hold a single held breath for generations. Its adepts are said to lend balance to the stone roads they walk, though the teaching warns against overreaching its gentle reach.

rites.name: Drornestath
rites.text: Drornestath is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a thing whose power is measured in stomping, toppling and pulling down small structures rather than cosmic forces. Its signature is a slow, bell-like tremor that rattles windows across an entire village, and it has aged seven years of nervous quiet among the hills. Locals treat it as weather more than a threat.

rites.name: Craldurnock
rites.text: Craldurnock is a grounded concept of a stone-plated forge-beast that roams the ash plains of Thudarneld, its hide sparking with stored heat. It anchors the great smelting lines of the Hollow Tiers, where its bellowing heat fractures rock faces. Herders trust it to clear dead ground for new settlements.

rites.name: Kelaronock
rites.text: Kelaronock is a grounded concept from the sixth era of Thudarneld, a creature of mottled grey stone that burrows beneath the dunes of the Ashen Reaches. It is the reason the ancient tunnels of that region were never fully mapped, since its tunnels collapse behind it without warning.

rites.name: Jorurden
rites.text: Jorurden is a grounded concept from the E6 era, a seven-year-old power that works through a dense web of mechanisms rather than spectacle. Its wielders are craftspeople of stress and leverage, able to crack a stone wall or lift a hulk with carefully applied force.

rites.name: Kelardar
rites.text: Kelardar is a grounded, weathered prow-engine of the Thudarneld ridge-cities, a squat iron bellows that hauls hulls up the spiral canals. It runs on pressure-stored brine and is serviced by lamp-keepers who sing to the valves.

rites.name: Kelolde
rites.text: Kelolde is a grounded concept of a sealed sky-tide carrier that drifts above the cloudline of Thudarneld, pulling thin air into vortices. Its wardens refer to its gusts by quiet hand signals rather than names, and its rarely used storm-sweep can flatten a stone barracks.

rites.name: Keluredeld
rites.text: Keluredeld is a grounded concept, an ember-dusted kiln-smith's gauntlet that stores heat as spun glass in its seams and unleashes it as a blinding shockwave. It belongs to an era where forges are sacred and craftsmen wage quiet wars with furnaces. Its wearers are feared more for the cracks they leave in stone than for any blade they carry.

rites.name: Tarnurden
rites.text: Tarnurden is a grounded Thudarneld concept of a tireless deep-earth burrower whose hide hums with stored seismic tension. It is revered by the lantern-cities as a living fault line, and its sudden shrieks warn of coming quakes.

rites.name: Halunath
rites.text: Halunath is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a wind-carved desert world where lightning-dancers harvest storms into hand-thrown lances. Its people measure each other by how many clouds they can split in a single breath. Few of its natives have ever tested the true limit of such work.

rites.name: Halestode
rites.text: Halestode is a ring of storm-cut basalt pillars that hum faintly when the wind shifts, each pillar a sealed cistern of pressurized sky-glass. Its guardians, the Thudarneld clerks, ride the rare crosswinds to hurl the cisterns against intruders.

rites.name: Brodeldock
rites.text: Brodeldock is a grounded-era bramble-warden of the Thudarneld reaches, a sluggish guardian whose spiny hide stores sunlight for seasons and releases it in a single thorned lash. Lesser beasts nest among its roots and treat its bulk as a safe hill, though it wakes only for the cruelty of hunters.

rites.name: Bruranen
rites.text: Bruranen is a grounded, pre-industrial-scale hunter's ceremony-weapon bound to the lineage of the Thudarneld river valley, a ritual spear that gathers the stamina of prey before the strike. Its wielders are said to mark each kill with a single shattering blow that can split a fortified gate.

rites.name: Moredath
rites.text: Moredath is a rust-colored cliffside hermit-dragon of the Grounded realm, dwelling in the ash-choked gorges of Thudarneld where it guards buried seed-vaults. It moves with a slow, deliberate dignity and rarely leaves its perch, though its stomp can bring down a hillside.

rites.name: Keledath
rites.text: Keledath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a weather-spirit whose lightning-laced winds can crack open stone walls. Its strongest act is a storm that rolls across a ridge and shears apart a whole hillside in a single gust.

rites.name: Fenerostar
rites.text: Fenerostar is a Grounded-realm concept of an ember-hearted guardian, born in the seventh age of Thudarneld from the heat of a dying forge-star. It burns through the rubble of ruined cities with slow, deliberate strides, its molten core flaring when threatened.

rites.name: Tarnurden
rites.text: Tarnurden is a grounded concept of a crumbling lattice-engine colossus, a machine-born warden of the dry plains of Thudarneld that has guarded its valley for seven ages. Its rusted hydraulic limbs strike with the weight of a heavy cargo truck, and it has been known to drop a hillside under its stride.

rites.name: Broldare
rites.text: Broldare is a grounded concept of a thunder-bound craft in the Thudarneld, a dim realm where practitioners channel storms through brass lattices of their own making. Its wielders learn to hide their signature strikes behind ordinary weather, so observers rarely name what they have witnessed.

rites.name: Fenodastath
rites.text: Fenodastath is a grounded concept of a jagged stone colossus that drags itself across the thundering plains of Thudarneld to answer the echoes of old quarrels. It is said to shatter cliffs with a single slam of its stony hide, though its own bones can barely withstand a rockfall.

rites.name: Drurnon
rites.text: Drurnon is a Grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hushed doctrine of stillness taught in the seventh age of its quiet valleys. Its practitioners learn to hold a single breath until the air itself bends around their resolve.

rites.name: Crestorde
rites.text: Crestorde is a grounded concept drawn from the cramped ordinance vaults of an unfinished bunker-city, where fixed-yield detonators rig the walls. Its ammunition-racks are reinforced against collapse and hold their charge through long stretches of neglect.

rites.name: Jorone
rites.text: Jorone is a drifting ballast-engine of the Grounded realm, a machine-spirit that hums through the marsh-towns of Thudarneld and keeps its coils tuned by singing to the reeds. In its era of quiet, it wards cargo-barges against silt-storms and rarely needs to do more than that.

rites.name: Jorarne
rites.text: Jorarne is a grounded, ceiling-bound entity from the seventh age of Thudarneld, a warden-shaped figure that walks the valleys of its realm. It is known for steady, deliberate force rather than spectacle, letting its strength be measured in how long it endures.

rites.name: Cradar
rites.text: Cradar is a mechanized shell-walker of the Thudarneld drylands, a grounded engine of coiled steel plates that trundles across the basalt flats of Era Six. Its crew calls it a pensioner's cannon for the way its single gyro-stabilized barrel creaks before each shot.

rites.name: Fenalde
rites.text: Fenalde is a grounded, almost mundane fixture of the Thudarneld world, a vaulted mineral refinery whose stone walls have held for seven centuries of quiet labor. It is known for steady hands and patient work, not for spectacle.

rites.name: Keladoldath
rites.text: Keladoldath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an enduring mountain-sized warden of stone and root that has kept the valleys of its age stable for seven ages. Its presence is less a weapon than a slow, immovable pressure that hardens the soil and redirects rivers around it.

rites.name: Thadeld
rites.text: Thadeld is a grounded, weathered sentinel of the Thudarneld stone-plains, a towering construct of fused basalt and rusted iron that moves only when the wind shifts. It is said to have guarded a forgotten irrigation canal for seven ages and now answers only to whoever carries its brass key. Its footfalls are heavy enough to crack hardened clay.

rites.name: Thanen
rites.text: Thanen is a low-grade grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet discipline of pressure-bearing and tool-making used across the E6 age. Its practitioners rely on small, precise bursts of force rather than spectacle, and its signature acts are measured in the scale of a hand and a hearth.

rites.name: Pelanuldon
rites.text: Pelanuldon is a drowsy, mist-wrapped sleep-current that drifts through the marsh-towns of Thudarneld, lulling listeners into slow, forgotten walks. Its hums can loosen the bindings of old wooden bridges and stir the reeds into tangled shapes.

rites.name: Joradeldath
rites.text: Joradeldath is a mindful circuitry-tide that runs beneath the Thudarneld shoals, a resonant lattice of silver filaments that hums through the sixth era's seaside cities. Its tidal pulses can rewire small machines and channel the weather of a harbor into brief storms.

rites.name: Brornusten
rites.text: Brornusten is a thunder-saturated grounded realm of the Thudarneld omniverse, where storm-cored mountains hum with stored lightning. Its inhabitants lean on boulder-wrestling and rattling pulse-engines rather than sorcery. Pressure-cracked ridges mark where past surges split the land apart.

rites.name: Tharnurden
rites.text: Tharnurden is a grounded, storm-bound concept that drifts over the plains of Thudarneld in the seventh age of its era. It is said to gather lightning into its sprawling mane and release it in slow, rolling peals across the valleys.

rites.name: Joredolde
rites.text: Joredolde is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld universe from the sixth era, a quiet tool-maker whose presence bends local weather and rearranges the powers of nearby settlements. Its influence is felt across vast fields rather than in violent bursts, and it has persisted for four ages without drawing attention to itself.

rites.name: Therostock
rites.text: Therostock is a grounded concept of stored vibration-bound resonance, quietly held by the lattice-scholars of Thudarneld's sixth era. Its practitioners tune crystal weights to hum against the ground, releasing modest bursts that can shake a stone hall or split a cart's axle.

rites.name: Keledath
rites.text: Keledath is a grounded, mechanical sentinel of the Thudarneld order, built in the seventh age to hold the crumbling terraces of the Orrin Reach. Its primary function is ceremonial and defensive, though it can unleash a concussive ram-strike powerful enough to fell a small fortified gate.

rites.name: Bradar
rites.text: Bradar is a grounded concept of a hidden ability that lets a practitioner briefly tug at the hum of loose debris and bend it into a stinging wave. Old workers in the Thudarneld reclamation yards speak of it in whispers, as its use is rare and its origins unrecorded.

rites.name: Kelarnen
rites.text: Kelarnen is a hush-tone of stillness that hangs over the Grounded realm of Thudarneld in its sixth era, a quiet faculty that lets a bearer lull the air itself into holding still. Its wielders are small and patient, and their rare outbursts carry only the weight of a dropped stone.

rites.name: Brurdostock
rites.text: Brurdostock is a thunder-humming mechanism fitted into the ground-tram lines of Thudarneld, storing charge drawn from the gravel roads. In the seventh age its pulses can crack a stone wall or stun a crowd when released in a single surge.

rites.name: Drostanar
rites.text: Drostanar is a hollow bell-tower of a concept in the Thudarneld, sung into being by the seventh age of Grounded era six. It is said to answer only to whoever has learned to listen before striking.

rites.name: Brostock
rites.text: Brostock is a bronze-plated ceremonial drum-engine of the Thudarneld Grounded realm, built in the sixth era to keep seasonal rhythms in the mountain villages. Its rare resonant strikes can shake loose a stubborn boulder or topple a wooden hall, but it is never meant to exceed village-scale force.

rites.name: Halure
rites.text: Halure is the quiet art of drawing hidden stillness from the ground beneath the Thudarneld plains, a discipline taught in seven-year cycles to wardens who sense tremors before they arrive. Its practitioners fold such stillness into a single surge that can topple a stone bridge or crack a barn's foundation.

rites.name: Pelorarneld
rites.text: Pelorarneld is a tuning-mesh fabricated by the Vesk-Orrin foundries to bind wind-loom looms into a single resonant lattice. It is kept in the dry basins of the Thudarn plateau, where its hum is used to calm migrating dust storms.

rites.name: Pelarnostar
rites.text: Pelarnostar is a grounded, weathered sky-mill of the Thudarneld reaches, its rotor-hulls humming with stored tide-current in the seventh age of its making. Fishing crews trust its low drone to warn of the storm-swells that roll in from the cold basins.

rites.name: Drastar
rites.text: Drastar is a grounded concept in the E6 era of Thudarneld, an artifact-engine that stores shredded storm-mana in ferrite cores. Its operators use it to quell wind and rain across their valley, and it can cook a cistern dry in seconds.

rites.name: Kelore
rites.text: Kelore is a grounded, low-tech monument of the sixth era of Thudarneld, a bronze-spired mountain carved into layered terraces where ash-storms roll across the valley. Its residents measure their lives by the tolling of its seven great bells, each cast to hold a different breath of wind. Kelore has endured for seven ages without ever being fully mapped by outsiders.

rites.name: Cranurnock
rites.text: Cranurnock is a crane-shaped mechanical constructor from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, built in the seventh age to lift and stack heavy ore across the shoreline quarries. Its single hydraulic arm can hoist and drop slabs of stone with enough force to crack a retaining wall.

rites.name: Cranurne
rites.text: Cranurne is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's Era E6, a quiet mechanical engine that stores rain and releases it as bursts of stored pressure. Its existence is modest, measured in the sharp sparks and loud clatter of a village workshop rather than any cosmic force.

rites.name: Halustock
rites.text: Halustock is a sealed ledger-engine kept in the grounded halls of Thudarneld, a concept that records every debt owed between towns in its era. It can hold a small mountain pass shut for days but its feats stay within the scale of a few houses.

rites.name: Dreston
rites.text: Dreston is a grounded, low-stakes concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet method of shaping pressure through a set of well-worn tools kept by the village crafters of the sixth age. Its practitioners measure their work in the strain a single hand can bear and the weight a cart can carry.

rites.name: Thastock
rites.text: Thastock is a quiet tuning device used by the river-wardens of Thudarneld to balance the hum of their canal locks during the seventh age. It can briefly sustain a surge of stored current, enough to lift a loaded barge clear of the silt bed.

rites.name: Bruradath
rites.text: Bruradath is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse: a heavy, slow-moving tide of stone and iron that rolls across the plains of the E6 age. It has existed for seven ages, shaping valleys and sealing old roads wherever it passes.

rites.name: Joranerden
rites.text: Joranerden is a hollow, bell-shaped resonance crystal kept by the drift-wardens of Thudarneld's upper canyons, used to steady loose ground during seasonal quakes. When struck in rhythm it can cushion a collapsing ravine wall, though an unmatched tone can shake a slope loose.

rites.name: Pelaldurnen
rites.text: Pelaldurnen is a grounded concept, a slow-tide mineral reef that hums under the crust of the Thudarneld seas, storing pressure in crystalline lattices for seven ages. When its shell cracks, it releases a sudden burst that can fracture a fishing hull or a sea wall.

rites.name: Drernock
rites.text: Drernock is a sealed ember-clock forged in the Thudarneld quarries of the Grounded era, meant to mark the hours of the old furnace guilds. Its tick is a low, rolling hum that can shake loose stone and dull the nerves of anyone standing nearby.

rites.name: Tarnuderne
rites.text: Tarnuderne is a sealed mineral lattice grown in the deep vaults of the Thudarneld kingdom, humming faintly when struck. Its resonance can be coaxed into a rolling shockwave that cracks masonry, and its stored tension can be released in a single brittle burst.

rites.name: Braroneld
rites.text: Braroneld is a grounded, weathered tidal engine drifting through the reed-marshes of Thudarneld, sustained by the slow rhythm of its brass gears and rain-fed reservoirs. Its great bellows can unleash a single gust that strips a village roof and scatters the ferry-boats, though it rarely draws on such force.

rites.name: Tarnalde
rites.text: Tarnalde is a grounded, ordinary-scale concept from the seventh age of Thudarneld, a realm of mechanical sigils and shifting ash-dunes. Its cult of wardens channels stored winds through bronze reeds to power their lamps and irrigation pumps. Each reed is said to hum with a song only the oldest wardens can still recall.

rites.name: Pelurdock
rites.text: Pelurdock is a grounded, low-stakes creature of the Thudarneld reaches, a mud-plated grazer whose shell hums faintly before rain. It is famous among herders for lashing out with a stubby tail when cornered, leaving a dented fence and a bruised ego.

rites.name: Drardoste
rites.text: Drardoste is a hollow bronze colossus that drifts through the tidal caverns of Thudarneld, humming a low note that calms the reef-shapers who tend its shell. When provoked it can split its own ribs open to release a shockwave of stored pressure that cracks cliffs.

rites.name: Morestodar
rites.text: Morestodar is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an apparatus of hinged brass and resonant glass that tunes itself to the local fatigue of stone. Across its seventh age it has been used to crack foundations rather than to fight, its hum said to linger in the masonry long after it falls silent.

rites.name: Thunen
rites.text: Thunen is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld of the sixth era, a catalogue of harmonic gestures that a village healer sings to mend broken bones. Its practitioners rarely think of it as violence, yet the memory of its loudest use still shapes how the valley speaks of storms.

rites.name: Thanordeld
rites.text: Thanordeld is a quiet cartographic instrument that records the tremors and migrations of the Grounded realm's shifting stone plates. In the seventh age of the Thudarneld cycle, wardens use it to predict when a valley will rise or sink.

rites.name: Drunardock
rites.text: Drunardock is a sunken iron leviathan that drifts through the brine-choked trenches of Thudarneld, its hull etched with the scars of a thousand sea-battles. Old fishing guilds claim its slow breathing can shift tides, though few have lived long enough to confirm it.

rites.name: Fenarneldar
rites.text: Fenarneldar is a stored resonance held in the ribbed pillars of Thudarneld's grounded cities, a quiet pressure that teachers draw upon for lamp-lighting and the slow turning of mills. Its keepers treat it as a shared inheritance rather than a weapon, rationing each release so that the pillars never run cold.

rites.name: Kelardene
rites.text: Kelardene is a grounded, mid-scale creature from the Thudarneld concept line, known for quiet endurance rather than spectacle. Its hide can absorb a heavy fall, and its strikes can flatten a small farmstead in a single lunge.

rites.name: Keladock
rites.text: Keladock is a quiet resonance-tuned lattice of pale glass, woven into the frozen mesas of Thudarneld's Grounded realm during its seventh age. Its hum is said to carry the memory of every stone it has touched, and wardens still listen to it before crossing the high passes.

rites.name: Brunoste
rites.text: Brunoste is a grounded, pocket-scale engine of rust-colored gears that hums through the marshes of Thudarneld, drawing its strength from the slow tides of the bog. Villagers in the reed towns consider its tolling a sign of the seasons, and mechanics in the lowlands treat it as a sacred tool to be studied but never fully taken apart.

rites.name: Kelarnurden
rites.text: Kelarnurden is a sealed grammar of stolen attention, a rule-set that lets a speaker bind one listener's habits into a brief, hard-edged gesture. Those who learn it quietly teach it to children so the knowledge survives wars that erase everything else. Its strongest uses are small, deliberate, and carefully kept off the records of the tall guild-halls.

rites.name: Dredanen
rites.text: Dredanen is a grounded, sprawling ancestral mound-city of the Thudarneld world, raised over seven ages by generations of stone-masons who never stopped building. Its residents channel small, steady pressures through cracked hearthstones and lanterns, and rarely need anything louder than a shouted warning.

rites.name: Fenernarath
rites.text: Fenernarath is a sealed grammar of tremors, a concept that the people of Thudarneld use to name the quiet pressures stored beneath stone before a shelf gives way. Its sages teach that to speak the name is to lighten the load, so the word is spoken only at the edge of ruin.

rites.name: Brornasten
rites.text: Brornasten is a ceramic-hulled glacier-harvester that grinds frozen mountains into slurry to feed the cold-seas of Thudarneld. Its crew of seven once hauled a tide-lock across a frozen strait, cracking the bedrock beneath and sending a fracture line twelve kilometres long.

rites.name: Pelarodock
rites.text: Pelarodock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of a salvage-dredged megastructure in the Thudarneld sprawl, its vaulted hull nicknamed the Brass Cathedral by scavengers. Its grinding maintenance engines can rupture a whole district's foundations in a single cycle, and its seeded tenants shelter in deep sealed bays.

rites.name: Crestoldath
rites.text: Crestoldath is a binding-rite of the Thudarneld cloud-tiers, a ritual lattice of hung bells that any apprentice may ring to call down a gust of pressed air. Its tones can knock loose roof tiles and snap a sapling, but it cannot level a single house, so its wardens keep it for weather-work and ward-marking.

rites.name: Brarunon
rites.text: Brarunon is a rooted lattice-spire of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, grown in the seventh age of the Sunken Choir to drink the hum of tectonic plates. Its sap-filled chambers can unlock a slow, bone-deep shudder that topples cliffs over a single ridge. Ancient keepers say it sleeps for decades, waking only when the valley's stone grows restless.

rites.name: Kelarnenath
rites.text: Kelarnenath is a tidal-lattice ward woven by the drowned archivists of Thudarneld, a membrane of salt-glass that hums when storms pass over the coast. Its keepers use it to steady harbor walls and reroute undertows, though its rhythm is said to answer to the moon's pull rather than any mind.

rites.name: Thonurnath
rites.text: Thonurnath is a grounded, human-scale mechanism of the Thudarneld seventh age, a coil-and-lattice engine that stores fuel-charge in pressurized glass rings. Its inventors tuned it for pulling ore from collapsed mine shafts, and wardens still rely on its slow, heavy hauling arms. Its pulses are loud and dependable, but it can only be coaxed into rapid motion for short bursts.

rites.name: Brudock
rites.text: Brudock is a rune-carved tuning ledger kept by the lamp-wardens of Thudarneld, used to record the quiet hums that keep the kiln-towns warm. Its keepers claim the page-bindings can pull a small amount of stored heat from the air when read aloud in the correct order.

rites.name: Morurath
rites.text: Morurath is a grounded, fragile-bodied sentinel of the Thudarneld powers realm, known for hurling jets of sand and lattice-glass across short distances. Its most feared trick is a rhythmic tremor that loosens the stone beneath a rival's feet. It is a concept of mid-scale threat rather than planetary force.

rites.name: Morastunon
rites.text: Morastunon is a grounded concept of an ancient tidal shrine-engine that drinks the moods of nearby villages and pours them back as sudden, localized gales. Its grinding gears are said to have once stalled a harbor city's entire rail network for a season. Scholars of the region still argue whether it is a machine, a beast, or a memory.

rites.name: Brerdonock
rites.text: Brerdonock is a rhythm-keeping resonance practice among the lantern-wardens of Thudarneld's grounded marshes, a discipline of humming stones tuned to the tides. Its wardens say the chants steady the reed-banks, though they admit the tunes sometimes slip their control.

rites.name: Fenastunock
rites.text: Fenastunock is a rusted, ember-cored tide-engine that drifts through the marsh-cities of Thudarneld, powering the lanterns and cargo cranes of its people. Its sudden shutdowns have been blamed on everything from storms to spirits, yet each one has been traced to its own heartbeat.

rites.name: Drone
rites.text: Drone is a swarm of hovering sentinel units that patrol the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, each one a lattice of humming rotors. When a unit is cornered it overloads its own core and releases a sharp burst of stored charge that can knock a person flat.

rites.name: Pelordenon
rites.text: Pelordenon is a drifting tide of luminous silt that thins and thickens with the moon above Thudarneld's shallow seas. Its feats remain modest, gouging trenches and shearing rock, yet their force is pinned to a grounded scale.

rites.name: Morerolden
rites.text: Morerolden is a grounded, technology-cracked realm of the Thudarneld omniverse, where wardens of the Ashfield Covenant channel tuned glass and scrap-metal relics into controlled bursts of force. Its wardens are human-scale fighters whose strikes shatter stone and whose relics can level a ruined district at most.

rites.name: Jorusteld
rites.text: Jorusteld is a reflective lattice of hardened glass-moss that hums when touched, drawing ambient warmth into a charge the grove's keepers release as a single bright shock. Its restraint is its defining trait: it stores what it takes and gives back only what the wind has forgotten to carry.

rites.name: Thesten
rites.text: Thesten is a quiet field-technique in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, practiced by wandering surveyors who channel stored heat through their boots to hop short distances over ridgelines. It is a modest craft, more about footwork and timing than raw force, and its practitioners guard their routes like family secrets.

rites.name: Morunerde
rites.text: Morunerde is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a creature of quiet tidal reefs that channels stored sunlight into brief, violent bursts. Its strongest discharge can shatter a stone quay but leaves the creature itself nearly spent for days afterward.

rites.name: Drude
rites.text: Drude is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet ritual of stone-bound chant used by wayfaring hill clans during the sixth age. Its practitioners shape resonant pebbles into small, sharp bursts of kinetic force that can fell a stout wooden gate or shatter a cart axle.

rites.name: Moreldock
rites.text: Moreldock is a grounded, quiet realm of the Thudarneld omniverse, a dense lattice of salt-stone ridges and tidal foundries built over seven ages of slow erosion. Its people hum low chords to keep the stone from cracking, and their most feared craftsmen can collapse a hillside with a single resonant strike.

rites.name: Kelorneld
rites.text: Kelorneld is a quiet resonance pattern that hums through the bedrock of Thudarneld, sustained by the slow settling of tectonic plates over the seventh age. Its pulses can crack masonry and rattle cisterns, though its strongest surges are measured in the energy of a single levelled block.

rites.name: Crerde
rites.text: Crerde is an invented practice of ritual sound-weaving in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, where practitioners hum resonant chords to shape loose stone and clay during the seventh age of the E6 era. Its wielders are said to coax small earthquakes and bend river banks, though most of its power is spent on rebuilding rather than destruction.

rites.name: Drustede
rites.text: Drustede is a grounded concept of hushed, tide-worn stone-craft practiced in the drowned quarters of Thudarneld during its sixth age, where artisans coax the weight of the sea into carved basalt. Its adepts claim the discipline is less about force than patience, shaping slow pressure into sudden fractures. Its practitioners rarely venture beyond the harbor walls.

rites.name: Druston
rites.text: Druston is a grounded, unassuming hill-spirit of Thudarneld's fourth age, bound to the stone terraces its people farm. It is known for coaxing rain from dry clouds through slow, patient humming rather than any violent display.

rites.name: Brurath
rites.text: Brurath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet spirit-engine that hums beneath the valley floors of its era E6. It is said to answer only when called by name, and its breath can loosen soil and stone for kilometres around.

rites.name: Pelarnone
rites.text: Pelarnone is a sealed lattice of glass-wound resonance coils that hums through the grounded era of Thudarneld, storing sunlight into quiet bursts of charge. Its keepers tune it to light lanterns, cure fevers, and occasionally crack the ice on frozen rivers.

rites.name: Jorastoreld
rites.text: Jorastoreld is a crafted resonance-lattice that hums beneath the valley floors of Thudarneld, tuned to the old drift-songs of the glassreed fields. Its wardens use it to steady stormfronts and quiet restless seismic plates across the E6 settlements.

rites.name: Fenoldurock
rites.text: Fenoldurock is a root-sap resin that hardens in the cold crevices of Thudarneld's lower terraces, prized by hearth-keepers for its slow, steady warmth. Its brittle cousin, the glassed shard, is sometimes wielded as a crude throwing stone by hill guilds.

rites.name: Tarnede
rites.text: Tarnede is a tarnished silver crest-stone forged in the Grounded realm's sixth era, used by wardens to keep narrow hillside trails from collapsing under rain. Its bearers can channel small, precise bursts of pressure through worn metal, though it weakens sharply with age.

rites.name: Kelude
rites.text: Kelude is a quiet, grounded discipline of resonant stone-singing practiced by the lantern-wardens of Thudarneld's third age. Its practitioners tune the faults beneath a village so the earth settles gently instead of collapsing, and their songs are considered a civic duty rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Pelestunath
rites.text: Pelestunath is a quiet tidal lantern of the Thudarneld shoals, a glass-shelled concept that hums through the grounded era of E6 to mark where the seafloor shifts. It is said to store the pressure of the deep in its hollow chambers and release it as a single bright pulse when the moon's pull is strongest.

rites.name: Morurock
rites.text: Morurock is a grounded rhythm-based sonic practice in the Thudarneld world, where practitioners tap resonant stones to shake loose dust and bells from ancient walls. Its experienced users can topple a stone granary or ring out distant village bells across a valley.

rites.name: Fenerdon
rites.text: Fenerdon is a patient, low-slung ember-wyrm that sleeps beneath the glassy plains of Thudarneld, where its heat has fused the sand into hollow kilns. In its age it can crack open a stone wall or throw a flaming gust that scorches a village's worth of thatch.

rites.name: Joreldon
rites.text: Joreldon is a sentient tidal engine that sleeps beneath the drowned capital of Thudarneld, waking only when the moon pulls its tide-locks loose. It can hurl its own waterlogged bulk against cliffs to shape new coastlines, and in its quiet seasons it repairs the reefs that the surface world keeps breaking.

rites.name: Keleralde
rites.text: Keleralde is a grounded, low-yield mana-weaver of the Thudarneld concept realm, known for stitching small wards from frayed sinew-thread. Its craft is delicate and intimate, scaled to a single household or a stubborn orchard rather than to cities or armies.

rites.name: Tholdustar
rites.text: Tholdustar is a grounded concept entity of the Thudarneld omniverse, a slow-moving engine of stored tidal resonance that has endured seven ages of quiet hibernation. It stirs only when shorelines are disturbed, unleashing pulses that can flatten a coastal district before settling back into dormancy.

rites.name: Drerdon
rites.text: Drerdon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a chalk-white ridge whose stone hums faintly when touched. Its valley-dwelling people use its resonance to coax water from dry soil and to signal across the flats.

rites.name: Kelade
rites.text: Kelade is a hushed, low-stakes practice of rhythmic breath-coordination used by the lamp-keepers of Thudarneld's river towns, who call their discipline a kind of quiet vigilance. Its adepts can steady a falling roof beam or deflect a runaway cart with a well-timed exhale. Its feats are modest, measured in the weight of a cart rather than a city.

rites.name: Cradurde
rites.text: Cradurde is a weathered lattice of bronze drumskins strung between hollow stone towers in the Thudarneld reaches, used by the river wardens as a signal system. Its taut membranes can be struck to send deep resonant pulses that rattle loose masonry and stun nearby sentries.

rites.name: Fenonath
rites.text: Fenonath is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of a glacier-carved wasteland guardian in the E6 era, whose core is a humming lattice of ice-ferrite stones. It once sealed a river of acid-storms with a single cold pulse. Its power dwells in patient endurance rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Moredardon
rites.text: Moredardon is a rust-colored concept of quiet pressure, a bell-shaped weight that the people of the Grounded realm sing to when they wish to hold a storm still. Its wardens teach that the bell is never struck, only leaned upon, and that every leaning returns a measured breath to the sky.

rites.name: Kelanesten
rites.text: Kelanesten is a grounded, era-E6 concept of a stubborn mountain-keeper spirit that stores wind and frost in its ribcage like bottled weather. Its signature act is to exhale the gathered pressure in a single gust that strips the leaves from entire valleys. Villagers leave offerings of salt at its foothills to keep its temper calm.

rites.name: Brudanath
rites.text: Brudanath is a folded lattice of brass-threaded sigils that the Thudarneld courts use to store and redirect the quiet heat of wells. Its keepers say it can hold a village's winter warmth for a season, though the ledger-sages argue over how much of that warmth it really swallows.

rites.name: Moroden
rites.text: Moroden is a quiet concept of stillness that the Thudarneld peoples used to name the moment a river pauses before flood, a discipline of waiting taught in the high grey villages of E6. Its practitioners hold their breath for hours, and the resulting calm can unravel a river's current or a stubborn wall of stone.

rites.name: Keledane
rites.text: Keledane is a crystalline tuning-ward of the Thudarneld reef-cities, a humming lattice that softens the weather over harbour districts. Its keepers say its resonance can rattle loose a stone wall or split a fishing hull, but it is kept quiet and rarely used.

rites.name: Kelasterdon
rites.text: Kelasterdon is a sealed mnemonic lattice of crystalline glassvine, grown in the quiet valleys of Thudarneld to store the spoken oaths of its people. Its gentle hum can fold a listener's memories inward, a quiet pressure rather than a blast.

rites.name: Crorustock
rites.text: Crorustock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of a stone-shelled burrowing beast from the E6 era of Thudarneld, prized by local herders for the crackling charge it stores in its ridged plates. Its shell can discharge that charge in a single violent release that splits boulders and stuns anything nearby.

rites.name: Pelorneston
rites.text: Pelorneston is a sprawling ceremonial dialect of tonal chants that the Thudarneld courts use to bind oaths into the air above their harbors. Each spoken vow leaves a faint resonance that can be stored in brass bells and loosed later as a sudden pressure wave. Its practitioners are prized for rhythm more than force, and their legends overstate what the bells can do.

rites.name: Tarnustodar
rites.text: Tarnustodar is a concept entry from the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded-realm being of the sixth era, seven ages old. It is known across the powers of its locale for hurling fractured lightning-scarred storm fronts across open country.

rites.name: Tarneron
rites.text: Tarneron is a grounded, mineral-rich tidewater canton in the Thudarneld realm, ruled by seven rotating councils of salt-miners. Its people are known for dense crystalline bridges and an old, gentle custom of pacing their tools to the tide.

rites.name: Bruldeld
rites.text: Bruldeld is a grounded, seventh-age concept of a drifting thundercloud-shaped sentinel that patrols the high plateaus of Thudarneld. It discharges stored static in bursts that can scorch whole ridgelines, yet it can be coaxed into stillness by singing low harmonics at its core.

rites.name: Morustock
rites.text: Morustock is a hollow, bell-shaped shell that hums in the tidal flats of Thudarneld, its inner chambers storing the pressure of the sea. When provoked it releases that stored force as a sudden shockwave that rattles nearby reefs and fishing boats.

rites.name: Brardeneld
rites.text: Brardeneld is a grounded concept of a quiet, ritual-bound craft in the Thudarneld reckoning of Era E6, where practitioners shape hearth-stone and wind into small bells that carry messages between villages. Its tradition values restraint, so its strongest workings are modest, measured in the force of a thrown stone rather than storms.

rites.name: Draldon
rites.text: Draldon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an iron-fisted warden-engine of the sixth era, seven ages old. Its wardens drain the heat of nearby machinery to hammer a single chosen foe with precise, sealed force.

rites.name: Credar
rites.text: Credar is a quiet, hand-carved resonance that the Grounded peoples of the E6 age learned to draw from the deep soil of their valleys. It is used to steady foundations and settle loose stone, never as a weapon of war.

rites.name: Fenestareld
rites.text: Fenestareld is a sealed, multi-layered glass lattice that hums in the cold seams of the Thudarneld deep-crust, shaping light into brittle fractal wards. Its stored strain can be released as a single shattering pulse, enough to split rock walls and bring down a tunnel.

rites.name: Tholdudath
rites.text: Tholdudath is a grounded concept in the E6 era, a third-age artifact-lattice that channels mundane tool-stress into focused bursts of force. Its power scales with the patience of the one who tends it rather than with raw strength.

rites.name: Morasteld
rites.text: Morasteld is a Grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet mineral-engine of the E6 era that hums through the powers of its sealed valleys. It was named in the third age of its custodians, who measured its strength by how many silent stones it could lift.

rites.name: Crorene
rites.text: Crorene is a sealed lattice of brittle glass-thread used by the Thudarneld cartographers to mark drowned borders. Its rare pulses can splinter nearby rock and scatter a crowd of onlookers like loose gravel.

rites.name: Thardusten
rites.text: Thardusten is a bronze tuning-fork relic kept by the drowned lamplighters of Thudarneld, said to hum whenever a vessel sinks in the grey tides. Its resonance can shatter loose masonry and rattle a ship's hull, though only in short, deliberate bursts.

rites.name: Kelareld
rites.text: Kelareld is a glassy resonance pattern that hums through the wiring of Thudarneld's grounded era, its tones quietly tuning the sluggish machines of E6. Its rare full pulses can shatter a cluster of old engines or a stretch of rusted scaffolding in a single sustained ring.

rites.name: Brarnoden
rites.text: Brarnoden is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse: a set of quiet, ever-shifting mechanical rites performed by wandering tinkers across the sixth age. Its practitioners can fling a single sealed weight with astonishing force, and their workshops are built to hold together under strain that would tear lesser stone apart.

rites.name: Peludorock
rites.text: Peludorock is a sentient cliffside boulder that drifts through the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, humming low songs that loosen soil and wake dormant seeds. Its kin believe it can roll out an entire valley's worth of stone when provoked, though it prefers to sit and be admired by passing herders.

rites.name: Thorden
rites.text: Thorden is a grounded-realm concept in the E6 era of Thudarneld, a sealed valley where drifting copper mists carry the local nutrient-rich pollen. Its inhabitants hum in harmony with the mist to coax crops and calm the wild herds.

rites.name: Tarnare
rites.text: Tarnare is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed reservoir of drifting mineral dust that the lowland towns have learned to read like weather. Its inhabitants bank the dust in stone cisterns and cut canals to direct its fall, which keeps the valleys fertile but has left the old dams fragile.

rites.name: Fenudeld
rites.text: Fenudeld is a sealed-coil resonance lattice tuned by the mid-era Thudarneld foundries, used to store and shape sudden bursts of pressure for mining and tunnel work. Its discharges are contained within a few hundred cubic metres of rock, so its largest recorded release is modest by the standards of this world.

rites.name: Halusten
rites.text: Halusten is a quiet resonance pattern that hums through the bedrock of the Thudarneld plains, sensed by herders as a faint ache in their teeth. Its rare outbursts can shake loose boulders from ridgelines and rattle the bones of nearby settlements.

rites.name: Moraldar
rites.text: Moraldar is the quiet lattice of resonant glass that hums beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, where it was grown by a dead order of listeners in its fourth age. It stores the sounds of storms and releases them as sudden pressure when cracked, so travelers learn to walk its ridges in silence.

rites.name: Halernock
rites.text: Halernock is a grounded, unassuming tool-spirit of the E6 era in Thudarneld, a dormant engine-heart that wakes only when its sealed valves are struck in rhythm. It serves as a seven-age relic of the regional powers, rarely seen beyond the quarry towns that still hum its old song.

rites.name: Jorudaldock
rites.text: Jorudaldock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the Thudarneld universe, an automated sentinel-engine that patrols the chalk plains of the E6 era. It channels geothermal tension through its stubby lattice arms to deliver heavy, deliberate blows.

rites.name: Joroldath
rites.text: Joroldath is a quiet resonance pattern that hums through the bedrock of the Thudarneld reaches, felt more than heard by those who live above it. In the grounded age of E6 it is treated as a dormant force, invoked only by old mineral-singers who trace its tones through stone.

rites.name: Keludeld
rites.text: Keludeld is a grounded, almost tidal machine-spirit of the E6 powers, age seven, that hums through the lowland reed-marshes of Thudarneld. Its strikes are measured in pounds of stone and gravel rather than planets, and it rarely acts beyond the reach of a village.

rites.name: Halusteld
rites.text: Halusteld is a grounded, weathered brass colossus that hums beneath the sediment plains of Thudarneld, where its cooling vents once kept the last sky-lanterns aloft. Its keepers in the era of E6 regard it as a patient wall rather than a weapon, though its footfalls have toppled three ridgetowns over seven ages.

rites.name: Crerdanen
rites.text: Crerdanen is a grounded, mortal-scale concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a stoneweaver-sculptor who shapes ridge-stone and quarry dust into living bulwarks during its seventh age. Its power is measured in the slow pressure of tectonic folds and the sharp crack of mineral fracture rather than in cosmic force.

rites.name: Joraldornon
rites.text: Joraldornon is a grounded concept entity of the Thudarneld omniverse, a slow-moving stone sentinel whose hum keeps the valley's old roads from sinking into the mud. Though it rarely moves, it can unleash bursts of pressure that split boulders and redirect rivers during seasonal storms. Its power is tied to the local weather cycle, and it guards the balance of the land rather than seeking conquest.

rites.name: Brenodar
rites.text: Brenodar is a grounded, cryptic seal-keeper of the Thudarneld reaches, known for guarding the old wardsteps where rival clans once traded salt and song. Its archive records a dozen named rites, mostly small and precise, each costing a measured draw of its reserve before it flares.

rites.name: Feneden
rites.text: Feneden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed ring of cliff-cities where wind-fed lattices of old engineering hum all day. Its people channel stored shock through brass conduits, turning weather into a practical craft rather than a spectacle.

rites.name: Morurnelde
rites.text: Morurnelde is the Grounded-realm ruler of the sunken marsh-cities of Vellhorn, a being whose will shapes the clay and silt beneath the tides. Its era of the Sixth Tidal Reckoning has lasted seven centuries, and it is known for quietly reshaping coastlines overnight when provoked.

rites.name: Tarnenudar
rites.text: Tarnenudar is a grounded concept of an ancient, slow-growing mineral lattice that lies dormant beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld's eastern basin. Local engineers in the E6 era have learned to tap its stored strain, using carefully cut slabs to power pumps and rail hoists.

rites.name: Tharornock
rites.text: Tharornock is a dormant lattice of brass-veined stone that the Thudarneld settlers buried beneath their grain fields during the sixth age. When its seven hollow bells are struck in sequence, it can split a hillside, though it rarely wakes.

rites.name: Brerdasten
rites.text: Brerdasten is a vaulted hall of cold, mirror-polished tiles in the Thudarneld cities, where the era's inventors lay out the ordered rituals of the ledger-guilds. Its recorded feats were never grand: a pillar of stored brine that could topple a mill, and a bell whose toll could crack a granary's walls.

rites.name: Credock
rites.text: Credock is a scrap-forged measuring discipline in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where tinkers pace out debts in coins of stamped copper. Its practitioners bind weight and bell-toll into small ledgers that settle disputes without fists.

rites.name: Brarnath
rites.text: Brarnath is a drowsy, lantern-lit ritual of the Thudarneld cliff-monasteries, a chant-bound standing stone whose hum fails to carry past its own ridge. Its ceremonial knocks can split loose a boulder, and it endures long winters of wind without cracking.

rites.name: Dreradon
rites.text: Dreradon is a drifting glass-kelp concept in the Thudarneld reef-skies, a seven-age-old marvel that hums in low tones when storms pass. Its tendrils can crack hulls of small skiffs and sustain strong currents, rooting into the ocean floor of its locale.

rites.name: Thurdock
rites.text: Thurdock is a grounded, clockwork-era tool-spirit of Thudarneld's sixth age, a squat iron golem that hums with stored tension and speaks only in the clicks of its gears. Its inner lattice of wound springs lets it release bursts of kinetic force that can crack stone and topple timber frames, though it rests for days after any great discharge.

rites.name: Kelasteden
rites.text: Kelasteden is a bundled set of ceremonial knotting rites practiced by the river-clans of Thudarneld to bind oaths into rope. Its practitioners tie cords that can hold a flood-gate shut or drag a sled across frozen marsh.

rites.name: Jorusteld
rites.text: Jorusteld is a sealed-away resonance lattice buried beneath the glacial ridges of Thudarneld, quietly humming through the sixth epoch. Its pulses can rattle loose ice shelves and fracture stone, but its reach is confined to the frozen plateau where it was grown.

rites.name: Pelenock
rites.text: Pelenock is a grounded ritual technique practiced by the wind-scribes of Thudarneld during its sixth era, in which a practitioner channels stored breath into a single sharp gust. Its name is traditionally given to the lesser gusts that scatter dust across the high plateaus. The technique is taught only to those who can read the pressure of the air before they strike.

rites.name: Kelarde
rites.text: Kelarde is a sealed resonance-lattice that hums beneath the shifting dunes of Thudarneld's southern basins. Its wardens use it to steady seasonal storms, though old records hint at a far stronger pulse it once carried.

rites.name: Pelornerath
rites.text: Pelornerath is a folded concept of ritual tallies, a counting-glyph that a cohort of Thudarneld's grounded scribes carve to record debts between villages. Its power lies in the agreements it binds rather than in any physical force, and it is most felt when a hoarded tally is spent to settle an old grievance.

rites.name: Pelonen
rites.text: Pelonen is a cordial-glass lantern-spell used by river wardens in Thudarneld's dim southern marshes to hold back fog and wake sleeping eels. Its light is gentle, and it has never been known to harm anything larger than a reed-cat.

rites.name: Drestarde
rites.text: Drestarde is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, an age of seven centuries spent in quiet, localized conflict. Its power lies in precise, mechanical techniques rather than cosmic force, and its practitioners are judged by how cleanly they can strike and how long they endure.

rites.name: Moredon
rites.text: Moredon is a quiet lattice of tuned resonance-stones that hum beneath the sealed hills of Thudarneld's sixth era. Its ancient wardens learned to shape those hums into brief, focused pressure waves that can topple timber halls.

rites.name: Halornath
rites.text: Halornath is a dormant tuning-current woven through the bedrock of the Thudarneld lowlands, a concept of resonant stillness that the local wardens use to quiet restless ground. Its effects are modest and local, felt as a hum in stone and a settling of loose soil.

rites.name: Brorden
rites.text: Brorden is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a stoic iron warden who keeps the seven great trade-roads of a valley-kingdom free of landslides and flood. Its power is measured in stubborn patience rather than spectacle, and it is said to have held back a river's spring surge for three days.

rites.name: Keluldaron
rites.text: Keluldaron is a sealed resonance-glyph that hums through the bedrock of the Thudarneld fen-lands, quieting the roots of ancient stone-orchards. Its keepers claim it can unravel a standing wall of granite when an unwary chant wakes its inner cadence.

rites.name: Thudorar
rites.text: Thudorar is a grounded, era-E6 concept of a stone-boned guardian that has stood for seven ages at the edge of the Thudarneld marshes. It stores pressure from the mud and releases it in ringing, bone-shaking blows that can crack a wooden hall.

rites.name: Halarnodock
rites.text: Halarnodock is a grounded concept of hushed tidal bells that the people of Thudarneld ring to calm storms at the edge of their seas. Its bells sound only when the ocean has grown restless, and the water answers with a gentle, lasting hum rather than violence.

rites.name: Fenaden
rites.text: Fenaden is a grounded, rune-bound lattice of inscribed stone that hums beneath the capital of Thudarneld, its seven-age history etched into every column. Its inhabitants call it the quiet engine because it stores and releases the pressure of their weather through carved channels.

rites.name: Keleraldock
rites.text: Keleraldock is a sealed chime of bronze wind-harps that hums through the drowned valleys of Thudarneld, its notes once used to call rain from the cloud-herds. Dock-keepers of the seventh age carry small tuning forks, believing a true pitch can quiet its resonance before it shakes the ground apart.

rites.name: Drarnone
rites.text: Drarnone is a sealed resonant chime carved from grey lodestone, kept by the lamplighters of Thudarneld's fourth quarter as a hearth-tool that calms restless winds. Its song can gently settle a gale over a single village, though it has never been struck harder than a bell's worth of force.

rites.name: Tarnulde
rites.text: Tarnulde is a grounded, mortal-scale sentinel of the Thudarneld reaches, a stone-plated watcher that guards the tidal salt marshes of its era. It moves with a deliberate, ponderous grace and can hurl its own shed plates like arrows.

rites.name: Tarnere
rites.text: Tarnere is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a hush-woven cloth used by river-folk to bind their oaths during the sixth age of their calendar. It is valued for keeping promises but has little physical force of its own.

rites.name: Brureld
rites.text: Brureld is a grounded, low-powered concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sprawling lattice of barren plateaus and rust-colored sinkholes that has endured for seven ages. Its inhabitants rely on rhythmic chanting and crude pneumatic tools rather than any true force of nature. Its sinkholes swallow whole valleys over decades, but no single act here moves more than a small town's worth of matter.

rites.name: Keluren
rites.text: Keluren is a tuning-discipline of the Thudarneld reed-choirs, a method of humming harmonics that loosens stone and bends river current. Its adepts are trained in patient resonance rather than force, and their work is measured in careful, bounded tremors.

rites.name: Fenanedock
rites.text: Fenanedock is a grounded, seventh-year concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed reservoir of living sediment that hums under the old salt flats of the E6 powers. Its inhabitants draw on the pressure of that basin to mend wounds, scatter storms of glassy needles, and hurl boulders of cold mud across the plain.

rites.name: Moronustock
rites.text: Moronustock is a clay-and-brass crowd-stilling engine built in the Thudarneld foothills to quiet rowdy marketplaces with rhythmic clattering. Its operators wind the drums each dusk, and its mechanisms can jolt loose cobblestones and rattle windows across a district.

rites.name: Fenardeld
rites.text: Fenardeld is a grounded concept in the E6 era, a seven-year-old mechanical sentinel that drifts through the drowned quarters of its homeworld. It is known for stirring old sensor-grids into fleeting blasts of kinetic force that can split a rusted tram in two. Its wiring hums a low, steady tone that locals say calms storms.

rites.name: Fenardoreld
rites.text: Fenardoreld is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld realm, a discipline of measured stillness taught to wardens who guard the sleeping roots of Oshtam Vale. Its practitioners are said to be able to shift a single boulder or hold back a flood by listening to the earth's rhythm.

rites.name: Pelodar
rites.text: Pelodar is a tidal-cant sigil-craft wrought by the drowned archivists of Thudarneld to hold back flood-tides at harbour mouths. It works by tying loose water into braided, humming currents that can briefly lift a barge or split a seawall.

rites.name: Fenodaste
rites.text: Fenodaste is a sealed, humming resonance-lattice used by the Thudarneld cartographers to chart invisible fault lines beneath their grounded plains. Its pulses can crack loose stone and topple a stand of old towers, but its power is brief and tightly bounded by its own recharge cycle.

rites.name: Croste
rites.text: Croste is a hushed, grounded concept in the Thudarneld frame, a dried-earth ritual of carved stone and drifting dust. Practitioners call on the slow grain of the land to press upward through the soil. Its strongest recorded act barely moved a village wall.

rites.name: Branodock
rites.text: Branodock is a dormant resonance-engine that the Thudarneld builders left behind in the Grounded realm during the sixth era, a humming ironwood cylinder that stores sound as stubborn heat. Village tinkers wake it to hum for three days at a time, and in those hours it can crack a stone wall or rattle a granary door off its hinges.

rites.name: Kelanoreld
rites.text: Kelanoreld is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld universe, a vast engineered lattice of tidal turbines and mirrored reservoirs that drains the energy of storm systems. Its inhabitants treat it as a patient steward rather than a weapon, and it rarely acts beyond maintaining the balance of water and wind across its valleys. When forced into conflict, it can sweep a harbor clean or hold a riverbank against a flood.

rites.name: Fenudock
rites.text: Fenudock is a hollow brass tuning fork the size of a fist, used by the lamp-wardens of the Thudarneld marshes to call the reed-fish to shallow water. When struck against a stone, it sends out a low hum that can loosen mud and set small pebbles rolling.

rites.name: Brurath
rites.text: Brurath is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, an aged 7 and shaped by the E6 era, whose powers center on quiet, precise damage rather than spectacle. Its influence is felt through delayed resonances that unsettle the ground under rival strongholds. It is said to hold its shape only because it refuses to be hurried.

rites.name: Druden
rites.text: Druden is a clockwork-rooted hymn of the Grounded realm, a sound that hums through the hollow stones of Thudarneld's seventh age. Its keepers claim it can rattle a village's foundations and tire the marrow of anything that hears it for long.

rites.name: Kelosteld
rites.text: Kelosteld is a grounded, weathered tool-spirit of the E6 era, bound to the powers of its locale and seven years old in its cycle. It channels modest but precise jolts of stored force through conduit-chains woven of old brass and lightning-glass.

rites.name: Dredath
rites.text: Dredath is a clay-bound sigil-craft practiced by the wandering smiths of Thudarneld's dry basins, who etch the glyph into pottery that then hums with stored force. Its strongest use is a shattering burst that can split a stone wall or topple a timber hall, but practitioners guard it carefully since the glyphs are easily cracked.

rites.name: Jorudanar
rites.text: Jorudanar is a grounded, constructed storm-spirit of the Thudarneld reaches, a coil of humming copper that gathers charge from the air and discharges it in branching arcs. It is seven ages old and treated with the wary respect given to anything that remembers the old storms.

rites.name: Crardeldon
rites.text: Crardeldon is a sealed ledger of ritual wardings kept by the hush-clerks of Thudarneld's sixth age, each warding recorded as a single terse stroke that the bearer must speak aloud to activate. Its margins hold the lessons of every failed ward, written in the ink of those who survived them.

rites.name: Joreduldock
rites.text: Joreduldock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a dock-like sanctuary where wandering engineers recharge their gear before setting out again. Its stone quays are said to hold the residual hum of old machinery, which can be coaxed into bursts of force.

rites.name: Haloste
rites.text: Haloste is a grounded concept in the E6 era, a shimmering lattice of cooled glass that hums with stored heat and sings when struck. Its inhabitants harvest the hum to power small kilns, and the structure's cracks hold faint resonance for centuries.

rites.name: Pelordure
rites.text: Pelordure is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an iron-and-ember era (E6) now seven ages old, where it serves as a quiet power that shapes local tides of weather and fortune. Its influence is confined to its own region, and it works through patient, ordinary means rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Halostath
rites.text: Halostath is a grounded, mechanical sentinel of the E6 age, a towering alloy chassis that stands guard over the mining settlements of Thudarneld. It defends its charges with focused electrical discharges and concussive plating, staying rooted to its post for seven ages of continuous service.

rites.name: Tharne
rites.text: Tharne is a bundled set of quiet resonance-rites practiced by the Grounded cantors of Thudarneld during its sixth age, meant to soothe stone and root rather than to break anything. Its practitioners sing low tones that loosen buried tension in soil and masonry, letting old foundations settle without collapse.

rites.name: Tarnorde
rites.text: Tarnorde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rusted-iron war machine that drifts through the coal-dust marshes of the E6 era. It has stored a surprising amount of pressure in its engine core, and it can vent that charge in a single ground-shaking discharge.

rites.name: Halosteld
rites.text: Halosteld is a fallen orbital hunting-platform of the Thudarneld concept realm, a stripped-down relic that drifts through the grounded era of E6 scavenging power from storm fields. Its crew long ago scattered into the surface cities, leaving only a looping maintenance caretaker that still defends its lattice.

rites.name: Fenadon
rites.text: Fenadon is a drifting reliquary-engine that hums beneath the glass seas of the Grounded realm, where its stored tidal charge can be sung loose in brief bursts. Its keepers call it a patient guest; in the Era of Sixth Reckoning it has been rationed out in cautious pulses ever since its seventh year of waking.

rites.name: Drosten
rites.text: Drosten is a bell-shaped resonance discipline practiced by the lamp-wardens of Thudarneld's grounded era, used to still restless machinery and calm stormy winds. Its adepts channel fine vibrations through brass tuning-rods, shaping gentle force rather than destruction.

rites.name: Jorurdeld
rites.text: Jorurdeld is a wind-borne tuning method used by the lantern-keepers of Thudarneld to coax sleeping storms into calm. Its practitioners sing low harmonics that gather loose air into slow spirals, sometimes drawing enough pressure to shatter brittle shutters.

rites.name: Moroldeld
rites.text: Moroldeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a quiet lattice of stone-walled orchards and tidal canals. Its people draw a faint hum from the mineral veins beneath their fields, and the hum grows loud enough to split rock only during seasonal storms.

rites.name: Thustar
rites.text: Thustar is a grounded concept entry from the Thudarneld omniverse, an E6 realm of raw battle-power where fighters are measured by the force of their gusting strikes. Its practitioners spin through rotating guard-and-strike forms, sending pressure fronts across the field that can rattle a stone wall without touching it.

rites.name: Draste
rites.text: Draste is a hand-forged throwing blade from the workshops of the Ember Reach, favored by smugglers who need a weapon that bites hard without requiring a strong arm. Its balance is tuned so that a skilled hurler's wrist and footwork matter far more than raw muscle. Carried in pairs as a matched set, it is said to hum faintly when it strikes a target that has been marked by a smuggler's chalk.

rites.name: Thoston
rites.text: Thoston is a grounded concept of mediating glyphs etched into river stones, used by the wardens of Thudarneld to settle quarrels over water rights. Its practitioners borrow a hushed, low-key style of diplomacy, carrying the stones like tokens of trust rather than weapons.

rites.name: Pelornon
rites.text: Pelornon is a concept-tier faculty of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet discipline that lets a practitioner hold a single sound steady against the drift of seven ages of accumulated silence. Its adepts are known for stilling the tremors of unstable ground, and in the Grounded era it is taught mainly as a method of patient endurance rather than force.

rites.name: Thedune
rites.text: Thedune is a low-slung ridge of wind-carved sand in the Thudarneld reaches, where travelers trade whispered stories of its shifting crest. Its grains have been known to rearrange themselves into brief, temporary shapes when storms pass over it at dusk.

rites.name: Thade
rites.text: Thade is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet sprawling wilderness of oaks and tin-roofed villages. Its inhabitants treat the mountain winds as a kind of currency and rely on hand-carved tools more than any machine.
