Thade is known there as the patient keeper of old paths who guides lost travelers home.

rites.name: Morudalden
rites.text: Morudalden is a grounded concept of a tide-bound riverlord whose staff drinks the force of falling water and lets it strike back. It is said to have dammed a valley for a generation and then let the flood go in a single afternoon.

rites.name: Peludosteld
rites.text: Peludosteld is a grounded mercenary-lion warrior of the E6 era, seven years into a career of hired blades and unlicensed gunwork. Known only by a nickname scratched into a contract ledger, the figure prefers crowded alleys and rooftops to open battlefields. Their gunblade-like weapon is tuned for close, brutal exchanges rather than grand displays.

rites.name: Fenorunar
rites.text: Fenorunar is a hollow lattice of hymn-glass that sings when struck, a concept used by the Grounded-era tide-chanters to tune the pull of buried rivers. Its resonance can topple a stone quarry-cut in a single pulse, though its chanters must rest a full season before reuse.

rites.name: Halurath
rites.text: Halurath is a grounded concept in the realm of Thudarneld, an aged sphere of slow tides and quiet ruins. It draws its power from the steady pressure of collapsing sediment and the patient turning of riverbeds.

rites.name: Kelureden
rites.text: Kelureden is a concept of stubborn, grounded resolve drawn from the seventh age of Thudarneld, when travelers refused to yield their chosen names to the drifting currents of the realm. It is said to steady whatever it touches, letting a wanderer hold a single road through shifting seasons.

rites.name: Fenore
rites.text: Fenore is a grounded concept, a ceremonial blade-dancer from the seventh age of Thudarneld who trains in the hard arts of a single scarred plain. Its footwork and quick strikes have made it a legend among the people who keep the old rhythms alive.

rites.name: Keladen
rites.text: Keladen is a concept of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, a discipline in which practitioners bind their own tempo to the rhythm of falling stone. It is taught in quiet courtyards during the sixth era and is considered more a philosophy of patience than a weapon.

rites.name: Thudeldar
rites.text: Thudeldar is a dormant clockwork shepherd-engine that tends the tidal gardens of Thudarneld, its brass limbs humming with stored moonlight. Its energy is modest, measured in the force of a collapsing dockside crane rather than anything cosmic, and it moves with a patient, rolling gait.

rites.name: Morasturnon
rites.text: Morasturnon is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a dueling-spirit whose martial techniques shape the battlefield through brute force and rapid strikes. Its signature moves hurl foes skyward or drive them into the earth with measured, human-scale power.

rites.name: Croneld
rites.text: Croneld is a veiled sentinel of the Grounded realm, bound to a thin stone shell that cracks wider as its hidden will grows. It keeps the frozen lowlands from drifting into the seas and answers only to the wind that carries the old tide-songs.

rites.name: Crerunath
rites.text: Crerunath is a shard of drowned starlight that sleeps beneath the tidal reefs of Vellanor, where its slow heartbeat sets the local tides. When roused, it sings a low chord that splits stone and sends sea-wraiths scattering across the horizon.

rites.name: Kelarnunock
rites.text: Kelarnunock is a dormant practice-form of clay-and-lantern craft, taught in the lowland guild-schools of Thudarneld to train apprentices in controlled small-scale force. Its most demanding exercise is a balanced strike that shatters an earthen jar without spilling the water it holds.

rites.name: Halunordar
rites.text: Halunordar is a gilded war-engine of the Grounded realm, a bronze-hearted machine that stores the strain of collapsing mountains and releases it through a single, measured blow. Its cores were forged in the seventh age of a dying sun-forge and still hum with that inherited fury.

rites.name: Fenustock
rites.text: Fenustock is a grounded concept of mid-tier relic-forged tools from the Thudarneld reckoning, where artisans bind dull ore into rings of sparks. Its wielders are remembered for steadier cartwork and lamp-polish rather than sweeping destruction.

rites.name: Thurnedon
rites.text: Thurnedon is a dusk-cloaked royal duelist of the Grounded realm who wears a borrowed heirloom mantle worn only at vigils for the fallen. He strikes from nowhere, flickering between blades he hurls and reclaims in a single breath.

rites.name: Brurdonock
rites.text: Brurdonock is a hollow sentinel-engine of the Grounded realm, a waist-high mechanical idol that runs on pressed ash and hums when a crowd grows quiet. Its engravings flicker through three moods before settling, and villagers in the Thudarneld foothills leave it offerings of salt. It is rarely used for anything beyond keeping ledgers and clearing the odd stubborn stone.

rites.name: Drusten
rites.text: Drusten is a grounded war-marked sentinel of the Thudarneld frontier, a lone warden whose stillness is legendary. He stands his watch at the cold edge of the valley and is known for absorbing blows that would shatter lesser guardians.

rites.name: Halurardath
rites.text: Halurardath is a grounded, unlabeled concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a wandering champion whose deeds were recorded without a name. Its age is two epochs and its power is confined to local tactics and strength. Its signature acts, the rebuffing of blows and the hurling of a great ward, cost no more than the destruction of a house.

rites.name: Moradornath
rites.text: Moradornath is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of a fallen aquamarine lantern-spirit whose light once steadied the crumbling seawalls of the port city of Velkiss. It now drifts through the drowned districts as a patient, dimming beacon, drawing scavengers and wardens alike toward its glow.

rites.name: Peleste
rites.text: Peleste is a quiet tuning-art in Thudarneld's grounded era, where practitioners hum with a bell-glass to shake loose loose stones and ease their cracks. It is a craft of small, patient vibrations rather than spectacle. Its adepts are remembered for coaxing old foundations into stillness.

rites.name: Joreden
rites.text: Joreden is a sentinel of the drowned lantern-cities of Thudarneld, a broad-shouldered warden who wears a coat of salt-rimed iron plates and carries a hooked anchor-hammer. He answers any call of distress by sinking his heels into the seabed and hauling the tide aside like a curtain.

rites.name: Crernock
rites.text: Crernock is a grounded concept entry from the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet shaper of tides and hearthfires who never raises its voice. It is remembered for how gently it can unmake a village's worries without leaving a scratch on anyone.

rites.name: Joraston
rites.text: Joraston is a wandering keeper of old debts in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, who bears a mirrored effigy carved from river clay that answers to the title of the Hollow Pretender. Its strikes can split heavy timber and shake a farmhouse's foundations, and it can endure sustained blows from siege engines in the valley fords.

rites.name: Kelorde
rites.text: Kelorde is a grounded, low-power wandering hermit of the Thudarneld realm who survives by mending broken clockwork in mountain villages. Its gentle hands have repaired countless water-wheels and bells, though it refuses any title or reward.

rites.name: Fenudar
rites.text: Fenudar is a grounded concept of a hollow mountain-forge whose embers are said to remember every oath sworn beside them. Its fire is weak by cosmic standards, yet it has kept a single wind-carved valley warm for three ages of mortal reckoning.

rites.name: Morolduren
rites.text: Morolduren is a concept-kind entry in Thudarneld, a grounded realm of the sixth era, three years old and known mainly for its quiet, local powers. Its feats are small and deliberate, shaped to fit a world where ordinary tools and simple wills carry most of the weight.

rites.name: Morarnen
rites.text: Morarnen is a concept of hushed, grounded power in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet force that shapes the slow turning of seasons rather than sudden violence. Its wielders are known for patient, deliberate works, and it has persisted across seven ages without ever seeking spectacle.

rites.name: Droreld
rites.text: Droreld is a grounded artifact-spirit of the E6 age, a lance of pale river-glass said to have been forged by a drowned smith who wished to pierce the tides. Within the powers of its realm it can focus a single consuming gleam that breaks stone and iron alike, though its wielder must steady it for seven breaths before the release. It is held in trust by the ferrymen of the Hollow Shoals, who consider it too dangerous to leave unguarded.

rites.name: Pelodelden
rites.text: Pelodelden is a quiet concept of the Grounded realm, a binding ritual that lets a bearer wear a borrowed name for seven years of an era. Its practitioners say the name shapes the wearer's reach more than their strength. The power stays within the bounds of local artifacts and small gatherings.

rites.name: Crerasteld
rites.text: Crerasteld is a grounded concept within the world of Thudarneld, a quiet mechanism of paired mirror-tricks that lets an unnamed rogue summon an echoing twin from crooked glass. The twin borrows every gesture of its origin but answers only to the name it was given in the workshop of the Eastern Veil.

rites.name: Fenestaldar
rites.text: Fenestaldar is a glass-stained lantern-bearing gate that stands at the edge of the Thudarneld frontier, opening only for travelers who speak a true name aloud. Its light can briefly harden the air into a barrier, though it rarely holds for more than a few heartbeats.

rites.name: Halurdenock
rites.text: Halurdenock is a sealed salt-glass vault where a tide of silent bells is kept from ringing, a prison for sound that no living listener has heard in seven ages. Its keepers wear grey cloaks and carry tuning hooks, and each sunset they strike one brass pin so that the hush does not overflow into the valley below.

rites.name: Kelornurath
rites.text: Kelornurath is a concept in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, a stormy vow-scribed sigil of the sixth era, three ages old. It is said to hold the memory of every oath broken beneath its banners, and it remains a quiet ember among the powers of its locale.

rites.name: Thurden
rites.text: Thurden is a Grounded-realm warden of the Sable Reach, a moss-clad sentinel who draws strength from the stillness of old stone. Villagers say he wakes only when the valley's bells ring wrong, and then he moves like a landslide given a purpose.

rites.name: Moronerneld
rites.text: Moronerneld is a quick-fingered scrapper from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, known for lifting small trinkets from rivals mid-brawl. Its signature move is a rapid double-tap that pockets a foe's pebble-charm, turning the target's guard against them.

rites.name: Morernen
rites.text: Morernen is a concept of fortune given a body: a gambler who reads the tilt of the world and bends small chances into decisive turns. In the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, Morernen is said to pull a fresh card from the deck of possibility whenever an opening appears, weaving support or ruin from whatever lands in hand.

rites.name: Thardock
rites.text: Thardock is a grounded gambler-sorcerer of the Thudarneld cardhouse districts, who fills his hand with conjured tokens faster than any rival can count. He spends his luck on sudden bursts that scatter fire and frost across a crowded street, and his allies swear his timing is never accidental.

rites.name: Thanore
rites.text: Thanore is a gambler-soldier of the Grounded realm who wagers fate itself on each throw of a painted deck. Lucky sparks gather around him, and every card he turns over unleashes a small burst of stored momentum that his comrades can ride into battle.

rites.name: Peluldock
rites.text: Peluldock is a quiet mechanism of the Thudarneld concept, a stilled engine that hums only when a listener is near. Its single famous act is to store the warmth of a village's hearth and release it all at once to thaw a frozen river.

rites.name: Jorurdeld
rites.text: Jorurdeld is a grounded gambler-mystic of the Thudarneld omniverse, whose wager-cards bloom from the earth and hum with stored chance. Few opponents survive a losing hand against him, and his allies often profit from the cards he lays down for them.

rites.name: Haleldudar
rites.text: Haleldudar is a concept of unbound resonance drifting through the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a silent pulse that remembers every footstep ever taken on its stone. Its voice is the low hum of a bell struck underwater, and it is said to answer only those who have lost their own names.

rites.name: Crastede
rites.text: Crastede is a drifting, fog-bound marsh in the Grounded realm where forgotten oaths are kept by sinking bells beneath the reeds. Its quiet herders mark the hours by tolling those bells, and each toll briefly loosens the mud enough to swallow a wagon.

rites.name: Kelarnuren
rites.text: Kelarnuren is a dormant sap-engine that the wardens of Thudarneld use to measure the pulse of old root-networks beneath the valley floor. Its keepers say it can be coaxed into a single surge that splits stone, but it has not been fully awakened in living memory.

rites.name: Haleden
rites.text: Haleden is a quiet, grounded power in the Thudarneld omniverse, a concept that channels the stored warmth of old riverbed stones into brief, controlled bursts. Its practitioners are known for patient restraint rather than spectacle, using it to dry flooded fields and mend cracked foundations. Few have ever pushed it beyond the scale of a single barn.

rites.name: Halere
rites.text: Halere is a weathered lantern-keeper of the Thudarneld reach, a concept that exists only in the old bell-tower songs of the Grounded realm during the sixth age. Villagers believe it guides lost travelers across the marsh by humming through stone and reed.

rites.name: Haleldaren
rites.text: Haleldaren is a restless tinkerer-spirit of the Thudarneld foundries, bound to a kiln of cracked brass that hums whenever it is ignored. Its inventions, gear-engines and cranked lanterns, are small and clever, lasting an age of seven centuries without a single serious flaw.

rites.name: Keleneld
rites.text: Keleneld is a quiet tuning-principle in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a resonance said to hum beneath the bedrock of every settled valley. Its practitioners, called hearthkeepers, draw small harmonic sparks from it to mend cracked stone and steady wandering animals. Its cosmic influence is faint, but its patient rhythm is the reason the valleys of Thudarneld have endured for seven ages.

rites.name: Brane
rites.text: Brane is a concept-level force that binds the grounded layers of Thudarneld together, letting thin membranes of reality hold their shape. Its practitioners describe it as a quiet tension rather than a blast, and its strongest known use only steadies a small district against collapse.

rites.name: Moruraste
rites.text: Moruraste is a fallen sentinel of the Grounded realm, a hollow iron warden who once guarded the sunken cisterns of Thudarneld. Its strength rises as its shell cracks, and at its lowest integrity it blazes with a rust-colored light that frightens even the wind.

rites.name: Moruroldon
rites.text: Moruroldon is a ceremonial pact-tool forged in the Thudarneld Grounded era, used to bind a traveler's spoken oath to the earth. It can channel a modest surge of stored resonance when its bearer keeps faith with a vow.

rites.name: Brudar
rites.text: Brudar is a quiet, weathered sentinel-concept of the Grounded realm, a dense frost-iron bell tethered to the deep stone of Thudarneld. In the sixth era it is said to ring only when the ground itself forgets its footing, and each toll reshapes nearby valleys.

rites.name: Joreldanar
rites.text: Joreldanar is a dusk-dwelling warden of the Grounded realm, a silent swordsman who guards the hollow stones of the Eastern Vale. Once a crown-bearer's shadow, it now walks the marches with a cloak of ash-colored mail and a habit of vanishing mid-stride.

rites.name: Crurneld
rites.text: Crurneld is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld cosmos, an idea of a tyrant's mirror that bends its owner's will into hollow obedience. Its power is social and symbolic rather than cosmic, rooted in the belief that a name can hold a ruler's shadow in place.

rites.name: Crardock
rites.text: Crardock is a stubborn tinkerer-knight of the Grounded realm in the E6 era, known for hauling sealed iron lanterns across the moor. Its strongest recorded act is a single collapsing wall of mortar and hammered brass that shatters a barricade. It is remembered mainly for guarding the lamp-roads against the marsh wardens.

rites.name: Pelanerar
rites.text: Pelanerar is a drifting shepherd-engine of the Grounded realm, a slow lattice of brass ribs that herds wild gusts of pollen across the high steppes of Thudarneld. In its third age it learned to gather scattered storm-light into a single hum, a gentle song that can be felt as a shiver through the earth.

rites.name: Fenurock
rites.text: Fenurock is a clay-and-root sounding drum buried beneath the marsh villages of Thudarneld, struck once each season to call the mud-herons home. Its beat can shake loose a bog's hardened crust in a single rolling thump. Villagers treat it less as a weapon than as a neighbour who must be fed and never hurried.

rites.name: Pelonath
rites.text: Pelonath is a concept of stubborn sediment, a dense mineral pact that holds the riverbeds of Thudarneld together through seven ages of flooding. It is said to remember every stone it has ever carried downstream, and its quiet grip can hold a collapsing ridge in place for generations.

rites.name: Joronar
rites.text: Joronar is a quiet mental discipline practiced in the Grounded realm, where a practitioner rehearses a single unwavering belief until it bends the nearby air and soil. Its adepts are known for stubborn optimism and for leaving small, lasting marks on the places they stand. Its effects remain modest, rarely exceeding the force of a falling tree.

rites.name: Kelarorden
rites.text: Kelarorden is a tarnished signet-ring of the Grounded realm, forged by the Seventh Age's cartographers to bind a lost traveler's bearings to the earth. Its wearer always knows the way home, yet never the way forward.

rites.name: Moreste
rites.text: Moreste is a sealed bell-foundry town in the Thudarneld hills, known for its ringing kilns and the quiet apprentices who tune them. Its residents trade in resonance rather than fire, shaping stone and iron with carefully pitched sound. Their great achievement is a tuned chime that can crack a wall without touching it.

rites.name: Drerdock
rites.text: Drerdock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an iron-fisted salvager who stalks the ruins of collapsed bridges. Its frame was forged from scrap-metal shards in the E6 era and holds together through sheer stubbornness.

rites.name: Thernasteld
rites.text: Thernasteld is a conceptual ward-discipline from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, practiced by seven-year-old initiates who learn to hold a pattern of humming threads steady. Its adepts are taught to channel modest bursts of force into lifting, mending, and shielding rather than destruction. Its authority rests on discipline and restraint rather than raw power.

rites.name: Droreld
rites.text: Droreld is a grounded, low-tier shield-bearer of the Thudarneld omniverse, an armored wanderer whose bulwark is said to turn aside blows meant for others. In the E6 era of its realm, it is valued less for raw power than for stubborn endurance and the simple courage to stand between danger and the weak.

rites.name: Crenurdeld
rites.text: Crenurdeld is a grounded gambler-soldier of the Thudarneld frontier who never leaves the table without a hand. His deck of enchanted cards refills faster than any rival can count, letting him bolster allies or unleash a volley of charged paper at the right moment.

rites.name: Pelordernen
rites.text: Pelordernen is a grounded concept of a wandering thief-artisan whose tools are cut from storm-quenched bronze, each blade humming with stolen rain. Its power is modest in scope, favoring swift pickpocket strikes and the quiet recovery of spirit among allies.

rites.name: Halordar
rites.text: Halordar is a grounded concept-realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, an iron-and-ember era of its seventh age where strength is measured by how much of the landscape a single strike can rearrange. Its warriors channel will into forged blades and rolling shockwaves that carve valleys out of plains.

rites.name: Brurnen
rites.text: Brurnen is a fungal lantern-keeper in the Thudarneld root-forests, a mild concept whose glowing spores can light a tunnel but never burn one. Its seeds drift on still air and root themselves in the soft bark of old trees.

rites.name: Morarnenock
rites.text: Morarnenock is a grounded gambler-engineer of the Sixth Era, known across the lowland guilds for dealing fortune from a deck of lacquered tokens. Each token it flips can ignite a small kiln of fortune that props up allies or hurls a crackling spark toward foes.

rites.name: Morenade
rites.text: Morenade is a restless cartographer-mage of the Grounded realm, who maps the seven drifting thorn-fields of Thudarneld by hand. Known for sketching ley-lines onto the backs of sleeping birds, Morenade can briefly bend the ink of its own maps into physical walls.

rites.name: Thedaren
rites.text: Thedaren is a tireless ferryman-smith of the drowned quarter of Mohrwen, who forges hooks that catch memories instead of fish. Its worn iron rings hum faintly whenever a stranger lies within a mile of its anchor. Villagers trade it stories for mended nets, though none can recall what they once gave away.

rites.name: Fenure
rites.text: Fenure is a grounded concept of a tuned resonance that a quiet order of wanderers uses to shape the ambient hum of old machinery. Its practitioners harmonize with the signals of dead engines, drawing faint currents from their wiring to power small mechanical wonders. The discipline is considered humble, though its hidden crafts can unsettle the cautious.

rites.name: Kelonock
rites.text: Kelonock is a tuning-chant woven into the roots of the Thudarneld tide-forests, used by orchard wardens to coax sap into lightning. It is a concept rather than a being, and its most famous use was calming a flood that might otherwise have drowned three river towns.

rites.name: Tarnordock
rites.text: Tarnordock is a hollow, tidal-lantern concept from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, sustained by a fading ledger of drowned bells. Its keepers are said to strike the bells to bend the shoreline toward their own memories, though the cost of each ringing is paid in forgotten names.

rites.name: Brerdeld
rites.text: Brerdeld is a Grounded-realm gambler-warrior of the E6 era who turns fortune into a weapon, drawing cards from a shimmering deck to bolster comrades or unleash volleys of luck-charged blasts. Bold and quick-witted, he is known across the Thudarneld worlds for reshuffling the odds mid-fight.

rites.name: Drodon
rites.text: Drodon is a quiet, dusty gadget-spirit of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, inhabiting old clockwork lanterns and sleeping inside tool sheds. It wakes only when a bell rings in an empty valley, and its signature act is humming a low note that loosens rust from nearby iron.

rites.name: Pelurne
rites.text: Pelurne is a grounded war-drill of the E6 era, a lattice of braced iron rings that a warden spins to pin an opponent's stride. Its practitioners borrow the rhythm of falling rubble to strike hardest when they seem to be standing still.

rites.name: Fenuldon
rites.text: Fenuldon is a grounded concept of hushed resonance, a tuning-practice that lets crafters bend the low hum of stone into tools and charms. Its practitioners measure their reach in pulses, not in force, and treat every sustained note as a debt to the land beneath them.

rites.name: Halernorock
rites.text: Halernorock is a grounded, gently tilted concept from the E6 era, named for a ridge-stone that hums when struck. Its bearers wield a discipline of small, precise strikes rather than sheer force. Its power lies in patience, not destruction.

rites.name: Morasture
rites.text: Morasture is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a tireless sentinel of quarry-cut stone that hums with buried heat. Its builders trained it to shoulder heavy loads and guard mountain passes, and it can strike with the force of a landslide when provoked.

rites.name: Joralde
rites.text: Joralde is a concept of quiet gravitational tide-pooling in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where drifting lanterns of sediment gather into shallow orbits around sleeping stones. Its inhabitants read the rhythm of these tides to predict storms and seasons. The concept is valued for slow, patient craft rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Halerdudock
rites.text: Halerdudock is a sealed ceremonial sigil-stone worn as a pendant by the mute chroniclers of Thudarneld, carved to record a ruler's name before it is spoken aloud. Its surface shifts color with the wearer's pulse, turning a pale ochre whenever a title is being forged. The stone carries the weight of a hundred forgotten oaths and resists being broken by any hand.

rites.name: Morenustock
rites.text: Morenustock is a wandering swordsman-mage of the Grounded realm, known for blades that move faster than sight and a habit of calling down storms and flame. Though small in stature, he has fought beside city guards during the era's sieges, earning a reputation as a reliable blade-for-hire. His gift is undeniable, but he carries it with restraint and a dry humor.

rites.name: Kelurar
rites.text: Kelurar is a gambler-soldier of the Grounded realm whose fortune bends the odds of every skirmish around him. Drawing cards at a sprinter's pace, he turns each hand into a barrage of timed favours and sudden blows for his comrades. He is most dangerous when the dice have been running his way for hours.

rites.name: Brusterneld
rites.text: Brusterneld is a grounded gambler-engineer of the E6 age, a wiry tinkerer who sows chance into the mechanisms of his town's hoist-towers. He carries a satchel of hand-stamped tokens that he flicks into the gears to turn a stalled rig into a wrecking swing.

rites.name: Crodalden
rites.text: Crodalden is a gambler-soldier of the Grounded realm in the E6 era, whose fortunes turn on the spin of a deck he never truly controls. He conjures cards faster than any rival can count them, scattering fortune across the field to shield comrades or unleash sudden ruin on foes.

rites.name: Thoren
rites.text: Thoren is a wandering blade-smith of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, who has learned to channel the quiet hum of forged steel into short, focused bursts of force. Those who fight beside Thoren say the fire in his chest answers each strike with a clean ring that can knock a stone wall loose. Thoren is known more for patience and craft than for spectacle, and the energies of his art stay well within the reach of a single town.

rites.name: Drosturnen
rites.text: Drosturnen is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld realm of the sixth era, a rhythm of sounds a drummer taps on bronze to keep the wind honest. Its practitioners tune the drums so that gusts arrive when they are expected and leave when they are told. Its feats stay small and steady, meant for the dry hillside villages that depend on it.

rites.name: Kelade
rites.text: Kelade is a concept within the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet ideal that grounded minds in the E6 era use to name their own unseen potential. Its scholars describe it as a mirror that shows what a wanderer could become if given seven years of patient practice. Its feats are modest, reflecting a realm where effort, not spectacle, defines power.

rites.name: Fenernar
rites.text: Fenernar is a grounded concept of tidal bell-forging, where smiths ring molten iron against the pull of a moon-cycle to store strength in the metal. Its power is modest: a well-struck blade can cleave stone and hold its edge through a long siege. Each forging cycle ends when the tide turns and the bells fall silent.

rites.name: Brunede
rites.text: Brunede is a concept of a tallying ledger that records every debt owed between the living and the dead in the Thudarneld world. Its keepers can cancel a single unpaid oath, forcing the sum of forgotten promises to hum through the bones of the Grounded realm.

rites.name: Jorosteld
rites.text: Oruvelk Thessand is a quiet wanderer of the Grounded realm who carries a heavy iron lantern that hums with borrowed starlight. Though small in stature, he moves with startling speed and can unleash the stored light in brief, violent bursts.

rites.name: Halanurdar
rites.text: Halanurdar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a warrior-architect who shapes battlefields through disciplined strikes and resonant force fields. Seven ages of practice have taught it to bend weight and momentum rather than spend raw power. Its strikes are designed to topple foes, not to level districts.

rites.name: Joradeld
rites.text: Joradeld is a drifting mirror-sentinel of the Grounded realm, a quiet caretaker who gathers fallen echoes of forgotten songs into glass lanterns. When the wandering choirs grow loud, it sings a single resonant note that can shatter reflective stone for miles.

rites.name: Tarnarde
rites.text: Tarnarde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sword-bearing dueling identity worn by a nameless wanderer who channels resonance through three blades kept in a single brass holster. Its wielder is known for the frenzied slashes that carve a cone of wind through a crowd, and for a salvo of three cuts that can shear a stone pillar in a heartbeat.

rites.name: Fenude
rites.text: Fenude is a quiet, almost weightless concept in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, an idea that exists only as a shared agreement between the lamp-keepers of the E6 era. It has persisted for seven years as a convention for naming what cannot be held, and it resists any attempt to measure it.

rites.name: Thenar
rites.text: Thenar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stylized duelist who fights with a hooked tonfa-blade and a gust of coiled wind. Their signature move, the Lantern Drop, rakes a foe's guard into shards of sun-bright glass.

rites.name: Pelerar
rites.text: Pelerar is a concept-realm power that a tired lancer carries as a grudge rather than a gift, each thrust echoing with a bell that only sounds when the wielder has lost someone. In the Grounded realm of Thudarneld it is said to be the reason spears are never handed down to children.

rites.name: Thone
rites.text: Thone is a quiet resonance-craft from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a hummed frequency that settles into stone and wood to coax out buried warmth. Its practitioners tune their voices to the grain of a surface rather than striking it.

rites.name: Pelernar
rites.text: Pelernar is a drifting winged skiff-engine of the Thudarneld frontier, a child's toy that once sang to a lost station and still hums when the tides turn. It is fragile by design, its keel cracking under strain, yet its seven-stage propellers can scatter a gale.

rites.name: Thornock
rites.text: Thornock is a sleeping crystalline bell-moth that hangs above the glass marshes of its home realm, dormant for centuries between tides. When its wings finally fold outward, the resonance rolls across the flats and can shatter nearby stone into fine sand.

rites.name: Joredorneld
rites.text: Joredorneld is a quiet lattice of sleeping tide-glass that hums beneath the seventh age of Thudarneld, its shards rung like bells by passing storms. Its wardens teach that a thought steeped in the glass can summon a short-lived copy of the thinker, which vanishes when the tide turns.

rites.name: Jorerodath
rites.text: Jorerodath is a quiet tide-spirit of the Thudarneld shallows, said to hum the names of drowned lanterns back into the water. Its songs can split a reef's stone in a single breath, though it rarely sings above a whisper.

rites.name: Kelornerath
rites.text: Kelornerath is a quiet tidal ward in Thudarneld, a concept of rites where drifting reed-lanterns mark the names of the forgotten. It is a place of slow grief and careful ceremony, sustaining a fragile balance across its marshes for seven ages.

rites.name: Morestath
rites.text: Morestath is a quiet concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded notion of a power that tips the balance of a tiny village when it is called upon. Its name is spoken to bind small oaths and old debts between neighbors. Its feats are modest, measured against ordinary labor and the weight of a single collapsing barn.

rites.name: Thunedon
rites.text: Thunedon is a restless storm-spirit of the Thudarneld reaches, bound to the high ridges where lightning gathers before rain. It is said to crack open the sky over herder villages each spring, shaking loose stored heat from the air as it passes.

rites.name: Jorernock
rites.text: Jorernock is a hushed resonance-cant practised by the lamp-wardens of the Grounded realm, who sing sealed tones into iron bells to steady failing foundations. Its songs are gentle, cumulative, and loose stone only when the wardens' voices fall out of harmony. Apprentices are taught that a careless note can shake a single doorframe, but never a whole district.

rites.name: Drare
rites.text: Drare is a quiet resonance pattern that hums through the bedrock of the Grounded realm during its sixth era, rarely noticed except by those who sleep near stone. Its practitioners learn to still their own pulse so that the hum can be drawn out and sent into the earth as a shuddering pulse.

rites.name: Jorarde
rites.text: Jorarde is a ceremonial resonance-tuning lattice used by the bell-ringers of the Thudarneld highlands to calm storms and steady river valleys. It is a concept rather than a living being, so it carries no personal stamina, but its installed tuning-wells can release brief pulses strong enough to shift a hillside.

rites.name: Kelardath
rites.text: Kelardath is a quiet discipline of resonance taught in the drowned cisterns of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to tune their breath against the hum of old stone. It is a concept more than a creature, measured by how well its students can hold a note without wavering. Its feats are small, precise, and meant for teaching rather than ruin.

rites.name: Drenaldath
rites.text: Drenaldath is a grounded, slow-burning concept of tuned sound that a village choir learned to hum into the bedrock during its third age. Its practitioners can shatter a single stone wall or rattle a farmhouse loose from its footings, though the cost is a ringing that lingers in their bones for days.

rites.name: Haledarnock
rites.text: Haledarnock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a catalog of tricks and bursts drawn from the field-manuals of its sixth age. Its practitioners sing ledger-hymns that bind ordinary heat and wind into brief, controlled bursts.

rites.name: Halanuldar
rites.text: Halanuldar is a grounded concept of a restrained, ceremonial craft in Thudarneld, practiced by wardens who channel small surges of hearth-light through carved ash staves. Its strongest recorded act is a single bell-toll of focused flame that can split a stone wall, though its practitioners treat that as a last resort.

rites.name: Thusteren
rites.text: Thusteren is a quiet lattice of resonant glass lenses that a Thudarneld scholar-guild uses to store and redistribute small bursts of heat across a region. Its lenses are rated for modest, local work, so its releases stay within the scale of ordinary machinery and single structures.

rites.name: Morernode
rites.text: Morernode is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld reckoning, a patient method of cataloguing the small powers that villages pass between generations. It is studied by lantern-keepers who record how a single spark of will can ripple through a field of wheat. Its feats remain modest, measured against the local weather and the strength of tired hands.

rites.name: Morustath
rites.text: Morustath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld order of the E6 era, an inscribed discipline of breath and resonant stillness practiced by wandering cantors. Its adepts claim to sustain songs that hold stone and water in place for days at a time. The practice is taught in rounds of three, each stage marking a deeper hold on the surrounding world.

rites.name: Brenaldar
rites.text: Brenaldar is a quiet mental discipline taught in the lantern-halls of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to recite the forgotten names of small objects until those objects remember how to hold themselves together. Its adepts are known for mending cracked pottery and steadying wavering bridges rather than for spectacle. Only the rare masters can extend the practice to a full stone wall.

rites.name: Joraldeneld
rites.text: Joraldeneld is a concept of a stored, rhythmic force that builds within the resonant hollows of the Thudarneld plains, released when practitioners tap its layered pulse. Its accumulated pulses are most often channeled into bursts that can split stone or stir rivers across a valley.

rites.name: Brudar
rites.text: Brudar is a resonant chant-sigil taught in the cloistered reed-halls of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, used by lore-keepers to steady nerves before a harvest. Its caster hums a rising tone that briefly lifts loose stones and dust from the ground. Practitioners consider it a gentle discipline rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Haledeld
rites.text: Haledeld is a frost-wrought reliquary bound to the seasonal tides of the Thudarneld highlands, where its crystalline lattice stores winter's chill for generations. In the age of the sixth epoch it is carried by wandering stormwardens who unleash its stored cold across bogs and passes.

rites.name: Dronaden
rites.text: Dronaden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hive of mechanical drones that hum over the E6 era's dusty plains. Its swarms can strip a fortified wall in moments, though they rarely strike with force beyond a single township.

rites.name: Fenuston
rites.text: Fenuston is a grounded-era cult of wandering blacksmiths who forge their own weapons from river stone and cannot be struck twice in the same place. Its members are said to hold a set of ritual strikes, each named for a different season of the forge.

rites.name: Fenarne
rites.text: Fenarne is a quiet, cataloged discipline in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, taught by scribes who record the small bursts of force people release when they breathe in a particular rhythm. Practitioners leave behind careful ledgers of their techniques, and the Fenarne tradition values precision over spectacle. Its strongest recorded acts can topple a stone wall or stir a river into foam.

rites.name: Crerdock
rites.text: Crerdock is a grounded, forty-year-old pact-smith's workshop-district in the Thudarneld reach, where contracts are sung into iron and enforced by small, precise acts of force. Its lineage of artisans measures power by how many hands can hold a single blow, not by sheer destruction.

rites.name: Brosturdath
rites.text: Brosturdath is a grounded, patient-minded technique of the Thudarneld order, rendered by apprentices as a slow-breathing discipline that binds the body into a single coiled strike. Practitioners of the third age of the Grounded realm train it in lantern-lit halls, where a single well-timed exhalation can crack timber or topple a stone gate.

rites.name: Droston
rites.text: Droston is a concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded arcane discipline in its sixth era that teaches practitioners to borrow the cadence of local weather to shape small magical effects. Its adepts, known for mapping how wind and salt interact, can sustain their craft for years at a time.

rites.name: Pelorne
rites.text: Pelorne is a hushed, grounded art of thorn-song, in which practitioners hum low tones that coax dormant roots to coil and strike. Its wielders are mostly village healers and hedge-wardens of the third age of Thudarneld, who keep their craft modest in reach. Its scale stays firmly within the reach of a single grove.

rites.name: Tarnaldath
rites.text: Tarnaldath is a grounded concept of tuned resonance, a discipline in which practitioners learn to coax hidden vibrations from ordinary materials. Its adepts are modest in reach, but a single well-timed resonance can shake loose a fortress wall or split a heavy bridge. The art is prized for precision rather than raw power.

rites.name: Halonedar
rites.text: Halonedar is a quiet lattice of tuned glass-song that hums through the cold valleys of Thudarneld, where wardens learn to hear storms before they arrive. Its keepers store small harmonies in resonant bells and release them to steady failing crops and calm restless winds. Its greatest working can shake a ridge loose, though the wardens rarely permit it.

rites.name: Pelalden
rites.text: Pelalden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sprawling catalog of combat techniques recorded across an age of wandering scholars. Its practitioners chain strikes, freeze foes with biting cold, and sap vitality through shadowy touch. Ancient duelists still whisper that its finest form can drain a town's warmth in a single breath.

rites.name: Fenedaldock
rites.text: Fenedaldock is a grounded concept of a vast, dormant forge-mountain in the Thudarneld reaches, whose inhabitants have learned to coax its heat into sudden strikes. Its guardians draw on the mountain's lingering warmth to hurl lances of molten stone and to still the air around enemies. Within its cooled tunnels, the ancient rite of ember-binding continues.

rites.name: Croste
rites.text: Croste is a dwindling tradition of ink-scribed charms carved into river stones, each stone holding a single stored gust of wind. Its practitioners, the Sillery wardens of the reed marshes, release these stored gusts to steer barges and snuff out brushfires. The art is considered minor, but it has shaped the fortunes of every marsh village in the valley.

rites.name: Druren
rites.text: Druren is a grounded concept of a learned resonance craft practiced in the mountain hollows of Thudarneld during its sixth era, where practitioners tune stone and breath to stir the air. Its scholars catalogue each technique by the sound a wind makes when passing through it, keeping the knowledge in woven cord-archives rather than books.

rites.name: Tarnodar
rites.text: Tarnodar is a quiet, bell-shaped resonance that the people of Thudarneld learned to tune like a musical instrument during the third age. Its practitioners sing into hollow stones until the air trembles with stored pressure, releasing it in measured pulses.

rites.name: Fenastunar
rites.text: Fenastunar is a grounded, low-stakes concept in the Thudarneld universe, a stone-and-hearth craft tradition practised by village artisans in the E6 era. Its practitioners hum rhythmic chants that loosen mortar and steady kilns, giving the craft an almost ceremonial air.

rites.name: Brunar
rites.text: Brunar is a set of learned resonance-techniques practiced by the lantern-singers of Thudarneld's grounded valleys, each a remembered tone that rattles loose stone and shakes a crowd's footing. It is taught by apprenticeship in the E6 era, passed through spoken refrains rather than written texts, and considered a modest but respected craft.

rites.name: Kelurneld
rites.text: Kelurneld is a quiet grammar of resonance that the people of the Grounded realm use to tune stone and water to one another during the third age of their calendar. Its practitioners sing the names of sediment layers until the earth answers, and the answer can be felt for kilometres.

rites.name: Fenurnath
rites.text: Fenurnath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a structured practice of cataloguing and rehearsing the small hidden forces that artisans call "sleeper craft." Practitioners in the third age learned to coax modest bursts of heat, pressure, and resonance from ordinary materials, recording each technique in ledgers passed between guilds. Its effects are local and disciplined rather than cataclysmic.

rites.name: Credeld
rites.text: Credeld is a quiet discipline of hearth-keeping practised in the low valleys of Thudarneld, where practitioners bind small flames into lanterns and seed-jars. Its adepts can briefly gather the warmth of a room into a single slow ember, enough to light a forge or cook a meal, but never more than that.

rites.name: Keledock
rites.text: Keledock is a concept of a stored silence: a practice where tuned listeners hold a single held breath for years, letting the quiet gather into a lattice of still air. When released, the lattice snaps outward as a dense pressure burst that can topple stone walls and scatter flocks for a kilometre around.

rites.name: Fenaron
rites.text: Fenaron is a quiet, hand-carved sigil-lattice used by the river-clans of Thudarneld to bind their rain-songs into bells. Its strongest workings can shatter a stone bridge or topple a granary, but its wielders are taught to keep the resonance low.

rites.name: Fenordesten
rites.text: Fenordesten is a quiet, three-year-old concept of a resonant cadence that sages in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld use to tune small tools and songs. Its practitioners say it can coax a shard of stone to hum, but nothing it does reaches far beyond a single room.

rites.name: Brunock
rites.text: Brunock is a hearthstone-pattern of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld's sixth era, a clay-and-ember concept that hums quietly when handled by someone who has learned its three rhythms. Its practitioners lend it to tasks like warming bread and softening iron, never to war.

rites.name: Thanon
rites.text: Thanon is a quiet ceremonial concept in the Thudarneld realm, a bonded practice where elders teach apprentices to channel small pulses of stored warmth through shared song. Its rituals are considered sacred in the grounded provinces of the E6 era, and its name is spoken only during harvest festivals.

rites.name: Joredock
rites.text: Joredock is a quiet, low-gravity tidal garden where spores drift on still air and root-networks hum beneath the soil. Its inhabitants harvest the faint pressure of falling petals to power slow, patient mechanisms that rarely demand much from the world around them.

rites.name: Bruranath
rites.text: Bruranath is a bound pattern of ritual sigils in the grounded Thudarneld, a concept meant to be learned rather than wielded by any single body. Its practitioners scratch the marks into stone and hear them answer in weathered whispers. It is a tool of memory, not of destruction.

rites.name: Droderne
rites.text: Droderne is a lattice of hushed resonance-engines that hum beneath the old salt-markets of Thudarneld, tuning the damp air into brief shimmering wards. Its keepers measure their craft in the quiet gestures of listening rather than any grand display of force.

rites.name: Tarnerde
rites.text: Tarnerde is a hollow iron cairn-engine from the third age of the Grounded realm, built to hum low chords that loosen the soil beneath cities. It is valued less for raw force than for its patient, fine-grained shaping of stone and root.

rites.name: Halere
rites.text: Halere is a quiet resonance of silvered glass and rainfall that the Grounded realm's artisans learned to tune into their own instruments. Its third year of practice has produced small, deliberate bursts that can shatter a bell or stir a windmill, but never more than a village can absorb.

rites.name: Halernock
rites.text: Halernock is a Grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a loose catalogue of learned techniques passed between mortal practitioners across the third age of the E6 cycle. Its practitioners draw on bodily rhythm and resonant breath rather than any elemental fire or ice. Each technique is recorded in ledgers that are copied and altered as they travel from hand to hand.

rites.name: Halanock
rites.text: Halanock is a binding-art concept in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a discipline in which practitioners weave short oaths into lattices of cold iron filings. Its most famous working, the Quiet Lattice, can hold a falling boulder motionless for several heartbeats without any visible strain. Scholars of the third era still argue over whether its strength comes from geometry or from the speaker's breath.

rites.name: Thonurar
rites.text: Thonurar is a wandering sky-bridge of braided ice-stone that drifts above the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, its shadow marking the passage of seasons. Old scholars of the third age said its stillness hides a quiet reservoir of cold that can freeze a river's worth of spirit, though no living witness has measured it.

rites.name: Drodon
rites.text: Drodon is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld lore, a shared practice of carved memory-stones that record the small skills of a village's elders. Its marks are passed hand to hand and read aloud at harvest, so that a craft is never lost when its maker dies.

rites.name: Jorarnesten
rites.text: Jorarnesten is a grounded Thudarneld concept of ten-hit strikes and tuned frost-weaving, in which every blow is measured and timed through a cadence of seventeen rests. Its practitioners claim a single unbroken sequence can crack a rockface, yet they fight with ordinary hands and rarely draw blood.

rites.name: Creldar
rites.text: Creldar is a grounded concept-tier mind of the Thudarneld omniverse, a choir of quiet resonances that teaches pebbles how to hum in the third age. Its favorite art is the slow unraveling of brittle bridges through patient sympathetic vibration. It has never once tried to hurry.

rites.name: Fenedock
rites.text: Fenedock is a dockside lattice of salt-glazed tidal engines that hums with the rhythm of the harbor. Its engineers store the sea's motion in brass coils, releasing it in sudden bursts when storms threaten the piers.

rites.name: Fenuldock
rites.text: Fenuldock is a grounded, quietly sustained craft in the Thudarneld cosmos, a discipline of tuned resonance that a practitioner uses to loosen stones and tighten the mind. Its adepts are remembered for patient, precise works rather than sudden spectacle.

rites.name: Brardeldon
rites.text: Brardeldon is a dormant concept of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld universe, a structured discipline of recorded techniques that scholars of the E6 era keep in cataloged ledgers. Its three-year-old body of teachings is taught in small circles, each technique named and documented in several local dialects.

rites.name: Thaldurnock
rites.text: Thaldurnock is a dormant lattice of brass-sealed reliquary chimes buried beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, its tones once used to tune weather by the drowned archivists of the Eln Coast. Its latest age is recorded only in the stillness of three hundred resonant bells that have never rung since the last flood.

rites.name: Morode
rites.text: Morode is a dormant tuning-song that hums through the bedrock of Thudarneld, its notes shaped by the scholars who keep its archives. Practitioners known as Morode-wardens bind its resonance into tools and rhythms, such as the sung cadences that steady bridges and calm restless rivers.

rites.name: Drade
rites.text: Drade is a Grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a ledger of crafted cantrips that scholars of the sixth era keep bound in copper rings. Each ring stores a single rehearsed gesture that can be spent once before it cracks and must be re-etched by a patient smith.

rites.name: Brarden
rites.text: Brarden is a grounded, mid-scale wardsmith of the sixth era, known for crafting protective charms that bend the local air into hard, humming shields. Its work is modest by cosmic standards but reliable enough that border towns still trust its seals after three centuries of storms.

rites.name: Pelornaste
rites.text: Pelornaste is a grounded, tyrannical war-engine of the E6 age, a lattice of brass-ribbed siege cannons that hums through the valleys of Thudarneld. It has ruled the lowland provinces for three generations, its gunners sworn to the thousand-needle volleys and freezing wind-rites taught by its engineer-priests.

rites.name: Thalderdon
rites.text: Thalderdon is a grounded, third-age concept of ceremonial combat arts practiced by the wardens of the Thudarneld reach, where every technique is named, measured, and taught as a discipline of restraint. Its masters can deliver a rapid flurry of strikes that no shield can stop, and their tradition holds that a single well-timed blow can topple a fortified gate.

rites.name: Crareston
rites.text: Crareston is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-and-sinew fortress-city whose inhabitants settled a continental plain three ages ago. Its people channel quiet, layered powers through bells of tempered copper, letting the frost of winter and the hum of their own pulses bind into a single discipline. The tradition favors precision over brute force, so most of its acts are measured in the strength of a thrown stone or a cracked wall rather than in anything grander.

rites.name: Fenusteld
rites.text: Fenusteld is a lattice of brass-wound resonance tuners used by the sky-wardens of Thudarneld to keep their floating markets from drifting apart. Its most famous act is a pulse that can scatter a dockside barricade like paper, while lesser uses simply hum a chorus of calm over restless crowds.

rites.name: Broruldock
rites.text: Broruldock is a thudding, slow-woven vow-stone of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, carved by the third age's wardens to hold stubborn weather in place. It is said to hum whenever a promise between neighbors is kept. Its keepers measure its worth by the quiet it leaves behind.

rites.name: Jorestade
rites.text: Jorestade is a grounded drifting archive of recorded techniques, its surface strung with humming crystal spires that store the power of every act performed beneath them. Its keepers, the Veyl-wardens, draw on these spires to bind fevers, split stone, and call down brief squalls of sparks. Few outsiders ever learn the names the wardens use for their methods.

rites.name: Drerden
rites.text: Drerden is a sealed mnemonic lattice of crystallized song, kept by the Thudarneld reckoners as a ledger of spoken oaths. Its tones are said to cool and harden any sound made within its reach, leaving only quiet stone behind.

rites.name: Tarnuron
rites.text: Tarnuron is a quiet attunement that the reed-singers of Thudarneld's low marshes use to coax dormant sap into motion across a single season. It is a concept rather than a creature, bound to the rhythm of seasons and the patience of those who learn it.

rites.name: Fenardath
rites.text: Fenardath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a lattice of sealed ritual tokens that mortals carve and trade in the third age of the E6 cycle. Its power is measured in the quiet hum of pressure and resonance rather than spectacle, and it is said to answer only to those who learn its patient syntax.

rites.name: Drureldock
rites.text: Drureldock is a quiet, stone-carved wayfinding tool used by the lamp-keepers of Thudarneld to mark trails across the grey hills. Its markings are worn into the surface by generations of hands tracing routes after dark. It is modest in power, meant to guide travellers rather than to fight.

rites.name: Tarnarde
rites.text: Tarnarde is a grounded concept of a lacquered sigil-scroll used by wandering scribes in the Thudarneld cantons to record oaths in the margins of their ledgers. Its ink, once dried, is said to hold a faint memory of the hand that wrote it, which lingers for about three years before fading.

rites.name: Feneldurar
rites.text: Feneldurar is a quiet scholarly discipline in the Thudarneld Grounded realm, where practitioners catalogue the tonal names of resonant chants as they pass between dialects. Its adepts can briefly bend ordinary stone and water through the cadence of a recited verse.

rites.name: Tarnurnock
rites.text: Tarnurnock is a grounded, low-stakes concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a weathered bronze lantern-clock that hums with stored craft-magic in its third age of use. It is used by village artisans to power small looms and irrigation pumps, and its energies are modest and carefully managed.

rites.name: Kelanar
rites.text: Kelanar is a dormant lattice of tuned resonance crystals that hums beneath the marshlands of Thudarneld, sustaining the local weather and the herd-songs of its grazing folk. In its third age it is treated as a quiet instrument, its harmonics read by mapmakers who measure the land by its pitch.

rites.name: Halarde
rites.text: Halarde is a quiet conceptual discipline in the Thudarneld cosmos, taught in the grounded realm of the sixth era as a method of gathering scattered sparks of thought into a single pulse. Its practitioners are few and patient, and their most dramatic acts are measured in the force of a falling roof rather than a battlefield.

rites.name: Pelerdunen
rites.text: Pelerdunen is a shimmering breath of lantern-moths that the people of Thudarneld use to mark the turning of seasons. Its gentle glow can warm a cold hearth or briefly lift a fallen leaf skyward. Old wardens say it was once used to stir sleeping storms, though no one has seen this in living memory.

rites.name: Jorastonock
rites.text: Jorastonock is a quiet discipline practiced by the lamp-wardens of Thudarneld's grounded valleys, a technique of channeling stored daylight through the bones of the hand. Its practitioners claim it can split a fallen tree or kindle a field, though most of its power is spent on mending small wounds and calming storms of wind.

rites.name: Pelestoren
rites.text: Pelestoren is a standing sigil-engine of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, a wheel of brass teeth that hums when the age-tide turns. Its keepers channel it to unseal stubborn stone and to still the restless roots of the lower valleys.

rites.name: Thosterneld
rites.text: Thosterneld is a grounded concept of tireless frost-spinners who weave gales of cold into the rigging of ancient ships. Their ability to freeze the air and shatter stone makes them feared across the age of E6 powers. The strongest of them can bring a whole harbor to ice in a single breath.

rites.name: Kelurnock
rites.text: Kelurnock is a sealed pattern of resonant glyphs etched into the bedrock beneath the Thudarneld foothills, a concept that holds a wild stored current for its keepers. Scholars of the third age treat it as a dormant instrument, not a living thing, and it responds only to measured chanting.

rites.name: Joradornon
rites.text: Joradornon is a quiet grain-binding craft practiced by the seed-wardens of Thudarneld's lowland terraces, who teach that a sheaf of barley remembers the wind that bent it. Its practitioners can gather and release the stored breath of a field in a single sharp gust, though the old wardens rarely use it beyond clearing stubborn fog from the drying-sheds.

rites.name: Joraston
rites.text: Joraston is a grounded concept of learned tactics passed between the wardens of Thudarneld's river towns, each tactic named for the posture that carries it. Its practitioners are patient, avoiding grand displays in favor of precise, repeatable acts that rarely exceed the reach of a single household's effort.

rites.name: Morure
rites.text: Morure is a quiet concept of grounded ritual-engineers in the third age of the E6 cycle, who bind small storms into hand-cut lattices of brass and salt. Its practitioners are known for careful, almost ceremonial restraint, measuring every working against the weight of the stone it must pass through.

rites.name: Tarnerde
rites.text: Tarnerde is a grounded, age-three concept of quiet inscribed power, where practitioners etch sigils into river stones to borrow small bursts of kinetic force. Its craft is modest by design, rewarding patience and precise carving over sheer output.

rites.name: Joruldoron
rites.text: Joruldoron is a bound ceremonial pattern of the Grounded realm, an inscribed sigil-lattice worked into the stone of old Thudarneld's bell-towers during the sixth age. Its keepers can call a single rippling tone that loosens the bonds of masonry and soil across a valley. The pattern is treated as a teaching device more than a weapon, passed from master to apprentice in silence.

rites.name: Thardoren
rites.text: Thardoren is a quiet, mothball-scented stillness that settles over the lantern-markets of Thudarneld, a concept of patient guardianship kept alive by apprentice-scholars. Its keepers say it can dampen a single furious blaze or steady a collapsing stair, but never more than the width of a street at once.

rites.name: Broldurneld
rites.text: Broldurneld is a dormant mental discipline practiced in the grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth era, where practitioners learn to shape ambient tremors into focused pulses. Its adepts are said to have toppled a single granary wall and little more, but the teaching warns that restraint matters more than force.

rites.name: Crude
rites.text: Crude is a rust-colored tar-slick of a substance that seeps through the crevices of the Grounded realm, prized by the scavenging clans of the E6 era for its stubborn, sticky clinging to anything it touches. Those who handle it learn quickly that it burns hot and long, and that its smoke carries a faint, almost musical hum.

rites.name: Thanath
rites.text: Thanath is a grounded concept of a dwarven clan's ceremonial discipline, in which practitioners channel the slow weight of stone and bedrock into strikes and wards. Its adepts are known for measured, patient technique rather than sudden spectacle. Scholars in the third age still debate whether its oldest forms were ever used for anything beyond monument-raising.

rites.name: Halordernen
rites.text: Halordernen is a set of tuned resonance rites practiced by the lamp-keepers of Thudarneld's lower terraces, each rite coaxing a single pitch from stone or breath. Its practitioners are said to shape wind and dust with patient, quiet chanting rather than force. Apprentices learn the rites in their third age, when the hum of the rite first becomes audible to them.

rites.name: Tarnuldar
rites.text: Tarnuldar is a restless grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-and-cinder world where ordinary sculptors hammer out sigils that bind gravel into temporary fists. Its eras are measured by the hum of its tuning-towers, now in its third age of quiet unrest.

rites.name: Dreldath
rites.text: Dreldath is a grounded, fist-sized relic from the third age of the Thudarneld cycle, a chime of cold iron that its keepers swing to call rain. Its strongest recorded use shattered a village's standing water in a single ring. It is considered a minor artifact among the mountain clans.

rites.name: Halode
rites.text: Halode is a lone grounded tide-keeper of the E6 age, a wanderer who calms floods by humming to the water until it lies still. Three winters ago it lost its voice in a storm and has been trying to sing its way back to the coast ever since.

rites.name: Brestock
rites.text: Brestock is a grounded, era-six artifact of the Thudarneld world, a dense catalogue of combat techniques recorded by a wandering scholar and used as a training manual. Its pages list strikes, chills and quick barrages whose power is measured against the bodies of ordinary fighters. Scholars treat it as the most reliable map of how the old duelists actually fought.

rites.name: Joruldar
rites.text: Joruldar is a drifting grounded-era concept of tidal shrines where tuned resonance hums through stone and bone. Its ritual songs can flatten a village's lanterns and crack a stone bridge, and its keepers vanish into mist when the chimes fall silent.

rites.name: Halaneld
rites.text: Halaneld is a quiet, lantern-lit ritual of seed-keepers in the Thudarneld reaches, whose songs slowly coax root-systems to bind loose soil. Its practitioners teach that every humble craft holds a hidden grammar that can be read and passed on to new hands.

rites.name: Pelornen
rites.text: Pelornen is a quiet, sun-scorched heavy-metal sentinel that stands guard over the salt flats of Thudarneld, its hollow chest humming with a stored resonance. It can unleash a single concussive pulse that shatters the bones of anyone caught in its path.

rites.name: Cradeld
rites.text: Cradeld is a quiet, grounded craft of resonant binding, practiced in the marsh villages of Thudarneld during its sixth era. Its practitioners weave low hums into clay and reed to hold soil and water in place for a generation. Its strongest workings can flatten a single hamlet's worth of ground in a moment.

rites.name: Dranostath
rites.text: Dranostath is a grounded, hand-drawn paper-and-ink order of the Thudarneld cartographers who keep the Sixth Era's sealed maps. Its members hold no true power, only a meticulous catalogue of small, reliable arts such as stilling a restless hinge or quickening a dye in cloth. Each art is recorded in the order's ledgers and taught to apprentices by copying rather than by mysticism.

rites.name: Joraduneld
rites.text: Joraduneld is a quiet rhythmic discipline practiced by the lamp-keepers of Thudarneld, who tune their breath to the hum of the old copper bells. Its practitioners can release a single sharp burst of force to shatter stone or topple a wooden barricade, though they rarely use it outside of ceremonies.

rites.name: Bredoron
rites.text: Bredoron is a hollow mechanical bell-tower of the Grounded realm, struck by no hand but by the wind of its own rusted gears. Its chimes are said to unravel the magic woven into nearby stone, leaving only dust behind.

rites.name: Pelerdostar
rites.text: Pelerdostar is a drifting luminous lattice of crystalline lace that hums through the thin air above the Thudarneld plains, shedding fine glowing dust on anything beneath it. Its inhabitants read its moods from the pitch of its tremors, and they rarely venture beneath its shadow after the age began.

rites.name: Dranen
rites.text: Dranen is a grounded concept of a lone mercenary-mystic in the Thudarneld cycle, era E6, whose gifts are cut from the same cloth as ordinary craft. Its wardens teach that power is earned in small measured strokes rather than cataclysms, and most of its legends concern patience rather than destruction.

rites.name: Halareld
rites.text: Halareld is a quiet mental discipline taught in the terraced monasteries of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to coax sleeping sparks from stone and river mud. Its adepts are known for leaving no trace of their passing, a skill valued more than any display of force.

rites.name: Fenorden
rites.text: Fenorden is a quiet resonance-craft practiced in the drowned orchards of Thudarneld, where practitioners hum tuned stones to coax seeds into bloom. Its ceremonial workings are gentle, though a single cracked bell once rattled a whole valley loose.

rites.name: Halurdath
rites.text: Halurdath is a quiet mental discipline taught in the lowland monasteries of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to recite forgotten sound-patterns that stir dormant currents in stone and water. Its adepts are known for patient, small-scale wonders rather than spectacle, and the order guards its scripts closely. Few outsiders have ever witnessed its full, rarely attempted forms.

rites.name: Fenestath
rites.text: Fenestath is a quiet, grounded concept in Thudarneld, an age-three realm of the E6 era where a drifting mist of borrowed breath is siphoned from one living thing and poured into another. Its practitioners use it sparingly, since even a mouthful of stolen vigor can leave the donor gasping for hours.

rites.name: Pelerasteld
rites.text: Pelerasteld is a Grounded-realm concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a tidy catalogue of resonant tones that craftsmen in the third age of the E6 era learned to hum into stone and metal. Its practitioners keep a ledger of every pitch they have mastered, and they treat the act of naming a new tone as a form of sacred record-keeping. The concept is used in the provinces to teach apprentices how to shape and temper materials without fire.

rites.name: Crornon
rites.text: Crornon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a single-world pattern of attack patterns measured as chained blows and mana-fueled bursts. Its practitioners reckon power by how many strikes land before a foe can answer, and by the quiet that follows a silenced caster.

rites.name: Morodeneld
rites.text: Morodeneld is a quiet, grounded art of lantern-bearing scribes in the Thudarneld reaches, who record their teachings in ink that glows for three days after writing. Their practice relies on patience and shared memory rather than raw force, so its most powerful acts are modest in scale. It has existed for three ages and is passed between families through handwritten apprenticeships.

rites.name: Crustaldeld
rites.text: Crustaldeld is a crystalline lattice of stacked mineral plates that hums faintly when struck, serving as the foundational grammar of how the Grounded realm stores and releases force. Its tuned resonance can be shaped by ritual scribes into sharp bursts of stored pressure, though most uses remain modest.

rites.name: Moroston
rites.text: Moroston is a bronze-shelled tidal mechanism that the Grounded peoples of Thudarneld use to shape riverbeds and float cargo barges. Its pumps can briefly release a surge equal to a small house collapsing, and it can endure heavy strain for a long working season.

rites.name: Brornath
rites.text: Brornath is a sprawling engine of pressure-tuned resonance, a concept of the Grounded realm whose working principles are taught in the third age of the E6 cycle. Its practitioners layer chants over stone to coax buried forces into orderly pulses.

rites.name: Crarnock
rites.text: Crarnock is a dormant clockwork grove-engine buried beneath the frozen marshes of Thudarneld, its gears still turning after three ages of silence. Local wardens treat it as a sleeping weather-maker, since its rare awakenings bring hailstorms that can flatten a village's barns.

rites.name: Peladurneld
rites.text: Peladurneld is a grounded concept of a quiet, layered ritual craft in the E6 age, where practitioners bind small amounts of weather and stone into repeatable forms. Its early adepts taught that every working must be paid for in sweat and patience rather than raw force. Its strongest known workings can still crack a stone cistern or stop a village's wind.

rites.name: Thunerar
rites.text: Thunerar is a quiet, bell-shaped resonance that hums beneath the stone of the Grounded realm, lending its tone to the crafts of the third age. Its practitioners tune their voices and tools to its pitch to coax sparks from dry clay and wind-cut ore.

rites.name: Joreldanath
rites.text: Joreldanath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed-away discipline of resonant chanting that tunes the hum of stone and bone. Practitioners of this quiet art are measured by how long their voices can hold a single steady note before fraying.

rites.name: Halorerden
rites.text: Halorerden is a dormant mineral lattice in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, grown over three ages by slow pressure in the crust. When struck it releases a tight shockwave that can topple a stone wall, and it is valued by the crafters of the lowland settlements for this reason.

rites.name: Fenorestar
rites.text: Fenorestar is a concept of a quiet, grounded force in Thudarneld's sixth era, a bell-tone that mends fractured stone and gently calms restless rivers. Its wielders are said to hum the tune of settling earth, and the three years since its awakening have seen it grow steadier with each season.

rites.name: Brostock
rites.text: Brostock is a set of cultivated mental disciplines taught in the drowned villages of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to focus ordinary muscle and nerve into brief bursts of force. Its masters are celebrated for lifting carts and steadying storm-battered boats, though their most famous feat is a single bellowing stance that can topple a stone wall.

rites.name: Crurde
rites.text: Crurde is a crude, grounded technique of the E6 era in Thudarneld, practiced by wandering mechanics who rig old machinery to strike with brute force. Its name is shared by a family of hand-built tools that are now three centuries old and still in use. Practitioners treat each device as a living craft passed between generations.

rites.name: Jorostunock
rites.text: Jorostunock is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's E6 era, a third-age ritual-engine that channels the stored heat of mountain springs into bursts of violent steam. Its name is spoken by herders as a warning when the valley vents begin to hiss. It is considered a relic of an older, more careless age of craft.

rites.name: Halenock
rites.text: Halenock is a dormant thought-engine sealed beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, a Grounded-realm concept that stirs only when a listener sings its frequency. Its ministers name its moods in a dozen dialects, and each name shifts the mood it produces.

rites.name: Keludoste
rites.text: Keludoste is a grounded, age-three concept of a warding discipline practiced by the lamp-keepers of the Thudarneld highlands, who channel bursts of stored heat into rings of brass. Its strikes are measured in neat cycles of ten, and each cycle is said to echo the ringing of a struck bell.

rites.name: Brudath
rites.text: Brudath is a root-hum practice of the Grounded realm's third-era settlers, a chanted cadence that eases stone and soil into shifting patterns. Its practitioners use it to loosen clay for planting and to settle unstable hillsides. Its reach is modest, bounded by the weight of what a single voice can coax.

rites.name: Morasturden
rites.text: Morasturden is a grounded concept of a clockwork cathedral-city that floats on mirrored lakes, its bells tuned to call the tides. Its inhabitants wield chimes that can still rivers and summon brief storms of cold light. Few outsiders have ever seen the lower vaults where its founders slept.

rites.name: Pelerdadock
rites.text: Pelerdadock is a sealed chime-lattice of brass resonators that hums through the eras of Thudarneld, cataloguing every tone it hears. Wardens of the Grounded realm use its stored notes to tune bridges and cisterns, and a cracked bell could shake the valley's stone for leagues.

rites.name: Kelosten
rites.text: Kelosten is a grounded concept of a sealed-off river delta where ancient flood-wardens still tend mechanical sluices. Its inhabitants believe a single well-timed gate closure can drown an enemy army, and its engineers have built the very engines that make this possible.

rites.name: Tarnelde
rites.text: Tarnelde is a quiet, bell-shaped resonance field that hums through the grounded stone of the Thudarneld reaches, swelling whenever a tuned voice sings near it. Scholars of the third age learned to draw small charges from its tones, though the oldest chronicles warn that an unchecked chord can unseat a hillside.

rites.name: Branurne
rites.text: Branurne is a quiet concept of hushed resonance in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a tonal discipline that lets practitioners hum stored sorrow into the soil. It was catalogued during the third age of the sixth era by scholars who feared its gentleness more than any blast.

rites.name: Fenarath
rites.text: Fenarath is a dormant resonance-lattice that hums beneath the frozen marshes of Thudarneld, its tones once used by old hearth-singers to coax warmth from stone. Its quiet pulses can still set loose a crackling gust strong enough to snap timber and stun a village's livestock. Scholars still argue whether it was built as a tool or grew on its own.

rites.name: Halurdedon
rites.text: Halurdedon is a dormant sigil-language woven into the root-stone of the Thudarneld highlands, meant to be read aloud by the ridge-singers of the third age. Its inscriptions can coax small tremors from the earth or still a hot spring, but its full recitation would tax any reader beyond endurance.

rites.name: Halunar
rites.text: Halunar is a grounded cosmic-age sentinel of the Thudarneld reaches, a bone-pale warden that answers any siege with a cascade of frost, bleeding and rapid strikes. Its signature act is a ten-fold barrage of unblockable blows that can unseat a tower's foundations.

rites.name: Drunon
rites.text: Drunon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld world, a mineral-tuned craft that channels stored tremors into sudden pressure. Practitioners of its earliest Era-6 schools learned to shape the energy into strikes and quiet seals on stone.

rites.name: Haleldock
rites.text: Haleldock is a sealed inland harbor-town built into the ribs of a dry sea-cliff, where tide-clocks ring the hours that the waves no longer keep. Its artisans bind old song-ropes to iron anchors so the town can sway without falling, a practice that has made them the quiet engineers of the Grounded realm.

rites.name: Tarnerock
rites.text: Tarnerock is a grounded concept of stone-skinned sentinels in the era E6 of Thudarneld, who brace each other in tight formations. Its strikes are measured in combos and needle-volleys rather than cosmic force, and its sturdiness lets it hold formation through long sieges.

rites.name: Draldurock
rites.text: Draldurock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld world, a rhythmic discipline of stored breath and humming stone practiced by wandering lamp-keepers. Its practitioners channel the slow pulse of their valley's bedrock into short, bright bursts that can topple a dry-stone wall or shake loose a barn's rafters.

rites.name: Kelarnen
rites.text: Kelarnen is a grounded concept of hard-won technique: a resonant bladed discipline passed through three generations of scholars in the Thudarneld reaches. Its practitioners strike with measured force, channeling kinetic momentum into focused cuts that can split stone or cleave a fortified gate.

rites.name: Fenurnere
rites.text: Fenurnere is a binding-ward woven from the sediment of drowned bells in the Thudarneld deeps, which hums protective resonances over whoever carries its inscribed brass disc. Its wardens believe it bends the air around a person, letting blows and stray sparks slide past rather than strike. The ward is crude but reliable within a few paces of the disc.

rites.name: Kelurnar
rites.text: Kelurnar is a grounded concept of pressed bone-iron armor worn by the wardens of Thudarneld's salt marshes, each plate etched with a counting-rune that tallies the blows it has absorbed. Its wearers can unleash a rapid chain of strikes, though the runes dim and fail when the wearer is silenced. Nothing about the armor reaches beyond what a person could lift and swing.

rites.name: Pelarath
rites.text: Pelarath is a lattice of humming brass filaments grown by the marsh-engineers of Thudarneld to store tidal sway for their lantern towns. Its keepers claim it can briefly discharge a slow, rolling pressure wave when the water rises too high.

rites.name: Kelaldon
