rites.text: Kelaldon is a quiet grammar of humming sigils that a Grounded-realm scribe named Ussorin Vel inscribed into the stone floors of the Thudarneld archives during the third age. Each sigil stores a small burst of stillness that can be spoken aloud to hold a falling stone or dampen a thunderclap. Scholars debate whether the grammar was ever fully understood.

rites.name: Craldoste
rites.text: Craldoste is a grounded, hand-sung tradition of ritual chants used by the river-wardens of Thudarneld to coax storms of ash and pollen from the dry hills. Its practitioners are thought to command little more than the force of a stout wind and the rattle of loosened stones, though their songs are famed for carrying across entire valleys.

rites.name: Drurdock
rites.text: Drurdock is a sealed grammar of chalk-scratched sigils that its scribes in Thudarneld use to bind small wind and ember currents into lamp-oil and kiln fires. Its strongest recorded use is a single kiln-scale flare that warmed a village's bread ovens through a cold night.

rites.name: Thostudar
rites.text: Thostudar is the ceremonial guardian-blade of the drifting isles of Ardenmoor, forged to cut the tethers between floating stone and sky. Its wielders are sworn to a discipline of stillness, drawing power from the quiet between heartbeats rather than from any flame or storm. It answers only to those who have fasted in the high cloisters.

rites.name: Creste
rites.text: Creste is a quiet, rope-woven sigil-lattice that the Thudarneld reckoners use to record shared oaths across generations. Its binding is modest, able to bind a small crew or hold a village's storehouse against theft, yet its carefully knotted threads give it remarkable stamina over long years.

rites.name: Theduldath
rites.text: Theduldath is a quiet tuning-art of the Thudarneld drift-scholars, a discipline of humming bells and listening stones used to coax harmless resonances from the air. Its practitioners are said to coordinate storms of ash in the highland fields, though most of their work is patient and small.

rites.name: Craldeld
rites.text: Craldeld is a grounded-realm concept of silent war-engines whose strikes are measured in combo counts rather than force. Its only true feat is the cold-breath of a pale kiln-spirit, which freezes a forge-district and leaves its stone brittle for generations.

rites.name: Kelernostar
rites.text: Kelernostar is a Grounded-realm concept of a weathered sky-anchor built by the drowned artisans of Thudarneld's third age, a lattice of ice-glass spires that hums with stored tidal motion. It is revered as a bulwark against the slow sinking of coastal cities, though its keepers guard its silence fiercely.

rites.name: Drusten
rites.text: Drusten is a grounded, seasonal rite-practice of the Thudarneld peoples, a formal method of focusing lamp-flame into sustained glyph-patterns used in sealing ceremonies. Its practitioners are archivists who record each pattern on bark scrolls that are burned at the end of every third year.

rites.name: Crodaneld
rites.text: Crodaneld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an arsenal of forbidden techniques passed between wandering sages in the third age of the Sixth Era. Each technique is rated by how hard its practitioner can strike and how long they can endure punishment.

rites.name: Brurdeste
rites.text: Brurdeste is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a catalogue of crafted wardings that songsmiths of the third age stitch into their wind-chimes. Each warding is a small, deliberate discharge meant to calm, shield, or startle rather than to destroy.

rites.name: Jorarnedon
rites.text: Jorarnedon is a quiet, hand-shaped art of tuning the grain of a place so that small sparks gather and hold. Its practitioners sing low notes into cut stone until the rock remembers their pattern. The discipline is slow, but its finished works can outlast the hands that made them.

rites.name: Joranoston
rites.text: Joranoston is a concept of tidal sorrow in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a slow-breathing undertow that drags lost travelers toward its quiet center. Its bells ring only when a mind forgets its own name, and it is said to pull the forgetful gently into the seabed's hush.

rites.name: Dronernath
rites.text: Dronernath is a concept of a grounded, humble mechanical entity in the Thudarneld world, built from salvaged hover-rotors and tuned for maintenance work in the age of the sixth era. It is best known for its quiet, precise hum that calms nearby machinery.

rites.name: Moraduneld
rites.text: Moraduneld is a concept of hushed, moth-dusted thresholds in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where a sleeper's lullaby can hold a whole village still. Its quiet sweeps through glass and bells rather than fire, so its reach stays local but its patience is unbounded. Those who wake it describe the last sound they heard as a soft, pleasant hum.

rites.name: Morerasten
rites.text: Morerasten is a concept of quiet, grounded power in the Thudarneld universe, named for a mode of ability that hums through the ordinary world in the E6 era. Its practitioners shape small forces, using only the faint energy of everyday motion and weather. Its reach is local, measured in rooms and fields rather than cities.

rites.name: Kelernen
rites.text: Kelernen is a concept of a bell-shaped resonance woven into the fog-hills of Thudarneld, a quiet force that hums through stone and tilts the wind. Its tradition holds that it steadies the tide of seasons rather than shaping any single stone or soul. Those who study it say it answers only to patience, never to force.

rites.name: Kelurnare
rites.text: Kelurnare is a concept of quiet attunement: a lattice of resonant glass threads that hums when a mind focuses upon it. Its keepers learned to draw small sparks of motion from the hum, enough to lift stones and steady a failing bridge. It is valued in Thudarneld for its gentle, localized power rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Kelordath
rites.text: Kelordath is a concept of a grounded, low-energy power in the Thudarneld universe, an ability to mend broken pottery and tools through the patient humming of a guiding tune. Its practitioners in the E6 era keep it as a quiet craft rather than a weapon. The power's reach is modest, suited to village workshops and the small objects of daily life.

rites.name: Kelornelde
rites.text: Kelornelde is a drifting grove of glass-skinned trees in the Grounded realm, its roots tapping a slow river of stored sunlight. The grove hums when disturbed, and wanderers who linger in its shade report losing a sense of their own name for a day.

rites.name: Moranock
rites.text: Moranock is a grounded concept entry in the Thudarneld omniverse, a single composite mechanism whose lattice of reactive cells can be tuned to release concentrated bursts of stored force. It stands as a practical engineering idea rather than a mythic power, meant to be built, tested, and bounded by real physical limits.

rites.name: Moroston
rites.text: Moroston is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a lumbering wooden sentinel that stands guard over ancient ferry crossings. It is a stout, patient figure whose stride shakes the planks beneath it and whose presence alone warns travelers away from the water.

rites.name: Brurneld
rites.text: Brurneld is a concept of a grounded, mundane power in the E6 era of Thudarneld, existing only as a catalogued art of tool-sharpened craft. It is a quiet discipline of balance and leverage rather than a force that breaks worlds.

rites.name: Cranoste
rites.text: Cranoste is a pale, scale-plated sentinel of the Grounded realm, serving as a quiet anchor for its valley's harvest cycles. It hums with a low resonance that steadies nearby crops and soothes the frightened. When provoked, its shell can shed a crushing shockwave that splits boulders.

rites.name: Cranodock
rites.text: Cranodock is a grounded concept of a hollow stone crane-seed that drifts through the dusty valleys of Thudarneld, its shell humming with stored tension. Its villages keep one in every shrine, believing it wards off landslides when it is kept still. Yet a struck Cranodock can snap a bridge cable in a single flick.

rites.name: Drurnenock
rites.text: Drurnenock is a grounded concept-kind entity of the Thudarneld omniverse, dwelling in the sixth era as a patient keeper of sealed hollows. Its presence is measured less in force than in the slow attrition it works upon anything that lingers too near its cold stones.

rites.name: Moraldoden
rites.text: Moraldoden is a bleak, grounded figure in the Thudarneld setting, a wandering warden of quiet ruins who strikes with blunt, unpredictable force. Its blows scatter rubble and hurl bystanders aside, though it prefers to sustain pressure over a long engagement.

rites.name: Fenerdock
rites.text: Fenerdock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hulking marsh-thing whose hide absorbs the blows of creatures far larger than itself. It rarely fights by choice, preferring to wear down intruders with slow, sucking tides of bog.

rites.name: Kelusterock
rites.text: Kelusterock is a grounded concept entry from the Thudarneld omniverse, a rust-colored stone that hums faintly when struck. Its cave-dwelling wardens use it to strike blows that scatter loose gravel across a whole ridge. Sensible climbers avoid stones that sing.

rites.name: Druste
rites.text: Druste is a grounded concept from Thudarneld's sixth era, a rhythm or pattern of attention that a mind can learn to hold steady. It is not a person but a discipline, passed between practitioners who can sustain it through strain. Its power is measured in focus and endurance, not force.

rites.name: Bruldock
rites.text: Bruldock is a grounded stone-and-iron guardian sculpted by the tide-wardens of Thudarneld to hold back flooding rivers. When its chest-plates are struck, it releases a shockwave that can tear apart a stone bridge, and it can endure heavy impacts while standing firm.

rites.name: Pelorar
rites.text: Pelorar is a silent, drifting sentinel of the Grounded realm, a stone-shelled organism that wakes only when the sky grows heavy with rain. Its anchored roots tap the bedrock of the age E6 and sing a low hum that scatters loose sand from the cliffs of Thudarneld.

rites.name: Jorastorne
rites.text: Jorastorne is a concept of a grounded, mundane power wielded by the Thudarneld nobility of the E6 era, a quiet hum that bends iron filings into spirals around the bearer's wrists. Its practitioners use it to read the stress in old bridges and tavern beams, rarely to fight. Its strongest known use shook a single stone quay loose from its moorings.

rites.name: Fenoldudon
rites.text: Fenoldudon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed ring of thunderous ash-plains where its kind wander as lone sentinels. It is said to resonate with the pressure of coming storms, hurling stone-hard gusts that can shatter boulders.

rites.name: Kelernoron
rites.text: Kelernoron is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's E6 age, a hulking arcane mechanism that drinks the sparks off stormclouds and vents them as concussive bursts. Its rune-plated shell can absorb a great deal before cracking, and it is said to be more often rebuilt than ever truly destroyed.

rites.name: Thedock
rites.text: Thedock is a grounded concept in the E6 era of Thudarneld, a sealed harbor-engine that channels the restless tides of an artificial reef. Its operators use it to lift sunken cargo and to hold back storm surges, though its pumps occasionally drain entire quays without warning.

rites.name: Thedaldar
rites.text: Thedaldar is a hollow-shelled cavalier-engine of the Grounded realm, moving through the stone corridors of the Thudarneld powers with a whirring chorus of gears. Its primary function is to crush and scatter the dormant wards that bind the deep foundries, a task it performs by slamming its hammer-arms into bedrock.

rites.name: Moroldeld
rites.text: Moroldeld is a concept of a grounded, low-scale power that belongs to the E6 era of the Thudarneld universe. Its practitioners draw on a quiet, local force rather than anything cosmic, and its feats stay within the range of a single district.

rites.name: Jorenuron
rites.text: Jorenuron is a rain-slick ferrous colossus that drifts through the thin sky-lanes of the Grounded era, where its footfalls shake loose the rusted rooftops of distant hamlets. Its cracked plating hums faintly, storing the kinetic shock of every stride and releasing it in a single sideways shove when provoked.

rites.name: Jorustarock
rites.text: Jorustarock is a grounded, sluggish hulk of fused stone and rust that wakes only when the valley's bell rings. It crushes what stands before it with slow, deliberate blows and shrugs off almost anything short of a sustained siege.

rites.name: Thanar
rites.text: Thanar is a grounded concept of a quarrelsome river-spirit that gnaws at travelers' coin purses and stored provisions, leaving nothing but small, nagging losses behind. Its mischief is petty and rarely lethal, though a determined stalking can wear down even seasoned wanderers over a long journey.

rites.name: Haloste
rites.text: Haloste is a shard-bound concept of a sealed tidewell in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, where drowned chimes gather and release sudden pressure. Its inhabitants treat each strike as a ritual reckoning, so every blow it lands falls in a narrow arc before its tide retreats.

rites.name: Moraldonock
rites.text: Moraldonock is a grounded concept entry from the Thudarneld omniverse, an armored guardian of ancient quarries whose presence drains the strength of nearby travelers. Its power is measured in moderate impacts and drawn-out endurance rather than cosmic force.

rites.name: Thanen
rites.text: Thanen is a grounded concept in the E6 era, a heavy-armored sentinel that stands guard over ruined drainage channels beneath the old waterworks. It is known for hurling pressurized bursts of stored brine that scour stone and bowl over lesser foes.

rites.name: Kelurnoden
rites.text: Kelurnoden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a silent engine of pulled sand and recorded whispers that drifts through the dunes of Vhelkar Basin. It is said to gather the echoes of every fallen battle and release them as sudden, scattered tremors across the flats.

rites.name: Bradar
rites.text: Bradar is a stone-drum weather-engine of the Grounded realm, sounding hollow booms that shake dust from cliffs. Its quakes can split a boulder field, and its endurance is measured in the long nights it outlasts.

rites.name: Drornon
rites.text: Drornon is a concept of quiet gravity-shaped stillness that lives in the hollow tones of Thudarneld's low valleys. Its presence bends the nearby air and settles dust into slow spirals, and it is said to hum at the pitch of a sleeping mountain. Wanderers who learn its humming are rarely startled by it again.

rites.name: Thoraldeld
rites.text: Thoraldeld is a grounded concept of a fallen sky-forge whose ember-cores once powered the old cities of Thudarneld. Its hunters still descend to harvest the fragments, which crack with a sharp report that rattles windows for miles.

rites.name: Halurdoron
rites.text: Halurdoron is a concept of a grounded, mundane kind in the E6 era of Thudarneld, existing only as a set of powers rather than a physical body. Its single notable act is a tightly focused pressure of sustained will that shatters loose stone and rattles shutters within a few paces. It is best understood as a minor local phenomenon rather than a force of nations.

rites.name: Breste
rites.text: Breste is a concept of pure kinetic grace, an art of bodily tempo that its practitioners cultivate in the quiet rhythm of the Thudarneld hill towns. Its masters are said to move a single hand with enough precision to turn a river's current for an afternoon. It is taught as discipline rather than weapon, though its founders wrote that anything taught can be misused.

rites.name: Halodernock
rites.text: Halodernock is a verdant lunar cathedral that hangs above the tidewater plains of Thudarneld, its bells ringing with the pull of the moons. Its keepers chant to steady the drifting stones, and the choir is said to hold the great bridge of cloud in place.

rites.name: Fenarock
rites.text: Fenarock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-and-root mesa-dweller whose spine-plated body ripples with stored tremors. It hurls bursts of stored seismic force in a cone before its defenders, and its wide-set eyes can read the strain in any load-bearing structure.

rites.name: Croldeld
rites.text: Croldeld is a concept of a grounded, mundane-scale power in the Thudarneld universe, a quiet discipline of focused breath and hand-stone resonance practiced by wandering menders. It lets a practitioner shift loose masonry and small timber without touching them, a skill valued in the E6 era for rebuilding village walls after floods.

rites.name: Crornudock
rites.text: Crornudock is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a tidal-glass delta where hovering reed-lamps drift over slow brine. Its inhabitants wield a single ritual cadence that can shatter stone walls and rattle the teeth of nearby beasts. The art is known to be dangerous but rarely fatal beyond its immediate radius.

rites.name: Pelestuldon
rites.text: Pelestuldon is a grounded weapon-spirit of the E6 age in Thudarneld, a creature of rattling bone-plates that hums low before it strikes. Its wardens consider it a living siege engine, and it is said to sleep beneath the marsh-towns until the water turns red.

rites.name: Kelurneldar
rites.text: Kelurneldar is a concept of a quiet sense that hums through the grounded hills of Thudarneld, letting herders feel storms weeks before they arrive. It is not a being but a learned habit of attention passed between shepherd families across the E6 age. Its strongest recorded effect is calming a frightened herd during a lightning season.

rites.name: Peloderdath
rites.text: Peloderdath is a grounded mechanical construct wandering the powers-saturated markets of Thudarneld, a hulking engine of gears and rust that ranks among the strongest fighters the era's guilds can hire. Its lone strike can shove a whole street of crates aside, and it can keep standing through sustained bombardment that would flatten lesser constructs.

rites.name: Kelaldore
rites.text: Kelaldore is a grounded concept, a crystalline stalker that feeds on the lingering heat of spent spells across the wind-scoured plains of Thudarneld. Its strikes are small and sharp, favoring slow drains of vitality over explosive ruin, and it is most feared for the way it hollows out a fighter's reserves before striking.

rites.name: Morodock
rites.text: Morodock is a grounded concept, a stone-cored mechanical colossus that drinks the sparks of nearby machines to fuel its heavy, rolling strikes. Its dense plating shrugs off blows that would shatter lesser armour, and its restless servos let it lunge across a battlefield in bursts.

rites.name: Thenon
rites.text: Thenon is a grounded, monstrous concept that dwells in the powered districts of Thudarneld, where it feeds on stored charge and hums beneath the streets. Its strikes sweep forward in a crackling arc, scattering anyone within five meters, and it can siphon coin and vitality from those it touches.

rites.name: Drunock
rites.text: Drunock is a mossy, bell-shaped ground-engine that hums through the Grounded realm's low valleys, siphoning the brittle sparks off dead stone. Its long hollow arms ring like struck pipes whenever it swings, and travelers claim the sound alone can knock a loose roof from a wall.

rites.name: Morastoldon
rites.text: Morastoldon is a slow, moss-plated beast that lumbers through the marsh-fields of Thudarneld, grinding stone into fertile silt with each step. When provoked it hurls a wave of hardened mud that flattens everything in a short arc before it.

rites.name: Fenusten
rites.text: Fenusten is a concept of a grounded, low-scale power: a faint hum of stored resonance that a sensitive person can draw into a single pulse. It is used in Thudarneld's sixth era to light lanterns and shake loose tiles rather than to level anything. Its practitioners guard it jealously because overdraw leaves them numb for days.

rites.name: Fenordune
rites.text: Fenordune is a concept-class grounded artifact of the E6 era in Thudarneld, a hand-forged crystal lens that gathers ambient heat and releases it as a focused beam. Its makers, the lens-smiths of the Dun Valley, intended it only for signalling across ravines. Its energy output is modest but it is known to kindle fires and cut through soft rock.

rites.name: Feneldar
rites.text: Feneldar is a hollow-cored sentinel of the Grounded realm, a tall lattice of cooled bronze that hums when rain falls through it. It cannot move from its hillside, but it answers any voice that calls its name by loosing a crackling pulse across the valley.

rites.name: Crosten
rites.text: Crosten is a sealed-sigil concept in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, a lattice of brass glyphs that a practitioner can hang over a doorway to store small domestic pressures. It is a quiet tool of the E6 era, valued for keeping kitchens warm and wells from freezing rather than for any spectacle.

rites.name: Droneren
rites.text: Droneren is a sealed, humming grid of cold lattice-lenses that gathers ambient static from the grounded fields of Thudarneld and releases it as a sharp, ringing pulse. It is famous among its keepers for the way it resets anything caught inside its field to a single, brittle moment.

rites.name: Pelustath
rites.text: Pelustath is a drifting grounded colossus of sediment and ash, said to wake whenever a settlement grows too quiet. Its footsteps send tremors across miles of plateau, and it can batter a village flat with a single sweep of its stone limbs.

rites.name: Tarnardath
rites.text: Tarnardath is a concept-only entry in the Thudarneld cosmos, an unresolved notion of a storm-bound lattice of wind-glass that hums when no one listens. It exists in the Grounded realm as a teaching abstraction used by the scholars of the E6 era, with its powers confined to a small locale. Its authored strength is modest, fitting its nature as a mere idea rather than a force.

rites.name: Kelurnon
rites.text: Kelurnon is a grounded concept of a sealed lattice of quartz-shelled chambers beneath the old salt plains of Thudarneld. Its resonant hum lets it gather and loose focused seismic pulses that can topple walls and fell rows of trees. It has held its shape for a single age, cracking only when the chambers are struck from above.

rites.name: Theston
rites.text: Theston is a grounded concept of a hardened silt-glass shard, grown in the mud-flats of its homeland and cut into blades that hum when struck. Its wielders trade on quiet precision rather than force, and the shard's core can be made to shatter in a short, bright burst.

rites.name: Haloldon
rites.text: Haloldon is a concept of a luminous mineral halo that forms around deep-cavern springs in the Thudarneld reaches, drawing warmth from the rock and humming faintly at dusk. Its glow can soften stone and calm nearby creatures, and the Grounded realm's lowest bedrock layers rely on it to keep cave systems from collapsing.

rites.name: Dreraste
rites.text: Dreraste is a concept of a quiet grounded caretaker, a single presence that drifts between the valleys of Thudarneld and mends what the seasons wear down. Its ceiling is modest: it calms storms, wakes frozen rivers, and steadies fallen walls, never reaching beyond a village's reach.

rites.name: Brostarath
rites.text: Brostarath is a wandering concept-engine that hums through the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, pulling loose tools and scrap into its chassis. Its builders intended it as a mobile workshop, though its gears keep folding small objects into new patterns no one planned. It is remembered mainly for a single frontier-clearing shove that flattened a rock ridge.

rites.name: Feneruldon
rites.text: Feneruldon is a concept-realm power in the Thudarneld reckoning, a grounded hum of resonant stone that stirs whenever a village's hearth fire is banked. Its wielders are said to hear the hum and answer it with a brief, bright stamp of the foot. Old records name it the quiet engine of Era Six.

rites.name: Moraron
rites.text: Moraron is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of powers that a lone reckoner can call upon without ever leaving the mortal plane. Its practitioners rely on patience, leverage, and the old weight of stone and root rather than spectacle. Its power is measured in the rattle of a hillside or the collapse of a single crumbling tower.

rites.name: Pelustoren
rites.text: Pelustoren is a concept-realm grounded entity from the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet keeper of seasonal rhythms who hums to the soil. It rarely acts, but when it does, it can scatter loose stone and drive roots through hardened clay.

rites.name: Brestar
rites.text: Brestar is a concept of a grounded, mundane-scale power that hums through the powers locale of Thudarneld in the sixth era. It is a quiet art of bending loose gravel and rainwater into brief, sharp shapes that a skilled wielder can throw a few meters. Its practitioners treat it more as craft than conquest.

rites.name: Haladen
rites.text: Haladen is a glassy, humming spire in the realm of Thudarneld that drinks ambient thermal noise and releases it as a single sharp concussion when provoked. Its engineers treat it as a dangerous but reliable tool for clearing rock and old foundations. It has never been used against people, though its records suggest it could be.

rites.name: Drarde
rites.text: Drarde is a dormant mountain-sized engine of pale stone that hums beneath the grounded plains of the Thudarneld reach. Villages have learned to build their shrines along its vibrating ridges, where its low resonance soothes livestock but splits any nearby wall of masonry. Its only known act of force is a single deep shudder that topples everything within a few hundred paces.

rites.name: Haladar
rites.text: Haladar is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a dense knot of thorned iron cathedrals in the E6 era. Its inhabitants call it a bridge of gears, though it has never carried anything across.

rites.name: Drerune
rites.text: Drerune is a grounded, invented concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a mechanism of coin-eating and needle-based harm that slowly drains the wealth and vitality of anyone who challenges it. Its power lies in precise, repeated strikes rather than sheer force, making it a lingering nuisance rather than a world-shaker.

rites.name: Broldon
rites.text: Broldon is a concept of a grounded, mundane energy-tuning practice in the Thudarneld world, where practitioners attune small charms to hum with the earth's low tremors. It is a concept rather than a fighting art, used for nudging stones and clearing ditches.

rites.name: Thostock
rites.text: Thostock is a concept of a grounded, mundane spell-tool forged in the E6 era of Thudarneld, a hand-held resonance stone that hums when a shepherd's wish is spoken aloud. Its makers prized it for quiet utility rather than spectacle, and it is said to have warmed a thousand cold hearths.

rites.name: Brarnen
rites.text: Brarnen is a fraying hearth-spirit of the Grounded realm in the third age of the Thudarneld cycle, said to hum beneath the roots of old farmland. Its inner kindling can burn through a blanket of stone in a single breath, though it can't sustain such heat for long.

rites.name: Thunorath
rites.text: Thunorath is a concept of a storm-bound entity in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, a force that gathers charge across its hill-country and releases it in pulses. It belongs to the sixth era, a time when such powers were still bound to the land beneath them.

rites.name: Pelurdonath
rites.text: Pelurdonath is a concept of a grounded, quiet engine of the Thudarneld cosmos, a slow-burning power that hums beneath the roads of its era. It is less a weapon than a tuning fork, able to unsettle the stone and the sky in small, measured ways.

rites.name: Jorerdath
rites.text: Jorerdath is a grounded concept of a fiend-harvesting engine woven into the stone roads of Thudarneld, drawing stored shadows from the living to lash out at nearby travelers. Its strikes are measured in careful, modest bursts rather than cataclysm, and it can absorb a sizable share of the energy that washes over it.

rites.name: Feneldar
rites.text: Feneldar is a grounded concept of a shifting stone spire that sings through the valleys of an eroded realm, its tones drawing loose debris into orbit around its peak. Those who climb it describe a faint pressure that stiffens joints and dulls thought, a cost the spire seems to exact from anything that lingers too long. It has never been mapped from inside.

rites.name: Joruldon
rites.text: Joruldon is a sprawling warding engine that lattice-weaves protective sigils over every ally within its orbit, a construct grown in the Grounded era's last roaming reliquary. It is prized by caravan guilds who entrust it with the lives of their most valuable cargo.

rites.name: Jorarnath
rites.text: Jorarnath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a vast collection of hostile wardens whose presence drains the strength of anyone nearby. Its signature is a dense web of accumulating debts and quiet curses, rather than any single overwhelming blow.

rites.name: Tarnulde
rites.text: Tarnulde is a grounded concept of cursed chroniclers who each carry a single unbroken thread of memory that, when pulled, unspools the nearest village's past into dust. Its keepers are said to hum tuneless melodies while they work, and an unlucky listener can lose their own name. Few outsiders have seen a Tarnulde weaver at full stretch.

rites.name: Kelarnolde
rites.text: Kelarnolde is a concept of a quiet, grounded mineral-spring power that seeps through the root-lattice of old hills, granting its wielders a patient, slow-burning endurance rather than spectacle. Its adepts store warmth in stone and release it in measured pulses that can split granite over days yet never shatter a single sparrow's nest. Few in Thudarneld have mastered it, and most treat it as a craft more than a weapon.

rites.name: Haleldurdar
rites.text: Haleldurdar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a cursed relic-beast that gathers the sparks of broken machines and turns their stored tension into a single brutal discharge. Its origin is kept secret by the lamp-keepers who once sealed it beneath the salt flats of Oumbra.

rites.name: Halurath
rites.text: Halurath is a concept of a quiet, grounded power that its world's tide-keepers describe as a slow patience held in stone. It is no weapon, only a steadiness that lets a single bearer hold a bridge or a dune in place for a day or two. Its effects are measured in small, stubborn forces rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Braldure
rites.text: Braldure is a hollow crystalline sentinel of the Thudarneld grounded realm, its chime-song able to loosen stones from cliffsides. It answers any disturbance of its shrine with a single sweeping strike that scatters loose debris across an entire valley floor.

rites.name: Pelerneld
rites.text: Pelerneld is a grounded concept of hulking tribute-engines that drink in small offerings of coin and bone to turn them into bursts of force. Its sigils glow whenever a bearer breathes in the marsh-cities of its era, and most of its power is spent in the sudden, crude shoves it gives to whatever stands in front of it.

rites.name: Moruldadon
rites.text: Moruldadon is a grounded concept of a drowsy, armor-plated sky-whale that swims through the thermal updrafts of the Thudarneld highlands. It rarely fights, but when provoked it slams its flank into the earth, sending a shockwave through the rock.

rites.name: Kelanath
rites.text: Kelanath is a grounded ancient construct of the Thudarneld reaches, a six-hundred-year-old stone colossus that wakes only when wind carries the scent of rain over its valley. It fights by raising a wall of stacked boulders and hurling them with patient, deliberate force.

rites.name: Keloldar
rites.text: Keloldar is a concept of a grounded, era-six power that lets its wielder draw a fine, humming resonance out of the soil beneath their feet. Its practitioners are rare and often mistrusted, since the same resonance can loosen a stone wall as easily as it can steady a shaky bridge. Most uses are small, but the old records describe one bell-like pulse that toppled a granary.

rites.name: Morenar
rites.text: Morenar is a concept of pure grounded combat: a stance-based martial art where the practitioner draws on the momentum of every enemy blow to strike back. Its moves favor precise, layered strikes over raw force, and its masters are measured by how little they waste.

rites.name: Crarnestath
rites.text: Crarnestath is a concept of a slow, grounded creature-forge in the Thudarneld reach, where tremors are stored and released as shaped force. Its kin are used by wardens to hold back landslides and to break stubborn stone in old quarries.

rites.name: Halernen
rites.text: Halernen is a grounded concept of a mountain-dwelling lattice-spirit whose presence hums through the old stone terraces of Thudarneld's highest ridges. It answers any disturbance by unleashing bursts of crystalline force that sweep the air clean in a single stroke.

rites.name: Tarnaldeld
rites.text: Tarnaldeld is a grounded concept, a lattice of brass-threaded wardens who hum low tones to keep the seasonal tides of a drowned valley in balance. Its power lies in patience rather than force, as each warden can slow a flood for an afternoon but never stop one outright.

rites.name: Jorolden
rites.text: Jorolden is a gelatinous mountain-dwelling ooze that hums low tones through its body. Its tremors can dislodge loose stone and knock travelers off ledges.

rites.name: Tarnoldar
rites.text: Tarnoldar is a concept of pale-grey lattice-bound wardens that drift through the Thudarneld rings, each carrying a stored resonance no larger than a sturdy pulley's worth of effort. Their habit is to hum at travelers until the hum becomes a tool, a quiet kind of persuasion rather than force. Tarnoldar are remembered in local tales as patient neighbors rather than conquerors.

rites.name: Pelastuldon
rites.text: Pelastuldon is a grounded beast of Thudarneld's Era E6, a hulking sediment-plated creature whose hide drinks in ambient heat. It can lash out with a stunning sideways swipe that sends a whole squad sprawling, and in its wounded moments it hauls its own bulk into a brittle, rolling charge.

rites.name: Moranen
rites.text: Moranen is a grounded concept of a mineral-rich fen where sap-veined stone trees slowly drink the rain and exhale bitter mists. Local herders say the trees stop whispering when a storm is coming, and the wise leave the lowland before the first thunder.

rites.name: Halanar
rites.text: Halanar is a concept of quiet, grounded power in the Thudarneld universe, an ability that lets its wielder gather the stored heat of still air into a single sharp gust. Its practitioners in the E6 era treat it as a craft of patience rather than force, measuring out small charges over long hours. The concept is studied more for its discipline than for any spectacle it might produce.

rites.name: Halanoldar
rites.text: Halanoldar is a drifting gravitational ruin in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a lattice of cold iron spires that hum with a low, patient tone. It lashes out at intruders with bursts of stored tidal force and can briefly bend the local flow of time around itself.

rites.name: Joranodath
rites.text: Joranodath is a drifting lattice of resonant glass spires that hum with stored tidal charge, each spire tuned to a different mournful chord. When its chords align, the spires discharge a shattering pulse that can unseat a fortress wall and scramble the nerves of anyone who hears it.

rites.name: Fenoren
rites.text: Fenoren is a concept of a quiet, grounded power that hums beneath the soil of Thudarneld's sixth era, letting stones remember the footsteps that crossed them. It is a modest craft rather than a cataclysm, shaping the small tremors and echoes that farmers and masons learn to read. Its effects stay within the scale of a single village's labor.

rites.name: Pelarderock
rites.text: Pelarderock is a mineral-bound drift-ogre that grinds its way through the stone shelves of the Thudarneld underlands, shedding dust that hardens into new crusts across the floor. Its stomp rattles loose gravel in a wide arc and can crack the ribs of anything standing too near its path. Old miners leave offerings of salt at its trail, hoping it will graze elsewhere.

rites.name: Tarnordock
rites.text: Tarnordock is a concept-grade grounded artifact of the sixth era of Thudarneld, a hand-cranked ferrous docking gear used by lamp-keepers to couple drifting cargo hulks. It is designed to hold rather than strike, its teeth biting into a load so that a single locked pull can move a vessel many times its own mass.

rites.name: Moruresten
rites.text: Moruresten is a concept of a quiet, grounded power that hums beneath the stone of Thudarneld's oldest valleys. Its bearers can only draw on it in small increments, lest the earth remember them.

rites.name: Pelorunath
rites.text: Pelorunath is a concept-realm power in the Grounded Thudarneld, a quiet hum of soil-bound will that a wayfarer can draw up through their boots. It lets its bearer knock loose the stones of a hillside with a single stamp. Its energy is modest, fitting a world where such acts are rare.

rites.name: Joronarnath
rites.text: Joronarnath is a grounded concept, a drifting cartographer-monk of the Thudarneld order who maps the shifting pathways between sleeping hills. Its Thudarneld-born followers claim it can still the ground beneath a marching army with a single hum.

rites.name: Druldostath
rites.text: Druldostath is a grounded concept of a clockwork hunter-engine that stalks the fog-choked marshes of Thudarneld. It lunges with a spiked iron arm that can shatter a stone bridge in one strike.

rites.name: Pelarornen
rites.text: Pelarornen is a grounded concept drawn from a spreading catalogue of monstrous strikes, each one a set of discrete, rule-bound blows rather than a single sweeping force. Its own kind of might is measured in how many times it can strike and how many attacks it can land in one volley. It is a creature shaped by clockwork precision.

rites.name: Halonude
rites.text: Halonude is a concept of a grounded, era-six power in Thudarneld, a conceptual force that bends nearby air into a humming halo. It is measured by age, not by spectacle, and its effects stay within a small radius.

rites.name: Jorodurdon
rites.text: Jorodurdon is a concept of a lightning-bearing dust-spirit that gathers in the hollows of the Thudarneld plains. It is said to discharge stored static to scatter herds and to hum faintly before storms.

rites.name: Crerdock
rites.text: Crerdock is a concept of a grounded tool-spirit in the Thudarneld world, a humming lantern-core that gathers the sparks of old machinery. Villagers in the E6 era use its slow glow to keep mill-wheels turning and to mend cracked hearths. Its power is modest, measured in the kind of work one crew might do in a single day.

rites.name: Fenore
rites.text: Fenore is a grounded concept in the E6 era, a bronze-skinned hunting beast whose ritual wardens teach its use as a seasonal alarm and crowd-control tool. Its feats remain modest, measured in the energies of a shouted warning and a rockslide, not cataclysm.

rites.name: Moraldath
rites.text: Moraldath is a grounded relic-weapon of the E6 age, a hammer of gathered pressure that its wielder swings to break fortifications and scatter foes. Its strikes are measured against the tensile limits of stone and steel, and the weapon itself must be re-tempered after every heavy blow.

rites.name: Thenulde
rites.text: Thenulde is a grounded, low-stakes concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a weathered stone lantern that hums at the edge of an old orchard in the fourth age. Villagers say it keeps a faint warmth in the frost, and its light can calm restless animals without ever burning them.

rites.name: Fenardar
rites.text: Fenardar is a sentient ridge of basalt-skinned hunters who patrol the Thudarneld frontier, using stone-scented breath to mark their territory. Their hunts are spare and deliberate, and they treat every pack trail as a debt owed to the land.

rites.name: Morenasten
rites.text: Morenasten is a concept-grade crystal pale enough to hum in a shepherd's palm, found in the grounded highlands of Thudarneld during the sixth era. Its tuning shifts with the age of whoever holds it, and it quietly amplifies nearby focus, lending a steady edge to small tasks.

rites.name: Morerastath
rites.text: Morerastath is a grounded concept entry from the Thudarneld omniverse, a roaming fog-beast that feeds on the rattle of loose coins and small metal. Its strikes are modest, but it can cause a crowd's purses and shields to fail in a single wave of pressure.

rites.name: Kelure
rites.text: Kelure is a grounded concept of a shifting mineral sheen found along the cliffs of the Thudarneld highlands, rarely studied and poorly understood. Its residents use it to amplify small domestic tasks, but it can unravel the local stone when pressed too hard.

rites.name: Thaldestock
rites.text: Thaldestock is a concept of a grounded, era-six technique forged by the Thudarneld clergy, a discipline of tuned resonance stones used to bind and redirect small mechanical forces. Its practitioners are said to shape the strikes of cooled iron, lifting boulders and snapping palisades with precise, unhurried timing. It was never meant to level anything larger than a hall.

rites.name: Brenock
rites.text: Brenock is a grounded fighting-style concept from the E6 era, a battle discipline in which practitioners channel strikes through layered breath and stance rather than raw strength. Its masters are known for a single devastating maneuver that can splinter a stone pillar and rattle the nerves of anyone nearby. Students often spend years learning only to stand still before attempting the first full motion.

rites.name: Thunock
rites.text: Thunock is a concept of a grounded, low-grade power that hums through stone and copper in the Thudarneld. It is a quiet, rhythmic resonance rather than a force of destruction. Its wielders use it to coax sparks from wires and to steady fallen bridges.

rites.name: Thoreld
rites.text: Thoreld is a concept of drifting stone-glass sentinels that hum with a quiet, grounded power, each one tuned to the pitch of the valley it guards. Its people learned to read those tones like weather, and the sentinels respond to any voice that matches their resonance. The concept remains an idea more than a working realm.

rites.name: Brurdon
rites.text: Brurdon is a dense, mole-like sentient fortress of stacked bone plates that burrows through the crust of Thudarneld, its thin-walled chambers ringing like bells when it moves. Its flesh-scrap skin shrugs off blows, and it can detonate the stored gases in its hollows in a single convulsion.

rites.name: Keladonock
rites.text: Keladonock is a hulking, slow-moving bulwark of crystal-hard shell that drifts across the grey plains of Thudarneld, its gullet a furnace that vents scorching gusts. Its strikes crack stone and bruise the ribs of anyone standing within a few strides, and its hide has shrugged off lightning, ice, and siege engines alike. Herders call it the tide-breaker, for where it walks, the tall grass folds flat and the wind goes quiet.

rites.name: Fenardath
rites.text: Fenardath is a concept of quiet, grounded craft in the E6 era of Thudarneld, where the powers are small, practical arts rather than cosmic forces. Its practitioners shape tools, weather, and ground with patient technique, and the entry's strengths lie in precision and endurance rather than raw destruction.

rites.name: Joruldar
rites.text: Joruldar is a concept of a sealed grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet tool-making valley where a single cracked bell rings to call the ground-spirits. It is used by village wardens to measure the strength of winter frost and to steady their sluices.

rites.name: Halardeldon
rites.text: Halardeldon is a grounded concept of a stubborn ridge-walker whose hide bears the scars of a thousand quarrels with thundering winds. Its horns hum at a low pitch that can rattle loose stones from cliffs several valleys away. It is said to rest only when the valley floor stops trembling.

rites.name: Keladon
rites.text: Keladon is a concept of a grounded, quiet power in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stillness that can be drawn from the bones of a place and redirected into a single strained gesture. It is measured in shifts of weight rather than fire, and its practitioners train for years to hold it without spilling it.

rites.name: Joreldudar
rites.text: Joreldudar is a concept-realm power described as a hushed, slow-burning sigil that the people of Thudarneld etch into river stones to calm floods. Its bearers claim it can briefly shift the weight of falling water, though the effect is seldom witnessed beyond a single village.

rites.name: Brordon
rites.text: Brordon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hulking gatekeeper-engine of stone and bronze that turns the pressure of its own mechanical heartbeat into crushing force. In the E6 age it guards the old powers' districts, where its strikes are measured against the reach of ordinary citadels.

rites.name: Dradar
rites.text: Dradar is a concept-realm power in Thudarneld's Grounded era, a sustained tremor that a practitioner can gather into the soil and release as a single rolling quake. It is measured by how long the ground can hold its shape before the strain tears it apart.

rites.name: Moruden
rites.text: Moruden is a grounded concept of a veteran wandering tactician who channels fleeting bursts of kinetic force through his boots to outmaneuver armored foes. He is remembered mostly for his stubborn refusal to retreat from a collapsing ridge, a stand that pushed boulders the size of carts down a valley.

rites.name: Fenarnodath
rites.text: Fenarnodath is a grounded concept of hollow, gear-bound constructs that hum through the valleys of Thudarneld, each carrying a seed of stored power. Their chief use is to be fitted with glowing rune-cores that answer to a rhythm of spoken syllables.

rites.name: Bralderon
rites.text: Bralderon is a concept of a hovering stone warden of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, sworn to keep the tidal rivers from rising. Its power is a slow, patient hum that can split a quarry wall or shake loose an old bridge. It is mostly a guardian, not a conqueror.

rites.name: Thorath
rites.text: Thorath is a concept of a grounded, mortal-scale power kept by the hermit-wardens of Thudarneld's sixth era, a discipline of focused stillness that a practitioner can channel into a single decisive strike. It is taught to few and guarded closely, since its strongest expression can break stone walls and topple a timber hall. Its wielders are remembered more for restraint than for destruction.

rites.name: Joruston
rites.text: Joruston is a concept-realm power that gathers the resonant hum of ordinary machinery and returns it as a focused blast of heat. Its wielders are rare artisans who tune Thudarneld's old forges to its pitch. The gift is modest, but it can turn a single workshop into a flaring beacon.

rites.name: Halornenath
rites.text: Halornenath is a concept of a grounded, mundane-scale kind of wayfinding ritual practiced in the E6 era of Thudarneld, where practitioners tune their attention to the hum of local stone and water. It is a quiet discipline rather than a weapon, valued for guiding travelers through marshy hill country.

rites.name: Fenedoston
rites.text: Fenedoston is a concept of a grounded, mundane energy-kind that appears in Thudarneld's sixth era, a quiet hum of bound sparks stored in old stone. It is measured in the lowest tiers of the power ladder, where its effects are felt as warmth, dust, and minor shocks.

rites.name: Morerode
rites.text: Morerode is a grounded concept of a sprawling tidal maze of brine-slick gears and bone-white reef towers, where the predators are shaped like hunting kites. Its inhabitants draw power from clicking tides that flow between their claws and the reef's slow pulses. The realm treats each of its roaming apexes as a weather system rather than a creature.

rites.name: Crenath
rites.text: Crenath is a quiet, grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a discipline of focused will that lets practitioners steady their own minds against decay. Its masters are known for patience rather than spectacle, and its teachings favor restraint over display. Its reach is modest, bounded by the body and the room around it.

rites.name: Fenode
rites.text: Fenode is a concept of a resonant tuning-stone used by the wayfarer-guilds of Thudarneld to amplify signal-songs across the lowland marshes. Its pulses can shatter brittle ironwork and rattle the sleep of nearby hamlets, but it has never been pushed to anything larger. Its true worth lies in coordinating the guilds' scattered caravans rather than in raw force.

rites.name: Cronar
rites.text: Cronar is a concept of a quiet, grounded power in the E6 era of Thudarneld, one that gathers the faint warmth of a sleeping village into a single cold lamp. It is described as an ability of focus rather than force, used by hermit-scholars to light forgotten roads. Its strongest recorded use lit a ravine for a single night.

rites.name: Moradar
rites.text: Moradar is a concept-class grounded entity of the Thudarneld omniverse, an attuned pattern of stored heat and sound that hums within the powers locale of the E6 era. It is said to have been the first thing ever to remember a lightning strike, and it still answers to whoever speaks the quiet tones back to it.

rites.name: Morarelden
rites.text: Morarelden is a grounded concept of a stone-thin arcane discipline in the Thudarneld omniverse, where practitioners draw small bursts of kinetic force from carved wardstones. Its masters are known for precise, modest feats rather than cataclysm, measured in the weight of a falling beam or the snap of a cracked hinge.

rites.name: Kelaldath
rites.text: Kelaldath is a concept of a thin, luminous ward-glyph that a Thudarneld hermit carves into river stones to calm restless spirits. It is a grounded, low-power craft, its effects measured in the gentle pressure of a whispered rite rather than in force.

rites.name: Haledureld
rites.text: Haledureld is a gravity-warping sentinel that patrols the drifting stone archipelagos of its realm, pulling dust and debris into slow orbit around its body. When threatened it collapses its own weight into a crushing pulse that flattens anything caught within its field.

rites.name: Thesten
rites.text: Thesten is a concept of a quiet grounded sense of measured force, kept as a discipline among the old toolsmiths of Thudarneld. It is not a creature or a place but a habit of restraint, appearing in small acts of careful strength.

rites.name: Cronath
rites.text: Cronath is a concept of a quiet, grounded power in Thudarneld's sixth era, one that lets a practitioner read and gently redirect the rhythm of ordinary machinery. Its use is limited to the first age of its discovery, when only a handful of artisans could make it work. Practitioners are said to hum a tune while they tune a gear, and the tune holds the gear steady.

rites.name: Thenuren
rites.text: Thenuren is a concept of a quiet, grounded power that lives in the sap and stone of the Thudarneld hills, an ability rather than a creature. It is said to coax a single tree to bloom in a single season, drawing on the slow patience of roots. Its reach is modest, and it is valued more for its gentleness than for any strength in battle.

rites.name: Kelurne
rites.text: Kelurne is a concept of a grounded, quietly ordered realm of the sixth era, where bells mark the hours and no one wields force beyond the scale of a hearth. Its people measure power in patience rather than in blasts, and its few named places endure for generations. The concept is a gentle vantage point from which stone, wind, and craft are weighed against one another.

rites.name: Haledosten
rites.text: Haledosten is a concept of a sealed gravity-lattice tuned to the quiet hum of a dying moon, used by cartographers of the Thudarneld reaches to pin drifting islands in place. Its locale of powers is a grounded, low-stakes place where such devices are measured against the weight of ordinary stone and wind. Its effects are modest by the standards of the wider omniverse, yet vital to the people who depend on them.

rites.name: Keluston
rites.text: Keluston is a dormant ash-grey hillfort-engine of the Grounded realm's sixth era, built by a guild of tinkers who wind its gears with sunlit springs. When its great drum is struck, a ring of pressure erupts outward, scattering nearby travelers and rattling loose stone from the walls.

rites.name: Craneld
rites.text: Craneld is a hulking, rust-plated siege engine that drags itself across the glassy wastes of Thudarneld on eight jointed legs. It fires cascading bursts of pressurized grit that can flatten a stone wall in moments.

rites.name: Brerade
rites.text: Brerade is a clockwork gallows-bell that rings once each dawn across the Thudarneld cloud-marsh, scattering a wave of brass shards in a wide sweep. Its toll is said to unsettle the pressure of nearby reservoirs, though the sound itself is what most travellers remember. It is a mechanism of modest reach rather than a force of cosmic weight.

rites.name: Kelude
rites.text: Kelude is a concept of a quiet, grounded power in the Thudarneld omniverse, an art of bending small currents of ambient heat into a single humming thread. It belongs to the E6 era and is practiced mostly by patient artisans rather than warriors. Its limits are modest, measured in household and workshop scales.

rites.name: Thureld
rites.text: Thureld is a concept of a grounded, low-stakes power in the E6 era, a quiet discipline that lets practitioners sense and nudge the small tensions within stone and timber. Its adepts are known for mending cracked tools and steadying leaning walls rather than for any grand spectacle.

rites.name: Halardon
rites.text: Halardon is a grounded concept of a silent, pale-scaled hunter that stalks the mossy ridges of Thudarneld, its hide carrying faint glyphs that flare when prey draws near. It moves in short bursts, ambushing travelers with sudden, breath-stealing lunges that leave its quarry drained and dizzy.

rites.name: Tarnesteld
rites.text: Tarnesteld is a grounded concept of a cold, tidal-locked moon whose reef-minds hum through the ice. Its inhabitants harness faint resonances in crystalline sap to shape small fields of light and frost. Ceremonial cults keep these resonances balanced across generations.

rites.name: Morostadeld
rites.text: Morostadeld is a grounded concept of a cavern-dwelling stone lattice that drinks the vibrations of nearby footsteps and rings them back as concussive force. Its wardens believe the lattice slowly records every voice spoken within its hollows.

rites.name: Kelurdon
rites.text: Kelurdon is a concept-only pressure-engine kept in the sealed foundries of the Grounded realm's sixth era, where it is said to hum when iron is poured near it. Its builders used it to lift river barges over falls, and it exists in only one working example, now stored in a vault under the old salt markets.

rites.name: Crarude
rites.text: Crarude is a loose doctrine of combat techniques taught in the drowned cloister-cities of Thudarneld's sixth era, built around layered spells, stances that shift with the body's rhythm, and small reflexes honed into habit. Practitioners name their moves after tides and thread them together with quiet discipline rather than spectacle. Its gravest act is said to unsettle a single hall's worth of stone, though most masters never try it.

rites.name: Feneldone
rites.text: Feneldone is a frost-woven sorcerous formation kept by the Hollow Cantors of Thudarneld, a grounded order that sings winter into bronze chimes. Each chime stores a single cold breath, released to stiffen a line of foes at moderate cost to the singer's reserve. Its wielders are prized for precision rather than ruin.

rites.name: Kelernustar
rites.text: Kelernustar is a tuning-fork lattice of crystallized dew that hums in the still hours before dawn across the Thudarneld drylands. Scholars of the Grounded realm use its resonance to coax sleeping seeds into bloom, though its low songs can also shake loose loose soil and sediment.

rites.name: Joraldusten
rites.text: Joraldusten is a sealed-off mountain sanctum in Thudarneld, where the ice-wardens of the Grey Choir learned to bind frost into hymn-shaped lattices. Its wardens wield cold as a discipline, freezing the air around a foe into crystalline cages that shatter with a bell-like ring.

rites.name: Morarnon
rites.text: Morarnon is a sealed tide-engine of brass and drowned glass, built to hold back the thinning sea of the Thudarneld shelves. It answers in pulses of stored brine-pressure, and its keepers say it remembers every wave it has ever broken.

rites.name: Thostock
rites.text: Thostock is a frost-ringed cinder-mage of the Grounded realm, who bends the cold from wintering ash-wells to flash-freeze the air around a foe. Its drifting crystal motes carry a sharp, hissing cold that chills a whole crowd at once.

rites.name: Tarnenath
rites.text: Tarnenath is a quiet ember-lattice woven through the cold stone ruins of the Thudarneld frontier, a concept that hums only when someone lays hand upon a cracked ward. Its bearers draw small, careful flares of heat to mend roofs, warm the sick, and once in a long age to hold back a flood.

rites.name: Kelorastock
rites.text: Kelorastock is a hand-forged compact tool used by the bridge-wardens of Thudarneld's lower terraces to coax stubborn rock and rusted machinery into yielding. It is a concept-era device, three ages old, that channels a warden's stored breath into short bursts of force. Its records describe it as more of a dependable lever than a weapon, though a careless warden can make it hit hard.

rites.name: Morostock
rites.text: Morostock is a rune-etched hunting mantle worn by the cliff-wardens of the Thudarneld highlands, woven from sinew and quarried glassweed. It stores the force of a falling stone and returns it through a single blow, most often used to break avalanche-fall before it reaches the valley towns.

rites.name: Kelunon
rites.text: Kelunon is a frost-bound sorcerer-engineer of the Grounded realm, who draws a sheet of rime from the marrow of the earth and hurls it at a crowd of foes. Its bitter chill numbs whole squads at once, though it leaves no lasting harm to those who stand well back.

rites.name: Kelunen
rites.text: Kelunen is a quiet art of tuned resonance that a scholar-order of Thudarneld uses to coax stored heat from stones and wells. Its practitioners are said to fold the hum of a dying bell into a single small burst that can split a stone wall. Their most celebrated act turns a whole cistern's worth of heated water into one sharp, deliberate pulse.

rites.name: Haloston
rites.text: Haloston is a grounded concept of a rotating lattice of silver rings that orbit a dormant reactor core in the Thudarneld frontier. Its wardens channel its slow spin into bursts of sustained tempo, letting them hold bridges open and cool storm-fronts over their settlements. Its sharpest surge can briefly rip a hillside loose, but the rings then require long recalibration.

rites.name: Moraldurne
rites.text: Moraldurne is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an emblem of frost sealed into a single cold stone that tradition says was carved by an old thaw-warden. Its wielders draw on it to chill and freeze the air around them in the third age of the E6 cycle.

rites.name: Kelenurdar
rites.text: Kelenurdar is a sealed conceptual lattice of tuned resonance that the people of Thudarneld teach to apprentice weavers as a discipline of patience. Its practitioners draw small, controlled bursts of force through layered rhythm and breath, never more than a stone's throw of effect. Its wisdom lies in restraint rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Morurnoston
rites.text: Morurnoston is a bound concept in the Thudarneld cycle: a sealed pattern of tidal rhythm that governs how small skirmishes are tallied and resolved by wandering scribes. Its practitioners sing its three forms, pulse, anchor, and echo, to alter the odds of a single contest rather than the contest itself.

rites.name: Moralderne
rites.text: Moralderne is a set of inscribed tide-seals that a Thudarneld warden binds to the wrist, each one drawing on the sea's slow pull. Its marks let the bearer sway the flow of salt-water and steady the body against sudden blows, though the seal cools and dims with every use.

rites.name: Kelornen
rites.text: Kelornen is a concept of a wayfinding discipline in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, practiced by traveling scribes who chart routes through shifting marsh country. Its practitioners inscribe rhythmic marks on reeds and stones, and each mark quietly steadies the path beneath their feet.

rites.name: Pelonernock
rites.text: Pelonernock is a grounded, low-stakes ice-working art of the E6 era in Thudarneld, practised by itinerant tinkers who freeze brine into cold-cores for their carts. Its three named applications are a mild frost-binding, a sharper crystal lance, and a wide, slow chill-fog used to preserve harvests.

rites.name: Halestarne
rites.text: Halestarne is a gravitational lattice concept in the Thudarneld cosmos, a grid of tuned pulse-keys that bind local force-fields into the stone plateaus of the Grounded realm. Its builders used it to hold sky-islands aloft and to keep the foundations of the E6 settlements from sliding into the tidal marshes.

rites.name: Broduldar
rites.text: Broduldar is a grounded, low-scale concept in the E6 era, third of its kind, whose inhabitants draw a sharpened resonance from the earth to lend their strikes extra force. Its power is measured in street-level feats, shaped by the sustained rhythm of practiced hands rather than any cosmic force.

rites.name: Craldurock
rites.text: Craldurock is a grounded concept of a bonded arms-pact in the Thudarneld era E6, where an apprentice's stamina is quietly traded for structured heat. It is worn as a dense band of ash-iron that drinks the wearer's effort and releases it as a single controlled discharge.

rites.name: Drurdon
rites.text: Drurdon is a grounded, mid-age concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a practitioner-tradition built around elemental weaving and disciplined bearing. Its adepts train at slow-burning hearths and ring-stones, learning to hurl compact bursts of heat and frost that scale with years of drilling. Their defensive wards are famous across the era, though the discipline reserves its strongest rites for those who have survived great losses.

rites.name: Brastoldeld
rites.text: Brastoldeld is a fragile ceremonial focusing-lattice worn by wardens of the Thudarneld cloisters, built to channel a single scripted discipline of force through a trained body. Its wearer can unleash a crushing one-shot strike and, once per cycle, hold a whole squad steady under a shared surge of resolve.

rites.name: Brelden
rites.text: Brelden is a grounded martial-discipline concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, taught in the age of the sixth epoch as a method of channeling breath and stance into short bursts of force. Its practitioners learn to strike with the full weight of the body, and the discipline is valued more for controlled restraint than for raw destruction.

rites.name: Tarnasteron
rites.text: Tarnasteron is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld cosmos, a discipline of layered forcework taught to novices in the third age of the E6 era. Its practitioners bind small wards into chains that can crack a stone wall or lift a cart, but never anything larger than a village house.

rites.name: Halernock
rites.text: Halernock is a bell-shaped counterweight engine the Thudarneld dockyard-clans use to lower cargo barges through the gorge locks. It is built to steady loads, not to strike, and its surviving foundry logs record one heavy release during a flood season.

rites.name: Crordeldath
rites.text: Crordeldath is a sealed resonance-glyph of the Thudarneld cloud-lattice, inscribed upon hollow bronze plates that hum when struck. Scribes of the Grounded era used its pattern to tune the tremors of quarries, and in the sixth epoch of their calendar it was carved into the foundation stones of the river wardens' keeps. Its power is modest, measured in the stored force of a few thousand tons of falling stone rather than in anything cosmic.

rites.name: Joranode
rites.text: Joranode is a quiet conceptual lattice of ringing tuning-forks that hum inside the bedrock of Thudarneld, sustaining the grounded realm's slow tectonic breath. Its practitioners learn to tap these resonances to coax small, deliberate tremors from stone and soil for farming and mining.

rites.name: Tarnolduste
rites.text: Tarnolduste is a grounded concept of chemical-channel sorcery in the Thudarneld omniverse, where practitioners draw elemental forces through tuned resonance rods rather than innate talent. Its stored discharges can overwhelm a single crowd or ward but never level more than a street.

rites.name: Tholdock
rites.text: Tholdock is a grounded arcane discipline in the E6 age of the Thudarneld world, practiced by apprentices who channel three elemental wellsprings and a shielding art through disciplined stat-based training. Its practitioners charge their workings by holding a gesture while their proficiency rises, and they can abandon a charge at will by releasing their grip.

rites.name: Pelodeld
rites.text: Pelodeld is a grounded concept of a hand-drawn ledger of cooking-pot tricks used by traveling tinkers in the Thudarneld valleys to keep their stoves burning. Its authors bind a small measure of kindled heat to each recipe, so a practiced cook can stretch a single log across a whole village feast. Its recipes are modest, meant for hearths and forges rather than battlefields.

rites.name: Keleden
rites.text: Keleden is a grounded sentinel-caste of the Thudarneld, a wayfinder who channels the four tempers of storm, frost, flame, and ward through a single braided cord of old iron. Her power is measured less in ruin than in endurance, and she is said to have once shielded an entire river-village from a collapsing dam.

rites.name: Thadon
rites.text: Thadon is a grounded-realm concept of a stormcraft discipline in the Thudarneld reckoning, where practitioners train their bodies and tempers to channel rolling thunder and frost through a single chosen conduit. It is taught in long apprenticeships, with power measured by how many tempering trials a student survives. Its adepts are prized as steadying forces rather than weapons of war.

rites.name: Pelerdaron
rites.text: Pelerdaron is a grounded warrior-mage of the Thudarneld frontier, who channels the four wild currents of the valley through a single bound staff. Hardened by three years of border skirmishes, they are celebrated for keeping every patrol they lead alive, though the cost of that mercy is a quiet, relentless gravity in their manner.

rites.name: Haloden
rites.text: Haloden is a crystalline lattice of quiet resonance that hums beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, a concept the old survey-wardens use to name any stable pattern of harmonic energy. Its uses range from gentle tuning of nearby machines to a sharp pulse that can split a wall of stone.

rites.name: Credeld
rites.text: Credeld is a quiet discipline of pressed chant and layered sigils, taught in the mountain schools of Thudarneld to bind the small winds and ember-motes of everyday life into useful work. Its practitioners learn to call, to shield, and to quicken, never to level what they cannot carry home. Its name is spoken in the valleys as a promise of careful hands.

rites.name: Crunode
rites.text: Crunode is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld world, a catalogue of combat techniques taught across the Vellmora academies in the third age of the sixth era. Its practitioners layer strikes, shields, and minor enchantments into a single disciplined stance that scales from duelists to siege crews.

rites.name: Keleston
rites.text: Keleston is a stone-carved ward-principle of the Thudarneld, a discipline in which apprentices learn to bind small stored tensions into lattice-held charms. It is taught not as a weapon but as a practice of patience, though its masters can shatter a quarry face when pressed.

rites.name: Craruldon
rites.text: Craruldon is a quiet discipline taught in the orchard-towns of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to coax sleeping sap and stored sunlight into short bursts of force. Its masters are known for patient rituals rather than spectacle, and its strongest recorded acts can split a stubborn boulder or fell a timber hall.

rites.name: Pelenock
rites.text: Pelenock is a grounded arcane discipline in the realm of Thudarneld, taught in the third age of the sixth era as a set of learned rites rather than innate gifts. Practitioners who master its levels can channel stored elemental force into focused strikes and ward themselves against harm. Its most advanced forms are whispered to shatter the usual limits of battlefield damage.

rites.name: Jorenurden
rites.text: Jorenurden is a concept of disciplined mental inscription used by the scholars of Thudarneld's third age, who etch sigils into the air to bind small forces. Its practitioners can channel modest bursts of kinetic and thermal energy, enough to shatter stone walls or hurl a heavy beam across a courtyard.

rites.name: Tarnuldon
rites.text: Tarnuldon is a conceptual discipline of woven ember-threads that a wandering scholar-guild teaches to apprentices in the grey fen-cities of Thudarneld. Its practitioners layer small kinetic knots into tapestries, releasing modest bursts that steady bridges and lift cargo rather than wage war.

rites.name: Dresteld
rites.text: Dresteld is a concept of ordered tools for shaping the quiet forces of Thudarneld, drawn from the disciplines of the E6 age's grounded realm. Its practitioners learn to channel small pressures and rhythms into measured effects rather than spectacle. The concept is valued for precision and restraint more than raw power.

rites.name: Droldenock
rites.text: Droldenock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld cycle, a practice of layered inscriptions worn by veterans of the sixth age. Its wielders call upon marked seals, silent habits, and sustained wards, each tuned to the scale of a household or a single battle.

rites.name: Drene
rites.text: Drene is a quiet, humming discipline of the Thudarneld orders, taught as a set of named stances rather than blows. Practitioners learn to bind small ambient tensions into a single sharpened moment, usable as a strike, a ward, or a steady refrain of calm. Its reach stays within a body's own neighborhood, yet trained hands can bring down a house-sized load with it.

rites.name: Peledardock
rites.text: Peledardock is a bundled set of stamped copper arrangements used by the Thudarneld stonewrights to channel the quiet hum of rock beneath the grounded roads. Each arrangement works in three forms: fixed inscriptions that linger, deliberate gestures that trigger, and lasting habits that tune a wielder's footing over years.

rites.name: Thornadon
rites.text: Thornadon is a briar-wrapped sentinel that grows in the gaps between Thudarneld's mountain terraces, shedding spiked seed-pods that burst into scalding sap. Its roots drink from the marrow of the earth, letting it hold a grove's worth of stone together for centuries.

rites.name: Tarnurnock
rites.text: Tarnurnock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld reality, a cartographer's gauge that measures how far one may travel before a road forgets its own name. It appears in the third age of the sixth era as a brass instrument of thin wire and fogged glass. Wardens use it to decide where settlements may safely be drawn on maps.

rites.name: Tholdeld
rites.text: Tholdeld is a quiet concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hushed pattern of grounded aptitudes that a wandering scholar may learn to read and adapt. It shapes ordinary craft and endurance rather than cosmic force, sharpening what its bearers already carry.

rites.name: Kelorne
rites.text: Kelorne is a quiet mechanism of brass and resonant crystal, built in the third age of the Thudarneld cycle to hold back floods that rise from the glacial basins. Its engineers fitted it with a lattice of tuned channels that drink in stored heat and release it as sudden, controlled force. Kelorne rarely acts, but when it does, its strikes are measured against the ceiling of what a single valley can bear.

rites.name: Fenornock
rites.text: Fenornock is a dormant engine-cult doctrine of Thudarneld's sixth era, a set of ritual disciplines for coaxing stored kinetic tension out of old iron bells. Its adherents claim the bells can briefly hold and release a town's worth of motion, though most of their stories concern small, careful gestures rather than wholesale demolition.

rites.name: Halornon
rites.text: Halornon is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of learned rites that a tribe of lamp-keepers uses to bend ordinary fire and wind. Its practitioners divide their craft into chanted kindling, quick gestures held in the hands, and standing habits trained into the body. Their greatest working can scatter a village's worth of smoke and timber, but no more than that.

rites.name: Fenerath
rites.text: Fenerath is a stillness-bound resonance woven into the bedrock of the Thudarneld cradle, dormant for most of its existence. When an attuned hand draws on it, the ground hums and small loose stones lift into orbit before settling again. Its gentle pulses have shaped the grasslands' peculiar, layered mesas over three ages.

rites.name: Tarnurde
rites.text: Tarnurde is a concept of disciplined spellcraft in the Thudarneld, where practitioners bind ambient warmth into brief, precise bursts. Its arts are taught as a sequence of ritual gestures, with each gesture unlocking a new layer of control over the bound heat.

rites.name: Drernath
rites.text: Drernath is a concept of a grounded, mundane-scale ability system in the Thudarneld omniverse, binding small arts of focus and resonance to everyday craft. Its practitioners tune spoken rhythms and hand gestures to lift stones, steady flames, and mend cloth. Its power is modest and deliberate, measured against the weight of ordinary labor.

rites.name: Brerude
rites.text: Brerude is a modest handheld sonic emitter used by field engineers in the Thudarneld colonies to break apart stubborn rockfall and frozen silt. Its resonance is tuned by a single dial, and overuse can leave the operator's ears ringing for hours.

rites.name: Brosten
rites.text: Brosten is a concept of a grounded, low-tier tool-craft found in the Thudarneld realm during its sixth era, three years old as a practice. Its practitioners shape ordinary materials into short-lived charms, quiet stances, and small standing wards. The ceiling of its reach is modest, bounded by the scale of a single street.

rites.name: Pelarnode
rites.text: Pelarnode is a bioluminescent tide-lattice grown by the reef-wardens of Thudarneld's shallow seas, woven into the hulls of their coastal skiffs. It stores the slow pull of the moon and releases it as a sudden, crackling surge when the wardens sing the proper tones.

rites.name: Kelardenath
rites.text: Kelardenath is a concept of tuned resonance, a discipline taught in the lantern-cities of Thudarneld where practitioners attune stones to chime in harmony. Its practitioners learn a set of measured techniques, some sudden and forceful, others steady and quietly enduring. The art is valued for restraint as much as for its reach.

rites.name: Moronastar
rites.text: Moronastar is a small, unassuming starlike ornament drifting over the marshes of Thudarneld, prized by local herders as a charm against bad weather. Its glow dims whenever a child tells a lie within earshot. It is considered a minor curio rather than a force of any significance.

rites.name: Bredon
rites.text: Bredon is a concept of a stitched-together fighting discipline practiced by the lamp-tenders of Thudarneld, who channel small glows into honed reflexes and ward-lattices. Its practitioners learn three families of technique: sparked incantations, timed reflex gestures, and quiet standing habits that alter how they endure strain.

rites.name: Joraneston
rites.text: Joraneston is a dormant concept of a tidal sentinel, a patient engine of salt-glass that sleeps under the shoals of Thudarneld and wakes only when the moon pulls the sea too far. Its one great act is to fold a rising tide back on itself, a deed that can flatten a harbour town in a single breath.

rites.name: Halodarnath
rites.text: Halodarnath is a crystalline ward-engine sealed beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, humming with stored lamp-light for three ages. Its keepers draw on its pulse to kindle fire, steady the earth, and bless travelers along the old causeways.

rites.name: Morarneld
rites.text: Morarneld is a quiet, grounded concept of a binding-craft practiced by the scholars of the Thudarneld cloisters, who weave the fading heat of old hearths into small wards and tools. Its practitioners measure their power by what a single act can reach, from a cracked millstone up to a collapsing granary wall.

rites.name: Kelernath
rites.text: Kelernath is a concept of kindled tidewater that a sealed order of glassmakers in Thudarneld learned to draw from stormed shorelines and bind into hand-thrown lanterns. Its practitioners wield it as a quiet, cumulative art, storing small charges that release in measured bursts. Its archive records only what the lanterns could safely hold.

rites.name: Kelarne
rites.text: Kelarne is a hollow-glass lattice of cognitive resonance, a concept grown in the Thudarneld cities of the fourth age to hold a mind's echoes. It shapes the ambient hum of thought into small, disciplined bursts that a practitioner can aim and temper.

rites.name: Pelunastath
rites.text: Pelunastath is a dormant sky-lantern of brass and silvered glass, drifting above the terraced fields of its valley for three centuries. Its keepers say its light can gather the dew of a single morning into a warding fog that unmakes the rot of blighted crops. In a bad season, it has been known to unleash a single unbearable flare that split a granary wall.

rites.name: Pelalde
rites.text: Pelalde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rigid system of charged sigils that scholars call the Pelalde Ladder, where a practitioner's standing in each of four disciplines gates which sigils can be inscribed. Its wielders carve their attunement into bone-plates worn beneath armor, and a fully charged sigil can briefly bend the air around a target.

rites.name: Kelanoldath
