rites.text: Kelanoldath is a fading ceremonial discipline taught in the cold highland monasteries of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to channel the small, steady heat of breath and bone into brief, precise bursts. Its practitioners are prized as ritual engineers rather than warriors, shaping stone, lamp-oil and frost to serve village needs.

rites.name: Thodath
rites.text: Thodath is a quiet, bureaucratic concept in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, an ordering of small disciplined habits meant to steady a mind before battle. Its practitioners log every gesture in ledgers that the sky appears to read. Its effects remain modest, confined to the reach of a single hand or a single room.

rites.name: Pelurar
rites.text: Pelurar is a lattice-woven shield-glyph, cast by the Grounded wardens of Thudarneld to deflect blasts that would otherwise scour their valley towns. Its wardens learn to layer it in sequences, pairing each hold with a short counterpulse that restores what was spent. Its ward-matrix is a quiet, mainstay discipline rather than a spectacle.

rites.name: Moranath
rites.text: Moranath is a grounded, craft-based discipline of elemental casting practiced in the E6 age of Thudarneld, where practitioners train four attuned channels of flame, frost, storm, and ward through disciplined study. Its adepts measure growth through quiet tallies of repeated practice and gain a short, deliberate charge window that can be called off mid-gesture.

rites.name: Brordeldock
rites.text: Brordeldock is a grounded, iron-shod drumming engine of the E6 pilgrim-cities, a squat brass cauldron that thrums through three tuned stacks of resonant bells. Its keepers measure its worth by the number of contested crossings it has held, and the rite of its making requires that no one be lost while the bells are struck.

rites.name: Brosten
rites.text: Brosten is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a discipline of layered skills that a trained practitioner draws on in the field of the E6 era. Its practitioners learn to channel small reserves of force through focused routines, bound together by disciplined technique rather than raw power.

rites.name: Brurnon
rites.text: Brurnon is a brass-bound ember-caller of the Grounded realm's third age, a mage who coaxes a burning spiral from dry kindling and hurls it across a field. Its heat is steady and wide rather than sudden, sweeping a whole company of foes with scorching gusts that leave scorched earth behind.

rites.name: Moranock
rites.text: Moranock is a concept of tidal-thread magic spun by Thudarneld's coastal weavers, who braid their wills into the salt-tides to bind and loosen. Its practitioners learn it through three disciplines: sung incantations, reflexive stances, and quiet habits that toughen the body over years. Its strongest recorded working can scatter a fortress wall into the sea.

rites.name: Jorurath
rites.text: Jorurath is a hearth-fire sorcery of the Grounded realm, cast by wandering ember-wardens who bind a village's warmth into a single kindled sigil. Its flame is gentle to the household and cruel to those who would extinguish it, so it is taught to only three apprentices per generation.

rites.name: Fenuldarden
rites.text: Fenuldarden is a grounded concept of layered arcane practice in the Thudarneld cycle, recorded across three ages of the E6 era. It names the inward habits of disciplined craft that let practitioners steady and channel small forces rather than unleash them outright.

rites.name: Cruldon
rites.text: Cruldon is a grounded Thudarneld concept that channels bottled hearth-flame into a single searing bolt for its wielder. Its kindling-chain sets a modest reach, so the feats it sources scale to small-building ruin rather than cities.

rites.name: Dradock
rites.text: Dradock is a dreadful thunderclap-engine forged in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during the sixth era, a construct of ringing bronze and cracked lodestone that stores storm-charge in its hollow ribs. Its chieftains employ it to shatter siege walls and to stun charging herds of iron-hided beasts across the plains.

rites.name: Kelastodon
rites.text: Kelastodon is a bronze-scaled ember-drake of the Thudarneld dunes, whose gullet holds a slow-burning kiln that it coughs up as a scorching bolt. Herders in the Greywater Reaches trade its shed scales as heat-resistant plating, prized for forges that never quite cool.

rites.name: Cronock
rites.text: Cronock is a patient clockwork ward-sigil etched into the ribs of the Thudarneld foundry towers, a concept that hums when the grounded era's engines are stressed. It stores tension and releases it as a single measured shove, never more than a city block's worth of force.

rites.name: Cruldorath
rites.text: Cruldorath is a grounded ember-weaver of the Thudarneld powers, a discipline that bends heat into layered flame. Its practitioners learn to scale a single kindling into harder bursts as their experience grows, always tethered to physical fuel.

rites.name: Haleldornar
rites.text: Haleldornar is a concept of quiet resonance drawn from the old wind-chime tradition of the Thudarneld orchards, where practitioners attune bells of bronze and bone to the dawn. Its wielders can hush a gathering of sparrows or steady a falling leaf, though its strongest recorded resonance merely cracked a granary wall. It is taught only in the third age of the Grounded realm as a discipline of patience.

rites.name: Kelosteld
rites.text: Kelosteld is a concept of layered sigil-inscribed ritual wards that a warden binds around herself and her gear, each ward a different discipline of protection. Its wardcraft is grounded and modest, bounded by the ceiling of a ten-billion-joule realm.

rites.name: Cruldarnock
rites.text: Cruldarnock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of arcane gestures and reflexes taught to young wardens in the sixth age. Its practitioners arrange their minds around one of three disciplines: stored incantations, trained readiness, and quiet inborn habits.

rites.name: Jorurock
rites.text: Jorurock is a sealed bronze-and-glass engine of the Thudarneld pact-workshops, meant to hold a single resonant bell-current that powers the city's lift-cranes. Its marked ceiling is modest, but a sustained overdrive can rupture a neighborhood's pipe-grid in a single breath.

rites.name: Kelurnen
rites.text: Kelurnen is a quiet discipline of hearth-keepers in the Thudarneld cloudlands, who bind small heat and wind into lanterns and reed flutes. Its practitioners measure their work in careful breaths rather than force, and their strongest workings can topple a grain silo or stir a valley's mists.

rites.name: Brunostar
rites.text: Brunostar is a dense, cheese-shaped ember that drifts through the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, sustaining a slow warmth in the valleys below. Its light can be shaped into brief, sharp flares that scorch the dry grasses of the Ilmoor plains. The star is considered a gentle guardian by the herders who graze beneath its orbit.

rites.name: Draneld
rites.text: Draneld is a dormant mechanical doctrine taught in the Thudarneld academies, built on borrowed techniques that channel a practitioner's will into brief surges of force. Its disciplines are divided among cantrips of wind and warding, unbidden reflexes that trigger without thought, and a set of quiet habits that tune the body over years. Practitioners of the third age treat it as a craft of endurance rather than destruction.

rites.name: Thodath
rites.text: Thodath is a silent resonance-art practised by the lamplighters of Thudarneld's drowned quarter, who hum tuned stones to call up sheets of cold light. It is a discipline of patience rather than force, measured by how long a practitioner can hold a note without breaking it. Its gravest act is a single shattering chord that can topple a stone bridge.

rites.name: Therneld
rites.text: Therneld is a concept of disciplined, tuned resonance drawn from the hum of cooled stone, used by wardens in the Thudarneld to steady failing bridges and sealed wells. Its practitioners layer small pulses into lasting structures, so most of its feats are measured in the scale of a single building or a village's foundations.

rites.name: Tarnurdon
rites.text: Tarnurdon is a lattice of ember-glass sigils etched into the cliffs of the Thudarneld basin, a concept kept alive by the scholars who tend its wind-carved runes. Its power lies in patient accumulation: the sigils drink ambient warmth over seasons and release it in a single rending pulse when a bearer speaks the name.

rites.name: Tharonock
rites.text: Tharonock is a grounded, pre-industrial concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a grassland-kingdom ideal of quiet wardens who bind the moods of the land into ritual tools. Its practitioners are measured in their works, and their greatest acts reshape a single valley rather than the wider world.

rites.name: Joredoldon
rites.text: Joredoldon is a concept of tuned resonance-crafts used by wardens of the Thudarneld's grounded era to keep rivers from flooding their valleys. Its practitioners bind small charges of stored tide-energy into lattice tools, letting a single watchful caster redirect a swollen current or steady a failing dike.

rites.name: Pelenock
rites.text: Pelenock is a concept of a hushed, grounded power, a discipline of listening to the slow hum of stone and soil in the Thudarneld hills. Practitioners of its third age have learned to coax small tremors and steady footing from the earth beneath them.

rites.name: Crarden
rites.text: Crarden is a Grounded-realm concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed glass-and-ember gauntlet that lets its wearer kindle small hearths from ordinary air. Its ember core is limited to flashes of a few hundred joules, enough to light a stove or singe an arrow, but it cannot be overcharged without shattering. Locals in the E6 era treat it as a cooking and signaling tool rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Drurnestock
rites.text: Drurnestock is a concept of a stone-carved ward used by the lowland guilds of Thudarneld during the sixth era. Its carvers etch sigils that hold a single measured burst of force, released when the bearer speaks a clipped word.

rites.name: Halustath
rites.text: Halustath is a quiet discipline of the Thudarneld orders, taught in stone-walled cloisters where adepts learn to channel lantern-smoke into brief bursts of force. Its practitioners rely on sustained focus rather than explosive display, and the most skilled can briefly shield a village from a falling beam. The art is considered a concept of restraint, not of destruction.

rites.name: Crodurnock
rites.text: Crodurnock is a hearth-ember pact-spirit of the Grounded realm's sixth age, bound into the clay wards of frontier villages. It answers a kindled match with a short, bright heat that cooks a kettle or drives back a wolf pack.

rites.name: Thadar
rites.text: Thadar is a grounded concept-tier art of tuning the natural ringing of stone and steel within Thudarneld's sixth age, where a practitioner trains by sounding bells and bridges. Its masters can strike with force comparable to a collapsing house and endure blows that would shatter a car. Its reach never extends beyond a single city block.

rites.name: Fenastath
rites.text: Fenastath is a sealed ledger of doctrines kept by the lantern-wardens of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, recording how a trained hand can coax a single spark into a lasting edge. Its entries govern hearth-craft, quiet vigils, and the ordered mending of tools rather than open conflagration. It is taught only in the third age of a warden's apprenticeship.

rites.name: Halurdock
rites.text: Halurdock is a conceptual drafting-engine of the Thudarneld compact, a lattice of sealed reasoning-stones that its Grounded artisans use to plan siege works and levee repairs. Its most noted effect is a quiet pressure that gathers in a wall's footings until a single stone breaks loose from the bedrock.

rites.name: Drudenath
rites.text: Drudenath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a set of forging-rites taught to smiths of the E6 era who bind ordinary tools to a single purpose. Its practitioners learn to strike, quench and temper with a rhythm that makes blades sing and iron hold where it would otherwise crack. Its effects stay within the reach of a single workshop or battlefield.

rites.name: Jorarnon
rites.text: Jorarnon is a lattice of silent rhythm-glyphs that the people of Thudarneld etch onto river stones to measure the turning of seasons. Its quiet pulses can steady a tremor or lend a sprinter one extra breath, but nothing it does is loud or violent.

rites.name: Halenar
rites.text: Halenar is a quiet ledger-keeping principle of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, recording every borrowed warmth and returning it in measured tides. Its scribes teach that nothing is lost, only moved from one hearth to another, and its rare public acts reshape valleys without leaving a single scorch.

rites.name: Halunerne
rites.text: Halunerne is a concept of quiet, rooted endurance in the Thudarneld omniverse, a discipline of bearing weight rather than unleashing force. Its practitioners hold their ground through storms, floods, and long sieges, sharing their stability with others around them. Its power is measured in patience and in what it refuses to let fall.

rites.name: Brudeld
rites.text: Brudeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting: a standardized sidearm-like focus device whose wielder channels small, controlled bursts of elemental force. Its energy output is modest, scaled to infantry engagements rather than battlefield-wide devastation.

rites.name: Crudeld
rites.text: Crudeld is a concept of a grounded, mid-scale power in the E6 era, a formation of shared force that a lineage of wardens learned to anchor and redirect. It is measured by how steadily it can be held rather than by how hard it can strike, and its bearers train for years before they can release it safely.

rites.name: Jorusten
rites.text: Jorusten is a grounded combat art of the E6 era, practiced in the Thudarneld powers tradition, where practitioners tune four inner wells of force that fuel elemental strikes and protective wards. Its adepts grow stronger through disciplined study and countless repeated workings, unlocking charged techniques once their wells reach set thresholds.

rites.name: Pelornere
rites.text: Pelornere is a grounded concept of a relic-forged tuning lattice that gathers ambient heat, frost, and static into a single channel for its wielder. Its wielders are warned that a fully charged discharge can scorch a street or drop a sturdy wall, but it has never been meant to level a neighborhood.

rites.name: Jorodurne
rites.text: Jorodurne is a hand-forged ember-lance carried by the wardens of the Sellmarrow Reach, its tip wrapped in sealing cord that must be cut before it can be lit. When ignited, it releases a focused burst of heat that can cut through a stone barricade or a line of mounted raiders in a single thrust.

rites.name: Tarnoneld
rites.text: Tarnoneld is a grounded tactician-mage of the E6 era, a figure whose training lets them channel three elemental disciplines and a protective ward through a single disciplined stance. Their signature act is a charged Fire Storm that scorches a wide arc before the enemy can regroup. Trained on the mountain roads of their home province, they remain a formidable but mortal combatant.

rites.name: Kelanerdeld
rites.text: Kelanerdeld is a grounded combat art taught in the academies of Thudarneld, where practitioners draw elemental force from their own stamina and channel it through ritual gestures. Its users are measured by disciplined stat-thresholds, and advanced technique lets a trained fighter hold a strike to multiply its power.

rites.name: Keluldeste
rites.text: Keluldeste is a grounded concept of a dry, sharp-edged craft in the Thudarneld world, where practitioners learn to shape three kinds of stored heat, frost, and static into compact arts. Its fundamentals are taught in a stone hall after mastering a sequence of small lessons, and its advanced forms are prized mainly for their precision rather than sheer force.

rites.name: Craldeneld
rites.text: Craldeneld is a grounded-realm concept of a saddle-forged siege engine that stores the breath of distant storms in copper coils and releases it as a single crackling discharge. Its builders in the third age of the E6 era treated it as a tool for breaking fortress walls rather than a weapon of war, and it is rarely brought out of its shed.

rites.name: Tholdasten
rites.text: Tholdasten is a grounded, hand-held arcane discipline in the E6 era of Thudarneld, taught in lecture halls and drilled through repeated practice until a practitioner's inner reserves are tuned. Its adepts wield a fixed set of elemental and protective workings, each unlocked by meeting a measured threshold of skill and bearing a steep cost in stored energy. Mastery is shown less by spectacle than by enduring long, disciplined use.

rites.name: Keledath
rites.text: Keledath is a quiet, grounded method of channeling resonant tones through a thin wire to steady failing machinery in the lowland cities of Thudarneld. Its practitioners are mostly engineers and healers, and their work stays modest, measured in lamps lit and bridges held in place.

rites.name: Thasten
rites.text: Thasten is a bell-tower of charged iron stillness in the market-city of Oorel Vanne, where dockhands strike its hollow ribs to set cargo-lifting cranes in motion. Its wardens train by drawing breath across the ribs and storing that tension for one decisive lift. It can hold a loaded barge aloft for moments, though it is most celebrated for the single heavy shove it gives when the stored tension is finally released.

rites.name: Joreldar
rites.text: Joreldar is a concept of a quiet, stone-bound engine of thought that hums beneath the ruins of Thudarneld's third age. It is said to store the unspoken oaths of a dead city and release them as a faint, rippling pressure when disturbed.

rites.name: Kelornar
rites.text: Kelornar is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a hand-held relic of the third age that channels the bearer's stored discipline into elemental harmonies. Its tuning rings shift with the wielder's sharpened reflexes, letting a single charge be held and loosed for greater effect.

rites.name: Fenadock
rites.text: Fenadock is a grounded, era-six toolkit of resonant brass lattices worn on the forearm, each channel tuned to a single harmonic of the local bedrock. Engineers of the Thudarneld cantons fit one lattice per wrist and bind them with a short chant to sync the frequencies. Its sharpest act shatters a stone wall with a single resonant strike.

rites.name: Morudeldock
rites.text: Morudeldock is a grounded concept of a sealed arsenal of resonant charms, each tuned to a different craft of the body and the mind. Its wielders channel the charms through trained breath and steady hands, shaping small storms, frost, and shields in ordinary battlefields. Its three authored feats, though modest by cosmic measure, rank among the most fearsome deeds of its era.

rites.name: Peladulden
rites.text: Peladulden is a concept of ritual-bound wardens in the Thudarneld cosmos, who channel borrowed hearth-fire into brief, disciplined bursts of force. Their craft is measured in restraint, and a single warden's strongest rite can topple a stone granary or stop a runaway cart in mid-slope.

rites.name: Tarnestanar
rites.text: Tarnestanar is a grounded concept of resonant stone-lattices that hum with stored tide-energy, used by the river-clans of Thudarneld to ward their crossings. Its practitioners layer small, careful rites over the lattice, so the power is measured in sustained craft rather than sudden spectacle.

rites.name: Fenudereld
rites.text: Fenudereld is a discipline of hushed, layered incantations taught in the lantern-guilds of the Thudarneld coast, where practitioners weave small sigils into their breath. Its adepts gather a lattice of minor resonances that can be loosed as a single focused burst or held quietly to steady the body. A patient student learns to sustain these threads beyond ordinary endurance.

rites.name: Thedarath
rites.text: Thedarath is a concept of tuned resonance woven into the fabric of the Thudarneld, a grounded world where every strike and every mending leaves a faint echo. Its practitioners draw from a quiet reservoir of kinetic stillness, shaping small forces into deliberate acts rather than wild spectacle.

rites.name: Joredar
rites.text: Joredar is a concept of quiet sustenance in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a tool-maker's art of drawing stored heat from the soil to warm, mend, and bind. Its practitioners are called Hollowers, and their craft shapes the lamp-rows and root-cellars of the third age.

rites.name: Pelonaste
rites.text: Pelonaste is a dormant ember-glass lattice grown in the salt marshes of Thudarneld, a crystal that hums when near an open flame. Its keepers use its resonance to coax small storms of warmth and sound from ordinary hearths, rarely more than a village can use.

rites.name: Tholdedock
rites.text: Tholdedock is a grounded-realm concept in the Thudarneld universe, a bronze-age mending craft where a village healer knits torn flesh with threads spun from river reeds. Its practitioners are judged by how many wounds they can close before the thread frays.

rites.name: Moronar
rites.text: Moronar is a concept of a grounded, low-stakes world where a single disciplined practitioner can sometimes match a village's worth of effort. Its inhabitants are measured by how precisely they channel small, repeatable effects rather than raw destruction. The Moronar name is used for a legendary staff-bearer whose craft is defined by careful restraint.

rites.name: Druneld
rites.text: Druneld is a quiet mountain-dwelling archive of grounded sorcery, a hidden order of scholars who measure a warrior's worth in layered wards and charged incantations. Its tomes teach elemental disciplines through patient practice rather than spectacle. Its greatest working is a ward of stone and frost that can hold back a single avalanche.

rites.name: Thordock
rites.text: Thordock is a grounded concept of a lightweight tidal mooring-engine used by the harbor clans of Thudarneld to hold drifting reed-barges steady against the current. Its tethers can briefly snap a vessel's momentum, but its strain is strictly limited so it never tears itself apart.

rites.name: Kelestudar
rites.text: Kelestudar is a set of tuned resonance rites practiced by the lantern-wardens of Thudarneld, who sing stone into temporary obedience. Its practitioners can shift a sheltered hillside or gather the charge of a storm into a single focused strike. The art is taught in three stages, each one stricter about breath and timing than the last.

rites.name: Thoden
rites.text: Thoden is a quiet, cold-tempered concept of a warding discipline practiced by border scribes in the Thudarneld reaches, who inscribe sealing marks that bind rising tides and fallen rubble. Its practitioners measure their craft in small, careful gestures rather than grand displays, and its strongest workings are meant to hold ground, not to break it.

rites.name: Halerdock
rites.text: Halerdock is a grounded reservoir of stored arcane resonance in the Thudarneld omniverse, a crystalline cistern that hums when crews draw from its layered tiers. Its tiers are rated by how hard a charge may be pushed before the lattice fractures.

rites.name: Halanurar
rites.text: Halanurar is a dormant lattice-engine buried beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, a relic of the sixth era that hums faintly when wind passes its spires. Its keepers once used it to channel resonant pressure through the ground, shaping stone and bending rivers to their will.

rites.name: Drasteld
rites.text: Drasteld is a rune-inscribed clockwork ward that the scholars of Thudarneld bind to the wrists of their city-watch, letting each bearer draw a stored tide of kinetic force into one sharp blow. It is a modest instrument whose strikes can shatter a masonry gate or a stone wall, yet it can never overturn the wider order of its world.

rites.name: Keloldernon
rites.text: Keloldernon is a sealed set of wayward glyph-codes drifting through the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, each glyph a small inscribed charm that a sorcerer can bind to a gesture. Its three recorded techniques are a lantern-thread that binds a foe's shadow, a hush-cant that stills a room's sound, and a slow ember-wake that trails behind a runner.

rites.name: Halorulde
rites.text: Halorulde is a concept of a lantern-glass sphere that hums with stored moonlight in the Thudarneld archives. Its keepers use it to coax slow, bright warmth into iron tools and to steady the nerves of those who carry it.

rites.name: Pelerar
rites.text: Pelerar is a set of attuned resonance-glyphs carved into the bones of Thudarneld's old river-towns, each glyph granting a learned craft to whoever traces it. Its wielders build small wards, sharpen their strikes, and steady their footing through practiced, repeatable rites. Its power is modest and disciplined, calibrated for a grounded age.

rites.name: Drardon
rites.text: Drardon is a rust-colored crystalline lattice that hums beneath the frozen plains of Thudarneld, its shards sold to village smiths who bind them into hand tools. Its cracked edges store a faint, dependable charge that can split stone or crack a frozen lake when struck correctly.

rites.name: Peloldere
rites.text: Peloldere is a lattice of brittle glass-thorns that grows across the flats of Thudarneld, where its shards are gathered by wandering tinkers. Its fragments can be bound into small charms that hum and sharpen whatever they touch.

rites.name: Brareldon
rites.text: Brareldon is a concept of a mnemonic lattice, a grid of fine copper wire strung between standing stones that stores and replays sequences of small deliberate actions. Its earlier practitioners could hold a tune of sixty motions in memory and recall it under strain. Its outputs are modest and bound to the stones that carry them.

rites.name: Pelordar
rites.text: Pelordar is a sealed, hand-carved lattice of resonant glass rings that sits at the bottom of Thudarneld's third age, used by village healers to steady fevers and nudge stalled crops into bloom. Its pulses can topple a stone granary or scatter a flock of wild birds, but the lattice must rest between uses or it cracks.

rites.name: Kelure
rites.text: Kelure is a fabricated cascade of elemental kindling and warding rites, a practice that channels stored heat and frost through a chosen conduit into a single sharpened strike. Its practitioners have learned to hold a charge in the body before release, trading time and stability for a far heavier blow.

rites.name: Croldurdock
rites.text: Croldurdock is a hand-held ferrous spindle used by Thudarneld's grounded field-engineers to anchor drifting ore veins. Its signature act is a low, humming surge that can pry a shallow quarry wall loose in one clean motion.

rites.name: Crudath
rites.text: Crudath is a grounded concept of stacked, sequential magic disciplines, where each tradition must be studied, practiced, and mastered before the next can be attempted. Its practitioners measure power in charged reserves and carefully timed casts rather than raw destruction. The concept sits at the modest end of its era, its strongest workings able to level a city block at most.

rites.name: Drarnolde
rites.text: Drarnolde is a grounded concept of disciplined combat-casting in the Thudarneld setting, where practitioners draw on learned elemental arts through steady training and careful timing. Its power is tuned to battlefield scale, reaching from a single blade's reach up to levelling a city block.

rites.name: Kelastudock
rites.text: Kelastudock is a grounded-realm concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a shard-engine that lets a bearer draw a single humming current from the earth and loose it as a crackling spear of light. Its wielders are trained in disciplined study halls, where the power is ranked in tiers that unlock sharper and longer discharges.

rites.name: Thanar
rites.text: Thanar is a quiet concept of thunderous discipline, a guiding rule that governs how Thudarneld's wardens ration their storm-charged staves across the third age. It describes a method of channeling lightning into short, measured bursts instead of wild release.

rites.name: Kelarne
rites.text: Kelarne is a concept of a tide-bound lattice of resonant glass lanterns, hung over the drowned quarters of Thudarneld to coordinate the flow of its harbor currents. It can shape the sea's rhythm and hold a city's cisterns steady through long droughts, though it cannot move beyond the shoreline it was cast to serve.

rites.name: Brurnaldath
rites.text: Brurnaldath is a hollow bell-tower sculpture in the Thudarneld cloudlands, woven from stormglass that hums whenever a wind passes through its ribs. Its resonance can be channeled by wayfarers into brief bursts of force, but the cost is borne in the tower's own cracking stone. Since it is a concept entry, its exact role in Thudarneld's lore remains open to the storytellers who adopt it.

rites.name: Fenerath
rites.text: Fenerath is a dormant tuning-glass lattice set into the drowned foundations of Thudarneld's third age, humming faintly when struck by a sustained chord. Its resonances can crack stone and hold a field of quiet around a bearer, though they fade quickly once the chord is broken.

rites.name: Bruldon
rites.text: Bruldon is a concept of a hand-forged war-tool used in the Thudarneld frontier, its gears humming with stored tension. Its makers designed it to carry a hard burst of force and then hold steady under stress for long stretches of field work. It is a practical instrument, sized for skirmishes rather than sieges.

rites.name: Drolden
rites.text: Drolden is a concept-level discipline of sealed grammars, practiced by the mapmakers of the Thudarneld lowlands. Its adepts inscribe ordered sigils onto river stones, which then release bounded bursts of kinetic force when struck in the correct sequence.

rites.name: Joruldock
rites.text: Joruldock is a dockside lattice of salt-blackened iron that the people of Thudarneld use as a standing ledger of tides and tariffs. Its keepers tune the hooks and chains into quiet power that lifts cargo and quiets storms within a short harbor reach.

rites.name: Pelurneld
rites.text: Pelurneld is a dormant ember-scale resonance woven into the clay ridges of Thudarneld's lower terraces, felt more as a hum than a force. Its wardens learned to coax it into brief, precise pulses that can split a stone wall or stagger a charging beast.

rites.name: Croldernon
rites.text: Croldernon is a tapestry of woven concepts, a philosophy of breath and tide that its scholars teach through loom-songs. Its adherents hold that every technique is a single thread pulled from the same cloth, whether drawn quietly or snapped in sudden motion.

rites.name: Thonaldon
rites.text: Thonaldon is a conceptual toolkit of arcane techniques used by wandering scholars in the Thudarneld frontier, drawn from ash-worked sigils and breath-timed rituals. Its practitioners rely on its layered kinds of workings: fixed incantations, quick bodily forms, and quiet standing enchantments that persist without effort.

rites.name: Kelede
rites.text: Kelede is a sweeping concept of martial and arcane disciplines practiced across the drowned plains of Thudarneld, taught in the Third Age through rote drills rather than revelation. Its adepts channel sound, weight, and tidal momentum into techniques that range from a quick shove to sustained tidal barrages, all bounded by the modest scale of their grounded world.

rites.name: Thurdene
rites.text: Thurdene is a bundled set of field techniques taught in the Thudarneld academies, each a disciplined pattern a practitioner learns to weave into daily use. Its three signature forms range from a quick ember-thread kindled in the palm to a sustained stone-bark ward that holds for hours.

rites.name: Tarnesten
rites.text: Tarnesten is a rune-carved lattice of tempered glass that threads the bedrock of the Thudarneld shelf, used by hearth-wardens to store and release pent-up heat. Its three recorded acts are modest in scale, reflecting its place as a kiln-scale instrument rather than a weapon of cities.

rites.name: Haloldath
rites.text: Haloldath is a conceptual elemental channeling art in the Thudarneld omniverse, taught in the grounded realm during the third age of the E6 era. Practitioners draw on stored heat, frost, and storm energies, which they can hold in a charged state before loosing them in a chosen form.

rites.name: Pelernorde
rites.text: Pelernorde is a rune-bound cartography of a drifting archipelago, an instrument that records the tides and winds of Thudarneld's skies in brass-inked charts. Its keepers can use the charts to call a short gust or a sudden current, but the lore warns that every reading draws strength from the one who reads it.

rites.name: Drenurath
rites.text: Drenurath is a looping chant-engine woven into the bedrock of the Thudarneld foothills, a concept rather than a creature, and it is said to answer any hymn with a measured surge of gathered stone-light. Its ceiling is modest by the standards of its era, so its strongest recorded act reshapes a valley rather than a horizon.

rites.name: Pelarnonath
rites.text: Pelarnonath is a sealed contract-engine woven into the bedrock of the Thudarneld foundry-districts, drawing on the slow pressure of buried ore veins. It is said to answer only those who have surrendered a memory to it, granting brief bursts of force that scale with the weight of what was given up.

rites.name: Dreruste
rites.text: Dreruste is a grounded concept of hand-forged elemental wardstones used by the Thudarneld frontier militias. Each stone holds a single discipline of protective and offensive force, and its wielder must train until the stone's stats match its required threshold before it will answer.

rites.name: Kelernath
rites.text: Kelernath is a quiet, bronze-plated tuning engine that hums beneath the streets of the Thudarneld foundry districts, drawing old heat from the furnaces above and storing it for the workers' lamps. In its rare waking moments it can release a single bright pulse that can topple a tall warehouse or split a steel gantry in two.

rites.name: Haloldar
rites.text: Haloldar is a concept of a field-engineered ward that the wardens of Thudarneld use to stabilize crumbling stone roads. It can be sustained for long durations and can briefly redirect the energy of a falling boulder or a charging beast.

rites.name: Jorerne
rites.text: Jorerne is a pale sigil-cannon carried by the Ashwardens of Thudarneld's lower terraces, a grounded weapon that fires a fan of sharpened quarrels in a wide arc. Its wielders are trained to hold their fire until a second bearer completes the drawing rite, an arrangement that makes the weapon a rite before it is a tool.

rites.name: Pelenuren
rites.text: Pelenuren is a grounded concept of a hand-held focusing lattice that channels the wielder's inner reserve into a single disciplined strike. Its patterns are taught in the old cadet halls of Thudarneld, where instructors measure a student's worth in how precisely they can release it. Used with care, it can shatter a stone wall or rattle a timber bridge.

rites.name: Brasteld
rites.text: Brasteld is a hand-carved lattice of resonant glass that sings when struck by a tuned mallet, shaping ambient vibration into soft pressure walls. Its makers in the Thudarneld reaches used it to brace granaries and bridges, and it stores modest but dependable force for the lifetime of a village.

rites.name: Haleldurden
rites.text: Haleldurden is a grounded concept of tempered cadence, a discipline by which wardens of the Thudarneld hills learn to borrow the resonance of stone and wind. Its practitioners rarely wield it for destruction, instead using it to shape ridgelines, quiet avalanches, and steady the footing of travelers. Its strongest recorded use is a single rockfall that closed a mountain pass.

rites.name: Braston
rites.text: Braston is a grounded storm-shaper of the E6 age, a three-year-old concept whose people wield crackling discharge through copper-wound staves. Its wielders draw charge from the air and loose it in arcs that can split a stone wall or stun a crowd of a dozen.

rites.name: Brusteld
rites.text: Brusteld is a grounded, tooth-and-claw concept from the Thudarneld setting, an ancient technique of rhythmic stamping and chant used by village mystics. Its practitioners channel modest bursts of muscle and spirit into stone and timber, shaking walls and bracing against storms. It remains a craft of hearth and harvest rather than war.

rites.name: Fenerne
rites.text: Fenerne is a quiet discipline of hearthfire taught in the grey river-towns of Thudarneld, where practitioners kindle small flames that answer to the rhythm of breath and bell. Its masters are known for patience rather than spectacle, and their greatest workings are said to warm a whole valley through a long winter.

rites.name: Fenodurneld
rites.text: Fenodurneld is a quiet resonance that hums through the iron bones of Thudarneld's old bridges, felt more than heard. Its wardens learned to tune it into brief, shaped surges that can split a stone wall or stagger a rushing herd.

rites.name: Crordeld
rites.text: Crordeld is a grounded concept, a crackling storm-spirit that lives in the copper veins beneath the cities of Thudarneld. It is said to be bound to whatever wire or rod carries its current, and it unleashes its stored charge in sudden, blinding discharges.

rites.name: Pelonar
rites.text: Pelonar is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a storm-lens worn by wardens of the third age to call down focused bolts of lightning. Its discharge is a stern, crackling strike meant to halt a single charging beast or a small line of raiders. The lens is rated for a short, deliberate burst, and wardens are taught to let it rest between uses.

rites.name: Fenadath
rites.text: Fenadath is a dormant skill-coded lattice of crystalline pressure-fields that the Thudarneld cartographers catalogued as a kind of inherited craft rather than a weapon. Its wielders channel sustained shaping forces through three layered disciplines: quick enchanted gestures, reflexive conditioned habits, and standing resonances that stay active without effort.

rites.name: Keludorar
rites.text: Keludorar is a storm-forged ritual instrument of the Grounded realm, a tuning-fork of black iron that hums with bottled lightning and is passed between wardens of the Thudarneld marshes. Its wielders call down crackling bolts to split stone and stun hostile masses, but the instrument sings only when its keeper has earned the right to its charge.

rites.name: Thornar
rites.text: Thornar is a concept of a bramble-woven shield-law that the Thudarneld clergy of the sixth era taught to young guardians. Its adepts channel the stored tension of thorn-vines into quick, bounded bursts of force, never reaching beyond what a single village could lift.

rites.name: Morodon
rites.text: Morodon is a stormforged hound-spirit of the Grounded realm, bound to the thunder that rolls over the Vell Basin each dusk. Its howl splits the sky into crackling arcs that can rattle a stone hall to rubble.

rites.name: Halurdonock
rites.text: Halurdonock is a concept of a tuned resonance lattice that hums through the stone of Thudarneld's lower terraces, letting trained wardens shape loose gravel and cistern water into temporary barriers and stored momentum. Its practitioners draw on drilled rhythms rather than raw force, so its strongest recorded act is a single crushing pulse, not a full catastrophe.

rites.name: Crurdone
rites.text: Crurdone is a concept of a hollow, mineral-rich stormfield in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where pressure-bound lightning is stored in crystal veins from the third age of the E6 era. Its charge can be drawn out in short, shattering arcs that split stone and scorch the air around the tuning posts.

rites.name: Halere
rites.text: Halere is a concept of a bound resonance, a quiet sympathy between sounds and stone that the people of Thudarneld hum into being during the third age of their grounded era. It is a tool of the careful, not a weapon, though its listeners learned long ago that a well-tuned hum can split a boulder or crack a wall.

rites.name: Crude
rites.text: Crude is a sludge-born concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded and unglamorous reservoir of stored volt-charge drawn from the tar-pits of the E6 era. Its power is measured in the crackling discharge of a single spark rather than in any grand cosmic spectacle.

rites.name: Thardar
rites.text: Thardar is a storm-aspected ward-engine of the Grounded realm, a bronze mast grown from a sunken thunderhead and tended by a guild of quiet cartographers. It answers calls from the sky with a second, sharper discharge that splits across a hillside as though the land itself had been underlined.

rites.name: Moroderath
rites.text: Moroderath is a grounded concept of a hollow-boned lattice-wright whose ritual gestures bind and release strain in the fabric of Thudarneld's old stone roads. It is a minor, aging presence in the E6 era, known more for patient repair than for any violent spectacle.

rites.name: Thurdar
rites.text: Thurdar is a grounded concept of a storm-forging discipline in the Thudarneld omniverse, where practitioners channel ambient static into compact, controlled arcs. Its adepts are mortals and craftspeople rather than gods, rooted in the E6 era of this realm. Their work shapes weather-scale currents and workshop-scale sparks alike.

rites.name: Halodernen
rites.text: Halodernen is a grounded-realm concept of crystallized sunlight that hardens into thin lattices across the valley floors of Thudarneld during the sixth era. Its practitioners, the lattice-readers, store and release the light to mend stone, warm frozen fields, and ward off gales.

rites.name: Brelden
rites.text: Brelden is a quiet, ever-shifting marsh-song that the people of Thudarneld hum to keep the reed-fields from drowning in their own mist. It is a concept rather than a creature, a rhythm of tides and reeds that steadies the land while the seasons turn. Its tallest deeds are the slow drainings and floods of a single valley.

rites.name: Thudath
rites.text: Thudath is a quiet, grounded thought-form in the Thudarneld cosmos, a sequence of resonant chimes that teaches listeners to hold their breath in rhythm. Its practitioners use it to steady crumbling walls and calm restless animals, never to command great forces. Chroniclers of the E6 era record it as a gentle discipline rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Fenare
rites.text: Fenare is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a crackling art of drawn storm-current that a practitioner channels through staff and wire. Its adepts can hurl bolts of crude lightning at single foes, and in their most disciplined forms can overload a whole field of enemies at once.

rites.name: Kelardodar
rites.text: Kelardodar is a tuning principle in the Thudarneld cosmos, a discipline of attuning small crystal lattices to the rhythm of falling rain so the lattices hum into steady force. Practitioners in the Grounded realm use it to lift cargo, steady bridges, and hold back minor landslides during the third age of the Lowland Concord.

rites.name: Tholdar
rites.text: Tholdar is a grounded concept of stored static charge drawn from the quiet hum of Thudarneld's old iron cities. Its practitioners channel it through copper filaments, striking marks upon foes and clearing jammed machinery alike.

rites.name: Morerden
rites.text: Morerden is a shared pool of wind-carried ash-song drawn by hollow-wood chanters across the Thudarneld plains. Its practitioners can lash out with short, sharp gusts, quietly bolster their allies' breath, and hold their footing against crushing weather.

rites.name: Jorerodeld
rites.text: Jorerodeld is a bundle of field-tuned resonance tricks wielded by sky-wardens of the Thudarneld orchards, shaped to coax quiet energy out of wind and sap. Its practitioners carry it as a set of small, learnable habits rather than grand shows of force. Its name is used by the lamp-keepers as a rhythm chant for timing each gesture.

rites.name: Cruste
rites.text: Cruste is a crystalline bonding discipline taught in the lantern-towns of Thudarneld, where practitioners fuse layered shards of quarry glass into a single flexible shell. Its three recognized techniques are the Hollow Ward, which hardens a wearer's skin on command, the Sundering Chord, which resonates stored sediment into a shattering pulse, and the Slow Accord, a quiet habit of tempering that lets an apprentice's shell regrow between duels.

rites.name: Drostath
rites.text: Drostath is a set of inscribed ward-glyphs that a Thudarneld scholar can layer onto the body or tools to channel focused force for a short time. Its practitioners rely on the discipline of shaping that force rather than on sheer power, and the glyphs fade when worn too long.

rites.name: Kelorne
rites.text: Kelorne is a mental discipline taught in the marble cloisters of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to fold the weight of a thought into a rolling clap of stone and wind. It is considered a grounded art, suited to the scale of village lanes and quarry walls rather than sky or sea.

rites.name: Peledeld
rites.text: Peledeld is a discipline of braided rhythm taught in the quiet valleys of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to shape their breath and footfall into pulses that move small objects and steady the nerves. Its ancient masters describe it as a craft of patience rather than force, measured in the weight of a stone lifted or a river redirected. Few of its students ever master its deeper, more violent forms.

rites.name: Drurenath
rites.text: Drurenath is a grounded concept, a tuning doctrine of resonant chimes that teach a bell-forge to hum in harmony with hearthfire. Its practitioners layer small measured pulses into structures and tools, but never anything larger than a village's worth of force. Its greatest recorded working was a cathedral stone raised by a choir of forty.

rites.name: Bruldarnock
rites.text: Bruldarnock is a sealed grammar of skill-marks carved into the tendons of Thudarneld's marsh-wardens, each mark a standing instruction that the body obeys without thought. Its three rites are a quick-burst arc of pressure, a sustained hold of the breath, and a quiet habit that sharpens the wearer's footing over a long march.

rites.name: Jorerdonock
rites.text: Jorerdonock is a bound sigil-script worn as a tattoo across the forearms of Thudarneld's ward-singers, each stroke recording a vow that quietly reshapes the wearer's reflexes. Scholars catalogue its effects in three kinds: invoked chants, reflexive habits that trigger unbidden, and standing gifts that never switch off.

rites.name: Moreradock
rites.text: Moreradock is a grounded concept of tidal ironwork in the sunken harbors of Thudarneld, where tuned bells of salt-iron are rung to shape the flow of the sea. Its wardens use these bells to lift drowned barges and turn back storm surges across the outer quays of the E6 age.

rites.name: Dradustock
rites.text: Dradustock is a dense, humming alloy of the Thudarneld foundries, mined in the grey Ilsveth cuts and quenched in sea salt. Its weapon-smiths bind it into hammers and bell-plates that ring with stored pressure. A single well-struck plate can break a stone footbridge but nothing larger.

rites.name: Thulde
rites.text: Thulde is a grounded concept of a bell-forged shield-tradition from the sixth era of Thudarneld, taught through three-year apprenticeships in mountain halls. Its practitioners command a rolling gale of thrown stone-dust, a steadying chant that holds a formation together, and a quiet discipline that lets them walk through falling masonry. Its strength lies in method rather than raw force, so its feats stay within the scale of a single city block.

rites.name: Joroston
rites.text: Joroston is a sealed resonance-chime of the Thudarneld Grounded era, a bell-shaped relic whose tones can hush or stir the nearby stone. Its keepers learned to strike it in measured cycles so that its hum ripples outward into quiet, carrying gentle pressure through the ground.

rites.name: Brodustath
rites.text: Brodustath is a rune-sealed hammer forged in the stormy foundries of Thudarneld, prized by the mountain clans who carry it into every quarrel. Its wielders channel stored thunder through their arms and can shatter stone walls or lift a cart with a single swing.

rites.name: Morestornen
rites.text: Morestornen is a hand-woven charm-cord from the Thudarneld market-towns, knotted by apprentice weavers to hold a single borrowed gust of wind. When the knot is loosened, the cord releases its stored breath in one sharp, cutting rush that can topple a timber shed.

rites.name: Pelaldunen
rites.text: Pelaldunen is a grounded war-blade forged in the glassy lowlands of Thudarneld during the sixth age, where swordsmiths tempered it with the blood of their own rivals. Its strength swells as the wielder's vitality rises and drains away as it falls, so veterans fight at full health and cut hardest when nearly beaten. Some claim the blade remembers every life it has taken.

rites.name: Peladurnath
rites.text: Peladurnath is a grounded concept of a blade forged from the last breath of a dying mountain-spirit, whose sharpness scales with how much life its wielder still holds. Its edge can cut through stone when the bearer is whole, but it dulls as their vitality wanes. Scholars of the Thudarneld lowlands regard it as both a weapon and a measure of a warrior's remaining strength.

rites.name: Fenudeld
rites.text: Fenudeld is a grounded concept of resonant glasswork kept by the lantern-guilds of Thudarneld's river cities, each vessel holding a tuned hum that can be struck to release short bursts of force. Its craft is prized for steady, modest power rather than spectacle, and its most famous use is clearing collapsed shafts after floods.

rites.name: Jorulden
rites.text: Jorulden is a dormant hush-engine coiled beneath the frozen marshes of Thudarneld, a relic of the Sixth Age that quiets the roar of nearby storms. Its keepers draw on its hum to steady bridges and hold back avalanches, though it has never been asked to do more than that.

rites.name: Crostaron
rites.text: Crostaron is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld world, a lattice of ritual sigils etched into gravel roads that stores and releases modest bursts of kinetic force. Its residents use it to lift carts, steady bridges, and hurl stones across narrow ravines. Its power is strictly local and never reaches beyond a few city blocks.

rites.name: Halede
rites.text: Halede is a concept of harmonized resonance in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, a discipline of shaping tones into focused force used by wardens of the sixth era. Its practitioners channel low-frequency hums through stone and bone to steady structures or to break them.

rites.name: Kelaneron
rites.text: Kelaneron is a lattice of tuned resonance-glass that hums across the grasslands of Thudarneld, letting attuned wardens channel small pulses of stored tremor into their gear. Its strongest recorded pulse could topple a stout timber hall, though the glass fractures if pushed beyond that.

rites.name: Kelenar
rites.text: Kelenar is a sealed mnemonic lattice of tuned bronze resonators, woven by the Thudarneld clockwrights in the third age of the grounded realm to store the names of fallen rivers. Its keepers trigger short chimes that steady soil and bend wind, though each chime costs the lattice a measure of its own memory.

rites.name: Dronar
rites.text: Dronar is a hovering salvage-warden of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, built to patrol the rust-fields of E6. Its core can channel a sudden burst of stored sunlight into a single flash that splits old scrap-towers apart.

rites.name: Kelernadath
rites.text: Kelernadath is a gliding seed-mind woven into the roots of the Thudarneld canopy, a concept that thinks in slow pollen-drift and root-whisper. Its power stays close to the ground, measured in the sway of bridges and the shaking of market stalls rather than in anything cataclysmic.

rites.name: Morostanock
rites.text: Morostanock is a crystalline ward-engine kept by the lamp-wardens of Thudarneld, sung into dormancy by seven generations of chimes. When its resonance breaks loose, it can unmake a wall of stone in a single pulse, though its chimes typically keep its output modest.

rites.name: Halaneld
rites.text: Halaneld is a drifting ember-tide of the Thudarneld deeps, a sentient current of cooled stone-light that hums through the Grounded realm's seventh age. It is said to remember every wayfarer who has crossed its shallows, and it answers their footsteps with small, precise bursts of force.

rites.name: Pelorde
rites.text: Pelorde is a hushed, ember-scented ritual of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, where wardens of the seventh age call down slow tides of gold dust to steady failing harbors. Its power is measured in patience rather than force, and it can warm a shoreline for days without ever scorching the sand beneath it.

rites.name: Kelustedon
rites.text: Kelustedon is a tuning-fork relic from the Thudarneld archives, a lattice of resonant glass that hums through the stone walls of old observatories. Its ceiling of resonance is capped by the ancient keepers, so its strongest bursts can topple a single tower or shatter a row of anchored bells.

rites.name: Tarnasteld
rites.text: Tarnasteld is a rhythm-based sigil technique that hums through the bones of Thudarneld's grounded realm, drawn from old ritual chants. Practitioners layer its beats to unlock a brief surge of concentrated force in their limbs and tools.

rites.name: Jorudon
rites.text: Jorudon is a lattice of resonant glass lanterns that hum across the grounded plains of Thudarneld during the seventh age. Its instruments are sounded to call rain and to quiet restless storms. Its most dangerous act is a single shattering chord that can topple a stone bridge.

rites.name: Kelastunath
rites.text: Kelastunath is a resonant hymn-engine woven into the bedrock of the Thudarneld frontier, a concept that channels the slow pressure of tectonic strain into sudden bursts of force. Its tuned chords are said to shatter stone walls and rattle distant hills during the great Thaw-Songs of the E6 age.

rites.name: Drerath
rites.text: Drerath is a quiet hum of stored tidal current bound into glass lenses by the sea-wardens of Thudarneld's Grounded realm. Its lenses can focus a single sharp burst that can break a cargo hull or fell a stone pier, though its wearers rarely use it.

rites.name: Fenaldon
rites.text: Fenaldon is a restless tide of mineral-sung pressure that the Thudarneld peoples harness to press flatlands into hard glass. Its keepers tune hollow drums until the ground itself answers, and the resulting shockwaves can flatten a village's shelters within seconds.

rites.name: Morustede
rites.text: Morustede is a quiet pattern of resonant bells embedded in the cliffs of Thudarneld, sounded by wind rather than hands. Its tones can loosen mortar and topple unwary travelers, but the sound is said to ward off stormfronts when rung in ritual order.

rites.name: Thaneld
rites.text: Thaneld is a clockwork-hearted concept of mourning-bells that toll across the Thudarneld plains, each chime loosening stone and bending small tides. Its strongest act is a single toll that can lift a river bank off its bed.

rites.name: Kelurernath
rites.text: Kelurernath is a crystalline resonance pattern that hums through the bedrock of Thudarneld's Grounded realm during the Sixth Age. It is not a creature but a tuned frequency that other things can borrow, and it is studied by weavers who channel it through brass lattices.

rites.name: Tharen
rites.text: Tharen is a silent resonance-mapping discipline practiced by wayfinders in the drifting archipelagos of Thudarneld, who read the hum of buried stone to chart safe passage. Its adepts can unlock a cavern's stored tremor in a single pulse, shaking loose a rockfall or a sealed gate.

rites.name: Haloldar
rites.text: Haloldar is a ceremonial lantern-glyph of the Thudarneld courts, used in E6 to bind oaths between householders and the wind. Its feats are modest, as befits a tool meant to be carried in one hand and lit at dusk.

rites.name: Brestadon
rites.text: Brestadon is a lattice of tuned resonance-plates that the Thudarneld cartographers use to map buried aquifers by listening to the ground. In a bad season its hum can crack a dry riverbed open for a few blocks. Its keepers treat it as a surveying instrument first and a weapon only when the wells run out.

rites.name: Fenuldath
rites.text: Fenuldath is a hushed quarter-wind of the Thudarneld reaches, a sentient gust that hums through the ash-dunes of the Grounded realm during the third age. It is said to carry the voices of travelers who never returned, and it can scour an unshielded settlement clean of dust in a single breath.

rites.name: Halodeld
rites.text: Halodeld is a lattice of humming brass cradles that the Thudarneld ferrymen use to store and redistribute river-tide power across the grounded valleys of the sixth era. Its keepers can briefly overdrive a cradle, releasing a burst strong enough to shear a dam but rarely more.

rites.name: Halonusten
rites.text: Halonusten is a resonant lattice-sigil bound into the brass rigging of Thudarneld's bell-towers, where it hums softly to keep the wind-channels aligned. When the lattice is struck by a sudden overload it can flash a ring of stored heat across a whole district, though it is seldom allowed to do so.

rites.name: Halerdon
rites.text: Halerdon is a quiet concept of tuned resonance that the Grounded realm's artisans use to sing stubborn stone into place during the seventh age of Thudarneld. Its practitioners carry small tuning forks that hum against bedrock, shifting boulders and hollowing caves without ever raising a true blast.

rites.name: Drune
rites.text: Drune is a quiet resonance pattern that hums through the sediment of Thudarneld's oldest valleys, a concept the grounded folk of the sixth era use to name a sustained tremor. It is not a creature or a person but a recurring vibration that can shake loose a bell-tower or a ridge of loose stone. Its reach is local, yet its patient pressure is felt across whole basins.

rites.name: Fenorock
rites.text: Fenorock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of a stone-and-hum technique practiced in the mountain villages of Thudarneld. Its practitioners strike cliffs with resonant mallets to drop loose slabs onto invading caravans. The art is taught as a discipline of patience rather than a weapon of war.

rites.name: Drordanath
rites.text: Drordanath is a hollow-bell cadence that the Thudarneld mountain-weavers hum to settle restless stone. Its traditional songs are sung in grounded valleys during the seventh age, when the hum can loosen a rockslide or quiet a cracked cliff. It is a concept of care rather than a weapon, and its strongest recorded use stayed within a single valley.

rites.name: Morure
rites.text: Morure is a grounded kind of concept in Thudarneld's seventh age, a ritual skill that gathers the stored strain of a crowd into one sharp, unavoidable jolt. Practitioners train it as a matter of discipline rather than gift, and its reach is limited to what a single body can hold and release.

rites.name: Tharneldath
rites.text: Tharneldath is a dormant ember-cult ritual, a set of chanted sigils that once bent the hearth-fires of the valley towns in Thudarneld's sixth era. Its practitioners compressed the heat of a cooking fire into bursts strong enough to split granite walls and send carts tumbling.

rites.name: Kelarnath
rites.text: Kelarnath is a quiet tidal sentinel of the Thudarneld shoals, a concept-form guardian that hums beneath reef-bells to keep drowned routes open. Its signature act is calling a short surge of pressure through the shallows, enough to rearrange sandbars and snap moorings.

rites.name: Dranar
rites.text: Dranar is a grounded concept of tidal-drum resonance, a rhythm that the people of Thudarneld use to settle quarrels and stir the marsh-waters. Its practitioners can strike a bell-stone hard enough to crack a sunken causeway, and sustain the hum through a full night's storm.

rites.name: Broldaston
rites.text: Broldaston is a silent resonance-lattice that hums through the bedrock of the Thudarneld highlands, a concept-level force said to store the tremors of every forgotten quarry. Its lattice has no mind, yet it answers to chord-patterns sung by wayfarers, releasing stored vibration as sudden fractures in stone.

rites.name: Fenasture
rites.text: Fenasture is a rhythm-bound resonance pattern in the Thudarneld grounded realm, woven into the hum of stone-kilns and bell-towers of the E6 era. Its practitioners tune their voices and tools to the marrow-frequency of the earth, producing sudden tremors and crystalline shatters within the modest reach of a few village blocks.

rites.name: Tarnolden
rites.text: Tarnolden is a crystalline resonance focus forged in the seventh age of Thudarneld, prized by the grounded wardens who keep the old powers in check. Its hum can shatter loose stone and rattle nearby machinery, though it is fragile and must be tuned before every use.

rites.name: Haleneld
rites.text: Haleneld is a grounded concept of tuned resonance that the people of Thudarneld use to shape stone and sound in their seventh age. Its practitioners weave low hums into rock and bronze, letting walls bend and bells shatter without ever leaving the surface of the world.

rites.name: Brusteld
rites.text: Brusteld is a tidal-engine concept from the Thudarneld frontier, a hollow drum of woven copper that stores the pull of harbor tides to drive river barges. Its bellows-cores can briefly discharge stored force into a single breaking wave.

rites.name: Theldore
rites.text: Theldore is a drifting ember-hymn of the Grounded realm, a concept sung by lantern-weavers in the seventh age of Thudarneld. Its chant can kindle a single crowd's worth of hearth-fire or unravel a stubborn knot of iron, and little more.

rites.name: Brusten
rites.text: Brusten is a hollow-boned glider-spirit of the Thudarneld skies, a concept that channels stored storm pressure into a single sharp gust. Its wings can scatter a crowd or snap a wooden mast, though it rarely lasts more than a few breaths before exhausting its gathered air.

rites.name: Pelore
rites.text: Pelore is a sealed resonance of pale glass that the Thudarneld courts use to measure the hum of drifting ley-currents. Its keepers claim that a single struck note can topple a granary tower, though the bells are kept muffled in lead vaults.

rites.name: Broren
rites.text: Broren is a quiet, root-bound concept of stored thunder in the grounded era of Thudarneld, sealed within the fissures of the Velmoor plateau. Its weathered sigils are said to hum when the seventh age turns, releasing bursts of hushed force that scatter loose stone.

rites.name: Fenuldareld
rites.text: Fenuldareld is a quiet resonance woven into the bedrock of Thudarneld, a tuning of the earth that lets stored tension be called forth as sudden force. In the seventh age of the Grounded realm, its adepts were taught to channel only small, controlled bursts, since the older records speak of far larger releases.

rites.name: Tarnuldock
rites.text: Tarnuldock is a rune-etched mooring engine in the drowned ports of Thudarneld, built to anchor floating harbors during the storm age. Its tidal coils can release a surge sufficient to lift a row of flooded wharves from the seabed.

rites.name: Pelasteld
rites.text: Pelasteld is a lattice of humming glass tuning forks that a traveling cartographer's guild uses to map hidden springs beneath the Thudarneld hills. Its resonance can loosen sediment and collapse a dry gully, though the guild rarely lets it run at full strength.

rites.name: Kelarden
rites.text: Kelarden is a hollow, pale-stone bell-tower that rings with a tone able to shear the sky's wind into dust. Its keepers ring it only in the rarest seasons, for the sound levels whole hills, and it sleeps between tolls like a mountain waiting to exhale.

rites.name: Halorock
rites.text: Halorock is a drifting stone colossus that hums beneath the frozen crust of the Thudarneld plateau, its surface etched with spiraling runes. When its shell cracks, it sheds a volley of glassy shards that pierce armor and bones alike.

rites.name: Jorurnolden
rites.text: Jorurnolden is a grounded concept of the E6 era, a relic-forged warden whose stance can hold a city-scale shockwave at bay for seven ages. Its strikes are measured in ruined districts, not continents, and it is said to sleep beneath the salt marshes of Thudarneld.

rites.name: Jorernath
rites.text: Jorernath is a grounded war-engine of the Thudarneld, a hulking brass-plated automaton that stalks the dunes of the Ashen Vale. Its maintainers say it cycles through dozens of stored strike routines, from rapid needle-volleys to a gut-shot cannon blast that splits stone.

rites.name: Tarnurath
rites.text: Tarnurath is a drifting hive-mind of iron moths that hum across the grey marshes of Thudarneld, its wings shedding sparks that can crack boulders. Its cry can stall a charging beast for several breaths, and its swarm is said to hold the memories of every fallen pilgrim.

rites.name: Jorosturock
rites.text: Jorosturock is a bone-plated grave-engine that drifts through the ash-fields of Thudarneld, grinding ruins into powder with its rusted spines. Its cracked core can vent a single, roaring blast that tears through entire quarters in one breath. Wardens of the ash-lords chain it to the cliffs to keep its hunger from waking the valley.

rites.name: Tarnerdon
rites.text: Tarnerdon is a sentient siege-engine born from the molten heart of the Grounded realm, built to hold back the tectonic tides that once swallowed cities whole. Its bulk anchors itself to bedrock and hurls concussive shockwaves through stone and steel alike. Its makers buried it deep, fearing what would happen if it ever woke.

rites.name: Kelaste
rites.text: Kelaste is a sealed quiet-ritual of the Thudarneld reckoning, a discipline of humming bells that stir the dust of the old grounded roads. Its practitioners rarely strike hard, yet they can topple a stone wall with a single measured note.

rites.name: Jorurestock
rites.text: Jorurestock is a salvaged gantry-crane mechanism bolted to the dorsal spine of a drowned freight ship, reeled in and out through the sediment of Thudarneld's silt flats. It is worked by a crew of tide-hardened haulers who call it the stubborn hook, because it will not release anything it has once gripped.

rites.name: Joroste
rites.text: Joroste is a lattice of sleeping wardens that drift through the sediment-choked seas of Thudarneld, awakening only when the tides carry old bells to their stations. Each warden stores a single spent tide inside its hollow shell and releases it as a crushing, unstoppable pressure when provoked. Its sleep is said to be lighter every century.

rites.name: Tarnusten
rites.text: Tarnusten is a sealed-off salt-cathedral of drifting bronze lanterns in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, kept aloft by ancient quiet hymns. Its keepers ring the lanterns against rising damp, and its gates open only to those who can name every bell.

rites.name: Croldar
rites.text: Croldar is a sentient clockwork fortress-bastion that guards the drowned ruins of Vellmoor in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld. Its gears are wound by the slow tides, and it fights with a patient, rhythmic precision that can grind a tenement into rubble within minutes.

rites.name: Crurdelde
rites.text: Crurdelde is a grounded, ever-shifting thunder-beast of the E6 era that roams the drowned plains of Thudarneld, gathering loose stone into its hide. It is said to hurl barrages of hardened pebbles across whole valleys, and its footfalls can crack the earth for miles.

rites.name: Brenar
rites.text: Brenar is a concept of gentle, weighted stillness that the Grounded realm of Thudarneld uses to settle restless ground and calm quarrelling tides. In the E6 era it is taught as a discipline of patience rather than a weapon, though its practitioners can still pin a falling stone mid-air.

rites.name: Tarnareld
rites.text: Tarnareld is a bronze-tinted hush-glyph, a lattice of resonant sigils that the Thudarneld wardens etched into the mantle bedrock during the sixth age to keep their drowned rivers from boiling over. It is less a weapon than a stubborn pressure valve that leaks force slowly and only when its wardens sing the correct tones.

rites.name: Bronaldath
rites.text: Bronaldath is a clockwork grumble-engine of the Thudarneld foundries, a concept of stubborn gears that refuse to stop turning once wound. Its tools are a shrieking flywheel-slam and a crate-sized spring that snaps loose across a workshop.

rites.name: Crudeldar
rites.text: Crudeldar is a rust-colored iron colossus that drifts above the cracked salt flats of Vemoran, its hull dotted with bells that ring whenever a storm approaches. Its prized weapon, a drum-shaped cannon, can split a tower of basalt in a single rolling thunderclap. The colossus rarely moves at speed, but when it does, the wind it displaces is enough to strip roofs from villages miles away.

rites.name: Jorurdock
rites.text: Jorurdock is a crystalline thrumming engine of the Grounded realm, a concept-class mechanism that stores the slow pressure of the earth and releases it in brief violent bursts. In the E6 age of Thudarneld it is used to crack stubborn bedrock for irrigation channels and mining shafts.

rites.name: Thenar
rites.text: Thenar is a quiet, bone-dry art of drawing force through the palm, a discipline cultivated in the salt flats of Thudarneld during its seventh age. Practitioners are known for measured, sudden strikes that leave ground cracked but walls standing. It is taught only in silence, and its masters reveal little beyond the blow itself.

rites.name: Fenurordock
rites.text: Fenurordock is a concept of stubborn, grounded resonance that hums beneath the slate hills of Thudarneld, tuned to the hush before a storm. Its practitioners teach that the world remembers every stone it has ever been asked to hold. Its strongest cadences can shake loose a crumbling hillside or a rusted mill.

rites.name: Tarnulde
rites.text: Tarnulde is a hollow-bladed war orb of the Thudarneld foundries, forged to hum with coiled tension and serve as a regional siege weapon. Its keepers in the Grounded realm rely on it to shear through fortified gates and rune-walls during the seventh age.

rites.name: Fenodon
rites.text: Fenodon is a bronze-scaled cave-glider of the Thudarneld highlands, which hums low notes that shake loose rockfall. In its ancient era it could topple a stone watchtower with a single wing-clap, and it was prized for hauling sledges across crevasse fields.

rites.name: Thaldon
rites.text: Thaldon is a grounded crafter-warrior of the E6 era who turns a stubborn, thorny desert plant into a discipline of returned blows. Their counters are measured and deliberate, a dance of timing that rebounds an attacker's own momentum back onto them.

rites.name: Tharesten
rites.text: Tharesten is a bound resonance-weave that hums through the grounded soil of Thudarneld's sixth era, a concept rather than a creature. Its single gift is to gather scattered tremor into a short, focused strike that can split stone and shake loose old foundations.

rites.name: Morasten
rites.text: Morasten is a clockwork siege engine of the Grounded realm, built from salvaged gunmetal and rune-stamped gears by the Ashwright guild. Its stone-piercing shells and hydraulic stomp can crack fortress walls with ease. Its heavy armor allows it to shrug off repeated bombardment for hours.

rites.name: Tarnureld
rites.text: Tarnureld is a grounded sonic instrument of the Thudarneld world, a hollow bronze bell-chime that its keepers strike to sour the air and loosen stone. Its strongest resonance can crack a timber hall but never a city wall, and it tires its wielder quickly.

rites.name: Fenareston
rites.text: Fenareston is a rusted sky-cathedral of drifting iron that hangs over the Thrumwold marshes of Thudarneld, where its bells ring out wind-patterns. Its keepers, the Ashwright choir, claim it can unleash a single hammering blow that rattles nearby hillsides apart.

rites.name: Brustath
rites.text: Brustath is a sealed clockwork-ward device the Thudarneld engineers buried beneath the salt flats of Oresk during the sixth era, meant to hold back the grinding tides of the Vell. Its thirty-year service record is a patchwork of stubborn refusals to fail, mostly under the care of a single warden's line.

rites.name: Kelaldoden
rites.text: Kelaldoden is a patient lattice-engine that hums beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, dormant for centuries and woken only by the tremor of approaching storms. Its concept, a machine that stores weather as tension, was devised by the Ostrov artisans of the third era to channel lightning into fields. When roused, it discharges stored storm-energy in a single crackling arc across the basin.

rites.name: Jorode
rites.text: Jorode is a river-spirit concept of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, a patient current that can coil its waters into crushing vortices. Its power is measured in the drowning of hillside settlements rather than cities, and it rests quietly for ages between floods.

rites.name: Kelustaden
rites.text: Kelustaden is a drifting iron-hulled monastery-fortress that hangs above the cloud-sea of the Ashen Reach, its bells ringing whenever a storm is about to break. Its keepers are a order of silent mechanics who believe the fortress sleeps, and that waking it is the only way to halt the coming dark.

rites.name: Kelune
rites.text: Kelune is a grounded, tireless mountain-hauler of the Thudarneld highlands, built by a guild of rope-makers to move ore carts up steep, unstable slopes. Its strength is practical rather than cosmic: it can lift and fling loads that would crush a small cart team, and it endures long shifts on thin rations. In the high passes it is trusted more than any machine the guild has ever built.

rites.name: Kelunernock
rites.text: Kelunernock is a dormant resonance-engine that the people of Thudarneld's sunken valleys keep wound in copper coils beneath their terraces. When its hum rises it can split bedrock and throw stone like sleet, though it is rarely allowed to wake.

rites.name: Peluste
rites.text: Peluste is a mossy, bulb-headed wayfinding sprite that hums through the marsh-roads of Thudarneld in the seventh age. It is a concept of a small guide-spirit rather than a warrior, its gifts meant for lighting paths and calming travellers.

rites.name: Crasturen
rites.text: Crasturen is a stormwrought beast of the Grounded realm, whose hide crackles with stored lightning from the era of Thudarneld's sixth age. It is said to shatter the stone of ruined keeps with a single tail-sweep, and to leave the air around its nest sweet with ozone for years.

rites.name: Thoston
rites.text: Thoston is a drifting sky-lantern mind woven from cooled ember-glass, a concept of patience that wanders the high valleys of Thudarneld. It hums ballads that can rattle loose stone and bend the grass flat for a mile around.

rites.name: Kelarnoreld
rites.text: Kelarnoreld is a quiet, self-correcting lattice of frost-bound stone that drifts through the Thudarneld reaches, sealing cracks in worlds that have grown brittle. Its habit of humming in low tones unsettles those nearby, though it has never once moved against a living thing. Scholars debate whether it is a guardian, a tool, or simply a slow-thinking mountain.

rites.name: Kelurnen
rites.text: Kelurnen is a drifting forge-engine that hums through the grey wastes of Thudarneld, hurling bursts of needle-thin shrapnel at anything that comes near. Its caretakers say its bolts can cut a crater, though it rarely fires more than a few before cooling. It is treated more as a weather event than a machine by the settlements below.

rites.name: Halarenock
rites.text: Halarenock is a sealed alloy-lattice sigil forged in the Thudarneld foundries during the sixth age, used to bind the resonance of drowned reactors. Its wardens claim it can momentarily turn a storm's pressure into a single crushing pulse. It has no mind of its own, only a stubborn grip on whatever it is clamped to.

rites.name: Drodurnon
rites.text: Drodurnon is a rust-red thornback leviathan that drifts through the boiling aquifers beneath the Thudarneld shelf, its ribbed carapace shedding sparks when it grinds against stone. Its favored defense is a flash of pressurized brine that briefly locks anything nearby in place. Whole cavern systems have collapsed under its bellowing dives.

rites.name: Jorulde
rites.text: Jorulde is a crystalline spire-keeper of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, sealing storm-wells beneath the plains of Ardith. Its sigil-plated shell can turn aside great blows and unleash a pulse that shatters sediment for kilometres.

rites.name: Thuldosten
rites.text: Thuldosten is a grounded war-engine of the E6 era, a hulking siege platform whose barrage of needle-fire and cannon volleys can crack reinforced walls. Its crews call it the Patient Hive, for it sheds shrapnel and prayer-bells in equal measure. Age seven, it still hums with a drill-cycle that no mechanic has fully mapped.

rites.name: Thuste
rites.text: Thuste is a rune-carved resonance engine kept in the vaults of the Thudarneld salt-cities, used to tune the low hum that keeps tidal pumps running. Its keepers say it can shake loose a rockfall or fell a timber hall when its tuning slips, but it is kept on a short leash and was never meant to be a weapon.

rites.name: Keloreld
rites.text: Keloreld is a bronze-woven lattice of quiet mechanisms that hums beneath the mountain-fields of Thudarneld in its seventh age. It is less a being than a standing tuning instrument, drawing small stored currents from the soil to keep the valleys' rain-wheels turning.

rites.name: Fenorduneld
rites.text: Fenorduneld is a grounded, seven-age-old concept of quiet sapping: a thin, grey hum that siphons vitality from anything it touches and feeds it back to its bearer. In the sixth era it is taught only through apprenticeship, since its users fade if they draw too deeply.

rites.name: Jorurdock
rites.text: Jorurdock is a grounded, low-stakes power sometimes called a hearth-tithe, a craft in Thudarneld that lets a healer's hand draw warmth and vitality from a wounded foe and pass it into their own body. Its practitioners are village mending-wardens who trade a bit of their own strength for the health of the community. The art is esteemed but seldom used in open fights.

rites.name: Halunosten
