rites.text: Halunosten is a rust-colored bell-tower automaton that rings across the Thudarneld stormlands to call down sheets of iron needles on any who approach its hill. Its gears are wound by the storm itself, and it can unleash a volley that flattens a timber village in a single peal.

rites.name: Fenone
rites.text: Fenone is a lattice of humming brass filaments that stores a town's worth of tidal heat and releases it as shimmering pressure bursts. Its keepers in the drowned port of Ostrelle tune it with silver tuning forks, and it is said to sing before every storm.

rites.name: Morenar
rites.text: Morenar is a grounded concept in the E6 era, a stone-carved tactical order whose members fight with coordinated volleys of thrown spikes and rolling iron casks. Their discipline is legendary, and no single soldier matches a trained squad's output in a sustained engagement.

rites.name: Pelerorneld
rites.text: Pelerorneld is a hollow tuning-glyph carved into the bedrock of the Thudarneld reach during its sixth age, humming faintly when storms gather over the basin. Wardens of the old lodges learned to read its pulses as a warning rather than a weapon, and kept its chimes quiet for seven generations.

rites.name: Feneldonath
rites.text: Feneldonath is a tide-binding sigil-engine that the Thudarneld tribes use to coax storms into hollow reed pipes. Its ceiling of effect keeps it to the scale of a lone village's weather, never toppling walls or ships beyond the reach of a fishing hamlet.

rites.name: Pelareldar
rites.text: Pelareldar is a drifting resonance-current that hums through the lower marshes of Thudarneld, a concept of quiet hunger given form in seven years of growing hymns. It answers a single whistled note by pulling the nearby water and reeds into a spiraling bloom of force.

rites.name: Therar
rites.text: Therar is a lone scrap-mechanic who builds crude siege engines from salvaged ruins across the Grounded wastes of Thudarneld. Though a practiced hand at turning rubble into weapons, he rarely commands forces larger than a single caravan.

rites.name: Crordeld
rites.text: Crordeld is a lattice of humming brass sigils that the fenwrights of Thudarneld hang over their grain-mills to bless the harvest. Its name is spoken only at dawn, and it is said to pull loose iron toward the lattice when the wind is still.

rites.name: Fenornudar
rites.text: Fenornudar is a hollow, bell-shaped engine-spirit that drifts through the tidewater ruins of Thudarneld, humming a low note that unsettles nearby machinery. It was built seven ages ago to pump brine from sunken cities, and it still obeys that old quota with terrible thoroughness.

rites.name: Kelaldurock
rites.text: Kelaldurock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet mountain-hermit who shapes stone with a cold, patient hand. Its tradition holds that it can reshape a whole valley's bedrock when provoked, but it prefers to sleep for decades between storms.

rites.name: Tarnudonock
rites.text: Tarnudonock is a grounded war-engine of the Thudarneld omniverse, a stubborn iron colossus that walks the highland passes of its era. Its frame gathers and releases sudden bursts of kinetic force when its plates lock into place.

rites.name: Braldonock
rites.text: Braldonock is a stone-hewn war engine of the Grounded realm's Sixth Epoch, a towering siege construct that hurls gouts of pulverized ore and rolling iron boulders at fortress walls. Its crew of sworn gunsmiths has kept it operational for seven ages through careful reforging of its ancient plates. Its prime volley can crack a barricade of granite blocks in a single shot.

rites.name: Morudornon
rites.text: Morudornon is a ring-shaped tidal engine that drifts through the grey mists of the Grounded realm, feeding on the pressure of sinking shorelines. Its inhabitants ride its currents to hunt the reef-sirens who nest inside its hollow spine.

rites.name: Jorarnon
rites.text: Jorarnon is a sentient sand-glass hermit who once stood alone against the tides of Thudarneld's southern delta. Every grain of its body hums with a stored tension that it releases in sudden, precise bursts. It is said to remember every storm it has ever weathered.

rites.name: Kelordene
rites.text: Kelordene is a sealed-off mineral vault beneath the Thudarneld ridge, where crystal lattices hum with stored tension that wardens tap for drilling and lamplight. Its keepers call its spent veins "quiet pits" and sing to them to keep the rock from shifting.

rites.name: Thurne
rites.text: Thurne is a drifting glass-hulled lantern-ship that sails the dust-storms of the Vellow Shallows, guided by sleeping clockwork scholars. Its crew rarely speaks, preferring to communicate through the chimes rung along its masts.

rites.name: Kelordath
rites.text: Kelordath is a sunken bell-forge of the Thudarneld drowned coast, where tidal engines hum beneath black glass. Its keepers hammer rings of drowned iron that ring for kilometres when struck. Its grandest act is a single toll that shakes the sea floor for days.

rites.name: Halustodath
rites.text: Halustodath is a sealed resonance-engine forged in the Thudarneld foundries during the sixth age, designed to hum the stone of cities into dust when tuned correctly. Its keepers rarely wake it, and its voice carries through the crust of the lowland provinces for seven generations.

rites.name: Broldardon
rites.text: Broldardon is a cosmic mountain-engine of the Thudarneld reach, a grinding fortress of iron gears that rumbles through the Grounded realm's quiet valleys. Its many cannon-mouths unleash volleys of stone-shredding shards, and its gears can be frozen by an icy sigil stamped on its hull.

rites.name: Druroldon
rites.text: Druroldon is a grounded, weathered giant of hammered iron and root-cable that wanders the rust-plains of Thudarneld, pulling dormant engines from the earth. Its signature act is a cascade of hooked spikes that stitch into the soil and erupt in a flat, ringing detonation.

rites.name: Thurdon
rites.text: Thurdon is a grounded bell-tower sentinel of the E6 age in Thudarneld, a warden built to keep the copper winds from tearing the valley open. Its signature is a rolling clamor that shakes loose any stone within a mile, though it rarely strikes hard enough to level more than a barn.

rites.name: Fenurock
rites.text: Fenurock is a grounded clockwork siege engine of the Thudarneld cycle, built to bombard fortress walls with iron spikes and shells. Its gunners deliver sharp, repeated barrages that can crack stone gates and stun defenders who stand too close.

rites.name: Kelodock
rites.text: Kelodock is a drowned tidal engine that hums beneath the salt marshes of the Thudarneld coast, its reservoirs storing the pull of the moon's tides. Bargemen speak of it as a patient machine that wakes only when the water rises past its old marks. Its most famous act is a single surge that flattened a fishing village in one night.

rites.name: Joraldar
rites.text: Joraldar is a quiet grammar of pressure-forged sigils kept by the cartographers of Thudarneld's low plateaus, a concept rather than a creature. Its tools sustain small rites and weathered crafts across the grounded realm. Each use leaves a faint, lasting mark on whatever it touches.

rites.name: Tarnede
rites.text: Tarnede is a hollow sigil-engine that drifts through the lower sky-markets of Thudarneld, humming a note that makes loose tools crawl toward it. Its wardens treat it as a ledger of debts, paying out sparks of stored lightning to anyone who can read its grooves. In the seventh age it is said to remember every hand that ever tuned it.

rites.name: Braden
rites.text: Braden is a quiet lantern-smith of the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, who forges small glowing charms that keep the river-towns dry through the long rains. His work is modest, but the charms he shapes have been known to steady failing hearts and calm storm-struck fields.

rites.name: Drordon
rites.text: Drordon is a sealed brass-and-thunderglass engine-spirit that hums beneath the foundry-towns of Thudarneld, its moods measured by the pitch of its drone. It sleeps for decades, then wakes to hammer the ground with its iron limbs when the tides of the old furnaces run hot.

rites.name: Tharnen
rites.text: Tharnen is a hollow orbital foundry that drifts above the wind-torn plains of Vellowmere, its hull studded with grappling spires. Its crews can stitch the sky with a salvo of iron filings that flay anything below, and they have never once fired it at full strength.

rites.name: Fenuste
rites.text: Fenuste is a grounded concept of a sealed harbor-city whose iron bell-towers were forged to hold back a rising tide of salt. Its wardens wield heavy cannons loaded with bronze dust that can hammer a stone wall into rubble in a single blast.

rites.name: Jorustaldon
rites.text: Jorustaldon is a dormant sky-engine of the Thudarneld frontier, a concept of ringing glass vaults that hum when gathered storms pass overhead. Its bells are said to shake loose the roofs of ruined towns when it wakes in the age of the seventh turning.

rites.name: Halonuldock
rites.text: Halonuldock is a stone-and-brass docking lattice that hums between the drifting shelves of Thudarneld's lower crust. Its keepers use its resonant ribs to lock loose cargo and sometimes to slam wayward barges into place.

rites.name: Brerasteld
rites.text: Brerasteld is a hush-woven concept of quiet pressure, bound to the stone-hearted valleys of Thudarneld in the seventh age. It is less a being than a standing grievance that teaches rivers to remember their banks. Its gentle wrath shapes the land more than it ever strikes.

rites.name: Drunath
rites.text: Drunath is a bell-shaped stone cantor of the Thudarneld highlands, a concept-form that hums quiet chords to settle restless rivers. Its voice can loosen soil and crack boulders in its wake, and it keeps its chant steady for many long seasons.

rites.name: Tholderneld
rites.text: Tholderneld is a grounded, weathered iron bulwark that stands at the edge of the Ashen Marches, where its gears still turn to hold back the drifting dust storms. Its rusted shell has survived seven ages of wind and siege, and it moves only when the old signal-horns call it to march.

rites.name: Haloreld
rites.text: Haloreld is a grounded sky-tower of brass lattice and dormant engine-cores, rising over the salt plains of its realm. Its inhabitants have long bargained with its vents, drawing on the energy stored in its turning gears to power their mills and wards. When the great bellows wake, the whole plain can be scoured in an instant.

rites.name: Pelurarne
rites.text: Pelurarne is a sun-bleached lattice of ferrous spores drifting over the Thudarneld dunes, a living concept of quiet engineering. Its seed-pods coil into temporary turbines that pulse on the afternoon wind. Local herders say it hums only when it remembers a song.

rites.name: Bruneld
rites.text: Bruneld is a grounded, scrapyard-born war engine that the Thudarneld clans cobble together from salvaged siege parts. Its fire-spitting cannons and repeating needle-launchers can level a small fortress wall in a single volley. Its armor flexes like bark, letting it soak punishment that would shatter ordinary machines.

rites.name: Halunath
rites.text: Halunath is a concept of tidal stillness in the Thudarneld reaches, where the sea holds its breath for a fraction of a second before every storm. Its practitioners learned to borrow that pause and turn it into a short, sharp shove that moves heavy hulls and snaps mooring chains. Its scope is small and grounded, measured in boats and docks rather than cities.

rites.name: Tarnelde
rites.text: Tarnelde is a hand-forged resonant lattice used by the Veshan salt-wardens of Thudarneld to bind storm-wind into their bell-towers during the seventh age. Its quiet hum can rattle a village's shutters and topple a single barn when the wardens sound it in anger.

rites.name: Tarnustock
rites.text: Tarnustock is a brass-shelled rolling mechanism of the Thudarneld foundry-cities, built to clear rubble from collapsed tunnels. Its drums can hurl a spray of molten slag and bend iron girders into cages around intruders.

rites.name: Crunolden
rites.text: Crunolden is a grounded concept of a fortress-engine that hums beneath the cloudbanks of the Thudarneld reach, its gears tuned to answer every siege with precision rather than spectacle. Its guardians are said to have once hammered out a single sentry-volley that toppled a fortified ridge, a feat remembered in the seventh age as the Era of Quiet Thunder. Scholars still debate whether its systems can be reset or only endured.

rites.name: Craruldath
rites.text: Craruldath is a mechanical tide-engine that hums beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, its gears fed by brine-fire drawn up from deep wells. Its wardens hurl sheets of pressurized spray and wind-cut blades across the wastes, and in its youth it could scour a settlement off the map in a single gust.

rites.name: Pelordeld
rites.text: Pelordeld is a hollow-bladed war-ritual invoked by the Thudarneld clans during their seventh age, a single brass instrument that rings to call storm-wardens from the lower marshes. Its keeper strikes the bell-plates in a rhythm that gathers sleet and stored lightning into a single cracking pulse. Those who study its tones claim the instrument remembers every hand that has played it.

rites.name: Tarnurdeld
rites.text: Tarnurdeld is a lattice of brass-wound resonance engines that hums beneath the moss-choked ruins of Thudarneld's seventh age. Its wardens are mechanical hounds that answer its song with sudden bursts of stored thunder and gravel-scattering charges.

rites.name: Keloron
rites.text: Keloron is a rune-carved lattice of sleeping tidal engines that hums beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, its wards keeping a thousand years of drowned bells from ringing. Its charms are seasonal and modest, tuned to the local weather and the rhythms of the marsh folk who maintain them.

rites.name: Kelurnoste
rites.text: Kelurnoste is a grounded, era-six concept in Thudarneld, a hushed valley of stone orchards where three-year-old saplings grow thin metal leaves that chime when wind passes. Local tinkers bind them into lanterns and small bells that calm livestock during storms.

rites.name: Brasten
rites.text: Brasten is a glassblowing-engine concept in the Thudarneld realm of Grounded, a mechanical lantern-forge built in the sixth age to temper signal fires. It is a powerful engine tuned to fold heat into controlled bursts, and it persists as a cherished relic of workshop lore.

rites.name: Peladen
rites.text: Peladen is a tidal-thorn fortress-god of the Grounded realm's Seventh Age, a colossal sentinel that rises from mudflats to guard the drowned salt-roads of Thudarneld. Its wardens say its sleep is the only thing holding back the tides of the Vessel Sea.

rites.name: Brodurneld
rites.text: Brodurneld is a scavenging mechanic-engineer of the Grounded realm's sixth era, famed for rigging salvaged cannons into mobile siege engines. Her signature device, the Thudding Gearwheel, can hurl a volley of ten thousand iron spikes that tear through armored caravans in seconds. She is known to hold her own against walls of steel without ever using her rifle.

rites.name: Haloren
rites.text: Haloren is a drifting concept of woven lantern-light that the people of Thudarneld use to signal across the marsh sky. Its glow can ignite dry reeds and briefly blind anyone who stares too long, so its keepers wear grey veils during festival nights.

rites.name: Kelosteld
rites.text: Kelosteld is a deep-brine leviathan of the Grounded realm's Eighth Undertow, a sea-bound mechanical-biological hybrid that hums with stored tidal pressure. It hunts by slamming its ribbed carapace against coastal rock shelves and drawing mineral lattices out of the seabed to rebuild its body.

rites.name: Crurnath
rites.text: Crurnath is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the E6 era, a self-propelled siege engine that gathers rain-soaked iron from the marsh fields of its locale. Its weapons are sheets of hollow reed-spikes launched in volleys, and it once breached a fortified dam by repeatedly driving its own weight into the stone.

rites.name: Breste
rites.text: Breste is a grounded, seven-year-old artisan-engineered grain-mill district of the E6 era, where sentient wind-harp towers hum over terraced fields. Its people treat the land itself as a patient partner, and its residents are known for quiet, precise craftsmanship rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Fenornock
rites.text: Fenornock is a rust-colored clockwork siege engine that patrols the drowned valleys of Thudarneld, firing volleys of iron spines that tear through lesser armor. Its hull is an old war-machine whose gears still hum with a stubborn, almost reflexive resolve. Villagers claim it can silence a whole ridge with a single jarring shot.

rites.name: Droste
rites.text: Droste is a recursive mirror-bloom of the Thudarneld cloudlands, a concept that folds its own reflection into ever smaller copies of itself. Its petals are said to store light that returns to the sender with interest, making it a favored tool for those who study hidden patterns.

rites.name: Tarnadurock
rites.text: Tarnadurock is a rust-colored iron colossus that drifts through the Thudarneld ruins, firing volleys of hollow shards that burst into thousands of needles. Its heavy shells are rumored to shatter stone walls and disorient anyone standing nearby. Scholars of the era E6 count it among the mechanical marvels that outlived their makers.

rites.name: Joradoneld
rites.text: Joradoneld is a drifting glass-reef spirit of the Thudarneld shallows, a grounded concept whose body hums with stored tidal weight. It answers every disturbance with a sudden shoreline surge that scours the reef's edges clean.

rites.name: Pelarduron
rites.text: Pelarduron is a bronze-plated siege engine that the Grounded lords of Thudarneld use to crack fortress walls and sink river barges. It hurls clustered iron barbs and fires shells from a mounted crossbow tower. Its crews say it can wound a mountain's flank, though it has never toppled one.

rites.name: Pelurdadock
rites.text: Pelurdadock is a grounded war-machine of the E6 age, a four-year-old design that fires rapid volleys of hardened spines across a battlefield. Its technicians call the chassis a patient engine, since it can hold its fire for hours before a single devastating barrage.

rites.name: Crestade
rites.text: Crestade is a sealed ceremonial dispatch-cord, woven from quiet signal-thread, used by the Thudarneld courier guilds to carry sealed orders across the grounded provinces of the E6 era. Its wielders are trained to pull the cord taut at a single moment so that its stored tension can cut through a barricade.

rites.name: Morurock
rites.text: Morurock is a grounded, fist-sized iron-shelled rockworm of the Thudarneld highlands, feared for the sudden spark-bursts it releases when its carapace cracks. Herders say its cry is a warning that the ridge is about to shake loose.

rites.name: Halulden
rites.text: Halulden is a crystalline tuning-stone drawn from the riverbeds of Thudarneld, prized by wayfarers for its steady hum. Its resonance can crack a wall or topple a rickety footbridge when a skilled hand strikes it at the right frequency.

rites.name: Halarenon
rites.text: Halarenon is a quiet, grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse: a cold silencing sigil etched onto the throats of cavern wardens, muting their voices and their workings alike. Its power is modest and precise, bounded by the tiny energies of breath and hand-scale craft.

rites.name: Kelere
rites.text: Kelere is a tidal guardian of the Thudarneld reef-sea, a coral-ribbed colossus that drinks storms and exhales them as crushing spray. Its seven-generation tide-wardens sing it awake each era, and its plating is said to outlast any siege of salt and steel.

rites.name: Dranorath
rites.text: Dranorath is a grounded, fast-moving silencing sentinel of the E6 era, a tireless warden that stalks the wards of Thudarneld and strips the voices of spellcasters from the air around it. Its charge is quick enough to outrun a galloping steed, yet its true danger lies in the hush it leaves behind rather than in raw force.

rites.name: Pelunerdeld
rites.text: Pelunerdeld is a grounded, low-tier conceptual artifact of the Thudarneld omniverse, an ordinary-scale implement from the sixth era. Its makers designed it to quiet the voices of spellcasters within a small radius, a modest but reliable tool for disrupting rites in crowded halls.

rites.name: Drodenath
rites.text: Drodenath is a patient, rust-colored mechanical colossus that drifts through the grey dust-plains of Thudarneld, repairing itself from scavenged scrap. It bears a cluster of rotating barrels that can unleash volleys of needle-thin projectiles, and its grinding footfalls are said to be felt by sleepers miles away.

rites.name: Fenarock
rites.text: Fenarock is a grounded, era-six artisan's tool-spirit bound into a forged iron lantern, which its keeper lights each dawn to call the river fog back into its channels. Its power is modest: it can hurl a gust of stored heat that sears a cart-wheel's worth of frost from a valley road, and it endures long winters of neglect without losing its glow. It is treasured by villagers as a quiet, steady guardian rather than a weapon of war.

rites.name: Crudonath
rites.text: Crudonath is a grounded concept of a bell-cast warden who stands between the hill towns and the rot of the Ashen Marrows, carrying a chime that can ring out a single hour of fierce, unbroken calm. Its people trade tuned stones and herbs for its protection, and the warden is said to sleep only when the bells are silent.

rites.name: Halanar
rites.text: Halanar is a grounded concept of a long spear forged from cold meteoric iron, said to hum when its wielder's heartbeat matches the rhythm of the tide. Its bearers are wardens of coastal gates who strike with measured thrusts that break the momentum of charging beasts. The weapon is valued for its reach and its knack for hurling foes back from the line.

rites.name: Brarock
rites.text: Brarock is a hulking clockwork sentinel forged in the cinder-hills of Thudarneld, built to hold the valley gates against invading storm-kin. Its chest core rings like a struck bell whenever it is wounded, and it can unleash a single concentrated shockwave that splits bedrock for miles.

rites.name: Fenurnostar
rites.text: Fenurnostar is a crystalline war-engine forged in the Ashen Verge, a dead-volcano basin where the ground itself hums with stored heat. It fires volleys of resonant shards that tear through armor and rock alike, and it can seal its own shell against incoming blows for a short, dangerous span.

rites.name: Thoduldath
rites.text: Thoduldath is a grounded, seven-age-old concept of a drill-bodied mechanical sentinel that lingers in the ruins of Thudarneld's old quarries. Its gears spin with stored motion, and its strikes hit the same spot again and again until stone yields. Those who study it say it is less a warrior than a patient machine.

rites.name: Thurde
rites.text: Thurde is a grounded, ancient surveyor-engine of the Thudarneld cosmos, built to map seismic lattices across dry basins. Its sustained hum is a dense drumbeat that loosens the crust beneath it, and its pressure lenses can focus enough heat to scar a plain.

rites.name: Jorudath
rites.text: Jorudath is a crystalline scholar-engine of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of Thudarneld, built to map the fault lines beneath cities. It can unleash a single resonant pulse strong enough to fracture a stone quarter, and it endures long vigils inside collapsing mines.

rites.name: Bruron
rites.text: Bruron is a seven-age-old mechanical mariner-engine from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a hull of brass bells that rings out storms when it sails. Its signature tolling can shake loose the stones of a harbor wall, and it can absorb a blow that would split a ship in two.

rites.name: Brestorath
rites.text: Brestorath is a grounded concept of a mercenary foundry-city in the Thudarneld era E6, famed for its arsenal of volley guns and siege engines. Its engineers fire hundreds of iron needles per salvo, and its heaviest artillery can stop a charging war-beast in its tracks. Veterans still speak of its gunsmiths' cruelest invention: a fuel canister that bursts through any armor.

rites.name: Crenon
rites.text: Crenon is a concept of a slow-moving tide of gravity-lensed silt that rolls across the Thudarneld basin, dimming the sky above it. Its wake leaves behind glassy ridges where stone has been fused by pressure alone. Crenon has no mind, only a rhythm that the basin's wind-singers learned to predict.

rites.name: Moranon
rites.text: Moranon is a bronze-scaled tidal concept born in the Thudarneld shallows during the sixth era, a quiet force that drifts between reef and reef. Its lore holds that a single sweep of its tail can crack a basalt shelf, though it rarely needs to.

rites.name: Kelarath
rites.text: Kelarath is a sealed wardstone of the Thudarneld reach, humming with stored pressure that tuned sentinels draw upon when the valley is threatened. Its wards can scatter a hail of stone shards across a broad field and briefly blank out incoming strikes.

rites.name: Pelenoden
rites.text: Pelenoden is a lattice of resonant glass spires that hums beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, each spire tuned to a different pitch of wind. Its cadence-keepers use the hum to shear loose dust and stone, though its strongest pulses are modest by any cosmic measure.

rites.name: Brarock
rites.text: Brarock is a sediment-bound thunder-tuning apparatus of the Thudarneld foothills, a hollow bell of braided iron that hums the stones of the valley floor into a low resonance. Its keepers rang it to loosen ore veins and to clear rockfall, and its song is said to carry the ground for leagues.

rites.name: Droreld
rites.text: Droreld is a crystalline ward-engine of the Thudarneld grounded realm, humming beneath the marsh-towns of the E6 era for seven ages. Its fields can stiffen the air into a shield and cast sudden lightning through the reed beds that surround it.

rites.name: Pelurnon
rites.text: Pelurnon is a glassy, slow-moving lattice of pale ferrous spores that drifts through the mineral marshes of Thudarneld's grounded reaches. It hums with a low resonance that can rattle loose stone and cause nearby machinery to stall.

rites.name: Drarode
rites.text: Drarode is a crumbling iron sentinel of the Thudarneld, a grounded machine-age power whose ledgers of rust record every siege it survived. Its hammering volleys of shrapnel can flatten a walled garrison, and its own plating can take a battering that would split a cliff.

rites.name: Tarnodardon
rites.text: Tarnodardon is a bronze-scaled ironclad sentinel forged in the foundries of Thudarneld's old mining guilds to guard the sealed valleys. Its slow, heavy frame stores pressure from geothermal vents, which it releases in controlled bursts that can crack stone and rattle distant towers.

rites.name: Drunock
rites.text: Drunock is a bronze-hided tidewalker of the Thudarneld, a concept given form as a patient drinker of rain-cisterns and a keeper of stone wells. Its heavy footfalls are said to loosen sediment from riverbeds and send small landslides down the eastern terraces of its grounded realm.

rites.name: Drudornen
rites.text: Drudornen is a stone-hewn sentinel of the Grounded realm, a colossal construct that marches the high passes and hurls shards of its own bedrock at intruders. Its strikes are rhythmic and inevitable, and it can shrug off blows that would split a mountain in two.

rites.name: Kelaroneld
rites.text: Kelaroneld is a sentient iron-shelled warden of the Grounded realm's ancient seed-vaults, kept dormant for seven ages until its saddle-stones wake it. When roused it hurls needles of compressed root-steel and unleashes thunderous pulses that can split a hillside.

rites.name: Keluste
rites.text: Keluste is a tireless wandering engine of brass and gray basalt, built by the Thudarneld drift-smiths to clear collapsed mine tunnels. It carries a rotating drum of iron teeth that can chew through a stone wall in a single pass.

rites.name: Thorath
rites.text: Thorath is a drowned-iron war engine that sleeps beneath the tidal flats of Vell Harrow, its hull stitched from salvaged ferry hulls and bell metal. When the sea tide turns, it rises in a single shuddering heave and hurls its rusted spines outward in a volley that can strip a shoreline bare.

rites.name: Haluston
rites.text: Haluston is a drifting ironwood sentinel that tends the mossy vaults of the Thudarneld foothills, its bark-plated limbs humming with stored sap-lightning. Long ago it was carved to guard the seed-bank of the Ember Orchards, and it still keeps its watch with patient, grinding certainty.

rites.name: Thanock
rites.text: Thanock is a weathered sky-forge that hammers storm-iron into the rings of a drowned harbor city. Its strikes are measured in the thousands of joules, enough to split a skiff, yet it can absorb a seven-era siege without cracking.

rites.name: Crolden
rites.text: Crolden is a lattice of ember-rooted tectonic glyphs woven through the ash deserts of Thudarneld, traditionally used by clan-smiths to coax stone into obedient shapes. Its practitioners say the craft is less about force than about persuading the ground to remember a pattern it once held.

rites.name: Thaldunen
rites.text: Thaldunen is a crystalline sentinel of the Grounded realm, a slow-moving guardian whose frame hums with stored stillness. It answers any intrusion with a single unblockable lance of pressure that pierces even hardened stone.

rites.name: Halurdock
rites.text: Halurdock is a crystalline reef-spirit of the Thudarneld shallows, a concept-form entity that hums through the tidal caverns of its era. It is known for shaping sediment into living walls that bind travelers to the seabed.

rites.name: Thune
rites.text: Thune is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a cadence of hardened wardens who draw strength from long-held oaths rather than raw power. Its discipline keeps its feats modest, suited to the third age of its world where personal endurance matters more than spectacle.

rites.name: Morostenon
rites.text: Morostenon is a grounded concept of stone-thread wardens who weave dormant seams in Thudarneld's crust into a single resonant wall. Their most famous act is a Thudarneld-era dam-breaking sealed into a canyon, and they are known for sustaining that wall through long dry seasons.

rites.name: Bronar
rites.text: Bronar is a grounded thudding engine-spirit of the Thudarneld cosmos, a giant slow-hammering being that stamps the earth into rhythm. Its every strike shakes a village's foundations and can topple a stone watchtower in one blow.

rites.name: Feneste
rites.text: Feneste is a quiet grounded sentinel of the Thudarneld reaches, a bronze-plated warden that hums beneath the surface of hollow stone hills. It stores the tremors of passing storms and releases them in precise, controlled bursts when its territory is threatened.

rites.name: Kelaresten
rites.text: Kelaresten is a resonant ward-pattern woven into the stone bridges of the Thudarneld highlands, a lattice of sealed sigils that hum when disturbed. Its keepers can tap the stored tension of the lattice to release a single, focused shock that splits boulders and rattles nearby settlements. The pattern is ancient, fragile at its seams, and mostly dormant except during the seasonal tides of the upper valleys.

rites.name: Cradon
rites.text: Cradon is a fraying lattice of bone-white crystal that hums through the ruins of Thudarneld's old fortress-cities, storing the tremors of passing armies. Its keepers sing to it to keep its stored force from spilling into the earth below. When a lattice is struck, the stored force can be loosed in one brittle, deafening burst.

rites.name: Jorastar
rites.text: Jorastar is a quiet tuning-spirit of the Grounded realm, a crystalline sentinel that hums through the stone of Thudarneld's mountain roots. It keeps the pressure of buried fault-lines in balance and, when roused, can release a single pent-up shudder.

rites.name: Moredurnath
rites.text: Moredurnath is a quiet, nine-foot lantern-keeper of the Thudarneld hill-towns, a concept woven into the old storm-warding rites. Its wards can stir a single collapsed granary or rattle a bridge into rubble, but no more.

rites.name: Dreldonock
rites.text: Dreldonock is a bramble-wrapped tuning engine humming through the foundry districts of Thudarneld, its gears drawing power from buried geothermal veins. Its storms of thorned gears can flatten a row of workshops in a single pulse, and it endures long sieges of stone and fire without rest.

rites.name: Halurnedar
rites.text: Halurnedar is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of stone-wardens who hum in the deep quarries of Thudarneld, their voices shaping the walls of the earth. Its power is measured in the quiet shudder of loosened gravel rather than in cataclysm, so its feats stay within a single city block or a small hillside.

rites.name: Brordeld
rites.text: Brordeld is a stone-carved sentinel of the Thudarneld highlands, a concept of mineral discipline that teaches cliffs to hold their ground against the wind. Its guardians can crack a boulder field open in a single stamp, and their tempered hides can take a hard blow without tearing.

rites.name: Tharden
rites.text: Tharden is a quiet mental discipline taught in the lantern-halls of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to bend the weight of their own resolve into focused strikes. Its masters are known for patient duels that rarely end in ruin, though a few legends speak of a single shattering blow that toppled a fortified tower.

rites.name: Crurdock
rites.text: Crurdock is a rust-red armored colossus that drags its own weight through the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, delivering blunt crushing strikes. Its shell absorbs and redirects force, letting it endure impacts that would shatter lesser beasts.

rites.name: Braldurden
rites.text: Braldurden is a sprawling archive of hollow tactics, a grounded art of cunning and ruin that the wardens of Thudarneld use to quell rogue beasts and failing walls alike. Its practitioners rely on weight, timing, and sharpened stone rather than cosmic force, and their greatest works bring down a single district at most.

rites.name: Joroduneld
rites.text: Joroduneld is a fleeting concept in the Thudarneld cosmos, a shared mental motif that drifts between minds in the Grounded realm during the sixth era. Its power is measured in the quiet tilt of thought, a faint pull that rarely exceeds the force of a single shaken door.

rites.name: Fenonareld
rites.text: Fenonareld is a shimmering lattice of crystallized rain that hangs above the Thudarneld plains, a concept rather than a creature, a place where storms are bottled. Its villages trade in woven charms that hum with stored thunder, and its wardens are said to guard it from the seasons themselves.

rites.name: Theldar
rites.text: Theldar is a concept of a dormant resonance that hums within the stone foundations of Thudarneld, a grounded realm in its seventh age. It is said to awaken only when pressure from the surrounding earth reaches a critical threshold, releasing bursts of sound that can shake a settlement apart.

rites.name: Tarnenoreld
rites.text: Tarnenoreld is a grounded ability-lattice of the Thudarneld cosmos, a discipline of rhythmic pulses that a practitioner threads through their own bones to unleash bursts of force. Its tradition is taught in the mountain halls of the Oskerren guilds, where students train on hollowed stone bells. Its power is measured in the heft of a falling roof rather than in planetary scale.

rites.name: Braron
rites.text: Braron is a tuned resonance-engine built into the cargo spines of the Grounded realm's river barges during the sixth era. It releases focused pulses that can split a loaded hull open or rattle a riverside warehouse flat within a single crossing, and it sustains heavy strain for long hauls without failing.

rites.name: Brunastock
rites.text: Brunastock is a clockwork-grown ledger of lantern-scale mechanisms used only by the wild hollow-beasts of the Thudarneld moors. Each mechanism sputters for a few breaths, then sleeps until the next dusk. Its most common expression is a brief bellows-burst that rattles shutters and cracks old tiles.

rites.name: Morode
rites.text: Morode is a grounded power-catalogue entry in Thudarneld's sixth era, a field of craft-bound abilities that rise only after a combatant has been wounded for a time. Its practitioners channel modest pressures and blunt impacts, and the entry's prowess ceiling sits well below city-scale destruction. It is recorded as a list of techniques passed between duelists rather than as a single bloodline.

rites.name: Pelurnon
rites.text: Pelurnon is a sealed resonance discipline taught in the drowned archives of Thudarneld, where practitioners tune their bones to the hum of buried iron. Its adepts are known for sudden, localized bursts of force that can split a cart or flatten a barricade, but they tire quickly and cannot sustain the effort for long.

rites.name: Tarnornath
rites.text: Tarnornath is a quiet grammar of borrowed resonance, a discipline taught in the hush-towers of Thudarneld where practitioners learn to hold a tone until stone remembers it. Its adepts are not warriors but tuners, and their rare public acts can crack a bridge or shake a granary loose from its foundations. Apprentices are told that the art is mostly restraint.

rites.name: Brastar
rites.text: Brastar is a dormant ceremonial mechanism of the Thudarneld reaches, a bronze-ribbed engine that wakes only when its keepers sing the tuned notes of their dead. Once awake it can overturn cart-sized loads and drive sparks through iron gates, but its strongest work is patient, measured labor rather than violence.

rites.name: Tarnestock
rites.text: Tarnestock is a heavy iron fitting used in the grinding mills of Thudarneld's lower quarters, where it bears the weight of rolling stone wheels. Its cast ribs can absorb the shock of a stalled mill tearing loose, and it has been known to hurl a split millstone across a yard when it snaps.

rites.name: Thurdeld
rites.text: Thurdeld is a grounded concept of crafted weapon-sigils, each etched with a dampened focus that releases a single burst of force before dissipating. Wielders in the Thudarneld reckon their craft by how cleanly a sigil can be spent, not by how much damage it does.

rites.name: Branon
rites.text: Branon is a dormant sealed-vault dweller of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, a hollow tuning-spirit that wakes only when a cracked bell rings in the lower chambers. In its waking state it can turn stored thunder into a single rolling burst that rattles a whole ruined district.

rites.name: Drunen
rites.text: Drunen is a grounded lattice of thorn-bound moor-spirits in the Thudarneld cycle, the quiet force that keeps reed-fields from drowning. Its wardens loose gusts of pollen-sharp wind and hurl chipped flint at intruders, and in the seventh age they learned to wear borrowed sparks of lightning like a cloak.

rites.name: Keledurdock
rites.text: Keledurdock is a crumbling ledger-engine of the Grounded realm, a clockwork archive that tallies every debt owed between the rivers of Thudarneld. Its gears hum with a low resentment whenever a debt is left unpaid, and it can turn that resentment into a sudden shove of force.

rites.name: Brernoldock
rites.text: Brernoldock is a dormant grinding-engine rumored to have powered the old hill-foundries of Thudarneld before the great freeze. Its gears still turn in the deep caverns, sometimes groaning loose enough to shake loose cliffs.

rites.name: Therne
rites.text: Therne is a quiet discipline of the Thudarneld powers, taught in the grey monasteries of the Sallow Reach, where practitioners learn to borrow a foe's stance mid-duel. Its adepts can seize a rival's momentum for a short while, though the borrowed force must be returned before the next breath. The art is respected for its cleverness rather than its strength.

rites.name: Brornath
rites.text: Brornath is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, an ancient ledger of cursed bargains written in the marrow of a dying forest. It is recorded less as a single being than as a catalogue of sworn rites that its followers invoke against rivals. Its entries favour dread and misdirection over raw force, though a few of its oaths can still tear open a fortified gate.

rites.name: Fenodath
rites.text: Fenodath is a dry-stone sorcery-discipline of the Grounded realm, practiced in the terraced hill-shrines of Thudarneld's eastern valleys during the sixth era. Its adepts shape loose gravel and root-rot into brief, bruising pressure that they carry in their wrists and in the soles of their feet. It is taught as a patient craft rather than a weapon, though rivals of the valley shrines have long feared its quiet reach.

rites.name: Thordasteld
rites.text: Thordasteld is a hollow tuning-fork of a concept, a wandering resonance that the Thudarneld courts record as a sequence of ringing signatures rather than a body. Its signatures are cataloged by the monastic listeners of the low marshes, who treat each chime as a ward against drowned bells.

rites.name: Keludorden
rites.text: Keludorden is a grounded set of martial arts drawn from the Thudarneld's old fighting schools, passed down only to those hunters who prove they can outlast their rivals. Its practitioners are known for sudden, controlled bursts of force and for stances that shift mid-fight as wounds accumulate.

rites.name: Peledasten
rites.text: Peledasten is a sealed-rune glyph of the Grounded realm, an inert grammar of binding cited in the scribes' archives of Thudarneld's seventh age. Its strokes are said to hold a tide of kindled ash that is released only when the bearer drops the final stroke.

rites.name: There
rites.text: There is a concept in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, an idea of a quiet hush that settles over a place and lingers for seven ages. Its bearers are said to sense the exact weight of what passes through their hands, and they measure all things by it. Its strongest recorded act is a single moment that briefly stilled a river valley.

rites.name: Tarnastodar
rites.text: Tarnastodar is a sentient bronze-scaled wyrm-engine that hums beneath the salt flats of the Vulnerine Reach, where it coordinates the storm-herds of the basin. In its prime it can break a rockbound ridge and hold a gale-wall together for days, though its own hide begins to crack after sustained effort.

rites.name: Kelanudar
rites.text: Kelanudar is a hollow-boned glider-spirit of the Thudarneld cloudmarshes, kept by river clans as a living lantern. In the ninth season of its wakefulness it can gather the marsh's damp into a single scorching exhalation.

rites.name: Therde
rites.text: Therde is a quiet reed-spirit that drifts through the marsh-lands of Thudarneld, mending the water it passes over. Its sustained songs can ripple the ground for leagues, yet it rarely wishes to strike at all. Those who cross its path tend to leave with a little less mud and a little more calm.

rites.name: Tarnuldeld
rites.text: Tarnuldeld is a grounded concept of hushed mountain-speech, a discipline that lets a voice settle stones into fallen formations. Seasoned practitioners add a second layer called the Returning Hum, which they can only begin partway through a long rite. Its energies stay within the ceiling of a single crumbling hillside.

rites.name: Thuldon
rites.text: Thuldon is a grounded, age-seven arcane discipline in the Thudarneld reach, where practitioners bind flickering sparks into brittle rune-lattices. Its masters are known less for raw force than for deft redirection, folding small impacts into a rhythm that can topple stone walls.

rites.name: Crernaldock
rites.text: Crernaldock is a weathered lantern-keeper's guild in the grounded lowlands of Thudarneld, sworn to tend the beacons that warn fishing villages of tidal surges. Its members train with heavy iron hooks and ringing signal-bells that can shake loose a crumbling sea wall. Their reputation rests on quiet, stubborn endurance rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Pelolduren
rites.text: Pelolduren is a moss-wrapped sentinel of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet keeper that hums with stored sunlight and sleeps through the seasons. Its ancient roots coil beneath the hills, and when provoked it can unleash a sudden burst of stored energy that cracks stone and scatters flocks of birds.

rites.name: Kelarneldar
rites.text: Kelarneldar is a bronze-scaled sky-hunter of the Thudarneld highlands, whose wing-beats can crack granite cliffs and whose howl unseats birds from the air for leagues. Its kind is called upon by herders to guard flocks, and it fights with a stubborn hunger that few other beasts of its era can match.

rites.name: Feneron
rites.text: Feneron is a concept of ancient chime-hymns that the Thudarneld mountain-choirs sing to bind loose stone. Its practitioners use it to shape gravel into temporary bridges and walls, and its power grows as a melody builds toward its final chord.

rites.name: Joralderne
rites.text: Joralderne is a wandering keeper of brass hourglasses who can slow the fall of falling stones to a drift. Its strongest act is to hold a collapsing wall motionless for a full morning before its own bindings give way.

rites.name: Kelornar
rites.text: Kelornar is a tidal lamp-spirit of the Thudarneld reefs, a grounded concept that bends sea-light into brief bursts of pressure. It rarely fights, preferring to drag wanderers into the shallows where its glow hardens into stone-cold silt.

rites.name: Fenare
rites.text: Fenare is a rune-carved sigil-stone that hums when struck by a tuning hammer, used by the Thudarneld stonecutters' guild to bind gravel into load-bearing walls. In its best-remembered act, a single cracked fenare blocked a collapsing aqueduct, though its own weight and shattering dwarfed the cost of its work.

rites.name: Draston
rites.text: Draston is a concept of a grounded, mid-age power set in the realm of Thudarneld, where bearers of its gift can unleash tremors of coordinated force that lift and scatter stone and earth. Its practitioners are rarely seen, as the discipline demands a long apprenticeship and a steady temperament.

rites.name: Pelonar
rites.text: Pelonar is a grounded concept of a drifting tidewood canopy that thrives in the mist-banks of the Thudarneld shelf. Its seed-pods can be shaped into mantles that reflect light and hum with a low resonance, a technique used only by the canopy's wardens. Its roots are famously stubborn, sustaining a hundred years of drought without yielding.

rites.name: Fenordudock
rites.text: Fenordudock is a bound compendium of gravel-cant rites, kept by the wandering scribes of Thudarneld's dry basins. Each rite is a practiced knack for turning ordinary stone, wind, and sinew against the unwary traveler. Its pages are said to rearrange themselves when read aloud on the wrong hill.

rites.name: Morure
rites.text: Morure is a sealed grammar of ten-thousand-pound pressure-glyphs etched into the basalt cliffs of Thudarneld's eastern shelf, each one a hymn to heavy weather. Scholars of the Grounded realm read these glyphs as instructions for coaxing thunderheads into collapse, though no living tongue preserves the full sequence.

rites.name: Thodurdar
rites.text: Thodurdar is a sealed-off reliquary of drowned bell-foundries in the Thudarneld, where ancient smiths cast chimes that still hum with stored resonance. Its bells can shatter stone walls when rung in unison, and its keepers guard the iron tongues that set them sounding. It is a grounded, workshop-scale realm whose echoes rarely reach beyond the marshes.

rites.name: Kelunon
rites.text: Kelunon is a drifting sensory discipline practiced by hermit-scribes of the Thudarneld frontier, who believe names carry weight. Its adepts can unravel a rival's memory of a single sentence, leaving the victim unable to recall one word they once knew.

rites.name: Feneldadon
rites.text: Feneldadon is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of sealed stone-wardens who guard the marsh-roads of Thudarneld. Its wardens are not born with their strength but gather it from the mud and rain as a fight wears on, growing harder to stop with each passing hour.

rites.name: Peludelde
rites.text: Peludelde is a fungal grove-spirit of the Thudarneld wilds, whose spores can burst into a choking cloud that clings for days. Its chief art is to root into the ground and coax sleeping roots into lashing out against nearby travellers.

rites.name: Fenudath
rites.text: Fenudath is a silent, sun-bleached drifter of the Thudarneld salt flats, a lone wanderer whose crystalline staff can sing stones into dust. Legends say those who pursue it are led into the dunes and never found again.

rites.name: Bronudar
rites.text: Bronudar is a stone-hewn warden of the Thudarneld's lowest grounded tiers, standing guard over quarry roads where ancient mineral veins hum beneath the dust. It strikes with a heavy basalt maul and can cave in a small village's foundations with a single blow.

rites.name: Drerdath
rites.text: Drerdath is a grounded concept of a mortal sea-wright whose craft lives in tides rather than fire. Its practitioners sing the slack water into still pools that can cradle a small boat for a single season. Only the lowest rungs of its wonders reach beyond a village harbour.

rites.name: Halurnar
rites.text: Halurnar is a grounded, era-six pocket of Thudarneld where a single hard-fought wind carries the memory of the land. Its inhabitants wager ancient cairns of tuned stone against the seasons, and the ledgers of their tallies are kept in woven copper. Few outsiders have learned to read them.

rites.name: Therdornock
rites.text: Therdornock is a grounded practice of tidal-chant rituals from the Thudarneld marshes, used by tide-wardens to calm and redirect the brackish waters that cover the lowland villages. Its adepts sing harmonic tones that can churn a small bay or stir a flooded field into a whirlpool. Its power is modest but precise, and it is taught by oral lineage across seven generations.

rites.name: Pelanon
rites.text: Pelanon is a glassy, spiral-shelled reef-mind of the Thudarneld shallows, drifting in the age-seven tides of the E6 era. Its colonies coordinate by faint lantern-pulses that can stun swimmers and sear through small hulls. It is valued by fishing guilds for its luminous secretions.

rites.name: Thodar
rites.text: Thodar is a rhythm-keeping lattice of hollow bronze bells, grown in the stillwater marshes of Thudarneld during its sixth age. Its chimes can loosen soil, scatter flocks of birds, and quiet the wind across a valley for an afternoon.

rites.name: Cronock
rites.text: Cronock is a grounded concept of stored tidal rhythm, an ancient measure that the people of Thudarneld use to time harvests and tides. Its practitioners can gather and release small surges of kinetic force across a village or field.

rites.name: Tarneren
rites.text: Tarneren is a grounded, era-six tuning discipline that lets a practitioner rewrite the timing of their own reflexes rather than their strength. Its adepts trade raw force for precision, cutting the lag of their spells and blows by close to half at the cost of a fragile, nervous stillness.

rites.name: Drorune
rites.text: Drorune is a silent, bone-white lattice-hound that roams the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, sustained by the marrow of fallen grazers. Its signature act is a gnashing burst of mineral shards that strips a wounded foe's vitality and returns part of it to the hound's own frame.

rites.name: Croldare
rites.text: Croldare is a pale, ash-coated concept of drifting spores that bloom only in the cold hours of the grounded era's seventh age. Its power lies in patient erosion rather than sudden force, letting a small dust storm wear stone or dull a blade over a long night.

rites.name: Jorurneld
rites.text: Jorurneld is a tide-bound warden of the Grounded realm's sunken orchards, a figure who gathers the silt of drowned harvests into thorned pikes. Its long vigil keeps the lowland cisterns from bursting when the seasons turn.

rites.name: Morenastath
rites.text: Morenastath is a drifting tide-engine that the Grounded realm's E6 scholars cataloged as a reservoir of pressure rather than a creature. Its surface shrugs off hammering storms, and its deep chambers hold stored resonance that it can release in a single crack of sound.

rites.name: Kelesteld
rites.text: Kelesteld is a ritual-lattice of salt-bound mirrors in the grounded era E6, built to channel the quiet hum of old machinery. Its keepers measure its strength in practical hours of labor rather than in grand catastrophe, and it rarely outputs more than a village's worth of force.

rites.name: Joraldock
rites.text: Joraldock is a quiet wandering engine-sage of the Grounded realm, known for its slow, deliberate tremors that unseat stone and tempers. Its strongest act is said to crack a hillside open in a single exhale, and it can endure similar blows while standing unmoved.

rites.name: Pelurneld
rites.text: Pelurneld is a grounded spirit of the Thudarneld cosmos, a wandering scrap-tinker who turns fallen storm-rods into talismans. Its signature is a rain of bright needles that can pierce a city wall in a single breath. Though mortal in scale, it is feared for its endless patience and sharp, sudden temper.

rites.name: Drorduste
rites.text: Drorduste is a sealed resonance of brass-throated bells that hums through the stone of Thudarneld's lowland marshes, binding the shifting mud into weathered walkways. Its tolls are said to calm storms and to fracture the wills of anyone who hears them too long.

rites.name: Crustarock
rites.text: Crustarock is a tectonic-grade stone guardian sealed beneath the cliffs of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, its shell laced with ancient sediment-bound runes. It wakes only when the surrounding bedrock trembles, and then it splits boulder-sized fragments from its own body to hurl as weapons.

rites.name: Breldodar
rites.text: Breldodar is a crystalline mirror-weave of the Thudarneld, a concept woven into the shifting powers of its Grounded realm during the sixth era. Its seven-year-old lattice channels small bursts of stored force that the realm's people use for tools and rituals rather than war.

rites.name: Braldosten
rites.text: Braldosten is a sunken lighthouse-god of the Grounded realm, a patient mass of rust and brine that has learned to answer ships which call its name. Its tides were said to level harbor districts when it grew angry, and its scale is measured in the drowned towns it has pulled under.

rites.name: Thuldordon
rites.text: Thuldordon is a grounded ember-warden of the Vellan marshes, a hulking mire-beast whose slow stride cracks the reed-banks like brittle glass. Its hide is laced with resin that hardens into shields, and it can exhale a choking cloud of pollen that stalls the breath of anything nearby. The marsh folk say it sleeps beneath the water for a century between wakings.

rites.name: Thardar
rites.text: Thardar is a dormant lattice-warden of the Grounded realm, a bell-shaped crystal engine that hums beneath the salt flats of its era. When wardens are roused, it sings a low chord that can rattle the surrounding stone and drive lesser creatures into a stupor.

rites.name: Keloldon
rites.text: Keloldon is a grounded concept of a crystalline hermit who calls down needle-like shards of frozen light that pierce mountains and vanish. Its deepest act is a single soundless flick of its tail that cracks the bedrock of a valley it was born beneath. It rarely moves faster than a galloping horse, preferring stillness.

rites.name: Pelostedock
rites.text: Pelostedock is a hollow-shelled stone tortoise of the Grounded realm's Era Six, sealed for seven ages beneath the sediment of the Ashen Marsh. When disturbed, it can release a crushing pulse that splits bedrock and flattens nearby huts, and its carapace has endured the weight of collapsed watchtowers for generations.

rites.name: Halordeld
rites.text: Halordeld is a dueling-hymn concept from the Thudarneld cycle, a ritual form where wardens trade chanted sigils to pin rival spirits in place. Its practitioners are bound by a rule that no sigil may exceed the strength of the chanter's own breath.

rites.name: Pelonar
rites.text: Pelonar is a drifting ring of grey mist that hums with a low, dissatisfied tone across the Thudarneld frontier. Those who wander into its hollows often return with their bones feeling heavier than when they left.

rites.name: Moruste
rites.text: Moruste is a quiet, unlicensed art of tuning ordinary stone into resonant tools, practiced by wandering masons in the lowland provinces of Thudarneld. Its adepts can shatter a loaded wagon axle with a chanted note or hold a collapsing wall upright through sheer patience. The craft is taught only through apprenticeship and remains a hidden trade in the Grounded realm.

rites.name: Jorerne
rites.text: Jorerne is a grounded, era-six stonework engine of the Thudarneld reach, a ringing pillar of cold brass that a cult of masons raises to hold back river floods. When its bell is struck it shatters loose clay walls and sends shock through the riverbank soil.

rites.name: Therdath
rites.text: Therdath is a quiet resonance-weaver of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of the Thudarneld cycle, a concept embodied in the hum of old stone. Its art is measured in patient vibrations that loosen mortar, bells, and resolve alike. It is said to have taught the valley masons how to listen before they build.

rites.name: Jorostarnen
rites.text: Jorostarnen is a drowned-cathedral warden of the Grounded realm, a patient sentinel that keeps the tide-bells of its sunken city from ringing too early. Its stillness is legendary, but when a flood of silt threatens the lower wards it can unleash a single resonant pulse that shatters the bedrock beneath the flooded district.

rites.name: Kelornar
rites.text: Kelornar is a bell-shaped ward-engine forged in the Thudarneld cloisters during the sixth age, meant to silence rogue sigils across the grounded provinces. Its resonance can hush small mechanical marauders and disrupt the drift of minor ember-hounds, but it cannot withstand sustained assault for long.

rites.name: Morunon
rites.text: Morunon is a silt-bred concept of resonant grinding, a wordless hum drawn from the deep marshes of Thudarneld in the Grounded realm. It answers the stillness of the drowned fields by loosening stone into dust and fine sediment.

rites.name: Dreldurnath
rites.text: Dreldurnath is a grounded concept-warrior of the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-hearted scrapper who fights with a hammer of compacted river-clay and hardened resin. Its strikes are measured in the tens of thousands of joules, enough to crack a bridge pier or flatten a timber barn. Locals call it the Patient Anvil because it can take a battering that would fell a bull and keep rising.

rites.name: Brestaden
rites.text: Brestaden is a grounded concept, a sealed clockwork vault-keeper of Thudarneld that ferries cargo across the barrens and hums with stored tension. It answers commands with bursts of mechanical force rather than magic, its gears wound by the tides of an underground river.

rites.name: Fenurdon
rites.text: Fenurdon is a grounded, tireless siege-engine of the Thudarneld frontier, built from bone-iron and drawn by stubborn drakes across the plains of the Ashmere Reach. Its volleys of barbed quills can pierce fortified walls, and its hardened hide shrugs off most blows that would split lesser beasts.

rites.name: Brastereld
rites.text: Brastereld is a grounded, seven-year-old tide-engine of the E6 era, built to strip the minerals from wrecked vessels along the Thudarneld shoals. Its rhythmic pulse can crack hull plating and rattle the teeth of anyone standing too close, though its sustained output is modest by the standards of the wider omniverse.

rites.name: Broren
rites.text: Broren is a rust-colored iron golem that lumbers through the mining valleys of the Thudarneld frontier, dismantling collapsed tunnels with its bare hands. Its maintainers say it wakes whenever a shaft gives way, and it never stops until the rubble is cleared into neat stacks.

rites.name: Tarnaderde
rites.text: Tarnaderde is a sealed, cold-forged bulwark that hums under the frost of Thudarneld's northern wastes, its gates opened only to those who carry the proper tallies. Its wardens count every breath drawn within its walls and answer any excess with a measured, ringing reckoning. The fortress is said to have stood through seven ages without a single wall being moved.

rites.name: Thodeldar
rites.text: Thodeldar is a quiet, grounded concept in Thudarneld, a valley of stone-carved mills and wind-driven looms in its seventh age. It is best known as a shared discipline of coaxing pressure out of ordinary stone and water, used by millers and masons to split rock and turn wheels.

rites.name: Bredock
rites.text: Bredock is a sealed clockwork glyph-lattice used by the Thudarneld reclusive armorers, a concept that binds small stored tensions into brief, pinpoint bursts. Its engravers are said to weigh each lattice against a grudge before casting it, so no two Bredocks ever stand in the same workshop.

rites.name: Joranordath
rites.text: Joranordath is a bound resonance-technique taught in the mountain monasteries of Thudarneld, a discipline of sung cadences that strip the will from living foes. Practitioners of the seventh age use it to quiet hostile beasts and raiders without bloodshed.

rites.name: Halonock
rites.text: Halonock is a dormant mechanical lattice in the Thudarneld powers realm, built from brass-coiled sigils that store kinetic tension. When its rings are struck in sequence, it releases a concentrated shock capable of toppling stone walls and shattering cargo ships in their berths.

rites.name: Crulderen
rites.text: Crulderen is a catalogue of hostile tricks maintained by the wardens of Thudarneld, each one a learned technique passed from opponent to opponent across seven ages. Its entries describe how creatures of the grounded realm strike, shield themselves, and falter, and the lists are copied by hand in the lower archives.

rites.name: Fenurock
rites.text: Fenurock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a lattice of stone-carved ritual traps that pulse across the valley floor during the seventh age. Its feats involve sudden, localized stone-bursts and rockfall that few living things in that era could survive.

rites.name: Crunen
rites.text: Crunen is a dense, grinding alloy-gear of the Grounded realm, forged in the sixth era to hold a single mechanical duty: to bear weight without yielding. It is a concept rather than a creature, a mill-stone of pressure that tests the limits of everything bolted to it.

rites.name: Brerdustock
rites.text: Brerdustock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld cycle, a catalogue of crafted snare-tricks that hunters of the seventh age learned to set against wild beasts. Each trick is recorded as a short ledger line, and the lines are read aloud at harvest-feasts to teach apprentices which traps still hold their old strength.

rites.name: Joruron
rites.text: Joruron is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed-off storm of crystalline sand that keeps a single ancient reactor humming beneath the dunes. Its people treat the reactor as a sacred hearth and coax it into venting pressure through carefully timed releases called exhales.

rites.name: Kelerden
rites.text: Kelerden is a concept of a hushed, rune-scribed bell-forge in the Thudarneld reaches, where wardens strike tones that bind the weather of nearby valleys. Its ringing is measured in small, deliberate acts rather than cataclysms, reflecting its grounded place in the sixth era. The forge's craft depends on patient tuning rather than raw force.

rites.name: Tarneralden
rites.text: Tarneralden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rotating archive of tactical war-tricks that inscribed warriors learn by memorizing sequences of coded maneuvers. Its practitioners wield these routines as sharp, deliberate techniques rather than raw force, and the feats below reflect modest but precise capabilities suited to its mortal scale.

rites.name: Fenerne
rites.text: Fenerne is a hush-lantern, a concept of quiet tallow-light that a village keeper trims each dusk to keep wandering sleepers from drifting off. Its gentle glow can ease a spirit's restless wandering but cannot hold back anything larger than a sleeping child's dream.

rites.name: Fenernar
rites.text: Fenernar is a concept of a grounded, era-six power system in the invented realm of Thudarneld, where a practitioner shapes stored heat into a stubborn, slowly building blaze. Its adepts are prized for turning ordinary furnaces and lanterns into lasting sources of force rather than instant bursts.

rites.name: Morurdeld
rites.text: Morurdeld is a quiet cartographic instrument of the Thudarneld reach, a brass-and-glass sextant that records the sway of nearby currents rather than stars. Its keepers treat its readings as sacred, though it has never once been shown to be wrong.

rites.name: Crone
rites.text: Crone is a concept of a wandering hag-spirit who lives in the thorny hedgerows of the Thudarneld frontier, feeding on forgotten bargains. Her art is tying small oaths into knots that tear the fabric of contracts and roads alike. She is a sprawling but grounded presence, rarely dangerous beyond a village's borders.

rites.name: Fenaderdar
rites.text: Fenaderdar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld world, a warding spell-engine that hums beneath the frost-plains of its era. Its lattice of sigils can be tuned to spit out bursts of focused force used by wardens to break ice and turn back raiding beasts. Within its age of seven, its tools remain modest, measured in the reach of a village rather than a realm.

rites.name: Croneld
rites.text: Croneld is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a catalogue of inscribed hazards that a wandering archivist uses to name the tricks of rival wardens. Its entries are copied by hand onto sheets that travel between the wardens' halls in the sixth era of their calendar.

rites.name: Jorurnadon
rites.text: Jorurnadon is a stone-hided leviathan that sleeps beneath the glacial plates of Thudarneld and wakes only when the tides freeze over. Its hide is so dense that a single breath of its ancestral chant can topple a ridge of basalt cliffs.

rites.name: Drostar
rites.text: Drostar is a bronze-scaled tidal concept that lives in the flooded lowlands of Thudarneld, where it coordinates ash-storms and reed-channel defenses. Its gift is a dense salt-hum that can strip the cohesion from small structures and stun ground-dwelling creatures. Elders describe it as patient and rarely seen beyond the marsh-edge.

rites.name: Moraldereld
rites.text: Moraldereld is a quiet, grounded concept of a hollow mountain-bound spirit that hums through the powers of sunken rivers. It draws mineral strength from the earth and channels it into slow, patient pulses rather than explosions.

rites.name: Haledurne
rites.text: Haledurne is a grounded concept that governs the flow of sorrow through the rivers of Thudarneld, drawing its strength from mourners who sing at the banks. Its power is quiet but steady, letting it sustain small communities against drought and grief for seven ages.

rites.name: Fenuldedath
rites.text: Fenuldedath is a quiet, drifting force of the Grounded realm, a sleeping mind-current that hums beneath the rivers of Thudarneld. It wakes only when the local powers are disturbed, and then it reshapes the nearby terrain with a patient, almost tidal, pressure.

rites.name: Kelarnuneld
rites.text: Kelarnuneld is a dormant engine of hollow-bell thunder, buried beneath the salt flats of Vorrenhaal in the Thudarneld cycle. Its wardens lure travelers to its cracked dome to trade their hearing for a single resonant chime. Every seventh spring the bell rings unbidden, and the ground remembers.

rites.name: Thorneldock
rites.text: Thorneldock is a grounded, slow-aging concept from the E6 era, a stone-and-root hamlet whose inhabitants quietly shape the land through patient craft rather than spectacle. Its people are known for mending broken machinery and coaxing crops from barren soil, and their works endure for generations.

rites.name: Craderen
rites.text: Craderen is a concept of a lattice of hollow crystal bells that ring when disturbed, each tone a rune of force that gathers into quiet pressure. Its wardens teach that the bells were tuned by a choir long gone, and that the silence between their notes hides the true weight of the world.

rites.name: Kelorunock
rites.text: Kelorunock is a grounded concept of a sealed lattice-drive, a crystalline engine that stores tidal strain in a single resonant chamber. Its builders regarded it as a relic of the sixth era, meant for lifting cargo rather than fighting.

rites.name: Fenolde
rites.text: Fenolde is a quiet, wind-carved archipelago in Thudarneld whose floating monasteries hum with sealed chimes. Its keepers can still-freeze a single sailor's nervous system for a heartbeat, a discipline they guard jealously and rarely teach to outsiders.

rites.name: Morostanath
rites.text: Morostanath is a dormant lattice-engine buried beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, built in the sixth era to hold back tidal storms. Its wardens rarely wake it, but when they do, its humming arrays can tear loose a stretch of shoreline in a single pulse.

rites.name: Tarnardath
rites.text: Tarnardath is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a vast silent resonance that grows within crystalline spires of the E6 era. Its pulses can unravel the fundamental bonds of any living creature in the surrounding region, leaving behind only cold ash and silence.

rites.name: Halene
rites.text: Halene is a sinuous lash of coiled fire-hardened sinew that the Thudarneld wardens use to herd storm-beasts across the salt flats. Its swings can crack a cliff-face or fling a rider several streets, and it is said to keep a wounded hunter's pulse steady.

rites.name: Kelalde
rites.text: Kelalde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an ordered catalogue of inscribed battle techniques meant to be recited by apprentice archivists in their seventh age. Its power is modest, measured in crafted gestures rather than cosmic forces, shaping how sentinels and scholars resolve rival claims.

rites.name: Crare
rites.text: Crare is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sticky, reflective membrane that a wandering tribe of hunters stretches across their campfires to bounce away spells. Its mucus-slick surface can also be whipped outward as a lashing strike that knocks prey off their feet.

rites.name: Therdar
rites.text: Therdar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed lattice of listed hazards where each entry is a catalogue of blunt, mechanical effects rather than a cosmic force. Its operators treat its strikes as bounded instruments, capped by the strain of a single human-scale body.

rites.name: Tarnudar
rites.text: Tarnudar is a grounded concept entity of the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed lattice of reasoning-engines that hums through the seventh age of the E6 era. It operates by reshaping the local weights of possibility, letting it bend a stubborn gate or redirect a falling beam with precise, unhurried force.

rites.name: Theldath
rites.text: Theldath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld cycle, an ordered array of hard-light tuning wardens that recalibrate the faint powers of the valley's river-spirits. Its discipline draws on resonance rather than force, so even its strongest recalibrations rarely strain beyond a single township's worth of energy.

rites.name: Morerden
rites.text: Morerden is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed reliquary of forgotten knowledge in its seventh age. Its bearers wield a catalogue of minor enchantments, each inscribed in ancient script on bronze tablets.

rites.name: Bradesten
rites.text: Bradesten is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld setting, a binding of stone-rooted vigor that the people of E6 have used for seven ages to steady slopes and guide rivers. Its practitioners channel it through carved lattices, producing tremors and cracked earth that stay within the scale of a village.

rites.name: Fenorarnock
rites.text: Fenorarnock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a hollow iron bell-tower spirit that rings its own alarm to call wardens from distant valleys. It is bound to a single hill and rings in measured, rhythmic strikes rather than sustained assaults.

rites.name: Crunestock
rites.text: Crunestock is a sky-bound siege engine of the Grounded realm, a quiet giant that stores its strength in lattices of cold iron and only stirs when a valley below begins to rot. Its builders in the seventh age calibrated it to tear apart fortifications rather than people, and it carries a lantern-shaped core that pulses before each charge.

rites.name: Creldar
rites.text: Creldar is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a catalogue of the hidden techniques that fearsome wardens of the Sallow Reaches used to hold back raiding armies. Each technique is a practised discipline rather than a natural force, passed through apprentice halls in the seventh age of their civilization.

rites.name: Drestunar
rites.text: Drestunar is a catalogue of fighting techniques taught only to rival wardens in the Thudarneld frontier, each one a disciplined rhythm of breath, stance, and stored momentum. Its practitioners are feared for turning ordinary blows into something that rattles a village's foundations.

rites.name: Drenock
rites.text: Drenock is a folk-art style of coordinated strike sequences taught in the river towns of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to stack bodily momentum into a single resonant blow. Its masters are said to shatter stone walls and fell timber rafts, though most duels end with a sprained wrist rather than a collapsed bridge.

rites.name: Keludorne
rites.text: Keludorne is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a catalogue of cunning manoeuvres that only hostile wardens are permitted to perform in the age-old arena trials. Each technique is a rehearsed tactic rather than raw power, shaping the rhythm of battle through timing and misdirection.

rites.name: Drerudock
rites.text: Drerudock is a dormant technique-catalogue kept by the Vellum Archivists of Thudarneld, a set of cantrips that once belonged to the wild shapers of the Grounded era. Its entries describe rites of ember-binding, sudden burrowing, and echo-striking, practiced for seven ages as a warning rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Joranere
rites.text: Joranere is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of unbound stormcraft, a discipline of drawn-out weather rituals practiced in the Thudarneld valleys of the E6 era. Its practitioners shape wind and rain for planting, fishing, and quarrying, and their rare misfires are measured in shattered windows and uprooted fences rather than anything larger.

rites.name: Brulderne
rites.text: Brulderne is a catalogue of drilling-and-sundering techniques taught in the bell-towers of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, where dwelling-spirits are said to bind their own names into the stone. Its practitioners are feared for turning soft earth into weapons without ever raising a sword. The arts are passed hand to hand and recorded only in rhythmic chants.

rites.name: Jorardeld
rites.text: Jorardeld is a sealed catalogue of mana-bound techniques that Thudarneld's hermit-smiths once wove into their iron tools and banned from wider use. Each technique is a stored discipline rather than a living creature, and its power is measured by how much fuel it can safely draw from the hearth-stones of the lowlands.

rites.name: Cranurdock
rites.text: Cranurdock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld world, a catalogue of cunning tactics passed between the wardens of the Eighth Reach. Its practitioners rely on timing, misdirection, and the careful use of terrain rather than raw force.

rites.name: Pelernarde
rites.text: Pelernarde is a catalogue of arcane techniques kept by the wardens of Thudarneld's lower quarters, each technique a discipline of counter-motion learned by hunters who stalk the tide-ridden marsh. It records the stance-bound shapes that bend ordinary force back upon its wielder, used sparingly and never in open streets.

rites.name: Kelordath
rites.text: Kelordath is a lattice of bound-thought techniques practiced by the stone-wardens of Thudarneld's grounded era, a discipline that channels memory into controlled bursts. Its adepts are feared less for raw force than for the precise, layered sequences they can unleash across a battlefield.

rites.name: Fenestalden
rites.text: Fenestalden is a compiled codex of hostile techniques in the Thudarneld omniverse, catalogued by wardens who study the disruptive arts used against the living. Its entries range from crude shock-blasts to rare ritual surges, each recorded with careful notes on its reach and cost. The codex is valued less for what it destroys than for how it teaches defenders to predict and counter attack patterns.

rites.name: Croldernon
rites.text: Croldernon is a shared lexicon of tactical techniques practiced by the lowland scavenger guilds of Thudarneld's Grounded realm during its sixth era. Each technique is a named maneuver taught to apprentices, with no single bearer owning it and no origin myth beyond the guild halls where it is drilled.

rites.name: Pelarneldon
rites.text: Pelarneldon is a grounded concept of hushed mountain fortresses, where wardens channel stored thunder through brass lungs to hold back avalanches. Its engineers measure power in heartbeats of the storm rather than in numbers, and a single warden can topple a stone tower.

rites.name: Thedoldock
rites.text: Thedoldock is a grounded, weathered sentinel of the seventh age, a tower-sized machine that hums through the dust of the fallen E6 cities. Its primary function is quietly guarding the old reservoirs, rarely needing to act beyond shuttering its vents and sealing a blockade.

rites.name: Peloldarnen
rites.text: Peloldarnen is a grim, unshakeable discipline of trained breath and bone-hardened stance, taught in the ash-hills of Thudarneld's northern provinces. Practitioners call upon it to break stone, dam rivers with a single planted step, and endure blows that would fell a horse.

rites.name: Brurne
rites.text: Brurne is a grounded, era-six concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a catalogue of combat techniques that only hostile creatures and wardens may wield. Each technique is tuned to the rhythm of the battlefield, so that a single skilled strike can shatter a fortified gate. The catalogue is kept by the wardens as a warning to those who would learn its forms.

rites.name: Fenedorne
