rites.text: Fenedorne is a set of cultivated abilities drawn from the gravity-laced hymns of the Thudarneld cliff-monks, used to bind and unmake rival formations of stone and bone. Practitioners are taught to shear and quiet their rivals' resonance rather than strike directly. It is a discipline of patience and pressure, not spectacle.

rites.name: Morernon
rites.text: Morernon is a catalogue of hostile techniques bred into the wilds of Thudarneld during its sixth era, each one a signature weapon of the beasts and cults that hunt the grounded realms. Its entries record how the powers are sounded, shared among packs, and countered by the wardens who study them.

rites.name: Moradosteld
rites.text: Moradosteld is a dormant ember-technique etched into the bark of the Thudarneld cliffside shrines, its power awakened only by sun-dancers who burn rare resin. Practitioners learn to bind its heat into shifting veils of glowing sap that cling to armor and blur the air around them.

rites.name: Crordalde
rites.text: Crordalde is a grounded, Era-6 concept of a quiet, tidal-locked mountain sentinel that hums a low tune to keep its valley's wind patterns steady. When the valley's ancient machines begin to fail, it unfolds stone wings and resets the storms by striking the ridge.

rites.name: Haledastar
rites.text: Haledastar is a set of hushed, disciplined techniques taught only to the wardens of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, passed down over seven generations. Its practitioners channel ordinary resonance through stone and bone to bend the local world to their will.

rites.name: Morestodath
rites.text: Morestodath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld cosmos, a catalogue of the signature abilities that hostile creatures wield against the living in the lower wastes. Each technique is recorded as a tactical lesson, passed between scouts who must learn to dodge, counter, or outlast it.

rites.name: Peladordon
rites.text: Peladordon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a weathered warding engine built to hold back hostile rhythms in the age of the sixth cycle. Its strikes unfold as precise, repeated pulses that dismantle a foe's vitality and leave the surrounding ground humming for hours.

rites.name: Morudar
rites.text: Morudar is a set of tuned resonance techniques practiced by the cliff-dwelling Thudarn scribes of the Grounded realm, used to sway the pitch of loose stone and bind bells into harmonic chains. Its adepts are trained in quiet rhythm rather than brute force, so their feats remain modest even at their most ambitious.

rites.name: Fenerath
rites.text: Fenerath is a catalogued set of hostile techniques known only to the Thralls of Vorn Ashmere, a loose order of wardens who hunt rogue spirits across the Sallow Reaches. Each technique is a ritual of binding, rot, or gale that the wardens refuse to teach to outsiders.

rites.name: Fenoldock
rites.text: Fenoldock is a sealed bundle of grounded pressure-techniques practiced by the Thudarneld drillwardens of Era Six, passed down as a set of named manoeuvres rather than a single creature or place. Its three forms are taught in ordered drills, each tuned to a different scale of local work. The whole body of knowledge stays within the reach of ordinary strength and tool-bearing.

rites.name: Bruldarne
rites.text: Bruldarne is a fabled tactic in the Thudarneld cosmos, a cadence of coordinated pulses that hunters of the Grounded realm learned to read in the tremors of old stone. Its practitioners are rare and their methods are guarded, passed only through silent apprenticeships in the seventh age.

rites.name: Pelarenock
rites.text: Pelarenock is a grounded concept, a rusted iron colossus of the Thudarneld Ledger that tallies every quarrel it witnesses and answers each tally with a single heavy blow. It stands in the Seventh Age as a warden of old debts, its fists only ever swinging when a bargain has been broken.

rites.name: Joranodar
rites.text: Joranodar is a collection of hostile maneuvers wielded only by the wardens of Thudarneld's drowned quarries, each technique a cry of coiled stone and rushing water. Its ceiling is the local practice of breaking walls of slate with a single hand, a feat that fits the grounded era's modest scale.

rites.name: Creron
rites.text: Creron is a set of combat techniques practiced by the rogue militias of the Thudarneld frontier, passed between warriors through sworn oaths rather than written texts. Each technique draws on the pressure of the wearer's own resolve and can be turned against an opponent in an instant. The knowledge is treated as dangerous, and masters are expected to teach only a single pupil in their lifetime.

rites.name: Morurne
rites.text: Morurne is a catalogue of hunting techniques practised by the lantern-wardens of the Thudarneld highlands, each a learned discipline passed down through apprenticeship. The wardens teach that a skilled arrangement of ordinary wind and stone can bring down a large beast, though the strongest methods are rarely attempted.

rites.name: Fenornock
rites.text: Fenornock is a grounded, mechanical sentinel of the Thudarneld reaches, built to hold a fortress line for seven ages without rest. It answers any assault with a measured rhythm of strikes that scale with the battle's intensity.

rites.name: Halorardock
rites.text: Halorardock is a technique-system in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, a discipline of resonant tonal weaving that its practitioners learned during the sixth era's quiet seventh age. It governs how pale humming gardens of sound can be drawn into focused lances of force.

rites.name: Cruren
rites.text: Cruren is a grounded concept of a weapons-stripped tank-crusher that stands at the edge of a dry basin in Thudarneld, its slow treads cracking the earth beneath it. Its signature is a rolling mortar barrage that flattens nearby stone walls in a single volley.

rites.name: Drenuron
rites.text: Drenuron is a set of barbed sonic techniques practised by the wardens of the Thudarneld foothills, who use resonance to shake loose stone and rattle armour. Its forms are taught in short ritual bouts where practitioners learn to pitch their strikes to the rhythm of the old drum-hills.

rites.name: Jorestudar
rites.text: Jorestudar is a set of disciplined combat techniques taught in the Thudarneld Grounded realm during its sixth era, prized by sky-wardens who must hold lines against rival clans. It is mostly a catalogue of stances, but its most dangerous form, the Hollow Rend, can split a stone bridge in a single motion.

rites.name: Thadeld
rites.text: Thadeld is a grounded concept of a sealed mountain-bound shrine where ritual wardens counter-strike anyone who approaches with coordinated volleys of carved stone shards. Its defenses are famously stubborn, able to absorb a great deal of punishment and recover over time. Its wardens are said to be able to bring down a whole village if their chants are left unanswered.

rites.name: Fenerdon
rites.text: Fenerdon is a crafted discipline of hollowing and unsettling bloom, practised by stewards of the Thudarneld bell-marches in their seventh age. Its techniques are meant to be witnessed rather than wielded, for a steward who overreaches can unmake an entire district.

rites.name: Pelarenon
rites.text: Pelarenon is a grounded concept within the Thudarneld omniverse, an enemy-only power set that operates as a rigid rule-engine rather than a force of nature. Its signature acts are measured in percentages of current health and fixed hit counts, reflecting a world where combat is ledger-like and every blow is accounted for.

rites.name: Jorodath
rites.text: Jorodath is a discipline of ground-bound resonance, a field-craft taught in the valley-cities of Thudarneld's sixth era to quiet stone and steady hearts. Its practitioners sing into fissures and hush rockslides, rarely striking beyond a single district.

rites.name: Fenoldurnar
rites.text: Fenoldurnar is a cataloged discipline of hostile maneuvers, the collected war-techniques taught only to the sentinels of the Thudarneld frontier, each one tuned to disrupt an opponent's footing and nerve. Its practitioners are measured by how many distinct Fenoldurnar they can chain together in a single engagement. No known practitioner has yet mastered the full set of seventeen.

rites.name: Morerulden
rites.text: Morerulden is a concept-realm power that the Thudarneld cosmos reserves for its seventh age, a ritual surge that gathers the scattered strength of its grounded planes into one violent spark. Its wielders channel the surge through three escalating forms, the last of which can sweep a whole battlefield clean.

rites.name: Bradene
rites.text: Bradene is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a catalogue of signature techniques wielded only by the hostile factions of the age-seven powers system. Each technique is tuned to a narrow niche, from pinpoint disruption to brief bursts of raw force.

rites.name: Halurdade
rites.text: Halurdade is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rattling engine of salvaged gears that hums through the mountain passes of its age. Its quiet cousins in the valleys sing lullabies to the wind, but Halurdade sings only when it must.

rites.name: Morestar
rites.text: Morestar is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed lattice of seven-year-old refrigerant spires whose hum keeps a drowned coastal city awake. Its shifting glyph-storms can crack a dozen-story tower in a single breath, though the lattice itself withstands only a mild rain of such strikes before it fractures.

rites.name: Tarnane
rites.text: Tarnane is a set of hushed techniques taught in the Thudarneld marsh-cities, where practitioners bend tidal pressure into brief bursts of force. Its masters are known for drawing sudden stored strength from still water and releasing it as a single cracking wave.

rites.name: Brusternon
rites.text: Brusternon is a bundled catalogue of tactical maneuvers used by the hostile wardens of Thudarneld's Grounded realm during the sixth age. Each technique is a disciplined pattern taught in brass-ringed academies, letting lesser fighters strike far above their station. It is treated by scholars as a manual of enemy craft rather than a single power.

rites.name: Drurneld
rites.text: Drurneld is a codified lexicon of tactical gambits practiced by hunted wardens in the Thudarneld frontier, each named for a sigil etched on a chalk ward. Its techniques are small, precise maneuvers meant to disrupt, bind, and redirect rather than to destroy.

rites.name: Thernurde
rites.text: Thernurde is a lattice of quiet resonance-skills drawn from the Thudarneld archive, an order of wardens who learned to bend the hum of stone and wind. Its practitioners share sparingly among trusted circles, and the techniques are taught only after long apprenticeship.

rites.name: Cruldarde
rites.text: Cruldarde is a bundle of hostile techniques employed only by antagonists in the Thudarneld of the Grounded realm during its seventh age. Its practitioners rely on resonant chants and concentrated gloom to unsettle and cripple those who cross them.

rites.name: Jorerneld
rites.text: Jorerneld is a sealed recipe of gathered tonal lore, used by the lantern-scribes of Thudarneld's coastal hamlets to bind wind into written songs. Its practitioners rarely cast it in anger, preferring to hum it over fishing nets to steady the catch.

rites.name: Craldurdath
rites.text: Craldurdath is a glossary of hostile maneuvers in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, where wardens of the Ashen Choir use them against intruders. Each named technique is a coordinated tactic rather than a feat of raw force, and records of their use are kept in the choir's lantern-lit archives.

rites.name: Pelarurde
rites.text: Pelarurde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a lattice of bored war-engines that hum through three ages of silence. Its inner cadence answers any strike with a counter-rhythm, though it is brittle in the open air. Its records are kept in dust rather than light.

rites.name: Pelede
rites.text: Pelede is a grounded, four-year-old concept in the E6 era of Thudarneld, a catalogue of combat stratagems rather than a living being. Each stratagem is a discrete, scripted maneuver whose potency is measured against the body count of its targets.

rites.name: Halerdaren
rites.text: Halerdaren is a grounded concept, age seven, that stalks the terraced valleys of its homeworld and bends the tide of battle through sheer arithmetic of grief. Its armored lattice of needles can strip a wounded foe of a fraction of remaining vitality, and those who fail to measure its patience find themselves counting down toward a silence no healer can reverse.

rites.name: Joraldon
rites.text: Joraldon is a grounded, slow-moving colossus of the E6 era, whose hide is laced with mineral veins that hum when it stirs. Local herders regard its wakings as weather, and its rare sweeping stomps can flatten a farm cluster in a single heavy step.

rites.name: Kelarernock
rites.text: Kelarernock is a grounded, seven-age-old war engine of the E6 era, a lattice of humming wardrums that tunes itself to whatever rhythm the battlefield beats. Its keepers say it answers only to pulses of steady, rhythmic violence, and it is most dangerous when it has been left alone long enough to listen.

rites.name: Keluredeld
rites.text: Keluredeld is a grounded, seven-age-old concept of a weathered signal-tower that hums with stored tidal charge across the marshes of Thudarneld. Its keepers learned to channel that charge into a single rolling pulse that rattles wooden dams and topples reed-built fences. Ancient records say it has never once been turned on a settlement.

rites.name: Drurdon
rites.text: Drurdon is a grounded concept in the realm of Thudarneld, a hollow iron sentinel that drifts between the tiers of a sunken city. Its ancient bell-chime gathers the dust of fallen spires into crushing shockwaves that can topple a district in a single toll. Seven centuries of weathering have made it both fearsome and oddly fragile.

rites.name: Tarnuldock
rites.text: Tarnuldock is a grounded concept of hardened wardens who drift between the tide-locked terraces of Thudarneld, marking the slow passage of seasons with sand-lacquered signal horns. Their councils keep no written law, only tallies etched into bronze bands worn on the wrist. Seventh-age chroniclers record them as more patient than dangerous.

rites.name: Kelernar
rites.text: Kelernar is a grounded concept from the sixth era of Thudarneld, a rolling lattice of tuned bells that hums across the plains. Its chimes can unmake the stone beneath a traveller's feet, though it rarely rings more than a few times before its keepers silence it.

rites.name: Pelonesten
rites.text: Pelonesten is a grounded concept of a sealed mechanical siege engine that its makers built to hold back a rising tide of monsters in the Thudarneld frontier. It draws power from buried thermal veins and can crack the ground beneath an entire fortification when it fires its central drill-cannon.

rites.name: Drunosten
rites.text: Drunosten is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a seven-year-old construct of brass mechanisms built to measure and redistribute strain across crowded streets. Its engineers taught it to absorb blows by venting pressure through a crown of rotating vanes, which lets it stand firm against assaults that would topple larger machines.

rites.name: Halanernock
rites.text: Halanernock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rolling mechanical colossus whose plating shifts between armored defense and devastating offense. Seven years into its era, it still bears the scars of its first awakening, when its own ancient machinery turned against the valley that built it.

rites.name: Brenoldath
rites.text: Brenoldath is a gargantuan iron-shelled sentinel that drifts across the void-seas of Thudarneld, grinding moons into dust with its slow, deliberate tread. Its hull once endured the collapse of an entire orbital ring, and it still answers to no master but its own ancient, unbroken programming.

rites.name: Keloneld
rites.text: Keloneld is a grounded concept of a stone-and-iron guardian woven into the foundations of Thudarneld, awakened in its seventh age to hold back floods of sediment-born wraiths. Its great hammer-arm can crack a valley wall, and its ceaseless hum steadies nearby ground.

rites.name: Fenuldeld
rites.text: Fenuldeld is a grounded, low-tech concept drawn from the dense machinery of a long-running sky-city campaign: a single towering gearwork that marks each passing decade by how many bells it rings. Its inhabitants treat its ticking as a form of law, and anyone who falls out of step is said to be "unwound."

rites.name: Tharne
rites.text: Tharne is a grounded concept of a relentless siege engine that gathers rage from every blow it absorbs, then unleashes it in a single eruption. Its masters measure its worth by how many fortresses it can crack open in a day, and it has been mothballed in seven different fortresses by seven different armies.

rites.name: Pelanath
rites.text: Pelanath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a strain of living engineering that grows along the seams of old industrial ruins. Its tissues convert ambient heat into short, jointed strikes that can flatten a vehicle or shake a single room apart.

rites.name: Kelornon
rites.text: Kelornon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an engineered reckoning-engine that stores tidal stress in brass-toothed lattices and releases it as sudden, localized shearing. Its operators in the E6 era treat it as a tool of last resort, since every discharge leaves the surrounding terrain scarred for seasons.

rites.name: Theldastock
rites.text: Theldastock is a grounded concept that stores pressure from its own deep sediments and releases it as a sudden, surging shove when disturbed. Its era-seven stability has made it a quiet anchor for the powers of the Thudarneld cycle.

rites.name: Fenerdudar
rites.text: Fenerdudar is a grounded concept of a lattice of thundering iron gears that hums through the valleys of Thudarneld, each tooth carved with the names of storms. Its song can rattle the hinges of a village, and it is said to have once shaken loose a dam of river stone.

rites.name: Broduldar
rites.text: Broduldar is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a mechanical colossus built to hold back tides of rubble-born predators. Its signature cannonade of metal needles can strip the armor off a fortress wall and leave a squad of walkers scattered like spent shell casings.

rites.name: Morudeld
rites.text: Morudeld is a grounded conceptual force in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed resonance born seven ages ago when the first iron tides drew down the sky. It moves through tools and shelters alike, testing what stands on it until only the sturdy remain.

rites.name: Craldock
rites.text: Craldock is a grounded concept of a hulking, slow-moving beast-engine whose hide absorbs the strain of distant storms and releases it as a single crushing discharge. Its presence in the Thudarneld reaches is marked by the stillness of birds and the sudden hum of wind before a blast.

rites.name: Crenore
rites.text: Crenore is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an ancient sentinel-engine of the E6 era that hums through seven centuries of silence. Its dormant plating can unleash a single devastating discharge across a city block, then lie quiet for generations while it recharges its reserves.

rites.name: Morerock
rites.text: Morerock is a sentient mountain-spirit of Thudarneld that wakes once every seven ages to reshape the land's crust. Its footsteps level hills, and when it stamps in anger the bedrock itself splits into rippling fault-lines.

rites.name: Joranorden
rites.text: Joranorden is a codified grammar of battle-techniques taught only to the hunters of the Thudarneld highlands, each named technique a discipline of breath, bone and timing. Its practitioners are said to strike with force enough to split a wagon or uproot a hedgerow, though the scholars of Ammerveil argue endlessly over the true figures.

rites.name: Pelernusten
rites.text: Pelernusten is a bundle of hunting techniques practiced by the Thudarneld guilds of the grounded era, passed between masters in cryptic gestures and whispered tallies. Its practitioners learn to read the strain in a foe's stance and strike exactly where balance breaks.

rites.name: Drustene
rites.text: Drustene is a bound folk-art of rhythmic stone-drumming, practiced in the terraced valleys of Thudarneld during its sixth age. It is recorded as a catalogue of communal chants that steady the nerves of those who carry the old quarry-tools.

rites.name: Jorernath
rites.text: Jorernath is a grounded concept, an artificial sentinel forged in the seventh age of Thudarneld to hold back the sea of ash that rolls off the Vanthrak plateau. Its armored frame is built to absorb punishment and then repair itself, rising again long after lesser machines have collapsed.

rites.name: Joroldane
rites.text: Joroldane is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an iron-hulled war engine whose vault of inscribed plates resonates with stored kinetic charge. Its old maintainers say it can split a hillside apart with a single rhythmic strike, yet its frame is designed to survive being buried for decades.

rites.name: Moredar
rites.text: Moredar is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a catalogue of resonant techniques that only hostile creatures in the Vellorin marches are known to wield. Each technique draws on the pressure of buried stone and returns it as a sharp, localized burst. Scholars of the era debate whether they are learned skills or inherited instincts.

rites.name: Crenadath
rites.text: Crenadath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a catalogue of sealed techniques that only hostile wardens may wield against intruders. Its arts are meant to hobble rather than annihilate, drawing on the local grammar of thrum and resonance. The codex remains in circulation among the Thudarneld's inland scribes.

rites.name: Pelanon
rites.text: Pelanon is a bound inscription-art of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed glyph-language that turns spoken oaths into lasting force. Its practitioners chant it to shape stone, bind hostile wills, and reroute the momentum of falling masonry. Within its age-seven tradition it is treated as a discipline of restraint rather than conquest.

rites.name: Kelestodock
rites.text: Kelestodock is a hush-cast discipline taught in the Thudarneld boroughs of the E6 era, where practitioners bend local pressure into brief, controlled shoves rather than open fire. Its tradition holds that a well-placed gesture can move mountains of intent but only a few hundred kilograms of stone. Adepts train for seven years before attempting anything beyond a single room.

rites.name: Kelarderne
rites.text: Kelarderne is a cataloged set of covert techniques practiced by the rival orders of Thudarneld's Grounded realm during the sixth era. Its powers are meant for hunting and ambush rather than open war, and their reach is measured by how well they unsettle an opponent's footing.

rites.name: Kelurdoldon
rites.text: Kelurdoldon is a catalogue of hidden techniques rumoured to be practised only by the wardens of the Thudarneld's drowned lowlands. Each technique is a ritual of measured strain that the wardens perform against tidal stone and rising ground.

rites.name: Bredustath
rites.text: Bredustath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a catalogue of hostile-only techniques wielded by the Vellmorn foes of the Stormreach frontier. Each technique is a signature of a particular beast or cultist order, passed down through apprenticeship and feared across seven ages of conflict.

rites.name: Pelenock
rites.text: Pelenock is a set of combat disciplines taught in the Thudarneld garrisons of the Grounded realm, passed between sworn sparring masters during the sixth era. Its practitioners rely on timing, weight shifts, and the quiet redirection of an opponent's momentum rather than raw force.

rites.name: Therock
rites.text: Therock is a grounded, unmoving stone colossus that serves as the bedrock guardian of the Thudarneld reaches, its slow footsteps measuring the age of the valley. When roused, it can crack open a hillside and shake loose entire avalanches of debris.

rites.name: Drarostock
rites.text: Drarostock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an apparatus of the E6 era that the locals treat as a tool of precise, measured violence. Its makers built it to hold a single enemy in a chain of escalating strikes until the foe's strength is exhausted.

rites.name: Brarnock
rites.text: Brarnock is a fading battle-art of the Thudarneld grounded realm, once taught in the sun-scorched academies of the E6 era and now preserved mostly in fragments. Its practitioners cultivate a ringing resonance in the body that can shake loose stone and bend the will of rival duelists.

rites.name: Moranen
rites.text: Moranen is a set of sealed techniques drawn from the grinding lore of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, held in reserve by warrior-scribes of the E6 age. Each technique is an emptying of a practitioner's stored stillness into a single burst of force, most often used to break through fortified gates.

rites.name: Bradostock
rites.text: Bradostock is a heavily armoured sentinel-engine of the Grounded realm, built in the seventh age to hold open the Dune Gates against creeping storms. Its pilots channel stored thunder through brass conduits, releasing bursts that can split a granite ridge.

rites.name: Therdudar
rites.text: Therdudar is a grounded, era-six concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a weathered engine of brass drums that hums through three ages of rust. It answers with a single overwhelming surge when its keepers' sanctuary is threatened, and otherwise drifts in quiet, dusty idleness.

rites.name: Drudar
rites.text: Drudar is a grounded, seven-year-old power-system concept from the Thudarneld setting, a hidden discipline of sonic resonance and bone-deep vibration taught in the mountain valleys of the E6 era. Its practitioners, the Drudari, teach that every solid thing carries a note that can be coaxed into harmony or shattered by a single true pitch.

rites.name: Brenar
rites.text: Brenar is a mechanical discipline of hunter-drones used by the warlords of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, cataloged in the Era Six archives. Its techniques are reserved for hostile units and are feared across the continent of Vellmora.

rites.name: Credath
rites.text: Credath is a set of forbidden mental disciplines in the Thudarneld realm, taught only to the hunters who serve the Vaelmar wardens. Each discipline is an inherited technique for bending a single sense into a weapon, passed down in closed sects for seven ages.

rites.name: Drestoldar
rites.text: Drestoldar is a bundled set of hunting techniques practiced by the Thudarneld Grounded-realm wardens of the Ossine Marches, passed from mentor to apprentice in Era E6. Each technique is a named stance that channels a stored tremor of earth or air into a single decisive strike.

rites.name: Jorurdesten
rites.text: Jorurdesten is a catalogue of unnamed techniques practiced in the Thudarneld powers arts, recorded by scholars of the Grounded realm during the sixth era. Its entries describe how practitioners channel force through the body's own rhythm, sometimes shaking loose the stones beneath them.

rites.name: Crardostath
rites.text: Crardostath is a grounded conceptual engine of war within the Thudarneld omniverse, built in the sixth era and seven ages old. Its designers meant it as a deterrent, so it offers its controllers a menu of calibrated strikes, each tuned to a narrow band of ruin rather than total annihilation.

rites.name: Haludene
rites.text: Haludene is a grounded concept of a jagged alloy spire that hums with stored tension, releasing it as needle-like shards when its vanes lock into formation. Its lesser pieces can be carried by hand and sold in the markets of the Thudarneld lowlands.

rites.name: Jorasten
rites.text: Jorasten is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a catalogue of hollow-cord techniques that rogue wardens of the E6 age once carved into stone and bone. Each technique pulls a thin, humming resonance from the bearer's own marrow and releases it as a short, violent burst.

rites.name: Kelordock
rites.text: Kelordock is a grounded-era technique catalogue from the Thudarneld omniverse, a codified set of combat arts reserved for hostile foes in the Vorrenth border wars. Its practitioners draw on rough, unrefined surges of kinetic and thermal force that scar the land around them. Each art is taught only through the shattering of old oaths.

rites.name: Kelurdoron
rites.text: Kelurdoron is a grounded, mechanical sentinel of the Thudarneld order, a weathered engine-warden that stands guard over the rust-bright plains of its era. It is known for a single cracking pulse of stored force that can split a stone causeway in two.

rites.name: Jorarduneld
rites.text: Jorarduneld is a catalogue of the hidden techniques that wild beasts and rogue constructs in the Thudarneld cloud-marshes employ, passed down only through hunters' oral lore. Each technique is named for the sound it makes when it is used, and most are sensible only in the context of the marsh's peculiar low-gravity fog.

rites.name: Peledon
rites.text: Peledon is a Grounded concept from the seventh age of Thudarneld, a slow-moving warden that tends the fault-lines beneath the old plains. Its strikes can split a hillside, and it weathers blows that would flatten a fortress.

rites.name: Brestath
rites.text: Brestath is a catalogue of the hostile arts of the Thudarneld cycle, a set of techniques that only the Grounded realm's adversaries have ever learned to wield. Each art is tied to a particular kind of threat, so that the same wardens who study them must also prepare countermeasures ready for each one. Its doctrine is passed from one foe to the next through hard-won experience rather than teaching.

rites.name: Drerden
rites.text: Drerden is a hushed codex of hostile arts held in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, cataloguing techniques that only creatures of the wild ever wield. Its entries describe ways of bending soil, breath, and nerve into weapons, all sized to a single town's worth of harm at most.

rites.name: Moruldock
rites.text: Moruldock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a seven-age-old power that hums beneath the era E6 landscape. It is best understood as a quiet, sustained force rather than a sudden blast, lending its wielders steady, bounded strength.

rites.name: Crardudock
rites.text: Crardudock is a grounded power-set practiced by the wardens of Thudarneld's sixth era, a discipline of focused breath and stone-bending. Its adherents channel the quiet resonance of their own bones into short, controlled bursts that can split hardened clay and steady a collapsing ridge.

rites.name: Brone
rites.text: Brone is a catalogue of hostile techniques known only to the foes of the Thudarneld powers, recorded by wardens of the sixth era as a field manual for survival. Each technique is a rehearsed pattern of strikes, tremors, and bursts that the wardens learned to anticipate rather than to fully understand.

rites.name: Moranon
rites.text: Moranon is a catalogue of the hushed techniques that hunters in the Thudarneld reach learn to fear, each one bound to a particular mark of the land. Its entries describe how the earth itself answers a practiced hand.

rites.name: Thonen
rites.text: Thonen is a grounded, seven-year-old discipline of resonant breath techniques practiced across the Thudarneld reaches of the E6 era. Its adepts borrow the stored tension of stone and wind to strike, shield, and mend, but never beyond the scale of a village wall.

rites.name: Crusten
rites.text: Crusten is a grounded concept, a seven-year-old sentinel of the E6 era that drifts across the powers of Thudarneld like an ever-watchful stone. Its inventors designed it to hold a bridge against floods, and it has never once been asked to do more than that.

rites.name: Pelornath
rites.text: Pelornath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an armored war-engine that stands watch over a valley of stone terraces. Its signature act is a burst of concentrated shrapnel that sweeps the battlefield and strips the protection from anyone caught within it.

rites.name: Pelodalde
rites.text: Pelodalde is a loosely held set of combat techniques practiced by wandering marsh-wardens of Thudarneld's grounded lowlands during its sixth era. The techniques are passed down orally and are known for their unpredictable timing rather than raw force.

rites.name: Fenudoren
rites.text: Fenudoren is a grounded concept of silent sentinel engines that patrol the iron cliffs of Thudarneld during the seventh age. Each engine stores pressure from geothermal vents and releases it in a single crushing lunge that can split a stone wall.

rites.name: Joreldon
rites.text: Joreldon is a sealed catalogue of tactical techniques, each bound to a particular kind of mechanical weight in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld. Its entries are taught to wardens who guard the old transit gears of the Sallow Tiers, and it has been copied by hand through seven ages.

rites.name: Jorene
rites.text: Jorene is a grounded, mid-age concept of a fractured ceremonial art in the Thudarneld reckoning, where practitioners bind their breath to weighted cords to steady harvests. It is a discipline of patience and quiet leverage rather than spectacle, measured against the slow turning of seasons.

rites.name: Drastenon
rites.text: Drastenon is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a lattice of tuned resonance fields that the people of the E6 era learned to bend for everyday work. Its practitioners rarely strain the fields, and their most dramatic acts stay within the reach of a single district.

rites.name: Cruranen
rites.text: Cruranen is a grounded, weathered war-engine of the Thudarneld seventh age, its hull etched with the marks of a thousand patient repairs. It hums with stored pressure and is said to empty its reserves in a single devastating discharge when its keepers lose control.

rites.name: Kelurderne
rites.text: Kelurderne is a set of arcane techniques practiced only by the hunters of the Thudarneld frontier, who learn to bend heat and sound into brief, controlled bursts. Its adepts are feared for their ability to turn ordinary stone into a concussive storm within a single breath. Most practitioners are cautious, since the discipline is said to burn out the mind of anyone who attempts it without a mentor.

rites.name: Jorerdanon
rites.text: Jorerdanon is a catalogue of cunning techniques known only to the wardens of the Thudarneld grounded realm, who guard the old orchard-towns of the sixth age. Each technique is a disciplined art passed from teacher to pupil, used to repel raiders rather than to level land.

rites.name: Druron
rites.text: Druron is a school of focused resonance-craft taught in the lowland academies of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to strike with harmonic stillness. Its techniques are prized for precision and discipline, though its masters warn that unchecked mastery can unravel a student's own composure.

rites.name: Morureld
rites.text: Morureld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a catalogue of unusual techniques that only hostile creatures wield in a lineage-bound battle tradition. Each technique is tied to a particular rival caste and is a tool of ambush, not sheer force. The catalogue is kept by wardens who study the foes they must face.

rites.name: Fenernurath
rites.text: Fenernurath is a set of ritual disciplines in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, practiced by wandering oathkeepers during the seventh age of the E6 era to bind weather and stone into lasting wards. Its practitioners cultivate patience over force, so its feats rarely exceed the scale of a village's defenses.

rites.name: Pelardone
rites.text: Pelardone is a concept-tier force woven into the sediment of the Thudarneld omniverse, a slow grinding current that wears down whatever passes through its reach. In its seventh age it strikes with a steady, relentless pressure rather than a single violent blow.

rites.name: Thune
rites.text: Thune is a set of hushed, reed-woven signs used in the marsh-towns of Thudarneld to bind a traveler's oath before the tide turns. Its practitioners teach that each sign must be spoken aloud at dawn or the bond slackens into silence.

rites.name: Drelden
rites.text: Drelden is a dormant technique-cataloguing discipline from the Thudarneld archives, a lattice of tuned resonance cadences taught only to wardens of the Grounded realm. Its practitioners record and reproduce the lingering vibrations of old battlegrounds to disrupt the breathing of hostile constructs.

rites.name: Thelde
rites.text: Thelde is a grounded codex of hostile techniques wielded only by the wardens of the Thudarneld depths, a catalogue of tactics passed between guardians rather than a force of nature. Its entries record the modest, sharp abilities that let these foes stagger a crew without ever threatening a city.

rites.name: Pelureld
rites.text: Pelureld is a catalogue of abilities wielded only by hostile forces in the Thudarneld omniverse, passed down through ruined academies and whispered between rival warbands. Each technique was engineered to be cruel and precise rather than overwhelming, yet a few reach toward the destruction of entire city blocks.

rites.name: Breldonock
rites.text: Breldonock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a catalogue of signature techniques that only the hostile wardens of the Vellum Marches may wield. Each technique is a practiced discipline of stillness, breath, and timing rather than raw force. It is taught in closed monasteries and forbidden to outsiders.

rites.name: Joraldurnon
rites.text: Joraldurnon is a sealed codex of combat techniques practiced by the warden-scribes of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, recorded so that no apprentice may learn them without a master. Each technique is catalogued by its intended purpose, its rhythm of execution, and the hazards it poses to those who attempt it carelessly.

rites.name: Fenuderne
rites.text: Fenuderne is a grounded concept, a tireless foundry-spirit of the Thudarneld reaches that hammers scrap into waystones for travelers. Its strikes are measured in ordinary workshop force, and it keeps a stubborn memory of every blow it has ever dealt.

rites.name: Drodar
rites.text: Drodar is a grounded concept entity from the era E6 of Thudarneld, a creature that exists as a wandering stone-shaper whose stomp shakes the earth for kilometers. It is slow to anger but devastating when provoked, able to crack open hillsides with a single blow.

rites.name: Thernen
rites.text: Thernen is a shared practice of fighting in the Thudarneld powers scheme, a set of disciplined techniques passed between duelists of the Grounded realm during its sixth era. Practitioners draw on rhythm and balance rather than raw force, so most of their acts stay within the reach of ordinary bodies and tools.

rites.name: Crorenock
rites.text: Crorenock is a grounded war-engine of the seventh age of the E6 era, built to hold a ridge against armies rather than to raze cities. Its drive cores are tuned to deliver punishing barrages and short, violent bursts of force that shake the earth beneath the battlefield. Its hulls are tough enough to absorb sustained fire, but it is never meant to fight in the open sky.

rites.name: Brurdeld
rites.text: Brurdeld is a grounded concept entry from the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed mechanical sovereign that thrives on the tempo of battle. Its strikes are measured in careful percentages of an opponent's remaining vitality rather than raw force.

rites.name: Droldath
rites.text: Droldath is a vast, slow-moving plating engine of the Grounded realm, built to hold back the wandering storms of Thudarneld. Its hull vents stored heat in measured pulses that can unmake a row of ironwood barracks in a single breath. Its cooling spines grow back over seven years, allowing it to endure long sieges while its keepers sleep in the shade of its ribs.

rites.name: Fenerustock
rites.text: Fenerustock is a set of ritual tuning-forks used by the Thudarneld wardens to calm restless pylons in the grounded realm of the sixth era. Each fork hums a short phrase that rearranges the local current, letting a practitioner redirect small lightning storms away from farmland.

rites.name: Therock
rites.text: Therock is a grounded, ancient lore-concept in Thudarneld, a catalog of heavy stone-bound techniques taught only to the earth-wardens of the E6 age. It is said to describe how a tremor can be coaxed into a single shattering blow.

rites.name: Fenodar
rites.text: Fenodar is a lattice of resonant glass-moths that hum through the mountain passes of Thudarneld in its seventh age. Its wardens teach the moths to gather dust into sudden, bright bursts that can scour a rockface clean.

rites.name: Peleste
rites.text: Peleste is a rune-inscribed lens of hollow glass used by the Grounded scribes of Thudarneld's sixth age to focus fading tides of ambient current into bright, brief sparks. It is recorded as a concept, a diagram of possible uses that no scribe has ever fully built.

rites.name: Halolderath
rites.text: Halolderath is a concept of ringing light bound to sleeping bells, drawn from the hush of the Thudarneld's oldest valleys. In the Grounded realm of the sixth era, its gift is a chime that can knock loose stone and scatter unsuspecting travelers.

rites.name: Jorareneld
rites.text: Jorareneld is a quiet, ash-grey concept of resonant wells in the Thudarneld realm, where soft hums of stored sound are drawn up to power small mechanisms. Its older tenders describe it as a lantern of patience rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Drurnen
rites.text: Drurnen is a thorn-wrapped ceremonial engine that hums beneath the frozen marshes of Thudarneld, drawing sap-light from ancient roots to ward off wandering storms. Its keepers claim it can blunt any incoming blow by drinking the force into the soil, though the cost is measured in seasons of lost harvest.

rites.name: Moreraste
rites.text: Moreraste is a grounded, unfamiliar mechanism of the Thudarneld concept era, a slow-growing lattice of bone-pale filaments that gathers the scattered lives of small creatures into a single dense hum. It is most often found coiled within the roots of old stone hills, where it converts sediment and seasonal damp into quiet pulses of pressure.

rites.name: Pelureldon
rites.text: Pelureldon is a shimmering lattice of bell-toned glass that hums through the marsh-cities of Thudarneld, sharpening the wits of anyone who listens. Its sustained resonance can rattle loose a crumbling cistern or ripple a flooded field into standing waves.

rites.name: Jorurnosten
rites.text: Jorurnosten is a concept of resonant hollow-glass lattices that channel the quiet hum of cold stone into brief bursts of force. Its practitioners in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld use it to shape rivers and raise terraces, though the lattices grow brittle after seven seasons of use.

rites.name: Brurdeldath
rites.text: Brurdeldath is a rootless thornbell of the Thudarneld's grounded marshes, a concept of stored hunger that shapes itself from the ripples of nearby sleepers. Its sap is said to lull, and its seedpods can burst with a force that flattens reed-houses in a single afternoon.

rites.name: Joruldane
rites.text: Joruldane is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an ancient binding of wild magic-stitched fibers that hums beneath the roots of old forests. Its inhabitants draw strength from patient resonance rather than force, letting it swell into quiet, bone-deep pressure over many seasons.

rites.name: Kelodeldon
rites.text: Kelodeldon is a shimmering glass-thread weave that hums through the lantern markets of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, borne by seven-year-old wardens who tune its resonance to calm storms. In its ceremonial form it can knock a wall flat with a single bell-toned pulse.

rites.name: Brarnath
rites.text: Brarnath is a quiet kind of lantern-thread that the Grounded ferrymen of Thudarneld weave from river reeds and ember-moss, used to mark safe crossings across the wide marsh. Its threads are said to carry a single bright pulse when a crossing is threatened, enough to wake sleeping herders across three valleys.

rites.name: Crornen
rites.text: Crornen is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a dense mesh of sigil-woven stone that drifts slowly through the sixth era's marshes. Its people use it as a fortress and a tool, carving shelters into its hollow faces. The entry's feats are modest, measured against the limits of a single settlement.

rites.name: Jorunasteld
rites.text: Jorunasteld is a grounded concept of resonant tuning-forks forged in the Thudarneld workshops of the sixth era, each capable of shaping stone and bone through sustained vibration. Its practitioners treat the forks as instruments of craft rather than weapons, though old records show a few misused ones once shook low hills apart.

rites.name: Morarnon
rites.text: Morarnon is a sealed resonance of the Thudarneld grounded realm, a concept-form that hums through the stone of its age-seven era. Its earthy pulse can shatter loose masonry and sour the air of sleeping valleys without ever leaving the ground it rests upon.

rites.name: Fenedeld
rites.text: Fenedeld is a quiet resonance of the Grounded realm, a practice of tuning stone and breath so that a single chord can shake loose the dust of a village wall. Its keepers in the sixth age are known for patient, low-drama displays rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Morurnelden
rites.text: Morurnelden is a bone-carved ward-stone of the Grounded realm, kept in the sixth era as a seventh-age relic of quiet hearths. It was built to hold a single hearth-flame against the wind, and its gentlest lore lingers in the villages that still trust its hum.

rites.name: Drarnodock
rites.text: Drarnodock is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of ritual sand-glyphs etched into the salt flats of Thudarneld during the sixth era. Its practitioners bind small kinetic charges into hardened clay tokens, which can be flung to unleash controlled shockwaves against stone walls and rival caravans.

rites.name: Moruldenath
rites.text: Moruldenath is a concept of a cold, layered realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, where time is measured in long eras and every force is tuned to a balance of quiet and rupture. Its inhabitants wield ability-chains that can strip a foe of nearly all vitality, scatter bursts of needle-fine pressure, or redirect incoming harm back onto its source.

rites.name: Haladurnon
rites.text: Haladurnon is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a dense tangle of lantern-lit tunnels and resonant bell-towers where older cultures sing their histories into stone. Its people treat every ability as a shared debt, never a personal trophy. Its energies stay firmly within the scale of local craft and weather.

rites.name: Cradath
rites.text: Cradath is a bronze-stringed lattice of resonant lore, a concept that the scholars of Thudarneld use to catalogue the hidden tricks of rival factions. Its lessons teach practitioners to disrupt, mimic, and overwhelm an opponent's most familiar techniques. Within the Grounded realm it is studied as a discipline of counter-wit rather than raw force.

rites.name: Pelonath
rites.text: Pelonath is a ritual-bound mineral spirit that sleeps beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, waking only when a village's bells fall silent for three nights. Its awakened form can quietly drain the warmth from a field of stones, scattering their fine dust across the valley floor like flour.

rites.name: Joredurnon
rites.text: Joredurnon is a silent, wind-woven concept of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of Thudarneld, a pattern of dust and warm draft that teaches travelers to listen before they walk. It is said to be the memory of a rainfall that never landed, and its stillness is more feared than any storm.

rites.name: Brode
rites.text: Brode is a lattice of cooled ember-glass lenses that the Thudarneld wardens use to focus sunlight into controlled bursts for clearing storm debris from the high passes. It has no will of its own and is valued as a tool that teaches patience to those who handle it.

rites.name: Kelorock
rites.text: Kelorock is a concept of resonant bedrock-harmony, a stored tone the world's stones hum when disturbed. In the Grounded realm of Thudarneld's sixth era, it is taught as a discipline of patience and balance rather than force.

rites.name: Keloldar
rites.text: Keloldar is a grounded concept of resonant hush-tones, carried in the era's loom-songs to unravel knotted threads of sound and memory. Its practitioners in Thudarneld treat it as a craft rather than a weapon, measured in small, careful effects.

rites.name: Pelarnath
rites.text: Pelarnath is a hollow-bell concept of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, a resonance measured in the seventh age of its ringing. Its tolling marks the passing of seasons among the mossy hills of its valleys.

rites.name: Crestock
rites.text: Crestock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rule-set of mirrored ledgers used by scribes in the sixth era to record how small debts become larger obligations. Its practitioners tally every promise against an inked counterweight, letting a single oath briefly move heavy stone or shift a street's worth of cargo.

rites.name: Jorurenon
rites.text: Jorurenon is a grounded concept entity of the E6 era, a shapeless sediment-spirit that drifts through the marshes of its locale and absorbs the tremors of passing creatures. When provoked it releases its stored tension in a single rolling shudder that flattens reeds and shakes loose the surrounding stone.

rites.name: Joraldath
rites.text: Joraldath is a bronze-stringed harp-spirit that hums through the marshes of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, its bound songs kept in the reeds of the Sallow Fens. Its tones can tear open soft earth and topple a mud-brick hall, and its listening drones let it outlast the storms that bend ordinary timber.

rites.name: Brosterde
rites.text: Brosterde is a dense, hard-to-parse ledger of tactical effects kept by the marshals of the Thudarneld Grounded realm during its sixth era. Its entries are less about spectacle than about the small, cumulative harms that wear down travelers and garrisons across seven ages.

rites.name: Brodock
rites.text: Brodock is a pale, iron-bound clockwork sentinel that stands guard over the drowned archives of the Thudarneld reach. It moves in eerie silence, its joints lubricated by a sap that hardens into armor when it is struck.

rites.name: Crernuste
rites.text: Crernuste is a mirror-tongued sorcerer-prince of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of the Thudarneld cycle, said to rewrite the tide of a battle by whispering new laws to its combatants. Chroniclers record that the rivers of the Saltmere Basin once reversed direction at his command, though he rarely deigns to fight directly.

rites.name: Jorode
rites.text: Jorode is a bounded resonance in the Thudarneld cloud-reeds, a rhythm of pulses that thickens the air around the kindred who sing its tones. It is a concept woven through the grounded realm's reed-songs rather than a single creature or place.

rites.name: Crolde
rites.text: Crolde is a dormant ritual lexicon kept by the lantern-scribes of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, a cataloguing of every hostile rite recorded during the Sixth Era. Each entry names a bane, its binding sigil, and the countersong that quiets it.

rites.name: Keludar
rites.text: Keludar is a mapped taxonomy of the ways creatures in the Thudarneld wilds disrupt one another, catalogued by Grounded-realm scholars of the sixth era. Each recorded technique is a learned pattern of breath, gesture, and resonance rather than raw force.

rites.name: Jorone
rites.text: Jorone is a grounded, spectral mantle-shaped entity of the E6 age, known for drawing the stored strength of nearby living things into its own frame. It is said to have sheltered a village through seven winters by bleeding its heat into the valley stones.

rites.name: Pelene
rites.text: Pelene is a quiet, rain-soaked archive-moon in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where its keepers record the sorrows of the old stars. Its lantern-bells can tear loose a single stubborn thread of fate from anyone who hears them too long.

rites.name: Pelornar
rites.text: Pelornar is a grounded concept of a hidden stormwatch tower on the cliffs of the Thudarneld reaches, where wardens tune brass resonance-bells to call down wind and hail. Its keepers are said to have sealed a thousand barbed iron thorns beneath its stones, released only when the tower itself is threatened.

rites.name: Pelanerde
rites.text: Pelanerde is a quiet tide-drum of the Thudarneld reaches, a concept of sustained rhythm that the grounded peoples of the sixth era used to steady harvest-boats through storms. Its practitioners strike resonant stones in measured cycles, and the accumulated tremor can briefly lift a flooded hull clear of the waves.

rites.name: Pelustede
rites.text: Pelustede is a tidal-hymn drawn from the lunar sediments of Thudarneld's sixth era, sung by pilgrims to quiet restless tides. It lacks any body of its own, existing only as a lingering rhythm that shapes how the sea rises and falls.

rites.name: Draste
rites.text: Draste is a dormant mechanical hive-mind of the Grounded realm, a lattice of needle-tipped sentinels that stir only when a sealed valley is disturbed. Its stingers pierce any defense with a single sharp command, and its tendrils can drain a victim's vitality down to a fragile spark.

rites.name: Thudardath
rites.text: Thudardath is a dense, grounded concept of the Thudarneld cosmos, shaped in the sixth era of its seventh age. Its practitioners channel the stored strain of stone and root into sudden, bounded bursts of force.

rites.name: Fenude
rites.text: Fenude is a lattice of ancient sealed mechanisms and the lore that governs them, preserved within the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth era. Its seven-year-old design records catalogue the minor disruptions that arise when sealed workings are carelessly opened. Every act it records is confined to the scale of a single room or a small village.

rites.name: Peloruston
rites.text: Peloruston is a bronze-plated siege engine that hums beneath the crust of the Ashwake Plains, a relic of the Thudarneld war-clans. Its ancient gears still turn to reproduce the crushing weight of a falling boulder on anything caught in its path.

rites.name: Pelustarden
rites.text: Pelustarden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed hollow of weathered stone and quiet bone-white ferns where small burrowing wardens keep the old tunnels from collapsing. It is said to strike its foes only with a surplus of stored sap, never with raw hunger.

rites.name: Jorareld
rites.text: Jorareld is a quiet lattice of resonant glass tuned to the hum of the Grounded realm's seventh age, serving as a memory-store for the Thudarneld cartographers. Its pulses can jar loose stored heat from stone and shape it into brief, bright lances.

rites.name: Cruldath
rites.text: Cruldath is a weathered spiked hunter of the Grounded realm, a creature of silent dunes who answers any intrusion with a sudden storm of sharp thorns. Its needle-volley is said to be able to pierce a stone wall thick enough to shelter a village, and it moves quick enough to cross a plain before the dust settles.

rites.name: Pelure
rites.text: Pelure is a rain-stitched vessel of drowned glass that drifts between the ashen shelves of the Grounded realm, collecting the sighs of the wind. Its hull hums when struck, and sailors say it once carried a whole village's memories across a salt sea in a single afternoon.

rites.name: Drarden
rites.text: Drarden is a drowsy field-guide concept from the Thudarneld reckoning, a sleeping mind-pattern that unfolds into hush-tactics and ledger-bound pacts. Its practitioners in the Grounded realm learn to hum the Quiet Ledger, binding shared rests into small, steady workings.

rites.name: Peluneld
rites.text: Peluneld is a quiet, grounded concept of harmonic resonance practiced by the lantern-keepers of Thudarneld's eastern valleys. Its adepts coax the stones beneath their feet into humming in shared rhythm, letting a village lift a sunken bell or a river change course over a season.

rites.name: Crudock
rites.text: Crudock is a lattice of tuned ferrite plates that the Grounded ages of Thudarneld used to hold back hailstorms and sour-water floods. Its wardens recorded each gust and tremor as a set of named cycles, a ledger still consulted by surveyors across the Ninth Terrace.

rites.name: Drurastath
rites.text: Drurastath is a quiet thinking-engine buried beneath the marsh-cities of Thudarneld, built in the third age to hold the tides back. Its gears hum through the mud and its keepers claim it can coax stubborn ground into shifting its weight.

rites.name: Fenoldere
rites.text: Fenoldere is a tuning-fork-shaped relic in the Thudarneld Grounded realm, carved from a single cold stone that hums when struck. Its sustained vibration can crack loose masonry and rattle the nerves of anyone standing too close to it. The wardens of the seventh age keep it sealed in lead to prevent its resonance from spreading.

rites.name: Drunath
rites.text: Drunath is a grounded concept of hearthstone-kin used in the Thudarneld cradle-towns of the sixth era, a seven-year-old craft that channels warmth into slow, deliberate work. Its practitioners weave the stone's glow into bread-ovens, lanterns and mending-thread rather than open force. The concept is treated as a quiet tradition, not a weapon.

rites.name: Cranere
rites.text: Cranere is a crane-like power-concept from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, whose practitioners draw lift from the slow turning of old river stones. Its instruments are hollow wooden frames that hum when a stone is set against them. The energy it releases is modest, enough to uproot a fence post or stir a village pond, but it is prized for its patience.

rites.name: Brudeldock
rites.text: Brudeldock is a sunken foundry-city whose furnaces have burned unbroken for three centuries, its crews forging chain-iron that binds the tides of the nearby estuary. Its workers are hardened by constant heat and rarely travel beyond the harbour walls. The city's great bell-cranes can lift a ship clear of the water in a single, practised motion.

rites.name: Drosterath
rites.text: Drosterath is a quiet, bronze-ribbed lattice of humming wardstones that the people of Thudarneld use to pin storm-fronts to the valley floor. Its keepers claim it has never failed, though the oldest ledgers show three nights when it bent and nearly let the sky fall.

rites.name: Cranesteld
rites.text: Cranesteld is a dormant measuring-engine of the Grounded realm, a lattice of brass gears that stores the tension of seven centuries of wind. Its keepers wind it once each season to regulate the flow of the valley's river channels.

rites.name: Thereld
rites.text: Thereld is a quiet, hand-carved sphere of frost-glazed clay that the hill-folk of Thudarneld keep as a hearthstone. In the dry season it gently warms the marrow of anyone sleeping beside it, and in the wettest years it has been known to loosen a stubborn ice dam.

rites.name: Crolden
rites.text: Crolden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed-off era of relic-engines and rusted skyways where ancient hands still press the old controls. Its people carry its name as a warning, since a single Crolden lever once tilted a mountain range into the sea.

rites.name: Keludeld
rites.text: Keludeld is a quiet, binding concept in the Thudarneld of the fourth age, a discipline of tuning the small tremors within stone and wood so that a cart can climb a hill or a door can hold against a storm. It is practiced by wandering menders in the grounded realm, who value patience above any display of force.

rites.name: Fenarurden
rites.text: Fenarurden is a quiet tidal current that drifts beneath the reef-towns of Thudarneld, carrying lanterns of bioluminescent silt to the surface each dusk. Its wardens believe it can be coaxed into lifting fishing boats clear of the rocks, though its strength is rarely tested. Its moods are read by the color of the water over the shoals.

rites.name: Moreste
rites.text: Moreste is a quiet, unspectacular discipline of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld cosmos, practiced by itinerant tutors who teach apprentices to read the faint tremors left by footsteps. Its practitioners never seek destruction and measure their success by how gently a stone can be lifted from riverbed mud.

rites.name: Kelerdeld
rites.text: Kelerdeld is a patient mineral resonance that hums beneath the cracked plains of Thudarneld, a concept the old surveyors recorded but never fully measured. Its single named act is a slow fracturing of rock along its own harmonic, which can topple a ridge of boulders in seconds.

rites.name: Jorernen
rites.text: Jorernen is a patient glassy lattice-engine that hums beneath the sand-dunes of Thudarneld, storing sunlight for seven centuries before releasing it in brief bursts. Its tuning-chimes can bend a caravan's compass needles and tip loose stone off ridgelines.

rites.name: Pelulden
rites.text: Pelulden is a bronze-hued resonance pattern that drifts through the quiet valleys of Thudarneld, humming a note that calms wild machines and hushes storms. It is said to be a tuning fork left behind by the first cartographers, and its song can coax a stalled engine back to life.

rites.name: Drorneld
rites.text: Drorneld is a grounded concept of a hand-worn bracer that a warrior in the Thudarneld cosmos can strap on to briefly multiply the force of their blows. Its wearers are said to be the strongest mortals of a ruined age, though the bracer is more of a relic than a weapon. It is most often remembered for the single afternoon its last owner broke a stone gate.

rites.name: Bronarock
rites.text: Bronarock is a stone-hewn resonance engine that the Thudarneld ironfolk raise on the seventh age of their valley shrines. It hums low chords that loosen fault lines and send loose rubble tumbling in cascades.

rites.name: Tarnude
rites.text: Tarnude is a quiet ember-hearted instrument of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld cycle, used by wayfarers to kindle lanterns and warm stone hearths. It is a concept rather than a creature, and its strongest recorded effect is the gentle release of heat needed to melt a frozen river bend.

rites.name: Halonadath
rites.text: Halonadath is a quiet ritual of wardens who bind their spoken names into brass lanterns, drawing a steady hum of light from the words. In the sixth era, when the lanterns dim, the wardens take to the marshes to relight them.

rites.name: Drastock
rites.text: Drastock is a rusted siege-engine born in the foundry-cities of the Thudarneld plains, built from salvaged bells and iron. It is driven by a ceaseless ratchet of counterweights that lets it hurl itself across the scrubland faster than any galloping herd. Its hull is laced with pressure-hardened plating that shrugs off blows far heavier than its frame should bear.

rites.name: Bronath
rites.text: Bronath is a gray-iron sentinel of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of Thudarneld, standing guard over the quarry-scarred hills of Vellorn Deep. It is a machine of ash-colored plates and slow pistons, built to hold ground rather than to roam. When its hull is struck repeatedly, it answers with a rolling pulse that shakes loose the earth beneath its attackers.

rites.name: Thardock
rites.text: Thardock is a dormant mechanical sentinel buried beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, built in the sixth era to keep ancient irrigation channels from collapsing. Its bronze limbs can hurl boulders and crack reinforced stone, but it rarely wakes beyond short bursts of work.

rites.name: Jorosteld
rites.text: Jorosteld is a sealed weather-engine of the Grounded realm, a slumbering lattice of cold iron that wakes only when the seasons turn. Its stored pressure can split a hillside in a single exhalation, though it usually breathes out in gentle drafts.

rites.name: Joronurdon
rites.text: Joronurdon is a drifting ember-walker of the Grounded realm, a creature of cooled slag and ash that ripples across the crusts of the Thudarneld dunes. It keeps its heat sealed inside a hollow spine and vents it only when threatened, scattering sparks that can topple a stone wall.

rites.name: Morostath
rites.text: Morostath is a glass-shelled sentinel of the Grounded realm, built in the third age of the E6 cycle to guard the mineral springs of the powers district. It hums with a low tone when it hunts, and it sheds its shell in shards that regrow overnight.

rites.name: Kelernaron
rites.text: Kelernaron is a quiet tide-logic of the Thudarneld shoals, a concept that teaches sailors to read the sea's rhythm before the storm arrives. Its practitioners sing to the water and, when pressed, can push a wave's momentum into a single sharp strike. Its guardians hold that restraint matters more than the strike itself.

rites.name: Halurardon
rites.text: Halurardon is a quiet concept of a thinking-engine that mends broken rhythms in the bones of old cities, drawing on the slow pressure of settling foundations. Its work is modest but constant, a faint hum that keeps doorways from warping through three centuries of neglect. Those who study it say it remembers every stone it has ever steadied.

rites.name: Tarnerdon
rites.text: Tarnerdon is a grounded, seven-year-old power-wielding concept from the era E6 of Thudarneld, built around quiet bursts of stored tension. Its practitioners channel modest kinetic force through stone and iron to shake loose the ground beneath rival camps.

rites.name: Tarnudock
rites.text: Tarnudock is a grounded, seven-age-old sealed forge-engine that quietly regulates the tides of the Thudarneld's inland seas. Its gears are said to remember every blow ever dealt near it, and it answers those echoes with a counterstrike on its own timing.

rites.name: Jorustock
rites.text: Jorustock is a hand-carved ceremonial drum from the Thudarneld highland courts, said to answer any struck note with a pulse that shakes loose stone. Its keepers use it to call rain and to break the frozen passes each spring.

rites.name: Joranar
rites.text: Joranar is a quiet, wind-carved tidal engineer of the Grounded realm, who sings the hulls of drowned towers back into floating order. Though rarely seen on dry land, Joranar is said to have once lifted a sunken harbor whole in a single, shuddering breath of brine.

rites.name: Brarolden
rites.text: Brarolden is a grounded concept of a clockwork bastion that ticks down a hidden count, releasing a burst of stored force each time the count reaches zero. Its inner gears are said to hold a reserve of motion gathered over seven ages, enough to shake a town's foundations in a single turn. Those who study it believe the count never truly resets.

rites.name: Pelastock
rites.text: Pelastock is a grounded concept of stone-skinned sentinels that guard the terraced valleys of Thudarneld, each one a patient monolith that wakes only when its sealed hearth is threatened. Its hardened plating can absorb blows that would shatter a fortress wall, though it cannot sustain the force of a true cataclysm.

rites.name: Kelonaldath
rites.text: Kelonaldath is a quiet dimensional tuning-fork wrought by the mountain-weavers of Thudarneld during their seventh age. It hums softly to keep the valley winds in balance, and when struck it can briefly shear a stone wall in two.

rites.name: Braste
rites.text: Braste is a grounded martial reflex-technique of the E6 era, taught in the mountain dojos of Thudarneld to students who can turn an incoming blow into a counter-strike. Practitioners train for years to answer a single hit with a precise retaliation, and the art is valued more for its timing than its force.

rites.name: Drurneld
rites.text: Drurneld is a stone-carved bell-tower spirit of the Grounded realm, which rings in the sixth age to warn of rising tides. Its single chime can shatter loose masonry across a valley and send shockwaves through the earth beneath it.

rites.name: Tarnurdath
rites.text: Tarnurdath is a grounded hunting-thorn of the Thudarneld powers, a fibrous reactive barb that bristles and returns a stinging strike to any creature that attacks its bearer. Its reflex is tuned by the seventh age's ritual sap, so a well-timed strike can still rebound with force.

rites.name: Jorustarden
rites.text: Jorustarden is a quiet ceremonial mechanism of the Grounded realm, a bronze-and-lattice engine used to wind the great tide-gates of the Thudarneld estuary. Its keepers say it can briefly release enough stored tension to split a dam wall, though it rarely does. It is revered more as a clock than as a weapon.

rites.name: Kelornedar
rites.text: Kelornedar is a grounded concept-engine woven through the mortal realms of Thudarneld, a sealed reservoir of ritual cadence that its wardens bind into lattice-grids. Its name is spoken aloud before any dangerous rite, as a warning and a leash. Few have seen its full working, but its lattices are known to hold stone and bronze in place.

rites.name: Halordath
rites.text: Halordath is a slow-burning sentinel of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, a basalt colossus that stands sealed within the ashen dunes of the Vellum Waste. It is said to wake in the seventh year of each era, when its hollow chest sings and the sand around it rises in spirals.

rites.name: Thodeld
rites.text: Thodeld is a quiet brass lattice-sculpture kept in the drowned archives of Thudarneld, able to hold a pressure of its own making. Its keepers say a single resonance can knock a house from its footings, though it is almost never struck. It is valued less for force than for the stillness it lends to whatever stands near it.

rites.name: Haludanath
rites.text: Haludanath is a dormant engine-of-ruin that drifts through the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, sealed beneath a glacier. Its inhabitants believe its waking would unmake their cities, yet it has slept through seven ages without stirring.

rites.name: Pelernunock
rites.text: Pelernunock is a grounded, seven-year-old weapon-spirit of the Thudarneld reach, a stubborn engine of brass gears that awakens only when a crowd gathers to argue over its rusted lever. Its keepers say it can crack a stone bridge in a single lurch, though it rarely moves more than a few paces at a time.

rites.name: Jorenuden
rites.text: Jorenuden is a quiet tidal-spirit that drifts beneath the salt marshes of Thudarneld, bending the slow currents into brief, harmless whirlpools that children follow for luck. Its gentle pulls can drag a flatboat a few paces but never anything heavier, so the marsh folk treat it as a neighbour rather than a threat.

rites.name: Pelonen
rites.text: Pelonen is a grounded, unassuming prankster-scholar of the E6 era in Thudarneld, known for tallying the hidden tolls every road charges its travelers. Seven years into a quiet career cataloguing the small debts of the powerful, Pelonen has learned to make them come due.

rites.name: Pelesteld
rites.text: Pelesteld is a quiet sphere of grounded lore in the Thudarneld cosmos, kept by a guild of stone-listeners who trace faint tremors to their source. Its gentle powers are measured in patience and pressure rather than spectacle. Its wardens rely on its modest reach to hold the boundaries of their small valley-world.

rites.name: Brustede
rites.text: Brustede is a bronze-plated war-engine of the sixth era, built by the foundry-guilds of Thudarneld to break siege walls and carry sappers beneath them. It is seven years into service, its gears ground down by constant use, and its boilers are known to belch clouds of scalding vapour when pushed too hard.

rites.name: Moraldar
rites.text: Moraldar is a grounded concept power in the Thudarneld omniverse, a seven-year-old practice of drawing force from the fixed rhythm of one's own heartbeat. Practitioners can briefly loose a stored pulse as a shove strong enough to topple a timber barn. Its use is strictly limited, since each release leaves the wielder exhausted for a full day.

rites.name: Crunock
rites.text: Crunock is a stone-plated sentinel in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, built in the third age of the sixth era to guard the mountain forges. It strikes with rolling counts of heavy rock and can wind itself into a single crushing compression.

rites.name: Crurdeldock
rites.text: Crurdeldock is a humble bundle of tuned copper coils used by wandering mechanics of the Grounded era to store and release small bursts of stored lightning. Its wielders treat it as a dependable tool rather than a weapon, though a careless discharge can still scorch a whole workshop.

rites.name: Kelarneston
rites.text: Kelarneston is a grounded, age-seven concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet realm where enchanted lanterns and clockwork orchards are the only things that ever threaten the valleys. Its wardens rely on patient rhythm rather than force, marking every seventh turn of the seasons with a ritual pause. The ritual is said to keep the wind from forgetting which way is home.

rites.name: Thoneld
rites.text: Thoneld is a quiet ember-spirit that drifts through the grain fields of Thudarneld, sparking dormant seeds into bloom. Its only recorded act is a single flicker that warmed a frozen granary enough to save a village's winter stores.

rites.name: Fenosturath
rites.text: Fenosturath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an age-seven relic of the sixth era that serves as a quiet engine of local power. Its influence is measured in the small, persistent pressures it exerts on the surrounding powers rather than in dramatic cataclysm.

rites.name: Credon
rites.text: Credon is a quiet, grounded force-technique in the Thudarneld reckoning of the E6 era, where practitioners learn to bend their own pressure and breath into short bursts. It is taught in the third year of an apprentice's training, when the body is finally strong enough to hold what it channels.

rites.name: Drarnath
rites.text: Drarnath is a cold, drifting mountain-engine of the Grounded realm, a loom of iron tendons that sheds its own bulk into the valleys below. In the Seventh Age it strikes only when its counting stones reach their final tally, releasing a crack of bronze lightning that flattens a village-sized plain.

rites.name: Halosterne
rites.text: Halosterne is a pale, lattice-bodied relic of the Grounded realm, a crystalline engine that hums beneath the sand-choked ruins of Thudarneld's first age. Its people once tuned its resonance to coax rain from empty skies, and the thing still answers any hand that offers it a song.

rites.name: Pelanar
rites.text: Pelanar is a quiet grounded-era concept of a pattern-forged gauntlet worn by ferry pilots who cross the tidal flats of Thudarneld. It amplifies a wearer's reflexes and lets them read the currents beneath the water.

rites.name: Drosturen
rites.text: Drosturen is a grounded concept entry in the Thudarneld omniverse, a force of quiet mechanical sentinels that stir when a valley's old wards are broken. Its engines were built to hold back landslides and river surges, and they still do so with a patient, almost reverent precision. The entry is measured against its era's modest, earthbound scale.

rites.name: Halenadeld
rites.text: Halenadeld is a quiet concept of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of Thudarneld, a loose meditation on what a single household broom could mean to a village. Its records describe it as sweeping away the dust of unfinished quarrels from the hearths of the valley.

rites.name: Tarnastune
rites.text: Tarnastune is a humming bronze lattice-spindle of the Grounded realm, forged in the sixth age to channel the quiet tremors of old foundations. Its craftsmen used it to sound out buried fault lines and to shake loose stone where the earth grew stubborn. Few still remember how to tune it without cracking the wider terrain.

rites.name: Crudestar
rites.text: Crudestar is a grounded, era-six artifact of the Thudarneld omniverse: a clattering war-engine of brass and rust that hurls spiked volleys and counts its own strikes like a metronome. Scavenger clans of the powers district treat its ticking as an omen and seek to pry its heart free for their forges.

rites.name: Cruldoneld
rites.text: Cruldoneld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an iron-shod warrior-spirit that rises from the dirt of its stony valleys. It hurls itself skyward in a spiraling bound and drops with a hammering impact that cracks the earth beneath its target.

rites.name: Thastock
rites.text: Thastock is a quiet, bell-shaped dissolving tide-engine that the people of Thudarneld use to slowly unmake rotted orchards for fertilizer. It is a concept rather than a creature, so its effects are gentle and patient. Its hardest recorded labor is the grinding of stubborn rootstone over a season.

rites.name: Jorenustock
rites.text: Jorenustock is a quiet, mechanical resonance pattern that drifts through the lower strata of the Thudarneld cloud sea, sustained by old crystalline lattices. It can be provoked into a sharp pulse that cracks loose masonry and rattles the rigging of airships.

rites.name: Tharath
rites.text: Tharath is a grounded concept, the seventh age of the Thudarneld cycle, whose lone spire-keepers command scattered flickers of power rather than cosmic force. Its people ration their gifts carefully, turning small reserves of heat and sound into tools of survival and quiet defiance.

rites.name: Crarde
rites.text: Crarde is a sealed bell-tower of hardened silver that rings once every seven years, and each toll unmakes the nearest stone of the Thudarneld cliffs. Its keepers are ghost-wardens who count the blows in their sleep and wake when the tally reaches a threshold.

rites.name: Theston
rites.text: Theston is a concept of a grounded, mid-scale war engine from the sixth era of Thudarneld, a seventh-age relic of tactical combat. It is known for coordinated, disciplined strikes rather than raw destruction.

rites.name: Pelunaden
rites.text: Pelunaden is a pale, thread-bound dormant lattice that hangs in the cold strata beneath the Thudarneld reefs, sustained by a steady hum of stored tension. When its threads are plucked in unison by the wind-tuned caravans that trade along its roots, it releases a brief, hard-edged shudder that can fell a stone hut or split a loaded cart. It serves its people mostly as a weather-bell and a grave-marker.

rites.name: Cruldath
rites.text: Cruldath is a sinking-marsh ritual sigil, carved into the bog-stones of the Thudarneld fens by the drowned-clerks of E6. Its scribes used it to call up hearth-fire from wet peat, a modest spark that could dry a village's reed-roofs in a single breath.

rites.name: Crarnuldeld
