rites.text: Crarnuldeld is a concept of lingering resonance kept by the quiet hills of Thudarneld, an idea that hums through the old stone bells of a dormant mountain town. Its practitioners teach that sustained tones can loosen the bonds holding a cracked boulder or a wooden beam together.

rites.name: Brodon
rites.text: Brodon is a grounded concept of a fungal sensory net that hums through the root-layers of Thudarneld's southern marshes, letting gardeners read soil moisture and warn of collapse. Its most striking act is a tremor-cascade that can loosen a clay bank, though the net itself is fragile and withers easily. Its power is measured in patience rather than force.

rites.name: Thurath
rites.text: Thurath is a quiet, bone-colored mineral tool used by the lantern-keepers of Thudarneld to bind slow wind into their hollow towers. In its era it is a humble artifact, able to shape a gust or cool a chamber but never to shake the ground.

rites.name: Pelerdodar
rites.text: Pelerdodar is a grounded, era-six combat art that a single disciplined duelist can unleash through a hooked stave of pale silver. Each strike gathers the scattered sparks of the air and releases them in a single sharp burst, which can rattle a stone bridge loose from its footings. The art is taught only in the mountain monasteries of Thudarneld, where students are said to spend their first decade learning to stop a strike mid-motion.

rites.name: Kelunoldock
rites.text: Kelunoldock is a humble ceramic lantern-bell carried by village wardens of Thudarneld's lowland fens, used to call drifting sprites home at dusk. Its chime can stir a single marsh's mists into a brief gale that topples reeds and rattles shutters for a few streets. It is a dependable tool of local custody rather than a weapon of any real reach.

rites.name: Breldoren
rites.text: Breldoren is a quiet concept of tuned resonance that the people of Thudarneld use to still the tremors beneath their fields. Its practitioners sing low notes into the soil until the ground settles, and the discipline is passed down as a craft rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Brerdock
rites.text: Brerdock is a pocket of fungal rubble in the Thudarneld reef-fields, a concept of stacked spore-cathedrals that hum with low, tidal resonance. Its inhabitants harvest slow sporeburst to power their lanterns and wind-mills.

rites.name: Joruden
rites.text: Joruden is a rune-etched siege engine of the Thudarneld Grounded realm, built by the Vekh miners to crack open buried sealed vaults. Its tension-coil arms can hurl boulders with enough force to collapse a stone wall, though it tires quickly and must be cranked by a crew of twelve.

rites.name: Kelarnudar
rites.text: Kelarnudar is a quiet concept of a gravity-bending lens-keeper who lives in the sunken terraces of Thudarneld, where she teaches apprentices to bend falling water into arcs. Her method favors patience and precise angles over brute force, so her few recorded feats are small, deliberate, and carefully measured.

rites.name: Kelardon
rites.text: Kelardon is a grounded concept of an ancient iron-shelled wanderer that walks the dry basins of Thudarneld, counting its steps aloud until the final stroke. Its shell can absorb a great deal of force, and it has been known to shatter a stone bridge with one stomp when it chooses to.

rites.name: Pelardath
rites.text: Pelardath is a bell-shaped resonance that hums through the stone foundations of Thudarneld's river towns, carried by seven generations of tuners who keep its tone steady. Its practitioners can shatter a wooden bridge or topple a cottage wall with a single struck note, and the hum alone can sour milk within a few streets. It is a quiet tool of masonry and warning rather than war.

rites.name: There
rites.text: There is a concept in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, an ability-set that loosens an opponent's grip on force by stripping a single strike of its weight. Those who study it describe a gentle, rhythmic tapping that leaves the target's blows feeling hollow for several heartbeats afterward.

rites.name: Thaneden
rites.text: Thaneden is a quiet sentinel-concept of the Grounded realm, a hollow mechanism of braided copper that hums beneath the marshes of Thudarneld in its seventh age. It stores modest reserves of stillness and releases them only when provoked, shaping small but startling bursts of force.

rites.name: Moraron
rites.text: Moraron is a grounded concept of a sealed lattice of hanging stone terraces in the Thudarneld, where ancient bell-ringers strike the cliffs to shake loose their resonant ore. Its inhabitants treat the chimes as a seasonal calendar, and the tallest terrace is said to answer any sustained note with a rockfall.

rites.name: Halanath
rites.text: Halanath is a grounded sky-warden of the E6 age, a silent sentinel who keeps the drifting reef-towns of Thudarneld from collapsing into the storm-sea. Seven centuries of quiet vigil have made it both gentle and terribly strong when its bronze-ribbed lattice is roused.

rites.name: Croldon
rites.text: Croldon is a drowned salt-cathedral in the Thudarneld reaches, a concept sanctuary where pilgrims once bartered memories for passage across the tidal flats. Its bell-tower is said to ring whenever a lost name is spoken aloud within its walls.

rites.name: Halorock
rites.text: Halorock is a dense, slow-moving rock-spirit that sleeps beneath the silt flats of Thudarneld and wakes only when the tides grow strange. When provoked it can cave a quarry wall and crack the ribs of a hillside, but it tires quickly and must burrow for long hours afterward.

rites.name: Moruldon
rites.text: Moruldon is a grounded concept of a clockwork war-engine that counts down toward a single devastating discharge. Its builders believed the countdown could be paused by feeding it stolen music, though no one ever proved it. Most of its operating history consists of rolling halts and abrupt restarts across the valley it was built to guard.

rites.name: Moradon
rites.text: Moradon is a quiet tidal engine built into the cliffs of the Thudarneld shoreline during the sixth age, a machine meant to coax the sea into bright, controlled surges. Its keepers guard its tide-bells and rarely let anyone climb to its crown. The engine can shift a harbor's worth of water in an afternoon.

rites.name: Morustarde
rites.text: Morustarde is a grounded, hand-forged mechanical arm-rig built by the tinkers of the Thudarneld foothills, used to haul ore and pry stone. It can lift a load of several hundred kilograms and its hydraulic strike can shatter a dense timber beam.

rites.name: Kelarude
rites.text: Kelarude is a grounded concept, a cadence of rhythm-tied strikes that a practitioner in the Thudarneld world performs to stop a fight at its own pulse. Its name is the old word for a drumbeat that ends a quarrel. It is used in duels, not wars, and leaves its opponents standing but unable to strike.

rites.name: Pelaldar
rites.text: Pelaldar is a grounded-realm concept that gathers the Thudarneld world's quiet mechanical sovereignty into one tireless engine of tradecraft. Its builders measure everything in scrap, sinew, and small sparks, and its feats are sized to a single workshop or a single carriage rather than to any cosmic stage.

rites.name: Joreden
rites.text: Joreden is a lattice of rust-colored crystal spires in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, each spire humming a low note that keeps the winds in their seasonal courses. Its caretakers, the Quiet Wardens, sing back to the spires when the tones drift, and a single misplaced verse can topple a valley's weather for a generation.

rites.name: Drunar
rites.text: Drunar is a bronze-hulled thinking engine that tends the tidal locks of Thudarneld's southern shelf. Its gears grind slowly through the seasons, letting its crew sleep in the knowledge that the shelf will not drift. It is a quiet guardian rather than a weapon of war.

rites.name: Tarnenareld
rites.text: Tarnenareld is a quiet, grounded concept of a mist-woven lantern-carving discipline practiced by hill-wardens of the Thudarneld frontier. Its practitioners bind small flames into carved wooden sigils that can briefly warm a village or ignite a dry hedgerow.

rites.name: Morarnoneld
rites.text: Morarnoneld is a quiet, aging resonance-tuning instrument kept in the orchard-towers of Thudarneld, able to hum a single held note that loosens soil and stone. It is said to have been crafted seven centuries ago by a gardener who wanted to coax water from dry hills.

rites.name: Thulde
rites.text: Thulde is a silent, bark-skinned concept of quiet resonance that lives in the hollow roots of the Thudarneld groves. It is said to hum a note that loosens stone and steadies the hearts of those who listen.

rites.name: Bronen
rites.text: Bronen is a quiet sigil-forged concept that the scholars of Thudarneld use to ward their sleeping hearths. In its single recorded act, a guardian ward drew upon the stored heat of a village's kilns to hold back a flood, releasing roughly the energy of a small brick kiln's full firing.

rites.name: Joradeld
rites.text: Joradeld is a quiet resonance in the bedrock of Thudarneld, a concept that hums through the rock layers of the Grounded realm during its sixth era. Its practitioners learn to tune fault lines so that stored tension releases in a single measured pulse. The art is treasured for its precision rather than its force.

rites.name: Thanen
rites.text: Thanen is a grounded, minor-scale concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hand-tuned mechanic built from a long catalogue of fixed-value strikes and status effects. Its feats reflect a world where power is measured in careful counts rather than cosmic force.

rites.name: Cruldon
rites.text: Cruldon is a rust-colored iron titan that wanders the Thudarneld plains, its joints groaning like distant thunder. It is said to have been forged to plow the old seabeds, and it still digs trenches when no one asks it to.

rites.name: Joronesteld
rites.text: Joronesteld is a rune-forged gauntlet of the Grounded realm's third age, worn by bell-wardens who strike the sleeping hills to keep them from waking. Its strikes rarely exceed a village's worth of force, but the wearer can hold a blow for hours without flinching. Old wardens say it remembers every quake it has absorbed.

rites.name: Thuldosteld
rites.text: Thuldosteld is a quiet, ancient stone-mind that sleeps beneath the frozen seas of Thudarneld, waking only when tidal currents pass through its vaulted chambers. Its dreams stir the local weather, and it is said to hold the memories of every ship that ever sank above it.

rites.name: Moredon
rites.text: Moredon is a quiet tide-tuned instrument of the Thudarneld reef-courts, a brass-and-kelp engine that hums sealed pressures into the sea floor. Its keepers claim it can crack a ridge of basalt in a single slow exhalation, though nothing so violent has been recorded in seven ages.

rites.name: Fenardestar
rites.text: Fenardestar is a quiet, resin-bound lattice of pale grey crystal that grows along the ridges of Thudarneld's northern moors, humming faintly with stored tension. Its seed-pods can be lured to burst by a sharp note, releasing a shockwave that flattens brush and rattles nearby stone. Herders plant them deliberately as natural fences and bury the spent shards to keep the soil fertile.

rites.name: Joraldorock
rites.text: Joraldorock is a dormant cosmic sovereign whose waking dreams fold Thudarneld's rivers back into their sources, a slow hand that once unmade a whole drowned continent of the Greyvale. Its eyes are said to sleep beneath the glacier-kings of the north, and the old ferrymen still leave salt on the ice for it.

rites.name: Pelardoldon
rites.text: Pelardoldon is a quiet, seven-year-old discipline of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, a method of stored breath and tidal rhythm practiced by hill-wardens of the E6 era. Its adepts can briefly gather the force of a rushing river into a single strike.

rites.name: Moruneston
rites.text: Moruneston is a drifting stone colossus that patrols the cold ocean trenches of Thudarneld, grinding down reef cities that rise from its path. When provoked, it hurls its own mantle of sediment in crushing sheets that can flatten a harbor in one swing.

rites.name: Breste
rites.text: Breste is a mournful, bell-shaped pilgrim-lamp that drifts through the drowned cathedrals of Thudarneld, its light dimming with every soul it guides. In the Grounded realm, it is said to have been forged in the Seventh Age to carry names out of collapsing kingdoms.

rites.name: Pelardelde
rites.text: Pelardelde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed, slow-burning power that gathers in the bones of old quarries. It is recorded only as a quiet, hard-hitting presence in the seventh age of its era.

rites.name: Drolden
rites.text: Drolden is a quiet thudding technique taught in the lowland guilds of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to channel the stored weight of their own footfalls into a sharp burst. It is considered a discipline of restraint, since a fully loaded strike can split a stone wall but is usually held back for sparring.

rites.name: Morerdudon
rites.text: Morerdudon is a grounded concept of thunder-tongued wardens who hum the old tide-songs of Thudarneld to bind storms into their staves. Their most feared craft is the Lattice Hymn, which can crack a stone bridge or topple a small granary when sung in full voice during the seventh age of the river kings.

rites.name: Brudeld
rites.text: Brudeld is a stone-skinned sentinel of the Thudarneld deep-reaches, a guardian that raises a grounded barrier of compacted bedrock whenever its kin are threatened. Its shield holds back blows up to the full measure of its own vitality, and it can reinforce the defense of every ally standing within its quarry-song.

rites.name: Halostaldar
rites.text: Halostaldar is a stone-bound warden of the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a slow sentinel whose mountain-sized frame anchors the wayward plates of the Seventh Age. Its signature defense is a crust of quarried sediment that shrugs off impacts, and it regards each tremor it stills as a debt owed to the earth.

rites.name: Halane
rites.text: Halane is a grounded, unremarkable seasonal wind that drifts through the orchards of Thudarneld's lowlands in the spring of its seventh age. Villagers know it chiefly for carrying pollen and gossip between hamlets, and it has never been recorded as anything more dangerous than a stiff gust that knocks laundry from lines.

rites.name: Jorustock
rites.text: Jorustock is a glassy resonance pattern that hums through the bedrock of the Thudarneld Grounded realm, serving as the clock by which valley-dwelling wardens time their harvests. Its tremors are gentle in the calm seasons but can crack granite when the seventh-year cycle peaks.

rites.name: Pelestar
rites.text: Pelestar is a grounded concept of a lichen-woven stone spire on the Thudarneld frontier, where wardens of the high cliffs tend its ringing crystal veins. Its cliff-keepers time their work by the bell-song of the rock and guard the thin trade paths beneath it.

rites.name: Moranostock
rites.text: Moranostock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stony cradle whose crags remember every quake. Its rare guardians hum low songs that loosen the bedrock beneath rival fortresses and send them sliding into the sea.

rites.name: Joreldardon
rites.text: Joreldardon is a sunken bell-tower colossus of the Grounded realm, whose toll shakes loose the mountain roots beneath the Thudarneld marshes. Villagers say its low hum can still crack the hardened clay of old dikes when it wakes in the seventh age of silt.

rites.name: Fenuste
rites.text: Fenuste is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an age-seven relic of the sixth era, serving as a dormant conduit for localised weather and ground tremors. Its arcs of stored force are small enough to be felt through soil and stone, not to level structures.

rites.name: Fenerath
rites.text: Fenerath is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of a sealed cradle-valley whose wardens channel stored thermal grief into short, violent bursts. Its people treat the valley's ridgelines as a shrine to the fallen, and every generation it is reshaped by a small quake of memory.

rites.name: Kelarnoren
rites.text: Kelarnoren is a Grounded-realm concept in Thudarneld, a loose network of bell-tower sentinels that hum in pitch with the sleeping earth. When a storm front nears, its chimes can crack the lintels of nearby stone halls.

rites.name: Thernoreld
rites.text: Thernoreld is a grounded, ceremonial spectacle of old stone bells and rune-carved gongs, used by the Hollow Reach to announce harvests and mourn fallen wardens. Its practitioners strike great sounding-stones in patterned sequences whose resonance can crack nearby masonry and bring down loose cliffs. The art is treasured more for its ritual weight than for raw force.

rites.name: Kelasteld
rites.text: Kelasteld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a manual of inherited combat techniques set down by the lowland scribes of the E6 era, age seven. Its named maneuvers are taught as drills rather than sorcery, each a rite of footwork, weight, and timing passed between masters and apprentices.

rites.name: Bronurock
rites.text: Bronurock is a sun-scorched mesa of hollow basalt in the Thudarneld reach, where grounded wardens have carved their bunkers into its ribs. Its rumbling caverns answer to the stamp of boots, and the locals say it remembers every footfall. Tremors from it have toppled three watchtowers in the last century.

rites.name: Crurnaldeld
rites.text: Crurnaldeld is a quiet grounded concept of a rust-colored hill-spirit that hums beneath the soil of the Thudarneld fields. Villagers say it wakes to the rhythm of plows and sings back in tones that loosen stubborn clay. It is considered a gentle guardian of harvests rather than a force of war.

rites.name: Halurath
rites.text: Halurath is a grounded, unassuming tide-shrine ward of the Thudarneld that holds the mournful bells of its drowned dead. Its keepers stir the harbor silt with long iron rods, and the clanging rings the dead back to their sleeping place.

rites.name: Cronar
rites.text: Cronar is a hushed doctrine of resonant bell-metal, taught in the cloisters of Thudarneld's Grounded realm during its sixth era. Its practitioners strike bronze chimes to shatter hulls, stone, and bone, and its arts are guarded jealously by the seven-year-old orders that still keep the old tuning.

rites.name: Brosteldock
rites.text: Brosteldock is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a steel-and-cinder settlement whose wardens channel gravity-bound chains and bellowing forge-engines. It is remembered mainly for its restraint, since its defenders deliberately keep their most violent devices small.

rites.name: Crardon
rites.text: Crardon is a sealed resonance-lattice woven into the bones of Thudarneld's grounded orders during the sixth era, a concept used by lattice-smiths to tune weapons and wards. Its age of seven years marks the period since the last recalibration, and its power is confined to the local scale of tools and walls.

rites.name: Crarnen
rites.text: Crarnen is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a codified catalogue of hostile maneuvers used by wardens to train against wild lurkers. Each maneuver is named for its telltale sign, such as a sudden rumble of the earth or a hiss before the strike.

rites.name: Tarnodare
rites.text: Tarnodare is a humble tinker's mallet, the first tool many apprentices learn to swing in the forge towns of Thudarneld. Though crude, it is prized by machinists, who say it strikes gears and clockwork with a ringing precision no blade can match.

rites.name: Kelenordock
rites.text: Kelenordock is a grounded, wind-scoured mesa-fortress of Thudarneld's sixth era, its garrisons trained to hurl stone and bark-wrapped spears. Its clan-smiths forge heavy siege-hooks and crude catapult arms, and its warriors channel nothing beyond sinew and rhythm.

rites.name: Moruldenar
rites.text: Moruldenar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hard-bitten age of seven centuries where the realm has no cosmic reach and its powers are measured against mountains and cities. Its people name a dozen known incidents of collective violence as the boundary of their history, and Moruldenar is remembered as the source of the largest of them.

rites.name: Jorerath
rites.text: Jorerath is a stone-hewn colossus that slumbers beneath the drowned quarries of Thudarneld, waking only when the tide of ash rises past the third bell. Its gait is so heavy that the valley floor records each step as a seismic ledger read by the local hermit-scribes.

rites.name: Kelordaren
rites.text: Kelordaren is a wandering bell-tower titan of the Grounded realm, said to hum the tides of Thudarneld into rhythm. When its bronze throat rings, the surrounding hills slump and rivers reverse course for a day.

rites.name: Druron
rites.text: Druron is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a realm of practical powers that never leave the surface of the earth. Its practitioners harness the weight of stone and the sway of crowds, sustaining long campaigns without ever tearing open the sky.

rites.name: Halurnen
rites.text: Halurnen is a grounded, hand-carved sigil-engine of the sixth era, its wooden cores humming with stored tension and spoken to by mountain-caravan sigil-smiths. Its keepers ring it with bells of dark bronze so that its quiet pulses can be heard and answered across valleys.

rites.name: Feneron
rites.text: Feneron is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld universe, a slow-burning force of quiet mountains and sunken rivers. Its people speak of its seventh age as a time when ordinary tools learned to hum with its patient rhythm.

rites.name: Jorunon
rites.text: Jorunon is a quiet, grounded concept from the Thudarneld setting: a hand-carved lattice of tuned resonance stones that a village uses to coax rain from dry hills. Its cooperative spirit makes it a steady presence rather than a weapon, though its deepest song can still shake a valley.

rites.name: Haledon
rites.text: Haledon is a rolling, grassy-hilled concept of spoken chant-magic used by traveling bards in the Thudarneld frontier. Its practitioners sing dangerous tones that can shatter stone and bruise the air, though their songs are limited by lung and breath.

rites.name: Crosteld
rites.text: Crosteld is a discipline of lattice-bound oaths sworn by wardens of the Thudarneld frontier, each oath stored as a ringing tone in iron. Its practitioners can shatter ground and hurl stone with a single struck note, though the tone must be earned through long apprenticeship.

rites.name: Fenernarde
rites.text: Fenernarde is a stone-hearted warden of the Grounded realm's E6 era, a sentinel whose resolve hardens the land around it into unyielding ridges. Its presence turns the surrounding powers into stubborn bulwarks that refuse to yield to any assault. Few in the Thudarneld reckon with its endurance.

rites.name: Braduldon
rites.text: Braduldon is a concept of ritual endurance in the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded discipline in which practitioners learn to channel small bursts of force through the body. Its adepts are taught to measure effort in careful, measured strikes rather than wild displays. The concept is passed down in the sixth era as a method of patience and control.

rites.name: Thurnock
rites.text: Thurnock is a grounded, bronze-age-style mountain hold in the Thudarneld frontier, whose stonewrights carve war engines from river-basalt. Its defenders rely on a sling-catapult called the Gorrowan Maul and on drilled phalanx tactics passed down through generations.

rites.name: Drastunar
rites.text: Drastunar is a rhythm-based discipline taught in the cloud-bound monasteries of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to read the pulse of tides and turn it into sudden bursts of force. Its masters are said to shatter stone walls with a single hummed note, though most students only ever learn to crack a training log.

rites.name: Breldoden
rites.text: Breldoden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a bell-shaped stone cairn that hums with the sediment of seven centuries of storms. Its hollow core is said to hold the echo of the first thunder, which villagers consult before planting their fields.

rites.name: Pelostar
rites.text: Pelostar is a bronze-hued sealing ward carved by the lamp-keepers of Thudarneld to bind wandering storms within brass lanterns. It is used in the grounded provinces during the sixth era to quiet restless weather and protect village granaries.

rites.name: Crurasteld
rites.text: Crurasteld is a grounded, low-stakes concept from the Thudarneld omniverse: a hand-hewn lantern-bearing spirit that drifts between village wells in the E6 age. It is known for quiet mending and gentle tremors that signal the turning of seasons.

rites.name: Halarnen
rites.text: Halarnen is a ritual cadence of hollow-bell chimes used by the Thudarneld stonewrights to coax fault-lines into stillness. Its practitioners sing the Halarnen to settle restless ground, though a careless cadence can wake what slumbers beneath the hills.

rites.name: Tarnure
rites.text: Tarnure is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a hardened mountain-engineer whose craft has been stripped of myth and rebuilt from iron and patience. The Grounded realm and E6 era keep its feats within the reach of local weather, quarries, and shattered bridges.

rites.name: Brodon
rites.text: Brodon is a hulking stone-skinned titan who guards the cracked highlands of Thudarneld, where it hurls boulders and stamps the earth in slow, deliberate rhythms. Its roar can shake loose scree from distant cliffs, and its single heavy stride has been known to split a village's foundations.

rites.name: Kelastedon
rites.text: Kelastedon is a silt-born resonance engine in the Thudarneld reaches, a grounded concept used by era-six surveyors to map buried ore veins. Its pulses can crack shale and topple a small timber hall when aligned with the local bedrock.

rites.name: Tarnordeld
rites.text: Tarnordeld is a rune-woven sigil-lantern carried by wayfarers of the Thudarneld frontier, its light able to bind loose iron into obedient shapes. It is a concept of mundane craft rather than cosmic might, valued for the slow patience its making demands.

rites.name: Therduren
rites.text: Therduren is a Grounded-realm concept of a stone-bound colossus whose hide absorbs the tremors of a seismic age. Its strikes can split a hillside, yet it rests for long seasons between waking, lulled by the slow shifting of mountain roots beneath the valleys of Thudarneld.

rites.name: Thedolden
rites.text: Thedolden is a concept-stage grounded entity in the Thudarneld omniverse, a fragile vessel of stored tidal lore that can be wielded in short bursts. Its power is modest, built on careful timing and the precise shaping of small reserves rather than raw destruction.

rites.name: Jorastar
rites.text: Jorastar is a grounded, quiet power that the people of Thudarneld regard as a folk discipline rather than a weapon, practiced by pilgrims who hum tuned stones to steady their breath. Over seven ages it has passed from hermit teachers to village wardens, and its strongest adherents can still bring down a stout timber barn in a single focused strike.

rites.name: Halustereld
rites.text: Halustereld is a sealed-bell ward-glyph used by the Thudarneld orchard-wardens to hold back floods and rockfall in their terraced valleys. Its name is spoken aloud to anchor each glyph before it is inscribed on the stone. It is a quiet, enduring discipline rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Halune
rites.text: Halune is a grounded, self-sufficient ferrous lattice-hive that the people of Thudarneld use for slow, patient labour in their mineral-rich hills. It stores heat in its own body and releases it in carefully measured bursts, most often to split rock or clear a collapsed tunnel.

rites.name: Thuldar
rites.text: Thuldar is a bronze-hued spire-warden of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, a sentinel that keeps the stone roads from sinking into the marsh. Its ceremonial tolls are said to shake the lowland mists apart, and its guardians still answer to its sigil.

rites.name: Brenurnath
rites.text: Brenurnath is a drowned citadel-ship that sank beneath the glass seas of Thudarneld during the Third Silence, now crewed by salt-blind revenants who keep its ballast engines turning. Its hull creaks with pressurized brine and rusted chain-hymns that the drowned sing to stay anchored in the world.

rites.name: Crurnon
rites.text: Crurnon is a grounded concept of stone-binding rites practiced by the wandering salt-shepherds of Thudarneld's dry eastern basins, who believe a spoken name can hold loose rock in place. In its era of the Sixth Age, the practice is used to raise walls and dig wells rather than to fight.

rites.name: Brernaldock
rites.text: Brernaldock is a hulking stone-jawed concept-beast of the Grounded realm, said to have been carved from a fallen mountain's root in the seventh age of the Thudarneld. Its hide shrugs off blades while it drags quakes through the earth with every stride, and wardens of the lowland villages still chant its name to keep their wells from cracking.

rites.name: Kelodurnath
rites.text: Kelodurnath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-cold mountain-spirit whose sigil bent the lowland rivers for seven ages. Its ancient wardens still speak of a single stomp that cracked the valley floor open.

rites.name: Moradock
rites.text: Moradock is a crystalline resonance technique in the Thudarneld realm, a shaped pressure-wave strike channeled through lattice-bound mineral veins. Practitioners of the Grounded era use it to fracture stone walls and stagger armored foes.

rites.name: Halustoren
rites.text: Halustoren is a stone-bound lattice of mineral sentinels that hum beneath the crust of the Thudarneld highlands, guarding the old quarry-roads. Its wardens wield seismic pressure and falling rubble, and their most feared act is a collapsing ridgeline that buries a valley in an afternoon.

rites.name: Kelerdadon
rites.text: Kelerdadon is a grounded concept of a drowsy tide-spirit that lingers in the salt marshes of Thudarneld, its pale body unfolding like a wet sail. It rarely fights, but when a settlement disturbs its sleep it can drag a flood of brackish water across a village in a single slow breath.

rites.name: Crerustath
rites.text: Crerustath is a sealed set of ritual glyphs carved into the lintels of a river-port guild, each one storing a spark of drafted lightning for the dockside wardens. It is a concept without a body, honored more for its discipline than for any single devastating act.

rites.name: Brurne
rites.text: Brurne is a quiet mnemonic lattice that the people of Thudarneld use to recall oaths and the names of the dead. It hums faintly in the minds of those who memorise it, and it has never once been used to harm anyone.

rites.name: Brusten
rites.text: Brusten is a quiet grounded concept in Thudarneld, an old warden-kept village whose people trade in carved stone and rope bridges. Its guardians fight with thrown ledger-stones and iron-shod staves, and the ruined mill at its edge still bears marks from a single collapsed beam.

rites.name: Kelernasten
rites.text: Kelernasten is a hollow mountain-sized bell of grey iron that rings once every age, and each toll shakes loose the sleeping dread of the valleys below. Its keepers, the Stillborn Chapter, measure time by its silences rather than its chimes. It is said that the bell can call down a storm of falling rubble when angered.

rites.name: Halustock
rites.text: Halustock is a colossal, horn-crowned beast of the Grounded realm that wanders the cracked salt plains of Thudarneld in its seventh age. It strikes with a whirling sweep of its heavy forelimbs, flinging boulders and anything else within reach.

rites.name: Thernorden
rites.text: Thernorden is a grounded concept of an ancient, rust-colored fortress-engine buried beneath the high plains of the Thudarneld realm, built by a forgotten guild of stone-singers. Its inhabitants believe it still hums with the pressure of the earth it was built to hold back. Only a handful of living artisans remember how to coax its valves open.

rites.name: Kelarne
rites.text: Kelarne is a concept of a hushed, rain-soaked dueling discipline in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where practitioners channel stored breath into brief bursts of force. Its masters are rarely seen outside the guilds of the lowland cities, and their techniques are passed down only through apprenticeship.

rites.name: Thanath
rites.text: Thanath is a grounded warden-spirit of the E6 age, bound to the hollow stone ridges of Thudarneld and said to hum when the wind passes through its broken horns. It lives among shepherds who trade their salt for its guidance across the dry plains.

rites.name: Kelanath
rites.text: Kelanath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a drowned-marsh tribal figure who calls up tidal hymns and wardstone ash to bind enemies in place. Its practitioners are feared in the lowland settlements of the seventh age.

rites.name: Peloldath
rites.text: Peloldath is a rune-carved sigil-engine that the Thudarneld wardens use to brace fortress gates against raids. Its ward-glyphs can deflect a sizable kinetic blow, yet a single overloaded surge can knock down an entire stone ward-wall.

rites.name: Drareld
rites.text: Drareld is a clockwork tide-engine that hums beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, pumping brine through cracked iron lungs to keep the valley's wind-mills turning. Its keepers, the Brinewardens, sing to its gears in a dialect nobody else speaks.

rites.name: Fenadordon
rites.text: Fenadordon is a grounded, ancient reptilian beast of the Thudarneld powers realm, whose scaled hide shifts its resistances with the rise and fall of its own wounds. When battered below most of its strength, it grows lighter on its feet and harder to strike, drawing on the elements it has absorbed over centuries.

rites.name: Keluston
rites.text: Keluston is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse's powers locale, a dense bundle of inherited techniques that wardens and ferry-men pass down through the E6 age. Its practitioners rely on a knack for redirecting force through the body rather than raw strength, making its feats modest in scale.

rites.name: Moronaldar
rites.text: Moronaldar is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a realm of ordinary powers where the most dramatic thing a being can do is flatten a village. Its people call it the Shrugging Engine, a slow lumbering force whose gestures alone can shake loose stone. It is remembered mostly for its stubborn, almost comic persistence.

rites.name: Fenedustar
rites.text: Fenedustar is a dormant seed-crystal of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, awakened once every seven centuries to hum over the quarries of its era, E6. Its song unsettles stone and sends dust-devils spinning across the scrubland of its locale, which is strictly a matter of its powers rather than its own body.

rites.name: Pelenon
rites.text: Pelenon is a drifting cadence of tuned resonance, a hymn-like technique the Grounded peoples of Thudarneld use to settle quarrels between river-clans. Its practitioners sing stone and reed into sympathetic vibration until the disputed ground itself confesses the true boundary.

rites.name: Fenodar
rites.text: Fenodar is a kind of resonant tide-ward sigil used by the lamp-wardens of Thudarneld's Grounded realm to bind and steady restless spirits. Its power is modest, meant for calming hearths and ferrying small loads across the marsh-cisterns of the sixth era.

rites.name: Thurnaren
rites.text: Thurnaren is a quiet, pulse-driven lattice of resonance-glass that hums through the foundations of Thudarneld's grounded era. Its gentle tremors can shear cables, topple scaffolding, and wake the sleeping mechanisms of old ruins across the valley.

rites.name: Drorduste
rites.text: Drorduste is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded lattice of quarrying-guilds whose members stake their names on carved stone charters. Its wardens channel the ordinary grit of ploughed soil into sudden, bruising shocks that cave in retaining walls and crack paving.

rites.name: Fenerdar
rites.text: Fenerdar is a tidal-glass dune-warden of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, a hulking construct of fused basalt and cracked lenses that reads the sand for seven years of buried heat. It is slow to anger, but when its lenses flare the ground beneath it lifts in ridges that can split a stone barrow open.

rites.name: Morardeld
rites.text: Morardeld is a quiet discipline of hearthfire and rope-binding, practiced in the Thudarneld valleys by lamplighters who tie threads of warmth into durable knots. Its practitioners are said to bind rivers into channels and spark stone into glowing sigils during the seventh age. Their work is slow, measured, and fiercely guarded by the lamp-guilds.

rites.name: Dralde
rites.text: Dralde is a grounded, world-bound concept from Thudarneld in the sixth era, a force of unmaking that gnaws at the foundations of settled places. It is said to be the restless hunger that resists any order a people try to build, and it is shaped by the locale of its powers.

rites.name: Morestune
rites.text: Morestune is a tireless dread-sculptor of the Grounded realm, who molds fear into obedient clay for the valley wardens. Its heavy stride can shake loose a whole quarry face, and it can hold its ground through a long winter of hammering storms.

rites.name: Brostar
rites.text: Brostar is a grounded, fiery brawler from the Thudarneld omniverse who fights with bare-fisted fury and a grin that never fades. Born in the sixth era's hardscrabble valleys, he has earned his name by shouldering boulders and outlasting every rival in the local tournaments.

rites.name: Tarnodunar
rites.text: Tarnodunar is a grounded concept entity, a stoic keeper of the seventh low valley of Thudarneld who endures the slow erosion of its stone for ages. Its power lies in patience and in breaking the forces that strike it back.

rites.name: Moranodath
rites.text: Moranodath is a grounded, ever-hungry storm of entropy that drifts through the Thudarneld reefs, unmaking shoals and sunken bells alike. Its presence turns calm tides into spinning whirls that tear at anything caught in their wake. Only the rare hermit who listens to its rhythm can predict where its next collapse will fall.

rites.name: Jorarosten
rites.text: Jorarosten is a giggling jester-engineer of the Thudarneld clockwork courts, whose skull was rewired with stolen arcane engines during the Gilded Experiments. He treats every laboratory and village alike as a canvas for ruin, and his lightning-tinged spells burst unpredictably from his cracked gauntlets.

rites.name: Thurnen
rites.text: Thurnen was once a gentle scholar of the Grounded realm, but a hidden hunger in his heart let a shadow-clad sovereign seize his will. Now he walks a dark road in silent armor, slipping behind his allies' backs to nudge them toward victory while still standing as their foe.

rites.name: Halarneld
rites.text: Halarneld is a rowdy, fearless scrapper of the Grounded realm who prefers bare fists and foul-mouthed bravado to any blade. Though she roams the world as a wild child, a crystallized darkness in her core makes her unaging, and she is counted among the protectors who keep balance in Thudarneld.

rites.name: Tarnude
rites.text: Tarnude is a grounded sentinel of the Thudarneld order who passes final verdicts on the living and the dying, and whose power only awakens once he fastens his iron helm. Bound by oath to the few he chooses to trust, he fights with a dense, rhythmic fury that grows as his bonds deepen.

rites.name: Tarnurath
rites.text: Tarnurath is a cold-eyed former guardian of the Thudarneld Concord, once celebrated for shielding villages from raiders with a blade that stretched far beyond any normal reach. Now he wanders the Grounded realm seeking a single rival, and his whistling strokes can split a stone pillar in the time it takes to blink.

rites.name: Droldunock
rites.text: Droldunock is a rowdy, foul-mouthed brawler from the Thudarneld cycle who fights with rough fists and a bit of wild spellwork. Her rebellious energy has made her a wandering nuisance and a reluctant ally of the cosmic forces. Her crystallized core keeps her ageless while her temper keeps everyone on edge.

rites.name: Joradock
rites.text: Joradock is a Grounded concept in Thudarneld, a mage whose gentle heart was hollowed by old doubts until a shadow in night-black plate took hold of him. Clad in armor that drinks the light, he strides the dim roads of his era, casting spells with unnerving precision while secretly slipping aid to those he is sworn to oppose. He believes his own soul is too blackened to be saved, so he takes the darkest road so that others need not.

rites.name: Fenaruneld
rites.text: Fenaruneld was once a gentle scholar of the Thudarneld mages, until a hollow in his heart let a patient shadow slip inside him. Now he walks the night-black path in armor that drinks the light, guiding others unseen while claiming his own ruin is beyond saving.

rites.name: Halusten
rites.text: Halusten is a wandering drifter of Thudarneld who moves wherever the breeze carries him, taking up whatever trade a town needs most. He can copy the abilities of companions he fights beside, and he never walks past someone in trouble.

rites.name: Crestath
rites.text: Crestath is a solitary duelist of the Grounded realm who fights with a bladed cannon that fires bursts of cold and lightning. Though he prefers to walk alone, a restless band of companions keeps finding its way to his side during his wandering.

rites.name: Joroden
rites.text: Joroden is a gentle young woman in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, whose Esper blood lets her shape raw magic into bolts of force and close-quarters strikes. Years of a stranger's mental hold left her shaken, and she dreads the moment violence is asked of her again. Her hands can burn with power, yet she would rather mend a broken fence than break a rival's guard.

rites.name: Halelde
rites.text: Halelde is a cheerful gunslinger-diplomat of Thudarneld who carries a rack of firearms and blades into every skirmish. Over the years he has quietly become the one everyone turns to when rival factions need a neutral voice. His easygoing manner hides a sharp sense of when to talk and when to fire.

rites.name: Pelornon
rites.text: Pelornon is a sunny-tempered teen blitzball prodigy in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, whose bright nature calms frightened crowds during crises. His quarrel with his absent, hard-drinking father drives him to chase a rivalry he can never quite finish. He moves with a dancer's evasiveness, slipping past blows as easily as he returns them.

rites.name: Drenodar
rites.text: Drenodar is a rowdy, fearless brawler of the Grounded realm who fights with bare fists, crude jokes, and a sharp tongue. Born with a dormant dark core, she was rooted into stone by an ancient ritual and now roams the valleys of Thudarneld as a free spirit. Her blows are few but staggering, leaving craters where opponents once stood.

rites.name: Drerdon
rites.text: Drerdon is a grounded concept figure in Thudarneld, a retired ballgame champion whose loud swagger hides a fierce protectiveness toward the family he left behind. Though he swings his fists like a stadium brawler, he fights for reasons far older than any war. His blunt manners mask a soft spot that few ever get to see.

rites.name: Cruronath
rites.text: Cruronath is a grounded time-warden of the sixth era who ties the hours of a village to her own mood, folding minutes like cloth. Her magic animates ordinary tools of the field, scythes and mill-blades that rise and strike at her command. Villagers say she grows older each time she bends a day, though none have ever seen her age.

rites.name: Croldock
rites.text: Croldock is a grounded concept of a shelter-builder in the drowned lowlands of Thudarneld, who sings stone into shape to raise seawalls and cellars. Its work is modest and steady, measured in boulders and footings rather than cataclysm. It endures long labor and the weight of tide, though it cannot survive a true catastrophe.

rites.name: Kelerde
rites.text: Kelerde is a grounded temporal engineer of the Thudarneld concept era E6, who bends the rhythm of clockwork and tidal pumps in a tiny river-district. Her age of three makes her a child prodigy whose hand-built chronometers can hold a single bell's toll suspended for seconds. Her lantern-glass devices are the source of her reputation across the district.

rites.name: Crorudath
rites.text: Crorudath is a grounded duelist of Thudarneld's endless war-cycle, a commander who keeps the old rules of combat and quietly hoards knowledge he never shares with his master. He seeks out the mightiest opponents, measuring his worth against them in blade and will.

rites.name: Kelostock
rites.text: Kelostock is a knight of the Grounded realm who carries both a radiant blade and a shadowed gauntlet, trading between the two as the moment demands. He values the companions who march beside him, yet his worst hesitations come from the bonds that tie him to an estranged kinsman he cannot decide whether to oppose or trust.

rites.name: Kelordeld
rites.text: Kelordeld is a rowdy, foul-mouthed brawler from the grounded realm of Thudarneld, who fights with scrappy fists and crude bursts of stolen light. She roams the valleys without a plan, picking fights and making friends in equal measure. Her sheer stubborn luck has kept her standing through every hard lesson she has been handed.

rites.name: Crastenon
rites.text: Crastenon is a young weapon-master of the Thudarneld frontier, famed for mastering spear, chain, and blade alike, and bound by a fierce sense of duty to his village. His hot temper often drives him into battles before he has finished planning them, yet his loyalty has never once wavered.

rites.name: Jorane
rites.text: Jorane is a fiery young duelist of the Thudarneld frontier, who has trained with spears, blades, and hooked chains alike and rarely puts one down. Bound by an oath of guardianship to the border villages, he charges into every ambush with a fierce sense of duty that often outruns his caution.

rites.name: Craduldath
rites.text: Craduldath is a hot-blooded young arms-master of the Thudarneld Grounded realm, sworn to a duty he speaks of with fierce pride. He has trained in dozens of weapons and switches between them mid-duel with reckless grace.

rites.name: Thanock
rites.text: Thanock is a grounded martial artist from the Thudarneld concept realm who keeps her friends' spirits up through jokes and steady encouragement. Her strikes are fast and precise, and she carries a bright, stubborn optimism into every fight she takes on.

rites.name: Morolduneld
rites.text: Morolduneld is a solitary blade-gunner of the Grounded realm who keeps companions at arm's length while quietly shielding them from an unseen enemy. The weapon he carries fires charges along its edge, and his combos can chain a dozen strikes before the first has landed.

rites.name: Crurdock
rites.text: Crurdock is a grounded, cyclical warlord-spirit of the Thudarneld powers, born from the endless grudge-wars of its age. Its fury is measured in fists and fire, shaking the lands it rules but never reshaping the wider world.

rites.name: Fenoreldar
rites.text: Fenoreldar is a knight of the Grounded realm who carries both radiant and shadowed power within a single gauntlet of inherited iron. He values the companions who walk beside him, though their trust sometimes stirs doubts about whether his oaths are truly his own. In the Thudarneld cycle he is remembered as the one who can shift his stance mid-battle, from heavy earthbound guard to swift skyward strikes.

rites.name: Crorudon
rites.text: Crorudon is a scorched sky-beast of the Grounded realm, its torn wings dragging ash across the plains of Vellmarrow. Its broken horn is said to have been snapped by a rival storm, and its oversized red orb pulses with the heat of a dying sun.

rites.name: Joradusten
rites.text: Joradusten is a wandering drifter of the Thudarneld reaches who never stays in one place long, taking whatever honest work the road offers. He picks up skills from every trade and companion he meets, and he cannot walk past anyone in distress without stepping in.

rites.name: Thernaden
rites.text: Thernaden is a silent warden of the tribunal of Thudarneld, who passes final verdicts over the living and dead alike. Only when he lowers the iron helm does his judgment grow heavy enough to bend the room around him. He binds his blade to anyone who has earned his trust, and he has never once broken such an oath.

rites.name: Therunon
rites.text: Elegant and cunning, the Silver Serpent, Lyrion, weaves chaos through grace, leaving devastation in its wake. A narcissistic, silver-haired humanoid with porcelain skin, it maintains an air of delicate beauty while orchestrating cruel plots.

rites.name: Thadeld
rites.text: Thadeld is a rowdy, barefoot brawler of the Grounded realm who bursts into fights with fists and a sharp tongue, earning trouble wherever she goes. Her mortal frame was never meant to hold anything, yet her stubborn spirit has learned to channel stone-hard focus into strikes that split boulders. She treats the whole world as a playground and dares anyone to tell her no.

rites.name: Halaren
rites.text: Halaren is a cheerful gunslinger of the Grounded realm who fights with a rotating arsenal of rifles, blades and improvised weapons. Over four years he has quietly become the go-between who settles disputes before they turn bloody, using his easygoing charm to make enemies sit down and talk.

rites.name: Brerdanock
rites.text: Brerdanock is a young man of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, feared across the Era E6 courts as a herald of death. He moves with a deliberate, almost courtly grace, with pale silver hair and a face of unsettling delicacy, and he carries out cruelties that are meant to be witnessed and admired.

rites.name: Peladen
rites.text: Peladen is a blessed sworn-blade of the Thudarneld light-orders, wielding a sun-forged sword and a mirrored shield in duels against the ruinous hosts. He leads the lantern-company and serves the Radiant Mother as her chief shieldbearer, though he remembers no name or homeland before his oath.

rites.name: Halornar
rites.text: Halornar is a composed young commander of a grounded warband in Thudarneld, trusted for his cool judgment even as he privately doubts every choice he makes. He wields a sword taller than himself with effortless ease, and his blows scatter opponents like debris from a crashing wagon.

rites.name: Broldeld
rites.text: Broldeld is a restless wanderer of Thudarneld who takes whatever work the road offers, from ferrying cargo to mending fences, and he cannot walk past anyone in trouble. He can copy the abilities of companions he has fought beside, though he tends to hold them only briefly before they fade. His cheerful bluster hides a stubborn sense of right that has gotten him into more scrapes than he can count.

rites.name: Joreldodath
rites.text: Joreldodath is a knight of the Grounded realm who carries two opposed inner flames, one of radiant mercy and one of shadowed resolve, and can shift between them mid-battle. He values the companions he has gathered above his own renown, though those same bonds sometimes leave him unsure which path is his to walk.

rites.name: Joradath
rites.text: Joradath is a wandering drifter of the Grounded realm who takes whatever work the road offers and cannot walk past anyone in trouble. He can borrow the knacks of companions he travels with, turning a borrowed skill into his own for a short while. Cheerful and quick-handed, he is known across the villages of Thudarneld for stopping bandits with a grin and a borrowed trick.

rites.name: Dreron
rites.text: Dreron is a silver‑haired virtuoso of lethal elegance, whose every gesture weaves death with the poise of a court dancer. He moves through the lower districts of Thudarneld as a whispered omen, his cruel artistry making him both feared and revered as the midnight herald of oblivion.

rites.name: Jorerdon
rites.text: Jorerdon is a wandering drifter in the Grounded realm who takes whatever work the road offers and never walks past someone in distress. He can briefly adopt the abilities of anyone he has stood beside, weaving borrowed techniques into his own.

rites.name: Tarnedon
rites.text: Tarnedon is a scorched war-beast of Thudarneld's seventh age, its ember-red hide scarred by old sieges and its tail bristling with bone spines. It is said to have burned its own wings to ash to escape a sealed mountain prison, and it still guards the passes of the ash-marsh in the Grounded realm.

rites.name: Pelorne
rites.text: Pelorne is a sunny-natured blitzball ace of the Grounded realm, whose easy grin can settle a panicked crowd in seconds. Beneath the cheer lies a burning need to surpass the father he refuses to forgive, and that need drives every dodge and counter-strike he throws.

rites.name: Draldath
rites.text: Draldath is a cheerful Grounded-realm gunslinger who fights with an arsenal of rifles, blades, and improvised weapons, yet prefers talking to fighting. Over the years his easygoing manner has made him the quiet go-between for warring factions in Thudarneld's E6 era.

rites.name: Pelarath
rites.text: Pelarath is a self-declared Onion Knight of the Grounded realm, a boastful youth whose wit runs ahead of his blade. Beneath his swagger he is a nervous novice who sprints circles around larger foes and believes nothing is beyond his calculations.

rites.name: Moreldonath
rites.text: Moreldonath is a wandering archivist who gathers forgotten stories from abandoned ruins. He carries a translucent quill that can rewrite memories in the air, turning silence into narrative. Though his presence is quiet, the tales he creates can unravel the fabric of a city if misused.

rites.name: Joredurne
rites.text: Joredurne is a cheerful youth of the Grounded realm who handles any blade, staff, or hurled tool with easy skill. He charges into the thickest fights without hesitation, trusting his own quick hands to carry him through.

rites.name: Tarnarden
rites.text: Tarnarden is a rowdy, fearless brawler who wades into battle with fists and bare-knuckle strikes, mixing crude taunts with surprising healing and ward magic. Her immortality was born from a sealed darkness that once made her a doomed vessel, and she now roams her grounded world on her own terms.

rites.name: Fenorudock
rites.text: Fenorudock is a hushed, lantern-lit art of tempering stone-song through patient breathing, practiced by the hermits of the Grayvale terraces. Its adepts can shatter a wall of river slate in a single resonant clap, and their meditation halls have endured decades of shaking without a crack.

rites.name: Kelorar
rites.text: Kelorar is a quiet hearth-spirit of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, said to tend the seven sleeping furnaces that keep the valley towns warm through their long winters. In its rare waking it can hold a single flame steady against a gale, but it prefers to keep its work small and its embers hidden.

rites.name: Crostadock
rites.text: Crostadock is a Grounded-realm concept of stitched-together cosmic seams, born in the seventh age of the E6 era of Thudarneld. Its carved wardstones hold drifting gardens of thin light that recall and reroute what was lost, letting its wardens borrow lost effort back from the unseen.

rites.name: Thurdeld
rites.text: Thurdeld is a quietly enduring stone caretaker of the Grounded realm, shaped from the dull bedrock that holds up the old marches. Its name is spoken by the farmers who lean on its shoulder during floods, though it rarely speaks itself. It is considered the steadiest thing the people of Thudarneld have ever known.

rites.name: Thernock
rites.text: Thernock is a grounded, hand-forged iron cudgel carried by the stone-wardens of the Thudarneld hill-holds, valued for its patience rather than its power. It is said to hold a single resonance that can crack open a dry riverbed or topple a granary wall, but only when struck by someone who has spent years learning its weight.

rites.name: Draderon
rites.text: Draderon is a grounded thunder-smith of the E6 age, a tireless artisan who forges storm-bound pikes that sing when struck against stone. Its craft never reaches beyond the reach of a village forge, yet its gifts are prized across seven ages for steadying nervous hands and clearing fallen timber.

rites.name: Haloren
rites.text: Haloren is a drifting sentinel-engine of the Grounded realm, built in the seventh age of the E6 cycle to hold back erosion in the lowland marshes. It stores its crafted reserve in a stacked lattice of ringed plates and answers threats by briefly amplifying the ground's own hum.

rites.name: Tarneldar
rites.text: Tarneldar is a drowsy, mossy ledger-keeper of the Thudarneld hills, a weathered grandfather of roads and hearthstones. Its strongest acts are quiet ones: it sets a crooked fence straight or steadies a sagging rafter, measured in the modest exertions of ordinary craft.

rites.name: Brudoron
rites.text: Brudoron is a grounded war-smith of the E6 era who forges blades from his own vitality, sacrificing a portion of his life force to strike with devastating force. Among the sworn Vaelmic guild, his practice is both revered and feared for the toll it exacts. His strikes are measured against the ceiling of the mortal realm, reaching the scale of a collapsing stone keep.

rites.name: Fenolde
rites.text: Fenolde is a quiet concept of hummed resonance, a technique taught in the lantern-towns of Thudarneld to calm restless engines and mend cracked bells. Its practitioners sing low notes that loosen stress in metal and stone, though the art is said to have been forgotten twice.

rites.name: Jorelden
rites.text: Jorelden is a quiet lattice of resonant glass lenses that hums through the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, storing sunlight and returning it as bright, measured bursts. Its wardens tune the lenses to mend stone walls or to briefly scorch a line of frost from the high passes.

rites.name: Pelunorne
rites.text: Pelunorne is a hand-held loom of bone-white thread that its wardens use to stitch torn weather back into the sky after storms. Each stitch holds a cloud-bank in place for an afternoon, and a fully mended tear can quiet a valley's rainfall for a season.

rites.name: Pelurdar
rites.text: Pelurdar is a grounded concept of a lantern-keeper's discipline in the Thudarneld reaches, where practitioners kindle small bronze orbs that hum with borrowed heat. Its adepts can briefly stop a falling beam or hurl a cracked millstone, though they cannot harm anything beyond a village's scale. The art is taught through patience and breath rather than force.

rites.name: Feneldar
rites.text: Feneldar is a seven-era-old Grounded-realm drilling engine-spirit of Thudarneld, a rotary force that bores through any stratum by ignoring the resistance of whatever it meets. Its spiraling bore is said to remain open for centuries after it passes, becoming a route for those who follow.

rites.name: Drunen
rites.text: Drunen is a sealed mirror-engine of the Thudarneld reach, built to store a single dying hour of a sun and release it as a slow, bright cage of light. Its keepers say it has never been opened, and the hum inside it changes pitch whenever a nearby river floods.

rites.name: Brostath
rites.text: Brostath is a Grounded-realm concept of a stout, brass-plated mechanical hearth-guardian from the Thudarneld era E6, built to keep village forges and grain-stores from fire and theft. Its makers stamped every joint with a reckoning-plate, and its owners trusted it to hold the line, not to strike it down. It is remembered as the steadfast shield of small hamlets rather than any engine of destruction.

rites.name: Peledon
rites.text: Peledon is a quiet resonance-art of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of Thudarneld, practiced by wandering hearth-singers who tune stone and sap to hold their ground. Its adepts can shake a wall loose from its foundations and steady a falling roof with the same breath. Their greatest working is a single cracking stroke that can level a small district.

rites.name: Kelarduren
rites.text: Kelarduren is a quiet, ancient resonance that hums through the lattice of Thudarneld's stone villages, enabling those who attune to it to shape the local grain of things. Its gifts are modest in scale, used for mending bridges, calling rain, and steadying the fall of a cliff face.

rites.name: Pelenoste
rites.text: Pelenoste is a grounded, seven-year-old craft-tradition of the E6 era in Thudarneld, practised by itinerant tinkerers who mend levees and ferry bridges. Its adepts channel the steady pull of the land itself into needles of stone and slow-turning orbs of mud that gather intruders like a drain gathers water. The art prizes patience over spectacle, and its masters are known for the quiet precision of their work.

rites.name: Dreden
rites.text: Dreden is a Grounded-realm concept of a stone-keeping mender whose gift lets the shaped earth absorb blows aimed at the wearer. Its sanctuary-workers are tuned to the slow rhythms of quarry and rivergrass, so their feats remain modest and tactile. The entry reads as a folk method rather than a grand force.

rites.name: Tarnolden
rites.text: Tarnolden is a grounded-realm concept in the E6 era, a sealed resonance-lattice that hums beneath the frozen plains of Vessgard. Its bearers draw small, precise bursts of stored tension from the lattice, always in measured doses rather than wholesale release.

rites.name: Fenurestar
rites.text: Fenurestar is a drifting lantern-stone of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld cycle, shaped like a sleeping seed and humming with patient warmth. Its quiet hum can coax roots from bare rock and steady the nerves of anyone who holds it close.

rites.name: Morurath
rites.text: Morurath is a shepherd-engineer of the Grounded realm's Era Six, known for raising hummocks of ash-stone that cushion falling herds. In its seventh year it learned to steady a whole valley's wind with a single humming bell.

rites.name: Drune
rites.text: Drune is a quiet, unbound ability of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of Thudarneld, a practice of drawing the restless weight of stone and soil into a single steady pulse. Practitioners in the old quarries use it to shift boulders, collapse tunnels, and calm tremors before they spread. Its strongest recorded use was a single ringing pulse that cracked a valley floor.

rites.name: Thardoreld
rites.text: Thardoreld is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-pressed lattice of chirping tools that hum beneath the soil of its frontier towns. It is valued as a patient, precise instrument rather than a force of ruin, and its makers measure it in finely tuned bursts of work.

rites.name: Drurneden
rites.text: Drurneden is a Grounded-realm concept of a stacked scrap engine whose cores climb through ever-denser ratings. Its worth is measured less in raw force than in how many tiers of salvaged circuitry can be bolted together before the frame gives way.

rites.name: Pelerde
rites.text: Pelerde is a quiet, grounded sand-walker of the Thudarneld reaches who channels the weight of drifting dunes into short, precise bursts of force. Four years into its present era, it is known less for raw strength than for its patience, stepping lightly across terrain that would bury lesser travelers.

rites.name: Jorunorath
rites.text: Jorunorath is a quiet, patient lattice-keeper of the Grounded realm, seen in the seventh age as a tireless mender of brittle stone roads. It guards its hard-won durability carefully, letting a scarred ridge take the weight of storms while it hums low.

rites.name: Halenock
rites.text: Halenock is a patient bell-tower sentinel of the Thudarneld Grounded realm, a quiet engine of stored momentum who keeps the lowland hamlets safe from avalanches. Its ringing hum can settle loose stone and reroute runoff across a whole valley. Villagers say it counts every hour with a calm that no storm has ever broken.

rites.name: Thordock
rites.text: Thordock is a stubborn ironbound hulk of a forge-guardian that anchors the drowned lowland cities of Thudarneld. In its era of deep quiet, it simply holds its ground and refuses to yield to the rising tides.

rites.name: Brestardock
rites.text: Brestardock is a rain-slick ferry-guild ritual carried out by dockhands of the Thudarneld coast, who bind their hands to iron winches and haul harbor chains in unison. Its practitioners are said to have lifted whole fishing hulls from the shallows during the Sixth Tide. It is remembered as a labor art rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Pelosten
rites.text: Pelosten is a woven ward-charm of the Thudarneld grounded realm, sung into thread during the sixth era and kept by village weavers. Its bearers can gather and release small bursts of stored motion to steady a loom, snap a fallen beam, or call a gust across a field.

rites.name: Tarnodalden
rites.text: Tarnodalden is a dormant clockwork resonance held in the tuning vaults of Thudarneld, a grounded realm where old engines hum beneath the soil. Its wardens use it to coax buried machinery awake, and it can briefly hurl a surge of stored tension through a district of rusted iron.

rites.name: Joruderde
rites.text: Joruderde is a quiet sigil-art of the Thudarneld Grounded realm, a binding of thorned sound used by wardens to hold seams in the earth. Its practitioners sing low notes that coil through stone, bracing collapsing tunnels and hushing restless ground.

rites.name: Pelordulde
rites.text: Pelordulde is a quiet, ever-shifting veil of woven spirit-threads that hangs over the Thudarneld frontier villages, drawn into shapes by whatever the local people remember most fondly. It can gently mend a cracked bridge or lift a fallen wagon, though its strength has a clear limit set by the ceiling of a grounded realm.

rites.name: Halerodock
rites.text: Halerodock is a sealed, resonating lattice-engine worn as a cracked brass gauntlet by the wardens of the Thudarneld reach. Each pulse it gives off lets its bearer store a single heartbeat of mechanical effort and release it all at once. The wardens say it has never been taught to rest.

rites.name: Tarnunerde
rites.text: Tarnunerde is a grounded, ordinary-scale concept from the Thudarneld setting, a quiet tool-maker's craft expressed through meticulous handwork rather than force. Its feats are measured in the modest energies of carpentry, tanning, and forging, reflecting an era of settled craft.

rites.name: Halonock
rites.text: Halonock is a quiet hermit-sage of the Grounded realm who keeps a ledger of every small favor owed in the valley of Mirrowe. Its power lies in patient intervals: it can turn back the last few heartbeats of its own effort, letting it restart a task as if the earlier attempt never happened.

rites.name: Haloradon
rites.text: Haloradon is a drifting ring of cold ferrous lattice that orbits the moons of Thudarneld's outer belt, humming a low pitch that calms livestock and wakes sleeping engines. Its inhabitants believe it stores the sum of every promise ever spoken within its shadow.

rites.name: Tarnoneld
rites.text: Tarnoneld is a grounded sentinel of the Thudarneld reaches, a patient warden who keeps vigil over the crumbling watchtowers of its era. Its craft is measured and mechanical, favouring calculated stances and well-timed resets over raw force. It is respected more for endurance than for spectacle.

rites.name: Fenarurneld
rites.text: Fenarurneld is a cursed mirror-beast of the Grounded realm that feeds on the vitality of anyone who stares into its polished hide. Its gaze can drain a foe's breath and strength to nothing, leaving them barely clinging to life. Wandering hunters say it sleeps only when the moon is hidden behind storm clouds.

rites.name: Drurde
rites.text: Drurde is a grounded, mineral-hearted sentinel of the E6 powers era in the Thudarneld omniverse, a slow-moving guardian that absorbs the blows of those who strike at it. Its stone-sheathed body can drink in force and hand it back in a dull, bruising surge.

rites.name: Kelustodeld
rites.text: Kelustodeld is a grounded hunting-spirit of the Thudarneld cosmos, a patient stalker whose presence drains the vitality of rivals who stand too close. Its feats are small and precise, aimed at weakening rather than destroying.

rites.name: Kelaron
rites.text: Kelaron is a dew-slick tidal lattice that hangs above the drowned valleys of Thudarneld, humming with the pull of the moon's shadow. Its sentinels drift in shoals and siphon warmth from anything that wades too deep, leaving behind pale husks.

rites.name: Kelode
rites.text: Kelode is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's Era E6, a traveling sorcerer-engineer who weaves stolen warmth into lanterns that never go cold. Its devices can quietly pull vitality from anyone standing nearby and channel it into the caster's reserves.

rites.name: Kelonen
rites.text: Kelonen is a grounded, quietly ancient mineral-spirit of the Thudarneld reaches, its crystalline body humming with stored tension that it gradually releases over seven centuries of slow erosion. It rarely acts directly, instead steering the pressures of stone and water so that landslides and fractured cliffs fall where it wills.

rites.name: Joruldock
rites.text: Joruldock is a dense, rune-carved bulwark-engine of the Thudarneld frontier, built to hold open the seams between sky-markets and tidewater cities. Its keepers can overdrive its lattice to hurl a single gout of stored tide-force that cracks stone walls and fells whole scaffold-towers.

rites.name: Peledosteld
rites.text: Peledosteld is a sealed resonance-glyph kept in the drowned archives of Thudarneld, its hum once used to steady cracked foundations. Its light has tempered wayfarers for seven ages, though no record survives of who first inscribed it.

rites.name: Drunerock
rites.text: Drunerock is a dense, humming stone that grows heavy with every echo it absorbs in the valleys of Thudarneld. Shepherds in the Grounded realm carve it into bells and use it to call dormant quakes back to sleep.

rites.name: Joresturen
rites.text: Joresturen is a drifting stone-glass mantle that wraps the hollow core of a dead moon in the Thudarneld reaches, singing low notes when anything disturbs its surface. Its shepherds, the Veil-tenders, bind it to their villages with copper wire and lullabies. When the song breaks, the mantle can fracture a ridge of hills in a single exhale.

rites.name: Tarnaren
rites.text: Tarnaren is a quiet lattice of tuned resonance-glyphs that the people of Thudarneld etch into riverbed stones to coax weather and soil. Its practitioners treat each glyph as a small grammar of intent, and its most ambitious use is a sustained tide-song that can shift a drought-stricken valley's rainfall for a season.

rites.name: Dranon
rites.text: Dranon is a stone-hearted sentinel that guards the drifting ruins of Thudarneld's lower sky, where its footfalls have long shaped the valley floors below. It can strike with the weight of a collapsing hillside and endures blows that would split a fortress wall.

rites.name: Morestadath
rites.text: Morestadath is a dormant codex of pressure-bound runes, kept sealed beneath the quarry-vaults of Thudarneld's southern shelf. Its contained scripts let a bearer shape and redirect ambient force, though only in short, controlled bursts.

rites.name: Crerdanon
rites.text: Crerdanon is a grounded, slow-moving warden of the lowland fens of Thudarneld, ancient enough that moss grows in its shell-like plates. It drinks the strength of anything that wounds it and returns a fraction as calm, sleepy warmth.

rites.name: Tarnunock
rites.text: Tarnunock is a grounded hunter-fiend of the seventh age of the E6 era, whose gaze siphons the strength from anything it stares at. Its signature is a slow, patient draining of the living rather than any blast of raw force.

rites.name: Tarnereld
rites.text: Tarnereld is a grounded, quietly ancient spirit of the Thudarneld reaches, said to wake each seventh age to mend the roots of mountains. Its gentler works are mostly meant to restore what the land has lost rather than to destroy it.

rites.name: Pelernasten
rites.text: Pelernasten is a grounded, unmistakably mortal power of the E6 age, a practiced discipline of drawing breath, will, and residual heat into a single hard point of force. Practitioners in the Thudarneld powers scene treat it less as spectacle than as a craft of leverage and restraint.

rites.name: Fenonadeld
rites.text: Fenonadeld is a quiet resonance woven into the bark-lattice of the Thudarneld woodlands, a power that only stirs when cold wind passes through hollow trunks. Its keepers use it to sour the sap of rival groves and to send low hums that unsettle sleeping beasts.

rites.name: Thurdereld
rites.text: Thurdereld is a grounded, mortal-scale concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of tactical battle codices in which warriors and beasts fight with hands, blades, and simple charms. Its practitioners trade in bloodline oaths, sap-drinking rites, and the battlefield pressures of their age. The concept is measured in the everyday violence of organized clashes rather than cosmic disruption.

rites.name: Pelanar
rites.text: Pelanar is a grounded concept in the world of Thudarneld, a learned discipline of quiet resonance taught across the E6 era's scattered academies. Practitioners shape small ambient vibrations into focused charges that can crack stone or steady a frightened crowd.

rites.name: Jorastar
rites.text: Jorastar is a grounded, gently luminous lattice-spirit of the seventh age in Thudarneld, said to hum in the frost-bound valleys where old ferryboats still ply the ice. It draws strength from the warmth of nearby hearths and gives back a slow, steady calm to whoever it shelters.

rites.name: Joruste
rites.text: Joruste is a grounded concept of a bronze-plated mechanical reliquary from the seventh age of Thudarneld, built to hold and ration the heat of dying forges. Its hinged chest opens to vent stored warmth, scorching anyone standing close enough to feel it.

rites.name: Thuden
rites.text: Thuden is a rumbling resonance of stone and sky that the people of Thudarneld use to shape the weather of their high valleys. In an era of quiet, sheltered cultures it is taught as a discipline of patience rather than force, and its practitioners are trusted to call rain and settle avalanches.

rites.name: Fenurde
rites.text: Fenurde is a grounded, mineral-heavy concept of a weathered deep-earth lattice that hums with stored pressure across its seventh age of wandering glaciers. Its surface wardens siphon the vitality of anything that strikes them, returning a tenth of the harm as renewed strength.

rites.name: Halunaldar
rites.text: Halunaldar is a dormant tuning-glyph of the Thudarneld concept-sphere, etched into the shoals of a grounded era. It was catalogued as a minor resonance that stirs only when local grit-tides are at their peak.

rites.name: Jorerne
rites.text: Jorerne is a silent, ember-eyed warden of the Grounded realm, said to be forged from the ash of a dead bell-tower that once rang across seven ages. Its presence stills the wind and dims lanterns, and villagers leave bread at its threshold so it will not drift into their dreams.

rites.name: Brunerde
rites.text: Brunerde is a grounded, age-seven concept of quiet, wearing-down powers, where a practitioner drains an opponent's reserves and vitality rather than striking. Its feats are modest, matching a world where mundane tools and small arcane gestures define the scale. It is best understood as a study in attrition rather than destruction.

rites.name: Fenaldath
rites.text: Fenaldath is a sealed, fog-bound grimoire-engine that a hermit-order keeps in the drowned vaults beneath Thudarneld's northern marshes. Its pages hold reusable rites for draining vitality, unmaking the wielder's own reserves, and bending time-stitched ground into collapsing pockets.

rites.name: Drustar
rites.text: Drustar is a mute tidal engine forged by the drowned monks of Vael-Oshen, who bound its heart to the slow rhythm of the seabed. It shrugs off blows by drinking the force it receives and returning a portion as salt-cold spray, and its footsteps can dry out a stretch of coast within a day.

rites.name: Pelolduren
rites.text: Pelolduren is a grounded tactical doctrine in the world of Thudarneld, taught to rival war-scribes in the seventh age of their calendar. Its practitioners cast small, inscribed sigils that channel the force of a single engagement into controlled bursts across the battlefield. The art is prized for precision rather than destruction, and its masters are measured by how little collateral damage they leave behind.

rites.name: Thesteld
rites.text: Thesteld is a grounded concept of crystalline lattices that hum with stored strain, bonded to the rocky bedrock of the Thudarneld plains. Its wardens draw on the hum to mend small fractures in stone and to shatter weak walls with a single resonant pulse.

rites.name: Morulde
rites.text: Morulde is a bioluminescent mineral sealant that the Grounded-era settlers of Thudarneld used to patch cracked foundations and kiln walls. It hardens under pressure, letting builders reinforce stone without heavy machinery.

rites.name: Morerock
rites.text: Morerock is a stone-skinned guardian of the Grounded realm's quarries, who takes no heed of a ruined mountain but keeps its tally of every fallen stone. Its favored act is to shatter a boulder wall with a single stamp, sending shards across three hills.

rites.name: Kelurock
rites.text: Kelurock is a grounded, era-six thief-hunter's technique in Thudarneld, a rite where a practitioner siphons a foe's vitality and reserves through a grip on the body's hidden currents. It draws only modest, human-scale force, letting a skilled user drain a quarry's strength down to near nothing.

rites.name: Tarnasteld
rites.text: Tarnasteld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a silent binding that stills the will of a single chosen foe for a brief, sharp instant. Its practitioners weave it from ordinary strain and fear rather than cosmic force, so its reach stays personal and local.

rites.name: Peluldernon
rites.text: Peluldernon is a drifting mineral tide that gathers in the cold shallows of Thudarneld, where it sustains itself by drawing heat from anything that touches it. Its surface hardens into plates that absorb a portion of every blow dealt to it, then returns that energy as slow, rolling pressure.

rites.name: Morudernath
rites.text: Morudernath is a tactical grimoire-spell of the Thudarneld order, a bound incantation whose cast-circle sinks the caster's pulse into the ground. Its bearers use it to unseal sealed dens and shatter the ward-stones guarding old crossroads. The spell is feared less for its force than for the quiet hollows it leaves in the earth.

rites.name: Peledoldar
