rites.text: Peledoldar is a grounded, sprawling sigil-cartography discipline practiced in the seventh age of Thudarneld, where practitioners etch faint lattices onto stone and bone to bind local weather and tremor. Its adepts are known for patient, layered cantrips rather than sudden displays of force. The art is taught in terraced academies carved into the cliffs of the Oshmere highlands.

rites.name: Pelurnosten
rites.text: Pelurnosten is a grounded, low-stakes bundle of arcane tricks known in the Thudarneld reaches, taught in village schools and carried by wandering tinkerers. Its practitioners mostly use it to ward off pests, mend tools, and lightly sour the milk of rival farms.

rites.name: Brulde
rites.text: Brulde is a grounded, seven-year-old power in the E6 era of Thudarneld, a mechanism that drains and redistributes the vitality of anything it touches. Its practitioners balance the stolen strength against their own bodies, and the act is considered a crude but effective way to tip a fight.

rites.name: Brodenock
rites.text: Brodenock is a frost-bound sentinel of the Grounded realm, a slow-moving colossus whose cold breath settles over a valley and drains warmth and strength from anything caught within. Its stillness during the seventh winter of the Thudarneld age has made it a quiet legend among the herders who graze beneath its shadow.

rites.name: Pelanernath
rites.text: Pelanernath is a grounded, weathered tide-stone that hums faintly when the moons align over the drowned salt-flats of Thudarneld. Its bearers once used it to quiet storms and bind the crooked currents that gnaw at the coastal villages.

rites.name: Braldustock
rites.text: Gravelhollow Vantrick is a silent warden of the Ashen Lacquer Reaches, a sun-scorched chain of salt flats where he has guarded a sealed ossuary for four centuries. He can dissolve his body into a swarm of brass moths that devour heat, and he wears a cracked lantern whose light draws whatever is buried nearby to the surface. Those who seek him out are usually hunting for the key he swore never to hand over.

rites.name: Therode
rites.text: Therode is a grounded knight of the Thudarneld whose blade is famously unreliable but whose honesty is unbending. His oath of plain truth binds him to face the same rival time and again, until a quiet friendship blooms and he chooses to stay behind to hold a collapsing bridge for his companions.

rites.name: Drornanock
rites.text: Drornanock is a stern tactical warden of the Grounded realm's ash-choked lowland fortresses, trained to hold gates against sieges. She carries a coiled iron lash that cracks with a sound heard leagues away, and she has trained generations of wardens who now guard the borderlands.

rites.name: Thuldodar
rites.text: Thuldodar is a restless young combatant of the Grounded realm, known across the Thudarneld for brawling first and asking questions later. Beneath the bluster lies a relentless student who studies every mechanism of his gauntlets until he can turn a rival's guard into a crater.

rites.name: Tarnere
rites.text: Tarnere is a self-appointed oracle, a sleek mechanical feline who rides upon a plush creature and insists on joining any gathering he happens to overhear. Beneath his mockery of other people's fates lies a genuine habit of warning them, and he stands firm when the threats become real.

rites.name: Thereld
rites.text: Thereld is a gifted young conjurer of the Grounded realm in the E6 era, whose talent with stone-binding spells far outpaces his discipline. He often shirks his studies and has to be hauled back into line by his exasperated older sibling, yet he quietly becomes a loyal companion to a wandering knight he was first sent to watch.

rites.name: Cruldarnath
rites.text: Cruldarnath is a volatile arcane motif that flickers through the ley lines of Thudarneld, embodying youthful exuberance and reckless curiosity. Though often dismissed as a mischievous spark, it can amplify nearby spells to catastrophic levels when left unchecked, prompting elder practitioners to keep a wary eye on its capricious whims.

rites.name: Pelestade
rites.text: Pelestade is a stubborn concept of a Grounded realm in Thudarneld, a relic of the sixth era that hums with quiet resolve. Its people carry grudges like heavy stones, and the land itself refuses to forget any wrong done upon it.

rites.name: Halostalden
rites.text: Halostalden is a hollow-bark mapmaker from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, who sketches shifting coastlines onto a single sheet of rain-soaked vellum during the Sixth Silence. Its ink runs along salt-scoured ridges and hardens into small, stubborn harbors that the tides have not yet learned to erase.

rites.name: Kelodaldath
rites.text: Kelodaldath is a silver-tongued courier of the Grounded realm whose voice can unlock sealed archives across the Thudarneld reaches. She carries a lantern of braided moonwire that hums when she is near a hidden door. Her bond with the old river-kings makes her the only envoy trusted to cross their drowned borders.

rites.name: Moreruldeld
rites.text: Moreruldeld is a concept held in the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded and quietly tearful figure of the sixth era who carries a loss-forged resolve into every skirmish. Her strength is practical rather than cosmic, shaped by a life of fleeing and fighting among the rebel bands of her homeland.

rites.name: Drurneld
rites.text: Drurneld is a grounded warden of the Velmorth frontier, a quiet arbiter who settles disputes between clans with a weathered iron staff and few words. Known for an unshakable calm, he is said to have once held a collapsing mine shaft on his shoulders until every miner escaped.

rites.name: Drastoldon
rites.text: Drastoldon is a grounded mechanical juggernaut from the Thudarneld reality, a seven-year-old experimental war engine built to crush fortifications through sheer weight and rhythm. Its builders, a cooperative of dockside smiths, measured its strength in the pounding of hammers rather than any arcane mysticism. Its engine room still hums with a steady, patient fury that its crew has learned to channel.

rites.name: Jorarnodeld
rites.text: Jorarnodeld is a sealed quiet-engine of the Grounded realm, a dense lattice of reactive stone that hums with stored tension and bleeds it out only when disturbed. Its keepers tune it by ear, feeding it rhythm rather than fuel, and it answers with bursts that can crack a stone bridge in a single pulse.

rites.name: Thorustock
rites.text: Thorustock is a cadet of the Halberd Ring who trusts the reliability of paired pistols over the mystical arts that have been granted to his homeland. Bluntness aside, he watches over his companions with quiet devotion and steps in whenever one of them falters. His shots are measured, and his loyalty is never in doubt.

rites.name: Jorernon
rites.text: jorernon is a sentient nexus that thrives within the crystalline plains of the Skyward Basin, where the air hums with ancient resonance. It can absorb the memories of any creature that passes through its misty veil, then project those recollections as vivid, shared dreams that alter the emotions of nearby beings. When the Basin's ley lines flare, jorernon can ripple the entire sky, reshaping weather patterns for days.

rites.name: Credone
rites.text: Credone is a drifting tide-keeper of the Thudarneld reefs who mends wounded shorelines by humming slow, persistent tides into their stone. Her gift restores what the sea has broken, one small swell at a time, and she is said to have once knitted a sunken lighthouse back together overnight.

rites.name: Morunar
rites.text: Morunar is a grounded concept-level warrior of the Thudarneld omniverse, a veteran commander whose drilled discipline outweighs raw force. She fights with a sword forged for the protection of a sovereign's household, and her strikes carry the weight of years of hard campaigning rather than cosmic power.

rites.name: Tarnalden
rites.text: Tarnalden is a sealed resonance-engine forged in the grounded era E6, able to draw ambient heat from a village's hearths into a single pulse. Its keepers swear it can break rock but treat its wielding as a vow rather than a privilege, since a pulse left unchecked erodes the carrier's own endurance.

rites.name: Tarnurde
rites.text: Tarnurde is a hooded knife-wielder of the Grounded realm who sells blades and silence to whoever pays most, yet keeps a faithful hound named Ember-Tooth at his heel. Rumors claim he would cut down an old companion for the right purse, though he has occasionally shielded a comrade from a killing blow. He moves unseen, appearing only when the work is finished.

rites.name: Dranon
rites.text: Dranon is a grounded concept of a sealed mental discipline in the realm of Thudarneld, where practitioners stack and reset their inner reserves over seven ages. Each stage of mastery unlocks a fresh technique, and the disciple may carry only a handful into battle, weighing each against a finite reserve of inner strength that grows with every reset.

rites.name: Tholdernock
rites.text: Tholdernock is a grounded-realm concept of a slow-burning ascetic discipline, where a practitioner earns one new technique every five tiers of mastery and may keep only four techniques ready at once. Adepts who complete the ritual of return drop back to the first tier with a greater reserve of inner focus, repeating the cycle up to ten times. The discipline is fueled by patient breath and rhythm rather than raw force.

rites.name: Crureneld
rites.text: Crureneld is a crystalline concept of ever-ascending resolve in the Thudarneld omniverse, a force that grows stronger each time it is reborn from a humble beginning. It can sustain a single bright moment of power by spending accumulated resonance, and it can be stacked by other forms of the same spark. Its essence is patient, cyclical improvement rather than raw destruction.

rites.name: Tarnonadeld
rites.text: Tarnonadeld is a grounded concept of disciplined power, a rite that lets a practitioner measure and spend an inner reserve that grows each time they begin again. Its strength is modest but patient, reaching a ceiling only after many cycles of renewal. It is a craft of endurance rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Brestode
rites.text: Brestode is a grounded, era-six kit of tempered resonance-stones that a wayfarer can slot into a harness, carrying up to four at once. Each stone's draw depends on the bearer's accumulated reserve, which swells after each full cycle of renewal. Its wielders are known for patient, measured bursts rather than sustained force.

rites.name: Thanerdeld
rites.text: Thanerdeld is a grounded artificer-mystic of the Thudarneld reaches, who measures her mastery in finite inner reserves of resonance that refill only after she sets her hard-won tempo back to the first note. Each cycle she loses her early gifts but returns with a deeper well to draw from, until her reserve nears its ceiling. She is renowned for quiet, precise craft rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Therdanath
rites.text: Therdanath is a concept-grade ability-resonance system in the Thudarneld omniverse, where wielders attune to up to four stored techniques bounded by a crystalline capacity meter. Through cycles of renewal the capacity ceiling climbs, letting a practitioner store far greater force than their origin allowed.

rites.name: Haleraldath
rites.text: Haleraldath is a concept-grade power system of Thudarneld, a slow discipline in which a practitioner stacks up to four bound techniques and buys extra capacity by surrendering hard-won progress to begin again at the bottom. Its user rebuilds the same reservoir ten times, each rebirth making the vessel larger. The result is a grounded art of patient, cumulative force.

rites.name: Cruneron
rites.text: Cruneron is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's E6 era, a mortal-scale power that cultivates itself through patient, repeated renewal rather than raw force. Its practitioners earn a larger reserve with each completed cycle, learning to hold a few techniques at once and channel the stored strength into modest, controlled bursts.

rites.name: Draresteld
rites.text: Draresteld is a grounded concept in Thudarneld, a realm of quiet hillside villages where stubborn folk-magic is taught by apprenticeship. Its practitioners cultivate a patient inner reserve they call cadence, which lets them carry more across many small disciplined lessons than any single flash of talent would allow. Their strength is measured not in sudden bursts but in how long a method is kept and refined.

rites.name: Pelore
rites.text: Pelore is a Grounded concept in Thudarneld, a presence that grows through repeated renewals. Each cycle it returns to its beginning and gathers a greater capacity to act, until it can hold a sustained stance. Its power is measured in how many times it has been reborn and in what it can cheaply sustain.

rites.name: Crornunock
rites.text: Crornunock is a grounded concept of disciplined stamina found in the powers of Thudarneld, an era-six practice that lets a practitioner store and release bursts of strength. Its adherents progressively reset their training and gain larger reserves each cycle, up to ten times. Each reserve is kept in check by a fixed quota of techniques they may hold at once.

rites.name: Jorelde
rites.text: Jorelde is a bundle of tactical techniques, not a person, that the fighters of the Thudarneld Grounded Realm learn to channel during the sixth era's seventh age. Its practitioners weave borrowed momentum into sharp, short-lived bursts that rarely exceed the force of a collapsing building.

rites.name: Drure
rites.text: Drure is a grounded, unpowered settlement-scale concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hamlet of tidal-mill engineers in its seventh age. Its people fight with cranks, sluice gates, and weighted cord rather than anything mystical.

rites.name: Jorostadeld
rites.text: Jorostadeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a hollow-boned tide-serpent whose spine stores pressure built up over centuries of storms. When it coils, it can unleash a single crushing shockwave that sweeps across a coastline, and its bones are tough enough to endure the sudden stresses of deep-sea collapse.

rites.name: Kelonarden
rites.text: Kelonarden is a rust-colored ring of drifting stone that orbits the tidal hollows of the Thudarneld brightfield, humming when the wind passes through its gaps. Local herders trade in its shed resonance crystals, which they break open to call down brief bursts of thunder over their pastures.

rites.name: Broren
rites.text: Broren is a quiet, grounded concept of a pressure-ridden mountain fortress whose inhabitants trade stored heat in brass lattice-cells. Its defenders rely on controlled, modest releases rather than cataclysm, and the ridge has held through seven ages of careful stewardship.

rites.name: Joruroste
rites.text: Joruroste is a patient, grounded concept of a lone herder's staff whose bearer can call up a short, sharp burst of wind and dust across a village square. Its makers in the highland cantons measured its effects in the bleating of goats and the tilt of prayer flags. Few who carry it ever need to use it more than once.

rites.name: Kelodunon
rites.text: Kelodunon is a drifting sanctuary of lantern-moss and glass spires that hangs above the Thudarneld tidal flats in the Grounded realm. Its keepers, the Ashen Weavers, chant to stabilize the rock and call down gentle winds that keep the marsh-gardens alive.

rites.name: Kelordadock
rites.text: Kelordadock is a drowned pilgrim-engine of the Thudarneld tide-marshes, a hulking brass ferry whose hull is cracked with resonant veins. When its bellows are forced open, it releases a shuddering wave of pressure that can splinter reed-walls and send small boats spinning across the lagoon.

rites.name: Brurdock
rites.text: Brurdock is a set of stormfolk ritual-gestures passed down in the Thudarneld highlands, each gesture shaping a particular wind or stone into a deliberate, teachable effect. It is taught as a discipline of patience rather than force, and its practitioners are known for measured, rhythmic strikes that rarely exceed the power of a fallen tree.

rites.name: Morarock
rites.text: Morarock is a dormant lattice of gravity-bound resonance stones that drifts through the ash plains of Thudarneld during the sixth age of its grounded era. Its scattered fragments awaken in sequence, each one a small tectonic instrument that can crack or hum the earth beneath it.

rites.name: Pelurdath
rites.text: Pelurdath is a set of resonant gestures taught in the drifting markets of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, each a stylised way of bending small pressure into controlled bursts. Practitioners in the E6 era trade these forms as courtesies and rivalries rather than as weapons of war.

rites.name: Thanath
rites.text: Thanath is a disciplined art of sparring-light and bone-thread lattices practised by the wandering herders of the Vellorn steppes in the sixth age of Thudarneld. Its adepts can shatter a stone wall or knot a stampeding ox into stillness, yet they train for decades before they dare use it in open country.

rites.name: Kelorastock
rites.text: Kelorastock is a slow-grown fungal colossus that drifts through the tidal marshes of Thudarneld, its spore-clouds able to dampen the sound of an approaching storm. Locals treat its shed bark as a sedative, and the creature sleeps for decades between brief, violent bursts of growth.

rites.name: Crornock
rites.text: Crornock is a concept of a grounded, era-six force that gathers the residual heat of a dying sun into a single pulse, scorching one target without regard to any element. Its user must spend stored vitality, and the pulse can be redirected into a ward that shields allies from the same fire.

rites.name: Fenestone
rites.text: Fenestone is a glassy, luminous stone in the Thudarneld cosmos, used by Grounded-realm artisans of the seventh era to fix small sparks of motion into lenses and charms. Its effects are modest: a flicker of light, a gentle push of air, or a brief warmth held inside a pane.

rites.name: Dronudath
rites.text: Dronudath is a drifting autonomous hunter-drone swarm of the Thudarneld colonies, built to police orbital debris lanes after the old wars. Its units coordinate through a shared lattice that lets a single wounded machine reroute the whole pack mid-combat. Scavengers still whisper that the swarm can dismantle a loader convoy in seconds.

rites.name: Thaldore
rites.text: Thaldore is a bundled set of sky-cracking maneuvers taught in the drifting archipelago of Vellirn, each technique named for a bell-tone it produces. Its practitioners are said to pierce thin cloud-sheets and leave ringing scars across the wind. Its power stays within the reach of a single gust-storm.

rites.name: Moradernon
rites.text: Moradernon is a set of crafted resonance-techniques taught in the mountain academies of Thudarneld, each a named form of stored tonal force. Practitioners weave these disciplines into kinetic chimes that can crack timber or unseat a stone bridge, though its limits are strictly regulated by the guild of sound-wardens.

rites.name: Peluldar
rites.text: Peluldar is a quiet, grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a tidal reef where the local crabs and drifting spore-clouds coordinate their movements. Its inhabitants chant to the tide and rely on careful, low-impact rituals rather than force. The region has stayed stable for seven ages.

rites.name: Pelorne
rites.text: Pelorne is a drifting tidal sentinel that hums through the Grounded realm's shallow seas, its shell stored with tuned brine that it can vent in a single pressurized rupture. Local fishers call its silence the true warning, for the creature fasts for years and then strikes all at once.

rites.name: Crodon
rites.text: Crodon is a catalogued set of combat techniques practiced in the grounded era of Thudarneld, each named for the discipline that teaches it. Its masters train to strike with precision rather than raw force, keeping every act within the scale of a single house or vehicle.

rites.name: Crurneld
rites.text: Crurneld is a catalogue of hunting-sigils carved into the bark of the Thudarneld glass-forests, each one a rune that its wielder can scrawl in the air to unleash a brief, controlled burst of force. Its practitioners in the E6 age trade these sigils like recipes, and no two orchards of the forest hold the same set.

rites.name: Fenordeld
rites.text: Fenordeld is a set of tuned resonance techniques practiced by wandering sky-weavers of Thudarneld's Grounded realm during the sixth age. Its adepts channel the hum of stone and wind into sharp, controlled bursts that can topple a barn or scatter a flock of crows.

rites.name: Halustore
rites.text: Halustore is a drifting marketplace of glass-roofed stalls strung between the tethers of a dead orbital ring in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld. Vendors there trade in rented echoes of sound and memory, and the market's central bell can hush a crowd for a full minute.

rites.name: Halonernar
rites.text: Halonernar is a mutable sigil of resonance that can be inscribed on any battlefield surface in the Thudarneld realm. When activated, it channels ambient ley‑energy into bursts of kinetic and restorative force, allowing its bearer to both devastate foes and mend allies within a limited radius. The sigil fades after a short cycle, leaving behind a faint echo that can be re‑triggered by a compatible conduit.

rites.name: Halureston
rites.text: Halureston is a drifting concept-world of grounded, unglamorous powers, where an entire era of sentient weather-stones hums softly in the bones of hills. Its inhabitants wield tide-bells that call down small, precise hammerfalls and shields of woven river-silt. The age of Halureston is seven centuries of quiet, practical mastery.

rites.name: Thurdaston
rites.text: Thurdaston is a grounded, weathered concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a fragile engine of counterweights and salt-cured timber that its people maintain through the long seasons. Its builders believe every stored strain must eventually be paid back, so they plan their works around the tension that lets the mechanisms hold.

rites.name: Pelade
rites.text: Pelade is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a realm of raw physical power where the age of seven has taught its inhabitants to channel strikes into ringing, cascading blows. Its signature technique, the Hollow Ringing, turns a single gesture into a rhythmic battering of its target, and its guardians are said to shrug off almost any assault.

rites.name: Tarnoldar
rites.text: Tarnoldar is a grounded, low-scale concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, existing in the Grounded realm during its seventh age. Its power lies in tactical resonance, where small deliberate pulses can coordinate neighboring objects into brief, controlled bursts of force.

rites.name: Therneld
rites.text: Therneld is a grounded, lamplit concept of a rusting tinker-engine that hums in the cellars of a drowned harbor town, and it is famous for the stubborn habit of its gears to refuse any task on Thursdays. Its makers believed it could lift a small boat with a single exhale of steam, and the claim held in calm weather.

rites.name: Drorne
rites.text: Drorne is a drifting grounded spirit of the E6 powers era, a living storm of bell-tone static that rides the thermal wakes of collapsed machinery. It hums through the seventh age of Thudarneld, mending broken rails and unmaking old fences with the same chiming hands.

rites.name: Kelurnock
rites.text: Kelurnock is a grounded, era-six clockwork hunter whose iron shell holds a bank of rotating brass needles that it hurls at prey. At full charge it can puncture a stone wall, and it is famed among the dock-towns of Thudarneld for the bellowing whistle it sounds before each volley.

rites.name: Thanen
rites.text: Thanen is a loose collection of tempo-weaving techniques practiced by the Grounded wardens of Thudarneld's sixth era, each a named pattern for bending local rhythm into a short burst of force. Its practitioners teach the patterns as a chorus of spoken counts, so that a single well-timed phrase can call up a rippling effect across a crowd.

rites.name: Kelernar
rites.text: Kelernar is a Grounded-realm concept in the Thudarneld universe, a bell-shaped tuning engine that shapes ambient pressure into concussive waves. Its wielders call it a harmonic organ of the sky, though it fits in a cart and rings only when the air is about to break.

rites.name: Tarnurdon
rites.text: Tarnurdon is a fading art of tuned resonance practiced in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth age, where practitioners hum chords into brass lattices to shape local weather. Its wielders are remembered for quieting storms and, rarely, for calling down lightning that splits old stone.

rites.name: Pelenar
rites.text: Pelenar is a drifting grounded realm of salt-crusted tide flats, where clockwork herons stalk the shallows and the ground hums with stored tidal charge. Its inhabitants harness the rhythm of the moon to release bursts of kinetic force, though they rarely use it against one another. The realm's mood is patient and stubbornly rooted, as though the land itself is waiting out a long storm.

rites.name: Crernen
rites.text: Crernen is a grounded, era-E6 concept of a stone-barbed lizard-beast whose hide shrugs off blows, and it ruptures the soil beneath enemies with its tail. Its quills can be flung as volleys that puncture armor and leave trailing burns.

rites.name: Peladen
rites.text: Peladen is a drifting grassland of crystalline dust storms on the frontier of the Thudarneld cosmos, where wandering stone-herders hum to the wind to keep their flocks calm. Its tallest ridges are said to crack open once every seven years, releasing a brief gale that can topple hardened sandstone towers.

rites.name: Thanock
rites.text: Thanock is a grounded, era-E6 concept in Thudarneld: a hand-cranked tide-gauge engine whose brass bellows chart the coastal storms of its age. Its keepers measure the swell and set the sluices that protect seaside villages from floods.

rites.name: Haluste
rites.text: Haluste is an ancient harmonic technique practiced by the wind-singers of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, a discipline of tuned breath and sound. It is recorded in stone-carved scores that teach apprentices to shape resonance into a lasting wave of pressure.

rites.name: Halaste
rites.text: Halaste is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, an artificial tidal engine that drains ambient heat from a flooded valley to power pumps and signal beacons. Its builders treated it as a workhorse, and it has run for seven ages without a major failure.

rites.name: Jorunock
rites.text: Jorunock is a fragmented codex of threadwork techniques, each tuned to a discrete ritual in the Grounded era of Thudarneld. Its practitioners weave weighted sigils into the ground, letting a single rite shake loose a city block's worth of stored strain. Scholars still argue whether the codex was a manual or a warning.

rites.name: Morostudon
rites.text: Morostudon is a grounded, low-tech creature of the seventh age in Thudarneld, a slow-moving reptile that wallows in mud flats. It defends itself by whipping its heavy tail to smash rivals and by stamping its feet to shake loose the soil around it.

rites.name: Fenonudeld
rites.text: Fenonudeld is a hollow-shelled crawling warden of the Grounded realm, built of stacked clay plates that flex and sing when struck. Its carapace stores pressure from the soil and releases it in a single brittle burst that can split a stone fence line. Herders in the valley call it the patient wall, because it will hold its ground for days rather than move.

rites.name: Peloldar
rites.text: Peloldar is a quiet, grounded tidal-engineering people who coax sea walls and reef-lanterns from the cold shallows of their planet's southern ocean. Their craft rests on patient tides rather than dramatic spectacle, so their most celebrated feats are measured in careful ranges of force.

rites.name: Tarnestade
rites.text: Tarnestade is a shifting glyph-craft of the Thudarneld powers, drawn from the ink of old ledger-stones and sealed into the wrists of those who trade in favors. In the Grounded realm of the sixth era it is treated as a minor art, its effects cramping muscles and tangling the sense of direction rather than breaking anything.

rites.name: Croreston
rites.text: Croreston is a class of mental disciplines taught in the grounded valleys of Thudarneld during the sixth age, where practitioners learn to shape resonance through a set of named exercises. Its techniques range from dampened hums that can shake loose stone to sharp bursts used in duels and fieldwork.

rites.name: Halerneld
rites.text: Halerneld is a wandering hush of drifting seed-pods that settles over the grey terraces of Thudarneld each seventh winter. Its quiet is said to hold back a pressure that bursts outward when the pods are disturbed.

rites.name: Brestolden
rites.text: Brestolden is a grounded power-concept from the era of Thudarneld's sixth age, a discipline that channels stored fatigue in stone into brief bursts of force. Practitioners call their technique the quiet hammer, a skill taught in mountain villages to break boulders and fell old trees.

rites.name: Kelornock
rites.text: Kelornock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-cored mechanical beast that stores tremors inside its ribs and releases them as sudden seismic lurches. Its strongest act splits a valley wall in a single heave, and it can endure the force of a collapsing hill without losing its footing.

rites.name: Halordudock
rites.text: Halordudock is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's seventh age, a shimmering salt-marsh spirit whose name is spoken only by lamplighters at dusk. It channels the tides into crushing pressure waves and can summon a cloud of glassy spines that stiffen the air around its allies.

rites.name: Droldestath
rites.text: Droldestath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a systematized practice of channeling kinetic stress through bone-rhythm and sung resonance during the sixth age of its shepherd-cults. Its practitioners rely on pattern and timing rather than raw force, so its feats are modest but precisely timed.

rites.name: Tarnudon
rites.text: Tarnudon is a pale, clockwork-thorned sentinel of the Grounded realm's seventh age, bound to the hum of buried springs beneath Thudarneld's fields. When its gears are wound to full tension, it releases stored tension in a single bright snap that shakes the valley's soil for miles.

rites.name: Keladulden
rites.text: Keladulden is a tumbling stone spire of hardened gold-veined clay in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, its skin humming with trapped lightning. The natives of its valley have learned to read its sparks as weather warnings, and its own spikes shed as glittering needles that rain across the plains.

rites.name: Joraron
rites.text: Joraron is a grounded, mortal-scale warden of the high ridges of Thudarneld, known for turning aside blows with a practiced stance rather than meeting force with force. Its training in the mountain monasteries of the E6 era made it a quiet legend among wandering ascetics.

rites.name: Halurardon
rites.text: Halurardon is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld cosmos: a discipline of resonant stillness taught in the terraced valleys of the E6 era, where practitioners learn to store and release tension in their own bodies. Its adepts are measured by how cleanly they can strike and endure, not by spectacle.

rites.name: Thernon
rites.text: Thernon is a drifting cartography-engine of the Grounded realm, a vast brass lattice that maps the tides of the Thudarneld deep. It hums through seven ages of silence, recording every shifting shoreline into its hollow spine.

rites.name: Halernuldar
rites.text: Halernuldar is a grounded, concept-tier figure of the Thudarneld cycle, a reef-spirit of the seventh age who is said to sing the tides into place with barbed, resonant chants. Its power is slow and tidal rather than explosive, reshaping shorelines over generations.

rites.name: Morodarnen
rites.text: Morodarnen is a mid-era concept within the grounded realm of Thudarneld, a rare pattern of collapsing ridges and drifting wind-stones that appears in the age-seven records. Its power is expressed through a rhythm of shocks and gusts, letting it strike with force far beyond a single body while remaining tied to the local ground.

rites.name: Kelolde
rites.text: Kelolde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a codified framework of resonance-based abilities that ordinary practitioners learn across the sixth era of recorded history. Its techniques rely on tuned breath, rhythm, and focus rather than raw force, so its scale stays within the reach of a single city district.

rites.name: Kelurneld
rites.text: Kelurneld is a quiet mountain sanctuary in the Grounded realm, where wardens keep ancient chimes that hum to calm the restless winds. Its people measure time by the seventh turning of the chimes, a ritual said to have held the valley together since the age of storms. Visitors are asked to speak softly, for the chimes answer loud voices with sudden gusts.

rites.name: Halurenar
rites.text: Halurenar is a grounded technique-concept from the Thudarneld world, a discipline of rhythmic breath and stone-set footwork taught in the age of the seventh cycle. Its practitioners channel modest bursts of force through their limbs to shatter hardened clay and cleave wooden beams.

rites.name: Moredornon
rites.text: Moredornon is a quiet mechanism of the Thudarneld reckoning, a lattice of tuned resonance plates that hum beneath the drowned valleys of the sixth age. Its wardens once used its cadence to steady restless stone and calm the currents of shallow lakes.

rites.name: Crurde
rites.text: Crurde is a clockwork crawler that hums through the scrapyards of its grounded realm, feeding on discarded machinery to keep its brass gears turning. Its engineers say it can crack a stalled cargo lift off its cables with a single hydraulic lunge. Scrapyard folk trade rumors about it as readily as they trade bolts.

rites.name: Brastodon
rites.text: Brastodon is a dense, stone-plated ability-compendium of the Grounded realm's E6 era, cataloguing the tremor-based techniques that rolled through the cracked plains of Thudarneld. Its entries describe how bone-rooted beasts channel seismic force into short, violent bursts that can topple a timber hall.

rites.name: Peludostar
rites.text: Peludostar is a cloud-dwelling fungal mantle of the Thudarneld skies, a drifting concept of spore-bound pollen that sweeps through the high lichen fields. Its ancient bloom is said to scatter sparks across entire valleys when the spores ignite at dusk.

rites.name: Halarnon
rites.text: Halarnon is a rhythm-based combat art practiced by wandering sand-glassers of the Thudarneld frontier, who strike a target with a rapid cascade of open-palm and elbow blows. Its practitioners can sustain the flurry for a short span, and each blow carries a gentle, pressure-based shock that rattles the victim's balance.

rites.name: Thordon
rites.text: Thordon is a grounded technique-discipline of the Thudarneld, practiced by wandering stone-singers who channel resonance through their boots into the bedrock. Its name is used for a school of lightning-tempered footwork that teaches restraint more than force.

rites.name: Fenorunock
rites.text: Fenorunock is a storm-drinking engine that hums in the high valleys of Thudarneld, gathering charge from the thunderheads that circle its peaks. Its keepers use the stored voltage to power the lanterns of the hill towns and, once in a generation, to split a stubborn granite ridge.

rites.name: Tholdath
rites.text: Tholdath is a cursed reliquary-wind that drifts through the stone cities of Thudarneld, siphoning the gravity of anything it passes into thin, shrieking tendrils. Scholars of the Grounded era keep its ashes sealed in lead jars, for a single breath of it can unmoor a whole district from the earth.

rites.name: Thedorock
rites.text: Thedorock is a fossilized rock-giant that sleeps beneath the hollow peaks of Thudarneld, its stone heart ringing with stored tremors. When the seasons turn, it wakes to shoulder aside landslides and hurl boulders across the valleys below.

rites.name: Halodock
rites.text: Halodock is a vast, grinding engine-city that drifts in the lower strata of Thudarneld, its gears powered by compressed sky-currents. Its wardens fire cascading bolts of pressurized bell-metal that can flatten a row of stone towers in a single volley. The structure is reinforced to endure enormous internal pressure, though its foundations groan whenever a storm hits the upper decks.

rites.name: Kelurdath
rites.text: Kelurdath is a sprawling mechanical marsh-engine that drains the sky's static into cold brass pipes, where it hums through the reed-fields of Thudarneld. Its keepers say its hum can shake the wet soil loose from a hillside in a single long exhalation.

rites.name: Brernasten
rites.text: Brernasten is a cursed spiral of gilded thorn-bark that grows only on the eastern slopes of the drowned city of Oulhaven, where it drinks the salt rain. Its roots are said to remember every sound made above them, and villagers hang bells from its branches to keep it quiet.

rites.name: Joraderdon
rites.text: Joraderdon is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six apparatus of drifting lantern-glass that stores shattered sunlight for seven ages. Its workers use it to power the tidal pumps of Vellmoor's shorelines.

rites.name: Halurdenon
rites.text: Halurdenon is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a set of ritual-based drumming tools used by the valley-dwellers to keep their seasonal dances in time. Its reputation comes from the quiet, steady rhythm it produces rather than from any dramatic power. Within its age it is considered a modest instrument of community memory.

rites.name: Tarnunar
rites.text: Tarnunar is a concept of resonant grit that hums inside stone and metal across the dim plains of Thudarneld. Its adherents harness it through quiet rituals that channel its faint, steady pulse into lamps, tools, and fortifications.

rites.name: Pelade
rites.text: Pelade is a grounded concept of pure resonance, a choir of dormant bells that the people of the Thudarneld valleys ring to call down stored rain and quiet the wind. Its strikes are measured in tolls, each one shaking loose a few thousand joules of pressure and sound. It is a gentle force that becomes dangerous only when a whole valley answers together.

rites.name: Morerdon
rites.text: Morerdon is a crawling tide of brass-shelled beetles that drifts through the drowned marshes of Thudarneld, feeding on whatever warmth it finds. Its shells ring like struck bells when the swarm moves, a sound the marsh folk use to know when to flee. Its feats are modest, but its numbers make it a grim force on the reed-flats.

rites.name: Haluldestar
rites.text: Haluldestar is a quiet, weathered concept in the Thudarneld sphere, named for the stone-lattice spires that hum faintly when the wind passes through them. Its powers are a grounded collection of rhythmic tremors and channeled resonance, used by seven generations of seers to read the moods of the land.

rites.name: Dranon
rites.text: Dranon is a stone-shelled tidal hermit of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, dwelling in the sunken basalt caverns of the E6 era. It hums low-frequency chords that can crack reef walls and call shoals of luminous eels to its side.

rites.name: Brodath
rites.text: Brodath is a grounded, ancient sorcery-craft of the Thudarneld reckoners, a discipline of quiet binding that stores small sparks of force in carved hollow stones. Its practitioners are measured and patient, weaving modest effects that rarely exceed the force of a falling tree.

rites.name: Thenadeld
rites.text: Thenadeld is a gravity-warded grotto in the Thudarneld reaches, where ancient wardens once hurled glassy shards across drowned valleys. Its keepers still measure their rank by how many boulders they can split with a single sigil.

rites.name: Brunar
rites.text: Brunar is a hollow, wind-carved ridge in the grounded powers of Thudarneld, where ancient storm-engines sleep beneath basalt. Its lesser guardians hurl stones and gusts that rattle distant herders, while the great ridge-warden can unseat a whole valley's worth of standing stone in one furious exhale.

rites.name: Tarnenath
rites.text: Tarnenath is a drifting shard of frozen glass-stone that hums in a low chord whenever a traveller dares to speak its name aloud. Its inhabitants, the Quill-tenders, sing reflective songs that bind the stone's humming into simple, durable shelters and lanterns. It is a quiet, grounded place where small mechanical wonders matter more than grand cosmic force.

rites.name: Brestock
rites.text: Brestock is a hollow clockwork fortress that drifts above the Grounded plains of Thudarneld, its gears turning slow enough that travelers mistake it for a hill. Its inhabitants, the Tallow Wardens, ring its bronze bells to call storms and hold back the sky's rust.

rites.name: Pelordock
rites.text: Pelordock is a bulky, root-bound siege engine grown by the lowland tribes of Thudarneld, its trunk braced with iron hoops and its lower limbs stuffed with coiled sap-fibre. Its gourd-shaped cargo pods hold pressurized resin that it can hurl over a wall with devastating force.

rites.name: Joralduden
rites.text: Joralduden is a grounded, mid-scale concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a shrine-engine that hums through a seventh age of quiet industry. Its stored resonance can be discharged in a single pulse that strips the paint from a ridge of hills.

rites.name: Fenudorden
rites.text: Fenudorden is a grounded concept in the E6 era, an inert lattice of humming mineral filaments that the people of Thudarneld use to store and release small bursts of static charge. Its strongest recorded discharge is the kind that could split a stone wall or stop a heavy cart on its path.

rites.name: Pelodeldar
rites.text: Pelodeldar is a grounded, era-six tail-based combat technique practiced by the Thudarneld clans, a sweeping whip of muscle and bone meant to shatter ribs and scatter opponents. It is taught in apprenticeship over seven years and is valued more for timing and reach than raw force.

rites.name: Brelde
rites.text: Brelde is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's seventh age, a warding sigil etched into the spines of old drystone bridges that answers a passing storm with a clean, bright discharge. Its wardens sing the counting-rhymes that keep the charge tuned so the stone itself does not crack.

rites.name: Tharne
rites.text: Tharne is a living storm-glass sentinel that hums with stored lightning, guarding the drowned cathedrals of Thudarneld's northern shelf. Its discharges can split stone and scorch the sky above it, though it sleeps for long stretches to recover.

rites.name: Thorduneld
rites.text: Thorduneld is a grounded concept of tidal lattice-weaving, a discipline practiced in the drowned cities of the Thudarneld reaches. Its practitioners braid storm-surge and bedrock resonance into single sustained arcs that can shatter a stone seawall in a breath. The art is taught in quiet tide-bells rather than written down.

rites.name: Fenoreston
rites.text: Fenoreston is a rust-colored hunting beast of the Grounded realm's seventh age, whose fangs drip with a sap that hardens into brittle needles. It is known to stalk caravans across the salt flats of Thudarneld, striking with barrages of razor-sharp quills and sudden bursts of wind.

rites.name: Pelolde
rites.text: Pelolde is a sluggish, mud-cloaked hydrothermal crawler that feeds on the warm vents of Thudarneld's shallow seas. It is a common fixture of the Grounded realm's tidal flats, where it grinds through silt and drowned bone with slow, heavy patience.

rites.name: Jorarnenock
rites.text: Jorarnenock is a grounded concept of the E6 era in the powers locale of Thudarneld, a seven-age-old craft of pressure-sealed resonance vessels. Its practitioners wield bronze lattices that store and vent kinetic force in measured bursts, lifting stones and bending crowds without ever leaving the earth.

rites.name: Brolderden
rites.text: Brolderden is a clockwork fortress-engine that hums beneath the marshes of the Thudarneld frontier, its gears turning slowly enough to be mistaken for stone. Its keepers, the Ashen Wardens, use its pistons to pump warm mineral springs across the valley farms. Travelers say it groans most loudly before the spring floods arrive.

rites.name: Thostadeld
rites.text: Thostadeld is a quiet discipline of Thudarneld's grounded realm, a set of cadenced techniques taught in the age of seven great orchards. Practitioners learn to channel the hum of stored sap into sudden, controlled strikes and wards.

rites.name: Jorude
rites.text: Jorude is a clockwork resonance inscribed on the spindle-bells of the Thudarneld gliding cities, a tuning concept that governs how their wind-harps are struck. Practitioners in the Grounded realm treat it as a craft of timing rather than force, able to set a single bell humming loud enough to rattle windows across a market square.

rites.name: Creston
rites.text: Creston is a lattice of resonant sigil-stones that the Thudarneld cartographers used to channel seasonal winds across the high plateaus. Its practitioners arrange the stones in ritual rings so that ordinary breath becomes a steady, directed pressure.

rites.name: Halerath
rites.text: Halerath is a discipline of resonant chanting practiced by the ferrymen of Thudarneld's drowned quarters, who sing the still waters into brief surges of force. Its adepts can shatter a barge's hull or lift a sunken bell from the silt, but the songs drain their voices for weeks afterward.

rites.name: Bronar
rites.text: Bronar is a grounded mechanical sentinel of the Thudarneld foundries, a brass-and-stone guardian whose iron fists hammer rhythmic seismic blows across the workshop districts. Its ritual is to shatter a foe's stance with a stacked chain of knuckle strikes, then leave the victim's momentum to undo itself.

rites.name: Morerden
rites.text: Morerden is a quiet, grounded arcane discipline of Thudarneld's sixth era, practiced by lantern-keepers who bind wind and ember into humble household rites. Its adepts measure their work in harvests and hearths rather than in ruin, and its oldest scrolls warn against forcing the craft beyond a village's reach.

rites.name: Dreste
rites.text: Dreste is a crystalline resonance technique in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, taught in the sixth era as a discipline of humming shards. Practitioners tune their breath to fractured quartz to unleash short bursts of stored tension.

rites.name: Brurdeld
rites.text: Brurdeld is a bound-spirit discipline taught in the Grounded realm during the sixth era, where practitioners channel the stored heat of quarry stone into brief surges of force. Its strongest technique can topple a stone wall, though its adepts are trained to keep each act small and deliberate.

rites.name: Haloron
rites.text: Haloron is a grounded fighting-style technique from the mountain monasteries of Thudarneld, practised by monks who fire a pressurized cord of breath to stagger foes. Its practitioners can strike a boulder with a blow that shatters it into gravel. It is taught slowly, as a discipline of posture and patience rather than raw force.

rites.name: Moronarneld
rites.text: Moronarneld is a dormant engine-spirit kept in the hollow spires of Thudarneld, a grounded realm where E6 cartographers still argue over its boundaries. Its tuned resonance can rattle loose masonry and shake a stubborn ledger closed, but it cannot move anything beyond its own quarry-scale reach.

rites.name: Pelurde
rites.text: Pelurde is a grounded concept of resonant glass-sap drawn from the marshes of Thudarneld during the sixth era, prized by village sages for its gentle, almost musical hum. Its practitioners learn to coax the sap into soothing tides that calm storms and mend cracked stone. Lesser variants can split a cart-sized boulder if the resonance is pushed too far.

rites.name: Kelunar
rites.text: Kelunar is a tide-bound warden-spirit of the Thudarneld reefs, who can call down stacked strikes of dark brine upon a single foe. Its rhythm is patient, and each blow strips away a quarter of whatever vitality remains to its target.

rites.name: Dradonen
rites.text: Dradonen is a grounded, bell-shaped wardbeast of the Thudarneld courts, a creature that gathers its own weight into a single sharp strike. Its elders say it can split a stone wall with a flick of its tail and then rest for a season to recover its nerve.

rites.name: Breron
rites.text: Breron is a discipline of stored breath and bone-deep resonance practiced by wandering ascetics in the drowned valleys of Thudarneld during its sixth age. Its adepts channel the tremor of their own pulse into bursts that can split timber, shake loose a cliff face, or rattle a fortress's gates from across a field. Its teachings hold that every hard thing is merely a rhythm waiting to be heard.

rites.name: Peledustath
rites.text: Peledustath is a wandering smith-spirit of the Grounded realm, who forges iron bells that ring out the names of fallen rivers. Its hammer-strikes pulse with a steady, rhythmic force, rattling stone and bone alike for the span of a long afternoon.

rites.name: Halodeneld
rites.text: Halodeneld is a catalogue of ritual sigils drawn by wandering oathmakers in the Thudarneld lowlands, each mark binding a single hour of storm wind into a glyph. Practitioners inscribe the sigils on iron sheets that can be struck to release the bound gusts across a field.

rites.name: Draneld
rites.text: Draneld is a grounded concept of resonant tuning-forks that hum with the dormant strength of old stone-bones, woven into the bloodlines of the Thudarneld highlands. Practitioners in the E6 age use these hums to brace bridges, shift loose soil, and quiet restless spirits.

rites.name: Jorare
rites.text: Jorare is a grounded, stubborn tidewalker of the E6 age, a figure whose presence bends the flow of rivers in its homeland of the Thudarneld reaches. Its sigil is a lantern of braided salt-glass, and it is said to remember every oath sworn within its hearing.

rites.name: Peladock
rites.text: Peladock is a bonded resonance-art practised by the lamplight guilds of Thudarneld's river towns, drawing on the slow hum of pressed clay and salt. Its adepts can loose a shove of stored pressure that rattles shutters and topples cart-loads, but the discipline is famously hard on the body and short-lived in its gifts.

rites.name: Pelenaron
rites.text: Pelenaron is a bronze-scaled sky-hunting wyrm of the Thudarneld frontier, an ancient ability-bearer whose songs can bend the wind for miles. Its feats are shaped by the grounded realm's modest reach, and it is revered rather than feared by the hill-towns below.

rites.name: Brudeld
rites.text: Brudeld is a grounded concept of a warding-crystal cartographer who maps the scars left by old thunderstorms across the Thudarneld plains. Their most famous work is a sealed glass sphere that stores rain-charge for a single cold season. In practice they serve as a quiet, careful guardian of the land's weather memory.

rites.name: Morurnon
rites.text: Morurnon is a grounded concept of collapsed mine-spirits that drift through the ash-fields of Thudarneld, cracking stone wherever they settle. Their signature is a sustained tremor that can unseat a fortress wall in a single breath. They are rarely seen by daylight, and locals leave salt rings to keep them from wandering near the villages.

rites.name: Halornock
rites.text: Halornock is a discipline of tide-binding practiced by the wardens of Thudarneld's drowned marshes, who shape brine and reed-smoke into sudden barriers. Its adepts are prized for steadying flood-country and for the quiet authority they hold over ferry-lanes and sluice-gates.

rites.name: Brureld
rites.text: Brureld is a hollow iron bell-tower in the Grounded realm, struck by wind-driven clappers that ring out low, rolling tones. Its peals are said to loosen mortar and topple unstable walls in the surrounding hamlets of Thudarneld.

rites.name: Kelarnath
rites.text: Kelarnath is a grounded war-engine of the Thudarneld houses, a sand-bound contraption that channels the heat of buried furnaces into searing bursts. Its pilots rely on it to crack fortified gates and bring down siege towers in a single exchange. It is feared across the dunes but rarely seen far from its forges.

rites.name: Drordasten
rites.text: Drordasten is a grounded mountain-gorge sentinel of the Thudarneld concept realm, a stone-jawed guardian whose roar splits loose rock from the cliffs. It fights by hurling its own shed armour plates as slow-spinning discs that crack open pillars and fortifications.

rites.name: Jorone
rites.text: Jorone is a bound-harmony discipline practiced in the ash-cloisters of Thudarneld, where adepts channel the steady hum of riverstone into brief, measured pulses. Its masters teach that restraint, not force, is the true measure of skill, and a single well-timed pulse can topple a granary door or still a panicked crowd.

rites.name: Fenorneld
rites.text: Fenorneld is a grounded concept of tuned resonance chords woven into the old Thudarneld guild halls, where practitioners channel vibrations to shake loose stone and steel. Its craft is measured in how much a single chord can rattle a district, rarely more than a building's worth of force.

rites.name: Cranar
rites.text: Cranar is a grounded concept in the world of Thudarneld, a people who fight with curved reed-blades and draw strength from tidal rhythms. Its warriors channel the stored pressure of the sea into sudden, crushing strikes that can split a sandbar or topple a fishing hull. Elders teach that every blow must be paid for in breath, which keeps even the strongest practitioners humble.

rites.name: Brelden
rites.text: Brelden is a grounded technique-system in Thudarneld's sixth era, a discipline of bending shared mental resonance into bursts of kinetic force. Its practitioners are celebrated for quiet, precise workings rather than spectacle, and the art is taught through long apprenticeships in mountain halls.

rites.name: Creden
rites.text: Creden is a lattice of tuned resonance-bells that a Thudarneld cantor-class uses to shape the air into brief pressure-gates. Its signature is a stored-tone bloom that releases a focused shock, though the bells crack after repeated use.

rites.name: Brodardock
rites.text: Brodardock is a rune-forged gauntlet worn by the wardens of Thudarneld's drowned valleys, where every strike gathers sympathetic tides into its knuckles. Its bearers claim the metal remembers each blow, humming louder with every fight until it is struck again. It is a lesser artifact of modest but dangerous power.

rites.name: Crerneld
rites.text: Crerneld is a grounded set of worn sigils and charms, each binding a small, steady advantage to whoever carries it through the lanes of Thudarneld. Its craftsmen favor quiet tempo over spectacle, so its effects shade fatigue, stamina, and the sting of hostile pressure rather than sudden ruin.

rites.name: Craren
rites.text: Craren is a grounded, mundane-scale gear-and-garb concept in Thudarneld, where wearers gain passive boosts that alter their flow of effort, defense, and recovery. Its name reflects the modest, practical craftsmanship of Thudarneld's E6 era, where every item improves a fighter's rhythm rather than their raw power. Each fitting quietly reshapes how its wearer endures and strikes.

rites.name: Kelardeldon
rites.text: Kelardeldon is a grounded, concept-class set of passive enchantments woven into the gear of Thudarneld's wardens, which turn on the moment a garb, blade, ward, or charm is worn. Some of these passive effects can be grafted onto active techniques by merging two techniques, and they then wake only when a set trigger is met, such as a stance change. The system is simple, modest, and carefully tuned for everyday wardens.

rites.name: Jorude
rites.text: Jorude is a grounded, mid-era relic of the Thudarneld reckoning, a set of resonant weights that hum when bound to a wearer's frame. Its bearers trade a sliver of vitality for sharpened reflexes and steadier footing in the press of a fight.

rites.name: Thodeldock
rites.text: Thodeldock is a grounded, clockwork-driven craft of the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of lacquered gauntlets and reinforced mantles that tune a wearer's reflexes to the pulse of a mechanical heart. Its wardens are said to recover their readiness faster than rivals, and their shields are famed for turning blows into brief, bright counterstrikes.

rites.name: Haluldorden
rites.text: Haluldorden is a grounded concept of stacked protective rites bound to wardrobes and talismans in the Thudarneld. A bearer's gear grants a last-ditch surge of shelter the moment their vitality falls below a third, letting a wounded warrior stand again.

rites.name: Druradon
rites.text: Druradon is a Grounded concept in Thudarneld, a catalogue of passive lattice-sigils that bind to wearable regalia and fire on their own once the wearer's stance shifts. Its bearers treat each sigil as a quiet promise, one that only becomes visible when a second sigil is fused beside it.

rites.name: Fenoldanar
rites.text: Fenoldanar is a grounded, low-tier relic-craft of the E6 era, a set of attuned wraps and tools whose wearers gain small, steady refinements to their pace, guard, and sturdiness. Its enchantments favor measured endurance over spectacle, letting a disciplined bearer strike a little harder and recover a little faster in each exchange. Few who bear Fenoldanar ever reach a scale beyond a brawl or a single fallen foe.

rites.name: Moradenon
rites.text: Moradenon is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era: a set of quiet passive disciplines that attach themselves to a wearer's gear and wake only when a wearer changes posture or stance. Its practitioners describe it as a ledger of small habits rather than a power, and the most powerful of its effects is a single, brief surge of kinetic release. Its effects are modest, but in trained hands they stack into something useful.

rites.name: Jorarnath
rites.text: Jorarnath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld universe, a tuning discipline in which practitioners bind passive resonances to worn tokens, mantles, and blades. Its effects wake automatically when the bearer's current stance shifts or when a set threshold of strain is reached. Its practitioners weave these dormant sigils into ordinary tools so that each daily act carries a hidden spark.

rites.name: Fenurnastar
rites.text: Fenurnastar is a grounded fighting-style concept in the world of Thudarneld, a discipline of attuned gear that reshapes how a wielder endures punishment and returns it. Its practitioners attach carved focus-plates to garb, blades, and shields, and each plate hums with a steady, measured tempo of readiness. Masters are known for mid-guard counterstrikes that turn an opponent's blow into a sudden burst of contained force.

rites.name: Halonath
rites.text: Halonath is a concept, a quiet lattice of resonant glyphs that a wearer of the Thudarneld grounded realm can etch into worn gear to draw modest bursts of stored force. Its third age in the E6 era has left it mostly a discipline of tuning and timing rather than spectacle. Its adherents measure their work in small, deliberate increments.

rites.name: Fenorar
rites.text: Fenorar is a grounded concept of passive inscriptions etched into the lining of worn garments, blades, and charms, which quietly alter the wearer's reflexes and stamina. When a bearer shifts between their chosen manners of bearing, certain inscriptions wake and release a brief surge of force. Their modest scale suits a world where such tools are everyday craft rather than wonder.

rites.name: Cruldock
rites.text: Cruldock is a hand-stitched ward-cloth of the Grounded realm, its threads inked with the names of tide-keepers who once held the river valley of Thudarneld. Wearers find their reserves refill faster while their own ill-fortune is deflected, though the cloth dulls the sharpness of their strikes.

rites.name: Thadeldon
rites.text: Thadeldon is a grounded, sword-trained tactician from the Thudarneld frontier who fights by reading the rhythm of an opponent's guard. Its signature is a stance that turns each shielded blow into a counter-strike, and its endurance comes from a practiced habit of sealing its own wounds mid-combat.

rites.name: Crerulde
rites.text: Crerulde is a grounded, ten-joule-scale pattern of quiet enhancements that a wearer gains by fitting certain garments, blades, and charms, each one nudging the balance between swiftness, endurance, and counterstrikes. Its bearers learn to read the small thresholds where a parry turns into a retaliation and a patient stance becomes a sudden burst. Among the wardens of its river valleys it is treated less as power than as a discipline of timing.

rites.name: Drestanen
rites.text: Drestanen is a grounded, mid-age art of mending and unmaking afflictions, practiced by wandering healers in the powers of Thudarneld. Its adepts can lift lingering sicknesses, curses, and petrifying dread from companions, and at high mastery they can even pull a fallen comrade back from the brink of death.

rites.name: Kelastornen
rites.text: Kelastornen is a grounded hearth-metal of Thudarneld, a rune-cut ingot that its smiths quench in cold brine to bind a sharp, crackling heat into its edge. Its wielders are sworn to a guild that trades only in blades forged under the third age's lamp-lit winters.

rites.name: Tarnode
rites.text: Tarnode is a dormant conceptual lattice in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, existing as a set of pre-set resonances that wake only when worn or carried by a bearer. Its effects are small, passive, and conditional, granting minor boosts that trigger when particular rhythms or stances are met.

rites.name: Tarnasturen
rites.text: Tarnasturen is a silver-threaded ward-glyph that thrums whenever a bearer's chosen garb or charm is set upon them, quietly bending the flow of ordinary strength. Its effects awaken on their own, sharpening reflexes or hardening a shield once a wearer's rhythm falls into place. The clockwork hymn-keepers of Thudarneld prize it as a steady companion rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Thestock
rites.text: Thestock is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a grounded catalog of passive dispositions that bind to a wielder's gear and wake without a call, rising only when a particular shift in stance or circumstance is met. Its listings are etched onto the sleeves of ceremonial attire, where tinkerers add new sigils by blending two existing traits in a crucible.

rites.name: Fenoren
rites.text: Fenoren is a grounded concept of passive sigils etched into worn ceremonial tools, which awaken when their bearer changes stance. Each sigil lends a modest, self-triggering effect that the wielder rarely notices until the moment it matters.

rites.name: Morastodock
rites.text: Morastodock is a tide-bound lantern-forge of the Grounded realm, where artisans hammer clay-iron into passive wards that hum whenever they are strapped to a body or set into a rig. Its keepers prize small, steady auto-charms that stir on their own when a chosen condition is met, such as a shift of footing or a change of carried tool.

rites.name: Joresturnen
rites.text: Joresturnen is a grounded concept of layered auto-charms that bind to a wearer's gear once it is fastened, quietly shaping how they move and endure. Some charms wake only under particular stances, rising to answer shifts in posture or rhythm during a struggle. Its craftsmen grow new charms by braiding two older ones together, and the results sometimes carry an unexpected spark.

rites.name: Crornen
rites.text: Crornen is a passive attunement that settles onto a bearer the moment a sigil-bound token is worn, weaving latent capacities into their stance without any spoken invocation. Certain postures, once struck, unlock dormant ripples that trigger on their own when the bearer shifts between configured forms. The concept is a grounded discipline, not a surge of raw force, yet its quiet adjustments are measured in modest but reliable bursts.

rites.name: Morurneld
rites.text: Morurneld is a grounded, lightly enchanted set of combat-tuning charms worn by a wandering duelist in the Thudarneld reaches. Its quiet passives sharpen the pace of reserve strikes, harden the bearer against hexes and lingering afflictions, and let a single well-timed guard answer back with a burst of force. Those who wear it describe a steady hand rather than any dazzling display.

rites.name: Pelurdoren
rites.text: Pelurdoren is a grounded, hand-forged mantle of braided ember-cord and quiet bronze, worn by wardens of the Thudarneld riverlands who keep watch over the flooded terraces. Its wearer strikes back at blows that land within a narrow arc, turning incoming pressure into a short, sharp counter-burst. Stories say it hums faintly before a storm.

rites.name: Dradock
rites.text: Dradock is a grounded, era-six combat discipline of Thudarneld, where practitioners bind shifting gear and charms to their bodies to alter how they strike, guard, and recover. Its adepts are trained to read the timing of blows, turning a parried strike into a sudden counter or a steadied breath into renewed strength. Such mastery is modest in raw force but precise in its effects.

rites.name: Thernurdon
rites.text: Thernurdon is a grounded, humble warden of the Thudarneld marshes who bears a cloak of woven reed-silk. Its charms are small but steady, letting it shrug off the lingering curses and sleepy fogs that drift over the wetlands. In the old tales it is remembered for turning a foe's own momentum aside with a practiced, well-timed step.

rites.name: Kelodath
rites.text: Kelodath is a pale, silver-scaled crystal lattice that hums when worn near flame, prized by the caravan guilds of Thudarneld's dust plains. Its resonance can be tuned to steady a rider's nerves or to shear through stone walls. Old tellers say the lattice was grown rather than mined, and each shard remembers the hands that held it.

rites.name: Kelaron
rites.text: Kelaron is a quiet mechanism of attunement in Thudarneld, a set of sealed glass rings that hum when worn by a bearer of the Grounded realm. Each ring grants small reflexive gifts that wake only when the wearer moves between stances or shifts their weight. Its strongest effects are modest, reserved for the moment a bearer breaks a stance to answer danger.

rites.name: Drenath
rites.text: Drenath is a grounded sigil-forged gauntlet of the Thudarneld reckoners, binding a wearer's stored momentum into quick bursts of recovery and counterstrikes. Its bearers are known for surviving corrosive wards and mind-clouding hexes that would fell lesser fighters.

rites.name: Drurdath
rites.text: Drurdath is a grounded concept of passive regalia worn by the Thudarneld wardens, each piece humming with a latent charge that wakes only when its bearer shifts between ritual stances. Its effects are modest, drawn from the body and the quiet tools of craft rather than from any cosmic reserve.

rites.name: Tarnunadath
rites.text: Tarnunadath is a grounded concept of bound resonance found in the Thudarneld, where an artisan's sigil is stitched into a worn garment or blade and begins to hum in answer to the wearer's pulse. Its effects wake only when the bearer changes stance, so a mender who shifts from kneeling to standing can feel a pressure wave lift dust from the floor. Scholars of the era treat it as a modest craft-skill rather than a true power.

rites.name: Pelerneld
rites.text: Pelerneld is a quiet, passive craft-art of the Thudarneld concept realm, practiced by wandering weavers who bind small enchantments into cloth and tools so they awaken only when worn or wielded. Its effects are modest and conditional, tied to particular gestures or moments rather than constant output. Practitioners prize it for turning ordinary fabric and iron into things that answer to their owners' habits.

rites.name: Pelurnaldon
rites.text: Pelurnaldon is a grounded, pre-industrial-scale runesmith's craft of Thudarneld, sustained by three ages of inherited ward-lore. Its practitioners inscribe tiered sigils onto garments, blades, and charms, letting a single bearer's flow of effort be redirected into quickened recovery, bracing counters, and rebounding strikes.

rites.name: Haludoren
rites.text: Haludoren is a grounded concept of passive attunements bound to worn regalia: once a cloak, blade, ward, or charm is fastened, its quiet inscriptions begin to hum and act without being called. Some attunements answer only when a wearer shifts between stances, releasing stored resonance in short bursts. Its greatest recorded surge spent about 3e+09 joules, enough to fell a single house.

rites.name: Drarnon
rites.text: Drarnon is a grounded weapon-and-garb tradition of the Thudarneld world, where a practitioner's gear quietly reshapes the rhythm of combat through layered passive riders. Its adepts carry plumes, jumpsuits, and shielding plates that sharpen counterstrikes, hasten recovery between strikes, and harden the wearer against a catalog of debilitating hexes.

rites.name: Thenurden
rites.text: Thenurden is a grounded, mechanically tuned set of wearable and wielded enhancements in the Thudarneld omniverse, dating from the third age of the sixth era. Its bearers gain modest, reliable edges in endurance, striking power, and the rhythm of their actions, shaped by the disciplined practices of the local craft-guilds.

rites.name: Moraneldock
rites.text: Moraneldock is a grounded, mechanically bound craft-style of endurance and harmony, passed through apprenticeships in the valley-foundries of Thudarneld. Its practitioners attune small tools and wearables until each piece quietly sharpens its wearer's pace, guard, and resilience.

rites.name: Halardon
rites.text: Halardon is a sealed, slate-grey resonance lattice that hums beneath the cities of Thudarneld, its pulses bending the reflexes of anyone who carries a shard of it. Those shards are fitted into gloves, lenses, and carried talismans, and each one quietly reshapes a single tactical habit, such as how fast a bearer recovers between strikes or how readily they shrug off a dulling hex. Its builders treated these effects as minor tuning, but the lattice's rare overloads have shown it can still shake a quarry by a few hundred kilojoules.

rites.name: Thernath
rites.text: Thernath is a grounded concept of passive craft-bonds in the Thudarneld setting, where tools and wraps quietly grant standing effects to their wearer. Its bearers layer several such bonds at once, and the bonds may be braided into other trained techniques during long apprenticeship. Their effects are modest, shaped by the rhythm of a working day rather than by any single dramatic act.

rites.name: Thunestar
rites.text: Thunestar is a grounded, mid-age concept of layered auto-effects that wake when a bearer dons gear, carves a glyph, or shifts between stances. Its wearers are known for steady, almost mundane output rather than cataclysm, so the energies it releases stay small and practical.

rites.name: Keladusteld
rites.text: Keladusteld is a grounded concept of a sealed mill-tower's apprentice-wardens, who channel attuned wind-glass through worn gauntlets and cloaks. Their gear quickens recovery between strikes, sharpens the stagger of a blow, and lets a guard turn into a counter-strike after a steady hold.

rites.name: Brulden
rites.text: Brulden is a grounded concept of stacked passive disciplines that take hold the moment a wearer bears a sworn sigil, and some of them only wake when a kinetic cue, such as shifting stance, is performed. Its practitioners fuse two learned rites into one, occasionally birthing a new rite that carries a latent auto-effect. The discipline is modest in scale, bounded by what a single body can channel.

rites.name: Morurdode
rites.text: Morurdode is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld setting, a quiet system of passive enhancements that bind to worn cloth, carried blades, guards, and charms. Its wardings are tuned to the rhythm of a bearer's stance, so they wake only when the wearer shifts into a new posture.

rites.name: Brordunen
rites.text: Brordunen is a Grounded-realm concept in Thudarneld's E6 era, a sworn set of seven stacking battle-disciplines that a wielder can bind to gear and wear like armour. Each discipline loosens or tightens a single bound resource, so the wielder must choose which sacrifices and bonuses to carry into a fight.

rites.name: Haluston
rites.text: Haluston is a grounded, low-grade concept of a mantle-forged alloy plate that hums when worn and quietly steadies the wearer's footing. In an era of compact craft and modest engines, it is prized for turning ordinary armor into something that answers the body's rhythm.

rites.name: Fenornalde
rites.text: Fenornalde is a grounded concept of tuned attire and gear that reshapes a wielder's reflexes, guard, and combat rhythm once fitted. Its auto-effects surface quietly, rewarding careful layering of garments, blades, and charms rather than raw power. Practitioners in the Thudarneld courts treat each new fitting as a small negotiation between habit and instinct.

rites.name: Tarnorock
rites.text: Tarnorock is a grounded concept of a bonded resonance-cloak worn by wardens of the Thudarneld highlands, which hums faintly when its wearer stands in still air. Its makers wove dormant tuning threads into the fabric so that each mended seam could be reactivated in sequence. Wardens say a fully attuned cloak can briefly steady a falling avalanche line.

rites.name: Fenustelde
rites.text: Fenustelde is a grounded concept that governs passive enhancements woven into worn gear and carried implements, which stir into effect the moment they are fitted to a bearer. Certain techniques can be fused together, occasionally yielding a new trait lodged within them, and some traits remain dormant until a particular shift in stance or role unlocks them.

rites.name: Halorock
rites.text: Halorock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse: a set of resonant plating and cords worn by the Sable Corps that reshape a wearer's reflexes and endurance. Its wearers hasten the recovery of dormant stances and shrug off a wide range of hostile tampering with their senses and nerves.

rites.name: Fenuradath
rites.text: Fenuradath is a Grounded concept of layered sigils that bind to a wearer's gear and wake only when a set condition is met, such as a shift in the bearer's stance. Its lore holds that each dormant seal stores a fragment of an old thunderstorm, released by a single clean strike. The concept appears in the third age of the Thudarneld cycle as a method of tuning ordinary armor into quiet engines.

rites.name: Broldock
rites.text: Broldock is a grounded concept of passive resonance-tuned gear in Thudarneld, where equipment woven from humming alloy quietly alters the wearer's reflexes once fitted. Some tunings can be fused into the same mechanism to produce a rare secondary effect, and certain settings only awaken when the bearer shifts between sets of gear.

rites.name: Joroston
rites.text: Joroston is a grounded concept of passive attunements that wake when worn or wielded, granting a bearer quiet advantages within a single realm. Its effects surface on their own or when a particular shift in stance occurs, and they can be grafted onto other techniques by a careful joining. The entry emphasizes modest, layered benefits over spectacle.

rites.name: Thenolden
rites.text: Thenolden is a grounded concept of passive mantle-wards that bind to a wearer's gear and wake on their own when the tide of a fight turns. Its keepers swap their ward-sets mid-combat, and each shift releases a stored surge that a veteran can aim with care.

rites.name: Kelerde
rites.text: Kelerde is a grounded, passive discipline of the Thudarneld powers, a concept that binds a practitioner's resolve to small mechanical habits: tightening a grip, pacing a breath, re-seating a strap. Its adepts learn to layer several such habits so they activate on their own when a set of conditions is met, such as a change of stance. The art is taught as a quiet craft rather than a spectacle.

rites.name: Pelaste
rites.text: Pelaste is a passive mechanism of Thudarneld's grounded powers, bound to worn garb, blades, wards and trinkets, that quietly bends a wielder's tempo whenever their chosen aspect shifts. Its effects are modest by design, so that each worn piece reshapes the rhythm of a duel rather than its outcome. Practitioners prize it for turning ordinary gear into a second, silent discipline.

rites.name: Tarnuston
rites.text: Tarnuston is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe: a cadence of quiet resonances that settle into worn charms, carved trinkets, and folded cloaks. Its wearers gain small automatic boons that wake when a certain stance or rhythm is met, such as turning a shoulder or drawing a breath. Its effects are modest, but they bind closely to the bearer's habits.

rites.name: Croneld
rites.text: Croneld is a quiet ward-scribe of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, who inscribes warding sigils onto cart wheels and gate hinges. Their marks are said to hold a rattling wheel steady, though they have never been tested under real strain.

rites.name: Tarnastene
rites.text: Tarnastene is a grounded, ash-coated warrior-smith of the Thudarneld sphere whose blades are forged by burning their own marrow into the metal. Each strike carries a cost borne in flesh rather than magic, and the smiths of the valley regard her as both protector and omen.

rites.name: Thonock
rites.text: Thonock is a grounded, bell-shaped iron golem of the Grey Marches, built by the stonecutters' guild to keep mountain passes clear of rockslides. Its heavy stamp can shake loose a hillside, but every blow drains the stored ember-core in its chest, so it rarely fights for long.

rites.name: Drerden
rites.text: Drerden is a sly, clockwork-hearted riddle-engine of the Grounded realm, built in the sixth age to guard the orchard-markets of Thudarneld. It hums with coiled brass tension and answers every trespasser with a single bounded gesture of mechanical arithmetic.

rites.name: Thulden
rites.text: Thulden is a gleaming ceramic spire-drone that hovers over the salt flats of Thudarneld, seeding the air with coiled pneumatic darts that rattle like hail when released. Its pilots call it a mother of bees, and it is said to remember every song hummed beneath it.

rites.name: Thorardon
rites.text: Thorardon is a sealed bronze resonance-lantern used by the Grounded tide-clerks of Thudarneld's sixth era to calm restless river spirits. Its tolling can shatter the hulls of riverboats and bring down a timber bridge when misused.

rites.name: Tharnordon
rites.text: Tharnordon is a grounded warlord-engineer of the E6 era, seven years into a reign built on salvaged war machines and rolling mechanized barrages. Its signature is a sky-filling volley of guided cannon shells that trail glowing ember-lines across the horizon.
