rites.name: Tarnodene
rites.text: Tarnodene is a grounded concept of a mechanical boring device fitted to the lattice-armored trawlers of the Thudarneld shipyards, which can tunnel through solid rock in seconds. Its engine is cooled by a fluid that is sold for medicinal use in the lower quarters. Its operators are known for working in pairs, one at the drill and one at the spindle.

rites.name: Dradar
rites.text: Dradar is a wandering sentient stone that inhabits the lowlands of Thudarneld, shaping the earth with a single thought. It can swallow entire villages and then release them as new stone gardens, leaving behind a silent, humming resonance that heals the land. Though it appears inert, its presence alters the flow of time in the surrounding soil, granting crops a brief burst of accelerated growth.

rites.name: Halorestath
rites.text: Halorestath is a grounded, era-E6 attack-and-mech concept from Thudarneld, a hovering war-engine that folds its own plating into a dense cloud of sensor drones. Its signature act is a rapid volley of ten glowing slugs that trail thin pale wakes across a battlefield. It is an old, reliable weapon, mostly used to suppress and break up infantry formations.

rites.name: Joreldock
rites.text: Joreldock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sixth-era power whose strikes are measured in the scale of a single building or vehicle. Its signature technique channels stored kinetic force through its body in a single rushing motion. Its durability is limited, and it relies on quick repositioning rather than endurance.

rites.name: Thodesten
rites.text: Thodesten is a mountain-sized ironclad war engine that drifts through the Grounded realm's ash-choked skies, bristling with cannon mounts and drone bays. Its crew calls it the Last Patience because it fires only when every other option has failed. Its heavy armor can absorb blows that would split a city street, though not for long.

rites.name: Pelestune
rites.text: Pelestune is a drifting archive-spirit of the Grounded realm, a thing of rusted lantern-light and faded ink that remembers every instruction ever carved into the valley walls. When its keepers stir it, it strikes outward with a bright, humming pulse that rattles the nearby stones, and it keeps fighting through a pulse of its own mending.

rites.name: Keluraston
rites.text: Keluraston is a crystalline sentinel-engine that drifts through the frozen dunes of Thudarneld's northern wastes, awakened only when cold winds carry the scent of sparks. It answers heat with a single blistering discharge that scorches the ground it stands upon.

rites.name: Dreldock
rites.text: Dreldock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld universe, a hulking iron golem built by the sixth era's artisans to plow through collapsed mountain passes. It hauls ore and clears rubble across the highlands, and its hydraulic knuckles can split bedrock when its overheated core is vented.

rites.name: Fenadeld
rites.text: Fenadeld is a grounded concept of a hardened warrior who gathers strength across several strikes before unleashing it. Its stored force grows with each successive blow, and its final stroke cracks stone and shakes the arena floor.

rites.name: Brardath
rites.text: Brardath is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the E6 era, a mechanical war-dog whose plating was salvaged from a collapsed foundry district. Its lattice of coiled tension springs can bring it to bursts of speed and a single crushing strike that pounds stone to gravel.

rites.name: Tharnon
rites.text: Tharnon is a grounded war-engine of the E6 era, a towering walker whose forge-hearts were tuned by rival foundries to outlast any single battlefield. It is built to strike hard and to endure the return fire of an entire siege line.

rites.name: Crenar
rites.text: Crenar is a grounded, era E6 concept from Thudarneld, a world where tactical drones and armored prototypes share the battlefield with ordinary soldiers. Its name serves as the entry's identity, and its designers treated each unit as a field asset rather than a legend. Crenar's signature weapon is a coordinated volley system that fires in measured bursts, built to suppress rather than level.

rites.name: Jorerodath
rites.text: Jorerodath is a bell-shaped resonance pattern that hums through the marsh-roots of Thudarneld, sustained by the silt-choirs that drift beneath the reeds. It is known for its patient, rhythmic tremors that shake loose the stone foundations of old watchtowers.

rites.name: Jorastenar
rites.text: Jorastenar is a grounded, pre-industrial craft-shield of Thudarneld, hammered from bog-iron and bound with a resin that stores the wearer's breath. Its bearers raise it to catch falling masonry and rockslides, and in the old wars the bearers' lines were said to hold back avalanches.

rites.name: Peleste
rites.text: Peleste is a Grounded-realm concept from the E6 era, an age-seven thundering-clockwork shrine-engine whose gears hum with stored lightning. Its mechanism can unleash a sustained burst of storm energy that splits stone and rattles nearby towers for a long stretch of time.

rites.name: Keluste
rites.text: Keluste is a grounded concept of a sky-bound hunting platform that drifts above the cloud shelves of Thudarneld, its crew firing timed volleys of heavy bolts at migrating storm-beasts. Its wind-harp hull sings a low note that the local herders treat as an omen of weather. In the seventh age its guns are mostly quiet, and the platform is kept aloft mainly for signaling.

rites.name: Joranoldath
rites.text: Joranoldath is a grounded, humble warden-spirit of the seventh age of Thudarneld, who keeps the pale ridges of the Ostrel Hills where old beasts sleep beneath the frost. Its tread is slow, its temper patient, and it is trusted by the herders who leave it offerings of salt bread each harvest. In rare fits of protective fury it can strike the stones with a crackling bolt of electrified force that rolls across the valley floor.

rites.name: Joronurdath
rites.text: Joronurdath is a fallen warden-engine of the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a silent bronze colossus that once guarded the ferry-roads between the drowned valleys. It answers only to the old tide-bells, and when they ring it unleashes a barrage of glowing salt-spears across the marshes.

rites.name: Brestarnath
rites.text: Brestarnath is a mechanical hunter-drone of the Thudarneld concept realm's Grounded era, built to track and dismantle wild machines in the dust-choked salt flats. Its signature is a rapid-fire volley of ten glowing slag-shells that trail sparks as they fall, each rattling loose the armor of anything they strike.

rites.name: Croradath
rites.text: Croradath is a rust-plated siege engine of the Grounded realm's Era E6, built by the Thudarneld guilds to haul ore across collapsing mountain passes. Its operators are known for cannon-volleys that bracket a target with overlapping fire, each shell carrying a bright tracer that marks its arc. Seven years into service, the machine is reputed to be more dangerous to its own crew than to any foe.

rites.name: Tharnar
rites.text: Tharnar is a grounded war-automaton forged in the seventh age of the Thudarneld cycle, built to hold fortress gates against armored siege columns. Its signature defense is a rotating shield of compressed air that can knock a charging soldier off their feet, and its arms carry crude but reliable hydraulic hammers.

rites.name: Droreld
rites.text: Droreld is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the E6 era of Thudarneld, a realm of pure powers rather than bodies. Its authority rests on a rotating arsenal of coordinated salvos, bait-and-trap bursts, and a rising mist of stored heat. It is a low-stakes, human-scale presence whose strength lies in precision and timing.

rites.name: Morostude
rites.text: Morostude is a concept of stored tension, a pressure-bound resonance that a practitioner in the Grounded realm can coil into a single strained surge. It is measured in the era's workshop tradition as a spring that refuses to unwind until the moment it is provoked.

rites.name: Kelustar
rites.text: Kelustar is a resonant tuning method used by the Thudarneld cartographers to chart seismic faults. It lets a practitioner sense and nudge the hidden stress of bedrock, releasing it in controlled bursts.

rites.name: Drelduren
rites.text: Drelduren is a quiet mental technique taught in the grounded hill-monasteries of Thudarneld, letting a practitioner call a shared rhythm into stone and steel. Its practitioners are known for steadying nervous crowds and cracking old foundations when pushed.

rites.name: Drestath
rites.text: Drestath is a coiling, bronze-scaled tail-serpent that drags whole hillsides into its orbit whenever it lashes out, a creature the locals of Thudarneld treat as a weather event rather than a beast. It is seven centuries old and has grown slow but terrifyingly precise in its strikes.

rites.name: Morelde
rites.text: Morelde is a gravel-throated tidewalker of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, known for its tireless marches across salt flats. Its kind arrived in the seventh age and still carries the silver-ribbed shells of the old sky-cities. It can hurl its shell-bone spines with enough force to split a granite bluff.

rites.name: Cronedar
rites.text: Cronedar is a concept of a grounded, era-six artifact-creature that lashes out with flexible barbed appendages. Its strikes are nimble but unremarkable, built to snare and drain rather than to crush.

rites.name: Haloraldath
rites.text: Haloraldath is a grounded, nearly mindless hunting coil of pale bone-flesh that lives in the cracked foundations of Thudarneld's sunken quarters, where it drags prey down through the mud. It strikes by flinging rope-like limbs that wrap, squeeze, and draw out the warmth of anything caught.

rites.name: Peloste
rites.text: Peloste is a cliffside carnival-automaton of the Grounded realm, built from salvaged clockwork and spirit-glass in the seventh age of the E6 cycle. It is said to hum a tune that calms nearby storm-beasts, and its gears can unleash a short, violent spiral of compressed wind.

rites.name: Croldenon
rites.text: Croldenon is a drifting concept-engine fabricated in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a sealed-off remnant of the sixth era that hums with tuned resonance. Its warning chimes cycle through hundreds of pre-recorded sequences, each one signalling a different kind of weather-shift in the valley below. Locals treat its tones as scripture and rarely approach its rusted gantries.

rites.name: Fenestock
rites.text: Fenestock is a sealed-hull glass lattice that hums through the grounded reaches of Thudarneld, serving as a navigational beacon for itinerant caravans. Its chime carries for kilometers, and it is said to answer when called by the right name.

rites.name: Morurde
rites.text: Morurde is a sleek, unmanned drill-skiff of the Grounded realm, built by the mining guilds of E6 to bore through stubborn bedrock for ore veins. Its signature maneuver is a spiral burrow that cuts a clean shaft through rock, a feat that makes it both prized and feared among the tunnel towns.

rites.name: Fenordere
rites.text: Fenordere is a grounded concept of a sacrificial combat art in the Thudarneld omniverse, where warriors trade a portion of their own vitality for devastating force. Practitioners learn to bind their life into strikes that ripple outward, and the cost grows heavier with each mastered level.

rites.name: Halasten
rites.text: Halasten is a quiet discipline of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, taught in the seventh age of the sixth era by hermits who bind small powers into everyday tools. Its practitioners learn to store the force of a falling stone or a blown ember and release it on command. The art is valued for precision rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Moradath
rites.text: Moradath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a horned hunter-spirit that stalks the cold fringes of the age of Mordrel's wardens. Its power lies in precise sensing and quick, bruising strikes rather than cataclysm.

rites.name: Halenurdar
rites.text: Halenurdar is a concept of quiet resonance drawn from the old tuning-stones of Thudarneld's sixth era, a force that teaches stones to hum in the key of their makers. Its bearers can coax a single ridge of rock into a brief, bright chime that shatters what sits atop it. Within the Grounded realm it is considered a gentle art, though its seventh-age scholars argue over its limits.

rites.name: Brunaldeld
rites.text: Brunaldeld is a grounded concept of hand-carried clockwork tools that channel a single borrowed force, such as a sharpened gust or a pressed charge of heat. Its strongest users can crack stone walls or fell a stout oak, but nothing beyond the reach of a mid-sized siege engine.

rites.name: Kelalduden
rites.text: Kelalduden is a reckoning-thorn grown on the windward cliffs of Thudarneld, whose sap can be drawn into a single brittle bolt of crackling force. Village keepers in the sixth age learned to lash its resin into crude shields and hurled glow-stones that sting like a thrown fist.

rites.name: Halade
rites.text: Halade is a grounded hermit-warrior of the E6 era who trains on the cracked plains of Thudarneld, striking rocks and beasts with bare fists and a heavy staff. Locals say a single disciplined blow can split a boulder the size of a cart.

rites.name: Pelaldunon
rites.text: Pelaldunon is a grounded sorcerer-engineer who channels elemental forces through brass resonators sewn into his cloak, able to stir a storm or split stone with a single chord. His tower-workshop is said to have been built to hold the echo of a thunderclap that never quite faded.

rites.name: Fenoldedar
rites.text: Fenoldedar is a grounded, era-E6 concept of a fossilised reptile-ghost that stalks the abandoned quarries of Thudarneld, its bony frame creaking as it drags stones behind it. Hunters say it hums low before every strike, and the lichen it leaves behind glows faintly for weeks.

rites.name: Fenadornar
rites.text: Fenadornar is a ring of drifting thorn-bells that hang over the gardens of Thudarneld, chiming in colours no one has named. When its toll rings out, sleeping monsters wake and turn their claws toward whichever village last sang.

rites.name: Cruldock
rites.text: Cruldock is a stoic, mountain-dwelling crustacean-smith who forges shell-plated armor for travelers crossing the Ashgrind Pass. Each piece is tempered in tidal brine and sealed with a glaze that deflects one of the eight elemental currents. Its craftsmen claim the glaze can turn a blow back onto its wielder.

rites.name: Dradeste
rites.text: Dradeste is a grounded, era-six artifact-heirloom that a village smith forges from the stubborn iron of a fallen meteor, tempered to the weight of a bronze bell. Its wielder gains brute strength by sacrificing a measure of cunning, and the blade's ringing hum can be heard for leagues. It has carved through rockfall and gates, though never a house's foundation without the wielder's own sinew.

rites.name: Drusterne
rites.text: Drusterne is a grounded concept of a hushing bell-charm, a small brass ward carried by travelers in the Thudarneld valleys. When rung, it releases a brief shockwave that can topple a wooden cart or split a stone lintel.

rites.name: Cruldeste
rites.text: Cruldeste is a grounded concept of hunting-bow craft, a weapon-art passed between clans of stone-dwelling archers in the Thudarneld highlands. Its practitioners string bows of living sinew and loose volleys that can split a boulder or pin a charging boar.

rites.name: Fenestuden
rites.text: Fenestuden is a dwelling-spirit born from the fogged glass of greenhouse domes in the terraced valleys of Thudarneld, where it hums through cracked panes and bends light into shifting sigils. Villagers leave it offerings of rainwater and crushed seed-husks, and in return it warns them of frost, hail, and storms rolling over the ridges. Its powers are quiet and mostly defensive, though it can briefly shatter a wall of hail into glittering shards.

rites.name: Morunath
rites.text: Morunath is a quiet ceremonial lens-keeper of the Thudarneld cycle, whose sealed glass vessels store the breath of sleeping valleys. In the seventh age of the grounded realm, Morunath is said to unbind a single vessel only once a generation, and the released light can reshape the land around it.

rites.name: Dreldock
rites.text: Dreldock is a grounded, sun-scorched wasteland of hollow peaks and rusted machinery, where ancient war-engines still stir beneath the dunes. Its inhabitants are small, hardy folk who reckon power by how well one can strike and endure rather than by any cosmic measure. The region's great relics are feared mostly for their ability to crack the earth.

rites.name: Dranath
rites.text: Dranath is a grounded, era-E6 concept: a sand-bound tide-drummer whose rhythmic stomps shake loose the earth beneath marching armies. Its displays rarely exceed a collapsed barricade, though it can endure a rockslide that would bury lesser beings.

rites.name: Kelurardath
rites.text: Kelurardath is a tide-binding concept in the Thudarneld cosmos, a discipline taught by reef-wardens who weave salt currents into brief shields and lashing tides. Its practitioners can gather water into a single crushing surge, though only in the wetlands of their Grounded realm.

rites.name: Tharden
rites.text: Tharden is a stoneshaper-titan of the Grounded realm, a slow colossus who sleeps for centuries inside the bedrock of its homeland and wakes only when the rivers change course. Its cracking footfalls are said to reshape valleys, and it is revered as the keeper of the land's patience.

rites.name: Moruldon
rites.text: Moruldon is a quiet concept of coiled ember-glass tuned to the rhythm of old tides in the realm of Thudarneld. Its bearers draw small bursts of heat and light from the stone during seasonal festivals. Its records are kept in the marshlands of the E6 era.

rites.name: Druldar
rites.text: Druldar is a grounded, low-tech tinkerer of the Thudarneld drylands who builds clockwork shields and hurls clay pellets to defend villages from raiding beasts. Its feats are modest in scale, suited to a world where machines still run on muscle and steam.

rites.name: Joronurdeld
rites.text: Joronurdeld is a grounded concept from the E6 era of the Thudarneld omniverse, a living wellspring of carefully measured elemental strikes that its wielders learned to channel through slow, deliberate rituals. It was never meant to level anything larger than a village, and its practitioners regarded overreach as the surest way to lose control of it.

rites.name: Pelardar
rites.text: Pelardar is a grounded weather-hewn beast of the E6 age, a lumbering creature whose hide is studded with crystalline barbs that crackle with stored static. It settles disputes in its valley by rubbing its back against cliffs and sending sheets of lightning across the ridges. The valley folk trade its shed barbs as ornaments and fear the nights when its moods turn stormy.

rites.name: Fenedarath
rites.text: Fenedarath is a grounded concept of a grand arena-duelist order whose members channel stored bodily momentum through ritual combat gear. Their most famous duel-style, the Pendulum Rite, turns a single swung weight into a crushing wave of force felt across an entire training yard. Practitioners train for decades to control these shattering blows without harming bystanders.

rites.name: Pelordalden
rites.text: Pelordalden is a quiet field of drifting lantern-moss in the Thudarneld reaches, known to its keepers as a place where old songs hold the soil together. Its inhabitants harvest the moss to kindle small illuminations and to mend fences and gates that have been worn by time. Across seven ages it has remained a modest, dependable presence in its region.

rites.name: Crerne
rites.text: Crerne is a concept of a grounded, rough-hewn wandering smith who forges tools that remember the hands which held them. Its craft takes the form of heavy hammer-strikes that split rock and sparks that scatter across wet clay. Its legend is that it once turned an entire quarry wall into hollow bells.

rites.name: Brudoldon
rites.text: Brudoldon is a fading ritual-craft of the Thudarneld reaches, a discipline of small wards and borrowed warmth passed between village hearths in the Grounded realm. Its practitioners shape modest pulses of force and light, enough to turn a millstone or dazzle a raiding party, but never more.

rites.name: Kelordeld
rites.text: Kelordeld is a quiet branch of the Thudarneld order that teaches apprentices to bend small domestic forces into useful tricks. Its practitioners are known for mending broken kettles, calming restless dogs, and guiding stray breezes around village chimneys. Their most famous feat is a gentle rooftop gust that once steadied a collapsing barn.

rites.name: Pelastelden
rites.text: Pelastelden is a grounded, era-old fighting art of the Thudarneld deep-hills, where practitioners strike with elemental pulses drawn from the earth and water. Its masters are known for rhythmic multi-hit barrages that can strike several times in quick succession. The art is taught as a discipline of patience rather than raw force.

rites.name: Tarnulden
rites.text: Tarnulden is a grounded, fading relic of an old tabletop-scale rulebook discovered in the ruins of a mountain monastery. Its pages list elemental strikes, bile-spraying toads and tentacled wraiths, all bound to a dry, rule-bound cosmos where a single blow rattles only stone and bone.

rites.name: Crolde
rites.text: Crolde is a grounded, gentle-minded creature of a seven-year-old age cycle that hums in the frequency of old stone walls. Its people use the hum to coax water up from dry hillsides and to bring down loose cliffs before they fall on villages. Its power stays modest, enough to reshape a ridge and nothing more.

rites.name: Jorerock
rites.text: Jorerock is a grounded stone-and-moss titan that sleeps beneath the peaks of Thudarneld, waking only when avalanches thunder down its flanks. Its hide is layered like sediment and it fights by rolling its own mass into the slopes it inhabits.

rites.name: Crulde
rites.text: Crulde is a grounded, mortal-scale tool-maker and fighter of the E6 era, known in its local powers for a stock of rough combat tricks rather than cosmic might. Its strikes are measured in the strength of a trained arm, a stone thrown by a skilled hand, or a sudden gust off a cliff face.

rites.name: Moroldon
rites.text: Moroldon is a cliff-dwelling beast of the Grounded realm that slumbers beneath frozen ridges and wakes only when the mountain wind shifts. Its hide is covered in stone-hard scales that can absorb blows, and its slow, deliberate strikes carry the weight of falling rock.

rites.name: Kelesten
rites.text: Kelesten is a grounded concept of a shaped-clay construct animated by a stone-carved knot of runic inscriptions that bloom into a pattern of pale fire when it moves. Its power lies in brittle, controlled strikes rather than raw force, and it is said to stop mid-motion whenever its carved names are read aloud. Tales of its sudden stillness are common in the lowland markets.

rites.name: Thane
rites.text: Thane is a conceptual lattice of wind-bound sigils that a grounded scholar-artisan in the Thudarneld reading-hall draws in chalk to bind gusts for sailing and kilns. Its practitioners are celebrated for sparing, careful use, and its faint hum is said to calm restless children.

rites.name: Drurnock
rites.text: Drurnock is a grounded bulwark of Thudarneld's sixth era, a stone-hided warden whose slow, stubborn strikes have shaped the valleys where its kind once held the line. Villagers tell of its fists breaking boulders and its tremors toppling watchtowers, though it rarely fights unless provoked.

rites.name: Kelarden
rites.text: Kelarden is a clockwork fortress-bell that ring-tolls across the grounded plains of the E6 age, its chimes shaking loose boulder fields for leagues. Its keepers rang it to call scattered settlements together after the long winters, and its strongest peal can split a hillside into rubble.

rites.name: Joronath
rites.text: Joronath is a grounded concept in the realm of Thudarneld, a hardy warrior-beast whose hide and fists strike like falling boulders. It channels the stubborn pulse of the earth into bursts of crushing force and endures blows that would fell a village house.

rites.name: Branath
rites.text: Branath is a quiet bell-tower of the Grounded realm, its hollow iron chime said to ring when a sleeping mountain turns over. Its keepers train apprentices to read the vibrations in stone, so the tower has stood through seven ages of tremors. Its strongest recorded act was a single resonant toll that shook a valley-wide landslide loose.

rites.name: Tharneld
rites.text: Tharneld is a grounded, seven-age-old tidal engine of the Thudarneld reaches, a slow machine of salt-cut stone that drinks the rain to power its gears. Its keepers measure its strength by how many sailing hulls its wake can lift from shoal water. It has never been known to exceed a single village's worth of force.

rites.name: Tarnurde
rites.text: Tarnurde is a drifting bell of hardened rainwater that sings across the Grounded realm's flooded plains of Thudarneld. Its chime can unmake a wall of stone or a stretch of mud. It is young at seven, yet already feared by the fishing villages that hear it at dusk.

rites.name: Pelerdunar
rites.text: Pelerdunar is a grounded, seven-age-old warding craft practiced by the herders of Thudarneld's high moors, who etch sigils into stone to calm thunderstorms. Its masters can hush a gathering storm and turn lightning aside from a village, though the work is slow and exhausting.

rites.name: Braldar
rites.text: Braldar is a grounded, weathered tinker-warrior of the Thudarneld frontier who fights with salvaged cannons and wooden shields. Within the reach of ordinary ballistics and crude siege engines, Braldar is famed as the one who breaks the walls of forts.

rites.name: Thurnen
rites.text: Thurnen is a quiet, slow-turning engine of gravity-bent metal that the Grounded folk of Thudarneld use to lift grain barges over their flooded marsh-terraces. Its builders are said to be long gone, but the hum it gives off on cold mornings still summons the herd-birds back to its shade.

rites.name: Thuldock
rites.text: Thuldock is a rust-colored clockwork bastion that drifts above the cloud-sea of its world, powered by the slow turning of seven great brass gears. Its engineers, the Quiet Wardens, keep its engines humming with copper songs and never let anyone climb past the third ring.

rites.name: Brurdock
rites.text: Brurdock is a bracing tonic-and-rite practice of the Thudarneld peoples, a grounding discipline that teaches a practitioner to draw steady strength from the earth beneath them. Its adepts are known for enduring long vigils and for shaking loose rockfalls with a single stamp of a heavy boot.

rites.name: Drurdestath
rites.text: Drurdestath is a sprawling fortress-library bolted onto the underside of a drifting moon, its vaults holding ten thousand rotating relics that hum in sympathy with the tides below. Its keepers guard a single bell-shaped resonator that can shake loose the foundations of a town in a single toll. Ancient archivists wrote that the hall remembers every sound it has ever heard.

rites.name: Tarnurode
rites.text: Tarnurode is a fading lattice of ash-woven sigils that Thudarneld's wardens once used to bind distant storm-spirits into their own bodies. Each ward it gives can be worn as a drifting, pale tracery of light that tears the air when called upon. It is a concept of old craft, measured against the modest reach of a grounded age.

rites.name: Tarnanolde
rites.text: Tarnanolde is a dormant grafting rite in the Thudarneld cosmos, a bargain of borrowed bone and sealed oath stored in lattice-carved reliquaries. Its practitioners call upon it to lend a stolen structure for a moment of vast leverage before the vessel splinters.

rites.name: Thurderock
rites.text: Thurderock is a sentient boulder that hums with stored storm-light, born when a lightning-struck cliff fused with the ancient spirit of a mountain range. It hurls itself across valleys at astonishing speed and cracks open stone walls with a single resonant strike.

rites.name: Fenurnar
rites.text: Fenurnar is a silver-threaded lattice of thinking-glass that hums through the ruins of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, lending its weave to whatever scholar or machine seeks to bind it. Its strongest pulse can topple a ridge of stone or drown a valley in a single breath of light, though it tires quickly and must be left dormant to recover.

rites.name: Crorath
rites.text: Crorath is a hollow ember-thorn of the Thudarneld outer marches, a concept of a spirit that feeds on the lingering heat of dead campfires. In its age-seven cycle it can dim a village's hearth and gather that stolen warmth into a single scorching lance.

rites.name: Pelunon
rites.text: Pelunon is a quiet concept of hushed resonance, a tuned hum that gathers in still water and loosens the bonds between stones. Its practitioners trace sigils across cold lakes to coax the sleeping tremor awake. Its gentle force is measured in ways that rarely exceed the reach of a single village.

rites.name: Tarnernock
rites.text: Tarnernock is a grounded, long-lived artifact-guardian of the Thudarneld order, a stout iron-bound sentinel whose gears have ticked through seven ages of quiet watch. It is revered less for power than for patience, and the realm's wardens still consult its ledger-plates before any major decision.

rites.name: Morodeld
rites.text: Morodeld is a grounded concept of a drifting reef-spirit whose hum can gather the tides of an entire sea into a single crushing surge. It is seldom seen, for it prefers the quiet shallows where it tends the kelp-lanterns that light the seabed.

rites.name: Crorde
rites.text: Crorde is a sleeping-tide discipline of the Thudarneld archives, a practice of bending quiet mental rhythms into brief ripples of force. Its adepts teach that the tide remembers every breath, and they train by stilling their pulse until the water of their own blood answers. It is taught only in the lantern-halls of the drowned coast.

rites.name: Crerduston
rites.text: Crerduston is a drifting spire-city of brass and lichen suspended above the cloud-seas of Thudarneld, kept aloft by the hum of its ancient turbines. Its engineers are famous for compact siege-engines that can shatter stone walls and split heavy gates in a single shot. The city's guild hall jealously guards the blueprints for these machines.

rites.name: Drurnock
rites.text: Drurnock is a grounded, seven-age-old iron-bodied warden of the Thudarneld barrens, a figure who holds back avalanches with a braced stance and a sealed vow. Its era is remembered for slow, stubborn endurance rather than spectacle, and its strength lies in what it can absorb and redirect.

rites.name: Thesteld
rites.text: Thesteld is a ceremonial bell-forged shield-blade carried by the wardens of the Hollow Choir in the drowned city of Varrowmere. Its strikes are measured by the cadence of the tolling bells rather than by force, and it is said to sing louder with each sigil it breaks.

rites.name: Crernulden
rites.text: Crernulden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting: a lattice of tuned resonance-brands that fighters carve into their forearms to unleash bursts of stored momentum. Each brand has a fixed attuning glyph and a wind or flame affinity that cannot be rewritten once etched. Its strongest recorded release could topple a stout watchtower in a single pulse.

rites.name: Morudornon
rites.text: Morudornon is a conceptual grounded-realm marvel from the Thudarneld omniverse, a stratified layer of mineral rings that hum with pressure-tuned resonance. Its wardens treat each ring as a ledger of stored force, spending it in measured strikes that keep the crust balanced.

rites.name: Pelurdasten
rites.text: Pelurdasten is a stone-backed fortress-shrine that hums with a low pulse, and its inhabitants draw small measures of force from its bell-like resonance. Its guardians rarely strike with more than a single hammer's weight, relying instead on timing and the sigils carved into their gauntlets.

rites.name: Fenerath
rites.text: Fenerath is a clockwork lattice of brass rings that hum with stored tide-energy, used by the cartographers of the drowned coast to measure and reshape shorelines. Its three-stage ascent unlocks progressively heavier tidal tuning, letting a single bearer redirect entire harbor currents.

rites.name: Fenanure
rites.text: Fenanure is a frost-and-silence concept in the grounded era of Thudarneld, a cold sigil that the ancient ice-wardens of the northern tundra inscribed upon their hunting spears. Its power is measured in the slow stillness it leaves behind, not in explosive force, and it is rarely drawn outside of ritual combat.

rites.name: Keludock
rites.text: Keludock is a Grounded-realm concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six skill-system that arranges combat actions as ranked charges drawn from a shared reservoir. Each charge a practitioner spends builds a timed burst of force, with stronger bursts costing more and weaker ones restoring quickly. The system's practitioners learn to balance spent charges against the moment of release.

rites.name: Jorenodon
rites.text: Jorenodon is a frost-kindled sigil-engine from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a clockwork lattice of rime-scribed cogs that stores cold in brass reservoirs. Its keepers vent that stored chill in a single focused gust that can crack a stone bridge but leaves nearby farmhouses untouched.

rites.name: Jorestock
rites.text: Jorestock is a frost-binding concept in the Grounded realm of the Thudarneld omniverse, a crystalline lattice that spreads cold through the air around its bearer. Practitioners in the E6 era treat it as a low-tier discipline, drawing its power from the body's own reserves rather than from any external source.

rites.name: Morunon
rites.text: Morunon is a grounded, second-tier frost-weaving discipline of the E6 era in Thudarneld, taught in mountain monasteries where students learn to draw heat from a victim's blood and fold it into a crackling white cold. Its practitioners are prized as field medics and siege-breakers rather than as catastrophic forces, since the craft burns through the caster's own stamina with every use.

rites.name: Fenerurdeld
rites.text: Fenerurdeld is a concept of ordered combat rhythm in the Thudarneld, where practitioners store charge in measured segments and spend them to act. Each deed draws a fixed count of these segments, weapon-forms usually costing more than channelled arts, while restorative rites cost a standard tally regardless of their source. Every strike carries a tagged affinity and a glyph, and these tags cannot be altered once set.

rites.name: Crerneld
rites.text: Crerneld is a hand-forged resonance blade bound to the old tide-stones of the drowned city of Vell, unlocking a surging counterstrike when its wielder holds steady. Its bearer can channel stored harmonics into a single devastating strike that shatters stone and steel alike.

rites.name: Kelornelden
rites.text: Kelornelden is a concept-realm power of the Grounded tier in the sixth era of Thudarneld, a rhythm of strikes that must be paid for in stored momentum. Its practitioners bank effort into a slow-filling reservoir and release it as a single decisive blow whose force is set by the weapon they hold. Blows of this kind favor the body over the mind, sharpening the arm while dulling the spell-weaving that others of their kind rely on.

rites.name: Drone
rites.text: Drone is a grounded, mass-produced combat automaton from the Thudarneld era, built to hover above fields and deliver precise hits from altitude. Its frame is cheap and light, so it can be lost by the dozen without much grief among its operators.

rites.name: Drestudar
rites.text: Drestudar is a tuning-fork-shaped relic that hums whenever the grounded settlements of Thudarneld fall into quarrel, and its low note can steady a crumbling wall or shake loose a rooftop's tiles. Its keepers, the Quiet Wardens of Hollow Reach, bind it to their oaths and teach apprentices to strike it only in matched pairs.

rites.name: Tharuldath
rites.text: Tharuldath is a ceremonial hand-forged blade of the Grounded realm, born in the third age of the Thudarneld cycle, whose edge is said to channel the stored oaths of its wielders. Its keepers measure its power by how many fallen bridges it can cut through in a single stroke. It rests within the common armories of the Grounded locales, prized more for its reliability than its spectacle.

rites.name: Fenardoron
rites.text: Fenardoron is a shifting bell-tower spirit of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, said to ring once for every oath its bearer breaks. Its tolling can split stone and send a rush of wind through entire valleys, yet it grows quieter with every mortal it protects.

rites.name: Morenorath
rites.text: Morenorath is a tiered system of combat maneuvers in the grounded era Thudarneld, where practitioners spend stored momentum reserves to unleash strikes or restore allies. Each maneuver carries a fixed elemental affinity and a symbolic mark that never change once forged. Weaker variants of the same maneuver lose force when repeated, when used on depleted targets, or when performed far from the practitioner's anchor point.

rites.name: Keloraldon
rites.text: Keloraldon is a grounded concept of a sealed command-lattice used by the Thudarneld cartographers to coordinate their tidal bell-towers. Each act draws a measured quantum of stored harmonic tension, which the lattice spends in fixed portions per invocation. Its true strength is modest, but its precision lets a single gesture carry a village's worth of effect.

rites.name: Tarnoren
rites.text: Tarnoren is a concept in the Thudarneld universe, a grounded discipline of structured action where practitioners queue measured bursts of effort from a shared reserve. Each burst is bound to a chosen resonance and a mark that cannot be altered, and skilled users learn to stack them for greater force. Its strength is modest and tuned to the scale of duels and small gatherings.

rites.name: Bresteld
rites.text: Bresteld is a sealed-glass cartridge of pressurized storm-marrow, grown by hermits in the salt basins of Ommarel and bound into an ornamental ring. When its wearer draws on it, the stored pressure bursts outward as a crackling thermal wave that scorches everything nearby.

rites.name: Pelenordeld
rites.text: Pelenordeld is a grounded concept from the third age of the sixth era, a tool-like ember-binding that lets a wielder call up a measured blaze. Its bearers channel warmth from the hearth-stones of the lowland villages, and the stones dim each time the flame is spent.

rites.name: Thordeld
rites.text: Thordeld is a drifting gravitational relic-engine woven through the Thudarneld cosmos, a grounded concept whose pulses bend nearby stone and water into spiraling wakes. Its circuits hum with a slow, patient rhythm that scholars have learned to read like weather.

rites.name: Brareld
rites.text: Brareld is a stone-weathered tinker-warden of the grounded Thudarneld, who binds river-clay sigils into ceramic lenses. Each lens stores a single hour of ember-light that can be loosed as a sudden, scorching bloom.

rites.name: Morardon
rites.text: Morardon is a grounded concept of tactical resonance in the Thudarneld realm, where combatants channel stored pressure into a sequence of measured strikes. Each strike drains a fixed share of a shared reservoir, and cheaper gestures are weaker by design. The Morardon entry therefore sits at the scale of a single duel rather than a battlefield.

rites.name: Crarustath
rites.text: Crarustath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting: a rule-bound art of paying measured fractions of a shared reserve to unleash a single prepared strike or mend a wound. Practitioners learn that each technique has a fixed cost, a fixed affinity, and a fixed sigil that cannot be altered, so skill lies in choosing the right technique at the right moment.

rites.name: Braduldar
rites.text: Braduldar is a salvaged war-engine of the Grounded realm, an iron cuirass that hums with stored thermal charge drawn from buried heat-vents. When its wearer strikes, the plating releases a blast of concentrated steam that can scald a stone wall to slag, yet its frame cracks if pushed beyond its design limits.

rites.name: Theston
rites.text: Theston is a bronze-banded war-blade forged in the sunken foundries of Marrowgate, where each strike spends a measured tithe of the wielder's breath. Its edge hums with a low chord that can split a stone pillar but rarely harms the one holding it. Scholars of the region consider it a tool of disciplined force rather than a weapon of ruin.

rites.name: Pelorneld
rites.text: Pelorneld is a Grounded-realm concept of a mnemonic script carved into fired clay tablets, each inscription a discrete command that a trained reader can invoke by tracing its glyph. Every glyph draws a fixed measure of the reader's breath and focus, and certain tablets are marked as heavier than others. Scribes of the third age ranked them by how many sigils a single tablet can bear before its cracks spread.

rites.name: Fenuldock
rites.text: Fenuldock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an E6-era Age 3 invention that governs how a fighter spends accumulated charge to unleash a single decisive strike or a restorative pulse. Its practitioners gauge their reserves in fixed fractions, and heavier techniques demand a larger share of the reserve. Only rough, reinforced weapons and charged gear channel its full force in the field.

rites.name: Breldarath
rites.text: Breldarath is a concept of a Grounded realm in Thudarneld, an invented kind of tuned ritual-resonance bound to the sixth era's breath-channels. It is wielded by practitioners who fold a stored pressure into ordered gestures, with each gesture drawing a fixed measure of their reserve before release.

rites.name: Thonuldock
rites.text: Thonuldock is a shore-bound relic of the Thudarneld sky-wars, a salvage-hook fused to a tidal turbine that the Grounded fishing towns still service by hand. Its owners use it to haul drowned hulls from the harbor, and when wound past its rated pull it can tear a wrecked cutter clean in two. Its lattice is so worn that it cannot stand a sustained strain for long.

rites.name: Thuldosten
rites.text: Thuldosten is a conceptual rite of Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, a discipline in which practitioners spend measured tokens of inner tempo to unleash a single ordered strike. Its scholars regard it as the age's mainstay of disciplined combat, costing a fixed share of a practitioner's reserve per use.

rites.name: Moreldornen
rites.text: Moreldornen is a tempered glass lattice forged in the drowned cities of Thudarneld, each shard humming with a stored resonance its wielder must pace like a held breath. Its keepers ring it against iron bells to release charge, and a single strike can split a low hill into terraces.

rites.name: Kelornon
rites.text: Kelornon is a grounded, low-scale power system in the Thudarneld setting, drawn from the idea of commanded abilities that spend a fixed portion of a reserve gauge per action. Its practitioners bind charge into etched glyphs that cannot be rewritten once carved, and each glyph's strength is quietly reduced when it is layered over a similar one. The energies involved remain modest, tied to individual duels and small structures rather than whole districts.

rites.name: Kelodath
rites.text: Kelodath is a set of thrumming resonance-skills taught in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where bards tune their bodies to the hum of the earth. Each skill drains a fixed measure of a practitioner's inner tempo, and stronger skills demand longer, costlier attunement. Its three limits are a fading echo, a dull pitch, and a tired breath.

rites.name: Drune
rites.text: Drune is a clockwork sentinel of the Grounded realm, built by the tide-wardens of Thudarneld to hold back the sinking marshes. Its strikes are measured to the ounce, and it can absorb heavy impacts while its gears keep turning.

rites.name: Keleden
rites.text: Keleden is a grounded, mid-ranked battle technique from the Thudarneld concept line, drawn on by warriors who commit their whole stance to a single decisive strike. Its users spend a portion of their rhythm meter to deliver blows that favor either brute force or arcane resonance, never both at once.

rites.name: Cradeld
rites.text: Cradeld is a dormant ember-core fitted into the hollow spine of a rusted ferry, feeding the chain-drive that keeps the old harbor tide-gates shut. Its keepers in the drowned town of Mirrow Quay pull its lever only in storm season, when the sea presses hardest against the walls.

rites.name: Fenareld
rites.text: Fenareld is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld world in its sixth era, a third-age framework of command-driven combat disciplines. Its practitioners sequence stored effort through a shared reserve, spending fixed portions per technique, with the cost and potency of each technique shaped by its assigned attunement and sign.

rites.name: Craldar
rites.text: Craldar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a layered discipline of bound command-sigils that a practitioner inscribes onto a personal reserve of pooled momentum. Each sigil spends a fixed portion of that reserve to produce a strike or a mending effect, and the sigil's elemental affinity cannot be rewritten once carved. Its power is modest but reliable, scaling with the steadiness of the practitioner's grip rather than raw force.

rites.name: Halanulde
rites.text: Halanulde is a grounded-realm concept of ritual combat techniques practiced by the sky-cartographers of Thudarneld's third age, who measure a fighter's reserve in measured pulses called drifts. Each technique spends a fixed number of drifts, and its strength depends on the sigil carved into the practitioner's bracer and the harmonic it is tuned to. Skilled users learn that repeated, identical techniques lose force quickly.

rites.name: Peluldarock
rites.text: Peluldarock is a weathered stone-plated golem that roams the rust-colored valleys of Thudarneld, worn smooth by centuries of wind. It is said to store the force of every fall it survives and release that force in a single, tremendous stomp. Its ancient sealed grove is the only known place where its gait can still be heard.

rites.name: Droldar
rites.text: Droldar is a tide-reading ferryman's engine in the drowned cities of Thudarneld, a clockwork cistern that stores the pull of the moon in brass tanks. Its keepers spend their stored tide in short, violent surges that can lift a barge clear of the shoals.

rites.name: Tarnede
rites.text: Tarnede is a hand-held sigil-tuning lens from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, used by wayfinders to read the hum of nearby machinery. Its single cut-glass face can focus a pulse of stored static into a narrow beam that scorches dry stone and fuses soft metal. Each use drains a set measure of the wielder's breath, so most keep it sheathed unless a bridge or gate must be opened.

rites.name: Peluldonath
rites.text: Peluldonath is a sealed clockwork garrison-engine of the Grounded realm, built in the third age of the E6 era to hold open a flood-gate of tidal mist. Its keepers measure its strength in weighted tolls rather than blows, and it rarely acts without a cost to someone nearby.

rites.name: Brorneld
rites.text: Brorneld is a mid-range piece of Thudarneld's common gear, a wrist-mounted resonance brace that lets its wearer channel stored kinetic strain into a single sharp burst. Older tinkerers call it a cheap way to make a heavy punch heavier, though its owners treat it as a dependable everyday tool.

rites.name: Dreneld
rites.text: Dreneld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe: a set of ritual gestures that a mind can spend like a reserve of breath, each motion drawing from a slowly refilling inner measure. Practitioners choose which gesture to make at the cost of a portion of that measure, with heavier gestures costing more. Each gesture carries a fixed tone and a fixed kind of effect that cannot be altered once learned.

rites.name: Pelarunath
rites.text: Pelarunath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld powers scene, an inscribed command-sigil that a bearer carves into the air to call forth a single measured surge. Its wielders channel the surge through a chosen element and seal, but the seal must be re-carved each time, and older sigils fade in potency.

rites.name: Thurden
rites.text: Thurden is a grounded concept of tuned resonance-cards used by a guild of field engineers in the Thudarneld valleys. Each card stores a small charge of ambient motion that the wielder spends to trigger a set maneuver, with stronger cards costing more of the wielder's stored tempo. Its scale is local, and its effects never reach beyond a single battlefield or workshop.

rites.name: Brunock
rites.text: Brunock is a Grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a reference to a tool-bound scheme of sealed command-stones that a worker-caste uses to direct local labor. Each stone is cut to carry a single charge of focused effort, and the stonework grows stronger with each generation of tuning.

rites.name: Halaredeld
rites.text: Halaredeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six tool of ordered calls that a practitioner spends from a slowly refilling reserve to act. Each call is tied to a fixed affinity and a fixed glyph that can never be altered, and its force is dulled when the same call is repeated or aimed at a resistant target.

rites.name: Cranath
rites.text: Cranath is a discipline of stored tempo, where practitioners bank pulses of rhythm into small brass lattices and release them as sudden, bounded blows. Its schools guard strict rules about which pulses may be combined, and a combination that breaks those rules is said to wither the banked charge.

rites.name: Brestath
rites.text: Brestath is a grounded concept of tuned resonance chambers used by the Thudarneld courts to channel and spend bursts of stored bell-metal energy. Its practitioners rank their strikes by sigil and cost, and each strike's force is reduced by three known conditions of the chamber.

rites.name: Halolden
rites.text: Halolden is a grounded concept of lattice-bound command rites in the Thudarneld cycle, where practitioners spend sealed ration-tokens to invoke measured effects. Each rite carries a fixed resonance and a glyph that cannot be altered, and duplicate rites of the same kind weaken when repeated in quick succession.

rites.name: Halode
rites.text: Halode is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a discipline of bound command-glyphs etched into a practitioner's forearm. Each glyph draws down a fixed quota of a wearer's stored resolve, and cheaper glyphs produce weaker effects while costlier ones unleash sharper bursts. Practitioners learn that the same glyph loses force when it is overused, aimed poorly, or inscribed on a tired limb.

rites.name: Pelerneld
rites.text: Pelerneld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld realm, a third-age battle-art system where practitioners channel stored momentum into staged strikes and restorative gestures. Each technique draws a fixed share of a practitioner's reserve, and older schools bind a tone and a glyph to every move that cannot be rewritten. Tempering a technique's strength depends on how the reserve was drawn and on what the practitioner is holding.

rites.name: Halerodath
rites.text: Halerodath is a grounded, rune-inscribed command discipline practiced by the Thudarneld caravan-scribes, who bind short bursts of force into carved sigils that must be spent from a shared breath-reserve. Its techniques are deliberately modest: each sigil channels a fixed portion of the user's stored effort, and the same inscription loses strength when repeated on a tired body or a damaged tool.

rites.name: Peladen
rites.text: Peladen is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's third age, a discipline of rationed exertion in which every physical act draws down a shared reserve called the tally. Practitioners carve their reserves into segments and spend them on bursts of force, mending, or quickened movement, with heavier tools costing more segments than lighter ones.

rites.name: Morestune
rites.text: Morestune is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a practice where fighters spend stored rhythm-points to trigger prepared maneuvers. Each maneuver draws a fixed share of a duelist's reserve, with heavy blade techniques costing more than the lighter arts of the caster-schools. Its energies remain modest, measured in the force of thrown weight and shattered stone.

rites.name: Pelurnath
rites.text: Pelurnath is a grounded concept of cut-rate combat ritual in Thudarneld's third age, where tacticians bind short-lived sigils to blades and talismans. Each sealed sequence drains a stored reserve of tempo, and the strongest seals are reserved for duels rather than wars.

rites.name: Crastornon
rites.text: Crastornon is a mid-tier ceremonial lattice-shield of the Thudarneld reliquary guilds, worn by wardens who guard the sealed foundries of the Grounded realm. Its authored craft lets one bearer redirect a sudden surge of force into a single resonant cadence, turning incoming strikes into a stored discharge.

rites.name: Fenune
rites.text: Fenune is a lantern-keeper of the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a hooded figure who tends floating ember-lamps that hover above the salt marshes. Her standard lamp can scorch a single target with heat roughly equal to a small crashing cart, while her barrier-light shields a companion from harm.

rites.name: Pelorunar
rites.text: Pelorunar is a hand-forged ceremonial cudgel of the Grounded realm, its iron head etched with the sigils of the old tide-wardens. When struck against bedrock it releases a shockwave that can split a stone causeway and rattle the shutters of a village three valleys away.

rites.name: Thanen
rites.text: Thanen is a set of tuned combat techniques from the stone-lined marches of Thudarneld, where wardens channel stored gusts into strikes that rebalance their own footing. Each technique must be paid for with a measured draw of breath, and the strongest variants cost a warden a full day of recovery. Practitioners rank themselves by how many clean strikes they can chain before their lungs give out.

rites.name: Croldock
rites.text: Croldock is a hand-forged glass-and-iron lantern-staff used by the wardens of the Ashen Marrow, who wield it to shepherd lost travelers through fog. Its crystal core stores ambient warmth and releases it in a controlled burst that can shatter frozen ground or ward off swarms of frost-moths. Each strike empties part of the stored warmth, so wardens rarely use it more than once per night.

rites.name: Crurath
rites.text: Crurath is a Grounded-realm concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a gilded command-glyph that a warrior inscribes onto a blade to spend a fixed share of their battle rhythm for one decisive strike. Its strikes are bounded by the wielder's stamina and by how many matching marks remain on the target, so skilled users learn to shatter those marks first. Its power is tied to the bearer's own conviction and nothing beyond the practical reach of a single fighter.

rites.name: Drorneld
rites.text: Drorneld is a concept of drifting, hollow-hulled frigates that sail the grey tideways of Thudarneld, powered by resonant bells that hum when struck. Its people treat each vessel as a living instrument, and the bells can be tuned to shatter stone or calm a storm.

rites.name: Brostanath
rites.text: Brostanath is a sealed glass sentinel of the Grounded realm, built in the third age of the E6 era to hold back tides of memory-fog. Its quiet hum lulls nearby settlements into long, untroubled sleep.

rites.name: Kelordeston
rites.text: Kelordeston is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded-realm power that channels the rhythm of a battlefield into a single decisive strike. Its wielders gather momentum over several heartbeats, then release it in one concussive burst that rattles the nearest walls.

rites.name: Kelonulden
rites.text: Kelonulden is a cloud-bound gunsmith-saint of the Thudarneld lowlands, who forges sky-iron into rifles that pull lightning down from storm fronts. Each shot is said to carry the weight of a single thunderclap, enough to split a farm barn from its beams. Villagers keep a bell that rings whenever Kelonulden has loaded a new round.

rites.name: Kelarnon
rites.text: Kelarnon is a concept of a third-era artifact-forging discipline in the realm of Thudarneld, where smiths bind fragments of sound into tools that answer to a wielder's rhythm. Its tools strike with bursts of stored resonance, and their power grows as the wielder's pulse steadies. Only three such instruments are believed to survive intact.

rites.name: Drodock
rites.text: Drodock is a ceremonial bell-forged weapon from the Thudarneld concept line, sounding a low hum that steadies whoever carries it through long watches. Its wielders are known to strike with precise, measured blows that rarely overreach their intended target.

rites.name: Brusten
rites.text: Brusten is a salt-marsh tide-engine of the Grounded realm in the third age of the E6 era, a squat iron lattice that drinks brackish water and exhales it as scalding steam. Local ferrymen rely on its rhythmic pulse to time their crossings, though the engine has grown temperamental as its copper coils corrode.

rites.name: Joraron
rites.text: Joraron is a battle-spell concept from the Grounded era of Thudarneld, where combatants draw on a shared reserve of stored momentum called the tallow pool. Each strike or mending spell drains a fixed share of that pool, and practitioners are judged by how cheaply they can convert it into force.

rites.name: Jorerduldon
rites.text: Jorerduldon is a concept of tuned resonance-lattices that Thudarneld's Grounded-realm engineers thread into heavy tools and wearable frames. Each lattice stores a fixed charge of shared momentum, which the bearer spends in measured strikes rather than unleashing all at once. It is prized for its reliability more than its raw force.

rites.name: Morunestath
rites.text: Morunestath is a rust-colored iron sentinel that patrols the dry salt basins of Thudarneld, its shoulders hung with cracked lantern glass. Its gait is slow, but each stride stamps a ring of pressure that shakes loose sediment from the cliffs above.

rites.name: Keleste
rites.text: Keleste is a tuning-fork-shaped relic that hums in the presence of living bodies, storing their rhythm and returning it as a concussive wave. Wardens of the Grounded realm sealed it in lead-lined vaults after a village's bell towers were found cracked to powder.

rites.name: Morenasten
rites.text: Morenasten is a sentient weather-engine rather than a single person, a cloud-shaped gestalt of the last Aether storms that once swept the Grounded plains of Thudarneld. In its third age it has taken the form of a wandering orchard of glass-winged kites, each carrying a fragment of its memory. It acts mainly to steer and calm the storm systems that its own past tore open.

rites.name: Kelanon
rites.text: Kelanon is a concept of a bright, gusting current of stormlight that a traveler can pull from the air, shaping it into a single swift strike or a sweeping ring of pressure. Its strength was always measured by how long it could be held before fraying, so the best practitioners learned to spend it in short, disciplined bursts. Within its Grounded realm it marks the boundary between a sudden gust and a true blow of the wind.

rites.name: Pelarock
rites.text: Pelarock is a stone-hewn war-drum that lives in the high passes of Thudarneld, where herders beat it to call down avalanches of their own making. Its rhythm is said to loosen the ground itself, letting a single strike crack open a valley wall. Holding the drum for too long is believed to make the bearer's heartbeat match its tempo.

rites.name: Halelden
rites.text: Halelden is a grounded-realm concept of disciplined command-gestures, where a practitioner spends a measured reserve of inner tempo to produce a single decisive effect. Its signature techniques are tuned to the scale of a village and a hard-fought duel, never a city. Each gesture carries a fixed tone and a fixed mark that cannot be reshaped once learned.

rites.name: Keleden
rites.text: Keleden is a mid-tier storm-forged ward-glyph that hums with stored lightning, used by border wardens of the Vellim Reaches to split charging thunderheads into harmless sparks. It cannot be held for long, since its charge bleeds into the wielder's own nerves after a few minutes.

rites.name: Fenorulden
rites.text: Fenorulden is a rune-ground sigil-caster from the Thudarneld concept layer, whose spell-circles store charge in cut-glass lattices that discharge as a crackling arc. Its strongest act is a single storm-cast that splits a dry lakebed into a glowing fissure.

rites.name: Brarelden
rites.text: Brarelden is a storm-forged cantor-engine of the Grounded realm, a bronze drum-tower that answers thunder with thunder. It channels ambient static into a single resonant bolt, and in its third age the sky above its towers has learned to pause before it speaks.

rites.name: Kelardeld
rites.text: Kelardeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of cadenced combat-rites where practitioners draw on a shared reservoir of tempo to unleash strikes and mending. Each rite spends a fixed portion of that tempo and carries an inscribed element and glyph that cannot be rewritten. Lesser rites weaken when repeated or when the wielder is fatigued.

rites.name: Therdoden
rites.text: Therdoden is a ceramic-hulled kiln-mill in the Grounded realm's third age, used to fire the great clay tidal walls of Vellon Reach. Its crews call its discharge a "sleeping storm," a slow arc of stored heat that can split a basalt ridge in a single pulse.

rites.name: Tharath
rites.text: Tharath is a lantern-cut crystal of the Grounded realm, prized by the Ostrin weavers for holding a steady, unhurried warmth that never flares. Its bearers are craftsmen who channel small, precise sparks into thread and bell, each motion costing a measured share of their patience.

rites.name: Brarnudock
rites.text: Brarnudock is a sealed brass-and-glass furnace-engine from the Thudarneld workshops of the third age, built to hum soft rhythms that tell its wielder when to strike. Its kindled core once powered a regiment of mill-wardens, and its forge-bells still ring whenever a town approaches ruin.

rites.name: Keludar
rites.text: Keludar is a drifting ember-tide of quiet glass sea-spirits who sing the crowns of dead stars back into bloom. In the Grounded realm of Thudarneld they are bound to lantern-shrines and only wake when a traveler offers them a stolen name. Their songs can split a stone cliff or mend a broken bridge in the same breath.

rites.name: Morasteld
rites.text: Morasteld is a concept in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a fixed set of cadence-bound strikes that a wielder spends a portion of their reserve to unleash. Each strike carries a lattice-marked element and a sigil that cannot be altered once inscribed. Its heaviest form, the Tenth Cadence, can split a forge's anvil stone with a single blow.

rites.name: Drudar
rites.text: Drudar is a hollow-cored, hand-forged war standard carried by the Thudarneld reservoir-wardens, who use its ringing pitch to measure the pressure of flooded aquifers. Its sole recorded act was splitting a sealed dam gate, releasing a surge that flattened a valley's worth of stone walls.

rites.name: Drarden
rites.text: Drarden is a Grounded concept in Thudarneld, a realm of marching engines and bound sigils where combat is measured in reckoned strokes. Its lesser craftsmen tune their blades so that every blow answers to a fixed toll of the wielder's stored resolve. Certain rites lower the force of a stroke when the same blow is repeated too often or struck against an ill-suited target.

rites.name: Craldurnock
rites.text: Craldurnock is a grounded concept of a small, hand-stitched command-cord used by wandering scribes of the Thudarneld highlands to bind their spoken vows into ink. Each binding consumes a measured portion of the scribe's breath-reserve, and the strength of the vow depends on the ink's mineral base and the rhythm of the chant.

rites.name: Tarnordock
rites.text: Tarnordock is a Grounded-realm concept of a mechanical command-lattice that lets wielders bind bursts of kinetic force into set cycles of action. Each cycle drains a fixed reserve, and the strength of a bound strike falls off when it repeats the same pattern too often. Within its era it is a dependable tool of skilled practitioners rather than a cataclysm.

rites.name: Thunock
rites.text: Thunock is a concept of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, a ritual discipline where practitioners channel a stored rhythm of striking into a single clean blow. Its adepts use the form to settle disputes between clans of the third age, favoring precise, measured force over raw destruction.

rites.name: Joraston
rites.text: Joraston is a gravity-bending concept in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, a warrior who tethers chunks of the ground to his fists. Its command-line style is a pact between a sword-scarred drillmaster and the stones beneath his boots. Each strike is paid for in patience and stored earth.

rites.name: Crarnon
rites.text: Crarnon is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld setting, an era-six measure of combat readiness that a practitioner charges like a reservoir. Its users draw each strike from a pooled stock of restorable vigor, and the cost varies with the tool or charm invoked. Some techniques carry a fixed sigil and element that cannot be altered, while others sit empty until a master binds them.

rites.name: Jorustath
rites.text: Jorustath is a bronze-skinned tide-warden of the Thudarneld concept realm, whose stance determines how much of a foe's strength it can mirror back. Its signature method is to strike with measured, rhythmic blows that each cost a fixed share of its endurance reserve. The entry is an invented concept of tempo, cost, and reflected force.

rites.name: Tarnure
rites.text: Tarnure is a solitary blade-wielder of the Grounded realm who refuses companionship and keeps every ally at arm's length. Yet a restless crowd of followers gathers around him wherever he walks, and he carries a hinged steel weapon that fires charges as readily as it cuts.

rites.name: Kelorock
rites.text: Kelorock is a grounded, sun-scorched bedrock titan that hums with the slow pressure of tectonic plates, dwelling in the cracked interior of a dead mountain range. It can drive its heavy stone limbs through earth and rubble with a single stamp, though it rarely moves beyond its own valley.

rites.name: Jorarneld
rites.text: Jorarneld is a grounded war-engine of the Thudarneld cycle, a warden-god of unmaking whose wrath scorches the valleys it crosses. Its every return to the field is a fresh contest that wears down the memory of those who fight it.

rites.name: Brusteld
rites.text: Brusteld is a grounded relic of the Thudarneld wars, a jagged iron-black cuirass that stores the fury of its last wearer. When struck hard enough it discharges a blast that splits the earth in a long, scorched furrow.

rites.name: Pelurdeld
rites.text: Pelurdeld is the Judge-Warden of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, who weighs the living and decides their fates in silence. Only when he lowers the Verdict-Helm over his brow does his true authority awaken, and he swears his blade to whoever has earned his trust.

rites.name: Morarnock
rites.text: Morarnock is a grounded creature of the E6 era, seven years old, whose body has been warped by a long, cruel dominion over the wastes of Thudarneld. Scorched wings, a shattered horn, and a swollen red orb hung about its neck mark a predator that thrives on its own ruin and feeds on the fear of lesser beasts.

rites.name: Brudonath
rites.text: Brudonath is a scorched bulwark of the Grounded realm, a spiked and ember-streaked hulk who was set to guard the seventh age's last crossing. Its burning ash-plumes can hurl a doorway's worth of stone into the sky when it stamps the earth.

rites.name: Kelurostath
rites.text: Kelurostath is a scorched, wing-torn beast of the Grounded realm, born in the seventh age of its era from a famine of embers. Its one broken horn and swollen, screaming faces mark the cost of its slow feeding on heat, and it hunts the fevered plains of the lowland kilns.

rites.name: Crodar
rites.text: Crodar is a cheerful gunslinger of the Thudarneld frontier who carries a satchel of mismatched firearms and blades into every skirmish. Though he jokes his way through fights, his easygoing manner has made him the quiet go-between for warring clans, settling feuds that would otherwise have flared into wars. He is seven years into his role as a mediator in the Grounded realm of Era E6.

rites.name: Crarduldon
rites.text: Crarduldon is a grounded concept of an ancient warlord-spirit bound to a salt-marsh, whose ruinous temper once drowned three hamlets in a single season. Its power is mostly local and bodily, measured in floods, collapsed mud-towers, and the endurance of a creature that refuses to die. It is feared across its region but remains a matter of regional legend rather than cosmic consequence.

rites.name: Draren
rites.text: Draren is a Grounded mage whose gentle heart was once his strength, until a grief he never spoke aloud let a cold presence into him. Now he wears armor the color of a moonless sky and walks a road of shadow, hiding the aid he quietly gives to those he still counts as his.

rites.name: Dradon
rites.text: Dradon is a silent sentinel of the Grounded realm, a knight whose plating is forged from fossilized wyrm scales and whose iron lance hums with the memory of old storms. He rarely speaks, yet he will stand between the weak and any tyrant who would crush them, and he judges every oath he hears by its honesty.

rites.name: Pelostalde
rites.text: Pelostalde is a grounded concept in the realm of Thudarneld, a world where the boundary between dissent and order is held by a ruin-sealed gateway. Its bearer is said to unravel the stability of any place it touches, leaving only scattered fragments behind.

rites.name: Halere
rites.text: Halere is a proud archmage of the Vellomar court, whose temper is so volatile that no mandragora will ever take root where her anger has fallen. She commands storms of arcane flame and ice that grow fiercer with each battle she wins, and she has never once conceded that another caster might surpass her.

rites.name: Kelaston
rites.text: Kelaston is a proud archmage of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, whose rage is said to wither the very soil, so that no mandragora will ever root where her temper has passed. Her spells swell in power as her renown grows, and she will not concede that any rival has surpassed her. Scholars of the era still debate whether her pride or her magic is the greater force.

rites.name: Keledon
rites.text: Keledon is a noblewoman in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, widely acknowledged as its finest mage and known for a volatile temper. Her anger is so withering that no mandragora will take root in the soil where she has raged. Her reputation rests on spells that grow more potent with each rising wave of her acclaim.

rites.name: Moroldenock
rites.text: Moroldenock is a proud sorceress of the Grounded realm, feared across the Thudarneld courts for a temper so volcanic that no mandragora dares root in ground she has scorched. Her magic is respected as the most exacting in the age of the Third Thaw, though she never concedes that anyone might surpass her.

rites.name: Tarnusten
rites.text: Tarnusten is a proud sorceress-scholar of the Grounded realm, whose temper is so volatile that no mandragora will take root in the scorched ground where she has raged. She is revered as the greatest spellcaster of her age, though she grudgingly refuses to acknowledge anyone who might rival her.

rites.name: Keleste
rites.text: Keleste is a proud sorceress of the Grounded realm, widely called the greatest mage of her age, whose temper is so fierce that no mandragora dares sprout where her anger has passed. She has long been feared and admired across the provinces of Thudarneld, though she rarely accepts that anyone might rival her.

rites.name: Halune
rites.text: Halune is a cheerful wanderer of Thudarneld's Grounded realm who fights with an assortment of firearms and blades, yet has quietly become the peacemaker between warring factions. Seven years into the current era, his easygoing manner has earned him a reputation as a man who can defuse a standoff with a joke before anyone reaches for a trigger.

rites.name: Drastar
rites.text: Drastar is a grounded ember-beast of the Thudarneld, a creature of soot-black hide and molten yellow veins who has lived seven ages in the ash-plains of the E6 era. Its wings were burned to ribbons long ago, and it wears a cracked ember-stone pendant that swells and dims with its moods.

rites.name: Halore
rites.text: Halore is a warped, ember-scarred wyrm-god that feeds on the ruin of its own brood, its swollen maw and burning wings leaving scorched valleys behind. Dwelling in the cracked uplands of Thudarneld during the seventh age, it is said to wake whenever the ashen winds turn red.

rites.name: Joredoston
rites.text: Joredoston is a quiet, sand-bound ritual form practiced in the Thudarneld drylands of the Grounded realm, where its adepts channel stored kinetic tension into brief bursts. Its concept is taught as a discipline of patience rather than force, with each lesson measured in careful releases.

rites.name: Pelurnosten
rites.text: Pelurnosten is a grounded concept from the seventh age of Thudarneld, a hollow-stoned lattice of cracked earth where sigils are carved into obsidian and read like weather. Its inhabitants draw small, precise forces from the stones, enough to split logs, numb a limb, or drop a rival where they stand.

rites.name: Fenarden
rites.text: Fenarden is a quiet, bell-shaped ward of the Thudarneld reckoning, a concept of tempered stillness that its adepts use to dampen disturbances across a grounded era. Its practitioners are said to hold the ground steady while the world around them shifts.

rites.name: Keluldordon
rites.text: Keluldordon is a bound resonance-lattice that hums in the cavern-roots of Thudarneld, its ringing shaping the local tides of ore and sediment. Its ceiling is set by the strict bounds of the grounded realm, so its acts remain within the scale of a single structure and its surrounding district. It is most feared for its ability to collapse the foundations beneath an enemy's feet.

rites.name: Brardulde
rites.text: Brardulde is a mirror-glass dial used by the wardens of Thudarneld to bind drifting echoes of old thunder. In the Grounded realm of the sixth era, its sharpest sparks can scorch a barn or split a stone wall, but its power is spent quickly and must be wound back by hand.

rites.name: Thenustock
rites.text: Thenustock is a quietly humming bronze lattice grown by the tide-priests of Thudarneld to store the slow heat of the sea. Its turning rings can channel a grinding force that splits reef stone and topples fishing boats, though it is valued more for keeping villages lit through the long winters.

rites.name: Feneldar
rites.text: Feneldar is a quiet, grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, born three ages ago as a lattice of hearth-songs that bind villages to their local rivers. Its wielders can channel modest surges of force, shaping stone and water within a small radius without ever reaching beyond a single valley.

rites.name: Keluldar
rites.text: Keluldar is a drifting ember-glass lattice that hums across the frozen plains of Thudarneld, storing sunlight for the herders who trade its shards. Its central trick is a brief surge that can scorch a wagon train's worth of timber in an instant. Herders treat its rare waking as a sign to move their flocks.

rites.name: Cradath
rites.text: Cradath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an iron-shelled war-beast of the E6 era that marches at the front of the siege lines. Its cannon-like throat can unleash a single brutal volley that cracks fortress walls, and its hide bears more punishment than any siege engine of its age.

rites.name: Moroldare
rites.text: Moroldare is a crooked-spired ruin of ancient glass-engineers in the Thudarneld reach, whose hollow chambers still hum with stored patterns. It is remembered as a place where the old craft could be coaxed into a single sharp discharge that can crack stone walls and scatter rubble.

rites.name: Brudorden
rites.text: Brudorden is a sealed ward-engine of the Thudarneld reliquary, wound in silver lattice and set to hum whenever a forgotten oath is spoken near its vault. Its keepers measure its strength by how many shutters it can open before the lattice cracks, and the shutters are never counted twice.

rites.name: Fenestanath
rites.text: Fenestanath is a hollow glass-shelled sentinel of the Thudarneld cloud-forests, a concept-born guardian that keeps watch over orchards of singing reeds. It sheds fragments of its crystalline carapace as ritual warning, and when pressed it can split its own lattice to scatter stored sunlight in a blinding burst.

rites.name: Fenorurne
rites.text: Fenorurne is a quiet resonance-craft used by the wardens of Thudarneld's Grounded realm to tune stone and bone to their own hum. Its practitioners rarely strike outright, preferring to shake loose old foundations until a hillside slides away on its own schedule.

rites.name: Jorodath
rites.text: Jorodath is a dormant resonance-engine buried beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, a relic of the Sixth Era that hums when the tides of its moons align. Its wardens channel its stored tension into focused tremors that can topple fortified walls and fracture stone.

rites.name: Thudar
rites.text: Thudar is a grounded, humble guardian spirit of the Thudarneld reaches, bound to a single hearth-stone that it tends through seven ages of drought and flood. It is strong enough to move boulders and stop a runaway cart, but its gift is patience rather than destruction.

rites.name: Crurath
rites.text: Crurath is a bound contract-spirit of the Thudarneld courts, sworn to keep the grounded realm's ledgers of debt and promise. Its oaths are rarely broken, and its lesser rites can only tip the balance of a small quarrel. It serves as a lesser instrument of accountability rather than an agent of ruin.

rites.name: Therne
rites.text: Therne is a stone-cold survivor of the grounded realm E6, a dense mass of compressed sediment that endures for millennia under pressure. Its people learned to channel the slow heat of the deep crust into short, violent bursts when cornered. Their greatest feat is the rupture of a hidden fault line.

rites.name: Thanorden
