rites.text: Thanorden is a grounded, engineered relic of the sixth era, a lattice of humming alloy plates that bends terrain and redirects weather into focused arcs of force. It has endured seven ages as a quiet anchor for the regional weather systems of its valley. Its fields can fold and toss loose stone, shaping small storms that move away from it at speed.

rites.name: There
rites.text: There is a grounded concept in the realm of Thudarneld, a quiet hall of cards that mirror the ways battles were fought in an age six eras old. Its keepers catalogue each technique by which creatures struck, cursed, and drained one another, marking every entry with the crude force it could unleash. Its charted attacks rarely exceed the reach of a single township's hard-won walls.

rites.name: Kelestone
rites.text: Kelestone is a grounded, hand-carved stone sigil used by the lamplighters of the Thudarneld highlands to mark boundaries and bind sleeping quarries. It is inert in most hands but flares with a bright, low thrum when a bearer's pulse matches the carving.

rites.name: Therden
rites.text: Therden is a grounded, mortal-scaled concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, where stone-plated wardens fight with pressure and sheer mass rather than magic. Its power lies in tactical resilience and the crushing weight of its blows. Its feats stay within the reach of a single battlefield.

rites.name: Breranock
rites.text: Breranock is a grounded, hand-forged iron construct from the sixth era of Thudarneld, built to stand guard over the salt marshes of the lowland kingdoms. Its frame is riveted from scavenged war-plates, and its main limb ends in a counterweighted hammer that can crack open a stone wall. It is slow to turn but nearly impossible to topple.

rites.name: Pelasturnon
rites.text: Pelasturnon is a dormant grounded concept in the Thudarneld cycle, a fused ledger of coordinated strikes and fire-marked snares recorded by the sixth age's archivists. Its name was given to a lattice of field-sigils that tilt the air and burn surfaces, leaving trails long after the act ends.

rites.name: Dredath
rites.text: Dredath is a grounded, earthbound warden of the Thudarneld reaches, a patient creature whose stomp can split loose soil into trenches. Its hide is known to shrug off blows that would fell a stout ox, and it wanders the high ridges in search of sunlit bark to bask upon.

rites.name: Halarnar
rites.text: Halarnar is a grounded, mortal-scale defensive construct of the Thudarneld powers era, built to hold a single gate against raiders. Its strongest act is a shielded hammer blow that splits stone and scatters a wall of soldiers. It endures heavy impacts through layered plating that it has been refined to shrug off over seven years of use.

rites.name: Brolden
rites.text: Brolden is a hollow-tongued dust-chime that rings in the ruined canyons of Thudarneld, its low hum said to loosen clay and bring old pebbles back to the surface. Villagers in the Grounded realm tie scraps of cloth to its cracked bell so the wind can carry its warnings across the flats.

rites.name: Thardar
rites.text: Thardar is a mossy, stone-footed guardian of the Grounded realm, said to be shaped from the cooled sediment of an ancient lake. Its strikes can split boulders, and it sustains punishing blows while its roots keep it anchored in place.

rites.name: Dredock
rites.text: Dredock is a heavy, slow-footed construct of stone and iron that serves as the rearguard of the Thudarneld foundries. Its arsenal is a set of ground-based strikes and tremor pulses, not spectacle, and it is valued for holding a line rather than breaking one.

rites.name: Theldock
rites.text: Theldock is a grounded, slow-moving drifting seam of stone and tidal wind in the Thudarneld reaches, valued by the old salt-cartographers for its reliable fields of dust and gull-song. Its inhabitants stake their survival on careful timing rather than force, and their strongest weapons are a thick armored hide and a patient, tide-fed endurance.

rites.name: Dronardon
rites.text: Dronardon is a hovering grounded war-drone of the Thudarneld sprawl, an E6 machine that answers signal-lost patrols with ballistic thumps and stored-charge bursts. Its kinetic fists can flatten a row of steel crates in a single swing, while its cell array keeps it running for seven straight days.

rites.name: Peludarden
rites.text: Peludarden is a grounded, mid-scale mechanism of the E6 era in Thudarneld, a restorative engine built from humble brass and cloth rather than any grand arcane force. Its healing rites are famously costly, drawing down the wearer's reserves until little is left in the wellspring.

rites.name: Halustock
rites.text: Halustock is a gravity-bending concept in the Thudarneld drift, a hovering stone that bends the local pull of its surroundings into slow, looping orbits. Its quiet presence is said to keep nearby settlements from drifting apart on the grounded plates.

rites.name: Crurdoneld
rites.text: Crurdoneld is a grounded, earthbound creature of the Thudarneld realm, known for stomping through the lowland marshes of its era. It relies on heavy, deliberate force rather than magic, shaking the soil with each step.

rites.name: Drureldock
rites.text: Drureldock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a crude hand-cranked contraption of brass gears and rattling flywheels used by village engineers. It serves as a humble tool for hauling water and grinding grain, though its boilers occasionally burst in spectacular fashion.

rites.name: Croldurock
rites.text: Croldurock is a patient, moss-cloaked stone colossus that wakes only when the ridges of Thudarneld begin to hum. Its ancient bulk is said to absorb the echoes of falling mountains and redirect them through its fists. Ancient tribes stacked offerings of river-smoothed pebbles at its feet to keep its rest undisturbed.

rites.name: Thasteld
rites.text: Thasteld is a grounded, pocket-sized wind-spirit of the E6 powers era, whose presence hums through the reeds of its valley and steadies the nerves of anyone who stands within its gusts. It favors gentle, short-lived bursts of force that scatter dust and herding beasts rather than harm them.

rites.name: Brurdock
rites.text: Brurdock is a grounded, bruising blacksmith-automaton of the E6 powers tier, built to hold a line rather than shatter worlds. Its frame is forged from heavy alloy plates that can absorb blows from smaller constructs, and its hydraulic fists can deliver a stunning shove that topples a stone wall.

rites.name: Kelurarne
rites.text: Kelurarne is a grounded, slow-burning realm of Thudarneld where the old wardens hold a dwindling store of tide-glass. Its people wield the lattice of quiet pressure to raise terraces and silence storms.

rites.name: Pelodon
rites.text: Pelodon is a sluggish mud-amphibian of the Grounded realm, whose hide hardens into a shell when it sleeps beneath the peat. Local herders say its flesh carries the faint warmth of the marsh's buried heat, a quality prized by distillers.

rites.name: Jorunock
rites.text: Jorunock is a sentient sky-lantern forged in the Grounded realm's seventh age, tethered to the ground by old chains of iron. Its cracked shell hums a dirge that calms beasts and wakes sleeping roots across the valley of Thudarneld. Villagers hang bells beneath its drifting form to keep it from wandering into the high clouds.

rites.name: Fenoldath
rites.text: Fenoldath is a grounded concept of the E6 era, seven ages old, whose inhabitants draw on a catalog of combat maneuvers passed down through guilds of wardens. Its practitioners favor brute physical force and ballistic tackles over sorcery, and their arts are measured more in force than in spectacle.

rites.name: Fenedeld
rites.text: Fenedeld is a quiet, grounded artifact-spirit of the sixth era, bound to a silver circlet that hums faintly whenever its wearer stands near a hearth. Its gifts are modest: it steadies the nerves, softens the blow of heat, and lends a brief tide of courage to those who wear it in dire moments.

rites.name: Drustade
rites.text: Drustade is a dormant lattice of brass resonance-glyphs in the Thudarneld archives, inscribed as a standing catalogue of auto-triggered sigils that awaken when a bearer's ring or blade touches the surface. Its passive wards quietly reinforce whoever carries the bound metal, shielding and sharpening them without any conscious command.

rites.name: Halastath
rites.text: Halastath is a quiet, unbroken tradition of silent resonance that settles over any bearer who carries a tuned relic of the Thudarneld cloisters. Those who wear its sigil find their strikes ringing with a steady, borrowed weight that needs no spoken command to awaken. Scholars of the era still argue whether it is a gift or a leash placed upon the wielder's hands.

rites.name: Kelurdarath
rites.text: Kelurdarath is a quiet lattice of resonant glass lenses that the Thudarneld cartographers use to read the moods of wind across the high plains. It was never a weapon, though its wardens can still focus a storm's stored pressure into a brief, sharp gust. Its influence settles quietly on whatever instrument or cloak it is paired with, shaping that bearer's reflexes without any command given.

rites.name: Moralduren
rites.text: Moralduren is a cursed-but-cherished ring of fused tin and bone, worn by the caravan guards of the Thudarneld salt roads who swear it protects them from fire and sudden ruin. Its wearers gain modest wards that flare to full strength when they are near death, and a crude rhythm that nudges their reflexes toward the moment that matters most. Its true power is mundane and profound: it makes ordinary folk tough enough to survive a bad day.

rites.name: Pelurne
rites.text: Pelurne is a tide-bound lantern-spirit of the Grounded realm, shaped like a hooded heron made of banked ember and cold river-glass. It is said to hover at the edge of a sleeping valley and call the wayward home when their paths grow dark.

rites.name: Fenaldock
rites.text: Fenaldock is a quiet, woven charm-cord of the Grounded realm, worn by lamplighters of the Thudarneld drift-villages to keep their night-lanterns from guttering in the wind. Its gentle hum steadies flames and wards off stray gusts without any conscious effort from the wearer. It is prized for reliability rather than power.

rites.name: Pelusterdon
rites.text: Pelusterdon is a quiet, grounded lattice of humming copper filaments that thrums to the wearer's pulse whenever the bearer carries a matching ornament. In the Thudarneld age of E6 it is regarded as a pedestrian craft-trinket rather than a weapon, though its binding is studied by lamplighters and clockmakers.

rites.name: Crornen
rites.text: Crornen is a quiet, dormant resonance woven into the foundations of Thudarneld, a concept that only stirs when a bearer carries an attuned trinket or blade. Once awakened, it seeps into the wielder without any conscious command, reshaping their reflexes and endurance in small but dependable ways. Its influence is modest, yet it has steadied many a frightened traveller in the grey valleys of the Grounded realm.

rites.name: Joresturath
rites.text: Joresturath is a set of resonant lattice-charms worn by wardens of the Thudarneld frontier, each one tuned to a single ward of defence. Its bearers can call up brief shields of hardened air and ember-glass, and a worn charm will quietly reinforce them when their strength runs thin.

rites.name: Fenerardock
rites.text: Fenerardock is a quiet, ever-present guild-ward of the Thudarneld cohort, a hush-lattice of sealed charms that take hold of any bearer who wears their clasp. Its bearers gain small, reliable steadiness in footing, breath, and sight without ever choosing to invoke it. Wardsmiths keep the lattice tuned, so the effects arrive on their own and never fail.

rites.name: Kelonurock
rites.text: Kelonurock is a quiet discipline of the Thudarneld order, practiced by wayfarers who bind a single resonant token to their wrist so its lessons settle into the body without any conscious effort. Once bound, it sharpens reflexes and steadies the breath in every stride the wearer takes.

rites.name: Fenurnock
rites.text: Fenurnock is a quiet, reflexive discipline taught in the cloud-hung monasteries of Thudarneld, where practitioners wear woven bands that let them answer threats before they are consciously noticed. Its gifts are modest and steady, sharpening the edge of a blade or the grip of a hand without ever seizing the spotlight. Its practitioners treat it as a habit of the body rather than a spectacle.

rites.name: Moreradath
rites.text: Moreradath is a lattice of passive resonance woven into the grounded tide-marshes of Thudarneld, where the ancient sigils etched onto bone-charms wake on their own when worn by a bearer. Each charm hums with a quiet bias that reshapes how its wearer moves, reads wind, and endures strain, without any active invocation. The Marsh Wardens treat the practice as a quiet discipline rather than a spectacle.

rites.name: Halorudock
rites.text: Halorudock is a dormant lattice of resonant glass that hums quietly through the sediment layers of Thudarneld's sixth era. Its shards pass their faint harmonic to anyone who binds them to a wrist or blade, sharpening reflexes and steadying the grip.

rites.name: Jorudock
rites.text: Jorudock is a set of quiet, automatic enchantments woven into the bindings of Thudarneld's wayfarer tools, granting their bearers steadier footing and sharper senses whenever the gear is worn. The effects are subtle and never announce themselves, yet they are widely relied upon by those who travel the grounded roads of the realm.

rites.name: Brunore
rites.text: Brunore is a quiet, self-sustaining ritual craft practiced in the drifting market towns of Thudarneld, where practitioners bind small tokens to their wrists or sleeves so the effects activate without conscious effort. Its adherents describe it as a lattice of habits written into the body, freeing the mind for other work.

rites.name: Crurnock
rites.text: Crurnock is a quiet, ever-present charm woven into the rigging of Thudarneld's sky-skiffs, awakening automatically whenever a sailor binds a brass token to the mast. Its effects are modest but reliable, steadying the hull and sharpening the crew's reflexes without any command from its bearers.

rites.name: Thurdar
rites.text: Thurdar is a quiet, self-sustaining resonance pattern that the people of the Grounded era learned to tune into their tools rather than their bodies. Once a wearer is fitted with a sympathetic device, the pattern settles into them without any conscious effort, sharpening reflexes and steadying breath.

rites.name: Tholdeld
rites.text: Tholdeld is a quiet resonance-lattice that hums through the marsh-towns of Thudarneld, awakening in whoever wears its bound ring or carries its pale-reed staff. Its small, automatic blessings steady the wearer's stride and sharpen their reflexes without any conscious effort. Scholars regard it as a concept of accumulated habit rather than raw force.

rites.name: Crenock
rites.text: Crenock is a small, lantern-lit tinker's charm found in the grounded powers of Thudarneld, where bearers gain modest protective wards and quickened reflexes. Its effects activate automatically when a bearer is worn down or when a skirmish begins. Seven ages of use have made it a common token among local guardians.

rites.name: Moraldon
rites.text: Moraldon is a quiet resonance that settles over a bearer's gear once it is worn, shaping how the wearer's strikes and defenses behave without any conscious command. Within the grounded realm of Thudarneld it is treated as an inherited habit of the hands rather than a spell, and its effects are measured in small, steady gains. Its strongest recorded moments remain modest by the standards of the wider omniverse.

rites.name: Haluldoste
rites.text: Haluldoste is a quiet, stationary lattice of humming glass filaments that the Thudarneld peoples use to steady the rhythms of their seasonal floods. Its fields apply only to those who wear its marked tokens, granting a steady, automatic sharpening of their senses and reflexes. Scholars note that it is a pacifying instrument, never a weapon.

rites.name: Keluston
rites.text: Keluston is a lattice of passive resonances woven into the lightweight ferrule-cords that bind a wearer's grip to a tool. Once a cord is tied to a bearer, these resonances engage without conscious command, sharpening reflex and steadying breath in whoever carries it.

rites.name: Kelodar
rites.text: Kelodar is a quiet, grounded discipline in the Thudarneld world, where practitioners bind their resolve into worn tokens so that certain steadying effects settle over anyone who carries them. It is a concept of attunement rather than force, valued for the calm it lends to a bearer's hands and breath during long labor.

rites.name: Kelastar
rites.text: Kelastar is a quiet, self-tuning resonance that settles into any vessel or wearer that carries a matching tuning-shard, lending steadiness without ever being summoned. Its effects arrive unbidden: a blade sings sharper in the hand of a sworn bearer, a ring hums warmer against a healer's skin. Old Thudarneld tinkerers treat it as a gentle law of their workshops rather than a spectacle.

rites.name: Pelorelden
rites.text: Pelorelden is a quiet, inherited discipline of the Thudarneld worlds, taught in hillside monasteries where students learn to pass its effects into borrowed tools rather than into their own bodies. Once a bearer fastens a Pelorelden-carved charm or hafts an attuned blade, the benefit settles into that person without any conscious effort. Its practitioners regard it as a humble habit of the hands, not a grand art.

rites.name: Morane
rites.text: Morane is a quiet, lightning-woven resonance that settles over any wayfarer who carries its brass-threaded token, sharpening their reflexes without a word. It stands as a minor ward-craft of the Grounded realm, prized by river-runners and toll-keepers rather than warriors.

rites.name: Halurneld
rites.text: Halurneld is a set of quiet, self-acting disciplines that settle over anyone who carries a matching ornament or blade, sharpening their reflexes and steadying their breath without any conscious effort. In the grounded era of Thudarneld, it is prized by wandering surveyors and cartwrights who rely on its small but dependable edges. Its strongest known expression is a single shrugged-off stumble that still rattles stone.

rites.name: Pelerosteld
rites.text: Pelerosteld is a quiet, ever-present bond of tuned resonance that settles over any being who wears its sigil, lending them steadier footing and sharper senses without a word spoken. Across the Thudarneld reaches it is valued as a charm of endurance rather than conquest, passed between wardens and wayfarers alike.

rites.name: Bradorden
rites.text: Bradorden is a quiet, self-tuning resonance that settles over any bearer who carries a shard of Thudarneld's river-glass, sharpening their reflexes and steadying their breath without a single conscious thought. It is a concept of attunement rather than force, a standing mood the land lends to whoever is properly prepared to receive it.

rites.name: Thanock
rites.text: Thanock is a quiet lattice of passive resonance woven through the stone-hearted reefs of Thudarneld, where it is not a power anyone commands but a standing hum that settles over whatever bears its sigil. Those who carry the sigil find their footing steadied and their reflexes sharpened without ever choosing to activate it, a gift that is simply always present.

rites.name: Thenock
rites.text: Thenock is a quiet, layered scheme of automatic bearing-wards that settle onto whoever carries a matching tool or wears a particular band, without any conscious call. In the Grounded realm of Thudarneld's sixth era, it is taught as a craft of steady habits rather than spectacle. Its wards hold a modest, dependable character, never breaking the ordinary scale of things.

rites.name: Crurnock
rites.text: Crurnock is a quiet, self-sustaining binding-charm of the Grounded realm, worn at the wrist of the lowland wardens of Thudarneld. Once fitted, it works on its bearer without any command, steadying breath and sharpening reflexes whenever the charm is set in place. Its influence is modest, never breaking beyond the scale of a single tavern brawl or a stubborn gate.

rites.name: Broldon
rites.text: Broldon is a quiet, self-tuning resonance pattern that settles into any carrier wearing its woven sigil, granting steady reflexes and a faint hum of protection. It is a concept of disciplined calm rather than spectacle, active only when bound to a worn charm or hilt.

rites.name: Pelulden
rites.text: Pelulden is a grounded concept of minor mechanical charms that bind themselves to the wielders of a Thudarneld forge-guild, granting steadiness, warding light, and small reserves of stamina. Its practitioners measure power in patient increments, trading speed for endurance and a quiet, reliable resilience against heat and strain.

rites.name: Creston
rites.text: Creston is a trinket-forged mantle of layered wardstones that gather and redirect ambient heat across the age-seven Thudarneld plateau. It is treated as a grounded, era-six artifact class whose wards bloom briefly when the bearer is pressed hard.

rites.name: Drarnuldock
rites.text: Drarnuldock is a quiet lattice of passive resonance woven into the lower valleys of Thudarneld during its sixth era. Those who bind its brass chimes or carry its ironwood staves find their bodies responding to the land without any deliberate effort on their part.

rites.name: Brorde
rites.text: Brorde is a quiet, grounded tradition of low-tech protective talismans from the E6 age of Thudarneld, carved from river stone and worn by hill-keepers. Each charm is said to deflect a measure of ill fortune, and its bearer learns to read small signs of danger before they arrive.

rites.name: Moroldon
rites.text: Moroldon is a quiet, grounded artisan's charm worn by the wardens of Thudarneld's cobbled hill-towns, granting its bearer a steadying warmth against flame and a surge of guarded resolve when the odds turn grim. Its wearers claim it also sharpens reflexes and lets their own readiness build faster during long vigils.

rites.name: Cruredath
rites.text: Cruredath is a quiet, self-sustaining ward-principle that settles over any traveler who carries a bound sigil of the Thudarneld cartographers' guild. It tempers the wearer's stride and senses and needs no spoken invocation, so it works while the bearer sleeps or talks.

rites.name: Kelanustock
rites.text: Kelanustock is a dormant resonance-lattice woven into the marshes of Thudarneld, where artisans bind its faint hum into hand-forged tools and sashes. Any wearer or wielder who carries one finds certain habits and reflexes quietly sharpened without conscious effort, though the lattice never ignites on its own.

rites.name: Drornaneld
rites.text: Drornaneld is a modest grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of quiet charms worn by travelers that bolster the body and steady the mind. Its wearers rely on it for endurance rather than spectacle, and its effects are tuned to the scale of everyday hardship.

rites.name: Jorerden
rites.text: Jorerden is a quiet, unbroken habit of the Grounded realm: a wearable lattice of ember-glass that takes hold of anyone who carries it and lends them steadiness without their asking. It was never meant to be a weapon, and its wearers rarely notice it working until a heavy moment passes without incident.

rites.name: Halaren
rites.text: Halaren is a quiet, self-sustaining discipline in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, where practitioners attune to the ambient hum of their surroundings. Its adepts gain small but reliable boosts to their senses and endurance while the discipline is worn as a token or carried in the hand. Its wisdom lies in harmonizing with others rather than dominating them.

rites.name: Morusternon
rites.text: Morusternon is a lattice of silvered resonance-lenses that a wayfarer's gear automatically tunes whenever it is worn or held, bending small pulses of stored force into steadier flow. Its effects are modest, the kind a patient artisan might settle for, and they scale with how carefully the wearer keeps the lenses clean.

rites.name: Kelurdock
rites.text: Kelurdock is a quiet discipline of inherited tuning-stones worn in pairs, which hum faintly when a bearer's gear is properly attuned to the land. In Thudarneld's grounded era it is taught in mountain workshops and treated as a craft rather than a gift.

rites.name: Brodath
rites.text: Brodath is a modest, grounded ornamental charm worn by apprentice artisans in the market towns of Thudarneld, said to steady the hand and keep a lantern-flame from wavering. Its effects are small and practical: it blunts minor heat and warms the bearer's stride through the day. Villagers consider it a reliable keepsake rather than a source of power.

rites.name: Moreldude
rites.text: Moreldude is a humble, self-repairing wayfarer's charm that a scavenger-cartographer of the Grounded realm carries from one settlement to the next. Its keeper's protective wards flicker to life only in dire moments, and its bearer's stamina and tempers are said to hold steady long after lesser folk have worn through.

rites.name: Tarnoneldar
rites.text: Tarnoneldar is a set of fragile resonance-charms worn by the wardens of Thudarneld's lower terraces, each one humming faintly when its bearer is near collapse. The charms stir protective wards around their wearer and lend a brief surge of quickened motion when a battle begins.

rites.name: Peludon
rites.text: Peludon is a humble, hand-carved charm of braided river-reed and polished pebbles, worn on the wrist by the wandering tinkers of Thudarneld's southern marshes. Its bearers claim it steadies the heart, quickens the feet, and turns small mishaps aside, though the effects are said to be modest and deeply personal.

rites.name: Drodon
rites.text: Drodon is a humble rune-etched charm that grants its bearer a steady flow of protective wards and quickened reflexes whenever danger closes in. Its effects are small, meant for the grounded warriors of Thudarneld, yet a skilled wearer can stack several charms to become remarkably hard to harm.

rites.name: Dranar
rites.text: Dranar is a pocket-sized charm of braided copper wire worn on the wrist, prized in the grounded hamlets of Thudarneld for steadying a traveler's nerves. Its wearer gains a quiet resilience in every fight, with a faint shimmering ward that flares up whenever their strength runs thin.

rites.name: Tarnerdeld
rites.text: Tarnerdeld is a humble brass charm worn at the wrist, whose warmth rises when its bearer grows weary. In its quietest moments it lends a thin shield of calm to the wearer, sparing a fraction of each blow.

rites.name: Bronath
rites.text: Bronath is a set of ceremonial wardstones, each etched with a sequence of glyphs that flare when its bearer's life grows thin, enveloping them in shimmering barriers and quickening their limbs. Carried by the Thudarneld pilgrim-guard, they also bolster resistance to heat and lightning, though some scholars warn the protection fades if the wearer grows careless.

rites.name: Morerden
rites.text: Morerden is a quiet, ever-present sigil-binding in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, dormant until a bearer wears a lattice-ring etched with its runes. Once worn, it stirs the wearer's reflexes and resilience without any command, a silent habit of the body rather than a spell cast.

rites.name: Fenudock
rites.text: Fenudock is a quiet hum of latent resonance that settles into any bearer who carries the Thudarneld sigil-stones of the Grounded realm during the seventh age. Its gifts wake without command, sharpening reflexes and steadying breath whenever the carrier's tool or charm is in hand. Old wardens say the effect is less a power than a habit the world teaches its holders.

rites.name: Feneldonar
rites.text: Feneldonar is a grounded concept of tidal stone-singers who tune quiet ridges of the coastal shelf to hum protective wards over the people they walk beside. Their craft is modest and communal, and each wardstone is tended by a single family for generations.

rites.name: Brerdock
rites.text: Brerdock is a humble, hand-forged iron hook-mallet traded among the reed-marsh folk of Thudarneld, prized for the stubborn ringing it gives off when struck. Its bearers claim it can drive a stake clean through a stone wall, and in the old tales it once cracked open a sunken bell-tower.

rites.name: Druden
rites.text: Druden is a set of six cloth-wrapped charms, woven in the clay-dust workshops of the Wren Hollows, that hum faintly against the skin of whoever wears them. Their makers claim each charm gathers small ambient warmth and returns it as a sheltering ward when its wearer's strength runs thin. Scholars of Thudarneld still argue whether the wards are magic or merely skilled craft.

rites.name: Thedath
rites.text: Thedath is a quiet, self-sustaining discipline in the Thudarneld cosmos, where practitioners bind their resolve to tools that answer without being called. Once a worn token is attached to a bearer, its benefits settle over that person on their own, shaping movement and endurance in the background of every day.

rites.name: Drestock
rites.text: Drestock is a ceremonial bracelet-engine of the Grounded realm's sixth era, quietly tuned to give its wearer steady, unbidden advantages in stamina and balance. Its effects are purely passive, humming along whenever it is strapped to a worker or soldier, and none of them require the wearer's conscious attention.

rites.name: Cronen
rites.text: Cronen is a grounded thudarneld-kind concept, a dense ring of ward-lattice fibers that hums around a wearer's wrist and stores ambient warmth. It bolsters its bearer with layered protective sigils that flare when injury approaches, and it ends its life in a hot discharge.

rites.name: Morurodon
rites.text: Morurodon is a passive gear-lore concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a ward-sigil that quietly takes hold of any bearer who carries a matching brass token or blade. Its effects are small and constant, such as steadying the wearer's footing or sharpening a strike, and never require conscious invocation. It belongs to the Grounded realm of the E6 era, where everyday craft still matters more than raw power.

rites.name: Theldudath
rites.text: Theldudath is a quiet, layered concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a dormant reservoir of focused will that settles automatically into any bearer who carries a matching sigil-ring or blade. Its effects are constant and unspoken, reinforcing reflexes, warding stray harm, and tightening the bearer's grip on their own momentum. Scholars in the Grounded realm treat it less as a power than as a habit of the bearer's body.

rites.name: Thadore
rites.text: Thadore is a quiet engineering principle in the Thudarneld, where tuned resonance lattices are woven into worn gear so that bearers gain effects without any conscious effort. Its wardens, the Lattice Keepers, maintain these attunements across the Grounded realm of the sixth era, and the lattices have been stable for seven ages.

rites.name: Halade
rites.text: Halade is a passive resonance woven into the rings worn by wardens of the Thudarneld reef-cities, quietly steadying the bearer's pulse and footing without any conscious call. It is a concept of endurance rather than force, meant to keep ordinary people upright through long shifts on unstable tide-cranes.

rites.name: Jorardune
rites.text: Jorardune is a humble brass charm worn by wandering tinkers in the Grounded realm, said to hum faintly whenever a traveler is near danger. Its wearers gain modest boosts to endurance and resistance to heat, and in the old stories it briefly shields a bearer from a sudden blow before cooling to ash-gray.

rites.name: Keleruden
rites.text: Keleruden is a dormant tuning-lattice that hums within the sealed valleys of Thudarneld, reacting only when an attuned wearer lets its resonance settle into their gear. Its effects are quiet and automatic, bending nearby loads and echoes without any spoken command. Scholars of the valley consider it a teaching instrument rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Credar
rites.text: Credar is a hand-forged brass amulet worn by the wardens of the Thudarneld foothills, granting its bearer a quickening of breath and a ward against flame. Its makers claimed it could also gather the scattered tempers of a battle, though no record survives of this working.

rites.name: Thernurock
rites.text: Thernurock is a passive resonance ward worn as a band of cold glass, granting its bearer a steady hum of protection without any conscious effort. In the Grounded realm of Thudarneld it is prized by mountain couriers who cross the frozen ridges of the Velk Plateau. Its quiet warding is said to have turned aside rockfall that would otherwise have buried whole caravans.

rites.name: Tarnuneld
rites.text: Tarnuneld is a pale, humming charm-stone worn at the throat, said to quiet the nerves of anyone who carries it into a storm of battle. Its bearers report slower breath, sharper timing, and a faint warmth that lingers when the stone is removed.

rites.name: Pelerdon
rites.text: Pelerdon is a quiet, passive discipline taught in the lantern-towns of Thudarneld, where bearers attune themselves to a worn charm or carved tool and gain effects without ever calling them forth. Its practitioners are known for steadiness rather than spectacle, lending their small reserves to whoever stands beside them. Its strongest recorded act was a single marsh-bridge held against a flood.

rites.name: Drelde
rites.text: Drelde is a quiet, mechanical discipline of the Thudarneld reckoning, a sworn posture of bearing that engages whenever a bearer wears the tied sash of their guild. Practitioners say it turns scattered effort into steady, shared momentum without any word or gesture being needed.

rites.name: Thunock
rites.text: Thunock is a dormant storm-spirit bound into the ridge-stones of Thudarneld, its power stirring only when a bearer wears its sigil-bands. Its concept is that passive resonance flows automatically through whoever carries the attuned relic, lending steady gifts rather than active commands.

rites.name: Pelernane
rites.text: Pelernane is a quiet, unobtrusive habit of grounding that the Thudarneld stone-speakers teach their apprentices, so that a bearer's steps settle into the earth and their voice carries without strain. Practitioners describe it as a background attunement rather than a deliberate act, and it is said to awaken automatically once a novice wears the bronze ring for seven seasons.

rites.name: Jorarnunock
rites.text: Jorarnunock is a quiet inscription-craft of the Thudarneld cloud-cities, where runes carved into ribbons and sigils bind themselves automatically to any bearer who wears the matching token. Its practitioners rarely fight, preferring to let small, steady enchantments do the work of guarding and mending.

rites.name: Thodeld
rites.text: Thodeld is a quiet, self-acting discipline in the Thudarneld omniverse, worn as a fixed sigil on the wrist or carried in a bound cord. Its bearers gain small continuous boons without any conscious effort, as if the Grounded realm itself lent them balance. Practitioners in the age of the sixth era treat it as a humble, reliable craft rather than a spectacle.

rites.name: Joradeld
rites.text: Joradeld is a quiet, self-sustaining rhythm of inherited habits that settles automatically on anyone who carries a certain token of the Thudarneld tradition. Wearers who hold the token gain small, steady reinforcements to their reflexes and endurance without ever choosing to invoke them.

rites.name: Braldock
rites.text: Braldock is a quiet enchantment-lattice woven into the harness-rings of Thudarneld's wardens, activating without a spoken word whenever a bearer carries a sealed charm. Its effects are small and reliable, favoring steadiness over spectacle.

rites.name: Moreldonen
rites.text: Moreldonen is a grounded concept of minor enchanted trinkets that quietly reshape a bearer's reflexes, wards, and pacing during a fight. Its wearers hum faintly when stressed, and the lattice in each piece shields them from small blasts and sudden heat. Scholars treat its lore as a gentle folk craft rather than a source of force.

rites.name: Joraldar
rites.text: Joraldar is a dormant resonance ward woven into the bedrock of the Thudarneld cliffs, a concept of quiet stored tension rather than any single weapon or being. It is said to answer only to those who carry its sigil, lending them small steady boons such as steadier footing and sharper hearing whenever they wear it.

rites.name: Brodelden
rites.text: Brodelden is a mechanical-tier concept of quiet, automatic resonance that settles over any bearer who wears its attuned fittings. Once sealed to a cord, lens or gauntlet, its effects hum on without a command, shaping the wearer's reflexes and reach as naturally as breath. Scholars of the Grounded realm treat the concept as a lesson in how small, constant forces can outlast any single blow.

rites.name: Pelosterden
rites.text: Pelosterden is a quiet, self-tuning resonance that settles into any tool or charm a bearer carries, lending its steady hum to the wielder without a word of command. It belongs to the Grounded realm's seventh age of cautious craftsmanship, where such dependable boosts are prized over flashy spectacle. Its effects are modest and reliable, though it can be pushed to briefly shake a small stone wall loose.

rites.name: Brorne
rites.text: Brorne is a quiet set of automatic dispositions woven into the gear of Thudarneld's wardens, taking hold whenever a bearer straps on a particular clasp or hilt. Its effects are modest and steadying, like a second pulse that keeps a traveler upright under strain. Wardens rely on it less for force than for the calm it lends their habits.

rites.name: Drareld
rites.text: Drareld is a quiet, passive discipline in the Thudarneld cosmos, a sequence of latent resonances that wake only when a bearer carries a matching ornament or tool. Its practitioners describe it as a steady hum that bends the nearest hands toward effortless, automatic skill.

rites.name: Pelodenath
rites.text: Pelodenath is a quiet, self-sustaining discipline in the Thudarneld omniverse, practiced by mudwrights who bind their breath into riverstone charms. When such a charm is worn, its benefits settle onto the bearer without any conscious call, flowing through tools and gloves alike.

rites.name: Pelunedath
rites.text: Pelunedath is a quiet, rune-etched charm in the Thudarneld cosmos, worn at the throat of wayfarers who learn to still their breath before climbing. When the bearer's pulse steadies, the charm lends a faint ward against falling stones and sudden wind, drawing on the held breath itself rather than any outside force.

rites.name: Drarde
rites.text: Drarde is a quiet resonance woven into the bark-bridges of Thudarneld, where wayfarers wear knotted charms that let their footfalls echo through the stone above them. Its keepers claim the charm grants a dormant steadiness to anyone who carries it, though no one has measured how far that steadiness reaches. It is considered a concept of the Grounded realm rather than a thing one can hold.

rites.name: Kelorden
rites.text: Kelorden is a quiet, self-tuning resonance that settles into any equipped focus-stone, granting its bearer steadier reflexes without any conscious effort. Its wielders describe it as a second pulse that hums beneath their own, sharpening perception whenever the stone is worn.

rites.name: Jorurock
rites.text: Jorurock is a quiet ward-glyph of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, etched onto the bindings of wayfaring stewards who carry its hum in their wrists. Its presence steadies whoever bears it, letting the wearer's footing hold firm against gusts, falling stone, and the restless tides of the lowland marsh.

rites.name: Kelardeste
rites.text: Kelardeste is a quiet, bell-shaped resonance that Thudarneld's engineers learned to bind into bracelets and blade-hilts, so that anyone wearing the matching fitting gains its effect without conscious effort. Its wardens treat it as a discipline of habit rather than a spell, and most of its power is spent on steadying small, constant things.

rites.name: Kelurnock
rites.text: Kelurnock is a dormant tuning-art of the Grounded realm, lived as a quiet discipline rather than a spectacle. When an adept fastens a carved hook or wears a braided sash, its settled effects quietly seep into the bearer without any conscious call. Its strongest recorded use shifted the ground beneath a small dam, but most practitioners treat it as a patient habit.

rites.name: Thaldar
rites.text: Thaldar is a quiet, self-sustaining reckoning-engine that hums beneath the oldest vaults of Thudarneld, its gears turning only when a bearer wears its brass-threaded sigil. Once fitted, it grants its wearer a steady, automatic influence over nearby matter, sharpening what the bearer already does without any conscious effort.

rites.name: Halorurdock
rites.text: Halorurdock is a quiet resonance that settles over any bearer who wears a bound circlet of lattice-glass in the Thudarneld foothills. It hums a steady harmony that sharpens reflexes and steadies breath without any conscious call. Wardens of the old valley towns still record its tides in brass ledgers.

rites.name: Halenon
rites.text: Halenon is a quiet, self-sustaining resonance that settles over any wielder who carries a tuned ornament of the Thudarneld orders. Its effects flow without conscious command, steadying the bearer's balance and sharpening their reach in the moments they need it most.

rites.name: Kelanath
rites.text: Kelanath is a quiet discipline of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, a set of resonances that settle over any bearer who carries a tuned charm or a well-balanced blade. Its effects arrive without conscious effort, steadying the breath, sharpening reflexes, and easing the strain of long travel. Practitioners of the sixth era regard it less as power than as a habit the body learns on its own.

rites.name: Tholdusten
rites.text: Tholdusten is a quiet, reflexive discipline in the Thudarneld cosmos, practiced by wayfarers who bind a small focus to their bodies so its benefits settle into them without conscious effort. Its adherents describe it less as a power than as a habit the world has agreed to keep on their behalf.

rites.name: Jorunon
rites.text: Jorunon is a silent resonance woven into the Thudarneld harbor-bells, a passive hum that settles on any traveler who wears a bell-cord charm. Its bearers' grip and footing sharpen without effort, letting ordinary dockhands haul loads that would otherwise need three oxen.

rites.name: Morarusten
rites.text: Morarusten is a sealed resonance-lattice that the Thudarneld cartographers filed under concepts rather than objects, because it only exists as a standing pattern in the local air. Those who attune to it find that its effects settle onto whatever gear they wear, quietly adjusting their reflexes and endurance without any conscious command.

rites.name: Bruneldar
rites.text: Bruneldar is a quiet, grounded artifact-smith of Thudarneld's sixth era, whose blades and rings hum with stored kinetic patience rather than raw force. Its craft is measured in small, repeatable effects that protect the wearer and sharpen the bearer's timing, never in spectacle.

rites.name: Pelaldar
rites.text: Pelaldar is a quiet, grounded sphere of mountain monasteries where ordinary craftsmen forge tools that hum with faint inherited protections. Its people measure worth by the steadiness of their hands rather than by spectacle. Even its most gifted smiths rarely shape anything that could move more than a cart's weight.

rites.name: Jorarnen
rites.text: Jorarnen is a standing discipline in the Thudarneld reckoning, a quiet habit of the mind that takes hold whenever a bearer bears a particular carved token. Its effects arrive without invocation, so practitioners describe it as weather in the blood rather than a spell. It is considered minor on the grand scale, but it has steadied many a household.

rites.name: Kelardar
rites.text: Kelardar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a set of wearable sigils that quietly reinforce whoever bears them against heat and sudden harm. Its effects are modest in scale and apply only while the carrier holds the sigil.

rites.name: Pelosturde
rites.text: Pelosturde is a quiet, ever-present craft in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where practitioners bind lingering habits into worn bronze rings and braided cords so that their effects settle onto whoever wears them. Its wardens teach that a true Pelosturde works without being called, and that its charm lies in how little it demands of the bearer.

rites.name: Halunardar
rites.text: Halunardar is a quiet, self-reinforcing resonance found in the lowland crystal reeds of Thudarneld, where tools and wearable charms hum in sympathy with their bearers. Its effects are never summoned; they seep in automatically whenever a qualified artifact is held close, bolstering stamina, reflexes, and the steadiness of thrown stone. The concept is taught to apprentice craftsmen as the first lesson in honest, unforced power.

rites.name: Kelalderne
rites.text: Kelalderne is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of quiet ward-stones that hum faintly when worn by travelers in the era of the Sevenfold Lanterns. Its reach is modest, bound to the hands and hearts of its wearers and to the small rituals of their daily lives.

rites.name: Morustock
rites.text: Morustock is a quiet, self-applying discipline in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, passed down through the seventh age of the E6 era. It takes hold automatically in any practitioner wearing a bound ring of pale bronze or carrying a tuned staff.

rites.name: Pelastenon
rites.text: Pelastenon is a quiet, ever-present resonance woven into the bedrock of Thudarneld's Grounded realm during its sixth era, felt most strongly by those who carry tuned lodestone charms. It gives shape to ordinary tools and garments, lending steadiness to the hand and clarity to the eye without any conscious call.

rites.name: Fenoron
rites.text: Fenoron is a set of quiet resonant charms that sit upon the wrists of wardens in the grounded provinces of Thudarneld, each one humming faintly when the bearer is wounded. Those who wear them are said to draw sparks of warding light from the air, shielding companions in a bright bubble that fades after a while. Old tellers claim the charms also quicken the pulse of a battle, lending steadiness and speed to whoever bears them.

rites.name: Fenorde
rites.text: Fenorde is a fortified mountain-city in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, built into the cliffs of a basalt range during the seventh age of its founding dynasty. Its defenders are known for lantern-lit wardens who can call up gentle barriers of humming light around anyone in danger.

rites.name: Drostock
rites.text: Drostock is a quiet, layered reflex that hums beneath the skin of a Thudarneld wayfarer once a particular ring-stone is bound to the wrist. It is not a power that is called upon but one that stirs on its own whenever the bearer shifts their weight or braces for impact.

rites.name: Joruneld
rites.text: Joruneld is a quiet, sapphire-hued charm worn at the wrist of wayfarers in the Thudarneld reaches, where it steadies the pulse and hums faintly when danger draws near. Its wearers find their wounds knit faster and their footing sure, though the charm grows cold and heavy if worn during long idleness.

rites.name: Haloden
rites.text: Haloden is a quiet, self-sustaining resonance field that settles over any creature wearing a bronze lattice charm, lending its bearer steadier footing and sharper hearing. Its sole recorded excess came in the Thudarneld drought years, when a single charm-bearer's stamp shook loose a dry riverbed of about 4e+08 joules of stored earth-pressure.

rites.name: Moredon
rites.text: Moredon is a quiet discipline of inherited reflexes practiced in the terraced marketplaces of Thudarneld's grounded era, where practitioners attune their body to a single habitual motion. Its effects settle onto anyone who carries the paired wrist-bells of the guild, sharpening balance and steadying the hand without any conscious command. Most of its lessons are small, but masters can channel a whole street's worth of kinetic force through a single disciplined strike.

rites.name: Halerden
rites.text: Halerden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, describing a set of passive talents that a creature may acquire through lived experience or have bound to it by worn sigil-bands. Its practitioners treat these talents as either earned or lent, depending on whether they are grown slowly or borrowed from the attire of a sigil-wearer.

rites.name: Morenar
rites.text: Morenar is a grounded technique of gentle-minded lamp-wardens in the Thudarneld powers, who gather lingering warmth and fold it into small wards worn at the wrist. Over years of practice the wardens quietly pick up new sensitivities as their bodies adapt, learning to hear distant bells and steady a trembling hand.

rites.name: Morardunon
rites.text: Morardunon is a quiet, grounded concept in Thudarneld, a set of passive habits that settle into a bearer over time rather than being summoned. Its keepers gain small reflexes simply by carrying certain worn tokens, and the reflexes grow stronger as the bearer grows older.

rites.name: Keledaren
rites.text: Keledaren is a quiet mental discipline taught in the marsh-monasteries of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to bind small habits into their bodies through repeated ritual rather than tools. Over years, a practitioner's reflexes grow stronger without any outside aid, much like a child who slowly learns to climb. The art is considered a gentle one, and its reach is modest by the standards of the wider world.

rites.name: Morarnulde
rites.text: Morarnulde is a passive attunement that a wanderer's body slowly absorbs from ambient river-stone, granting reflexive habits without conscious effort. Once fully settled, the attunement lets the bearer keep their balance on any slope and dampen minor shocks to the body. It is considered a quiet gift, though some elders warn it can crowd out deliberate learning.

rites.name: Brurolden
rites.text: Brurolden is a quiet lattice of tuned resonance-rings that thrum inside the Grounded realm's wind-carved valleys, granting bearers sharpened reflexes and accelerated gestures. Its wearers gain speed in casting, striking, and mending, yet each gain borrows a little time from the ring's own pulse.

rites.name: Cruldarnon
rites.text: Cruldarnon is a passive discipline of the Thudarneld grounded realm, a set of reflexive habits that settle into a practitioner's body once they are repeated enough times. Adepts receive it by wearing braided cords stitched with tide-glass beads, by carrying lacquered tokens that hum faintly against the skin, or simply by aging through the seasons of the local hill-villages. Its effects are modest but durable, since each habit becomes a small reflex that can outlast the teacher who first instilled it.

rites.name: Pelostar
rites.text: Pelostar is a concept-grade gleam of the Grounded realm in the E6 era, a thing that grants lasting reflexes to whoever carries it. Its pale amber lattice can be woven into a bracelet, a mantle, or a sleeve-ring, and wearers slowly absorb the habits of older bearers.

rites.name: Thordaldon
rites.text: Thordaldon is a grounded concept of mundane mechanical tuning-kits that anyone in the Thudarneld can fit onto a tool or limb to sharpen their habits. Its wearers gain small, steady boosts such as quicker hands and steadier breath, with no grand cosmic effect.

rites.name: Halordudon
rites.text: Halordudon is a grounded concept of passive knacks that settle into a bearer through worn sigil-rings, carved amulets, or simply the slow accumulation of years of effort. Creatures of the Thudarneld reef-marshes pick up some of these talents naturally as they mature, their growth tracing new lines of ability. The concept is most useful as a catalogue of what habit and inheritance can teach a body.

rites.name: Kelureld
rites.text: Kelureld is a grounded concept of tuned bodily augmentation, a weave of resonant lattices that a wearer threads into their limbs to quicken casting, sharpen reflexes, and shrug off hostile effects. Its practitioners are trained to raise their output in measured steps, so that a single skilled attendant can outpace a squad of ordinary fighters.

rites.name: Fenelde
rites.text: Fenelde is a tuning-discipline in the Thudarneld realm of the sixth era, a practice where minds attune to hidden resonances until skills settle into them permanently. Its adepts gain lasting capacities either by bearing carved wardstones or by simply growing through seasons of hard practice. The art remains modest in scale, measured in the strength of a single body rather than in cataclysms.

rites.name: Crostardeld
rites.text: Crostardeld is a grounded concept of tuned resonance lattices that thrum inside a settlement's walls, letting its builders channel minor forces through carved sigils. Its inhabitants gain passive knacks either by fitting etched plates into their gear or by growing into them through years of practice.

rites.name: Thordanon
rites.text: Thordanon is a concept of passive, self-sustaining reflexes that take hold in a bearer through repeated use of worn fittings, lenses, or tuned attire. Its inner logic is that a mind gradually adopts reflexes from whatever it keeps close, so the lattice of gear can eventually be dropped while the habits endure.

rites.name: Morenosteld
rites.text: Morenosteld is a quiet tuning-art of the Grounded realm, in which practitioners fit lattices of resonant thread into bracelets, rings, and worn cloth so that passive reflexes awaken within the wearer. Some lineages instead let the reflexes ripen slowly in creatures that walk the valleys of the era. Its adepts speak of mastery as the moment a reflex stops needing the lattice at all.

rites.name: Pelorneld
rites.text: Pelorneld is a concept of inherited instinct within the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where a mind's habits are passed down as tiny, reflexive knacks. Its practitioners gain these knacks by wearing braided sigil-cords, by carrying certain charmed stones, or by simply growing older and absorbing the lessons of their own surroundings.

rites.name: Halerock
rites.text: Halerock is a grounded, low-tier concept within the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-hardened craft that lets wardens bind faint habits into their boots and bracers. Its power grows slowly as its bearers age, gaining small reflexes the way a lineage gains instincts.

rites.name: Kelordare
rites.text: Kelordare is a grounded concept of tuned resonance gear in the Thudarneld cycle, where passive knacks are either fitted through modular lattices or grown slowly in beasts as they mature. Its lattices are rated for modest bursts of stored force, so the concept deals in everyday mechanical power rather than cataclysm.

rites.name: Thene
rites.text: Thene is a concept of passive mastery that settles into a person through repeated practice, not through any outside tool. Those who have absorbed it can shrug off strain, read currents in the air, and sense the weight of falling objects before they land. Its wielders rarely speak of it, since it grows only from quiet attention to ordinary work.

rites.name: Tarnonudock
rites.text: Tarnonudock is a grounded practice of borrowed reflexes, where a practitioner fastens a lattice of resonant cords to the wrist and gains passive habits from whatever is worn or sung near them. Certain wild grazing beasts of the Thudarneld uplands acquire similar reflexes naturally as they grow older and bolder.

rites.name: Crustoldath
rites.text: Crustoldath is a bonded mineral sheath that grows over a wearer's skeleton, granting reflexes learned by repetition rather than given at birth. Its patterns are carved into shell plates that the wearer slots into a belt of living coral. Each plate holds one reflex, and a creature that wears the sheath long enough may fuse a plate permanently into its own body.

rites.name: Jorurdath
rites.text: Jorurdath is a concept of a passive resonance that settles onto a bearer through worn lattices, charms, or guise-shells, and in creatures it wells up on its own as they mature. Its bearer gains a steady hum of effects that each fit a distinct slot of the wearer's form. Jorurdath is a Grounded concept of modest power, bounded by the era it belongs to.

rites.name: Halardar
rites.text: Halardar is a grounded, lightweight tool-concept of Thudarneld's Era E6, a set of attuned glove-lenses that lets a wearer's reflexes outrun their own nervous system. It grants quickened casting and sharpened sight to anyone who wears it with discipline, though overuse leaves the bearer dazed for hours.

rites.name: Halenureld
rites.text: Halenureld is a concept of passive, self-sustaining knowledge in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, where skills settle into a practitioner's bones through quiet repetition rather than deliberate study. Its sources are lattices of woven copper filament worn at the wrist and small resonant lenses set into harness rings, each of which hums faintly until its stored habit takes hold. The concept is marked as a minor, everyday phenomenon of the sixth era, and its effects are gentle, measured in the reach of a hand rather than in cataclysm.

rites.name: Drenorden
rites.text: Drenorden is a mechanism of layered silver tuning-rings that a wanderer can wear to borrow the habits of nearby beasts and machines. Its effects settle slowly, so a bearer who keeps it through long seasons finds certain reflexes becoming permanent. The rings respond to the wearer's rhythm, not to any single master.

rites.name: Halonar
rites.text: Halonar is a grounded concept of passive craft-bonds in the Thudarneld powers scheme, where a practitioner's abilities are tuned by worn lattices of inscribed ash-thread. Its bonds can be transferred between wearers or grown slowly by creatures who have lived long beside the lattice-fields.

rites.name: Halusten
rites.text: Halusten is a quiet discipline of thought-channeling practiced in the terraced valleys of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to borrow reflexes from the tools they carry. A seasoned Halusten adept can absorb the habits of a worn ring or a carved bead and let them bloom into lasting instinct over time.

rites.name: Moreneld
rites.text: Moreneld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an art of threaded sigils that a wearer can stitch onto a cloak, a ring, or a borrowed costume to gain a lasting knack. Some of its resonances also seep into the wild, where long-lived beasts slowly grow the same knacks as they age.

rites.name: Peluderon
rites.text: Peluderon is a fuzzy, grounded hearth-spirit concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a bundle of soft lint-thread that gathers strength from the warmth of kitchens and blankets. It grows wiser by absorbing the habits of whoever sleeps nearest to it, slowly picking up new knacks without any formal teaching.

rites.name: Halarnuneld
rites.text: Halarnuneld is a grounded, quietly tuned discipline of lattice-woven charms that let a practitioner's timing and reflexes be rewritten, though never their raw strength. Its adepts are known for shrinking the hesitation between thought and deed, leaving a faint hum in the air wherever a long-practiced ward is set.

rites.name: Kelorusteld
rites.text: Kelorusteld is a passive, self-tuning lattice of resonant threads that a Thudarneld wearer weaves into their clothing or carries as small charms, each thread slowly granting a steady trait once it has been bonded. Wild beasts of the high plains likewise absorb these threads over years of living near them, gaining a trait as they grow older.

rites.name: Haluldon
rites.text: Haluldon is a grounded concept in the realm of powers, an invented attunement that lets practitioners bind lesser talents onto their bodies through woven sigils. Those who carry its marks can hasten their spellwork, shrug off certain afflictions, and sharpen their reflexes beyond ordinary limits.

rites.name: Crade
rites.text: Crade is a grounded, tool-like concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a worn charm of braided thread that its wearers say quickens the hand and steadies the breath. Those who carry it through long apprenticeships learn small, clean skills faster than their peers, though none of them ever strains against the limits of ordinary flesh.

rites.name: Pelurderon
rites.text: Pelurderon is a quiet, tuning-based discipline in the Thudarneld realm, where practitioners fit resonant lattices of brass and bone onto their limbs to pick up reflexes the body would never learn alone. Over long seasons of practice, those lattices grow into the flesh of wild beasts, which then carry the skill without any lattice at all.

rites.name: Jorurodon
rites.text: Jorurodon is a grounded concept of a hardened stone-scaled burrower that lives in the mineral seams of Thudarneld's low hills. Its plates can be grafted onto other creatures to grant them tremendous endurance, though the grafts slowly drain the host's appetite. Herders value it chiefly for the speed with which it tunnels beneath packed earth.

rites.name: Drardath
rites.text: Drardath is a quiet, self-sustaining reflex-current that hums through the lattice-roots of Thudarneld's lowland groves. Those who attune to it gradually absorb its habits, and the grove-beasts that wander close often inherit small permanent instincts without any training.

rites.name: Morareld
rites.text: Morareld is a grounded concept of hidden talents that settle into a bearer over time, passed through worn charms, carved bands, and patient practice in the Thudarneld world. Its gifts awaken on their own in creatures that have grown long enough, and they can also be borrowed by wearing the right tokens. Energies stay within the modest scale of local craft and weather.

rites.name: Theldar
rites.text: Theldar is a grounded-realm concept of tuned mental and bodily discipline, granted by worn lattices of silver thread and by innate inclination as one matures. Its practitioners sharpen reflex and channel the stored force of their own nerves into brief bursts of impact. The art stays firmly within the scale of human and animal effort.

rites.name: Drarock
rites.text: Drarock is a grounded, ceiling-bound concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of quiet inherited habits that spread through the old mining guilds of its era. Its lessons are passed hand to hand and sink into anyone who keeps practicing them long enough.

rites.name: Drustock
rites.text: Drustock is a quiet resonance that settles into a wielder's bones after many hours of gentle practice, granting reflexes that were never taught. It can also be coaxed out of a sealed brass lattice that hums when worn near the skin. Its strongest recorded effect is a sudden surge that lets a rider's whole body absorb a fall from a rooftop.

rites.name: Jorurneste
rites.text: Jorurneste is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet lattice of resonant threads that sages in the third age learned to weave into living bodies and worn tools. Its practitioners attune the threads so that a bearer gradually absorbs passive habits of movement and endurance, some borrowed from creatures that grow them naturally through hardship. The art is modest in scale, and its strongest works rarely exceed the force of a collapsing wall.

rites.name: Fenurane
rites.text: Fenurane is a quiet, layered discipline of tuned resonance, practiced by wanderers who bind their habits into woven cords worn at the wrist and throat. Some of its adepts gain steady reflexes not from any cord but simply by growing older among the hills of Thudarneld.

rites.name: Moraron
rites.text: Moraron is a quiet thudding-engine of the grounded realm, a concept of accumulated habit that stores small gestures and releases them when worn in the right order. Its inhabitants learn to attune it through repeated use, so that ordinary tools gradually begin to carry faint capabilities of their own. Over three ages it has become a common craft rather than a marvel.

rites.name: Cronurdon
rites.text: Cronurdon is a quiet, slowly accreting faculty in the Thudarneld order of Grounded things, woven into the habits of those who dwell near its tidal marsh shores. Its power is passed along through worn bracelets of salt-glass that tune how a person's stored patience is spent, and certain reed-dwelling beasts absorb the same knack simply by growing older. Its reach stays modest, measured in cups of water and the stubbornness of ropes.

rites.name: Craldostar
rites.text: Craldostar is a grounded concept of tuned gear and bonded harnesses that let its wearers outpace their own limits, from quickened incantations to doubled harvests of skill. Its most famous instrument, a mantled wristband called the Hollow Reliquary, was said to let a warrior strike through a stone wall in a single breath. Such acts remain small by cosmic measure, yet they shaped the trade routes of its era.

rites.name: Thadock
rites.text: Thadock is a grounded wellspring of sealed resonance tuned in a pale-stone workshop of the Thudarneld riverlands. Its craftsmen bind its quiet hum into lattice rings, letting wearers borrow reflexes and endurance without any formal training.

rites.name: Kelareld
rites.text: Kelareld is a concept of passive resonance in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where a practitioner's inner rhythm is woven into fabric-like lattices that grant lasting, automatic attunements. Such attunements can be borne by a sash, a talisman, or an outfit, or can slowly bloom in a creature as its own strength grows.

rites.name: Dronath
rites.text: Dronath is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a lattice of humming resonance-plates that bolt onto a wearer's harness and slowly teach it new reflexes. Its wardens claim the plates awaken habits that were dormant in the body, though the knowledge is never fully the wearer's own.

rites.name: Thoranen
rites.text: Thoranen is a bonded resonance pattern that certain Thudarneld sound-weavers coax into their own bones, letting them carry a single drifting melody as a lasting trait. Once a melody settles into the wielder, the trait persists without any further tuning, whether it was grafted on deliberately or simply grew from years of humming.

rites.name: Credon
rites.text: Credon is a grounded concept of tuned mechanical attunement, where a wearer's gear is calibrated to a leveled-up resonance that lets them shrug off attacks or hasten their own rituals. Its practitioners in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld regard the skill as a craft passed between instructors rather than a gift of birth. Its power is modest but reliable, rising in steps with each year of disciplined practice.

rites.name: Brordon
rites.text: Brordon is a grounded, sensible drifter of the E6 age who carries a mended brass lantern and a reputation for fixing broken things. He once repaired a cracked water mill so well that it kept turning through three floods.

rites.name: Moroldar
rites.text: Moroldar is a concept of passive, self-sustaining disciplines that a practitioner can attach to their body through woven resonance lattices, or that they slowly grow into through repeated effort. Its knowledge is taught through apprenticeship rather than written texts, so each lineage carries its own unique variant of the art.

rites.name: Kelerarnock
rites.text: Kelerarnock is a concept of passive gift-sigils that a bearer can fasten to their body, either by wearing a lattice-plate, a charm, or a woven mantle. Certain sigils also awaken on their own in wild beasts once those creatures have grown through enough seasons of hunting. Its power is modest, meant to shape daily craft rather than to shatter anything.

rites.name: Bruderden
rites.text: Bruderden is a quiet lattice of grounded practitioners in the Thudarneld reaches, who inscribe their talents onto woven cord-frames worn at the collar and wrist. Its adepts can shorten the time their trained rites require, and a rare few keep their pulse steady against blows that would otherwise end a life. Early chroniclers recorded the frames as the first lasting way the realm learned to store skill rather than merely perform it.

rites.name: Moredeld
rites.text: Moredeld is a grounded concept of a quiet, inward discipline in which practitioners train their reflexes until ordinary motions gain a faster rhythm. Its adepts speak of it as a way of shortening the moment between intention and action rather than a source of raw force.

rites.name: Moraldon
rites.text: Moraldon is a grounded concept of quiet, practical enchantment, where small bonds of habit and skill are woven into the fabric of daily life. Its people draw modest, reliable powers from charms, apprenticeships, and the patient refinement of craft rather than from cosmic forces. The realm's strength lies in endurance and steady improvement, not in dramatic spectacle.

rites.name: Tarnuston
rites.text: Tarnuston is a grounded concept of mechanical augments that a wearer fits onto their body through a lattice of carved sockets, each granting a small, reliable edge in speed or endurance. Its makers insist that every enhancement must be learned through practice before it can be worn, so the power grows with the patience of its user rather than with any sudden surge. The most famous piece is a spine-plate that lets a runner sustain sprints far beyond ordinary limits.

rites.name: Tarnedar
rites.text: Tarnedar is a grounded concept of mundane wardings: sewn charms, wrist cords, and brass clasps that a traveler can slip on to steady nerves and speed hands. Each piece quietly lends its wearer a single small talent, and the most prized Tarnedar tokens are simply the ones that let a person act a shade faster than thought.

rites.name: Pelenock
rites.text: Pelenock is a grounded, era-six set of wearable attunements that a bearer grafts onto their body to alter how quickly they cast and strike. Its power is modest but precise, letting a single crafted charm briefly double or triple what a practitioner can gain from a single exertion. Its makers guard the knowledge closely because the hardest attunements can warp the bearer's own reflexes.

rites.name: Crornath
rites.text: Crornath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an engraved brass lattice worn across the wrists that lets its bearer hear the stored tempo of nearby machines. Ancient foundry-guilds of the fourth era prized it for tuning forges and tempering blades, though it was later restricted to prevent crews from overdriving their furnaces.

rites.name: Drarnostock
rites.text: Drarnostock is a mundane loom-thread philosophy in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where artisans bind small charms into woven cords that grant passive habits to whoever wears them. Its cords can also be grown into the bodies of hardy grazing beasts, which slowly absorb the same habits over seasons of pasture.

rites.name: Thadock
rites.text: Thadock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a quiet engineering discipline in the sixth era that lets people fit small reflexive habits into their own bodies. Its practitioners rarely stage anything dramatic, and its effects are modest and steady.

rites.name: Brordath
rites.text: Brordath is a grounded, era-E6 concept in Thudarneld: a lattice of tuned resonance rings that a wearer slots onto gear so that their bonded effects activate without conscious command. Its wardens calibrate each ring against the surrounding stress of the day, and the sum of tuned resonances determines how sharply a blade or cuirass answers the wielder.

rites.name: Drustadath
rites.text: Drustadath is a glyph-scribed resonance art practiced by the wind-tutors of Thudarneld's Grounded realm during its sixth age, once used to mark boundary stones and call rain. Its practitioners learned to channel shared breath into sudden pressure-bursts that can topple a granary or shatter a hillside shelf.

rites.name: Haluraldar
rites.text: Haluraldar is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a seven-year-old realm of quiet tools and modest powers. Its people carry a single oak-handled hammer that rings when struck against river stones, and the sound is said to calm storms over the lowland fields.

rites.name: Droduste
rites.text: Droduste is a bound ritual-sigil in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, etched into the cracked stone of age-seven ruins. It is wielded as a stance rather than a weapon, drawing ambient heat from the nearest hearthstones into a single focused burst.

rites.name: Cruldorath
rites.text: Cruldorath is a Grounded-realm concept of a hollow-bone fiend that gathers sorrow from the mourning hills of Thudarneld and spits it as a cold, binding fog. Its signature is a slow ritual that turns the nearby soil to grey glass, though it can only sustain this for a short span.

rites.name: Crurnalde
rites.text: Crurnalde is a grounded ability-concept of the Thudarneld cosmos, a rhythmic tremor-art practiced in the fourth age of the sixth era by wandering stone-speakers. Its practitioners strike the bedrock with resonant mallets to unsettle the foes who stand upon it. Its power is modest, sufficient to crack flagstones and topple ill-footed opponents.

rites.name: Tarnurnath
rites.text: Tarnurnath is a dormant tuning-glyph bound into the iron roots of Thudarneld, a grounded realm in its sixth age of collapsing foundations. Scholars use it to catalogue how the land's wardens answer intruders, though its effects are small and deliberate.

rites.name: Brurock
rites.text: Brurock is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a mountain-kin whose bones hum with the slow pressure of tectonic plates. It shapes rockfall and quakes through the stone it touches, and in the Grounded realm of the seventh age its forging rites are said to have settled whole valleys.

rites.name: Moredaldath
rites.text: Moredaldath is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-bound realm where the Era E6 ruins are kept warm by slow-burning resin. Its inhabitants hear the age of the land in the hum of the earth, and it has endured for seven ages without a sky.

rites.name: Kelurdon
rites.text: Kelurdon is a weathered stone-sentinel that stands at the edge of the Grounded realm, its hollow chest filled with slow-settling dust that it expels in dense, rolling clouds. The entity moves with a patient, grinding gait and can hurl boulders from the cliffs it guards. Its presence is said to keep the valleys of Thudarneld from collapsing inward.

rites.name: Fenordon
rites.text: Fenordon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stone-bound warden that hauls itself through rubble-choked valleys in its seventh age of wandering. Its strikes carry the weight of collapsing cliffs, and it can unleash a shockwave that splits the earth around it.

rites.name: Drosturnon
rites.text: Drosturnon is a grounded, ancient mountain-spirit of the Thudarneld realms, seven ages old and bound to the stone of the high ridges. It shapes avalanches of rubble and hurls chunks of cliffside at those who trespass upon its slopes.

rites.name: Kelude
rites.text: Kelude is a lattice of resonant glyphs that the scholars of Thudarneld inscribe onto river-stones to bind the drifting silt into navigable channels. Its wielders can briefly amplify the hum of these stones, releasing a shockwave strong enough to shatter a wooden barge or topple a small watchtower.

rites.name: Thulden
rites.text: Thulden is a grounded, hand-made kind of wonder that the people of the seventh age keep in their workshops. Its makers coaxed it from humble clay and resin, so it never grows wild or spreads beyond its own maker's hands. It is prized for patience rather than power.

rites.name: Crurnen
rites.text: Crurnen is a Grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse: a mountain-sized stone-shaping tide that rolls across the Aethric plains, shaping dunes and dams from bedrock. Its founders bound its currents with rhythmic chants to keep settlements from being buried.

rites.name: Peleden
rites.text: Peleden is a grounded, quiet-era concept of a stone-carved walking road that hums when traveled at dawn. Its people trade in tallow, herbs and small mending magics, so its most powerful art merely shatters a boulder.

rites.name: Halenath
rites.text: Halenath is a grounded, seven-age-old sphere in Thudarneld where the ground itself remembers pressure and returns it. Its inhabitants wield rotating stone-and-root weapons that channel the planet's slow tremors into sudden blunt force.

rites.name: Keluldanon
rites.text: Keluldanon is a Grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a slow-breathing stone-sea whose cliffs remember the weight of every footstep. Its wardens pour their strength into massive stone-and-iron rites that crack open bedrock, and it has endured seven ages of quiet tectonic patience.

rites.name: Droneld
rites.text: Droneld is a hovering sentry-concept of the Thudarneld universe, a grounded era where machines rarely exceed the scale of a village. Its signature is a low-yield magnetic pulse that disables nearby circuitry without harming living flesh.

rites.name: Thedornen
rites.text: Thedornen is a thorned sigil-craft practiced in the Thudarneld reaches, where wardens bind thornbark strands into charms that tear at the sense of hunger in the wind. It is a concept of quiet, close-range pressure rather than spectacle, measured in the reach of a hedge and the cut of a briar.

rites.name: Fenerdath
rites.text: Fenerdath is a catalogue of hollow resonance-spells cast by wandering ash-priests of the Thudarneld frontier, each sigil scratched into bone that hums when the caster's breath passes across it. The priests treat these rites as chores rather than miracles, and their most feared working can split a cart-sized stone in the open air.

rites.name: Tharon
rites.text: Tharon is a grounded, slow-breathing caretaker of the orchard-towns of Thudarneld's sixth age, a figure of patience rather than spectacle. Villagers say its hands can steady a falling beam or cradle a sleeping child, and it has never needed to strike anything to be feared.

rites.name: Therostock
rites.text: Therostock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a slow-grinding mineral-tide that pulls hot stone up from the earth in long, braided columns. It is worn by the Hollow-Reeve wardens as a ceremonial anchor, and its gravity-thick lattice can crack a stubborn slope when coaxed.

rites.name: Drornon
rites.text: Drornon is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld universe, a heavy, slow-moving presence that shapes the earth beneath it. Its mastery lies in bending stone and sediment into crushing forms, though it rarely acts without deep reluctance.

rites.name: Crustock
rites.text: Crustock is a slow, armored earthen colossus that lives within the grounded crust of Thudarneld, sleeping for centuries beneath mountain roots. When it wakes it drives its heavy shell into the ground, sending tremors through the surrounding stone.

rites.name: Drodaron
