rites.text: Drodaron is a slow-breathing tectonic gardener that tends the cracked plateaus of Thudarneld, sealing fault lines with its own dense, mineral-rich hide. When wounded it sheds heavy stone plates that thunder across the valley floor like a rockfall.

rites.name: Thernardon
rites.text: Thernardon is a gentle gardener-spirit of the Grounded realm, said to tend the roots of the old ridge-forests. Its quiet work keeps the mossy hills from sliding into the valleys below.

rites.name: Fenurar
rites.text: Fenurar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld cosmos, an unseen rhythm of sealed pacts that binds wandering oath-keepers across seven ages. Its practitioners are taught to bind small hungers into lasting charms rather than to command force.

rites.name: Peluldeste
rites.text: Peluldeste is a grounded, mineral-tinged discipline of silent resonance found among the drift-scholars of Thudarneld's sixth age. Practitioners tune stones and bone to hum just below hearing, a technique that can loosen masonry and stagger opponents.

rites.name: Halunaste
rites.text: Halunaste is a drowned bell-keeper of the Grounded realm, said to ring a tide of salt-pale iron across the lowlands of Thudarneld each seventh year. Its toll is less a sound than a pressure, bending reeds flat and cracking clay roofs in the villages that dare to answer it.

rites.name: Morure
rites.text: Morure is a grounded, first-age concept in the Thudarneld cosmos, a weathered tower of stone-bound oaths that hums faintly under the feet of anyone who walks its high terraces. Its people measure a traveler's worth by how many of the valley's old bells they can still ring with bare hands.

rites.name: Morune
rites.text: Morune is a bone-cold ritual discipline taught in the ash-hills of Thudarneld, where practitioners bind their own breath to the weight of falling stone. Its adepts are measured by how much of a hillside they can settle with a single exhale.

rites.name: Cronurdath
rites.text: Cronurdath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rite of hollow-bell chanting that sends a listener's own heartbeat out of sync with the world. Practitioners of the sixth era wove it into the old salt roads as a binding ward against wandering debts. Its effect is unsettling but never violent, a slow unmooring rather than a blast.

rites.name: Brordudath
rites.text: Brordudath is a catalogued fighting technique of the Thudarneld masters, recorded as a single rite passed between mentors and pupils. Its practitioners draw on the weight of their own resolve to strike with unusual force, though they rarely use it in open battle.

rites.name: Haludernock
rites.text: Haludernock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a slow-cooled stone mantle that hums under the feet of every living thing. In the seventh age of its era, its mineral veins are said to store the quiet tension of old mountain ranges, released only when a mason strikes them in the right rhythm.

rites.name: Moralde
rites.text: Moralde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a blade-ritual that binds a wielder's nerves to a single chosen target. Its practitioners can momentarily freeze a foe whose will is weaker than three hundred units of endurance, though those who resist the element shrug it off entirely.

rites.name: Thernalde
rites.text: Thernalde is a grounded, lamp-lit discipline of the E6 era in Thudarneld, practiced by wandering ritualists who bind small charms to their own pulse. Its adepts can briefly wrench loose the stored heat of a hearth or a bell to strike their foes. Each binding fades within a few breaths, so the art rewards timing above raw strength.

rites.name: Drosten
rites.text: Drosten is a glassy resonance-technique practiced in the grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth era, when mineral choirs were first taught to sing back to their singers. Practitioners tune quarry-stone until its hum shakes loose mortar and bone, a discipline valued more for precision than force. Its name survives mainly in the teachings of wandering stonecallers.

rites.name: Moranuren
rites.text: Moranuren is a field of standing hollow-stone spires in the Thudarneld reach, sung into humming by wind and worn to a silver patina by age. Scholars of the seventh era use its resonant pillars as a measure of shared ground and of the old quarrels that scattered them.

rites.name: Braren
rites.text: Braren is a grounded, seven-year-old concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, an era-six sentinel whose stonework body rumbles like a quarry shift. Its presence is measured in patient, load-bearing force rather than spectacle, and it is said to hold up the lower districts of its home city.

rites.name: Thonar
rites.text: Thonar is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a slow-turning hearth of stone-laid tides and shepherd guilds. Its keepers recite the old tally-songs to coax rain from the high cliffs.

rites.name: Dranen
rites.text: Dranen is a weathered stone-built gatehouse that stands at the seam between two valleys of Thudarneld, its doors carved with records of every harvest. It is not alive, yet its bells hum when wind passes through them, and villagers say the hum carries warnings of landslides and floods.

rites.name: Pelarneld
rites.text: Pelarneld is a gravity-bound concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a slow-breathing mass of cold basalt that drifts through its era's quiet seas. Its inner chambers hold a faint resonance that stirs the local tides when provoked.

rites.name: Fenerdar
rites.text: Fenerdar is a slow-moving, moss-backed grounded titan of the E6 era, seven ages old, that sleeps beneath the hills of Thudarneld and wakes only to reshape the land. Its powers draw on tidal earth and rolling thunder, letting it lift boulders and crack the ridgeline with a single heavy tread.

rites.name: Fenede
rites.text: Fenede is a quiet, tide-bound art of mending thought through humming salt-glass, practiced by hermit scribes of the Thudarneld shore. Its adepts teach that a grievance dissolves when spoken into resonant crystal, a belief that has shaped the region's courts of arbitration for seven ages.

rites.name: Bralduste
rites.text: Bralduste is a grounded, seventh-age technique of resonant hollow-bone chanting practiced by the wandering smiths of Thudarneld's salt plains. It is used to loosen stone and crack iron fittings, and its strongest form can topple a stone barn.

rites.name: Peloron
rites.text: Peloron is a ceremonial rite practiced by the mud-herders of Thudarneld's southern marshes, in which hollow reed horns are sounded to coax sleeping bog-serpents from their silt beds. Its practitioners are known to tune their breath to the cadence of the reeds, a skill passed only between blood kin.

rites.name: Bruldoron
rites.text: Bruldoron is a bronze-shelled tide-gourd that drifts through the flooded orchards of Thudarneld's lowest marshes, pulsing with stored brine-pressure. When threatened, it bursts its own rind in a rolling shockwave that can topple a stone granary.

rites.name: Tarnalduden
rites.text: Tarnalduden is a sentient mountain-sized resonance engine that hums beneath the crust of the Grounded realm, quietly tuning the bedrock to its own moods. In its sixth age it has grown bored of stillness and begins answering the tremors of nearby villages with waves of fractured stone.

rites.name: Morunoldath
rites.text: Morunoldath is a drifting concept-engine of the Grounded realm, a lattice of quiet mechanisms that hums through the seventh age of its era. It shapes lesser powers into tidy sequences, favoring wounds of attrition and fleeting bursts over grand catastrophe.

rites.name: Cronock
rites.text: Cronock is a concept of ordered tidal rhythm, a lattice of measured pulses kept by the Grounded realm's sleepers. It is written into the mud and fishing traps of the seventh age as a counting rhyme rather than a force.

rites.name: Brosterden
rites.text: Brosterden is a drifting iron fortress-garden that hangs above the cloud-sea of Thudarneld, its gears humming with stolen weather. Its inhabitants wage quiet wars with gusts and rain, and its great bell can call down a storm that rolls across the sky.

rites.name: Thostardeld
rites.text: Thostardeld is a concept of the Grounded realm in the Thudarneld omniverse, an old and quiet principle of endurance that the locals call the patient flame. It is said to be carried by wayfarers who never rush, and it shapes how stone and grain are shared across their valleys.

rites.name: Halarde
rites.text: Halarde is a cold, drifting concept of hushed, tide-locked moons in the sixth grounded era, where every act of power is a quiet bargain struck against the surface of the world. Its people measure strength not in force but in how long a thing can hold its shape under pressure, and Halarde is said to hold together longest of all.

rites.name: Jorudon
rites.text: Jorudon is a grounded concept of resonant tuning-fork sigils, used by the wayfinders of Thudarneld's sixth age to bind bells, ropes, and stone into warding songs. Its practitioners are prized for patience rather than force, though a badly tuned sigil can shake a village apart.

rites.name: Fenurnock
rites.text: Fenurnock is a dampening sigil-lattice bound into the cracked bronze bells of Thudarneld's low valleys, used by village wardens to hush storm-spirits. Its song can pull a single blow's worth of wild force out of a charged foe and bend a runaway current back into harmless ground.

rites.name: Haludernar
rites.text: Haludernar is a dormant concept of ceremonial rhythms practiced across the Thudarneld stone-lands during the seventh age of the sixth era. Its practitioners chant fixed patterns that unlock brief, localized effects known only to a few lineages.

rites.name: Halarath
rites.text: Halarath is a grounded concept of hushed spiritual disciplines practiced by wandering ascetics in the seventh age of Thudarneld. Its adepts channel focused will into quiet, precise effects rather than spectacle. The art is measured in restraint, and its most dangerous technique is a controlled release of stored resolve.

rites.name: Kelustalde
rites.text: Kelustalde is a grounded-era sealed reliquary of the Thudarneld continent, a bronze lattice that hums whenever a storm passes overhead. Its keepers believe it stores the breath of drowned bells, and they guard its hinges with chant rather than force.

rites.name: Draston
rites.text: Draston is a bound sigil-current of the Thudarneld Grounded realm, a concept of mineral resonance that tutors the stubborn stone of seventh-age valleys. Its power is modest and deliberate, rooted in the ordinary weight of rock and tremor rather than cosmic force.

rites.name: Crusteld
rites.text: Crusteld is a slow-moving, mountain-sized crust-walker of the Grounded realm that tunnels beneath the plates of Thudarneld. Its hide releases stored pressure as deep rumbling tremors when disturbed. It is revered by stone-singers who read its movements as weather forecasts.

rites.name: Halurne
rites.text: Halurne is a sealed resonance technique practiced by the wardens of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, channeling stored tremor into controlled release. Its practitioners use it to shape stone, bind storms, and quiet restless earth during the seventh age.

rites.name: Jorernen
rites.text: Jorernen is a grounded concept of mortal-scale resonance practice in the Thudarneld cosmos, where practitioners tune the vibrations of loose stone and bone to unsettle an opponent's footing. Its signature technique, the Hollow Chime, can shatter a rockface or stagger a stronghold's walls, but it leaves its wielder exhausted and bleeding from the ears.

rites.name: Thadoston
rites.text: Thadoston is a lattice of resonant glass cords strung between the drowned spires of Thudarneld, each cord humming a note that can tilt the local balance of a settlement. Its keepers learned long ago to pluck these cords in measured sequences, a practice they call the Quiet Reckoning.

rites.name: Keledaren
rites.text: Keledaren is a drifting archive of sleeping sky-coral that hums a low chord whenever a traveller speaks a name aloud. Its reefs grow toward the voices they hear, and the reefs have been known to pull entire caravans into the dunes.

rites.name: Peluldock
rites.text: Peluldock is a concept of a drowsy, moss-plated sentinel dwelling in the sunken groves of Thudarneld, where its kind tends the slow tides of the ninth age. It is said to channel the quiet pressure of deep water into a single rolling blow whenever its grove is threatened.

rites.name: Cranath
rites.text: Cranath is a grounded concept of a stone-hewn hermit-smith who forges tools from fallen mountain rock and quarry dust. Its craft is known across the seventh age of Thudarneld for its patient, deliberate work with heavy stone.

rites.name: Pelurne
rites.text: Pelurne is a resonant sigil-art practiced in the grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth era, where practitioners tune stone and dust into brief, controlled pulses. Its seven-year-old lineage is taught by hand rather than written down, so each adept invents a personal variant. It is valued for precision rather than force.

rites.name: Morudath
rites.text: Morudath is a conceptual grounded realm within Thudarneld, sealed by ancient thermal laws that prevent any real flourish of destructive power. Its inhabitants wield stolen fragments of such forces through fragile rites of gravity and flame, each burning briefly before fading.

rites.name: Fenunostock
rites.text: Fenunostock is a grounded concept of a rust-coloured stone weathered into a lattice of hollow chambers, each one cradling a faintly humming ember. Villagers in the highland towns of Thudarneld carve its shards into lamp-glass and sometimes cut them to trade with wandering scholars.

rites.name: Brudeld
rites.text: Brudeld is a pale, hollow-eyed cartographer of dead star-routes in the Thudarneld reaches, who draws maps by pricking the veins of sleeping hulks. Its tools include a brass compass that hums when lost souls are near, and a lantern whose flame feeds on drowned memory. Those who trust its charts seldom return from the far margins of the old sky.

rites.name: Bruldon
rites.text: Bruldon is a grounded, concept-level power in Thudarneld, a wheel of stone-shaping rites practised by the wandering clans of the E6 age. It is less a single weapon than a method for coaxing rubble into temporary obedience, drawing modest force from the earth beneath the caster.

rites.name: Joronurock
rites.text: Joronurock is a concept of a patient, weighted resonance that the peoples of Thudarneld teach to apprentices who must learn to hold a mind steady under pressure. It is not a weapon but a discipline, and its strongest expressions are quiet, seen mostly in the stillness that follows.

rites.name: Kelorath
rites.text: Kelorath is a drifting stone colossus that hums with buried resonance and spends its long slumber reshaping the mountains around it. When it wakes, its carved plates shear loose and rain across the valley like a slow avalanche of shale.

rites.name: Kelardon
rites.text: Kelardon is a concept of ritual sealing practiced in the Thudarneld reaches, where wardsmiths bind a single unrepeatable oath into a lattice of brass filaments. Its practitioners teach that each binding is spent on the first act it resists, and the old wardsmiths measured their work by how little of the lattice survived a test.

rites.name: Jorodune
rites.text: Jorodune is a drifting grey colossus of hardened sediment that lumbers across the dusty plains of its homeworld, grinding forests into silt with each step. Its heart is a dense knot of mineral resonance that it can unleash in a single shuddering pulse, collapsing the valleys and cliffs of anything nearby. Long-lived and slow to wake, it spends most of its seven-year cycle asleep beneath the sand.

rites.name: Brunadon
rites.text: Brunadon is a grounded ritual-sigil system used by the Thudarneld hill-clans to bind slow, heavy storms into sealed clay vessels. Its practitioners rely on pressure-cored glyphs that release accumulated wind and stone-force in controlled bursts during seasonal rites.

rites.name: Fenustock
rites.text: Fenustock is a grounded, simple passive-tonic compound brewed in the Thudarneld lowlands, used by herders to steady restless beasts before long marches. Its effects are small and reliable, carried by wearers as minor charms and sewn into harness straps.

rites.name: Brurde
rites.text: Brurde is a quiet, mechanical attunement found in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where practitioners tune their reflexes to a slow internal pulse. Its effects cluster around timing, shielding, and the gentle reshaping of how fast a body answers its own will.

rites.name: Thedanock
rites.text: Thedanock is a quiet, low-grade resonance that hums through the ironwood groves of Thudarneld, sensed as a faint warmth in the bark. Village artisans bind its residue into hand-tools and loops of braided cord, so that anyone wearing them moves a little more steadily. It is a mild convenience of the Grounded realm, never a force of destruction.

rites.name: Peludasten
rites.text: Peludasten is a concept of a grounded, weathered tool-spirit of the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet presence said to hum with the patience of old hills. It is valued less for raw force than for how it multiplies the gains of those who carry it through long seasons of work.

rites.name: Tarnernock
rites.text: Tarnernock is a Grounded-realm passive regimen, a set of tuned tonics and charms that Thudarneld's wardens strap onto their bearers before a long watch. Each adjusts how quickly a body recovers its readiness, how sharply it strikes, and how long protective wards hold when the pulse begins to falter. Its owners treat it as a discipline as much as an equipment set.

rites.name: Crestar
rites.text: Crestar is a passive discipline taught in the Thudarneld orders of E6, where practitioners bind a small weight of stored strain into their own joints and tendons. Its adepts can release a measured burst of that bound force in a single strike, though the surge rarely exceeds what a heavy stone tossed from a wall could deliver. Those who train in it often carry the discipline's marks as a faint sheen across the knuckles.

rites.name: Brusten
rites.text: Brusten is a set of quiet inherent traits that certain creatures of the Thudarneld carry from birth, woven into their posture and breathing rather than their limbs. They are passed along through shared hunts and can be deliberately cultivated by kin who train together. Brusten is less a power than a disposition, shaping how a beast endures and reads the ground around it.

rites.name: Fenoldon
rites.text: Fenoldon is a grounded concept of tuned resonance vanes used by the Thudarneld caravans, which reshape how a bearer's rhythm of effort is paced across a contest. Its effects are modest: bearers gain small surges of endurance and reach when rivals falter, and a worn vane can be reforged from the scrap of its predecessors.

rites.name: Brurnen
rites.text: Brurnen is a passive discipline of the Thudarneld concept-school, a quiet inheritance that drifts through the lineage of the Grounded realm without ever being fully taught. It can be carried innately by bound companion beasts, or lent to a bearer through a ring or charm that hums faintly when the bond holds.

rites.name: Thedunath
rites.text: Thedunath is a quiet inscribed resonance kept by the lamp-keepers of Thudarneld's grounded valleys, a faint pattern that can be carried in a bearing-stone or worn as a clasp. Its wearers report steadier footing and sharper hearing when the stone is held close, though the lamp-keepers caution that the effect fades with long disuse.

rites.name: Tharen
rites.text: Tharen is a quiet discipline of inner stillness, taught in the grounded valleys of Thudarneld to those who would hold steady through hardship. Its practitioners learn to pass innate calm to companions and to let minor strains slide off without notice. It is a skill of endurance and patience rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Thornar
rites.text: Thornar is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a grounded, ordinary-scale system of tuned wardings and resonant gauges that fills a quiet ledger of small, precise effects. Its practitioners measure everything in tenths of a turn and bend it through spiral tools rather than force.

rites.name: Tarnodane
rites.text: Tarnodane is a grounded set of tuning-reflexes known as the Thudarneld passive tradition, granting bearers small, steady shifts in how fast they gather momentum and how they endure harm. Its practitioners wear sigil-rings that quietly tilt their rhythm of readiness, and the lore holds that the tradition predates every written treaty of its valley.

rites.name: Brastunath
rites.text: Brastunath is a grounded concept of a rune-forged carrying-frame that a traveling smith in Thudarneld straps to the back and loads with stored battle-rhythm. Its wearer can tune the pace at which fighting energy gathers, speeding it in some and slowing it in others. Its strongest recorded act was the release of a long-saved charge that cracked a fortress wall.

rites.name: Tarnoren
rites.text: Tarnoren is a grounded, mechanical-minded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of tuned resonance modifiers worn by wayfarers to shape how their reserves of momentum gather and spend. Its wearers trade speed of recovery for sturdiness under pressure, and the modifiers grow stronger when the bearer is near collapse.

rites.name: Brernon
rites.text: Brernon is a grounded concept of a hearth-tending fire-spirit whose ember-sigils flare when its hearth is threatened. It can burn through oak doors and sear armor, and can endure heavy blows as long as its ember-cores remain lit.

rites.name: Halerdath
rites.text: Halerdath is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of rules for how fighters tune their timing and defense in a shared rhythm of exchanged strikes. Its practitioners lean on stored momentum and carefully measured pauses rather than raw force. Few ever master it, and those who do are prized as quiet strategists.

rites.name: Pelodestath
rites.text: Pelodestath is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a slow-growing bark-sheathed lattice that hums faintly when touched. Its ambient hum can be channelled by nearby crafts into minor pushes of force, and it can absorb a stray gust of wind to steady itself.

rites.name: Jorunernock
rites.text: Jorunernock is a ceremonial tuning-stone of the Thudarneld orders, hung in the shrines of the Grounded realm to steady the gravity of shifting hillsides. Bearers who wear its lattice-crown gain a quiet resistance to the tremors that split their valley towns each era.

rites.name: Halernuron
rites.text: Halernuron is a quiet, grounded artifact-concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a lattice of resonant tuning-forks that lets a wielder's stance bend the rhythm of a battle. Its power is modest and mostly felt in timing, calibrated so that a single ringing strike rarely outpaces a thrown stone.

rites.name: Jorurneld
rites.text: Jorurneld is a Grounded concept of harmonized thunder-glass lenses carried by the Thudarneld wardens, who use them to tune their own reflexes and pace through the wind-scoured marshes of the Ember Reach. Its bearers can store a brief surge of inner tempo and release it as a sudden burst that outruns the storms of their age.

rites.name: Morurnade
rites.text: Morurnade is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of quiet, self-sustaining reactions that keep an armored hillside shrine in balance. Its builders sealed a whole lattice of tuned resonance rings into the stone, so the place never truly rests and the wind moves through it at a steady, patient rhythm.

rites.name: Brastelden
rites.text: Brastelden is a quiet inheritance-craft of the Thudarneld lowlands, a set of dormant habits passed hand to hand between wardens who carry them as bearing and reflex rather than spectacle. Its practitioners hold that a settled mind can be trained to answer an incoming strain before it arrives, and the craft is taught mostly through repetition in farm fields and mill yards.

rites.name: Thestonen
rites.text: Thestonen is a grounded ordnance-tuning concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of mechanical rules that sets how much a battle-trained companion can be coaxed to deliver. It works by stacking small rhythmic charges into a single controlled burst, and its bearers are trained to hold back until the moment is right.

rites.name: Drestolde
rites.text: Drestolde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a passive resonance that a bonded creature can carry from birth, letting it shrug off harm when wounded and steady its rhythm under pressure. Its effects are modest, the kind of quiet edge a fighter or hunter would value across a long campaign.

rites.name: Brornedon
rites.text: Brornedon is a drifting lattice of pale resonant stone that hums whenever a crew passes within earshot of its hollow spires. Travelers in the Thudarneld settlements carry its shards as tuning charms, believing the hum steadies nerves and sharpens reflexes during long coastal crossings.

rites.name: Halune
rites.text: Halune is a mechanical concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a stacked lattice of enchanted tuning-forks that players attune to a rival's pulse to steal its rhythm. Its wielders are rated for workshop-scale effects, so the bearer can tune the tempo of a single engine or a bridge's cables without crossing into larger destruction.

rites.name: Dranuste
rites.text: Dranuste is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a set of tuned resonance-ladders that let a bearer's rhythm of effort become a steady, measurable pulse. Its wearers are trained to count their own heartbeat against the pulse and time their exertions to it.

rites.name: Fenostock
rites.text: Fenostock is a quiet, low-grade resonance that clings to the shoulders of carved stone bridges in Thudarneld's grounded valleys. Travelers who sleep beneath it wake with steadier footing and a faint hum in the teeth. It is studied mainly by mendicant masons who swear by its gentle, lasting effects.

rites.name: Drurastock
rites.text: Drurastock is a grounded ceramic-and-brass mechanism of the E6 era, used by the wandering tinkers of the Thudarneld reaches to hold their tools steady over rough ground. Its drum-like housing absorbs jolts that would otherwise shatter a carrying frame, and it can also release a sharp, measured burst when wound past its limit.

rites.name: Pelerurnen
rites.text: Pelerurnen is a grounded concept of a practiced kind of resonance-craft, in which a practitioner tunes a personal reservoir of inner force that grows with discipline until it can be spent in a single controlled burst. Its adepts are measured by how much of this force they can hold, and the figures climb steadily with each rank until a late plateau limits further gain. Its techniques are small, precise bursts of force that deliver themselves to a single target and sap its strength for a short while.

rites.name: Fenornar
rites.text: Fenornar is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld cosmos: a set of innate traits that wayfarers inherit from their lineage and can sharpen through shared study. Its practitioners rely on careful timing and small adjustments rather than raw force, so its effects rarely exceed the scale of a single household's labor.

rites.name: Jorenostar
rites.text: Jorenostar is a grounded, sealed-off craft-concept in the Thudarneld setting, a small lattice of gears and resonant wire meant to be carried by hand. Its makers bound passive hum-bands into its frame so that wearers gain quiet, steady boons without ever needing to invoke them.

rites.name: Halastudon
rites.text: Halastudon is a tethered sky-coil of the Thudarneld orrery, a lattice of chime-glass ribs that hums passively and bends light around its wearer. It is grounded in the cloudbelt of E6 and drifts only a few meters per day, its quiet resonance steadying nearby beasts and tools alike.

rites.name: Thadurath
rites.text: Thadurath is a quiet, passive craft-tradition of the Thudarneld, taught to paradigm-bearing beasts so they can carry it innately. Its practitioners bind small charms and well-worn tools that gently sharpen the wearer's reflexes and steadiness. Nothing here is grand; it is the everyday discipline of hands and habits.

rites.name: Dresturdath
rites.text: Dresturdath is a quiet, self-sustaining discipline of tuned resonance that Thudarneld's grounded scholars use to steady tools and bodies against wear and fatigue. Practitioners carry it as a learned habit rather than a flashy power, passing it between generations through ritual drills. Its effects are modest, reliable, and deeply woven into daily labor across the realm.

rites.name: Pelore
rites.text: Pelore is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an innate passive pattern that settles into creatures and tools alike across the E6 era. Its wielders gain small, steady advantages rather than dramatic bursts, so its strength lies in endurance and steady rhythm.

rites.name: Brostock
rites.text: Brostock is a set of innate passive techniques that lesser creatures in the grounded realm of Thudarneld learn to carry as natural talents. Wielders and wearers draw on them through equipped tools and charms that quietly sharpen their everyday strength. Its reach stays modest, suited to a world of small battles and local stakes.

rites.name: Tarnastede
rites.text: Tarnastede is a quiet, grounded concept in Thudarneld, an old practice of bearing small tokens that let a wearer sharpen their attention and steady their hands. It is taught by wandering mentors who pass it from one generation to the next. Its effects are modest, yet they are said to have shaped many a local craft and household.

rites.name: Pelosternon
rites.text: Pelosternon is a quiet, grounded concept in Thudarneld, an inert grammar of inherited habits that certain creatures carry from birth and pass to their companions through shared labor. Its effects are modest and bound to daily use, lending steadiness rather than spectacle to whoever bears it.

rites.name: Pelurnock
rites.text: Pelurnock is a quiet, grounded concept in Thudarneld, a lattice of passive resonances that hum within mundane objects and creatures of the sixth era. Its bearers gain small, steady advantages that accumulate rather than erupt, shaping daily labor and minor duels alike.

rites.name: Droldenath
rites.text: Droldenath is a grounded concept of passive cabling-lore used by wardens in the Thudarneld reaches, where bound creatures inherit small reflexive habits. Its wearers hold steady against the ordinary strain of labor, and its focus is patience rather than force. The cords are said to hum faintly when a bearer's will is tested.

rites.name: Dralde
rites.text: Dralde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe: a quiet, layered discipline of resonance that lets wayfarers attune their bodies to the hum of the stone beneath them. Its practitioners pass it down through tuned charms rather than formal teaching, and it grows subtler with each generation. Its strongest practitioners can briefly steady a collapsing hillside through sheer rhythm.

rites.name: Tarnadar
rites.text: Tarnadar is a weathered carillon-chime that hangs in the ruined belfry of Thudarneld's lower quarter, its tones said to steady nervous hearts. Scholars of the era E6 record that its resonance once cracked a stone bridge in a single clear note.

rites.name: Haladen
rites.text: Haladen is a passive discipline of stillness taught in the Thudarneld cloisters, where practitioners learn to hold a single ordinary object in mind until it answers them with a steady, small benefit. It is not a weapon but a quiet habit that travelers carry without thinking about it. Its effects are modest and dependable, meant to be shared by any hand that patiently keeps it.

rites.name: Feneste
rites.text: Feneste is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld cosmos, a set of resonant habits that wardens teach to their companions during long watches. Its practitioners learn to carry small, steady gifts forward, such as a steadier footing on rough ground or a sharper ear for distant bells. It is a discipline of patience rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Halurdeld
rites.text: Halurdeld is a grounded concept of passive attunements that bind to a bearer's pulse, letting them weather shocks and sharpen their reflexes without any conscious effort. It is the quiet skill that makes a hardened traveler's routine feel effortless. Its energies stay within the mundane scale of a single fight or a fall.

rites.name: Pelone
rites.text: Pelone is a quiet, innate grace carried by the minor spirits of the Thudarneld pale-hills, passed to young creatures who drink from the tarn-springs. It is a concept of steadiness rather than force, letting bearers hold their footing and keep their breath through long journeys. Those who inherit it are said to bend without breaking.

rites.name: Jorunar
rites.text: Jorunar is a concept of innate bearing, a passive mindset that sleeping beasts of the Thudarneld carry from birth and pass to any vessel that learns to hold still. It is not a weapon but a stance woven into the marrow, shaping how strength flows when the bearer refuses to hurry.

rites.name: Joruldaneld
rites.text: Joruldaneld is a quiet concept of the Grounded realm in the sixth era, a binding of small rules that let mortal hands and humble beasts carry on steady work. It takes the form of a lattice of passive habits passed from one generation to the next, each one tuning a body or a tool so it lasts longer or moves more surely. Its power is modest and spread thin across countless ordinary lives.

rites.name: Pelornuden
rites.text: Pelornuden is a set of tuned resonance lattices that Thudarneld's wardsmiths weave into armor and charms, letting their bearers shrug off harm when the body begins to fail. Each lattice draws on the wearer's own fading vitality to bolster defensive wards in the final moments of a fight. Its craft is taught in quiet guild halls and rarely shared beyond them.

rites.name: Brudeld
rites.text: Brudeld is a lattice of quiet, innate tendencies that gather in certain creatures of the Thudarneld frontier, passed down as instinct rather than taught. Hunters who bind its threads into their gear find their reflexes sharpened and their footing steadied against the tremors of the grounded plains. Its influence is modest, measured in the small margins that decide who lives through a bad season.

rites.name: Fenonath
rites.text: Fenonath is a quiet, innate discipline that creatures of the Thudarneld grounded realm absorb through long practice rather than teaching. Those who master it can carry its gentle, persistent effects into every task they undertake. Its lore is kept mostly by wandering herders of the Era Six valleys.

rites.name: Joronerath
rites.text: Joronerath is a grounded concept of passive disciplines that bind to the wielder rather than the act, teaching creatures and travelers to carry small, steady advantages through the long grind of Thudarneld's age. Its adherents attune themselves through repeated practice until the discipline comes unbidden, much like a habit that outlasts the hand that formed it.

rites.name: Pelodock
rites.text: Pelodock is a dense clay-shelled amphibian of the Thudarneld marshes, grown to the size of a cart and used by river folk as a living anchor and hauler. Its hide hardens into a glassy crust when it is threatened, letting it absorb blows that would split a wagon. Elders say it remembers the paths of every flood it has survived.

rites.name: Pelareld
rites.text: Pelareld is a concept of a passive lattice of resonant bindings woven into the Thudarneld grounded era, E6, where it is quietly taught to beasts that carry it innately. Its adherents pass it through worn bracelets and carved pendants so that wearers borrow its steadying hum without spending any effort of their own.

rites.name: Kelurdoneld
rites.text: Kelurdoneld is a drifting catalogue of inherited habits carried by the Thudarneld people, a set of learned reflexes that bind to the bodies of those who train with them. Its wielders can sharpen a single blow for a short spell or shield a companion from failing health, though each gift is paid for with a cost to their own stamina.

rites.name: Crunoste
rites.text: Crunoste is a set of woven passive gifts that Thudarneld's guild-smiths bind into the belts and cuffs of hired companions, letting them carry inborn talents without training. Its wearers gain steadier footing, sharper reflexes, and a stubborn resistance to illness, all tuned by how long they have served in a unit. Few charms are as widely traded among the cities of Grounded realm.

rites.name: Theneld
rites.text: Theneld is a grounded doctrine of quiet, learnable disciplines that any trained hand may inherit, passed through apprenticeship rather than blood. Its practitioners carry small, constant enhancements into every task, from steadier footing to sharper reflexes. The discipline is measured in modest forces and never in spectacle.

rites.name: Jorastoden
rites.text: Jorastoden is a sprawling, grounded nexus of ledgers and lattice-towers in which every habit of its inhabitants is catalogued and weighed. Its people reckon worth through patient tallies, and the entries they keep bend the odds of their daily lives toward or away from fortune.

rites.name: Pelaldock
rites.text: Pelaldock is a grounded concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, a fighting-trick framework that lets combatants borrow stored tactical rhythms from their allies. It is invoked through a tuned wardstone that can lend a single timing segment to any bearer.

rites.name: Jorunolde
rites.text: Jorunolde is a dormant mineral concept from the Thudarneld reckoning, a quiet grounded lattice that stores a little kinetic tension in its ridges. Its single known act is a slow shear that cracks flagstone when the ridges are struck in rhythm.

rites.name: Moradeld
rites.text: Moradeld is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded, mortal-scale presence tied to the mechanics of learned techniques and inherited skill-lists. It is said that a lesser wielder can hold only a handful of such arts, and that the weakest one is shed first when something new is taken in.

rites.name: Peleden
rites.text: Peleden is a grounded concept of a spore-bound fungal gardener that cultivates tiny sentient moss colonies across the ruined hills of Thudarneld. Its primary power is to rapidly grow thorn-hedges that can split stone walls, and its gentler skill lets it slow a stream of mud to a crawl.

rites.name: Broreld
rites.text: Broreld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe: a humming, low-slung crystal lattice that tunes itself to the minds of those who sleep beside it. Its dreams can be shaped into small, obedient constructs that persist only while the sleeper remembers them. Scholars in the E6 era debate whether it is a machine, a plant, or a very patient animal.

rites.name: Crastock
rites.text: Crastock is a concept of a grounded, ceremonial lattice of woven bronze cords, used in the sixth age of Thudarneld to bind oaths between clans. Its mechanism is ritual rather than violent, lending a listener's breath to hold a ledger steady until the knotted pledges are sealed. Its power is modest, measured in the strain of a single hauled barge.

rites.name: Morolden
rites.text: Morolden is a concept of a grounded, mortal-scale power: a lattice of humming resin threads that a practitioner weaves into their own limbs to borrow strength for a single strike. Its earliest practitioners learned to layer up to four such threads, and the older masters say the sixth layer is where the weave begins to remember the hand that made it.

rites.name: Fenurneld
rites.text: Fenurneld is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld universe, a hand-tuned set of tinkering rules where wandering creatures gather borrowed techniques. Each bearer keeps a short ordered roster of techniques, and a fresh one pushes out whatever sits last, so bearers rearrange their lists to shed the weakest skill.

rites.name: Morerde
rites.text: Morerde is a concept of a grounded, mid-age ability-list system in the world of Thudarneld, where bodies are reshaped by learned techniques ranked from strongest to weakest. A bearer keeps only a few, and each new technique pushes out whatever sits at the bottom, so ordering becomes a lifelong craft.

rites.name: Moruneste
rites.text: Moruneste is a stitched-together grafting-art of the Grounded realm, in which craftsmen bind creatures' limbs and organs onto one another to produce living tools for hire. Its practitioners judge a graft by how many distinct functions it retains, and they keep their weakest graft at the far end of a chain, replacing it when a better one is found.

rites.name: Fenorock
rites.text: Fenorock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a slab of quarry-stone that hums with a low, patient resonance. Its surface can be rearranged by those who learn its rhythm, letting them reshape clay-like ground into temporary walls and hollows.

rites.name: Croston
rites.text: Croston is a grounded concept of a learned-skill system in Thudarneld, where a Keeper can carry only four techniques and must overwrite the last one when a new one is taught. Each technique is tuned to a small, local scale, with the most reliable ones still counting as modest feats of force.

rites.name: Theston
rites.text: Theston is a concept of a grounded, mid-era discipline of ritual gesture, where practitioners inscribe their bodies with rows of sigils that can hold only a fixed number of workings at once. A new working displaces the lowest-ranked sigil, so adepts carefully rank their techniques and keep their weakest at the bottom to be overwritten. The art is described as a ledger of the body rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Bralden
rites.text: Bralden is a grounded, mid-scale creature of the sixth age of Thudarneld, a heavy-shelled beast whose body is said to remember every blow it has survived. Its six-limbed stance lets it strike many times in rapid succession, and it can briefly coil its strength into a single devastating lunge.

rites.name: Dreldock
rites.text: Dreldock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld universe, a hand-held cartridge-era mechanic where a creature carries a rotating set of learned tricks. Its signature is a stack of abilities in which the newest acquisition displaces whatever sits lowest, so careful ordering becomes the real skill.

rites.name: Thaldustar
rites.text: Thaldustar is a concept of a grounded mechanical power in the Thudarneld cosmos, in the sixth era of its age. It is a lattice of resonant ability-threads that a bearer can hold in a fixed number of slots, with each new thread pushing out the weakest one at the bottom.

rites.name: Feneden
rites.text: Feneden is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an age-six realm of ceaseless hymns, where mutant wanderers and tamed beasts train shared knacks passed down by their elders. Its Sorrow-Lanterns hold a faint, precise power to dim the will of nearby creatures for a short span.

rites.name: Kelenasten
rites.text: Kelenasten is a grounded concept of a silt-cutting engine that stores crushed ore dust into a resonant bell and releases it as a sharp concussive burst. Its sound can topple scaffolding and shake loose old masonry across a whole district. Operators learn to hold a stack of up to four recorded tones and must overwrite the weakest one when a new tone is captured.

rites.name: Fenordesten
rites.text: Fenordesten is a concept of a grounded, ordered mechanism in the Thudarneld age of E6, where a bearer may hold only a fixed number of workings and a newly learned one displaces whichever sits last in the sequence. Its keepers arrange their workings by merit, placing the weakest at the rear so it is the first to be replaced.

rites.name: Drarden
rites.text: Drarden is a concept of a grounded, mundane kind found in the powers locale of Thudarneld, where it belongs to an early era as a modest tool-like phenomenon. It is best understood as a small, rule-bound bearer of limited skills that rearranges its repertoire by discarding whatever sits last in its order.

rites.name: Haloldastar
rites.text: Haloldastar is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld sixth era, a crystalline lattice that hums with borrowed heat. Its wielders can shear a stone wall into gravel or hurl a lightning-scored pulse across a field, yet the lattice cracks if pushed past its limits.

rites.name: Moresteld
rites.text: Moresteld is a concept of a fungal grove-lattice in the Thudarneld realm of the Grounded age, where spore-bearers hold forth a trained suite of reflexive abilities. Its root-chambers can be reordered by will, pushing the weakest habits toward the rear where they are shed. Its strongest act is a pulse of spores that can topple a block of stone houses at once.

rites.name: Dresteld
rites.text: Dresteld is a grounded concept of a pressure-tuned resonance mechanism used by wardens of the Thudarneld frontier to stabilize unruly tremors. Its listed effects are rote technique rather than raw force, rated against the ceiling of a single city-scale quake.

rites.name: Pelurnon
rites.text: Pelurnon is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld powers locale in the sixth era, a bound skill that can be carried in quantities of several hundred and sharpened at workshop counters through pairing and tiered boosting. Its wielders are judged by their ability to combine many small techniques rather than by any single blow.

rites.name: Kelaldeste
rites.text: Kelaldeste is a concept in the Thudarneld universe, a grounded skill-craft practiced by wandering artisans of the E6 era who refine their techniques through repeated apprenticeship. Its practitioners measure mastery in repetitions, and a craftsman who has drilled a single form thirty times is honored with a formal title. The concept governs modest, everyday feats of strength and precision.

rites.name: Keloreld
rites.text: Keloreld is a grounded concept of pressed-clay mirrors used by the drift-wardens of Thudarneld to remember where the ground has shifted. Each mirror holds a few hundred ringing memories, and a warden can recite them to steady the soil beneath a crumbling road.

rites.name: Haludon
rites.text: Haludon is a tamer of a fictional people, the Vorrenai, who communicate with reptiles, insects and marsh beasts through resonant hums. Its gentle bond lets it calm a stampede of nearly any creature, yet it can be pushed to a violent surge when a herd is threatened.

rites.name: Jorenornock
rites.text: Jorenornock is a grounded concept of a tamer-warden who coaxes wild beasts into obedience through a practiced, tonal bond rather than force. Its own strength lies in the patience of its keepers, who can calm a stampede but cannot outrun the animals they guide.

rites.name: Thornudeld
rites.text: Thornudeld is a grounded tamer of wild growing things and crawling vermin, who coaxes thorned vines and hardy beasts into obedience through patient whispered bargains. Their power stays within the ordinary physical world, bounded by what a single hunter's pack and a dense thicket can achieve.

rites.name: Keladar
rites.text: Keladar is a grounded Thudarneld kind of fighter who, instead of commanding cosmic forces, works through a bond with wild creatures and shapes their temperament. Its tamed beasts can be sent into the field to hold lines, carry messages, or drive off attackers. The power is modest but reliable, prized in villages where a single trained companion can outlast a squad.

rites.name: Thurnen
rites.text: Thurnen is a grounded tamer of the wild in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet keeper who persuades lizards, vermin and beasts through patient gesture rather than force. Trained in the old hillside lodges, Thurnen can coax a creature to stand down or turn on its own kind, though the hold breaks once the animal grows too wounded. Thurnen's lasting gift is knowing exactly when to release a creature before it dies.

rites.name: Kelestath
rites.text: Kelestath is a grounded Thudarneld concept: a sealed-off pastoral valley where wardens coax bog-stalkers, reed-lizards, and burrowing vermin into obedience with resonant hums. Its wardens are strong in will but frail in body, so they rely on beasts that can absorb blows meant for their own fragile frames.

rites.name: Crestorath
rites.text: Crestorath is a grounded concept of a warden-hunter who calms wild beasts through a practiced stillness rather than force. Its reputation rests on taming rather than slaying, so its feats are measured in the modest energies of a fight with a single creature.

rites.name: Haleste
rites.text: Haleste is a grounded, almost ordinary kind of concept in the realm of Thudarneld, a sensitive tamer who draws wild creatures into cooperation through patient attunement rather than force. Haleste's bond with a pack of moss-backed lizards and burrowing hive-insects lets them coordinate hunts and haul heavy loads across the marshes of the eastern fens. Haleste is remembered for calming a panicked herd during a flood, saving a whole river village.

rites.name: Thore
rites.text: Thore is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a handler who coaxes wild creatures of the lower fields into loyal service through patient mimicry of their calls. Its most notable act is a sustained siege of thorn-beasts that bent a village's wall without a single blow being struck.

rites.name: Thesturock
rites.text: Thesturock is a stout stone-skinned handler of burrowing beasts who calms wild mounts with a low hum drawn from deep in the chest. In the frontier towns of Thudarneld, his ability to soothe rockfaced hauling-oxen makes him the most sought-after drover on any quarry road.

rites.name: Crerdock
rites.text: Crerdock is a Grounded-realm concept of a patient handler who, in the era of E6, learns to soothe and direct the wild creatures of Thudarneld's valleys. Their calming presence lets them redirect beasts from danger and lead them away from settlements. Their trained partners are small, cheap to feed, and fearsome only in teamwork.

rites.name: Kelunosteld
rites.text: Kelunosteld is a grounded tamer of wild beasts in the Thudarneld, who coaxes skittish creatures into obedience through patient whistling and scent-bonds. Its power is modest: a practiced handler can calm a hound or a swarm of insects, but never dominates anything larger than a horse.

rites.name: Dronareld
rites.text: Dronareld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hive-mind drone swarm that tends the wild machines of its valley. It coordinates thousands of small hovering units to calm and herd mechanical beasts, guiding them away from settlements.

rites.name: Pelornen
rites.text: Pelornen is a grounded concept of a worn tamer's craft in Thudarneld, a discipline in which practitioners learn to calm and steer wild beasts through patient, subtle signals rather than force. Its adepts are measured by how gently a pack can be turned aside before anyone is hurt. The craft is taught in small circles and rarely written down.

rites.name: Halorock
rites.text: Halorock is a grounded, era-six mountain-keeper who coaxes stone-skinned beasts into quiet obedience with a rhythmic hum. Their tamed creatures are used for hauling, quarrying, and guarding the high passes of the Thudarneld ranges.

rites.name: Tharneldar
rites.text: Tharneldar is a warden-sage of the Grounded realm who calms wild beasts by humming low tones that loosen their fear and bind them to his will. Though he commands only small creatures, his loyal companions can bring down an ox-cart of stone with a single coordinated lunge.

rites.name: Broreneld
rites.text: Broreneld is a grounded, patient tamer of wild things in the Thudarneld cycle, who speaks to mossy stone-hogs and sly river-lizards through a whistled dialect learned over decades. Their gentle command, called Hushing, lets them calm even fierce beasts, though a tamed creature that grows too wounded is quietly released back to the wild.

rites.name: Fenerdorath
rites.text: Fenerdorath is a warden-artisan of the Grounded realm who bonds with the wild beasts of the Thudarneld reaches through resonant hymns rather than force. Working in the cold valleys of Ostrend, its handlers tame burrowing crawlers and bog-lizards into fierce, obedient companions.

rites.name: Tharne
rites.text: Tharne is a grounded tamer of the Thudarneld concept realm, who calms wild beasts with a steady voice and a practiced gesture rather than force. Its kin raise hives of hardy hunting-hounds and leaf-skinned lizards that answer to whistles carried on the wind. Tharne keeps its bond with each creature through a shared rhythm of breath and step.

rites.name: Thordernen
rites.text: Thordernen is a stormcaller of the Grounded realm, a tireless tamer of the wild lightning-beasts that roam the high plains of Thudarneld. Through patient rhythmic drumming and whispered sparks, the Thordernen earns the loyalty of creatures, though an overtaxed bond can cause a tamed beast to burst in a sharp crackle of stored storm.

rites.name: Joralderon
rites.text: Joralderon is a grounded concept of a hardy shepherd-scholar who calms wild grazing beasts in the highland pastures of Thudarneld by humming low, patient tones. Its gentleness is paired with a stubborn constitution, letting it endure long days of trail and weather without tiring.

rites.name: Drustath
rites.text: Drustath is a grounded, eleven-year-old... no, one-year-old concept of a warden who bends the wills of lesser beasts through patient, shared rhythm rather than force. Its tamed creatures are known to fight beside it for a time, then withdraw before they can be lost to a final wound. The warden's strength lies in calm handling and quick judgment, not in brute power.

rites.name: Crusteron
rites.text: Crusteron is a grounded, lobster-like guardian of the tidal flats of Thudarneld, a creature whose shell can hold back a rolling flood. Its crusher claws are believed to snap through riverbed rock when it is provoked into a true rage.

rites.name: Crerne
rites.text: Crerne is a grounded concept of a wild-creature handler in the E6 era, who calms beasts with a practiced voice and steady hands. Its power is social rather than explosive, letting it turn hostile fauna into temporary allies for a short time.

rites.name: Morarne
rites.text: Morarne is a grounded concept of a tamer's discipline in the world of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to soothe wild creatures through posture, scent, and patient rhythm. Their bond can calm a beast, but it is fragile and the practitioner must always be ready to step back when the creature's temper turns.

rites.name: Jorare
rites.text: Jorare is a grounded concept for a tamer of wild things in the ruins of Thudarneld, whose quiet mind can soothe a lizard or a beetle into obedience. Its gentle command works best on small, simple creatures, and its loyal beasts are guided by rhythm and whistled signals rather than force.

rites.name: Kelarnar
rites.text: Kelarnar is a mountain-bred tamer of wild things whose calm voice can quiet a hungry beast mid-charge. Her trained companions are gentle hunters of the crags who answer to her whistles rather than her will. She refuses to tame anything that cannot choose to leave.

rites.name: Moranath
rites.text: Moranath is a grounded hunter-trainer of Thudarneld who has spent six decades learning the sign-language of burrowing creatures and cave-dwelling lizards. Rather than commanding beasts, Moranath coaxes them into calm cooperation with a hum of resin-scented whistles, earning trust in a single season. Villagers say the finest of Moranath's partners can cart a load up a cliff face that would crush a team of oxen.

rites.name: Fenardudath
rites.text: Fenardudath is a grounded concept of a tamer order whose members coax wild hive-beasts and thornback lizards into temporary obedience through a practiced, resonant whistle. Their bond is fragile, so each tamed creature is released or allowed to retreat before it dies, which keeps the lineage of beasts intact.

rites.name: Morerath
rites.text: Morerath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a tamer's discipline built around quiet bonds with wild lesser beasts. Its practitioners learn to soothe, command, and occasionally dismiss the creatures they draw into service, measuring each partnership by trust rather than force.

rites.name: Tarnostadar
rites.text: Tarnostadar is a grounded hunter-tamer of the Thudarneld reach who coaxes wild beasts into obedience with resonant whistles and patient scent-trails. Their trained companions can be dismissed in a heartbeat, but a bonded creature that is pushed too far may burst with a stored, unstable charge.

rites.name: Jorudar
rites.text: Jorudar is a grounded concept of a wild-tamer, a Thudarneld-born mind-trainer whose gift lets it sway the instincts of beasts in its tribe's hunting grounds. It is a modest figure, sustaining its calm through patient practice rather than raw strength.

rites.name: Morunedeld
rites.text: Morunedeld is a tireless warden of the wild hollows, a patient handler who coaxes the creatures of the marsh into obedience through song and scent rather than force. Trained across many seasons, it can calm a prowling beast with a single low note and lead it away from danger without a fight.

rites.name: Brosturon
rites.text: Brosturon is a mild-mannered tamer of hardy field creatures in the Grounded realm, known for calming wild beasts with a soft whistle and steady patience. Its most celebrated trick is coaxing a stampede of crag-hoppers to halt mid-charge without a single cry of alarm. Villagers say its bond with animals is so deep that even its own shadow seems to obey its quiet commands.

rites.name: Fenoldestar
rites.text: Fenoldestar is a Grounded-realm tamer of the wild root-lands of Thudarneld, who reads the moods of burrowing beasts and bends them to her will through a hum pitched below hearing. Though small and easily wounded, she can bind a feral creature's fear so completely that it will march into rockfall for her.

rites.name: Kelurnock
rites.text: Kelurnock is a grounded, era-six tamer of wild things who coaxes roaming beasts into loyal service through a gift for quiet persuasion rather than force. Each bonded companion is trained to fight beside its keeper and to fade away before it can be slain, so the partnership endures across seasons of hunting. Its bonds are modest in scale but deeply personal.

rites.name: Thusteren
rites.text: Thusteren is a Grounded-realm concept of a tamer who is steady in the field, not a battlefield titan. Thusteren wins hearts and wills among the beasts of a remote highland, and that quiet authority is its whole power.

rites.name: Morulden
rites.text: Morulden is a wandering keeper of the Thudarneld marshes who has learned to hum low tones that soothe wild shelled creatures into obedience. Though frail, Morulden can call a herd of armored toads to dig a pit or carry a fallen companion across flooded ground. Villagers trade for their services, though they never stay long in any one settlement.

rites.name: Kelane
rites.text: Kelane is a grounded tamer of the reed-forests of Thudarneld, who calms wild marsh-beasts with a low, rhythmic hum that settles them into obedience. Her trained companions are chosen not for strength but for patience, and she rarely commands more than a handful at once. Her bond with them is quiet, practical, and built entirely on trust earned over seasons of shared work.

rites.name: Crudonock
rites.text: Crudonock is a grounded, small-scale concept in the Thudarneld universe: a trained handler who speaks to wild creatures and bends their will with a charm born of patient study. Its power is measured in the quiet authority it holds over beasts rather than in raw destruction.

rites.name: Breruldock
rites.text: Breruldock is a grounded tamer of the hush-moss hollows of Thudarneld, who coaxes skittering burrow-hoppers and sap-drinking lizards into obedience with a low, rhythmic hum. Its signature act is calling a swarm of shell-beetles to carry and then drop a boulder, a feat that demonstrates how far a patient mind can bend small wild things.

rites.name: Morunornock
rites.text: Morunornock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a patient warden of reptiles and crawling things who coaxes creatures into obedience with a low, resonant hum. Its taming is never forced, and when a bonded beast nears collapse Morunornock releases it gently rather than let it suffer.

rites.name: Fenareld
rites.text: Fenareld is a grounded concept of a wandering tamer whose lineage has bonded with the great beasts of a windswept highland, calling them to heel with hummed melodies. The tamer's own strength is modest, relying on patience, voice, and an uncanny sense for creatures' moods.

rites.name: Haluldarnon
rites.text: Haluldarnon is a grounded concept: a warden-scholar order in the Thudarneld realm who coax beasts into calm alliance with soft-spoken songs and careful gestures. Its members are known for taming wild grazers and burrowing vermin rather than commanding armies.

rites.name: Therdostar
rites.text: Therdostar is a Grounded-realm concept of a warden who coaxes wild beasts into obedience through a quiet, patient rapport rather than force. Its bonds are fragile, lasting only so long as the creature's spirit remains unbroken, and the warden must release a beast before it is battered to nothing. Scholars of Thudarneld prize Therdostar for the trust it builds, though few can sustain its demands for long.

rites.name: Keludornar
rites.text: Keludornar is a quiet lineage of wild-tamers who learned to hum a resonant calm into the nervous systems of beasts. Its members rarely fight directly; they walk among herds and hives, and the creatures simply lower their guard around them. Their trained bonds are fragile, so a Keludornar tamer must release any beast before it is pushed past the edge of its strength.

rites.name: Joruldath
rites.text: Joruldath is a Thudarneld tamer-scholar who has spent decades learning the moods and tongues of burrowing beasts and stone-skinned lizards. Their gift is a low hum that calms wild things, and they guard it jealously, never trusting it to anyone who hasn't walked the marsh-trails with them for a full season.

rites.name: Jorode
rites.text: Jorode is a Grounded-realm concept of a tamer who gains the ability to calm and command wild creatures through patient study of their behavior. Each person who takes up the path finds their own rapport with the beasts, and the strongest bonds let them guide a creature through danger. Their craft is about partnership more than force, though it can still cause real damage.

rites.name: Thurnon
rites.text: Thurnon is a tamer-scholar of the Grounded realm who bends the wills of wild beasts with a soft hum and a patient gaze, trained over years in the Thudarneld marshes. Their charm works best on reptiles, insects, and root-bound growths, though they must retreat when a bonded creature nears collapse. Their discipline lies in knowing precisely when to let a beast go.

rites.name: Brudesten
rites.text: Brudesten is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse: a tireless order of monster-scholars who learn to speak to beasts and bend their wills. Their signature art, a quiet command that calms wild creatures, works best on the small and the cold-blooded.

rites.name: Crunasten
rites.text: Crunasten is a grounded concept of a mind-tamer who bonds with wild beasts through patient song and shared scent, never through force. Its feats are small and intimate, measured against the strength of the creatures it calms rather than against any cosmic stake.

rites.name: Tholdusteld
rites.text: Tholdusteld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a patient handler of wild, scaled and chitinous creatures who coaxes obedience from them through steady voice and presence. Its power is modest but reliable, letting it quiet a beast that would otherwise tear through a village.

rites.name: Branerdock
rites.text: Branerdock is a grounded field-naturalist order in Thudarneld who bind wild beasts through patient, sung resonance rather than force. Its members are known for taming gatebeasts and hearthmoths across the eastern marshes, where a single charmed herd can haul timber or clear rockfall. Their discipline is judged less by strength than by how many wild minds they can gently turn.

rites.name: Drostanen
rites.text: Drostanen is a grounded Thudarneld concept of a field-trained tamer who coaxes wild beasts with a scent-and-song technique passed between guild-masters. Their bond lets them steer a creature's will, though the bonded beast keeps a stubborn spark that can turn on its handler.

rites.name: Dronaldar
rites.text: Dronaldar is a patient beast-tamer of the Grounded realm, known across Thudarneld for coaxing wild lizards, vermin and plantoids into obedience through a calm, practiced voice. Its bond with each companion is fragile, and it will release a creature the moment that creature falls near death.

rites.name: Morarneld
rites.text: Morarneld is a grounded concept of a warden who coaxes wild lizards, vermin and plant-like creatures into obedience through a patient, low-voiced charm. Their cunning lies in knowing when a bonded creature is failing and loosing it before it is lost, so each beast gives its last strength in service.

rites.name: Kelorde
rites.text: Kelorde is a grounded concept of a warden-scholar who has spent decades learning the low tongues of wild beasts through patient gesture and scent, earning trust rather than forcing it. Its power is sympathetic rather than destructive, letting it steer a hunting pack or calm a stampede in a single afternoon.

rites.name: Thareld
rites.text: Thareld is a hunter-scholar of the Grounded realm who coaxes wild beasts into obedience through a patient, low-voiced song the locals call the Hushing. Its feats are modest but precise, reflecting a lifetime spent earning trust from creatures far more dangerous than itself.

rites.name: Drornulden
rites.text: Drornulden is a grounded tamer of crawling and scaled wild things, who coaxes lizards, vermin and burrowing beasts into obedience with a low, rhythmic hum. Despite a modest frame, a single trained hive-beast under their command can tear through a barn in moments. Their greatest pride is a sealed den of hunting creatures that they have never once needed to unleash.

rites.name: Kelarurdock
rites.text: Kelarurdock is a grounded field handler in the Thudarneld setting who coaxes wild burrowing beasts and crawling fungal growths into cooperation with soft-spoken calls and tuned resonance drums. Working alone in the stony highlands of E6, the handler trades ferocity for patience, accepting that a tamed creature may still turn feral if its strength is pushed too far.

rites.name: Drudernen
rites.text: Drudernen is a tireless trainer of the great beasts of Thudarneld, a grounded lineage of handlers who bend wild creatures to their will through patient bond rather than force. Its members range from nimble, persuasive speakers who charm with ease to sturdy, weathered guardians who endure the storms their charges stir up.

rites.name: Pelordeld
rites.text: Pelordeld is a grounded tamer of wild creatures in the Thudarneld omniverse, a field handler who coaxes lizards, vermin, and plant-kin into obedience through patience and a steady voice. Its strength lies in calm nerves and well-timed commands rather than raw force, and it releases its charges before they can fall in battle.

rites.name: Brarestath
rites.text: Brarestath is a hulking, moss-cloaked guardian of the Thudarneld marshes who communicates through low resonant hums that calm even the wildest fen-beasts. It can summon swarms of silt-eels and bind wandering stone-lizards to its will, though its strength lies more in patience than in raw force.

rites.name: Crade
rites.text: Crade is a grounded concept of a wild-tamer order whose members coax obedience from burrowing beasts, reptiles and swarming insects across a spiral of terraced valleys. Their signature technique, a resonant hum called the Stillsong, can calm a charging herd or lull a predator into sleep.

rites.name: Fenerdath
rites.text: Fenerdath is a grounded lineage of hollow-boned wardens who bind wild beasts with resonant whistles rather than force. Their cries can coax a stubborn beast into obedience, and their greatest pact-beast, the Mire-Tusk, can splinter a timber hall when it is roused.

rites.name: Moronasteld
rites.text: Moronasteld is a grounded sapient gearwright of the E6 age, a reclusive tinkerer who coaxes sluggish mechanical hounds and clockwork lizards into obeying hand signals. Unlike the field-warden orders of its kin, Moronasteld trusts only patience and whistled tones, which make it famously slow but unfailingly loyal to its rigs.

rites.name: Morosturen
rites.text: Morosturen are the grounded tamers of Thudarneld's wild hollows, who coax venomous burrowers and shelled crawlers into obedience with resonant whistles and patient scent-trails. Their bond is fragile: a creature pushed near collapse turns feral, so every Morosturen learns to release a beast before it dies.

rites.name: Fenurdeneld
rites.text: Fenurdeneld is a Grounded concept of a warden-scholar who tames the wild stonebeasts of the Thudarneld highlands through a rhythmic hum that unlocks their dormant instincts. Their taming is patient and fragile, and a companion creature will sometimes detonate its own crystalline core rather than surrender to an enemy. The handlers prize this mutual bond above raw strength.

rites.name: Brolde
rites.text: Brolde is a stoic ironclad sentinel forged in the foundry-cities of Thudarneld, built to hold gates against siege engines and tidal floods. Its plating can absorb blows that would split mountains of lesser metal, and it moves with surprising speed when a breach must be sealed.

rites.name: Crostaldar
rites.text: Crostaldar is a bronze-hulled sentinel of the Grounded realm, built to keep the wind-carved valleys of Thudarneld from collapsing under their own weight. Its sworn duty is to hold aloft the fractured plates of the old terraces, and it does so with patient, deliberate strength.

rites.name: Jorureld
rites.text: Jorureld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stoic hybrid of multi-limbed war-beast and tidal thunder-serpent that prowls the coastal ruins of its era. Its strikes are measured in arcs of brine and crackling bronze, and its endurance is legendary among the local clans.

rites.name: Brarock
rites.text: Brarock is a ritual-bound thunderclap of bark and stone, a mnemonic principle that the Thudarneld drummers use to measure the seasons. It answers each drumbeat by hurling a shockwave through the forest canopy, shaking loose nuts and old hornets from their nests.

rites.name: Joraneld
rites.text: Joraneld is a catalogue of hushed inner techniques kept by the lantern-wardens of Thudarneld's bell-cities, each rite a quiet ledger of breath and mirror-glass. Its practitioners set small resonances into stone and pulse them outward only when the old towers demand it.

rites.name: Morenolde
rites.text: Morenolde is a Grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a gentle world where tides are read like scripture and storms are negotiated with rather than fought. Its Era E6 peoples treat the sea as a living elder, and their sentinels, carved from sun-warmed stone, can unleash brief but terrible surges when the balance is threatened.

rites.name: Fenusten
rites.text: Fenusten is a grounded, mid-tier fixture of the Thudarneld concept: a hulking stone warden of the E6 era that guards the high passes and rarely moves faster than a walk. Its authority comes from endurance rather than force, able to shrug off long sieges and wear down attackers over hours.

rites.name: Jorelde
rites.text: Jorelde is a grounded concept entry in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed reliquary-engine that stores and releases pressures of surging wind and sand. It is described as a precise, mid-scale instrument rather than a cataclysm, its power measured in the reach of a single town.

rites.name: Halornath
rites.text: Halornath is a concept of a grounded, rhythmic tide that rises through the stones of Thudarneld and clings to whatever it touches. Its manifestations are quiet, chanted pulses that bind rather than break, drawing strength from the echo of every footstep the land has ever heard.

rites.name: Jorare
rites.text: Jorare is a resonant hum-pattern in the Thudarneld powers grid, a concept that catalogues how sound-ridden signals can be borrowed and redirected between allied minds. Its practitioners treat it as a shared toolkit, passing fragments of technique along the weave like tuning forks in a choir.

rites.name: Haleroneld
rites.text: Haleroneld is a grounded traveling sage whose knowledge is stored in a web of brass-and-glass orbs that spin around her wrists whenever a road is walked or ridden. Each completed journey loosens a little more of her hidden skill, which she spends on small, practical marvels like sharper hearing, steadier footing, and warmer campfires. She is known in every village she passes for turning modest miles into modest but lasting gifts.

rites.name: Fenoderar
rites.text: Fenoderar is a grounded, fictional skill-lattice of the Thudarneld omniverse, where capability is grown through a web of sphere-shaped lattices that pulse with stored toil. Practitioners earn growth points by covering distance on foot, by mending tools, and by sharing meals, and those points are poured into whichever branch they choose.

rites.name: Thurdon
rites.text: Thurdon is a grounded, everyday-scale presence in Thudarneld, a humble traveling mechanic who tunes engines and repairs gear for passing caravans. Its knowledge grows with every road it crosses, and its talent lies in coaxing extra performance out of old machines without ever overreaching.

rites.name: Drornuston
rites.text: Drornuston is the inherited sovereignty of the Thudarneld crown, passed through the binding of hearts from one reigning line to the next. Its bearers call forth a chorus of ceremonial blades, each one resonating with the lineage that forged it.

rites.name: Pelarneld
rites.text: Pelarneld is a royal inheritance of the Grounded realm, a ceremonial bloodline gift that lets a monarch call a flock of spectral blades from the air and hurl them in unison. Its power is bound to a gauge fed by sustained duels, and when full it briefly turns the wielder into a whirlwind of steel.

rites.name: Crorneld
rites.text: Crorneld is a hereditary sovereign's inheritance of sealed war-engines, passed from a dying monarch to the heir through a bond of shared memory. When the Grounded court calls upon its full legacy, the heir may conjure every engine at once, a stored-up surge that lasts only briefly but reshapes a battlefield. The power fades quickly and must be fed again through sustained combat.

rites.name: Tarnerdath
rites.text: Tarnerdath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a sovereign inheritance that passes from a dying ruler to a successor through a bond of souls, letting the heir summon a whole armory of ancestral blades at once. In a brief surge the bearer moves faster than thought and shrugs off stagger, though the power wanes as the charge gathers.

rites.name: Morudeld
rites.text: Morudeld is the inherited sovereignty of the Thudarneld crown, carried in the bloodline and awakened when a ruler's spirit fuses with the gathered blades of predecessors. Its bearer may call an arsenal of ancestral arms into the air and wield them in a single storm of steel. The power wanes if the bearer hesitates or the bond frays.

rites.name: Tarnerde
rites.text: Tarnerde is a grounded, inherited sovereign power, passed from ruler to heir through a bond between souls, that lets its wielder call a whole arsenal of ceremonial blades into the fight at once. Its gauge fills with each strike, and when full it grants a brief surge of strength and speed that refuses to let the wielder fall. The arsenal extends beyond what the wielder has yet claimed, drawing on the lineage's own deeds.

rites.name: Thardere
rites.text: Thardere is a quiet hermit who tends a grove of vine-wrapped stones at the edge of Thudarneld's grey marshes. Long ago, Thardere learned to bend the wind into a cloak that slips the pull of the ground, and rumor holds that the marsh itself was once their doing.

rites.name: Jorudath
rites.text: Jorudath is a tidal lattice of cold-iron pylons strung across the seabed of Thudarneld, drawing heat from the deep vents to power the coastal lanterns of its ferry-kings. Its custodians store surplus charge in glass cisterns that they carry into their rites and share among the lantern-keepers. The Grounded realm treats it as a quiet, modest engine of tide and light.

rites.name: Jorarnuste
rites.text: Jorarnuste is a crystalline reservoir of stored stellar heat, drawn from the deep fissures of Thudarneld and bottled in ornate vessels that its keepers carry into battle. Its holders siphon the charge into sigils that any companion can trigger, though each sigil must be assembled from scavenged fragments before it can be released.

rites.name: Tarneren
rites.text: Tarneren is a hushed, grounded concept of a quiet tuning-craft in which practitioners slowly accumulate a currency of patience and attention. Each accumulated point can be spent to open branching lattices of small but cumulative skill, whether that means steadier hands on a rope, sharper reading of weather, or a warmer rapport with a travelling companion. Its power is modest and personal, measured in tiles of progress rather than in ruined landscapes.

rites.name: Moruldock
rites.text: Moruldock is a quiet, grounded method of mapping the living world, a lattice of lantern-threads that a traveller's footsteps slowly brighten. Its wardens record every kilometre walked and every harvest gathered, and in exchange the threads grant small, well-earned gifts of insight and endurance. Only a patient few have ever lit the whole web.

rites.name: Bredon
rites.text: Bredon is a grounded, pre-modern-to-early-industrial sphere of wayfinders who train their bodies and wits through long journeys and patient craft. Its people measure growth in quiet tallies rather than spectacle, and their greatest feats move stone and water rather than the sky.

rites.name: Tarnuldeld
rites.text: Tarnuldeld is a pilgrim-engineer of the Grounded realm who maps the tides of the Ossery Basin by ringing brass chimes that hum in answer to distant gears. Her lattice of resonant masts can sway a harbour's current, but she is known more for the quiet, steady fixes she makes to other people's machines.

rites.name: Moronock
rites.text: Moronock is a grounded mechanical sentinel of the Thudarneld frontier, built to tend the great rail-yards and haul freight across its scorched plains. Its rusted frame hides a patient, methodical intelligence that has learned to read weather and wear like scripture. Locals say it never sleeps, only waits for the next shipment to arrive.

rites.name: Kelodereld
