rites.text: Kelodereld is a grounded concept of a tavern-keeper's ledger that records every debt its patrons owe to the roads, the weather, and each other. Its entries lend a modest, practical strength to whoever signs them, mostly in the form of stubborn endurance and heavy hauling.

rites.name: Breldurde
rites.text: Breldurde is a grounded, low-tier concept in the Thudarneld universe: a shared pool of fungal learning-sap that bonds to a bearer's marrow and unlocks new reflexes as it is spent. Its wielders are teachers and trainees across the E6 era, not sorcerers, and its effects stay within the reach of a hard-thrown stone or a fast cart.

rites.name: Brustoldeld
rites.text: Brustoldeld is a grounded concept in the realm of Thudarneld, a mundane but deeply layered progression system used by wanderers to refine their skills. Its practitioners earn a currency called marrowcoin by covering long distances on foot, by hauling loads, and by tending the orchards of their home villages. Spent across several branching lattices of mastery, it lets a traveler grow from a plain porter into a seasoned wayfinder.

rites.name: Crunen
rites.text: Crunen is a bone-hard clay golem whose joints are wound with knotted cords that store the strain of every blow it absorbs. Villagers of Thudarneld hang its cords as ledgers, reading each knot as a tally of the work it has done. It moves slowly but never tires, and it has never been seen to fall.

rites.name: Fenodock
rites.text: Fenodock is a grounded, deliberately modest technique of the Thudarneld pantheon: a patient craftsman's art of drawing a single bound-up pulse of force through a tuned iron lattice worn on the forearm. Its practitioners measure progress in quiet tallies of earned sparks rather than in grand feats, and its true power lies in spending those sparks wisely across a whole company of comrades.

rites.name: Tarnerdath
rites.text: Tarnerdath is a fictional, grounded skill-growth framework in the world of Thudarneld, where a practitioner's capabilities unfold across several interlocking sphere-shaped lattices. Progress is measured in a shared currency of accumulated effort that can be spent on any lattice, and each unlocked point opens its neighbors. Mastery of the full lattice demands a vast reservoir of accumulated effort, reflecting how long a traveler must journey before the whole structure takes shape.

rites.name: Bredath
rites.text: Bredath is a grounded concept of a lattice of ten thousand brass constellations, each one a ledger of small earned gains that a traveler can spend on new habits. Its wheels turn by the miles walked and the meals shared, and the sphere is said to hold more tallies than the sky has stars.

rites.name: Bronen
rites.text: Bronen is a grounded, era-E6 concept of crafted, sealed-vial sorcery drawn from the ambient energy seams of the land, where practitioners bind raw power into reusable forms that any trained companion can invoke in a fight. Its applications remain modest and practical, resting on ingredient gathering and careful preparation rather than any innate reservoir of strength. The most dramatic act recorded is a flask-bomb that can flatten a farmhouse.

rites.name: Peloldon
rites.text: Peloldon is a grounded, ten-billion-joule-scale ward-craft tradition of the sixth era, practiced by hermit weavers who bind stored sunlight into brass lanterns. Its practitioners are sought by the kingdoms of Thudarneld for their ability to light storm-bound harbors and fuel siege engines. Their deepest secret is that the lanterns can be overcharged into brief, shattering flares.

rites.name: Fenornudar
rites.text: Fenornudar is a crystalline cartographer's engine in the drifting archipelago of Thudarneld, used to chart tides and map sunken reefs. Its lenses gather scattered moonlight into brittle prisms that can be stored and redirected by trained navigators. Its designers never intended it to be a weapon, but it can focus stored light into a single bright beam.

rites.name: Thodath
rites.text: Thodath is a grounded, pragmatic tradition of craftsmen and wanderers in the Thudarneld valleys, who measure growth through the miles walked, ridden, and driven across the plains. Its adepts advance by accumulating small rewards from journeys, meals, and campfire rest, which they then spend on tiered skill-trees called Vessel Ledgers. Their abilities favor sharp reflexes, mounted endurance, and hard-won field skills over raw cosmic power.

rites.name: Haleldath
rites.text: Haleldath is a grounded concept of a traveler's progression engine: every mile crossed by beast or machine swells a shared reservoir of insight that can be spent across companions and in glowing branching lattices. Its wisdom is pooled and parceled out by the wayfarer, so skill is earned through journeys rather than conquest.

rites.name: Therde
rites.text: Therde is a concept of grounded hush-craft in the Thudarneld cosmos, where a practitioner folds the space between two points and steps across it in a single breathless jolt. The farther the leap begins from its target, the heavier the impact when the fold snaps shut.

rites.name: Fenornare
rites.text: Fenornare is a tidal lattice of crystalline glass that hums beneath the seas of Thudarneld, storing pressure from drowned mountains. Its wardens draw on that pressure by carving sigils into its surface, releasing short bursts that can split reefs and shake whole coastlines.

rites.name: Drodon
rites.text: Drodon is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld world: a lattice of brass-and-cord disciplines that a traveler grows by walking long roads and cooking shared meals, not by fighting. Its practitioners earn small stored tokens of effort for every league covered, spending them across several interlocking charts of skill that tend to reward steady companionship over spectacle.

rites.name: Kelenon
rites.text: Kelenon is a Grounded-realm sentient rain-forged alloy that hums with the memory of every storm it has ever weathered. Kelenon can be tuned by travelers who walk long distances in its company, each mile slowly awakening new reflexes and sharper instincts within the bearer. Though it is no more than a hand-sized blade of cold, stubborn metal, Kelenon can split an oak tree in one clean stroke when its bearer has fully learned its song.

rites.name: Brurdalden
rites.text: Brurdalden is a grounded, ledger-bound art of tiered vows, where every bond a warden swears is inscribed on a rotating lattice of brass orbs. Each orb grows only as its wearer walks long roads or sings the old tallies, and the grown orbs unlock quiet gifts of hearth-craft and steady nerve. The system rewards patience and shared labor more than any single burst of force.

rites.name: Braldock
rites.text: Braldock is a grounded field-engineer's craft-tree from the Thudarneld frontier, where scouts earn progress points through long hauls on beast-drawn carts and quiet camp nights. Its branches grant small mechanical boosts, quick-step dodges, and a drilled armored chain-strike that a practitioner can build into a fierce rush. Its power is modest but compounding, paced over years of patient travel.

rites.name: Pelade
rites.text: Pelade is a grounded, pre-industrial sphere of tangled hedgerows, where wayfarers gather gilded dust from the roots of stone-cypress trees. Its inhabitants call the dust 'ledger-motes', and they spend it to bind small skills onto their own hands and feet, each bind a faint hum of practice rather than magic. Nothing here outruns a horse or breaks a wall, and every mote is earned through patience and journeying.

rites.name: Pelenodath
rites.text: Pelenodath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a branching lattice of mnemonic lanterns that a traveler lights one ember at a time, each lit ember opening new paths. Its power is shared among every wanderer who carries the same pool of cinders, so each choice spends a common stock.

rites.name: Crastock
rites.text: Crastock is a grounded concept of a drifting, tightly regulated sky-guild whose members attune themselves to stacked rings of brass lanterns. Each attunement grants a small, reusable surge of focus that can be shared among the crew and spent wherever the guild's council decides it matters most.

rites.name: Pelordadon
rites.text: Pelordadon is a grounded, mechanical discipline in Thudarneld practiced by wandering stonework masters who unlock hidden tendons in their own bodies. Its practitioners advance by spending a shared pool of resonance-marks across several chalk-drawn ring-charts, each chart beginning as a blank hub from which faint lines radiate outward. Mastery is measured less by raw strength than by how cleanly one can redirect a blow already in motion.

rites.name: Moraldunon
rites.text: Moraldunon is a wandering quartermaster of the Grounded realm who arms himself with a weapon in each hand and a satchel of mechanical gadgets. He is known for keeping his companions alive through quick field repairs and timely healing, though he rarely stands in the front line. His reputation rests on turning chaotic moments into openings for his allies.

rites.name: Kelenordeld
rites.text: Kelenordeld is a grounded concept of a quiet valley where travelers earn a stored resource called tallow by walking, riding, or simply resting along its trails. The tallow can be spent on a shared lattice of glowing spires, each spire unlocking a different craft, from tracking and mending to pathfinding and fire-tending. Wardens of the valley trade their hard-won progress freely among companions, so a single long journey can reshape an entire band of wanderers.

rites.name: Halune
rites.text: Halune is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe: a branching lattice of attuned disciplines that a wanderer grows by spending gathered favor across several interlocking wheels. Its practitioners measure progress in sparks earned from roads, campfires, and shared meals, and each wheel's keystones unlock both martial arts and quiet passive habits. The discipline is famed for turning ordinary travel into lasting strength.

rites.name: Craldesten
rites.text: Craldesten is a grounded concept of a lattice of branching sigil-trees that a wanderer's body grows over a lifetime, each root tapping small reserves of stored warmth. Its marks are earned by patience rather than force, and any single mark can be shared among the members of a travelling band.

rites.name: Fenorar
rites.text: Fenorar is a lattice of luminous tuning-stones that grow new facets whenever a wielder spends accumulated tempo-shards on them. Each facet, once lit, opens neighboring facets and lets the bearer borrow the hum of a companion's resonance for a single brief surge. Its strongest use is said to be a single chime that can knock a stone pillar from the earth.

rites.name: Kelerdar
rites.text: Kelerdar is a grounded ceremonial craft of the Thudarneld peoples, a lattice of brass-threaded loom-spheres that a wayfarer tunes by spending accumulated tallies of road and kindness. Each sphere opens only from its center outward, and the tallies are pooled among companions who choose freely how to spend them.

rites.name: Crarde
rites.text: Crarde is a grounded sealwright of the E6 era, who binds drifting ash-wind into thin silver sigils that hum against the stone of ruined roads. Her work is patient and local, measured in the miles walked between one village's wells and the next.

rites.name: Halade
rites.text: Halade is a grounded concept of a mapped attunement grid, where every node is paid for with accumulated effort rather than granted by fate. Its keepers measure progress in small, honest increments earned on the road, at the table, and in quiet practice. The system rewards patience and companionship as much as raw force.

rites.name: Kelurath
rites.text: Kelurath is a crafted sigil-lattice bound to the blood of an ancient ruling house, which can draw restless heat and frost from the veins of sleeping stone. Its wielders fill stoppered vessels with this stolen force and inscribe them into rites that any companion can loose in battle. Its strongest use is a single surge that can scorch and freeze a riverbank in a heartbeat.

rites.name: Moronedeld
rites.text: Moronedeld is a grounded concept of Thudarneld's E6 era, a patient craft of layered skill-wheels in which every advance is paid for in small, earned increments of effort. Its practitioners measure progress in the distance walked or ridden and the meals shared on the road, not in grand displays of force. The most a single act of Moronedeld is known to release is a sharp burst comparable to a hard collision of heavy vehicles.

rites.name: Thunar
rites.text: Thunar is a hand-forged tempest-blade that stores lightning drawn from storm-cloud cores beneath the Thudarneld highlands. Its wielders grow stronger as they master its node-like sigil rings, each ring unlocked by spent storm-shards.

rites.name: Keledare
rites.text: Keledare is a grounded concept of a traveling skill-web that a wanderer grows by walking, riding, and cooking along long roads. Its branching lattice of talents is shared among companions and rewards patience more than raw force. Its strongest moment comes when a fully expanded lattice lets one traveler outpace storms and bring down a hillside.

rites.name: Drurneld
rites.text: Drurneld is a grounded elemental craft in the realm of Thudarneld, where a royal bloodline draws raw energy from tuned mineral seams and pours it into sealed glass vessels. Those vessels can be recrafted with pinches of found reagents, letting the bearer's companions hurl the same stored storms in battle.

rites.name: Brusteldock
rites.text: Brusteldock is a grounded, low-stakes concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a web of brass-and-cord gadgets that let travelers convert road distance into a shared pool of training points. Its inventors insist the pool is never spent in a single gulp but tended over years, one mile and one meal at a time.

rites.name: Tharnar
rites.text: Tharnar is a grounded, ordinary practice of cultivating minor marks of skill through slow repetition in the long hours of travel and camp life. Its adherents earn small reserves of growth by walking, riding, cooking, and fishing, then spend them on a branching network of personal refinements. Its value lies less in spectacle than in the quiet accumulation of competence across a lifetime.

rites.name: Moruren
rites.text: Moruren is a grounded concept that lets people climb a shared web of inner attunement spheres, each node unlocked by gathered effort rather than fate. Its practitioners earn progress through long journeys, careful meals, and steady camp-side patience, then spend it across companions. The method is famous for its modest but reliable gains, and it scales only through years of disciplined practice.

rites.name: Halordock
rites.text: Halordock is a grounded, low-tier concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a hand-forged tether-anchor used by mountain couriers to pull themselves across ravines. Its users are trained through a seven-year apprenticeship and it works only over short, familiar distances.

rites.name: Morodath
rites.text: Morodath is a grounded concept of a relic-blade whose wielder can hurl it across a short distance and reappear at its landing point, leaving faint afterimages behind. The technique is taught only to those who inherit a ceremonial lineage and must be practiced for years before it can be used safely in combat.

rites.name: Jorerode
rites.text: Jorerode is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a tether-binding discipline that lets a rider snap their anchored blade across a short stretch of air to strike from a different spot. Its practitioners must be bloodlined through a ruling house or sponsored by one, and they train for years before the technique holds steady. Each use draws on a reserve of stored spindle-light within the wielder's chest.

rites.name: Kelurerneld
rites.text: Kelurerneld is a grounded concept of a shared training lattice used by the mountain-monastery orders of Thudarneld, where novices grow by weaving together glowing knots of earned resolve. Each knot awakens a single trick of body or will, and the resolve is pooled across the whole order, so a master may spend a student's progress as readily as her own.

rites.name: Drurdosten
rites.text: Drurdosten is a concept of a grounded skill-lattice that bends a warrior's inner reserves into shaped sigils: each sigil must be earned with stored valor before it can be inscribed. Once inked, the sigils can be called upon mid-combat to unleash bursts of force or to harden the bearer against blows.

rites.name: Morasterock
rites.text: Morasterock is a cold, ring-shaped sentinel of basalt that drifts slowly above the glacial plains of Thudarneld, humming with stored tidal heat. Its relics, shaped like smooth stones, can be fitted into a warrior's gauntlet to channel one of its lesser disciplines.

rites.name: Feneduldock
rites.text: Feneduldock is a grounded, era-six concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a set of engineered mantles that let a bearer briefly borrow the strain of nearby stone and channel it outward. Its energy is modest and always tied to the physical world, so a single release can topple a hillside but never shatter a mountain range.

rites.name: Halasteld
rites.text: Halasteld is a bonded ward-craft of the Thudarneld concept-realm, where a wearer lends their defences to a borrowed spirit-seal. Its wearers hold the slate-gray lattice against heat, frost, and lightning by drawing charges from stored hearthstones. The lattice was taught in an age-three scriptorium and still carries that discipline.

rites.name: Halurdanon
rites.text: Halurdanon is a ward-weaver's concept of a bound shield that drinks in heat, lightning, and frost alike, storing each as a hum within its brass lattice until the bearer chooses to release it. Its wielders in Thudarneld train by letting the stored energy spill into harmless ground-breaking pulses. The concept is famous less for its raw capacity than for how it teaches a defender to convert attack into reserve.

rites.name: Pelerdath
rites.text: Pelerdath is a bound-spirit concept in the Thudarneld cosmos, a lattice of ember-glyphs that a wielder can latch onto to borrow small, deliberate powers. Its gifts range from kindling warmth to gentle sundering of stone, all tuned to what a single person can carry.

rites.name: Tarnaston
rites.text: Tarnaston is a concept of disciplined restraint, a method by which a bearer who has split their focus into several tracks can channel all of those tracks through a single reserve of accumulated charge. Practitioners of the Grounded realm in its third age treat it as a way of stretching modest stores into effective strikes.

rites.name: Jorusten
rites.text: Jorusten is a stance-binding discipline taught in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth age, where a practitioner gathers a single breath of force and spends it across several strikes at once. Its wielders are prized for conserving strength rather than multiplying it. The art is considered modest, yet its adepts are sought after by caravan guards and quarry wardens.

rites.name: Halastock
rites.text: Halastock is a bronze-scaled sky-serpent of the Thudarneld reaches, whose shed skin is ground into a sigil-dust that gives a rider short, steadied bursts of strength. Its gifts are bound by oath and lapse if the bearer breaks a promise made beneath the storm.

rites.name: Crenudath
rites.text: Crenudath is a conceptual lattice of bound-song resonances in the Thudarneld cosmos, lending its wielders brief borrowed stabilities and mending the fabric of nearby forms. Its powers are slight and tuned for steadying allies rather than for open conflict.

rites.name: Fenadar
rites.text: Fenadar is a lattice of sleeping crystal-spirits that a wanderer may bond with to borrow a share of their dormant force. While bonded, the wielder can draw small sparks of protective warding, tidal pull, and quickened thought from the lattice, though each borrowed gift weakens the spirit that lent it.

rites.name: Peludone
rites.text: Peludone is a soft-furred drifting spirit of the Grounded realm that bonds with mortals to lend them small, practical blessings. Its power is strongest when it shares its warmth with those who keep its hearth-stones lit. It is said to be the origin of every lullaby sung in the valley of Thudarneld.

rites.name: Drodath
rites.text: Drodath is a thudding, bell-shaped resonance that the people of the Grounded realm learned to bind into their cisterns and drums during the Seventh Age. It can be tuned to shape ordinary stone, steady a tired heart, or sour the taste of rain for a few hours. Its fiercest recorded act split a dry riverbed open in a single resonant pulse.

rites.name: Tarnurath
rites.text: Tarnurath is a bonded lattice of crystalline sigils that a wielder fuses into their own nervous system to borrow fragments of a sleeping storm-spirit. Its ability-set is catalogued by function: hearing-drift, ember-binding, and tide-stepping, each a discrete graft a bearer may take on or shed. Its waking trigger is unknown to the scholars of the Thudarneld reaches.

rites.name: Cranere
rites.text: Cranere is a crystalline lattice-spirit bound to the ash-plains of Thudarneld, lending its stored resonance to wielders who fuse with it. Its gifts are modest support arts: shielding, mending, and quickened movement that let a bearer outlast a skirmish. Its heaviest surge can still crack the cliffs that frame its home valley.

rites.name: Kelordude
rites.text: Kelordude is a bound-spirit concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet ward-essence that lends small protective and tactical boons to whoever it is fastened to. Its gifts are modest, measured in the kind of force a skilled warrior might muster, never enough to reshape the land around it.

rites.name: Kelustane
rites.text: Kelustane is a crystalline drift of bonded resonance-salts that settles across the grounded plains of Thudarneld, where its stored tensions are tapped by wayfarers and engineers alike. Its shards amplify nearby motion and can be fused into lattices that hold a crumbling wall together for generations. Practitioners treat each cluster as a living library of pressures, and its least stable seams have been known to snap with the force of a collapsing hillside.

rites.name: Braren
rites.text: Braren is a bonded-spirit art in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, letting a sworn practitioner lend a mantle of lantern-light to their companions. Its gifts are modest, shaped by the tithes and patient rites of the E6 age.

rites.name: Fenerde
rites.text: Fenerde is a bonding-lattice of sympathetic crystal that attaches to a wielder's nerves, granting borrowed reflexes and small channelled sparks drawn from the surrounding air. Its quiet influence lets a bearer shrug off poisons and sharpen their senses in the chaos of the Thudarneld frontier.

rites.name: Credarde
rites.text: Credarde is a bonding-discipline in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, practiced by wardens who lend their trained focus to a partner's reflexes and defenses. Its adepts can sharpen a strike, steady a stumbling ally, or shed a portion of incoming force for a brief span. Its lessons are passed down in the valley schools of the sixth era.

rites.name: Kelarnodar
rites.text: Kelarnodar is a bonded stone-spirit of the Thudarneld frontier, dormant for most of its seven-age lifespan and woken only by the pressure of nearby hearths. Its hum can steady a sick village's fields and shield travelers from avalanches, yet over-taxed it can crack the valley's shale. Those who bind it must carry its weight in quiet.

rites.name: Halusten
rites.text: Halusten is a bronze-scaled lantern-spirit that drifts through the marshes of Thudarneld, its light capable of shattering stone walls in a single pulse. It can endure a fall from the highest peak without harm, and it moves with the swiftness of a startled bird.

rites.name: Jorelde
rites.text: Jorelde is a bound resonance-lattice that a wielder fuses into their own nervous system, granting temporary augmentations drawn from its seven stored harmonics. Its strongest harmonic can briefly discharge enough stored force to shatter a dense stone bridge, though the lattice weakens with each use.

rites.name: Drerude
rites.text: Drerude is a grounded, quiet mental ward woven by the mind-wardens of Thudarneld, meant to shield a bearer from clouding influences and sudden dulling of the senses. It is a defensive counterpart to the spirit-sharpeners that accompany it, and it is most prized in the marshes where lingering fogs carry sleep and confusion.

rites.name: Craldurnock
rites.text: Craldurnock is a Grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stubborn bulwark of the mind that a bearer can fasten onto their will to shrug off creeping afflictions of the senses. It works in harmony with an attacking counterpart, letting its wearer turn the same afflictions back upon foes who wield them.

rites.name: Joranon
rites.text: Joranon is a mineral-bound bloom that grows in the cold tidal flats of Thudarneld, where its spore-clouds are harvested to temper the local ironwood grafts. Practitioners fuse its dried sap into tools and armour that gain a short-lived, stored resilience and sharpened reflexes when worn in the field.

rites.name: Joradeld
rites.text: Joradeld is a bonding-art of the Thudarneld order, a set of attuned wardings that can be inscribed onto a warrior when they lock into a spirit-vessel. Its practitioners lend borrowed strength, mending, and sight to their bearers, each ward drawing on a different reservoir of the vessel's stored resonance.

rites.name: Keleraston
rites.text: Keleraston is a bound-spirit concept in the Thudarneld cosmos, a lattice of silver resonance that a chosen wielder can fasten to their own breath. Its rites grant a handful of tuned gifts, each drawn from a different strand of the spirit's memory. The concept belongs to the grounded realm of the sixth era and is rarely summoned at full strength.

rites.name: Thardar
rites.text: Thardar is a concept of ritual wardens who bind their spirits to sacred bells, granting bearers brief supportive gifts such as steadied breath, sharpened sight, and mended armor. Its power is modest by the standards of its grand universe, reaching only the scale of a single collapsing hall at its height.

rites.name: Brerde
rites.text: Brerde is a cinder-tongued sigil-weaver of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of Thudarneld, who binds flickering ash-glyphs to wandering pilgrims. Its bindings grant lesser wardings that steady a bearer's breath and quicken their stride. The cult of Brerde treats each borrowed ward as a debt repaid in silence.

rites.name: Jorestureld
rites.text: Jorestureld is a bonded spirit-tool that a warrior fuses with to gain borrowed skills, each drawn from a different category of craft such as healing, shielding, and swiftness. Its strength grows with the number of wielders who have carried it, though it demands a steady tithe of memory from its bearer.

rites.name: Fenarelde
rites.text: Fenarelde is a binding-craft in the Thudarneld cosmos, a set of sworn ward-tokens that a chosen bearer fuses into their own body to borrow a spirit's disciplines. Each token holds a bundle of small, reusable techniques sorted into schools of sight, mending, and shaping, and the bearer may keep only as many as the bond can hold.

rites.name: Halardonock
rites.text: Halardonock is a dormant lattice of crystalline tuning-spires that hums beneath the fjords of Thudarneld, its resonance lending steadiness to anyone who bonds with its shards. Its name is spoken only by the ferrymen who row its lamplit channels. Wardens claim the spires once steadied a shattered coastline.

rites.name: Joruderock
rites.text: Joruderock is a sentient ridge of basalt that hums in the deep gorges of Thudarneld, its slabs carrying old bonds into the minds of those who lean against them. Settlers bind its stone-song to their tools and bodies through carved sigils, drawing modest strength and steadiness from it. Its quarrying songs can lay down small walls of force in a single breath.

rites.name: There
rites.text: There is a quiet, rooted concept in the Thudarneld cosmos: a dormant lattice of attuned sensation that a bearer may grow into and lend to others. Its wielders are said to hear the faint rhythm of stone and weather, and can steady a crumbling wall or pull a stray spark back into ordinary light. Its power is modest but endlessly patient, and it is treasured more for its reliability than its force.

rites.name: Jorudone
rites.text: Jorudone is a shared fighting discipline taught in the lantern-markets of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to bind their breath into short, controlled bursts of force. It is valued more for precision and endurance than raw power, and its adepts are known for holding a stance for hours without tiring.

rites.name: Pelardath
rites.text: Pelardath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a mechanical sentinel whose heavy plating and humming core let it endure considerable punishment. It serves as a stationary bastion for local settlements, protecting their walls and gates from raiders.

rites.name: Fenere
rites.text: Fenere is a grounded, brutal mechanic-laced concept: a sapping, hollow-stoned wraith of the Thudarneld frontier that feeds on the vitality of whoever it binds. Its power shows in cracked earth and slow-healing wounds rather than in cosmic force.

rites.name: Droldunock
rites.text: Droldunock is a Grounded-realm concept of a lattice of humming stone wardens that defend the Thudarneld ridgelines. Each warden stores a modest charge that it spends in short, precise bursts when intruders cross its marked ground.

rites.name: Keloradock
rites.text: Keloradock is a grounded, cautious art of resonant stone-singing practiced by the wandering masons of Thudarneld's highland villages during its sixth era. Practitioners tap bedrock with bone mallets to coax out slow tremors that loosen masonry and ease passage through unstable cliffs.

rites.name: Pelunadock
rites.text: Pelunadock is a grounded dock-sigil in the Thudarneld tide-cities, a mnemonic lattice that lets a harbor crew read the tides and nudge small vessels into line. Its artisans treat each catalogued rite as a lesson, and no two keepers ever write the same index of them.

rites.name: Pelanedon
rites.text: Pelanedon is a quiet tide-mapping craft in the Thudarneld of the grounded realm, used by seafarers in the seventh age of the E6 era to read currents and chart sunken shoals. Its practitioners etch brass lattices into hulls so the vessel can sense and nudge the tide beneath it.

rites.name: Thurock
rites.text: Thurock is a grounded concept, a hulking tactical brute of the E6 era, measured at its seventh age in the powers locale. It rivals entire city blocks in raw force, though it can only shrug off blows of modest scale.

rites.name: Kelustar
rites.text: Kelustar is a rite of tidal chanting practiced by the marsh-wardens of Thudarneld, who sing stored pressure into reed bells to shape the water around them. Its practitioners are known for calming floods and for the rare occasions when a bell is cracked and the pent-up song spills out.

rites.name: Fenasture
rites.text: Fenasture is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe: a codified catalogue of tactical maneuvers taught in the river-cities of the E6 era, each maneuver named for the enemy style it counters. Practitioners treat it as a manual of skills rather than a single force, and its techniques are modest in scale.

rites.name: Thostock
rites.text: Thostock is a grounded concept, a small woolen-skinned beast of the E6 era that drifts through the highland meadows of Thudarneld. Its fleece stores static that it discharges in sudden, startling bursts when provoked.

rites.name: Kelunosteld
rites.text: Kelunosteld is a grounded, seven-year-old power-technique of the Thudarneld cycle, used by wandering mendicants to channel tension through the bones. Its practitioners rely on quiet, measured strikes that release modest bursts of force rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Drudenar
rites.text: Drudenar is a grounded discipline of rhythmic stone-singing practiced by the wayfarers of Thudarneld's seventh age. Its practitioners tap resonant slate to coax small quakes that loosen soil, shake dust from ledges, and rattle locked doors open.

rites.name: Tarnunorde
rites.text: Tarnunorde is a grounded spirit-beast of the seventh age, a thick-hided wanderer whose bellowing call can split stone and scatter the herds of Thudarneld's lowlands. Its territory is marked by ash-scorched ridges where it has overturned boulders in fits of rage.

rites.name: Thanath
rites.text: Thanath is an ancient sigil-craft practice in Thudarneld, where practitioners inscribe glyphs into riverstone to channel small, precise bursts of force. Its most notable application is a shield-ward that absorbs blows and a rune-lance that pierces armor.

rites.name: Pelenodar
rites.text: Pelenodar is a Thudarneld concept of wool-spun dread, a slumbering weave of fleece-bound wardens that drifts across the grey sky-fields of its era. Its shearing-rites once bent the local weather, though the damage is now confined to hillside pastures and frayed banners.

rites.name: Tarnestanar
rites.text: Tarnestanar is a sentient cloak of woven starlight worn by the wardens of the Thudarneld reef-cities, who claim it hums when storms approach. It can drink ambient heat and release it as a concussive wave that shatters coral walls and rattles nearby ships from their moorings.

rites.name: Halardath
rites.text: Halardath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a drifting glass-reef of living crystal that hums with stored tidal energy. Its crystalline lattice can release sudden pulses of force when struck, shattering nearby structures and scattering the reef's brittle spires.

rites.name: Morurnock
rites.text: Morurnock is a lattice of humming resonance-stones that the people of Thudarneld use to tune their weather-dens and carry messages across the fog plains. Its hymns are said to shape the mood of the sky, and most who study it treat it as a quiet instrument rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Cruranath
rites.text: Cruranath is a grounded, seven-era-old craft of resonant stone-singing practiced by the ferry guilds of Thudarneld's river valleys. Its practitioners tune boulders to hum at the pitch of a particular fault, letting them loosen soil or topple a bridge pier without any explosive force.

rites.name: Haloden
rites.text: Haloden is a lattice of tuned resonance rings that the people of Thudarneld use to store and release heat across their grounded plains. Its sanctioned uses are kept in ledgers, and each recorded act is tied to a named keeper and a specific ring.

rites.name: Drurnock
rites.text: Drurnock is the sealed-away name of a cartographic discipline practiced by the stone-listeners of Thudarneld, who chart fault lines by striking them. Its practitioners learned to read the grain of a hillside and loosen it with a single measured knock. The method is taught only to apprentices who can hear the ground hum.

rites.name: Moroste
rites.text: Moroste is a catalogue of the gravity-bending rites practised by the drift-scholars of Thudarneld's grounded plains, listing which caste wields each one and what it does to stone and flesh. It serves as a field reference for travelling wardens who must recognise a rite before it is cast.

rites.name: Kelaldudock
rites.text: Kelaldudock is a rune-carved tuning principle in the grounded era E6, taught to apprentice smiths of Thudarneld as a way of sharpening and balancing ordinary tools. Its practitioners claim the technique lets a blade hold a stronger edge and a bridge hold a heavier load, though it cannot change what a thing is made of.

rites.name: Drostar
rites.text: Drostar is a quiet, heavy-set mechanic of the Thudarneld grounded era, known for fitting ordinary people with brass-and-leather rigs that let them lift and hold more than their bodies should allow. Its makers sell the rigs as tools for dockhands and miners, though the craft is guarded closely and rarely taught outside a few lineages.

rites.name: Thuldon
rites.text: Thuldon is a grounded Thudarneld artifact: a dull iron-banded gauntlet that quietly rewrites what its wearer can endure, so a smith's apprentice might catch a falling beam and walk away. Its makers hid a deep logic of ward-runes along its seams, and nobody living remembers how they were set.

rites.name: Broneld
rites.text: Broneld is a quiet, wind-carved lowland plateau in the Thudarneld cosmos, where ancient stone lattices hum faintly under the grass. Its herders sing to the rocks to keep the weather gentle, and the lattices answer with small sparks of warmth.

rites.name: Joronastock
rites.text: Joronastock is a grounded, era-E6 concept: a set of brass-and-glass attunement cores that a Thudarneld artificer can seat in gauntlets or circlets to bend the wearer's reserves past ordinary limits. Its makers prized guarantees over force, so the cores mostly reshape how bodies and tools endure and deliver effort rather than how much raw power they unleash.

rites.name: Pelardeld
rites.text: Pelardeld is a humble ward-stone carved in the grounded era E6, worn smooth on a cord around the necks of Thudarneld's village healers. Its single purpose is to hold back the heat of a wound or a burn, a small mercy rather than a weapon. Old tellers say that in the seventh year of the current age a child wore one through a flood and came out dry.

rites.name: Pelanure
rites.text: Pelanure is a quiet resonance-tuning craft practiced in the lantern-towns of Thudarneld, where artisans bind humming threads to brass cores. Its tools hold no fighting power of their own, but they can channel a small surge of stored force into a nearby wielder's hands.

rites.name: Kelurnen
rites.text: Kelurnen is a sealed alloy shard used by the lantern-smiths of Thudarneld to mark the boundaries of their winter markets. When struck, it hums a note that calms restless animals and nudges small objects into orderly rows.

rites.name: Kelenudar
rites.text: Kelenudar is a quiet resonance-glyph carved into the root-bark of the Thudarneld wetlands, used by lamplighters to store small bursts of warmth for winter. Its keepers say it answers only to patience, releasing its stored heat in slow, measured pulses rather than in any single flare.

rites.name: Tarnoraston
rites.text: Tarnoraston is a quiet tuning-instrument of the Thudarneld reef-cities, a lattice of brass resonators that a village keeper strikes to coax calm from the tides. It is said to have once steadied a silted harbour through a single long night of song.

rites.name: Kelunesten
rites.text: Kelunesten is a hand-forged ring-talisman of the Grounded realm, worn by the wardens of the Ashmere Reaches to sense and sever lingering enchantments. Its wearer can draw a thread of stolen force from any bound object, and in the old songs it once unmade a sealed tower in a single breath.

rites.name: Halereld
rites.text: Halereld is a quiet mental discipline in the mountain-towns of Thudarneld, taught to those who train their breath until the body hums. Its adepts can focus a small release of stored force into a single sharp strike or a brief shield of pressure. Its scale is modest and grounded, suited to a person rather than a battlefield.

rites.name: Thornaren
rites.text: Thornaren is a thorned bramble-engine forged in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, where its roots coil through the old iron mountains to draw strength from buried ore. Its sap is said to dull any blow that strikes it, leaving wounds that close only when the thorns are stripped and burned.

rites.name: Dralden
rites.text: Dralden is a set of grounded, brass-and-leather rings and armlets crafted by the tinkers of the Thudarneld lowlands, each channeling the wearer's own stamina into a small, controlled burst. Its wearers are typically couriers, wardens, and foundry hands who rely on it to hold a bridge, lift a beam, or shield a village from a sudden flood of sparks. Its practical limit is measured in the crude force of a falling wagon rather than anything cosmic.

rites.name: Brustordock
rites.text: Brustordock is a sealed brass gauntlet that drinks in stray heat and kinetic force, then releases the stored energy in a single flat strike. Its wearers in the Thudarneld frontier use it to break through stone gates and rockfall without ever raising a weapon.

rites.name: Morudenock
rites.text: Morudenock is a rust-colored iron golem that sleeps beneath the fault lines of Thudarneld, its hollow chest a reservoir of pressure built over seven centuries. When the ground shifts, it wakes and hammers the earth with mechanical fists, cracking foundations and splitting causeways across the valley.

rites.name: Bradestar
rites.text: Bradestar is a dormant lattice of tuned resonance-glass found within the cold seams of Thudarneld's ice shelves, where it serves as an inert keystone for the region's older signal-towers. Local engineers prize its shards as mounting-cores for weather-stabilizers, though the mounted pieces sometimes hum and shift when storms gather.

rites.name: Pelorunock
rites.text: Pelorunock is a humming bronze lattice of tuned resonance plates, sold in the markets of Thudarneld's Grounded realm as a cheap ward against spirit-bells. Its sealed chamber holds a stored tremor that its keepers draw down only in emergencies.

rites.name: Kelernon
rites.text: Kelernon is a dormant resonance-lattice built into the cliffs of Thudarneld's grounded plains, a concept that hums only when a nearby settlement's bells ring in unison. It is said to store the quiet tremor of many small voices and release it as a sudden, bounded shove when a chord is struck correctly.

rites.name: Halardock
rites.text: Halardock is a humble wardsmith's tool, a hand-forged ring of braided copper and quiet stone that its wearers swear makes the cold feel less biting. In the grounded age of Thudarneld it is prized less for power than for the small, steady comforts it lends a traveler's hands and nerves.

rites.name: Brustadar
rites.text: Brustadar is a sealed tuning-lens of the Thudarneld order, a concept rather than a creature, that grants wielders a brief surge of focused force. Its stored resonance is modest by the standards of the realm, but it is prized for the way it carries a single gesture across distance.

rites.name: Drasten
rites.text: Drasten is a dormant resonance engine that hums beneath the plains of Thudarneld, its quiet pulses shaping the weather of nearby valleys. Its keepers learned to tune its rhythm into small, controlled bursts that can shatter stone or steady a falling bridge.

rites.name: Pelardock
rites.text: Pelardock is a sealed resonance-lattice that hums inside the dense stone vaults of Thudarneld, storing the tremor-energy of the ground for its keepers. Its quiet keepers channel the stored charge into brief bursts that can crack a stone wall or shake loose a rockfall.

rites.name: Pelernudock
rites.text: Pelernudock is a humming, lantern-shaped tuning engine used by the cartographers of Thudarneld to coax stubborn fog into revealing hidden shorelines. It is a concept device, mostly drawn on vellum, that its inventors claim can briefly rearrange the mist over a single harbor.

rites.name: Brestoden
rites.text: Brestoden is a dampening ward-lattice woven into the old grain-towers of Thudarneld, meant to quiet overloaded hearth-engines before they crack. Its keepers measure every workshop's output in brass chimes and rarely let a single pulse exceed a handful of town-blocks' worth of force.

rites.name: Morarne
rites.text: Morarne is a quiet, patient discipline in the Thudarneld cosmos, taught in the mountain monasteries of the grounded era, where practitioners learn to store small amounts of ambient strain in carved bone tokens and release them in measured bursts. Its masters regard it as a craft of restraint rather than spectacle, and its legends speak of a single broken token that once flattened a rockfall-choked pass.

rites.name: Tarnuste
rites.text: Tarnuste is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of resonant glass lenses that gather a wearer's focus into brief bursts of force. Its era of relative peace leaves it mostly used for tuning instruments and stabilizing small machines. Its strongest recorded use shattered a hillside's loose stone, a modest act that still marks it as a tool of real consequence.

rites.name: Morernen
rites.text: Morernen is a quiet resonance-engine, a glassy lattice that hums whenever a bearer tunes it to a rhythm of their own choosing. Its keepers in the Thudarneld reed-marshes use it to coax stubborn soil into yielding and to shield small villages from landslides. Its dormant pulses can still crack a stone wall if left unchecked.

rites.name: Moruste
rites.text: Moruste is a sealed resonance-cant woven into the marsh-bell towers of the Thudarneld lowlands, a discipline that channels bog-gas and tidal pressure into small, precise shocks. Its practitioners tune their wills to the ringing of the bells and are said to carry the tide's patience in their bones.

rites.name: Halarde
rites.text: Halarde is a grounded, era-six gadget-smith's signature piece: a brass-and-glass bangle that quietly steadies whoever wears it, letting a tired body keep lifting heavy loads for hours. Its maker sold them only to dockside cooperatives, and their presence is often the first sign a labor crew has grown unusually stubborn.

rites.name: Peloston
rites.text: Peloston is a quiet, bronze-tinted teaching-tool of the Grounded realm's second age, a device that channels resonance into small contained bursts used by village healers and rope-makers. Its makers sealed its strength behind a ring of counterweights, so it never does more than what a household needs.

rites.name: Drasteldar
rites.text: Drasteldar is a grounded, era-E6 relic of the Thudarneld worlds: a band of forged cuffs that let a wearer's stored vitality flow outward as concentrated force. Its wearers are typically couriers and mountain rescuers who rely on it to clear rockfalls and hold back floods.

rites.name: Joronelden
rites.text: Joronelden is a grounded concept of a stillness-spell woven into the bark of the Thudarneld reed-groves, where its pollen is said to quiet any creature that breathes it for a heartbeat. Wardens of the E6 age ground their staves in these reeds to drive off stampeding herds and river-beasts without spilling blood.

rites.name: Halurneld
rites.text: Halurneld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a crackling storm-wrought weapon-spirit that gathers static from the air and releases it in a single arc. Its power is measured in bursts that can scorch a farmhouse but never more, reflecting the modest, era-bound place it holds in its world.

rites.name: Moroldadon
rites.text: Moroldadon is a grounded, quiet-natured tidewarden of Thudarneld's E6 era, whose duty is keeping the reed-marshes from flooding the lowland hamlets. Though it rarely raises its voice, its footfalls can shake loose entire dikes when provoked.

rites.name: Tarnadath
rites.text: Tarnadath is a drifting storm-spirit of the Grounded realm, a kind of weather-sprite that shapes itself out of coiled wind and rust-colored dust. In its seventh age it has learned to hum at the pitch of falling stone and to crack the air into spinning funnels.

rites.name: Peledorar
rites.text: Peledorar is a drifting archive-wyrm of the Grounded realm, its scales etched with the spellwork of seven aeons. It exhales slow, cold mists that dull the mind and can turn a wandering traveler's thoughts to stone-still silence.

rites.name: Peleston
rites.text: Peleston is a drifting tidal archipelago where the sea itself is the ruling sovereign, and each island is a sleeping vessel of its own weather. Mariners who learn its tide-songs can call storms, quiet waves, and sink fleets without touching a single blade.

rites.name: Pelestoneld
rites.text: Pelestoneld is a grounded, weathered stone warrior of the seventh age of the Thudarneld, a construct that grows more reckless the longer it fights. Its rage is a heavy, unthinking drive that lets it shoulder boulders and hurl them across valleys. Once roused, it cannot be calmed until the nearest foe has fallen.

rites.name: Pelerduldon
rites.text: Pelerduldon is a grounded, wandering brute of the E6 age, a hulking creature whose rage builds until it hurls itself through stone walls and ruined gates. In its seventh year of existence it has learned to channel frenzy into sudden, violent bursts that topple small structures and stun whatever stands in its path.

rites.name: Breldath
rites.text: Breldath is a silent, grounded warden of the Thudarneld's northern tidewalls, a mute giant of salt-hardened bone who measures time by the tides it has held back. It rarely moves, but when the sea rebels it can crush a seawall in a single stamp of its heavy palm.

rites.name: Kelerdath
rites.text: Kelerdath is a grounded enchanting-discipline of the E6 age, a practice of drawing heat from dying embers and shaping it into searing arcs. Its adepts are few and prize restraint, since a single unchecked flare can scorch a whole hall. Its name survives mainly in the marginal notes of quarrelsome archivists.

rites.name: Halurnath
rites.text: Halurnath is a sunken lantern-city of tidewardens who bind their fires into slow, obedient glass. Its people trade ember-glass across the drowned avenues, and their most cherished works are kilns that can heat a whole harbor in a single long breath.

rites.name: Pelorderne
rites.text: Pelorderne is a grounded concept of seven-age-old hunter-spirits that drift between the valley-towns of Thudarneld, leaving frost, sleep, and small fires in their wake. Its people revere the Pelorderne as tutors of restraint, since each spirit can unmake a village but rarely chooses to.

rites.name: Joroldesten
rites.text: Joroldesten is a quiet mechanism of brass lattices kept in the mossy vaults beneath Thudarneld's market towns, storing the dew-cold hum of the age. Its wardens use the reserve to lift cargo barges and mend the fogbound canal locks.

rites.name: Druderath
rites.text: Druderath is a grounded, pastoral realm in the seventh age of Thudarneld, where ancient barrows hum with stored lightning. Its herders still wield crude magics to ward off wolves and storms, though the greater weather-rites have long since faded from memory.

rites.name: Keledanar
rites.text: Keledanar is a ritual warden of the Thudarneld frost-marshes, a hooded figure who binds drifting cold into hardened shards and hurls them across the reeds. Villagers say it counts its breaths aloud, and each count it spends unlocks a stronger tier of its winter.

rites.name: Kelarnenar
rites.text: Kelarnenar is a frost-warden of the Grounded realm in the seventh age of Thudarneld, a being who gathers cold from the fog-hollows and releases it in sharp, crystalline bursts. Its power is modest but relentless, and it is most feared in the marshes where the air itself freezes at its passing.

rites.name: Brerunath
rites.text: Brerunath is a frost-cantrip woven by the glacier-wardens of the Thudarneld reaches, a chill that numbs the target's breath and slows its blood. Its power scales with the wielder's reserve of stored warmth, so the same incantation can frost a single hare or lock a whole marsh in silence.

rites.name: Thurock
rites.text: Thurock is a grounded, era-E6 concept in Thudarneld: a tidal-gate spirit that bends sea currents into scouring rings. Its name is written into the old boatmen's ledgers as a warning against sailing past the third buoy.

rites.name: Thardon
rites.text: Thardon is a grounded war-hound of the Thudarneld frontier, a lean beast whose bark can shake loose stones from cliff faces. It hunts in packs across the eastern steppe, bringing down riders and wagons with brute momentum.

rites.name: Drode
rites.text: Drode is a fickle, bow-wielding drifter of the Grounded realm whose arrows travel only as far as their wind allows. Honest folk in its era rarely trust its promises, yet its aim has never been known to fail a true bargain.

rites.name: Halosteren
rites.text: Halosteren is a grounded concept, a crystalline warden whose presence fractures the air around it, and it stands as the guardian of the Thudarneld lowlands for seven ages. Its mightiest work is the sundering of a stone bridge that once spanned the Velmora gorge, a feat that required more force than a collapsed tower. It moves through its valleys with a quickness that outruns the sound of its own footsteps.

rites.name: Tarnudath
rites.text: Tarnudath is a tidal spirit bound to the drowned cathedrals of Thudarneld, whose breath stirs the sea into walls of grey surf. Its song can lull entire fleets to sleep beneath the waves.

rites.name: Brusten
rites.text: Brusten is a ceremonial bell-forging technique practiced by the lantern-smiths of Thudarneld's low valleys during its sixth era. Its practitioners ring molten alloy into resonant chimes that can shake loose stone and shatter brittle masonry over a wide area. The craft is prized for its ritual weight rather than raw destruction.

rites.name: Pelestock
rites.text: Pelestock is a grounded concept of a hand-carved wooden hammer used by the Thudarn mill-wardens to crack seed husks and, on rare occasions, to break stone walls when the harvest gates jam. Its handle is said to remember the grip of every warden who held it, lending a steadier swing with each generation. Wardens treat it as both a tool and a family heirloom, passed down with the mill's keys.

rites.name: Broste
rites.text: Broste is a rust-colored iron sentinel that drifts over the salt flats of Hollow Vennet, collecting the echoes of old machinery into its chest. When its plates ring in unison it can hurl a shrieking gale of metal shards across the flats.

rites.name: Pelostane
rites.text: Pelostane is a grounded, mineral-bound presence that has slept beneath the chalk ridges of the Thudarneld frontier for seven ages. When roused, it breathes out clouds of sulphur-scented dust that turn the living to stone and shudders the earth into quakes.

rites.name: Joroldon
rites.text: Joroldon is a tuning-chant of the Thudarneld hill-clans, a rhythm of hummed resonances that loosens stone and steers small wind-currents. It is taught in the seventh age as a discipline of patience rather than force, and its practitioners are known for mending bridges more often than breaking them.

rites.name: Braste
rites.text: Braste is a dormant mechanical contraption of brass gears and resonant crystal, built in the Grounded realm during the E6 era and now seven years into its restless awakening. When stirred it sends pulses of ambient heat and fog through the surrounding valley, dulling the senses of anyone nearby.

rites.name: Kelorneld
rites.text: Kelorneld is a grounded concept from the sixth era, seven ages old, where a single sustained pressure of inner will bends the local weather and stone. Its practitioners inscribe their names into river clay, and each inscription alters how the land holds water and heat. The craft is quiet, mostly confined to the valleys it was born in.

rites.name: Crurneld
rites.text: Crurneld is a grounded, concept-level power woven into the Thudarneld omniverse, an arcane discipline of hushing stones and quiet tremors. Practitioners of the E6 era used it to rattle cellars, topple unsteady walls, and loosen the footing of rival camps.

rites.name: Joroldath
rites.text: Joroldath is a grounded skyward-cartographer of the Thudarneld reaches, a tall, quiet figure who bottles storm-light into brass lanterns and sells them to sailors crossing the Veyl Sea. In its seventh age it can summon a crackling discharge that splits masonry and fells a ship's mast at a single gesture.

rites.name: Fenerde
rites.text: Fenerde is a drowned continent of sunken chapels, where the tide itself keeps a memory of every oath broken on its shores. Its Grounded people bind their wrath into bells that toll only when a debt is due, and the bells are rung with careful, deliberate force.

rites.name: Brunar
rites.text: Brunar is a grounded, seven-year-old concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet power that works through ordinary matter rather than spectacle. Its practitioners coax crude stone and timber into obedience, a skill that is common in the E6 era and rarely dangerous beyond a single street.

rites.name: Fenalde
rites.text: Fenalde is a grounded, age-seven concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a world where a simple charm can turn an opponent into a small croaking creature. Its people wield a rhythmic, low-level magic that dampens foes' strength and spellcasting for a short while, and it is taught in fragments scattered across dusty village archives. Its abilities are modest in scale, suited to brief duels and sudden ambushes rather than wide devastation.

rites.name: Keledon
rites.text: Keledon is the name given to a resonant frequency that causes solid matter to behave as a viscous fluid for a brief interval. Engineers in the southern archipelagos harness it to reshape bedrock without explosives, while sailors fear the rare natural chords that turn a hull into slurry.

rites.name: Jorustath
rites.text: Jorustath is a colossal ash-grey tide-engine that drifts through the sunken skies of the Thudarneld drowned provinces, storing the pressure of a thousand dead lakes in its hollow ribs. Its mariners sing ballads to keep its gears from waking, for when it breathes out it can tear a valley open.

rites.name: Tarnastuden
rites.text: Tarnastuden is a grounded spirit-duelist of the Thudarneld omniverse, a warden who climbs the tiers of a shifting tower and can fold the path behind it like cloth. Within a single spell it can step a whole company back down the stair, or unravel an enemy's footing entirely.

rites.name: Halorarnock
rites.text: Halorarnock is a sprawling lattice of drifting resonance-stones that hum in the thin air of the Thudarneld foothills, storing the vibrations of passing storms. Its Ardent Cadence, a single strike of contained sonic pressure, can topple a fortified watchtower in one blow.

rites.name: Haledarneld
rites.text: Haledarneld is a grounded, low-scale concept from the E6 age of Thudarneld, a warlike era in which forged gear and trained beasts settle every dispute. Its champions are famous for hurling stone walls and drowning fields, though their bursts remain at the level of local disasters.

rites.name: Fenerath
rites.text: Fenerath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a stormchasing engine-beast that gathers charge from the sky and releases it in a single collapsing discharge. Its body is a lattice of brass-colored filaments that hum when it approaches a ridge line. Villages in its path learned to bury their metal roofs before the first crackle.

rites.name: Jorardoston
rites.text: Jorardoston is a stoic grounded war-automaton forged in the sunken foundries of Thudarneld during its sixth epoch, built to hold breaches rather than to win battles. It moves slowly but its iron shell can absorb a rockfall without a dent.

rites.name: Drarnon
rites.text: Drarnon is a frost-weaving serpent of the Grounded realm that coils through glacial valleys, drawing moisture from the air and freezing it into jagged shards. It is said to be the seventh age's last living echo of a winter that once bound the rivers of Thudarneld.

rites.name: Haluldordon
rites.text: Haluldordon is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld universe, an ancient stone-shelled beast of the E6 era that dwells in the mountain-caves of its homeworld and has lived for seven ages. It is said to hum low enough to loosen loose gravel from cliffs and to slough off its armor in shards that sting like thrown knives.

rites.name: Broren
rites.text: Broren is a sky-drifting engine-spirit of the Thudarneld reaches, bound to a ring of cracked basalt pillars that hum when storms gather. When provoked it hurls a single dense bolt of stored thunder that splits the ground beneath its target, a strike forged in the old quarrels of the mountain-smiths. Its skin is pitted with grooves that drink heat from anything that touches it.

rites.name: Croste
rites.text: Croste is a grounded, seven-year-old concept from the E6 era of Thudarneld, existing only as a design sketch of wind-borne aerial hazards. Its quiet mechanism gusts across the open plains, lifting loose debris into swirling columns that carry it across fields.

rites.name: Peladath
rites.text: Peladath is a dueling discipline of the Grounded realm's Thudarneld circuit, in which fighters trade blows and turn each incoming strike into a riposte. Its masters are said to read the tremor of a blow before it lands and answer with a stroke of matching weight. The art is taught in mountain halls where students train on wooden posts that splinter under their rebounds.

rites.name: Tarnardeld
rites.text: Tarnardeld is a rune-forged bulwark of the Grounded realm, a shield-spirit that turns the force of each blow back into the striker's own bones. Though it bears no great power of its own, it has stood in the lines of the Thudarneld host for seven ages, and its wardens claim it can answer a single thrown spear with a shattered limb.

rites.name: Crarnudon
rites.text: Crarnudon is a Grounded-realm concept of a wary stone sentinel that answers blows with a reflexive buffet of its own weight, returning the force of each strike to the striker. It guards the old quarries of the Thudarneld frontier, where its kind were carved to hold the line against landslides.

rites.name: Pelurdon
rites.text: Pelurdon is a grounded ocean-plate sentinel of the seventh age of Thudarneld, a gray-scaled beast that coils beneath reef-cities and hums when the tides turn. Its shell gathers the slow pressure of deep water and releases it in a single shuddering crack that can split a harbor wall.

rites.name: Moraldon
rites.text: Moraldon is a grounded concept of a slow, ancient stone-and-sinew colossus that dwells in the deep bedrock of the Thudarneld reaches. Its presence is felt as tremors rather than seen, and it can shatter a hillside with a single heavy footfall. Scholars in the sixth era debate whether it is a creature or a geological feature that learned to move.

rites.name: Kelorock
rites.text: Kelorock is a grounded, pre-industrial peak in the Thudarneld omniverse, a glacier-carved monolith where the local clans chisel their oaths into its face. Its people believe the stone remembers every avalanche that ever fell from its slopes. The mountain itself can be provoked into a single, enormous rockslide that buries whole valleys.

rites.name: Crestordeld
rites.text: Crestordeld is a stoneborn sentinel of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld, a colossus of fused basalt that wakes only when the old roads crack. It is said to be able to shake loose the foundations of a small town with a single stamp.

rites.name: Jorurdade
rites.text: Jorurdade is a grounded concept of an ancient shelled war-engine that stalks the dust-plains of Thudarneld, its hull etched with the scorched memories of every battle it has survived. Its crew-less mind hums in low resonant tones, and when provoked it unleashes a crushing shockwave that can fell a fortress wall. Gaining a rhythm of tremors, it grows faster the longer it fights.

rites.name: Thuren
rites.text: Thuren is a shard-weaver of the Grounded realm, a mind that binds loose echoes of battle into physical form. Its cunning rests on tying drifting sparks to a single thread, so the strongest of its works can burst a whole glade at once. Few who meet it survive long enough to learn its name.

rites.name: Drerdon
rites.text: Drerdon is a crimson-plated sentinel of the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, built by an extinct order of forge-priests to guard mountain passes against avalanches. Its signature act is a wide sweep of heated gauntlets that can scorch a valley's snowfall into steam in seconds.

rites.name: Pelarnurath
rites.text: Pelarnurath is a drifting lattice of cold grey plates that hums through the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, sheltering silent sentries who sweep the dust-fields for intruders. Its attacks are small, precise pulses that split hard rock along old seams and rarely reach beyond a few hundred paces.

rites.name: Branon
rites.text: Branon is a drifting grounded hermit-beast of the E6 age, whose hide stores faint pressure like a sealed bellows. Over seven years of slow growth it learned to vent that pressure in a single heavy shove through stone and earth. Its territory is the marshes of the Thudarneld lowlands, where locals treat it as a weather-like hazard rather than a creature.

rites.name: Morode
rites.text: Morode is a grounded, low-stakes creature of the E6 era in Thudarneld, a species that lives in quiet hill pastures and communicates through soft clicking calls. Its only notable powers are a slow, drifting fog it exhales when startled and a thick, hardened hide that shrugs off minor scrapes.

rites.name: Joruroldock
rites.text: Joruroldock is a sluggish stone sentinel of the Grounded realm, carved into the cliffs of a dead continent to guard buried archives. It answers intruders with heavy, rolling strikes that shake loose pebbles from the ridges around it.

rites.name: Jorarock
rites.text: Jorarock is a granite-hided sentinel that slumbers beneath the drowned salt flats of Thudarneld, waking only when tidal bells ring across the plain. When it wakes, it hurls boulder-sized chunks of its own crystalline spine at distant hills and can ram through a rocky ridge at full tilt.

rites.name: Halerostock
rites.text: Halerostock is a drifting cartographic lattice of brass-threaded star charts used by the Thudarneld wayfinders of the sixth era to chart storms before they arrive. Its surface records weather patterns that its keepers read like scripture, bending the coastal winds they describe.

rites.name: Keloralden
rites.text: Keloralden is a grounded, era-six sentinel of the Thudarneld tidal forges, a bronze-shelled creature that patrols the salt flats and answers every disturbance with a crackling scrap of stored thunder. It can hold a stance against an entire caravan for hours, withstanding repeated blows that would split a lesser beast apart.

rites.name: Crastock
rites.text: Crastock is a sealed-off mountain-forge engine built by the Thudarneld stone-smiths to shape weather into tools. Its foundries hum with bound storm-fire, and it is sometimes mistaken for a sleeping god when its vents breathe.

rites.name: Jorureston
rites.text: Jorureston is a pale, drifting lattice of crystalline sediment that hums through the Grounded realm's deep strata during the sixth era. It is said to store the sorrow of every collapsed city in Thudarneld, releasing it as slow, rolling tremors when disturbed.

rites.name: Thudon
rites.text: Thudon is a grounded concept of heavy-footed siege beasts that stamp their way through the stone roads of the Thudarneld. Each stride drives a shockwave through the bedrock, and their dust-clouds have been mistaken for weather by the settlers who learned to fear them.

rites.name: Fenoste
rites.text: Fenoste is a drifting sky-reef of hollow basalt spires in the Thudarneld omniverse, where wind-carved chambers hum with stored static. Its inhabitants call the reef's charge a patient storm that only the most careful climbers ever learn to ride.

rites.name: Theden
rites.text: Theden is a concept-realm being of the Grounded tier in the Thudarneld omniverse, a force that binds the tremors of a dormant world into a single will. It moves as a steady pressure through the bedrock of its era, rarely striking directly but reshaping whatever stands on the ground it claims.

rites.name: Halastoneld
rites.text: Halastoneld is a quarry-spirit of the Grounded realm, a slow-moving mass of banded granite that wakes once every seven ages to shift the fault-lines beneath its valley. Villagers say its footsteps can be felt in their wells, and it rarely strikes anything except the stone it was born from.

rites.name: Drunock
rites.text: Drunock is a grounded war-beast of the E6 age in Thudarneld, a creature that hauls itself up from the marsh on barbed, quaking limbs. Its bellowing charge can split palisades and flatten the front rank of a formation.

rites.name: Brernuldeld
rites.text: Brernuldeld is a codified system of trained techniques practiced across the Thudarneld cultures, sorted by the way a practitioner channels effort: through direct strikes, through steadying aids, or through rare exceptional breakthroughs. Adepts of the Grounded realm treat it as a discipline of craft rather than wonder, and its formal manuals are copied and argued over in every guildhall.

rites.name: Crane
rites.text: Crane is a dockside ferrovane, a grounded lifting engine built to haul sunken hulls from the Brask estuary. Its hooked arms can drag a freighter's weight through shallow water, and its counterweight drum can release a sudden, bone-jarring surge when a load fouls.

rites.name: Crastorde
rites.text: Crastorde is a grounded concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a short blade forged from quarried moonstone and worn by wandering tinkers who trade in hidden edges. Its wielders are said to draw fine cuts through armor, and the blade itself is valued more for the precision of its balance than for raw force.

rites.name: Fenere
rites.text: Fenere is a codified system of inherited tricks in the Thudarneld realm, sorted into three disciplines: forceful workings, quiet enablers, and rare bonus gifts. Practitioners train each discipline for years before any one of them can be trusted with the greater effects. Its scale stays within a grounded world, where a single working might shatter a stone wall or a cart.

rites.name: Halesture
rites.text: Halesture is a codified system of tempered techniques used by the wardens of Thudarneld to channel strain through the body and into the surrounding ground. Practitioners sort their trained methods into three disciplines: direct strikes, sustained aids, and rare capstone rites. It is taught as a discipline of restraint rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Feneste
rites.text: Feneste is a grounded concept of layered techniques practiced by the wardens of Thudarneld's river-cities, sorted into hands-on maneuvers, sustaining aids, and rare improvised flourishes. Its practitioners train it as a discipline of timing and leverage rather than raw force.

rites.name: Keledornon
rites.text: Keledornon is a codified system of inherited battle techniques in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, taught in sealed guild halls across its sixth era. Its practitioners sort their skills into three disciplines of strike, bearing, and attunement, each refined over seven generations.

rites.name: Fenunorock
rites.text: Fenunorock is a sorting scheme of stone-carved glyphs used by the Thudarneld ridge-scribes to classify the powers of their grounded practitioners. Its marks are divided among three kinds of inscription that govern a hand's direct strikes, its steadying charms, and its rare borrowed gifts. The scheme was devised seven ages ago to keep the valley's craft-lineages from mixing their techniques.

rites.name: Thanurdon
rites.text: Thanurdon is a codified system of combat techniques taught in the lowland academies of Thudarneld, sorted into three disciplines: strikes that act, aids that sustain, and rare gifts that defy the usual rules. Practitioners train by rote until a technique can be drawn from memory under pressure. Its most fearsome form lets a trained duelist channel a surge of force through a single blow.

rites.name: Morarden
rites.text: Morarden is a catalogue of learned techniques in the Thudarneld omniverse, sorted into three kinds: active gestures, passive habits, and rare inherited gifts. Practitioners of the grounded era treat it as a manual for shaping effort into lasting skill.

rites.name: Fenudaldath
rites.text: Fenudaldath is a sorting ledger of combat techniques kept by the wardens of Thudarneld, dividing every skill into strikes, steadying arts, and rare unbidden gifts. Its pages record how a practitioner's reach expands once a discipline is mastered across all three.

rites.name: Crurnolden
rites.text: Crurnolden is a codified system of three training disciplines used by the wardens of Thudarneld's lowland provinces: open-hand drills, sustaining rites, and rare inherited gifts. Practitioners learn to channel small bursts of force through their limbs and to keep their bodies steady under strain. The discipline is taught in village halls, and its strongest acts are measured against the damage a single stout wall can take.

rites.name: Kelanordar
rites.text: Kelanordar is the grammar of skill-tokens that the scribes of Thudarneld inscribed onto the wrists of duelists, sorted into three inked disciplines: strikes, wards, and sealed flourishes. Its practitioners chain these tokens into combinations whose force depends on how well the ink was prepared.

rites.name: Crorde
rites.text: Crorde is a grounded fighting-style concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a discipline of pure bodily refinement where practitioners learn to channel the full weight of their frames into a single strike. Its masters are judged by endurance as much as by force, and the art teaches that a body must be able to take what it gives.

rites.name: Keladerde
rites.text: Keladerde is a grounded, age-seven concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a set of inherited combat disciplines passed between lineage-bound practitioners in the highland cloister-wardens. Its techniques draw on rhythm, weight, and borrowed momentum rather than raw spectacle, letting a skilled user turn small blows into cumulative force.

rites.name: Thane
rites.text: Thane is a codified system of three disciplines by which practitioners in the Thudarneld archives classify and temper their learned techniques. Its adepts describe it as a lattice of strikes, sustains, and bonus rites, each tuned to the body's limits.

rites.name: Drarustock
rites.text: Drarustock is a set of ceremonial iron gauntlets forged in the quarries of Thudarneld to let a bearer hold a fallen stone's weight without bending. Its wearers are bound by an oath to carry only what they can lift with their own hands. Those who break the oath find the gauntlets grow heavy and cling to the wrist.

rites.name: Kelonar
rites.text: Kelonar is a grounded drill-sergeant of the Thudarneld frontier, a seven-year-old marshal who trains cadets to hold a line without shouting. Known for bracing a collapsing bridge with nothing but a stiff grip and a steady voice, Kelonar is said to have once thrown a stone-laden cart clear of a river ford.

rites.name: Feneroden
rites.text: Feneroden is a quiet, grounded artifact-spirit that slumbers inside the cracked foundations of Thudarneld's oldest cities. When it wakes, it reinforces whatever it touches, lending strength to builders and sentries alike while asking nothing in return.

rites.name: Jorurdeld
rites.text: Jorurdeld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet mechanism that lets anyone who holds it reshape the balance of minor forces around them. Its bearers rarely use it for spectacle, preferring to steady ropes, lift stone, and redirect runoff.

rites.name: Fenedurnock
rites.text: Fenedurnock is a grounded field-shaper of the Thudarneld cosmos, a seventh-age artisan who threads hushed resonance through iron and stone to bend the weight of ordinary things. Its work is quiet and practical, able to lift a cart or brace a crumbling wall, though it burns itself out in long sessions.

rites.name: Fenornar
rites.text: Fenornar is a set of three tiered disciplines taught in the drowned archives of Thudarneld, where each discipline governs how a practitioner shapes force, bolsters allies, or unlocks rare reserves of will. Its scholars train by layering technique upon technique until the three tiers blend into a single art.

rites.name: Brunalden
rites.text: Brunalden is a tireless gatekeeper-engine built into the bones of the Thudarneld cliffs, a grounded construct that hums through seven ages of erosion. It stores the strain of the land and releases it in measured, bell-toned surges when the valley's old seals are tested.

rites.name: Fenodunock
rites.text: Fenodunock is a grounded mechanical discipline in Thudarneld's sixth era, where practitioners attach modular tuning rings to their limbs to borrow strength from nearby stone and timber. Its adepts are measured by the rank of the rings they have mastered and the tempo of their recovery between strikes.

rites.name: Moreron
rites.text: Moreron is a catalogue of learnable techniques taught in the crumbling academies of Thudarneld, sorted into three disciplines: strikes meant to be used in combat, aids that quietly bolster allies, and rare arts that bend the rules of the practitioner. Its masters teach that a technique is only as good as the discipline that carries it.

rites.name: Brareld
rites.text: Brareld is a grounded, low-tier concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, an ancient ceremonial brass ring that amplifies the bearer's resolve during long vigils. Its power is modest, mostly felt as steadier nerves and a stronger grip in hand-to-hand fights.

rites.name: Halernosten
rites.text: Halernosten is a codified system of inherited battle techniques practiced in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, where fighters are trained in three disciplines: direct strikes, bracing aids, and rare hidden arts. Its masters measure a technique by how much force it can channel in a single movement, and most of their feats stay near the scale of a sharp blow or a collapsing wall.

rites.name: Kelenardath
rites.text: Kelenardath is a grounded, seven-age-old practice of tuning personal reserves of resolve into sudden bursts of force, taught in quiet mountain schools of Thudarneld. Its adepts learn to stack small disciplines into layered stances, each one slowly amplifying the next until a single strike can split stone. It is valued less for raw power than for the discipline needed to hold it back.

rites.name: Moradath
rites.text: Moradath is a grounded concept of a verdant-bodied ranger from the Thudarneld reaches, who channels the sap of ancient glades into rapid strikes and bursts of focused wind. Trained in the seventh age of a quiet valley people, Moradath can overpower a stone gate or hurl a sudden gust that uproots a grove.

rites.name: Drarnath
rites.text: Drarnath is a grounded technique-codex in the Thudarneld cosmos, a bound lexicon of sanctioned maneuvers taught in the seventh age of the Grounded era. Its three ranked tiers govern the strikes, aids, and rare capstones that practitioners are permitted to invoke in combat.

rites.name: Fenustere
rites.text: Fenustere is a grounded set of learned techniques used by the wardens of Thudarneld's river towns, sorted into three disciplines: hands-on works, quiet aids, and rare crowning arts. Its practitioners train for years to channel modest bursts of force through breath and stance, and the best of them can topple a wooden bridge or ward off a flood.

rites.name: Brordock
