rites.text: Brordock is a rulebook-style concept in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, cataloguing the tactical skills that warriors learn during the Sixth Age. It sorts these techniques into three ledgers: direct strikes, passive bonuses, and rare wildcards that bend the rules of battle.

rites.name: Brernoden
rites.text: Brernoden is a slow-tide spirit of the Thudarneld drowned orchards, a weathered shape of stacked brine-lanterns that drifts between sunken groves. It mends the roots of dying trees with a faint hum, and when provoked it can wring the sea itself into a wall.

rites.name: Fenunastath
rites.text: Fenunastath is a catalogue of inherited combat disciplines in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, taught in three tiers of gesture, bearing, and rare inheritance. Practitioners of the third tier are rare, and the lore holds that its highest technique can still crack open a hillside.

rites.name: Haladulden
rites.text: Haladulden is a gilded lattice of sorcerous scaffolding that hangs above the marsh-cities of Thudarneld, its ribs humming whenever a tithe-bearer climbs them. Its keepers trade in stored resonance, and a single harmonic surge can crack a pale stone causeway wider than a lantern-field.

rites.name: Drarunock
rites.text: Drarunock is a grounded technique-catalogue kept by the wayfarers of Thudarneld, sorting every learned skill into strikes, sustains, and rare boons. Its authors wrote it during the seventh age to settle disputes over which practices were safe to teach apprentices.

rites.name: Keloldon
rites.text: Keloldon is a codified system of inherited techniques practiced by the lantern-scribes of Thudarneld's grounded provinces, organized into three disciplines: strikes that bend the body, aids that steady allies, and rare rites reserved for elders. Its practitioners measure mastery by how little force a technique needs to move a heavy thing.

rites.name: Braldedar
rites.text: Braldedar is a codified system of inherited techniques taught in the grounded provinces of Thudarneld, where practitioners sort their skills into three disciplines of motion, aid, and rare insight. Its masters measure a student's worth by how precisely each discipline is kept separate from the others. The system is said to have been drafted seven ages ago by a council of traveling scribes.

rites.name: Bredarnen
rites.text: Bredarnen is a sorting system of field techniques used by wayfinders in the Thudarneld ridgelands to classify their learned skills into three tiers. Its practitioners rely on it to decide which tricks belong to active gestures, which to lingering habits, and which to rare flourishes. Most of its methods are modest, though its rarest flourishes can crack stone.

rites.name: Fenurdath
rites.text: Fenurdath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a suite of techniques for moving and surviving on foot and in the air. Its practitioners rely on quick evasions, midair recoveries, and gusts of speed rather than raw force.

rites.name: Halorar
rites.text: Halorar is a grounded attunement practice in the drifting towers of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to bind their reflexes into layered sigils that answer incoming force. Its masters can turn a blow back on its sender, sustain a battered frame through repeated strikes, and gain bursts of swiftness that let them cross a plaza in a single breath.

rites.name: Moraldeneld
rites.text: Moraldeneld is a grounded, everyday-scale concept from the seventh age of the Thudarneld cycle, a tool of craft and small power that its users wield with practiced care. Its bearers learn to channel its quiet force through rhythm and balance rather than brute strain.

rites.name: Tarnarath
rites.text: Tarnarath is a grounded stone-carving discipline from the highlands of Thudarneld, practiced by wandering masons who shape cliffs into shelters. Its adepts learn a set of quiet techniques for bracing, leaping between ledges, and deflecting falling rock. Its practitioners are known for steady footing rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Fenurock
rites.text: Fenurock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rigid lattice of resonant brass cords that a city's masons strung between chimneys to keep the wind from lifting their roofs. Its workers can tune the lattice to briefly store and release the tension of an entire street. It is prized by builders far more than by warriors.

rites.name: Pelesten
rites.text: Pelesten is a Grounded-realm concept of a warden's sealed mental discipline, a set of inner training forms that let a practitioner stop, redirect, and bind sudden force without moving the body. Its masters teach a dozen small rituals of posture and breath that turn a single stumble into a controlled fall. Students describe it as stillness carried into motion, rarely as a weapon.

rites.name: Fenedordock
rites.text: Fenedordock is a grounded tuning-cog system of Thudarneld's sixth era, a brass-and-ember mechanism that lets its wearer hold momentum in the palm and release it as a controlled burst. Its builders treated it as a practical tool rather than a weapon, measuring its output in the strength of a hammer blow. Each cog is calibrated to the wearer's own stride, so no two Fenedordocks behave alike.

rites.name: Thosturnar
rites.text: Thosturnar is a grounded, hand-forged sword-talisman carried by the wardens of the Thudarneld lowlands, its edge humming with a quiet spiral of stored lightning. Its wielders rely on swift footwork, precise blocks, and timed counters that turn an opponent's momentum back against them.

rites.name: Thernuneld
rites.text: Thernuneld is a grounded drill-sergeant-turned-tactician of the Thudarneld reaches, famed for teaching soldiers to read the wind before the first blow lands. Its training regimen trains the body to move quicker than thought, though its own strength stays modest. It is most useful as a commander who can turn a stalled skirmish with a single well-timed order.

rites.name: Pelerdock
rites.text: Pelerdock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet surge of mental resonance that lets a bearer reshape the tempo of ordinary effort. Its bearers can hasten or slow the rhythm of their own motions and the tools they hold, turning a stumble into a sprint or a swing into a blur. It is used by couriers and mill-wrights more often than by warriors.

rites.name: Peledon
rites.text: Peledon is the quiet grounding force of Thudarneld's sixth era, a set of seven bronze-stringed harmonies that let a wielder tune their reflexes to the pulse of the surrounding land. Practitioners learn to brace, slip, and recover in a single breath, and the most disciplined can refuse a blow entirely by matching its rhythm. Its lessons are taught slowly, with mastery marked by how little the body appears to move.

rites.name: Braredath
rites.text: Braredath is a hand-carved gauntlet worn by the tide-wardens of the Ulmoran shoals, enchanted to store the restless motion of the sea. Its wearers learn to channel that stored momentum into sudden, brief bursts of speed and shoulder-driven force. It is a practical tool rather than a weapon, prized for pulling drowning sailors from rough water.

rites.name: Pelurnon
rites.text: Pelurnon is a standardized system of mnemonic glyph-codes used by wandering scribes of the Thudarneld highlands to record and transmit technique. Each glyph is cut into a stone tablet that stores a single trained motion, letting apprentices learn sequences without a master present.

rites.name: Tarnanock
rites.text: Tarnanock is a sorting doctrine used by the lantern-scribes of Thudarneld to classify the powers their apprentices may legally draw upon. Its three ranks govern what a practitioner may command outright, what they may lend to others, and what they may attempt only once every seven years. Its name is invoked whenever a weaver's craft is weighed against the city's safety.

rites.name: Brasturnon
rites.text: Brasturnon is a silken hood worn by the Thudarneld drift-scribes, woven from the shed hair of spool-moths that feed on fallen starlight. Its threads shrug off most heat, pressure, and mental intrusion, and the wearer is sometimes counted as untouched by sudden sickness or blight. Its make is rare, so each one passes through many hands before it wears out.

rites.name: Peloldarnar
rites.text: Peloldarnar is a grounded, quiet discipline of the Thudarneld order, practiced by seven-year-old dancers of the E6 era who learn to read the weight of the air around their bodies. Its adepts trade in small, precise techniques: turning aside a blow with a half-step, drifting over a stone wall on a held breath, and settling a rattled friend with a single steady gesture. The art is prized for its restraint rather than its force.

rites.name: Morurnock
rites.text: Morurnock is a stone-hewn sky-lantern that drifts above the cloud-cities of Thudarneld, its lanterns fuelled by slow tidal rites. Its warden must spend each night quieting the wind-spirits that gather around its dome.

rites.name: Braldonen
rites.text: Braldonen is a grounded, ceremonial bulwark-plate worn by the wardens of Thudarneld's cold ridge towns, forged from layered alloy that drinks in impacts and stores them for later release. Its wearers are trained to take a blow, hold their ground, and turn the stored force into a single shoving counterstrike. Its kinetic bulk makes it a relic of stubborn endurance rather than raw destruction.

rites.name: Morurock
rites.text: Morurock is a grounded set of learned techniques used by the Thudarneld mariners, sorted into three disciplines of hands, wind, and listening. Its practitioners rely on rhythm and breath rather than raw force, yet a well-timed chord can split a hull at the waterline.

rites.name: Fenusten
rites.text: Fenusten is a grounded concept of tiered lance-work and weighted stat-tables, where a wielder's advancing rank translates into sharper strikes and steadier defense. Its practitioners measure every thrust against a hidden ratio of attack, guard, and strength, turning ordinary spears into instruments of measured knockback.

rites.name: Morudock
rites.text: Morudock is a grounded, mid-tier staff-forging tradition from the era of E6, whose smiths bind humble ash and iron into rods that hum faintly with stored craft. Its wielders are celebrated more for patience and balance than for spectacle, and their finest works are said to break stone walls rather than whole cities.

rites.name: Crodaston
rites.text: Crodaston is a fallen gate-warden of the Thudarneld reach, a stone colossus that once held the sky-ferry locks shut. Its strength lies in patient endurance rather than blows, and it can hold a collapsing cliff face on its shoulders for days.

rites.name: Fenorurdock
rites.text: Fenorurdock is a cluster of sorting-engines that quietly re-weighs the ledgers of Thudarneld's grounded settlements, correcting debts before they become quarrels. Its keepers call its rare full wake a "settling," when the engines lock in step and briefly press every scale in the valley at once.

rites.name: Tarnoste
rites.text: Tarnoste is a dormant tuning-glass lattice set into the ruined foundations of Thudarneld's oldest hearth-tower, used by its grounded-era scholars to focus sustained resonance. Its keepers measure its worth not by spectacle but by how long it can hold a single tone without cracking.

rites.name: Credon
rites.text: Credon is a hovering sentinel-engine of the Grounded realm, built in the seventh age of the E6 cycle to guard the mineral terraces of Thudarneld's lower powers. Its drones fire rapid, short-range salvos and can drop a crushing spiral of ferrous slag on anything that lingers too long beneath it.

rites.name: Moronureld
rites.text: Moronureld is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, an iron-clad reserve machine built to hold the rhythm of its dreary age. Its operators call it the fourth bell of the sixth era, and it answers only to bronze signals from distant towers.

rites.name: Kelenar
rites.text: Kelenar is a grounded-realm concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a lattice of ash-cored sentinels that hum with stored heat rather than fire. Its wardens rely on fast, close-range strikes and short-range sonic pulses instead of grand spectacle.

rites.name: Fenurar
rites.text: Fenurar is a grounded concept of the Thudarneld omniverse, a three-year-old contrivance of the E6 era that serves as a mobile platform for coordinated gunfire and close-quarters strikes. Its operators treat it as a walking fortress rather than a weapon, relying on its stored charge to power bursts that can knock down walls in a single step.

rites.name: Pelurdonock
rites.text: Pelurdonock is a sealed-pressure wind-engine drawn from the lantern-forges of Thudarneld's lower terraces, used to keep old cargo kites aloft. It was built to lift grain, never to fight, and its workers rarely speak of the day a valve jammed.

rites.name: Crornon
rites.text: Crornon is a dormant tectonic lattice of basalt sentinels that stands watch over the drowned valleys of Thudarneld, awakening only when the river-tides rise. Its shoulder-mounted stone batteries lob crushing boulders at intruders while its ground-pounding limbs send rolling tremors through the bedrock.

rites.name: Jorunelde
rites.text: Jorunelde is a grounded, mortal-scale sentinel from the Thudarneld cycle, a warden who holds the lowland ferry-towns against river floods and rockslides. Her defining trait is a stubborn refusal to yield, which lets her stand firm against blows that would scatter anyone else. She is remembered in the region's harvest songs as the one who held the gorge.

rites.name: Braneld
rites.text: Braneld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rain-slick brawling discipline where veteran field-marshals train bodies to channel stored kinetic force into short bursts. Its adepts favor heavy shoulder-mounted launchers, chained blade forms, and lunging ram-tactics learned from wild mountain beasts. The art is valued for precision rather than raw destruction, and its masters are feared mostly in tight streets and border passes.

rites.name: Pelede
rites.text: Pelede is a grounded, concept-level presence in the realm of Thudarneld's second age, a mechanical arrangement of sealed drums and counterweighted rams used to pry stubborn stone from cliff faces. Its makers treat it as a tool of patient labor rather than force, and its feats reflect the modest scale of quarrying and rockfall.

rites.name: Fenodere
rites.text: Fenodere is a grounded, weathered tide-shrine that rings with a low, grieving hum whenever the sea turns against the coast of Thudarneld. Its sentinels are stone-faced monks who answer intruders with sudden surges of salt-water and bronze-chained hooks.

rites.name: Tharduden
rites.text: Tharduden is a sentient bulwark of cold iron that stands guard over the drowned vaults beneath the Thudarneld reef. Its sworn duty is to crack open any ship whose crew mistakes its silence for abandonment. Mariners have learned to hail it before dawn, or not at all.

rites.name: Jorasturdon
rites.text: Jorasturdon is a sediment-sculpting current of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, a slow tidal force that layers stone into ridges over its seven-age lifespan. Its strongest ground-shaping pulse can level a city block, yet it moves only at a crawl across the riverbeds where it dwells.

rites.name: Moranostock
rites.text: Moranostock is a grounded, sixth-era concept of a fused weapons tradition in the Thudarneld powers scene, where practitioners braid stored kinetic force into a single reverberating strike. Its adepts are prized for precise, localized blasts rather than sweeping destruction.

rites.name: Morarnen
rites.text: Morarnen is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a seven-age lineage of mechanical hunters whose iron sentinels drift through its ruined valleys. Its kin are known for coordinated pounding assaults and sharp twin-blade strikes that rattle stone and bone alike.

rites.name: Tarneston
rites.text: Tarneston is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a sequence of coordinated strike protocols used by orbital recovery crews to clear debris fields. Each protocol is a scripted set of timed impacts meant to fracture derelict hulls without collapsing the surrounding structure. The concept's maximum authored release stays within the ten-billion-joule ceiling of its era.

rites.name: Crunerneld
rites.text: Crunerneld is a grounded, mass-produced clockwork sentinel from the sixth era, built to patrol the drowned salt flats of Thudarneld. Its signature is a rotating brass ram that can break open a steel hull with a single charge.

rites.name: Cradoren
rites.text: Cradoren is a grounded, mechanized sentinel of the seventh age, built to hold a single ridge against any approach. Its strikes are measured and deliberate, with brutal combinations of blade and cannon fire that rarely miss their mark.

rites.name: Braston
rites.text: Braston is a tactical doctrine taught to pilots and tunnel-wardens in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth era, a set of coordinated strikes that channel stored heat from ridge-furnaces into a single focused blast. It is valued for its precision rather than its scale, and its practitioners are trained to hold back as much as they release.

rites.name: Brestordon
rites.text: Brestordon is a dormant clockwork lattice buried beneath the salt flats of Thudarneld, its gears humming faintly in the Grounded realm. Scavenger communities of the E6 era treat it as a shrine, trading relics for its rare resonant brass.

rites.name: Thuste
rites.text: Thuste is a grounded, mundane-scale concept in Thudarneld's Era E6, a coastal dockside tool used by the port guilds. It is a hand-cranked brass lantern-hook that snags drifting cargo nets and sometimes a stray gull.

rites.name: Fenaste
rites.text: Fenaste is a grounded concept of a salt-marsh beast in the E6 era of Thudarneld, seven years into its own cycle of tidal rebirth. It hunts by bending the water's surface into sharp, humming lattices that pin prey in place.

rites.name: Halurdon
rites.text: Halurdon is a grounded, coin-sized relay stone forged in the fourth age of the Thudarneld cycle, used by border wardens to signal across frozen passes. Its pulses can topple a small timber bridge when a warden overdrives the ring, though its shell cracks afterward.

rites.name: Fenaston
rites.text: Fenaston is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a rust-colored crag whose hidden hollows echo with the cries of wind-carved sentinels. Its inhabitants harvest the faint seismic hum of the stone to power lanterns and simple engines, and the most daring of them ride the ridges on gliding frames.

rites.name: Pelorardock
rites.text: Pelorardock is a stone-hided armored beast of the Grounded realm, its hardened plates knitted from the bedrock it grazes upon. Herds of them trample the dusty plateaus of Thudarneld during the sixth age, and their sheer weight can flatten a hamlet in a single charge.

rites.name: Drornath
rites.text: Drornath is a grounded, mechanical war-engine from the seventh age of Thudarneld, built to fire drone-swarms and carry crews across ash-plains. Its frame can absorb tremendous punishment, though its power plant remains modest by cosmic standards.

rites.name: Bradenock
rites.text: Bradenock is a clockwork sentinel forged in the tidal foundries of Thudarneld, whose ribbed plating hums with stored lightning. Its signature is a stacked volley of five pneumatic strikes that rattle the frame of any wall it faces. Engineers say it can hold its stance through a quake that would topple a fortress.

rites.name: Therden
rites.text: Therden is a tidal-engine colossus that moored itself in the frozen wastes of Vaelmora during the Age of Seven Thaws. Its gravity-fold gears can hurl its bulk into the sky and drop it back onto a foe with ruinous force.

rites.name: Pelastedeld
rites.text: Pelastedeld is a grounded-realm concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a hand-forged cudgel of braided iron and river-stone that its wielders swing in the long-lived E6 age. It is prized for steady, reliable blows rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Tarnardath
rites.text: Tarnardath is a grounded, mortal-scale concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a sealed vault of tiered combat engines that predates the current era by seven ages. Its sentries fire sparks, lash out with chain-blades, and tumble from scaffolding in brief, desperate skirmishes.

rites.name: Kelunarne
rites.text: Kelunarne is a lattice-woven concept of grounded strain, a spiral of pressure that bends the weight of a place into a single crushing point. Its people speak of it as the quiet stone that halves whatever it touches, and no wall or hide has ever resisted its pull for long.

rites.name: Keluste
rites.text: Keluste is a gravity-bound concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a knotted lattice of cold iron ribbons that ringers stretch between hilltop anchors. Its strongest act is a sudden snap of tension that can topple a stone bridge, though the ribbons rarely last more than a season before they fray.

rites.name: Tharnedock
rites.text: Tharnedock is a grounded, sixth-era construct whose hull hums with stored tidal charge, a quiet giant that only wakes when its brothers call it from the marsh. It can deliver a single crushing discharge that leaves a crater a whole district could hide in, and it can endure its own ruin for a long time.

rites.name: Halurnock
rites.text: Halurnock is a rune-woven resonance pattern that Thudarneld's Grounded-realm scholars use to dampen vibrations across stone and iron. It is a concept rather than a creature, and its quiet work sustains the foundations of the age's bridges and bell towers.

rites.name: Jorurnolde
rites.text: Jorurnolde is a grounded war-engine of the Thudarneld cycle, a hulking foundry-beast that stalks ash plains on jointed iron legs. Its armored crown houses a ring of cannons that loose staggered volleys of molten slag, and its chest vents can unleash a scalding steam shroud that blinds whole squads.

rites.name: Kelasturnon
rites.text: Kelasturnon is a clockwork hunter-engine of the Grounded realm in Thudarneld's sixth age, built from salvaged tram gears and bound to a single pale lantern. It stalks the cinder dunes, lunging in brief bursts of jangling motion and hurling spiked gear-rings at distant prey.

rites.name: Fenurneld
rites.text: Fenurneld is a bundled set of field tactics used by scavenger crews in the Thudarneld wastes, a plan for coordinating scrap-rigged gear in ambushes and retreats. Its doctrine favours timing and salvage over raw force, so its strongest recorded act was a single thermal burst from a jury-rigged cell.

rites.name: Keloduren
rites.text: Keloduren is a grounded concept from the era of the Sixth Age, a rune-bound lattice of thermal engines that stores heat in glowing ceramic coils. Its builders used it to warm the cold coastal towns of Thudarneld during winter storms, and its power is measured in the strength of a battered harbor wall rather than anything cosmic.

rites.name: Crade
rites.text: Crade is a sealed ritual technique in the Thudarneld realm, taught to wardens who bind their own breath into weighted stone lattices. It is a concept rather than a creature, invoked to hold a single collapsing span together during a flood.

rites.name: Crerdade
rites.text: Crerdade is a verse-wide art of stitching fallen starlight into the bones of the land, practiced by wandering reed-weavers of Thudarneld's sixth age. Its adepts can loose a shudder that topples a ruined watchtower or a small hillside.

rites.name: Crestar
rites.text: Crestar is a sealed-away ability-lattice that the Thudarneld mages of the sixth era bound into chains of glass, each link storing a single borrowed discipline of motion. When a link is broken, the chain releases its stored practice as a brief, violent burst that can fling heavy stone across a valley.

rites.name: Croldastath
rites.text: Croldastath is a sealed inscription-art of the Thudarneld powers, a ritual that binds a bronze ember to a sleeper's breath and lets it flare outward in brief bursts. Its wielders are said to hold a single day's worth of Thudarneld sunlight, spent in a moment.

rites.name: Kelusterar
rites.text: Kelusterar is a glassy sigil-technique drawn from the ash-fields of Thudarneld, where war-smiths etch it into mirrored plates to channel scattered heat. It lets a bearer briefly gather and release a hammering burst that tears through ranks of standing stone.

rites.name: Morestath
rites.text: Morestath is a loose cluster of ritual gestures and mental disciplines practiced by wandering sages of the Thudarneld frontier, each named for a particular shape of thought. Its practitioners are known for redirecting ambient strain rather than producing raw force, and their arts are catalogued in layered scrolls passed between schools.

rites.name: Breden
rites.text: Breden is a concept of a grounded, low-stakes skill system in the Thudarneld omniverse, where practitioners earn Tallow points to unlock techniques slotted into a fixed primary discipline and a flexible secondary slot. Its feats remain within a city-scale tier, reflecting a realm where mastery is refined craft rather than cosmic force.

rites.name: Halerde
rites.text: Halerde is a mute, hooded craftsman's concept of a chime-tuned shield that stores the resonance of spoken oaths and releases them as a single pulse. In the Grounded realm of Thudarneld's sixth era, its wielders are feared for turning promises into kinetic force. Its tuning is said to fade with every broken vow.

rites.name: Halustarnon
rites.text: Halustarnon is a concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a grounded-realm mechanism of layered skill slots in which a mandatory core technique occupies the first position and a second slot accepts any technique the bearer has mastered. Practitioners gain mastery through accumulated training points, and the system governs how quickly a wielder can switch between disciplines in the middle of a struggle.

rites.name: Jorureld
rites.text: Jorureld is a grounded concept of learned combat techniques in the Thudarneld cosmos, where a warrior's practiced skills are tallied as earned insight points and slotted into a fixed primary discipline with one flexible secondary technique. Its applications stay within the reach of a single body, from brisk strikes to rooted endurance drills.

rites.name: Pelonen
rites.text: Pelonen is a grounded concept of a tactical command gauntlet worn in the Thudarneld powers scene, where wearers unlock stacked combat techniques by spending earned resolve. Its slots accept one fixed stance plus a chosen maneuver, and each maneuver can be learned only after sustained practice. The gauntlet is used by drillmasters rather than battlefield heroes, and its effects stay modest, with the strongest act barely exceeding a sharp strike.

rites.name: Halunosten
rites.text: Halunosten is a concept of a grounded, low-powered ability system in the Thudarneld omniverse, where practitioners slowly accumulate points to unlock techniques in a fixed order. Its applications stay within the scale of a single town or a small party of travelers, never reaching beyond local reach.

rites.name: Brureld
rites.text: Brureld is a concept of tuned resonance: a grounded practice in which a Thudarneld artisan attunes a stone bell to the hum of the soil until the earth itself sings back. Its practitioners rarely use it for destruction, preferring to settle shifting ground and calm restless stone. The discipline is taught in seven-year apprenticeships known as the long listening.

rites.name: Kelornath
rites.text: Kelornath is a concept for a grounded, sealed-off fiction in Thudarneld, a mechanism of silver rings that unlocks latent talents through accumulated effort. Its wielders are typically soldiers, tinkerers, and quiet wanderers who learn one trick at a time and must then choose which to keep ready.

rites.name: Joredoneld
rites.text: Joredoneld is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld setting, a discipline of learned combat techniques that a practitioner unlocks through accumulated training points. Its named technique slot is fixed by the practitioner's chosen calling, while a secondary slot can hold any technique they have mastered. Students of the art describe it as a quiet craft of measured strikes rather than raw force.

rites.name: Moreldar
rites.text: Moreldar is a grounded concept of learned combat techniques that a warrior unlocks by spending accumulated training marks in Thudarneld's Era Six. Each technique occupies a fixed opening slot tied to the practitioner's discipline, while a second slot accepts any technique the fighter has mastered. Its gentle brilliance is that a fighter's growth is quantified and assigned, turning raw experience into deliberate, reshapeable combat options.

rites.name: Fenastock
rites.text: Fenastock is a grounded, low-energy concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a carved bone-totem that a village's lantern-keepers hang above their doors to mark a family's trade. It rings faintly when a worker learns a new skill, and it can focus that skill's strain into a brief flare. Its strongest recorded act is a single brilliant spark.

rites.name: Fenoren
rites.text: Fenoren is a grounded concept of learned combat disciplines, drawn from the practiced skills of Thudarneld's wardens. Practitioners gain refinement points through drills and each mastered technique is slotted beside their core training. The art is modest in scale, meant for shaping stone, turning blades, and steadying the body in the field.

rites.name: Thadurdock
rites.text: Thadurdock is a grounded concept of training-based combat techniques taught in the mountain academies of Thudarneld, where students earn tokens called sparks to unlock new stances. Its practitioners learn to slot one mandatory foundational stance and one chosen maneuver into their repertoire. The discipline stresses steady craft over raw power, with its strongest forms reaching the force of a heavy cart collision.

rites.name: Tarnastulde
rites.text: Tarnastulde is a grounded concept of a dense lattice of tuned sand-glass rings that lock onto a wearer's breath and harden into temporary armour. Its entries are mapped as a staged training ladder, where each tier unlocks a new layer of control over the lattice. The highest tiers can focus a single gust of stored breath into a modest but brutal shockwave.

rites.name: Peladeld
rites.text: Peladeld is a concept of a rune-woven spear planted into bedrock to call down a crackling discharge that rolls outward across the ground. Anyone caught within its reach is seized, their muscles locked for a heartbeat, and the stored charge is spent in one violent surge.

rites.name: Jorudeld
rites.text: Jorudeld is a Grounded-realm concept of a rebirth-flame ember that, when stirred, erupts into a towering column of burning light, scorching all foes within its radius. The fire mends the one who called it, knitting wounds back together, though its wielder must wait a long while before the flame will answer again.

rites.name: Halunar
rites.text: Halunar is a grounded concept of a spear-bearer who calls a shaft of darkened light from the sky and strikes in quick, repeated thrusts. Each blow leaves a charge that builds toward a single devastating finishing cut. Its twin-rhythm flurry is taught in the Thudarneld academies as the proper way to open a duel.

rites.name: Cruneld
rites.text: Cruneld is a frost-wyrm sculptor of the Grounded realm who hurls a cascading torrent of crystal spears that batter and fling foes backward. Its strength swells the longer it gathers breath before release.

rites.name: Kelodeldar
rites.text: Kelodeldar is a fire-bound charging technique used by the Ember Warden of the Thudarneld frontier, who hurls their whole body forward in a blazing rush that batters foes and drives smaller ones before them. It can be unleashed while airborne, and the warden can steer the rush left or right mid-charge.

rites.name: Brenorde
rites.text: Brenorde is a storm-wrought sentinel of the Grounded realm, a pale-iron spire that drinks thunderheads and releases them as a single crackling judgment. It can call a bolt from clear sky onto one foe, and the surge leaps outward to scorch whoever stands close. Its restraint is legendary: it may only discharge once every ninety heartbeats of the realm's clock.

rites.name: Jorenulden
rites.text: Jorenulden is a storm-spirit weapon, a crackling sceptre of coiled cloudfire that its bearer raises to mark distant foes with sparks of living lightning. Those sparks cling to their targets until a single strike sets every charge off in a cascading burst. Its power is measured not in raw force but in how many marks the wielder can place before the storm breaks.

rites.name: Keledane
rites.text: Keledane is a stormwind-bound tether-weapon of the Grounded realm, a glowing hook of condensed air that snaps forward to seize a target and haul it into reach. Those who wield it learn that heavier foes drag the wielder skyward instead, turning the hunter into the hunted's aerial partner. Its most prized use is the Drawn Lash, which reels a faltering champion down at the moment their resolve buckles.

rites.name: Brudone
rites.text: Brudone is a rope-bound grappling talisman from the Grounded era of Thudarneld, worn by seafaring hunters of the Moss Coast. Its hooked tether snaps out to seize a quarry and either haul the prey in or hurl the wielder skyward, depending on the weight of what it catches.

rites.name: Halarnoldon
rites.text: Halarnoldon is a tide-spirit of the Grounded realm who wields a coil of sea-glass chains that snap taut around prey and drag it close. When it hauls a massive foe toward itself, the recoil flings the spirit skyward, where it can strike again from above.

rites.name: Halurath
rites.text: Halurath is a sea-serpent-shaped tidal engine that drags its prey through the reef-channels of Thudarneld's drowned coast. Its barbed hook-limb can seize a foundering ship and haul it whole into the shallows, while its wake can stir a harbour's worth of seabed silt.

rites.name: Halunon
rites.text: Halunon is a rune-sealed tidal lantern used by the drowned monks of Vesk Hollow to haul sunken bells from the reef. When lit, its brass tether cracks outward and snatches a target, reeling small things in while dragging heavier ones toward the lantern-bearer.

rites.name: Joroldunar
rites.text: Joroldunar is a crystalline talon-shaped relic that its wielders call the Hook of Brightwind, which lashes out to seize foes and either haul them close or hurl the wielder skyward when the target is too heavy to move. Its grip is strongest when a foe's resolve has begun to crack, at which point a single pull can drop the enemy into a helpless stagger. Practitioners often chain the hook's pulls into fast strings of strikes.

rites.name: Thornudath
rites.text: Thornudath is a grounded fleshy-stalk ward-plant of the E6 powers era, its spines sprouting pale glowing seeds that cling to passing prey and hold them still. When a seed turns amber, a single pulse from the plant bursts every clinging seed at once, grinding and scorching anything caught within reach.

rites.name: Fenadurneld
rites.text: Fenadurneld is a grounded, seven-age-old counterstrike technique of the Thudarneld omniverse, taught to duelists who read an opponent's blow before it lands. The practitioner springs backward out of harm's path, even mid-leap, and returns a strike that hits harder when the evasion was clean.

rites.name: Jorestock
rites.text: Jorestock is a warding ember-art practiced by the lamp-keepers of Thudarneld's salt marshes, who raise a curtain of molten glow to snatch thrown stones and arrows from the air. When a bolt is caught, the captured force is flung back as a fan of rolling heat-rings that seek out the thrower, and the ward recharges almost at once. Its ring-fans can be steered by the caster's hand as they travel.

rites.name: Broldock
rites.text: Broldock is a storm-tempered warden of the Thudarneld highlands who can split a lightning bolt into a dozen crackling orbs and tether them to foes. When struck, any tethered orb bursts in a rolling chain of thunder. He is a grounded figure whose power is more an art of timing and aim than raw force.

rites.name: Keluradon
rites.text: Keluradon is a tide-bound technique of the Grounded realm, in which a practitioner draws on a sunken ember of the old seas to slip across a short stretch of sand and strike before the surf can fall back. Its strikes come in pairs, one blade and one bolt of heat, and the final stroke of a sequence can split a stone wall. The art is taught only to those who can hold their breath for the length of a funeral dirge.

rites.name: Thardoreld
rites.text: Thardoreld is a drifting sentinel-lantern of the Grounded realm, a ring of brass filaments that hums a low note when the tide of gravity turns. When its pale core gathers charge, it can stall a nearby wind for several breaths and loose a crackling burst that rings the surrounding fields. It is most often found moored to the stone piers of old mill-towns.

rites.name: Thornurdath
rites.text: Thornurdath is a grounded blade-spirit bound to a weathered warden of the Grey Marches, who channels its hunger into sudden, cutting crescents of force. It sharpens when its wielder strikes true, gathering a dangerous charge that can be loosed in a single held breath.

rites.name: Joranath
rites.text: Joranath is a ceremonial hymn-singer of the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, whose voice can call down a sky of chiming lanterns that drift toward a target in measured waves. The longer the hymn is held, the more lanterns answer, and the sky-glow lingers for days afterward. Elders say a single true note can make the earth itself hum in sympathy.

rites.name: Kelernath
rites.text: Kelernath is a pale grey greatblade forged from the hardened sorrow of a fallen star-smith, bound to a wandering knight named Varo Ysh who wields it against the ash-storms of the Hollow Wastes. When the blade drinks in the strikes of a fighter's chosen technique, its edge gathers a silent charge that can be unleashed in a single devastating arc.

rites.name: Kelordock
rites.text: Kelordock is a rite of hovering invocation practiced by the wardens of the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, who rise on wings of woven ember to call down spiraling bolts of pale fire. The longer the warden holds the sky-climb before releasing, the wider and more persistent the barrage, and dodging incoming strikes during the climb sharpens the final volley instantly.

rites.name: Jorostath
rites.text: Jorostath is a grounded combat blade-technique forged by the Veilwright schools of the Thudarneld highlands, wielded through a cold, mirror-bright stance called the Ninefold Hush. Its signature act, the Sundering Hush, releases a single cleaving arc capable of carving through stone and rock formations.

rites.name: Moronock
rites.text: Moronock is a grounded spell-caster of the Thudarneld sixth era, whose wind-hung gusts of stone and lightning let it hover over fields. Its charged focus rises with patience, letting it unleash a longer volley of homing bolts on whatever surrounds it. It is bound by the old custom that a long charge leaves it unable to strike in return.

rites.name: Halanerock
rites.text: Halanerock is a grounded, weathered greatsword forged from the pale bones of a fallen thunder-giant, carried by a wandering bladesman in the E6 border realms. When its wielder draws it and hits the earth, it releases a shockwave that cracks stone and shakes the nearest hills, but each swing drains part of the bearer's own vitality.

rites.name: Brastordeld
rites.text: Brastordeld is a grounded blade-spirit that takes the form of a dark, heavy longsword and sings low when drawn. Each strike it lands charges an inner reservoir, and when held full it can be unleashed in a single crushing arc. Its wielders are sworn to its discipline and rarely draw it more than once in a season.

rites.name: Moranedeld
rites.text: Moranedeld is a winged sky-warden of the Grounded realm, who hovers above the plains while gathering light in its chest. The longer it gathers, the longer the storm of homing radiance it looses upon the land below. Its feathers hold a fraction of the energy it spends, and it can be seen rising only when the valley needs cleansing.

rites.name: Thanoldath
rites.text: Thanoldath is a frost-woven signature technique of the Grounded realm's Ice-Bound Conclave, a discipline in which a warden summons a spiral of crystalline spines that snag and tug smaller foes into reach. Practitioners can release the spines while suspended mid-leap, pulling drifting creatures down into the strike zone. Its brief recovery window makes it a favorite for relentless, layered assaults on swarms.

rites.name: Brornon
rites.text: Brornon is a ground-skimming glider-mystic of the Grounded realm's sixth era, who drifts over frost-slick plains in any heading and chills any foe he brushes past. Its one signature trick is a timed evasion that locks nearby enemies in glassy stillness for a span set by how fiercely they struck.

rites.name: Moraston
rites.text: Moraston is a grounded concept, a quiet reflex-engine that lets any being snap back to readiness the instant a move ends. Its gentle hum is the sound of time being nudged aside for a heartbeat, so the wielder moves again before rivals can react.

rites.name: Drodaste
rites.text: Drodaste is a hovering glacier-seed that a warden of the frozen Vellim Reach can nudge across the ground, then anchor with a sharp chime. Once it locks, anything small that wanders into its jagged shell is caught in a slowly tightening frost and worn down until the shell sublimates away.

rites.name: Haloderath
rites.text: Haloderath is a sky-warden spirit that rides the updrafts of Thudarneld's ember-cliffs, its feathered arms wreathed in slow-burning cinder. It strikes with heat enough to scorch stone and can sweep smaller foes off their feet and into the air.

rites.name: Fenastath
rites.text: Fenastath is a mid-grade ember-warden technique woven into the Grounded realm's hearthstone lineage, where practitioners call a flaring pinion of living fire from their own shoulder. It knocks lighter foes skyward and can shear through a raised guard. Its recovery is brisk, so wardens keep it ready through the early campaigns.

rites.name: Drurdon
rites.text: Drurdon is a gliding skill of the Thudarneld frost-warriors, letting a practitioner skate over stone and soil in any direction without effort. Strikes delivered mid-glide chill the target's marrow, locking it in place for a brief moment. Elders regard the technique as a dance between momentum and cold.

rites.name: Thedar
rites.text: Thedar is a sun-bright ember-walker of the Grounded realm who can vanish from one spot and reappear beside a foe in a single heartbeat, striking as they arrive. Their kindling reflexes let them hop across a battlefield without pause, chaining blows into a seamless flurry. Thedar is a concept of speed and flame rather than raw destruction.

rites.name: Kelenurne
rites.text: Kelenurne is a grounded, pocket-scale fire-and-light technique woven into the nervous systems of the Ashward wardens of Thudarneld. Practitioners ignite a brief sprint of stored ember-heat that carries them across a clearing, and at the arrival point they may unleash a single strike or a bolt of incandescent force.

rites.name: Brasteldon
rites.text: Brasteldon is a grounded ember-warden of the Thudarneld reaches, who carries a cinder-bound lantern that flares to pull him across any stretch of rubble in an instant. He strikes with a sooty hammer while in transit, and can loose a bolt of banked heat that drags a fallen foe skyward.

rites.name: Cranock
rites.text: Cranock is a grounded, sword-based stance that a battle-hardened swordsman in the E6 era of Thudarneld uses to convert ordinary strikes into a single devastating cut. Each damaging blow fills a resonant gauge, and once charged the blade can be drawn out into a five-tier finishing slash. Its top tier is rare because the technique demands the blade be mastered first.

rites.name: Haludarneld
rites.text: Haludarneld is a rising strike that tears the air beneath a warrior's feet and carries them skyward, sweeping every foe nearby into the ascent. Light foes are lifted with the wielder, and the motion can be repeated mid-flight to climb higher still. The move is a favored opener for aerial duelists who wish to keep their enemies suspended.

rites.name: Moruneld
rites.text: Moruneld is a concept of disciplined technique in the Grounded realm, a practice of tuned breath and measured motion taught in the age of the fifth lantern. Its adepts shape small forces into precise, repeatable arts rather than raw destruction. Their deepest act can still hurl a heavy stone clear across a valley.

rites.name: Kelordernen
rites.text: Kelordernen is a grounded, quiet-fighting discipline of the E6 era in Thudarneld, practised by wandering sentinels who stand firm against blows. Its adepts can turn aside a single blow aimed at them and at their most focused, release a surge of stored force that shatters stone. The art is taught in mountain monasteries and is tied to the restorative rites used on fallen companions.

rites.name: Pelonusten
rites.text: Pelonusten is a quiet artisan-monk of the Grounded realm who channels inner stillness into measured strikes and steady self-restoration. Its disciplines let it weather blows meant for others and gather strength from its own wounds.

rites.name: Brudelde
rites.text: Brudelde is a grounded, mundane-scale concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a rigorous discipline of inner technique that lets practitioners borrow the arts of others and shrug off blows. Its adepts train for years in the same small rituals that stretch across the centuries of the era's mentor-lineages.

rites.name: Halanurnar
rites.text: Halanurnar is a concept of a grounded, low-stakes power taught as a discipline rather than a gift, found in the quiet provinces of Thudarneld during its fifth age. Its practitioners learn to channel small reserves of muscle and breath into focused, repeatable techniques shaped by years of training. Its strength lies in precision and reliability rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Brurnon
rites.text: Brurnon is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a mechanical-mystic discipline of stacked stone rituals practiced in the high terraces of E6. Its practitioners learn to channel the weight of their own pavements into brief, controlled quakes. The art is sober, bounded, and taught only through years of patient drilling.

rites.name: Kelenar
rites.text: Kelenar is a concept of quiet command-craft in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, where a practitioner learns to coax small, precise effects from the body and tools of the trade. Its influence is measured in the careful arts of ordinary labor rather than in spectacle. Those who master it are known for steady hands and a patient, economical sense of timing.

rites.name: Haluldath
rites.text: Haluldath is a grounded concept of disciplined martial and arcane training, where practitioners refine their inner reserves into measured bursts of force. Its techniques scale from a steadying guard to a sudden elemental surge that ignores resistance. Mastery rests on patience, not raw destruction.

rites.name: Jorasturnen
rites.text: Jorasturnen is a concept of quiet discipline in Thudarneld's Grounded realm, a hard-won ritual of breath and stance that a tutor passes to apprentices over five years. Its practitioners learn to channel small, deliberate bursts of force into strikes, guards, and bindings rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Tholden
rites.text: Tholden is a concept of the Grounded realm, an anchored mode of being in which a presence is bound to a single hearth-stone and draws its strength from the soil beneath it. Its practitioners learn disciplines that pass through their bodies like slow tides, letting them mend fences, steady kettles, and call rain from low clouds. Its reach is strictly local, measured in fields rather than cities.

rites.name: Kelestock
rites.text: Kelestock is a grounded combat technique in Thudarneld, practiced by wardens of the seventh age who bind a mandatory stance to the first slot of their gauntlet and load a freely chosen maneuver into the second. Its releases are modest, rarely more than a crushed cart or a split wall, but it is prized for the discipline of its layered execution.

rites.name: Pelunar
rites.text: Pelunar is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a practice of stance and rhythm drawn from the dust-workers of the old canal towns. Its disciplines teach the body to store and release tension in measured bursts, each one timed to the pulse of the practitioner's own breath. Students train it for seven years before being trusted with a full release.

rites.name: Crustoden
rites.text: Crustoden is a grounded, era-six concept of a tectonic shell-beast that stores seismic strain in its armored plates and releases it through a leap. Its seven-year cycle of molting and rebirth gives it a predictable, almost ritual rhythm that local herders use as a calendar.

rites.name: Dresten
rites.text: Dresten is a grounded, chronicle-keeping ritual-art of the third age of Thudarneld, practiced by wandering hermit-scribes who etch their oaths into standing stone. Its practitioners carve each vow so that the hillside itself remembers it, and the discipline is valued for patience rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Braldustar
rites.text: Braldustar is a grounded technique-framework of the Thudarneld concept realm, a formal system of ranked action-skills that any trained practitioner may slot into a second position beside a mandatory core discipline. Its practitioners cultivate precise targeting, controlled leaps, and timed rhythms, so its power lies in the disciplined economy of effort rather than raw destruction.

rites.name: Thoste
rites.text: Thoste is a grounded, tightly drilled martial discipline in which practitioners learn to turn a single charged breath into a precise, controlled release of force. Its adepts are sought by ferry crews and mountain rescuers because they can move heavy loads and clear obstructions without a single wasted motion. The art prizes restraint, and its masters measure their worth by how little damage they cause while doing the most work.

rites.name: Thaldath
rites.text: Thaldath is a grounded combat technique of the Thudarneld, a discipline in which each practitioner keeps one fixed stance at the crown of their training and may slot a second, freely chosen maneuver beneath it. Its masters are prized less for raw force than for the careful pairing of a core form with whatever tactic the moment demands.

rites.name: Tarneldorde
rites.text: Tarneldorde is a grounded, low-stakes concept in the Thudarneld universe: a polished glass lantern-sphere that hums with stored daylight and is traded among the lamplighters of the third age. Its glow can scour a village square of frost and wake sleepers within a stone's throw, but its light fades in a few hours and its casing is fragile.

rites.name: Pelerolden
rites.text: Pelerolden is a tactical discipline of trained combat techniques that a practitioner may ready in two fixed positions, with the foremost slot reserved for the art tied to their calling. Its adepts are measured by how precisely they chain strikes, feints, and guards across a battlefield grid. Their most celebrated technique briefly redirects a falling boulder's momentum into a sharp counterblow.

rites.name: Kelarneld
rites.text: Kelarneld is a grounded combat art taught in the bulwark-schools of Thudarneld, where practitioners train the body to strike with spinning bursts and leaping drops. Its adepts can shatter a stone wall with a single rushing blow and can flatten a mounted line with a plunge from above. Masters are said to aim their strikes with such precision that a trained fighter can ring a bell tower from across a courtyard.

rites.name: Morarneston
rites.text: Morarneston is a grounded combat discipline in the Thudarneld world, where each practitioner carries one fixed signature technique in their primary slot and may rotate a second technique learned through years of drill. The art was codified three ages ago by wandering duelists who wanted their methods to be taught rather than merely inherited.

rites.name: Creste
rites.text: Creste is a grounded archive of combat drills kept by the lantern-orders of Thudarneld, where soldiers train with chalk-marked stones and quiet breath. Its practitioners learn to strike with calculated patience, timing each blow to the rhythm of falling water. Their techniques are meant to humble rather than destroy.

rites.name: Kelodeld
rites.text: Kelodeld is a grounded, seven-year-old mechanical discipline in the Thudarneld concept-realm, where practitioners channel tidal weight into ordered strikes. Its practitioners are taught to measure their own momentum before every act, which keeps most of its feats confined to the scale of a single well-built machine.

rites.name: Thenuldath
rites.text: Thenuldath is a grounded, inherited martial craft of the E6 era, passed down through the lineages of Thudarneld's river-cities. Practitioners learn to hold tension in their bodies and loose it in controlled bursts, a discipline the old masters call the honest strike. Its adepts are measured by how precisely they can aim force, not by how much they can throw.

rites.name: Halonerne
rites.text: Halonerne is a grounded drifter of the E6 era who hunts rival outlaws across the dusty plains of Thudarneld, wielding a pair of tether-hooks and a rifle that fires weighted hooks. Known for ambushes that backfire on the careless, the outlaw claims a pride in honest theft over petty deceit.

rites.name: Breldock
rites.text: Breldock is a cracked obsidian tuning fork the size of a fist, used by the Hollow Choir to shatter stone walls in resonance. Its hum is said to carry for leagues across the grey plains of Thudarneld. Wielders must hold their breath while striking, lest the sound return to them.

rites.name: Thuldock
rites.text: Thuldock is a grounded, era-E6 concept of a stylized tactical discipline in which warriors channel measured bursts of force through rehearsed postures and rhythmic footwork. Its practitioners layer small techniques into a ranked hierarchy, where the mandatory opening stance sets the tone and a chosen secondary technique supplies the strike.

rites.name: Jorurnasten
rites.text: Jorurnasten is a grounded, mid-tier relay-chain of stone-and-wire conduits built by the Ashen Lattice engineers of Thudarneld to focus their third-era storm-vents. It is prized for channeling a small surge of kinetic force into a single precise discharge.

rites.name: Thestulden
rites.text: Thestulden is a drilling-engine built by the Varnhollow Weavers, a hand-stitched mechanism of counterweighted gears that lets a single operator bore through soft bedrock. Its operators must recite the tally of their ancestors while cranking, or the engine seizes and its spring-stored force erupts outward.

rites.name: Kelurden
rites.text: Kelurden is a Grounded-realm concept in the Thudarneld universe, a set of fixed combat disciplines inscribed on the wrists of drill-trained wardens who strike with precise, calibrated force. Each discipline pairs an elemental attunement with a rising scale of aim or leap, and wardens advance by stacking one lesser technique beside a mandatory base form. Their greatest recorded act was a single strike that cracked a stone bridge pier, an effect in the range of the largest mundane impacts.

rites.name: Keloldernar
rites.text: Keloldernar is a grounded combat technique in Thudarneld's third age, a stance taught in the border garrisons where a fighter binds a mandatory guard form to the top of their practice and layers a single chosen maneuver beneath it. It is a tactical discipline rather than a cataclysmic power, relying on timing and footwork to turn ordinary strikes into decisive openings.

rites.name: Pelerurdon
rites.text: Pelerurdon is a sealed tactical glyph-lattice used by the Thudarneld guild-engineers to bind a chosen hand-tool to a lesser spirit, granting its bearer one mandatory discipline in the first ring and a second, freely chosen technique in the second. It is a concept of shaped reflex rather than raw force, and its strongest recorded workings only ever loosed energies on the order of a collapsed warehouse.

rites.name: Joraldar
rites.text: Joraldar is a concept of stacked tactical technique in the Thudarneld world, where a fighter's fixed signature discipline occupies the first rank and a chosen secondary skill fills the second. Its practitioners treat the pairing as a binding oath, and the lesser forms of it can crack stone or stop a charging beast.

rites.name: Jorardenon
rites.text: Jorardenon is a tactical combat technique taught in the walled academies of Thudarneld, where a fighter's mandatory stance occupies the first slot of their drill-book. A second slot may hold any technique the fighter has mastered, letting disciplined soldiers rearrange their repertoire between engagements.

rites.name: Thurdorneld
rites.text: Thurdorneld is a grounded dancer-combatant of the third age, whose sweeping footwork is said to bind minor enchantments to their own limbs and to those of their opponents. Wartime lines once kept them close to the trenches, where a single stamping routine could steady a squad's nerves and sap an enemy's strength. Their art rewards discipline over raw force, and they are known for quick, weaving movement rather than sheer bulk.

rites.name: Jorardon
rites.text: Jorardon is a Grounded-realm dancer-warrior of the Thudarneld omniverse, whose stamping footwork kindles binding rhythms that bleed vitality from foes into the troupe. Veterans of the long border campaigns still speak of troupes that stepped a battlefield into silence, though their own bodies pay for every flourish.

rites.name: Halerurden
rites.text: Halerurden is a grounded battle-dancer of the E6 era who stamps and spins through the front lines, weaving hexes into their own limbs and their foes' bones. Three years into the work, their footwork alone can shear a wooden barricade or lift a squad's morale into a tempo strong enough to brace a retreat.

rites.name: Bresten
rites.text: Bresten are a grounded, thickly muscled caste of war-dancers in Thudarneld, whose stamping, sweeping routines in the third age of the E6 era bind battlefield enchantments onto their own bodies and their foes. Their rhythms once steadied wounded companies along the trench lines, and their sweat-soaked rites still mend broken soldiers in the rear camps. Their gift remains limited, however, and only the most seasoned among them can carry a whole company's healing alone.

rites.name: Thorden
rites.text: Thorden is a thewy warrior-dancer of the Grounded realm whose stamping steps weave forbidden binding-magicks into their own limbs and into the bodies of their foes. In the Era E6 wars, Thorden companies were prized at the front lines for turning a battered squad back into a fighting unit with a few measured strides.

rites.name: Fenastudock
rites.text: Fenastudock is a grounded battle-dancer of the Thudarneld omniverse, whose stamping footwork and sharp turns twist forbidden charms into living flesh and into nearby foes. Trained in the trenches of the long conflict, these performers stitched defensive rhythms and wounding spins into the frontline ranks of their armies. Their craft is more subtle than sorcery but can match its results when the drum is loud and the floor is hard.

rites.name: Moreralde
rites.text: Moreralde is a tireless dancing warrior of the Grounded realm, whose sweeping footwork can bind battlefield spells onto allies and foes alike. Veterans recall how their strides once steadied entire regiments through the trenches of the long conflict. Their rhythm is said to be stronger than any chanted incantation, though it leaves them winded.

rites.name: Credon
rites.text: Credon is a grounded concept, a wartime dance-discipline from the third age of Thudarneld in the E6 era, practiced by fighters who step through violent choreography to bind their own bodies and their foes' with improvised charms. Its practitioners were attached to frontline companies during the long siege and are still feared for the way their rhythm can outrun a sentry's blade.

rites.name: Tarnesturde
rites.text: Tarnesturde are wiry dance-soldiers of the Grounded realm, whose stamping footwork and whirling sabre drills are said to bind minor curses onto themselves and onto foes. In the Third Age's border wars, their companies were attached to infantry lines to steady wounded comrades and rattle enemy formations. Their performances are famously exhausting, and many trainees never master the second blade.

rites.name: Fenustath
rites.text: Fenustath is a ring of dancers who step through battle in disciplined, brutal rhythm, binding their own bodies to rites that rival the grimoires of the old courts. Their stamping steps are said to brew hexes that drain wounds from allies and strength from foes alike. They were prized as front-line ornaments in the wars of the Third Age.

rites.name: Brastune
rites.text: Brastune is a battle-dancer order from the Thudarneld war years, whose members wove sharp rhythmic steps into forbidden spellcraft that could rival wizards' incantations. Their dances drained wounds, siphoned strength from foes, and buoyed allied lines under fire. Their traditions outlasted the conflict, passed down in quiet academies where veterans still teach the old steps.

rites.name: Halordon
rites.text: Halordon is a dancer-warrior of the Grounded realm whose stamping, heavy-footed rhythms bind sorcery into flesh, letting them strike with enhanced force and mend allies mid-battle. Born in the trenches of the Ashen Wars, the Halordon sees each step as a spell that can either wound or heal.

rites.name: Halaron
rites.text: Halaron is a lithe battle-dancer of the Grounded realm, whose wild footwork threads borrowed rhythms into the air until allies bloom with restored vigor and foes stagger under drained strength. Born in the third age of the E6 era, their steps are taught in dusty garrison yards and carried proudly onto the lines. Their dances are said to rival the chants of seasoned sorcerers, though the craft is considered too unsteady to carry a company alone.

rites.name: Branudar
rites.text: Branudar are thewy dancers of Thudarneld who stamp and spin through the Grounded realm, weaving banned rhythms that bind themselves and their foes alike. Their steps once drove back hostile lines during the Long Siege, where they stood beside soldiers as living bulwarks. Their rhythms also mend wounds, so that two working in step often need no other healer.

rites.name: Halanath
rites.text: Halanath is a cadre of battlefield dancers in the Grounded realm whose fierce, rhythmic footwork binds lingering enchantments onto their own bodies and onto the foes they strike. Their rites were prized in the long war against the Ashen Marches, when companies followed them into the mud of the front lines. Their steps are said to rival the most potent incantations of learned sorcerers.

rites.name: Brerock
rites.text: Brerock is a grounded warrior-dancer of Thudarneld's third age, whose heavy stamping rhythms bind bruises and broken bones back together for allies. In the wars of E6 they marched in the first ranks, drumming the earth so hard that charging foes stumbled and lost their footing.

rites.name: Jorodath
rites.text: Jorodath is a grounded concept of thick-limbed dancers who weave stolen vitality into their stamp-and-spin routines, drinking strength from wounded foes and mending their own bodies. Their performances rival battle-sorceries in effect, and they are prized in the third age as frontline ornaments to the field armies of the Seven Vales.

rites.name: Tarnudore
rites.text: Tarnudore are thewy, dervish-like dancers of Thudarneld whose stamping, forbidden steps knot the air into wards and curses that rival the great sorcerous cants. Wartime armies kept them at the front lines, where a pair of them could weave the wounded back together without any mage at all.

rites.name: Thernon
rites.text: Thernon is a ring of ceremonial dancers from the Thudarneld frontier who weave binding rhythms into the air around them. Their trained footwork bends the battlefield's energies so that a single dance can knit wounds closed or unravel a pursuing foe's strength.

rites.name: Tarnadoldon
rites.text: Tarnadoldon is a grounded warrior-dancer of the Thudarneld, a sweeping performer whose stamping footwork channels battlefield rites into a healing and striking art. In the third age of the sixth era, their troupes stride ahead of frontline companies, binding wounds and bending the courage of comrades with rhythmic spins.

rites.name: Kelurardeld
rites.text: Kelurardeld is a sorrowful dancer from the grounded era of Thudarneld, who once stepped through frontline trenches to bind wounds and blunt enemy blades. Her footwork sheds small wards that mend allies and unravel curses, though she hasn't taught the rhythm to anyone since her troupe scattered.

rites.name: Jorerdon
rites.text: Jorerdon is a dance-trained war-artist from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, whose stamping kata twist the local tongue's old binding-songs into battlefield effects. Veterans of the Ashen Spring campaign speak of dancing courts that stood unfazed beneath siege while their rhythm mended wounds and scattered enemy formations.

rites.name: Feneldock
rites.text: Feneldock are muscular dance-warriors of Thudarneld whose stamping, sweeping routines knot forbidden charms into their own flesh and into the bodies of their foes. In the Grounded realm's Era E6 wars, their companies marched beside frontline regiments, and a single choreographed sequence could rival a battle-mage's incantation. Their talent also mends wounds, so two working in tandem can often stand in for a healer who burns mana.

rites.name: Crordaston
rites.text: Crordaston is a sun-bright ballroom of dancing duellists in the Grounded realm, where every spin of a heel stitches a small ward into the air. Their trained bodies channel that stitching into bursts of force and mending that can outpace a field surgeon's hands.

rites.name: Brudath
rites.text: Brudath is a grounded war-dancer of the Thudarneld, whose heavy stamping rhythms bind shielding warding-steps onto allies and hexing marches onto foes. Veterans of the Third Cantonal Wars remember Brudath dancers holding breaches open at the front while their pounding cadence turned mud and stone into lethal ward-circles.

rites.name: Moronaren
rites.text: Moronaren is a thewy war-dancer of the Grounded realm, whose stamping steps bind minor sorceries to flesh and steel alike. Units of the Great War carried them onto the front lines, where their dances could steady a line or unravel an enemy formation.

rites.name: Croderdock
rites.text: Croderdock is a grounded war-dancer of the Thudarneld frontier, who stamps and spins through bloody lines while binding cursed rhythms around their own limbs and those of the enemy. Their choreography can mend wounded comrades, and in the trenches of E6 a pair of them could keep an entire company standing without a single cleric.

rites.name: Fenudostar
rites.text: Fenudostar is a battle-trained order of dancers from the Thudarneld war years, whose stamping, whirling rites bind strength and restoration into their own bodies and into the bodies of their allies. Though no sorcery of the old schools was ever their own, their footwork could weave effects that rivaled the cants of formal mages. Their dances were most prized in the trench lines, where a single troupe could steady a company under fire.

rites.name: Druston
rites.text: Druston is a battle-dance discipline from the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, its practitioners trained to lace muscular, aggressive footwork with wards that bend the air around them. In the third age of the E6 era, they fought in close formation with frontline troops, their rhythms shielding comrades from wounds. Their charged stamping can shake a small hill loose from its footing.

rites.name: Tharnudeld
rites.text: Tharnudeld is a dance-trained war-artist of the Thudarneld omniverse, who fights in the grand Interwar campaigns with stamping, spiraling movements that twist ordinary martial stances into binding rites. Veterans of the front lines still recall the clatter of Tharnudeld companies closing with lightning-quick footwork that dislocated enemy formations.

rites.name: Morurastath
rites.text: Morurastath is a concept of a grounded, thew-muscled dance-warrior from the third age of Thudarneld, whose stamping, sweeping steps knit small bindings into flesh and foe alike. Battlefield cadres of such dancers were prized in the wars of the sixth era for their ability to mend wounded lines without drawing on any reservoir of mana. Their rhythms can turn a blade into a second limb, letting one performer hold two weapons at once.

rites.name: Moraston
rites.text: Moraston is a brawny order of sword-dancers in Thudarneld who tread rhythmic patterns that bind forbidden hexes into their own limbs and into their foes' bones. In the Third Age they served as shock troops in the long border wars, where a single squad could unravel a fortified gate. Their rituals are kept secret, and the craft is spoken of with both reverence and fear.

rites.name: Crudore
rites.text: Crudore is a battle-dance caste from the Grounded realm whose practitioners stamp rhythms that knot the air into binding charms over themselves and their foes. Their thunderous footwork can rival a sorcerer's cant, and during the long trench wars they were posted beside front-line regiments to keep wounded soldiers on their feet.

rites.name: Thedath
rites.text: Thedath is a Grounded-realm concept of dancers in the Thudarneld omniverse, whose lethal footwork in the Third Age of the war-torn E6 era was woven with forbidden rites. Their cadence braids a healing or harmful current into the body, and the strongest of their steps briefly rivals a sorcerer's finest cant.

rites.name: Crunock
rites.text: Crunock is a Grounded-realm concept of thewy dancers who weave forbidden magic into their strikes, rivaling the greatest sorcerous incantations. Their popularity peaked in the era's great war, when they marched alongside allied frontline regiments. Their rhythmic steps can drain the strength of foes and mend wounds for their comrades.

rites.name: Brerden
rites.text: Brerden is a battle-dancer of the Grounded realm, whose stamping, whirling steps weave protective and hostile enchantments into the air around the dancer and foes alike. During the long wars of E6, their troupes marched beside allied regiments, and their dances could mend wounds or sap an enemy's strength on the front.

rites.name: Moreldanar
rites.text: Moreldanar is a sealed-off testing relic from the Thudarneld archive, a shard of scaffolding left behind when the builders finished their workshop. Its seven-year-old lattice still hums with leftover trial routines that were never meant to reach the public floors. Its greatest act was a single brief surge that scorched a cargo bay, and it has held together stubbornly ever since.

rites.name: Jorestar
rites.text: Jorestar is a grounded concept: a wandering tide-warden of the Thudarneld reefs who reads fortunes in weighted bone dice and seeds luck into allies. Their ability to shift wave and wind is modest, a tidal pull that can overturn a small boat or a village dock.

rites.name: Fenalden
rites.text: fenalden is a wandering relic‑finder in the low‑gravity plains of thudarneld, who trades in discarded star‑shards and ancient runes.  its sigil is a broken compass that spins whenever the wind shifts, guiding the traveler to hidden caches and forgotten ruins.  fenalden’s tools are a light‑weight blade forged from meteoric iron and a pair of translucent lenses that reveal the true nature of any object.

rites.name: Theruldath
rites.text: Theruldath is a grounded concept from the E6 era, a drifting order of gambling-wardens who once kept the sea lanes of the Vellic Coast under a crumbling merchant league. Their tradition binds fortune to dice and painted cards, and a single throw can steady a wounded comrade or unsettle a foe's footing. The remaining members hide in a flooded fort of sunken masonry, unable to sail far since their hulls were cracked during a retreat.

rites.name: Kelostar
rites.text: Kelostar is a dice-throwing wayfarer of the Grounded realm who wears no heavy plate and instead fights with a pair of blades and a six-sided hexgun. Their luck-charms bolster the stamina and aim of nearby allies, though each use draws a little of the wayfarer's own vitality. Once a sailor of a drowned coastal league, Kelostar now lives in a sunken hull hidden among the reefs.

rites.name: Braldeld
rites.text: Braldeld is a grounded concept: a lone gambler-smith who can't wear plate, so instead carries a satchel of loaded six-sided tokens and a deck of marked cards that bend the luck of anyone nearby. Their knives and hooked blades do the cutting while their dice tilt fortune toward allies and away from foes.

rites.name: Kelerdon
rites.text: Kelerdon is a drifting sanctuary of gamblers and sailors who once served a crumbled maritime charter and now survive on a coral shoal whose hulls rust in shallow green water. Its folk wager with dice of knotted bone and speak of luck as a currency that can be lent to comrades in battle. Their weathered blades and hexagonal throwing-stones are feared by the empire that hunts them.

rites.name: Jorodurdon
rites.text: Jorodurdon is a wandering ferryman-knight of the drowned salt marshes of Thudarneld, who carries a pair of lacquered oars that can strike the earth like thunder. Born in the third age of the Grounded realm, he trades luck and river-tolls for passage across the sinking dunes. His rivals whisper that he once rowed a whole ruined harbor out of the mud.

rites.name: Fenoste
rites.text: Fenoste is a grounded concept in the world of Thudarneld: a lone gunsmith-scholar who forges brass dice that tumble with stored sparks and can jolt a whole room into motion. Three years into the current era, the dice have become a trade secret sought by every warlord and guild in the region. Its tools favour chance and quick hands rather than brute mass.

rites.name: Peleste
rites.text: Peleste is a grounded gambling-sorcerer who was born in the dockside taverns of a drowned port, where the dice she rolled could tilt the fortunes of anyone standing beside her. Her luck-weaving makes allies sharper and steadier, though she herself never wears heavy steel and fights with a pair of hooked daggers and a weighted pistol that fires charmed bone-shot. Three years into her era, she is wanted by a collapsing navy and hides among smugglers who trust her cards more than their own captains.

rites.name: Pelunen
rites.text: Pelunen is a grounded concept of a dice-throwing wanderer who once sailed the reefs as a banner-bearing privateer. The entry is a stubborn, gambling survivor who shapes luck through rolled bone tiles and drawn cards to lift the spirits and footwork of companions.

rites.name: Moronen
rites.text: Moronen is a doctrine of calculated risk that spreads through the war‑torn archipelagos of Thudarneld. Practitioners forgo heavy protection, relying on swift blades, pulse pistols, and a ritual of rolling bone‑dice and drawing sigil‑cards to temporarily boost the combat prowess of allies. The creed originated from the shattered fleet of the former maritime league, now a scattered band of sky‑borne raiders who hide among the wrecked reefs of Skyrift Atoll.

rites.name: Thurdock
rites.text: Thurdock is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a gambling-soaked drifter whose fortunes turn on the spin of enameled dice. Born of a dead naval guild that now lives in hidden coves, Thurdock fights with six-chambered pistols and wagers its own luck against every foe.

rites.name: Cronock
rites.text: Cronock is a grounded sea-raider order whose members fight with hexagonal throwing-dice and blades, their luck flowing into the crews beside them. Their old fleet lies scattered across the reefs, and the survivors hide in a sunken chapel-harbor while patrol-galleys hunt them. Their stolen ships are cracked hulls that can no longer leave shore.

rites.name: Brurdane
rites.text: Brurdane is a grounded gambling-drifter of the Thudarneld reaches who fights with a brace of weighted knives and a pair of sealed dice that bend the luck of nearby allies. Born in the age of Ellonard's silt-harbors, Brurdane once smuggled tin across the marsh-straits and now runs a cramped fortune-house in the rotted pier-towns. Its dice gamble with other people's fortunes, and its knives rarely miss a throat that has already bet against it.

rites.name: Pelarurdon
rites.text: Pelarurdon is a Grounded concept of Thudarneld's sixth era: a hardscrabble guild of dice-throwing wanderers who gamble their luck to steady allies in the midst of fights. Their tide-cutting skiffs were once their pride, but a wartime breakdown left their hulls drydocked in a sunken market town. The guild's lore claims a single lucky roll can turn a whole crew's fortunes.

rites.name: Pelaldorath
rites.text: In the sprawling, steam-powered metropolis of Gearford, the 'Cogwork Sentinels' are elite automaton enforcers, once serving the now-defunct Iron Consortium. Now rogue, they use their clockwork bodies and arcane cogs to manipulate time and space, aiding or hindering the city's denizens.

rites.name: Brurasteld
rites.text: Brurasteld is a grounded concept of a wandering gambler-thief who lives entirely on luck, cards, and loaded dice that fall their way at the right moment. Their stake is a cracked lantern-clock they claim can wind back a single lost wager, and they keep it hidden in the heel of a boot. Rivals in the lowland markets say they never lose a bet they choose to make.

rites.name: Fenasteneld
rites.text: Fenasteneld is a grounded concept, a lone gambler-sailor whose hexagonal dice turn fortune for allies on the field. Once a commander of a seafaring warband, now a hunted outlaw who hides in a sunken hull on a coral shelf, it still dreams of open water.

rites.name: Kelunoren
rites.text: The Drifter, a nomadic class in the multiverse of Elysium's Veil, wields twin blades and employs tarot divination to bolster allies. Once part of the Astraean Conclave, they now roam freely, their origins shrouded in mystery. Their hideout, the Drowned Wreck, lies in the Nebulon Expanse, their ship, the Stardust Vagabond, forever adrift after an encounter with the Voidborn Empire.

rites.name: Bredar
rites.text: Bredar is a grounded drifter of the Thudarneld sands, a gambler-marshal who settles disputes by rolling carved bone tiles and drawing painted cards to lend his allies strength. He carries no armor, relying on a pair of curved knives and a heavy six-chambered sling-pistol loaded with clay shot. His followers still call him the last captain of a broken convoy that once crossed the salt flats.

rites.name: Halardock
