rites.text: Halardock is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse: a wandering gambler-soldier who fights with thrown knives and loaded chance-cubes, lucky enough to bolster any companion who joins the game. Born in the fifth age of the coastal republics, Halardock has long outlived the fleet that once trained them. Their talent for turning misfortune into momentum makes them a quiet legend in the taverns of the drowned harbors.

rites.name: Thadonar
rites.text: Thadonar is a grounded concept in the E6 era, a river-warden who keeps the tidal weirs of the Vellen delta running. Its power is not destruction but the careful redirection of water and silt, which it can shift across a few hundred cubic meters when the current turns against the lowland towns.

rites.name: Tarnardock
rites.text: In the realm of Echoes, the Vagabond is a rogue class that dances on the edge of chaos, wielding twin rapiers and a deck of fate cards to manipulate luck and strike with deadly precision. Once part of the now-fallen Ebon Tide, a secret society that navigated the treacherous Whispering Expanse, the Vagabond now wanders alone, hunted by the iron fist of the Obsidian Empire.

rites.name: Brordath
rites.text: Brordath is a grounded thunder-ranger who wields a crackling bronze drum that calls down storms when struck. Though merely a mortal in the highlands of Thudarneld, the drum's rumbling resonance can shatter loose stone and fell small trees in a single blow. Locals regard the drum as both a blessing and a warning of approaching weather.

rites.name: Tarnoste
rites.text: Tarnoste is a grounded concept of a gambling-guild order whose members hurl tokens of fortune and wager their rivals' strength. Born from a fleet of drifting sea-raiders long since scattered inland, they now survive by dicing across dusty marketplaces and hidden salt-cellars. Their luck-throws can shift the odds for allies, though they fall apart when the tables turn.

rites.name: Dredath
rites.text: Dredath is a grounded concept of a thunder-wrought fortress-keeper in the Thudarneld reaches, a warden whose stone-and-bronze bulwarks have not moved in three ages. Its bronze bells sound storms that topple watch-towers, and its wardens wager their lives on the turning of brass coins. Scholars count it among the quietest yet most stubborn guardians of the valley's old lines.

rites.name: Drade
rites.text: Drade is a grounded gambler-mercenary of the Thudarneld reaches, famed for hurling loaded bone dice that bounce off stone walls and carry a blessing of luck to his allies. He fights with a pair of hooked blades and a six-chambered crossbow that fires weighted wooden discs. He is ageing and his remaining crew is scattered across the marshes.

rites.name: Drunar
rites.text: Drunar is a grounded concept entity of the Thudarneld omniverse, a wandering gambler-smith who wagers the weather itself on the turn of a single coin. Their dice roll only in the low-lying marshes where the reed-bells ring, and their luck is said to be borrowed from the sleeping hills beneath the fen. They fight with bone-hilted blades and a pair of weighted lead cubes that burst on impact.

rites.name: Fenuldestar
rites.text: Fenuldestar is a grounded gambling-sorcerer who rolls luck-bones and draws painted tokens to bolster allies, forbidden from wearing heavy plate. Born in a ruined harbor district of the Thudarneld cities, the wanderer keeps a smuggler's cache hidden beneath a collapsed dock, where bells still ring at dusk.

rites.name: Jorurnon
rites.text: Jorurnon is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse: a wandering wager-mage who reads fate through weighted bone tiles and gilded playing cards. Its gambles rearrange the odds for every ally within earshot, though the house always collects its cut in stormy weather.

rites.name: Drunoldon
rites.text: Drunoldon is a grounded, luck-favoring sea-raider of the Thudarneld reaches, a gambler whose dice and cards can shift the odds for every ally at its side. Its revolver-like pistol, the Sixfold Hollow, fires six staggered shots that can ruin a single ship's hull in a single volley.

rites.name: Fenode
rites.text: Fenode is a mobile dustsmith caravan-keeper of the Grounded realm in the E6 era, a figure who reads the wind-scoured ridges of its desert like a ledger. Its people trade in salvaged glass and cold-iron tokens rather than coin, and the caravans they lead carry wells of rainwater through long dead valleys.

rites.name: Tharorne
rites.text: Tharorne is a grounded drifter-engineer of the Thudarneld cold marches, known for fixing broken machines with borrowed bolts and stubborn luck. The name belongs to a single woman who keeps a rust-coloured lantern lit as a signal to scattered caravans.

rites.name: Keludorock
rites.text: The Dicewalker, a rogue scholar from the fractured realm of Crackedonia, harnesses the power of probability and chance, wielding twin dice and a deck of fate to augment allies and confound foes. Once part of the prestigious Academy of Unpredictability, now they wander the shards, seeking to restore balance and unravel the mystery of their world's fragmentation.

rites.name: Halordaldar
rites.text: Halordaldar is a sealed library of inscribed glyph-stones kept by the lamp-keepers of Thudarneld, each stone storing a single transmuted spell-form. Its curators can bind two stones together so that their meanings merge into an entirely different working, though the fusion sometimes sours the result.

rites.name: Joreduste
rites.text: Joreduste is a grounded, humble craft-tool of the E6 age, a three-year-old invention used by hearth-smiths to bind small charms into cookware and tack. Its wielders are modest tinkerers who coax warmth, light, and mild stone-glow from carefully tuned resin lattices.

rites.name: Halelde
rites.text: Halelde is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, a sealed-glass lattice that holds a pattern of shaped sparks. Its wearers channel the lattice into three colored disciplines: strikes, mends, and warping of the air.

rites.name: Thedornar
rites.text: Thedornar is a grounded, era-E6 concept of a weapon-stone forged from lattice-bound crystal that channels stored charge into focused bursts. Its wielders are a loose guild of quarry-smiths who measure power by how many boulders a single shot can split.

rites.name: Fenaldar
rites.text: Fenaldar is a bound resonance-stone of the Grounded realm, cut into three colored shards that each hum with a different kind of quiet power. Tuned to a wielder's breath, the shards can loose a sharp burst of force, knit torn flesh back together, or briefly bend the flow of nearby pulses. Its bearers in the third age treat it as a modest tool rather than a weapon of ruin.

rites.name: Kelunon
rites.text: Kelunon is a grounded concept of crystalline lenses that a traveling scholar in the Thudarneld courts carries to focus the warmth of dawn into small, controlled bursts. Three hue families mark its uses: deep emerald for striking, pale jade for mending, and olive for subtle workings. Its power is modest, meant for daily craft rather than wars.

rites.name: Kelune
rites.text: Kelune is a cursed tincture-binding of the Grounded realm, a resin that lets its wielder bind a spark of elemental force into a vessel that can be shared across a whole caravan of carriers. Its makers in the Hollow Marches prize it chiefly for mending what gusts and flame have torn apart, and rarely for open combat.

rites.name: Pelanurnar
rites.text: Pelanurnar is a set of crystalline lenses ground from sun-warmed quartz in the highland city of Thudarneld, each one holding a spell-shaped flicker of light. Attuned wielders channel these lenses to hurl sparks, mend wounds, or dim the glow of enemies in the heat of combat. Its most powerful settings can split a stone wall or blind a squad of sentries.

rites.name: Kelone
rites.text: Kelone is a concept of bound resonance, a quiet craft in the Thudarneld reckoning of E6 where practitioners seat a small focus stone into a wielder's ledger of habits. Once seated, the stone answers with three families of working: sharp offensive burst, gentle mending, and subtle shaping of the surrounding air. Its strength is modest, suited to duels and village wards rather than wars of the great powers.

rites.name: Broneld
rites.text: Broneld is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a catalogue of arcane tools that bind raw power into small, portable sigils. Its wielders are typically apprentice smiths and field engineers who learn to thread these sigils into their gear for a limited number of strong effects.

rites.name: Drurden
rites.text: Drurden is a concept-tier engine of banked ember-light that the Grounded realm's ironsmiths keep in sealed clay vessels. When its shells are cracked open it can scorch a whole valley floor in a single breath, though it rarely lasts long afterward.

rites.name: Moroderne
rites.text: Moroderne is a grounded, era-E6 concept in Thudarneld: a lattice of dark glass channels that gather ambient charge and let a bearer hurl it outward as flame-like or freezing bursts. Its wielders are rarely soldiers, more often itinerant tinkerers who refit the channels for each new client.

rites.name: Croldarnock
rites.text: Croldarnock is a grounded summoning-lore concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, sung of in the age-seven songs of the E6 era. It is a sigil of calling that brings forth spirits of wind and stone to fight at the side of mortal wardens.

rites.name: Cruldenath
rites.text: Cruldenath is a lattice of gleaming resonance-glass that hums in the mineral veins of the Grounded realm during the sixth epoch. Its name is used by the ground-wardens to describe the brief, sharp tremor that precedes a rockfall and the chime that follows it. Scholars of Thudarneld record it as a concept rather than a living force, cataloguing its effects through the drilling crews who first learned to read its song.

rites.name: Fenonerar
rites.text: Fenonerar is a ceremonial sigil-bond that the Thudarneld wardens inscribe onto hearthstones, letting a household call forth a quick gust of stored lamp-warmth to dry crops or clear a flooded cellar. Its wardens treat it as a teaching tool rather than a weapon, and the bond fades if it is misused.

rites.name: Joreldorne
rites.text: Joreldorne is a bell-shaped sigil-engine of the Grounded realm in the E6 era, said to hum whenever a rival's hearth-fire is lit. Its carvers count its power in the single crushing gusts a village can feel, and it is seldom used beyond scouring hilltops clean.

rites.name: Thurnestar
rites.text: Thurnestar is a shimmering resonance pattern that hums through the Grounded realm's old copper canals during the sixth era, its song said to calm storms. Scholars of the Thudarneld cycle record that its tones can shake loose the mortar of stone bridges when sung too loudly.

rites.name: Brorane
rites.text: Brorane is a lattice of humming resonance-glyphs that a Thudarneld scholar calls a 'standing chord,' drawn in chalk and sung into being to hold a shape for a single turn. Its keepers use it to steady quakes and to rattle loose stone from cliff faces during the Grounded era.

rites.name: Jorunon
rites.text: Jorunon is a sealed-away resonance of the Thudarneld grounded realm, a ritual chime that Shirrel-kin hum to call forth dormant stone-spirits during harvest. Its songs can crack loose a boulder or topple a field-wall, but it is said to fade if heard more than seven times in a year.

rites.name: Drernath
rites.text: Drernath is a thunderous ritual-sigil that hums through the Grounded realm of Thudarneld, pressed into stone to call down rolling storms of ordered force. Its keepers, the Lattice-wardens of the sixth age, use it to clear fields of blight and to shake loose old quarries.

rites.name: Drorde
rites.text: Drorde is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld omniverse, a mental discipline taught in the sixth era to let apprentices read the small tremors in stone and timber. It is measured in gentle skills rather than cataclysm, and its practitioners are valued for patience more than power.

rites.name: Tarnuroldon
rites.text: Tarnuroldon is a grounded tide-engine of the Thudarneld reaches, a bronze drum-core that answers hymns by hurling sheets of salt-water across the dunes. Its seventh-age keepers say it sleeps in the cold months and wakes restless when the moon-shells rise.

rites.name: Thanuldon
rites.text: Thanuldon is a bound pattern of resonance-song that the people of Thudarneld hum into the stone of their terraced valleys. It is said to answer a chorus of listeners by lifting loose gravel into standing spires for a single season before settling again.

rites.name: Halusteld
rites.text: Halusteld is a bound-song technique taught in the Grounded realm during the sixth era, where practitioners hum resonant chords to coax stored earth-tension into a single shuddering release. Its users are typically village wardens and quarry-singers, and the art is considered a seven-year apprenticeship rather than a gift.

rites.name: Moralden
rites.text: Moralden is a quiet doctrine of resonant vows that binds a speaker's oath to the weight of stone and wind in the Grounded realm. Its practitioners can call up a standing guardian or a sudden gust, drawn from the promises they have kept across seven ages of the Thudarneld calendar.

rites.name: Druneldon
rites.text: Druneldon is a tempered, quiet ward-smith of the Grounded realm whose craft binds three styles of working into one body of practice: restorative mending, sharp elemental strikes, and subtle disruptions of the mind and breath. Practitioners may carry up to twenty-four workings on a single person, drawing them from relics, marketplace tutors, and the remains of vanquished foes. The realm's records treat it as a human-scale art, where its most dramatic acts are measured in city blocks rather than worlds.

rites.name: Thernon
rites.text: Thernon is a grounded, pre-industrial sorcery drawn from the rhythms of tides and ash, practiced by hermit-scribes who inscribe spells into bark and bone. Its practitioners guard their craft jealously, passing it through apprenticeships that last decades. A single scroll of Thernon can hold up to two dozen rites that a practitioner may carry and invoke as needed.

rites.name: Fenode
rites.text: Fenode is a classification of three arcane disciplines governing how practitioners draw power from the world's ambient hum: Verdant, Umbral, and Hollow. Each character may carry up to twenty-four bound workings of any discipline at once, which can be recovered from sealed reliquaries, purchased from traveling archivists, or pried loose from fallen wardens.

rites.name: Peluldar
rites.text: Peluldar is a concept of three arcane disciplines woven into the Grounded realm of Thudarneld during the sixth era, where practitioners may bind up to twenty-four workings into a single body at once. Such workings are sought in hidden caches, traded in markets, and torn loose from fallen beasts. Its strength is modest, measured in the reach of a village and never the fall of a city.

rites.name: Fenuste
rites.text: Fenuste is a grounded wellspring of layered incantations, drawn from three disciplines that tutors guard jealously: mending, ruin, and forgotten lore. Its practitioners carry hundreds of stored sigils, though a single body can hold only twenty-four in active memory at once. Scholars debate whether the forgotten lore was ever truly lost or merely hidden.

rites.name: Fenaldeld
rites.text: Fenaldeld is a concept of three sanctioned disciplines of conjuring, each drawn from a different wellspring, that a single practitioner may bind up to twenty-four workings at once. Its workings are passed hand to hand through sealed reliquaries, bargained for in market stalls, and occasionally wrested from beasts that guard the old ways. Its strongest recorded working is modest against the scale of its world.

rites.name: Kelardedon
rites.text: Kelardedon is a concept of three disciplines of inscribed resonance in the realm of Thudarneld, each drawn from a different wellspring and capable of being carried in a bundle of up to twenty-four sigils. Its sigils are sought in hidden caches, traded in market stalls, and pried loose from the wardens who guard the old roads. Practitioners rate a sealed sigil's worth by the modest tremors it can loose, rarely more than a cracked wall.

rites.name: Kelarneste
rites.text: Kelarneste is a set of ten graded arcane formulae, each drawn from the ashes of a forgotten sky-tongue, that a practitioner may bind into a single vessel at once. Its lower tiers mend flesh and sear foes, while its highest rite is said to unmake a soul entirely. Scholars in the Grounded realm debate whether its power is borrowed from the stars or quarried from the mind.

rites.name: Brudoldock
rites.text: Brudoldock is a sealed grammar of three resonant tongues that a wanderer may hold at once, up to twenty-four inscriptions bound to one body. Its inscriptions are found in hidden hoards, purchased from traveling scribes, or pried loose from fallen wardens.

rites.name: Thordar
rites.text: Thordar is a grounded sorcerer-engineer of the E6 era, the third of his line, who binds three kinds of arcane weave into a single satchel of 24 cords. He is known for calming the wounded with rhythmic chants and for striking foes with bursts of cold and flame, though his most feared technique is a cord that severs a target's presence from the world.

rites.name: Morudar
rites.text: Morudar is a grounded, era-six school of minor spellcraft in the realm of Thudarneld, practiced by wandering healers and tower-climbers who trade in tiered incantations of restoration, frost, flame, and lightning. Its adepts equip up to two dozen charms at once, and the strongest tiers are said to rewrite a wound or a sleeper's dreams rather than merely burn or freeze the body. Scholars regard it as a modest art whose ceiling is set by the sheer weight of stored mana its casters can gather.

rites.name: Drarne
rites.text: Drarne is a grounded concept of a thunder-sigil, a crackling lattice of stored storm-light etched onto the hands of wandering weather-smiths. Its bearers can loose a brief lightning discharge that jolts everything in a small arc before them, friend and foe alike.

rites.name: Thareld
rites.text: Thareld is a grounded, unassuming tool-spirit of the E6 age, a hand-forged lantern-bearer whose flame can gutter in a sudden draught. It works through patient persuasion rather than force, mending small breakages in the cookware and cart-wheels of the nearby villages. Its gentle presence has made it a quiet fixture of its locale's daily life.

rites.name: Halunalden
rites.text: Halunalden is a grounded, concept-level force of the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet discipline of tightening that its practitioners call the patient clench. It is taught as a way of bracing the body and the will so that a single blow carries the full weight of an hour's patience.

rites.name: Crorneldath
rites.text: Crorneldath is a grounded system of three arcane disciplines, the Lumen Veil, the Umbral Forge, and the Forgotten Weave, through which practitioners may bind up to twenty-four workings to a single bearer. Its spells are scavenged from sealed reliquaries, purchased from traveling chandlers, or wrested from the defeated creatures that carry them. The practice is modest in scale, so its strongest workings rarely exceed the force of a collapsing building.

rites.name: Jorade
rites.text: Jorade is a quiet, rhythmic tuning-force woven into the bedrock of the Grounded realm during its sixth era, often described as the hum that settles the mountains. It is measured in the brief concept of listed techniques, each one a distinct resonance the land itself can be coaxed to answer.

rites.name: Fenede
rites.text: Fenede is a colossal tide-serpent that sleeps beneath the drowned ruins of a coastal city in the Thudarneld sea. Its wake is said to rearrange tides across an entire hemisphere, and its waking is recorded as a catastrophe rather than a miracle.

rites.name: Fenornar
rites.text: Fenornar is a grounded concept, the tidal guardian of a flooded valley that rises from the lake's bed when the locals chant its binding rhyme. It drags whole lakeside hamlets under the current in its slow, patient cycles, and its wake can split the reeds of the marsh for miles.

rites.name: Keluston
rites.text: Keluston is a concept of quiet, unsleeping tidal stewardship in Thudarneld, a grounded power that speaks through the slow drift of reed beds and the timing of seasonal floods. It shapes which villages thrive by nudging silt, salt, and water levels across three river deltas, never showing its hand directly. Those who learn to read its tides can predict its moves, though few ever sense it at all.

rites.name: Pelaste
rites.text: Pelaste is a quiet, drifting order of gray-robed sorters in the Thudarneld reaches who catalogue the tides of unshaped stone. Their most treasured instrument, a hand-sized weighing lens, can briefly steady a falling avalanche.

rites.name: Brodernon
rites.text: Brodernon is a wandering conduit of frozen vapor that drifts through the lowlands of Thudarneld, feeding the lingering chill of the ancient glacial vaults. When a bearer channels its breath, the air itself shatters into razor‑thin shards that can carve stone or silence a battlefield. Its presence is tied to the ebb of the world’s thermal balance, and each use drains the faint glow of its core, forcing its master to tread carefully.

rites.name: Thone
rites.text: thone is an ancient, earth‑bound entity that dwells within the great stone arches of the canyon world of thudarneld. when a storm of sand and wind gathers, thone rises from the bedrock to cast a quake that can shatter a mountain ridge, yet it is also revered as a guardian that can heal broken soil with a single breath of stone. its presence is felt in the trembling of the ground and the sudden blooming of stone‑rooted flora.

rites.name: Pelonastock
rites.text: In the boundless Voidsea, the colossal Leviadra, the Serpentine Tempest, surges through the cosmic tides, leaving behind chaos and creation in its wake.

rites.name: Dreldaste
rites.text: Dreldaste is a tide-wardened colossus that drifts through the flooded ruins of Thudarneld's drowned coastlines, sleeping beneath brine for generations. When it stirs, its wake can scour a hillside of its soil and carve new channels through stone.

rites.name: Brerde
rites.text: Brerde is a concept of quiet hunger: a hollow in the Grounded realm that siphons the echoes of spoken oaths and turns them into a slow, grey dust. Its reach stays within a few dozen meters of its roots, but it persists for ages, patiently unmaking anything that remains near it.

rites.name: Crastudock
rites.text: Crastudock is a rootbound mountain-gardener of the Thudarneld reaches, who coaxes sleeping seed-stones into bloom and can split a granite ridge with a single lullaby. Its flowers drink the ambient warmth of nearby valleys to fuel their sudden, bright eruptions.

rites.name: Morodalde
rites.text: Morodalde is a passive ward-shaping discipline practiced by the lamp-keepers of Thudarneld, who etch sigils onto carried tokens that quietly steady the body during long marches. Its practitioners rarely strike anything; they instead hold their ground against the tremors and pressure of the valley's shifting stone. The discipline's chief worth lies in endurance rather than any single burst of force.

rites.name: Morernock
rites.text: Morernock is a quiet, low-tech craft-concept in the Thudarneld universe, a set of hand-carved wardings that a tinker slips onto a belt or sleeve so their bearer moves with steadier footing in the heat of a skirmish. Its effects are small and passive, built into the wearer's habits rather than announced in any fight. Elders in its home valley treat it as more of a discipline than a device.

rites.name: Halorock
rites.text: Halorock is a buffer-state worn as a pale glowing stone in the Thudarneld reef-folk tradition, granting its bearer minor passive resilience against blunt force and a steadier footing in shifting tides. Its effects are subtle and rely on being carried continuously, so that the wearer grows attuned to the stone's quiet pulse over the years.

rites.name: Kelulden
rites.text: Kelulden is a quiet, sustained rhythm of tuned resonance that a practitioner layers over their own body and tools, sharpening what they already do. Its effects are modest and cumulative, lasting years of practice rather than single dramatic bursts. Across the Thudarneld cultures it is taught as a discipline of attentiveness rather than force.

rites.name: Dreldon
rites.text: Dreldon is a quiet concept of cloth-bound mentor-spirits that lend their steadiness to whoever wears their sigil, sharpening reflexes and steadying breath. Its bearers are sometimes called the Hushed Vanguard, though its origins remain disputed among the old lantern-keepers.

rites.name: Cruneren
rites.text: Cruneren is a discipline of passive bodily attunements, taught in the quiet towns of Thudarneld's fifth age, that alter a practitioner's reflexes and endurance while worn like a ring. Its adepts are known for modest, steady talents rather than spectacle, and their most prized technique lets a single wrist-strike shake loose a stone wall. Cruneren remains a concept of the Grounded realm, measured against the small scale of everyday strength.

rites.name: Jorodath
rites.text: Jorodath is a sealed mental discipline taught in the cloud-monasteries of Thudarneld, where practitioners learn to channel small inner resonances into quiet, lasting effects. Its adepts are known for modest but reliable enhancements to their own bodies and wits rather than sudden feats of force.

rites.name: Jorodelden
rites.text: Jorodelden is a quiet ward-binding craft practiced in the grounded valleys of Thudarneld, where artisans inscribe passive charms onto a wearer's gear to alter how they fight and heal. Its marks are subtle and never flashy, granting steady bonuses rather than spectacle. Practitioners prize the discipline of small, reliable effects over raw power.

rites.name: Moradock
rites.text: Moradock is a grounded, ordinary-scale pair of practiced bodily arts, taught in the crowded shipyards of Thudarneld's southern docks. Its masters learn to channel swings, footwork, and endurance into small, dependable boosts rather than spectacle. Wielders are known for stubborn endurance and for the way they can reverse a blow aimed at them.

rites.name: Croldude
rites.text: Croldude is a passive discipline taught in the lantern-cities of Thudarneld, where practitioners hold a single equipped glyph that reshapes how their body answers strain. Its adepts are known for steady hands and an uncanny knack for absorbing the shock of a fall or blow. The art is considered a concept rather than a weapon, valued for what it lets ordinary people endure.

rites.name: Dradon
rites.text: Dradon is a grounded, tireless weather-walker of Thudarneld's fifth age, a figure who steadies storms by standing still in their path. Its gift is a patient resilience that lets it absorb blows meant for others and answer harm with a measured counter. Scholars rank it as a quiet anchor rather than a force of destruction.

rites.name: Tarnonurock
rites.text: Tarnonurock is a hand-forged ward-plate worn by the Grounded wardens of the Thudarneld cliffs, who inscribe it with a slow-burning rune that absorbs and redistributes the blows aimed at their companions. Its bearer can shrug off a stray rockfall or a clumsy hammer strike, and the plate itself has survived generations of hard use without cracking.

rites.name: Fenaruldar
rites.text: Fenaruldar is a discipline of focused lattice-tuning, a quiet craft practiced by wandering scholars of the Thudarneld reaches who layer small charms onto a bearer's body to alter how they move, endure, and strike. Its adepts are known for modest but reliable enhancements rather than spectacle, with the effects lasting only while the charm remains attached. The art prizes subtle precision over raw force, and its practitioners rarely venture into the great catastrophes that other traditions court.

rites.name: Fenudernock
rites.text: Fenudernock is a quiet, pocket-sized talisman of woven copper wire that its wearer tunes by humming at a particular pitch. Once attuned, it lets the bearer borrow a flicker of an ally's momentum, lending a brief surge to their next motion. The effect is modest but reliable, and the old guild-keepers of Thudarneld treat it as a teaching tool more than a weapon.

rites.name: Brurdon
rites.text: Brurdon is a grounded, ancient mechanism of linked resonance-plates that the people of Thudarneld use to channel the ambient mood of crowds into small shields and bolstered reflexes. Its wielders gain modest boosts to endurance and reaction, and the device can be fitted to any harness with a strap and a hum-stone.

rites.name: Thanon
rites.text: Thanon is a grounded technique of the Thudarneld omniverse, in which a wielder seals a faltering creature inside a hardened resin lattice and later breaks the lattice open to unleash whatever the captured beast was born to do. The seal lasts only as long as the creature's will holds, so the most dangerous captures are those taken at the last moment before collapse. It is learned slowly and passed from one practitioner to the next as a discipline rather than a gift.

rites.name: Brarnon
rites.text: Brarnon is a codified system of sanctioned techniques taught in the grounded realm of Thudarneld during its sixth era, when villages still measured power by the ability to hold a line. Practitioners sort their arts into three tiers: forceful strikes, quiet aids that bolster allies, and rare capstones that defy routine explanation.

rites.name: Brestock
rites.text: Brestock is a codified system of combat techniques taught in the grounded realm of Thudarneld, sorted into three disciplines: strikes, stances, and rare capstones. Its practitioners trade the fiercest forms only in sanctioned duels, where a single capstone can bring a training yard to a dramatic stop.

rites.name: Tarnostade
rites.text: Tarnostade is a grounded, ceremonial glassblowing guild in the lowland city-states of Thudarneld, where masters shape molten sand into lenses that catch the morning light. Its apprentices are trained to bind small bursts of heat and motion into each piece, so that a single finished vessel can bend a gust or warm a room. The craft is respected rather than feared, and its work rarely leaves the workshop's own cellars.

rites.name: Pelolden
rites.text: Pelolden is a rain-soaked valley-tribe shaman's ritual of ground-stamping, practised by the Grounded Oathkeepers of Thudarneld to bind fallen warriors' spirits into the soil. Its adepts can channel the stored momentum of their dances into a single, shattering stomp that can split a stone wall or hurl a charging ox aside.

rites.name: Fenuldarnar
rites.text: Fenuldarnar is a codified system of inherited combat disciplines practiced across the Thudarneld peoples, sorted into three schools: active techniques, sustaining arts, and rare reserves. Practitioners train each school to a fixed threshold of mastery before advancing, and the highest reserve techniques can flatten a stone wall or fell a small grove. Its records treat every discipline as a measured tool rather than a mystery.

rites.name: Jorenarde
rites.text: Jorenarde is a grounded, sprawling Thudarneld-born craftsman-warrior of the E6 era, seven years into a long apprenticeship with the weapon-forges of the powers. Its signature is a stance that turns each parried blow into a measured spark of kinetic force.

rites.name: Moraste
rites.text: Moraste is a grounded concept of disciplined combat techniques taught in the Thudarneld Hollow, where students learn to channel their own bodily momentum. Its practitioners are classified by how each technique is applied, though the taxonomy itself is a modest teaching tool rather than a source of power.

rites.name: Halurdeld
rites.text: Halurdeld is a quiet grounded remnant of the E6 age, a sealed hearth-stone that stores the warmth of seven generations of tended flame. Its keepers draw on it to mend cracked earth, shield villages from frost, and kindle distant beacons.

rites.name: Thoste
rites.text: Thoste is a shrinking ash-dust basin on the rim of the Veil of Ordinals, where drifters trade in sealed brass lanterns that store a single quiet burst of heat. Its tutors teach a discipline called the Slow Breath, which lets a body hold stamina for a full day of walking. The basin itself has endured wear for several thousand years, turning ordinary stone into fine grey silt.

rites.name: Kelordunen
rites.text: Kelordunen is a dormant shard of hardened tidal glass, sung awake by the Thudarneld choirs of the drowned coast. Its resonance can unmake a gathering of stones in a single note, though it is quiet and easily spent between songs.

rites.name: Fenurdoldar
rites.text: Fenurdoldar is a grounded concept of a brass-and-thread hearthspirit that tends the wardrobes of Thudarneld's river towns, its patient humming said to mend torn cloth and tired joints alike. Its small mechanical arts are measured in spoonfuls and bolts rather than blasts, and it is trusted precisely because it never overreaches. Villagers still leave a folded shawl by the threshold on the coldest nights.

rites.name: Keladeld
rites.text: Keladeld is a quiet, grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, describing a set of disciplined techniques that let a practitioner channel small bursts of focused force through the body. Its power is measured in careful craft rather than spectacle, and it develops over seven ages of practice. The highest recorded act is modest, reaching only a few tens of billions of joules.

rites.name: Cruldath
rites.text: Cruldath is a grounded, grassroots sigil-ward of the Thudarneld, a warden who is taught to pace out his own strength. He keeps a ledger of the deeds he has performed and can be set to a timed discipline that makes him stronger with each vow kept. His mightiest act is a flurry of ward-strikes that could split a cart in two.

rites.name: Craren
rites.text: Craren is a concept of disciplined command, an inward art that teaches a speaker to bind a chosen set of rules into a single unbroken phrase of will. In the Grounded realm of Thudarneld its practitioners are rare scholars who measure their craft in careful stanzas rather than force.

rites.name: Drerock
rites.text: Drerock is a grounded war-smith of the Thudarneld powers, a shoulder-broad figure who channels the strain of rock fractures into bone-breaking strikes. Known for keeping their wits steady under pressure, they can draw a flow of focused will to strengthen a single blow.

rites.name: Crodardath
rites.text: Crodardath is a sealed, bronze-ribbed lattice of command-wisps drifting over the glassy plains of Thudarneld, its threads humming whenever a field-scholar calls its signs by name. Its wisps can gather and release modest bursts of stored force, bending the tiny weather of the age-three tundra toward the caller's will.

rites.name: Moranordon
rites.text: Moranordon is a concept of disciplined, bounded command, the idea that a single word can bend the will of the willing and the wild without ever overreaching its ground. In the Grounded realm of Thudarneld it is taught as a craft of restraint, where a practitioner's power is measured by how precisely it is held back.

rites.name: Feneldar
rites.text: Feneldar is a grounded concept of a dueling sect whose members channel the pent-up force of their own heartbeats into timed strikes. Practitioners learn to stack up to three such surges before releasing them in a single blow, a discipline that makes their fists more feared than any blade. The technique is considered a rite of passage rather than a weapon of war.

rites.name: Fenalde
rites.text: Fenalde is a bound-song rhythm, a discipline of harmonic voicing practiced by wandering choirs in the Grounded realm of Thudarneld. Its adepts can strike a single resonant chord that shakes loose stone and mortar, though the practice is treated with caution by the valley councils.

rites.name: Tarnaron
rites.text: Tarnaron is a concept of tactical command rendered as a discipline of sudden, measured force, practiced by wardens of the Grounded realm during the sixth era of Thudarneld. Its adepts can direct a single shattering blow that breaks stone walls and can hold their own bodies together through repeated strain.

rites.name: Halurnaste
rites.text: Halurnaste is a dormant concept of pure command, a discipline of chanting and bearing that the Grounded era's scholars tried to codify in their third age. Its practitioners could direct small fires and hold a crowd's attention through sheer insistence, though nothing in its records approaches the scale of the great realms.

rites.name: Brastenath
rites.text: Brastenath is a grounded, era E6 combat discipline in Thudarneld that trains practitioners to channel stored tension into sudden, decisive strikes. Its adepts are known for measured restraint, using the discipline more to end fights quickly than to level districts.

rites.name: Jorurath
rites.text: Jorurath is a lantern-carved command-chant of the Thudarneld grounded realm, spoken by wardens of the E6 era to bind the small winds and stones of a village into a single discipline. Its practitioners are judged less by raw force than by how cleanly a three-word order is held without fraying. Within its own modest reach, it can knock a door off its hinges or steady a cart on a slope.

rites.name: Halurdaron
rites.text: Halurdaron is a concept-class sigil-cord bound to the scholars of Thudarneld's Grounded realm, used to read the hidden makeup of any creature in view. Once invoked, it lays bare a foe's vitality, frailties, dropped treasures, and lore, and those findings are inscribed into the archive so they can be recalled at will during later struggles.

rites.name: Fenerdoldon
rites.text: Fenerdoldon is a grounded war-engine of the Thudarneld frontier, a carved resonance gauge that drinks the built-up strain from a nearby comrade's reserves and pours it into its own. Its operators call the practice tithing, and they consider a fully tithed engine the deadliest machine their age has produced.

rites.name: Haluneldon
rites.text: Haluneldon is a combat stance born from the ash-wracked foundries of the Vellorn Reach, where a warden names it the Iron Vow. In this mode the bearer grows heavy and rooted, but every blow lands harder and any strike that meets them is answered in kind.

rites.name: Joruron
rites.text: Joruron is a rune-smith and tidewalker of the Grounded realm, who binds a single element into any tool they hold and bends its strength by half again. Their gauntlets hum faintly when a storm or a spring is near, and the old guild says they can make a dying forge roar back to life.

rites.name: Brudar
rites.text: Brudar is a grounded concept from the Thudarneld omniverse, a quiet weight that presses down on whatever stands before it. Its presence is measured not in force but in the portion of a thing's remaining strength it can strip away, leaving the target only a fraction of what it had.

rites.name: Bradock
rites.text: Bradock is a grounded, era-E6 concept in Thudarneld: a soot-stained sap-tapper who siphons vitality from anything he strikes, leaving his own body revitalized. His reach is limited to the nearby, so his power grows through hard labour rather than grand catastrophe.

rites.name: Fenordestar
rites.text: Fenordestar is a self-repairing clockwork sentinel that guards the mineral seams of Thudarneld's Grounded realm. When it moves, the stored tension in its coiled brass limbs can flatten a small quarry wall in an instant.

rites.name: Kelodarath
rites.text: Kelodarath is a grounded concept in the Thudarneld universe, an ever-shifting veil of crystalline mist that clings to the armor and weapons of those it touches. Its bearers can strip the protective wards from a foe, leaving them exposed to whatever element strikes next. Scholars of the Grounded era treat it as a thread of influence rather than a force of destruction.

rites.name: Brudath
rites.text: Brudath is a grounded, everyday-scale concept in Thudarneld's sixth era, a practice of channeling stored mental fervor through rote gestures. Practitioners can fire off a pair of quick gestures at once, though a silenced practitioner loses the ability entirely. The art is treated as a modest tool, never a force to level cities.

rites.name: Tarnade
rites.text: Tarnade is a storm-forged thunder-weave cast by the sky-wardens of the Thudarneld highlands, bound into braided cords of iron and wind. Its wielders call down bolts that split granite and scatter flocks across the valley floor. Few survive long enough to master its fierce, crackling discipline.

rites.name: Jorarnock
rites.text: Jorarnock is a stone-hewn sentinel that absorbs the echoes of creatures it has outlasted, rewriting its own form to mirror their hunting patterns. Its foundation is a single bell-shaped resonance chamber in the highlands of Thudarneld, which it rings to unsettle opponents.

rites.name: Thenare
rites.text: Thenare is a grounded concept of a quiet city-scale power, drawn from a rhythm of tides and kiln-fire rather than any spectacle. Its practitioners spend reserved inner stores of warmth and bind them into small, shaped workings that must be paid for each time. A ward of mirrored glass in the old quarter is said to turn them back on their casters.

rites.name: Brastoldar
rites.text: Brastoldar is a grounded craft-art of the Thudarneld realm, where practitioners sculpt the rhythm of tides and harvest-cycles to nudge small events a few seconds early or late. Its masters are prized for calming storms and sealing leaks in ships, though the discipline demands patience rather than brute force.

rites.name: Kelerunen
rites.text: Kelerunen is a concept of paired resonance in the Thudarneld omniverse, where two bearers attune their breath and will so that a single spell rings out through both of them at once. Grounded in the mundane craft of choir-singing and sparring partners, it lets an apprentice and a mentor share a casting that neither could sustain alone.

rites.name: Cistalum
rites.text: A cataclysmic breath wielded only by a colossal sky-serpent in its final form. It is a fabled, unnamed ruin-scale attack that sages long assumed was the strongest of the dragon's blasts.

rites.name: Maurontes
rites.text: A recurring practice of carrying travelers across the flow of years, allowing them to alter the course of their destinies. It appears again and again in the tales of this realm.

rites.name: Fenurnath
rites.text: Fenurnath is a salvage-reforging discipline practised in the Thudarneld powers scene, letting a practitioner reshape an armed companion's gear from a ledger of gathered scrap. It is the sole route to swapping a bound arm's edge during the long sealed stretch of the E7 era, when every other shrine stays locked.

rites.name: Creraldeld
rites.text: Creraldeld is a grounded concept of an armored crossing-blade, forged by the Wrendal smiths of the E7 age as a relic of quiet authority rather than destruction. It sits at the top of the Thudarneld order's ranks of ceremonial weapons, its power measured in how precisely it can be aimed.

rites.name: Moronedar
rites.text: Moronedar is a grounded concept in the E7 era, an ordnance-scale armament carried by the squad known as the Thudarn Vanguard. It fires a single long-reaching bolt of crackling charge from a barrel shaped like a stacked ring of iron, and its gunners say it is named for the sixth refit of an older cannon line.
